1-4-billion-year-old-mushroom-fossil-in-: An intact fossil of a mushroom about 1.4 billion years old was found in northeastern Brazil, according to Michels. He says this himself, without naming a source, in an episode about mushrooms, where it serves to show how ancient fungi are.
101-year-old-recalls-a-giant-graveyard-f: A man who was 101 years old recalled that, in the 1920s or 1930s, men ploughing land for a vineyard near a nuraghe, one of the ancient stone towers of Sardinia, suddenly began digging up the remains of gigantic people. He said a group of vans then pulled up, people got out carrying equipment, and he hid; they took the remains away, and a passage in the tower was sealed. Tim Alberino, a guest who looks into stories of ancient giants, passes this on, crediting a person named Anna Tuary, and tells it twice, adding the vans and the sealed passage the second time, as a sign that evidence of giants was found and removed.
111-and-222-synchronicities-during-the-r: During a 2026 trip in Texas that reunited Air Force veterans who say they were abducted by aliens fifty years earlier, the numbers 111 and 222 kept turning up: one traveller landed at 1:11, and a man named Omar, from the YouTube channel Yes Theory, took off at 1:11. Michels tells this himself, from the trip, as a string of meaningful coincidences. He presents them as a sign that the reunion felt somehow guided.
13-year-old-corbell-hears-knapp-s-lazar-: The filmmaker Jeremy Corbell says that around 1990, at 13 years old, he heard the journalist George Knapp interviewing a man named Bob Lazar on the radio. Corbell tells it as his own memory, "I heard George Knapp's voice interviewing a guy named Bob Lazar on the radio," and gives it as the moment that started his lifelong interest in UFOs and his later work with both men.
15th-16th-century-explorers-accounts-of-: European explorers of the 1400s and 1500s are said to have reported seeing cities in the Amazon rainforest, and later research is said to have backed their stories up. Michels raises this himself while talking with the writer Graham Hancock. He says these explorers' accounts drove Hancock's research and that Hancock then confirmed them, which would mean large lost settlements once stood in the jungle.
17-days-of-drone-swarms-over-langley-202: In 2023, the story goes, swarms of unknown drones flew over Langley Air Force Base in Hampton, Virginia, for 17 days in a row. Michels tells this several times on his own. In one telling he says "we have no defense against this" and repeats a claim by Chris Mellon that there may have been a mothership. The former fighter pilot Ryan Graves adds that the base houses F-22 fighter jets, and that they were moved to another base for fear of losing them. A news anchor, in a clip played on the show, reports that Air Force officials confirmed several unmanned drones flew over the base "last December," but the clip gives no 17-day figure. If true, it would mean unknown craft could fly freely over one of the country's key fighter bases.
170-odd-q-cleared-witnesses-of-ufos-at-s: About 170 people holding Q clearance, the US security clearance for access to nuclear secrets, are said to have seen UFOs around America's most sensitive sites, and in some cases the objects are said to have shut those sites down. Michels raises this himself, in passing and without naming a source, while talking with the journalist Ross Coulthart. If true, it would mean unknown objects have been able to interfere with US nuclear facilities.
1800-case-balls-of-light-come-out-of-the: In a case from the year 1800, balls of light are said to have risen out of the sea, hovered beside a ship, followed it, and then shot off into the clouds. The researcher Kevin Knuth describes it to Michels without naming where the account comes from. He tells it to show that sightings like this go back long before modern times.
1890s-airship-mystery-and-nymza-per-walt: In the 1890s, people across the United States reported mysterious airships in the sky. A researcher named Walter Bosley, a friend of a Dr. Joseph P. Farrell, ties those sightings to a group he calls NYMZA. Salvatore Pais, a Navy scientist who holds patents on unusual craft designs, brings this up in passing without explaining what the group was. He says the idea worries him and asks who these people really were, since it would mean someone was flying craft in secret long before anyone was supposed to be able to.
1890s-airship-sightings-as-a-culturally-: In the 1890s, people reported seeing airships that were right at the edge of what the technology of the time could do, and Michels uses this to suggest that strange sightings take the shape of whatever the era is about to invent. He tells it in his own words in one episode. In another he credits the idea to the psychiatrist John Mack, and frames it as UFOs inspiring or foreshadowing technology that was just about to arrive.
19-non-negotiable-demands-to-change-the-: In 1996, the makers of Dark Skies, a television series about a hidden alien presence, were handed "a list of 19 non-negotiable demands" for changes to their first episode before Don Ohlmeyer, a senior executive at the NBC network, stepped in. The television writer Bryce Zabel, who made the show with a writer named Brent Friedman, tells this from his own experience, in a talk that also touches on the filmmaker Steven Spielberg, as part of a story about how much control others had over a UFO drama on network TV.
1904-chilean-cattle-mutilations: In 1904, a series of cattle mutilations, cases where cattle are found dead with parts of their bodies cut away, is said to have happened in Chile. Michels brings it up as something he was told by a man named Chris Ramsay, calling it "like this Chilean cattle mutilation series." If true, it would put such cases decades before the ones usually talked about.
1911-superconductor-discovery-as-a-model: In 1911 a physicist named Onnes found that some materials, when cooled, carry electricity with no resistance at all, something then thought impossible, and that this came from strange quantum effects acting across the whole material. A researcher named Deep Prasad draws a lesson from it on Jesse Michels's show in 2022, without naming a source: when anything seems to break the laws of physics, it is probably an emergent effect of hidden quantum behaviour. He uses this as a model for UAPs, unidentified flying objects, suggesting their strange movements might be explained the same way.
1918-us-expeditionary-force-into-russia: In 1918 the United States paid for and sent a full military expedition into Russia, according to the lawyer Dan Sheehan. He tells it as background without naming a source, linking it to Robert Lansing, the US secretary of state of the time, to show how far back hidden American foreign actions go.
1930s-homesteader-accounts-of-cattle-mut: Strange cattle mutilations and other odd happenings were reported on Skinwalker Ranch, a property in Utah, as far back as the 1930s, by the first families who settled there. Brandon Fugal, the ranch's owner, says his team's research turned up these old accounts, though he does not name the sources. He tells it to show that the strange activity on the ranch goes back long before anyone famous was looking at it.
1934-plot-to-overthrow-fdr-via-general-s: In 1934, according to a guest named Dan Sheehan, a group tried to recruit General Smedley Butler, a former commandant of the US Marine Corps, to lead an uprising of war veterans against President Franklin Roosevelt's government. Sheehan passes it on as something he was told. If it were true, it would mean a plot to overthrow an American president from inside the country.
1941-fbi-vetting-of-silas-newton: A government file from July 1, 1941 vouched for Silas Newton, a man tied to the story of a flying saucer said to have crashed at Aztec, New Mexico. The file is from the FBI, the US federal police agency, and it says he "appears to be a good American citizen, has no accent in his speech." Michels reads this from the FBI files, alongside a book called It Came to Earth at Aztec and the work of the researchers Scott Ramsey and Suzanne Ramsey, as something that bears on whether Newton can be believed.
1942-fbi-file-laurel-canyon-address-norf: A 1942 file kept by the FBI, the US federal police, on the inventor Townsend Brown shows him living in Laurel Canyon in Los Angeles, on Wonderland Boulevard, and Michels says it may hold a clue to his secret life, with threads leading to Norfolk, Virginia, and to compromising material that could be used for blackmail. Michels tells this himself in his documentary on Brown, whom he calls a CIA scientist who built UFOs, drawing on Brown's biographer Paul Schatzkin and the physicist Paul LaViolette.
1944-press-reports-of-silver-spheres-ove: In 1944, during the Second World War, the press reported strange silver balls seen in the sky over Germany. The writer Marik von Rennenkampff points to two of these reports: a Newsweek article from 1944 called "The Silver Sphere Puzzle", and an Associated Press news wire story from Christmas Day 1944 headlined "Balls of silver seen over the German Reich intrigue science." He brings them up to show that odd objects were being reported in the papers years before the modern UFO era.
1945-state-department-document-on-nazi-l: By 1945, according to a researcher named Jason Simosa, the US State Department, the government's foreign affairs office, had noticed a wave of new companies tied to Nazi Germany appearing in Latin America. He describes a State Department document from that year saying that "hundreds of new companies have been set up in Nicaragua and Argentina". Simosa summarises it in a discussion that draws on the writer Peter Levenda, and he raises it to suggest that Nazi money and people found new homes abroad after the war.
1945-trinity-crash-as-the-source-of-a-la: In the summer of 1945, a craft is said to have crashed near the Trinity site in New Mexico, the nuclear test ground, and Michels says a "larger piece" of recovered material came from that crash. The fullest version comes from Jacques Vallée, a veteran UFO researcher, who passes on what Paola Harris, Remy Baca and Jose Padilla told him and what appears in the book Trinity: The Best-Kept Secret. He places it at San Antonio, New Mexico, and says the witnesses looked through a missing panel and saw "three creatures" that were "human-like" with "two eyes." Michels, who calls it Vallée's new book in 2022, dates the crash to August 17, 1945, and elsewhere says it came 20 days after the July 1945 test. In another episode, though, he puts it in 1948 as one of a run of crashes near nuclear sites. A researcher named Jason Jorjani, working from Vallée's book, says the Mexican witnesses described the beings as looking like praying mantises, and an unnamed witness heard on the same episode describes them as bald, with "slang eyes, teardrop eyes, no ears." A guest named Marik von Rennenkampff, crediting Vallée and someone named DD Johnson, is more careful: "There was a crash there. Unclear." The story matters to them because it would tie the earliest crash to the first atomic test.
1946-military-search-of-swedish-lakes-fo: In 1946, during the wave of "ghost rockets", unexplained rocket-like objects reported in the skies over Sweden that year, the Swedish military reportedly searched the bottoms of several lakes around the country for crashed objects. A researcher named Clas Svahn tells it, without naming a source, and says that "all they found were indentations at the bottom." If true, it would mean something hit the lakes but nothing was ever recovered.
1947-national-security-act-and-majestic-: The National Security Act of 1947 created the US Air Force, the CIA and the National Security Council, the President's top security body. The researcher Dylan Borland goes over this on Michels's show without naming a source and asks how closely Majestic 12, a secret group said to handle UFO matters, was tied into that council. If true, the UFO secret would sit inside the structures set up that very year.
1949-battellewright-field-contract-on-ti: In 1949, a private research organisation called the Battelle Memorial Institute is said to have had a contract with Wright Field, an Air Force base in Ohio that later became Wright-Patterson, to study alloys of nickel and titanium, the family of metals that later gave Nitinol, a metal that springs back to its shape. Michels tells this himself on two episodes, without naming a source, and points out that Wright Field is where wreckage from the reported 1947 crash near Roswell, New Mexico, was rumoured to have been taken. He tells it because, if the timing holds, it would suggest the research was prompted by that wreckage.
1949-green-fireball-meeting-at-los-alamo: In 1949, at the Los Alamos weapons laboratory in New Mexico, the physicist Edward Teller and the meteor expert Lincoln LaPaz both took part in a meeting about the "green fireball problem", bright green lights seen in the skies over New Mexico at the time. Michels tells this himself, pointing to a 1949 document from the meeting that has both men's names on it. He raises it because it shows a top weapons scientist was involved in studying the lights.
1950s-anti-gravity-research-went-quiet-p: In the 1950s, the story goes, there were groups researching anti-gravity, ways to cancel or control gravity, and then they suddenly went quiet. The physicist and researcher Hal Puthoff, speaking in general terms, offers two readings: either "nobody ever got anywhere," or "it did get somewhere and it went black," meaning it vanished into secret, classified government work. A guest named David Grusch, appearing as a witness and passing on what he was told, says the anti-gravity groups lasted "up until the early sixties" and then "totally vaporized." If the second reading is right, a working breakthrough on gravity could have been hidden away for decades.
1950s-ffrdcs-and-a-program-to-dole-out-r: In the 1950s the US government set up FFRDCs, research centers paid for by the government but run by outside organisations, and Jesse Michels wonders whether there was also a program at the time to hand out retrieved material, meaning material from crashed unknown craft, to these places. He suggests, without naming a source, that such material could have sped up and inspired new technology. He raises it in a 2026 conversation with a researcher who goes by UAP Gerb, linking it to an Army officer named Philip J. Corso.
1950s-flying-butane-tanks-in-air-force-o: In the 1950s, reports from the Air Force's criminal investigations office described photos of what looked like flying butane tanks, and David Grusch, a former Air Force intelligence officer, says these were the same kind of thing as the Tic Tac, the white oval object shaped like the mint that Navy pilots reported in recent years. He tells Michels that "the tic tac of today was the flying butane tank photo of the 1950s," passing on what he was told about those old files. If so, the military has been seeing the same objects for some seventy years.
1950s-gravity-research-by-bryce-dewitt-d: Back in the 1950s, the physicist Bryce DeWitt was writing about superconductivity and about spinning superconductors that might disturb gravity, alongside work by the physicists Stanley Deser and Richard Arnowitt. Michels brings this up himself, without naming a source, as a sign that serious scientists were looking at ways to control gravity decades ago, which would matter if such work later went secret.
1950s-underground-bunker-under-secret-mo: The journalist Ross Coulthart says he is in "no doubt whatsoever" that a deep underground military bunker was built in the 1950s under Secret Mountain, near Sedona in Arizona. That would put a hidden military site, possibly tied to UFOs, in the Arizona desert. The first time he tells it, he credits two people named Jeremiah Hostetler and Alexandra Hostetler. When he repeats it on a later episode, he names no sources.
1952-h-bomb-test-as-a-signal-to-the-cosm: The 1952 hydrogen bomb test in the Pacific may have been heard by someone or something watching Earth, and taken as a sign that humans were nearly ready to travel out and visit, says the mathematician Eric Weinstein, offering it as his own worry rather than from any source. In another telling he says the signal was that we were close to "God-like knowledge," and Michels repeats it secondhand as a signal that we were close to "root level knowledge." If true, it would explain why visitors might take an interest in us after that date.
1952-mit-lincoln-lab-audio-of-dod-saucer: There is said to be a real audio recording from 1952 of a senior official from the Department of Defense, the US military's headquarters, briefing scientists about flying saucers at Lincoln Laboratory, a research lab run by the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. A US congressman named Eric Burlison says "we found out" about the file, first placing it in the 1940s and then correcting himself to 1952. If so, it would show the military briefing top scientists on saucers early on.
1952-official-denial-of-secret-developme: In 1952, during a wave of UFO sightings over Washington, D.C., a US official told the public that "the recent sightings are in no way connected with any secret development by any department of the United States." The official is not named in the episode where the statement is played. It matters because it rules out the most common explanation, secret American aircraft, for what people were seeing.
1952-washington-d-c-sightings: In July 1952, waves of unexplained lights and objects are said to have appeared over Washington, D.C., the US capital. Jesse Michels gives the dates as July 19 and 20 and July 26 and 27. He says the sightings set off newspaper headlines like "saucers on the White House lawn" and sent the CIA into a frenzy over how to handle the UFO problem. He also says they prompted a call from President Harry Truman to Edward J. Ruppelt, then head of Blue Book, the US Air Force's UFO study of the 1950s and 60s, and he credits that detail to the aviation journalist Curtis Peebles. A former government official named Karl Nell says the objects showed up on radar and to the eye over two weekends, that jets tried to intercept them, and that it led to the biggest press conference since the Second World War. Bob Maguire, who worked as a CIA contractor, passes on that Truman "lost his lunch over it", and the physicist John Brandenburg mentions it briefly. Michels says he recently met one of the last living witnesses. If it happened as they say, UFOs once flew over the seat of American power in full view.
1952-washington-dc-flyover: In 1952, unexplained objects are said to have flown over Washington DC, and the papers ran headlines about flying saucers over the White House lawn. Michels brings it up himself in passing during a conversation with a congressman, as a moment when the subject reached the front pages.
1953-kingman-crash-and-upshot-knothole: A craft is said to have crashed near Kingman, Arizona, in 1953, possibly knocked down by American nuclear testing. A researcher who goes by the online name UAPGerb says testimonies point to the crash, and that the nuclear tests of Operation Upshot-Knothole, a series of US atomic bomb tests that year, may have "messed with" the craft. The UFO historian Richard Dolan says only that there is "no question in my mind that Kingman was the real thing," crediting the researcher Raymond Fowler. Dolan says nothing about the bomb tests bringing it down. If true, it would mean nuclear blasts can disrupt such craft.
1954-atomic-energy-act-moved-craft-custo: An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb tells Michels he thinks a recovered craft was moved in 1954. His reason is that the Atomic Energy Act of that year gave new powers to laboratories that the government owns but private companies run, such as Sandia, so they could house it. If he is right, that would explain where crashed hardware ended up. The act, passed by Congress on 30 August 1954, does let the Atomic Energy Commission hire others "to produce special nuclear material in facilities owned by the Commission". It says nothing about housing a craft, and it names no laboratory.
1956-montgolfier-vacuum-tests-in-paris: In 1956, the inventor Townsend Brown is said to have tested his devices in a vacuum at the Montgolfier facility in Paris. Michels tells it, drawing on a writer named Paul Schatzkin and a document he calls the Montgolfier report: a French Air Force officer named Jean-Louis Cornillon, "technical representative for one of France's largest aircraft companies, Sud Aviation," arranged the experiments. If true, it would mean a major French aircraft maker took Brown's work seriously enough to test it.
1957-afghanistan-ufo-event-reported-to-w: A declassified government document sent to Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, the Air Force base where UFO reports were studied, describes a UFO event in Afghanistan in 1957. Michels says he found it himself while looking into whether Henry Kissinger oversaw a program to recover crashed UFOs. He offers it as proof that the US government was collecting UFO reports from far beyond its own borders.
1957-ufos-head-toward-eisenhower-s-summe: In 1957 a UFO is said to have flown toward the summer home of President Dwight Eisenhower. Michels tells this himself, crediting a UFO researcher named Brad Sparks, who he says "thoroughly documented" it. Michels also mentions Chris Mellon, a former Pentagon intelligence official, and records from NORAD, the North American air defense command, and from Blue Book, the US Air Force's UFO study of the 1950s and 60s. If true, it would mean an unknown craft headed straight for the president.
1960s-nasa-electrostatic-accidents-spin-: In the 1960s at Kennedy Space Center in Florida, static electricity is said to have caused deadly accidents: one set off a solid rocket by mistake and trapped 11 people inside a spin test facility, with some killed, and the fire in the Apollo moon programme is counted as another. A NASA scientist named Charles Buhler tells this, passing on what he learned inside the agency, and says NASA has lost about 14 people to electrostatics in all. He tells it to show how powerful and dangerous electric charge can be, which matters to his own work on propulsion.
1960s-patent-for-nuclear-powered-tunneli: The UFO campaigner Steven Greer says his archive holds "the actual 1960s patent for a nuclear-powered tunneling device", which he connects to the engineering company Bechtel. In his story, machines like this dug hidden underground links between secret military sites in the American West, such as the Area 51 base in Nevada, and between Washington and the Virginia mountains. Greer tells it himself as something he holds the paper for, and it would mean a secret tunnel network was built decades ago.
1963-f8-atlas-missile-tracked-by-a-tagal: In 1963 an Atlas missile, an American long-range nuclear rocket, was launched from Vandenberg Air Force Base in California and followed in flight by an unknown object tagging along beside it. Michels tells this himself and says it is even written in the official report, which he does not name. If true, it would mean something unexplained was shadowing US nuclear missile tests.
1964-nickel-found-in-drill-site: A nickel dated 1964 was recently brought up from a drill site on the mesa at Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property known for strange reports, according to the ranch's owner, who took part in the work and mentions a man named Chris Roberts in telling it. The owner raises it as one more odd find in the ground there, an old coin turning up where drilling is going on.
1970s-flanagan-samples-find-calcium-sulf: Calcium sulfate salt inside the Queen's Chamber and Grand Gallery of the Great Pyramid at Giza comes from dilute sulfuric acid reacting with the chambers' limestone, according to a pyramid researcher named Geoffrey Drumm, who reads this as a sign that a chemical process once ran inside the pyramid. He takes the finding from samples analysed in the 1970s by a man named Richard Flanigan, as reported in the writer Christopher Dunn's book The Giza Power Plant. He adds pock marks he says he saw himself on recent tours.
1970s-muon-scan-of-the-central-pyramid: In the 1970s, scientists scanned the middle pyramid at Giza using muons, tiny particles from space that pass through rock and can reveal hidden empty spaces. Jeffrey Drum, a researcher, tells Jesse Michels he has the paper on this scan with him. He later says the physicist Luis Alvarez was part of the team, and that they scanned a room called the Belzoni chamber and the area above it. According to Drum, they found nothing there, a point he raises while discussing what may lie inside and beneath the pyramids.
1972-rand-very-high-speed-transit-system: In 1972 the RAND Corporation, a US research organisation that does studies for the military and government, wrote a theoretical study of a very high-speed transit system. An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb lists it on the show, without naming a source, among a run of documents he says hint at advanced propulsion work going on behind the scenes.
197374-radar-station-crew-see-a-cigar-sh: In 1973 or 1974, the crew of a mountain radar station in the far north of Sweden are said to have seen a cigar-shaped object. The Swedish UFO researcher Clas Svahn tells it from his own interviews, saying he spoke with six people at the station. If true, it would be a sighting by trained military radar staff.
1974-coyame-crash-and-cia-directed-retri: The story is that in 1974 an unknown craft crashed near Coyame in Mexico, and that the United States quietly went in and took it. Michels tells it from a report that he says leaked in the 1990s. In that version the object collided with something in mid-air, "the whole Mexican team ends up dead," and the object "is airlifted out by US forces." An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb calls it a favourite of his, while admitting "there's not a ton of supporting evidence." He describes a document called the DEB report as a plan directed by the CIA, the kind an "OGA," or other government agency, would draw up to gather rapid reaction teams and equipment to go and collect the craft. In another episode he mentions Coyame alongside the Majestic documents, papers said to come from a secret UFO group, and says toxic material has sometimes leaked out of crash sites. Neither teller says they took part. Both sum up documents they have read, and if those documents are real, they would show a US crash recovery operation run outside its own borders.
1974-film-ufos-past-present-and-future: In 1974 came UFOs: Past, Present and Future, which Michels calls the leading UFO documentary of its time. In one episode, talking with the historian Richard Dolan, Michels frames it as a turning point. It came after Blue Book, the US Air Force's UFO study of the 1950s and 60s, and after the Condon Committee report, a university study for the Air Force that played UFOs down, and in 1974 someone he does not clearly name "seems to flip." In a later episode he adds that the TV writer Rod Serling, his own father's godfather, produced the film, something he says he had not known.
1975-norad-report-of-ufos-over-malmstrom: In 1975, according to a report from NORAD, the joint US and Canadian air defence command, UFOs were seen again over the nuclear missile sites at Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. Robert Salas, a former Air Force missile officer, brings up the report, saying "there is a NORAD report of UFO sightings again over Malmstrom missile bases," as proof that strange objects kept coming back to the nuclear weapons.
1975-nuclear-base-incursions-cable-to-th: In 1975, unknown objects intruded over US nuclear weapons bases, says the researcher Marik von Rennenkampff, and a military cable, a formal message sent to the Pentagon, recorded the incidents. He urges Michels to read the cable for himself and mentions John Greenewald Jr., a man known for collecting government records. If true, it would mean the military itself wrote down unexplained visits to its most sensitive sites.
1980-object-sank-in-a-northern-swedish-l: In 1980, the researcher Clas Svahn says, an object landed and then sank in a lake called Damaya in a national park in the far north of Sweden. Svahn says his group has been to the lake and picked up radar readings that show something lying in the mud at the bottom. If that is right, the object might still be down there.
1980s-physicists-wormhole-billiard-ball-: In the 1980s, physicists who became interested in wormholes, imagined shortcuts through space and time, worked out the math of a billiard ball going through one and running into its own past self. According to Eric Wargo, a writer on precognition, they found that the ball's path could always come out self-consistent. He brings it up without naming a source, as a sign that sending things back in time need not create paradoxes.
1980s-shift-from-secrecy-to-flooding-the: The idea is that sometime in the 1980s the United States changed how it handled the UFO question. It moved from keeping secrets and denying everything to "flooding the zone", burying the subject under so much noise that the truth gets lost. Michels offers this as his own sense of things, in an episode with the UFO writer Richard Dolan, and if it were true it would mean the confusion around UFOs was partly made on purpose.
1980s-spinning-gyroscope-mass-loss-paper: In the 1980s, some papers reported that a spinning gyroscope, a fast-turning wheel, lost some of its mass when certain electrical and other components were applied to it. A researcher named Dave Rossi mentions these papers on Jesse Michels's show in 2025, without naming them, and says this kind of work went private from the late 1970s. If true, it would point to a way of weakening gravity's pull on an object.
1981-black-sea-exercise-sighting-cameras: In 1981, during military exercises on the Black Sea, "several dozen unidentified craft flew in directly," and people photographed them with simple cameras, according to a former president of a Russian republic who says he was there. As the story goes, the cameras were then taken away and the people present signed promises to keep it secret. That would mean the Soviet military saw a mass sighting and covered it up.
1982-dream-of-2060-flying-cia-ufos-after: In a dream he had in 1982, a former chief at the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency, named Rolf Mowatt-Larssen says he saw himself in the year 2060, travelling with UFOs through a world already ruined by "the great nuclear war of 2034." Mowatt-Larssen tells it as his own memory of what he calls "the chameleon dream of the future," in which he was "going back and forth" in an apocalypse. Taken as he tells it, the dream would be a glimpse of a coming war.
1984-string-theory-takeover-the-only-gam: In 1984, after a mathematical breakthrough in string theory known as the Green Schwarz anomaly cancellation, the physicist Ed Witten steered the whole field of theoretical physics to bet everything on string theory, according to the researcher Eric Weinstein. Weinstein tells it himself without naming a source, saying Witten, the son of the physicist Lewis Witten, "directs the entire field uh to put its energies on one bet," and he also names the physicist Richard Feynman. He tells it to argue that physics narrowed itself into a single "only game in town."
1985-night-encounter-my-god-bugs: One night in 1985, at his cabin in upstate New York, the writer Whitley Strieber says he came face to face with strange beings, and his first thought was "my god, bugs." Strieber tells it as his own experience, the one he wrote about in his book Communion. If true, he met nonhuman beings in his own home.
1987-new-science-encyclopedia-diagram-of: A 1987 reference book called the New Science Encyclopedia is said to show a diagram, based on the Pioneer 10 and 11 space probes, of a large object far beyond the planets, about 50 billion miles away and labeled with "equal gravitational pull." Matt LaCroix, a researcher of ancient history, describes it, calls the object a dead binary star, credits the astronomers Thomas Van Flandern and Robert Harrington, and at one point dates the book to 1983 rather than 1987. If true, it would mean a hidden companion star sits at the edge of our solar system.
1988-resume-to-teller-leads-to-eg-g-and-: In 1988, when he decided to go back into science, Bob Lazar sent his resume to the physicist Edward Teller and asked him about a job. Lazar is a man who says he later worked on alien craft at S-4, a secret site in the Nevada desert, and he tells the resume part himself, saying he never met Teller again. Michels goes further: he says Teller got Lazar his job with EG&G, a defense contractor, and that there is now too much evidence to dismiss this, which would tie a famous government scientist to Lazar's hiring. In a later episode the host mentions the EG&G job in passing and places it around 1989.
1988-saic-anti-gravity-study-for-edwards: In 1988 a corporation known as SAIC was hired to study electric propulsion and anti-gravity, meaning ways to fly by cancelling or pushing against gravity, for Edwards Air Force Base, a US Air Force base in California. Michels tells this himself in his documentary on the inventor Townsend Brown, naming James Woodward and Ferris Williams in connection with the study. He raises it to show that the military was still quietly looking into anti-gravity decades after Brown's work.
1990-air-force-low-voltage-vacuum-test-o: In 1990 the US Air Force tested the Biefeld-Brown effect in a vacuum, Michels says. This is the claim, tied to the inventor Townsend Brown, that a high voltage across a device can make it push itself along. Michels tells it himself, without naming a source, and his point is that the test used only 19,000 volts, far below the millions of volts Brown worked with, so it may not have been a fair check.
1990s-drilling-near-the-sphinx-overseen-: In the 1990s, drilling was done near the Sphinx in Giza, Egypt, to find out whether there was a hidden room there, and the Egyptian archaeologist Zahi Hawass was in charge of it. A researcher named Luke Caverns says this to Michels without naming a source. He raises it because it would mean someone has already looked for chambers under the Sphinx.
1990s-magazine-expose-on-assets-moved-fr: In the 1990s, a magazine ran a big exposé claiming that secret things kept at Area 51, a hidden US Air Force test site in Nevada, may have been moved to a new place called "Area 52" at Dugway, a military testing ground in Utah. An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb remembers the story from memory and is not sure whether it ran in Popular Science or Popular Mechanics. He brings it up as a hint that the most secret work may have left the famous base for a quieter one.
1990s-meeting-of-eg-g-head-greer-dick-d-: In the 1990s, a meeting was set up between one of the heads of EG&G, a defence contractor, the UFO activist Steven Greer, a congressional staffer named Dick D'Amato and another man, Alfred O'Donnell, and at that meeting UFOs were taken off the table. UAPGerb, an online researcher, relays this from what others have said, crediting the journalist George Knapp. If true, it would mean people tied to defence contracting steered officials away from the subject.
1991-azores-case: In 1991, something is said to have been seen off the Azores, islands in the Atlantic Ocean. Steven Greer, a campaigner for UFO disclosure, mentions it only in passing, "1991 off the Azores," as one case from the book Disclosure: An Illustrated History. He gives it as one example among many sightings he says governments have kept quiet.
1991-bob-lazar-video-on-gravity-wave-a-a: A 1991 video shows Bob Lazar, a man who has said he worked on recovered craft in Nevada, explaining two kinds of gravity he called gravity wave A and gravity wave B. The researcher Eric Weinstein says the podcaster Joe Rogan pointed him to it, and that at first it looked like "this guy Bob Lazar seemingly talking nonsense." He brings it up because, if the ideas meant something, Lazar would have been describing real physics behind such craft.
1991-paper-on-technology-assisted-consci: The UFO researcher Steven Greer says that in 1991 he wrote a paper about what he calls technology-assisted consciousness, the idea that machines can link up with the mind, and that it went "all through the aerospace industry and CIA," the US spy agency. He tells it first-hand, saying the paper is part of what put him "on the radar" of powerful people.
1991-radio-caller-underground-work-along: In 1991 a caller to a Las Vegas radio show said he had been hired to run electricity 3,000 feet underground at a Nevada test site, through Reynolds Electronics, a subsidiary of the defense contractor EG&G, and that military personnel there were working alongside beings that looked like aliens. Michels tells this himself, in an episode with a NASA doctor, as something from the record of that broadcast, without naming the caller. If true, it would mean the government is working with non-human beings underground.
1992-torr-and-li-superconductor-paper: A guest named Dave Rossi describes a 1992 paper by the physicists Douglas Torr and Ning Li which, he says, showed that a quantum property of spin in superconductors, materials that carry electricity with no resistance, sits in the gaps of the material's crystal structure and not in the paired electrons that carry the current. Rossi sums up the paper himself without naming another source. He brings it up because, to him, it points toward unusual physics that could matter for exotic propulsion.
1994-air-force-holographic-projector-con: In 1994 the US Air Force is said to have looked at an idea for a holographic projector, a device that could make images appear in the air. Michels tells this himself, drawing on a 1999 article by the reporter William Arkin. He raises it because such a device could, in principle, produce things in the sky that people might take for real craft.
1994-nellis-tonopah-range-video: A video is said to have been filmed in 1994 over the Nellis and Tonopah range in Nevada, a restricted stretch of military airspace used for testing aircraft and weapons. Michels brings it up himself, without naming a source, in an episode where he challenged a UFO skeptic named Mick West to a debate, stressing that this is closed testing airspace and that Nellis is famous. The point of raising it is that something strange caught on film in such a guarded place would be hard to dismiss as ordinary traffic.
1996-sighting-of-a-round-craft-over-the-: In 1996, a round craft was seen over a military site called Fua outside Stockholm, Sweden. It looked like a hot dog when seen from one angle, according to the treasure hunter Dennis Asberg, who says he saw it himself after waking unusually early that day for a reason he still doesn't understand. He mentions a Swedish UFO group called UFO Sweden in connection with it, and he tells it as a first-hand sign that something unknown was flying over a military base.
1997-contact-10-000-people-paid-10-milli: In 1997 in Washington, someone told Steven Greer that at least 10,000 people had each been paid $10 million or more to make sure they cooperated with a hidden effort. Greer, who says he was there, repeats the line on the show as he says he heard it: "We have given at least 10,000 people $10 million each or more to secure their cooperation with what we're doing." If it were true, it would mean that secrecy about UFOs has been bought on a huge scale.
1997-greer-briefing-with-admiral-wilson: In 1997, in Washington DC, a man named Steven Greer is said to have held a briefing on UFO matters with a Navy admiral named Thomas R. Wilson, joined by two other men, Willard Miller and Stephen Lovekin. An online researcher who goes by the name UAPGerb mentions the meeting in passing, without naming a source. It matters to those who tell it because it would mean a senior military officer was directly approached about secret UFO knowledge.
1997-unod-declaring-the-programs-illegal: In 1997, Steven Greer, who campaigns for the release of government UFO secrets, says he and his group issued an "unless otherwise directed" memo that would treat the secret UFO programmes as illegal unless officials ordered otherwise. Greer tells Michels he did it himself and says, "I put a I think a two or three month clock on it." He presents it as a way of forcing officials to act on the programmes or answer for them.
1998-remote-viewing-of-the-world-s-futur: In 1998, a former Army sergeant named Lyn Buchanan says, he was given the job of using remote viewing, a practice of trying to perceive distant places or times with the mind alone, to look at the future of the United States. He tells Michels that the session grew into a view of the whole world's future, all the way up to the year 2050. If true, it would mean a trained viewer was asked to look decades ahead, and says he did.
1999-paper-when-disclosure-serves-secrec: The UFO campaigner Steven Greer says he wrote a paper in 1999 called When Disclosure Serves Secrecy, and he tells Michels to "go look it up". Disclosure here means the government revealing what it knows about UFOs. Greer tells it about his own work and does not say on the show what the paper argues, though the title suggests that a public reveal can be used to keep the real secrets hidden.
19th-century-baron-trump-time-travel-boo: In the 1800s, there were books called The Adventures of Baron Trump about a boy named Baron Trump and his time-traveling adventures with a figure Michels calls Don. Michels brings them up himself, without naming a source. He first places them vaguely in the 19th century, and in a later episode he dates them to the 1890s, pointing to the names as an odd echo of Donald Trump and his son Barron.
2-a-m-buzzing-and-knocks-in-florida-home: Years after earlier strange events, the author Peter Levenda says he was at home in Florida at about two in the morning when he heard buzzing and knocking in the house. Levenda tells it as something that happened to him, and he brings it up alongside the writer Whitley Strieber, who is known for his own accounts of night-time visitors.
20-second-ufo-sighting-the-same-day-2016: A dramatic UFO sighting lasting about twenty seconds happened right in front of a group at Skinwalker Ranch in Utah, on a day sometime after 2016. That is how Brandon Fugal, the property's owner, tells it, as something he saw himself. He gives it as proof that the ranch is a place where strange things really show up.
200-mainstream-scientists-want-to-study-: More than 200 mainstream scientists are now said to want to study UFOs and the strange events around them. Chris Bledsoe, a man who says UFOs appear around him and whom scientists have studied, tells this, passing on what he was told by a doctor named Anna Brady-Estevez. If true, it would mean the subject is moving from the fringe into ordinary science.
200-watchers-swear-an-oath-on-mount-herm: Two hundred fallen angels called the Watchers are said to have come down onto the top of Mount Hermon and bound themselves together there with an oath. A researcher named Tim Alberino tells this from the Book of Enoch, an ancient religious text that is not in most Bibles, which he reads in R. H. Charles's English translation alongside Genesis 6. In his words, "they bound themselves on the summit of Mount Hermon," and he tells it as the start of a story about beings who came down from above and mixed with humans.
2003-nasa-patent-for-an-asymmetric-barre: Michels says NASA holds a patent on an asymmetric, barrel-shaped capacitor, a device that stores electric charge, from its Marshall Space Flight Center in Alabama, and links it to the inventor Thomas Townsend Brown, whose electric-charge ideas he ties to antigravity flight. He tells it from the patent and a Guardian newspaper article, but his own tellings differ: once he dates it to 2003 and names a scientist called Larry Smalley, at another time to 2004 under a senior engineer named John Campbell. If true, it would mean NASA quietly pursued Brown's ideas.
2004-carrier-encounter-drop-from-81-000-: In 2004, off California, an aircraft carrier group is said to have tracked a craft at about 81,000 feet, over 15 miles up. When planes were sent up and their instruments began to pick it up, it dropped to 24 inches above the water in under a second. Charlie Foltz tells this on Michels's show, passing on what someone he names told him, as a sign of motion no known aircraft can match.
2006-raytheon-atflir-patent-and-gimbal-r: A patent filed around 2006 by the defence company Raytheon, for a camera and targeting pod on Navy jets known as ATFLIR, is said to explain why the object in Gimbal, a Navy video of an unidentified object that appears to rotate, seems to turn. The UFO skeptic Mick West brings the patent up himself, saying "this was uh a patent from I believe 2006." If he is right, the rotation would come from the camera's own movement rather than the object.
2007-firestonewest-paper-on-the-younger-: In 2007, the scientists Richard Firestone, Allen West, George Howard and others published a paper proposing that a cosmic impact set off the Younger Dryas, a sudden cold spell near the end of the last ice age. The researcher Randall Carlson describes the paper in his own words. He tells it because, if true, it would mean a disaster from space reshaped the world early humans lived in.
2007-national-press-club-event-with-inte: In 2007, at the National Press Club in Washington, a well-known meeting hall for journalists, a group of officials and military figures from several countries spoke in public about UFOs. The UFO investigator and filmmaker James Fox says he and the journalist Leslie Kean put the event on together, and he names Parviz Jafari, an Iranian fighter pilot, among the people tied to it. Fox tells it as someone who helped organise it, and it matters to him because it put officials from around the world on record.
200k-funded-fifth-dimension-gravity-theo: The physicist John Brandenburg says an unnamed government funder paid about $200,000 for his theory that gravity is tied to a fifth dimension. He tells it from his own experience: when he handed in his report, he says, they told him, "Thank you, Dr. Brandenburg. Here's your check. Don't let the door hit you when you go out of the building," and nothing more came of it.
2011-irkutsk-mass-ufo-sighting: In 2011, Russia's main state television station, Channel 1, aired a report on what was said to be a mass UFO sighting in the Irkutsk region of southeastern Siberia. Michels tells it from that broadcast, bringing it up in an episode about strange three-fingered bodies found in Peru.
2013-white-house-rumours-of-confirmation: In early 2013, rumours from the White House said the government was planning something called "confirmation, not disclosure": admitting the phenomenon is real without revealing everything about it. A researcher named Jason Simosa says this is recorded in the latest published journals of Jacques Vallée, a scientist who has studied UFOs for decades, where Vallée writes down the rumours he heard. Simosa raises it as a sign that a limited, managed admission was being planned from the top.
2016-trip-with-tyler-and-garry-nolan: In 2016, the religion scholar Diana Pasulka travelled to a crash retrieval site in New Mexico, a place where an unknown craft is said to have come down, and her book American Cosmic opens with that trip. She tells it as something she took part in. In the book she had to hide her companions under false names: one she calls Tyler, and the other, she says, has since come forward as a man named Garry Nolan.
2017-disclosure-as-a-managed-release-of-: The 2017 release of UFO information to the public, which came through a New York Times story, was a careful plan to give out only some of what the US government knew. A US congressman named Eric Burlison says so on Michels's show in July 2026, calling it "their attempt of trying to compartmentalize what they could release without giving away our good tech." If he is right, the release was shaped to protect secret American technology.
2017-new-york-times-article-as-a-new-pro: The 2017 New York Times article by the journalists Leslie Kean and Ralph Blumenthal, which revealed a secret Pentagon program that looked into UFOs and featured the former official Luis Elizondo, struck the writer Greg Bishop as the start of a new project that was using the UFO subject for its own ends. Bishop says this was his reaction when he first read it, without naming a source, which would mean the famous story was itself a managed move rather than a simple leak.
2017-release-of-three-ufo-videos-to-the-: In 2017, Michels says, Luis Elizondo, who ran a small Pentagon office that studied unexplained aerial reports, tried to brief Defense Secretary Jim Mattis on UFOs and was blocked by officials in between. So Elizondo and his friend Christopher Mellon, a former deputy assistant secretary of defense for intelligence, went off script and got three UFO videos cleared for public release by the Pentagon. They brought the videos to the journalist Leslie Kean, and they ran in the New York Times, a source people trusted. Michels names them: the Tic Tac, after a white oval object shaped like the mint, along with Go Fast and Gimbal. He stresses that Navy intelligence had never before admitted the videos were real. A lawyer named Dan Sheehan says the release was fully authorized, cleared by the Defense Department's Office of Prepublication and Security Review, the office that approves material for publication, and dates the front-page story to December 17, 2017. The skeptic Michael Shermer tells it differently, as the moment the government said UAPs, its term for UFOs, are real and Elizondo repeated that the government says so. Either way, it is told as the moment official footage of unknown objects went public.
2017-revelations-of-osap-ufo-study-group: In 2017, Michels says, it came out that government UFO study groups existed, and he ties them to something he calls OSAP, though he does not spell out what that is. He mentions it in passing, without naming a source, as part of the wave of UFO news that year.
2019-aiaa-scitech-presentation-slides-4-: Salvatore Pais, a Navy scientist known for patents on unusual craft, points listeners to slides 4 to 9 of a talk he gave at the 2019 SciTech conference of the American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics, a professional body for aerospace engineers. He says those slides lay out the ideas behind his work. If so, the core of his claims is already on the public record.
2019-decision-with-corrado-malanga-to-sc: In 2019, the scientist Filippo Biondi and his friend Corrado Malanga decided to try to scan the inside of the Great Pyramid of Khufu at Giza in Egypt. Biondi tells Michels this himself and, in a later episode, says the scan was done in 2020 using radar from the second-generation Italian Cosmo-SkyMed satellites, work written up in a paper on finding "undiscovered high-resolution internal structures" in the pyramid. If the method works as he says, it would show hidden structures inside and beneath the pyramid without digging.
2020-pan-starrs-object-turns-out-to-be-a: In September 2020, Pan-STARRS, a telescope survey that scans the sky for moving objects, found an object in space that was as baffling as an earlier strange visitor, and it turned out to be a booster rocket left over from a NASA launch in 1966. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, in an episode with the Harvard astronomer Avi Loeb, as an example of how hard it can be to tell human junk from something stranger.
2022-scans-finding-hidden-chambers-in-th: In 2022, scans of the Great Pyramid of Giza in Egypt found hidden chambers beneath it, according to a researcher named Jay Anderson. He says this on Jesse Michels's show in 2025, without naming who did the scans or where he read it, as a sign that the pyramid still holds secrets.
2023-marco-leal-interview-inconsistency-: A surgeon named Italo Venturelli, from the hospital in Varginha, Brazil, where a creature is said to have been treated, says people who caught gaps in an interview he gave in 2023 to a man named Marco Leal are "right because I couldn't tell everything even in 2023". He tells this himself to Michels, and links it to what he later told the UFO filmmaker James Fox about the hospital's intensive care unit. If true, it would mean he held back part of the story for years and only told more of it later.
2024-egyptian-japanese-radar-survey-find: In 2024, a team of Egyptian and Japanese researchers is said to have found an L-shaped structure underground in the western cemetery next to the Great Pyramid of Giza. Michels describes the survey himself: the team used ground-penetrating radar, which sends radio waves into the earth, and electrical resistivity tomography, which maps what lies below by passing electric current through the ground. He brings it up as a sign that more may be hidden under the site than is known.
2024-law-protecting-icig-whistleblowers-: A 2024 law passed by the US Congress is said to protect whistleblowers who go to the inspector general of the intelligence community, a watchdog office over US spy agencies, so they cannot be prosecuted for espionage if they reveal secrets of the CIA or the Department of Energy. A whistleblower named Dylan Borland describes the law without naming a source, saying such people "are not allowed to be prosecuted for espionage." If true, it would make it safer for insiders to speak about hidden programmes.
2025-jfk-files-release-and-trump-s-answe: After the 2025 release of the files on President John F. Kennedy's assassination, President Donald Trump was asked directly who killed Kennedy. Michels says, in his own telling, that Trump answered only that they had released the files and done "a historic thing", as if the release were the answer. The National Archives' own notice of 18 March 2025 says that, on Trump's order of the day before, "all records previously withheld for classification" in the Kennedy collection were released, and "without redactions".
22-000-year-old-footprints-in-north-amer: Human footprints in North America are said to be more than 20,000 years old, much older than people were long thought to have arrived. The author Graham Hancock says they are in New Mexico, 23,000 years old, mixed with tracks of mammoths, giant sloths and other extinct Ice Age animals, and that they have been properly dated; Michels repeats it as 22,000 years, from Hancock's TV series Ancient Apocalypse. If true, it would push back the story of people in the Americas by thousands of years.
23-year-us-remote-viewing-program-1972: The United States is said to have run a remote viewing program, an effort to use people who claimed they could describe distant places or targets with only their minds, for 23 years, from about 1972 to 1995. Michels tells this himself in two episodes. In one he argues that if the program lasted that long, covert versions probably still exist today. In the other he names it Stargate, says the CIA, the US spy agency, put this kind of work to use through it, credits a remote viewer named Joe McMoneagle, and suggests the program may still be running. If true, it would mean the government took psychic spying seriously enough to fund it for decades.
30-missiles-lost-to-ufo-activity-1966-67: Between September 1966 and March 1967, the story goes, US Air Force nuclear missile bases lost 30 missiles to UFO activity, meaning the weapons were knocked out of action while strange objects were around. If true, unknown craft were able to switch off part of America's nuclear force. Robert Salas, a former Air Force officer, tells it in the same words in two episodes: "we lost 30 missiles to UFO activity." In one he names Minot and Malmstrom Air Force Bases. In the other, an episode where he speaks as someone who was there, he places the losses at Malmstrom. Michels repeats the same figure in a separate episode. He credits the researcher Bob Hastings and his book UFOs and Nukes. So the account comes from a man who served at the bases and from a host passing on a researcher's work.
36-people-who-say-they-flew-the-craft-uf: Thirty-six people came to the UFO researcher and author Grant Cameron and told him they had flown the craft, meaning UFOs. Cameron says he gathered their accounts in his book UFO Sky Pods, and in one telling to Michels he adds that these people came to him "mysteriously." If their stories hold, humans would already be piloting these vehicles.
3i-atlas-anomalous-composition-2025: 3I/ATLAS, an object from outside our solar system that was seen passing through in 2025, appears to contain nickel without the iron that normally goes with it. The researcher Kevin Knuth says this, drawing on the astronomer Avi Loeb, and explains that in nature the two metals are usually found together. If that is right, the object's makeup would be very unusual for a natural rock.
40-meter-metallic-object-in-the-labyrint: Deep in an underground labyrinth in Egypt, beneath the ancient site of Hawara, there is said to be a metallic object 40 meters long and shaped like a Tic Tac, a white oval like the mint, which Michels calls "a UFO." Michels raises it in several episodes, crediting a researcher named Ben van Kerkwijk, a scan report and a blog post about the scan, and a researcher named Jeffrey Drum, and he notes that the ancient writers Herodotus and Pliny the Elder described the labyrinth. The comedian and podcaster Joe Rogan repeats it second hand from van Kerkwijk, calling it "the 40 meter metallic object that's shaped like a tic tac."
40-people-told-icig-of-reverse-engineeri: Some 40 people have allegedly gone to the Inspector General of the Intelligence Community, the official watchdog that takes complaints from inside US spy agencies, and said they took part in a secret program to reverse-engineer unknown technology, meaning to take it apart and copy it. Michels raises this himself, without naming a source, during a debate with the UFO skeptic Mick West. His point is that you would have to be very strange to make that claim to such an office if it were not true.
4602nd-monthly-report-s-ufo-b-section-19: In the 1950s, says the researcher Scott Ramsey, the 4602nd, an Air Force intelligence unit, kept a section called UFO B in its monthly report that counted how many UFOs had been seen. Ramsey describes the reports himself without naming a source. If true, it would show that the military was tracking UFO sightings as routine business.
4602nd-squadron-history-on-reassuring-th: In the 1950s, a US Air Force intelligence unit called the 4602nd Air Intelligence Service Squadron is said to have written in its own official history that part of its job was calming the public about UFOs. Michels quotes the document directly: the aim was "reassuring the public mind that no tangible evidence existed to support the fears of an invasion from outer space." He brings it up because it suggests the unit's goal was reassurance, not just investigation.
4chan-whistleblower-a-decade-working-on-: An anonymous poster on 4chan, an online message board, claimed to have spent about a decade working on crash retrievals, the recovery of crashed craft of unknown origin, in the late 1990s and early 2000s. Chris Ramsay, a YouTube creator, passes this on to Jesse Michels from the whistleblower's thread, without being sure of the exact details. If true, it would mean secret recovery work on such craft went on for years.
4chan-whistleblower-fewer-bodies-found-i: The YouTuber Chris Ramsay passes on a claim from an anonymous self-described insider who posted on 4chan, an anonymous online message board, that crashed craft recovered in recent years contain a lot fewer bodies than before. Ramsay relays it from the poster's thread, as a hint that whoever flies the craft has changed.
4chan-whistleblower-hamburger-shaped-mot: An anonymous person on 4chan, an online message board where anyone can post without a name, claimed to be a whistleblower and said that UFOs are built to order for specific jobs. The online researcher UAPGerb repeats one version, pointing to the post and to a name, Chris Ramsay. In his telling, there are places in the Bahamas that house "that large hamburger shaped mother ship that 3D prints UFOs to spec." UAPGerb adds "if that 4chan whistleblower is to be believed." Michels gives his own version in an episode with a treasure hunter named Dennis Asberg. He says the poster claimed these UFOs are "built to spec," made for set purposes, and that they sit on the ocean floor. His telling does not mention the hamburger shape or the Bahamas. The tellers raise it because, if true, it would mean a factory for craft is hidden under the sea not far from the United States.
4chan-whistleblower-higher-ups-think-the: An anonymous poster on 4chan, an anonymous online message board, claimed to be a government insider and said that people high up believe the visitors simply do not care about humans and treat Earth like a zoo. The online video maker Chris Ramsay passes this on to Michels, quoting the poster: "they just don't care about us... It's more like a zoo." If true, it would mean whatever is here watches us without any real interest in our affairs.
4chan-whistleblower-nukes-jets-and-boats: An anonymous whistleblower posting on 4chan, an anonymous online message board, claimed that the military has gone after an unknown craft in the ocean near the Bahamas with nuclear weapons fired from submarines, with jets and with boats, and that none of them came back. A YouTube creator named Chris Ramsay relays the post, quoting the poster: "We've sent nukes after it like on submarines. We've sent jets. We've scrambled like boats. Like none of them come back."
4chan-whistleblower-orange-light-orbs-sc: Orange lights in the sky are scanning for minerals or living things, and if one comes up close to you, you have likely been abducted or soon will be. This is what an anonymous whistleblower wrote on 4chan, an online message board, as Chris Ramsay, a YouTube creator, relays it to Jesse Michels. It would mean these lights are surveying Earth and its people on purpose.
4chan-whistleblower-underwater-mobile-co: An anonymous poster on 4chan, an online message board where users do not give their names, claimed his job had been to monitor huge underwater "mobile construction units" on the ocean floor near the Bahamas and the Bermuda Triangle, which were said to be building unidentified craft. The YouTuber Chris Ramsay retells the post on the show. If true, something would be building craft under the sea.
536542-ad-darkness-and-cooling-linked-to: From 536 to 542 AD, people in Europe are said to have gone weeks and months at a time without seeing the sun, a dark, cold spell blamed on volcanoes or on dust from a comet. Randall Carlson, a researcher of ancient disasters, tells it from the records of monks who lived through it, and links it to the ideas of the astronomer Fred Hoyle. He tells it to show that the sky has struck human history hard before.
5412-committee-howard-hughes-and-the-s-f: The story goes that after President John F. Kennedy fired Allen Dulles, the head of the CIA, an angry Dulles and the Wall Street bank Brown Brothers Harriman brought back a covert team called the S force to "take out" Kennedy. The story ties this team to the 5412 Committee, a secret White House group that approved covert operations in the 1950s, and to Richard Nixon and the billionaire Howard Hughes. Michels tells it himself as "the narrative I've heard", without naming a source, in an episode with a historian of the CIA.
60-minutes-whistleblower-told-to-turn-do: A man who quit a government job said on the television news program 60 Minutes that a woman came to him and said, "We got to turn down the temperature on this thing." Eric Haseltine, a former senior official of the National Security Agency, the US electronic spying agency, brings this up with Michels as a sign that officials work to cool public interest in a subject. He does not say which report he means. If it is the 60 Minutes report on Havana Syndrome, the unexplained injuries reported by US officials, aired 8 March 2026, there a former CIA officer who resigned recalls hearing on arriving at the unit studying these cases, "Our job is to bring down the temperature on AHI at headquarters", AHI being the agency's term for the cases; the report does not say who said it or that it was a woman, and its subject is not UFOs.
65-corrections-to-human-evolution-as-a-p: Briefing papers at S-4, a secret site in Nevada, are said to have stated that aliens made 65 corrections to human evolution. Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft at S-4 in the late 1980s, tells this, repeating what a colleague he names only as Barry told him, and says the claim appeared in the briefings: "the aliens had made 65 corrections to um you know, in the evolution of humans." Lazar suggests it may have been planted there as a marker.
8-000-years-of-ceremonial-site-artifacts: An archaeologist named Chris Roberts has documented more than 8,000 years of artifacts from ceremonial sites at Skinwalker Ranch, a property in Utah. Brandon Fugal, the ranch's owner, passes this on from Roberts' work, as a sign that people have treated the land as special for thousands of years.
9-11-as-a-diversion-from-disclosure-2001: Steven Greer, a campaigner who wants governments to reveal what they know about UFOs, says the September 11 attacks of 2001 happened "a few months later as a direct consequence" of a push for that kind of disclosure earlier the same year. He gives this as his own reading, without naming a source, and he means that the attacks pulled the world's attention away from the UFO question.
911-calls-from-the-facility-intercepted-: Around 2008 to 2010, children at a facility called Baker Victory Services in Western New York tried to get out and call 911, the US emergency number, but the phone lines were being watched. A man named Jordan Jose, who says a secret UFO program took him as a child, tells this from his own experience. If true, it would mean the place was kept under close surveillance so no one could ask for help.
98-of-classical-knowledge-lost: About 98 percent of the knowledge of the ancient Greek and Roman world is said to have been lost, with places like the Library of Alexandria and the city of Corinth tied to that loss. The philosopher Jason Jorjani repeats the figure and says he is "getting this figure from Carl Sagan", the astronomer. If true, it would mean most of what the ancients knew is gone from the record.
a-1-40-scale-model-of-the-red-pyramid-ex: A model of Egypt's ancient Red Pyramid, built at one fortieth of full size, blew apart from the pressure that built up inside it, according to Geoffrey Drumm, a man who studies what the pyramids were for and says he helped build it. Drumm says "it completely exploded due to the pressure on the inside," and he tells it as a sign that the pyramid was built as a working machine and not only as a tomb.
a-30-mile-perfectly-straight-edge-on-mar: Negatives from Mars mapping by NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory show a perfectly straight edge about 30 miles long on the planet's surface, according to the remote viewer Joe McMoneagle. He says he saw it himself and that "you don't get a 30 mile edge like that" by nature, which he takes as a sign that something on Mars was built.
a-bone-on-mars-in-a-jpl-negative: A photographic negative from a NASA lab's Mars mapping work shows what looks like a bone lying on the planet's surface, according to Joe McMoneagle, a former Army remote viewer (someone trained to try to describe distant places with the mind). McMoneagle says he saw it himself in negatives from the Jet Propulsion Laboratory, NASA's lab that builds and flies its planetary probes, and he says plainly: "this is a bone on Mars." If he is right, Mars once had animal life.
a-chicago-teacher-s-students-talk-about-: A teacher in Chicago told the filmmaker Ky Dickens, who made a documentary about children said to read minds, that her students talked about "the hill", a place some of these children describe meeting one another in their minds. Dickens passes on what the teacher told her. To her it was another sign that children who had never met were describing the same shared place.
a-congressman-on-the-progress-of-reverse: Asked whether secret programs to reverse engineer craft, meaning taking them apart to learn how to build them, are getting anywhere, an unnamed congressman seems to say he believes the programs exist but doubts they have worked. "If they had it," he says, "we would own the skies." His words are played in Michels's documentary episode about a scientist named Townsend Brown.
a-dramatic-event-at-the-end-of-the-ice-a: A sudden, dramatic event linked to the North Atlantic ice cap ended the Ice Age quickly and "eviscerated" North America, wiping out its giant animals, according to a researcher of ancient sites named Luke Caverns. He tells it on Jesse Michels's show in 2025, citing an evolutionary biologist he does not name. If true, it would mean a catastrophe, not slow change, reshaped the continent at the end of the Ice Age.
a-female-gray-with-a-baby-gray-at-the-mo: At a base at Mount Zeil, a mountain in Australia, a former Army sergeant named Lyn Buchanan says he saw a female "gray", one of the small grey-skinned beings of UFO lore, together with a baby gray. Buchanan tells it as something he saw himself, put simply: "I saw a gray female with a baby gray." If true, it would mean such beings have young.
a-few-dozen-uap-reports-are-real-some-kn: After going through many thousands of reports of unidentified flying objects, a small number, a few dozen, hold up as real, and some of them he knew about firsthand from inside the government. That is what Eric Haseltine, a former US intelligence official, tells Jesse Michels. He says he has "guilty knowledge" of some cases from his time inside, mentions a colleague named Chris Gilbert, and credits a book called The New Science of UFOs, so the claim comes from someone who says he saw the material himself.
a-founder-s-grandfather-saw-roswell-base: In 1947 at Roswell, New Mexico, where something was said to have crashed that summer, the men on the air base are said to have been visibly spooked. Michels passes this on from the founder of a large Fortune 500 company, whom he does not name, who told him, "my grandfather was in the 9th Atomic bomber Squadron, he was stationed at Roswell in 47." It is told as a family memory that the people on the spot believed something out of the ordinary had happened.
a-genetics-biologics-component-to-the-pr: The secret effort to recover crashed craft is said to include a genetics or biology part. The researcher Dylan Borland says on Michels's show that he knows this, in connection with a witness named David Grusch, and if true it would mean the work covers living matter and not just machines.
a-hidden-entity-picking-recruits-from-th: Jordan Jose, who says he was taken into a secret UFO program as a child, believes that some hidden group uses GATE, a school program for gifted and talented children, to recruit people. In his words, a "different entity" works "behind the scenes" to find a pre-selected pool of children and pull them into the programs, which would mean ordinary schooling is used to choose recruits.
a-man-falls-from-a-hotel-window-on-teleg: In the late 1970s, on Telegraph Avenue in Berkeley, California, someone jumped from a hotel window three stories up. A man named Brent Friedman, a guest on an episode about Hollywood, the CIA and UFOs, says he saw it: he looked up and saw an open window with a curtain blowing. He tells it as a moment he witnessed himself and never forgot.
a-man-named-bernie-proposes-esp-as-a-sav: A man named only as Bernie was the first to suggest that ESP gifts, meaning abilities like sensing things without the ordinary senses, should count as a savant skill, a rare exceptional talent, in autistic people who do not speak. The documentary filmmaker Ky Dickens tells this as part of her research for a series on telepathy in such children, also naming the researcher Diane Powell. If true, it would place mind-reading alongside other known savant abilities.
a-member-of-congress-saw-a-ufo-come-out-: A member of the US Congress is said to have been fishing on a lake with his son when an unidentified object came up out of the water. Luis Elizondo, a former Pentagon intelligence official, says members of Congress have taken him aside to tell him such things, and repeats this one without naming the member. If true, it would mean lawmakers themselves have had sightings.
a-mutual-friend-e-saw-a-rectangular-craf: A woman known only as E once saw a craft shaped like a rectangle, according to the researcher Deep Prasad, who says she is a friend he shares with Michels. Prasad passes on what she told him and keeps her name private. He finds it striking because she is the only person he knows who has seen that shape.
a-police-officer-s-report-of-seeing-a-de: In 1996 in Varginha, a town in Brazil where strange creatures were reported, a police officer is said to have written a report saying he saw a dead being. Italo Venturelli, a neurosurgeon at a hospital in the town, mentions this report in passing while talking about what happened there. If true, it would be a written official account of a non-human body.
a-reptilian-being-appears-in-barbara-lam: One afternoon, Barbara Lamb, a therapist who works with people reporting alien encounters, came in from her garden and found a reptilian being standing in her house. Dan Sheehan, a lawyer, passes this on to Jesse Michels as something she told him. He mentions it alongside John Mack, the Harvard psychiatrist who studied people reporting abductions, and an archive of Lamb's recorded sessions. Told this way, it suggests the beings her clients describe came to her directly too.
a-small-pentagon-group-dealt-with-the-ta: In the 1960s, only a tiny handful of people at the Pentagon are said to have known about and dealt with the "tall whites." These were tall, pale beings who, the story goes, kept a base on the military ranges of Nevada that was treated like a foreign embassy. This comes from Charles Hall, a man who says he spent three years near these beings while working on those ranges, and it would mean the US military kept quiet, diplomatic contact with visitors from elsewhere.
a-space-kid-calls-the-nine-a-sandbox-197: "The Nine", a group of non-human intelligences that some people in 1970s Ossining, New York, said they were in contact with, was described by one of the young people around that circle as just a sandbox for humans to play in. The researcher Greg Malatzi relays this from an unnamed person he calls a "space kid", a view that would make the Nine less a council of masters than a kind of playground.
a-traumatized-area-51-worker-saw-reptili: A man who worked at Area 51, a secret Air Force test site in Nevada, is said to have seen reptile-like beings in a basement there and to have come away deeply shaken. Michels repeats it as something told to him by a couple named Garrett McNamara and Nicole McNamara, who said they met the man, possibly a friend of a friend, and that "he was totally traumatized." If true, it would mean non-human beings were kept at the base.
a-uap-class-attacks-with-microwave-weapo: A man named James Valor, from Skywatcher, a startup that tries to call up UFOs, says one type of unidentified craft his team met in the early 2020s attacked them. He says these craft used microwave weapons and turned off the team's systems. He tells it as a witness, and if true it would mean that some of these objects are hostile and can disable equipment.
a-uap-hits-the-team-with-an-energy-weapo: James Valor, who works with Skywatcher, a startup that tries to call up UFOs and record them, says that in 2025 one of these objects hit his team with an energy weapon. He says he was there: during a U-turn, before a team member could get up on something he calls NAYA, the object struck them, and he says this happened "constantly".
a-ufo-control-panel-inside-a-hangar: Inside a hangar, Army Sergeant Lyn Buchanan says he walked past a control panel he recognized right away as coming from a UFO, one he says he had seen and operated before. He says the hangar was a metal Quonset building, the curved prefab kind, full of wreckage from midair collisions, and that he went there in the late 1980s, about a year after an interview with the Defense Intelligence Agency, the Pentagon's military spy agency. He tells it first-hand as a sign that the government holds pieces of non-human craft.
a-voice-yelling-freeze-saves-him-before-: A soldier in Vietnam, sometime between 1967 and 1969, was walking down the steps into a bunker at a small army camp called Two Bits when he heard someone yell "freeze." He stopped, looked around, and the whole bunker "just vaporized." Joe McMoneagle tells this as the soldier it happened to, and he tells it as an early moment when a warning he could not explain saved his life.
a-witness-saw-the-craft-over-the-hospita: In 1996, in the Brazilian town of Varginha, a witness says the strange craft was seen out over the town's hospital. The documentary filmmaker James Fox, who has spent years interviewing people about the Varginha events, says he recently met this person himself. The story matters to him because the same hospital is where, by other accounts, a living creature was taken.
aaro-appointed-to-head-a-space-tiger-tea: AARO, the Pentagon office set up to look into unexplained objects in the sky, was put in charge of a small special team to study such objects in space, according to a researcher who is a guest on the show. The guest only mentions this briefly and does not give a source or any details. It suggests the government is taking these sightings beyond Earth's air seriously.
aaro-asks-hastings-to-bring-in-nuclear-s: In 2023, the Pentagon's office for investigating unexplained aerial reports, known as AARO, asked to interview military veterans who had seen strange objects near nuclear weapons sites, according to the researcher Robert Hastings, who has long collected such accounts. Hastings says a retired Senate Armed Services Committee investigator named Kurt McConnell contacted him and passed on the request that he gather some of those veterans. He tells it first-hand, as the man who was asked, and it would mean the government was taking the nuclear-site reports seriously enough to hear the witnesses.
aaro-briefing-ai-quantum-and-the-grusch-: Someone deep inside the US national security world once said that what they were really watching was a triangle: artificial intelligence, quantum technology and "the Grusch stuff", meaning the claims of David Grusch, a whistleblower who testified under oath about hidden government programmes for recovered craft. Matthew Pines, a guest well connected in national security, says he was told this, and he ties it to the Pentagon's office for studying unexplained aerial reports. Michels repeats it several times and places the speaker differently each time, as a CIA man, someone at the Pentagon, or someone at the RAND Corporation, a government-funded research centre.
