aaro-did-not-record-the-veterans-intervi: When AARO, the Pentagon's current office for investigating unexplained objects in the sky, interviewed military veterans about UFOs seen at nuclear weapons sites, its staff are said not to have recorded those interviews. Robert Hastings, a researcher who has gathered such veterans' accounts and who arranged for them to speak to the office, tells this. He raises it as a sign that the office did not take the testimony seriously.
aaro-director-s-true-anomalies-2024: The Pentagon has said it has "true anomalies", cases that leave it stumped, and that is coming from Jon Kosloski, the new director of AARO, the Pentagon's office for UFO reports. The writer Marik von Rennenkampff repeats this from what Kosloski said in 2024 or 2025. If true, it would mean the military's own office admits some cases cannot be explained.
aaro-director-says-aaro-works-with-uarcs: At a US Senate hearing in 2024, Jon Kosloski, the director of AARO, the Pentagon office set up to investigate unexplained aerial sightings, reportedly said his office works with university-affiliated research centers and with federally funded research and development centers, outside research bodies that do contract work for the government. An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb points this out, without naming a source, mentioning Senator Kirsten Gillibrand in connection with the hearing. He raises it because it would mean UFO work reaches beyond the Pentagon into universities and government-funded labs.
aaro-fishes-for-the-program-name-and-the: Dylan Borland, a man who says he knows about a secret government UFO program, says that in 2023 AARO, the Pentagon office set up to look into reports of unidentified flying objects, pressed him for details. He says from his own experience that they wanted the names of the people he knew working on the program and the name of the program itself, and that he refused to give them.
aaro-found-som-1-01-crash-packaging-manu: AARO, the Pentagon office set up to study unexplained objects, is said to have found a manual, called SOM 1-01 (heard on the show as "Psalm 101"), explaining how to package and unpack debris, craft and bodies from an extraterrestrial vehicle crash. An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb relays this from what he was told, citing the office's officials Tim Phillips and Sean Kirkpatrick, which would mean the government once had procedures for handling alien crashes.
aaro-head-john-kosloski-came-from-the-ns: The man who now heads the Pentagon office that investigates unexplained aerial reports, John Kosloski, is said to have come from the National Security Agency, the US spy agency that intercepts communications. Michels says this himself, in a conversation with a former Air Force sergeant named Dan Sherman, calling him a former NSA director, and raises it to show how closely that agency is tied to the subject.
aaro-hired-sancorp-2020: AARO, the Pentagon office that now investigates unexplained aerial reports, hired a company called SANCorp, which a researcher who goes by UAPGerb says specialises in guarding against insider threats and whistleblower leaks. UAPGerb says this on Jesse Michels's show in 2026, and adds that Tim Phillips, an official tied to the office, said on a podcast that SANCorp was hired to connect AARO with subject matter experts. Gerb tells it to suggest the office was more focused on stopping leaks than he claims it admitted.
aaro-historical-report-misstated-michael: The Pentagon office set up to investigate UFOs, called AARO, published the first volume of its historical report in 2024, and the online researcher known as UAPGerb says it got one witness badly wrong: a man named Michael Herrera. UAPGerb tells Michels that "we know for a fact" Herrera's testimony "was lied about" in that report, pointing to Herrera's own written memorandum of what he said and to Sean Kirkpatrick, who ran the office. If so, the government's official history would be misrepresenting the people who came forward.
aaro-leadership-change-from-kirkpatrick-: In 2024 the leadership changed at AARO, the Pentagon office set up to look into reports of unidentified flying objects: a man named Kirkpatrick left, and a new director named Jon Kosloski took over. Michels mentions the "change of the guard" in passing while talking with Ryan Graves, a former Navy fighter pilot, and says Graves was the one who told him who the new leader was.
aaro-resolution-of-aguadilla-video-2013: AARO, the Pentagon office that now investigates UFO reports, explained the Aguadilla video, a 2013 heat-camera recording of an object over the airport at Aguadilla, Puerto Rico, according to the UFO skeptic and researcher Mick West. West says this in a debate with Michels, insisting "they did" resolve it and that the case existed before the office's other work. He raises it to show that famous UFO videos have been given ordinary explanations.
aaro-s-latin-motto-2022: AARO, the Pentagon office set up in 2022 to look into unexplained objects in the sky, has a Latin motto that translates roughly as "the universe is what our thoughts make of it." A Pentagon whistleblower named Matthew Brown points this out to Michels, saying he may not have the translation exactly right. He finds it a telling choice of words for an office meant to study these things.
aaro-s-mfr-marks-borland-s-triangle-sigh: Dylan Borland, a man who says he saw a triangle-shaped craft and later gave his account to AARO, the Pentagon office that looks into unidentified objects, says that office's paperwork proves his story. He says that in 2023 AARO wrote up his interview in a memorandum for record (an official note of the meeting), which listed his triangle sighting as unclassified. He says they then classified his other drawings of craft and technology of unknown origin and moved them into a special access programme, a tightly restricted secret project, which he takes as proof that they are real.
aaro-says-go-fast-is-possibly-parallax-2: The Go Fast video, footage from 2015 off Jacksonville, Florida, that seems to show a small object racing over the water, may be explained by parallax, according to the Pentagon's All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office, the office that now looks into UFO reports. Parallax is a trick of viewpoint, where a moving camera makes a slow object look fast. Michels reports that the office said this, while debating the UFO skeptic Mick West.
aaro-scif-briefing-showing-only-resolved: In 2023, the Pentagon office set up to look into unexplained flying objects gave lawmakers a briefing in a secure room for classified material, and it showed only cases it had already solved, such as one that turned out to be a balloon. Congressman Eric Burlison, who was there, describes it as literally a slideshow of 'we looked into this and here's what it was.' He names the office's leaders, Sean Kirkpatrick and Jon Kosloski, and tells it to suggest the briefing left out the cases that still have no explanation.
aaro-sends-odni-a-false-mfr-2023: Dylan Borland says that between 2023 and 2025, the Pentagon office that handles reports of unexplained objects in the sky, called AARO, sent a false memorandum for record (a written note made for the official file) to the Office of the Director of National Intelligence, the body that oversees all US spy agencies. Borland tells it as someone who took part. He says that when he went to that office on September 10, 2025, a man named Jon Kosloski was AARO's director, and that if his account is true, the office meant to look into these questions was putting false things on paper.
aaro-staffing-1-600-cases-and-a-baffled-: By 2024, AARO, the Pentagon office that now looks into reports of unexplained objects in the sky, had a staff of roughly three to four dozen people, and that week it had been declared at full operational capability. The commentator Marik von Rennenkampff says this, without naming a source, and links it to the office's director, Jon Kosloski, its pile of about 1,600 cases, and how puzzled its own leadership is by some of them. He raises it to show how small the government's effort is next to the size of the question.
aaro-told-the-wsj-the-shutdown-was-an-em: In 2025, a Pentagon office set up to look into unexplained aerial sightings, known as AARO, is said to have told the Wall Street Journal reporter Joel Schectman that a shutdown of nuclear missiles had been some kind of EMP test. An EMP is an electromagnetic pulse, a burst of energy that can knock out electronics. The story comes from Robert Salas, a former Air Force officer who says he was there when the missiles went down, and he tells it to explain where the newspaper's account of that shutdown came from.
aaro-under-kirkpatrick-as-a-fly-trap-for: The Pentagon's UFO investigation office, in its first years under its director Sean Kirkpatrick around 2022 and 2023, was really a trap to catch UFO information as it came in, and probably had ties to older secret programmes. Michels says this himself as his own view, without naming a source, and if he is right it would mean the office was built to contain information rather than reveal it.
aaro-undercut-by-cia-and-air-force-figur: The Pentagon office set up in 2022 to investigate UFO reports, the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office or AARO, is said to have been undermined from inside by CIA and Air Force people, chief among them its first director, Sean Kirkpatrick. If true, the official channel for UFO witnesses was working against them. The analyst Matthew Pines says that once the subject moved into AARO "it's kind of compromised by the CIA air force guys right like Kirkpatrick." The filmmaker Jeremy Corbell, crediting the former program head James Lacatski, Tim Phillips and the reporter George Knapp, goes further and says "AARO was acting as a counterintelligence against the American public," a trap that harassed whistleblowers. Michael Herrera, a man who says he saw a huge craft in Indonesia and dealt with the office himself, says he understands it was "a front" for finding out what people knew "and then either trying to shut them up or just publicly dismissed the person," naming Kirkpatrick and a later official, Jon Kosloski.
aaron-paul-wrote-messages-back-and-forth: Around 2023, a man named Aaron Paul is said to have exchanged messages with Bob Lazar, a man who has said he worked on recovered craft in Nevada. The hip hop musician Flying Lotus tells it as something he heard from Paul himself, saying "Aaron yo he's he's wild. He he talked to Bob Lazar." He tells it to show how far the interest in Lazar's story reaches.
aatip-as-part-of-a-government-disclosure: As recently as 2015 and 2016, AATIP, a small Pentagon office that studied unexplained aerial reports, was part of a government effort to slowly reveal what it knows about UFOs, according to Jake Barber, a helicopter pilot who says he flew a recovered UFO. Barber passes this on from what he was told. If true, it would mean the office was part of a planned move to tell the public.
aatip-modeled-uap-using-general-relativi: A small Pentagon office that studied unexplained aerial reports, known as AATIP and run with the private space company Bigelow Aerospace, is said to have explained unidentified flying objects using Einstein's general relativity, the theory that treats gravity as a bending of space and time. Hal Puthoff, a scientist who says he worked on the program, says it was the best they could do: "let's accept Einstein's GR as being the theory." Luis Elizondo, who says he worked in the same office and credits Puthoff, puts it more strongly, calling the bending of space and time "absolutely the fundamental theory," not just a possibility, for how these objects might move.
aatip-oap-and-the-uap-task-force-as-red-: Several US government UFO studies from 2007 to 2021 may have been 'red teams' for an older secret program, playing the outsider to test how well that older program, which he calls the legacy program, kept itself hidden. That is the theory raised by Dylan Borland, a former Air Force intelligence specialist. The efforts he means are AATIP, a small Pentagon office that studied unexplained aerial reports, a follow-on effort called OAP, and the UAP Task Force, a Pentagon group set up to look into unidentified aerial phenomena. He links this to the DIRDs, research papers on advanced and exotic technology that the Pentagon office commissioned, and calls it "the fun" with these programs. If true, the public studies were partly a test of how well the deeper secret held.
aatip-study-of-260-000-cases-and-a-possi: AATIP, a small Pentagon programme that studied unexplained aerial reports, is said to have looked at 260,000 cases with seven levels of analysis, perhaps the biggest study of UFO data ever made, and to have found that an existential threat may exist. A researcher named Jason Simosa tells this from the journals of Jacques Vallée, a scientist who studied UFOs for decades, and says Vallée "hints at" the threat two or three times. If true, it would mean the government saw real danger in what it found.
aatip-the-dod-s-ufo-program-and-its-22-m: According to Jesse Michels, the US Department of Defense ran a secret UFO study from 2007 to about 2012. He calls it AATIP, the Advanced Aerospace Threat Identification Program, and in some episodes AAWSAP or OAP, the Advanced Aerospace Weapons Systems Application Program. He says Senator Harry Reid of Nevada, then Senate Majority Leader, got it $22 million together with Senators Daniel Inouye and Ted Stevens of Alaska, that it was run through Bigelow Aerospace, a private space company owned by Robert Bigelow, and that some of the work was done at a property called Skinwalker Ranch. Michels tells it himself across many episodes. He names Luis Elizondo as its former director and says it was made public in a New York Times article in December 2017 that the journalist Leslie Kean helped break. He tells it because it would mean the government studied UFOs officially and with real money, and he adds that a slimmer follow-on program came after it.
aawsap-idea-of-baiting-ufos-with-nuclear: Insiders on a Pentagon-funded study of UFOs, called AAWSAP, are said to have thought about luring UFOs with nuclear material. Michels tells this twice, citing a book by Luis Elizondo, a former Pentagon official who has spoken out about UFOs. The second time, Michels names the book as Imminent and adds that the plan was to then bring the craft down with directed energy beams and high-powered radar.
aawsap-set-up-to-take-a-lockheed-held-uf: A secret Pentagon-funded study of UFOs from the late 2000s, known by its initials AAWSAP and run under the Defense Intelligence Agency by contractors including Bigelow Aerospace, a private space company in Las Vegas, is said to have been set up partly to take over a UFO held by the arms maker Lockheed Martin, until a CIA official blocked the handover. If true, a defence company has had an alien craft for decades. Michels tells it, crediting the former intelligence officer David Grusch and the late Senator Harry Reid, saying the program was meant to give "outsider civilian scientist eyes" on the craft, and names Jim Ryder, a vice president at Lockheed's space technology centre, as involved in the transfer. Citing an article by the journalist Chris Sharp in the outlet Liberation Times, Michels says Glenn Gaffney of the CIA "was the gatekeeper" and "blocked the transfer" of a craft Lockheed collected in the 1950s. The physicist Eric Davis, who worked with the program, says Gaffney, of the CIA's science and technology branch, was "very antagonistic" about a company, which he does not name, releasing its collection of crash retrieval materials to them. The journalist Ross Coulthart traces the story to a 2017 New York Times article by Leslie Kean and Ralph Blumenthal and suggests the craft came from a crash in Kingman, Arizona, in 1953, and a researcher known as UAPGerb also names it as the Kingman material and dates Lockheed's attempt to 2008.
aawsap-to-aatip-to-elizondo-to-new-york-: There is a direct line, says the national security writer Marik von Rennenkampff, from AAWSAP, a Pentagon-funded study of unexplained aerial reports begun in 2007, to AATIP, a small Pentagon office that studied such reports, to Luis Elizondo, a former Pentagon official, and then to the New York Times, which made the program public in 2017. He draws this chain on Jesse Michels's show in 2025, in an episode about a debate with a skeptic. His point is that the public story did not come from nowhere but grew out of a real government program.
abandoned-radar-base-found-near-alvado-1: On a mountain peak near Alvado, New Mexico, an old radar base still stands "just like they left it in 1957," says a man named Scott Ramsey, who went there himself. Ramsey says that in 1999 he and others came looking for radar bases, checked every high peak in the area toward Santa Fe, and hiked up through about two feet of snow to find it. He links it to the Atomic Energy Commission, the US agency that once ran the country's nuclear work, as part of his search for evidence of a crash in the region where he says alien bodies were recovered.
abductee-carol-s-missing-pregnancy-and-h: A woman called Carol is said to have been abducted, to have lost a pregnancy that simply vanished, and to have a part-alien daughter, and she was furious at the people working on UFOs. A guest named Dan Sheehan tells this on Michels's show, passing on what he was told, and says her case was studied by John Mack, a researcher of abduction accounts. If true, it would mean abductions involve human pregnancies.
abductee-friend-grabs-a-gray-by-the-neck: A woman who says she has been abducted is said to have grabbed one of her captors, a gray, the small grey-skinned being common in abduction stories, by the neck and squeezed it before she passed out. A researcher named Tim Alberino tells it as something his friend told him about one of her experiences. If true, it would mean the beings are solid enough to be held.
abductees-tell-alberino-of-a-forced-hybr: People who say they were abducted describe being forced into a breeding programme meant to make human and non-human hybrids, according to a guest named Tim Alberino, who repeats what abductees have told him. If true, it would mean someone or something is using people against their will to make a new kind of being.
abductees-whose-memories-come-back-when-: Some people who believe they were taken by aliens say their buried memories came flooding back when they saw the cover of Communion in a bookstore. Communion is a book by the writer Whitley Strieber about his own reported encounters with beings. Michels tells this, passing on what Strieber has said: "they'll see the cover of Communion."
abduction-and-implant-prevalence-estimat: About 3% of all Americans are said to have been taken by aliens, some of them left with implants in their bodies. A scientist named Steve Colbern, who studies objects said to be alien implants, gives this figure, passing on the estimate of a doctor named Roger Leir who worked with him. If true, it would mean millions of people have been abducted.
abduction-memory-returns-25-years-later-: Lyn Buchanan, a former Army sergeant who served in a military unit that trained people in remote viewing, the practice of trying to see distant places with the mind, says a memory of being abducted came back to him 25 years after it happened. He tells it himself: when a woman said something to him, "it all came flooding back," and he says the memory was then checked by remote viewers in the late 1980s.
abduction-phenomenon-shatters-the-wester: The Harvard psychiatrist John Mack, who studied people who said aliens took them, argued that the one thing the Western mind cannot forgive is something from the spirit world crossing into the physical world. He says that is exactly what happens in abduction reports, which is why they can shatter a Westerner's whole set of beliefs. Mack gives this as his own view, without naming a source.
aborymon-the-enochian-angel-in-john-dee-: An angel called Aborymon was recently discovered inside the Sigillum Dei Aemeth, a magical seal tied to John Dee, a scholar at the court of Queen Elizabeth I of England. This angel belongs to the Enochian system, the angel language Dee said he received. Matthew Brown, a former Pentagon insider who speaks as a whistleblower, mentions it in passing without saying where the finding comes from, as part of his wider picture of how unseen beings have dealt with people.
abraham-dines-with-angelic-beings: In the Bible's book of Genesis, Abraham meets a group of angelic beings at Mamre, in ancient Canaan, and sits down to dinner with them. The researcher Tim Alberino retells it from Genesis as an old account of people sharing a table with beings from beyond, which would matter as early testimony of such contact if read literally.
abramelin-the-hermit-of-luxor-in-the-boo: In an old magical text called The Book of Abramelin, the figure of Abramelin is a hermit who lives in the Egyptian desert near Luxor. Matthew Brown, a guest billed as a Pentagon whistleblower, describes him this way on Michels' show, summarising the book without pointing to any other source.
ac-gravity-llc-wins-a-dod-contract-and-l: A physicist named Ning Li, who worked on the idea of controlling gravity, is said to have founded a company called AC Gravity LLC with a fellow researcher named Larry Smalley in Huntsville, Alabama, and won a contract from the US Department of Defense right away, after which she went quiet. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source. He raises it as a hint that the military took her gravity work seriously and may have pulled it out of public view.
acacia-as-the-tree-of-life-in-egypt-free: The acacia tree, the story goes, was the Tree of Life in ancient Egypt, its leaf holds a prominent place in the symbols of Freemasonry (a centuries-old fraternal society with secret rituals), and the Ark of the Covenant, the sacred chest of the Hebrew Bible said to hold the tablets of the law, was made of acacia wood. Michels draws these links himself in a conversation with the writer Graham Hancock, whom he credits. The suggestion is that one sacred symbol may run through Egyptian, biblical and Masonic tradition.
account-of-a-tic-tac-type-craft-over-pen: In 1967, a craft shaped like a Tic Tac, a white oval like the mint, was seen over Pennsylvania. Steven Greer, a doctor who founded a group pressing for the release of UFO secrets, tells Jesse Michels there is a good account of it in a book he is giving him. He names the book as Disclosure: An Illustrated History, and when he mentions the 1967 Pennsylvania case again he does not describe the shape. If true, it would mean craft like the ones Navy pilots later reported were being seen decades earlier.
acquaintances-say-puharich-was-mossad-19: Andrija Puharich, a scientist linked to the CIA who is said to have contacted an alien council, was secretly working for Mossad, Israel's intelligence service, in the 1970s. That is what a researcher named Greg Malatzi says he was told by several people who knew Puharich and only spoke about it late in their lives. If true, it would mean a foreign spy service stood behind one of the stranger contact stories of that decade.
acquiring-william-corliss-s-sourcebook-p: The papers of William Corliss, an American writer who spent years on a series of books called the Sourcebook Project, a catalogue of strange and unexplained reports, were taken from the United States to Sweden. Clas Svahn, a Swedish UFO researcher who says he acquired them himself, tells the story to Jesse Michels. The archive is part of why Svahn is said to hold so much UFO evidence.
active-military-personnel-bring-uap-vide: Service members still on active military duty have been coming to Congressman Eric Burlison and showing him their own videos of unexplained aerial objects, which the government calls UAP. Burlison says this has happened to him personally since about 2023 in his role as a member of Congress. If true, it would mean people inside the military are bypassing their chain of command to get evidence to lawmakers.
actuators-pulled-out-of-portals: There are said to be actuators, the parts that make a machine move, that "they pull out of the portals." The researcher Grant Cameron mentions this only in passing on Michels's show, as something he heard from a man named John Sillison, and he names Ron Pandolfi and Dan Smith in the same conversation. If true, it would mean someone is recovering working hardware from something called portals, though Cameron does not say what the portals are or who does the pulling.
adam-and-eve-as-a-memory-of-genetic-mani: The broadcaster Joe Rogan says on the show that he takes the Bible's story of the first human beings, Adam and Eve, to be "a recounting of a genetic manipulation," meaning that someone altered earlier humans to make us. The King James Bible, published in 1611, says God "created man in his own image," formed him "of the dust of the ground" and breathed life into him, and made the woman from a rib taken from Adam during "a deep sleep." It says nothing about genes or earlier humans, so the genetic reading is Rogan's own.
adamski-photos-unanalyzed-diaries-read-b: Photographs taken in the 1950s by a man named George Adamski were never properly analysed, and Adamski also kept diaries, which a man named Glenn Steckling has read. The researcher Clas Svahn brings this up as a summary of his own, naming no source, as material that could still shed light on Adamski's story.
adamski-s-contact-with-a-man-from-mars-1: In the 1950s, a man named George Adamski said he had met a being who told him he came from Mars. The philosopher Jason Jorjani brings it up briefly with Michels, without naming a source. He uses it as an example of the kind of contact stories people were telling at the time.
adamski-s-martian-and-venusian-nordic-so: In the 1950s, a man named George Adamski claimed to meet beings from Mars and Venus who lived throughout the solar system and were, in his words, far more enlightened than us. The philosopher Jason Jorjani sums up Adamski's claims on Michels' show, and the story is tied to a work called Closer Encounters. He tells it as an example of visitors being cast as wise teachers of humanity.
admiral-meeting-at-a-cemetery-at-midnigh: In 1996, Brent Friedman, a man who worked around Hollywood, says he was told to meet a Navy admiral at a cemetery at midnight near Long Beach Harbor in California. The plan was passed to him by a contact he calls JC: the admiral "is going to come off of the ship with a cover story of visiting a deceased friend." Friedman tells it as part of his own story, and the secrecy of the meeting suggests the admiral had something about UFOs to share that he could not say openly.
admiral-richard-byrd-antarctica-stories: The story is that Admiral Richard Byrd, the American polar explorer, had some strange encounter in Antarctica. Michels raises it with a guest simply by asking, "Do you know Admiral Richard Byrd?" Tim Gallaudet, a retired US Navy admiral, mentions it on another episode second hand, crediting a diver named Becky Schott and placing it in the 1940s: "someone thought that Admiral Byrd had some encounter when he was down there." If true, something unexplained would have been met at the bottom of the world.
admiral-wilson-returns-to-close-out-a-pr: A Pentagon scientist named Eric W. Davis recalls meeting a Navy admiral named Thomas R. Wilson in Las Vegas sometime between 1997 and 2002. Davis says Wilson told him he was back because he had to go up to a site he would not name, though Davis understood he meant Area 51, a secret Air Force test base in the Nevada desert, to close out a project there. Davis tells it from that conversation, which he says he was part of, and he also mentions a former Army officer named John B. Alexander in connection with it.
advanced-lost-civilization-and-ancient-e: An advanced civilization rose and was lost before ours, and ancient Egypt is evidence that this is not humanity's first time around. Joe Rogan, a comedian and well-known podcast host, says this to Michels, placing himself in the school of the researcher Randall Carlson and the writer Graham Hancock, who argue for such a lost civilization.
advanced-theoretical-physics-group-study: A private group called the Advanced Theoretical Physics working group is said to have met to study the physics of UFOs. Its members reportedly included the physicist Hal Puthoff, Oke Shannon, John B. Alexander and others. The online researcher who goes by UAPGerb says that in 1985 the Army general Albert Stubblebine and the defense company BDM founded it at BDM's headquarters in McLean, Virginia. He cites Oke Shannon's notes and names Ferris Williams and Kenneth Shoulders. In another episode UAPGerb also credits Kit Green. Michels tells it several times, and his dates vary. In one episode he places it in the 2000s, at the Pentagon and Los Alamos, the US weapons lab. In another he puts it in the 1980s and 1990s and calls Shannon a Los Alamos project manager, linking in Ferris Williams' "5D" model. Elsewhere he names Eric W. Davis among those involved. The tellers raise it because it would mean serious scientists and officials quietly studied UFO physics for years.
aec-official-tests-the-device-on-himself: In 1962 or 1963, at a New York City company called Intelectron, an official from the Atomic Energy Commission, the US agency that ran the country's nuclear work, is said to have doubted a device the company was working on, told them "test me," tried it on himself, and found that it worked. The researcher Greg Malatzi tells this on Jesse Michels' show. He sums it up without naming a source, though he points to the writer Annie Jacobsen and to letters from the Atomic Energy Commission. If true, a skeptical government official saw the device work on his own body.
aerial-battles-over-basel-and-nuremberg: The philosopher Jason Jorjani says huge battles between UFOs were seen in the skies over European cities such as Basel in Switzerland and Nuremberg in Germany, and that the printed news sheets of the time reported them. He draws this from Wonders in the Sky, a book by the UFO researcher Jacques Vallée, and tells it as proof that such sightings go back centuries.
aerial-survey-record-altered-or-missing-: The aerial photo record of Skinwalker Ranch, a ranch in Utah, is said to be largely empty for the years 1964 to 1969, as if someone deleted it. This comes from the ranch's owner, who speaks as a first-hand witness and mentions a Dr. Taylor and a man named Erik Bard. To the owner, the gap suggests that someone wanted what happened on the ranch in those years kept out of sight.
aerial-view-shows-replanted-trees-in-lin: At Hart Canyon near Aztec, New Mexico, where a flying saucer is said to have crashed in 1948 with alien bodies aboard, an aerial view of the area reportedly shows trees that were replanted in neat lines. Scott Ramsey, who has spent years investigating the site, says he and others later got to see that aerial view. To him it suggests that someone cleaned up and replanted the crash site to hide the damage.
aerospace-companies-ask-for-pasulka-s-an: Diana Pasulka, a professor who studies religion, says that around 2012, while she was researching beliefs about angels and similar beings, people at aerospace companies started contacting her to ask for her data. She tells it from her own experience and stresses it was "not just one, I got a lot," which would suggest the aerospace world had a quiet interest in her work.
aerospace-companies-seek-patent-rights-o: Aerospace companies want patent rights over technology from unknown craft, says a lawyer named Dan Sheehan, so that they, not the public, control it "for the next thousand years". He says this on Jesse Michels's show in 2024, without naming a source, while talking about a 2023 law that was being weakened. If true, it would mean private firms are fighting to own whatever the government has recovered.
aerospace-company-s-government-customers: An aerospace company that worked on a secret program reported to a government customer, and that customer was not always the CIA: sometimes it was the Air Force. A researcher named Eric W. Davis says he heard this from the company itself, which he dealt with often during a Pentagon-funded study of unexplained aerial phenomena, and he tells it to show which agencies were behind such work.
aerospace-corp-executives-questioned-in-: Around 2023 or 2024, a congressional committee that checks on the government sent a letter to a company called Aerospace Corp, and two members of its executive team came to a secure classified room in Washington to answer questions, but they said they knew nothing. Congressman Eric Burlison tells this from his own role in getting them there. He tells it as an example of hitting a wall when asking companies about secret UFO work.
aerospace-corporations-hold-uap-knowledg: Private aerospace companies are said to hold knowledge about UAP, the official term for unidentified flying objects, and to keep it out of reach of FOIA, a US law that lets anyone request government records, because it is treated as company property. Hal Puthoff, described in the episode as a CIA expert on UFOs, says this, adding that the whole arrangement was set up to work that way, which would mean the public has no legal route to the material.
aerospace-employee-with-an-object-moving: A person working at one of the big aerospace companies has had something moving around inside their body for several years, Michels says. He tells this himself and will not name the person, saying he does not want to get them in any kind of trouble.
afib-after-the-hypnosis-session: Mario Woods, a former guard at a nuclear site who says he was taken by beings from a UFO, says something went wrong with his body right after a hypnosis session in Georgia meant to bring back his memories of it. He says that when the man running the session, whom he names as Robert Upson, finished, "something was wrong with me," and he developed AFib, an irregular heartbeat. He tells it from his own experience, as a sign of what digging up those memories cost him.
afosi-agent-has-crew-sign-non-disclosure: In 1967, in the squadron commander's office at Malmstrom Air Force Base, a missile crew was made to sign a non-disclosure agreement, a promise in writing not to talk about what had happened. Robert Salas, a former Air Force officer who says he was on that crew, says his commander introduced him to a man from AFOSI, the Air Force Office of Special Investigations, which is the Air Force's own investigative service. Salas tells it as a sign that the Air Force wanted the event kept quiet.
afosi-confiscates-footage-and-swears-mis: In the 1960s, men who worked at US nuclear missile sites kept seeing UFOs near the nuclear facilities, and each time, according to the story, the Air Force Office of Special Investigations, the Air Force's own investigators, showed up, took the film and swore the men to secrecy. Michels tells this himself in his interview with a former intelligence officer named David Grusch, citing a man named Bob Jacobs. The point is that the Air Force was hiding sightings at its most sensitive sites.
afosi-founding-director-a-devout-catholi: The founding director of the Air Force Office of Special Investigations, the Air Force's own investigative and counterintelligence service set up around 1948, was a devout Catholic who had wanted to go to seminary and suddenly found himself in intelligence. The researcher Jason Simosa says this without naming a source, linking that office to the early days of a secretive group of officials known as the Collins Elite. He tells it because it would mean religious belief shaped how part of the government first handled the UFO question.
afosi-officer-harassing-a-ufo-whistleblo: In at least one case, the person harassing a UFO whistleblower was proven to be an officer of AFOSI, the US Air Force's own investigations branch. Matthew Brown, a guest billed as a Pentagon whistleblower, says this on Michels' show, passing on what he was told. He gives no names, place or date.
afswp-established-at-sandia-base-1947: In 1947 the military set up a special weapons project, known by its initials as AFSWP, at Sandia Base in Albuquerque, New Mexico, a center for handling atomic weapons. An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb tells Michels this and links it to James Forrestal, the defense chief of that time. He brings it up to show where secret programs of that era were based.
age-of-disclosure-claims-of-a-reverse-en: Michels says that in The Age of Disclosure, a documentary film, senior insiders state that the United States has a programme that reverse-engineers UFOs, meaning it studies recovered craft to copy how they work. He names Jim Semivan, a former high-ranking CIA officer, and Chris Mellon, a former deputy assistant secretary of defense for intelligence. In another episode he adds the senior intelligence official James Clapper and says the film's speakers also claim that non-human intelligence is real and that America is in an arms race over it with China and Russia. Michels raises it to show how cleared, high-level people now speak openly about such a programme.
age-of-disclosure-documentary-us-holds-c: According to Michels, a documentary called The Age of Disclosure, which he describes as just out, has senior officials saying that the US holds recovered saucers, keeps them in hangars to work out how they function, and has alien bodies found with them. He names former CIA director John Brennan (the CIA is America's foreign spy agency), former director of national intelligence James Clapper, and David Grusch, a former intelligence officer at the agency that analyses satellite and map imagery. In a later episode Michels describes the claim as decades of crash retrievals carried across generations, and ties it to Area 51, the secret Air Force test site in Nevada.
age-of-disclosure-joint-doecia-effort: The secret government work on UFOs was a joint effort between the Department of Energy and the CIA's science and technology branch, according to people interviewed in the documentary film Age of Disclosure. Michels relays this himself, saying that in the film people as high up as the director of national intelligence say it "was a joint effort." If true, it would place the programme inside two powerful agencies with little outside oversight.
agencies-deny-grusch-access-to-programs-: Between about 2019 and 2022, a former US intelligence officer named David Grusch went to the agencies that had written certain reports about secret UFO programs and asked to be let in, and they refused him. Grusch tells this himself, and he says the refusal was the proof: when they deny you access, he says, you know the thing is real.
agency-men-say-they-follow-the-varginha-: James Fox, who has been investigating the Varginha case, a reported capture of a live alien by the army, says he once met government agency men who told him they were watching his work. He says he was there, and that they told him, "Oh, yeah. No, we know exactly what you've been doing," with a person named Leslie part of the account.
agents-ask-buchanan-to-influence-gorbach: In 1991, agents asked Army Sergeant Lyn Buchanan, working at Fort Meade, an Army base in Maryland, to influence Mikhail Gorbachev, the Soviet leader, with his mind. Buchanan says that when Gorbachev gave the speech that ended communism, the words in it were the very words he had been 'pumping into him.' If true, it would mean a mental technique helped shape the end of the Soviet Union.
agents-followed-gebauer-s-daughters-to-s: Government agents are said to have followed the two young daughters of a man named Leo GeBauer to school. Michels tells this himself, saying one of the daughters later told it to researchers named the Ramseys. He brings it up as a sign that GeBauer, who was linked to stories of crashed craft and alien bodies, was being watched.
aggressive-helicopter-experiment-where-e: In 2024, a very aggressive experiment involving a helicopter at Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property known for reports of strange happenings, went badly, with "everything" going wrong. Brandon Fugal, who owns the ranch and says he was running the experiment, gives no more detail than that. He tells it as a sign that something at the ranch reacts when it is pushed.
agnew-bahnson-s-diaries-space-brothers-a: A man named Agnew Bahnson, who backed a physics institute at the University of North Carolina in Chapel Hill in the 1950s, wrote in his diaries that the "space brothers", friendly visitors from space, came to him and told him to get in touch with a researcher named Thomas Townsend Brown because they wanted to build a spaceship. Michels tells this himself on two episodes, saying the diaries were found years later. In the second telling he ties them to a 1957 conference at that institute, gathered with the physicist John Wheeler and attended, he says, by Freeman Dyson, Richard Feynman and Peter Bergmann, and suggests the space brothers may have pushed Bahnson toward this work.
agnew-bahnson-s-novel-the-stars-are-too-: A businessman named Agnew Bahnson wrote a science fiction novel, The Stars Are Too High, which Michels says is about man-made flying saucers and a fake alien invasion staged to unite the world. Michels brings it up in several episodes, and he describes the plot in different ways: sometimes the plotters are rogue Nazi scientists brought to America after the war who work with American scientists, and sometimes they are rogue anti-gravity scientists deep inside intelligence agencies. He dates it to 1959 in one telling. He raises it to suggest Bahnson knew something about secret anti-gravity work.
agnew-bahnson-s-plane-crash-1960: An American industrialist named Agnew Bahnson died in a strange plane crash in the early 1960s, and according to Michels his family believes to this day that he was in effect killed. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, in an episode about secrecy around UFOs. If true, it would suggest that someone wanted Bahnson silenced.
aguadilla-airport-thermal-object-2013: In 2013 a heat-sensing camera filmed an unexplained object near the airport at Aguadilla, Puerto Rico. Some describe the object as plunging into the ocean and coming back out. The UFO skeptic Mick West discusses the video in a 2025 debate episode, placing it over the airport at what he calls a "big tourist destination". Michels tells it in a 2026 episode with a Navy admiral. He describes "this, you know, 3 minute video of a trans medium object", meaning one that can move between air and water. According to Michels, it "seems to descend into the Atlantic Ocean and then come out as well." If that reading is right, it would point to a craft able to pass through water and air in ways ordinary aircraft cannot. The two men frame it very differently. West treats it as a video to be explained, while Michels gives no ordinary explanation for it.
aguadilla-analyzed-in-a-200-page-scu-doc: A 2013 sighting at Aguadilla, Puerto Rico, is said to have been studied in a report of about 200 pages by the Scientific Coalition for UAP Studies, a group of researchers who study unexplained objects in the sky. Michels brings it up himself, in a debate with a skeptic, saying it was written by "a bunch of different experts, people with PhDs." He tells it to show that the case was examined seriously by trained people.
aguadilla-object-as-two-wedding-lanterns: In 2013, an object was filmed flying over Aguadilla, Puerto Rico, and one explanation is that it was two lanterns released at a wedding. Mick West, a skeptic who analyses UFO videos, says the idea came from Ruben Lianza, whom he describes as the head of Brazil's UFO investigation department, and he mentions it alongside AARO, the Pentagon's office for unexplained aerial reports. If right, one of the best-known UFO videos would have an ordinary cause.
ai-agent-swarm-solves-navier-stokes-2026: No single AI program could solve the Navier-Stokes problem, a famous unsolved maths question about how fluids flow, but 10,000 AI agents working together for 88 hours suddenly found a solution, according to the researcher Deep Prasad. He says this on Jesse Michels's show in 2026, without naming a source. He tells it to show that swarms of AI can crack problems that no one program can.
ai-at-moscow-conference-judged-apollo-ph: At an artificial intelligence conference in Moscow about two years before the episode, with Russian president Vladimir Putin present, an AI system is said to have judged photos from Apollo, the American moon landing missions, to be synthetic, meaning faked. The comedian and podcaster Joe Rogan tells it, passing on what he heard from Bart Sibrel, a filmmaker who argues the moon landings were staged. If true, it would cast doubt on the moon landing photos.
ai-reads-the-buga-sphere-symbols-as-the-: An artificial intelligence program read the symbols on the Buga Sphere, a ball marked with strange symbols that turned up in Buga, Colombia, as meaning "The circuit," according to the journalist Ross Coulthart. Coulthart says he did this himself in 2025: he photographed the sphere and uploaded the picture to an AI, something he says he is "increasingly doing these days." If the reading is right, the markings would carry a meaning rather than being decoration.
ai-solves-the-navier-stokes-equations-in: An artificial intelligence solved the Navier-Stokes equations, the math that describes how liquids and gases flow, in just 88 hours, according to an unnamed researcher who appears as a guest. The researcher stresses that this problem had stumped mathematicians for hundreds of years, in an episode arguing that AI may be something like alien technology.
air-force-academy-friend-flew-a-back-eng: A friend of Robert Salas from the Air Force Academy, the US Air Force's officer school, told him he had actually flown a craft similar to a UFO. Salas, a former Air Force officer, repeats this to Michels and says that because of it he is convinced the United States has back-engineered, meaning copied the workings of, recovered craft and even flown some models. If true, the government would hold and fly technology built from crashed craft.
air-force-academy-religious-training: The US Air Force Academy in Colorado was training its people in religious studies, according to the researcher and author Peter Levenda. He tells it as something he heard a couple of years ago, without naming a source, and says he was "appalled" by it, raising it as a sign that belief and the military are more tangled than people think.
air-force-and-cia-created-two-weeks-afte: Roughly two weeks after the 1947 Roswell incident, when something crashed near Roswell, New Mexico, the US passed the National Security Act of 1947, the law that created the Air Force and the CIA at the same moment. That is the point made by Jake Barber, a former helicopter pilot who says he flew a UFO recovery mission, talking to Jesse Michels. He offers the timing as a hint that the new security setup was shaped by what was found at Roswell.
air-force-captain-oliveira-at-the-nation: In 1954, at Brazil's national war college, the Escola Superior de Guerra, an Air Force captain named Oliveira said that the UFO phenomenon is real. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, as evidence that Brazil's military was taking the subject seriously very early.
air-force-censorship-of-pan-starrs-image: The US Air Force is said to have heavily censored images from Pan-STARRS, a sky survey telescope that scans the whole sky and that found the strange interstellar object called 'Oumuamua. Michels says this himself, without naming a source, as an example of the military controlling what astronomers are allowed to see and share.
air-force-cooperation-with-stargate-1997: Michels says the US Air Force worked closely with the science-fiction television series Stargate SG-1, which starred Richard Dean Anderson and began in 1997. As proof, he points out that two serving Air Force Chiefs of Staff, Michael E. Ryan and John P. Jumper, "appeared on the show as themselves." He raises it himself, without naming a source, as a sign that the military may have wanted to shape how the public thinks about secret space programs.
air-force-disinformation-drives-paul-ben: From about 1979, an Air Force counterintelligence agent named Richard Doty is said to have fed false UFO stories to Paul Bennewitz, a researcher in Albuquerque, and driven him to madness. Jesse Michels tells it many times. He says Bennewitz had seen strange, advanced craft at Kirtland Air Force Base, and Doty was given the job of running a psychological operation on him. Michels draws on the writer Greg Bishop and on Project Beta, Bennewitz's own paper about what he believed. He also mentions records obtained under the Freedom of Information Act, a US law that lets anyone request government records. In one telling Michels says the campaign helped drive Bennewitz to suicide, and in another he notes that John Lear, a figure in UFO circles, visited him. The historian Peter Levenda says, "We know that Richard Doty did it." The historian Richard Dolan says Bennewitz was very intelligent and that Doty "led him astray". Some tellers place it in the early 1980s. If true, it would show the military deliberately spreading UFO lies to cover something real.
air-force-documents-on-hans-kohler-s-cap: In the 1940s in Germany, a German man named Hans Kohler is said to have been caught by American forces, and Michels says there are now Air Force documents showing "Hans Kohler was apprehended by the Americans." Michels says this himself and does not name or quote the documents. To him, the papers back up the story that the Americans took custody of Kohler.
air-force-flies-benowitz-to-archuleta-me: In the early 1980s, the Air Force is said to have flown Paul Bennewitz, a New Mexico man caught up in UFO claims, by helicopter from Kirtland, an Air Force base in Albuquerque, to Archuleta Mesa on the Jicarilla Apache reservation, where props had been set up for him to see. Greg Bishop, a researcher who studied the Bennewitz case, passes on what he was told by the men around it, the Air Force intelligence agent Rick Doty and the UFO writer Bill Moore, and he says Bennewitz was very excited when he described the trip. If true, it would mean the military deliberately fed a believer a staged scene to steer what he believed.
air-force-funding-of-the-movie-stargate-: The US Air Force helped fund the movie Stargate, the Kurt Russell film about a portal found by a pyramid, Michels says. He brings it up twice on his own, without naming a source, as a curious hint that the military takes an interest in stories about ancient gateways.
air-force-going-public-plan-called-off-2: Between 2009 and 2010, a man named Ed was part of an Air Force plan to tell the public about these mysteries, and a two-star general shut the plan down. An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb tells Michels this, repeating what Ed told him. If true, the government came close to going public years before anyone heard about it.
air-force-hunts-for-scientist-x-1950: In 1950 an unnamed lecturer known as Scientist X gave a talk in Denver, Colorado, and two hours after it ended, Air Force investigators showed up and began questioning students for clues about who he was. Michels tells this himself, citing people named Hansen, Unger and George Kohler, in an episode about claims of a crashed craft and alien bodies. If true, it would show the Air Force taking the lecture seriously enough to hunt down its speaker.
air-force-interrogations-demotions-and-d: After airmen at Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota reported a strange encounter in 1977, their Air Force interrogators are said to have spent most of their time trying to explain the experience away, and the men faced demotions and denial. Michels tells this himself, framing the story of two of the witnesses, an airman named Mario Woods and a fellow airman named Michael. He says that what hurt most was not the event but how they were treated afterwards.
air-force-lieutenant-colonel-makes-marin: Around 2009 or 2010, at Camp Hansen, a Marine base on Okinawa in Japan, an Air Force lieutenant colonel had a group of Marines sign a non-disclosure agreement, a pledge of secrecy, covering what they had seen in Indonesia, and warned them of the price of talking. Michael Herrera, a former Marine who says he saw a 300-foot UFO in the Indonesian jungle, says he was one of them and was told "flat out that if you talk about this, you can go to prison or you can be executed over it." He says the paper was a top secret agreement tied to the Indonesia event, which would mean the government treated what they saw as a guarded secret.
air-force-lieutenant-colonel-ran-arv-tes: An Air Force lieutenant colonel claims to have run a program, from roughly 1998 to 2008, that tested "alien reproduction vehicles", meaning craft built to copy alien ones, along with technology derived from them, at Edwards Air Force Base's flight-testing unit and the Nevada test ranges. A researcher who goes by the online name UAPGerb says he knows this officer and passes on what he was told, which would mean the military has flown copies of non-human craft.
air-force-lunex-crewed-moon-base-plan-19: Between about 1957 and 1961, the US Air Force reportedly drew up detailed plans, under the name Lunex, for its own crewed mission to the Moon and a base there, tied to Vandenberg Air Force Base in California. An unnamed guest researcher says, without naming a source, that he "recently learned" of these plans. It would mean the military had its own Moon ambitions separate from the civilian space agency.
air-force-manned-orbiting-laboratory-can: The US Air Force once planned a Manned Orbiting Laboratory, a small military space station with a crew, and it was cancelled in June 1969, exactly one month before the Apollo mission first landed on the Moon. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, in an episode about a hacker who says he found a secret NASA space program. He points to the timing as a hint that the military space effort may not simply have ended.
air-force-pilots-report-drones-up-to-36-: US Air Force pilots have reported drones flying as high as 36,000 feet, with 30 or 40 such reports over the last couple of years, according to the national security writer Marik von Rennenkampff. He says this on Jesse Michels's show in 2025, without naming a source, as a sign that unknown objects are showing up where pilots fly.
air-force-project-blue-book-1947: The US Air Force once set up its own program to investigate UFO reports, which Michels calls Operation Blue Book. He tells it himself, without naming a source. In another episode he adds that the program was run by Edward J. Ruppelt, whom he calls an Air Force general, and that Ruppelt seemed fairly open to the idea that the phenomenon was real.
air-force-roswell-reports-project-mogul-: In the 1990s, the US Air Force put out two reports on Roswell, the New Mexico town where a crashed flying saucer was reported in 1947, explaining the debris as a secret balloon project called Project Mogul and the bodies as crash-test dummies. The skeptic writer Michael Shermer summarises them, calling them the 94 report and the 96 report, and says the 1994 one was about the balloons. In his telling, the Air Force admitted it had made up the original cover story because it did not want the Russians to know it was launching high-altitude spy balloons.
air-force-takes-over-navy-ufo-investigat: From the late 1940s through the 1950s, when sailors had UFO encounters, Air Force personnel would come aboard Navy ships, throw their weight around and take over the investigations, which made the Navy men angry. The UFO researcher Richard Dolan tells this on Michels' show, passing on what he heard from a man named Donald Kho. If true, it would mean the Air Force was quietly taking control of UFO reports from the other services.
air-traffic-controller-watches-the-f-5-c: In 1986, an unknown object played hide and seek with F-5 fighter jets chasing it over São Paulo, Brazil, popping up again at a very distant point. Jose Manuel Fernandez, an air traffic controller at the city's Congonhas airport, says he watched it happen. He tells it as a witness to show the object moved in ways the jets could not match.
aircraft-instruments-go-haywire-at-edge-: Instruments on fixed-wing planes flying over Skinwalker Ranch in Utah, a property known for reports of strange happenings, are said to go haywire when they reach the edge of an invisible zone over the land that people there call "the bubble." The owner of the ranch says this on the show as something his team has seen and recorded: the planes "actually document that there's something." If true, it would mean that whatever is at the ranch has a physical edge that machines can detect.
aircrew-briefing-to-congress-not-a-false: Military aircrew who tracked an unexplained object in 2015 told members of the US Congress in a briefing that they knew it was not a false hit, meaning not a radar or sensor error. A commentator named Marik von Rennenkampff raises this in a debate episode with Michels, asking what the crew could have meant if not that something real was there.
akhenaten-abandons-amun-and-pharaohs-dep: In ancient Egypt, after the king Amenhotep III died, his successor Amenhotep IV is said to have announced that he would no longer worship Amun, the god the great Karnak temple was built for, and would honour only the one true sun god, the Aten. He took the name Akhenaten and shut Karnak's doors, and the art of the time suddenly changed, with royal figures shown with long, stretched skulls. This is told by a researcher named Luke Caverns, who gives no source and says nobody knows where the skull shape came from or why it showed up right then.
akhenaten-tribute-at-the-hale-solar-labo: When the astronomer George Ellery Hale designed his Hale Solar Laboratory in Pasadena, California, in the 1920s, he put a tribute to Akhenaten, the ancient Egyptian king who worshipped the sun, in the arch above the entrance. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, as one sign that ancient sun worship ran through the founding of American space science.
akhil-knows-what-his-mother-manisha-watc: A mother named Manisha says her nonspeaking son Akhil can tell her exactly what happened in a movie she watched while he was in another part of the house, playing on his iPad where he could not hear it. The filmmaker Ky Dickens relays this from her documentary series The Telepathy Tapes, which follows children said to read minds. If it were true, it would mean information can pass from one mind to another without words.
akil-knows-about-the-amputee-athlete-fil: A mother from New Jersey named Manisha says her son, Akil, who appears in a documentary about telepathy among children who cannot speak, knew about a movie she had watched downstairs without him. She says he described it as a film about an athlete whose leg was amputated and who got into the Special Olympics. She tells this as something she saw herself, and if true it would suggest the boy picked up her experience by reading her mind.
akil-writes-the-next-word-before-it-is-w: The filmmaker Ky Dickens, who made a documentary about nonspeaking children said to read minds, says she watched a boy named Akil in New Jersey in 2023 write words before anyone showed them to him. She says she saw it herself: as soon as a word on a list was crossed out and someone started thinking about the next one, Akil would start writing it, with a woman named Manisha also part of the test. If true, it would point to the boy picking up thoughts directly.
al-jazeera-clip-of-invisible-figure-clim: In 2004, in Iraq, possibly near the city of Tikrit, a clip from the Arab news network Al Jazeera showed a nearly invisible blob with limbs climbing up onto an American Abrams battle tank and down into the gunner's hatch. John Blitch, a scientist who worked for the Pentagon's advanced research agency, says he saw the clip, and he links it to the US news anchor Katie Couric, who he says played it about three times in slow motion. He tells it as a hint that some kind of invisibility technology was being used.
al-qaeda-negotiating-with-pakistani-nucl: After the September 11, 2001 attacks, the terrorist group al-Qaeda was trying to buy a nuclear weapon from Pakistani nuclear scientists so it could set it off in the United States. Rolf Mowatt-Larssen, a former CIA officer who worked on the case at the agency's counterterrorism center, says so from the inside, naming George Tenet, then head of the CIA, and his own book A State of Mind: Faith in the CIA. If true, the country came close to a nuclear attack in the years after 9/11.
alberino-measures-the-tombs-of-the-giant: The ancient stone tombs on the Italian island of Sardinia known as the Tombs of the Giants are said to be big enough to hold the bodies of real giants. Tim Alberino, a researcher who says he went there himself with a tape measure, reports: "yes, you can fit the bodies of giants in those tombs." He tells it to back up his view that giants once lived on Earth.
alberino-s-aid-expedition-to-san-antonio: In 2023, the filmmaker Tim Alberino travelled to San Antonio de Pintoyaku, a remote village in the Peruvian Amazon, on an expedition to bring aid. Alberino, who was there, says that when he arrived he was greeted for the first time in his life by what he calls a small army of men holding loaded shotguns.
alberino-s-ufo-hovering-above-his-car: The filmmaker Tim Alberino says a UFO once came down and hovered silently about 40 feet above his car, "like I was supposed to see it." He tells it as his own sighting, and in a second retelling adds that it happened about 14 years ago in February, at a strip mall in Brook Park, Ohio, near a NASA research center called NASA Glenn, with a friend named Tony beside him.
albert-bender-s-three-men-in-black-telep: In the 1950s, a man named Albert Bender said three men in black, the dark-suited visitors said to call on UFO witnesses, appeared out of thin air in his attic, with glowing orange eyes and a smell of sulfur, and took him to Antarctica. The researcher Jason Jorjani tells it from Bender's own account, which he credits to a book he calls The Saucers and the Three Men. He brings it up because, if true, it would mean those visitors were not ordinary government agents but something able to move a person across the world.
albert-bruce-collins-sees-a-cracked-egg-: In 1948, a man named Albert Bruce Collins is said to have seen a recovered craft being carried on a lowboy trailer, a low flatbed for heavy loads, at the University of California, Berkeley. The online UFO researcher known as UAPGerb passes on Collins's statement, which comes from the files of Leonard Stringfield, a researcher who collected accounts of crashed craft. Michels tells a version without naming Collins or giving a date. He describes an egg-shaped craft, cracked, with a sphere inside, taken to the Berkeley labs to be studied. If true, it would mean a university helped examine a crashed craft soon after the war.
albert-stein-s-deathbed-call-to-sheehan: A man named Albert Stein called Dan Sheehan from his deathbed in a hospice in northern Minnesota. Sheehan, a guest who says he was involved in many famous American cases, tells it as a call he received himself. He presents it as a last confession from someone who knew something important.
alcibiades-killed-for-talking-about-the-: The ancient Greek Alcibiades is said to have been killed for talking openly about the mysteries of Eleusis, secret religious rites held in ancient Greece. Michels mentions this himself in passing, without naming a source. A researcher named Luke Caverns says only that Alcibiades got in trouble for it, not that he was killed, and places it in Athens. The tellers bring it up to show how closely the secrets of those rites were guarded.
alcubierre-s-1994-faster-than-light-solu: In 1994 a Mexican graduate student named Miguel Alcubierre, at the University of Mexico, is said to have solved Einstein's equations of gravity, known as general relativity, in a way that allows faster than light travel. A guest named Karl Nell tells it this way, linking it to NASA. Michels tells it twice: once stressing that the trick needs negative energy, and once pairing it with work by a NASA researcher named Harold "Sonny" White on a chip using the Casimir effect, a tiny force that appears between objects placed very close together. If it works, it would mean travel between stars is possible within known physics.
aldo-rebelo-on-varginha-1996: In 1996 in Varginha, a town in Brazil, an unknown craft is said to have crashed and a living creature is said to have been captured, and Brazil's former defence minister Aldo Rebelo, now a presidential candidate, says it really happened. In his own interview with Michels, Rebelo says: "The phenomenon existed. It was there. The objects were there. The creature was seen." Michels, who travelled to Brazil to interview him, later sums up Rebelo's answer as "Yeah, this happened", treating it as an unusual confirmation from a senior official.
aldous-huxley-at-the-round-table-foundat: In the 1950s the writer Aldous Huxley was a close friend of the man who ran the Round Table Foundation, a private research group in Rockland, Maine, and was there all the time. A researcher named Greg Malatzi says so in his own summary, drawing on a book called The Sacred Mushroom, to show how close the famous author was to the group's work.
aldous-huxley-takes-a-high-dose-of-lsd-w: The writer Aldous Huxley is said to have asked his wife, as he lay dying in 1963, to give him a very high dose of LSD, a powerful psychedelic drug. Michels mentions it himself, somewhat tentatively, while talking with the neuroscientist Andrew Gallimore about how such drugs might open the mind to other realms.
aldrin-s-communion-as-masonic-ritual-on-: After landing on the Moon in 1969, the Apollo 11 astronaut Buzz Aldrin is said to have taken communion, the Christian ritual of bread and wine, right there on the lunar surface. Michels tells this himself in two episodes. In one he calls it the first religious ceremony ever held on the Moon. In the other he goes further and describes it as a Masonic ritual, a rite of the Freemasons, a secretive fraternal society. If read his way, it would mean the Moon landing carried a hidden ceremonial meaning.
alex-dietrich-on-ufologists-enjoying-ant: Alex Dietrich, a Navy pilot who saw the 2004 incident in which fighter jets from the aircraft carrier USS Nimitz met an unexplained flying object, has said that UFO enthusiasts seem to enjoy the anticipation of an answer. Michael Shermer, billed as America's top skeptic, quotes her on Michels' show and gives her the last word, saying her remark sums up 75 years of the hunt for aliens.
alex-jones-s-on-air-prediction-of-an-att: Before the attacks of 2001, the radio host Alex Jones is said to have warned on air that if a terrorist group hit the World Trade Center, everyone would know who to blame. Michels tells it himself in two talks about dreams and seeing the future, offering it as a possible case of premonition. In the second he puts the remark on CNN and has Jones addressing Osama bin Laden directly: take down the Twin Towers and I will come after you.
alexander-says-mj-12-was-continuity-of-g: Majestic 12, a secret group said in UFO lore to have managed the government's UFO secrets, was really a plan to keep the government running in a catastrophe: that is what John B. Alexander, a retired Army colonel, is said to have stated. A UFO commentator who goes by UAPGerb relays that Alexander called it "specifically a continuity of government program." The researcher Grant Cameron says he heard Alexander say in an interview, "Yeah, there was, but it didn't have anything to do with UFOs." If so, the famous group existed but had nothing to do with flying saucers.
alfred-krupp-and-axel-wenner-gren-in-nas: In 1955, the story goes, a man named Alfred Krupp travelled to Nassau in the Bahamas with Axel Wenner-Gren, a Swedish multi-billionaire and one of the richest men in the world. The researcher Jason Simosa tells it on Michels's show without naming a source, and he places the trip after a gathering he calls the Maison Rouge meeting, as part of a thread he follows from wealthy, powerful men to a hidden network behind UFO secrecy.
alfred-o-donnell-told-george-knapp-of-a-: A senior manager at a contractor called EG&G, named Alfred O'Donnell, is said to have told the reporter George Knapp that the US held a recovered flying saucer along with living beings. A guest who goes by the name UAPGerb, passing on what O'Donnell reportedly said, places the saucer at a site next to Area 51, a secret test site in Nevada, "with live biologics," and says it was moved there in the early 1950s, "1954 to be exact." Michels tells it differently, saying that in 2023 O'Donnell told Knapp the saucer was recovered in New Mexico, together with "a live being that had humanlike features." If true, the government would have held both a craft and a living non-human being for some seventy years.
algorithm-analysis-of-john-ward-s-mars-a: A researcher who studies odd shapes on Mars ran computer tests on strange features that a man named John Ward picked out of photos taken by NASA's Mars Global Surveyor probe and the HiRISE camera that orbits Mars. The researcher, a guest of Michels, says he used "fractal and texture-based algorithms" to judge how likely it is that the shapes formed naturally. The point is to see whether any of them might have been made by someone.
alice-scully-says-photos-of-the-aztec-cr: Photographs of the Aztec crash, a flying saucer said to have come down near Aztec, New Mexico, in 1948, still exist. A woman named Alice Scully told this to a man named Chris Evans, and Scott Ramsey, who has spent years investigating the Aztec case, repeats it to Michels. If true, there would be pictures of the crash someone has kept hidden.
alien-autopsy-document-and-the-other-edg: A researcher named Grant Cameron says that in the 2000s he was sent a set of papers connected to a man named Edgar Mitchell, including a document describing an alien autopsy, that is the examination of an alien body, which named a man called Kit Green. Cameron tells this first-hand as the person who received them, and he lists among the papers a condolence letter tied to Charles Lindbergh and a record of meetings of NIDS, a private research institute, also naming a man called James Rigney. If genuine, the papers would link known figures to the study of alien remains.
alien-autopsy-photos-in-s4-briefing-1988: Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked at a secret site called S4 in the Nevada desert around 1988 and 1989, says the briefing papers he read there included autopsy photos of a small gray being. He tells it as something he saw himself: the body had a T-shaped cut in the chest, and one single organ had been taken out. If true, it would mean the government had a body that was not human and had studied it.
alien-bases-as-government-granted-reserv: Alien bases on Earth are said to sit in places that the US government or other governments have handed over, like reservations, under a deal of "you stay away from us and we'll stay away from you." Lyn Buchanan, a former Army sergeant, puts this forward as his own view on the show. If true, it would mean world governments have quietly made a deal with visitors and let them keep land of their own.
alien-bodies-and-a-live-gray-recovered-a: In 1947, at Roswell, New Mexico, the site of a famous crash, the military is said to have recovered alien bodies, and the story as filed also includes a live "gray," the small grey-skinned being of UFO lore. The researcher John Brandenburg tells it only briefly, saying "I'm quite confident that they recovered bodies." He names no witness and points only to a work called Cosmic Awakening. If true, the government has held non-human remains since 1947.
alien-bodies-studied-in-secret-by-biolog: The claim is that the United States holds the bodies of non-human beings, and that biologists have studied them in secret. The author Whitley Strieber, who says he has met such beings, states it flatly without naming a source: "we have bodies here that ... biologists have studied here and that those studies are ended." A former Air Force officer named Robert Salas gives it as an impression he picked up second hand, speaking of genetic studies on tissue from recovered beings, and he does not say the work has stopped. If true, it would mean the government has physical proof of other beings.
alien-channeling-at-the-national-photogr: In 1959, at the National Photographic Interpretation Center, a US government center in Washington that studied spy photographs, a group is said to have held a session where someone channeled an alien, meaning they claimed to pass on its words. The UFO researcher Grant Cameron tells it twice, giving no source, and calls it the famous story attached to Arthur Lundahl, the center's head. He links it to Frances Swan and Wilbert B. Smith. In Cameron's fuller version he dates the meeting to July 9, 1959, and cites an 11-page memo about it. The contact began with automatic writing, where a hand writes messages seemingly on its own, and then switched to a voice. When Lundahl asked for proof, the voice told them to go to the window, and "this flying saucer goes flying across in front of the Capitol." An unnamed narrator in the same episode tells it more cautiously. He calls the channeled being "the commander" and says the group "supposedly" saw a UFO, without naming anyone present. If true, it would mean government photo experts witnessed contact on request.
alien-image-in-the-west-desert-test-cent: There is said to be an image of an alien hanging in the cafeteria at the West Desert Test Center, part of Dugway Proving Ground, a US Army testing range in Utah. A researcher who goes by the online name UAPGerb shows it on the podcast, saying "this is in the cafeteria at the West Desert Test Center," and credits a man named Ryan W. Harris. In a later episode Michels describes it as "a little gray alien being" in the cafeteria at Dugway. If true, it would hint that people at the base treat aliens as part of their own lore.
alien-information-theory-reality-as-a-sl: A book called Alien Information Theory lays out the idea that our reality is only a slice of a larger structure with more dimensions. Its author, the neuroscientist Andrew Gallimore, says that readers often take the book to be a statement of what he personally believes, suggesting the picture is more an exploration than a creed.
alien-involvement-with-earth-spans-more-: Contact with aliens is not the business of a single nation, according to a former sergeant named Dan Sherman, who says the NSA, the US electronic spying agency, hired him in the early 1990s to communicate with aliens. Sherman says that a man he dealt with in that work told him "it was more than one country." If true, several governments would share the secret.
alien-propulsion-via-electromagnetic-ene: The alien craft are said to move by working with electromagnetic energy and with time itself. This comes from a former Army sergeant named Dan Sherman, who says the National Security Agency, the US government's signals spy agency, hired him to communicate with aliens in the early 1990s. He tells it as what he learned at a place he calls Base 2, and he links it to Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft at a secret site in Nevada.
alien-reproduction-vehicle-pilot-and-pil: A whistleblower says he flew an 'alien reproduction vehicle', meaning a human-built craft copied from a UFO, and a second man says he managed all the pilots who flew such craft out of Edwards Air Force Base in California. The UFO researcher Steven Greer describes both witnesses on Michels' show, relaying what they told him. If true, it would mean the US was flying copied alien craft.
alien-reproduction-vehicles-exist-and-ar: Alien reproduction vehicles, meaning human-built copies of alien craft, exist and are kept at storage sites. Michael Herrera, a former Marine who says he saw a huge UFO in the Indonesian jungle, tells Michels he knows where some of them are stored but will say no more.
aliens-anti-gravity-methods-homopolar-ge: A craft seen over Fillmore, California, used more than one method to overcome gravity, according to Steve Colbern, a scientist who studies objects said to be alien implants in human bodies. Colbern speaks as someone who was there. He says one of the methods is a homopolar generator, a simple electric generator built around a spinning disc in a magnetic field, and he links the other to the Biefeld-Brown effect, a claimed push produced when high voltage is put across charged plates. If he is right, it would show how such craft move.
aliens-call-humans-water-beings-1990: A being Dan Sherman says he was in contact with always called humans "water vessels or water beings, water humans." Sherman, a former Army sergeant, says the National Security Agency, the US government's code-breaking and eavesdropping agency, hired him to communicate with aliens, and he describes this from his own time at a site he calls Base 2, between 1990 and 1993. If true, it would mean the beings saw people mainly as bodies made of water.
aliens-have-two-sexes-and-eliminate-wast: A former Air Force sergeant named Dan Sherman, who says the NSA, the US government's code-breaking and signals spy agency, hired him to communicate with aliens, says the beings he dealt with in the early 1990s have both female and male sexes. He also says they eliminate bodily waste. Sherman tells it from his own time on the program at a place he calls Base 2, and if true it would mean these beings are physical creatures with biology much like ours.
aliens-have-visited-humanity-for-a-very-: Aliens have been coming to Earth for a very long time, and many times over. That is the impression of a former Army sergeant named Dan Sherman, who says the National Security Agency, the US government's signals spy agency, hired him in the early 1990s to communicate with aliens. He tells it as something he came to understand through that work, and if true it would mean visits are old, not new.
aliens-on-time-travel-and-wormholes: Steve Colbern, a scientist who studies objects said to be alien implants in human bodies, says the beings he links to a craft over Fillmore, California, told him they have time travel. He tells it as something he heard directly. According to Colbern, they said they don't like to use it much, and they especially avoid long jumps, a hint at how such beings might move through time and through wormholes, which are shortcuts through space.
aliens-take-people-to-build-a-critical-m: A man introduced on the show as the president of a Russian republic, not otherwise named in these tellings, says aliens took him in 1997, and that he asked them why they take some people: "like they took me and tomorrow they might take you and so on." He tells it as something that happened to him, and the story's point is that the beings are taking people one by one to build up a critical mass of humans who have had contact.
