aliens-tell-him-they-created-humans-and-: In 1997, according to Kiran Ilum Xenov, a former president of one of Russia's republics, he was taken aboard an alien spacecraft and the beings there told him they had made humankind. He tells it as his own experience, recalling them saying that the only achievement of human civilization is that they created us as intelligent beings, and that humanity is not yet ready.
aline-griffith-on-skorzeny-taking-over-t: According to the journals of Aline Griffith, an American woman tied to wartime intelligence work, an operation she knew changed sharply eight or nine years after her time, when Otto Skorzeny, a former German wartime commando officer, came in and took it over. The researcher Jason Simosa tells this from her journals, which also name a man called Frank Ryan, and places it in the 1950s. He tells it because it would mean a former Nazi commander ended up running a postwar secret network.
allan-sandler-s-vandenberg-atlas-rocket-: There is said to be film of an Atlas rocket launch at Vandenberg Air Force Base in California showing two discs flying around the rocket's tip, footage tied to a filmmaker named Allan Sandler. The UFO investigator James Fox describes the footage this way, passing on what he was told. The researcher Grant Cameron dates the film to 1964 and says that a producer named Bob Emenegger told him the reel was never sent back, saying, "I guess it's in Alan Sandler's vault," in Oregon. If true, it would mean a real UFO was caught on film at a military launch.
alleged-photograph-of-one-live-and-one-d: In Varginha, Brazil, in 1996, a man named Pedro Aguiar is said to have pulled out a photograph showing two strange creatures, one alive and one dead. A man named James Fox, who looked into the case, says people described this to him, and he tells it because such a photo would back up reports that creatures were captured there.
allegro-s-theory-that-the-eucharist-was-: A scholar named John Marco Allegro concluded that the Eucharist, the Christian rite of sacred bread and wine, was at heart the Amanita muscaria, a red-and-white mushroom that causes visions. Michels tells this himself, drawing on Allegro's book The Sacred Mushroom and the Cross, published in 1970, and calls the idea deeply heretical.
allen-dulles-arranged-transfer-of-the-ma: In the 1940s a crashed craft known as the Magenta object was moved from Italy to the United States, with the American intelligence official Allen Dulles arranging the steps so that President Harry Truman could have it transferred. Harold Malmgren, a former presidential advisor, tells this on Michels' show, mentioning his daughter Pippa Malmgren. In another episode Michels, citing Malmgren, tells it differently: the craft left Italy through the Nazi 'ratlines', secret escape routes for Nazis after the war that the German spy chief Reinhard Gehlen helped run, and was moved by the Knights of Malta, a Catholic order, with no word of Dulles or Truman.
allen-dulles-cuts-off-ruth-paine-s-warre: In 1964, during hearings of the Warren Commission, the official inquiry into President Kennedy's assassination, the commission member Allen Dulles is said to have cut off the testimony of a witness named Ruth Paine. If true, it would suggest he was steering what went on the record. The author Peter Levenda tells it from the commission's published volumes, saying simply, "He stops her." Michels comes back to it in a later episode and says what Dulles was supposedly hiding. "Apparently," he says, Dulles did not want it known that Paine "had actually been at the summer house." He links that detail to a woman named Mary Bancroft. Levenda points to the record itself, while Michels adds a reason for the interruption.
allen-dulles-witnessing-a-saucer: Allen Dulles, a longtime head of the CIA, is said to have seen a flying saucer and checked that the door was locked, part of a story the philosopher Jason Jorjani says he has heard too. Jorjani mentions it only in passing to Michels, as something others have told him, and if true it would put the head of US intelligence among the witnesses.
allergen-test-and-immune-boosting-drink-: Before working at S-4, a secret site in the Nevada desert where he says alien craft were kept, Bob Lazar says a nurse there tested him for allergies and gave him something to drink that was supposed to boost his immune system. Lazar tells this himself, as something done to him around 1988 or 1989. Elsewhere he has told a version in which a drink caused gaps in his memory.
allied-foo-fighter-investigations-with-r: During the Second World War, Allied airmen reported strange lights following their planes, which they called foo fighters, and a study was set up to look into them. Kurt McConnell, a former Senate staffer, says one of the people assigned to that study was Dr. Howard Robertson, a scientist from Caltech, and he also names the physicist Luis Alvarez. He tells it without naming a source, to show that top scientists were looking at these things from the very start.
allied-skiers-sabotage-the-heavy-water-p: During the Second World War, a team of Allied skiers in Norway knocked out a plant making heavy water, a special form of water needed for Nazi Germany's atomic research. Michels mentions it in passing, from memory, in an episode with a writer named Jason Jorjani about a claimed Nazi UFO program. He brings it up as an example of how far the Allies went to stop secret German weapons work.
alonzo-mcdonald-in-vallee-s-journals-197: A man named Alonzo McDonald, who worked in President Jimmy Carter's White House in the late 1970s, was "uniquely involved" in the UFO question, according to the published journals of the UFO researcher Jacques Vallée. The researcher Jason Simosa points to this, telling it as something you find "if you read Vallee's journals," and ties it to another story about a lawyer being shown government UFO files at that time. If true, it would put the subject inside the White House at that time.
alsace-entity-who-said-the-witness-had-t: A strange being once appeared to a witness in Alsace, a region of eastern France, told him he had the time wrong, and then asked, "am I in Italy or Germany?" The witness answered that he was in Alsace. The UFO researcher Jacques Vallée tells this on Jesse Michels's show as a case he summarises without naming a source, the kind of odd, confused exchange that would suggest such visitors are not quite at home in our time and place.
altntepe-425-miles-away-shares-the-same-: An ancient site in Turkey called Altıntepe is said to share the same carved symbols as a group of other ancient sites, even though it lies about 425 miles away from them. The researcher Matt LaCroix brings this up in his talk with Michels about something big that he believes happened around 12,000 BC, without naming a source. If true, it would mean the same set of symbols spread much farther than people usually assume.
amanita-muscaria-esp-research-at-the-rou: In the 1950s at the Round Table Foundation, a private research group in Rockland, Maine, people took a mushroom called Amanita muscaria in extensive tests of whether it gives extrasensory perception, the ability to sense things beyond the normal senses. A researcher named Greg Malatzi describes this in his own summary, crediting a book called The Sacred Mushroom, as an early attempt to unlock such abilities with drugs.
amazon-shaman-with-a-wife-in-the-spirit-: A shaman in the Amazon was left by his wife because he also had a wife in the spirit world. The writer Graham Hancock tells this on Michels' show, passing on what he was told, as an example of how real the spirit world is to those who visit it.
amazonian-ayahuasca-as-a-technology-for-: The peoples of the Amazon who developed ayahuasca, a plant brew drunk for its visions, created what amounts to a true drug-based technology, one for building relationships with the beings met in that state. The neuroscientist Andrew Gallimore says this on Michels's show, speaking in general terms without a named source. If he is right, the brew is less a ritual than a tool for deliberately making contact.
amazonian-tribesmen-identify-a-grey-as-m: When people showed a tribe in the Amazon an image of an alien grey, the small grey-skinned being of many UFO stories, the tribesmen said it was Makunwabu, a being they already knew. Jay Anderson, a UFO researcher, tells Michels this as something he was told. If true, it would mean the same beings appear in old native traditions.
ambiance-exercise-and-step-16-of-control: Controlled remote viewing, a trained method for trying to describe distant places or hidden targets using only the mind, includes a drill called the ambiance exercise, according to Lyn Buchanan, a former Army sergeant who did the work himself. Buchanan describes it as part of the training, tied to step 16 of the method. He gives it as an insider's account of how the skill was taught.
amelia-evaluated-at-the-treffert-center-: A girl named Amelia, one of the children said in the episode to be able to read minds, was reportedly evaluated in the 2020s at the Treffert Center in Wisconsin, named for the doctor Darold Treffert, who worked there. The researcher Diane Powell mentions it in passing, without naming a source. It is raised because a formal evaluation there would lend weight to claims about the girl's unusual abilities.
amelia-found-able-to-spell-read-minds-se: A girl named Amelia, whose family had not known she could communicate, was found to be able to spell, and then, her mother Mora says, to read her mother's mind, see spirits and ghosts, read hieroglyphics, and know Hebrew, Portuguese and Spanish. The documentary maker Ky Dickens tells the story, which she covered in The Telepathy Tapes, her series about children said to be telepathic, passing on what Mora told her. If true, it would mean the girl had abilities no one can explain.
amelia-reads-hebrew-and-identifies-hiero: A girl named Amelia, who communicates by typing, is said to have read and translated Hebrew she had never been taught, and to have identified hieroglyphics she had never seen. Her mother, Mora, says that a helper named Ally showed Amelia some Hebrew, Amelia translated it, and when Mora asked who had taught her, Amelia typed "the rabbi." The filmmaker Ky Dickens, who made The Telepathy Tapes, a documentary about children like Amelia, retells it second hand and says the hieroglyphics test was run by Amelia's spelling therapist and babysitter, in a story offered as a sign that these children can know things nobody taught them.
amelia-s-spanish-teacher-says-she-knows-: A girl named Amelia, one of the children in The Telepathy Tapes, a documentary series about children said to read minds, knows so much Spanish that her teacher said she knew more than the teacher's own children. Michels tells this himself, passing on the teacher's words as they appear in the series. It is meant to suggest that Amelia picks up knowledge in ways no one taught her.
amelia-says-an-angel-took-her-to-see-god: A girl named Amelia, from the American Midwest, said that an angel had taken her to see God once or twice, and she named a rabbi and the Dalai Lama, the Tibetan Buddhist leader, as her teachers. The filmmaker Ky Dickens, who made a documentary about children said to read minds, passes this on to Michels as something Amelia told her sometime between 2021 and 2024. She also names a person called Mora as a source.
amentum-owns-parts-of-eg-g: A company called Amentum is said to own parts of another company known as EG&G. Matthew Brown, who is presented on the show as a Pentagon whistleblower, says this on Michels's show in August 2026, adding that it can be seen "if you look in their history." He raises it to draw a line of ownership between the two firms.
america-named-after-the-peruvian-god-ama: The name America comes from Amaru, a god of Peru, and the explorer Amerigo Vespucci changed his own name to sound like it, not the other way around. A guest named Kurt Metzger says this as something he was told, which would mean the continents carry the name of an old native god.
american-heart-association-testifies-aga: Brigham Buhler, a guest who campaigned to have soft drinks removed in a measure before the Texas Senate in Austin sometime in the 2020s, says the American Heart Association, a large US charity focused on heart health, "showed up to testify against us at the original one." Buhler was there himself, and he offers it as a sign of "the world we live in now," where a health group sided against cutting soft drinks.
american-orthodox-catholic-church-demand: Around 1965 in the Bronx, New York, the head of a small church called the American Orthodox Catholic Church, a man known as Propheta, began demanding that other churches submit to FBI background checks before he would accept them. The historian Peter Levenda tells this on Michels' show. In a second telling Levenda says Propheta's own people were vetted by FBI director J. Edgar Hoover himself, and places it in 1968 or 1969 instead.
american-pilots-trained-to-fly-ufos-desp: In a deep underground facility in California, American pilots were trained to fly UFOs, though flying them caused a displacement in time. The philosopher Jason Jorjani tells Michels this was passed on to Lyn Buchanan, a psychic spy from a US Army program that used mind-reading techniques, by the people running it. If true, the military would already be flying such craft.
american-soldier-s-off-record-sighting: An American soldier is said to have seen a UFO above the top of his own house but refused to say so publicly, because he feared he would lose his US pension. Italo Venturelli, a senior surgeon who has his own story to tell, repeats what the soldier told him, as a sign that witnesses keep quiet out of fear.
ammonia-smell-and-staining-inside-the-re: Inside the Red Pyramid, an ancient pyramid at Dahshur in Egypt, there is "chemical staining all over the walls and an intense smell of ammonia" coming from the final chamber, says a researcher named Geoffrey Drumm, who says he went in himself in 2017. Drumm, who says an alien gave him the true purpose of the pyramids, offers it as a sign that the pyramid once served some chemical process rather than as a tomb.
amsterdam-secret-space-program-symposium: The writer Peter Levenda, billed on the show as a CIA historian, says he once gave a talk in Amsterdam, around 2007 or 2008, at a gathering about a "secret space program", a supposed hidden government effort in space, where UFOs and the Kennedy assassination came up. He tells it first-hand and says that talk is why people later assumed things about his views. He mentions the UFO writers Richard Dolan and Timothy Good in connection with it.
amy-reynolds-taken-and-found-at-a-petrol: A woman named Amy Reynolds was taken while her friend, a woman named Petra, watched it happen through a window, and soon afterwards the friends got a call saying Amy had been found at a petrol station 790 kilometres away. The researcher Mike Masters tells it on Jesse Michels's show as one of his favourite cases, summarising it without naming a source. If true, it would mean someone was moved a huge distance in a very short time.
an-advanced-civilization-made-the-geneti: A civilization more advanced than ours may have made the genetic mix seen in the strange three-fingered bodies found near Nazca, Peru, some 1,800 years ago. That is the view of a researcher named Thierry Jamin, who gives it on Michels' show without naming a source. "If you go back 1,800 years, it's crazy," he says, and if he is right, someone in the distant past was mixing genes with skill beyond ours.
an-alien-pilot-teaches-buchanan-to-fly-a: A non-human pilot once took Lyn Buchanan, a former Army sergeant, to the front of a flying craft and let him take the controls, and Buchanan says he learned how to fly it. He tells it as his own experience. In one telling he adds that he was taken from the parsonage of a country church in East Texas, sometime between 1963 and 1965, and that the craft landed somewhere that was not Earth.
an-angel-with-a-sword-over-jerusalem-dur: In the Bible, after King David counts his people in a census and a plague follows, an angel is said to stand over Jerusalem with a drawn sword. Michels tells it himself from the Bible, in an episode about Air Force veterans who say they were abducted by aliens. He raises it as an ancient account of a powerful being appearing in the sky.
an-anonymous-frontier-physicist-s-experi: A very high-level physicist, a friend of Michels, had an experience of his own that Michels mentions. Michels passes it on second-hand and keeps the man anonymous, giving few details beyond who the friend is.
an-insectoid-working-in-a-row-of-humans-: During a classified mission at a military facility, Lyn Buchanan says he walked past a row of humans at work and saw among them one of "what they call the insectoids," an insect-like being. Buchanan, a former Army sergeant, tells it as something he saw, but hedges that "it could have been a soldier that just put on an alien hat," because the minute he saw it he looked away and kept walking. If it was what it seemed, it would mean a non-human being working alongside military staff.
an-nsc-staffer-told-andreessen-and-horow: The tech investors Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz are said to have been told by a staffer on the National Security Council, the White House body that advises the president on security, that whole areas of physics had been classified in the past. The analyst Matthew Pines calls it hearsay but gives the line as "we have classified entire areas of fundamental physics before, don't think we can do the same for AI." Michels repeats it as backing for the idea of hidden physics, and in another telling credits an interview Andreessen gave to the journalist Bari Weiss, where Andreessen says he was told only "two or three guys" would be allowed to do AI. The researcher Eric Weinstein says the pair were told "do not invest in AI startups" and that math itself could be classified, and a guest named Pippa Malmgren, crediting Weinstein, says many technologies, "particularly in the nuclear space," were put out of public reach. If true, it would mean the government has hidden parts of basic science before.
an-ultra-orthodox-community-in-israel-ha: A family named Golden, including Arthur Golden and Ben Golden, live in a very ultra-Orthodox community in Israel and, as the story goes, 'have their own Hill'. Ky Dickens, maker of a documentary about children said to read minds, tells this on Michels' show, passing on what she was told.
anakah-and-tristan-s-off-world-past-live: Two people named Anakah and Tristan say they remember past lives on other planets, outside the Earth, and that they are here on a mission to make humanity's first contact with aliens go more smoothly. Jeffrey Mishlove, a psychologist with a PhD who studies psychic matters, relays their claims to Michels.
analysing-element-115-with-barry-at-s4-1: A man named Bob Lazar, who says he worked on alien craft at S4, a secret site near Area 51 in the Nevada desert, says that in 1988 and 1989 he and a colleague named Barry were working on element 115, a very heavy substance he links to how the craft were powered. He tells Michels the element was not discovered by them as such, but was something he and Barry were studying. He speaks from his own part in the work, and if true it would mean scientists were studying exotic material from a craft not built by people.
analysis-by-merrick-s-colleagues-points-: The object in the FLIR1 video, an infrared clip a Navy jet recorded in 2004 over the Pacific off Southern California, was a "Tic Tac shaped craft": a white oval object shaped like the mint. The guest Marik von Rennenkampff says he has "fairly high confidence" in this, resting it on analysis by an unnamed California scientist, during an episode where he faces the skeptic Mick West, who reads the same footage as a distant aircraft or a balloon. If true, it would mean the video shows a real craft of unusual shape.
analysis-of-coburn-s-toe-implant-skewed-: A small object was taken from the toe of a man named Coburn in California, with money from a man named Haime Masan and through a doctor named Roger Leir, and testing found odd isotope ratios (the mix of atom types in an element) and signs of very tiny engineered parts. The scientist Steve Colbern says he did the testing himself, because the lab where he worked had the equipment and no one else was lined up to do it, and the results were later written up in a paper; he tells it as evidence that the object was not natural or ordinary.
analysis-of-heavy-element-real-deal-mate: People who analysed material from 'the real deal', meaning genuine recovered UFO material, found it super weird, full of heavy elements like europium and californium. David Grusch, a former intelligence officer turned whistleblower, says this on Michels' show, passing on what those analysts told him. He says it in two episodes, naming the elements only in the second.
analysis-of-san-augustine-new-mexico-cra: A scientist named Steve Colbern, who studies objects said to be alien implants in human bodies, says he analyzed wreckage from a UFO crash at San Augustine, New Mexico, in 1947. He tells it as his own lab work. If true, it would mean physical pieces of a crashed craft from that year still exist and have been tested.
analysis-of-titanium-nanotube-sphere-lat: A sphere recovered in Mexico and studied in the United States was made of a titanium alloy with carbon nanotubes, tiny tubes of carbon, built into the metal, according to Steve Colbern, a scientist who studies objects said to be alien implants and who says he worked on it. Colbern thinks the nanotubes gave it thrust through the Biefeld-Brown effect, a claimed push produced by high voltage across charged surfaces. He says the sphere was later stolen, so it would have been physical evidence of an engineered flying object that is now gone.
ancestor-rediscovers-the-seven-lost-span: An ancestor of the researcher Luke Caverns went looking for the seven lost Spanish gold mines of southern New Mexico, found them within a year, and opened mines some 450 years old. Caverns tells this family story to Michels as something passed down to him.
ancestry-search-places-sherman-in-omaha-: A search on the family-history website ancestry.com showed that Dan Sherman, a former Air Force sergeant who says the National Security Agency hired him to communicate with aliens, likely lived in Omaha, Nebraska, in 1993 and 1994. Omaha is near Offutt Air Force Base. Michels tells this himself, crediting the search to a man named Richard Geldreich, and offers it as support for Sherman's account of where he served.
ancient-architects-on-the-giza-water-tab: A study about the water lying underground at Giza, the plateau in Egypt where the great pyramids stand, was taken apart by a member of the research community who goes by the name Ancient Architects. The researcher Jeffrey Drum shows this work on Michels's show, crediting Ancient Architects and saying that person basically debunked the study, though he does not name the study itself.
ancient-as-above-so-below-symbol-on-prop: There is a symbol on Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property known for reports of strange events, that the ranch's owner says dates "from ancient times" and seems to stand for "as above, so below," which he calls a Masonic symbol, meaning one tied to the Freemasons, a centuries-old secret fraternity. The owner, who is not named in these tellings, speaks as someone who knows the land first-hand, and he raises it in an episode about a UFO said to lie under the ranch, as though the symbol hints that what happens in the sky mirrors something underground.
ancient-chess-pieces-in-mongolian-burial: Kiran Ilum Xenov, a former president of a republic inside Russia who says he was taken by aliens in 1997, says archaeologists digging burial mounds in Mongolia found chess-like figures, some more than 5,000 years old. He also mentions Peru, and he offers the find, without naming a source, as a sign that chess was a gift from beings not from Earth.
ancient-chinese-diagram-of-twin-serpent-: An old Chinese diagram is said to show twin serpent creator gods twisted around each other like a double helix, the spiral-ladder shape of DNA. The writer Peter Levenda says he found it himself, calling it "a diagram from ancient China going back 600 years," and he points to a work called Stairway to Heaven. If true, people long ago drew something that looks like the shape of life's genetic code.
ancient-precision-buildings-in-peru-leba: The ancient buildings of Peru, Lebanon and Egypt, the pyramids among them, were built "with such precision" that they must be the work of another civilization, according to a man named Kiran Ilum Xenov. Xenov, whom the episode presents as the president of a Russian republic who says he was taken by aliens in 1997, offers this to Jesse Michels as his own view, without naming a source.
ancient-south-american-bird-models-resem: Some small ancient models from South America, usually described as birds, are said to look like airplanes. Greg Rogers, a guest the episode calls a NASA doctor, mentions them in passing without naming a source, as an example of old objects that may not be what they are labelled.
ancient-spartan-doctor-s-treatise-descri: In ancient Sparta, a doctor wrote a treatise describing the lasting mental harm of combat, what we now call post-traumatic stress disorder. A doctor named Greg Rogers, who has worked with NASA, says this from his own knowledge, as proof that war trauma has been recognised for thousands of years.
ancient-temples-dismantled-and-items-rem: Certain ancient temples, in the region around Lake Van in Turkey, were deliberately taken apart and things were removed from them. The researcher Matt LaCroix says so on Michels's show, telling it on his own account without naming a source, and says he has found very compelling evidence that it happened, which would mean someone has been hiding traces of the deep past.
ancient-terrestrial-civilization-with-ne: An advanced civilization may have lived on Earth hundreds of millions of years ago, possibly travelling at close to the speed of light, with all evidence later wiped away as the planet's surface was reshaped. Eric Haseltine, billed as a former senior official at the National Security Agency, the US electronic spying agency, raises this on Michels' show as one of the ideas explored with Chris Gilbert in the book The New Science of UFOs.
andres-gomez-emilsson-s-dmt-accounts-at-: At a psychedelic science conference in Denver in 2025, the consciousness researcher Andrés Gómez Emilsson shared his accounts of DMT, a powerful drug that many users say opens a realm of other beings. The neuroscientist Andrew Gallimore tells Michels he spoke with Emilsson there just days before, bringing it up as one more report of what people meet on the drug.
andrew-basiago-claims-he-went-back-to-th: A man named Andrew Basiago claims he travelled back in time, through a secret government programme, to see the Gettysburg Address, the short speech Abraham Lincoln gave at Gettysburg, Pennsylvania, in 1863. Michels states the claim himself, while talking with the researcher Grant Cameron, stressing that Basiago says this quite literally.
andrew-gallimore-dmt-experiments-and-ent: A researcher named Andrew Gallimore runs experiments with DMT, a powerful psychedelic drug, in which people report meeting beings that seem to fall into the same consistent types from one person to the next. Michels brings this up only in passing, noting that his guest, the scientist Donald Hoffman, is working with Gallimore. The point is that if different people meet the same kinds of beings, those beings might be more than imagination.
andrija-puharich-the-ossining-space-kids: Andrija Puharich, a researcher whom Jesse Michels calls the father of much of the CIA's mind control work under MK Ultra, the agency's secret programme of the 1950s and 60s, also came into contact with what he took to be non-human intelligences. Michels says Puharich worked with so-called "space kids" in Ossining, New York, who channelled messages, a story tied to a group of beings known as the Council of Nine. Michels tells it from the work of others, citing a researcher named Greg Malatzi and a work called Mind Traveler. It would mean that a man inside the government's mind research was also talking with beings he believed were not human.
andy-hall-s-article-supporting-the-chemi: A writer named Andy Hall, linked to the Thunderbolts Project, a group that argues electricity shapes the universe, is said to have written a long article on his website backing the idea that the pyramids were chemical manufacturing plants powered by the Earth's electricity. Geoffrey Drumm, the researcher who proposed that idea, tells this himself, saying the article praised his work and gave reasons it was right.
angel-hair-and-an-ablative-craft-hull: The outer skin of a UFO may be ablative, meaning it is built to burn or wear away on purpose to protect the craft, and that shedding could explain angel hair, the fine wispy threads sometimes reported falling after sightings. Luis Elizondo, a former Pentagon official who ran a small UFO study office, offers this as his own idea and says he wrote about it in his book Imminent, published in 2024.
angel-hierarchies-of-aquinas-line-up-wit: The ranks of angels described by Thomas Aquinas, the medieval Christian theologian, are said to match many modern encounters with what people now call non-human intelligence, beings that are neither human nor animal. Jesse Michels passes this on from a conversation between Karl Nell, a retired Army colonel, and Diana Pasulka, a professor who studies religion. In another episode he makes the point in his own voice, credits Iamblichus, an ancient Greek philosopher, as well, and gives "irradiated light" as one detail the old accounts share with today's sightings. If it holds, today's encounters would be part of something people have been describing for centuries.
angleton-and-others-on-george-c-marshall: Many of the key figures in the hidden history of UFOs, including James Jesus Angleton, who went on to become a central figure at the CIA, the US spy agency, all seem to have served on the team of General George C. Marshall, the top American general of the Second World War. Pippa Malmgren, appearing alongside her father Harald Malmgren, a former presidential advisor, says this is what she keeps finding, without naming a source, and she also mentions John F. Kennedy and James Forrestal. If true, it would mean one close-knit circle from the war years shaped how secrets were kept afterward.
angleton-and-reuben-efron-s-mail-interce: Between 1959 and 1963 the CIA secretly opened and read the mail of Lee Harvey Oswald, the man accused of killing President John F. Kennedy, in an operation linked to James Jesus Angleton, the agency's counterintelligence chief, and to a man named Reuben Efron. That is according to Jeremy Riss, a researcher, who credits the JFK files (the government's records on the assassination) but names no particular document. Riss says Efron's name is in those files, and that when one person was asked whether they knew Efron and said no, that was a lie, which would mean the CIA was watching Oswald more closely than it admitted.
angleton-as-oss-man-in-italy-1940: A man named James Jesus Angleton was, so the story goes, the American intelligence officer working in Italy in the 1940s for the OSS, the United States' wartime spy service. Michels passes this on from a woman named Pippa Malmgren, who he says made it clear to him that Angleton was the US OSS person involved in Italy at the time. If true, it would put Angleton at the centre of American secret work in postwar Italy.
angleton-may-have-pushed-mj-12-as-counte: The so-called Majestic 12, or MJ-12, documents are papers that describe a secret group said to have handled UFO matters for the US government, and Jesse Michels suggests they may have been pushed out, or even made, by James Jesus Angleton, a longtime counterintelligence officer at the CIA, the US spy agency. Michels raises this himself on three episodes, without naming a source, and grows firmer each time: first as a maybe, then as something he has heard and does not know is true, and finally as his personal belief that Angleton created many of the documents in the 1980s and 90s, mainly to catch Soviet spies. If so, the papers would be a spy trap rather than a window on real UFO secrets.
angleton-probably-leaked-the-mj12-docume: James Jesus Angleton, the CIA's longtime head of counterintelligence, was probably the person behind the leak of the MJ12 documents, papers that describe a secret group of twelve officials said to handle crashed UFOs. Michels says this was passed on to him by Harold Malmgren, a former senior Washington official, who told him Angleton "is probably responsible for the MJ12 docs getting leaked." If so, the papers would have come out of the heart of the intelligence world on purpose.
angleton-s-father-and-the-knights-of-mal: James Jesus Angleton, the longtime spy-catching chief of the CIA, and his father Hugh Angleton are said to have been tied to the Knights of Malta, an old Catholic order of knights, in 1930s and 1940s Italy and the Vatican, and through it to secret knowledge of UFOs. Harold Malmgren, a former advisor to US presidents, says "the relationship needs to be uncovered," and that they knew about UFOs "because Angleton was there." Michels goes further and states that both men were Knights of Malta. In a later episode he says Malmgren was obsessed with the idea that the order had something to do with a craft said to have crashed near Magenta, in northern Italy, in 1933.
angleton-signed-cia-wiretap-of-marilyn-m: In 1962 the CIA, the US spy agency, is said to have wiretapped the actress Marilyn Monroe, catching her threatening to hold a press conference a couple of days before, in his words, "they killed her," in a document signed by James Jesus Angleton, the agency's head of counterintelligence. Steven Greer, a former emergency doctor who campaigns for UFO disclosure, tells this and says the wiretap is reproduced in a briefing document he put together. If true, it would tie her death to what she was about to reveal.
angry-owens-gives-mishlove-a-sore-throat: In 1976, a man named Ted Owens, who claimed psychic powers, is said to have hurt a researcher over the phone just by getting angry. The person on the other end was Jeffrey Mishlove, a researcher of psychic phenomena with a PhD, and he tells it himself: "He got angry and within minutes I could feel this sensation in my throat." Mishlove wrote about Owens in a book called The PK Man, where "PK" stands for psychokinesis, the claimed power of mind over matter. Jesse Michels retells the story secondhand in another episode, with the writer Jason Jorjani as guest. His version is a bit more dramatic: Mishlove suddenly could not breathe during the call. If true, it would suggest that one person's mind can affect another's body at a distance.
animals-found-dead-at-the-varginha-zoo-a: In 1996, a strange being was reportedly captured in the Brazilian town of Varginha, and animals at the town zoo that came into contact with it were later found dead. Ahmed Foratu, a guest on the show, tells this second-hand from the documentary filmmaker James Fox. Fox adds that a scientist named Marco Le told him on camera that the cause of death was completely unknown, something he had never seen before, which would suggest the creature carried something deadly.
anna-paulina-luna-calls-for-aaro-defundi: In 2025 Representative Anna Paulina Luna, a member of the US Congress, posted on social media that the Pentagon's current UFO investigation office is a hopeless cause, part of a push to cut its funding. The journalist Ross Coulthart brings up her posts from that week, citing them as a sign that lawmakers have lost faith in the office.
anna-paulina-luna-on-joe-rogan-read-the-: A US congresswoman named Anna Paulina Luna told Joe Rogan, host of a popular interview podcast, that anyone curious where unidentified flying objects come from should read the Book of Enoch, an ancient religious text, here in a translation by the scholar R. H. Charles. In her words, the book "talks about the fall of angels," which created "the precursor of civilization that led to the first flood," and her remarks come up on an episode with the researcher Tim Alberino as a hint that these beings may be very old.
anna-paulina-luna-s-mk-ultra-hearing-202: In 2026 a member of the US Congress named Anna Paulina Luna held a large congressional hearing on MK Ultra, a secret CIA programme of mind-control experiments, according to the writer and skeptic Michael Shermer. Shermer mentions it in passing while debating Jesse Michels, saying the researcher Avi Loeb is friends with Luna, who "seems to be an insider", and that her hearing on MK Ultra took place "just yesterday".
anne-finds-the-letters-link-the-visitors: After reading the letters readers sent about the beings they called visitors, Anne Strieber concluded that these beings have something to do with death. Her husband, the author Whitley Strieber, tells Jesse Michels that she came out of her office one day and said, "Whitley, this has something to do with what we call death." The letters came in response to his book Communion, about his own encounters, in the late 1980s. If she was right, the visitors would be bound up with the dead and not simply with other planets.
annie-jacobsen-s-source-o-donnell-roswel: The claim is that the craft said to have crashed near Roswell, New Mexico, in 1947 was a hoax built under the Soviet leader Stalin with help from the Nazi doctor Mengele. The idea is tied to a source named Alfred O'Donnell, whom Michels says was also the source for the author Annie Jacobsen in her book Area 51, and who she talked about on the interviewer Lex Fridman's show. In another episode Michels puts Jacobsen's version differently: he says she has the bodies as geriatric-looking children used as crash dummies, and there he names neither O'Donnell nor Stalin. If true, it would mean the famous crash was a human trick, not anything from elsewhere.
annie-jacobson-hunt-for-the-horten-broth: At the end of the Second World War in 1945, the Americans badly wanted to find the Horten brothers, German aircraft designers who built flying-wing planes for the Nazis. Michels tells this as something the journalist Annie Jacobsen wrote in her 2011 book Area 51, about the secret Nevada air base.
anomalous-craft-show-interest-in-white-s: Unknown craft have shown a special interest in White Sands, a military missile testing range in New Mexico, and in nearby Los Alamos National Laboratory, where America's nuclear weapons were first built, according to Matthew Brown, a former Pentagon official turned whistleblower. Brown says he has more to say about how these anomalous technologies have hovered around those sites, which would suggest they are watching America's most sensitive weapons work.
anomalous-metal-containing-51-elements-i: A strange piece of metal is said to hold 51 elements blended together, among them plutonium and even human DNA, at a time when humans could only get about 15 elements to blend. Chris Bledsoe, a man featured on the show as someone who seems to draw UFOs to him, says this was told to him by someone else, whose name is not given. If true, it would mean the metal was made by something far beyond human skill.
anomalous-objects-seen-by-a-navy-acousti: On a Navy ship off Japan whose job was gathering intelligence by listening underwater, the crew is said to have seen unexplained objects on two occasions. Tim Gallaudet, a retired Navy rear admiral, passes this on from a man he knew, an acoustic specialist who retired as a Navy captain and served on one of those ships. Gallaudet tells it as more evidence that strange objects show up at sea.
anonymous-navy-friend-says-the-abyss-sce: A friend of Jesse Michels in the Navy, whom he does not name, told him that a scene in The Abyss, a film by the director James Cameron set in the deep ocean, where a glowing object appears, "isn't too far off from the truth." Michels passes this on second-hand. If true, it would hint that something like that glowing thing has been seen in the deep sea.
anonymous-navy-scientist-on-extended-ele: Jesse Michels says a top Navy scientist told him about extended electrodynamics, a broader version of the theory of electricity and magnetism that the scientist ties to the physicists James Clerk Maxwell and Oliver Heaviside. Michels says he interviewed this man for his film on an inventor named Thomas Townsend Brown, which he calls 'The Man Who Built UFOs for the CIA', and that the scientist stayed anonymous for fear of reprisals from his superiors. Michels brings it up in several episodes as a possible physics behind unexplained craft, calling the man a scientist in one and a whistleblower in another.
anonymous-sources-bodies-came-from-a-sub: The strange three-fingered bodies said to have been found around Nazca, in Peru, actually come from a large underground tunnel system. Michels says this himself, and he says it was told to him by a few different sources he does not name. If true, it would point to where the bodies really came from and what else might lie below.
anonymous-usaf-colonel-and-fighter-pilot: A US Air Force colonel and fighter pilot, never named, had a dramatic UFO encounter in about 1980, according to what he told the UFO documentary maker James Fox. Fox repeats it second-hand and gives no details beyond the rough year and how dramatic it was, saying it happened "in 1980 or something like that."
anonymous-whistleblower-on-crash-retriev: Around 2009, a man is said to have served on a crash retrieval team, a crew that recovers downed craft of unknown origin, out in the far north of the Nevada desert, on land once called the Nevada Test Range. Steven Greer, a UFO researcher and activist, passes this on from an anonymous whistleblower who told him he was "on a team retrieving these objects." If true, such recoveries were still going on in recent years.
another-aerospace-company-leaves-the-wor: A second aerospace company that had been working on unexplained craft, trying to figure out how they worked, is said to have dropped that work by the early 1970s. Eric W. Davis, a physicist, tells it from memory of what a senior vice president at that company told him: in Davis's words, the company "kind of uh left that whole line of work." If true, it would mean more than one private firm once had this work and at least one walked away.
another-channeler-also-predicted-the-cha: In 1986, a second channeler, meaning a person who claims to pass on messages from spirits or other beings, is said to have predicted the explosion of the Challenger space shuttle, just as another channeler had. The parapsychologist Jeffrey Mishlove tells it: after the disaster he heard from the Foundation for Mind Being Research, a group in the San Francisco Bay Area, that they knew of another channeler somewhere who had made the same prediction. If true, two separate people foretold the same event.
antarctica-as-the-nordics-main-subterran: Antarctica is said to be the main underground and undersea base of the "Nordics", a human-looking group of beings that some UFO stories describe. The philosopher Jason Jorjani says this to Michels in his own words, without naming a source, and refers back to an earlier conversation the two had about these beings. If true, it would put a hidden non-human presence beneath the ice of the far south.
anthony-hopkins-finds-feifer-s-annotated: The actor Anthony Hopkins is said to have stumbled on a copy of the novel The Girl from Petrovka, by the writer George Feifer, lying on a bench at Leicester Square tube station in London around 1972, and the copy turned out to be Feifer's own annotated one. The skeptic writer Michael Shermer tells it without naming a source: Hopkins was "heading for home" when he "chanced upon a book on a bench." It is told as a striking coincidence, the kind that seems to mean more than chance.
anti-drone-technology-fails-at-pseg-sale: In 2024, staff at the Salem and Hope Creek nuclear power plants in Salem County, New Jersey, run by the power company PSEG, are said to have aimed anti-drone equipment at several drones flying over the site, and the equipment, which normally works on any drone, failed completely. Robert Hastings, a researcher who has long collected reports of UFOs at nuclear sites, relays this from an unnamed person with access to the plant's internal messages. If true, the objects were something ordinary drone defences could not touch.
anti-gravity-researcher-amy-eskridge-and: Amy Eskridge, a scientist in Alabama who studied anti-gravity, died in 2022, and Michels says that near the end of her life she kept talking about a "sixth force" of nature. He describes her death as happening "under very mysterious circumstances." In another episode he goes further, crediting her father Richard Eskridge: people were attacking her with directed energy, meaning beam weapons, and she had burns on her hands at the end. A news report played on the show says only that she was "openly studying anti-gravity technology when she died in 2022," with nothing about the sixth force or the burns. If true, it would mean someone wanted her research stopped.
antikythera-mechanism: The Antikythera mechanism is an ancient device that works almost like a small computer for tracking the sky, and it was found in a shipwreck in the Aegean Sea. Michels brings it up on three episodes, in his own words and without a named source, each time as proof that ancient people were more advanced than we think. Once he places the find on a Greek island instead, and mentions it next to a book called Forbidden Archaeology.
anton-bilton-s-proposed-dmt-telepathy-ex: A man named Anton Bilton thought about giving people DMT, a powerful psychedelic drug, and placing them in side-by-side Faraday cages, metal enclosures that block radio signals, to see whether they could share thoughts. Michels mentions the idea in passing, in a talk with the neuroscientist Andrew Gallimore about DMT and the visions it brings.
antonio-villas-boas-has-intercourse-with: In Brazil in 1957, a man named Antonio Villas Boas is said to have been taken aboard a craft and to have had sex with a being who looked like a woman. The researcher Mike Masters describes it, saying Villas Boas called her a woman who looked a little different from women he knew, with slightly higher cheekbones and a pointier chin. Michels mentions the case himself on an episode about Brazil, placing it in the 1960s and calling it one of many cases where people seem to interact with the beings and go up on the ships. It is told as a case of physical contact between humans and visitors.
anunnaki-came-to-earth-to-mine-gold: Beings called the Anunnaki, known from ancient Middle Eastern stories, came to Earth to mine gold and other precious metals. A guest named Geoffrey Drumm repeats this on Michels's show as the story of the Anunnaki, without citing a source, in a conversation about what he believes the pyramids were really for.
apollo-11-crew-observes-a-glowing-arista: During Apollo 11, the 1969 mission that first landed people on the Moon, the crew is said to have looked at Aristarchus, a crater on the Moon, after astronomers in Germany reported it looked unusually bright. A researcher on the show tells it second-hand, naming the crew, Neil Armstrong, Buzz Aldrin and Michael Collins, and offering only that "apparently" the German astronomers had seen the glow. It belongs to a group of stories claiming the Apollo 11 astronauts saw strange things on or near the Moon.
apollo-11-halfway-to-the-moon-window-foo: The claim is that film shot during Apollo 11, the 1969 mission that put men on the moon, shows the astronauts saying they were about halfway to the moon when they were really still close to Earth. The podcaster Joe Rogan raises it with Michels, passing on what he says a man named Bart Sibrel has: uncovered footage in which the crew say they are hundreds of thousands of miles out, or halfway there. If true, it would mean that at least part of the trip was staged for the camera.
apollo-11-post-flight-press-conference-l: The press conference the Apollo 11 astronauts gave in 1969, after returning from the first Moon landing, looks deceptive, "like a hostage video," in the words of Joe Rogan, the comedian and podcaster. Rogan urges people to watch it and leans on the view of a body language expert he does not name, the suggestion being that the astronauts were hiding something about the trip.
apollo-11-timing-trinity-anniversary-and: Apollo 11, the first mission to land people on the Moon, was launched on July 16, 1969, exactly 24 years after the Trinity test, the first atomic bomb test, which opened the nuclear age, and the timing is also tied to the astrological sign of Aquarius. Michels points this out himself, without naming a source, suggesting that if the date was chosen on purpose, the launch had a ritual meaning.
apollo-11-trio-of-lights-frame-1969: Footage from the Apollo 11 Moon landing in 1969 is said to show a group of three lights, the same pattern also seen in Apollo 17 footage. A guest named Maaneli Derakhshani, who has studied the images, points this out without naming a source. He raises it because the same trio turning up on two missions would suggest something was really there on the Moon.
apollo-11-watched-by-craft-on-the-moon-a: During Apollo 11, the 1969 mission that first landed people on the Moon, the crew is said to have been watched by craft on the lunar surface and followed on the way there, with the astronaut Neil Armstrong speaking on a private channel after landing. The scientist Steve Colbern, who studies objects said to be alien implants, repeats this from unnamed whistleblowers at NASA, the US space agency, who he says reported that Armstrong "was on a private channel after landing on the moon." If true, it would mean the first Moon landing had company that was kept off the public broadcast.
apollo-13-zapped-because-of-a-nuclear-de: Apollo 13, the 1970 NASA moon mission that had to turn back after an explosion on board, may not have failed from a mechanical fault but been "zapped by the aliens" because it may have carried a nuclear warhead. That is what Steve Colbern, a scientist who studies objects said to be alien implants, says he found out, pointing to the Atomic Energy Commission, the old US agency in charge of nuclear material.
apollo-14-blue-orb-above-mitchell-blacke: A photo from the 1971 Apollo 14 moon landing shows a blue ball of light hanging in the lunar sky above the astronaut Edgar Mitchell, and in one archive copy that spot is said to be blacked out. A researcher named Maaneli Derakhshani makes the claim on the show without naming a source. He says the orb is "very obvious above uh Mitchell" in the version kept by a second archive, while the scan held by the Lunar and Planetary Institute, a US science archive of moon images, hides it. He also mentions the journalist Ross Coulthart. If true, it would mean something unexplained was photographed on the moon and later covered up.
apollo-17-insectoid-metallic-probe-in-lu: A photo from Apollo 17, the 1972 NASA moon landing with astronauts Eugene Cernan and Harrison Schmitt, shows something in the lunar sky that, once the image is brightened a little, "almost looks like an insectoid type probe," a bluish metallic object. The guest Maaneli Derakhshani describes it himself, from NASA's public archive of Apollo images. If true, it would mean some unknown device was near the astronauts on the Moon.
apollo-17-trio-of-blue-lights-1972: A photo from Apollo 17, the 1972 Moon landing mission, is said to show three solid-looking blue lights, spaced almost evenly apart, in a small patch of the lunar sky. Maaneli Derakhshani, a researcher, describes this from a raw scan of one of the mission's photo frames, which he studied himself. If the lights are real objects, something would have been in the sky above the landing site.
apollo-8-launched-on-the-winter-solstice: Apollo 8, the NASA mission that first carried astronauts around the Moon, launched on 21 December 1968, the winter solstice, the day the sun is symbolically reborn after the longest night of the year. Michels points this out himself, without naming a source, as part of his argument that the space programme was steeped in old pagan symbolism.
apollo-astronauts-given-suicide-pills-19: The Apollo astronauts who went to the Moon were all given some kind of pill that would kill them if anything went wrong. The documentary filmmaker James Fox repeats this from a woman named Fay Ann Potter, who said NASA officials had told her so. If true, it would mean NASA planned for its astronauts to die rather than be stranded or caught in some disaster.
apollo-crew-followed-by-something-to-the: The crew of Apollo 11, the first moon landing mission in 1969, is said to have been followed by something on the way to the moon. A UFO documentary maker named James Fox says he heard this from Fay Ann Potter, the sister of the astronaut Buzz Aldrin, who told him Aldrin had said "they were followed by something to the Moon"; in another telling he calls it simply a UFO encounter Aldrin had on the way. Michels tells it differently, saying Aldrin himself admitted openly in several interviews that "this thing" was following them. If true, it would mean something unknown shadowed the first trip to the moon.
apollo-intersecting-shadows-suggest-mult: Some photos from the Apollo Moon landings of 1969 show shadows that cross each other, which some take as a sign of more than one light source, when the Sun should be the only one. The podcaster Joe Rogan raises it in conversation with Michels, saying people like to try to dismiss these intersecting shadows. If the point held, it would mean the pictures were not lit by sunlight alone.
apollo-lunar-dust-in-charles-s-lab-and-l: About 200 grams of Moon dust from the Apollo missions, NASA's Moon landings of 1969 to 1972, sits in his own lab, says Charles Buhler, a NASA scientist. He tells it first-hand. The conversation also turns to the retroreflectors, mirrors the astronauts left on the Moon that bounce laser light back to Earth, as physical traces of those landings.
apollo-lunar-photo-lights-and-buzz-aldri: The claim is that small blue lights seen in photos from the Moon missions, and the flashes of light the astronaut Buzz Aldrin said he saw inside his cabin, were caused by cosmic rays, fast particles from space hitting cameras and eyes. Michael Shermer, a well-known skeptic, says the Harvard astronomer Avi Loeb thinks so and that Loeb is "probably right". The physicist Maaneli Derakhshani also credits Loeb, tying it to a trio of blue lights from the Apollo 17 mission. Michels, on the same episode, credits instead the astrophysicist Neil deGrasse Tyson, who he says treated the Apollo 17 sightings as "case closed, cosmic rays". If the explanation holds, these lights would be ordinary physics rather than anything flying near the Moon.
apollo-telemetry-data-and-original-foota: The telemetry from the Apollo missions, the NASA flights that landed men on the moon starting in 1969, is said to have been destroyed, along with original footage. Telemetry is the data radioed back from a spacecraft. The comedian and podcaster Joe Rogan says it on the show: "all the telemetry data was destroyed, which is crazy," and he tells it as something that raises questions about what records of the missions survive.
aquarius-document-analyses-benowitz-film: In 1981, around Kirtland Air Force Base in Albuquerque, New Mexico, a UFO researcher named Bill Moore handed a local man named Paul Bennewitz, who had been filming strange lights near the base, a paper called the Aquarius document, which supposedly dealt with his films. The writer Greg Bishop, who researched the affair, says the paper "actually mentions access only to MJ12", meaning MJ-12, a supposed top secret committee in charge of UFO matters. Bishop calls the Aquarius document fake and says it was the first time anybody had mentioned MJ-12 at all, so the famous name may have started in a planted paper.
aquinas-s-mystical-experience-at-mass: Thomas Aquinas, the medieval Catholic thinker, is said to have had a sudden spiritual awakening during mass while writing the Summa Theologica, his long effort to explain God through reason. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source. He uses it to show that even the most rational mind can be changed by a direct mystical experience.
aquino-and-phoenix-program-psychological: A man named Michael Aquino served as a psychological warfare officer in the Vietnam War and was part of the Phoenix program, a US operation in that war. The writer Peter Levenda says so without naming a source, in a conversation tied to his book The Lovecraft Code. He tells it to place Aquino inside the military's mind-influence work.
archaeological-retrieval-of-craft-from-t: Matthew Brown, a former Pentagon official who has come forward as a whistleblower, describes craft being dug up from the ocean floor like an archaeological dig. He points out that something buried under tens of meters of sediment must have been lying there a very long time, since that much sediment takes ages to build up, which would mean the craft are very old.
archaeologist-who-excavated-amenemhat-ii: The archaeologist who dug out the pyramid of Amenemhat III, an ancient Egyptian king, is said to have argued that it was never a real tomb. In his view it was only a symbolic tomb for the king's ka, the life force the Egyptians believed every person had. The researcher Luke Caverns tells this, citing an archaeologist of the 1800s whose name, he says, "starts with a P." If true, at least some pyramids were not built as burial places.
archive-research-nixon-could-slip-his-se: Richard Nixon, US president from 1969 to 1974, is said to have slipped away from his security detail many times, including around his Florida home in Key Biscayne. Grant Cameron, a longtime UFO researcher, says he had heard claims that Nixon could never get away from his guards, so he checked Nixon's records at the National Archives and found that "sure enough he got away from his security lots of times." He tells it to show that a president could have gone somewhere unseen, against the claim that he could not.
archuleta-reports-a-crashed-plane-to-the: In 1948, a man named Valentine Archeletta called the Air Force, at Kirtland Air Force Base in New Mexico, to say, "Hey, one of your planes crashed over here. You need to come get it," about something that had come down on his ranch. Scott Ramsey, who tells the story, passes on what Archeletta said, and tells it as the start of a crash that, in Ramsey's account, was no ordinary plane.
area-51-barely-discussed-before-lazar-19: Area 51, a secret military test site in the Nevada desert, was hardly ever talked about before 1989, when a man named Bob Lazar went public with claims about the place. That is how Michels puts it himself, without naming a source, as a way of saying that one man's story is what put the base on the map.
area-51-caller-extradimensional-beings-c: In 1997 a caller to Coast to Coast AM, a late-night American radio show then hosted by Art Bell, said that what we think of as aliens are really "extradimensional beings," beings from another dimension, that "an earlier precursor of the space program made contact with." The caller presented himself as someone with first-hand knowledge of Area 51, a secret US military test site in Nevada, and the recording comes up in an episode with the hip hop artist Flying Lotus. If true, it would mean contact was made long ago and kept secret.
area-51-confirmed-under-the-obama-admini: Area 51, a secret military base in the Nevada desert, was not officially admitted to exist until the Obama administration, according to the comedian and podcaster Joe Rogan. He says the government confirmed it then because "they wanted to expand the barriers for entry" around the site. If so, one of the best-known secret places in America was officially unacknowledged for decades.
area-51-crash-either-secret-us-testing-o: A crash linked to Area 51, the secret US air base in Nevada, may have been either secret American testing or some outside intelligence watching the nuclear bomb tests of the 1940s and 50s. Ralph Larson, a former CIA official, raises the two options while responding to the host, saying Jesse Michels has made this argument but that he himself has not researched it.
area-51-equipment-acquired-from-other-go: There is equipment at Area 51, the secret US test site in Nevada, that the United States got from other governments, according to John S. Herrington, a former US Secretary of Energy. He said this himself in an interview with Michels, which suggests the base studies foreign hardware as well as American aircraft.
area-51-programs-moved-to-dugway-proving: About 35 to 40 percent of the secret programs at Area 51, the highly secret Air Force test site in Nevada, are said to have moved to Dugway Proving Ground, an Army testing range in Utah. A researcher who goes online by the name UAPGerb points out that Steven Greer, a well-known UFO activist, often repeats that figure, and that an anonymous witness known only as "AH" said "the exact same thing" in recorded testimony from 2000, kept in an archive of witness interviews. If true, much of the secret work people link to Area 51 would now be done in Utah.
area-51-sensor-program-for-detecting-ufo: Area 51, the secret US Air Force test site in Nevada, once ran a sensor program meant to look for UFOs. Michels says someone stated this publicly in The Age of Disclosure, a documentary film about government UFO secrecy, and raises it in an episode with a former director of the NSA, the US spy agency that intercepts communications.
area-51-was-only-groom-lake-dreamland-wa: Area 51, the secret US test site in the Nevada desert, was "merely Groom Lake," a dry lakebed there, and the place known as Dreamland was really Areas 53 and 54, says a man named Charles Hall. Hall, who says he spent three years around 1965 on the Nevada test ranges living alongside tall white aliens, tells it from his own time there. If he is right, the most secret work happened outside the famous Area 51.
area-51-workers-sickened-by-burning-haza: Workers at Area 51, a secret military test site in the Nevada desert, are said to have been made sick by hazardous waste burned there. When one former worker took photos of the site from the highway and told a federal judge, "I used to work there," pointing at buildings in the distance, the government's lawyers denied seeing any buildings in the pictures. The physicist John Brandenburg tells this as something he heard, and offers it as an example of how far the government would go to deny the base exists.
area-6-lockheed-martin-aerial-operations: A place called Area 6, near Yucca Flat in the Nevada desert, is home to an aerial operations facility owned by Lockheed Martin, the big American weapons and aircraft maker, according to an online researcher who goes by the name UAPGerb (UAP being the government's term for unidentified objects in the sky). He says so to Jesse Michels while explaining how he believes the Pentagon's secret UFO work is organised, without naming a source.
ariel-school-girl-to-john-mack-in-space-: At the Ariel School in Ruwa, Zimbabwe, where in 1994 a group of children reported meeting strange visitors, one girl told the psychiatrist John Mack, who interviewed the children, "I think in space there's no love, but down here there is." Michels tells this himself on four different episodes, in slightly different ways: once as Mack tries to understand how telepathy worked in the encounter, once as her answer to why the visitors came, and once without Mack, adding that this love is why the being came down to interact. He tells it as a hint at what the visitors might want from us.
ariel-school-landing-near-a-uranium-mine: In 1994, the story goes, a large group of children at the Ariel School in Ruwa, Zimbabwe, saw a silver craft come down from the sky and land in a field near their school. Michels tells it several times, putting the number at 60, 61 or 62. He adds that a being came out and spoke to the children by telepathy, and that the school sat next to a uranium mine, which he links to UFOs taking an interest in nuclear sites. The UFO investigator James Fox says he looked into the case himself, calls it an alleged landing and puts the number at about 66. He also says the children were told something like 'you don't understand how special you are,' the same message he links to a case in Brazil. David Grusch, a former intelligence officer, tells it secondhand as about 100 children seeing upright, human-like beings he calls NHI, short for non-human intelligence, and a retired Army officer named Karl Nell says beings showed themselves to the children in the middle of the day. Others tell it as summaries: the writer Marik von Rennenkampff says the children's pictures were identical, while the author Peter Levenda and the YouTuber Chris Ramsay say their drawings and stories were alike but did not always match.
ariel-school-witnesses-reunite-in-los-an: Former pupils of the Ariel School in Ruwa, Zimbabwe, who as children reported a craft landing near their school, agreed in 2013 to meet again for the first time, about twenty years after the event, in Los Angeles. The UFO investigator James Fox tells this first-hand, as the person who brought them together. He tells it to show the witnesses still stood by what they saw.
aristotle-s-passage-on-the-ancestors-bel: The ancient Greek philosopher Aristotle wrote a passage saying that the oldest human ancestors were right to believe in something divine running through nature. A researcher named James Madden brings it up on Michels' show from memory, without naming the work, and gives Aristotle's line as: "our most ancient ancestors were not wrong when they posited that there was a divinity surrounding nature." Madden offers it as a sign that the old sense of the sacred in the world was taken seriously by one of philosophy's founders.
aristotle-the-planets-are-intelligences: For Aristotle, the ancient Greek philosopher, the planets were literally intelligences, thinking beings, and not anything like flying ships. James Madden, a guest who brings ancient philosophy to the question of UFOs, makes this point on Michels's show from his own reading, to show how differently older thinkers understood the lights in the sky.
ark-moved-from-axum-to-lake-ziway-during: During Italy's occupation of Ethiopia, from 1935 to 1941, the Ark of the Covenant, the sacred chest of the Hebrew Bible, was reportedly carried out of the Ethiopian city of Axum and hidden for safekeeping on an island in Lake Ziway. The writer Graham Hancock passes this on as what Ethiopians themselves told him. If true, it would mean the Ark was really kept in Ethiopia and was moved to protect it.
ark-of-the-covenant-as-a-device-that-str: The writer Graham Hancock says on the show that, according to the Book of Exodus, the Ark of the Covenant, the sacred chest the Israelites carried through the desert, "strikes people dead with bolts of fire that come out of it." No verse in the books of Moses in the King James Bible, published in 1611, says fire comes out of the Ark. The closest passage tells how Aaron's sons offered "strange fire" and "there went out fire from the LORD, and devoured them," and Aaron is warned to keep away from "the mercy seat, which is upon the ark; that he die not." The deaths at the Ark itself come later, in the books of Samuel, where a man named Uzzah "died by the ark of God" and the men of Bethshemesh were struck down for looking inside it, and neither passage mentions fire.
ark-of-the-covenant-claimed-kept-at-aksu: The Ark of the Covenant, the sacred chest that in the Bible held the tablets of the Ten Commandments, is said to be kept in a chapel beside the Church of St Mary of Zion in Aksum, a town in Ethiopia. The writer Graham Hancock tells Jesse Michels he went there himself and was told "we have the Ark of the Covenant here", a search he wrote up in his book The Sign and the Seal. If true, one of the most famous lost objects in history would still be in one place, guarded.
arkani-hamed-s-positive-geometries-outsi: Physicists led by Nima Arkani-Hamed at the Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton are said to be finding what they call "positive geometries outside of spacetime", mathematical structures that seem to sit beneath space and time and from which physics can be worked out. The scientist Donald Hoffman describes this work, naming Arkani-Hamed as one of its first pioneers and also mentioning the physicist David Gross. Hoffman raises it because it would mean space and time are not the bottom layer of reality.
armageddon-as-a-kinetic-war-against-the-: A researcher named Tim Alberino says on the show that Armageddon, the final battle in the Bible's Book of Revelation, "is a war with the son of God returning to the earth," and that he believes it will be a "kinetic war," meaning a real, physical one. In the King James Bible, published in 1611, Armageddon is the place where the kings of the earth are gathered "to the battle of that great day of God Almighty," and in a later chapter a rider on a white horse, called Faithful and True and "The Word of God," makes war on the beast and the kings, and the rest "were slain with the sword of him that sat upon the horse, which sword proceeded out of his mouth." That chapter does not call the rider the Son of God, and the idea that the war is physical is Alberino's reading.
armageddon-dream-with-the-number-747-and: In 1976, while posted at Fort Knox, a US Army base in Kentucky, Rolf Mowatt-Larssen had an "incredibly vivid" dream that he was fighting in something like the battle of Armageddon, and the dream featured the number 747 and cubes with numbers on them. Mowatt-Larssen, who later became a senior CIA officer, tells it as his own experience and points to his book A State of Mind: Faith in the CIA. He brings it up as an early sign of the strange experiences he went on to have.
armed-trespasser-on-grillmair-s-property: On December 20, 2025, a scientist named Carl Grillmair called the police to report an armed man trespassing on his large property in Llano, California, according to sheriff officials and court records. Michels tells this from those court records and reporting in the Los Angeles Times, in an episode about top American scientists who have gone missing. He brings it up as one of a string of troubling events around such scientists.
army-adapting-nhi-derived-electro-optic-: In the early 2000s the US Army is said to have wanted to put electro-optic cloaking, a way of hiding things from sight with light and electronics, on its next generation of combat vehicles. The story holds that the cloaking came from studying technology of non-human origin. UAPGerb, a researcher known by that online name, passes this on from someone he spoke with. If true, technology taken from non-human craft would be making its way into ordinary military vehicles.
army-interplanetary-phenomenon-unit-conf: The claim is that the US Army had a small unit called the Interplanetary Phenomenon Unit, which it says existed from 1947 to 1950 to look into unexplained things in the sky. A researcher who goes by UAPGerb tells this on the show without naming a source, and says the unit's existence was first confirmed in 1986 to a UFO researcher named William Steinman, and ties it to a report and a field order from the unit. If true, the Army had its own UFO group from the very start of the modern UFO era.
army-money-continues-after-the-round-tab: A group called the Round Table, which met in Maine and is said to have tried to contact an alien council, wound up around 1957, but the man at its center kept getting money from the US Army the whole time. The researcher Greg Malatzi says this and points to Army funding records, saying "there's records of that." If true, it would mean the military was quietly paying for the work.
army-officers-visiting-the-utah-ranch-fo: People who spent time studying a ranch in Utah known for strange events, called Skinwalker Ranch, say that something from the ranch followed them home. The researcher Jacques Vallée puts it this way: trained army officers went to the ranch for a few days, went home, and then "boom," some phenomenon was following them. He gives no source for this. Michels tells the story more than once. In one telling he speaks of researchers in general who say "stuff follows me around in my home" and that they had to rid themselves of it. In another he points to the testimony of a man named Jake Barber and to the people who studied the ranch under a man named Robert Bigelow, saying "these things seem to sort of follow them home." He also credits a book, Skinwalkers at the Pentagon, by Colm Kelleher, George Knapp and James Lacatski, which he says reports "hitchhiker effects" among many of the scientists who worked there. The tellers differ on who exactly was followed, army officers, scientists or Barber, but if true it would mean that whatever happens at the ranch does not stay there.
army-public-affairs-source-terrified-of-: A man who served in the US Army's Office of Public Affairs in the mid-2010s said he was not really afraid of the CIA, the US spy agency, but was terrified of the NSA, the agency that runs America's electronic surveillance. The online UFO researcher known as UAPGerb passes this on from the man himself, who is not named. It is told to suggest which agency insiders fear most when it comes to secrets.
army-r-d-golden-age-and-institutions-to-: From about 1959 to 1969, the US Army is said to have gone through a golden age of research and development, led by a man named Philip J. Corso, and Corso said that institutions were also set up during that time to study extraterrestrial technology. An online commentator who goes by UAPGerb tells this, summing it up without a single source. He mentions Corso and a man named Arthur Trudeau, and points to the Army's own research and development guides. If true, the Army quietly built a home for studying alien hardware.
army-research-laboratory-finds-lifter-th: In the 2000s the Army Research Laboratory, the US Army's main science lab, tested "lifters", light devices that rise when high voltage is run through them, and found that they pushed at least 10 to 20 percent harder than the electrically charged air flowing off them, called ion flow, could explain. Gary McKinnon, a British hacker who says he found evidence of a secret NASA space programme, tells this to Jesse Michels, citing the lab and a group called Blaze Labs. If true, it would hint that some other force is lifting the devices.
army-trucks-cordoning-off-the-hospital-1: In 1996, army trucks covered in green tarps gathered at the entrance of the Hospital Regional in Varginha, a town in Brazil, according to Italo Venturelli, a surgeon who says he saw them himself. He gives this as part of the wider account that a craft crashed near Varginha that year and that a living non-human being was captured and brought to local hospitals. If true, the trucks would show the military sealing off the place where the being was taken.
arranging-and-conducting-the-bobby-ray-i: When Jay Anderson, a UFO interviewer, sat down with Bobby Ray Inman, a retired top US intelligence official, Anderson says Inman was relaxed until the subject turned to UFOs, and then, "even when I'm just asking the question," he "starts getting tight." Anderson arranged and did the interview himself in the 2020s, and he tells it as a sign that the topic touched a nerve for a man who had been at the top of the secret world.
arrest-by-national-high-tech-crime-unit-: A British hacker named Gary McKinnon, who says he broke into NASA and military computers and found signs of a secret space program, says he was arrested in London in 2002. He recalls an officer introducing himself as Jeff Donsson from the National High-Tech Crime Unit, a British police unit for computer crime, and telling him he was under arrest for computer misuse. McKinnon tells it as the person who was arrested.
arrest-of-supervisor-and-100-million-abu: A supervisor at Baker Victory Services, a facility for children in Western New York, was arrested on something like 210 felony counts of record manipulation, and a $100 million lawsuit over years of sexual abuse claims was settled. That is how Jordan Jose, a man who says he was taken into a secret UFO programme as a child, describes a news article about the place. Elsewhere he says the facility was sued so many times over abuse claims, by other people and not by him, that it had to close.
arriving-gods-will-be-received-as-saviou: A group of beings will one day arrive on Earth and be welcomed as the gods returning, and that welcome will lead to Armageddon, the final battle at the end of the world. This comes from a researcher named Tim Alberino, who says it in his own words: "that group will be received as the gods returning to the earth." He draws on the Book of Revelation, the last book of the Christian Bible, and on a work called Birthright, and he tells it as a warning that people could mistake their own downfall for salvation.
arson-at-puharich-s-house-1978: In 1978 the house of a man named Puharich in Ossining, New York, burned down, and the fire department found it was deliberately set. A researcher named Greg Malatzi tells this without naming a source, adding that to this day nobody really knows who set the fire.
art-bell-s-material-said-to-come-from-ro: Art Bell, the host of the late-night radio show Coast to Coast, is said to have ended up with small pieces of material thought to come from Roswell, New Mexico, where something is said to have crashed in 1947. Michels raises this himself as a rumour, adding that he thinks the pieces came from Roswell. In another episode he wonders out loud whether Bell was actually shown a UFO, since he had 'these little bits and pieces of UFO stuff', and there he does not tie them to Roswell. If it were true, a radio host would have held physical wreckage of a craft not made by people.
art-bell-s-satellite-transmission-failur: During a famous 1997 broadcast of Coast to Coast AM, a late-night radio show about the unexplained, a caller claiming to be from Area 51, a secret US Air Force base in Nevada, came on, and the show's whole satellite transmission system went down, taking it off the air. The host of that show, Art Bell, says this himself in a recording played on the episode. If true, it suggests someone did not want the call heard.
arthur-c-clarke-s-sri-lanka-mountain-por: The science fiction writer Arthur C. Clarke once wrote a book about a portal, a kind of doorway to somewhere else, on top of a mountain in Sri Lanka. That is how Michels tells it, in passing and without naming the book or saying what the portal was meant to do. If it were so, it would mean a famous writer had taken the idea of a real-world gateway seriously enough to write a book about it.
arthur-c-clarke-says-nasa-found-large-li: In Sri Lanka in 2000, the science fiction writer Arthur C.
