Clarke is said to have declared that NASA had "basically discovered large forms of life on Mars," with the astronaut Buzz Aldrin in the room. A researcher on the show passes this on second-hand. If true, a famous writer would have spoken openly about large life on Mars in front of one of the men who walked on the Moon.
arthur-young-puharich-and-the-seances-wi: An inventor named Arthur Young is said to have taken part, along with a researcher named Andrija Puharich, in seances in which people claimed to be in contact with a group of non-human beings called the Nine. Michels mentions this himself, in passing and without naming a source, while talking with the parapsychologist Jeffrey Mishlove. If true, it would mean serious figures of the time were sitting in on claimed contact with otherworldly intelligences.
arthur-young-s-quest-to-invent-the-bell-: Arthur Young, the inventor who went on to design the Bell helicopter, chose his life's project by going to the US Patent Office in Washington and looking for problems nobody had solved, and the helicopter was one of them. The parapsychologist Jeffrey Mishlove tells this as Young's own account of how he started, beginning in the 1920s.
arthur-young-s-reflexive-universe-spirit: A thinker named Arthur Young held that the whole universe is "spirit descending into matter and then matter ascending back into the realm of spirit," an idea from his 1976 book The Reflexive Universe. A guest with a doctorate named Jeffrey Mishlove passes this on, as something Young taught. If it holds, it would make the physical world one stage in a round trip that ends back in spirit.
arv-idea-comes-from-lazar-sorensen-and-m: The idea of the ARV, short for alien reproduction vehicle, a supposed human-built copy of an alien craft, took hold in the UFO community because of three men: Bob Lazar, Brad Sorensen and Mark McCandlish. The researcher Eric W. Davis says this on Michels's show without naming a source, tracing where the notion came from rather than vouching for it.
arv-spelled-out-as-alien-reproduction-ve: In a 2018 Pentagon briefing on a secret programme he calls Immaculate Constellation, the letters ARV were spelled out as "alien reproduction vehicle", according to Matthew Brown, a former Pentagon official who has become a whistleblower. Brown says this is "to the best of my recollection", names the former Pentagon official Luis Elizondo in connection with it, and reads the wording as a sign of counterintelligence at work, a phrase planted on purpose rather than a plain description.
as-a-child-he-sensed-the-tube-tv-turning: As a boy, Dan Sherman always knew when the old tube television had been turned on in another room, he says, sensing it when his father switched it on. Sherman, a former sergeant who says the NSA, the US intelligence agency that intercepts communications, hired him to communicate with aliens, tells this about himself. He offers it as an early sign of the unusual sensitivity he says he had.
as-above-so-below-engraving-possibly-by-: On Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property known for reports of strange happenings, someone carved the old saying "as above, so below" into the rock, and Michels says nobody knows who made it or why. He suggests it might be the work of Augustus Walley, a legendary buffalo soldier (one of the Black US Army soldiers of the late 1800s) who was given the Medal of Honor. In a later episode he leaves Walley's name out, points to the inscription again and asks whether it is a coincidence that the buffalo soldiers were Freemasons, members of a brotherhood known for its secret symbols.
ascent-through-the-seven-hekhalot-in-eno: Ancient Jewish mystics described climbing through seven heavenly palaces, called hekhalot, using breathing techniques, visualisation and prayers repeated like mantras. Michels tells this himself, drawing on the Book of Enoch, an ancient Jewish religious text he cites in the translation by R. H. Charles, and on the Merkavah texts, writings of early Jewish mystics about visions of God's throne-chariot. He brings it up in an episode about the idea that we live in a hologram.
asha-calls-spelling-pseudoscience: The American Speech-Language-Hearing Association, the professional body for speech therapists in the United States, says that "spelling," a method where people who cannot speak point to letters on a board to communicate, is "not a valid form of communication" and has called it pseudoscience. Ky Dickens, a filmmaker whose documentary follows nonverbal autistic children, tells this without naming a source, as the main professional pushback her subjects face.
asher-s-first-words-to-j-tune-into-my-he: The very first thing someone named Asher said to a person called J was "tune into my heart." The filmmaker Ky Dickens, who made a documentary called The Telepathy Tapes about children said to read minds, relays this from those involved. It is told as an example of communication that seems to pass heart to heart rather than through ordinary speech.
asheville-viewer-s-videos-of-pulsating-l: In 2024 a viewer in Asheville, North Carolina, wrote to Jesse Michels saying he had seven videos, about 30 minutes of good footage, of pulsating lights in the sky from the night before. Michels reads out the message himself, as one of many reports of strange lights that year.
asis-operative-lent-to-mi6-to-bug-kuwait: In the early 1990s, British intelligence (MI6, Britain's overseas spy service) quietly borrowed a technical bugging specialist from Australia's own overseas spy service and used him to plant listening devices in Kuwaiti government offices, so that Britain could win business in Kuwait at Australia's expense. The Australian investigative journalist Ross Coulthart tells this, drawing on sources he names, as an example of allies spying for commercial gain, even against each other.
asked-to-blow-the-whistle-because-legacy: Matthew Brown, a former Pentagon employee who became a whistleblower, says that around 2023 and 2024 people in that community told him Congress needed whistleblowers because a so-called legacy program, a long-running secret effort said to deal with UFOs, "was not being managed correctly." He says this is why he came forward, and if true it would mean such a program has run without proper oversight from Congress.
asked-to-take-part-in-congressional-test: In 2025, a former Air Force sergeant named Dan Sherman, who says the National Security Agency, America's eavesdropping and code-breaking agency, once hired him to communicate with aliens, was asked to take part in testimony before the US Congress. Sherman says this himself, mentioning that the request came only recently, which would put his account in front of lawmakers.
asked-to-work-on-electron-flow-for-back-: A man named Chris Bledsoe, who says UFOs appear around him and who the episode says is studied by NASA, says he was once asked to work out which way electrons move. He tells it first-hand, as proof that people were trying to copy alien technology long ago.
asking-mary-his-purpose-in-the-middle-ea: While posted in the Middle East sometime between 2011 and 2016, Ralph Larson, a former CIA officer, says he asked a presence he calls Mary what his purpose there was. The answer came without words: "You're here to be here." Larson tells it as his own experience and mentions a Jesuit priest friend he does not name.
assyrian-branch-settles-the-old-holy-lan: A branch of the Assyrians, the ancient people of Mesopotamia, moved into what he calls an "old Holy Land" in eastern Turkey and was later destroyed there, according to the researcher Matt LaCroix. LaCroix offers it to Jesse Michels as his own belief, without naming a source, in an episode about a great event he places around 12,000 BC.
asteroid-bennu-study-finds-nucleic-bases: A scientific study of Bennu, an asteroid, is said to have found nucleic bases, the chemical building blocks of the genetic material in living things. Eric Haseltine, introduced on the show as a former director at the NSA, the US intelligence agency that listens in on electronic signals, mentions the study only in passing and does not say who did it. He raises it because, if true, life's raw ingredients would be floating around in space.
astra-on-the-skunk-works-org-chart-1993: Between 1993 and 1996, a writer named Nick Cook says he was shown an organisation chart of the Skunk Works, the aircraft maker Lockheed's secret design unit in Palmdale, California, and that at the top of it, above the place he expected, was something called Astra. Cook says he saw this himself and recorded it in his diaries. He tells it as a sign that a hidden program, perhaps tied to antigravity research, sat above even the Skunk Works.
astral-experience-on-the-hill-after-zoom: After a video call with a guest from The Telepathy Tapes, a podcast about non-speaking autistic people said to communicate by telepathy, Jordan Jose had an out-of-body experience in a place he calls 'the hill.' Jose, who says he was taken into a UFO program as a child, tells it himself: there, "they" showed him an image of a boy named Ken, a non-verbal autistic child who had been with him in a children's program called Baker Victory. To Jose this tied the telepathy story to his own childhood.
astronaut-crew-quarters-something-came-b: At the astronauts' crew quarters at Cape Canaveral, the Florida launch site, something is said to have come back with the crews after every flight and stayed. Chris Bledsoe, a man known for his own UFO encounters, passes this on from a man named Timothy Taylor, who said that "every time that thing went up, when it came back down, something came with them and it was still there." If true, spaceflight would have brought back some kind of presence that still lingers in the building.
astronaut-says-the-moon-technology-was-d: An astronaut from NASA, the US space agency, is heard saying he would go back to the Moon in a nanosecond, but that "we don't have the technology to do that anymore. We used to, but we uh destroyed that technology." The astronaut is not named, and his words are played on Michels's show in a July 2025 episode with Jay Anderson and Kurt Metzger. It is brought up as if it hints that something was lost or hidden after the Moon landings.
astronaut-ufo-code-names-per-edgar-mitch: NASA astronauts had secret code names for UFOs, according to Edgar Mitchell, an Apollo astronaut who walked on the Moon. Michels heard this from a man in Japan named Takano Josen, who was close to Mitchell and passed on what Mitchell had told him. If true, it would mean astronauts saw these things often enough to need words for them.
at-an-lax-pedestrian-death-all-sound-van: At Los Angeles International Airport in the 1980s, Brent Friedman says he was beside a woman who had been struck and was dying, and although the airport "is a very noisy place," he "heard nothing except her breathing," time seemed to slow, and the moment she died "all of the noise came back." Friedman, a guest on an episode about Hollywood and the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency, tells it as something he lived through himself, a moment where ordinary reality seemed to pause around a death.
at-t-breakup-testimony-before-judge-gree: A former presidential adviser named Harold Malmgren says AT&T, the giant American telephone company, hired him as "the final witness" in the government case that broke the company up, heard before Judge Harold Greene in Washington in the early 1980s. Malmgren tells it from his own part in the case, as evidence of how close he stood to major decisions.
at-the-table-with-john-mack-in-england-o: Joe McMoneagle, a guest who speaks on the episode about past life on Mars, says he sat at a table in England in 2004 talking with the psychiatrist John Mack on the very day Mack died there. McMoneagle tells it first-hand, as a personal memory of their last conversation.
atf-attempt-to-link-guest-to-the-oklahom: After he refused to cooperate with an investigation by the ATF, the US federal agency that handles firearms and explosives, the agency tried to tie him to the 1995 Oklahoma City bombing, says Steve Colbern, a scientist who studies objects said to be alien implants. Colbern tells it as something that happened to him, and he believes it was a way to punish him. He mentions Timothy McVeigh and an unnamed author writing a book on Oklahoma City.
atlantean-survivors-may-live-among-us-wi: Survivors of Atlantis, the legendary lost civilisation, might still live among us, with bases under the sea or on the Moon. When Michels puts this to the researcher Randall Carlson, Carlson calls it a loaded question and answers, very provisionally, yes. He offers it as his own tentative view, with no source named.
atlantic-article-on-obama-briefing-edite: In October 2010 the magazine The Atlantic published an article that said, in Michels's quote, "President Obama was briefed this morning on a power failure at FE Warren," an Air Force base in Wyoming. Michels reads this out himself, calling it "a pretty telling article", and pays close attention to how it was worded, which he notes was later edited. He brings it up in a conversation about UFOs being seen over nuclear bases, as a sign that something at the base went wrong serious enough to reach the president.
atlantis-as-a-multi-site-ice-age-civiliz: Atlantis, the legendary lost civilization, may not have been one island but an advanced Ice Age culture spread across several places: North America, the Azores islands in the Atlantic, the Sahara, the Amazon, and coastlines now under the sea. The writer Graham Hancock offers this as his own view, saying "I think it was more than one place," and mentions the researchers Randall Carlson and Jimmy Corsetti. If true, it would mean a forgotten civilization was far larger than the old story suggests.
atlantis-as-an-island-empire-on-the-mid-: Atlantis, the lost civilisation described by the ancient Greek philosopher Plato, may have been a real island empire in the middle of the Atlantic, near the undersea mountain chain called the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, with great seafaring and navigation skills. The researcher Randall Carlson argues this in his Atlantis lecture, saying that if Plato's account is "legitimate to some extent" it describes "a midatlantic island-based empire." Michels later credits Carlson and says he finds the Azores, a group of Atlantic islands, interesting as a candidate.
atlantis-s-rebellion-and-the-flood: The people of Atlantis sinned by ceasing to sacrifice to the gods, so Zeus called the Olympian gods together and chose to wipe the world clean in the flood better known as Noah's. That is how a philosopher named Jason Jorjani tells it to Michels, saying it is what Plato recounts in his dialogues the Timaeus and the Critias, and if true it would tie Plato's lost island to the Bible's flood. In Benjamin Jowett's English translation of the Critias, though, the Atlanteans' fault is that "the divine portion began to fade away" in them and they grew "full of avarice and unrighteous power". Zeus "collected all the gods", and the text breaks off as he starts to speak, with nothing on sacrifice, a flood sent by Zeus, or Noah, while the Timaeus says only that Atlantis vanished in "violent earthquakes and floods" in "a single day and night" and gives no cause.
atlantis-search-atlantic-region-matching: A team says it has found a region of the Atlantic Ocean that matches every detail the ancient Greek philosopher Plato gave of Atlantis, the lost island he described in his dialogues. Tim Gallaudet, a retired US Navy admiral who says he is part of the search, tells Jesse Michels this, naming a colleague, Maaneli Derakhshani, and keeping the location secret. If true, Atlantis would be a real place under the sea.
atlantis-search-presentation-to-victor-v: A retired Navy admiral named Tim Gallaudet says that in the 2020s he and others gave a presentation on searching the ocean for Atlantis, the legendary lost island city, to an explorer named Victor Vescovo. Gallaudet says Vescovo was interested and answered, "All right, I'm in." He tells it as someone who was in the room, and if true it would mean a serious search for Atlantis has a backer.
atlas-launch-scrubbed-from-the-records-1: Bob Jacobs, who says he was involved in the event, tells of an Atlas rocket launch in 1964 at Vandenberg Air Force Base in California. He says the official word was that no Atlas launch took place that day. He also says a man he names only as Robert later found Vandenberg's own launch files, which described that very launch in detail, so the record looks scrubbed.
atomic-energy-act-s-special-nuclear-mate: The claim is that a 1954 nuclear law is worded so broadly that any material recovered from a crashed craft would count as secret nuclear material the moment it was found. The whistleblower David Grusch, a former intelligence official, makes the case on the show. He says the Atomic Energy Act of 1954, which Congress passed on 30 August 1954, defines "special nuclear material" as "any material that releases any kind of atomic energy". If that were so, crash material would be locked away under nuclear secrecy. Michels repeats the idea in several episodes. Once he goes further and says Grusch shows the wording "was written in a sneaky but deliberate way to protect our UFO secrets", and elsewhere he says such material is "born secret". An online researcher known as UAPGerb is also credited with it, and one telling comes from a speaker who is not named. The act itself reads differently. It names plutonium and enriched uranium, plus any other material that the Atomic Energy Commission, the civilian agency then in charge of nuclear matters, finds "capable of releasing substantial quantities of atomic energy", and only with the President's "written" assent. Its secret category, "Restricted Data", covers data about weapons and nuclear material, not objects, and the words "born secret" do not appear in it.
atomic-energy-commission-born-secret-res: In 1946, the Atomic Energy Commission, the US agency set up to control nuclear matters, created a category of "restricted data": anything collected that showed alpha, beta or gamma radiation would be "born secret", meaning classified from the moment it existed. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, in an episode about Hollywood, the CIA and UFOs. He brings it up because, if true, any radioactive material from an unexplained object would have been hidden from the public automatically.
atomic-energy-commission-contract-for-pu: In 1963 or 1964 a scientist named Puharich, whom the episode calls a CIA scientist who contacted an alien council, got a contract from the Atomic Energy Commission, the US government agency then in charge of nuclear research. An unnamed researcher who is a guest on Jesse Michels's show gives the dates in conversation with the host, without naming a source.
atomic-energy-commission-grant-to-intele: In the early 1960s a small company called Intelectron, based in New York City's Hell's Kitchen, got a $300,000 grant, at least a million dollars in today's money, from the Atomic Energy Commission, the US agency then in charge of nuclear research. The researcher Greg Malatzi tells it from the grant documents and the work of the journalist Annie Jacobsen, in an episode about a scientist tied to the CIA, the US spy agency, who was said to have contacted an alien council. If true, it would mean the government was quietly paying for this company's work.
atomic-energy-commission-nuclear-secrecy: In the 1950s, the secrecy around nuclear weapons was laid on top of UFO secrecy, so the two were hidden together around Los Alamos, the New Mexico lab where the atomic bomb was built, and other nuclear sites run by the Atomic Energy Commission, the government agency in charge of American nuclear work. Michels offers this as his own reading, once in a conversation with a helicopter pilot named Jake Barber and later in an episode about a Secretary of Energy. The second time he goes further: he calls nuclear secrecy a "Trojan horse" for UFO secrecy, traces it back to the Manhattan Project, the wartime effort that built the bomb, and forward to the Department of Energy, and points to the Atomic Energy Act, the law that set the rules for nuclear secrets. If he is right, the walls built to guard the bomb would also have hidden whatever was known about UFOs.
attempted-abduction-and-face-cutting-of-: In 2023, in San Antonio de Pintuyacu, a village in the Peruvian Amazon, a 15-year-old girl named Talia is said to have nearly been abducted and had her face cut, and the police went out there because of it. Tim Alberino, a documentary filmmaker who went to the area, passes this on from what he was told locally. He tells it as part of a wave of attacks reported in that region.
attempts-to-discredit-lazar-s-los-alamos: People tried to discredit Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft at a hidden site called S4 near Area 51, the secret military base in Nevada, by claiming he never worked at Los Alamos, the nuclear weapons lab in New Mexico, and was never at S4. Joe Rogan, the comedian and podcaster, says the Los Alamos job has been confirmed and that Lazar really was at S4, drawing on the reporting of George Knapp, a Las Vegas television journalist. If so, Lazar's story would hold up better than his critics claim.
aubrey-marcus-had-a-dmt-experience-durin: After four or five days in a darkness retreat, days spent in total darkness, a man named Aubrey Marcus says he had a full experience of DMT, a powerful psychedelic compound, without taking anything. The neuroscientist Andrew Gallimore, who studies DMT, passes on Marcus's words: "this wasn't like DMT. This was a DMT" experience. If true, it would suggest the body can make enough of the substance on its own to produce the trip.
audience-member-with-magnetic-ear-implan: At a live show with Area 52, a podcast hosted by Chris Ramsay, a man in the audience said he had an experience as a child and now has something in his ear that a magnet will stick to from the outside. Michels tells this himself, as something he heard there in person. He brings it up because it resembles the implant stories told on the show.
aurora-black-triangle-program-1987: A secret aircraft programme called Aurora, tied to black triangle shaped craft seen over the North Sea and to Groom Lake, a secret test site in Nevada, appeared as a line item in the 1987 US congressional budget with $2.3 billion set aside for it, something the aircraft maker Lockheed "had trouble explaining away." Michels tells this himself, drawing on the aviation writer Nick Cook and crediting the 1987 budget, the defence magazine Jane's Defence Weekly and British Ministry of Defence documents, which would point to a hidden, well-funded aircraft programme.
aurora-budget-line-item-1980: Jesse Michels says that in the 1980s there was an entry in the US government budget, a line item, that went by the name Aurora. He mentions it in passing, without naming a source or saying what the money was for, as one more sign of hidden projects of that era.
aurora-in-the-1986-budget: Michels says that Aurora, a name tied to a rumoured secret American aircraft project, shows up as a line item in the 1986 United States budget, for something like 2 billion dollars, he thinks (he first says 1968, then corrects himself). He tells it himself, mentioning the aerospace engineer Ben Rich and documents from Britain's Ministry of Defence, its defence department. If true, it would mean a secret aircraft project left a trace in the public budget.
aurora-rumoured-at-raf-machrihanish-1987: Aurora, a rumoured secret American aircraft, was said for a while to be flying out of a remote Scottish airbase called RAF Machrihanish, run by Britain's Royal Air Force, sometime between the late 1980s and late 1990s. A researcher and writer named Nick Cook mentions it on Michels' show as something he heard, without naming a source: "there were rumors it was based out of the UK for a while." If true, it would mean a hidden American project was operating from British soil.
aurora-texas-airship-crash-and-alien-bur: In 1897, a sky ship is said to have crashed into a wind tower in Aurora, Texas, and the townspeople buried an alien there, right beside the cemetery of Chris Bledsoe's family. Bledsoe, a man who says UFOs are drawn to him, tells Michels about it as the first such report he had heard of in America, and as something passed down to him. To him it means his family has a link to one of the country's earliest crash stories.
austin-meeting-where-puthoff-said-skinwa: At a meeting in Austin, Texas, a question about Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property known for reports of strange happenings, made the room go silent, and the physicist Hal Puthoff said, "Well, we need a skiff for this one," meaning a SCIF, a secured room for discussing classified material. So says the author Peter Levenda, who was there along with others including the former Pentagon official Chris Mellon. In one version Levenda says they had asked about an appearance at the ranch and the equipment there, and Michels, retelling it, adds that Levenda had to leave because he lacked the clearances, which would suggest the ranch is tied to secret government work.
australian-aboriginal-oral-tradition-con: Australia's Aboriginal peoples are said to keep a very old oral tradition, perhaps 30,000 years old, that is short and easy to pass on and deals with non-human intelligence, beings that are neither human nor animal. Diana Pasulka, a professor who studies religion, passes this on from Indigenous friends she does not name. If true, people would have been describing contact with such beings for tens of thousands of years.
australian-man-leaves-edgar-mitchell-s-h: In 2016, an Australian man was caught leaving the Florida house of the astronaut Edgar Mitchell with files, according to a UFO investigator named James Fox, who says he caught him. Fox links it to the Wilson memo, notes said to describe a private aerospace program for reverse-engineering unknown craft. He tells it to show how such papers came out of Mitchell's house.
australian-man-records-astronaut-private: A man in Australia is said to have recorded astronauts' radio, and when they switched to a different, private channel, he could switch along with them and keep listening. Charlie Foltz, a guest on an episode about alien abductions, recalls meeting this man but cannot remember who he was. If true, the man may have heard things the astronauts said off the public line.
australian-officer-says-buchanan-also-kn: An Australian officer once told Lyn Buchanan, a former US Army sergeant, that he was the one who had knocked out their computers in Australia as well. Buchanan tells it himself, recalling the encounter in a cafeteria at the Bureau of Indian Affairs, a US government agency, where the man said: "you're the one that knocked out our computers over in Australia." It is told to suggest Buchanan's effect on machines had reached well beyond the United States.
australian-special-forces-paid-cash-for-: Members of Australia's special forces say they were paid in cash to take part in American operations to recover crashed unidentified craft. Ross Coulthart, an Australian investigative journalist, says the soldiers themselves told him they had been involved in these retrieval missions. If true, the US recovery effort would reach well beyond American forces.
autec-submersible-ufo-rumors-near-nassau: There are, Michels says, "tons of rumors" about a site in the Bahamas near Nassau that he calls ATIC, short for a weapons training facility known as AUTEC. He tells this himself, without naming a source, and in another episode adds that the facility has underwater cables that nobody knows the destination of. He brings it up because a hidden military site under the sea would be a natural place for stories of craft that travel underwater.
autopsy-on-a-soldier-likely-wounded-by-a: In 1996, near the Brazilian town of Varginha, a young soldier named Marco Eli Chereze is said to have helped catch a strange being, then fallen ill and died. Doctors then carried out an autopsy on him. Michels calls it an autopsy "on a soldier that was likely wounded by an alien being." He says the lead doctor was Armando Fortunato. Michels says the soldier seemed to die of "a bacterial infection that we've never seen the likes of before." He passes on what doctors told him, naming a Dr. Cesario among them. A doctor named Ahmed Foratu, who says he took part, tells it more plainly. He says that when the body arrived at the Forensic Medical Institute, "there was no mention of contact with extraterrestrials." In his account it was sent for autopsy to check for a possible professional error. If the host's framing is right, the soldier's death would be physical evidence that he had touched a living alien.
avesta-s-island-continent-that-froze-ove: The Avesta, the ancient holy scripture of the old Iranian religion of Zoroastrianism, says the Aryan people came from an island continent at the centre of the world that froze over. The researcher Jason Jorjani tells Michels this from his own reading, without naming a further source, and the story links Iran with Antarctica. If true, it would mean an ancient text remembers a homeland lost under ice.
avi-loeb-s-calculation-against-fravor-s-: In 2004, near the aircraft carrier USS Nimitz off San Diego, a Navy fighter pilot named David Fravor says an unidentified object dropped from 80,000 feet to sea level almost instantly. The skeptic Michael Shermer brings this up on Michels's show and points to a calculation by the researcher Avi Loeb that argues against that drop, which matters because if the drop was real, no known craft could have made it.
aviation-week-editor-threatened-over-sor: After an interview with a man named Sorensen ran in the 1990s, the magazine's people are said to have received threats, "like Men in Black type encounters," meaning visits from the sort of mysterious figures in dark suits who are said to warn UFO witnesses. The story comes from a UFO researcher who goes by UAPGerb, who says he later spoke with the unnamed editor of that interview and heard it from him directly. If true, it would mean someone wanted to scare people away from what the interview revealed.
aviators-reports-to-graves-leading-to-th: Ryan Graves, a former Navy fighter pilot who saw UFOs himself, says that after he spoke out he "became a beacon" for people to call and report their own incidents, mostly fellow aviators "but all sorts of people." He tells it first-hand, as part of how those accounts built up to the 2023 hearing in the US Congress on unexplained objects in the sky.
avro-car-in-nasa-wind-tunnel-1961: In 1961 the Avro car, an experimental flying-saucer-shaped aircraft, was tested in a NASA wind tunnel. Michels mentions it himself, without naming a source, in an episode about anti-gravity craft with the writer Nick Cook, as evidence that the government was seriously building saucer-shaped machines.
avrocar-as-cover-for-roswell-craft-work-: The Avrocar, a saucer-shaped aircraft built in Canada in the postwar years, was probably a cover for something deeper, according to Michels, who gives this as his own view. He points to the rumours that the craft said to have crashed at Roswell, New Mexico, in 1947 was taken to Wright Field, an Air Force airfield in Ohio. In his telling, the saucer project would have hidden work on that craft and the recruitment of German scientists who had worked for the Nazis.
avrocar-project-moved-to-wright-pat-as-p: The Avrocar, a 1950s project in Canada to build a working flying saucer, is said to have been quietly moved to Wright-Patterson Air Force Base in the United States under the name Project Y, or Silverbug. A researcher named Dan Sheehan tells it this way. Michels tells it in several episodes, saying it officially failed in 1961 but in reality moved to the US, dating it to 1952 in one telling and to the 1950s and 60s in another, and linking it to two men named John Frost and Henri Coanda. If true, the US military would have kept working on saucer-shaped craft after the public was told the effort had ended.
axelrod-oni-nimitz-investigator-studying: A man known by the made-up name Axelrod is said to study strange events at Skinwalker Ranch, a ranch in Utah known for reports of odd happenings. Michels says Axelrod was the lead investigator for the Office of Naval Intelligence, the US Navy's intelligence service, on the Nimitz case. That case covers the 2004 sightings of unexplained objects by Navy pilots flying from the aircraft carrier Nimitz. Michels says this himself, in an episode with the ranch's owner, without naming a source, and to him it suggests that the same officials who looked into the Navy sightings are now looking at the ranch.
ayanis-andesite-foundation-under-mud-bri: At Ayanis, an ancient site in Turkey, the foundation is said to be made of andesite, which Matt LaCroix, a researcher of ancient ruins, calls one of the hardest stones on Earth, with mud brick built on top. LaCroix shows it without naming a source. He means that a far more skilled, older people laid the stonework and that later builders added cruder walls above it.
azores-as-sunken-mountain-tops-of-a-lost: The Azores, a group of islands in the middle of the Atlantic Ocean, are the tops of mountains from a land that sank beneath the sea along the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, the undersea mountain chain running down the ocean, according to the researcher Randall Carlson. Carlson tells Jesse Michels this as his own reading, without naming a source. If true, it would mean a large land once stood above water in the mid-Atlantic.
aztec-1948-craft-powered-up-at-wright-fi: A craft said to have been recovered near Aztec, New Mexico, in March 1948 is reported to have been taken to Wright Field, a military airfield, and to have turned translucent when it was powered up there. Jesse Michels passes on the account of what he calls a firsthand witness who claimed to have worked on the craft at Wright Field. Scott Ramsey, an author who has written a book on the Aztec crash, tells it from what the man told him. Ramsey says the engineer had ties to Eastman Kodak, the photography company, and recognised the craft from his book: "I'm pretty sure this is the Aztec craft I worked on. I read your book." Ramsey also credits someone named Lipish. If true, the story would mean the military had a working craft it could switch on and study.
aztec-craft-taken-to-los-alamos-then-wri: A craft said to have come down at Aztec, New Mexico, in 1948 was first taken to Los Alamos, the government laboratory in New Mexico, and then moved to Wright Field, an Air Force base in Ohio. Michels tells this himself, citing a man named Scott Ramsey, who is listed as a witness to the story. If true, it would trace the path of a recovered craft into the hands of the US military's scientists.
aztec-crash-and-its-debunking-1948: A craft is said to have crashed near Aztec, New Mexico, around 1948, and it was the first such crash case ever written about. The researcher Richard Dolan says he believes it, and he traces how it was told: early writers such as Frank Scully and JP Cahn, then a big book by a researcher named William Steinman, then a later revival by Scott Ramsey and Suzanne Ramsey, even though Wikipedia labels it a hoax. If true, it would be one of the first known recoveries of a crashed craft.
aztec-crash-possibly-brought-down-by-the: A craft said to have crashed near Aztec, New Mexico, in 1948 may have been brought down by the Lashup radar network, a chain of radar stations built over New Mexico to guard against Soviet bomber attacks. A researcher who goes by the online name UAPGerb calls this one of the leading theories, without naming a source; if true, it would mean early military radar could knock such craft out of the sky.
b-2-bomber-money-diverted-to-illegal-man: The B-2 stealth bomber, a US Air Force plane built to avoid radar, is priced at about $2 billion each, but according to the UFO researcher Steven Greer it probably costs less than $100 million to make. Greer tells Michels that the difference is quietly moved into illegal secret projects building man-made UFOs. If true, it would mean huge sums of defense money are funding hidden programs that no one approved.
b-2-colonel-whispers-about-electrogravit: At a conference in Las Vegas in 2008, a colonel connected with the B-2 stealth bomber is said to have leaned forward and whispered, "That's bullshit," when the talk turned to electrogravitics, the idea of moving an aircraft with strong electric fields instead of ordinary engines. The researcher Richard Dolan says he was there, and he links the moment to a paper by Paul LaViolette on electrogravitics and the B-2, an idea that goes back to the inventor Thomas Townsend Brown. Dolan tells it as a hint of what people close to the bomber may know about how it flies.
b-2-uses-biefield-brown-effect-1992: The B-2 stealth bomber, America's radar-dodging long-range bomber, is said to use the work of the inventor Thomas Townsend Brown on using strong electric fields to push aircraft or move air around them, which Michels sometimes calls electric gravity. Michels tells this himself in several episodes, pointing to a story in the aviation trade magazine Aviation Week from March 1992, and also to Paul Schatzkin's biography of Brown, The Man Who Mastered Gravity, and to the researcher Paul LaViolette. In other tellings he adds that Brown spread false information to protect his work and that the defense company Northrop Grumman paid him off with a very small sum for the rest of his life.
baalbek-trilithon-stones: At Baalbek in Lebanon, a set of huge blocks called the trilithon stones sits about 30 feet above the foundation blocks, placed with precision, each weighing at least 800 tons and up to about 1,000 tons. A guest named Jay Anderson describes them on Michels's show without citing a source, as a sign that whoever built the site could lift weights that are hard to explain.
baass-project-forum-and-ttsa-as-holdover: Around 2011, documents from BAASS, a private aerospace company that ran a government-funded UFO study, are said to describe a "Project Forum": a plan to get celebrities, media personalities and other popular people in California talking about UFOs. The online researcher known as UAPGerb tells this from those documents, naming a man called Tom Dong and Luis Elizondo, a former Pentagon official, and he sees To the Stars Academy, a later company that took UFO material public, as a holdover of that plan. If true, it would mean the later public UFO push had been planned years before.
baba-vanga-predicts-his-kalmykia-preside: Around 1990, a telegram from Bulgaria brought a young man to the blind Bulgarian seer Baba Vanga, and she told him, out of nowhere, "you'll go back home. You'll be the leader. You'll be president there." The man telling it is the one she said it to: he went on to become president of Kalmykia, a small republic inside Russia, in the early 1990s. If true, she saw his future years before it happened.
baba-vanga-s-april-1995-prediction-of-th: In April 1995 Baba Vanga, a Bulgarian fortune-teller, and her niece called a Russian regional leader, saying "Kerson, come here," and told him about his future presidency of the world chess federation. The man himself, a former president of a republic within Russia, tells Jesse Michels this as something that happened to him, and mentions the Guinness book of records in the telling. If true, the seer foresaw his rise before it happened.
baba-vanga-says-beings-live-underground-: A man introduced as the president of a republic within Russia says beings live underground, and that he is "sure" of it, not just guessing. He says the Bulgarian clairvoyant Baba Vanga told him so in the 1990s: she would sometimes point at the ground and say "they are talking there. They are there." He passes this on as something she told him in person, and if true it would mean someone is living below the surface of the Earth.
baba-vanga-talks-with-souls-and-entities: In the 1990s, in her yard in Bulgaria, the famous blind seer Baba Vanga told a visitor that unseen beings are all around us. The visitor, a former president of one of Russia's republics, says he asked her whether we are alone, and she struck him lightly and said, "What's wrong with you? Are you stupid or what? Can't you see? It's all around you." He tells it as his own meeting with her, one he takes as her saying she spoke with souls and entities that fill the world.
babson-louis-witten-and-bryce-dewitt-gra: In the 1950s a man named Babson is said to have reached out to the physicist Louis Witten, then coming out of Johns Hopkins University, and to have helped start gravity research efforts involving Witten and another physicist, Bryce DeWitt, at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill. The researcher Eric Weinstein tells this, without naming a source, in an episode about claims of antigravity aircraft. He raises it because private money flowing into gravity research then could point to a hidden interest in controlling gravity.
babson-s-gravity-research-foundation-in-: In the 1950s a wealthy patron of science named Roger Babson ran a Gravity Research Foundation in New Boston, New Hampshire, aimed at beating gravity. The mathematician Eric Weinstein mentions it and says the usual reason given, that Babson's sister drowned in a pond, is not very believable. Michels describes Babson as obsessed with finding the solution to antigravity. People bring it up because, if there was a hidden reason, it would point to serious early interest in antigravity.
backlash-over-the-2021-transients-paper-: The astronomer Beatriz Villarroel says that in 2021 she published her discovery of nine transients, points of light in old sky photographs that appear and then vanish, with her colleague Jeff Marcy, an astronomer who she says had been cancelled in a sexual harassment scandal in 2015. She tells it first-hand, as the reason her work met a backlash from other astronomers.
bae-colleagues-on-the-program-assume-bor: In the 2010s, colleagues at BAE Systems, a large defense contractor, heard Dylan Borland talk about "the triangle" and assumed he had been read in, meaning formally cleared and briefed on a secret programme, because they themselves were. Borland tells it first-hand and says that was how his whole involvement began. If true, it would mean a hidden programme was running inside the company.
bae-falcon-works-joint-ventures-with-loc: BAE Systems, a large British defence company, has a secret projects division called Falcon Works, its "version of Skunk Works," the advanced projects arm of the American aerospace firm Lockheed Martin, and the two run joint ventures "on material sciences, on engineering, on engines, on all of it." That is what Dylan Borland, a former US intelligence employee turned whistleblower, says from his own experience. If true, it would mean that secret aerospace work is shared across companies in two countries.
baghdad-phantom-mission-report-released-: A military mission report about the "Baghdad Phantom," an unexplained object linked to Baghdad, Iraq, is said to have been released years early, when it was meant to stay secret until 2047. The journalist Jeremy Corbell says so, citing named sources. In his words, it was the "mission report from the Baghdad Phantom. That was supposed to be declassified in 2047."
baghdad-phantom-seven-still-images-then-: An unexplained object nicknamed the Baghdad Phantom was caught on camera over Baghdad, Iraq, according to the filmmaker and journalist Jeremy Corbell. Corbell says that he and the television journalist George Knapp first reported on it by releasing seven still images. He says video of it later came out in the government's own first release, which he presents as official backing for what they had shown.
bahamas-yacht-trips-with-eldridge-reeves: A circle of men that included William Stephenson and the researcher Thomas Townsend Brown went on trips to the Bahamas aboard a yacht owned by a man named Eldridge Reeves Johnson, according to Jesse Michels. Michels draws this from a book called A Man Called Intrepid. He brings it up as part of his case that the people behind the secrecy around UFOs were tied together in one tight, private network.
bahnsen-s-notes-on-unexplained-effect-19: In the 1950s in Chapel Hill, North Carolina, a man named Agnew Bahnson wrote in his private notes that "there's something going on here that we're unable to account for," about an effect he could not explain. The researcher Paul Schatzkin, who has studied the inventor Townsend Brown, brings this up from Bahnson's notes without pointing to a published source. He tells it as a sign that serious experimenters were seeing something new.
bahnson-funds-brown-s-gravitator-experim: In the 1950s, a North Carolina man named Agnew Bahnson, head of a research body called the Institute of Field Physics, was quietly paying for the experiments of the inventor Thomas Townsend Brown, who was trying to build "gravitator" devices meant to manipulate gravity. Michels tells this himself across several episodes, without naming a source. In one he says the work was done at the back of Bahnson's house and that "strange phenomena occur," and in another that Brown was claiming positive results. If it were so, it would mean private money was backing gravity-control research in the middle of the century.
bahnson-funds-bryce-dewitt-institute-at-: In the 1950s, the story goes, a wealthy North Carolina industrialist named Agnew Bahnson paid to set up a physics institute at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill and put a young physicist named Bryce DeWitt in charge of it. The researcher Eric Weinstein tells it on two occasions without naming a source. The first time he is unsure of the man's name, calling him "bainson" with "some sort of tobacco or air conditioning fortune". The second time he says Bahnson worked with the physicist John Wheeler to find DeWitt, describes the place as an institute for anti-gravity, and points to an old newspaper clipping. Jesse Michels tells it twice in his own words. He names it the Institute of Field Physics, links it to a 1957 conference at Chapel Hill attended by the physicists Richard Feynman, Peter Bergmann, Freeman Dyson and John Wheeler, and says its work "often" concerned gravitational anomalies. The tellers bring it up because, if a private fortune was funding gravity research in those years, it would suggest serious early interest in ways to control gravity.
baiting-for-shootdowns-as-cover-for-psio: Luring unknown craft so they can be shot down, says Matthew Brown, a former Pentagon official speaking as a whistleblower, is really a cover story for something else: using people with psychic powers "as breeding stock" to produce "some sort of super psychic child" generations later. Brown says this on Michels's show, and he says it twice, the second time without the part about a future psychic child.
baker-victory-services-day-treatment-cen: A school at 650 Ridge Road in Western New York, run by Baker Victory Services, outwardly served neurodivergent children and kids with behavioral health needs but secretly supported "defense contractor research for psychic potential development," according to a man named Jordan Jose, who says he was a pupil there from about 2008 to 2010. Jose says a game he played as a child began "a two-year journey" that put him in that school, which he says has "since been shut down, sued six ways to Sunday." If true, children were being tested for psychic abilities under cover of a school.
baker-victory-services-training-to-quant: At a place called Baker Victory Services, much of the work was training people to "quantum unentangle", which means cutting the hidden links that tie them to things they are connected with. Michels says this himself, without naming a source, while interviewing a guest who says a UFO program took him as a child. If true, it would suggest the program was training people's minds, not just watching them.
bald-shin-patches-and-jack-s-tumors-sent: The story goes that in 1976 a man named Jack Weiner had tumors growing in the exact spots on his legs where bald patches had appeared on his shins, and that tissue from them went from a Vermont teaching hospital to an Air Force pathology institute near Washington DC. A man named Charlie Foltz, who presents himself as a witness to the events, tells this on an episode about alien abduction, passing on what Weiner told him and pointing to a pathology report on the tumor. Told this way, it would suggest the military took a quiet medical interest in the marks left on people who say they were taken.
balls-of-light-over-hanford-plutonium-si: In 1945, months before the first atomic bomb test in New Mexico and the bombings of Japan, glowing balls of light hovered over Hanford, the Washington state site making plutonium for the bomb, and jet fighters tried and failed to chase them away, according to the host. Michels tells it several times, crediting the researcher Robert Hastings and his book UFOs and Nukes and naming a pilot called Bud Clem as the witness, though once he credits a Lieutenant Commander Brown instead, and once he ties it to an Air Force study he calls Project Twinkle, which he says was deleted from the Air Force archives. He offers it as one of the earliest cases suggesting that something has been watching nuclear sites from the very start.
baltic-anomaly-history-lightning-smoke-n: A strange object lies in the Baltic Sea, and according to Michels lightning has struck it, smoke has been seen coming out of it, and ships from NATO, the Western military alliance, have circled it. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, and calls it "super strange". If true, it would mean military forces were paying close attention to something odd on the seabed.
baltic-sea-anomaly-expedition: The story is about a strange round object on the floor of the Baltic Sea, out in the open water between Sweden and Finland, that some say looks like a crashed UFO. A treasure hunter named Dennis Asberg, who found it, says it first appeared on side scan sonar, a device that maps the seabed with sound, on 19 June 2011. He remembers his partner Peter Lindberg and a man named Floris laughing and saying, "Dennis, here is UFO." Michels went out to the site himself in 2025, together with a man named Ammar Kandil, and describes it as about 60 km out at sea, "the epicenter between Finland and Sweden." In another episode Michels says the thing looks like the Millennium Falcon, the flat round spaceship from Star Wars. The astronomer Beatriz Villarroel tells it more distantly, as something she once heard about: a team of divers found something off the Swedish coast that "looked like a crashed UFO or looked like an artificial structure." So the story comes from the finder himself, the host who visited, and a scientist passing on what she heard, and if the object is what it looks like, it would be a wrecked craft lying on the seabed.
baltic-sea-anomaly-not-attached-to-the-s: A strange shape lying at the bottom of the Baltic Sea is said not to be attached to the seafloor at all, and to give off electromagnetic activity. Michels passes this on from a friend of his, a sea explorer named Dennis Asberg, who told him so. If true, the object would be something resting there, not a rock formation.
banister-pistol-whips-jack-martin-1963: In New Orleans in 1963, a man named Guy Banister and a man named Jack Martin got into a fist fight over the assassination of President John F. Kennedy, and the story's title has Banister pistol-whipping Martin. The author Peter Levenda, whom the episode calls a CIA historian, tells it to Jesse Michels without naming a source, as a sign that the two men knew something about the killing worth fighting over.
bannister-effect-after-the-first-4-minut: The British runner Roger Bannister ran a mile in under four minutes at Oxford in 1954, a mark long thought impossible, and within two and a half years ten other runners had done it too. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, calling it the Bannister effect, the idea that once one person proves something can be done, others quickly follow. He uses it to suggest that belief itself changes what people are able to do.
baptist-preacher-prays-over-the-bodies-1: In 1948, in Hart Canyon near Aztec, New Mexico, a preacher named Solon Brown is said to have been asked to pray over the bodies of beings found in a crashed saucer. He answered, "Well, I'm not Catholic. I'm a Baptist preacher, but I'd be more than happy to say a prayer over him." Scott Ramsey passes on Brown's words as they were told to him, as part of the case for a crash with bodies at Aztec.
barber-goes-to-the-senate-intelligence-c: Jake Barber, a former helicopter pilot who says he once flew a helicopter to recover a UFO, says he decided to go to Washington to tell everything. He says he went to the Senate Intelligence Committee, the group of senators who oversee the spy agencies, and to the CIA's internal watchdog, and that they asked him for help. The journalist Ross Coulthart tells it on a separate episode only as Barber's first-hand account being handed to that Senate committee, and he does not mention the CIA watchdog.
barber-hints-at-the-two-aerospace-primes: The two big aerospace contractors said to be involved in recovering crashed unexplained craft are, according to a helicopter pilot named Jake Barber, exactly the two companies anyone would guess first. Barber, who says he took part in such retrievals himself, says it in a 2025 conversation with Jesse Michels and the researcher known as UAPGerb: "if you took two guesses, you'd get both of them right on the first try." If true, it would mean the country's best-known defence builders hold this hardware, though Barber never names them.
barber-one-to-two-craft-a-year-recovered: A man named Jake Barber has said in public that one or two unknown craft a year were recovered over the test range where he worked. A commentator who goes by UAPGerb repeats this on the show as Barber's own public claim, saying "over his specific range 1 to two a year." If true, it would mean recoveries of unexplained craft happen often, not once in a lifetime.
barber-s-group-back-channeled-the-psioni: In 2023, around the time of the US congressional hearings on UFOs in Washington, a quiet group from inside secret government programs is said to have privately passed an explanation to a man named Michael Herrera, who says he saw a 300-foot UFO in the Indonesian jungle. The explanation was about what they call psionic asset transfer, which involves people said to have psychic abilities. Jake Barber, who says he once retrieved a UFO with a helicopter, tells it as his own doing: "We back channelled it. That was us." Herrera confirms it from his side and stresses how rare this was, saying it "didn't happen to" other whistleblowers such as Hecker, DC Long or Steven DNA, so it would mean someone inside the programs had singled him out.
barber-s-symptoms-compared-with-john-bur: Jake Barber, a former helicopter pilot who says he helped carry away a UFO, says he had the same kind of health symptoms as John Burroughs. Burroughs was one of the airmen, along with Jim Penniston, involved in a reported encounter in Rendlesham Forest in Suffolk, England, in 1980. Barber says Burroughs also had trouble with his records at the VA, the US government agency that handles veterans' health care, much like his own, and he tells this as a sign that their experiences were alike.
barber-s-team-brought-in-for-dod-59-agen: A helicopter pilot named Jake Barber, who says he once retrieved a UFO, says that in 2024 his team was brought in for the Department of Defense at Picatinny Arsenal, an Army base in New Jersey. He says more than 59 local police bodies were working there without coordinating, along with the FBI, the Department of Defense and private partners. Barber tells it as someone who took part, and it would mean the response to events there was large and disorganized.
barber-s-team-saw-the-same-octagonal-eig: In 2023, according to Jake Barber, a former helicopter pilot who says he took part in recovering a UFO, his team saw an eight-sided craft he calls an "eight-gon". Barber says it is exactly the craft that another witness, a man named Michael Herrera, says he saw, which to Barber means two separate accounts point to the same object.
barber-sent-to-red-team-whistleblowers-a: In 2023, at a whistleblower conference held at the National Press Club in Washington DC by the UFO activist Steven Greer, a helicopter pilot named Jake Barber says he was in the audience on his employer's orders, sent "to look for whistleblowers". He calls this red-teaming: probing the people coming forward to find out who knew what. Barber says it was there that he heard a man named Michael Herrera, who says he saw a 300-foot craft in the Indonesian jungle, tell his story. Herrera himself says he was suspicious when Barber first approached him, but that Barber has since been open about his role as a red-team asset, while Michels, putting it to Greer, describes it as Barber coming to infiltrate Greer's camp.
barber-story-contractor-and-mercenary-re: Private contractor teams and hired mercenary units are said to compete with each other to recover crashed unknown craft. The commentator Matthew Pines raises this as one of the odder parts of the account given by a man named Jake Barber, who has told of taking part in such recoveries. If true, the recovery of these objects would not be in the hands of one government team alone.
barry-says-the-secrecy-sucks-1987: Between 1987 and 1989, at a secret site in the Nevada desert he calls S4, a man named Bob Lazar says he turned to a coworker named Barry Castilio and asked, "Can you believe this is being kept secret?" According to Lazar, Castilio answered, "it sucks. I know." Lazar tells it firsthand, as a sign that even the people inside the program were uneasy about hiding what they worked on.
basalt-bas-relief-carrying-hermetic-teac: Near Lake Van in Turkey, there is said to be a huge carved stone block made of basalt, a dark volcanic rock, about 3 feet by 3 feet by 4 feet, with sacred teachings carved into it in relief. The researcher Matt LaCroix describes it to Michels without naming a source. He says he thinks these teachings became the basis of Hermeticism, an old body of mystical and philosophical writing, which would mean that tradition is far older than people usually think.
basel-group-extended-the-dmt-state-to-90: A research group in Basel, led by a scientist the guest names as Matias Leaki, has stretched the state brought on by DMT, a powerful and usually very short-acting psychedelic, to 90 minutes. The neuroscientist Andrew Gallimore mentions this on Michels's show, citing the group but no paper, because a longer stay would let people spend real time in the realm they report meeting beings in.
bases-on-the-far-side-of-the-moon: Someone is said to have bases on the far side of the Moon, the side that never faces Earth. A scientist named John Brandenburg puts it forward as his own reasoning: "you would have bases there, but you have them on the far side interestingly enough. It's almost as if you're afraid we'll see them." A man named Chris Bledsoe, who says UFOs often appear around him, tells it differently. He does not say bases. He says that from photos of the Moon he has seen, "there is something behind it hidden back there." If true, it would mean someone is hiding a presence just out of our sight.
bat-filled-structures-smell-different-fr: The ancient tombs at Saqqara in Egypt that are full of bats smell different from the Red Pyramid, one of Egypt's great old pyramids, according to Geoffrey Drumm, who researches what the pyramids were for. Drumm says he has been inside Mastaba 17, a large stone tomb, and the Tomb of the Birds, both packed with bats, and he uses the difference in smell to argue that the pyramid is a different kind of building.
battelle-analysis-of-1947-1952-sightings: A research institute called Battelle carried out what Michels calls "a very very deep analysis" of UFO sightings from 1947 to 1952, and he says that 33 percent of the most credible sightings stayed unknown. Michels brings this up himself in a debate with a skeptic, as evidence that the best cases could not be explained away.
battelle-biologics-lab-at-fort-detrick: Battelle, a research contractor, is said to run some kind of biological materials lab at Fort Detrick, a US Army base in Maryland. An online UFO researcher who goes by UAPGerb says that if any group is studying "actual biologics," meaning bodies or tissue that is not human, it is probably Battelle. He offers this as his own guess, without naming a source.
battelle-brainstorms-injectable-interfac: A research organisation called Battelle worked on a program it called Brainstorms, an interface that could be injected into the body to link the brain with machines, alongside the Air Force Research Lab and Carnegie Mellon University. Michels tells this himself and points to Battelle's own 2020 press release, which he says announced that the team had "progressed to phase two of the program". He brings it up to show how far military-backed brain technology had gone.
battelle-memorial-institute-linked-to-gi: Michels says there is a link between the Battelle Memorial Institute, a private research organisation, the US school programmes for gifted and talented children, and a secret group he calls 'the Cabal' that is said to run the government's UFO programmes. He raises this in an episode with the UFO researcher Steven Greer and credits it to a senior government official he does not name. If true, it would mean the group behind the UFO secrets also reaches into how bright children are picked out and taught.
battelle-studied-roswell-lightweight-met: Battelle Memorial Institute, a private research laboratory in Ohio, is said to have studied very lightweight metals taken from the 1947 crash at Roswell, New Mexico. The online researcher known as UAPGerb says there is research suggesting this, linking it to Project Stork, a study Battelle did for the Air Force, but he names no single source. If true, a civilian lab would have handled crash material from the start.
battle-of-los-angeles-and-the-marshall-b: In 1942, during what came to be called the Battle of Los Angeles, a UFO appeared and flew down the California coast, and the matter was briefed all the way up to George Marshall, a top American wartime leader. Michels tells this himself in two episodes, without naming a source; in the second he gives the route as Santa Monica to San Diego and calls Marshall Secretary of State. He tells it because, if true, it would mean the highest levels of the wartime government knew about a UFO well before the subject became famous.
bauval-hancock-and-schoch-on-sphinx-weat: Since the 1990s, the writers Robert Bauval and Graham Hancock and the geologist Robert Schoch have argued that the limestone of the Great Sphinx in Egypt shows damage that hints it is far older than usually thought, linked to an alignment with the stars of Orion around 10,500 BC. Michels sums up their work in a sentence, saying they have been "saying very interesting things" about the Sphinx. If they were right, a lost civilization would have built it long before recorded history.
bay-of-pigs-bombers-arrive-late-because-: At the Bay of Pigs in 1961, the failed invasion of Cuba by US-backed exiles, the bombers sent from Nicaragua to support the landing arrived late because they were in a different time zone, according to Dan Sheehan, a guest on Jesse Michels's show. Sheehan tells it without naming a source and brings up a man named Anastasio Somoza along the way, as part of a story he links to President Kennedy and secrets about UFOs.
bayer-letters-with-third-reich-generals-: There are letters, says Brigham Buhler, a guest talking about the drug industry's dark past, that went back and forth between the German drug company Bayer and generals of the Third Reich, the Nazi state, about trials carried out in the camps. Buhler mentions the letters in passing as something he has been told about, and does not describe what they say. If true, it would tie a major drug maker directly to Nazi human experiments.
bayer-ships-hiv-contaminated-hemophilia-: In the 1980s, the story goes, the drug company Bayer knowingly shipped large amounts of medicine for hemophilia, a disorder that stops blood from clotting, that was infected with HIV, the virus that causes AIDS, into poorer countries. Brigham Buhler, a guest who talks about the drug industry, brings it up as an example of what drug makers have done, saying they "knowingly shipped a massive amount" of these drugs abroad. If true, it would mean a company knowingly sent tainted medicine to sick people.
beach-photo-of-a-suited-being-in-baja-ca: A young woman taking photos on a beach at sunset in Baja California, Mexico, is said to have caught a being in a suit in one of her pictures. Ammar Kandil, a guest said to sit on a huge store of UFO evidence, tells it as a friend-of-a-friend story: the woman is his best friend's sister's best friend. He says it came to mind because it reminded him of another account.
beam-over-the-canoe-taken-aboard-wand-ja: In 1976, on the Allagash Waterway, a river route through the Maine woods, a craft hung right on top of a canoe and a beam came down around it, according to Jim Weiner, who was in the canoe. Weiner says he was taken aboard and that a wand-like tool was jabbed into his ribs, an account he tells as one of the strange abduction details he believes the government will never disclose.
bechtel-and-monsanto-possibly-handling-a: Big companies may have helped handle alien bodies and biological specimens in secure underground facilities: the engineering and construction firm Bechtel, and the chemical and farming company Monsanto, which Michels says was "most likely dealing with biological specimens." Michels tells this as something he was told, without saying who told him.
beckwith-s-neutrino-light-detector-seize: An inventor named Bob Beckwith is said to have built a detector that picked up bursts of neutrino light, neutrinos being tiny particles that pass through almost everything. According to the UFO activist Steven Greer, who repeats what Beckwith told him, Beckwith then got a national security order from the National Reconnaissance Office, the US agency that runs spy satellites. If true, the government would be shutting down private inventions it considers sensitive.
bedrock-mound-inside-the-great-pyramid-i: The natural hill of rock that the Great Pyramid of Giza in Egypt was built over rises much higher inside the pyramid than people assume. That is the opinion of a researcher named Jeffrey Drum, who says on Michels' show, without citing a source, "in my opinion, the bedrock mound is actually much taller than we think." If so, more of the pyramid's core would be living rock than built stone.
bedrock-shafts-along-the-causeway-as-ind: Shafts cut into the bedrock along the causeway of Khafre, the long ancient road leading up to one of the pyramids at Giza in Egypt, were part of the plateau's industrial machinery. The researcher Jeffrey Drum gives this as his own opinion on Michels's show, as part of his case that the pyramids sat on top of some kind of energy works.
beehive-like-interior-of-the-craft-and-a: A former nuclear missile security guard named Mario Woods says he was taken aboard a craft in South Dakota and saw an inside like a beehive, with "multi levels" and "all these small Grays everywhere going to and fro". The Grays are small grey-skinned beings, the classic picture of an alien. Woods tells it twice on Michels's show: in one telling he also describes being held in a pyramid-shaped field, and in the other he dates the event to 1977 and leaves out the pyramid.
beethoven-s-bone-conduction-1800: The composer Ludwig van Beethoven went deaf in Vienna in the early 1800s, and he kept hearing music through bone conduction, sound carried through the bones of the skull rather than the ears. Michels mentions it himself, without naming a source, in an episode about a CIA scientist who says he contacted an alien council. He uses it as an example of sound or signals reaching a person without passing through the usual senses.
befriending-john-wheeler-at-a-new-jersey: A man named Bob Maguire, who describes himself as a contractor for the CIA, says he got to know the physicist John Wheeler, a figure tied to the Institute for Advanced Study, a research centre in Princeton, at a retirement community in New Jersey. Maguire tells it firsthand: he lived in New Jersey for a while, worked for an outfit that served the intelligence community, and his wife was a nurse at the retirement community, which is how the friendship began.
behavior-control-tests-on-holmesburg-pri: Tests meant to control human behaviour were carried out on inmates at Holmesburg Prison in Philadelphia, a full decade after MK Ultra, a secret government programme of mind-control experiments, had supposedly been shut down. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, in an episode about the history of drug companies and human experiments. If true, it would mean such experiments went on long after officials said they had ended.
being-said-because-he-s-here-1977: During an encounter in 1977 in the missile field of Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota, a being said something was happening "because he's here," according to an Air Force veteran named Mario Woods, who says he was abducted by aliens there. Woods, who was present, recalls that it named no one, neither him nor the other man with him: it "just said because he's here."
being-shows-longitudinal-scalar-waves-as: Dave Rossi, a man who says aliens taught him advanced physics, says that in 2021, at his home, a being showed him a kind of wave that exists all around us. He calls them longitudinal or scalar waves, waves that push and pull along their direction of travel, and says the being showed them to him as slinkies, which for him means hidden physics was handed over directly.
being-taken-to-campinas-pathologist-then: In 1996 in Brazil, a captured being was reportedly taken to Campinas, to a famous pathologist named Badan Palhares, a friend of a doctor named Rodrigues, and then sent on to Area 51, a secret US military base. Italo Venturelli, a surgeon whose hospital is said to have operated on the being, repeats this as "the story" he was told, and the same words come up again in a later episode, said there by a speaker in a clip. If true, it would mean a creature found in Brazil ended up in American hands.
beings-at-mount-zeil-let-pat-price-know-: Beings at Mount Zeil, a mountain in Australia, are said to have let a man named Pat Price know that they knew he was watching them, and this frightened him. A former Army sergeant named Lyn Buchanan tells it, saying that when Price "did that one," meaning when he looked at the site from afar with his mind, "they let him know that they knew he was there." Buchanan passes it on as what Price went through; if true, it would mean the beings could sense being observed.
beings-landing-in-townsend-brown-s-yard-: Small beings are said to have landed in the yard of Thomas Townsend Brown, an American inventor who studied links between electricity and gravity, got out, and given him information. Chris Bledsoe, a North Carolina man who says he has had his own UFO encounters, tells this as something he was told by a man named Timothy Taylor. Bledsoe says that when they reached Zanesville together, Taylor revealed who he was and that he was helping Brown's daughter finish a book about her father. From Taylor, Bledsoe says, he learned the story of Brown "having visitors come and land." Michels adds another source: Brown's daughter, Linda Brown, did an online question-and-answer session on Reddit, a discussion website. In it, Michels says, she spoke of pale beings coming down and entering the house, into the kitchen. If true, it would mean an inventor of gravity-related devices had been in contact with visitors.
beings-say-they-will-not-allow-nuclear-w: In 1964 at Vandenberg Air Force Base in California, beings told a nuclear missile guard named Richard Barth that they would not let humanity go to nuclear war, and that "they needed to stop these missiles from launching". Barth says this happened during his own abduction. He adds that his sense was they would leave us alone "unless we screwed up", which, if true, would mean someone outside humanity is keeping watch over our nuclear weapons.
beings-under-mount-shasta: People have long said that beings live beneath Mount Shasta, a mountain in northern California. The UFO researcher Grant Cameron mentions this in passing, as something people "always talk about," without giving a source of his own.
belgian-air-force-commander-says-ufos-ar: The top commander of Belgium's air force is said to have stated that UFOs are real. A man named Charlie Foltz, himself a witness to UFO events, passes this on as something he was told. If true, it would mean a senior military leader of a Western country openly accepted the phenomenon.
belgian-wave-triangles-1989: During the Belgian wave, a run of UFO sightings across Belgium in 1989 and 1990, the objects people reported were triangles. An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb mentions this in passing, without naming a source. He brings it up as part of a pattern of triangle-shaped craft that, if real, would point to one kind of vehicle being seen again and again.
bell-as-a-thorium-mercury-overunity-powe: The Bell, a device said to have been built by Nazi Germany at the Skoda Works near Prague between 1937 and 1944, is described as an "overunity" machine, one that gives out more energy than goes into it. AC and DC power went in, and a nuclear reaction of thorium and mercury did the rest. The researcher Jason Jorjani says an unnamed elderly man in Serbia told him this. If true, the Nazis built a power source that broke the normal limits of physics.
bell-integrated-into-the-saucer-airframe: In 1944, at the Skoda Works, a big weapons factory near Prague, German engineers are said to have taken the rockets out of a disc-shaped aircraft and put in "the bell," a bell-shaped device said to be a secret Nazi power source, making a flying saucer. The researcher Jason Jorjani tells it in his own words, crediting a work called Closer Encounters: "They took the rockets out, put the bell in it, and there's your flying saucer." If true, it would mean Nazi Germany built a working saucer during the war.
bell-project-dates-to-1937-per-a-serbian: A secret German project known as the Bell, which the researcher Jason Jorjani ties to what he calls Hitler's UFO programme, is said to have begun as early as 1937. Jorjani says he was told this by an elderly, unnamed person in Serbia who had "relatively direct knowledge." If true, the project would have started years earlier than is usually said.
bell-scientists-experienced-temporal-dis: In the 1940s, scientists working on "the Bell", a device said to have been built in a secret Nazi programme, felt time flowing at a different rate than people outside the laboratory did, according to the researcher Jason Jorjani. Jorjani tells this to Jesse Michels by citing reports from the writers Igor Witkowski and Joseph P. Farrell. If true, it would mean the device was somehow bending time itself.
belt-montana-truck-driver-sees-light-lan: In 1967, a truck driver passing through the town of Belt, Montana, about 35 miles from a nuclear missile site, is said to have seen a light come down into a ravine. Robert Salas, a former Air Force officer who says a UFO shut down ten of his nuclear missiles that year, passes on the driver's account. Michels tells it more briefly, saying a local truck driver and a police officer are both "on record having seen the UFO in the area," without mentioning the ravine. Both tell it as outside support for the strange events at the missile sites.
ben-rich-and-reverse-engineered-aerospac: An aerospace engineer named Ben Rich is said to have hinted that some American aircraft technology came from studying craft that were not built by people. John Blitch, a former scientist at the Pentagon's advanced research agency, does not repeat the details but says he has no reason to call Rich a liar.
ben-rich-called-ufos-unfunded-opportunit: Ben Rich, who ran Lockheed's Skunk Works, the company's secret aircraft design shop, is said to have called UFOs "unfunded opportunities" in the 1990s. Michels recalls that the defence writer Nick Cook once told him this. If true, it hints that a top aircraft builder saw UFOs as technology waiting to be paid for and built.
ben-rich-deathbed-claim-that-we-can-go-t: Ben Rich ran Lockheed Skunk Works, the aircraft company's secret design division. The story is that late in life, some say on his deathbed, he said the US already has the means to travel to the stars. In Michels's best-known version, a journalist asks him how, and Rich replies, "have you heard of ESP?," meaning extrasensory perception, or powers of the mind. "Well, that's how," he says. In other tellings Michels names a man called John Andrews of Testors as the person Rich said it to, or dates the remark to 1995 and quotes Rich saying the technologies "are locked up in black projects," meaning secretly funded programs. The UFO researcher Grant Cameron says it was a man named Jan Harzan who asked the question, and that Harzan answered that ESP "means everything in time and space is connected." If true, it would mean a top aircraft designer was saying that star travel works through the mind.
ben-rich-on-an-international-board-of-di: Ben Rich, the director of Skunk Works, the secret aircraft design unit at the company Lockheed, is said to have complained that control of the UFO subject had run away to "an international board of directors", a kind of private corporate group. Michels repeats this on several episodes, relaying Rich's words. The details shift as he tells it: once he places it in letters Rich wrote in the early 1990s to John Andrews of what he calls Testor Motor Corp, credited to the book Forbidden Science by the UFO researcher Jacques Vallée, and once he says Rich said it on his deathbed to Andrews.
ben-rich-s-deathbed-remarks-to-jim-gooda: Near the end of his life, around 1993 to 1995, Ben Rich, the head of Lockheed's secret aircraft design shop, the Skunk Works, is said to have told the aviation writer Jim Goodall: "Jim, we have things out in the desert," meaning somewhere other than Area 51, the well-known secret Nevada base. Goodall tells it himself as what Rich said to him in the hospital, and in a later retelling adds that Rich called the things "50 years beyond what you can comprehend." It would mean the US holds technology far ahead of anything known.
ben-rich-s-ucla-speech-1990: Late in his life, in the 1990s, Ben Rich, the former head of Skunk Works, the secret aircraft design division of the company Lockheed, is said to have made very strange remarks during a speech at UCLA, the University of California, Los Angeles. Michels tells it himself, citing Rich, and in another episode gives the gist of the remarks: that the United States already has the power to travel to the stars and to take ET home.
