In that second telling he does not name UCLA as the place. If Rich meant it, a top aerospace insider was hinting at hidden technology far beyond what is known.
ben-rich-says-the-math-in-maxwell-s-equa: In the 1990s, Ben Rich, who ran Skunk Works, the secret aircraft design division of the company Lockheed, said that some of the math in Maxwell's equations, the basic equations of electricity and magnetism, was "a little off." Michels mentions this himself, without giving a source, as a hint that insiders believed there was physics beyond what textbooks teach.
ben-rich-skunk-works-considered-burying-: In the 1970s, Lockheed's Skunk Works, the company's secret aircraft design shop, is said to have thought about shelving stealth, the technology that hides planes from radar, before work on it even began. The aviation journalist Nick Cook repeats this from Ben Rich, who ran the Skunk Works, quoting him: "we considered actually burying the whole thing. I mean, before we even got started." It shows how close a major technology came to never being built.
ben-rich-we-have-the-technology-to-take-: Ben Rich, the engineer who once ran Lockheed's secret aircraft division known as the Skunk Works, is said to have told an audience: 'We now have the technology to take ET home.' Michels repeats the line in two episodes. In the later one he places it at the end of a speech Rich gave at the University of California, Los Angeles in 1993, and says several people who were there heard it. If he meant it, it would suggest the US had secretly built craft that could travel to the stars.
ben-van-kerkwijk-on-the-hawara-labyrinth: A huge labyrinth, a maze of buildings, once stood in the Hawara region of Egypt, and the researcher Ben van Kerkwijk talks about it, drawing on accounts by the ancient Greek historian Herodotus and the Roman writer Pliny the Elder. Michels raises this with a scientist who has scanned beneath the pyramids, noting that van Kerkwijk had just described it on the show of the podcaster Joe Rogan. If true, it would point to a vast lost structure still hidden under the Egyptian sand.
bendix-employee-captured-by-the-tupamaro: In the 1970s, a man working for Bendix, an American aerospace and electronics company, is said to have been taken straight from his office in Uruguay by the Tupamaros, an armed left-wing group there. The writer Peter Levenda, billed as a historian of the CIA, tells it as something he heard, and says he believes the man was killed.
bendix-field-engineering-as-a-cia-non-of: A writer named Peter Levenda, who has written about the CIA's history, says that in the 1970s the field engineering division of Bendix, an engineering company with offices on Broadway in Manhattan, was a front for the CIA. He says that when the CIA or someone else wanted to send a person abroad under non-official cover, meaning posing as a private worker rather than a government employee, they used Bendix Field Engineering Services. Levenda says he knew this from working there, where the division was legendary among staff.
benedict-gross-and-epstein-proposal-for-: In the 2000s, Harvard University is said to have funded work on evolutionary dynamics, linked to the scientist Martin Nowak, that grew out of a proposal by the Harvard mathematician Benedict Gross and the financier Jeffrey Epstein. The mathematician Eric Weinstein points to a Harvard document that, he says, refers to "an imaginative proposal by Benedict Gross and Jeffrey Epstein." If true, it would show Epstein had a direct hand in shaping research at Harvard.
benjamin-franklin-and-the-french-muse-lo: The American founding father Benjamin Franklin is said to have belonged to a lodge of the Freemasons, a secretive fraternal society, in France, and to a special kind of lodge named for the Muses, the Greek goddesses of the arts. The researcher Diana Pasulka mentions it in passing on Michels's show, in a talk about religion and UFOs, without naming where she learned it.
benjamin-libet-s-neural-timing-studies-1: In the 1970s and 80s, a scientist named Benjamin Libet ran what are described as landmark studies on the timing of activity in the brain. The researcher and writer Eric Wargo brings them up in passing, without naming a source, as groundwork for his ideas about the mind and time.
bennewitz-involuntarily-committed-1980: In New Mexico in the 1980s, a man named Paul Bennewitz was put into a mental hospital against his will. The physicist John Brandenburg says so briefly, simply agreeing that "they involuntarily committed him." If true, it would mean Bennewitz was silenced, though Brandenburg does not say here who did it or why.
bennewitz-sees-craft-at-kirtland-1979: In the late 1970s a civilian named Paul Bennewitz, living near Kirtland Air Force Base in New Mexico, says he saw strange craft rising and landing on the base. Jesse Michels says this is what put Bennewitz on the radar of military counter-intelligence people: he saw a craft "vertically taking off and landing at Kirtland Air Force Base." The physicist John Brandenburg repeats what Bennewitz said, placing the sightings over Manzano Mountain, a mountain at the base where nuclear weapons are stored, and saying he saw UFOs there a lot. The writer Greg Bishop, who researched Bennewitz's story, describes the objects as "glowing orbs" lifting off the ground somewhere on the base, flying over a mountain and coming down. Bishop dates it to 1977 and 1978 rather than 1979. The tellers tell it because UFOs over a nuclear weapons site would be a serious matter, and because of what the government did to Bennewitz afterwards.
benowitz-builds-receivers-to-intercept-b: Between about 1979 and 1981, a man named Paul Bennewitz is said to have built his own receiving equipment and used it to listen in on radio transmissions coming from Kirtland Air Force Base in New Mexico. The researcher Greg Bishop tells this as a summary, without naming a source, and hedges it with an "apparently". It matters because it would mean a private citizen was picking up signals from a military base.
benowitz-kirtland-video-of-a-saucer-with: Around 1980, near Kirtland Air Force Base in New Mexico, a man named Paul Bennewitz filmed footage that, in one clip, shows something shaped like a saucer with a Pacific Southwest Airlines passenger plane flying behind it. Greg Bishop, a guest who has looked at the footage himself, describes it, and he brings it up as part of the story of a man he says was driven to madness by the subject.
benowitz-photographs-an-alleged-undergro: In the early 1980s a New Mexico man named Paul Bennewitz became convinced there was an alien base underground at Archuleta Mesa, a flat-topped hill in northern New Mexico, and went there with a camera to take pictures of it. The writer Greg Bishop tells the story on an episode about how the alien question drove Bennewitz to breaking point. Bishop puts it simply: "there was an alien base underground at the Archeletta Mesa. He went there with a camera and took pictures."
benowitz-placed-in-a-mental-health-facil: In the 1980s, a man in Albuquerque, New Mexico, named Paul Bennewitz is said to have been put in a mental health facility for about a month. The researcher and writer Greg Bishop tells this to Michels, without naming a source, on an episode about how talk of aliens drove this man to break down. The story matters to Bishop because it shows what happened to Bennewitz after he got pulled into UFO claims.
benowitz-s-apro-membership-application-1: Sometime between 1977 and 1979, a man named Paul Bennewitz applied to join the Aerial Phenomena Research Organization, or APRO, a civilian UFO research group based in Arizona. Greg Bishop, who has looked into Bennewitz's life and says he has seen the form, says one question asked for his favorite UFO book, and that Bennewitz wrote only "Books by Hynek," meaning the UFO researcher J. Allen Hynek. Bishop tells it to show where Bennewitz's interest in the subject stood before his later troubles.
benowitz-s-drawings-of-an-alien-craft-fl: In the early 1980s near Archuleta Mesa in New Mexico, a businessman named Paul Bennewitz made drawings of what he said was a craft the aliens had given to the US government, which the government flew without really knowing how, until it crashed. The researcher and writer Greg Bishop tells this, summing up what Bennewitz said and pointing to the material known as Project Beta. If true, it would mean the government was flying an alien craft.
bentov-puharich-and-geller-together-in-t: In the 1970s three men, a scientist named Puharich, an inventor named Itzhak Bentov and the psychic Uri Geller, were together in an apartment in Tel Aviv, Israel, according to a researcher named Greg Malatzi. He says there are photographs of the three there, and he also points to tape recordings made by Puharich and Bentov. He raises it to show the three worked closely together.
bentov-s-mysterious-death-in-a-plane-cra: Itzhak Bentov, the author of a book called Stalking the Wild Pendulum, died in a plane crash in 1979, a death Michels presents as part of a pattern of scientists lost under strange circumstances. Michels tells it himself, without naming a source, in two episodes. In the later one he gives the details: Bentov was 55 when American Airlines Flight 191 crashed soon after taking off from Chicago's O'Hare airport.
bentwaters-guards-see-multicolor-disc-re: In 1980, guards at RAF Bentwaters, an air base in England, are said to have seen a large disc in many colours quite close to them, an object that, as the story goes, pulled a rod back into itself. The researcher Robert Hastings tells it on Michels's show, saying a couple of the men have gone on the record about it, though he does not name his source. He gives it as part of his case that UFOs keep watch over nuclear weapons bases around the world.
bentwaters-nukes-flown-to-kirtland-for-a: Shortly after the strange events of 1980 near RAF Bentwaters, an air base in England, two small nuclear bombs are said to have been taken from a bunker there and flown on a large C-5A cargo plane to Kirtland Air Force Base in New Mexico to be checked. Robert Hastings, a researcher who studies UFO reports at nuclear weapons sites, says he heard this from an unnamed retired colonel who handled weapons security for NATO, the Western military alliance. If true, it would mean the military feared the weapons had been affected by whatever happened.
bentwaters-rendlesham-1980-multi-witness: In 1980, at Bentwaters, a Royal Air Force base in England run jointly with the US military, a number of servicemen are said to have seen a UFO. Michels tells this himself across three episodes, naming the witnesses as two US Air Force men, Jim Penniston and John Burroughs, and Colonel Charles Halt, an officer who investigated the event afterwards. In one telling he adds that Halt's investigation found that everything checked out. In another he calls the witnesses three Air Force sergeants and also brings in a British peer named Lord Hill-Norton. Michels cites it because many trained military witnesses on one base would make it hard to dismiss.
berkeley-parapsychology-professor-quits-: In the 1970s, as a graduate student at the University of California, Berkeley, Jeffrey Mishlove began studying a man named Ted Owens, who claimed to be in telepathic contact with aliens. Mishlove says firsthand that one of his professors in parapsychology, the study of claimed psychic abilities, quit his thesis committee over it, saying "we just can't combine these two fields", meaning that even psychic research would not touch aliens.
bermuda-bar-a-stranger-s-birthday-unlock: In a bar in Bermuda, a stranger typed his own birthday into a woman's locked phone and it opened, according to the magician and YouTuber Chris Ramsay, who was there. Ramsay says it was he who told the man, "put in your birthday," and he tells it as one of the strange coincidences that make him think something more is going on.
bermuda-triangle-anomalies: The Bermuda Triangle, a stretch of the Atlantic Ocean long known for stories of lost ships and planes, is said to show real, measurable oddities. A retired US Navy admiral named Tim Gallaudet says on the show that there seems to be "data" and "evidence of anomalies" there. He speaks as a former senior official, though he does not say what the data is. Michels tells a similar version that he heard from a former NASA engineer, NASA being the US space agency. In that version, there is "a little patch" in or near the Triangle with "tons of electromagnetic anomalies", meaning strange readings in magnetic and electrical fields. So one teller speaks of official data in general, and the other of electromagnetic readings passed on secondhand. If true, it would mean something physical and unexplained is going on in that patch of ocean.
bermuda-triangle-compass-deviations-from: Compasses go wrong in the Bermuda Triangle, a stretch of ocean off Florida known for stories of ships and planes going missing, because metal meteorites landed under the sea floor in very ancient times. That is the personal belief of Greg Rogers, a NASA doctor, who offers it as his own explanation rather than something he saw.
beta-israel-tradition-of-bringing-the-ar: The Beta Israel, the Jews of Ethiopia, also called the Falashas, have a tradition that their ancestors fled Israel carrying the Ark of the Covenant, the sacred chest of the Bible. As the story goes, they kept it for several hundred years on an island in the Nile, Elephantine in Egypt, then brought it to Ethiopia, by Lake Tana. The writer Graham Hancock tells this on two visits to the show, passing on what the Beta Israel say, and the second time he also points to an Ethiopian text called the Kebra Nagast, all in support of his view that the Ark ended up in Ethiopia.
bettis-lab-naval-nuclear-power-and-weste: In the 1950s a research lab in Pittsburgh called Bettis became the first to develop nuclear power for the US Navy, and western Pennsylvania later saw many UFO sightings, among them the case at a place called Kexsburg. A researcher named Dylan Borland puts the two side by side on Jesse Michels's show, without naming a source, and suggests the nuclear work and the sightings in the same region may be linked.
betty-and-barney-hill-abduction-and-the-: In 1961, Betty and Barney Hill, a couple in New Hampshire, said they were taken aboard a craft by strange beings. It is often called the first or most famous US abduction case. Jesse Michels tells it many times. He says the couple were interracial and were civil rights activists. He says Barney reluctantly said sperm samples were taken from him, and that Betty later drew a star map that seemed to point to a binary star system like Zeta Reticuli. Michels also raises a doubt from the scholar Diana Pasulka's book American Cosmic: the beings' wraparound eyes might echo a CBS science fiction show of the time, The Outer Limits. The researcher Clas Svahn adds that the beings examined Barney's false teeth and used a needle on the couple. The researcher Jason Jorjani points to Barney's first statements, and the show plays hypnosis audio of Barney himself saying the figure in the window "looks like a German Nazi". If true, the case would be one of the earliest reports of people being taken by non-humans.
betty-and-barney-hill-abduction-possibly: Betty Hill and Barney Hill, a couple in New Hampshire, said they were abducted in 1961. The researcher Steven Greer says it "very likely was" done by humans, not by visitors from elsewhere, because the way it happened "would not be consistent with interstellar transdimensional technologies." If he is right, one of the best-known abduction stories would be a human operation.
betty-and-barney-hill-told-the-air-force: Betty and Barney Hill, a New Hampshire couple who said they had a UFO encounter in 1961, gave the US Air Force one account and later gave a psychologist a different one. A researcher named Chris Ramsay makes the point on Michels' show in passing, without naming a source, using the Hills as an example of how stories of such encounters shift depending on who is listening.
betty-andreasson-luca-told-that-nordic-a: A woman named Betty Andreasson Luca is said to have been taken in the 1960s from her family home to a place underground or underwater, where tall, angel-like, fair-haired beings told her they had brought Christ into the world and would soon bring him back. The researcher Jason Jorjani retells it on Michels's show, also naming her daughter Becky Andreasson, without citing a source. He tells it to back his idea that beings from elsewhere shaped human religion.
betty-hill-s-1950s-crash-debris-buried-i: In the 1950s a woman named Betty Hill and a relative were sitting on a porch on a warm night when something crossed the sky and crashed. They went out into the field and brought back debris, which ended up buried in her backyard. A UFO researcher named Clas Svahn says Hill told him this, and a recording of Hill herself places it during a visit to family in Maine, when they first thought the object was "a plane".
beverly-hovering-metallic-object-1966: In 1966 in Beverly, Massachusetts, nine witnesses, two of them police officers, are said to have seen a metallic object shaped like a plate. The writer Marik von Rennenkampff cites the case briefly, without naming a source, as an example of a sighting backed by several credible witnesses.
beyond-skinwalker-investigation-at-brads: Strange things are said to have shown up on cameras at Bradshaw Ranch near Sedona, Arizona, during an investigation called Beyond Skinwalker, named after Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property known for reports of odd events. The teller, a guest on Michels's episode with the owner of Skinwalker Ranch, says firsthand: "I went there myself and there were some strange things that came up on the cameras," and names a Dr. Taylor and a witness named Erik Bard as part of the story.
bezos-s-grandfather-lawrence-gise-ran-th: Jeff Bezos's grandfather, Lawrence Preston Gise, is said to have been director of the Western Division of the Atomic Energy Commission, the US body that ran nuclear research, in the 1960s. The commentator Matthew Pines says the former government trade official Harold Malmgren told him this. If true, it would tie the family of one of the world's richest men to secret government science.
bial-foundation-as-the-biggest-funder-of: The Bial Foundation in Portugal is the biggest funder of parapsychology, the study of claimed mental abilities such as telepathy. That is according to the researcher Rupert Sheldrake, who says "about half their grants" go to this field. He mentions it in passing, without naming a source, as a sign of where money for this kind of research comes from.
biefeld-affidavit-confirming-anomalous-e: The inventor Townsend Brown, critics say, never met a man named Paul Alfred Biefeld, whose name is tied to a strange electrical effect Brown studied in Ohio. But a sworn written statement from Biefeld that came out later is said to show they did. Paul Schatzkin, who has studied Brown's life, tells this himself, with only the affidavit as a source: "Paul Biefeld definitely met Townsend Brown." If true, it backs up Brown's account of how his work on the effect began.
biefeld-brown-effect-and-townsend-brown: There is something called the Biefeld-Brown effect, in which electrically charged devices seem to push themselves along, and it is tied to an inventor named Thomas Townsend Brown. Michels names it himself in passing, as an example of a discovery that has been made, and says he is "obsessed with this Townsend Brown character."
biefeld-brown-vacuum-tests-1990-air-forc: Michels says that in 1990 the US Air Force tested the Biefeld-Brown effect in a vacuum. That is the claim by the researcher Thomas Townsend Brown that high voltage can push an object forward with no moving parts. But the Air Force used only 19 kilovolts, far less than the millions of volts Brown used, and an earlier vacuum test in Paris in 1956 also comes up, with a man named Jacques Cornillon listed as a witness. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, to argue that the Air Force's negative result did not fairly test Brown's claim.
big-black-triangle-hovers-over-vandenber: A huge black triangle is said to have come in from the Pacific Ocean and hovered over Vandenberg Air Force Base in California. Jeff Natelli tells it first hand: he says he went to the scene on October 14, 2003, and "talked to five shaken witnesses." They described "a massive triangular craft larger than a football field" that hovered without a sound for about 45 seconds over their entry gate, then "shooting away at impossible speed." Matthew Brown, a former Pentagon official, repeats the story from Natelli, saying the triangle came "out of the Pacific Ocean flying into Vandenberg." If true, a large unknown craft sat in plain view over a military base.
big-meteor-over-aland-the-day-after-the-: In June 2025, the day after a search trip, a big meteor was seen over Åland, a group of islands in the Baltic Sea, and over the waters nearby. The treasure hunter Dennis Asberg mentions it, saying "it was on the news," so he is passing on news reports, not his own sighting. He brings it up because it came right after his team's trip to look at a strange object on the seafloor.
bigelow-aerospace-shut-down-during-covid: Robert Bigelow, a businessman who funded UFO research, is said to have had his space company shut down by the governor of Nevada during the COVID crisis, around 2020. The parapsychologist Jeffrey Mishlove says Bigelow told him this, and that Bigelow then turned away from UFO work toward research on whether the mind survives death.
bigelow-buys-the-ranch-and-starts-nids-m: In 1996 the businessman Robert Bigelow is said to have bought Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property known for strange sightings, after the story of the Sherman family who lived there reached him, and then to have set up monitoring of the land by his private research group, the National Institute for Discovery Science. Brandon Fugal, the ranch's current owner, tells it as the ranch's history passed on to him. If true, it marks the start of serious scientific watching of the place.
bigelow-crashes-in-russia-china-south-am: Bob Bigelow, a businessman who has funded UFO research, is said to believe that craft have crashed in Russia, in China and in South America, and that they are being "seeded" around the world on purpose. Grant Cameron, a longtime UFO researcher, relays this from a man named Timothy Taylor, who says he asked Bigelow whether other countries had crashes and got that answer. If true, crash material would not be held by the United States alone.
bigelow-refuses-to-return-negative-exper: Robert Bigelow, a businessman who once owned Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property known for strange reports, is said to refuse to go back there because of the bad things he went through, which also hurt his family. The ranch's current owner tells this on the show, citing Bigelow and the journalist George Knapp: "he had such negative experiences. It impacted his family." If true, it would mean whatever is at the ranch can harm the people who deal with it.
bigelow-s-22-million-program-steered-by-: Around 2008, the story goes, $22 million in government money went to Bigelow Aerospace, the company of a businessman named Robert Bigelow, to research UFOs, with the help of Harry Reid, then the Senate Majority Leader. A guest named Steven Greer, relaying what he was told, says it was "all set up" with Colonel John B. Alexander, an Army officer he calls Bigelow's "consigliere," or right-hand adviser, steering how the money was used. Michels tells it in his own words as Bigelow working with Reid "in an official government capacity in order to kind of reverse engineer UFOs," without mentioning the sum or Alexander. If true, a private company would have been paid by the government to study and copy unknown craft.
bigelow-s-desert-alien-encounter-meet-us: The businessman Robert Bigelow is said to have started his space company because he had an encounter with aliens out in the desert, and they told him to meet them in space. Steve Colbern, a scientist who studies objects said to be alien implants in people's bodies, says an unnamed doctor told him this. If true, it would mean a private space company was born from a meeting with aliens.
bigelow-says-aliens-are-walking-among-us: Robert Bigelow, a businessman who funds research into UFOs, has said in interviews that aliens are walking among us. Michels brings this up himself in a conversation with the researcher Jeffrey Mishlove, pointing to those interviews without naming any one of them. If Bigelow is right, visitors would not just be passing through the skies but living unseen among people.
bigelow-tells-fox-they-re-walking-among-: The story is that in Las Vegas in 2009, a man named Bigelow told James Fox, plainly, "they're walking among us," meaning beings from elsewhere. Fox tells it himself, as the person who heard it, and links it to his film I Know What I Saw. If true, a well-placed figure was saying that non-human beings are already living among people.
bigelow-to-receive-ufo-material-from-loc: In 2008 a billionaire named Robert Bigelow was supposed to receive UFO material from Lockheed Martin, a large American defence company, but the transfer was blocked by a man named Glenn Gaffney. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, while speaking with the researcher Jeffrey Mishlove. If true, it would mean a private defence company held UFO material and someone stepped in to keep it from leaving.
bigfoot-rumours-in-d-sector-1964: In 1964, in D sector at Vandenberg Air Force Base in California, guards scared the new men by telling them Bigfoot was out there and would get them, says a former nuclear missile guard named Richard Barth, who served there and says he was later abducted by aliens. Barth adds that there was no talk of UFOs at all that he knew of, which matters because it means nothing had primed him for what he says came later.
bill-casey-never-raised-ufos-1980: John S. Herrington, who served as Secretary of Energy in President Reagan's cabinet in the 1980s, says the subject of UFOs never came up in that cabinet. He says that if it had been on the agenda of Bill Casey, a fellow cabinet member, Casey would have talked to him about it, which Herrington offers as a sign that the subject was not in front of the government's top people.
bill-clinton-s-tar-baby-remark-to-rockef: In 1995, at the Wyoming ranch of the wealthy philanthropist Laurance Rockefeller, President Bill Clinton is said to have told Rockefeller that the UFO question was like the story of the tar baby, an old folk tale about a sticky figure that traps whoever touches it. A UFO researcher named Grant Cameron tells this without naming a source, as a sign that the president saw the subject as something he could not touch without getting stuck.
bill-colby-s-death-before-delivering-a-z: In 1996 a man named William Colby, whom the UFO activist Steven Greer says had been let in on the secret, was trying to get a zero-point device to Greer's group when he died in a river south of Washington DC. A zero-point device is a machine said to draw energy from empty space. Greer tells this to Michels as part of his own story, and if true it would mean someone was willing to kill to keep such a device out of public hands.
bill-gunston-article-b-2-has-electrograv: A respected British aviation writer named Bill Gunston is said to have written that America's B-2 stealth bomber could not fly as well as it does on its engines alone. The suggestion is that it gets a hidden boost from electrogravitics, the idea that high voltage can push against gravity. That idea is tied to Townsend Brown, an American inventor. The story comes mainly from Nick Cook, a British aviation journalist. He calls it "this astounding article." He says that when you run the B-2's weight and engine figures, "it would have been incapable of the performance figures credited for it." Cook links the article to the publications Military Power and Air International. In a later retelling he says only that Gunston found the B-2's performance data "does not add up," with no word on electrogravitics. Michels also tells it, and dates it differently. He places the article in Air International magazine in 2000, and says Gunston was "very sure" Brown's work had made it into the B-2. If true, it would mean a working gravity-defying technology was already flying in a US warplane.
bill-hamilton-feeds-witnesses-to-greer-s: In 1997 a UFO researcher named William Hamilton III, known as Bill Hamilton and author of the book Cosmic Top Secret, is said to have been in touch with Steven Greer, a UFO activist, and to have passed witnesses on to Greer's Disclosure Project, an effort to gather insiders willing to testify about secret UFO knowledge. A researcher who goes by the name UAPGerb tells this on two episodes, summarising without naming a source. In the second telling UAPGerb gives one example: Hamilton handing Greer a key witness known only as "Brad S." If true, it would mean some of Greer's witnesses came to him through another researcher instead of finding him on their own.
bill-holden-kennedy-on-air-force-one-say: In 1963, on Air Force One heading to Berlin, President John F. Kennedy is said to have told his chief steward Bill Holden: "I know this is true and I know these are real, but the whole matter is out of my hands and I don't know why." The UFO activist Steven Greer repeats this as Holden's account, and in a second telling he gives no Berlin trip and says Kennedy said "the same thing" as President Eisenhower. If true, even a president would have been shut out of the UFO secret.
bill-lear-cut-john-lear-out-of-his-will-: Sometime in the 1970s, a man named Bill Lear is said to have written John Lear out of his will. Bob Lazar, whom Michels spent two days with, says John Lear showed him the will himself, "every paragraph."
bill-lear-figuring-out-gravity-control-1: In 1956 the inventor Bill Lear was said to be working on a way to control gravity. Michels says Lear built the Lear Jet, the first private jet. He quotes a 1956 article in Jane's Defence Weekly, a military magazine, which says that "William Lear, the autopilot wizard, is already figuring out gravity control for the weightless craft to come." In another episode Michels tells it a little differently: he has Lear himself saying in 1956 that he believed anti-gravity was possible because UFOs display it. If true, it would mean a leading aviation figure took UFO-style propulsion seriously decades ago.
bill-moore-admits-sowing-disinformation-: At a conference of MUFON, a large civilian UFO research group, the UFO researcher Bill Moore stood up and said he had been working for the government and had been told to spread false information among UFO researchers. The physicist John Brandenburg says he was in the audience. He remembers the speaker as Stan Moore, the man who first leaked the MJ-12 document, a paper describing a secret panel that handled crashed saucers. He says Moore confessed his job was to watch over a government psychological operation aimed at a man named Paul Bennewitz. The UFO historian Richard Dolan dates the talk to the late 1980s and says Moore admitted he had helped to 'mess up' Bennewitz. The online researcher UAPGerb sums it up simply as Moore saying he was told to sow disinformation into the community. If true, it would mean the government deliberately muddied the UFO field from the inside.
bill-moore-did-work-for-the-cia-1960: A man named Bill Moore did jobs for the CIA, the US spy agency, but says he was never on its staff. The researcher Grant Cameron passes on Moore's own words to him: "I didn't work for them, I did some work for them, but I didn't work for them." If true, it would mean Moore had a quiet working tie to the agency.
bill-moore-interviewed-t-townsend-brown-: A UFO writer named Bill Moore is said to have interviewed Thomas Townsend Brown, an inventor known for work on moving objects with electricity, sometime in the 1970s or 1980s. The researcher Greg Bishop mentions it in passing, crediting a work called The Cosmic Conspiracy, simply saying "Bill Moore interviewed T. Townsend Brown." It matters because it links a UFO writer to a man some see as a pioneer of anti-gravity research.
bill-moore-s-spy-training-and-soviet-pos: In the early 1980s, the UFO researcher Bill Moore is said to have been given spy-style training and set to work passing mail along and doing things involving Soviet spies. The writer Greg Bishop tells this as what Moore himself described, without saying who was directing him.
bill-moore-warns-steinman-off-mrs-wang-1: In the 1980s, the researcher William Steinman is said to have been talking with a Mrs. Wang, connected to a man named Eric Henry Wang, when another UFO researcher, Bill Moore, phoned him and asked, "What are you talking to Mrs. Wang for?" The UFO researcher Grant Cameron tells it as what Steinman told him. If true, it suggests Moore somehow knew who Steinman was speaking to and wanted him to stop.
bill-napier-links-the-younger-dryas-impa: The Younger Dryas impact idea holds that something from space hit or exploded over Earth about 12,800 years ago and set off a global disaster, and the researcher Randall Carlson says it was an astronomer named Bill Napier, at an astrophysical observatory in England, who first proposed it came from the Taurids, a stream of comet debris that Earth passes through. Michels repeats the idea on several episodes but credits Carlson and the author Graham Hancock instead of Napier, sometimes calling the object a comet bursting in the air and once an asteroid that struck the Earth.
bill-ray-s-remote-viewing-of-buddha-1980: In the 1980s, a man named Bill Ray, a member of a military remote viewing unit that tried to see distant places and people with the mind alone, is said to have been asked to remote view the Buddha, and he found it life-changing. Lyn Buchanan, a former Army sergeant who served in the unit, tells this as something he knows about Ray, without giving details of what Ray saw.
bill-richardson-siphoning-us-nuclear-sec: Michels claims that in the 1990s Bill Richardson, who was Secretary of Energy, the cabinet official in charge of America's nuclear weapons labs, was close to the Clintons and was "just systematically siphoning American nuclear secrets." Michels says this himself, without naming a source, in an episode about Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft at a secret Nevada site.
bill-sweetman-s-1980s-look-at-sap-compar: In the 1980s, after Ronald Reagan became president, a writer named Bill Sweetman is said to have made a deep study of special access programs, the most tightly sealed secret projects in the US military, and of how they were split apart and sometimes duplicated. A researcher named Eric W. Davis mentions this to Michels from memory, saying he thinks it was Sweetman, and he raises it to show how hidden programs can be walled off so that even insiders do not see the whole picture.
bill-todman-jr-touched-a-living-ufo-in-a: A film producer named Bill Todman Jr. is said to have been climbing in the Tetons, a mountain range in Wyoming, when he came into a meadow and found a UFO "just sitting right hovering right there," which, as the story goes, he touched and found to be alive. The lawyer Danny Sheehan tells it second-hand, naming Todman along with Bob Rehme and Mason Neufeld as people tied to the story. If true, it would mean UFOs can be living things.
bill-uhouse-kingman-based-simulator-and-: A man named Bill Uhouse claimed that at side sites of Area 51, a secret military test base in Nevada, a training simulator was built for flying an alien craft or a human-made copy of one, modeled on a craft from a reported crash at Kingman. The UFO researcher UAPGerb repeats Uhouse's claim, which also ties in with talk of a being called J-Rod. If true, it would mean people were being trained to fly recovered alien technology.
billy-meier-s-early-photos-show-the-spor: Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft at a secret Nevada site called S4, says that the first photographs taken in the 1970s by Billy Meier, a man known for his UFO photos, are "100% genuine". Lazar's reason is that they show a craft like the one he calls the sport model, the disc he says he saw at S4, which would mean Meier photographed the same kind of craft.
billy-meier-s-faked-photos-including-din: Some of the photographs taken by Billy Meier, a man in Switzerland known for his pictures of supposed alien craft and creatures, were faked, and one dinosaur image was copied from a book. The researcher Clas Svahn says this, adding "I have that book at home." He is pointing to the source he says the picture was copied from, which would undercut Meier's photos.
billy-meier-s-past-as-a-middle-east-inte: Billy Meier, a Swiss man known for claiming contact with beings from space, is said to have first worked as a field intelligence agent in the Middle East, getting the name Billy while working in Tehran. The philosopher Jason Jorjani tells this twice, drawing on a book called Closer Encounters, and says "The guy was 007. He was a James Bond style super spy." If true, the famous contactee would have had a hidden past in spy work.
billy-meier-s-pleiadians-1970: In the 1970s, a Swiss man named Billy Meier claimed he was in touch with kind beings from the Pleiades, a star cluster, who were going to come and save everyone. The philosopher Jason Jorjani mentions Meier's claims to Michels in passing, without naming a source, as one example of contact stories that cast aliens as saviours. He brings it up while arguing that such stories shape how people see beings from elsewhere.
binary-dead-star-drives-the-great-year-a: The claim is that our sun has a dead companion star, and that this hidden partner is the "entire reason why the great year exists," the Great Year being a long cosmic cycle, and "why we have resets of civilizations." A researcher named Matt LaCroix puts this forward on the show without naming a source. He credits a 1987 reference book, the New Science Encyclopedia, says the American space agency NASA has covered it up, and adds that the cycle shows up in ice cores from Antarctica and Greenland and that the companion is coming close now: "we're right in it right now."
biologics-as-soft-tissue-drones-in-consc: The living beings said to be found with crashed craft, often called 'biologics', may not be pilots at all but something like soft-tissue drones serving a conscious craft. Jake Barber, a helicopter pilot who says he lifted a UFO with his helicopter, puts it forward on Michels's show in 2025, passing on what he was told by a man he names only as Dave. If true, the bodies would be tools of the craft rather than its crew.
biondi-and-malanga-s-2022-sar-claim-of-e: In 2022, the Italian radar specialist Filippo Biondi and his engineering colleague Corrado Malanga said that satellite radar scans showed eight hollow tube-shaped structures, about 20 meters wide, deep beneath the Khafre pyramid, the second of the great pyramids at Giza in Egypt. Michels tells this himself, calling it "one of the boldest claims in the last century" in ancient archaeology, and in a later episode gives the size and the pyramid. If it held up, it would make the questions of how and why the pyramids were built far stranger.
biondi-s-patents-on-the-method-a-second-: A researcher named Filippo Biondi, who claims to have found a huge energy grid beneath the pyramids of Egypt, says he holds a patent on the method he uses. He tells Michels he is now submitting a second patent, which is being filed in the United States. He speaks of it as his own work, and it would mean his method is being formally protected.
bishop-carl-stanley-tips-the-fbi-about-f: In 1963, a bishop from Kentucky named Carl Stanley is said to have told the FBI, the US federal police, to look at two men in New Orleans, David Ferrie and Jack Martin, because they were involved in the assassination of President Kennedy. The researcher Peter Levenda tells it on Michels's show without naming a source, as part of a wider story about hidden hands behind world events.
bishop-mcintyre-at-edwards-afb-in-1954-d: A churchman known as Bishop McIntyre is said to have been hanging around Edwards Air Force Base in California in 1954. That is the year President Dwight D. Eisenhower is rumoured to have made a secret deal with aliens there. Michels tells it himself and says, unlike the MJ-12 papers, a disputed set of documents said to describe a secret UFO panel, this comes from real records, which he does not name.
bismuth-magnesium-layers-could-shrink-te: A metal piece made of thin layers of bismuth and magnesium, said to come from the 1947 Roswell crash in New Mexico, contains tiny channels for guiding waves, far smaller than the waves themselves. The physicist Hal Puthoff says he checked the piece himself and found these miniaturized channels, which he calls quite an accomplishment. Jesse Michels, relaying what Puthoff told him, adds that the material could shrink such channels for terahertz waves, a very high radio frequency, though Puthoff in his own telling does not mention terahertz.
bismuth-magnesium-sample-said-to-be-from: A tiny piece of metal made of thin layers of bismuth and magnesium is said to come from Roswell, New Mexico, where some say a UFO crashed in 1947: Jesse Michels, passing on what the physicist Hal Puthoff told him, says an army officer found it in his grandfather's archives, with a diary note calling it a piece from Roswell, though Puthoff himself says it was sent anonymously by someone claiming to be an army officer, and in one telling Michels has the grandfather as a colonel in the Roswell cleanup who left it in a safe. Michels says he saw the piece himself with the Stanford scientist Garry Nolan, who keeps it in his lab and got it by way of a researcher named Jacques Vallée. Michels adds that the bismuth layers are thinner than a human hair, that nobody could find evidence of anyone ever making such a thing, and he guesses it might allow magnetic levitation, which would point to a vehicle not made by any known maker.
bismuth-recurring-at-s4-1988: Bismuth, a heavy metal, keeps coming up in UFO stories, and Michels says there is a reason a man named Bob Lazar kept hearing about it at S4, a secret site in Nevada where Lazar says he worked in the late 1980s. Michels tells this himself in two episodes; in the second he speaks of bismuth in UFO lore in general and does not name S4. He brings it up because, if true, the metal may have a real part in how such craft are said to work.
bissell-mentions-the-1933-magenta-crash: In June 1933 a disc-shaped craft, about 10 to 12 meters across, is said to have crashed near Magenta in Lombardy, northern Italy, and been taken by Benito Mussolini's Fascist government. The fullest source is David Grusch, a former US intelligence officer turned whistleblower, who says it was "the first recovery in Europe," that the craft was partly intact, and that Italy kept it at a secure air base until 1944 or 1945. Harold Malmgren, a former presidential advisor, says he heard of it from Richard Bissell, a senior CIA official whom Michels calls the agency's number two and the founder of Area 51, the secret Nevada base, and that Bissell told him "this didn't start last week. He mentioned 1933 Magenta." Michels returns to it often, adding a news blackout, telegrams from the Stefani news agency, and the claim that the craft went through the Vatican to the United States under President Franklin Roosevelt, though once he calls it hypothetical and once he places it near Bologna. Robert Salas, a former Air Force officer, says a new book by an Italian researcher named Roberto Pinotti documents it, and that Mussolini put Guglielmo Marconi, the inventor of radio, in charge of studying the craft. Other guests, such as Jay Anderson, mention it only in passing, crediting Grusch. If true, it would mean governments were recovering such craft well before the Second World War.
bissell-places-area-51-at-the-nevada-nuc: The CIA official Richard Bissell is said to have founded Area 51, the secret Nevada air base, in 1955 and to have placed it on purpose at the Nevada Test Site, where hundreds of atomic bomb tests were happening in the early 1950s. Michels tells this himself, citing Bissell, in an episode with a former presidential advisor named Harald Malmgren. The point is that the bomb tests made the area an ideal cover for keeping secrets.
bissell-returns-to-the-cia-after-his-ous: Richard Bissell, a senior official at the CIA, the US spy agency, was pushed out in 1961, but the rumour is that he left work on a Friday and was back on the Monday because he was too indispensable to certain activities. Michels repeats this as a rumour, without naming a source, as a hint that Bissell was tied to secret work that could not do without him.
black-ball-darting-around-the-security-t: In 1977 a black ball "about six times the size of a beach ball", which looked as if it had vents on it, darted around a security truck at a nuclear missile launch site near Nisland, South Dakota. A former missile security guard named Mario Woods says he was there and saw it, and in both tellings he names a man called Michael Johnson. In a later telling Woods gives its size as four to six feet across.
black-ball-of-no-light-formed-by-the-emi: At a secret Nevada site called S4, sometime between 1987 and 1989, a device Bob Lazar calls an emitter is said to have made "a little black ball in the air where no light was escaping, looking like a little black hole." Lazar, who says he worked on alien craft there, tells it firsthand and names a coworker, Barry Castilio, as part of the scene. In one telling he adds that the emitter was rotated to make the ball, which would mean the device could bend space or light.
black-sites-staffed-by-refugees-who-didn: Secret government facilities, often called black sites, are said to be run day to day by refugees from other countries who applied for resettlement under what he calls P3, a refugee category, and were turned down. They are kept on instead as janitors, cooks and maintenance staff. This comes from Michael Herrera, a former Marine who says he saw a huge craft in the Indonesian jungle, repeating what someone told him, and it would mean these hidden places keep their secrets by using workers with nowhere else to go.
black-suvs-helicopters-and-a-30-ft-hole-: In 1999, near Hart Canyon outside Aztec, New Mexico, where a craft carrying alien bodies is said to have crashed long ago, there were black SUVs and helicopters, and a large hole in the ground, according to Brett Lanner, who was there. Lanner says they came across a round hole about 30 feet deep and 30 feet across, which he takes as a sign that someone was still digging at the crash site.
black-widow-night-fighters-redeployed-to: In 1947, the story goes, the military sent the Black Widow, a night fighter plane from World War II, to patrol the skies around Roswell, New Mexico. The researcher John Brandenburg tells it as something he found out himself, and he credits a set of documents he calls Cosmic Awakening. If true, it would mean the military was watching the night sky over Roswell closely that year.
blacked-out-blue-van-to-an-underground-t: Between 1990 and 1993, Dan Sherman, an Air Force sergeant who says the National Security Agency, the US agency that intercepts communications, hired him to talk to aliens, says he was driven from a facility in Maryland near the agency's complex to an underground training school. He says the ride was in an unmarked blue van with blacked-out windows, and he names a Captain White as part of his account.
blacked-out-bus-ride-south-to-s-4-1988: Around 1988 and 1989, workers were driven from Area 51, the secret Air Force test base in Nevada, south to a hidden site called S-4 on a bus whose windows were blacked out, over a "long bumpy ride". Bob Lazar, who says he worked on alien craft at S-4, describes the trip from his own experience. The blacked-out windows, as he tells it, kept workers from knowing exactly where they were going.
blacker-than-black-floating-sphere: A soldier is said to have been brought into a room and shown a floating sphere "blacker than black" that gave off "a sense of just complete evil and darkness." A congressman named Eric Burlison tells this on the show, passing on what the man himself told him. In Burlison's telling the man served in special forces and saw the hovering black sphere while in the field overseas during the wars; if true, it would mean soldiers have met something that felt actively hostile.
blacker-than-black-holes-above-the-insul: Between 1988 and 1989, at a secret Nevada site called S-4, Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft there, says he saw holes above a part of a craft he calls the insulator ring that were blacker than black. He tells it firsthand: they "almost look like bottomless pits in there. But I know they're solid," and he names a coworker, Barry, as being there.
blackhawk-near-miss-with-low-flying-f-4-: While flying in a Blackhawk, a US military helicopter, over Germany near the Rhine River valley, a NASA doctor named Greg Rogers says his crew nearly crashed because of an F-4 Phantom, a fighter jet, flying low across their path. Rogers, who was aboard, puts it bluntly: "we nearly died because of what that F4 pilot had done."
blanchard-boy-did-we-screw-up-1947: Colonel Blanchard, the commander at Roswell Army Air Field in New Mexico, the base at the centre of the 1947 claim that a crashed flying saucer was recovered, is said to have laughed later about the affair and said, "Boy, did we screw up." The physicist John Brandenburg tells this in 2025, passing on what he says came from Blanchard and from Roswell veterans. To him it suggests that the base's handling of the event, not the event itself, was the mistake.
bledsoe-and-grusch-videos-throttled-on-y: Two interviews about UFOs were held back on YouTube even though, by one insider's account, neither broke any rules. The podcaster Danny Jones says a Google representative told him that his own video with Chris Bledsoe, a man who says he has UFO encounters, and Jesse Michels's video with David Grusch, a former intelligence officer turned whistleblower, showed no rule breaks or internal red flags the representative could find. Jones tells it to suggest the videos were held back for reasons other than the platform's rules.
bledsoe-drawing-cell-diagrams-for-taylor: Chris Bledsoe, a carpenter from North Carolina who says UFOs appear around him, says that between 2008 and 2011 he worked for a research team led by a man named Timothy Taylor. He says they sent him scientific papers to read at night, and his job was to draw whatever came out of him, including diagrams of cells. He also names Diana Pasulka, a scholar who studies the subject, in telling it.
bledsoe-group-films-moving-dots-weeks-la: A congressman named Eric Burlison says that a group around a man named Chris Bledsoe went back to the lawn of the US Capitol in Washington a few weeks after an outing Burlison had joined. They did "the exact same thing" without him and, he says, this time they filmed dots moving in the sky. Burlison repeats what the group told him, and he tells it as a sign that whatever they saw the first time came back.
bledsoe-memoir-names-taylor-as-a-nasa-in: A man named Chris Bledsoe, who describes many encounters with beings he calls otherworldly, wrote a memoir that openly names a man called Timothy Taylor as an insider at NASA, the US space agency, who befriended him after those encounters. Michels says this himself to back up another person's account of Taylor. It matters because it would place a space agency figure close to people who report such contact.
bledsoe-prophecy-of-missiles-fired-at-ir: Chris Bledsoe, a man who says he has had UFO encounters for years and meets a being he calls the Lady, says she warned him in 2012 about missiles in the future, and that he wrote in his book UFO of God of a time "when Iran and Israel began to exchange missiles at one another." He says the sign of the moment will be when the blue star Regulus appears red on the horizon at dawn, in the gaze of the Sphinx at Giza. Bob McGwier, an engineer described as a CIA contractor, retells it second-hand from Bledsoe as a vision of missiles fired at Iran and stopped by these beings, a version that has a 2026 date Bledsoe himself does not give.
bledsoe-s-craft-bigger-inside-than-outsi: A craft seen in North Carolina is said to have been about 30 feet across on the outside, but when the man looked inside, it seemed as big as a football field. The story belongs to Chris Bledsoe, a man known for repeated UFO experiences, and it is passed on by the UFO researcher Grant Cameron, who repeats what Bledsoe tells. If true, it would mean the craft holds more space inside than its outer size allows.
bledsoe-told-that-rockets-fail-because-t: Chris Bledsoe, a man who says UFOs show up around him, was reportedly told around 2007 that rocket launches go wrong because they carry weapons. The YouTuber Chris Ramsay tells it from Bledsoe: someone asked whether there were weapons on the rockets, was told yes, and answered that this is why they fail, because 'they' do not want them to work. Bledsoe tells it himself in 2026 a little differently, crediting a man named Timothy Taylor and saying that every weapon-carrying launch draws the craft up to look at it.
bledsoe-tries-to-call-in-uap-on-capitol-: In the 2020s a man named Chris Bledsoe, who says he can call in unexplained craft, tried to summon some on the lawn of the US Capitol in Washington DC. A US congressman named Eric Burlison says he was there: Bledsoe "did his thing", while Burlison "politely quietly sat and waited". UAP is the official term for unexplained objects in the sky.
blessed-animal-bladders-hung-on-the-fenc: In 2016, Native Americans are said to have been hanging animal bladders along the fence at the edge of Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property known for reports of strange events, and blessing them. Brandon Fugal, the ranch's owner, tells it and credits the account to the security guards from the time of Bigelow, an earlier owner, as if the bladders were meant to guard against something on the land.
blink-182-bandmate-had-intelligence-comm: Another member of the rock band Blink-182, besides the guitarist Tom DeLonge, who went on to work on UFO projects, had relatives in the US intelligence agencies. The researcher Jay Anderson brings this up on the show as something he was told, hinting that the band's link to the UFO world may run deeper than DeLonge alone.
blitch-backs-randy-anderson-s-crane-stor: A scientist named John Blitch, who worked for the Pentagon's advanced research agency, says he believes "every aspect" of a story told by a man named Randy Anderson about Crane, a Navy weapons research site in Indiana. Blitch came to hear it after being introduced through David Grusch, a former intelligence officer. Blitch does not retell the story's details here, but his word matters because he is vouching for Anderson as someone he has heard firsthand.
blitch-has-been-inside-several-undergrou: A scientist named John Blitch, who worked at DARPA, the Pentagon's agency for advanced research, and who says he was abducted by an alien, says he has been inside several underground military facilities. He mentions this in passing as something he saw himself, without saying where or when.
blitch-s-brief-saic-tenure-never-read-in: John Blitch, a former scientist at DARPA, the Pentagon's advanced research agency, who says he was abducted by an alien, says that in 2001 he worked briefly at SAIC, a large defense contractor, in Littleton, Colorado. He says he was never "read in", meaning never cleared into any secret program there, and he names a man called Art Morris in the account.
blitch-vets-barber-s-four-man-team-on-hi: Around 2024 or 2025, a scientist named John Blitch, who worked for the Pentagon's advanced research agency, brought a helicopter pilot named Jake Barber and Barber's four-man team onto his boat to vet their story about retrieving crashed craft. Blitch tells it himself and says he "was looking for inconsistencies between those folks", to see whether their accounts held together.
blog-post-predicting-that-within-a-decad: Within about ten years, humanity will admit that we are not the only intelligent, even super intelligent, life on this planet. That is the prediction Deep Prasad, a young researcher, says he set down in a blog post called Curiosity as a Time Capsule, and he repeats it to Jesse Michels in 2022. If he is right, such an admission would come by around 2032.
blood-on-pillow-after-1988-camping-trip: After a camping trip in 1988, a former nuclear missile guard named Richard Barth woke up to find blood on his pillow. Michels raises it with Barth himself, repeating what Barth had told him earlier, in an episode about Barth's account of being taken by aliens. The point is that the blood could be a physical trace of an abduction.
blown-out-of-a-special-electronics-helic: In 1967 near Pleiku, in Vietnam, a special electronics helicopter is said to have been hit "right in the belly" by an RPG, a shoulder-fired rocket-propelled grenade, and blown up, throwing out the soldier Joe McMoneagle. McMoneagle tells it firsthand, as part of his own life story before the work he later describes on Michels's show.
blue-beings-appearing-at-joe-dispenza-s-: A meditation teacher named Joe Dispenza is said to report that during his deep meditations, blue beings show up in the room at his retreats. They tell him the people at the gathering need to "vibrate higher" before the beings can fully appear and heal them. Michels passes this on as something Dispenza says, in a conversation with a guest named Jeffrey Mishlove, who holds a PhD.
blue-book-closed-in-1969-citing-condon: The US Air Force shut down Project Blue Book, its study of UFO reports from the 1950s and 60s, in 1969, and pointed to a university study to justify it. Robert Salas, a former Air Force officer, tells Michels that when the Air Force got out in 1969 "they even quoted the Condon investigation," meaning the Scientific Study of Unidentified Flying Objects, a report led by the physicist Edward Condon and published by the University of Colorado on 31 October 1968. The researcher Bryce Zabel tells it without Condon, as the Air Force "holding the line" and saying "we're washing our hands of that." The Condon report itself concludes that "further extensive study of UFOs probably cannot be justified in the expectation that science will be advanced thereby," and that defence needs could be met "without the continuance of a special unit such as Project Blue Book." An Air Force fact sheet from January 1985 states that "on December 17, 1969, the Secretary of the Air Force announced the termination of Project BLUE BOOK," and that the decision rested on the Colorado report, a review of it by the National Academy of Sciences, and past Air Force experience. To the tellers, it marks the moment the government publicly stepped away from the subject.
blue-book-heads-grow-increasingly-anti-u: Every head of Blue Book, the US Air Force's UFO study of the 1950s and 60s, became more and more hostile to UFOs from 1952 until the study ended in 1969. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source; in a later episode he puts it more strongly, saying the Air Force used Blue Book to push the subject to the margins. If true, it would mean the official study was steered toward dismissing UFOs rather than examining them.
blue-book-kecksburg-material-sent-to-pro: Files from Project Blue Book, the US Air Force's UFO study of the 1950s and 60s, are said to show that material from a 1965 incident at Kecksburg, Pennsylvania, where something was reported to come down, was sent to a project code-named Greengrass. The UFO researcher Grant Cameron says he read one document saying so, looked the name up, and found it pointed to Mount Weather, a government site in Virginia. If true, it would tie the Kecksburg case to a secure government facility.
blue-book-landing-case-with-an-alien-foo: Among the files of Project Blue Book, the US Air Force's UFO study of the 1950s and 60s, now kept at the National Archives, there is said to be a landing case where the first military officer to arrive drew a diagram of the alien's footprints. This comes from James Fox, a UFO investigator who says he went through the files himself. To Fox, it shows that the military took landings seriously enough to record the physical traces.
blue-book-s-robert-friend-sees-the-chann: In 1959, Robert Friend, then head of Blue Book, the US Air Force's UFO study of the 1950s and 60s, was shown a session in Washington where a person claimed to be receiving messages from beings in space, and the government photo analyst Arthur Lundahl was also named in the affair. When Friend tried to follow it up, a general told him another agency had it and to keep his hands off, and nothing more was heard. The UFO researcher Grant Cameron tells this, crediting an 11-page memo about a meeting on July 9, 1959, and it would mean some other agency, not the Air Force, was quietly handling the subject.
blue-book-special-report-14-contradicts-: A 1950s Air Force study called Special Report 14, part of Blue Book, the US Air Force's UFO study of the 1950s and 60s, is said to tell a different story in its numbers than in the press release that went out with it. A researcher on the show, whose name is not given, says that if you look at the report's own data table, something like 21 percent of almost a thousand cases were left as unknown. He credits the point to the UFO researcher Stanton Friedman, and tells it to suggest the public was given a more reassuring picture than the Air Force's own data showed.
blue-dwarfs-drag-a-man-behind-a-curtain-: In the 1970s, in a shop in Manhattan near West 55th Street, between 7th Avenue and Broadway, a man in a brown suit was dragged back behind a curtain by small blue beings, according to the writer Whitley Strieber, who is known for describing his own encounters with visitors. Strieber says he saw it himself at what he calls the "horror store," with the man trying to get out while the blue dwarfs pulled him back, and he names his wife Anne Strieber in the telling.
blue-energy-humanoid-takes-rossi-in-his-: Dave Rossi, a man who says aliens taught him advanced physics, says that in 2021, at his home, he was taken in his sleep by a humanoid figure made of something like blue energy. He tells it in nearly the same words on two different episodes, though the second time he gives no date or place.
blue-extraterrestrial-manifesting-physic: In a series of seances held in the 1990s in the English village of Scole, known as the Scole experiment, a blue extraterrestrial being is said to have appeared in solid form, so solid that a sitter could touch it. The researcher Jeffrey Mishlove tells this on the show, passing on what a man named Robin Foy, who sat in those seances, told him. If true, it would tie contact with beings from elsewhere to the world of spirit mediums.
blue-winged-angel-uap-over-barber-s-hous: Over the home of a helicopter pilot named Jake Barber, an unexplained object he and his family call "the angel" keeps appearing: it is blue, seems to have wings, materializes, hangs over the house where neighbours see it, and then "shoots into outer space". Barber tells this himself on two episodes, once mentioning his son. Michels repeats it second-hand and links it to Barber's crash-retrieval work, and one telling places the house with the scientist John Blitch instead.
bluegill-recovery-of-spherical-debris-in: In October 1962, during an American nuclear test called Bluegill Triple Prime, a warhead set off high over Johnston Atoll in the Pacific, an unknown object is said to have been knocked out of the sky and partly recovered by the US Navy. If true, it would mean the government shot down and kept a UFO in the early 1960s. The main source is Harold Malmgren, an adviser to four presidents, who tells the show himself that a test report described the blast knocking down a device that had been following the missile, that "the Navy had recovered" it, and that he later went to Albuquerque and held pieces of it. A former Senate staffer, Kurt McConnell, says Malmgren heard it directly from Richard Bissell, the number two at the CIA, who told him "we downed a UFO that was monitoring closely monitoring that test and it tumbled into the ocean." A researcher named Jeff Cruickshank wrote a report studying the ships' deck logs, the daily records kept on board, and a retired Navy admiral, Tim Gallaudet, who worked on it with him, says they point to "some partial recovery of either that object or something related to it." McConnell says the logs mention highly radioactive debris, one piece "described as a black sphere" and another as "a green tube." The journalist Ross Coulthart cites an analysis by Douglas Dean Johnson that he says backs Malmgren, and Michels adds that people on the ground at the time widely rumoured a UFO shootdown.
bluegill-triple-prime-as-a-proto-sdi-x-r: Bluegill Triple Prime, an American project of 1962 and 1963, was an early version of the Strategic Defense Initiative, the later US plan to shoot down missiles, here using X-rays as a missile defense. Michels makes this link himself, drawing on a paper by the RAND Corporation, a research group that works for the US government, and on a man named Harold Malmgren, whom he had interviewed. If true, the idea of that kind of defense would be decades older than the public plan.
bluegill-triple-prime-as-missile-defense: Bluegill Triple Prime was a 1962 nuclear test set off high above the Pacific, and the claim is that it was really a defense against Russian long-range nuclear missiles, an early version of the 1980s American plan for missile defense in space. Jesse Michels repeats this from his guest Malmgren, billed in the episode's title as a CIA chief, who ties it to a paper from the RAND Corporation and to work at the Institute for Defense Analysis, both American defense research groups.
bluegill-triple-prime-led-to-excalibur-a: A 1962 American nuclear test high in the atmosphere, called Bluegill Triple Prime, is said to lead straight to President Ronald Reagan's 1980s space weapons plan, nicknamed Star Wars and formally the Strategic Defense Initiative, and that plan is said to have been really about shooting down UFOs. Michels draws the link himself, naming the physicist Edward Teller and Reagan. In a later episode he credits the claim to Harald Malmgren, a former presidential advisor, saying "Harold apparently said that this whole thing was actually devised to take down UFOs." A researcher who goes by the online name UAPGerb makes a similar case without the Bluegill link. He argues that from 1983 parts of the Reagan plan, a lethality and target hardening program and a particle beam weapons program, were meant to be space-based microwave weapons "to shoot down UFOs."
bluegill-triple-prime-object-tumbles-fro: When the United States set off a nuclear warhead high above Johnston Atoll in the Pacific in 1962, in a test called Bluegill Triple Prime, an unknown object is said to have come tumbling out of the fireball, and it was caught on film. If true, a UFO was close enough to a nuclear blast to be knocked down by it. Michels tells it often, crediting the researcher Jeff Cruickshank: according to many on the ship watching the test, "a bright fiery object tumbled out from the plume of the blast." He says it can be seen in footage shot from two aircraft called Kettle 1 and Kettle 2, filmed by the contractor EG&G, that the footage still exists, and that a cleaned-up version has a white triangle laid over the object. He also cites a report from the Flight Dynamics Laboratory at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, Navy ship logs, the presidential adviser Harold Malmgren, and the retired admiral Tim Gallaudet, and mentions a rumour that the debris went to Sandia Labs, a weapons laboratory. A former Senate staffer, Kurt McConnell, describes the declassified film himself: "as soon as that fireball erupts, you see this object come tumbling out of the fireball" heading for the ocean, and he credits the Los Alamos and Lawrence Livermore weapons labs.
bluegill-video-sanitized-with-superimpos: Film of Bluegill Triple Prime, a 1962 American nuclear test over Johnston Atoll in the Pacific, is said to have been censored later by putting a white triangle over a UFO in the footage. Michels relays this from a researcher named Jeff Cruickshank, and in another episode he dates it to a 1998 declassification review, saying the Defense Special Weapons Agency, a Pentagon office led by Dr. Byron L. Ristvet, "applied a large white triangle to the footage". If true, it would mean the government hid a UFO seen during a nuclear test.
bob-baker-mitre-paper-on-ning-li-s-ac-dc: A researcher named Bob Baker is said to have written a paper, under the MITRE Corporation, a US research company that works for the government, about the physicist Ning Li's idea of 'AC/DC gravity', a way of producing gravity-like effects. Dave Rossi, a guest who says he learned advanced physics from aliens, mentions it in 2025, saying it was presented at one of the conferences on high-frequency gravitational waves in the 2000s. He raises it as a sign that serious institutions looked at gravity control.
bob-ballard-s-search-for-atlantis: The lost city of Atlantis is now said by some to lie in the Red Sea, and the ocean explorer Bob Ballard, a consultant to a navy school who works at an institute in Connecticut, has been involved in looking for it. John S. Herrington, the US Secretary of Energy, mentions this on the show as something he has heard, as part of a wider talk about hidden history.
bob-beck-at-ossining-during-the-space-ki: In the 1970s a man named Bob Beck was present at Ossining, New York, at the very time of experiments with children that the teller calls the "space kids". An unnamed researcher on the show says this, without naming a source, and adds that Beck was "most certainly CIA", the US foreign intelligence agency, which would tie the agency to those experiments.
bob-beckwith-philadelphia-experiment-and: An engineer named Robert Beckwith is said to have been somewhat involved in the Philadelphia Experiment, a rumoured US Navy experiment of the 1940s, and later to have done work with extremely strong magnetic fields and with teleportation. Michels raises this himself, hedging that he only thinks this is what Beckwith claims, while talking with a guest named Dave Rossi. If true, it would mean secret wartime research went on into moving matter in exotic ways.
bob-brier-s-examination-suggests-tutankh: Tutankhamun, the boy king of ancient Egypt, may have died from a blow to the back of the head, according to an examination of his body by a scholar named Bob Brier, perhaps in the 1990s. The researcher Luke Caverns passes it on from Brier's work: the way the blood pooled at the back of the skull looked, he says, like the king had been hit there. If so, the king may have been killed rather than dying of natural causes.
bob-jahn-from-boeing-plasma-physics-to-t: A plasma physicist named Bob Jahn, who had worked at the aircraft maker Boeing, went on to run the PEAR lab at Princeton University, which Michels describes as a parapsychology lab, studying things like the mind's effect on matter. Michels brings it up himself, without a source, to show a serious physicist moving from aerospace into the study of the paranormal.
bob-jahn-s-random-event-generator-resear: The story is that at Princeton, starting around 1979, an engineering dean named Bob Jahn ran a lab called the Princeton Engineering Anomalies Research lab, which tested whether people could nudge random event generators (machines that spit out random results) just by willing it, and that the Navy took an interest. Michels brings it up several times, once dating the lab to 1978, crediting a researcher named Dean Radin with decades of similar work, and once citing a book by a researcher named Herb Metts; Metts himself, on an earlier episode, says the lab's final chart, built with a researcher named Brenda Dunne and described in books like Margins of Reality, shows "pretty definitively" that subjects could do what they were asked. If true, it would mean the mind can affect matter in a measurable way.
bob-lazar-at-mit-possibly-placed-for-def: Bob Lazar, a man famous in UFO circles for his claims about secret government work, spent time at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology or at one of the defense research labs tied to it, Lincoln Labs or Draper, and he was put there on purpose for defense work. A researcher named Eric Weinstein offers this as a guess: "my sense is he was put there to work on um something defense related," and he places it in the early 1990s. Lazar himself, speaking to Jesse Michels, says it flatly, "I was sent there," and puts it before 1988. If true, it would mean Lazar was quietly placed inside the defense research world.
bob-lazar-at-s4-1989: A man named Bob Lazar says that in 1989 he worked on an actual alien craft at S4, a secret site in the Nevada desert. Michels brings him up himself, saying Lazar is the only person who has claimed to have worked hands-on with a craft. That would make him a rare inside witness to the government studying alien technology.
bob-lazar-briefed-on-project-looking-gla: A man named Bob Lazar, who says he worked at a secret site in Nevada, was briefed on Project Looking Glass, a programme Michels names but does not describe. Michels says this himself twice in one episode, citing Lazar and a man named Timothy Taylor, and once places it in Nevada in 1988 and 1989. If true, it would tie Lazar to a second secret programme beyond the one he is known for.
bob-lazar-on-parallel-engineering: What happens at secret US sites may not really be the copying of captured alien craft, which is called reverse engineering. It may be closer to "parallel engineering", building something alongside them. Michels says this is what Bob Lazar tells you if you go deep enough with him. Lazar is a man who says he worked on alien craft at a secret site in Nevada. Michels links the idea to the musician Tom DeLonge and his book series Sekret Machines.
bob-lazar-s-claim-of-reverse-engineering: A man named Bob Lazar says that in the late 1980s he worked at S4, a secret site just south of Area 51, a secret military base in the Nevada desert, taking apart the propulsion of "a craft that was not made by human hands"; Jesse Michels retells this often, saying Lazar went public on television in 1989, got the job through the physicist Edward Teller, was flown in on unmarked planes and counted nine alien craft there, with the dates given variously as 1987 or 1988 to 1989. The podcaster Joe Rogan also recalls Lazar describing craft that bend gravity around themselves, and Michels says Lazar "for sure worked at Area 51, probably worked at S4." If true, it would mean the US government holds and studies craft from somewhere else.
bob-lazar-s-sport-model-grown-out-of-the: Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft at a secret Nevada site he calls S-4, is said to have described one craft, which he called the sport model, as if it had been grown out of the vacuum of empty space itself. The Navy scientist Salvatore Pais, who holds patents on unusual craft designs, repeats this, and in a second version remembers Lazar's words as the craft being like something 3D printed in our spacetime, placing it at S-4 in 1989. Pais says this is exactly what his own equation for a single unifying force describes, so to him Lazar's account fits his physics.
bob-lazar-walks-underneath-the-craft-198: Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on reverse-engineering alien spacecraft at a secret site in Nevada called S-4 in 1989, tells of walking underneath one of the craft. Michels only raises the moment as a question to his guest, the UFO researcher Grant Cameron, asking what happened when Lazar walked under it. If true, it would mean the government held a real craft of non-human origin.
bob-maguire-measures-his-girlfriend-s-im: A man named Bob McGwier, described in his episode's title as a CIA contractor, says his girlfriend has an implant in her head that gives off radio signals he can measure. He tells it himself: he says he has a video online of moving a field meter, a device that picks up radio waves, across her head and "watching that implant pulse RF transmissions," meaning radio-frequency signals. Michels repeats the story on a later episode with the writer Whitley Strieber, calling him Bob Maguire. In that version Michels says McGwier put an RF detector over her head and could measure the frequency coming out. So one telling comes from the man who did it and the other is the host passing it on. It is told because an implant that sends signals would point to someone deliberately tracking or affecting her.
bob-s-letter-from-nixon-thanking-him-for: In the 1970s, a man in Los Angeles known only as Bob is said to have received a letter from President Richard Nixon that read, "Thank you for your cooperation on the project we're working on." The UFO researcher Grant Cameron, who says he knew of it at first hand, says this letter is what made Bob controversial, since it would suggest the president was tied to whatever secret project Bob was part of.
bobby-fischer-s-claim-that-russian-parap: The chess world champion Bobby Fischer is said to have complained that during his matches in the 1970s the Russians brought in gurus, Russian parapsychologists who studied mind powers, to interfere with his play. The surgeon Italo Venturelli passes this on in 2026, telling listeners to look it up. If true, it would mean the Soviets tried to use mental influence in a world championship.
bobby-ray-inman-acknowledges-the-nationa: Bobby Ray Inman, a former top US intelligence official, is said to have mentioned a National Underwater (or Undersea) Reconnaissance Office, and in doing so to have treated it as a real organisation. Tim Gallaudet, a retired Navy admiral who was the Navy's chief oceanographer, relays this from the researcher Sam Gerbus, and says that despite his access to classified undersea programmes he had never heard of such an office. If true, it would mean a secret agency watching the oceans exists even beyond the knowledge of the Navy's own top ocean expert.
bobby-ray-inman-refers-bob-oechsler-to-s: Around 1988 or 1989, Bobby Ray Inman, a former head of the National Security Agency, the US code-breaking and eavesdropping agency, is said to have spoken by phone with a UFO researcher named Bob Oechsler and pointed him to a naval intelligence director named Sumar Shapiro and to a man named R. Evans Hineman. A researcher who goes by UAPGerb tells the referral without naming a source, and Michels, who plays parts of the recording on several episodes, has Inman saying of recovered craft, "10 years ago the answer would have been no," and that "as time has evolved, they're beginning to become more open on it is a possibility." Michels hears this as Inman all but admitting the US holds UFOs, which would mean a top intelligence man knew of them.
