bobby-ray-inman-tape-recorded-at-the-ida: A tape exists, says the researcher Grant Cameron, of a man named Bobby Ray Inman being asked questions about UFOs, and it was recorded at the Institute for Defense Analyses, a US defence research organisation. Cameron mentions it in passing as one of the things that taught him a lot, without saying who made the tape. If true, it would place a candid conversation on the subject inside a defence research setting.
boebert-asks-about-hybrid-program-at-hea: At a congressional hearing on UFOs in the 2020s, a member of Congress named Lauren Boebert asked about hybrids, meaning a programme involving human-alien hybrids. Michels recalls it himself, laughing, as "just a really weird moment in the congressional testimony."
bondi-and-negative-mass-at-the-1957-chap: At a 1957 physics conference in Chapel Hill, North Carolina, the meeting Jesse Michels credits with founding the study of quantum gravity, an Austrian mathematician named Hermann Bondi gave a talk on negative mass in general relativity: matter with a minus sign that would push against gravity rather than fall with it. Michels says he got this from the mathematician Eric Weinstein, who frames Bondi's point as a question about whether mass must always be positive, and Michels says he has the conference report, The Role of Gravitation in Physics, which has a chapter on the talk. He raises it as a hint that serious physicists looked at antigravity long ago.
bones-on-religion-humans-and-aliens-part: A contact Dan Sherman calls Bones once told him that humans and aliens are part of the same creation. Sherman is a former Army sergeant who says the National Security Agency, the US spy agency that intercepts communications, hired him to speak with aliens. He says this happened while he was posted at a site he calls Base 2, sometime between 1990 and 1993. If it is true, it would put people and visitors under one shared origin, which bears on religion.
bonnybridge-ufo-hotspot-and-stepfather-s: Bonnybridge, a place in Scotland near the town of Falkirk, is described as a Scottish UFO hotspot with so many sightings that it is "almost like a tourist attraction," where people go to see UFOs. The computer hacker Gary McKinnon tells this as something passed on by his stepfather, who lived near Bonnybridge and had sightings of his own there.
book-of-enoch-cut-from-the-tanakh: The Book of Enoch, an ancient religious text first found in Ethiopia, was once part of the Tanakh, the Hebrew Bible, and was later cut out of it. That is the claim of the researcher and philosopher Jason Jorjani, who gives it as his own summary without naming a source. He says the book keeps a "backstory" that the shorter account in Genesis 6 leaves out. If he is right, it would mean a key part of the old story was deliberately removed from the scriptures.
book-of-enoch-excluded-but-holding-truth: The Book of Enoch is an ancient religious text, known in English through a translation by R. H. Charles, that was left out of the Bible. The claim is that Catholic teaching holds it still contains truth. Dylan Borland, who appeared on the show to talk about what officials told him of aliens, passes this on from the Catholic priest and writer Malachi Martin, whom Borland calls one of the first people to read the Dead Sea Scrolls, the ancient manuscripts found in caves near the Dead Sea.
book-of-enoch-watchers-mating-with-human: In the Book of Enoch, an ancient Jewish religious text left out of most Bibles, heavenly beings called the Watchers come down to earth, take human wives, and father a race of giants. Michels raises it himself as background: the Watchers "mated" and "there were giants in the earth in those days." The broadcaster Joe Rogan repeats it as something he heard from Anna Paulina Luna, saying the Watchers "came down and bred with men and created the Nephilim," the name for those offspring, and he reads it as a memory of genetic engineering. A researcher named Tim Alberino says the Watchers' first sin was lust, that "they lusted after the daughters of men," and ties this to the sixth chapter of Genesis, while a guest named Jay Anderson leaves out the mating and the giants and only places the Watchers' descent on Mount Hermon in Lebanon. The Book of Enoch, in R. H. Charles's English translation, tells it in Enoch's own voice: the angels "saw and lusted after them," two hundred of them came down "in the days of Jared on the summit of Mount Hermon," taught their wives "charms and enchantments," and the women "bare great giants." The King James Bible, published in 1611, gives a shorter version in Genesis 6, where "the sons of God" took wives of "the daughters of men" and "there were giants in the earth in those days." Genesis does not call them Watchers or angels, give their number, or name Mount Hermon: those details come only from the Book of Enoch. People tell the story because, if it is true, beings from outside humanity once mixed their blood with ours.
book-of-job-as-a-deliberate-mithraic-kab: The idea is that the Book of Job in the Bible was written on purpose as a coded text mixing the worship of Mithra, an ancient Persian god, with Jewish mystical teaching, by the Magi, the priests of the Achaemenid Persian Empire who, he says, helped rebuild Israel in what he calls "the first Zionist project in history." A researcher named Jason Jorjani makes this argument on the show, drawing on his own book Iranian Leviathan, without naming other sources. If right, a central biblical book would have Persian priestly roots.
book-of-revelation-people-who-cannot-die: The Book of Revelation, the last book of the Christian Bible, is said to describe a time of disaster on earth when a group of people cannot die. Tim Alberino, a researcher who says giants were captured in Afghanistan, raises it himself from his reading of the text. He uses it to link ancient prophecy to the strange beings he talks about.
book-of-the-watchers-dated-to-around-300: The Book of the Watchers, the oldest section of the ancient Jewish text known as 1 Enoch, was written at least around 300 BC, according to the researcher Tim Alberino. He gives the date himself, without naming a source, to show how old the tale of the Watchers it contains really is, which matters to him because it means the story of beings called the Watchers is very ancient.
book-s-claim-of-alien-contact-at-bentwat: A book called Left at East Gate claims that in 1980 there was actual contact with aliens at RAF Bentwaters, a military air base in England, during a series of UFO sightings there. The UFO documentary maker James Fox brings the claim up and says the men who were at the base at the time, including Gordon Williams, Charles Halt, Jim Penniston and John Burroughs, dispute that any such contact took place.
book-that-foretold-the-texas-tower-snipe: A book described the Texas Tower sniper, a gunman who shot people from a tower in Texas in 1966, before it ever happened. The researcher Peter Levenda says so but does not name the book. He brings it up as an example of a story that seems to have seen the future.
boomerang-shaped-craft-over-tucson: A boomerang-shaped craft flew over Tucson, Arizona, in broad daylight, lower than the height planes use when circling to land at an airport. Eric W. Davis, introduced in the episode as a Pentagon scientist, says he and his wife saw it themselves. He brings it up as his own sighting, with no date given.
bootsie-galbraith-sees-a-ufo-called-in-b: A woman named Bootsie Galbraith was in Mexico with a man named Steven Greer when, she said, he called in a UFO and everyone there saw it. Whitley Strieber, who says he has met aliens himself, repeats what Galbraith told him. If true, it would mean someone could summon a craft on purpose in front of witnesses.
booze-fighters-take-over-hollister-steal: In 1947 a gang of World War veterans on motorcycles, who called themselves the Booze Fighters as a play on Foo Fighters, the wartime name for strange lights pilots saw, took over the town of Hollister, California for a day and threw a drunken party downtown. A guest named John Brandenburg tells this on the show, passing on what he was told, as an event that grabbed the newspaper headlines that year and pushed other stories aside.
borderland-society-knew-of-ufo-crashes-b: An occult research group from the 1940s, the Borderland Society, is said to have known about some UFO crashes before the US Army or Air Force did, and Michels says there are documents showing it. He tells this in four episodes, each time in his own words. In some he credits a researcher named Richard Geldreich with finding it, and the details shift: once it covers sightings as well as crashes, once the group learns of them through remote viewing (sensing far-off places with the mind) in the 1940s and 50s, and once it knew of crashes before they even happened. If true, a private group of mystics would have been ahead of the military on its own secrets.
borland-claims-first-hand-knowledge-of-c: A man named Dylan Borland says he has direct, first-hand knowledge of crash recovery, meaning the retrieval of downed craft that are not of human make. He says he has also seen the reverse engineering of that technology, how it was built into other systems, and its power source. He makes the claim in his own words in a clip shown on an episode with Jeremy Corbell, and if it were true it would mean such craft have been recovered and studied in secret.
borland-goes-to-the-icig-after-grusch-te: In 2023 a former intelligence officer named David Grusch testified before Congress about secret government UFO programmes. Right after that, a man named Dylan Borland says, he went with his lawyer to the Inspector General of the Intelligence Community, the office that takes whistleblower complaints from inside US spy agencies. Borland tells this about himself ("Dave testifies. I go to the ICIG"), as the moment he took his own account to an official channel to back up what Grusch had said.
borland-on-stage-will-neither-confirm-no: At a live stage event, Dylan Borland, a man the show presents as a whistleblower, was asked about Project Rubik's Cube, a reported secret programme, and would neither confirm nor deny it. Borland describes the moment himself on an episode with the filmmaker Jeremy Corbell: "I can neither confirm nor deny," he says, and he adds that people should "ask for a damn receipt for the whistleblowers."
borland-pulls-aaro-reports-on-baiting-cr: Around 2023 there were government reports and briefings on how to lure unknown craft and bring them down, and Dylan Borland, a former Air Force intelligence specialist, says he pulled them himself. He says his access through the Defense Threat Reduction Agency, a Pentagon agency for weapons of mass destruction, let him "pull reports and briefings from Arrow," meaning AARO, the Pentagon office set up to investigate unidentified aerial phenomena, including "reports about baiting craft uh and how to take them down." If true, the government is not just watching these craft but working out how to capture them.
borland-s-alleged-classified-drawing-of-: Dylan Borland, a former government official, is said to have made a drawing of a hieroglyph-like symbol, reportedly one seen on a UFO, while giving testimony to the US intelligence agencies' watchdog. The filmmaker Jeremy Corbell says the Office of the Director of National Intelligence, which oversees US spy agencies, told him this, and Michels repeats it to Borland, saying the drawings were made for that office. Borland answers in 2026 that this is only Corbell's account, built on what he calls an illegal leak to Corbell from someone in that office's inspector general, and treats the symbol as hypothetical.
borland-s-alleged-classified-icig-drawin: Dylan Borland, a former Air Force intelligence specialist who says he saw a triangle-shaped craft, is said to have drawn not only the triangle but also a pyramid-shaped power source in his classified testimony to the ICIG, the inspector general's office that takes whistleblower complaints for the US intelligence agencies. The filmmaker Jeremy Corbell tells this on the show, relaying what he heard, with the journalist George Knapp also named in the account. Michels later repeats it to Borland himself, telling it second-hand from Corbell's appearance, saying Corbell talked about a pyramid structure as the power source. If true, it would mean Borland gave investigators details of how such a craft is powered.
borland-s-congressional-testimony-on-the: In the summer of 2012, at about 1:30 in the morning, a triangle with three equal sides, roughly 100 feet across, took off from near a NASA hangar on a military base. NASA is the US space agency. This is the account of a man named Dylan Borland, who says he saw it himself on his way back to his barracks while his team was waiting out the weather, and who put it in testimony he gave to the US Congress. If it is true, a large unknown craft was flying freely from an American base.
bormann-alive-in-argentina-cashing-check: Martin Bormann, a top Nazi official, escaped to Argentina after the Second World War and was still alive in the 1960s, cashing checks in his own name through the American bank Chase in Buenos Aires. A researcher named Jason Jorjani says so on Michels' show without naming a source, also mentioning Argentina's leader of the time, Juan Perón. If true, it would mean a senior Nazi lived openly for decades with help from a major Western bank.
born-next-to-the-army-s-first-nuclear-te: A scientist named John Blitch, who worked for DARPA, the Pentagon's advanced research agency, says he was born near Idaho Falls, Idaho, right next to the first nuclear test reactor the US Army had set up. He tells it himself as part of his own life story, which takes in the 1950s and early 1960s and leads up to his account of being taken by an alien.
bose-s-paper-published-under-einstein-s-: In the 1920s, the Indian physicist Satyendra Nath Bose is said to have sent his paper to Albert Einstein, the German physicist, with the complaint that nobody was listening to him, and Einstein backed it so it got published. Greg Rogers, a doctor who has worked with NASA, the US space agency, tells it on Michels's show without naming a source, as an example of an outsider's idea getting through only because someone famous vouched for it.
boskin-commission-s-1-1-cpi-overstatemen: In the 1990s, a government panel called the Boskin Commission, which looked at how US inflation is measured, is said to have built a 1.1% overstatement by hand into the consumer price index, the official measure of rising prices. A researcher named Eric Weinstein tells Michels this, without naming a source, and calls it a crime the commission committed against the American people, an example in his telling of officials quietly working against the public.
boss-tells-fox-the-government-admitted-t: The US government has actually admitted that it recovered something at Roswell, New Mexico, in 1947, according to what a UFO investigator named James Fox says his boss once told him. Fox recalls answering "really?", and he names Richard vanle and Renee Harris in telling it. He tells it as a moment he learned the recovery was not just rumour.
bostick-on-strange-effects-at-high-megav: A man named Bostick is quoted as saying that "strange things happen at high mega voltage across short distances", meaning when millions of volts are packed into a small gap. Michels tells this himself as something he has read, linking it to the inventor Thomas Townsend Brown, who worked with high voltages. If true, it would hint that powerful electricity can produce effects that ordinary physics does not expect.
bought-ranch-as-skeptic-intending-to-don: The current owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property famous for reports of strange happenings, says he bought it in 2016 as a skeptic of all the stories told about it. He says he had actually planned to give the land to the Boy Scouts of America. He tells this about himself, which matters because it means he did not come to the ranch expecting to find anything unusual.
boyd-bushman-talks-antigravity-1990: Boyd Bushman, an engineer at the aerospace company Lockheed Martin in Fort Worth, Texas, spoke on camera about antigravity, a supposed way to cancel or push against gravity. The writer Nick Cook tells Jesse Michels he did the interview himself, for a documentary he was making at the time called Ben Rich Secret. If what Bushman said were true, a big defence firm would have been working on technology that defies gravity.
bozeman-cattle-mutilation-with-ufo-repor: In 1988 near Bozeman, Montana, two cows were found dead and, in his words, "surgically manipulated," at a time when people there were also reporting UFOs. This is what people call a cattle mutilation: livestock found dead with parts cut away, which some link to UFOs. The physicist Kevin Knuth, presented on the show as a NASA whistleblower, tells it as something he was close to himself.
bracewell-probe-possibly-lurking-in-the-: In the 1960s the astronomer Ronald Bracewell imagined that an alien civilization might send a robot probe to watch other star systems, and went further to suggest such a probe might already be hiding somewhere in our own solar system, for instance at the balance points between Earth and the Moon where an object can stay put. Michels recounts Bracewell's idea himself, in an episode with the astronomer Beatriz Villarroel. If true, there could be an alien device near Earth right now.
brad-sorensen-shown-alien-reproduction-v: In 1988, a man named Brad Sorensen is said to have been shown three flying saucers built by the US, copied from alien craft, at a private showing during a military air show. The story usually comes through the aviation illustrator Mark McCandlish, who heard it from Sorensen. Jesse Michels describes the craft as bell- or acorn-shaped "flux liners" or "alien reproduction vehicles," with wear and tear as if they had been flown. The story places this at Palmdale, California, but most tellers put it at Norton Air Force Base. UAPGerb, an online UFO researcher, tells the most detailed version. He says the visitors went behind a black curtain to find "mama, baby, and papa bear," three saucers hovering off the ground. He also describes a "pulsar craft" carrying 121 nuclear warheads that the men bragged could destroy Russia in 20 minutes. UAPGerb adds that Sorensen admitted it in 1990 to Bill Scott, a senior editor at the aviation magazine Aviation Week & Space Technology. He cites the UFO writer Bill Hamilton's book Cosmic Top Secret, and says he believes the story is legitimate. If true, it would mean the US had already built working copies of alien craft by the late 1980s.
bradshaw-ranch-high-strangeness: A property called Bradshaw Ranch, in Secret Canyon near Sedona, Arizona, is said to be the center of Sedona's "high strangeness", a term for clusters of odd, unexplained events. Michels calls it "notorious" and "ground zero" for these happenings, drawing on a book called Merging Dimensions, and he raises it because, if true, it would make the ranch a hot spot for that kind of activity.
brain-implants-link-experiencers-to-the-: Implants put in people's brains are said to connect them to a shared group mind of the grays, the small gray-skinned beings of abduction accounts. A scientist named Steve Colbern, who studies objects said to be alien implants taken from human bodies, says the implant "turns you into a walking bug" and "connects you to the gray hive of mind," adding that he was told this himself: "They told me that too." If true, people who report these encounters would be linked into an alien collective without knowing it.
brain-shown-to-secrete-dmt-endogenously-: The writer Graham Hancock says research at the University of Michigan has shown that the brain itself can make DMT, a powerful psychedelic compound, which scientists once thought came from the lungs, and that DMT receptors are found all over the brain. He credits this work to a researcher there named Jimo Borjigin. It matters to him because it would suggest the visionary experiences DMT produces are built into the brain.
brake-lines-cut-after-leaving-bae: Dylan Borland says that after he left BAE, a defense company, someone cut the brake lines on his car. He tells it as something that happened to him and says the police found that the lines were cut "100%." He brings it up as a sign that leaving and speaking out put him in danger.
bramley-plague-spreaders-are-the-sumeria: The writer William Bramley, in his book The Gods of Eden, is said to argue that whoever spread the great plagues through Europe belonged to the same group that ruled over humanity in ancient Sumer, the early civilisation of what is now Iraq. The philosopher Jason Jorjani sums up Bramley's idea, without quoting the book directly. If true, it would mean one hidden faction has steered human history from its earliest cities onward.
brandenburg-s-xenon-129-nuclear-signatur: A plasma physicist and propulsion scientist named John Brandenburg says Mars carries the chemical traces of a nuclear war: unusually high levels of xenon-129 and argon-40, especially around Cydonia, a region of Mars. Telling it himself, he says the excess was measured by the Viking missions, NASA's Mars landers, and that xenon-129 comes only from supernova explosions or hydrogen bombs, and there was no supernova on Mars. He says that when it hit him he wept, because 'they were all dead.' The philosopher Jason Jorjani, who spent several days with him in New Mexico, repeats the claim, and so do Michels and a former DARPA scientist named John Blitch. Some of them leave out the isotopes or Cydonia, and they place his realisation either in the 1980s or in the 2010s.
brandon-fugal-skinwalker-ranch-phenomeno: Whatever happens at Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property known for reports of strange events, is said to be 'reflective', mirroring the people who go there. The UFO researcher Grant Cameron says this view comes from Brandon Fugal, the businessman who owns the ranch, who uses the idea when he visits. If true, the phenomenon would respond to its observers rather than act on its own.
brandon-fugal-to-have-marrs-sphere-teste: A strange sphere connected to the late author Jim Marrs was to be flown to Utah and tested in a lab, with the Utah businessman Brandon Fugal agreeing to carry it in his private jet. The Australian journalist Ross Coulthart tells this, saying that when he asked about the object he was told, "I'm sorry, Ross," because Fugal had already taken on the testing, which would mean the object was thought worth serious scientific study.
branscomb-allegedly-offers-condon-his-cl: In the 1960s, a physicist named Lewis Branscomb, then director of the National Bureau of Standards (the federal agency that sets measurement standards), is said to have offered the physicist Edward Condon a deal: help bury the UFO question and get your security clearance back. Condon chaired a government committee studying UFOs, so if the story is true, that study's conclusion was settled in advance. Michels tells it himself, with the word "allegedly" and without naming a source.
branscomb-tells-condon-to-get-his-cleara: The story is that in 1966 a man named Lewis Branscomb went to the scientist Edward Condon and suggested he take on the Air Force's UFO study, and that it might be "time you get your clearance back," meaning his security clearance, the permission to see secret material. The source is an interview with Condon recorded by the American Institute of Physics, a scientists' organisation that keeps oral histories. Michels quotes it in one episode, where he also names the astronomer Donald Menzel. In another he reads out how the interviewer brings it up. A former Air Force officer named Robert Salas retells the same exchange from that interview. In his version Branscomb told Condon that "the Air Force needs someone to head up this UFO study," and Salas places the study at the University of Colorado. All three tellings rest on that one interview transcript, not on anyone's memory of the event. They tell it because, if a security clearance came with the job, the public UFO study may have had a secret side.
bray-s-navy-uap-disclosure-2021: Michels says that Scott Bray, a US Navy official, publicly disclosed information about UAP around 2021. UAP stands for unidentified anomalous phenomena, the government's newer term for UFOs. Michels mentions it in passing from memory, without naming a source, as one of the moments when the Navy spoke openly about these sightings.
brazil-ordinance-551gc3-on-reporting-ufo: Since 2009, any branch of Brazil's military that sees a UFO has had to report it to the Central Aerospace Defense Command, the body that guards Brazil's airspace. Michels says this comes from a rule called Ordinance 551GC3. He points to it as a sign that Brazil's armed forces treat UFO sightings as a formal matter.
brazil-s-night-of-ufos-1986-host-summary: In May 1986, 21 unidentified objects were spotted in the sky over four Brazilian states, with air bases near Brasília and Rio de Janeiro involved. Michels sums this up himself, leaning on an official statement from the Brazilian Air Force and on an air force brigadier named Octávio Júlio Moreira Lima. If true, it would mean a whole country's military tracked many unknown objects in one night.
brazil-sightings: People who saw strange things in Brazil described them in words different from the ones used elsewhere. That is according to the researcher Peter Levenda, who mentions it only briefly and gives no dates or details. His point is that how witnesses describe a sighting depends on the language and culture they come from.
break-in-at-brown-s-house-passport-taken: Someone broke into the home of Matthew Brown, a former Pentagon employee who has come forward as a whistleblower, and the only thing taken and never recovered was his civilian passport. Brown tells it himself and says his grandfather's ashes had also been moved and put out, and he points to a police record of the break-in.
break-ins-at-the-homes-of-legacy-program: In 2018, people working on a secret effort known as the Legacy programme at BAE Systems, a large defence contractor, had their homes broken into, according to a man named Dylan Borland, who knew them there. Borland repeats what happened to these colleagues rather than to himself. He tells it to suggest that people close to such programmes were being watched or pressured.
breakaway-civilization-behind-the-men-at: Whitley Strieber, an author known for writing about his own encounters with what he calls visitors, believes a "breakaway civilization" exists: a hidden group that has split off from ordinary society and works on its own. He links this to the strange men who have turned up at his door, and uses a term associated with the UFO historian Richard Dolan. If true, it would mean some of what people blame on aliens is really the work of a secret human group.
breakaway-civilization-built-on-crash-re: The people inside the classified world who have kept secret the recovery of crashed craft since 1947 are, in this view, really a separate civilization that has broken away from our own. Richard Dolan, a historian of government UFO secrecy, offers this as his own idea, linking it to the historian Arnold Toynbee, and it would mean a hidden society running alongside the public one.
brent-hears-that-harrington-worked-on-ab: A man named Harrington is said to have worked on ABSCAM, an FBI bribery sting aimed at members of Congress around 1980 in Washington. A guest named Brent Friedman says he heard this from his own mother, and he tells it as part of who Harrington was.
brent-offered-secret-agent-man-by-barry-: In the late 1990s in Los Angeles, the screenwriter Brent Friedman was offered a job on a spy television show called Secret Agent Man, with the film director Barry Sonnenfeld as executive producer. Friedman tells it himself, "years later," in an episode about Hollywood, the CIA and UFOs, as one step in his own career in that world.
brent-sees-a-fatal-motorcycle-crash-at-a: In 1968, when he was five years old, Brent Friedman says he watched a woman die in a motorcycle crash in the Berkeley Hills of California. Friedman, a guest on an episode about Hollywood and UFOs, describes it as something he saw himself: her back tire hit some water, the bike slid, stopped, flipped her, and she was gone.
brett-weinstein-advised-not-to-air-rober: Michels says he once asked a fellow podcaster, Bret Weinstein, whether he should air an interview with a scientist named Robert Malone. According to Michels, Weinstein told him that he had lost a third of his family's income and would not air it. Michels tells this from his own experience, to show what speaking on touchy subjects can cost.
brewster-lights-over-the-haunted-house-g: Around 1985 or 1986 in Brewster, New York, six bright white lights hung in formation just above the treetops over a road near the garage of a house said to be haunted, drifting slowly and making no sound at all. Charles Buhler, an engineer who later worked on propulsion research with ties to NASA, says he saw them himself after someone took him outside and showed him. He tells it as one of the early sightings that shaped his interest in unexplained craft.
brian-fitzpatrick-s-cattle-mutilation-bo: A book called The Operator, by a writer named Brian Fitzpatrick, is "the biggest reveal about cattle mutilations out there," according to Tim Gallaudet, a former Navy admiral. Cattle mutilations are cases where cows are found dead with parts strangely cut away, and Gallaudet recommends the book as the key account of them, though he does not say what it reveals.
briefing-attendees-rebuild-the-aquarius-: In 1977, the people at a secret briefing on Project Aquarius, said to be a hidden US government UFO program, met afterward in a motel near Washington and wrote down everything they remembered of it. The physicist Eric W. Davis, who worked as a Pentagon scientist, passes this on, linking it to a White House official named Alonzo McDonald and the UFO researcher Bill Moore. He tells it to explain where the written version of the Aquarius briefing came from.
briefing-dia-head-general-patrick-hughes: In the 1990s, a three-star general named Patrick Hughes, head of the Defense Intelligence Agency (the Pentagon's military spy agency), was briefed on UFOs. The briefing was given by Steven Greer, a doctor who campaigns for governments to release what they know about UFOs. Greer says he did it himself: "I briefed a three-star general, Patrick Hughes." If true, it would mean UFO claims reached the very top of military intelligence.
briefing-on-engineered-isotopic-ratios-o: Material from recovered craft has a makeup that could not occur naturally, according to David Grusch, a former Air Force intelligence officer, who says he was briefed on it between 2019 and 2022. He says intelligence reports described "isotopic ratios that would have to be engineered," meaning the mix of atom types was deliberately made. In a later telling he passes on what the analysts told him directly: heavy elements like europium and californium arranged in ways that "make like no sense," which, if true, points to a maker that is not human.
briefing-senate-intelligence-committee-i: A man named Steven Greer says that when he first started meeting with senior investigators for the Senate Intelligence Committee, the Senate committee that oversees the US spy agencies, they did not know that certain secret facilities existed. Greer says he briefed them in person. He tells it on the show to suggest that UFO secrets are kept even from the officials who are meant to oversee them.
briefing-the-institute-of-noetic-science: Steven Greer, who campaigns for the government to release what it knows about UFOs, says the astronaut Edgar Mitchell once invited him to brief the board of the Institute of Noetic Sciences, a research institute Mitchell founded to study consciousness. Greer tells it as something he did himself, years ago, in the 1990s, as a sign that serious figures took his work seriously.
briefings-to-senate-intelligence-committ: Jordan Jose, a man who says he was taken into a secret UFO programme as a child, says that between 2023 and 2026 he briefed past members of the Senate Select Intelligence Committee, the Senate panel that oversees US spy agencies. He says he also briefed several federal agencies known by three-letter initials and gave them "the locations, the names, etc." He tells it about himself, as proof that he has put his account before people in government who could check it.
brigham-s-senate-testimony-with-rfk-on-e: Brigham Buhler, a businessman who speaks out about the drug industry, says he testified before the US Senate alongside Robert F. Kennedy Jr., known as RFK. He tells Jesse Michels that the testimony tied back to the warning former US president Dwight D. Eisenhower gave in his farewell address. His point is that powerful industries have grown too close to government.
bright-light-over-catalina-identified-as: During a 2021 skywatching effort over the Catalina Channel, the stretch of sea off Southern California, the team saw a bright light that they later found was the International Space Station. The scientist Kevin Knuth, who was there, tells this, and he mentions a fellow researcher named Matthew Szydagis and a scientific paper written about the mission. He tells it to show the team checked what they saw and ruled out ordinary things.
bringing-tom-delonge-and-lue-elizondo-to: In 2017, two men were brought to see a piece of metal said to come from a crashed UFO, kept around Zanesville, Ohio. One was the rock musician Tom DeLonge, who started a UFO research company. The other was Luis Elizondo, a former Pentagon intelligence official who ran a small office studying unexplained aerial reports. Chris Bledsoe, a North Carolina man who says he has had many UFO encounters, says he took them there himself, though he is unsure whether it was Ohio or Pennsylvania. He also names the physicist Hal Puthoff and a man named Timothy Taylor.
british-and-french-governments-release-u: Around 2007 and 2008, the British and French governments are said to have released UFO documents that had been secret. The documentary maker James Fox recalls this himself in 2024, as a moment when official files on the subject came out. He brings it up as a sign that governments abroad were opening up before the US did.
british-gravity-research-memo-stamped-wr: The story is that there is a memo about British research into controlling gravity, and that the copy a researcher named Greg Bishop saw was stamped with the name of Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, an Air Force base in Ohio, and was missing about five pages. Bishop tells it from what he saw himself, and says a legend grew around those pages: the text reaches a point saying something was achieved in the mid-twentieth century, and then cuts off. If true, it would hint that a gravity breakthrough was recorded and then pulled out of the file.
broad-haven-students-draw-silver-disc: Ten students at Broad Haven in Britain are said to have seen a silver disc and then drawn pictures of it that came out identical. Marik von Rennenkampff mentions it briefly, without a source, in a challenge to the UFO skeptic Mick West on Michels's show, as a case where several witnesses agree on what they saw.
broken-bleed-line-cuts-f-18-control-line: On a training flight over a range in Saudi Arabia, a broken bleed line, a pipe that carries very hot air drawn off the engine, cut through control lines inside an F-18 Navy fighter jet. Ryan Graves, a Navy fighter pilot who was there, tells it as first-hand experience, saying it was "essentially like a plasma beam just cutting things inside the jet." He tells it to show how dangerous ordinary failures in these jets already are.
brookhaven-stony-brook-and-renaissance-a: The idea is that a cluster of Long Island institutions served as a hidden money pot for secret science: Brookhaven National Laboratory, a government research lab, the nearby Stony Brook university, and the investment firm Renaissance. Jesse Michels floats it as a question to a guest, pointing out that Brookhaven is home to the Cosmotron, which he calls the largest particle accelerator in the US. If he is right, serious physics could have been funded out of public view.
brookings-report-recommends-possible-wit: NASA commissioned the Brookings report, a study by the Brookings Institution, a Washington research group, in 1959, and it was published in 1960. As the researcher Maaneli Derakhshani describes it, the report raised the possibility of withholding from the public any discovery of artifacts left by beings from other worlds. He brings it up to suggest that keeping such finds secret was considered from the start of the space age.
brother-victor-pushed-down-an-elevator-s: The writer Peter Levenda says that in 1968 a man known as Brother Victor was pushed down an elevator shaft and had both legs broken. It happened, he says, around the Russian Orthodox Church Outside Russia at Park Avenue and 93rd Street in Manhattan. Levenda says he was there in that world at the time, and he tells it as a sign of the dark dealings around that circle, though he leaves vague who 'they' were.
brought-into-the-king-s-chamber-by-timot: Jay Anderson, a guest on the show, says he was personally taken into the King's Chamber, the main granite room deep inside the Great Pyramid of Giza in Egypt, by a man named Timothy Hogan. He tells this as something he did himself, sometime in the 2020s, to show he has had close access to Hogan and to the pyramid.
brown-brothers-harriman-versailles-repar: The claim is that a group of American bankers and lawyers tied to the peace deal after the First World War went on to fund Hitler's rise through a New York bank. A guest named Dan Sheehan tells it, passing on what he was told, and links names including the diplomat Robert Lansing, the brothers John Foster Dulles and Allen Dulles, and the German industrialist Fritz Thyssen to the Treaty of Versailles, the agreement that ended that war and set German war payments. He says that "in 1924 George Herbert Walker leaves Brown Brothers" Harriman, a Wall Street bank, and sets up the Union Bank of New York, paid for entirely by partners of that same firm, which he says then helped finance the Nazis before 1939.
brown-founds-nicap-hillenkoetter-on-boar: An American inventor named Thomas Townsend Brown is said to have founded NICAP, the National Investigations Committee on Aerial Phenomena, in 1956, a civilian group set up to track and study UFO reports. Michels tells this himself in two episodes. In a documentary about Brown, he says Brown created it after returning from the International Geophysical Year, a worldwide scientific effort of that era, and he names a former head of the CIA, Roscoe Hillenkoetter, as one of the people tied to the group. In another episode he calls NICAP the first civilian UFO tracking program and leaves out Hillenkoetter. It matters to him because it would link a secretive government scientist and a former spy chief to the earliest public UFO research.
brown-has-met-someone-who-saw-a-ufo-in-a: The claim is that a real UFO is being kept in a hangar, and that someone has seen it there. Michels asked Matthew Brown, a former Pentagon official who has come forward as a whistleblower, whether he had met anybody who he thinks has seen a UFO in a hangar. Brown answered simply, "Yes," but gave no names or details.
brown-meets-teller-and-lemay-driven-by-s: In the 1950s a scientist named Townsend Brown, who worked on ways to move craft without ordinary engines, is said to have met the physicist Edward Teller and the Air Force general Curtis LeMay. His daughter Linda Brown recalls that he was often driven home in a black Cadillac by a man she later came to know as Robert Sarbacher, a scientist tied to talk of UFO secrecy. Michels tells this from the biography The Man Who Mastered Gravity by Paul Schatzkin, and from Linda Brown's memory. It would place Brown close to the top of the era's science and military world.
brown-repeats-the-vacuum-experiment-at-b: In the 1950s, the inventor Thomas Townsend Brown is said to have repeated his experiment in a vacuum, this time at the Institute of Field Physics in North Carolina, a lab backed by a businessman named Agnew Bahnson. Michels tells it himself, without naming a source. He brings it up because a result that holds in a vacuum could not be explained by moving air.
brown-s-1953-winter-haven-proposal: A 1953 proposal by the scientist Thomas Townsend Brown, written in Winter Haven, Florida, is said to lay out almost exactly what insiders now describe as America's secret UFO program. Michels makes this claim himself in his documentary about Brown, comparing the old plan to later insider accounts. A host named Jack brings up a different line from it. He says the proposal argues that the physicist Oliver Heaviside had a very adequate theory of gravity back in the 1890s, and that we would be right to listen to him. If Michels is right, the plan for such a program was on paper as early as 1953.
brown-s-electrometers-pick-up-anomalies-: Thomas Townsend Brown, a scientist the episode calls a CIA scientist who built flying-saucer-like devices, is said to have built instruments he called electrometers that picked up odd signals following the sidereal calendar, time kept by the stars rather than the sun, and possibly caught neutrinos, tiny particles that pass through almost everything. A woman named Linda Brown tells this in a documentary episode about him, passing on what he told her, and says he ran these devices up to the end of his life on Catalina Island, California, around 1985. If true, his instruments were sensing something coming from space.
brown-s-experiments-replicated-worldwide: The high-voltage anti-gravity experiments of the researcher Thomas Townsend Brown have been repeated all over the world, as far away as Japan. Michels says this himself, without naming who did the repeat tests, in an episode with a former NASA chief about anti-gravity propulsion. He brings it up to suggest that Brown's results are not a one-off.
brown-s-lost-1929-paper-the-minor-quantu: In 1929, Thomas Townsend Brown, the researcher at the center of one of Michels' documentaries, wrote a paper called The Minor Quantum that has since been lost. Michels mentions it himself, without saying how he knows of it, while telling the story of Brown's early years. For Michels it matters because Brown is the man he calls the scientist who built UFOs before anyone had heard of them.
brown-s-navy-resignation-letter-1942: In 1942 the scientist Townsend Brown, who worked on electric propulsion ideas, is said to have received a letter ordering him to move his equipment from the University of Philadelphia to the Navy at Norfolk, Virginia, and this is tied to his later letter resigning from the Navy. The researcher Jan Lundquist tells it in a 2024 documentary on Michels's show, working from Brown's resignation letter. It is part of the story of how the Navy took over Brown's work.
brown-s-paper-the-structure-of-space-wri: The inventor Thomas Townsend Brown wrote a scientific paper called The Structure of Space in the early 1940s, while he was working at Martin Corporation, an American aircraft maker. Michels tells this himself in a documentary about Brown and notes that the paper still survives and can be read. It matters to him because it shows Brown working on ideas about space and propulsion long before later claims about secret flying craft.
brown-s-patents-bought-by-sharper-image-: Patents from the inventor Thomas Townsend Brown, who worked on using electricity to push objects through the air, are said to have ended up with Sharper Image, the gadget retailer, which used the idea in its ion air purifiers. Michels mentions this himself, hedging with "I believe" and naming no source. He raises it to show that Brown's unusual work reached ordinary consumer products.
brown-s-saucer-shaped-gravitator-and-fou: The physicist Thomas Townsend Brown built a device he called a gravitator, which Michels says "looked exactly like a flying saucer", as part of his search for a way to beat gravity. Michels also says Brown went on to help found NICAP, the National Investigations Committee on Aerial Phenomena, which Michels calls "the first civilian UFO study group". Michels tells both points himself across two episodes, the first only about the saucer shape and the second about the founding.
brown-s-task-force-captures-miethe-1945: In Germany in 1945, a task force that the inventor Thomas Townsend Brown was part of reportedly helped capture Richard Miethe for the Allied forces. Michels describes Miethe as a mysterious high-voltage physicist and tells this himself, without naming a source. If true, it would tie Brown to wartime German research on high-voltage technology.
brown-s-work-continues-in-black-aerospac: The research of Thomas Townsend Brown, an inventor whose name these episodes tie to moving craft without fuel, is said to live on inside the most secret parts of American aerospace. Michels says this as his own belief: the work survives 'in the form of whispers' in hidden sub-sections of 'black' programmes, meaning projects that are officially secret and unacknowledged. If so, the government would still be quietly developing what some call antigravity propulsion.
brown-s-work-in-the-b-2-and-floyd-odlum-: Michels says that Floyd Odlum, whom he calls the majority owner of the aircraft maker Northrop, funded the inventor Thomas Townsend Brown's work in the 1960s and paid him 2,000 or 4,000 dollars a month (Michels can't remember which), then kept paying Brown's family the same until Odlum died. Michels tells this himself without naming a source. He ties it to the idea that Brown's ideas found their way into the B-2, the stealth bomber Northrop later built, which would mean a major aircraft company quietly backed this fringe research for decades.
brown-s-work-witnessed-by-top-government: The work of the inventor Thomas Townsend Brown, which Michels ties to antigravity propulsion, was witnessed at the highest levels of the US government and military, Michels says. He draws on a biography of Brown by the writer Paul Schatzkin and names figures linked to the story, among them Curtis Lame, the physicist Edward Teller, the jet maker Bill Lear and a man named Agnew Bahnson. Michels makes the point to argue that Brown can't simply be written off as an amateur crank.
brown-spent-his-career-looking-for-a-nuc: The inventor Thomas Townsend Brown, known for work on using electricity to move craft, is said to have spent the rest of his career searching for a nuclear power source. Michels mentions it himself, without naming a source, in an episode about two days he spent with a man named Bob Lazar, and finds it telling. The suggestion is that Brown believed his ideas needed far more power than ordinary sources could give.
brown-spoke-of-biblical-ufos-and-aliens-: The inventor Thomas Townsend Brown, who worked on unusual propulsion, is said to have talked constantly about UFOs in the Bible and about aliens, privately and with his family. Michels says he learned this from Brown's daughter, Linda Brown, which would show the inventor's private beliefs went far beyond his public work.
brown-tells-josh-reynolds-the-philadelph: The Philadelphia Experiment, a story of a secret 1943 Navy experiment in Philadelphia later told in a book and a movie, was greatly inflated, according to the scientist Townsend Brown himself. Michels says Brown told this to his friend Josh Reynolds, who worked closely with him. It matters because Brown is often linked to that story, and here he is said to play it down.
brown-terminated-by-navy-joins-martin-ne: Michels says that the researcher Thomas Townsend Brown, after a long stint in the Navy, was suddenly let go in 1942 with no explanation despite strong performance, and then joined the Martin aircraft company the same year Skunk Works, Lockheed's secret aircraft design shop in Burbank, California, under the engineer Kelly Johnson, was formed. Michels tells this himself across three episodes, once crediting naval records and once Brown's FBI file, and only the first telling mentions the unexplained firing, while another gives the year as 1942 or 1943. He raises it to suggest Brown's work drew quiet interest at high levels of aerospace.
brown-university-shooting-2025: On Saturday, 13 December 2025, a man named Claudio Neves Valente carried out a planned shooting at the Barus and Holley building of Brown University in Providence, Rhode Island. Michels tells this himself in an episode about American scientists going missing, drawing on a US Department of Justice transcript of videos Valente made. He places it among a string of troubling events involving scientists.
brown-used-ion-wind-work-to-cover-for-el: The inventor Thomas Townsend Brown is said to have used his work on ion wind, where charged particles push air and create thrust, as a cover for his real interest, electrogravitics, the idea that strong electric fields can make a force like gravity. Michels says this himself, without naming a source. If true, Brown's ordinary-sounding research was hiding a more radical claim.
bruce-erickson-s-theory-that-ransone-was: A researcher named Bruce Erickson suspects that Valerie Ransone, a woman who figures in the 1970s story of a CIA scientist said to have contacted an alien council, was really a kind of spy. An unnamed researcher who appears as a guest passes on Erickson's guess. The CIA is the US foreign intelligence agency, and the idea would cast her role in that story in a very different light.
bruce-maccabee-judged-the-arv-photograph: Photos said to show ARVs, short for 'alien reproduction vehicles', human-built copies of alien craft, were judged likely hoaxes by Bruce Maccabee, a physicist who studied UFO photos. The physicist Eric W. Davis says this in 2024, recalling that Maccabee told him the pictures 'definitely looked like hoaxes'. It counts against the photos as proof of such craft.
bruno-sammaciccia-the-nordics-with-under: In 1950s Italy, a man named Bruno Sammaciccia and his associates are said to have been contacted by tall, human-looking beings known as Nordics who kept underground bases, and who were opposed by a rival group called the Contrari. The philosopher Jason Jorjani tells this from his own book, Closer Encounters, where he covers the case, as an example of beings he believes have shaped human beliefs.
bryce-dewitt-paper-on-superconductors-an: In 1968 a physicist named Bryce DeWitt wrote a paper on superconductors, materials that carry electricity with no resistance, and on gravitational drag, a pull linked to gravity. Michels brings it up himself as a question to a Navy scientist named Salvatore Pais, who holds patents for unusual flying machines. Michels raises it because, if such work existed, it would suggest serious science on controlling gravity was being done at the same time the government was closing its public UFO study.
bryce-dewitt-s-institute-funds-townsend-: The physicist Bryce DeWitt, who helped found quantum gravity, a field that later led to string theory, ran the Institute of Field Physics in North Carolina, and at the same time it was paying for the high-voltage gravity experiments of the researcher Thomas Townsend Brown. Michels tells this himself in three episodes, without naming a source. In other versions he says Wright Field, a military air base, sponsored a 1957 meeting of top physicists at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill while the university backed Brown's anti-gravity work, and in one he names the Air Force general Curtis LeMay as a sponsor, calls the institute a CIA outpost studying anti-gravity, and mentions a video of a champagne celebration there. If true, mainstream physics and secret anti-gravity research would have been funded side by side.
buchanan-bilocates-to-cydonia-on-mars-la: Lyn Buchanan, a former Army sergeant, says the first time he felt himself in two places at once, he was in the Cydonia region of Mars (he calls it "the Sedona region at Mars"). He tells it as something that happened to him, and he says what he saw there was later matched to a photograph at the home of a man named Hal Puthoff, which would mean his mind had really reached Mars.
buchanan-finds-the-mount-hayes-base-auto: A former Army sergeant named Lyn Buchanan says that when he took on the target of a base at Mount Hayes, Alaska, he found its equipment had been automated and no people were left there. He tells it as his own work, from one of the assignments he says he carried out.
buchanan-remote-views-alien-mining-bases: Lyn Buchanan, a former Army sergeant trained in remote viewing, a method of trying to describe distant places with the mind alone, says he used it to look at what seemed to be alien bases on the Moon. He says that for most of them, "what I got... was minerals," which suggests to him that they were mining sites. He tells it as his own experience, and if true it would mean someone is taking resources from the Moon.
buchanan-s-30-year-database-scoring-remo: For about thirty years, Lyn Buchanan has kept a database scoring how accurate remote viewers are. Remote viewers are people trained to describe distant places or things by mind alone, a practice the US military once studied. Buchanan, a former Army sergeant who was one of those viewers, says he built and kept the database himself, as a way of measuring whether the practice works.
buchanan-s-eyes-turn-brown-while-he-acce: An Army sergeant named Lyn Buchanan says that while he was using remote viewing, an attempt to perceive distant people and places with the mind alone, to reach into Saddam Hussein, the leader of Iraq, a woman watching him told him, "Your eyes turned brown and your voice deepened." He says this happened during his time in a remote viewing unit at Fort Meade, an Army base in Maryland, and the story would mean the viewer can take on traits of the person he is reaching. Michels later repeated it on another episode, calling Buchanan a government spy and saying something like this had happened to him, without naming Saddam or the colour brown.
buck-charlson-inventor-of-power-steering: Jeffrey Mishlove, a researcher with a doctorate who studies psychics, UFOs and the afterlife, says one of his major backers was Buck Charlson, the Minnesota inventor of power steering and of the Gerotor, a kind of pump. Mishlove tells it himself, as proof that a hard-headed engineer supported his work on the unexplained.
bud-hopkins-videotaped-on-ufos-dragging-: In about 1987 Budd Hopkins, a researcher known for working with people who say they were abducted, said on camera that UFOs "are dragging us kicking and screaming into the science of the 21st century." The writer and filmmaker Greg Bishop says he recorded this himself while filming Hopkins for a documentary. He brings it up as an early sign of the belief that the subject would push science forward.
budd-hopkins-abductees-all-drew-the-same: In New York in the 2000s, several people who say they were taken aboard alien craft were each asked to draw what they saw inside the ship, and according to the story they all drew the same symbol on the wall. The man who asked them was Budd Hopkins, an artist who spent years interviewing such people. The documentary filmmaker James Fox tells it as something he was present for, and he also names the journalist Leslie Kean. If true, it would suggest the people were describing a shared real experience.
buddha-s-teaching-of-four-more-inhabited: There are four more planets in our solar system like Earth, where practically the same people live, as the Buddha wrote 2,600 years ago, according to Kiran Ilum Xenov, the former president of a republic in Russia who says he was taken by aliens in 1997. He offers it as an ancient teaching. If true, it would mean we are far from alone even close to home.
budgets-on-the-order-of-billions-from-tr: Secret programmes are said to run on budgets on the order of billions of dollars. A Pentagon scientist named Eric W. Davis says this comes from his own interviews with people at TRW and Lockheed Martin, two large American defence contractors: "It was on that order from my interviews with TRW and Lockheed Martin people." If true, it would point to very large hidden spending.
buer-shows-no-brush-discharges-occur-in-: In an electricity lab at NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Florida, tests showed that brush discharges, small spray-like electrical sparks that leak off charged surfaces, do not happen in a strong vacuum. Charles Buhler, a NASA scientist who did the work, describes it first-hand as "showing that there's no brush discharges in high vacuum conditions." He brings it up because it matters to his claim that a push from electric charge alone, which he presents as a kind of antigravity propulsion, is real and not just air leaking sparks.
buer-shows-particle-charging-depends-on-: Charles Buhler, a NASA scientist who worked in the electrostatics lab at Kennedy Space Center, says he was the first to show that how much electric charge a particle picks up depends on how it moves, not on its size. He tells it as his own finding, as part of the background to his claim that he and his team have built a working antigravity drive.
buga-sphere-given-to-jaime-maussan-2025: In 2025 the Mexican journalist Jaime Maussan, known for his UFO reporting, was given a metal sphere, which Michels calls an aluminum object, that had been filmed in Buga, Colombia. That is why it is called the Buga Sphere. Michels says he saw it himself while visiting Maussan in Mexico City, and he mentions it in two episodes. In the second he adds that there are more than four minutes of video of it flying around Buga and that it was scanned at Maussan's place, which is why it matters: it would be a physical object to study, tied to footage of it in flight.
buga-sphere-matched-to-a-9-litre-fuel-ta: A metal ball found in Buga, Colombia, in 2025, which some people hold up as a strange object, may really be an ordinary fuel tank: there is a type of tank that holds exactly 9 litres and has holes like the ones on the sphere. The investigative journalist Ross Coulthart passes this on from a man named Ronnie Vernet, who made the match. If it holds, the sphere would be a piece of everyday hardware and not a mystery.
buga-sphere-symbols-recognised-by-mario-: The symbols on the Buga Sphere, a metal ball reported from Buga, Colombia, were recognised by two men who say they had their own UFO experiences. Michels says he showed photos of the symbols himself to Mario Woods, who says he had an encounter at Ellsworth Air Force Base in 1977, and to a man named Randy Anderson. He tells it on an episode with the journalist Ross Coulthart, as a sign that the sphere may be tied to those older encounters.
bugged-seattle-hotel-meeting-and-the-jou: In 1947 a meeting in a Seattle hotel room, linked to the pilot Kenneth Arnold and a man named Fred Crisman, is said to have been secretly bugged. According to the writer Peter Levenda, who tells it without naming a source, a local journalist got hold of a tape of the whole meeting and died shortly afterward, which hints that someone wanted it kept quiet.
building-owner-s-scientist-boyfriend-tol: In the early 1950s, a very prominent scientist told the woman he was seeing that a spaceship had crashed in New Mexico and that bodies had been recovered. The UFO investigator James Fox tells it second-hand: he heard it from the woman herself, the 88-year-old owner of a building, who repeated what her boyfriend had told her. If true, it would be a scientist's private word that a craft and its crew were recovered.
bulwer-lytton-offered-the-crown-of-greec: The British writer Edward Bulwer-Lytton, author of a novel called The Coming Race, was at one point offered the crown of Greece and turned it down. The researcher Jason Jorjani says this in passing on an episode about Nazi Germany and flying saucers, without naming a source. He offers it as a sign of how much standing Bulwer-Lytton had in his day.
burchett-five-ocean-areas-where-craft-em: Tim Burchett, a US congressman from Tennessee, is said to have stated that there are five places in the world's oceans where unknown craft come out of the water. The podcaster Joe Rogan repeats it, saying "they've identified five areas" where these things emerge "on a regular basis." Michels brings it up several times, calling them five "hot spots" under the oceans, and once says five or six deep-water areas with a higher rate of sightings. If true, it would mean the craft have bases or routes beneath the sea.
burchett-s-five-to-seven-undersea-bases-: A member of Congress named Tim Burchett has said there are five to seven undersea bases, and a retired Navy admiral named Tim Gallaudet thinks he knows where that came from. Gallaudet says on the show, as his own guess without naming a source, that someone who had seen an email from a naval intelligence commander is the person who talked to Burchett. If so, the claim of hidden bases under the sea would trace back to a message inside the Navy.
buried-ufo-too-big-to-move: Somewhere at a sensitive site he will not name, there is said to be a UFO so big it could not be moved, so it was either buried or had something built on top of it. The journalist Ross Coulthart says this on two of Michels's episodes, passing on what his sources have told him. He says he stands by it, as he did when he first said it in conversation with Joe Rogan, and if true it would mean a craft was recovered and hidden right where it lay.
burisch-and-his-wife-s-strange-vlogs: A man named Dan Burisch and his wife made some very odd home videos. A researcher who goes by the online name UAPGerb says he saw them himself while spending time with the YouTuber Chris Ramsay, who showed them to him and called them the most bizarre videos. He says nothing more about what is in them.
burkhard-heim-and-martin-s-rias-anti-gra: The German physicist Burkhard Heim is said to have been brought to the United States after his early work, and to have worked with the Martin company, an aircraft maker that later merged into Lockheed Martin, through a Martin research unit called RIAS that is linked to anti-gravity research. Michels tells this himself, hedging with "I think" and naming no source. If it is true, a big American defense firm was looking into anti-gravity using a foreign theorist's ideas.
burkhard-heim-at-lockheed-and-extended-h: A German physicist named Burkhard Heim is said to have moved to the United States and worked for Lockheed Martin, the American aerospace company, in the 1950s, where he was renowned as a total genius. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, in an episode about the alleged UFO insider Bob Lazar. He brings it up as part of the idea that advanced physics research, of the kind Heim was known for, went quiet in that decade.
burles-sees-grusch-on-the-news-and-conta: In 2023 a congressman named Eric Burlison says he was watching the news when David Grusch came on. Grusch is a whistleblower who went on to testify before Congress about UFOs. Burlison says that seeing him on screen led him to get in touch with Grusch directly, which is how his own part in the push for answers in Washington began.
burn-marks-on-the-northeast-side-of-the-: The Colossi of Memnon, a pair of huge ancient stone statues in Egypt, have burn marks only on their northeast side. The researcher Matt LaCroix says this without naming a source. He tells it as a clue to some great event in the distant past, since the marks face just one direction.
burned-memo-project-aquarius-references-: One of two documents said to come from inside the US government, a so-called burned memo or a Project Aquarius paper, mentions a Project Zodiac, according to an online researcher who goes by UAPGerb. He says he cannot remember which of the two it is, and ties the matter to a man named Lee Graham. If true, it would link these secret UFO programmes to one another.
burned-out-campfire-shows-three-hours-of: In 1976, on a camping trip at Smith Brook on Eagle Lake in Maine, Charlie Foltz and his companions went out on the water. When they got back to shore, he says, their campfire had burned out completely, which told them three hours had passed that they could not account for. Foltz was there himself, and he calls it the 'missing time' people talk about in abduction stories, meaning gaps in memory linked to being taken by aliens.
burnt-tree-and-bare-elongated-circle-at-: In 1996, near Varginha in Brazil, a craft is said to have struck a tree that was then found "burnt to a crisp," next to a long, bare, oval patch of ground. Carlos de Souza, a surgeon whose hospital he says treated a being from the case, describes seeing the site himself and saying "My god" when he saw the tree. He also names a woman called Claudia Kovu in the account. He tells it as physical evidence that something really came down there.
burroughs-suffers-physical-effects-1980: After a reported UFO encounter in Rendlesham Forest in England in 1980, a US Air Force airman named John Burroughs, one of the witnesses, is said to have suffered physical and psychological effects. Michels mentions this himself, without naming a source, in an episode about UFOs seen near nuclear bases. If true, it would mean the encounter did lasting harm to the people who were there.
bush-and-lbj-briefed-on-jfk-assassinatio: In 1963, George H. W. Bush, later president, and Lyndon B. Johnson, then vice president, are said to have been briefed on the assassination of President John F. Kennedy at a meeting on the Dallas ranch of the Texas oilman Clint Murchison, "not the one in Waco but the one in Dallas." Dan Sheehan, a guest presented as someone tied up in many of America's famous conspiracy cases, tells it as something passed on to him, and he also brings in J. Edgar Hoover, then head of the FBI. If true, it would mean powerful men knew of the killing ahead of time.
busko-s-work-rules-out-plate-defects-in-: Old photographic plates of the night sky from the late 1950s show brief points of light that appear and vanish, and work by a researcher named Ivo Busko is said to show that these are not chemical stains or flaws in the plates. Instead, the light really passed through the telescope's optics. Michels passes this on from what he was told, linking it to the astronomer Beatriz Villarroel, who studies these flashes. If it holds, something real was in the sky when the plates were exposed.
buzz-aldrin-a-33rd-degree-freemason-per-: The Apollo astronaut Buzz Aldrin is said to state, in one of his own books, that he is a 33rd degree Scottish Rite Freemason, the highest rank in one branch of the Freemasons, an old fraternal society. A guest named Maaneli Derakhshani says this to Michels on an episode about the Moon, without naming which book. He raises it to tie the space programme to secret societies.
buzz-aldrin-cancels-his-interview-in-mon: In the late 1990s, the astronaut Buzz Aldrin, the second man to walk on the Moon, agreed to an interview at a hotel in Monte Carlo, then pulled out at the last minute, saying "I'm not doing the interview." The documentary filmmaker James Fox says he had chased Aldrin around the world for it, and he tells it himself in two episodes, linking it to the Microsoft co-founder Paul Allen. Michels retells it twice: once placing it in the 2000s and saying Fox "cornered" Aldrin, and once adding Aldrin's line, "What would my testimony do anyways?"
buzz-aldrin-chased-a-disc-in-a-military-: The astronaut Buzz Aldrin is said to have had a UFO encounter while flying a military jet, years before he went into space. The UFO filmmaker James Fox says Aldrin's sister, Fay Ann Potter, told him her brother had this experience as a pilot. Michels repeats Fox's account twice, once saying it happened over Japan and that the sister spoke of two sightings, and once placing it in World War Two, which would suggest one of the best-known astronauts saw something unexplained in the air.
buzz-aldrin-ordered-to-leave-armstrong-b: During Apollo 11, the first Moon landing in 1969, the astronaut Buzz Aldrin was told that if anything happened to Neil Armstrong when Armstrong stepped outside, Aldrin was not to play the hero and try to save him. The documentary filmmaker James Fox tells this as something a woman named Fay Ann Potter told him. It is told as a sign of how much was quietly planned and kept from the public around the landing.
buzz-aldrin-s-apollo-11-sighting-retold-: Buzz Aldrin, the astronaut on Apollo 11, the 1969 mission that first landed people on the Moon, has an account of something he saw during that flight, and it was talked over on Larry King Live, a TV talk show. Michael Shermer, a researcher known as a leading skeptic, says he was on that show himself, alongside Aldrin and a couple of UFO people. Shermer brings it up as an example case while debating UFOs with Michels.
buzz-aldrin-s-masonic-lodge-on-the-moon: The astronaut Buzz Aldrin, a Freemason, is said to have set up a Masonic lodge on the Moon during the Apollo 11 mission, called Tranquility Lodge 2000 and chartered by the Grand Lodge of Texas. Michels tells it himself across three episodes. Once he speaks only of a Masonic flag planted on the Moon, alongside NASA's launch pad 33, and once he cites the Masonic Grand Lodge of Ohio as his source, a sign to him of the Freemasons' ties to the space programme.
buzz-aldrin-s-ufo-sightings-and-james-fo: Buzz Aldrin, the second man to walk on the Moon in 1969, is said to have told his sister that as a fighter pilot in Japan he saw a foo fighter, a glowing ball of light of the kind military pilots reported, and that he saw UFOs on the way to the Moon. Michels passes this on from the UFO investigator James Fox, who got it from Aldrin's sister. In a later episode Michels tells it differently, putting the sighting in World War II, leaving out the trip to the Moon, and describing Fox chasing Aldrin for an interview in Monte Carlo in the late 1990s that never came off.
buzz-aldrin-tells-conan-o-brien-the-land: The Apollo 11 astronaut Buzz Aldrin is said to have told the late-night talk show host Conan O'Brien that the footage of the 1969 Moon landing was animation. An unnamed researcher who appears as a guest on Michels's show points to "this particular exchange between Buzz Aldrin and Conan O'Brien" but does not describe it further. The guest raises it to suggest that the landing images the public saw were not real camera footage.
byrd-took-the-sixth-floor-depository-win: After President Kennedy was shot in Dallas in 1963, a man named D. Harold Byrd is said to have removed the sixth-floor window of the book depository building tied to the shooting and put it in the trophy room of his house. The researcher Dan Sheehan tells this on Michels's show without naming a source, while arguing that Kennedy's death was linked to what he knew about UFOs.
c-17-drops-off-a-mystery-box-at-a-guarde: In North Dakota around 2012, a C-17, a large military cargo plane, is said to have landed in the middle of the night and dropped off a box at a guarded hangar, in what was "this whole ordeal." A guest named Dylan Borland relays this from an unnamed member of the military security forces known as a "Raven," who described the scene to him. Borland tells it as a hint of something being secretly moved and kept.
c-d-jackson-released-the-zapruder-film-w: The story goes that after President John F. Kennedy was shot in 1963, the best film of the killing was held back from the public in a way that hid part of what happened. The film is the Zapruder film, a home movie that Michels calls "the clearest footage of the assassination." A researcher named Jeremy Riss says the man who led its release was Charles Douglas Jackson, and he says it without naming a source. Michels tells the rest himself, also without a source. He says Life, a big American news magazine, bought the film. Then, he says, instead of showing it in full, "they only published black and white stills with certain key frames missing." Michels also says the film stayed held back into the 1970s, which Riss does not say. The two tell it independently, a researcher and the host, and they agree on Jackson's role. If it were true, it would mean one well-placed man shaped what the country was allowed to see of the assassination.
c-d-jackson-visits-betty-and-barney-hill: Charles Douglas Jackson, a government man whom Michels says ran psychological warfare and was deeply involved in MK Ultra, the CIA's secret mind-control research program, is said to have turned up at the New Hampshire home of Betty and Barney Hill two weeks after the couple's famous 1961 encounter with what they said was a UFO. Michels brings this up himself in three episodes without naming a source. In one he also ties Jackson to Henry Luce, the publisher of Time and Life magazines, and in another he leaves out the two-week timing. He tells it to suggest that intelligence and propaganda figures were watching UFO cases closely from the beginning.
cahn-behind-flater-s-complaint-1953: In Denver in 1953, according to a researcher named Scott Ramsey, a man named JP Khan was the one who contacted a man named Herman Flader, which in Ramsey's view puts Khan behind a complaint Flader made, a matter that also touches J. Edgar Hoover, then head of the FBI. Ramsey, who studies a reported saucer crash said to have held sixteen alien bodies, offers this to Michels as his own reading without naming a source, because if true it would mean the complaint was steered by someone else.
california-attorney-general-asks-fbi-to-: On April 25, 1951, according to Michels, a man named JP Khan got the office of California's Attorney General, the state's top law officer, to ask the FBI, the US federal police agency, to look into a man named Silas Newton. Newton had claimed to be doing secret government research, and the request questioned those claims and accused him of being part of a hoax. Michels tells this from the FBI's own files on Newton, as a sign of how seriously officials took Newton's claims.
caliph-al-mamun-s-raiders-find-the-great: Arab raiders led by Caliph al-Mamun, a Muslim ruler, broke into the Great Pyramid of Giza in Egypt and found it empty inside. The writer Graham Hancock tells this without naming a source or a date. It matters because an empty pyramid raises the question of whether it was ever a tomb at all.
call-cutting-out-while-pitching-lazar-in: Michels says that when he was pitching an interview with Bob Lazar, a well-known figure in UFO circles, his phone call kept cutting out just as he said it. He tells this as something that happened to him, hinting that someone may have been listening in.
call-from-a-metallic-alien-voice-1970: A scientist is said to have picked up the phone and heard a metallic voice, some kind of alien intelligence, speaking to him. A researcher named Greg Malatzi tells it briefly on the show, without naming where he got it, and places it in the 1970s. Jesse Michels tells a fuller version. He names the man who got the call as the physicist Jack Sarfatti and puts the call in the 1950s. In his telling the voice came from the future and told Sarfatti he would meet "the others" and would end up working on, as Michels puts it, "building UFOs essentially." Michels credits a book called The Hippies Saved Physics, and he mentions the names Hal Puthoff, Hans Bethe and David Kaiser alongside it. If true, it would mean that some unknown intelligence reached out to steer a young scientist toward exotic physics.
call-to-art-bell-show-and-emails-with-an: Richard Barth, a former guard at a nuclear missile site who says he was abducted by aliens, says he once called in to Art Bell's show, Coast to Coast AM, a late-night US radio programme about the paranormal. He says he then emailed with an author who later told him he could not put Barth in any more books because he "couldn't collaborate it," meaning no one else could back up the account. Barth tells this himself, as part of how hard it has been to get his story taken seriously.
call-to-space-command-about-a-classified: In the 1980s, someone phoned Space Command, the US military command for space operations, and asked to join a secret programme about an alien threat. The caller was John Brandenburg, a physicist who argues that Mars once had life destroyed by nuclear war, and he tells it himself. He says he told the man who answered, "I've heard there is an extraterrestrial threat whose existence is classified. I'd like to help with that program," and the man replied, "Oh, okay. Here, let me see if I can connect you with somebody," as if such a programme existed.
callahan-hides-a-copy-of-the-jal-1628-ra: A US aviation official named John Callahan copied the radar data from Japan Air Lines flight 1628, a flight whose crew reported an unknown object, and hid the copy in a box under a table so the CIA would not take it. The physicist Kevin Knuth, a former NASA scientist, tells this as Callahan's own account, set at the Federal Aviation Administration, the US air traffic agency, in Washington. He uses it as an example of UFO evidence that was nearly lost.
called-back-from-leave-through-a-blizzar: In the early 1990s, a young Air Force sergeant on leave was called back to his base and had to drive back through a snowstorm before starting duty at a posting he calls Base 2. Dan Sherman, a former Air Force sergeant who says the National Security Agency, the US spy agency for communications, trained him to speak with aliens, tells it as his own memory: "There was a blizzard the entire way home." It is part of how he says his secret assignment began.
calling-george-noory-s-show-while-bob-ha: A former nuclear missile guard named Richard Barth says he once phoned in to Coast to Coast AM, a late-night American radio talk show hosted by George Noory, on a night when a man named Bob Hastings was the guest. Barth tells it himself to Michels, in passing, as the way he first came to talk with Hastings, and he does not say when the call happened.
caltech-astronomer-99-chance-planet-nine: An astronomer at Caltech, the California Institute of Technology, said there is a 99 percent chance that a hidden large planet, nicknamed Planet Nine, exists far out beyond Neptune. A researcher named Matt LaCroix tells this on Michels' show without naming the astronomer, and in another moment gives the reasoning instead of the number: the orbits of objects in the Kuiper belt, the band of icy bodies at the edge of the solar system, are "super skewed" and "perturbed by something." If true, an unseen planet would be shaping the outer solar system.
camera-battery-and-memory-card-taken-fro: In 2009, on a ship at Subic Bay in the Philippines, someone took the battery and the memory card from a camera that was stored in a locked locker. Michael Herrera, a guest who says he saw a huge craft, about 300 feet across, in the Indonesian jungle, tells this as something that happened to him: he went to the camera and "the battery is missing and the memory card is missing." If it is true, someone wanted to make sure no pictures were kept.
