camp-david-napkin-picture-mailed-to-chri: A picture of a napkin bearing the presidential seal from Camp David, the US president's country retreat, is said to have been mailed in an envelope to Chris Bledsoe, a man who says UFOs appear around him, by a man named Tim Taylor. Bob McGwier, who has worked as a CIA contractor, says he recognised both Bledsoe's address and the Camp David napkin from a photo the researcher Grant Cameron posted on Facebook, and he calls the letter "ironclad proof" that Bledsoe's story was taken all the way to President Barack Obama. Bledsoe tells it the same way himself, saying plainly that Taylor briefed Obama on him.
canadian-scientists-in-the-legacy-progra: Scientists from Canada have taken part, and still take part, in the "legacy program", the name used for a secret effort said to recover and study craft that were not built by people. The investigative journalist Ross Coulthart says so, passing on what he has been told by sources. If true, it would mean the effort is not only American.
candle-flame-frozen-at-the-emitter-s-foc: Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on strange technology between 1987 and 1989 at S4, a secret site in the Nevada desert, says a colleague there named Barry Castilio showed him an "emitter", a part of a reactor-driven device, that was working. According to Lazar, Castilio put a lit kitchen candle right at the emitter's focal point, powered up the reactor, and the flame stopped flickering. Lazar tells it to Michels as something he saw himself, and if true it would mean the device did something strange to whatever sat at its focus.
canopy-leak-at-night-80-miles-from-the-c: One night, about 80 miles west of his aircraft carrier and around 30,000 feet up, a Navy fighter pilot named Ryan Graves says the canopy of his jet, the clear cover over the cockpit, suddenly began to leak. Graves tells it as something that happened to him on a flight, with no date given.
cape-canaveral-as-cover-for-non-space-pr: Cape Canaveral Air Force Station, the military launch base on the Florida coast, makes a handy cover for secret work that has nothing to do with space, according to a NASA doctor named Greg Rogers. Rogers, who says he worked there in the 1990s, explains it this way: "If you put project X on Cape Canaveral Air Force Station they can always say oh well it's just related to the space program." If he is right, any odd hardware or activity at the base could be hidden behind the space program.
cape-girardeau-crash-with-small-bodies-a: In 1941, something is said to have crashed near Cape Girardeau, Missouri, leaving small bodies behind, and a reverend or priest was asked to give last rites because one of them was apparently still alive. John Blitch, a scientist who worked for DARPA, the Pentagon's advanced research agency, and who says he was himself taken by an alien, retells it on Michels's show without naming his source.
captain-hollanda-lima-s-encounter-with-a: A Brazilian military officer, Captain Uyrangê Hollanda Lima, says he met a being in a space suit near Colares in northern Brazil, and the being gave him a hug. Michels tells this from the report of Operation Prato, the Brazilian military's investigation into strange sightings around Colares in the late 1970s, which Hollanda led. If true, the man in charge of the official inquiry had a close encounter himself.
captain-viriato-s-radar-track-at-mach-15: In Brazil in 1986, a military officer known as Captain Viriato is said to have tracked an unknown object on radar moving at Mach 15, fifteen times the speed of sound, in a zigzag pattern. Michels tells it himself, without naming a source, in an episode about Brazilian UFO cases that the country's defense minister is said to have confirmed. No known aircraft could fly like that.
captain-warns-sherman-he-won-t-be-allowe: Some time between 1990 and 1993, at a place he calls Base 2, a captain warned a young sergeant that he would not be allowed to leave the work he had been given. The sergeant, Dan Sherman, tells it himself. He says the National Security Agency, the US agency that listens in on communications, hired him to talk with aliens, and he remembers the captain saying, "I honestly don't think you're going to be able to get out." If true, it suggests the programme did not let its people walk away.
captured-german-nuclear-scientists-wiret: At the end of the Second World War in 1945, the physicist Werner Heisenberg and the others on Germany's nuclear program were captured and held in a country house in England, and the whole house was secretly wiretapped. Michels tells this himself, saying he "believe[s]" that is where they were kept, and points to the transcripts of those recordings. It is told because the secretly recorded talk would show what the German scientists really knew.
captured-german-ss-documents-at-the-nati: Microfilmed German documents seized after the Second World War, including papers of the SS, the Nazi elite guard led by Heinrich Himmler, sit in the National Archives in Washington, and the writer Peter Levenda says he went to read them. He tells it first-hand: "I wanted to see the captured German documents from the war. They had this a bunch of microfilm." It is where his research into the Nazi leadership's hidden interests started.
captured-russian-and-chinese-weapons-sho: A man named Randy Anderson says that in 2014, underground at Naval Surface Warfare Center Crane, a Navy weapons research base in Indiana, he and others were told about Russian and Chinese weapon systems that had been captured. Anderson tells it as something he was present for, and if true it would mean the base held foreign hardware out of public view.
car-crash-outside-the-dark-skies-office-: In the 1990s, a car crashed outside the North Hollywood office of Dark Skies, a television production, and as a man lay dying, a writer named Brent Friedman says he felt the man's whole life pass through him. Friedman, who was there, says, "I feel all of his energy go through my body like his soul." He tells it as a personal brush with something beyond the ordinary.
car-fried-by-energy-weapon-en-route-to-f: A scientist named Steve Colbern, who studies objects he believes are alien implants in human bodies, says someone zapped his car with "some kind of an energy weapon" while he was driving through a canyon. He was on his way to the office of a doctor the transcript gives only as Dr. Builder, to film him testing an implant while it was still inside a patient's body. Colbern says a mechanic later told him the car's computer was fried, as if it had been hit by an EMP, an electromagnetic pulse that can knock out electronics, which to Colbern suggests someone wanted to stop that filming.
careful-handling-of-david-grusch-before-: Before David Grusch, a former intelligence official, went public in 2023 and testified under oath to Congress about UFOs, the journalist George Knapp and the filmmaker Jeremy Corbell are said to have been part of carefully bringing him forward. Bryce Zabel, a guest on an episode about Hollywood and UFOs, mentions this in passing as something he knows from those involved. It matters to the tellers because it shows people working behind the scenes to get a whistleblower safely to the public.
caretaker-tom-lewis-collapses-during-dri: At Skinwalker Ranch, a property known for strange events, the caretaker Tom Lewis is said to have collapsed while the team was drilling beneath a mesa. The ranch's owner, Brandon Fugal, tells it as someone who was there, and says the caretaker was "brought to his knees". This happened as a radio signal at 1.6 gigahertz appeared during the drilling. Another witness on the same episode calls it a heart episode and says a team member called Dragon got the man out at once, without naming him or mentioning the signal. Both tell it on a 2026 episode with Jesse Michels. To them it suggests that whatever lies under the ranch can harm the people who dig toward it.
cargo-cult-text-written-for-delonge-to-s: The rock musician Tom DeLonge asked the writer Peter Levenda to write a text he could show people, meant for insiders, explaining what the two of them were trying to do, a piece built around the idea of a cargo cult, where people copy the outward signs of a technology they do not understand. Levenda tells Jesse Michels he wrote it himself and that it became the opening pages of their book Sekret Machines: Gods.
cargo-cults-building-landing-tracks: On remote Pacific islands, groups known as cargo cults are said to have built landing strips in the hope that craft from the sky would come back. Michels tells it himself, saying cargo cults in French Polynesia build landing tracks for what are presumably alien craft that their mythology says will return. The researcher Peter Levenda tells it more plainly, as planes landing on South Pacific islands in the early 20th century, with no mention of aliens. Another researcher, Jason Simosa, repeats it from Levenda, placing it in French Polynesia but admitting he is unsure where it happened. It is told as an example of how people make myths around visitors from the sky.
carl-jung-s-flying-saucers-1958: In 1958 the Swiss psychiatrist Carl Jung published a book called Flying Saucers: A Modern Myth of Things Seen in the Skies, which looked at why so many people were reporting saucers. Michels raises it in several episodes. In one he says Jung read the saucers as mandalas, the circle that stands in Sanskrit tradition for a complete and whole mind, and in that telling he dates the book only to the 1950s. A researcher named James Madden, talking about the book from his own reading, describes how its argument moves. He says Jung starts out treating the saucers as a rumor that spreads through a crowd. As the book goes on, Madden says, Jung finds them harder to wave away, and by the end he is noting "and yet they're on radar." The tellers raise the book because it suggests that one of the great students of the human mind could not fully explain the sightings as psychology.
carl-jung-s-scarab-beetle-as-a-time-loop: The Swiss psychiatrist Carl Jung had a skeptical, down-to-earth patient who told him she had dreamed of being given a golden scarab beetle, and as she told the dream, a real scarab beetle came to the window sill of his office. Michels tells the story himself in three episodes, each time without naming a source. In one he treats it as a kind of time loop, where the dream reached ahead to the beetle, and in the others he tells it simply as a strange coincidence from therapy.
carl-nell-points-to-thomas-townsend-brow: Karl Nell, a former defense industry executive who Michels says ran a business with $2 billion in yearly revenue and costs and was chief technology officer of a company owned by the defense contractor Northrop, has pointed people to Thomas Townsend Brown, an inventor of unusual ways to move aircraft. According to Michels, Nell told people to "go just watch Jesse's video" on Brown. Michels brings this up twice, in two different episodes, as a sign that someone this senior takes Brown's ideas about exotic propulsion seriously.
carl-pflock-broke-into-a-congressman-s-o: A man named Carl Pflock is said to have broken into a congressman's office and taken away evidence about a reported crash of a craft at a place called Aztec. Michels tells this on the show, passing on what Scott Ramsey, his source on the Aztec story, told him. If true, someone went to great lengths to keep that evidence out of sight.
carl-sagan-and-the-golden-disc-1970: The astronomer Carl Sagan helped put together the Golden Disc, a record sent out on a spacecraft in the 1970s that has now left our solar system. Luis Elizondo, a former Pentagon official who worked on unexplained aerial reports, brings this up when speaking about Sagan.
carl-sagan-as-a-majestic-member-1960: The astronomer Carl Sagan, the philosopher Jason Jorjani suggests, was secretly part of Majestic, a rumoured top-secret US government group said to handle the UFO question. Jorjani says he is "pretty convinced" of this but names no source, and if true it would put one of science's best-known public voices inside the secret.
carl-sagan-calls-brandenburg-why-are-you: When a scientist named John Brandenburg began speaking in public about his idea that life on Mars was wiped out by a nuclear war, the famous astronomer Carl Sagan called him on the phone and asked, "Brandenburg, why are you causing this trouble?" Brandenburg tells it firsthand. He places the call in the 1980s, while he worked at Sandia, a US government science laboratory, and says he felt "very deeply honored" and that Sagan, like everyone, called him by his surname. Michels repeats the story on two other episodes, once with Sagan's words and once only saying that Sagan called when Brandenburg went public. If true, it would mean one of the best-known scientists of his day personally tried to discourage the idea.
carl-sagan-met-with-kit-green-and-got-in: Late in his career, the astronomer Carl Sagan met often with Kit Green, a CIA man interested in UFOs, and became very interested in UFOs himself. Michels says this in two episodes, without naming a source, and in one he adds that Sagan also held covert meetings, possibly about UFOs, that the public never knew about. If true, one of the best-known sceptics of UFOs would have been quietly looking into them.
carl-sagan-s-early-ufo-interest-and-turn: The astronomer Carl Sagan grew up writing about UFOs in his diary and argued about them often with his mentor, then somehow turned hard against them, as in his book The Demon-Haunted World. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, in a talk with a religion scholar named Diana Pasulka. He brings it up as a puzzle: why would a man so drawn to the subject become one of its fiercest doubters.
carl-stanley-dies-a-month-after-his-bron: In 1965 a man named Carl Stanley went through a consecration, a ceremony that makes someone a bishop, in the Bronx in New York. Then he went back to Kentucky and, in the words of the researcher Peter Levenda, "he's dead within a month." Levenda tells it without naming a source, as a strange turn of events tied to the ceremony.
carlin-tunnel-proof-of-concept-scan-2024: In 2024 a tunnel known as the Carlin Tunnel was scanned as a test, to show that a radar method for seeing underground works on a structure whose shape is already known. A researcher named Jeffrey Drum shows this scan, tied to the radar scientist Filippo Biondi, in an episode about claims of large structures beneath the Egyptian pyramids, as support for those underground findings.
carlos-de-souza-witnesses-the-crash-and-: In 1996, near Varginha in Brazil, a craft is said to have come down on a place called the Molini Farm, and a passing driver saw it happen. He was Carlos de Souza, an ultralight pilot and geography teacher. He tells it himself. He says he was on the highway when "I saw an object pass over the road and I noticed that the object was having problems. It was smoking." He says he followed it, and that the rear of the craft bounced and "was completely destroyed." James Fox, a documentary filmmaker, retells what de Souza told him. In Fox's version, de Souza drove up a dirt road to the farm, saw the craft "struggling to stay in the air," and then watched it hit the ground. Michels repeats the account, crediting Fox and his documentary Moment of Contact. He describes a cigar or "tic-tac" shaped craft, an oval like the mint, with a puncture and gas coming out the back. A doctor named Ahmed Foratu adds what he heard from the teacher: that he touched the wreckage, but police took it and ordered it handed over to the army. The story is told because it would be an eyewitness to a crashed craft.
carlos-eire-s-they-flew-and-the-historic: Carlos Eire, a well-respected professor of religious studies at Yale, wrote a book called They Flew about Christian saints who were said to rise into the air, such as St. Joseph of Cupertino, Teresa of Avila and Francis of Assisi. Michels brings up the book himself as serious scholarship on these accounts. To him, it suggests that reports of people defying gravity have a long and documented history in Europe.
carlos-struggles-to-find-the-crash-site-: In the 2022 documentary Moment of Contact, a witness named Carlos de Souza goes back to look for the spot near Varginha, Brazil, where he says a craft crashed, and he can't find it. Michels describes the scene, which also features James Fox: Carlos arrives and says "It wasn't here. In fact, the landscape has changed." Michels reads this as a sign of honesty, since he thinks a liar would simply have pointed and said "Here it is."
carlson-has-seen-ufos: The researcher Randall Carlson says he has seen UFOs, unidentified objects in the sky, with his own eyes. He mentions it in passing to Michels while talking about the parapsychological, and gives no time, place or details of what he saw.
carlson-s-1995-warren-wilson-college-lec: In 1995, at Warren Wilson College in North Carolina, a set of lectures argued that a space impact caused the Younger Dryas, a sudden return to ice-age cold near the end of the last ice age. Randall Carlson, an independent researcher of ancient catastrophes, says he gave them himself: "five lectures" where he "talked about the younger dus, the mass extinctions, the rapid climate change." He tells it to show he was making the case years before it became widely discussed.
carlson-s-masonic-initiation-and-becomin: A researcher named Randall Carlson tells Michels he is a Freemason, a member of the old fraternal society organised in local groups called lodges. He says he was "raised" in March 1979, the Masonic word for receiving the full third degree of membership, and became master, the head, of his own lodge in 1990.
carlson-visits-quarries-exposing-the-bla: In a few quarries you can see the "black mat" out in the open, a dark layer in the ground that some researchers tie to an ancient catastrophe. The researcher Randall Carlson says he has gone to three or four of these quarries to look at the layer himself. He mentions it as first-hand support for his view that the layer is real and can be seen.
caroline-yacht-1933-expedition-and-steph: In 1933, the yacht Caroline, belonging to a man named Eldridge Reeves Johnson, is said to have docked at Nassau in the Bahamas, where a man named William Stephenson, who used Nassau as a base of operations, came aboard and had dinner with Johnson. The researcher Paul Schatzkin tells it without naming a source, in Michels's documentary about the inventor Townsend Brown, as part of the web of contacts around Brown's early work.
carrington-event-solar-storm-1859: In 1859 a huge solar storm, known as the Carrington event, knocked out electrical lines, and Michels says a storm like that today would take out the entire power grid. He brings it up himself, without a source, in a conversation with the biologist Rupert Sheldrake. He uses it to show how exposed modern life is to forces from the sun.
carter-asks-cia-director-george-h-w-bush: After he won the 1976 election, and before he even moved to Washington, Jimmy Carter is said to have called the head of the CIA, George H. W. Bush, down to his home town of Plains, Georgia, to brief him on UFOs, and Bush refused. Dan Sheehan, a guest presented as someone tied up in many of America's famous conspiracy cases, tells it as an account passed on to him. If true, it would mean the spy agency kept UFO secrets even from an incoming president.
carter-praying-with-his-head-on-the-tabl: After President Jimmy Carter was briefed on UFOs in 1977, he is said to have put his head down on the table and prayed. Eric W. Davis, a physicist who has worked on Pentagon research, passes this on from a man named Alonzo McDonald, who told Davis and a man named Dan Sheehan that Carter "has a habit of putting his head down on his table like this and praying." Davis tells it to suggest the briefing shook the president deeply.
carter-purge-of-senior-cia-officers-who-: When Jimmy Carter took office in 1977, he is said to have purged nearly the entire senior ranks of the CIA, the US foreign spy agency, and many of those hundreds of officers may have been overseeing parts of the "legacy program", the supposed long-running secret government effort around UFOs. A researcher named Matthew Pines raises this with Michels, without naming a source, and asks what those officers went on to do, hinting that the program's knowledge may have left government with them.
carter-s-1976-ufo-briefing-by-cia-direct: In 1976, right after Jimmy Carter won the presidency, he is said to have called the head of the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency, down to his home town of Plains, Georgia, to brief him on UFOs, and that head was George H. W. Bush. Michels tells this from the lawyer Dan Sheehan. In a later episode he tells it again in his own words, without naming Sheehan or Plains, and is unsure about the order of Bush's jobs; if true, it would mean a new president's first concern was the UFO question.
casino-skim-money-driven-in-cadillacs-to: In the early 1960s, money skimmed off the top of casinos was packed into Cadillacs and driven between places like Las Vegas, New Orleans, Miami and Mexico City to pay for a secret training base, with the mob bosses Carlos Marcello and Meyer Lansky named in the story. The lawyer Dan Sheehan tells it and says he knows the man who sold them the Cadillacs, since that man owned the big dealership there. It is told as a sign that organised crime money paid for covert work in those years.
catalina-as-a-ufo-hotspot: Catalina, an island off the coast of Southern California, is said by many to be a hotspot for UFOs that move between air and water. Michels brings this up more than once, crediting a book called Undersea UFO Base by a writer named Preston Dennett, and he says Catalina "might be the world's biggest hotspot of transmedium water-based UFOs," meaning objects that pass between sky and sea. He adds that a scientist named Townsend Brown spent the end of his life there. Separately, a retired Navy admiral named Tim Gallaudet, arguing that the oceans are full of such objects, names the Catalina Channel itself as "a hot spot," without crediting Dennett. If true, it would mean these objects favour one stretch of water close to a major American coastline.
catholic-archival-reports-of-aerial-phen: The claim is that Catholic archives, including those of the Vatican, hold reports from Catholics in Europe, Canada and the United States describing strange things in the sky, dating from 1200 to 1800. A scholar named Diana Pasulka says she found these herself while working in the archives. If so, sightings like today's would go back many centuries.
catholic-church-helps-nazis-escape-to-so: Around 1945, people in the Catholic Church decided to work with Nazis, hide them, give them false papers and get them out to places like Bolivia and Argentina. The researcher Peter Levenda tells this without naming a source. If true, it would mean a church network helped Nazis escape after the war.
cattle-mutilations-done-by-humans: The cattle mutilations, cases where farm animals are found dead with organs cut out, are said to be done by humans and not by aliens. Steven Greer, a UFO researcher, tells Michels this flatly, without naming a source, and says the researcher Linda Moulton Howe is wrong to think aliens are behind them. If true, it would mean people are staging these cases.
cattle-mutilations-in-the-bigelow-era-19: Skinwalker Ranch in Utah, a property famous for strange reports, is said to have had many cattle mutilations, cows found dead and cut in odd ways, while it was owned by the businessman Robert Bigelow from 1996 to about 2016. Brandon Fugal, the ranch's current owner, tells it about his predecessor's time, pointing to Bigelow's necropsy reports, animal autopsies, and a doctor he names as Dr. O'nett. To the tellers it is part of why the ranch is seen as a hotspot for the unexplained.
cattle-mutilations-in-the-missile-field-: In 1977 cattle were said to be turning up dead and mutilated around the nuclear missile field near Ellsworth Air Force Base, in the weeks before a night when airmen there report being abducted. Mario Woods, a former guard at a nuclear missile site, says cattle mutilations were going on in the area and that Linda Moulton Howe, a journalist who investigates such cases, was there. Jesse Michels tells it from what an Air Force veteran named Michael Johnson told him: cattle had been dying around the missile field in the weeks before that November night, and a camera was confiscated. The tellers bring it up as a sign that something strange was already happening around the nuclear weapons.
caught-on-the-last-trip-and-banned-from-: Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked at S4, a secret site in the Nevada desert, says that in 1989 he made trips out near Groom Lake, the dry lakebed by the secret base, and that the first time, the people there did not know they were out there. On the last trip, he says, they were caught, and he was banned from S4. Lazar tells it to Michels as his own experience, and it is, in his account, how his time at the site ended.
causeway-shafts-are-waterproof-and-hold-: Shafts under a causeway on the Giza Plateau in Egypt, where the great pyramids stand, are said to be waterproof, so water outside them cannot get in and they hold air instead. The researcher Filippo Biondi says this is his own reading, on Michels's show, in an episode about what he calls a massive energy grid beneath the pyramids.
cave-of-poisoned-aboriginal-tribe-litter: Somewhere in Australia there is a cave where a whole tribe of Aboriginal people was given poisoned food, and the cave is "just littered with human bones." The comedian and podcaster Joe Rogan tells this on Michels's show, passing on what his friend Adam Greenree told him after visiting the site.
caves-running-under-the-giza-plateau: Beneath the Giza plateau, the site of Egypt's great pyramids, there are said to be caves running under the whole area. The researcher Luke Caverns says that diggers there hit a cavern, and that by passing through cracks in its walls you reach caves stretching under the entire plateau. Another researcher, Jeffrey Drum, says simply that it is known for sure that caves and tunnels lie below Giza, without describing how they are reached. Both raise it as a sign that the pyramids sit on hidden spaces still little explored.
ce5-night-in-sedona-with-greer-s-team-an: On a night at an off-grid spot off a trail near Sedona, Arizona, Michael Herrera says he sat with a group trying to call down UFOs through meditation and signals, a practice its followers call CE5. The group was led by a man named Steven Greer's team and included the singer Demi Lovato and a woman named Paola Harris. Herrera, who was there, says they saw glowing orbs and disc-shaped craft appear and vanish, among them a gold disc, and that something unseen struck a blow.
centcom-bottleneck-on-uap-information: The filmmaker and journalist Jeremy Corbell says that US Central Command, the military command in charge of the Middle East, is a bottleneck for reports of UAP. UAP stands for unidentified anomalous phenomena, the government's term for UFOs. He says the command holds the information up before it reaches the public, and ties the claim to reporting he has done with the television journalist George Knapp.
centcom-formation-of-12-metallic-orbs-sk: US Central Command, the military command that covers the Middle East, is said to have recorded a formation of 12 metallic balls flying in a box-shaped pattern low over the ocean. Michels reads this from a report called Immaculate Constellation, which a former Pentagon official named Matthew Brown has spoken about, and its line reads: "Central command discusses cuboid formation of metallic orbs on USG networks," meaning US government computer systems. If true, it would mean the military was quietly sharing reports of unknown objects among its own people.
cern-physicists-report-beings-coming-thr: Beings are said to be coming in and out through portals at CERN, Europe's large particle physics laboratory near Geneva. A researcher named Astrid Stuckelberger says physicists at CERN told her this personally: "There are beings from portals coming in and out." She tells it on two episodes, and in the later one dates it to around 2021 or 2022 and adds that she knows physicists who are doing "very strange experimentation."
cernan-s-telepathic-message-on-apollo-17: On the way to the Moon in 1972 on Apollo 17, the last crewed Moon mission, the astronaut Eugene Cernan got a kind of telepathic message saying "We don't really want you here," and that is why no one went back after that. Michels tells this as something he heard from a man named Takano Josen. If true, it would explain why the Moon landings stopped.
cesar-demands-10-000-to-talk-to-rfk-jr: A man called Cesar is said to have demanded money, ten thousand dollars by the story's title though the spoken words sound like more, before he would talk to Robert F. Kennedy Jr., the son of the murdered senator Robert Kennedy. Dan Sheehan, a guest presented as someone tied up in many of America's famous conspiracy cases, says he talked to Kennedy about it and that Kennedy was going to meet the man to get him to talk, but the man insisted on being paid.
cesario-says-chereze-kept-linking-his-il: In Varginha, Brazil, in 1996, a police officer named Marco Chereze is said to have helped catch a strange being, then fallen ill, and he kept telling his doctor, known as Cesario, that the sickness might have come from that creature. Michels relays this as what he believes Cesario said, in an episode with a surgeon who says his hospital operated on an alien. If true, it would tie the officer's illness directly to contact with a non-human being.
cesario-says-the-antibiotics-he-gave-che: A doctor named Cesario, who treated Marco Chereze, a Brazilian military police officer said to have handled a strange creature captured in the town of Varginha in 1996, says he threw everything at Chereze's infection and that the antibiotics "should have saved his life but it didn't do anything." Chereze died weeks later. The documentary filmmaker James Fox, who investigated the Varginha case and spoke with the people involved, repeats what Cesario told him, as a sign the illness was unlike anything known.
chaldean-and-sumerian-traditions-of-gods: Ancient peoples of Mesopotamia, the Chaldeans and before them the Sumerians, are said to have kept traditions of gods escaping a great catastrophe. The researcher Randall Carlson, who studies ancient disasters, mentions these traditions without naming a specific source, as support for the idea that old myths remember real cataclysms.
changes-inside-barber-s-program-after-th: Jake Barber, a helicopter pilot who says he flew in a secret effort to recover unknown craft, says things inside his program "started getting really weird" around the time the New York Times published its 2017 article on the subject. He tells it as someone who was in the program then. To Barber, the timing suggests that the article's coming out changed how the people behind the program acted.
chapel-hill-gravity-conference-kicks-off: A conference on gravity at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill is said to have set off a burst of research into anti-gravity in the 1950s. A researcher named Eric Weinstein calls it famous and says it "kicks a lot of this off," and Michels returns to it across many episodes, mostly dating it to 1957 (once to 1956), saying it was hosted by a man named Agnew Bahnson and brought together top physicists such as John Wheeler, Richard Feynman and Freeman Dyson, along with Louis Witten from the Martin company. Michels also says it was sponsored by Wright Air Field, which became Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, a place he calls "perhaps the epicenter of all UFO mythology," and ties the meeting to the birth of quantum gravity and string theory. A guest named Bob Maguire credits Wheeler with starting it, backed by two industrialists, with Feynman as first speaker. To the tellers, it suggests serious science and military interest in controlling gravity began there.
chariots-of-fire-as-angelic-vehicles: The Bible describes vehicles called "the chariots of God or the chariots of Israel or the chariots of fire," and these can be read as craft used by angels. Tim Alberino, a guest who came on the show to tell of a giant he says was captured in Afghanistan, offers this reading of the biblical stories himself. If he is right, ancient scripture would be describing flying vehicles.
charlemagne-and-the-tyrants-of-the-air: In the time of Charlemagne, the medieval king of the Franks, sightings of craft in the sky over France were said to be so common that panic broke out at the French court, and Charlemagne considered declaring war on these "tyrants of the air." The philosopher Jason Jorjani tells this on the show, drawing on the book The Gods of Eden by William Bramley. If true, people were seeing and fearing unknown things in the sky more than a thousand years ago.
charles-and-drew-s-electrostatic-thrust-: In experiments run by Charles Buhler and a colleague named Drew, devices meant to produce electrostatic thrust, a push made by electric charge without fuel, were tested in a shielded chamber in Buhler's lab. The claim is that you power the device up, unplug it from the wall, and the thrust "continues indefinitely." A researcher named David relays this claim, which also involves Buhler and a man named Tim Ventura, and he sounds wary as he tells it. If it held up, it would be a push with no power going in.
charles-buhler-leaves-nasa-for-propellan: In the 2020s, Charles Buhler, whom Michels calls NASA's top scientist in electrostatics (the study of static electric charge), left the space agency to start a company building a gravity-based propulsion system that needs no fuel thrown out the back. According to Michels, Buhler says this system comes from the work of the earlier inventor Thomas Townsend Brown. Michels tells it himself as a sign that Brown's ideas are being taken seriously at the top.
charles-buhler-leaves-nasa-to-found-exod: Charles Buhler, said to be NASA's lead scientist on electrostatics, the study of static electric charges, at Cape Kennedy, has left NASA to start his own company. Michels says the company is called Exodus Space and works on propellantless propulsion, moving a craft without pushing out fuel or exhaust. He says Buhler credits the idea to Thomas Townsend Brown, an inventor of such ideas. Michels tells this himself in two episodes, once without naming the company, as a sign that this kind of propulsion is being taken seriously.
charles-burney-and-the-ivory-tower-of-ur: A scholar named Charles Burney, whom a researcher named Matt LaCroix calls "the grandfather of Urartian history," shaped how academics understand Urartu, an ancient kingdom around Lake Van in what is now Turkey. LaCroix brings him up on Michels' show without naming a source, as the figure behind an established, ivory-tower view of the region's past that LaCroix wants to question.
charles-fort-we-are-property-like-britis: Humans are said to be the property of some other, hidden power, owned the way Britain held India under the Raj, its period of colonial rule there. The idea goes back to the writer Charles Fort, a collector of strange and unexplained reports. The philosopher Jason Jorjani tells it in a 2025 episode. He says Fort was "the first person to theorize about this with regard to the UFO phenomenon", back in the 1920s, and Jorjani is the one who uses the comparison with British India. If true, it would mean that humanity is run by something it cannot see. Salvatore Pais, a Navy scientist who holds patents on unusual craft designs, points to the same idea in another 2025 episode. He quotes Fort's line, "I believe we are property", and tells listeners to "read that book". The book is Fort's The Book of the Damned, published in 1919. Pais does not mention the Raj.
charles-hall-and-the-tall-whites-at-indi: In the 1960s, a man named Charles Hall, whom Michels calls a colonel and a whistleblower, says he lived for years alongside tall, white alien beings while stationed at Indian Springs Valley in Nevada. Michels brings Hall up on three different episodes, once saying he had just interviewed him. In those later tellings he places it at Area 51, the secret Air Force test site in Nevada, instead of Indian Springs.
charles-hall-flown-by-the-tall-whites-to: In the 1960s, at the Nevada Test Site near Area 51, a secret military base, a man named Charles Hall says he hurt his knee and was flown by the Tall Whites, tall pale beings he says he lived alongside, up to their base to see whether he needed surgery. Hall tells it at first hand, naming the base as Area 53 or 54, describing the craft as a cargo ship and saying US generals were there, and he writes about these years in his book Millennial Hospitality. Michels retells it more briefly, as Hall being flown from Area 51 to Area 52 and then Area 53.
charles-hall-s-air-force-service-records: Charles Hall, a man who says he served at a secret Nevada test site in the 1960s, really was in the Air Force, and Jesse Michels says he has the proof. Michels says it himself, citing Hall's DD214, the official record the US military gives when someone leaves service: "He was in the Air Force and I have the record." He brings it up against people who doubt Hall's stories from his time there.
charles-manson-as-mk-ultra-patient-1968: Michels says that Charles Manson, the cult leader whose followers committed murders in Los Angeles in 1969, was a patient of MK Ultra, the CIA's secret mind-control research program. He credits a friend in Los Angeles, the writer Tom O'Neill, with documenting this well, and links it to a psychiatrist named Jolly West. In a later episode he repeats it more cautiously, saying Manson was "probably" a patient and naming no source, an idea that would tie one of America's most notorious crimes to government experiments.
charles-s-path-from-hidden-momentum-to-p: A NASA engineer named Charles Buhler says he has found a way to make a device push itself using electric charge alone, with no fuel thrown out the back. He tells Michels that he first saw the strange forces in his lab in 2010, and that for two years he and a collaborator he calls Drew believed the push came from turning momentum stored in electric and magnetic fields into ordinary motion, an idea his wife pointed out and they then tested. It was not until 2018, Buhler says, that he realised he "didn't even need the current", only static charge, which he presents as a new kind of propulsion.
charlie-duke-vs-bart-sibrel-debate-on-da: In 2025 a podcast host named Danny Jones put Bart Sibrel, a leading figure among those who say the Moon landings were faked, face to face with Charlie Duke, one of the last living Apollo astronauts, then 90 years old, and the two argued it out. Michels mentions this himself while talking with the comedian and podcaster Joe Rogan. He brings it up as a striking clash over whether people really walked on the Moon.
charlie-red-star-sighting-at-carman-mani: In 1975, near the town of Carman in Manitoba, Canada, the light known locally as Charlie Red Star suddenly appeared in front of a car full of watchers. The UFO researcher Grant Cameron says he was there: they had turned the car to go back in, and "boom, it appeared from the left to the right." He tells it as his own sighting of the light that people in the area were reporting.
charlie-s-career-turns-to-medical-art-an: Charlie Foltz, a witness in the Allagash case, an alien abduction he and others say they went through in 1976, says he was training himself to be a school teacher before it happened. Afterward, he says, his career turned instead to medical art and imaging. He tells it himself on Michels's show, as one of the ways he says the experience changed his life.
charlie-s-unexplained-punch-biopsy-scar-: A man named Charlie Foltz says he has a small, unexplained scar near his scrotum that looks like a punch biopsy scar, the small round mark left when a doctor takes a plug of skin for testing. Foltz ties it to what he says happened to him in 1976 at the Allagash Waterway, a wilderness area in Maine, and he tells it on an episode about alien abductions. If true, it would be physical evidence that he was examined by someone during an abduction.
charon-ferryman-myth-comes-from-the-epic: In Greek myth, Charon is the ferryman who carries the dead across the river Styx into the underworld. A researcher of ancient history named Matt LaCroix says this image came from the Epic of Gilgamesh, an ancient poem from Mesopotamia, which he calls "the oldest recorded record of that." He gives no further source beyond a work called The Epic of Humanity, and he tells it to show that later myths borrowed from much older stories.
chase-and-yonas-cognitive-enhancement-pa: Around 2020, two engineers at Lockheed Martin, an American weapons and aircraft company, named Charles Chase and Gerald Yonas, filed a patent called "cognitive enhancement using feedback", meaning a way to boost thinking. Michels tells this himself while discussing a UFO book the Pentagon tried to censor. He raises it as a sign that a big defense company was working on ways to improve the human mind.
chase-brandon-book-on-hillenkoetter-and-: A former CIA man is said to have hidden real secrets about the 1947 Roswell crash inside a novel. Roswell is the town in New Mexico where many believe a craft from elsewhere came down. The man is Chase Brandon, who Michels says worked as the CIA's liaison to Hollywood. His book is The Cryptos Conundrum, published, as Michels has it, in 2012. Michels says Chase Brandon may be a pen name. Michels raises the book again and again. He says it deals with Roscoe Hillenkoetter, "one of the first CIA directors," and how he handled Roswell. Other times he stresses a secret committee on non-human intelligence, or a group called the Office of Strategic Assessment. He also says the book opens with a quote from the philosopher Francis Bacon: some truths are so strange they have to be hidden in fiction. Michels credits the UFO researcher Stanton Friedman as well. The other teller is a UFO researcher named Grant Cameron, who speaks without naming a source. He says the book was about how the CIA handled the Roswell crash, and that "according to some of the stories" the manuscript went through official review eight times. If true, it would mean the CIA let a true account out under cover of fiction.
chase-brandon-opens-a-cia-liaison-operat: Around 1996, a man named Chase Brandon is said to have arrived in Hollywood to open a CIA office, the CIA being the US Central Intelligence Agency, to advise filmmakers on subjects like UFOs. Bryce Zabel, a guest who was working in Hollywood at the time, tells it as something he saw happen. Michels adds that Brandon, the official CIA liaison to Hollywood, was a cousin of the actor Tommy Lee Jones, a star of the alien film Men in Black. To the tellers, it suggests the government had a hand in how films showed aliens.
chase-county-nebraska-deputy-sees-30-50-: Over the winter of 2019 to 2020, a sheriff's deputy in Chase County, Nebraska, is said to have reported seeing 30 to 50 drones along with a large mothership, while reports from Colorado said the drones flew not as a pack but as a single unit. Marik von Rennenkampff, a guest on an episode debating UFO skepticism, reads these out from reports and names a man called Doug Johnson as a source. If true, it would mean large, coordinated groups of unknown craft flew over the American plains.
chase-letter-after-june-1967-meeting-of-: In June 1967 an Air Force officer named Lewis Chase held a big meeting with other base UFO officers, the people at each Air Force base assigned to handle UFO reports, and afterward wrote a letter about it. Robert Salas, a former Air Force nuclear missile officer, brings it up as a document from the time the Air Force was paying the University of Colorado to study UFOs. He tells it as part of the paper trail on how the Air Force handled reports of UFOs near nuclear missile bases.
checking-out-scientology-while-setting-u: A physicist named Hal Puthoff says that in the early 1970s, while setting up a remote viewing program, an effort to test whether people can describe distant places using only the mind, he and his team looked into "everything": Silva Mind Control, a self-help mind training course, Scientology, and more. Puthoff tells Michels he found some of Scientology's techniques "definitely of value" but cut ties with the group in the mid 1970s.
chemical-analysis-of-the-red-pyramid-sta: Chemical tests taken around 2022 of the staining on the walls of the Red Pyramid, a pyramid at Dahshur in Egypt, are said to prove conclusively that the stains have nothing to do with bats. Geoffrey Drumm, who says an alien showed him the true purpose of the pyramids, tells this on Michels's show without naming who did the tests, as support for his view that the pyramids had some other use.
cheney-and-bush-as-possible-disclosure-g: In the 2000s, President George W. Bush may have thought about revealing what the government knows about UFOs, and the name of his vice president, Dick Cheney, keeps coming up in that talk. Michels says this himself, as things you hear around, without naming a source. If true, the decision to keep UFO secrets would have reached the White House.
chereze-family-wins-death-certificate-af: After a long legal fight, the family of Marco Chereze, a man who died in Varginha, Brazil, after the events there in 1996, finally got his death certificate, issued by a laboratory called IPD. The filmmaker James Fox tells this, passing on what a researcher named Roger Leir and a woman named Marta told him, as part of the case that a live creature was captured in Varginha.
chereze-s-12-14-day-illness-and-visits-t: In 1996 in Varginha, Brazil, where some say a strange creature was caught, a military policeman named Marco Chereze fell ill with an infection that lasted about 12 or 14 days, and he saw three or four doctors about what they took for sciatica, a kind of back pain. This comes from Ahmed Foratu, a witness at the hospital in Varginha, who says he saw it first-hand. Those who tell the wider story link Chereze's death to his contact with the creature.
chereze-s-rare-infection-1996: In Varginha, a town in Brazil, a soldier named Marco Chereze is said to have died in 1996 of an infection after contact with a creature people there say they saw that year. A man named Armando Fortunato tells Michels the infection was "extremely rare, not impossible," pointing to a doctor named Gianini. If true, it would suggest the soldier caught something unusual from the being.
chereze-s-sister-says-he-had-contact-wit: In 1996, in the Brazilian town of Varginha, where people say a strange creature was caught, the sister of a military police officer named Marco Chereze said her brother had had contact with the alien. Chereze later fell ill and died. Ahmed Foratu, a guest who speaks as a witness to the hospital events in Varginha, passes on what the sister said, as a sign that Chereze's illness was tied to the creature.
chernobyl-dogs-rapidly-evolved: Dogs living around Chernobyl, the site of a nuclear disaster, have evolved faster than any other dogs. Michels mentions this himself from an article he says came out that month, which he does not name, in an episode with a guest who says aliens taught him physics. He brings it up as an example of how radiation might drive fast change in living things.
chess-game-with-gaddafi-on-russia-day-20: In 2011, in Tripoli, Libya, a Russian regional leader went to see Muammar Gaddafi, Libya's ruler, during the war there and played chess with him. The teller is the former president of one of Russia's republics, who also says he was taken by aliens in 1997, and he tells it as something he did himself: at first Gaddafi "was nowhere to be seen," and then "I arrived. It was the 12th of June, Russia day." He tells it to show the unusual access he had to world leaders.
chetan-prakash-shows-quantum-wave-functi: A scientist named Donald Hoffman says his collaborator, the mathematician Chetan Prakash, has shown that the wave functions physicists use to describe free particles in quantum theory are "precisely the same thing" as Markov chains, a mathematical model of processes that move step by step at random. Hoffman tells Michels this holds in certain cases and that he thinks it is quite general, which to him would mean the basic stuff of physics could come out of something deeper.
chief-neurosurgeon-requests-meeting-via-: During his filming in Varginha, Brazil, the chief neurosurgeon at the town's main hospital, Hospital Regional, a doctor named Italo Venturelli, unexpectedly asked to meet, by a back way in. The documentary filmmaker James Fox tells this in a clip from his own film, in which his team says, "We received an unexpected request for a meeting from the chief neurosurgeon at Hospital Regional." It matters because that hospital is where, in the 1996 Varginha accounts, a being from the crash was said to have been treated.
chief-of-aerospace-medicine-attached-to-: A senior doctor who served as a chief of aerospace medicine, the field that looks after the health of pilots and astronauts, is said to have seen something unexplained while working with NASA, the US space agency, and the Air Force. Michels says he interviewed the man himself, but does not name him or say what was seen. It is told as a sign that even top-ranking people in these agencies have had sightings.
childhood-daylight-disc-sighting-1963: Around 1963, in Charlotte, North Carolina, a boy saw a "perfectly seamless disc" in broad daylight. That boy was Steven Greer, a guest who argues that UFO secrets are kept by a small group of powerful people around the world, and he tells it as his own childhood memory.
childhood-fall-from-a-garage-roof-soften: Dan Sherman, a former military sergeant who says a US intelligence agency hired him to communicate with aliens, says that as a child at home he was up by a garage roof when a branch snapped and he fell about 25 feet. As he tells it, the fall was softened by a kind of warmth. Sherman tells it to Michels as his own memory, as an early sign that something unusual was around him.
childhood-lights-near-the-gateway-arch: As a boy in O'Fallon Park in St. Louis, Missouri, near the city's Gateway Arch, Michael Johnson says he would see lights going by in the sky. Johnson, an Air Force veteran who says he was later taken by beings, tells it as one of his own childhood memories.
childhood-saucer-over-football-field-art: A former president of a Russian republic, named Kiran Ilum Xenov in the transcript, says that as a boy playing football he and a few dozen other boys watched a saucer hover over the football field. He tells Michels this was one of several sightings in his life, along with others at Artek, a well-known Soviet children's summer camp near Mount Ayu-Dag in Crimea, and later during his service in the Soviet army.
childhood-sighting-of-a-wobbling-reddish: Around 1976, in the UK, a twelve-year-old looked out of his bedroom window and saw a reddish-orange glowing light moving in an arc down to the horizon. The boy was Gary McKinnon, a computer hacker who says he later found signs of a secret space programme inside the files of NASA, the US space agency. He tells it as the one sighting he had himself.
childhood-ufo-and-nasal-brain-implant-at: Steve Colbern, a scientist who studies objects he believes are alien implants in human bodies, says that at age five, in Oxnard, California, he had an experience with a UFO. He tells Michels he thinks that is when "they" put an implant into his brain through his nose, which, if true, would make him one of the people he studies.
childhood-visits-from-little-gray-beings: A scientist named John Blitch, who worked for DARPA, the Pentagon's agency for advanced research, says that as a child in Peabody, Massachusetts, he was visited by "little gray guys" in his bedroom. He tells it as his own memory from the 1960s and 70s. It is part of why the episode calls him a scientist abducted by an alien.
children-gain-psychic-powers-after-seein: In the early 1970s, children in the United States, Britain and China were said to suddenly do psychic things after watching Uri Geller, a performer who claimed mind powers, on television. The researcher Greg Malatzi tells this from newspaper articles of the time, in a story that also involves a man named Andrija Puharich. It is told as a sign that something about Geller seemed to spread to the people watching him.
children-shifting-random-number-generato: A man named Jordan Jose, who says he was taken into a secret UFO-related program as a child, claims that he and other children could push random number generators, machines that spit out chance results, far away from chance just by thinking. He tells Michels this happened around 2008 to 2010 at a place in Western New York called Baker Victory Services, and that the kids pushed the machines by many "sigmas", a statistical measure of how unlikely a result is, and held them there for hours. If true, it would mean the mind can directly affect physical machines.
children-taught-physics-by-the-ghost: Some children say a visitor they call "the ghost" comes and teaches them physics. Dave Rossi, a guest who says aliens taught him advanced physics too, says he has met such families and been allowed to talk with the children, who told him, "the ghost comes and tells me." If true, it would mean these lessons are not his alone.
children-who-witnessed-the-irkutsk-light: In 2011, children in the Irkutsk region of Siberia, in Russia, said they saw a strange light in the sky, one of them recalling: "I heard a rumble, and then I saw a pink light. Everything was lit with pink color. I thought it was an alien." Michels brings in their words from a report on Russia's Channel 1, a national television station.
chilean-navy-ufo-video-solved-as-a-dista: A spectacular-looking UFO video filmed by the Chilean Navy, released by the journalist Leslie Kean in a Huffington Post article that the teller dates to 2016 or 2017, turned out to show a distant plane. The well-known UFO skeptic Mick West tells it as a case he looked into, and he stresses that official investigators spent two years ruling things out and were still wrong. He uses it to show that even long official studies can miss an ordinary answer.
chimney-rock-marks-the-moon-s-18-6-year-: At Chimney Rock in Colorado, two tall pinnacles of rock are said to frame the exact spot where, once every 18.6 years, the moon can be seen rising between them. A researcher named Randall Carlson describes this to Michels, without naming a source, as evidence that the people who used the site were tracking the moon's long cycle with care.
china-agrees-to-forgo-a-nuclear-program-: In 1963 China, then led by Mao Zedong, agreed not to pursue any nuclear program at all. Dan Sheehan, a researcher, says this without naming a source. He tells it as part of the story of President John F. Kennedy, and it would mean a major nuclear deal was reached that year.
china-holds-at-least-one-craft-via-putho: China holds at least one recovered craft of unknown origin, according to Eric W. Davis, a physicist who has worked on Pentagon research. Davis says he knows this through a scientist named Hal Puthoff, who he thinks may have learned it officially through work for the Defense Intelligence Agency, the Pentagon's military spy service. If true, the US would not be the only country holding such a craft.
china-injecting-children-to-raise-iq-202: China is said to be injecting its people, its children, with something to raise their intelligence. The comedian Kurt Metzger says he got this from the podcaster Joe Rogan, who in turn said intelligence people had told him, so it reaches the show third-hand.
china-reverse-engineering-downed-craft: China is said to have craft of unknown origin that came down on its territory and to be working to copy their technology. Bob Maguire, a former contractor for the CIA, the US spy agency, says "we know for a fact" this is happening, without naming a source.
chinese-academy-of-social-science-psychi: A man named Dan Sheehan says that on a visit to Beijing in the 1990s, a woman named Jen Jo Jing took him straight to a laboratory at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, a Chinese state research body. There, he says, she showed him all the experiments they were running on psychic abilities as they tried to work out what it all was. Sheehan tells it as something he saw himself, and if true it would mean China's government was studying psychic powers.
chinese-journal-of-ufo-research-tacitly-: China publishes a magazine called the Journal of UFO Research, and the claim is that it ran with the quiet approval of the Chinese Communist Party in the late 1990s. A former US intelligence officer turned whistleblower named David Grusch mentions it as a sign that China treats the subject more openly than the United States.
chinese-nationals-detained-after-drone-i: In 2024, after drones flew into the airspace over MacDill and Langley, two US Air Force bases, Chinese citizens were taken into custody. Jake Barber, a former helicopter pilot who says he once carried a recovered craft, says this is what is known about those incidents. He brings it up to point to who might be behind some of the drone sightings.
chinese-papers-on-tracking-ufos: China has published a couple of scientific papers on how to track UFOs, Michels says in passing during a talk about UFO physics and government disclosure. He does not name the papers. He raises them as a sign that other countries are studying the subject seriously too.
chinese-spy-balloon-as-standard-of-evide: In 2023 a Chinese spy balloon drifted across American skies, and everybody could see it. Michael Shermer, a researcher and skeptic who debated the host, brings it up without naming a source. He offers it as the kind of plain, shared evidence he says a real visiting craft would also leave.
chinese-spy-balloon-over-the-aleutians-a: Michels suggests that the Chinese spy balloon of January 2023, which flew over Alaska's Aleutian Islands and then over Montana near Malmstrom, an Air Force base with nuclear missiles, was really testing the limits of American radar. He tells this himself, naming no source, in a conversation with a startup that tries to capture UFOs on camera. His point is that the balloon may have been finding out what US radar can and cannot see.
chinese-uap-task-force-reported-in-south: China set up its own team to study UAP, the government term for UFOs, and said so openly in a newspaper. That is the claim told on the podcast. A former intelligence officer named David Grusch, who says he was told about secret programs that recover crashed craft, points to an article in the South China Morning Post newspaper. He dates it to "June 2021" and says its message was "Oh yeah, we have a UAP task force too." Luis Elizondo, the former head of a small Pentagon office that studied unexplained aerial reports, tells it separately. He remembers it a little differently: he calls the paper "the China Morning Sun", dates it only to "a couple years ago", and says the article was about something called "the five continents initiative". Both bring it up to suggest that the United States is not the only power quietly studying the subject.
chinese-ufology-after-mao-and-the-falun-: The study of UFOs in China, according to the UFO historian Richard Dolan, took its shape from the death of the Chinese leader Mao Zedong in 1976 and runs up to the government's crackdown on Falun Gong, a spiritual movement, in the late 1990s. Dolan says "everything revolves around" Mao's death and draws on the writer Paul Dong, suggesting that Chinese UFO research rose and fell with the country's politics.
chirality-as-evidence-for-god-in-the-cas: Chirality, the fact that the molecules of life come in one handed form rather than a mirror-image mix, is offered as evidence for God. Greg Rogers, a NASA doctor, says he put the argument in a book he wrote years ago, The Case for God, which he does not date.
choosing-among-sar-images-for-the-gran-s: For a scan of Gran Sasso, a mountain in Italy, a researcher had to order several satellite radar images and pick the best one. The radar is SAR, synthetic aperture radar, which builds pictures from radar echoes bounced off the ground from space. Filippo Biondi, an engineer who works with this radar, describes doing it himself, saying he had to "order um different images in order to choose the best one," as part of explaining how his method for seeing under the ground works.
chris-aubeck-s-book-saucers-shows-saucer: A book called Saucers, by a writer named Chris Aubeck, shows that saucer-shaped objects are actually rare in reports of strange things in the sky. The Swedish UFO researcher Clas Svahn, who keeps a very large archive of such reports, brings up the book and praises Aubeck: "he's fantastic. His books are fantastic."
chris-bledsoe-case-in-north-carolina: A man named Chris Bledsoe of Fayetteville, North Carolina, says that from 2007 on he met beings in a craft, saw UFOs appear at his house, and once a year receives prophecies from a divine figure he calls "the Lady", whom Michels links to the Egyptian goddess Hathor. Michels tells this himself across several episodes, and says that once Bledsoe began attracting UFOs he was visited by high-ranking people, among them the physicist Hal Puthoff, whom Michels places at the CIA and NASA, and Jim Semivan, a senior CIA officer, while also crediting a man named Timothy Taylor and the book UFO of God. Michels tells it as a case where serious intelligence people took an experiencer's story seriously.
chris-bledsoe-claims-similar-ufo-sensiti: A North Carolina man named Chris Bledsoe claims a special sensitivity to UFOs, saying he can somehow sense or connect with them. Michels mentions him in passing to his guest, the UFO researcher Jacques Vallee, as one of "a couple of other people who sort of claim similar things."
chris-bledsoe-flies-a-craft-down-the-cap: In 2007 a man named Chris Bledsoe is said to have found himself flying a craft along the Cape Fear River in North Carolina: "Suddenly the window opened and there was the Cape Fear River," as he put it. A UFO researcher named Grant Cameron tells this on the show, passing on what Bledsoe told him. If true, an ordinary man was taken aboard and even shown the controls of an unknown craft.
chris-bledsoe-s-inconclusive-visit-to-sk: A man named Chris Bledsoe visited Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property famous for reports of strange events, during filming there, but the footage was never shown. The ranch's owner, Brandon Fugal, tells Michels, "We didn't end up airing um that content," and the visit is described as having turned up nothing conclusive.
chris-bledsoe-s-lady-and-the-guardians-2: Starting in 2007, a man named Chris Bledsoe has reported many encounters that look nothing like craft or lights, but rather a glowing feminine presence he calls the Lady. Bledsoe believes she is a non-human intelligence linked to the Big Dipper, the familiar pattern of stars, and that her companions call themselves the Guardians. Michels tells this himself in two episodes, passing on what Bledsoe says.
chris-bledsoe-s-message-from-the-lady: A being Chris Bledsoe calls "the lady" gave him a message: she has had many names through history, God is God, we don't know what we think we know, and people need to stop, think again and "be good children" because "we're going off the cliff." Bledsoe, a man who says he has had these encounters himself, gives the message in his own words in a clip on an episode with the researcher Grant Cameron.
chris-invited-to-take-part-in-revealing-: Chris Bledsoe, a man who says UFOs appear around him, says he has been invited, by way of Egyptian antiquities authorities, to go to Giza, the site of the great pyramids in Egypt, and take part in releasing "something that was hidden." He tells Michels it is set for 2027, and does not say what the hidden thing is.
chris-langan-sees-a-disc-near-malmstrom: A huge oval saucer was suddenly hanging in the sky over a campground near Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana, according to a man named Chris Langan. He says he was working for the Forest Service, the US agency that runs the national forests, and was sitting in one of its pickup trucks when he looked up and saw it. Langan tells it as his own sighting, and Michels repeats it on another episode, saying Langan saw UFOs near the base.
chris-mellon-s-aerospace-insider-contact: Chris Mellon, a former Pentagon intelligence official, had set up a meeting with a man who worked inside a secret UFO program, but two weeks before they were to meet, the man suddenly died of a heart attack. Michels tells this story twice, in 2022 and 2023, as something Mellon has said. The first time he only says Mellon almost met the man, and the second time he adds the heart attack and the timing. It is told as a sign of how hard it is to get insiders to talk.
chris-mellon-says-disclosure-green-light: A UFO researcher named Grant Cameron says that the push for the US government to reveal what it knows about UFOs did not die when Hillary Clinton lost the 2016 presidential election. Cameron tells Michels he phoned Chris Mellon, a man involved in that effort, the same day and asked whether it was dead, and Mellon answered: "Green light still going. It's even bigger than before."
chris-mellon-wants-to-learn-what-cia-sci: Chris Mellon, a former Pentagon intelligence official, is said to have wanted to put one of the CIA's recent Directors of Science and Technology, the head of the agency's science branch, on the spot, saying "we need to figure out what she knows about UFOs." Michels tells this himself, as something Mellon said to him. It suggests that people pushing for disclosure believe the CIA's science office holds UFO knowledge.
chris-ramsay-s-own-associative-remote-vi: In 2023 the YouTuber Chris Ramsay trained in associative remote viewing, a practice of trying to sense with the mind a picture linked to an outcome that is not yet known, and he says the results were "really crazy," "like good results." Ramsay tells it himself and says this is what led him to start his Area 52 channel. To him it suggests the practice works.
chris-ramsay-sees-tic-tac-over-nellis: While on a commercial flight over the Nellis test range, a military testing area in Nevada, a man named Chris Ramsay saw a white oval object shaped like a Tic Tac mint, like one Michels had shown on screen. Michels passes this on from Ramsay during a debate with the UFO skeptic Mick West, as a case of an ordinary passenger seeing such an object.
chris-s-reaction-to-anomalous-metal-and-: Chris Bledsoe, a man said to attract UFOs, says that when he reacted to a piece of strange metal in Zanesville, Ohio, a NASA man named Timothy Taylor told him he had only ever seen two other people react that way. Bledsoe tells this himself, repeating Taylor's words, as a sign that something about him is unusual.
chris-s-rosetta-stone-project-to-decode-: Chris Bledsoe, a man who says UFOs appear around him, says he is working on a project he calls a "Rosetta Stone", using sensors and quantum computing with artificial intelligence to decode the phenomenon he experiences. He tells Michels he thinks that with enough data they can get "actual real time communication through the light and through sensors," which would mean talking back to whatever is behind the lights.
christian-herter-s-rule-against-meeting-: In the 1950s, Christian Herter, then a top politician in Massachusetts, had a rule that no one from the mafia could come to talk to him unless he also invited the press. Harold Malmgren, a former presidential adviser, says Herter told him this himself. In the recording the words come out as "inviting the president," though the story is about having reporters there. It is told as an example of how an honest politician kept organised crime at arm's length.
christopher-dunn-s-theory-of-advanced-to: The claim is that the granite at the Giza pyramids in Egypt was cut with tools far more advanced than anything archaeologists have found. Mario Woods, a former guard at a nuclear site, relays the work of Christopher Dunn, an engineer, and also names the geologist Robert Schoch, saying the tools used to carve the granite "are not in the archaeological array of tools of copper and wooden chisels". Michels mentions Dunn on another episode more generally, as someone who has "done all this work on just engineering anomalies" of the pyramid itself. If true, the pyramids' builders would have had technology the record does not explain.
chuck-clark-s-road-trip-tape-of-a-wobbli: A home video from the mid 1990s is said to show an orange, disc-shaped object wobbling in the night sky near Area 51, a secret Air Force test site in the Nevada desert. A UFO investigator named James Fox, who has seen the tape, credits it to a man named Chuck Clark and places it near Rachel, a tiny town close to the base. Fox describes the moment the object appears: "the next thing you see is a orange disc shaped thing just wobbling." A man named Logan, who went with Michels on a trip to the area with Bob Lazar, a man who says he once worked on alien craft there, tells it from what he was told. His version is different: he says the footage, "supposedly authentic", was shot by two college kids who wanted to see Area 51, he believes in 1995. He places it at the black mailbox, a roadside landmark where people gather to watch the sky. To those who tell it, the tape is a rare piece of film of a craft flying near the base.
chupa-chupa-beams-at-colares-1977: In 1977, in the small town of Colares in northern Brazil, people reported flying objects, known locally as "Chupa Chupa", that shot beams of light down at the ground as they flew. Aldo Rebelo, a former Brazilian defense minister, tells it on the show: "As it was flying, the object would cast down a beam of light." Coming from a former minister, it would mean the Brazilian state takes the case seriously.
cia-activity-underneath-disneyland: Walt Disney is said to have been a Rosicrucian, a member of a secretive mystical order, who let the CIA "do stuff to him underneath Disneyland," and that this is why Disney child stars "turn out how they do." The comedian Kurt Metzger says it twice on the same episode and insists "that's real," without naming where he heard it.
cia-and-andrija-puharich-s-elf-telepathy: The CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency, is said to have been running experiments as early as the 1960s under a doctor named Andrija Puharich, using extremely low frequency radio waves, in work linked to telepathy and to children dubbed 'space kids'. Michels says this himself, presenting it as something known, without naming a source. If true, it would mean the government was testing radio waves on the mind decades ago.
cia-approaches-puthoff-over-russian-psyc: In the early 1970s, after a researcher named Hal Puthoff wrote up psychic experiments at the Stanford Research Institute that he says came out accurate, the CIA came knocking at his door. Puthoff tells it himself: the agency told him they had been looking for him, because the Russians had spent millions of dollars for years on this work at their best institutes with their best people. If true, it is how the US government began its own interest in psychic spying.
cia-brings-anomalous-experience-files-to: The CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency, is said to have approached Garry Nolan, a Stanford scientist, with files on people who had gone through strange, unexplained experiences. Michels tells this himself in two episodes without naming a source, and in the second he dates it to about 2016 and says the files dealt with how encounters with UAP, the government's term for UFOs, affected people's bodies. If true, it means the agency wanted outside scientists to study the physical harm from these encounters.
cia-compartment-so-restricted-nothing-wa: A former CIA officer named Rolf Mowatt-Larssen says there was a matter inside the CIA so tightly held that nothing about it was put into any kind of record. He tells Michels this was a "very specific thing", "highly unusual" and "irregular" even by the agency's standards, though he does not say what the matter was.
cia-created-ufo-news-outlet-appearing-ar: Around 2018, when a film about a man named Bob Lazar came out, a UFO news outlet appeared online, run from overseas, that was in truth set up by the CIA, the US spy agency. That is the claim of the filmmaker and journalist Jeremy Corbell, who says he has it from named sources and puts it bluntly: "That is a CIA stood up media source." If true, it would mean the spy agency was shaping UFO news from the inside.
cia-director-bob-gates-s-first-visit-to-: In the fall of 1992, Bob Gates, then director of the CIA, the US spy agency for foreign affairs, made his first visit to Moscow and gave a toast there. Rolf Mowatt-Larssen, a former CIA officer, says he was on the trip and will "never forget" it. He tells it as a moment he saw himself.
cia-document-mandating-shaping-the-emerg: A document from the CIA, the US spy agency, set out a mandate to "shape the emerging UAP narrative", UAP being the government's newer name for UFOs, according to Jeremy Corbell, a filmmaker who reports on the subject. Corbell says he was shown this document himself, and he names the journalist George Knapp and the Navy pilot David Fravor in telling it. No date is given, but if true it would mean the agency set out on purpose to steer how the public came to understand UFOs.
cia-documents-describing-flat-mirror-lik: In the 1950s, papers of the CIA, the US spy agency, described UFOs as "flat mirror-like objects that reflect light". Michels says this himself, without naming the exact documents, during a heated debate with a well-known skeptic. He cites it to show that the government's own records from that time described something solid and physical.
cia-formed-at-behest-of-brown-brothers-h: The CIA, America's main foreign spy agency, was formed in the 1940s at the urging of Brown Brothers Harriman, a private investment firm. Michels says this is the core of a history of American intelligence by a man named Dan Sheehan, covering the years after the OSS, the US spy service of the Second World War. Michels raises it in a talk with the analyst Matthew Pines to suggest that private money helped shape the secret side of government from the start.
cia-funded-psychological-conditioning-at: At an institute in Montreal, Canada, people are said to have undergone "massive psychological conditioning" while the place was funded for a long time by the CIA, the US spy agency, in the 1950s and 60s. The researcher Peter Levenda brings this up in passing as an example and names no source for it, though the story is linked to a man named Ewen Cameron. If true, it would mean an American intelligence agency was paying for efforts to reshape people's minds on foreign soil.
cia-gateway-documents-show-psionics-were: CIA files from the 1980s known as the Gateway documents show the agency took psionics, claimed powers of the mind, seriously, according to the journalist Ross Coulthart. Coulthart makes the point on two episodes, in 2025 and 2026, saying "you've only got to read the CIA Gateway documents in the CIA files, and they show that that's actually not true" to anyone who says such ideas were never taken seriously by the government.
cia-implants-a-chip-in-lynn-kyle-s-skull: A man named Lynn Kyle is said to have had a chip put in his skull without his knowledge by his psychologist, who worked for the CIA, the American spy agency, and this is offered as the origin of the tinfoil hat. The comedian Kurt Metzger tells it, passing on the story from Kyle and from a man named Carlos Delgado. If true, it would mean the agency secretly implanted devices in people.
cia-jump-room-to-mars-that-obama-used: The story goes that people from the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency, ride an elevator up to the fifth floor of a building, cross over, and from there "jump" to Mars, and that Barack Obama, the former US president, has been there. The UFO researcher Grant Cameron tells it on the show, passing on what Andrew Basiago, a man he cites by name, has said. If true, it would mean the government secretly has instant travel to another planet.
cia-killed-ahmad-shah-massoud-before-9-1: Ahmad Shah Massoud, who led the Northern Alliance, an Afghan group fighting the Taliban, is said to have been killed by the CIA, the US foreign spy agency, just before the September 11, 2001 attacks; the story also holds that the US created al-Qaeda, the group behind those attacks, to fight the Soviet Union in Afghanistan. The philosopher Jason Jorjani says this to Michels, without naming a source, calling Massoud "a decent guy". If true, it would mean the US helped build the enemy it later fought.
cia-memo-calls-ufos-a-national-security-: In 1952 the CIA wrote a memo calling UFOs a matter of national security that could set off mass hysteria and panic. Michels tells this himself and quotes the memo: "The flying saucer situation contains two elements of danger, which in a situation of international tension have national security implications. These are psychological and air vulnerability." He credits the memo to Walter B. Smith of the CIA and offers it as proof that the agency took the subject seriously.
cia-memo-popularizing-the-term-conspirac: A memo from the CIA, the US spy agency, written in the 1970s, said the agency would popularize the word "conspiracy" so that people would look away from certain subjects. Michels says this himself while debating a well-known skeptic, without naming or quoting the memo further. If true, it would mean the government deliberately shaped how the public talks about hidden matters.
cia-offer-to-head-an-elf-research-depart: Sometime between 1977 and 1979, a man named Bob Beck is said to have come to the house of Andrija Puharich, the scientist this episode is about, with word that the CIA, the US spy agency, wanted someone to head a research department on ELF, meaning extremely low frequency radio waves. A researcher on the episode, who is not named, tells it in summary and says it rests on Puharich's own handwritten notes on a legal pad. If it happened, it would mean the spy agency was quietly looking for people to lead work on these waves.
cia-office-of-research-and-development-c: After MK Ultra, the CIA's secret programme of experiments on the human mind, its work was carried on by a CIA division called the Office of Research and Development, led by a man named Stephen Aldrich. Michels takes this from The Search for the Manchurian Candidate, a book by the writer John Marks. He tells it as the link between the CIA's mind experiments and the later US research into remote viewing, the claimed ability to see distant places with the mind.
cia-official-blocking-transfer-of-a-non-: An official named Greenwald, director of science and technology at the CIA, is said to have blocked the transfer of a UFO between the aerospace companies Lockheed and Bigelow.
