Michels says this himself in a heated episode with the filmmaker Jeremy Corbell, pointing back to an earlier interview with James Lacatski, a former Pentagon intelligence official, and citing the Las Vegas journalist George Knapp. If true, it would mean a private company holds a craft and the CIA has stepped in to control where it goes.
cia-oga-and-jsoc-perform-crash-retrieval: Recovering crashed UFOs is said to be handled by the CIA's OGA, short for "other government agency", created in 2002, together with JSOC, the Joint Special Operations Command that runs the US military's elite special forces. An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb says this, citing reporting by a man named Chris Sharp and others. Michels says the UFO crash retrieval program is rumoured to work closely with JSOC, and names a secretive unit called Grey Fox, or ISA, as part of it. If true, it would mean special forces units are the ones picking up crashed craft.
cia-osi-takes-ufo-research-underground-b: In 1952 the CIA's Office of Scientific Intelligence, its science analysis branch, took the real UFO investigations underground, while Project Blue Book, the Air Force's public UFO study of the 1950s and 60s, served as a psychological operation on the American people. Michels tells this himself, once calling it a long-standing rumor and once crediting a researcher named Richard Dolan and saying the hidden side was run by the Battelle Memorial Institute, a private research institute, under a project called Stork; if true, the public study was a decoy. A 1997 history published by the CIA and written by the historian Gerald K. Haines says the Office of Scientific Intelligence formed a special study group in 1952, that the agency was urged to "conceal its interest from the media and the public", and that an Air Force intelligence center "tried to persuade the public that UFOs were not extraordinary". It does not say the research went underground or call Blue Book a cover.
cia-paid-paramilitary-bases-for-cuban-ex: Between about 1960 and 1962, a set of armed training camps for Cuban exiles was set up and paid for by the CIA, the US spy agency, at places like No Name Key in Florida, Swan Island, the Everglades and Lake Pontchartrain. A researcher named Dan Sheehan tells this in summary, without naming a source. He tells it as part of the background to the killing of President Kennedy.
cia-plan-for-a-jesus-vision-over-havana-: The CIA, the US foreign spy agency, is said to have once planned to make a vision of Jesus appear in the sky over Havana, to persuade Cubans to overthrow their leader, Fidel Castro. A researcher named Peter Levenda tells Michels this without naming a source, as an example of how a government might stage something that looks like a miracle.
cia-psychiatrist-explains-why-hall-was-c: The story is that in the 1960s, on the Nevada weapons ranges, a CIA psychiatrist told a man named Charles Hall why he had been picked: 41 men had gone out before him and all came back compromised, some of them burned. Hall tells this himself, as someone who says he spent three years with tall white aliens near Area 51, a secret Air Force site in Nevada, and repeats the unnamed psychiatrist's words, a story he also tells in his book Millennial Hospitality. If true, the government was sending men into contact with these beings and losing many of them.
cia-regressionists-regress-burroughs-fro: In the 1980s, two hypnotists tied to the CIA are said to have used regression, a method of taking someone back through buried memories under hypnosis, on John Burroughs, a witness in the Rendlesham Forest case, a well-known UFO sighting in an English forest. The UFO researcher Grant Cameron tells this second-hand, as something he says he has from the people involved, and links it to two men named Bob Emenegger and Allan Sandler and to Sandler's studio in New York. If true, it would mean an intelligence agency was quietly probing what a witness remembered.
cia-remote-viewing-program: The CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency, is said to have run a remote viewing program: an effort to train people to describe faraway places and things using only their minds. The researcher Steven Greer brings it up without naming a source. He calls it "the cheap end" of secret government work and mentions Bob Monroe, a name he connects with the work. The researcher Nick Cook, also giving no source, says the government had doubts but "went ahead and did it anyway and funded it for 18 years or something." Michels raises it in two episodes. In one he says the CIA's work on remote viewing and parapsychology, the study of mind powers such as telepathy, is documented, pointing to a 2017 release under the Freedom of Information Act, a US law that lets anyone request government records. In the other he says simply that "it's been declassified." All the tellers bring it up as proof that the government took strange abilities seriously.
cia-robertson-panel-1953: In 1953 a panel of scientists convened by the CIA, known as the Robertson Panel after the physicist Howard P. Robertson who chaired it, is said to have recommended that the government debunk UFO reports. The former official Karl Nell tells Michels that declassified documents show the panel decided the government should debunk the topic to misdirect the public and "actually infiltrate" the civilian UFO organisations. A Senate staffer named Kurt McConnell tells it too, dating it to 1952 and 1953, naming Robertson and the physicist Luis Alvarez, and adding that the panel, in secret, also recommended ways to detect and track the objects. The panel's own report, dated 16 February 1953 and covering meetings held 14 to 18 January, does set out an educational programme with two aims, "training and 'debunking'," the second to bring "reduction in public interest in 'flying saucers'" through "television, motion pictures, and popular articles." It also urges security agencies to "strip the Unidentified Flying Objects of the special status they have been given and the aura of mystery." On the civilian groups, the report says they "should be watched" and that "the possible use of such groups for subversive purposes should be kept in mind"; it does not say they should be infiltrated. To the tellers, it would mean public doubt about UFOs was shaped on purpose.
cia-s-charles-cabell-the-dallas-motorcad: A CIA officer named Charles Cabell looked at Project Blue Book, the US Air Force's UFO study of the 1950s and 60s, and called it a very shoddy operation. Michels says this is written up in a book by Edward J. Ruppelt, which he does not name. He tells it in an episode that also links Cabell to Dallas, where President Kennedy was killed, to show one man turning up in many secret affairs.
cia-s-scientific-engineering-institute-f: In the 1960s and 70s, members of a research office at the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency, set up the Scientific Engineering Institute near Boston, a company secretly owned by the agency, with a rural lab on a farm of several hundred acres. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, in an episode about human experiments. He raises it as an example of the agency running hidden research behind a private front.
cia-screening-genetic-databases-for-nord: A man named Kit Green, said to be at the CIA, the US spy agency, is said to run a program that taps into consumer DNA-testing databases such as 23andMe and Ancestry.com to search for Nordic genetic markers. The philosopher Jason Jorjani tells this on the show, passing on what a man named Lyn Buchanan told him: "we know that Kit Green at the CIA has some program to access the 23 and me and like whatever ancestry.com databases." If true, the government would be quietly screening people's genes for a particular ancestry.
cia-sends-mooney-s-cherokee-book-and-ask: A book arrived at his home in North Carolina, sent by people from the CIA with a note saying "Read this," and they asked him about Native American DNA. Chris Bledsoe, a man known for reporting repeated UFO encounters, tells Jesse Michels this happened to him. The book was Myths of the Cherokee, published in 1891 by James Mooney, a collection of the tribe's old stories, which suggests the agency thought his experiences linked to those traditions.
cia-shut-down-the-reverse-engineering-ef: According to the physicist Eric W. Davis, the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency, shut down a secret effort to reverse-engineer recovered craft in 1989, because neither its own people nor the companies working on it had made any progress after several decades. Davis says he was told this firmly by someone else and is passing it on. He tells it because it would mean a long-running government program to copy unknown technology existed and failed.
cia-stargate-program-s-hits-questioned-1: The CIA, the US spy agency, ran a program called Stargate that used "remote viewers", people who claimed they could see distant places or hidden targets with their minds alone. The researcher Michael Shermer, arguing the skeptic's side with Michels, admits that "yes, they got some hits", meaning some correct answers, and he does not say where he learned this. He brings it up to question what those hits really prove.
cia-telepathy-drawing-tests-at-sri-1970: The psychic performer Uri Geller says that in the 1970s the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency, took him to Stanford Research Institute, a research lab in California. There, he says, people made drawings miles away and he had to receive them by telepathy. Geller tells it as his own experience, and if true it would mean the US government was testing psychic powers.
cia-visits-nolan-s-stanford-office-to-re: In the 2010s, people from the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency, came to the office of a Stanford University scientist to bring him into the study of UFO cases. Garry Nolan, the Stanford medical scientist himself, tells it first-hand: "when I got involved, the CIA came to my office." If true, it would mean US intelligence was quietly seeking out top scientists to look at this subject.
cic-agent-tricks-schauberger-into-signin: After the Second World War ended in 1945, an agent of the Army's counterintelligence branch named Neil Gershimer tricked an inventor named Victor Shawberger into signing all his work over to the United States, and that work ended up at Brookhaven National Lab, a government research lab on Long Island. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, in an episode asking whether Henry Kissinger oversaw a program to recover crashed UFOs. If true, it would mean the US quietly took over a European inventor's work and kept it in a national lab.
cic-interrogates-viktor-schauberger-for-: After the war in 1945, agents of the Counter Intelligence Corps, a US Army spy-catching unit, questioned an Austrian inventor named Viktor Schauberger for nine months, knowing all about his most secret work. Michels tells this from the book The Hunt for Zero Point by the historian Nick Cook, in an episode on whether Henry Kissinger oversaw a program to recover crashed UFOs. It matters to him because it suggests the Americans took Schauberger's unusual work very seriously.
cicada-3301-as-an-intelligence-recruitme: Cicada 3301, a series of hard, anonymous puzzles posted online, is said by many to have been set up by the NSA, the US electronic spying agency, or the CIA, its foreign intelligence agency, to recruit talented code breakers. Michels repeats this himself as what "a lot of people think", without naming a source. If true, spy agencies were using a public internet game to find new staff.
cigar-shaped-craft-near-turtle-mountain: A cigar-shaped object was seen near Turtle Mountain, on the road from Cuba, New Mexico, according to a woman named Christa, who tells Michels she saw it herself. "It looked like a cigar," she says. She also brings a United Airlines pilot into her account, and if she is right, a strange craft was flying over that stretch of New Mexico road.
cigar-shaped-object-in-distress-seen-by-: In January 1996, probably on the 13th, several people near the Brazilian town of Varginha are said to have seen a large cylinder-shaped craft, a bit bigger than a school bus, flying low before it came down. The documentary filmmaker James Fox, who made a film on the case called Moment of Contact, tells it more than once. He says there are a number of witnesses, and that he interviewed firsthand witnesses himself who called it cylindrical, shaped like a school bus. Fox adds that a doctor named Armando Fortunato, who did the autopsy on a military officer who later died, has two farmer friends who saw exactly this object before it crashed. A guest named Ahmed Foratu also speaks of people close to Varginha who saw a ship the size of a bus heading toward the city in those days. His version does not call them farmers and does not say the craft was in trouble. Taken together, the accounts would mean a real craft came down near the town, the start of the wider Varginha story.
cinclant-code-zebra-alert-over-object-of: Sometime in the 1980s, the US military's Atlantic Command in Norfolk, Virginia, is said to have gone to a full Code Zebra alert, a top-level alarm, over an unknown object off Newfoundland. The UFO researcher Steven Greer tells it from a man named Merle Shane McDow, who he says was working under that command at the time, and he names Admiral Harry Train, its commander, in the story, which appears in a book called Disclosure: An Illustrated History. If true, it would mean a top naval command treated an unexplained object as a real threat.
citizen-hearing-on-disclosure-2013: In 2013 a set of public hearings called the Citizen Hearing on Disclosure was held where people gave testimony about UFOs, and it is all on YouTube, according to Jake Barber, a helicopter pilot who says he retrieved a UFO. Barber recommends watching it, without saying what was said there.
city-of-11-000-structures-found-in-ecuad: A lost city of about 11,000 structures is said to have been found in the jungle of the Ecuadorian Amazon. A researcher named Luke Caverns mentions it in passing on the podcast, hedging that he thinks that is the number, and gives no further detail. If true, it would mean large ancient societies lived in places long thought to be empty wilderness.
civilizations-switching-on-at-the-same-t: Great early civilizations in Egypt, the Indus Valley in what is now Pakistan, and along China's Yellow River all seem to have "switched on" at about the same time, around 3000 BC. The writer Graham Hancock makes the point on Michels' show without naming a source, saying it was "exactly the same period that the engine of the Indus Valley civilization was switched on." To Hancock, such timing hints at a shared source or lost earlier influence behind them all.
cky-tv-film-of-object-jumping-from-the-g: In May 1975, a crew from CKY, a television station in Manitoba, Canada, is said to have filmed an object near the town of Carman leaping from the ground to 5,000 feet in the space of three or four film frames. The researcher Grant Cameron tells it, crediting a CKY documentary about the film. A passage from the French researcher Jacques Vallée, from a work titled UFOs: It Has Begun, gives more detail: on May 13th, 1975, a cameraman named Alan Carr filmed two separate sightings over Carman in front of four witnesses. Cameron adds something he says he learned by talking to the man who shot it: he was not a cameraman at all but a film editor at the studio. So the tellers agree on the film but differ on who held the camera. It is told because an object rising that fast would be beyond any known aircraft.
claiborne-pell-jack-reed-and-biden-a-ufo: Claiborne Pell, whom Michels describes as a senator from Delaware long interested in UFOs, is said to start a line of UFO interest in the US Senate that runs on to the senator Jack Reed and to Joe Biden. Michels says this himself, without naming a source. If true, interest in UFOs has been handed down quietly among a group of lawmakers.
claim-that-the-bacteria-looked-genetical: The bacteria behind the deadly infection tied to the 1996 Varginha case in Brazil looked as if it had been genetically engineered, according to a doctor that the documentary filmmaker James Fox calls Dr. Eel. Fox repeats this as his understanding of what he heard the doctor say just the day before. If true, it would suggest the infection came from something made, not natural.
claimed-carl-sagan-aliens-are-real-state: A story went around that the astronomer Carl Sagan once said he thought aliens were real, and that the remark was later blacked out of the record. The skeptic Michael Shermer brings it up to knock it down: he says he asked Sagan's widow, Ann Druyan, a friend of his he calls Annie, and she told him that never happened. If the story were true, one of the best-known doubters in science would have privately believed.
claims-of-secret-ships-to-europa-heard-a: At Contact in the Desert, a conference where people gather to talk about UFOs and contact with other beings, the writer Peter Levenda heard claims that ships may be secretly flying to Europa, an icy moon of Jupiter. He passes it on as something said there, in his words that "it could be possible we're sending ships to Europa on a regular basis." If true, it would mean a hidden space programme far beyond anything made public.
clandestine-christian-ex-special-forces-: A secretive group of Christian former special-forces soldiers once sought out a sitting member of Congress in Washington, DC, according to the congressman himself, Eric Burlison. He tells Michels he took part in it: the group, as he puts it, "kind of bumped me" while he was at a different meeting in the city, some time between 2024 and 2026. He tells it as one of the ways people with hidden knowledge of the UFO subject have tried to reach lawmakers.
clapper-and-brennan-speak-of-roswell-and: Two of President Obama's top intelligence chiefs, his director of national intelligence James Clapper and his CIA director John Brennan, are said to appear in a film, The Age of Disclosure, saying that the 1947 crash at Roswell, New Mexico, was a real event and that a being survived it. Michels raises this on several episodes, asking why such senior officials would say so if it were not true. His versions differ: once he says they speak of four beings leaving the craft and only "one surviving or something", naming a man called Jim Semivan instead of Brennan, and once he says only that they appear in the film.
clapper-asks-nsa-director-mike-rogers-fo: James Clapper, who oversaw all US intelligence agencies, is said to have called Mike Rogers, head of the NSA, the US agency that intercepts communications, and asked him for all of the agency's UFO data. Michels says Rogers himself told this in a public interview. If true, it would mean the country's top intelligence official was gathering UFO records from inside his own agencies.
clapper-on-ufo-detections-at-area-51-in-: The former US intelligence chief James Clapper says on record that the US was regularly detecting UFOs in the restricted airspace around Area 51, a secret military test site in Nevada. Michels cites this from The Age of Disclosure, a documentary in which Clapper appears, and mentions John Brennan along with him. Michels brought it up while debating a well-known skeptic, as proof that top officials take the sightings seriously.
clarkdale-cement-plant-as-egress-to-secr: A cement plant in Clarkdale, Arizona, is said to be an exit point from a hidden secret facility, which the episode treats as a UFO base. The journalist Ross Coulthart tells this, passing on what a source told him. If true, an ordinary-looking industrial site would be the doorway to an underground program.
class-1-tetra-objects-fly-in-formations-: According to James Valor of Skywatcher, a startup that says it can call up UFOs, the objects his team calls "class 1" or "tetra" usually fly in groups, in formations of three to twenty, during the company's sky-watching operations between 2021 and 2025. Valor says he saw this himself, and he tells it to Michels as one of the regular patterns his team has logged, which would mean the objects come back in organized groups.
class-2-tic-tac-objects-about-40-feet-lo: Skywatcher, a startup that tries to summon UFOs, sorts what it sees into classes, and its second class is the "tic-tac", a white oval object shaped like the mint, about 40 feet long. James Valor of Skywatcher says these were seen during the company's operations in 2022, in 2023 and in February 2025. He tells it as one of the people who saw them.
class-3-as-a-holographic-projection-or-l: Some of the strangest things seen in the sky may be projections, like holograms, or glowing balls of charged gas made by lasers, according to James Valor of Skywatcher, a startup that says it tries to call up UFOs and record them. Valor, who says he took part in the company's work between 2021 and 2025, offers this as an idea about a type of sighting the team calls Class 3, and he stresses it is "still only theory": "isn't everything in holographic sky projection?" If he is right, some of what people see up there may be a picture rather than a solid craft.
class-3-blob-a-pepto-bismol-colored-clou: One kind of unexplained object looks like a pink cloud the colour of Pepto-Bismol, with a golden core that vibrates, according to James Valor of Skywatcher, a startup that says it can call UFOs into view. Valor says he has seen these himself during the company's watches between 2021 and 2025, and that the team files them as "Class 3," a "spot" he describes as a cloud. For him it is one of several repeatable types of object, which would mean the sightings can be sorted and studied.
class-4-spheres-seen-only-during-restric: Skywatcher, a startup that says it can call up UFOs, describes a kind of object it calls "class 4": a sphere that it says its team saw only while restricted government activities were going on nearby. Speaking as witnesses in their interview with Michels, the Skywatcher team says they saw it over several years in a row, which would suggest these spheres turn up only around certain government work.
class-6-uap-shuts-down-three-systems-aft: Around 2003, on a hilltop in the western United States, an unexplained flying object is said to have shut down three systems after a directed-energy weapon, a weapon that fires focused beams of energy, was aimed at it. The object is called a "class 6" in the story. Someone from Skywatcher, a startup that tries to make UFOs appear on purpose, says they were there. "Somewhere around 2003 we spent the year west," he says, "and we had opportunity to bring for a government event energy weapon." Michels tells it again later, from a man named James Fowler. In his version the object was a jellyfish-shaped craft, it happened in the 2020s, and "it just shut down the directed energy before it even went out." To those who tell it, it shows the objects can switch off our weapons before they are even fired.
class-7-jellyfish-outruns-the-little-bir: In 2025, an object the team calls a "jellyfish", which they rank at grade 7 on their own scale, changed course and moved into the wind, getting away from their Little Bird, a small helicopter, that was flying toward it. This is told by Skywatcher, a startup that says it can summon UFOs, which says it has video of the chase. If true, something in the sky was moving against the wind faster than a helicopter could follow.
class-7-object-hovers-overhead-before-th: During a 2025 field operation by Skywatcher, a private company that tries to call in UFOs, a large object the team ranks as "class 7" is said to have flown over and hovered right above them. Team members say they could see it as chrome with their bare eyes. James Valor, a team member who says he was there, tells how they sent up a helicopter to chase it, but "even before the helicopter arrived, he flew up and hovered right above us." Another Skywatcher member, also there, places it on the fourth day of the operation. That member says it hung about 800 meters up for around five minutes and knocked out their sensors, and credits a colleague named Rory. To the team, it would mean the objects respond when called.
classical-greek-theater-aeschylus-promet: Ancient Greek theater, the Prometheus plays of the playwright Aeschylus, first let people sit as spectators in different seats on different nights, and the claim is that this gave rise to perspective, both in geometry and in the sense of a personal point of view. The philosopher Jason Jorjani makes the case himself, citing the psychologist Julian Jaynes and his book The Origin of Consciousness in the Breakdown of the Bicameral Mind, along with Jorjani's own book From Prometheus to Atlas.
classified-able-archer-crisis-felt-insid: In 1983 the world came as close to nuclear war as it did during the Cuban Missile Crisis, but the public never knew, according to the scientist John Brandenburg, who was working then at Sandia National Lab, a US government research laboratory in New Mexico. He calls it the Able Archer crisis and says it was kept secret: "Only people on the lab premises inside the fence knew how bad things were." He tells it from his own time at the lab, and if true it means a near brush with nuclear war was hidden from the public.
classified-asset-documents-show-a-late-1: In the late 1980s the Soviet Union is said to have recovered a crashed UFO in Russia. Eric W. Davis, a Pentagon-linked scientist, says he saw the evidence himself: through a Pentagon-funded study programme he calls "assap" he had a link to a US intelligence agency that got the information not from open KGB records but from its own spy inside the Soviet system. If true, it would mean America's Cold War rival also held such craft. Michels later brings it up again, citing Davis and crediting a work called The Age of Disclosure. His version differs: he dates it to 1989 and says the Soviets got a directed energy weapon, a weapon that fires focused energy, from the craft.
classified-dod-payloads-as-evidence-of-a: Secret cargo for the US military is routinely launched into space from Vandenberg Air Force Base in California, and some see that as a sign of a hidden space program. An unnamed researcher who appeared as a guest says this without naming a source, speaking of launches from roughly the 1980s and 1990s. If true, it would mean some of what goes into orbit is never shown to the public.
classified-f-117-crash-near-bakersfield-: A secret F-117, a US Air Force stealth jet built to be hard to see on radar, is said to have crashed near Bakersfield, California, in about 1986. Michels mentions it himself in passing, unsure of the year, without naming a source, as an example of a secret aircraft that crashed while it was still hidden from the public.
classified-lists-of-uncorrelated-targets: Since the early 1960s, according to the astronomer Beatriz Villarroel, there have been secret lists of "uncorrelated targets": objects tracked in orbit around Earth that cannot be matched to anything known. She says she only learned this recently, and passes it on as something she was told, with the American space military, NASA and the European space agency mentioned in connection with the tracking. If so, unexplained objects around Earth would have been logged quietly for decades.
classified-navy-diver-unit-experimenting: A former top Navy admiral named Tim Gallaudet says there is a special unit of Navy divers that has experimented with liquid breathing, where a diver breathes a fluid instead of air. He tells Michels this as someone who knows about it directly, but he will not say where the unit is based. If true, it would mean the Navy is quietly testing technology that lets people go deeper under the sea.
classified-paper-comparing-human-and-et-: Lyn Buchanan, a former Army sergeant who served in a military unit that trained people to describe distant places using only the mind, says that in the 1980s he was told to write a paper comparing human psychic ability with that of aliens. He tells it first-hand and says that as soon as he turned the paper in, it disappeared. If true, it would mean someone in the military was treating alien psychic ability as a real subject to study.
classified-scif-testimony-to-congress-20: In 2025, more information about secret UFO work was given to Congress in a SCIF, a sealed and guarded room for discussing classified matters, at the top secret level. Jake Barber, a former military helicopter pilot who says he flew a recovered UFO under his aircraft, tells it as someone involved: "more has been shared with Congress in a in a in a skiff in a top secret uh TSCI." He says it to signal that what he says in public is only part of what lawmakers have heard.
classified-signals-lab-picks-up-a-signal: A secret signals lab picked up a signal coming from a tiny object taken from his body, says the writer Whitley Strieber, who believes the object is an implant and who says he has met aliens. He tells Michels that between 1993 and 1996, at the Southwest Research Institute, a research organisation in San Antonio, Texas, the signal came and then switched off, and the staff told him, "We've got a signal, but we can't tell you anything about it because the lab's classified." He also names a man called William Malow in the account, and if it happened, the object was sending out something that a secret lab could detect.
classified-tooth-implant-1960: In the early 1960s, at a New York City company called Intelectron, the inventor Andrija Puharich is said to have created a tooth implant, a device placed in a tooth, which Puharich himself said was classified. The researcher Greg Malatzi tells this without naming a source, as an example of Puharich's secret government-linked work.
classified-video-meeting-smiling-officia: During a secret video meeting in 2025, an official smiled and suggested the objects might not be from our planet, according to James Valor of Skywatcher, a startup that says it can call UFOs into view. Valor says he was in the meeting, held over video "in secret mode," and that the man on the screen "a little smiled." He tells it as a hint that people with access to classified information think the objects may be from somewhere else.
claudio-valente-quits-his-job-and-vanish: One day in 2013 a man named Claudio Valente is said to have reported to work in Portugal, at a place the record calls SAPO, announced it would be his last day, and then vanished. Michels tells this in an episode about scientists who go missing, drawing on a source named Sergio Bastos. He tells it as one of a set of puzzling disappearances among people with technical work.
clay-shaw-phones-fred-crisman-during-the: Two men named Clay Shaw and Fred Crisman knew each other well enough that Shaw phoned Crisman in the late 1960s in New Orleans. That was while Jim Garrison was investigating the Kennedy assassination. The researcher Peter Levenda says this without naming a source, and he tells it because it would tie the two men together at the center of that investigation.
clearance-games-at-bae-2015-2018: A man named Dylan Borland says that while he worked at BAE Systems, a large defence contractor, from 2015 to 2018, people there were "playing this game" with security clearances, meaning the permissions that decide who can see secret work. Borland tells it from his own time there, as part of his larger story about being kept from information he thinks he should have had.
clementine-mission-as-photo-reconnaissan: The claim is that Clementine, a 1994 mission that sent a spacecraft to photograph the moon, was really a spy-photo mission to check whether someone was building bases on the moon that the US didn't know about, and whether they were growing. A guest named Maaneli Derakhshani passes this on from a man named John Brandenburg, alongside a book called Aliens on the Moon: The Truth Exposed. If true, the US suspected someone else was already building on the moon.
cliff-wong-on-faking-an-orb-with-a-drone: A glowing orb in the sky, the kind often reported as a UFO, could be faked by towing a balloon behind a drone, according to a drone expert named Cliff Wong. Eric Haseltine, a former senior official at the National Security Agency, the US agency that intercepts communications, tells this on Michels's show: he says he asked Wong, whom he calls "the world's expert on drones," how he would fake such things, and this was the answer. He raises it to show how some sightings might be staged.
clinic-doctor-turns-away-captured-creatu: In 1996 in Varginha, a town in Brazil where people say a strange creature was caught, a clinic doctor is said to have been brought the creature and told the men to "get it out of here," saying he did not know what it was. The documentary maker James Fox tells this from his investigation of the case, linking it to a man named Marco Eli Chereze. It is one piece of a larger story that a living non-human being was captured there.
clinical-examination-by-beings-1976: In August 1976 near Allagash, Maine, Charlie Foltz says he was taken aboard a craft. He says he struggled to get up and saw a face bending down to look into his eyes, and then the beings began a clinical examination of him. He recalls a panel coming down from above and covering his whole torso, with a blue light shining straight down from it. Foltz tells it as his own experience.
clinton-and-obama-both-deny-anything-und: Presidents Bill Clinton and Barack Obama are both said to have remarked that there is nothing underground at Area 51, the secret US military test base in the Nevada desert. A researcher named Jason Simosa, who has also visited the area himself, says this without naming a source and calls it a weird thing for a president to say, as if the denial itself hints at something there.
clinton-and-the-alh-84001-meteorite-as-s: In the 1990s President Bill Clinton publicly announced findings about ALH 84001, a meteorite from Mars that some scientists thought might hold signs of ancient life. Michels brings it up himself, without naming a source, in an episode with Dan Sherman, a former Air Force sergeant, as an example of the government slowly releasing hints that we are not alone.
clinton-briefed-on-ufos-by-civilian-bruc: In the 1990s, a CIA officer named Ron Pandolfi is said to have arranged for Bruce Maccabee, a Navy physicist and civilian UFO researcher, to brief the Clinton White House on UFOs. Michels tells it as Maccabee briefing President Bill Clinton himself. A researcher named Jason Simosa tells it from Maccabee's own account, and his version differs. According to Simosa, Pandolfi called Maccabee at short notice and asked him to repeat a lecture he had once given the CIA, this time for the president's science adviser. If true, it would mean UFOs reached the top of government through a back door.
clinton-ends-the-superconducting-super-c: On October 30, 1993, President Bill Clinton signed the law that killed the Superconducting Super Collider, a huge planned particle-smashing machine for physics research in the United States. The mathematician and commentator Eric Weinstein tells this without naming a source. He tells it as the moment American big physics was cut off.
clinton-era-investigation-finds-40-tons-: An investigation during the Clinton administration in the 1990s is said to have found 40 tons of Nazi gold that had been shipped out of the Bank of Lisbon by submarine. A researcher named Peter Levenda mentions this to Michels without naming a source, as a sign of how much wealth the Nazis moved out of Europe in secret.
clinton-era-pressure-on-the-dod-that-sha: In the 1990s, under President Bill Clinton, the US defence department was put under pressure that included a "red team", a group set up to break into the military's most secret, unacknowledged projects, according to Jake Barber, a former helicopter pilot who says he once carried a UFO with his helicopter. Barber tells it as part of his own story and says his path into that world was shaped by that time: "it's no coincidence that it happened during the Clinton era." If true, a president's own push against hidden programs helped set his course.
clinton-era-technology-transfer-to-china: In the 1990s, according to the former US Secretary of Energy John S. Herrington, American military technology was passed to China through the Commerce Department under President Bill Clinton and through the Defense Department. Herrington says this himself, and points out that "every single Chinese fighter looks like American fighter F-15," an American jet fighter. He tells it as an example of how sensitive American technology ends up in foreign hands.
clinton-s-televised-statement-on-rock-84: In 1996 President Bill Clinton went on television to talk about a rock known as 84001, which the episode ties to Mars, and said that it "speaks to us across all those billions of years and millions of miles, it speaks of the possibility of life." His own words are played on Michels's show in a March 2025 episode about whether Mars once had life. They are offered as a US president publicly raising the chance of life beyond Earth.
clinton-said-he-didn-t-think-they-d-tell: Bill Clinton, the former US president, was once asked in an interview whether the government had signs of alien life or a hidden program, and answered, in effect, that he did not think they would tell him even though he was president. Rolf Mowatt-Larssen, a former CIA officer, retells this, describing it as something he knows of Clinton saying. It matters because it would suggest such secrets are kept even from the president.
clock-gear-found-inside-marble-in-brazil: Workers in Brazil cutting slabs out of marble mountains have found pieces of a clock inside the stone, even a gear. That is the account of a man named Kiran Ilum Xenov, who says he was taken by aliens in 1997, and he names no source and gives no date. If true, it would mean some made object got sealed inside rock that formed long before anyone could have built a clock.
close-encounters-as-a-celebration-of-an-: The 1977 Hollywood film Close Encounters of the Third Kind, about people meeting aliens, was in this telling the US government's way of celebrating, through the movies, a deal it had struck with the "gray aliens," the small grey-skinned beings of many UFO stories. A scientist named John Brandenburg puts this forward from his own book, which he names as Cosmic Awakening, without pointing to any other source, and mentions the astronomer J. Allen Hynek, who worked on the film. If true, it would mean the film was a coded public signal of a secret agreement.
close-encounters-contains-a-visual-refer: The 1977 Steven Spielberg film Close Encounters of the Third Kind, whose climax takes place at Devils Tower in Wyoming, is said to contain a whole set of visual nods to Project Serpo, a story about a secret programme in which Americans supposedly went to live with aliens. Bryce Zabel, a guest on an episode about Hollywood, the CIA and UFOs, says this to Michels without naming a source, and tells listeners to set aside whether they believe the Serpo story. If true, it would mean the film was hinting at something its makers had heard about.
close-encounters-of-the-third-kind-as-in: Steven Spielberg's 1977 film about first contact with aliens, Close Encounters of the Third Kind, is said to have drawn on real UFO material, down to crates on screen labeled TRW and Lockheed, two big American defense and aerospace companies. Michels points this out himself, without naming a source, and links the film to the astronomer J. Allen Hynek and the UFO researcher Jacques Vallée. If true, the film carried real hints about who handles UFO material.
close-up-witnesses-sensed-being-watched: People who saw these objects up close have said they had a feeling of being watched, according to David Grusch, a former US intelligence official. Grusch says he has talked to several such witnesses who told him they "got that vibe, too", which he shares as backing for the same feeling. If true, it would suggest the objects are somehow aware of the people seeing them.
closed-session-testimony-on-rocky-flats: John S. Herrington, a former US Secretary of Energy, says he has gone back to Congress several times to testify in closed, restricted sessions. He tells Michels the sessions were about security issues at the Energy Department, especially at Rocky Flats, Colorado, a government site run under that department. He does not give dates, and he raises it as part of his own history with secret government matters.
closing-down-the-first-base-and-transfer: A former Air Force sergeant named Dan Sherman, who says he was hired by the NSA (the US National Security Agency, which handles electronic spying and codes) to communicate with aliens, says he was the one who closed down the first base where his secret program ran, sometime between 1990 and 1993, before moving to a second base. He tells Michels the whole base shut down, "not just our aspect of it." Sherman tells it as his own experience, as one step in how the program he describes moved from place to place.
clyde-tombaugh-and-earth-s-small-moons-g: In the 1950s, the astronomer Clyde Tombaugh is said to have written an article saying Earth had some smaller moons orbiting about 500 miles up, tied in this story to gray motherships sitting in orbit. Steve Colbern, a scientist who studies objects said to be alien implants in human bodies, tells it as a researcher summarising, crediting the article but not quoting it. If true, it would mean large unknown objects were circling close to Earth and were noticed by a serious astronomer.
clyde-tombaugh-s-ashes-on-new-horizons-2: When NASA sent the New Horizons spacecraft to explore Pluto in 2006, it carried 30 grams of the ashes of Clyde Tombaugh, the scientist who discovered Pluto. The Harvard astronomer Avi Loeb tells this without naming a source. He calls it the most embarrassing thing, since anyone finding the craft would find human remains aboard.
coanda-1936-lenticular-aerodyne-patent: In 1936, the engineer Henri Coanda filed a patent for a "lenticular aerodyne", a lens-shaped, saucer-like flying machine. Michels tells this himself, in an episode about whether the physicist Robert Oppenheimer worked on UFOs. He raises it to show that people were designing disc-shaped aircraft well before the modern UFO era.
coast-to-coast-call-drops-at-the-lost-ti: While on Coast to Coast AM, a late-night radio show, Richard Barth, a former guard at a nuclear missile site who says he was abducted, was asked by the host George Noory whether he had any lost time during the event, a gap in memory people often report after such encounters. Barth says that just as he went to answer, "everything just went blank" and the call dropped.
coast-to-coast-callers-claiming-time-tra: In the 1990s, people called in to Coast to Coast, the late-night radio show hosted by Art Bell, claiming they were doing time travel work at Area 51, a secret military base in Nevada. Michels recalls this himself, as something he heard on the show, in an episode with a hip hop artist who is fascinated by UFOs. He brings it up to show that people claiming to be government insiders, or whistleblowers, are not new.
coating-compound-found-in-the-bent-pyram: Inside the Bent Pyramid, an ancient Egyptian pyramid at Dahshur, a coating compound has been found that would have shielded the limestone walls from a harsh chemical reaction. The pyramid researcher Geoffrey Drumm says "we've" found it, speaking as one involved, and offers it as evidence that the pyramids were used for chemical processes.
coburn-s-implant-scans-of-experiencers: A scientist named Steve Colbern says he has done about 400 scans on people looking for objects they believe were implanted in their bodies by non-human beings. He tells it as his own work, and names a man called Roger Leir in connection with it. If the scans show what Colbern looks for, they would be physical traces of contact.
cocoa-beach-light-that-exploded-split-in: In 2013 a light over Cocoa Beach, Florida, near Patrick Air Force Base, seemed to explode, broke into six lights and then followed a couple, according to Charles Buhler, a scientist who has worked at NASA, the US space agency, and who says he was one of the two people there. "It's not one light anymore. It's split into six," he recalls. If he is right, whatever it was could split apart and track people on the ground.
cold-war-english-russian-playing-cards-f: During the Cold War there were playing cards printed in both English and Russian so Americans could talk with hostages or captives who spoke the other language, according to Greg Rogers, a NASA doctor. Rogers says he saw them himself. As he explains it, you showed a word in English and the other person read it in Russian, so "it was a means for us to communicate."
colleagues-close-the-door-and-reveal-hid: A former US intelligence officer named David Grusch says that colleagues he had known for years came into his office, shut the door, and told him there was "other stuff" that he and his team were not being given access to: hidden programs. Grusch tells Michels this as his own experience, and he tells it twice. Once he places it around 2019 to 2021. The other time he says it happened at the NGA, a US intelligence agency that works with satellite imagery and maps, that the people had come into his life about 14 years earlier, and that they brought him "crazy intel reports." He tells it because it is how he says he first learned that secret programs were being kept from the people meant to oversee them.
colleagues-grandparents-were-ufo-report-: During the 1940s, some people working on the Manhattan Project, the US wartime program that built the atomic bomb, are said to have been the ones handling UFO reports. A whistleblower named David Grusch tells this on the show, passing on what colleagues told him: their own grandparents were "the UFO report people on the Manhattan Project." If true, UFO secrecy would reach back to the start of the atomic age.
collecting-the-borderland-science-resear: The archive of the Borderland Science Research Association, an old California group that studied fringe science and UFOs, sat in a man's garage in Eureka, California, until it was boxed up and shipped to Sweden. The Swedish UFO researcher Clas Svahn, who collects UFO records, says he did it himself: "I met with this guy in his garage and we packed it all together and sent it back to Sweden." He tells it as part of how he saved a large store of early UFO material.
collection-of-9-11-precognitive-dreams-2: Within three days of the 9/11 attack on the World Trade Center in New York, the biologist Rupert Sheldrake put up posters in Washington Square and ran ads in the Village Voice, a New York weekly paper, asking "did you dream of the World Trade Center?" He tells Jesse Michels he collected more than 75 dreams people sent him. He saw it as a chance to study whether people can dream of events before they happen.
collins-elite-blocking-uap-research-as-d: The Collins Elite is said to be a group of evangelical Christians inside the US government, embedded in the CIA, who decided UFOs were demonic and worked to block research into them. Michels raises it with Luis Elizondo, who once ran a small Pentagon office that studied unexplained aerial reports and who writes about it in his book Imminent. Michels says the group studied the phenomenon in a program called Stack Five at Wright airfield, a military base, and concluded it was all demonic, as the author Nick Redfern writes in his book Final Events. In another episode Michels calls it a rumor and asks the author Peter Levenda what he knows. A researcher named Jason Simosa, going on Redfern's sources, says it became a funded program in 1952 through the CIA's Directorate of Plans, its covert operations branch, with about 12 people on it full time. The physicist Maaneli Derakhshani says only that he has heard rumors of it. If true, it would mean religious belief inside government shaped how UFOs were studied, or kept from being studied.
collins-elite-met-aliens-and-considered-: A secret group inside the US government called the Collins Elite met aliens and then asked whether they could use them to kill people, according to a guest named Kurt Metzger. He says he read it in Final Events, a book by the writer Nick Redfern, and sums it up as: "first we met aliens and then we're like, can we use this to assassinate people?"
colonel-alexander-s-precognitive-sentien: At Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property known for reports of strange events, an Army colonel named Alexander came up with what he called precognitive sentient phenomena: something there that seems aware and seems to know in advance what the investigators will do. The philosopher Jason Jorjani passes on Alexander's idea, pointing to a book called Closer Encounters.
colonel-blanchard-announces-a-crashed-fl: In 1947, at the Roswell Army Air Field in New Mexico, when everyone was seeing UFOs, the well-liked base commander, Colonel Blanchard, is said to have called the local newspaper and announced, "Look what we found. We found a crashed flying saucer." The physicist John Brandenburg tells it on the show, passing on what veterans of the Roswell base said. If true, the military itself once publicly announced recovering a flying saucer.
colonel-coleman-s-b-25-ufo-encounter-ove: In the 1950s, an Air Force officer named Colonel William Coleman is said to have had a dramatic run-in with a UFO while flying a B-25 bomber over Alabama. The documentary maker James Fox mentions it in passing as a case that led him to track Coleman down, calling the plane a "B-55" as he speaks. It would mean a senior military flyer met something unexplained in the air.
colonel-hohman-sold-sdi-to-reagan-using-: In the 1980s in Washington, a military officer is said to have helped sell President Ronald Reagan on SDI, the Strategic Defense Initiative, a plan for missile defence in space, by pointing to an alien threat the officer knew was false. Steven Greer, an activist who campaigns for UFO secrets to be made public, says a Colonel Hohman told him this, quoting him: "We knew that was false, but it got billions of dollars for SDI." Greer also brings in President Jimmy Carter, and tells it to show how a fake alien danger could be used to win money and power.
colorado-2019-2020-sightings-over-missil: Michels says the sightings over Colorado in 2019 and 2020 happened partly over nuclear missile silos, and that they mirrored sightings from 1965. He says this himself, without naming a source, while debating Mick West, a well-known UFO skeptic. If true, it would add to a long pattern of strange objects showing up near America's nuclear weapons.
colossal-biosciences-to-run-ancient-dna-: In 2025, Jesse Michels says, he decided to have the small three-fingered mummies from Peru tested for ancient DNA, and he reached out to a friend named Ben Lam at Colossal Biosciences, a company that works with genetics. Michels tells this himself in a 2025 episode about the mummies. The tests could help show what the bodies really are.
colossal-dna-test-on-the-wolf-carcass-is: A wolf carcass found at Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property known for reports of strange events, was DNA-tested, and most of the DNA could not be identified. Brandon Fugal, a businessman who owns the ranch, says he sent it himself to Colossal Biosciences, a gene-science company: "it comes back the majority of it they can't identify." If true, the animal would carry genetic material no one can place.
columbia-tv-threatens-to-burn-your-negat: In 1995 a boss at Columbia TV, the Sony-owned television studio in Los Angeles, threatened to shut down the TV series Dark Skies and destroy its film unless the actors stopped wearing black suits, says Bryce Zabel, the writer and producer who made the show. Zabel says he was there and the words are "seared in my head": "Get your actors out of the black suits today or we will shut down your production and burn your negative." He links it to the film Men in Black, made around the same time, and names its director Barry Sonnenfeld, the director Steven Spielberg and Spielberg's company Amblin, and if true it shows how hard studios guarded the look of the men in black on screen.
columbus-uses-a-predicted-eclipse-to-mak: Christopher Columbus is said to have told island natives that if they did not do what his crew asked, he would block out the sun in three days, and three days later a solar eclipse came, so they gave in. The video maker Chris Ramsay tells it, placing it in the Bahamas and linking it to the science fiction writer Arthur C. Clarke. He uses it to show how a group with advanced knowledge can seem to have magic power over others.
coming-out-after-retirement-daily-mail-a: A doctor who worked with NASA, the US space agency, named Greg Rogers says he went public after retiring, first in an interview with the journalist Josh Boswell published by the UK Daily Mail newspaper on 4 May 2025, then in an interview with a man named Ty Roberts at the International UFO Bureau in Oklahoma City for a programme called Total Disclosure. Rogers tells this first-hand; he is the man who says he saw a UFO in a secret hangar, and these interviews are where he first told that story.
commander-david-fravor-works-at-bae-2004: A Navy commander named David Fravor, one of the pilots in the Nimitz incident, now works at BAE, a large defense company. That incident was a 2004 sighting of an unexplained object by Navy pilots flying from the aircraft carrier Nimitz. Michels mentions this himself in passing, in a 2026 conversation with Dylan Borland, and hedges it with "I believe."
commander-george-hoover-on-aliens-saying: A Navy officer, Commander George Hoover, is said to have spoken about a message that visiting aliens often give people: "you don't know how powerful you are." Jesse Michels brings this up himself in his 2023 interview with a former intelligence officer named David Grusch, putting it down to Hoover without saying where or when Hoover said it. If true, it would suggest the visitors see some hidden power in human beings.
commercial-mining-pilot-tests-of-the-sar: A radar imaging method used to look deep underground, said to have revealed structures beneath the pyramids of Egypt, has also been tried out by mining companies, according to the researcher behind it, Filippo Biondi. The method uses SAR, synthetic aperture radar, a way of building pictures from radar signals. Biondi says he ran many private trial tests with companies under secrecy agreements and that they were "more than 100% successful," which he offers as proof that the method really works.
communicating-with-the-logical-alien-he-: Dan Sherman, a former Air Force sergeant who says the National Security Agency, the US agency that intercepts communications, hired him to talk to aliens, says that between 1990 and 1993 at an overseas base he was in contact with an alien he nicknamed Spock because it was so logical. He tells it as his own experience, also covered in his book Above Black, and says he only saw two of these beings, Spock being the first. If true, it would mean the US government was using people to talk with aliens through the mind.
communion-letters-held-in-the-archives-o: After the writer Whitley Strieber published Communion, his book about his own encounters with strange beings, readers sent him huge numbers of letters about their own experiences, and he says four or five thousand of them now sit at Rice University in Houston, Texas. Strieber tells it first-hand. He says they are held in a collection called the Archives of the Impossible, founded by a Rice scholar named Jeff Kripal, which would mean thousands of ordinary people's accounts are kept for study.
communion-prompts-nearly-half-a-million-: The story is that after the writer Whitley Strieber published Communion in 1987, a book about his encounters, nearly half a million people wrote letters to him and his wife. A guest named Bryce Zabel, who talks about Hollywood and UFOs, tells this on the show, passing on what Strieber said. Told this way, it would mean huge numbers of people felt they had lived through something similar.
communion-released-early-because-of-some: In 1987, the book Communion, the writer Whitley Strieber's account of being visited by strange beings, is said to have reached shops earlier than planned. Strieber says he had been given a publication date and then suddenly the books were in bookstores, which he puts down to "some kind of resistance" to the book coming out.
community-backlash-and-social-services-v: A North Carolina man named Chris Bledsoe, who says he attracts UFOs, says that after his experience in 2007 his community turned against him. He tells Michels it caused him so much trouble that he stopped speaking to half or even two-thirds of his own family, cousins included. In another telling he says social services came to his house and tried to have him removed from it. Bledsoe tells it from his own life, to show what speaking up about what he saw cost him.
compartmentalization-carried-over-from-t: The habit of splitting secret UFO work into sealed-off pieces, so that no one sees the whole, is said to be carried over from the Manhattan Project, the wartime US program of the 1940s that built the atomic bomb. An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb says this, crediting the claim to David Grusch, a former US intelligence officer who has testified about hidden UFO programs. It would mean today's secrecy was built on the model of the bomb project.
complex-equations-in-vinod-s-automatic-w: In the 1950s, at a research group in Maine called the Round Table Foundation, a man known as Dr. Vinod is said to have filled a notebook through automatic writing, meaning writing that comes out without the writer's conscious control, and very complex equations came through in it. The researcher Greg Malatzi describes this, pointing to the document known as the Nine notebook. If true, the messages would have carried knowledge their writer did not seem to have himself.
compton-belkovich-heat-anomaly-on-the-lu: NASA, the US space agency, is said to have found from infrared (heat) imaging of the whole Moon that one area on the far side, called Compton-Belkovich, gives off 20 times the average heat of the rest of the far side. A researcher appearing as a guest tells this without naming a source. He brings it up as a sign that something unusual sits under that one spot.
concrete-crane-slab-at-the-crash-site-19: Somewhere in Hart Canyon near Aztec, New Mexico, where a craft is said to have crashed in 1948, someone in a hurry mixed concrete for a crane slab, Michels says. He tells this after going to the site himself, and names a man called Carl Flock in connection with it. A rushed slab there would point to heavy lifting at the crash site, as if something had been hauled away.
condon-committee-coordinated-with-air-fo: A 1966 UFO study at the University of Colorado, led by Edward Condon, was paid for by the US Air Force and was supposed to stay free of its influence, but Michels, telling it himself, calls the result "an absolute hit job" on the subject. The study's own final report, Scientific Study of Unidentified Flying Objects, delivered on 31 October 1968, says its contract with the Air Force's science research office provided $313,000 for the first 15 months and required that its "planning, direction and conclusions" be "conducted wholly independently of the Air Force." It adds only that the Air Force was ordered to hand over its earlier records and to lend staff at its bases when the field teams asked, and describes no other coordination.
condon-report-and-its-links-to-atomic-se: The Condon report, the US Air Force-funded UFO study led by the physicist Edward Condon that ended in 1969, was tied to the world of atomic secrets, because Condon had been "very close friends" with J. Robert Oppenheimer, the physicist who led the atomic bomb laboratory at Los Alamos, ever since they studied in Göttingen, Germany, in the 1920s. Michels makes this case himself, without naming a source, and links it to the Los Alamos Primer, the lecture notes given to the first bomb builders, and to the McMahon Act and the Atomic Energy Act of 1954, the laws that put nuclear knowledge under strict secrecy. If true, the official UFO study was run by someone schooled in keeping nuclear secrets.
condon-report-closes-blue-book-1968: A 1968 scientific report on UFOs from the University of Colorado, led by Edward Condon, shut down Blue Book, the US Air Force's UFO study of the 1950s and 60s, and brushed off its cases with ordinary explanations, even though, Michels says, more than 30 percent of the cases stayed unidentified; he tells this himself on several shows, once crediting the astronomer J. Allen Hynek, who worked with Blue Book. The report, Scientific Study of Unidentified Flying Objects, sent to the Air Force on 31 October 1968, concludes that "nothing has come from the study of UFOs in the past 21 years that has added to scientific knowledge," but it only offers Condon's "impression" that Blue Book could be dropped, calling that "a question for defense specialists," and the text read here gives no overall share of unidentified cases. An Air Force fact sheet from January 1985 records that the Secretary of the Air Force ended Blue Book on 17 December 1969, a decision based partly on the Colorado report.
condon-s-letters-with-colonel-robert-hip: Letters from the 1960s are said to show that the physicist Edward Condon, who led an Air Force-funded study of UFOs, was working closely with an Air Force colonel named Robert Hippler, and that Hippler wanted the study to find UFO research "a waste of money." Michels tells this himself across several episodes, without naming where he read the letters, and he is not always equally sure: once he says only "I believe there are letters too," and elsewhere he adds that Condon "kind of implicitly" went along. If true, it would mean the study's verdict against UFOs was steered before it began.
condon-worked-with-manhattan-project-fig: The physicist Edward Condon, the story goes, was in the inner circle of the Manhattan Project, the US wartime programme that built the atomic bomb. David Grusch, a former intelligence official turned whistleblower, says only that "Condon was involved" and links him to Vannevar Bush, the government's wartime science chief. Michels goes further, on his own account. He says Condon was so close to J. Robert Oppenheimer, the physicist who led the bomb laboratory, that he is "partly credited" with choosing Los Alamos, New Mexico, as its site. Michels adds that Condon studied in Göttingen, Germany, under the physicist Max Born and helped draft the McMahon Act, a 1946 atomic energy law. A document backs part of this: the Los Alamos Primer, written at the laboratory in April 1943, says its notes on the physicist Robert Serber's opening lectures "were written up by E. U. Condon." The Primer says nothing about who picked the site.
condon-wrote-the-mcmahon-secrecy-languag: Edward Condon, a scientist who Michels says later dismissed UFOs entirely, wrote the McMahon Act of 1946, a law on atomic secrecy that Michels calls the precursor to the Atomic Energy Act of 1954. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, across several episodes, and in one credits David Grusch, a witness who testified to Congress, for the idea that the Atomic Energy Commission set up UFO secrecy in 1954. Michels says this means Condon "is basically writing up UFO secrecy before he then debunks the entire thing."
conflicting-accounts-of-who-sent-puharic: Around 1970 and 1971, Andrija Puharich, a researcher of psychic powers, went to Tel Aviv in Israel to meet Uri Geller, a performer famous for claiming to bend spoons with his mind, and there are two stories of who sent him. The researcher Greg Malatzi says Puharich's own lectures name a foundation as the sender, but that Geller later said, "he was sent by the CIA, like directly." If Geller's version is right, the US spy agency was behind one of the best-known psychic investigations of the time.
congress-denied-a-scif-for-grusch-s-clas: When the former intelligence officer David Grusch was due in 2023 to give members of Congress the classified part of his account of secret UFO programs, they are said to have been refused a SCIF, a sealed and secured room where secret matters can be discussed. If true, someone in government was making it hard for lawmakers to hear him. Grusch, who testified publicly before Congress that summer, tells it himself on the show. He says "the members are pretty incensed" because, as he puts it, "they couldn't reserve a SCIF." An unnamed speaker who appears to be one of those lawmakers tells it more bluntly in a later episode, saying "we were denied access to the skiff." That speaker frames it as an outright refusal rather than a booking problem, and does not name Grusch.
congress-of-vienna-vatican-monarchies-an: At the Congress of Vienna in 1815, the great meeting of European powers in the Austrian capital, the Vatican, the ruling royal families and the Knights of Malta, an old Catholic order of knights, banded together to hold back revolution. A researcher named Jason Simosa tells it on Michels' show without naming a source, pointing to the Austrian statesman Klemens von Metternich and saying "they colluded a thing called the Congress of Vienna." He tells it as an early link in a chain of secret societies he connects to the hiding of UFO knowledge.
congress-sends-borland-to-aaro-at-the-en: At the end of March 2023, members of Congress put Dylan Borland, a former government worker who has come forward as a whistleblower, in touch with AARO, the Pentagon office set up to look into UFO reports, and he went to meet it. Borland tells this himself: "they got me touching Arrow and I went to Arrow. Uh that was the end of March." If so, Congress was sending its own witnesses straight to the military's UFO office.
congressional-and-senate-hearings-reveal: In 2024, according to Jesse Michels, public hearings in Washington, first in the House of Representatives and then in the Senate, brought out the existence of a secret program called Immaculate Constellation. Michels gives this as his own framing in a December 2024 episode, without naming a source, and raises it again in January 2025 with a Navy scientist named Salvatore Pais, where he mentions no Senate hearing and just calls it "this idea of this, you know, top secret program." If true, it would mean Congress had learned of a hidden government effort tied to the UFO question.
congressional-attempts-to-study-ufos-blo: Since the 1970s, efforts in the US Congress to at least study UFOs are said to have been blocked by religious groups who felt "God does not want us to do this," with lawmakers falling back on talk of "Angels and Demons" out of fear. The writer Peter Levenda, introduced on the show as a CIA historian, tells this as his own summary, drawing on the book Sinister Forces. If true, it would mean faith, not science, kept the subject off the agenda.
congressional-report-on-the-1944-maison-: The writer and researcher Peter Levenda says the US Congress published a report in June 1945, before the war in Asia was over, about what was in effect the Maison Rouge meeting, a gathering held in 1944 in Strasbourg, France. Levenda summarises this himself without naming who pointed him to it. He brings it up as an official record that the meeting took place and that Congress knew of it.
congressional-research-service-ufo-study: In 1977 President Jimmy Carter is said to have asked for a special study of everything the US government knew about UFOs. Dan Sheehan, a lawyer who says he served as special counsel on the project, tells Michels he took part. In his account the request went through the congressional science and technology committee to the Congressional Research Service, the research arm of Congress at the Library of Congress in Washington. He names a researcher there, Marcia Smith, and tells it as a sign that a president wanted to know what the government held on the subject.
congressional-safe-harbor-bill-gutted-20: In 2023 the US Congress is said to have come close to passing a bill that would have protected, or given amnesty to, people holding UFO secrets so they could come forward. Lawmakers are then said to have gutted it. Steven Greer, a campaigner for UFO disclosure, says it "was gutted by Turner, Rogers, Pelosi, some other people." Dan Sheehan, a lawyer who says he was involved, puts the main blame on Mike Turner. Turner is a congressman from Ohio whose district includes Wright-Patterson, an Air Force base. Sheehan says Turner stopped "the full bill." He names it as the UAP Disclosure Act, UAP being the government's term for UFOs, and also mentions Congressman Dan Crenshaw. Michels says simply that "the UAPDA was killed by Mike Turner." The story matters because, if true, a few lawmakers blocked the best chance yet to make the government reveal what it knows.
congressional-source-puts-crash-retrieva: Someone in Congress is said to be almost completely sure that secret programs exist to recover crashed craft that are not of human making. The national security writer Marik von Rennenkampff says that in the 2020s he asked an unnamed congressional source point blank how confident they were, and the answer was "hovering around 100%." If so, people inside Congress would believe such programs are real.
congressman-on-progress-of-reverse-engin: An unnamed congressman says he believes secret programs exist to study recovered craft that are not of human make, and he mentions the Wilson memo, a leaked document said to describe such a program, but he doubts they have made much progress copying the technology. His reason, given on an episode built around an interview with a whistleblower: "we would own the skies if they had it."
congressman-schiff-and-the-deleted-roswe: A US congressman named Schiff, looking into Roswell, the reported 1947 crash of something in the New Mexico desert, is said to have found that all the archival records about it had been deleted. The documentary filmmaker James Fox passes this on, saying Schiff "noted that all of the Roswell stuff was deleted, all the archival material," and the story is set around 1997. If true, it would mean the official paper trail for the most famous UFO case was wiped out.
congressman-witnesses-odni-official-apol: A US congressman named Eric Burlison says that in 2026 he sat in on a blunt meeting between David Grusch, a former intelligence officer who has spoken out about hidden UFO programs, and someone from the ODNI, the office that oversees all US intelligence agencies. Burlison tells Michels that, from what he saw, the official was basically apologizing for how Grusch had been treated over the years. If so, it would mean the intelligence world was admitting it had treated Grusch badly.
consciousness-based-secret-space-program: An Army sergeant named Lyn Buchanan, who did remote viewing, an attempt to perceive distant places with the mind alone, says he has travelled to other planets using only his mind, being in two places at once. Asked about this kind of mind-based space program, he answers simply, "Yeah, I've done that." If true, people could reach other worlds without any craft.
consecrating-holy-prophet-aluyah-during-: Around 1968 or 1969, during the Biafra war, a civil war in Nigeria, a small group in the Bronx, New York, made a man called Holy Prophet Aluyah a bishop, with people from the Nigerian embassy there to watch, according to the author Peter Levenda, who writes about secret history and says he took part. "We consecrate him a bishop," he recalls. "And the Nigerian embassy is there." He tells it as part of his own past, and if true it puts a foreign government at a little-known religious ceremony in New York.
construction-worker-visited-by-a-blue-be: A construction worker named Dave Rossi says a blue being appeared in his bedroom. Rossi tells it himself, but only briefly. To him it was "more of a feeling rather than a visual," a one-time thing that has never happened again, and in his telling he does not mention physics. Michels retells it twice, citing Rossi, and adds more. He says the being passed on advanced physics ideas, "downloads" as he calls them. He also says this brought Rossi to the notice of two researchers in this field, Eric W. Davis and Hal Puthoff. If true, it would mean real scientific knowledge can come through such encounters.
consulting-for-a-jeans-company-on-shadin: A scientist who studies how people see, named Don Hoffman, says he once advised a jeans company on how shading and stitching change the way the eye reads a shape. He tells Michels that during his talk the company's CEO jumped out of his chair, went up to the screen and said, "Our jeans make my butt look bad." Hoffman, who will not name the company, tells it from his own work to show how much what we see depends on tricks of perception.
consumer-product-safety-commission-swat-: In the 2000s, the Consumer Product Safety Commission, the federal agency that polices dangerous products, raided the home of Bob Lazar, a man famous in UFO circles who ran a science-supply business called United Nuclear. Lazar tells it first-hand: they came "with a SWAT team" and "woke my wife up out of bed with, you know, an M-16 pointed in her face." He tells it as an example of the heavy-handed government pressure he says he has faced.
contact-from-steven-greer-s-disclosure-p: In 2025 someone from the Disclosure Project, a group run by the UFO activist Steven Greer that gathers people willing to speak out about government secrets, reached out to Dan Sherman and offered him legal protection as a whistleblower if he would testify. Sherman, a former Air Force sergeant who says the National Security Agency, the US spy agency that intercepts communications, hired him to talk with aliens, tells this himself. "Not Steven Greer himself, but somebody else now," he says, adding that he and Greer had talked long ago. If true, he was being asked to tell his story officially, with protection.
contact-in-the-desert-appearances-replac: The author and historian Peter Levenda says he was invited to speak at Contact in the Desert, a UFO conference, as a stand-in. He tells Michels he was first asked long ago to replace someone. Then, around 2017, he was asked to step in for another speaker, Jim Marrs, who was sick that year.
contact-with-a-being-and-taken-aboard-a-: A man named Steven Greer, who says secret UFO knowledge is held by a hidden global group, says that in 1973, at a fire lookout tower in the Blue Ridge Mountains near Boone, North Carolina, he was taken aboard a craft. There, he says, a being about five feet tall with "beautiful deer-like eyes" came over and touched him on his right shoulder. Greer tells this to Michels as his own experience, and elsewhere in the conversation he names it as the root of the special work he went on to do.
contents-of-the-cave-and-the-three-body-: A cave in the Nazca region of Peru is said to have held more than 200 body parts: lone heads, limbs and other appendages, and in many cases whole bodies still intact. Michels describes the find himself and cites a man named Leandro as a witness to it. If true, the find would point to strange bodies kept hidden in the Peruvian desert.
contesting-account-and-aaro-position-on-: A former Air Force man named Robert Jacobs has told of something strange seen during a 1964 missile test filmed near Big Sur, California, launched from Vandenberg Air Force Base, but another man with very good credentials says Jacobs mixed up which test date it was. Kurt McConnell, a former US Senate staffer, raises this rival account without naming the man. He sets it beside the view of the Pentagon office that now investigates UFO reports, and if the rival account holds, Jacobs's story would rest on a confused date.
continuity-of-government-succession-harr: In the 1980s the United States had a plan to keep the government running after a disaster, with a ranked list of officials who would take over in turn, and John S. Herrington says he was number 16 on it. Herrington, then the Secretary of Energy, remembers it because his daughter sewed a big 16 on the back of his swimsuit.
contractor-ms-finds-a-craft-being-disass: A contractor known only as MS is said to have walked into a remote building in the Avery section of Dugway Proving Ground, a military test range in Utah, while reading electric meters, and found a craft there. An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb tells this in two episodes, passing on what he was told. The two tellings differ: in one the craft seemed to be in the middle of being taken apart, in the other the unnamed worker, a contractor for a Martin company at the West Desert Test Wing, saw it "hovering in the air being tested on." If true, the military would be studying an unknown craft in the Utah desert.
contractor-saic-likely-involved-in-psion: SAIC, a large US government contractor, was likely involved in psychotronic or psionic research, meaning research into the supposed powers of the mind. Michels says this himself in a 2025 episode with a guest known as UAPGerb, and names no source for it beyond his own reading of the contractor's role.
control-room-camera-challenge-produces-t: Inside the control room at Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah ranch known for strange reports, Erik Bard says he spoke out loud to whatever might be there: "If you got something you want to show me, show me. If you got something you want to tell me, tell me." He says the very first screenshot after that showed letters on the screen pulled into the words "I living." The ranch's owner, Brandon Fugal, tells it too, adding that the letters were pulled together out of order "in a millisecond" with no explanation, and if true it would mean something at the ranch answered back.
controlled-remote-viewing-created-by-ing: Controlled remote viewing is described as a method of trying to sense distant places or hidden things with the mind alone. Lyn Buchanan, a former Army sergeant who says he practised it himself, tells Michels it was created by a man named Ingo Swann and used by the military for intelligence gathering for many years. He says businesses use it now, but stages 8 through 18 of the method are not taught to the public.
controller-reports-objects-descending-fr: In 2004, off San Diego, crews with the aircraft carrier USS Nimitz were told that unknown objects had been tracked for days dropping down from very high altitude. Michels quotes an account in which "the controller told us that these objects had been observed for over two weeks coming down from over 80,000 feet." A guest named Marik von Rennenkampff, speaking as a witness and relaying the account of a man named Kevin Day, gives it as about "10 days" of "tracking anomalous objects at 28,000 ft heading south at 100 knots," which he calls "very strange tracks." It is told because it would mean the objects were seen over a long stretch, not in a single passing moment.
cook-interviews-ning-li-at-a-2003-confer: A writer named Nick Cook, who has investigated secret antigravity research, says that in 2003 he sat down and interviewed Ning Li, a scientist known for her antigravity work, at a conference just outside Washington DC. Cook tells Michels this as something he did himself. It matters because, in a related story, that conference is said to be the last place Li was seen in public.
