cook-s-visit-to-the-bell-site-in-the-wal: Deep in a mine at Waldenburg, in what is now southern Poland, is the site where a Nazi-era machine called the Bell was supposedly installed, part of a story about secret German antigravity work. The British journalist Nick Cook, author of a book called The Hunt for Zero Point, says he visited it in person with a man named Igor Witkowski, calling it a very atmospheric visit. Michels retells it twice, once tying the site to the tunnels of the Skoda works and saying Cook saw the test rig underground, and once adding a boat ride under the ground to where the rig can be seen and linking it to a man named Hans Kammler.
cooper-s-ufo-in-orbit-1963: Gordon Cooper, an American astronaut, is said to have told of an object that came close to him while he was in orbit around the Earth in 1963, and Charlie Foltz thinks he said it was green. Foltz, who comes on the show as a witness in his own alien abduction story, is passing on what he recalls Cooper saying. If true, an astronaut met an unknown object in space.
coordinated-hit-job-on-malmgren-after-je: After Michels interviewed a man named Harold Malmgren in 2025, a damaging piece was written about Malmgren, claiming an archivist had never heard of him, in what Michels sees as a coordinated attack. Michels tells this himself, and points to Malmgren's Wikipedia page as part of the story. For him it is a sign that someone wanted to discredit what Malmgren had said.
cop-manuel-sandoval-chases-a-disc-from-c: One night in 1948, a disc came wobbling low over the small town of Cuba, New Mexico, and a local policeman named Manuel Sandival chased it along Old Highway 44 all night. Michels tells this himself, and says Sandival had long been saying he would do exactly that if he ever saw one. He tells it as part of a larger account of a craft said to have come down on a nearby mesa, which, if true, would put a lawman on the trail of a crash as it happened.
copperfield-s-great-wall-walk-through-an: In the 1980s the stage magician David Copperfield appeared to walk through the Great Wall of China and to make the Statue of Liberty disappear. A researcher named Chris Ramsay brings this up with Michels, without naming a source, to show how well a skilled illusion can fool huge numbers of people.
corbell-and-coulthart-find-witnesses-who: Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft in the late 1980s at a secret Nevada site called S4, was really there, according to people found by the filmmaker Jeremy Corbell and the journalist Ross Coulthart. Jesse Michels says this himself in a 2026 episode, after spending two days with Lazar, saying Corbell and Coulthart "found a bunch of people who have verified Bob's presence at S4." If true, it would back up the part of Lazar's story that his doubters most often question.
corbell-first-meets-bob-lazar-at-john-le: The filmmaker Jeremy Corbell, who makes documentaries about UFOs, says he first met Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft at a secret site in Nevada, at the Las Vegas house of John Lear, a pilot known for his UFO claims, some time in the 2010s. Corbell says that the first thing Lear told him was, "Lazar's coming over." He tells it as his own memory of how he came to know Lazar.
corbell-fought-for-grusch-to-testify-in-: Before David Grusch, a former intelligence officer turned whistleblower, testified to Congress in 2023 about UFOs, there were people who did not want him to speak, according to the documentary maker Jeremy Corbell. Corbell tells Michels he was part of it himself: "I fought to make sure he could talk in Congress," he says, adding that "they didn't want him to testify" and that Grusch would say the same. He tells it to show that Grusch's public hearing almost did not happen.
corbell-presses-jacques-vallee-on-lazar-: A filmmaker named Jeremy Corbell says he once pushed the veteran UFO researcher Jacques Vallée on the subject of Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft, when the two of them were alone at Corbell's ranch. Corbell tells Michels about it as something he did himself, but he does not say what Vallée answered.
corbell-s-2018-iraq-jellyfish-ufo-video: A video filmed over Iraq in 2018 shows an object shaped like a jellyfish. The UFO researcher Jeremy Corbell made it public. Michels mentions it in passing, crediting Corbell with releasing "a video that was caught in Iraq in 2018 of a jellyfish shaped UFO."
corbell-s-private-source-on-the-existenc: A secret site called S-4, in the Nevada desert, really exists, according to the filmmaker Jeremy Corbell, who says a private source of his confirmed it. That, he says, is why he knew Bob Lazar, a man who has said he worked on unexplained craft at S-4, "was telling it as it is." It would mean Lazar's account of the place holds up.
cordyceps-mind-controlling-bullet-ants: In the Amazon, bullet ants, a large stinging ant, are said to take in cordyceps, a parasitic mushroom that takes over their brains and movements. The fungus steers each ant up to higher ground, and there a mushroom stalk grows out of the ant's head. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, while talking about mushrooms as a kind of mind control.
coricancha-andesite-stonework: The fitted stone walls of Coricancha, an ancient temple site in Cusco, Peru, are built from andesite, a hard volcanic rock, and a researcher named Luke Caverns calls them "the most impressive stonework in all of the ancient world." Caverns says he has seen the work in person, and he brings it up as evidence that the old builders had more skill than we usually give them credit for.
corona-spy-satellite-program-offered-as-: A sighting by Jacques Vallée, a French-born scientist and UFO researcher, was once explained away as a Corona satellite. Corona was a run of highly secret spy satellites, paid for by the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency, and first launched in 1960. In a 2025 episode, Michels grants that the Corona satellites did fly a nearly polar orbit, but he calls it "a very insufficient explanation" for what Vallée saw.
corporal-armando-vanishes-for-15-minutes: In Chile in the 1970s, a corporal named Armando Valdés is said to have vanished completely from the six men in his platoon and come back 15 minutes later, but for him five days had passed. The researcher Mike Masters tells this without naming a source, as part of his case that the beings people meet may be humans from the future. If true, it would mean time ran differently for the corporal than for the men around him.
correspondence-with-whitley-strieber-on-: Peter Levenda, an author of secret history whom the episode calls a CIA historian, says he had conversations about the UFO question with the writer Whitley Strieber, who had first contacted him years earlier about something unrelated. Levenda tells it as his own experience and ties it to his book Sinister Forces. If it is as he tells it, two well-known writers on the subject were comparing notes directly.
corso-and-the-telepathic-steering-helmet: Philip J. Corso, an Army officer, claimed that in the 1950s he worked at the Pentagon handing out recovered UFO material to private companies, and that some of it was used to steer weapons with the mind. Michels sums up Corso's claim this way, alongside the guest Dan Sheehan. A researcher who goes by the online name UAPGerb adds detail from Corso's account. He says the Foreign Technology Division, a military unit that studied foreign weapons, tried to use recovered technology to let human brain waves guide intercontinental and other ballistic missiles, and he dates this to about 1958 to 1962. If true, it would mean crashed-craft technology went into American weapons.
corso-government-panic-over-ufos-at-new-: Around 1947 the US government went into panic because many UFOs were being seen in New Mexico, where it was testing V-2 rockets, the German-designed rockets of that era, and working on nuclear weapons. The physicist John Brandenburg says so, citing the book The Day After Roswell by Philip J. Corso, and tells it to suggest the craft were drawn to America's rocket and nuclear sites.
corso-in-post-war-italy-knight-of-malta: Colonel Philip J. Corso, an Army officer who later became famous for his book The Day After Roswell, in which he claimed the Pentagon reverse engineered alien materials, served as a high-ranking intelligence officer in Italy after the Second World War. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, in an episode with the former presidential advisor Harald Malmgren. He raises it to place Corso in the secret postwar intelligence world long before his later claims.
corso-manuscript-trapped-being-asks-to-l: In the 1950s, the Army officer Philip J. Corso is said to have met a trapped non-human being who asked him to turn down the radar so its kind could get away. A researcher who goes by the online name UAPGerb brings this up from Corso's manuscript, his written account, paraphrasing the being as saying, "Hey, lower the radar so we can get out of here." If true, it would suggest that radar itself was bringing down or trapping these craft.
corso-recruited-to-the-army-foreign-tech: Philip J. Corso, an Army officer, stated that in 1960 he was recruited into the US Army's Foreign Technology Division, a Pentagon unit for studying technology from outside the US, working under the general Arthur Trudeau. The online researcher known as UAPGerb tells this and points to Corso's official military records as backing. It matters because it would place Corso in the very office where strange recovered technology might be studied.
corso-s-claims-of-a-covert-roswell-group: The story goes that wreckage from a 1947 crash near Roswell, New Mexico, was handed to a secret government group under Roscoe Hillenkoetter, the first head of the CIA, the US spy agency, and that Philip J. Corso, an Army colonel who ran the Army's foreign technology desk, then quietly passed pieces of it to private companies such as Bell Labs so they could copy it. Michels repeats this often from Corso's book The Day After Roswell, and others pass it on too: a researcher called UAPGerb puts it between 1958 and 1962 under General Arthur Trudeau, and other guests say it sped up integrated circuits, lasers and fiber optics, with tellers differing over whether the material went to Bell Labs, defense contractors in general, or the Wright-Patterson air base in Ohio. In a clip Corso himself says "number one was the integrated circuit. Number two in importance was laser," which, if true, would mean some everyday modern technology grew out of crash material.
corso-s-co-author-gave-him-24-hours-to-e: Michels says that Philip J. Corso, author of The Day After Roswell, a book published in 1997 about the crash people say happened near Roswell, New Mexico, in 1947, got only 24 hours from his co-author, William J. Birnes, to edit it before it came out. Michels brings this up on three episodes. He calls it the reason there is "clearly some BS in that book". Once he also mentions an earlier draft by Corso called Dawn of a New Age, and once he passes on a claim from a researcher who goes by UAP Gerb: that the co-author "inserted all sorts of fake stuff in there almost to stigmatize Corso," which, if true, would mean the book's weakest parts were not Corso's own.
corso-s-manuscript-dawn-of-a-new-age-vs-: Philip J. Corso, an Army officer who wrote The Day After Roswell, published in 1997, is said to have left a manuscript called Dawn of a New Age that differs from the published book. A researcher who goes by UAPGerb raises this himself, without naming a source, as a sign that Corso's first account of crash technology was not exactly what reached print.
corso-says-the-day-after-roswell-was-rus: The story is that the 1997 book The Day After Roswell, written by Philip J. Corso with William J. Birnes, was rushed to print. The book is about Roswell, New Mexico, where something is said to have crashed in 1947, and Corso claims in it to have handled what was recovered. A UFO investigator named James Fox says Corso himself told how the book was hurried out with Birnes, and Fox also names a man called Michael Hessman. An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb (UAP stands for unidentified anomalous phenomena, the newer word for UFOs) adds a rumour that Corso had only 24 hours to edit it. UAPGerb also passes on Corso's son's account: that Corso put his hand to his head and said, "I can't believe this." Both are repeating what others told them, not what they saw. The point of the story is that if the book was rushed, its mistakes might come from haste rather than from Corso making things up.
cosmic-zoo-explanation-for-diverse-craft: The owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a property in Utah known for reports of strange lights and craft, floats the idea that we are living in a kind of cosmic zoo, with Earth watched by many different visitors. The owner raises it on the show as a possible reason so many different kinds of craft are reported, which would mean more than one kind of outsider is taking an interest in us.
cosmonaut-drew-an-object-that-stopped-be: A Soviet space crew is said to have had an unknown craft stop right beside them halfway through their orbit, and a cosmonaut drew a picture of it. The physicist Kevin Knuth tells this twice, the second time adding that photographs were taken and crediting a source whose name comes through as Akan Atanv. If true, it would mean an unknown object kept pace with a spacecraft in orbit.
cosmonaut-fooled-crewmate-with-ice-parti: A Russian space traveller, a cosmonaut, is said to have once pranked a crewmate in their capsule by passing off drifting ice particles outside the window as a fleet of UFOs. The Swedish UFO researcher Clas Svahn tells it as a story one of the cosmonauts he spoke to told him. It shows how easily something ordinary in space can look like a fleet of craft.
cosmos-club-tied-to-a-ufo-crash: The Cosmos Club, a private club in Washington, DC, is said to be linked in some way to a UFO crash. Michels mentions it only in passing in a 2026 episode, saying "you hear of things like" this, and credits it to an online commentator who goes by Dark Journalist. He gives no detail of what the link was or which crash he means.
coulthart-detained-by-cbp-after-grusch-s: Ross Coulthart, a reporter who broke a story in 2023 about a man named Grusch, says that afterwards he was stopped and held at the US border by CBP, the US Customs and Border Protection agency. He tells it himself, as something that happened to him. He shares it as a sign that reporting on this subject brought trouble from his own government's border officials.
coulthart-republican-presidents-briefed-: Republican presidents of the United States sometimes seem to be told about UFO secrets while Democratic presidents are not, according to the journalist Ross Coulthart. The researcher Jason Simosa passes this on second-hand, saying Coulthart recently pointed out the contrast. If true, it would mean that who learns the secret depends on party politics rather than on holding the office.
coulthart-s-changing-sources-on-the-dron: During the 2024 wave of drone sightings over the United States, the journalist Ross Coulthart is said to have kept citing his sources with great confidence while those sources kept changing the story. The hip hop musician Flying Lotus tells this from watching Coulthart's reporting at the time: "my sources say this and my sources say that."
cousteau-s-atlantis-obsession-shared-wit: Jacques Cousteau, the famous ocean explorer, is said to have admitted to his friend Robert Maxwell, a publisher, and his family that his whole interest in oceanography came from an obsession with finding Atlantis, the legendary lost island. The philosopher Jason Jorjani tells it, adding that this is why Maxwell's daughter, Ghislaine Maxwell, was obsessed with Atlantis from childhood. It would mean one of the best-known scientists of the sea was secretly hunting a myth.
cover-contract-through-the-bia-near-whit: In 2001 a secret team worked under a cover contract with the Bureau of Indian Affairs, the US agency that deals with Native American tribes, on a sovereign tribal nation close to White Sands Missile Range in New Mexico. That is how Jake Barber, a helicopter pilot who says he flew a recovered UFO, describes it, and he says he was part of it. If true, it would mean UFO work was hidden behind ordinary government contracts.
cover-up-of-retrieved-craft-and-beings-s: Since about 1947, according to Robert Salas, a former US Air Force officer, there has been a serious effort to cover up anything about recovered craft and the beings inside them. Salas states this as his own view without naming a source; if true, it would mean the government has hidden such recoveries for most of a century.
coyame-lights-around-mountain-peaks: People living near Coyame, in the Mexican state of Chihuahua, often talk about colored lights that wink on and off around the mountain peaks. Michels repeats this from Mexico's Roswell, a book by the writers Noe Torres and Ruben Uriarte about a claimed UFO incident in the area. He tells it as part of why the region is seen as a hotspot for strange activity.
craft-beam-lasers-over-nuclear-stockpile: In 1975 or 1976, unknown craft flew over Loring Air Force Base in northern Maine and shot laser-like beams down, as if mapping where the nuclear weapons were stored. Charlie Foltz tells this in summary, without naming a source. If true, it would mean something was surveying America's nuclear arms.
craft-crash-in-northern-iran: A craft crashed in northern Iran and the United States had to try to go in after it, according to Steven Greer, a UFO researcher who runs a campaign to make government UFO secrets public. Greer mentions it only in passing on a 2025 episode with Jesse Michels, giving no date and no source, saying "there was one that crashed and went down in northern Iran that we had to try to go in." If true, it would mean crash retrievals reach well beyond American soil.
craft-entering-and-leaving-the-atmospher: Unexplained craft come in and out of Earth's atmosphere, according to a Pentagon whistleblower named Matthew Brown. He says he knows this from material he saw while working on the inside, and from other people's testimony as well.
craft-flew-due-north-to-a-soft-landing-1: In 1948 a craft that came down at Hart Canyon near Aztec, New Mexico, is said to have traveled "due north exactly" before a soft landing. The researcher Scott Ramsey, who has studied the site, says this from his own reconstruction of its path, which would suggest the craft was still under some kind of control.
craft-holed-by-gunfire-over-los-alamos-1: A researcher named Scott Ramsey offers a guess, and he calls it "only theory": a craft that came down in 1948 may have been hit by gunfire, something like a .50 caliber rifle or machine gun, while flying over Los Alamos, the New Mexico site where America built its atomic bomb. He thinks a hole like that might have caused "mass decompression" on board. He gives this as his own idea for why the craft and its crew were lost, and cites no source.
craft-hovered-over-new-underwood-reservo: In 1977 a craft hung over the water at the New Underwood Lake Reservoir dam in South Dakota, says Mario Woods, a former Air Force security guard at nuclear missile sites, who says he was there. He places it by its position inside a triangle drawn between two missile sites called November 1 and November 5, the reservoir, and back to the November 1 control post. If he is right, an unknown craft was sitting right beside American nuclear weapons.
craft-hovering-in-s4-hangars: Visitors are said to have gone all the way into S4, a secret site near Area 51 in Nevada, ridden down in big elevators, and seen three or four craft hovering inside the hangars. The lawyer Dan Sheehan relays this second-hand, tying it to a man named Oscar Wolf and to Bob Lazar and Dan Burisch, two men who have each made claims about the site. If true, unexplained craft would be kept under the Nevada desert.
craft-hull-material-as-an-electret-1987: Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft at a secret site called S4 in the Nevada desert in the late 1980s, believes the craft's hull was made of an electret. An electret is a material that always carries an electric field, he explains, just as a magnet always carries a magnetic one. Lazar gives this as his own idea from what he says he saw there, in one version placing his time at the site in 1988 and 1989, and if true it would help explain how the craft worked.
craft-looks-different-up-close-than-from: A craft he worked on looked like a proper craft when you stood close to it, but "when you get far away, it doesn't look right." That is what Bob Lazar says, a man who claims he worked on alien craft in 1988 and 1989 at S-4, a secret site in the Nevada desert, and he tells it as something he saw himself. If true, it would mean the craft bent how it looked to anyone watching from a distance.
craft-s-power-system-explained-aboard-li: During a 1976 encounter at Eagle Lake, Maine, a witness named Charlie Foltz says he was taken aboard a craft, asked how it was powered, and was told it "works like the submarine working with a bubble of air." Foltz tells it himself as part of his own abduction account and also puts it another way, as a gravity-based drive that runs at different "atmospheres" the way a submarine works at different depths, which would hint at how such craft move if true.
craft-shot-down-before-crashing-1996: In 1996 near Varginha, Brazil, a craft that is said to have crashed there was shot down first: people say someone fired on it and it was already falling when it arrived. Italo Venturelli, a surgeon tied to a hospital where a captured creature is said to have been taken, passes this on from others, pointing to a young man named Carlos de Souza as the witness who will tell you so. If true, it would mean someone attacked the craft before it came down.
craft-vanishing-into-mountains-in-the-ui: Unknown craft have been seen flying into mountains and vanishing, and Jesse Michels calls this a documented pattern, pointing to Utah's Uinta Basin as a place where it happens often. Michels says this himself and does not name a source. If true, it would suggest these craft have hidden places inside the land.
craft-wall-turns-translucent-and-shows-3: Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft at S-4, a secret site in the Nevada desert, in 1988 and 1989, says that while he was there he saw a craft's wall turn see-through, and in one summary of his story it then showed three-dimensional symbols. Lazar tells it to Michels in two episodes, both times in the same few words, "I saw the wall become translucent," and the second time he gives no place, date or symbols. If true, it would point to a material far beyond anything people know how to make.
crane-as-the-navy-s-off-world-reverse-en: Naval Surface Warfare Center Crane, a Navy research base, is said to be the center of the Navy's efforts to take apart and copy technology from beyond Earth, just as Wright-Patterson, an Air Force base, is said to be for the Air Force. Michels tells this himself, passing on what unnamed contacts told him. If true, each military branch would have its own hub for studying craft not made by humans.
crane-brinton-s-last-lecture-on-humanity: In May 1968, Crane Brinton, the chairman of the Department of Intellectual History at Harvard, gave a last lecture on what he saw as humanity's next step in evolution, says Dan Sheehan, who was in the room as a young man. According to Sheehan, Brinton told the students that this was why so many young men there refused to go and fight in the war in Vietnam. Sheehan tells it as a remark that struck him, from a senior scholar speaking directly to his generation.
crane-symbols-match-sheehan-s-drawings-2: In 2014, at Naval Surface Warfare Center Crane, a Navy research base in Indiana, a man named Randy Anderson says he saw symbols that closely match drawings made by a man named Dan Sheehan. Anderson tells it as something he saw himself, and in his words, "what he had draw is very close to what I seen." He tells it because, if true, two separate people would have recorded the same strange markings, which he links to technology he believes is not human.
cranial-modification-told-to-have-been-o: Peoples around the world, including the Maya, reshaped their children's skulls, and when one group was asked why, they said their ancestors had been told to do it by the gods. The anthropologist Mike Masters gives this from a 1995 paper by the researchers Gerszten and Gerszten, who interviewed the group. He raises it because it would suggest the practice began as imitation of visitors seen as gods.
crash-debris-analysed-as-aluminum-and-ba: Debris from a crashed object was tested in the 1950s and found to be aluminum and barium, and barium also shows up in the work of the inventor Townsend Brown: written on a chalkboard at the labs where he worked, and in his Winterhaven proposal, a plan in which he meant to use barium in a motor for his "gravitator discs". Michels tells this himself in his documentary on Brown, citing a man named Michael Swords. He raises it because the match would tie the crash debris to Brown's own designs for flying craft.
crash-debris-and-government-pen-at-archu: In the early 1980s on Archuleta Mesa in New Mexico, a police officer named Gabe Valdez is said to have found broken brush, signs that something had been lifted away, and a pen marked "US government property." The writer Greg Bishop passes this on as what Valdez told him. It would suggest the government had quietly picked something up from the mesa.
crash-investigations-with-usaf-cia-invol: Michels says, without naming a source, that when unexplained craft crash, the US Air Force and the CIA, the US spy agency, always seem to be involved. He gives cases in Virginia and in Brazil as examples, which would point to a single hidden hand behind crash recoveries.
crash-retrieval-program-head-refused-to-: The man who headed a secret programme to recover crashed craft during that era, named as Glenn Gaffney, refused to be interviewed, according to the physicist Eric W. Davis. Davis says this in connection with the film project Age of Disclosure: "I would love to talk to the head of the crash retrieval program during that era, but he refused to talk to us." Had Gaffney talked, he could have spoken to whether such a programme exists.
crash-retrieval-traced-back-to-sarbacher: Stories of governments recovering crashed alien craft are said to go back to the scientist Robert Sarbacher in 1950, and even earlier, to Italy under the dictator Benito Mussolini in 1933. A UFO researcher who goes by the online name UAPGerb tells Michels this in passing, without naming a source. If true, it would mean such recoveries began well before the famous 1947 events in Roswell, New Mexico.
crash-site-regraded-for-soybeans-after-t: A surgeon named Carlos de Souza, whose hospital he says operated on an alien, says that a reported crash site near Varginha, Brazil, sat untouched for 26 years. Then, right after a documentary by the filmmaker James Fox came out, someone came and graded the land, and in his words removed "more than 30 meters of earth." De Souza says Fox went to the site shortly afterwards and saw the regrading too. He wants someone to explain the timing, because if he is right, it would look like evidence was cleared away once people started paying attention.
crash-sites-with-bob-wood-that-turned-ou: Joe McMoneagle, a guest who appears on the show to talk about life on Mars, says he went to a number of crash sites with a researcher named Bob Wood, and every one of them turned out to be an American plane. He says he was there himself, and the story matters because it suggests some reported crashes of unknown craft were really crashes of our own aircraft.
crash-tech-moved-from-wright-patterson-t: A crashed UFO might have been taken to Wright Patterson, an Air Force base in Ohio, and its technology later passed into private hands. Scott Ramsey offers this openly as speculation, without naming a source. If so, the study of such craft would sit with companies rather than the government.
crashed-craft-found-with-nothing-inside: When unknown craft crash, a lot of people say nothing is found inside them, no crew and no bodies. Michels says this himself on an episode with the writer Randall Carlson, passing it on from unnamed others. If true, it would hint that such craft fly without anyone on board, like drones.
crashed-saucer-from-the-1940s-and-a-secr: If the United States holds a flying saucer that crashed in the 1940s, and another country holds one too, then there must be an agreement between those countries not to talk about it. A researcher named Peter Levenda puts this to Michels as his own reasoning, without naming a source, to explain why no government has spoken openly.
crashes-as-deliberate-seeding-gorilla-in: Some crashes of unknown craft may not have been accidents at all, but a kind of deliberate seeding, like dropping an object into a gorilla's cage to see what it does. David Grusch, a former Air Force intelligence officer, passes on this idea from someone he calls Luis. If true, it would mean whoever made the craft let humans find them on purpose.
crawling-inside-the-craft-three-seat-lik: Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft at a secret site called S-4 in Nevada in 1988 and 1989, says he crawled inside one of the craft and found three things that looked like seats, which are described as amplifiers that were part of how it worked. Another guest, Jeremy Corbell, repeats what Lazar told him, stressing that Lazar says he was inside a craft from another planet and saw others too, without mentioning the seats. If true, it would mean someone in the US was handling a craft that was not made by humans.
critias-s-myth-of-athens-war-with-atlant: An ancient Athens is said to have fought a great war against Atlantis, a powerful island nation, about nine thousand years before the time of the Greek philosopher Plato. The story comes from two of Plato's dialogues, the Timaeus and the Critias, read here in Benjamin Jowett's English translation. In them a speaker named Critias tells Socrates the tale, which he says reached his family from Solon, the Athenian lawgiver. Critias opens by saying that "nine thousand was the sum of years which had elapsed since the war" between those who lived "outside the pillars of Heracles" and all who lived within them, and he tells of "a mighty power which unprovoked made an expedition against the whole of Europe and Asia, and to which your city put an end." The researcher James Madden, summarising it for Michels, calls it a myth, "another good lie" told by Critias. The researcher Matt LaCroix treats it as real early history, crediting both Plato and the later Greek writer Plutarch and calling the fighters "proto-Athenians". Michels himself puts the war 9,000 years back and recalls the festival where the tale was first told. The text reads differently from the word myth: Critias calls it "a tale which, though strange, is certainly true," Socrates repeats that it is "not a mere legend, but an actual fact," and the festival was the Apaturia, where the elder Critias, nearly ninety, told it to the younger, then about ten. If true, it would mean a forgotten chapter of human history lies far older than recorded Greece.
critique-of-the-khafre-pyramid-sar-scan-: In 2025 a team linked to a researcher named Filippo Biondi used radar imaging (SAR, a satellite radar method that can build pictures of what lies under a surface) and announced structures inside the Khafre pyramid, one of the great pyramids at Giza in Egypt. A researcher named Luke Caverns says they did not really detect anything new: according to him, they took a 3D model of the king's chamber and the small chambers above it in a different pyramid, copied it five times inside Khafre, and said "this is what they're detecting." He tells it as his own critique of how the result was presented.
crohn-s-disease-healed-after-the-2007-or: A man named Chris Bledsoe says that after an encounter with glowing orbs of light in North Carolina in 2007, his Crohn's disease, a long-lasting and painful illness of the gut, simply went away. Bledsoe tells this himself, as the person it happened to. In his words, "my Crohn's was gone," and he had "no more sickness." Michels repeats it during the same conversation, saying that on the one hand Bledsoe was cured of Crohn's. Michels places the encounter in January 2007. The two are not separate witnesses, since Michels is echoing what Bledsoe has told him. It matters to them because it would mean the encounter did something real to his body, a healing he links to the orbs.
crookes-tube-jump-observed-by-brown-as-a: As a student at Caltech in Pasadena in the 1920s, the inventor Townsend Brown is said to have seen the wire carrying high voltage into a Crookes tube, an early glass vacuum tube, jump when the power was applied. The journalist and author Nick Cook tells this in a documentary about Brown as the moment that started Brown's lifelong work on whether electricity could produce motion or lift, work that was later linked to UFO-like craft.
crowley-s-lam-entity: The English occultist Aleister Crowley is said to have had an alien-like being, an entity known as Lam, seem to show up to him. Michels brings this up only in passing, in a 2026 episode with Tim Alberino, describing Crowley as "another guy" who had such an encounter.
crown-prince-hans-adam-s-armageddon-agen: At a 1994 meeting at the Pierre Hotel in New York, Hans-Adam, then Crown Prince of Liechtenstein, is said to have explained a plan to make the public hate aliens so much that an interplanetary war would follow, bringing Armageddon so that Christ would return. The UFO researcher Steven Greer says he was there, and he presents the words as a direct quote; his account also names Laurance Rockefeller, Budd Hopkins, John Mack and David Jacobs. If true, it would mean powerful people wanted to steer public fear of aliens toward a religious end.
cruickshank-s-archival-research-into-ken: The claim is that a researcher named Jeff Cruickshank has dug through the archives of President John F. Kennedy, looking at declassified records from the 1960s alongside the MJ12 documents, papers said to describe a secret group of twelve that handled UFO matters. A guest named Matthew Pines mentions this in passing, calling it a forensic, historical deep dive, without naming his source. If the work holds up, it would test whether those papers fit the real Kennedy-era record.
cryo-chambers-on-mars: It is said that there are cold-sleep chambers on Mars, with people who were left there. The philosopher Jason Jorjani passes this on from Joe McMoneagle, who worked as a psychic spy, or "remote viewer", for the US Army, and who reported seeing it that way. If true, people from somewhere were stored on another planet.
cryptography-to-speak-with-angelic-being: The first code-makers of Europe used secret writing to talk with angelic beings, as Michels puts it in a conversation with the philosopher Jason Jorjani. He names the German abbot Johannes Trithemius, whom he places in the 13th century, along with the English scholar John Dee and Dee's partner Edward Kelley, and says their cryptography was always aimed at reaching these beings. If so, the roots of code-making would lie in attempts at contact with something not human.
ct-scan-of-the-implant-arranged-by-an-un: The writer Whitley Strieber says an insider, whom he does not name, wanted him to get a CT scan, a detailed X-ray image of the inside of the body, of an implant: a small object he believes was placed in his body. Strieber tells it as something he took part in himself, in California, and he credits the scan as a record of the object. If true, it would mean someone on the inside took his implant claim seriously enough to want it imaged.
cumbre-vieja-eruption-and-lyn-buchanan-s: When the Cumbre Vieja volcano on the Spanish island of La Palma erupted in 2021, the researcher Jason Jorjani says he was messaging a man named Lyn Buchanan, whose earlier warning the story turns on, asking, "Lynn, do you think this is it? Like, should I leave New York?" Jorjani tells it as something he lived through himself, since he was in New York at the time and took the warning seriously enough to ask whether the city was in danger.
current-astronauts-with-their-own-experi: Some astronauts still working today have had their own unexplained encounters, according to Ryan Graves, a former Navy fighter pilot. He says he has spoken with them himself, though he gives no names or details. If so, people now flying in space would be seeing these things too.
curse-of-king-tut-s-tomb: The tomb of Tutankhamun, an ancient Egyptian king, is said to bring misfortune to those who disturb it. The researcher Luke Caverns says nearly everyone on the excavation led by the archaeologist Howard Carter met with tragedy, and that several died from poisoning after breathing the air inside the chamber. Michels, speaking himself, puts it differently: a couple of people tried to x-ray it and then died mysteriously. It is told as a warning about what may lie sealed in such places.
curtis-lemay-chases-townsend-brown-down-: The Air Force general Curtis LeMay once went after the inventor Thomas Townsend Brown down a flight of stairs, according to Brown's daughter Linda Brown, who says she saw it. Michels passes the story on in two episodes, calling it a chase and placing it in the 1950s, while Linda Brown, telling it herself, says LeMay "kind of followed my dad down the steps." It is told as a sign that Brown's work had caught the attention of the most senior military men.
curtis-lemay-gave-d-harold-byrd-a-civil-: Curtis LeMay, a top US Air Force general, once gave a Texas businessman named D. Harold Byrd an award for his work with the Civil Air Patrol, a volunteer civilian branch attached to the Air Force, when Byrd was younger. Jesse Michels brings this up himself, without naming a source, in a 2025 episode about President John F. Kennedy with a lawyer named Danny Sheehan. He offers it as a sign that Byrd had close ties to military power.
custody-chain-manhattan-project-to-aec-t: In the 1940s, recovered UFO material is said to have been held first by the Manhattan Project, the secret wartime effort to build the atomic bomb, then passed to the Atomic Energy Commission, the agency that later ran US nuclear work, and on to the Department of Energy. David Grusch, a former intelligence officer who became a whistleblower, tells it as what he was told: "The Manhattan Project would have custody of it, and then it would go into the Atomic Energy Commission." Michels repeats Grusch in a different way, saying the same people from the Manhattan Project laid their system of atomic secrecy over UFO secrets. The analyst Matthew Pines also echoes Grusch, naming the Atomic Energy Act of 1946, the law that set the rules for nuclear secrecy, as the framework these programmes sat under through the 1940s, 50s and 60s. If true, it would mean UFO secrets were hidden inside the nuclear secrecy system from the start.
custody-of-the-trinity-craft-passed-thro: A strange craft said to have been recovered in 1945, around the time of Trinity, the first atomic bomb test, would have been held first by the Manhattan Project, the wartime US effort that built the bomb, then by the Atomic Energy Commission that took over nuclear work after the war, and then by the Department of Energy, "which has its own line of clearances." The French computer scientist and longtime UFO researcher Jacques Vallée lays out this chain on two episodes of Michels' show; in one he links it to the researcher Paola Harris and the bomb's scientific leader J. Robert Oppenheimer, and in the other he speaks only of UFO material in general from the 1940s on. If true, it would mean such material sat inside the nuclear secrecy system, out of the military's ordinary view.
cybertruck-bomber-s-email-to-shoemate-ab: Matthew Livelsberger, a Green Beret soldier who blew up a Tesla Cybertruck in Las Vegas in 2025, had emailed a man named Sam Shoemate saying the mysterious drones seen over New Jersey and the East Coast in the previous two months were cutting-edge Chinese drones that fly by gravitic propulsion, a way of moving by manipulating gravity. Michels tells this on two episodes, saying Shoemate described the email on the podcast of Shawn Ryan, and once citing the FBI as well.
cydonia-said-to-hold-pyramids-the-remnan: Cydonia, a region of Mars, holds several pyramids that are the remains of a city, along with the famous "Face on Mars", a rock formation that looks like a face. Michels mentions it himself in two episodes, once with a psychic spy named Joe McMoneagle, and in the second he credits the idea to a writer named Richard Hoagland and his book Dark Mission. If true, it would mean someone once built on Mars.
cymatics-experiment-in-the-king-s-chambe: The claim is that scientists in the King's Chamber, the stone room at the heart of Egypt's Great Pyramid, stretched a membrane over the granite box called the sarcophagus. They used it like a Chladni plate, a surface that turns sound into visible patterns as sand settles on it. They sprinkled Egyptian sand on it, played the chamber's own vibrating frequency through it, and the sand formed the Eye of Horus, an ancient Egyptian eye symbol. A guest named Jay Anderson tells this on Michels's show and says it came from a man named David Elkington, who he says took part in the experiments. If true, it would suggest the chamber was built with sound in mind.
d-harold-byrd-s-vought-built-flying-sauc: In the 1940s and 1950s, the aircraft maker Vought, tied to a businessman named D. Harold Byrd, built all the flying saucers for Wright-Patterson, an Air Force base in Ohio, under a man named Alfred C. Loading. A researcher named Dan Sheehan tells this without naming a source. If true, it would mean the US was building saucer-shaped craft itself from the start.
daily-mail-cia-office-of-global-access-r: A little-known CIA office called the Office of Global Access is said to be the main part of a worldwide program that recovers crashed UFOs. Michels tells it many times, saying the story came from reporting in the Daily Mail, a British newspaper. In his words, the office is "the main you know part of the crash retrieval program all around the world." A researcher who goes by the online name UAPGerb credits the journalist Christopher Sharp with breaking the story. He says the office "was created under the DS&T in the year 2003", meaning the CIA's science and technology branch. Michels names a man called Doug Wolf as linked to the office, which he says did "rapid response" retrievals "all over the world" in the early 2000s. In one telling he adds, without citing the paper, that it is "rumored to coordinate closely" with the military's top special forces command and with teams that respond to nuclear emergencies. If true, it would mean the CIA has a standing team for collecting crashed craft around the globe.
daily-mail-egg-shaped-ufo-from-area-51-2: An egg-shaped craft of unknown origin is said to have been recovered at Area 51, the secret military test site in the Nevada desert. Michels brings it up in a 2024 episode as something the British newspaper the Daily Mail reported "a year ago", which puts the report around 2023. If true, it would mean the United States holds a recovered craft that nobody can explain. A guest named Marik von Rennenkampff tells it in an early 2025 debate episode, but he traces it to a different source. He says a man named Eric Taber went to AARO, the Pentagon office that now investigates UFO reports, and spoke of an egg-shaped craft being retrieved. Von Rennenkampff adds that he believes this was at Area 51. He passes on what Taber said rather than anything he saw, and he gives no date.
daily-sensor-observations-of-spheres-off: In 2014 and 2015, Navy fighter jets training in a big block of sky off Virginia Beach on the US East Coast picked up round objects nearly every day, says Ryan Graves, a fighter pilot who flew there. He says the objects showed up once their jets got a newer radar, and that the radar, a camera pod used for aiming, and the seeker head of a heat-seeking missile all detected the same things, which told them a physical object was there. Graves says they did not assume these were UFOs and wondered if a foreign adversary was spying by soaking up their radar signals, and another guest, Marik von Rennenkampff, repeats his account.
dalai-lama-meets-john-mack-about-aliens-: The Dalai Lama, the Tibetan Buddhist leader, is said to have met the Harvard psychiatrist John Mack in the 1990s to talk about aliens, and the two found their worldviews in close kinship. Michels mentions it himself, without naming a source, in an episode about the idea that we live in a hologram. He brings it up to show a major spiritual figure taking the alien question seriously.
dale-new-mexico-as-a-tall-white-playgrou: The country around Dale, New Mexico is "one of the tall white playgrounds," a place where tall, pale beings he calls the Tall Whites like to spend time. So says Charles Hall, a man who says he spent three years living alongside these beings at Area 51, a secret Air Force base in Nevada, and he speaks from what he says he saw himself. If true, it would mean these beings move freely around parts of the American Southwest.
dalton-fury-bin-laden-in-sights-three-ti: An officer of the Army's elite Delta Force, known as Dalton Fury, had Osama bin Laden under direct watch three separate times at Tora Bora in Afghanistan in 2001 and was refused permission to strike. John Blitch, a scientist who worked for the Pentagon's advanced research agency, tells Michels that Fury said this in disguise to the journalist Scott Pelley on the television news program 60 Minutes, and if true it would mean the man behind the September 11 attacks could have been stopped. That report, "Elite Officer Recalls Bin Laden Hunt", aired on 5 October 2008. In it Fury says two of his unit's plans, coming over the mountains from Pakistan and mining the passes into Pakistan, were "disapproved" higher up, and the report notes that "The military wouldn't tell 60 Minutes who rejected the plans or why." It says nothing of three sightings, and on the night his team was "about 2,000 meters away" from where they thought bin Laden was, Fury himself chose not to advance: "It wasn't worth the risk at that particular moment to go up there and play cowboy."
dam-flooded-the-egyptian-labyrinth-in-th: In the 1960s, the story goes, a dam built to help Egyptian farmers sent water into the Egyptian labyrinth, a vast ancient maze-like building, and flooded it. The podcaster Joe Rogan tells it to Michels, passing on what a man named Ben van Kerkwijk told him, and he points to the ancient Greek historian Herodotus and the Roman writer Pliny the Elder as the old writers who described the labyrinth. If it is true, a great ancient structure would be lying underwater and out of reach.
dan-burisch-and-j-rod-at-s4-2003: A microbiologist named Dan Burisch is said to have worked at S4, a site tied to Area 51, the secret military base in the Nevada desert. There, around 2003 and 2004, he is said to have dealt with "J-Rod", a living extraterrestrial that had been recovered and was kept six or seven levels underground. The guest known online as UAPGerb passes this on as what Burisch has said, and if it were true it would mean the US government held a live alien being.
dan-howe-vouches-for-dan-sherman-s-elint: A man named Dan Howe is said to have vouched for Dan Sherman, a man who has told of working in a secret program and whose account came up under the name Project Preserve Destiny. According to the online UFO researcher who goes by UAPGerb, Howe sat him down at a gathering and spoke for a long time about how Sherman's description of ELINT, short for electronic intelligence, meaning the gathering of signals from radar and other electronic systems, was "just beautifully on the money." UAPGerb tells this on the podcast as something Howe told him in person, and if Howe is right, Sherman's insider account fits how such systems really work.
dan-sheehan-discredited-through-stigma-1: In the late 1980s, someone tried to discredit the lawyer Dan Sheehan by tying him to the stigma around UFOs, because he was digging into the Iran-Contra affair, a 1980s US scandal over secret arms sales to Iran, through a legal group called the Christic Institute. The mathematician Eric Weinstein tells Michels this, passing on what he understands from Sheehan, and says Sheehan was probably fed wrong information so that he would "swing at a bad pitch." The point, as Weinstein tells it, is that UFO stories can be used as bait to make a serious investigator look foolish.
dan-sherman-and-nsa-project-preserve-des: A former Air Force sergeant named Dan Sherman says that in the early 1990s he was taken to a building of the National Security Agency, the US government's eavesdropping and code agency, in Laurel, Maryland. There, he says, a Captain White told him he was part of Project Preserve Destiny, a secret effort that began in 1960 after the US made contact with an alien species in 1947, and he was trained to receive messages from that species through tones. Sherman tells this first-hand on the show and in his book Above Black, and Michels has retold it several times, once adding that Sherman says he was genetically altered in the womb after his mother was abducted while pregnant.
dan-sherman-taken-to-an-nsa-complex-for-: In the 1990s, a man named Dan Sherman says he was taken to a complex of the National Security Agency, the US government's code-breaking and eavesdropping agency, in Maryland, possibly at Fort Meade, and given headphones for training with sine-wave tones. Michels relays this from Sherman's own account in the book Above Black. If true, it would mean a secret government programme was training people to pick up signals of some unusual kind.
dan-wilson-links-green-fireballs-to-radi: In the late 1940s, glowing green lights in the sky known as green fireballs are said to have appeared at the same times as radiation drifting across the American landscape. The researcher Robert Hastings, who studies UFOs at nuclear sites, credits a researcher named Dan Wilson with spending many hours tracking down these sightings, which would tie the lights to nuclear activity.
daniel-gockerell-triangle-sighting: A man named Daniel Gockerell says he saw a triangle-shaped object in the sky. The filmmaker Jeremy Corbell, who makes documentaries about UFOs, mentions it to Michels as a small story. He passes it on from Gockerell, who told it as a guest on Corbell's own show, Weaponized, and he gives no time or place for the sighting.
daniel-s-encounter-with-a-being-by-the-t: The biblical prophet Daniel, standing on the bank of the Tigris River, sees a being "with a face like lightning and eyes like torches," and in another episode Michels points out that the being's first words to him were "fear not," spoken before Daniel received his prophecy. Michels tells it himself from the Book of Daniel, as an old account of a meeting with something not human. In the King James Bible, published in 1611, Daniel calls the river Hiddekel, the Hebrew name for the Tigris, and describes "a certain man clothed in linen" whose face was "as the appearance of lightning" and whose eyes were "as lamps of fire," and who said, "Fear not, Daniel."
daniel-sheehan-as-chief-of-station-for-t: A man named Daniel Sheehan is said to have served in the 1970s as "chief of station" in Washington, DC for the Jesuits, the Catholic religious order. The phrase usually means the head of a spy agency's local office, and the researcher Matthew Pines says it half joking, calling them "intelligence bad guys," and gives no source. If taken at face value, it would cast a Catholic order as running its own intelligence network in the American capital.
dannion-brinkley-s-holographic-life-revi: A man named Dannion Brinkley, who nearly died, is said to have gone through what he called a "holographic panoramic, three-dimensional review" of his whole life. In it he had to replay every moment from the point of view of the other people involved, so that, having killed people as a soldier in the Vietnam War, he felt what it was like to take a bullet from himself. The researcher Rizwan Virk, presented as an MIT scientist, passes this on from Brinkley to Michels as a hint that reality may work like a hologram.
danny-jones-interview-throttled-over-a-m: In 2025, an interview Chris Bledsoe gave to the podcaster Danny Jones had its reach held back because he talked about some technology at NASA's Mission Control, Bledsoe says. Bledsoe, a man NASA is said to study because UFOs seem to appear around him, tells it about his own interview, as a sign that someone did not want that subject aired.
danny-s-dmt-laser-experiments-reveal-cod: A man Michels calls only "Danny" does experiments where he shines lasers through a diffraction pattern while on DMT, a powerful psychedelic drug, and the patterns are said to reveal a kind of code behind reality. Michels calls Danny his "buddy" and raises the experiments with the neuroscientist Andrew Gallimore in a 2025 episode, asking what he makes of them. Gallimore offers a different explanation, laser speckle, the grainy pattern any laser makes.
danny-sheehan-says-he-has-coordinates-fo: A man named Danny Sheehan said in 2024 that he has the map coordinates of an underwater UFO base, placed in the sea off Baja California, near Guadalupe Island. A guest named Marik von Rennenkampff repeats this as something Sheehan told him: "he said that he has coordinates for a UFO underwater base." If it were true, it would point to a hidden base under the ocean that someone could actually go and find.
danny-sheehan-shown-blue-book-files-and-: A lawyer named Dan Sheehan says that in the late 1970s, at the request of President Jimmy Carter's administration, he was let into a secure room in Washington to look at the files of Blue Book, the US Air Force's UFO study of the 1950s and 60s. There, he says, he saw clear photos of a crashed UFO, with strange symbols around the base of its dome, which he traced. Sheehan tells it firsthand and Michels often repeats it, but the details shift: the room is a basement room in the Madison building, the craft is on a mountaintop, in a snowy field or stuck in an embankment, and one telling puts it as early as 1974.
darkness-retreat-study-testing-for-spike: A study planned in Florida in 2025 will test whether people kept in total darkness for days produce a surge of DMT, a powerful psychedelic chemical the body is thought to make in small amounts. The neuroscientist Andrew Gallimore says he and New Nordics, a group he works with in Florida, are paying for the study. If such a surge were found, it would suggest the brain can reach DMT-like states on its own.
darpa-man-talking-to-a-computer-with-his: Around 1974, a man at DARPA, the Pentagon agency that funds advanced research, is said to have told a visitor, "I'm talking to this machine with my mind." The UFO researcher Grant Cameron tells this as something he heard from a man named Bob Emenegger, who was the visitor. If true, it would mean the military was trying out mind-to-computer links decades ago.
darpa-n3-brain-machine-interface-program: In 2018, DARPA, the Pentagon agency that funds advanced military research, launched a program called N3, short for "next generation non-surgical neurotechnology": a way to link the brain to machines without surgery. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, in a 2026 episode about a UFO book he says the Pentagon tried to censor. He brings it up as a sign that the military was interested in reaching into the human mind.
darpa-programs-with-nine-figure-budgets-: Some programmes at DARPA, the Pentagon's agency for advanced military research, are said to have had budgets in the hundreds of millions of dollars and, in certain cases, to have been made secret and moved to Area 51, the classified Air Force test site in the Nevada desert. The researcher John Brandenburg says this on the show. He links it to a DARPA programme manager named John Blitch who came to see him, but he says plainly that Blitch never said it and that the link to the secret site is his own guess.
darpa-robot-mission-to-search-tora-bora-: In 2001 and 2002, a team from DARPA, the Pentagon's agency for advanced research, is said to have sent robots into the caves of Tora Bora in Afghanistan to search for Osama bin Laden, working out of Bagram Airfield. John Blitch, who says he took part, explains that he went because his former boss, a man named Jumo Brown, asked for him by name, and he names others involved, including Allan Mack and Tim Gallaudet. Blitch, who in the same conversation says he was abducted by an alien, tells it to show the kind of secret military work he did.
darpa-s-far-exception-and-canceled-steal: John Blitch, who worked at DARPA, the Pentagon's advanced research agency, in the late 1990s, says he oversaw $130 million in projects, half of it robots and half a stealth programme that was cancelled about a month after it got going, "for no reason." He tells it from his own experience and says it matches what a General Trudeau told Philip J. Corso, an Army colonel who claimed he handed crash material to industry, to do, suggesting the cancellation was a cover for hidden work.
darpa-sid-program-protection-would-kill-: There is said to be something called SID inside DARPA, the US military's research agency, that will simply kill anyone it judges to be a threat from inside or outside. The claim comes from a researcher who goes by UAPGerb online (UAP is the government's term for UFOs), summarising without a named source, though he connects it to David Grusch, an intelligence officer turned whistleblower, and to a tweet of his own about it. If true, it would mean a secret programme guarded by lethal force.
darpa-smart-dust-field-tests-1990: By 2001, DARPA, the Pentagon's agency for advanced research, was field testing "smart dust," tiny sensors so small they can float like dust. Jesse Michels says this himself, without naming a source, in a 2026 episode about a UFO book the Pentagon tried to censor. He raises it as an example of how far secret military technology had already come.
darpa-special-access-program-to-reverse-: Around 2000, John Blitch ran a highly restricted secret project, the kind the military calls a special access program, to copy the camouflage of octopus and squid. He worked at DARPA, the Pentagon's agency for advanced research, and also says an alien once abducted him. He describes the work as his own, mentions the researchers Roger Hanlon, Benny Hochner and Tamar Flash alongside it, and tells it as an example of the military turning nature's tricks into technology.
darwin-s-dog-that-inherited-a-fear-of-bu: Charles Darwin, the naturalist, is said to have reported a dog, belonging to someone he knew, that got very frightened every time it walked past a butcher's shop, as if it had inherited the fear. The scientist Rupert Sheldrake tells this case and says it appeared in a paper in Nature, the science journal, though he gives no date or further detail. He brings it up because, if true, it would suggest that fears and memories can pass down from one generation to the next.
daryl-bem-s-backward-causality-study-and: The psychologist Daryl Bem of Cornell University published research in the Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, appearing around 2010 and 2011, that claimed to show backward causality: people seeming to respond to events before those events happened. According to the well-known skeptic Michael Shermer, other researchers then tried to repeat the experiments and could not get the same results, and he says this is how psychology's "replication crisis" began, the wider discovery that many published findings do not hold up. Shermer gives this from his own knowledge of the field, mentioning other researchers such as Ray Hyman, Richard Wiseman and Stuart Ritchie.
dating-the-sphinx-by-its-vernal-equinox-: The Great Sphinx at Giza is said to be about 12,500 years old rather than 4,500, because that is when, at sunrise on the spring equinox, it would have looked straight at the constellation of Leo, the lion, while the three belt stars of Orion stood due south. The writer Graham Hancock tells this himself, crediting the researcher Robert Bauval, and the researcher Randall Carlson repeats it from them. Jesse Michels also brings it up twice but credits Hancock with the geologist Robert Schoch, stressing that the Sphinx was carved as a lion in honour of the age when the slow shift of the sky put the sun in Leo.
daughter-s-question-at-the-church-of-the: A former CIA officer named Rolf Mowatt-Larssen remembers a question his daughter asked at the Church of the Holy Sepulchre in Jerusalem, a church built where Jesus is said to have been crucified and buried. The CIA is the US spy agency for foreign intelligence. He tells it as her father: it happened the first time she went there and saw what is shown as Jesus's cross, though what she asked is not spelled out.
dava-holloman-film-withheld-from-vallee-: The story goes that in the 1970s the Defense Audiovisual Agency, a US military office that kept official film and video, held a film that two well-known UFO researchers, Jacques Vallée and the astronomer J. Allen Hynek, were invited to come and see. The physicist Eric W. Davis tells it from memory. He says the agency was run by two retired generals, one perhaps named Jerry Miller, and that Vallée writes about the episode in his book Revelations. As the title has it, the film was in the end withheld from the two men, which would mean the military was holding footage it chose not to show even to invited researchers.
dave-altman-connects-the-transient-dates: The astronomer Beatriz Villarroel says that dates in her data when brief, unexplained points of light appeared in the sky lined up with the wave of UFO sightings over Washington, D.C. in July 1952. She credits the link to a colleague, Dave Altman, the media manager for her project, which she calls WASCO, who asked her: "Do you know what happens on or what happened on 19th of July, 1952?" If it holds, her sky records would match a famous run of sightings over the US capital.
dave-rossi-s-fourth-orb-in-the-mh370-vid: A man named Dave Rossi is said to have spotted a fourth glowing orb in videos that some say show orbs around MH370, the Malaysian passenger flight lost over Southeast Asia in 2014. A Navy scientist named Salvatore Pais, who holds patents on UFO-like craft, passes this along, adding that it is why another man who studies the videos, Ashton Forbes, "now goes by four orbs." If it held up, the videos would show more around the plane than had been counted before.
david-ferrie-s-mysterious-death-1967: In 1967 in New Orleans, a man named David Ferrie died in mysterious circumstances, either by suicide or, as some suspect, killed and made to look like it, while Jim Garrison's investigation into President Kennedy's assassination was under way. The author Peter Levenda tells this without naming a source. It matters because a death in the middle of the investigation would silence a possible witness.
david-flynn-s-cydonia-book-reprinted-by-: A book called Cydonia by a writer named David Flynn, named after an area on Mars, was once so hard to find that copies sold for two to three thousand dollars, until Flynn's daughter reprinted it. The guest Tim Alberino says this from his own experience of the book, as a sign of how sought-after it was.
david-grusch-comes-forward-at-great-pers: In 2023 a former US intelligence officer named David Grusch went public with what he said he knew about the government and UFOs, and he lost his position and put his credibility on the line to do it. The UFO investigator James Fox tells it this way, saying Grusch came forward "at great personal sacrifice." Fox's point is that someone who gave up that much would have had little reason to make it up.
david-grusch-testimony-and-icig-report-2: A man named David Grusch is said to have sworn, before Washington, that the United States has been "generationally exploiting non-human technology", in other words studying and using machines that humans did not make. The filmmaker Jeremy Corbell brings this up on Michels' show in 2026 as something Grusch said publicly, "hand to God and to country", and ties it to a report from the Inspector General of the Intelligence Community, the office that looks into complaints inside the US spy agencies. If true, it would mean the government has been keeping such technology for generations.
david-grush-s-congressional-testimony-20: In 2023, David Grusch, an intelligence officer with the US agency that studies satellite and map imagery, testified under oath before Congress that the US government has a program dealing with UFOs because they are real. Jesse Michels dates the hearing to July 26, 2023, in Washington, and calls it Grusch blowing the whistle. Grusch himself says on the show that his claims rest on interviews with over 40 witnesses over four years. A former military official named Karl Nell says Grusch told the House Oversight Committee that a government program studies UFOs because they are real. The journalist Michael Shellenberger calls it "really strong testimony". The cognitive scientist Donald Hoffman describes sworn testimony from high-ranking officials who said they had seen "non-human biologics and non-human technology", without naming Grusch. If true, it would mean the government has hidden real non-human craft.
david-huggins-encounters-with-mantids-gr: A man named David Huggins claimed to have had encounters with alien beings, including tall insect-like creatures called mantids, small gray-skinned beings called grays, and a woman who was part human and part alien, in the US South and in underground places. The philosopher Jason Jorjani retells Huggins' claims, saying Huggins described the mantids as being "in charge of these little grays." If taken at face value, it would suggest a ranked order among different kinds of beings.
david-jay-brown-s-field-guide-to-dmt-ent: A book by the writer David Jay Brown, the Illustrated Field Guide to DMT Entities, sets out to catalogue the beings people say they meet on DMT, a powerful psychedelic drug. These include the "machine elves" made famous by the writer Terence McKenna and insect-like figures that seem to operate on the user. The neuroscientist Andrew Gallimore mentions the book to Michels as an example of how people try to describe these encounters, which matters to him because so many users report meeting similar beings.
david-morales-fired-the-fatal-shot-from-: The shot that killed President John F. Kennedy in Dallas in 1963, it is claimed, came from the grassy knoll, a small slope beside the motorcade's route, and was fired by a man named David Morales. The lawyer and activist Dan Sheehan says so on two episodes with Michels, which would mean a team of shooters, not one man. In the second telling he gives the name as Roger Morales and calls him the team's "dead eye" marksman.
david-ruiz-a-three-fingered-humanoid-spe: Strange three-fingered bodies found in Peru belong to a humanoid species, maybe a hominid like us, and not to beings from another planet. That is the view of David Ruiz, a researcher who says he has studied them for eight years and has never once used the word extraterrestrial. If he is right, it would point to an unknown human-like species here on Earth.
davis-asks-the-aps-historian-in-1984-whe: In 1984, at a meeting of the American Physical Society, the main professional body of US physicists, the physicist Eric W. Davis says he asked the society's historian where research into anti-gravity had gone. Davis tells it himself and says the question was prompted by Bob Forward, a physicist at Hughes Research Labs in Malibu who had been studying anti-gravity there, which hints that such research once existed in the open and then dropped from view.
davis-at-the-aerospace-corporation-in-hu: At the Aerospace Corporation's office in Huntsville, Alabama, there were only a few physicists with doctorates and they all spent their time on engineering, says the physicist Eric W. Davis, who has worked on Pentagon studies of UFOs. The Aerospace Corporation is a research group that works for the US military's space programmes, and Davis says he worked there for four and a half years, which is why he can say how few people there did real physics.
davis-briefs-senate-intelligence-and-arm: Eric W. Davis, a physicist who has done research for the Pentagon, says that starting in 2019 he briefed the staff of two US Senate committees, the one that oversees intelligence agencies and the one that oversees the armed forces. He says these briefings took place in classified settings, meaning closed and secret, and that he briefed the first group in 2019. He tells it as one of the people who did the briefing, as part of how Congress was told about UFOs.
davis-hired-by-cia-as-winpac-branch-chie: In late 2003, the CIA, America's foreign spy agency, hired a scientist named Eric W. Davis to be branch chief scientist of WINPAC, its center for weapons intelligence and arms control. Davis says this about himself as part of his own career. It matters because it would place him inside the intelligence world, the same world he speaks about when he discusses UFOs.
davis-joins-nids-bigelow-s-institute-199: The physicist Eric W. Davis says he worked at the National Institute for Discovery Science, a private research group in Las Vegas that Bob Bigelow founded in 1995, as its director of aerospace physics and astrophysics research. He tells it about himself, which places him inside a privately funded effort to study unexplained phenomena from its early days.
davis-meets-grusch-at-the-aerospace-corp: At the Aerospace Corporation, a research group that works for the US military's space programmes, in Colorado Springs, the physicist Eric W. Davis met David Grusch, a former intelligence officer who later spoke out publicly about UFOs, and passed him his data. Davis says this happened to him while he worked there, and that the introduction was made by Jay Stratton, a former Navy intelligence officer. It matters because it puts Davis's information behind Grusch's later claims.
davis-s-papers-for-marc-millis-s-propuls: Eric W. Davis, a physicist who has done research for the Pentagon, says he wrote papers for a program on advanced propulsion physics at NASA, the US space agency, run by a NASA researcher named Marc Millis. Davis says the work had nothing to do with UFOs and that he was simply contributing what he knew. He tells it about his own work, setting it apart from his UFO-related work.
davis-says-puthoff-interviewed-brad-sore: The physicist Hal Puthoff is said to have personally interviewed a man named Brad Sorensen. The guest known online as UAPGerb passes this on as something the physicist Eric Davis told him, and his own words break off mid-sentence: "cut off, well, Hal Putoff interviewed Brad Sorenson." If true, it would mean Puthoff took Sorensen's account seriously enough to question him himself, though what Sorensen said is not given here.
davis-takes-sap-security-training-he-and: A man named Eric W. Davis says that while working at the Aerospace Corporation, a research company, he went through security training for special access programs, the most tightly restricted kind of secret US government project, where only people on a named list may know about them. He also says he and David Grusch, a man who has come forward as a witness, talked about how secrets might be hidden inside SCIs, short for sensitive compartmented information, a separate category of classified intelligence, rather than inside special access programs. Davis tells it from his own experience, to explain where information about UFOs could be kept out of sight.
davis-told-definitively-that-we-are-moni: The physicist Eric W. Davis, who has worked as a scientist for the Pentagon, says he was told as fact that humanity is being watched and does not control its own airspace or the space around Earth. Davis says he is one hundred percent sure of this because it was told to him "definitively, not speculatively," as in "we know this to be true," though he does not name who told him. If true, it would mean someone inside government knows another presence is watching us.
davis-uses-dia-deputization-to-get-acces: A Pentagon scientist named Eric W. Davis says he got inside a secret program that recovers crashed craft. He used his security clearances and a letter from a Defense Intelligence Agency official named Jim Lacatski that made him an official representative of that agency, which is the US military's main intelligence service. Davis says he never saw any craft or bodies, but he reached the people who ran the program at the management level, and they told him "all of that was real, that all of it happened," which if true would mean the government holds non-human craft.
dc-fusion-center-foia-on-psychotronic-ef: A Washington, D.C. fusion center, a hub where federal and local agencies share intelligence, is said to have released a file on how certain technologies affect people's bodies and minds. The researcher Dave Rossi tells it without naming a source. As he describes it, someone used FOIA, a US law that lets anyone request government records, to ask about some political groups, and what came back included a file he thinks was called "effects on the human body." Rossi calls this a leak and offers it as a sign that the government has looked into such effects.
dead-labrador-nelly-photographed-as-a-ba: Chris Bledsoe, a North Carolina man known for reporting UFO encounters, says that in 2007, after a trip to see a rocket launch at Cape Canaveral in Florida, he photographed his dead Labrador, Nelly, rising out of her grave as a small ball of light. In his words, "she comes up out of her grave in a little ball of light. and I took that picture." He tells it first-hand, mentions a man named Timothy Taylor, and points to his book UFO of God, and he offers it as a sign that something of a living being goes on after death.
dead-man-switch-set-up-in-first-call-wit: In his very first conversation with a man named Jeremy Corbell, Dylan Borland says he told him, "I don't know you. You don't know me. I'm going to go become a congressional whistleblower," meaning someone who reports hidden wrongdoing to Congress, and they set up a dead man switch, an arrangement to release information if something happened to him. Borland tells this about himself, as a sign of how much danger he felt he was in.
dead-sea-scrolls-isaiah-matches-text-a-t: The copy of the biblical Book of Isaiah found among the Dead Sea Scrolls, ancient Jewish manuscripts discovered near the Dead Sea at Qumran, is said to match word for word a version of Isaiah written a thousand years later. The podcaster Joe Rogan repeats this on Michels's show as something a guest of his own, a man named Wes Huff, explained to him on Rogan's podcast. It is told as a sign of how faithfully ancient texts were copied down the centuries.
dean-koontz-novel-predicting-covid-and-t: A novel by the American thriller writer Dean Koontz, The Eyes of Darkness, is said to have predicted COVID: it centers on secret experiments with a perfect bioweapon called Wuhan 400, made at a lab near Wuhan, China, and is set in 2020. Michels tells it himself, saying the book was written in 1981, and offers it as a possible case of a writer glimpsing the future.
dean-radin-had-to-disparage-remote-viewi: The researcher Dean Radin is said to have been part of Stargate, a US government programme started, in this telling, by the CIA, that tried to use remote viewing, describing faraway places by mind alone, and to have had to speak badly of remote viewing in public while he worked on it. The physicist Maaneli Derakhshani passes this on from Radin, naming also the podcaster Joe Rogan and the physicist Hal Puthoff. If true, the government was quietly taking seriously something its own people were made to dismiss.
death-of-bilgames-ziusudra-the-last-to-b: An ancient Mesopotamian clay tablet called The Death of Bilgames (Bilgames is another name for Gilgamesh, the legendary king) is said to tell how the gods called the Anunnaki gave immortality to Ziusudra, the Noah figure of the flood story, and that he was the last man ever to receive it. The researcher of ancient history Matt LaCroix brings it up as an "obscure tablet", without naming any other source. He tells it because, if true, it would mean the old gods once granted eternal life to humans and then stopped.
death-of-bill-steinman: A UFO researcher named Bill Steinman is said to have died near Goodyear, Arizona, of a massive heart attack one January a few years back, while his wife Sheila Steinman was in the kitchen. Scott Ramsey, a researcher who has looked into a claimed crash of a craft carrying alien bodies, tells this as what Sheila Steinman told him.
death-of-john-norseen-2007: A researcher named John Norseen is said to have died on September 27, 2007, while travelling on business for Concurrent Technologies, the company he worked for. Michels gives the date himself, without naming a source, in an episode about American scientists who have died or gone missing. He raises it as one case in that pattern.
debrief-at-ellsworth-with-rick-doty-pres: After a UFO incident, Mario Woods, a former Air Force guard at nuclear missile sites, was questioned at Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota by Captain Jack Reed of the Air Force Office of Special Investigations, its criminal and counterintelligence branch, with a new agent named Richard Doty sitting next to him. Woods tells it himself in three episodes, mostly dating it to 1977, and says he only recognised Doty years later when he saw him on the TV show Ancient Aliens. Michels, retelling it, says five men were in the room plus an unnamed civilian in a gray tweed suit. It matters because Doty is a known figure in UFO stories, and his being there would tie the base's response to the intelligence services.
debris-blocked-shafts-between-khafre-and: Shafts in the ground between the pyramid of Khafre, one of the great pyramids at Giza in Egypt, and the Sphinx are blocked with rubble but lead down to large underground structures beneath Giza, according to Filippo Biondi, a scientist who scanned beneath the pyramids. Biondi says that based on his team's scans they are very confident the shafts are connected to these underground facilities. If true, it would mean there is a hidden world of chambers under the plateau.
deceptive-fairy-gentry-in-medieval-folkl: In the old folklore of Brittany and Ireland, the fairy folk were beings that country people knew lied to them all the time. A philosopher named Jason Jorjani tells Michels this, drawing on the work of Jacques Vallée, a researcher who compared fairy lore with UFO encounters, to suggest that the beings people meet today may be just as untrustworthy.
deciding-to-go-public-kasparov-calls-for: Kiran Ilum Xenov, then president of the Russian republic of Kalmykia and head of the World Chess Federation, says he was taken by aliens in 1997 and decided to speak about it in public.
