He says the 13th world chess champion, Garry Kasparov, at once asked what kind of chess federation president could have met aliens, and called for him to be removed and replaced. It is his own account, and it shows the price he says he paid for going public.
decision-to-stop-briefing-new-legacy-pro: The claim is that someone made a deliberate choice to stop telling new members of the "legacy program" how the program began. The legacy program is said to be a long-running secret US effort around UFOs. A guest described as a Pentagon whistleblower, Matthew Brown, says a man named Dylan Borland told Michels this fairly directly in an earlier conversation. If true, people inside the program would be working without knowing its own history.
declassified-air-force-documents-on-ufos: Throughout the Cold War, UFOs were reported at every kind of American nuclear site: where weapons were made, where missiles were stored and where they were deployed. Michels says this is shown by hundreds of declassified Air Force documents, naming places such as Hanford in Washington, Savannah in South Carolina, Fort Hood in Texas, Los Alamos, and the missile bases Malmstrom and F.E. Warren. He raises it to suggest that whatever was behind the sightings was paying close attention to American nuclear weapons.
declassified-cia-memos-on-exotic-gravity: CIA memos from the 1950s that have since been made public point to universities such as Indiana, Purdue, Princeton and MIT as outposts for exotic research into gravity, Michels says. He tells it in his own words from those memos. If true, it would mean serious secret work on controlling gravity was going on at top schools decades ago.
declassified-upshot-knothole-report-puts: A once-secret report on Operation Upshot-Knothole, a series of nuclear bomb tests in Nevada in 1953, confirms that a man named Arthur Stansel Jr. was on site for the testing. Michels cites the report himself in an episode about whether Henry Kissinger oversaw a program to recover crashed UFOs. He uses it to show that Stansel's presence at those tests is backed by an official record.
decoded-messages-of-aliens-with-a-dying-: In Albuquerque, New Mexico, in the early 1980s, a man named Paul Bennewitz believed he had decoded messages showing that aliens from another planet were here, trying to set up a base, and that "they needed Earth women or something." The researcher Greg Bishop, who has studied Bennewitz's case, recounts what Bennewitz came to believe, and he tells it as part of the story of how the belief took over Bennewitz's mind.
deconfliction-language-in-the-1971-treat: The United States and the Soviet Union are said to have written wording about UFOs into their arms talks of 1971, known as SALT, the Strategic Arms Limitation Talks. Pippa Malmgren, speaking on the episode with her relative Harold Malmgren, a former presidential advisor, points to the 1971 SALT treaty. Michels raises it on two other episodes and calls it public and open source. He says the two sides agreed to coordinate on the UFO question because the US worried the Soviets would mistake such objects for American attacks. In another telling he puts it as a recorded promise to coordinate with the Soviets on unknown objects in their airspace, and once he also links it to President John F. Kennedy. It is told because it would mean both superpowers took unknown objects seriously enough to put them in a treaty.
deconfliction-line-used-before-strike-on: After militias working for Russia attacked a group of Americans in Syria, the story goes, the US called the Russians on the deconfliction line, a direct channel the two militaries use to avoid accidental clashes, before striking back. Bob Maguire, a former CIA contractor, tells Michels this as something he was told. It shows how the two powers warned each other even while fighting through others.
deep-prasad-harassed-during-uap-science-: The researcher Deep Prasad says that during his scientific work on UAP, the official term for UFOs, some unpleasant people messed with him, as if he had hit a nerve among government insiders. When asked whether he was wrong to see it that way, Prasad answers about himself, "You are not wrong at all," which would mean his research touched something someone wanted left alone.
deep-underground-bases-at-s4-and-dulce: Deep underground military bases are said to lie across the United States, and some are rumored to house other beings: at S4, a site said to sit near Area 51, the secret Air Force test base in Nevada, and at Dulce, New Mexico. Michels says this himself in a 2025 episode. He draws on rumors linked to men named Phil Schneider, Bob Lazar, Dan Burisch and Richard Sauder, without saying what each of them claims.
deep-underground-bases-from-air-force-pr: Deep underground military bases are said to have a long history in the United States, starting in the 1950s and 1960s from Project RAND, an Air Force research effort. A UFO researcher who goes by the online name UAPGerb tells Michels this, without naming a source, on an episode about a supposed new secret base in Utah. He brings it up to show that hidden underground sites have been planned for decades.
deep-underground-bases-since-1948-with-n: The United States military has been building deep underground bases since the late 1940s, according to two researchers on the podcast. The researcher known as UAPGerb says these bases "absolutely exist." He says they have been a major focus of the Defense Department and the US Army Corps of Engineers since 1948. That year, he says, America brought over Nazi scientists, including Xavier Dorsch, head of a Nazi construction organisation, to work at an underground laboratory under the Air Materiel Command, an Air Force research command. The researcher Richard Dolan tells it differently. He credits the documentation gathered by a writer named Richard Sauder, which he thinks makes "a very very strong case" that the military was studying how to go deep as early as the 1940s and 50s. Dolan does not mention Dorsch or the Nazi scientists. Both say this would mean a hidden network of facilities underground.
defense-bases-deliberately-placed-at-nat: Michels wonders aloud whether some US military sites, such as Area 51, a secret Air Force test site in Nevada, and places like Skinwalker Ranch, a ranch known for reports of strange events, were built on purpose at natural "portals" where unexplained things appear. He puts this to his guest, a researcher known as UAPGerb, as a question he admits sounds "really trippy", drawing on the book UFOs and Nukes by the researcher Robert Hastings and on claims by a man named Jake Barber. If so, the location of these bases since the 1950s would have been chosen for reasons the public was never told.
defense-department-contacts-privately-en: Between 2021 and 2024, people inside the US Defense Department told Dave Rossi they could not back him officially but cheered him on in private, he says. Rossi, a guest who says aliens taught him advanced physics, describes these meetings himself, as a sign that his ideas were taken seriously behind closed doors.
dehomag-ibm-s-german-subsidiary-ahead-in: In the 1930s and 1940s, a German branch of the American computer company IBM, called Dehomag, was way ahead in technology, transistors included. Michels says this himself, without naming a source, while talking with the philosopher Jason Jorjani about Nazi Germany's secret technology projects. The point is that Germany may have had electronics more advanced than people usually assume.
deinococcus-radiodurans-survives-three-y: A hardy bacterium called Deinococcus radiodurans survived three years in outer space, according to studies done on the International Space Station, the orbiting lab. Dr. Gilbert tells this without naming the studies. If true, it suggests life could ride between worlds.
delgado-remote-controls-a-bull-with-a-br: In Spain in the 1960s, a scientist named Jose Delgado is said to have put an implant into a bull's head and then steered the animal by remote control, and there is film footage of the experiment. The researcher Greg Malatzi describes it, without citing a source beyond the footage, as "basically being able to remote control a bull." He raises it because, if true, it would show that a brain could be controlled from the outside as far back as the 1960s.
delonge-already-had-ten-advisers-by-nove: By November 2014, the musician Tom DeLonge is said to have already gathered ten advisers for his effort to get the UFO story out. The researcher Jason Simosa says he got this from the author Peter Levenda, who worked closely with DeLonge and said there were already ten advisers when he joined that month. It matters because it would show DeLonge's network of insiders was built well before it went public.
delonge-in-secure-facilities-2010: A guest named Tom DeLonge says that in the 2010s he went inside secret, high-security government buildings. He describes it from his own experience: the codes, the alarms and the armed guards to get in, and rooms that lock you inside and are sealed airtight. He tells it to show how close he got to the people who keep secrets on this subject.
delonge-iraq-war-linked-to-groups-connec: The musician turned UFO researcher Tom DeLonge once suggested that some of what the United States did in Iraq after 2003 may have been tied to groups of people there who were "connected with certain nonhuman entities and were helping them proliferate." The researcher Jason Simosa repeats this to Michels from DeLonge's early interviews, given before anyone knew who DeLonge's advisers were. If true, it would mean a war was partly about beings that are not human.
delonge-on-2016-radio-weapon-systems-bui: In 2016, the musician Tom DeLonge is said to have told a radio interviewer, when asked about archons, ruling spirits from ancient Gnostic belief, that weapon systems were being built "because we know they're coming back." A researcher named Jay Anderson recalls this to Michels, describing DeLonge as speaking very excitedly. If true, it would mean someone was preparing to fight beings expected to return.
delonge-on-coast-to-coast-with-george-kn: In 2011 the musician Tom DeLonge appeared on Coast to Coast AM, a late-night American radio show about the unexplained, with the journalist George Knapp. The researcher Jason Simosa mentions this without naming a source, to argue that DeLonge was already in the circle of UFO conversations years before he became publicly known for them.
delonge-s-advisers-went-quiet-when-asked: Around 2016 and 2017, the rock musician Tom DeLonge, when he went public about UFOs, said there was a big genetic side to the subject. He said his advisers answered his other questions, but went quiet the moment he asked about hybrids, meaning mixes of human and alien. The researcher Jason Simosa repeats this as something DeLonge said, and tells it because the silence would suggest hybrids are a topic the people in the know will not touch.
delonge-s-contact-at-lockheed-skunk-work: Around 2015 the rock musician Tom DeLonge is said to have got in with Skunk Works, the secret advanced aircraft division of the defence company Lockheed Martin, through someone he knew who worked there. A researcher named Jason Simosa says the UFO researcher Jacques Vallée confirms this original story. A commentator named Jay Anderson adds detail: the contact invited DeLonge to introduce the bosses on stage at a family and friends gathering, and DeLonge said he wanted ten minutes with the boss afterwards. Jesse Michels mentions it briefly too, saying DeLonge was getting in touch with Lockheed Martin and meeting executives, which, if true, would put a musician in direct talks with one of the most secretive aircraft makers in America.
delonge-s-meetings-at-the-pentagon-and-n: Around 2015 and 2016, a man named DeLonge, who was pushing to bring UFO stories to the public, was flown to the Pentagon (the US military headquarters), met someone there, and was then told, "Okay, now you're going to NASA," the US space agency, where he met more people. The researcher Jason Simosa tells this without naming a source, and he guesses that Pete Worden, whom he calls a one-star general at NASA, "may have been there." He tells it to show that officials took DeLonge seriously enough to send him from one agency to the next.
delonge-s-nro-sources-on-predicting-epis: The musician Tom DeLonge has said that high-level sources in the NRO, the US agency that runs spy satellites, told him government scientists had worked out ways to predict when and where unknown craft would appear. The online UFO researcher who goes by UAPGerb retells this as something DeLonge said, apparently on the podcast of the host Joe Rogan, around 2017. If true, it would mean the government can anticipate these visits rather than just react to them.
delongepodesta-disclosure-meeting-with-r: In January 2016, the story goes, a group of men met in Washington to talk about the government making public what it knows about UFOs. Among them were the musician Tom DeLonge, the political adviser John Podesta and a man named Robert Weiss. The UFO researcher Grant Cameron describes the meeting, which he connects to the Podesta emails, a set of Podesta's private emails that later became public, and he offers it as a sign that people close to power were working on disclosure.
delta-and-omicron-flight-configurations-: The craft he studied had two ways of flying: with all three of its amplifiers, the parts that drive it, used for travel it was in "the delta configuration," and with only one used it was in "the omicron configuration." Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft from 1987 to 1989 at S-4, a secret site in Nevada, describes this from what he says he learned firsthand. If true, it would be an inside account of how such a craft is flown.
demand-for-more-stories-set-in-the-water: Bryce Zabel, who made the 1996 UFO television series Dark Skies in Los Angeles, says a man he calls "the captain" told him that in the second season "you need to do more stuff in the water." Zabel tells it as something said to him directly, hinting that someone wanted the show to point viewers toward the oceans.
demodulating-soviet-french-venus-balloon: In the mid-1980s, a Soviet and French probe heading for Halley's Comet swung past Venus and dropped two balloon probes into its atmosphere, and Bob Maguire, a former contractor for the CIA, says he helped decode their radio signal for NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory. Maguire says he did this work himself at the Institute for Defense Analysis, a research group that works for the Pentagon, and tells it to show the kind of technical work he did.
demons-as-the-spirits-of-dead-nephilim-g: Demons, in this account, are the spirits of dead giants, the Nephilim of ancient Jewish writings, that left their bodies when the giants were killed and still roam the world. The filmmaker Tim Alberino tells it to Michels as "ancient Hebrew cosmology", and later in the same talk ties it to the Book of Enoch, an ancient Jewish text, in the translation by the scholar R. H. Charles. If true, it would explain where evil spirits come from.
dendera-light-bulb-relief: At the Dendera temples in Egypt there is an ancient stone carving that looks like a light bulb, says a guest named Jay Anderson, who speaks of having gone there. He calls it the classic light bulb carving. He brings it up as a sign that the ancient world may have known more than we think, perhaps even electric light.
denial-at-the-meeting-at-swedish-militar: In 2011, at the Swedish military headquarters in Stockholm, a treasure hunter named Dennis Asberg says an officer flatly denied that the military had visited the site on the seafloor where Asberg's team had found a strange object. Asberg says he answered, "I have filmed you. So, I know you have been there." He tells it as something he lived through, as a sign that the military was quietly interested in what he believes may be a UFO on the seafloor.
dennis-kucinich-laughed-off-a-debate-sta: Dennis Kucinich, a Democrat who ran for president, was laughed at on a debate stage once his name was tied to UFOs, and his campaign collapsed. A researcher named Jason Simosa tells this on Michels' show from memory, placing it around "2010 election I think," without naming a source. He tells it to show how costly it is for a politician to touch the subject.
dented-white-van-seen-at-the-facility-an: Sometime between 1990 and 1993 in Maryland, a white van with a dent in it turned up near a training facility and then seemed to be following him near his Holiday Inn, says Dan Sherman, a former sergeant who says the National Security Agency, the US spy agency that listens in on communications, hired him to talk with aliens. He tells it as something he saw himself. He says he checked the van he spotted at the hotel exit against the one from the facility, and it had "that same exact uh dent". If true, it would mean someone was keeping watch on him during that work.
department-of-energy-holds-both-ufo-secr: The US Department of Energy, the agency that runs the country's nuclear weapons labs, likely holds many secrets about UFOs and attempts to copy their technology, and it also ran the Human Genome Project, the 1990s effort to map all human genes. Jesse Michels puts these two together himself, pointing to a link between UFOs and nuclear sites, in a 2025 episode about medical experiments with a pharmacy businessman named Brigham Buhler. If true, it would mean one agency sits on both UFO secrets and humanity's genetic blueprint.
department-of-energy-manages-ufo-secrecy: Jesse Michels says that people who follow the subject think, and more or less know, that the US Department of Energy plays a large part in keeping UFOs secret and in recovering crashed craft. He says this himself and does not name a source. If it were true, the agency would be one of the main keepers of the secret.
department-of-state-cleared-report-gover: A man introduced on the show as a Pentagon whistleblower, Matthew Brown, says that what he can say in public is "largely based on the department of state cleared report and then inferences drawn from that report." By this he means a report the US State Department has approved for release. He gives it to explain where the limits of his public claims come from.
department-of-war-releases-ufo-files-on-: On May 8, 2026, Michels says, the Department of War, as the Pentagon is now called, released hundreds of UFO-related documents, videos and audio recordings after President Donald Trump ordered government files on alien life and UFOs made public. Michels says Trump first gave the order in a post on Truth Social, his social media site. He also says the files sit on a dedicated website with 500 million hits, more than the whole US population, and in another episode he talks about the release as something the president is still weighing. A congressman named Eric Burlison credits the White House aide Stephen Miller and says the first batch was footage from MQ-9 Predator military drones that caught something very strange. The skeptic Michael Shermer says there have been three releases so far and that the photos and videos are covered with big blacked-out rectangles. A retired Navy admiral named Tim Gallaudet calls them the PURSUE files and says they are still a work in progress and carry no metadata, the background data that tells when and where a recording was made. He adds that they hold a great deal of UAP activity, UAP being the government's term for UFOs. Told this way, it is the government opening its own UFO files on a president's orders.
deputy-chris-porritt-s-myers-era-testimo: A deputy sheriff named Chris Porritt went on record that strange things were going on at Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah ranch famous for reports of odd events, back in the 1980s when Kenneth and Edith Myers owned it, long before the Sherman family arrived. Brandon Fugal, the ranch's current owner, repeats Porritt's account. He tells it because, if true, it would mean the strange events at the ranch go back much further than the later owners.
derinkuyu-underground-city-found-by-a-ma: Derinkuyu, a vast underground city in Turkey, was found when a man fixing up his home knocked down a wall by accident and opened a doorway into it. The researcher Matt LaCroix tells this without naming a source. He tells it as an example of how much of the deep past may still lie hidden.
descartes-as-jesuit-agent-sent-to-infilt: The French philosopher René Descartes is said to have been an agent of the Jesuits, a Catholic religious order, sent to infiltrate the Rosicrucians, a secretive mystical brotherhood of his time. The philosopher Jason Jorjani makes this argument on two episodes, drawing on his own book Prometheus and Atlas. In the second telling he puts the mission differently: Descartes, he says, set up "this extremely reductionistic mechanistic scientific paradigm" to keep everything occult under the church's control. If true, it would mean modern science's narrow view of the world was shaped on purpose to hide hidden knowledge.
description-of-the-osiris-shaft: The Osiris Shaft on Egypt's Giza Plateau is described as a three-level, triple-chamber structure reaching 33 meters underground, set on the eastern causeway that runs from the central pyramid down to the valley temple and the Sphinx. A researcher named Jeffrey Drum lays this out for Michels without naming a source, as part of his claim that a vast energy system lies beneath the pyramids.
deser-and-arnowitt-graviton-essay-1954: Two physicists, Stanley Deser and Richard Arnoux, wrote a paper about gravitons, the theoretical particles thought to carry gravity. Their paper won the 1954 essay prize of the Gravity Research Foundation, a group that rewarded essays on gravity. Michels tells this in an episode about antigravity, drawing on a piece called The G Engines Are Coming by a writer named Michael Gladish, as a sign that serious scientists were working on controlling gravity in the 1950s.
desert-meeting-with-the-boys-upstairs-fo: Late one night around 1978 or 1979, in the desert near Joshua Tree and Twentynine Palms in California, a group went out hoping to meet what they called "the boys upstairs" and saw four lights slowly coming down. Jeffrey Mishlove, a guest with a doctorate who talks about psychics and the afterlife, was there and says his "mouth dropped open." He names a person called Valerie Ransone in the story, and says the lights turned out to be flares dropped by the Marines.
desert-trip-with-jake-barber: Michael Herrera, a guest who says he saw a 300-foot UFO in the Indonesian jungle, says a man named Jake Barber once took him on what he calls "a nice little trip out to the desert." Herrera tells it as something he went through himself, and he says that trip "proved to me that this guy was legit," though he does not say on the show what happened out there.
desmond-leslie-said-nazis-posed-as-venus: George Adamski, a man who said in the 1950s that he had met friendly visitors from Venus, was in fact contacted by Nazis posing as Venusians, according to the writer Desmond Leslie, who co-wrote the book Flying Saucers Have Landed with him. The philosopher Jason Jorjani relays this second-hand, saying Leslie's daughter told him that "her father said always said that it was Nazis who contacted Adamsky." If true, it would mean one of the best-known alien contact stories was a human deception.
detlev-bronk-and-alien-autopsies: A scientist named Detlev Bronk, who later ran the Rockefeller Foundation and was president of Johns Hopkins University, was in charge of what were called alien autopsies, Michels says. In one episode he says this with no source. In another he cites the Majestic 12 documents, papers said to describe a secret group of officials who handled crashed UFOs, and says the bodies came from a claimed crash at a place called Aztec and maybe from the 1947 Roswell case. If true, it would put a leading figure of American science at the center of studying alien bodies.
detlev-bronk-named-as-an-mj12-member-194: A scientist named Detlev Bronk, whom Michels calls president of the Rockefeller Foundation, a large American charity that funds research, was listed as one of the Majestic 12. That is the name of a secret committee that disputed papers, the MJ12 documents, say managed the UFO question from 1947 on. Michels brings this up himself, citing those documents, in an episode asking whether Henry Kissinger oversaw a program to recover crashed UFOs, because it would tie respected establishment figures to such a group.
detlev-bronk-rumored-to-be-on-majestic-1: Detlev Bronk, whom Michels calls the president of the Rockefeller Foundation, was rumored to be on Majestic 12 and to have done all the early alien autopsies. Majestic 12 is a rumored secret group of top officials said to have handled crashed UFOs in the late 1940s. Michels tells this himself in a 2026 episode, framing all of it as rumor.
dia-nro-witness-imaging-objects-in-space: The claim is that a man who worked for the Defense Intelligence Agency, the Pentagon's military spy service, and with the National Reconnaissance Office, which runs US spy satellites, photographed unexplained objects out in space. Steven Greer, who runs the Disclosure Project, a drive to collect testimony from insiders about UFOs, relays it from one of that project's unnamed witnesses. If true, US spy satellites would be imaging such objects in orbit.
diana-pasulka-calls-chris-bledsoe-a-mode: The religion scholar Diana Pasulka has compared Chris Bledsoe, a North Carolina man who reports long-running encounters with strange beings and lights, to Paul Bennewitz, the man at the center of a 2025 episode titled "'Aliens' Drove This Man Insane!". Michels repeats this himself, saying Pasulka "came out and she said I think Chris Bledsoe is a modern Paul Bennewitz." The comparison would mean Bledsoe's story could follow the same troubled path as the earlier man's.
diana-pasulka-on-the-rituals-rocket-team: Rocket teams in the United States are said to perform ritual-like ceremonies before a launch. The YouTuber Chris Ramsay brings this up with Michels, pointing listeners to the religion scholar Diana Pasulka, who he says talks about it a lot. It would suggest a near-religious side to space work.
diana-pasulka-s-research-in-the-files-of: A religious studies professor at the University of North Carolina Wilmington named Diana Pasulka has gone through many of the old files on St. Joseph of Cupertino, a Catholic saint from Italy, and she is said to agree with a point Michels makes about him. Michels tells this himself, calling Pasulka a friend and saying she has gone "very deep" on the saint, though he does not say what the files contain.
diana-pasulka-s-turn-while-writing-her-b: A professor at the University of North Carolina Wilmington named Diana Pasulka is said to have changed her mind while writing a book: she began as an outside scholar, but in the second half she "goes down the rabbit hole herself" and comes to think "there's something extremely real". Michels tells this from his own reading of the book, which the record names as Heaven Can Wait, as a sign that even careful academics can be won over.
diane-powell-meets-akil-after-his-mother: In 2022 a mother named Manisha in New Jersey saw Diane Powell, a researcher who studies children said to read minds, being interviewed by the writer Deepak Chopra, and got in touch with her. Powell says this is how she came to meet Manisha's son Akil, one of the children she studies. She tells it as the start of her own work with the boy.
diane-powell-s-inbox-full-of-parents-say: Around 2022 and 2023, the email inbox of a researcher named Diane Powell filled with messages from parents, all saying something like "I'm finding that my child can read my thoughts." The documentary maker Ky Dickens, who made a film called The Telepathy Tapes, says she saw this firsthand. She tells it as a sign that many families were seeing the same thing, which, if true, would point to children with telepathy, meaning the ability to read minds.
diane-powell-s-medical-licence-revoked: A doctor named Diane Powell lost her medical licence, the story goes, because she looked into telepathy, the idea that one mind can pick up another's thoughts without words. Michels raises it while talking with the filmmaker Ky Dickens, who made The Telepathy Tapes, a documentary about children said to read minds. He calls it an "atrocity" that Powell's licence "was revoked at one point right just for looking into this stuff." In a later episode he says it more sharply: "Her medical license got revoked for studying these telepathic children," and he credits The Telepathy Tapes. Dickens, passing on what Powell told her, ties it to something else. She says it happened when Powell wrote her book The ESP Enigma, about ESP, short for extrasensory perception, meaning knowledge that comes from somewhere other than the ordinary senses: "she had her medical license revoked because she was talking about ESP." So the two tellers disagree on the cause, a book or the work with the children. Either way, if it is true, a doctor was punished by her own profession for studying the subject.
diane-powell-takes-on-john-mack-s-legacy: In 2004 John Mack, a psychiatrist who studied people who said they had met aliens, was hit by a car and killed in London, and at his memorial the people gathered there told the psychiatrist Diane Powell that she had to take on his legacy. Michels tells this himself, passing on Powell's own story, and the episode ties it to an Oregon house where things lined up in meaningful ways for her, though he gives no detail of that. He tells it to explain how Powell came to carry on Mack's kind of research.
diary-of-merer-records-tura-limestone-be: An ancient Egyptian logbook known as the Diary of Merer, kept by an official named Merer, is said to record blocks of fine white limestone from the Tura quarries being shipped to Giza for the "horizon of Khufu," the name for King Khufu's pyramid. The researcher Luke Caverns cites it as a ledger showing these blocks being brought up to Giza. It matters because it would tie the building of the Great Pyramid to Khufu's own time and workers.
dick-and-vallee-precognize-each-other-s-: The science fiction writer Philip K. Dick and the UFO researcher Jacques Vallée each seemed to sense the other's work before seeing it, says the researcher Eric Wargo, who tells it as his own summary without naming a source. He says that in 1974 and 1975 Vallée was writing The Invisible College, his book on UFO contact, published in 1975, while Dick was writing the first draft of what became VALIS, his novel about a divine signal, published in 1981, an early version of which was the novel Radio Free Albemuth. If true, Wargo suggests, it would be a case of two writers picking up each other's ideas ahead of time.
dick-billings-on-doctoring-the-zapruder-: In 1963 the Zapruder film, the home movie that caught President Kennedy's assassination, was supposedly taken to Rochester, New York, and altered there. The lawyer Dan Sheehan tells Michels this. He says a man named Dick Billings, linked in Sheehan's account to the magazine publisher Henry Luce, "sat and told me about the whole thing." If true, the best-known film of the killing would not show what really happened.
dick-billings-visits-sheehan-over-the-se: A lawyer named Dan Sheehan says that while he was working on a sealed racketeering lawsuit, filed by his public-interest law group, the Christic Institute, over the Iran-Contra affair (a 1980s scandal over secret US arms deals and covert operations), a stranger came to his office at 1324 North Capitol Street in Washington. The man had heard how Sheehan answered a question and said "there aren't two men in the world that would have answered that question that way." He introduced himself as Dick Billings, who had been the chief staff writer for a congressional committee that investigated assassinations, and told Sheehan, "I think I can help you out on this case."
dick-cheney-at-the-top-of-the-secrecy-py: Former US vice president Dick Cheney is said to have sat at the top of the secret system that hides UFO knowledge. The claim comes through a journalist named Walter Kirn, who asked David Grusch, a former intelligence official turned UFO whistleblower, who "sits atop the pyramid of classified information," and says Grusch answered, "Dick Cheney." Michels repeats this several times, noting he introduced Kirn to Grusch, and calls Cheney "the gatekeeper for all legacy UFO programs," though once he softens it to "someone like" Cheney. An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb tells it the same way and adds that Cheney held the role "for quite a while," up to about 2009.
dick-harper-falsified-personnel-records-: After a reported 1948 UFO crash and recovery near Aztec, New Mexico, a man named Dick Harper, linked to MacDill, an Air Force base, is said to have doctored personnel files so no one could be shown to have been there. The researcher Scott Ramsey says Harper told him that about 200 people took part in the recovery, "so I kept 200 personnel records to make sure nobody was ever really an Aztec." If true, it would explain why paper records of the people involved are so hard to find.
dick-russell-s-1994-taped-interview-with: In 1994 a man named Dick Russell is said to have met and tape-recorded an interview with Puharich, a scientist the episode's title calls a CIA scientist who contacted an alien council. A researcher named Greg Malatzi relays the account, in which the speaker says the tape was made "literally the year before Puharich died/was found dead mysteriously." The tape would be one of the last records of the man in his own words.
dick-russell-s-day-long-interview-with-s: The journalist Dick Russell is said to have spent a whole day in the 1990s interviewing Sidney Gottlieb, the CIA chemist who led its mind-control experiments, at Gottlieb's house. A researcher named Greg Malatzi tells Michels this, calling it one of the only interviews with Gottlieb that he knows of. It matters because Gottlieb almost never spoke about his work.
dicom-ct-scans-show-capillaries-feeding-: CT scans of small three-fingered bodies found in Peru are said to show tiny blood vessels feeding eggs inside one of the reptile-like bodies, the type researchers call J-type. Michels tells it from the work of an independent researcher named Gonzalo Chavez, who helped set up the website tridactyls.org, pointing to the scan files made public there in DICOM, the standard format for medical images. Michels raises it because, if true, it would mean these bodies were once living, egg-bearing creatures and not something put together.
dictators-outlawed-freemasonry: Hitler, Mao and Stalin all outlawed Freemasonry, the old secret fraternal society. The researcher Randall Carlson says this in passing without naming a source. He brings it up as a sign that dictators saw the group as a threat to their power.
die-glocke-and-spinning-mercury: The story is that Nazi Germany built a secret bell-shaped machine, called Die Glocke (German for "the Bell"), that spun mercury and may have been an attempt at anti-gravity. Much of it traces to Igor Witkowski, a Polish journalist, and the defence writer Nick Cook says Witkowski told him the whole Bell story in person, adding the codename "Kronos" and a site at Waldenburg. Michels tells it in several episodes: he names the SS officer Hans Kammler as its head, says the SS medical chief Ernst Grawitz and the physicist Walther Gerlach reportedly worked on it, and says an SS officer named Jacob Spornberg documented "magnetic field separation, vortex compression"; once he frames it as a rumoured time-slowing project in a Nazi "wonder weapon" programme. Kurt McConnell, a former US Senate staffer, says he has read Witkowski's books and those of the writer Joseph Farrell on it, and Michels later says McConnell and Cook raised it and that he thinks the Bell is "no longer fictional". If true, the Nazis would have been working on a way to defeat gravity.
different-pieces-of-legacy-hardware-held: The filmmaker Jeremy Corbell says different pieces of recovered non-human hardware are kept in different places, and that it is public knowledge that a US congressman named Burlison has been going to various sites to see that hardware. If true, Congress would be physically chasing down craft the government has hidden away.
dimethyl-sulfide-found-on-exoplanets-as-: Scientists have found a chemical called dimethyl sulfide on planets circling other stars, some 120 to 240 light years from Earth, according to a researcher named Chris Gilbert. He mentions it in passing on Michels's show without naming a source, and he treats it as a possible sign that life exists beyond Earth.
dinner-companion-with-chameleon-like-eye: On his first trip to Egypt, in 2017, Geoffrey Drumm sat down to dinner with a man whose eyes were "big bulbous eyes like chameleon," and they seemed to move on their own, one looking off somewhere else. Drumm, a guest who says an alien told him the true purpose of the pyramids, tells this as his own experience. In one telling he puts it at a hotel and says the man quizzed him about the Serapeum, an ancient underground site in Egypt, and that when Drumm tried to message him later, the man had "disappeared in thin air."
dinner-in-san-jose-with-a-female-crash-r: A woman who worked on a secret program to recover crashed craft once had dinner with him at a German restaurant in San Jose, California, says Eric W. Davis, a scientist who has worked with the Pentagon. Davis says his source's wife drove him to the woman's home, they picked her up and the three went into town to eat, sometime between 1977 and 1989. He tells it as a meeting he was at himself, offered as a sign that such programs had real people working in them.
dinosaur-extinction-by-chicxulub-impact-: The dinosaurs were wiped out 66 million years ago when a comet or asteroid struck the Earth, an idea put forward by the scientists Luis and Walter Alvarez and, as the story goes, ridiculed at first. The writer Graham Hancock tells it on two episodes, saying "nobody disputes now" that the impact happened, with the proof being the Chicxulub crater, buried deep under the Yucatan in one telling and under the Gulf of Mexico in the other, and stressing that the idea "wasn't accepted until they found the crater." Michels tells it himself, crediting Luis Alvarez alone with the theory that "an asteroid hit the earth 66 million years ago" and killed off the dinosaurs. It is told as an example of a mocked idea that turned out to be accepted.
dinosaurs-and-roman-battles-on-benowitz-: In the early 1980s, a man named Benowitz in Albuquerque, New Mexico, is said to have had images of dinosaurs and old Roman battles appear on his CRT, an old-style tube computer screen, images he linked to messages he believed came from aliens. The writer Greg Bishop tells this as something a man named Gabe Valdez told him, saying Valdez went to the house and saw some of it himself.
dire-wolf-carcass-found-at-dry-gulch-cre: Brandon Fugal, the owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property known for reports of strange events, says his team came across the rotting carcass of a large wolf-like animal at Dry Gulch Creek on the ranch, filmed as it happened, sometime in the 2020s. He says a biologist named Ben Woodruff matched it to a dire wolf, a giant wolf long thought extinct, and the find appears in the TV series The Secret of Skinwalker Ranch. Fugal tells it as something he was part of, and if true it would add a creature out of the deep past to the ranch's list of oddities.
direct-witnesses-scott-interviewed-1948: A flying saucer is said to have crashed near Aztec, New Mexico, in 1948, and the researcher Scott Ramsey says he spoke with people who saw it firsthand. He names them as Doug Noland, Ken Farley, a local preacher, the preacher's son and one other man. If their accounts hold, they would be eyewitnesses to a crashed craft.
directional-scopaesthesia-paper-from-alm: The biologist Rupert Sheldrake says he studied almost a thousand accounts of people who sensed they were being looked at and turned toward whoever was staring. He wrote this up in his most recent paper on the subject, "Directional Scopaesthesia and its Implications for Theories of Vision" (scopaesthesia is the feeling of being stared at). As Sheldrake tells it, the cases point to a different idea of how vision works, one where looking might reach out beyond the eyes.
disappearance-mountain-near-ruwa-zimbabw: Near the town of Ruwa in Zimbabwe, the story goes, there is a mountain tied to disappearances, close to where a famous UFO sighting happened in the 1990s. The philosopher Jason Jorjani mentions it to Michels as one of several such places, without saying who told him. If true, it would link a known sighting site to a strange spot where people are said to vanish.
disappearance-of-los-alamos-employee-mel: In 2025 a 53-year-old woman named Melissa Casillas, an administrative assistant at Los Alamos National Laboratory, the US government research laboratory in New Mexico, went missing near Ranchos de Taos, New Mexico. Michels tells this in an episode about American scientists going missing. He draws on what was said by Sierra Casillas and Mark Casillas, two people who share her surname, and on a GoFundMe, an online fundraising page, set up in her case.
disappearance-of-malaysia-airlines-fligh: On March 8, 2014, Malaysia Airlines flight MH370 took off from Kuala Lumpur with 239 people on board and vanished. Jesse Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, in a 2026 episode about American scientists who have gone missing. He brings it up as part of a pattern of unexplained disappearances.
disappearance-of-monica-reza-near-mount-: A woman named Monica Reza vanished on June 22, 2025, near Mount Waterman in the Angeles National Forest in California, and Michels calls her "the woman who taught us how to tame fire." He tells the story himself, citing the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department, in an episode on why top American scientists are going missing. He counts her among those cases, which would point to a pattern if true.
disappearance-of-sharon-the-space-kid-ps: A girl named Sharon, one of the "space kids", psychic children studied in the 1970s by the researcher of psychic powers Andrija Puharich, is said to have simply disappeared. The researcher Greg Malatzi passes on what people who knew her back then told him: they are convinced she was "the real deal" and was pulled into a secret project like the rumored Montauk experiments, the kind of thing shown in the TV show Stranger Things. If true, it would mean a government program took in a child for her psychic gifts.
disc-sighting-on-a-blue-ridge-mountain-1: On a crystal clear October afternoon in 1973, on a mountain in the Blue Ridge near Boone, North Carolina, a disc-shaped craft appeared in the sky that looked just like one he had seen at age eight. That is what Steven Greer says, a man who argues that UFO secrets are held by a hidden global group. He tells it as his own sighting from when he had just turned 18, though he says he can't be sure it was the same craft.
disclosure-day-trailer-said-7-billion-bu: Jesse Michels points out that when the trailer for Disclosure Day, a Hollywood film about the world learning the truth about UFOs, came out, its line was "7 billion people have the right to know the truth," while the finished film says 8 billion. Michels noticed this himself and raises it while talking with the screenwriter Bryce Zabel. To him the small change hints at how carefully the film's message was being shaped.
discovery-and-translation-of-the-necrono: In the 1970s, at the Warlock Shop in Brooklyn Heights, New York, run by a man named Herman Slater, a manuscript came to light, and when the writer Peter Levenda looked at it he said, "This looks like it says necronomicon", the name of a legendary book of magic. Levenda tells this as someone who was there and worked on the text, and says it became the book later published as the Necronomicon.
discovery-of-dmt-s-effects-by-stephen-sz: DMT, a short-acting and very powerful psychedelic compound, first had its effects on the mind found in 1956 by a Hungarian physician named Stephen Szára, who injected himself with it in a hospital and then gave it to colleagues. The neuroscientist Andrew Gallimore tells this as a summary of the drug's history, without naming a source: "DMT was discovered in 1956 by this Hungarian physician." He tells it because it marks where the modern study of the drug's strange visions begins.
discovery-of-the-immaculate-constellatio: A former Pentagon official named Matthew Brown says that in 2018, on a classified computer system in the Pentagon policy office of the Under Secretary of Defense, he came across a briefing about a program called Immaculate Constellation. As it was described to him, it was a special access program, meaning a tightly restricted secret program, that ran the worldwide spying, surveillance and tracking of UAP, the government's term for UFOs, using both assigned and unassigned sensors. If he is right, the military has been watching these objects around the world in an organized, hidden way.
discovery-of-the-martian-ocean-shoreline: The physicist John Brandenburg says that in the 1980s he and colleagues found an ancient shoreline on Mars near Cydonia Mensa, a region of the planet, showing that Mars once had an ocean. He tells it as his own discovery and credits a conference paper he wrote in 1986 on the planet's ancient ocean. He raises it because a past ocean would make it more likely that Mars once held life.
disney-accelerator-brain-controlled-rock: Around 2020, in a lab run by Disney's accelerator, a programme that helps young companies, a team built a rock nicknamed Rocky that you could move with your mind, says Eric Haseltine, a former senior official at the National Security Agency, the US spy agency. He says he worked there himself and that "in the lab we invented a rock that you could move with your mind".
disney-laser-plasma-electronic-fireworks: While working at Walt Disney Imagineering, the company's design and engineering arm, Eric Haseltine says his team built electronic fireworks out of light. They pointed a powerful pulsed laser at one spot in the sky and poured in so much energy that the air turned into glowing charged gas, "ball lightning." Haseltine, billed on the show as a former director at the National Security Agency, the US spy agency for communications, describes this as work he did himself.
disney-s-ward-kimball-expects-government: In the 1950s, a man who worked for the film producer Walt Disney, named Ward Kimball, reportedly expected the government to hand over real UFO footage for a documentary he thought would be made. A researcher named Bryce Zabel tells this on the show while going through the history of Hollywood, the CIA and UFOs, and he does not name his source. If true, it would mean someone close to Disney believed the government was ready to show real UFO film to the public.
dispute-over-debunk-of-a-uap-video-boost: There is a dispute over a video from a test called Bluegill Triple Prime that shows an object tumbling out of a fireball. Some say the object is a rocket booster, others an instrument pod, and the dispute is over attempts to explain the video away. In a 2025 episode, Michels says that Jeffrey Krookshank, an analyst he is in touch with who has studied the footage "really deeply", told him that a man named Dean Johnson is "actually kind of really scared."
diver-calls-it-the-most-important-dive-o: Stefan Hogeborn, a diver who went down in 2012 to a strange shape found on the floor of the Baltic Sea, calls it "probably the most important dive I've ever done in my life." He says this from someone with about 6,000 dives behind him, speaking as one who made the dive himself, on an episode with the treasure hunter Dennis Asberg.
diver-finds-a-breathing-organic-object-o: In the 1960s, a diver is said to have found an object underwater off Hawaii that seemed organic and seemed to breathe. Michels tells it second-hand, mentioning the UFO researcher Richard Dolan: a UFO witness named David Noble White Crow, a Native American man, was stationed with the diver who apparently dove on the object. If true, it would point to something alive and unknown under the sea.
diver-sucked-into-a-giant-grouper-s-mout: The story goes that in the 1960s, a diver working at an oil platform in the Gulf of Mexico was approached from behind by a huge, curious grouper fish. It opened its mouth and sucked him in backwards. Joe McMoneagle, a guest known as a former psychic spy for the US government, tells it as something he heard from someone else, and he does not name the diver in the telling.
djoser-depicted-in-the-saqqara-step-pyra: Deep in the tunnels under the Step Pyramid at Saqqara in Egypt, there are carvings on the walls of the early pharaoh Djoser, shown in his famous striding pose during the Heb Sed, a royal festival of renewal. A researcher named Luke Caverns describes this without naming a source. He sets it against the later pyramids, which he says have no decoration inside at all, a contrast that would mean those later pyramids may not have been built the way we usually assume.
dmt-keeps-oxygen-deprived-neurons-alive-: The neuroscientist Andrew Gallimore says that brain cells starved of oxygen survive longer when DMT, a powerful psychedelic compound, is present. The story connects this to a protein on cells called the sigma-1 receptor. Gallimore gives it as a laboratory finding without naming the study, and it would suggest DMT has a protective job in the brain.
dmt-laser-diffraction-shows-the-same-sym: People on DMT, a powerful psychedelic drug, all saw the same symbols when a laser was shone a certain way, or so a man named Danny Jones told a guest named Randy Anderson. Anderson, who says he saw alien technology at a military base, passes it on to Michels: "everybody was seeing these same symbols." If true, it would hint that the drug opens onto something shared and real, not just private visions.
dna-and-rna-building-blocks-found-in-met: A few years back, scientists from Japan and from NASA, the US space agency, confirmed that the basic chemical building blocks of DNA and RNA, the molecules that carry life's genetic code, were found inside meteorites that fell in Canada, the US and Australia. Michels tells this himself as something extraordinary, without naming the study. He raises it because it would suggest the ingredients of life can come from space.
dni-team-encounters-orbs-at-western-us-m: Around 2025 or 2026, a team working for Tulsi Gabbard, the Director of National Intelligence (the head of all US spy agencies), flew by helicopter to a spot on a military base in the western United States and found themselves dealing with glowing orbs. Congressman Eric Burlison tells it, linking it to the government's recent releases on UAP, its term for UFOs. If true, it means top intelligence staff have met these things up close.
dni-tulsi-gabbard-s-platform-pledge-to-e: Tulsi Gabbard, the Director of National Intelligence, the official who oversees all US spy agencies, has made it part of her platform to make public what the government knows about UAP, the official term for UFOs. Jesse Michels says this himself in a 2025 episode with a pharmacy businessman named Brigham Buhler, quoting her as saying "I want to expose information on UAP UFOs." If true, it would mean the country's top intelligence official wants the secrets out.
dobrynin-asks-about-the-excitement-over-: Sometime in the 1960s in Washington, the Soviet diplomat Anatoly Dobrynin is said to have asked an American official why everyone was so excited about UFOs. The man he asked was Harold Malmgren, an adviser to Presidents Kennedy, Johnson, Nixon and Ford, and Malmgren tells it himself as something that happened to him. He says Dobrynin "did ask at one time um why is everyone so excited about these unidentified flying objects?" and adds that he had never talked about it before. If true, it would mean the Soviets were quietly probing what Washington knew about UFOs at the height of the Cold War. Jesse Michels repeats the story later in a different episode, retelling Malmgren's account rather than telling it firsthand. In his version the two men were friends, and Dobrynin raised UFOs himself and said he was very interested.
doc-brown-in-back-to-the-future-as-a-nod: The idea is that Doc Brown, the inventor in the film Back to the Future, is a quiet tribute to a real scientist named Thomas Townsend Brown, who did experiments with capacitors, devices that store electric charge, and whom people reportedly called "Doc Brown". Michels makes this case himself across several episodes: the film is set in 1985, which he says is the year Townsend Brown died, the character's full name is given as "E.M.T. Brown", and the film's "flux capacitor" echoes Brown's capacitor experiments. He credits the director Steven Spielberg with the nod, and in a 2026 episode he adds that he spoke to Brown's daughter directly, "who is sure that the character is based on him." If true, it would mean Hollywood was winking at a man Michels sees as a hidden pioneer of flying-craft research.
doc-edgerton-eg-g-and-filming-the-manhat: An MIT engineer named Harold "Doc" Edgerton is said to have found a new use for stroboscopic cameras, which use very fast flashes of light to freeze motion. According to the story, this camera work and other new wartime technology ended up being used in the Manhattan Project, the US wartime effort to build the atomic bomb. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, as background to a story about a secret hangar.
doctors-who-treated-a-soldier-questioned: In 1996, in the Brazilian town of Varginha, some doctors who had treated a sick soldier were questioned by Brazil's federal police, the country's national police force. This comes from a surgeon named Italo Venturelli, whose hospital is said to have operated on a strange being that year. He passes it on as something he was told, not something he saw. If true, it would mean the authorities took a close interest in that soldier's case and in the people who cared for him.
document-shows-pandolfi-supplying-gravit: A document has turned up that shows a government scientist named Ron Pandolfi finding the speakers who briefed the Jasons, a group of top scientists who advise the US government, on gravitational waves, which are ripples in space and time. The UFO researcher Grant Cameron brings it up without saying who found the document or where. He tells it to show Pandolfi working behind the scenes, arranging who briefs the government's own scientific advisers.
documentary-project-with-secret-dating-e: In 2024, a man named Matt LaCroix says he is leading "a very significant documentary" filmed at ancient sites in Turkey, Peru, Bolivia and Minorca, with new dating evidence he is keeping secret for now. He names people working with him, including Robert Schoch, Robert Edward Grant, Arturo Ponce de Leon and Paul Wallace. LaCroix tells it as his own project, and if the evidence holds it would push these sites back to around 12,000 BC, much older than usually thought.
documented-link-between-the-ufo-phenomen: The claim is that UFOs and the 1963 killing of President John F. Kennedy are connected, and that the link can be shown on paper. The author Peter Levenda says he has done just that: "I've shown through documentation the connection with the UFO phenomenon and the Kennedy assassination." He points to his book Sinister Forces. The people he names include J. Edgar Hoover, the head of the FBI, the former CIA officer E. Howard Hunt, and the men Guy Banister, Jack Martin and Fred Crisman. The UFO historian Richard Dolan reaches a similar view by a different path. He says "the UFO subject" must be "brought into" the Kennedy story, and he credits sources he names as Philip Lavell and Dan Sheehan rather than Levenda's work. Both raise it because, if true, it would tie the UFO secret to one of the darkest events in American history.
dod-officials-advise-against-disclosure: High-ranking people in the Department of Defense, the US military's headquarters, have told him not to go public with what he knows, says Dave Rossi, a man who says aliens taught him advanced physics. Rossi tells it as advice given to him directly. He says their reasoning has always been that "people will not see what you see".
dod-pays-bob-monroe-to-train-him-in-out-: In the 1980s, Joe McMoneagle says, the US Department of Defense paid Bob Monroe, known as the "Journeys out of the body guy" after his book on leaving one's body, to train McMoneagle in out-of-body experiences at the Monroe Institute in Virginia. McMoneagle, a guest who talks about seeing alien life on Mars with his mind, tells it as something that happened to him.
doe-and-battelle-institute-as-ufo-secret: The idea is that the Department of Energy, the US government agency in charge of energy and nuclear research, and the Battelle Institute, a private research organisation, may be where UFO secrets are kept. A researcher named Bob Maguire says he kept pointing at both and kept asking why people weren't looking at them, and he mentions a person named Linda Thompson along the way. If he is right, the search for hidden UFO knowledge has been looking in the wrong places.
doe-check-finds-no-nuclear-tests-on-shut: A check with the US Department of Energy, the agency in charge of nuclear weapons, reportedly found that no nuclear tests took place on March 16 or March 24, 1967, the dates when nuclear missiles were said to have shut down. A former Air Force officer named Robert Salas says this, crediting a man named James Clattz, though he does not name a written source. The point is that a nearby test blast cannot explain the shutdowns, which Salas links to a UFO.
doe-genesis-project: The Department of Energy, the US agency that runs the country's national laboratories, has a Genesis project. Michels thinks it is a way to collect the information from all the national labs and run it through artificial intelligence. He says this himself, as his own understanding, in a 2026 episode about the Secretary of Energy speaking on UFOs.
doe-hazing-ritual-fake-alien-and-roswell: A former CIA officer named Rolf Mowatt-Larssen says that in the mid 2000s, new political appointees at the Department of Energy were put through a hazing ritual in a vault at its Washington headquarters. They were given a mock briefing on a top-secret program saying the US really did have aliens, one injured and one not, and had obtained alien space technology through Roswell, the 1947 crash in New Mexico. Mowatt-Larssen says he saw this himself, and on one telling he dates it 2006 to 2009 and points to his book A State of Mind: Faith and the CIA.
doe-holds-the-nation-s-most-important-se: Some of America's most important secrets are kept at the Department of Energy, the US government department, not at the CIA, the US spy agency, says Rolf Mowatt-Larssen, a former CIA chief. He says he learned these secrets himself while working at the Department of Energy around 2005 to 2008, and that the department "does stuff" beyond what people expect, which would mean the deepest secrets sit somewhere few people look.
doe-intelligence-director-never-briefed-: Rolf Mowatt-Larssen, a former CIA officer who was director of intelligence at the Department of Energy, the US agency in charge of nuclear weapons, says that in that job, around 2005 to 2008, he was never briefed on unidentified objects showing up at nuclear sites. He says it openly, from his own time in the post. If such incursions happened, it would mean they were kept even from the man running the department's intelligence.
doe-nest-as-the-hazmat-crash-retrieval-t: A man named Jonathan Weygandt says that in Peru in 1997 he came upon a crashed craft, and that people from the Department of Energy were at the scene. A researcher who goes by UAPGerb thinks these were "highly likely" the Department of Energy's Nuclear Emergency Support Team, a unit trained to deal with nuclear and dangerous materials. If he is right, an existing hazard team would double as a crash-recovery team. He ties this to the 1954 Atomic Energy Act, a law on nuclear secrets, and in another conversation he links it to EG&G, a defence contractor, and to the Wilson-Davis memo, notes said to record a talk about hidden UFO programmes.
doe-says-it-cannot-locate-kettle-2-foota: The US Department of Energy answered a formal request to declassify a piece of film called the Kettle 2 footage by saying it could not find it. Michels tells this himself, pointing to a mandatory declassification review request, a legal route for asking that secret records be reviewed for release, dated October 21, 2023 and tied to a man named Jeff Cruickshank. He raises it as a sign that footage people believe exists keeps going missing.
doe-srt-and-nnsa-office-of-secure-transp: Two security units inside the US Department of Energy, the government department that runs the country's national laboratories and nuclear weapons work, may be the ones that pick up crashed UFOs and carry recovered material between those labs. That is the view of a researcher who goes by UAPGerb, who names an armed guard force known as the Special Response Team and the Office of Secure Transportation, the unit that moves nuclear material for the department's nuclear weapons agency. He offers it as his own guess, "highly likely involved" in his words, without naming a source, and if he is right it would mean the hidden handling of such material runs through ordinary federal security channels.
doe-using-the-alien-motif-as-cover: Michels suggests that the US Department of Energy, the government body that oversees nuclear and high-energy physics research, may be using the idea of aliens to throw people off. Speaking for himself in a 2026 episode, he says "there's something going on with high energy physics," and that the department may be hiding it behind "this sort of alien motif." If so, some UFO stories would be cover for secret physics work.
dog-whistle-draws-uaps-daily: A private group says it has a "dog whistle", a signal it switches on that draws UAPs, the official name for UFOs, to them day after day. Jake Barber, who works with the group, says it first-hand: "After we turn on the dog whistle, UAPs literally come to us day after day." James Valor, who also says he saw it, tells it in almost the same words in an interview about Skywatcher, a startup that tries to summon UFOs. Valor credits someone he calls Mr. K and places the work between 2021 and 2025. If true, it would mean these objects can be called in on demand and studied.
dogs-that-know-when-their-owners-are-com: Some animals have senses that are better than ours: dogs that seem to know when their owners are on the way home, and animals that seem to sense an earthquake before it hits. The scientist Rupert Sheldrake says this was the subject of his own book, Dogs That Know When Their Owners Are Coming Home. If he is right, animals would be picking up something that ordinary senses cannot explain.
doj-trial-under-military-order-number-on: A British computer hacker named Gary McKinnon, who says he broke into NASA and US military systems and found signs of a secret space program, says the US Department of Justice told him he would be tried under Military Order Number One. In his words that meant "Guantanamo status," the treatment given to terror suspects held at the US military prison in Cuba. He tells it to show how seriously, and how harshly, the US government reacted to what he did in the 2000s.
dolan-finds-timothy-good-s-above-top-sec: The UFO historian Richard Dolan says that in 1994, in an ordinary bookstore in Syracuse, New York, he came across Above Top Secret, a well-known book about government UFO secrecy by the British writer Timothy Good. Dolan tells it first-hand as the moment that drew him into the subject, which if true makes a chance bookstore find the start of his years of research.
dolan-s-early-appearances-and-stanton-fr: Around 2001, at early talks in places like Laughlin, Nevada, and St. Louis, Missouri, the well-known UFO researcher Stanton Friedman sat him down alone and tested him, says the UFO historian Richard Dolan, who tells it as something that happened to him. Dolan says he had just written a big, fat book and Friedman was sizing him up, asking him straight out, "So, what's your opinion on Bob Lazar?" Lazar is a man who says he worked on alien craft for the government.
dolan-s-uso-database-shows-em-interferen: The researcher Richard Dolan says that about one in ten of the cases in his database of USOs, unidentified objects seen in or coming out of the world's oceans, involved electromagnetic interference, meaning electrical equipment was disrupted. He describes this as a pattern he noticed himself while collecting the cases, and he does not name a source. If it holds, it would point to a shared physical effect behind the sightings.
dolmens-tied-to-a-cult-of-giants: Dolmens, the ancient stone structures made of big upright slabs topped by a flat capstone and found in places like Sardinia and Minorca, were linked to a cult that worshipped giants, according to the researcher Tim Alberino. He gives this as his own belief, without naming a source, and says the link is "not just because they're large stones, but they're associated with the cult of giants." If he is right, these monuments would be traces of an old giant cult spread across Europe.
don-carter-s-kirtland-interdisciplinary-: In 1962, a man named Don Carter, head of advanced research at Kirtland Air Force Base in New Mexico, was bringing together groups of experts from many fields, and the statesman Henry Kissinger was among them. Jesse Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, in a 2025 episode with a UFO writer named Greg Bishop. He raises it as a hint that serious people were quietly studying the subject at that base.
don-paul-thanks-greer-for-those-stuck-in: Steven Greer, a guest who says UFO secrets are kept by a global group of insiders, says a man named Don Paul once picked him up in Los Angeles and dropped him at the rental where he was staying. Greer says Paul thanked him on behalf of people trapped inside "legacy programs," the long-running secret projects Greer says hold this material. Greer tells it first-hand.
don-phillips-humans-have-the-fastest-com: People carry inside them a computer faster than any machine humans will ever build, says Don Phillips, a man who speaks from his time at Lockheed's Skunk Works, the company's secret aircraft design shop. Phillips offers it as his own view of what the human mind can do, on an episode about a UFO book the Pentagon tried to censor.
donald-barr-dalton-school-and-the-novel-: Jesse Michels points to what he calls the weirdest thread linking the financier Jeffrey Epstein to UFOs: a man named Donald Barr, once an officer of the OSS (the American spy agency of the Second World War), was headmaster of the Dalton School, a private school in New York, around the time Epstein got a job teaching there in the 1970s. Michels adds that Barr wrote a science fiction novel called Space Relations, which he describes as a story of aliens keeping humans as sex slaves, and he draws in Barr's son, the later US Attorney General William Barr, and Epstein himself. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, as a sign of strange early ties between Epstein, intelligence circles and alien themes.
donald-hornig-listed-as-present-at-kecks: A government summary of the 1965 Kecksburg incident, in which an object is said to have come down in the woods near Kecksburg, Pennsylvania, lists Donald Hornig, a senior science adviser to the US government, as present at the scene. The physicist Kevin Knuth says he found this himself: "Donald Hornig was listed as being present," he says, linking the find to the Hornig family, including Lily Hornig. If true, it would put a top government scientist at a crash site that is officially played down.
donald-menzel-caught-destroying-plates-p: In the 1950s, a Harvard astronomer named Donald Menzel is said to have been caught destroying old photographic plates, the glass plates on which observatories recorded the night sky. The witness, as these tellers describe her, was Dorrit Hoffleit, a respected Harvard astronomer who worked under him and wrote about it in her memoirs. The astronomer Beatriz Villarroel, who studies old sky images, tells it most fully. She says Menzel helped the US Air Force explain away the 1952 Washington sightings and then, two or three months later, became director of the Harvard Observatory and destroyed a third of its photographic plates. Jesse Michels repeats the story several times, calling Hoffleit "very reputable" and pointing to her biography as the place where she records it. Why it matters to them: if those plates held images of strange objects in the sky, a record that could have been studied was lost.
donald-trump-controls-resorts-internatio: For about a year in the 1970s, Donald Trump was reportedly the person basically in charge of a company called Resorts International, which did business in the United States and the Bahamas. A researcher named Jason Simosa says this on the show without naming a source. He brings it up as part of a larger story linking a secret society to the UFO cover-up.
donald-trump-jr-interviews-ross-coulthar: Donald Trump Jr., the son of President Donald Trump, interviewed the reporter Ross Coulthart in 2025. Jesse Michels mentions it in two episodes. In one, he says it happened on the eve of Coulthart breaking the story of a man named Jake Barber, who says he worked recovering crashed craft. Michels brings it up as a sign that the subject was reaching people close to the president.
donna-hare-ufos-airbrushed-out-of-images: In the 1970s, in Building 8 of NASA's Johnson Space Center in Houston, images showing UFOs were being airbrushed clean, according to a NASA worker named Donna Hare. She says she pointed at something in a photo, asked a man "Is this a UFO?", and he smiled and said "I can't tell you that." Michels repeats her account several times, adding that she came forward through the Disclosure Project, an effort by a man named Steven Greer to gather official witnesses, and that her story is why a British computer hacker named Gary McKinnon went after that building. A guest called UAPGerb mentions her too, linking her to a 2001 disclosure briefing document. If true, it would mean NASA hid evidence of UFOs from the public.
donut-craft-his-father-showed-him: His father once called him over at their old house to look at a donut-shaped craft in the sky, says Dave Rossi, a man who says aliens taught him advanced physics. Rossi tells it as something he saw himself, one of three times, and calls it "your typical" donut-shaped craft.
donut-shaped-ufos-above-rossi-s-old-hous: Dave Rossi, a guest who says aliens taught him advanced physics, says donut-shaped UFOs would show up above his old house, "a few that would be above it." He tells it as something he saw himself and brings his father into the story.
doolittle-sent-to-investigate-swedish-gh: Dwight D. Eisenhower, the American general who later became president, sent General James Doolittle to look into the Swedish ghost rockets. These were mysterious rocket-like objects reported over Sweden and Finland in 1946. Michels says "we do know for a fact" that this happened, telling it himself in his 2023 episode with David Grusch.
door-to-door-survey-of-1-600-swedes: About one Swede in ten has seen something unexplained in the sky, says Clas Svahn, a Swedish UFO researcher. He says his group knocked on doors and talked to 1,600 people across Sweden, and 10 percent of them said they had seen something, which would mean such sightings are far more common than most people think.
doty-admits-befriending-benowitz-and-mis: In the early 1980s in Albuquerque, an Air Force intelligence agent named Rick Doty befriended a local businessman named Paul Bennewitz, who believed he was picking up alien signals, and fed him misleading stories; Doty later admitted he had been tasked to do it. Michels tells this himself, in a conversation with the writer Greg Bishop, quoting Doty's admission that he befriended Bennewitz that way on orders. If true, it means a government agent deliberately pushed a man deeper into alien beliefs.
doty-and-lear-spread-quackery-around-the: In the 1980s, while the Majestic 12 papers were going around (documents said to describe a secret US group handling UFO matters), the subject was promoted alongside what Michels calls "all sorts of quackery." He says an agent of the Air Force Office of Special Investigations, the Air Force's own investigative and counterintelligence service, named Richard Doty claimed there were six alien beings, and a man named John Lear said there was a "soul catcher" on the Moon. Michels tells this himself, as an example of how the topic was muddied in that decade.
doty-s-alien-crystal-that-showed-the-cru: A former Air Force counterintelligence agent named Richard Doty says the most amazing thing he ever saw in the military was an alien crystal that showed scenes of the crucifixion of Jesus. The UFO researcher Grant Cameron passes the story on to Michels as something Doty tells. If true, it would mean such an object holds a record of events in human religious history.
doty-s-claim-he-was-an-area-51-guard: A man named Rick Doty once said he had been a guard at Area 51, the secret US Air Force test site in the Nevada desert. A guest named Greg Bishop repeats this from Doty to Michels, and adds right away that he has "no idea" whether it is true.
doty-s-disinformation-to-moulton-howe-an: Documents about the origins of humanity that Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft at a secret Nevada site, says he was shown look very much like the ones an Air Force intelligence agent named Richard Doty showed the journalist Linda Moulton Howe at Kirtland Air Force Base in New Mexico. Jesse Michels makes this comparison himself in two episodes: in 2025 he says Lazar admits he was forced to drink a liquid before being given the material, and ties it to what Doty gave Howe and a businessman named Paul Bennewitz in 1979, while in 2024 he speaks only of Howe. If true, it would suggest Lazar was fed the same planted story Doty is known for passing on.
doty-s-rival-version-1964-at-white-sands: A landing that some say was caught on film at a New Mexico air base happened in May 1971, by one account. A former Air Force man named Richard Doty says it was really 1964, at White Sands, a military test range in New Mexico, and that "they got lost." The researcher Grant Cameron tells this second-hand: he says a filmmaker named Bob Emenegger told him it was "absolutely" May 1971, and then Doty came along saying "no no no." The date matters because it decides which event, and which piece of film, people are actually talking about.
doty-shows-linda-moulton-howe-documents-: In 1982, the story goes, a man named Rick Doty got in touch with a UFO researcher named Linda Moulton Howe and showed her documents, among them papers about something called Project Garnet, said to be a secret government UFO project. Michels lays out the meeting himself in an episode with the writer Greg Bishop. He frames it as one researcher contacting another and does not say where he learned of it. Bishop adds a second-hand piece. He says he talked to Tom Adams, a researcher of cattle mutilations (unexplained killings of livestock), who told him Howe came to visit a couple of days later. According to Adams, she was "very excited" and "over the moon." If the papers were real, they would point to a hidden official programme. Michels gives the meeting, and Bishop gives Howe's mood afterwards as Adams described it to him.
doubting-four-funds-including-renaissanc: In the early 2000s, the researcher Eric Weinstein says, he did not believe the stories told about four investment operations: those of Bernie Madoff and Jeffrey Epstein, and the funds Renaissance Technologies and D.E. Shaw. He tells it as his own past doubt, "I didn't believe the following four funds," to show that he has long been suspicious of how some fortunes were explained to the public.
doug-alt-the-portal-is-real: A man named Doug Alt once told the UFO researcher Grant Cameron that a portal Cameron had asked him about was real. Cameron says Alt came back to him years later, asked "Remember that question you asked me a couple years ago?", and then said "It's real." Cameron passes this on secondhand, in a conversation that also involves a government scientist named Ron Pandolfi, and he does not say much more about what the portal is.
doug-and-bill-enter-the-craft-1948: In 1948, in Hart Canyon near Aztec, New Mexico, two men named Doug Noland and Bill Ferguson are said to have found a crashed saucer and then gone inside it. Michels retells this from Doug Noland's own account: "According to Doug, he and Bill enter the craft." It is one piece of a larger story of a crash at Aztec that, if true, would mean a craft and its crew were found there.
doug-noland-and-bill-ferguson-find-the-s: In 1948, two men named Doug Noland and Bill Ferguson climbed to the rim of a mesa in Hart Canyon, near Aztec, New Mexico, and found a flying saucer 100 feet across. Michels narrates the scene himself in a 2026 episode about a supposed crash there, which he presents as having left 16 alien bodies.
doug-sees-beings-through-the-punctured-p: In 1948, in Hart Canyon near Aztec, New Mexico, a man named Doug Noland is said to have put his eye to a punctured porthole on a crashed saucer and seen two small figures slumped over a control panel. Michels tells this himself in a 2026 episode, adding that Noland "was specific about that hole for the rest of his life"; Noland was with another man, Bill Ferguson, when they found the craft. It is part of a larger story of a crash near Aztec that, if true, would mean alien bodies were recovered there.
doug-wolf-first-oga-director-with-nro-ca: Doug Wolf, the first director of an office known by the letters OGA, had spent 16 years before that at the National Reconnaissance Office, the US agency that runs spy satellites. An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb says this on Michels's show without giving a source. He raises it while laying out how he thinks the Pentagon's secret UFO program works, and the career link would tie that office to the world of spy satellites.
dousing-remote-viewing-target-sites-with: The researcher Chris Ramsay says that in the US government's remote viewing program, which ran from the 1970s to 1995 and tested whether people could describe faraway places using only the mind, target sites were sometimes doused with liquid nitrogen and the viewers' results got more accurate. He tells it without naming a source. If true, it would mean something physical at the site affected what the viewers picked up.
dr-brett-cohen-agrees-the-great-pyramid-: The Great Pyramid of Giza in Egypt was once a working chemical plant that produced sulfuric acid, according to Geoffrey Drumm, a researcher who argues the pyramids were machines.
