He says another researcher, Brett Cohen, agrees that the pyramid made sulfuric acid, though Cohen pictures a completely different way it worked and different stages of the chemical reaction. Drumm brings this up alongside the work of an engineer named Christopher Dunn, as support for the idea that the pyramid was built to do a job and was not just a tomb.
dr-bug-we-can-t-take-your-soul: A being he calls Dr Bug told him, "we can't take your soul", says John Blitch, a scientist who worked at DARPA, the Pentagon's research agency for advanced technology, and who says he was taken by an alien. Blitch tells it as something said to him directly during his own encounter.
dr-carvalho-s-35-colares-patients-interv: In 1977, in the Brazilian village of Colares, a local doctor named Dr. Carvalho treated 35 patients who all had the same sunburns and puncture wounds, and two women died of a stroke, after reports of lights in the sky attacking people. Michels tells this from a book called Forbidden Science, saying the UFO researcher Jacques Vallée went to Brazil and spoke to the doctor himself. If true, it would mean the strange lights physically harmed people.
dr-fernando-jane-saw-the-creature-s-foot: In 1996, in the Brazilian town of Varginha, where several people say a strange creature was seen and caught, a doctor named Fernando Jane says he passed through the regional hospital and saw the creature's foot, and only the foot, because so many military people were around it. A witness named Jose Marcus Mora tells Michels this as something Jane told him. If true, it would place the creature inside a town hospital under military guard.
dr-g-as-a-consortium-of-anti-submarine-s: The mysterious scientist known only as "Dr. G" may not have been one man at all, but a stand-in for a group of eight or nine scientists who had worked on anti-submarine research. Dr. G was the source behind a book by the writer Frank Scully called Behind the Flying Saucers, about a saucer said to have come down near Aztec, New Mexico, around 1948. A researcher who goes by the online name UAPGerb tells this, giving all the credit to two researchers, Scott Ramsey and Suzanne Ramsey, for digging up the short list of names behind the pseudonym.
dr-italo-venturelli-meets-live-being-in-: In 1996, at the regional hospital in Varginha, Brazil, Italo Venturelli says he stood face to face in intensive care with a being "totally different from a human being," with a white face and red eyes, showing no pain, calm and, as he says, "highly intelligent, at least more than I was." Venturelli, the hospital's chief neurosurgeon, tells it first-hand in several interviews, saying a colleague, Marcos Vinícius, had stitched the being and that it "looked at me with a very beautiful look"; Michels repeats it on another episode, saying the meeting lasted four minutes, and if true it would mean a living non-human creature was treated in a Brazilian hospital.
dr-iya-whitley-s-work-on-helping-infants: A space psychologist named Iya Whitley is trying to train babies to keep their synesthesia, the blending of the senses where someone might see colors in sounds. Jesse Michels mentions her himself, without naming a source, in two 2025 episodes, and in the one with Dan Sherman, a former Army sergeant who says the National Security Agency hired him to talk to aliens, he says the aim is communicating with aliens. If true, it would mean someone is preparing children for a kind of contact that ordinary senses can't handle.
dr-iya-whitley-says-astronauts-see-thing: A doctor named Iya Whitley says that astronauts all see strange things in space. Michels passes this on from what she told him, without giving any details of what they see. If true, it would mean that seeing odd things in space is common among people who have been there.
dr-jannini-s-lab-report-death-from-pulmo: In 1996 in Varginha, Brazil, where a strange creature is said to have been captured and treated, a doctor named Jannini reportedly wrote a laboratory report saying the creature died of a lung infection that led to septicemia, an infection spreading through the whole body. A surgeon named Ahmed Foratu, who says his hospital operated on the being, describes the report to Michels. If true, it would be a medical record of an alien's death.
dr-marcos-vinicius-neves-operates-on-the: In 1996, a strange being said to have been captured in Varginha, Brazil, was taken to the city's regional hospital, and a doctor named Marcos Vinicius Neves is said to have operated on it. According to the account, the being had swelling from a head injury, and the doctor relieved the pressure. The documentary filmmaker James Fox tells it on Michels's show. He has interviewed witnesses to the Varginha case and passes on what he understands, citing another doctor there, Italo Venturelli. If true, Brazilian doctors would have treated a living non-human being.
dr-vinod-falls-into-a-trance-and-first-c: In 1952 a man known as Dr. Vinod arrived at the Round Table Foundation, a research group in Maine, and on his very first night there fell into a trance without warning, the start of messages said to come from "the Nine," a council of beings beyond Earth. The researcher Greg Malatzi tells it as "the story goes," pointing to the group's tape recordings, session transcripts and the journals of Andrija Puharich, a man who ran the sessions. In a second mention Malatzi only says the early channeling through Vinod all took place in 1952, without singling out the first night.
draft-notice-after-leaving-the-church-19: Peter Levenda, a writer on hidden history, says that in the late 1960s in New York he left the church he had been part of, and that as soon as he did, he got a notice from Selective Service, the US military draft office, that he was being drafted. He tells it as part of his own life story.
draft-uk-us-extradition-treaty-written-i: In 2003, a draft of the treaty that sets the rules for Britain sending suspects to the United States for trial was, according to Gary McKinnon, written in American English. McKinnon, a British hacker who says he found signs of a secret space program in NASA computers and then fought being sent to the US, says his lawyers noticed this, along with documents from the General Accounting Office, the US Congress's auditing agency. He tells it to suggest that the American side wrote a treaty that was meant to be British.
dragon-feels-his-late-father-s-presence-: A man named Bryant Arnold, known as Dragon, has felt his late father's presence on Skinwalker Ranch, a property in Utah known for reports of strange happenings. The ranch's owner, Brandon Fugal, tells Michels this as something Dragon told him, saying Dragon has "felt his father's presence" there, which would add the dead to the ranch's list of odd experiences.
dragon-wagon-used-to-haul-the-craft-away: In 1948, after a craft is said to have come down in Hart Canyon near Aztec, New Mexico, a "dragon wagon", a heavy hauling vehicle, backed its way up a road newly cut to the site so the craft could be hauled away. Michels tells this drawing on the writer Frank Scully and his book Behind the Flying Saucers. If true, it would mean a crashed craft was quietly carted off by an organised recovery team.
dream-at-dionysiou-1800s-paris-brothel-t: While staying at Dionysiou, a monastery on Mount Athos in Greece, Ralph Larson, introduced on the show as a former chief in the CIA (the US foreign intelligence agency), says he dreamed he was walking down old Paris streets and into a brothel, "I just want to see what's going on," and there he met a figure who turned out to be the Virgin Mary. He tells it as his own experience and ties it to Harry Haller, the main character of the novel Steppenwolf.
dream-of-infiltrating-the-order-of-the-b: A former CIA officer named Rolf Mowatt-Larssen is said to have had a dream about the Order of the Broken Cross, which Michels describes as an apocalyptic cult in Jerusalem, and about getting inside it. Michels brings it up as Mowatt-Larssen's own experience, in an episode where the former officer talks about time and seeing ahead, so the dream is offered as a possible glimpse of things to come.
dream-of-jesse-matching-the-nas-tweet-re: He once dreamed that Jesse Michels came to his East Coast home to get provolone cheese, and the dream matched a reply to a post by the rapper Nas on social media, says Dylan Borland, who says a top government official told him that aliens run everything. Borland tells it as his own experience, a sign to him that dreams can line up with real events.
dream-of-sadat-s-assassination-as-it-hap: A former CIA officer named Rolf Mowatt-Larssen says that while he was at Fort Bliss, Texas, in 1981, he dreamed of the assassination of the Egyptian president Anwar Sadat in Cairo at the moment it happened, and felt he was actually there. He says it was his first such dream, which he gives as September 6, 1981, and that he writes about it in his book A State of Mind: Faith in the CIA. He tells it as one reason he calls himself a kind of time traveler, someone who can see events from afar.
dream-visit-from-a-great-uncle-at-the-mo: In 1972 in Berkeley, California, Jeffrey Mishlove says his great-uncle came to him in a dream, what he calls "a visitation," and he learned later that it happened at the very moment the man died. Mishlove, a guest with a doctorate who talks about psychics and the afterlife, tells it as his own experience, a hint that the mind can reach past death.
drew-s-privately-funded-vacuum-chambers: A man named Andrew Arjima, called Drew, has paid for his own vacuum chambers, sealed tanks with the air pumped out that are used to test equipment as if in space, and keeps one at his house, says Charles Buhler, a NASA figure who claims work on propulsion without fuel. Buhler says it as someone who knows Drew and his setup firsthand: "He's got one at his house."
driving-past-bennewitz-s-thunder-corpora: In the 1980s, the road into Sandia Lab, a US national weapons laboratory in Albuquerque, New Mexico, ran right past the office of Paul Bennewitz, a local businessman whose company was called Thunder Corporation. A scientist named John Brandenburg, who worked at Sandia, says he drove past it every morning. He tells it as a bit of local color tying him to a man who figures in UFO history.
driving-past-epstein-s-victoria-s-secret: He used to drive past the New Mexico ranch, Zorro Ranch, later tied to the financier Jeffrey Epstein and known locally as the Victoria's Secret ranch, all the time, says Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft for the government. Lazar says he lived very close to it in the years he lived in New Mexico and calls it "really strange".
drone-flights-over-nevada-nuclear-testin: Several mystery drones flew over the US nuclear testing range in Nevada, just north of Las Vegas. Michels mentions it himself in a 2024 episode with Robert Hastings, a researcher of UFO reports at nuclear sites. He raises it as a sign that something may be watching American nuclear sites.
drone-only-tfr-set-up-over-picatinny-ars: About a month before Thanksgiving 2024, Jake Barber says, a temporary flight restriction, a no-fly order from aviation authorities, was put over Picatinny Arsenal, a US Army base in New Jersey, and it was aimed only at drones. Barber, a guest who says he picked up a UFO with his helicopter, tells it as something he knows directly and points to the timing as a clue that someone knew in advance.
drone-survey-shows-rust-like-lines-and-c: A 2025 survey with an underwater drone showed strange lines, cracks and what looked like rust, like metal, on a large shape lying on the floor of the Baltic Sea, says Dennis Asberg, the treasure hunter who found it. Asberg says he saw the footage himself, and he offers it as a sign that the shape may be a made object rather than rock.
drum-s-visit-to-the-giza-plateau-to-look: A researcher named Jeffrey Drum says he went out to the Giza Plateau in Egypt to look at the area around the Osiris Shaft, a deep shaft cut into the rock near the pyramids. He tells it as his own trip, and in one version says he went right after a conference in Malta and that extra shafts were found near the causeway, the old raised road leading to the pyramids. He ties the visit to water samples taken from the shaft and to his idea that the Great Pyramid made sulfuric acid, which, if true, would make it part of a large ancient energy system.
drumm-puts-his-head-in-the-magnetic-hole: At the Oami Gaishi stone circle in Japan, there is a huge andesite stone with a hole exactly the shape of a head and a strong magnetic field, and he put his head inside it, says Geoffrey Drumm, a researcher who says an alien showed him the true purpose of the pyramids. Drumm tells it as something he did himself in the 2020s, a hint to him that ancient stones were built for a purpose involving magnetism.
drumm-s-evaluation-of-the-biondi-team-s-: The researcher Geoffrey Drumm says that when he first studied a team's 2020 paper on hidden structures under the Giza plateau in Egypt, he gave it about even odds of being right. The team is led by a scientist named Filippo Biondi, and they later wrote a second paper on the Khafre pyramid. Drumm tells Michels this as his own reading of the papers, as a way of showing how his view of their claims has changed since 2020.
dsp-fast-walkers: "Fast walkers" is a name for unknown objects that streak quickly past Earth in orbit and are picked up by the Defense Support Program, or DSP, a set of US military satellites built to spot missile launches. A guest named Max raises them in passing, saying something was "probably the fast walkers that the DSP" saw. The point would be that military satellites have recorded unexplained objects in space.
dsp-satellite-infrared-anomaly-during-th: In 1976, when jets of the Shah's air force chased an unknown object over Tehran, Iran, a US military satellite may have picked up something unusual too. A researcher who is a guest on the show says two aerospace researchers, Lee Graham and Ron Regehr, claimed they had studied printouts from the Defense Support Program, American satellites that watch for heat from space, for the exact day and time of the chase. If so, the encounter would have been recorded by a machine as well as by the pilots.
dtra-held-aec-records-saying-ufos-are-ex: Old records from the Atomic Energy Commission, the US agency that ran nuclear weapons work after the Second World War, are said to have concluded that UFOs are "extraterrestrial vehicles", and to have been kept by the Defense Threat Reduction Agency, a Pentagon agency that deals with weapons of mass destruction. A UFO researcher who goes by UAPGerb tells this on Michels' show in 2026, repeating what a man named Dylan Borland said on another podcast, Weaponized. In a second pass UAPGerb drops the agency as the keeper and suggests the records may link instead to crash records from the Armed Forces Special Weapons Project, the military's early nuclear weapons unit, and to the Sandia nuclear laboratory.
dtra-official-collecting-documents-on-ex: An unnamed speaker says that the official in charge of gathering everything the Defense Threat Reduction Agency, a Pentagon agency that deals with weapons threats, held on extraterrestrials, "little green men" as the official put it, sat down at the speaker's computer. The speaker says the official pulled every such document off that machine and off the systems in their secure room for classified work. The speaker tells it as something they saw.
duell-s-diary-records-meeting-the-presid: A diary from the 1950s is said to show a meeting with the president on the very day that President Dwight D. Eisenhower was supposedly briefed on UFOs, according to the Majestic 12 papers. Those papers claim that a secret group of officials, called Majestic 12, handled the matter. Michels raises this himself in 2024, saying a diary he calls Duell's has come out and records "meeting with the president" on that day. In a 2025 episode, crediting the researcher Richard Dolan, he puts it more broadly: the papers knew of meetings and diary entries, which he there calls Dulles's, that "no other source did." If that holds, the papers' authors had inside knowledge.
dugway-chief-scientist-reveals-a-huge-su: A huge underground facility lies beneath Dugway Proving Ground, a US Army testing site in Utah, reached through an entrance hidden in a shed west of a mountain called Granite Peak. That is what the base's chief scientist told a person identified only by the initials MS, according to a researcher who goes by the online name UAPGerb and who relays the account second-hand. If true, it would point to a large secret site hidden under an already restricted range.
dugway-grey-beard-we-had-the-triangles-o: Between about 2019 and 2022, an old hand at Dugway Proving Ground, an Army testing range in Utah, would casually say things like "Oh, we had the triangles out again last night." A researcher known online as UAPGerb tells this as something he heard there himself. He takes it as a hint that triangle-shaped craft were flown or tested at the site as a matter of routine.
duke-researchers-brain-implants-let-para: Researchers at Duke University, including a scientist the teller calls Dano, put electrodes into the brains of paralyzed people, who could then control robot arms and even walk. Eric Haseltine, a former senior official at the NSA, the US electronic spying agency, tells Michels about this work, which he connects to a talk at the Aspen Institute, a policy forum. He brings it up as proof that the brain can be wired directly to machines.
dulce-base-shootout-in-lazar-s-briefing-: Secret briefing papers described a shootout in an underground base at Dulce, New Mexico, where 64 special forces soldiers were killed by gray aliens because they carried weapons they were not allowed to have. That is how the researcher Grant Cameron sums up what Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked at a secret site called S-4 near Area 51, the Air Force's hidden Nevada test base, says he read in the papers he was shown there. Cameron gives it as a summary of Lazar's account, without naming any other source.
dulles-brothers-draft-the-versailles-war: The brothers Allen Dulles and John Foster Dulles, then young lawyers at Sullivan and Cromwell, a New York law firm, helped write the war payments Germany was made to pay in the Treaty of Versailles, the peace treaty that ended the First World War in 1919. The lawyer Dan Sheehan tells this without naming a source. He brings it up to show how early the two brothers sat close to the centre of world power.
dulles-greenlights-the-s-force-against-j: In 1963, Allen Dulles, the former head of the CIA, reportedly gave the go-ahead to a group called the S force to act against President John F. Kennedy. A researcher named Dan Sheehan says this, naming Dulles and the CIA official Richard Bissell, but he does not give a source. If true, it would tie Kennedy's killing in Dallas to people inside the CIA, which Sheehan connects to what Kennedy knew about UFOs.
dulles-keeps-holding-court-in-his-george: After Allen Dulles, the head of the CIA, the US spy agency, was pushed out in the early 1960s, he did not leave Washington, and he went on running his own circle from his townhouse in the Georgetown neighbourhood. A researcher named Dan Sheehan tells it without naming a source, and he links Dulles to other spy officials of the day, Richard Bissell and James Jesus Angleton. If true, it would mean Dulles kept his influence over the intelligence world while out of office, in the years leading up to President Kennedy's killing.
dulles-reactivates-howard-hughes-s-s-for: In the 1960s, the story goes, Allen Dulles, the head of the CIA whom President John F. Kennedy threatened to fire, used his position at Brown Brothers Harriman, a private bank, to bring back the "S Force", a private operation set up by the billionaire Howard Hughes, and turn it against Kennedy. Michels tells this twice as the account of a man named Dan Sheehan. In the second telling Michels adds that the S Force began with Richard Nixon, who was Vice President under Eisenhower and head of the 5412 committee, the group that oversaw covert operations, working with Hughes, and he ties it to Cuba between 1959 and 1963. If true, it would mean a private intelligence force was aimed at a sitting president.
dutch-museum-moon-rock-turned-out-to-be-: After the first Moon landing in 1969, during a goodwill tour by the Apollo astronauts, the American ambassador to the Netherlands gave a former Dutch prime minister a supposed moon rock, which ended up in a Dutch museum and later turned out to be petrified wood. Michels brings it up himself, in an episode about the comedian Joe Rogan, a little unsure of the details, saying he thinks it came through the astronaut Neil Armstrong. He uses it to ask what else about official space history might not be what it seems.
dylan-borland-nhi-involved-in-the-cover-: A whistleblower named Dylan Borland is said to believe that the nonhuman intelligence behind UFOs is itself helping to keep the secret hidden. Michels says he asked Borland directly whether these beings were involved in the cover-up, and that Borland answered, "yes, I for sure know that." If true, it would mean that the hiding of the truth is not only the work of human governments.
dylan-borland-s-triangle-over-langley: Dylan Borland, a witness who was on the military base at Langley, says that in 2012 a light flew toward him across the base from near the NASA hangar and a triangle formed around it: an equilateral craft one to two stories thick, with 90 degree edges and a flowing gold glow like lava or plasma, and as it took off above him he felt the air go charged. He tells it himself, says he gave it to Congress and to AARO, the Pentagon's current office for unexplained aerial reports, in a classified written record, and thinks the craft came round to do a scan of the base. An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb, the filmmaker Jeremy Corbell and Michels all retell it from Borland's account, Michels dating it to 2012.
dylan-borland-the-energy-system-is-the-m: The most closely guarded secret is not the craft but the energy system that powers it, according to a man named Dylan Borland. An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb (UAP is the government's term for UFOs) quotes Borland to Michels: "the most sensitive thing is not the craft it's the energy system." If true, the real secret would be a power source, not the vehicles.
dyson-s-cross-country-drive-with-feynman: Sometime between 1947 and 1949, the physicist Richard Feynman was driving from Cleveland to Albuquerque and offered to take a young Freeman Dyson, also a physicist, along for the ride "just to see the country." Dyson tells this in his own words, as a trip he took himself, in an episode about a contractor for the CIA, the US spy agency.
e-howard-hunt-links-jfk-s-death-to-ufo-i: E. Howard Hunt, a former officer of the CIA, America's foreign spy agency, is said to have claimed that President John F. Kennedy was killed in 1963 at least partly because of his questions about UFOs. Michels has told this several times, passing on what others say Hunt said: in some tellings the claim comes through Hunt's son, Saint John Hunt, and in others through a man named Douglas Caddy, who says he kept asking Hunt what the killing was really about until Hunt, near the end of his life, answered "the alien presence." The versions differ on whether UFOs were part of the reason or the whole of it, but if true, a president's death would be tied to the UFO secret.
e-howard-hunt-s-everglades-group-burned-: The researcher Dan Sheehan says that in 1963 a second armed group was training in the Florida Everglades with the CIA officer E. Howard Hunt as its go-between, and that US marshals burned the group out. He tells it without naming a source, as part of a larger story he links to Robert F. Kennedy and to the killing of President John F. Kennedy.
e-howard-hunt-s-occult-novels-attacking-: E. Howard Hunt, a CIA officer who also wrote novels, published occult novels that, read closely, attack the Kennedys by showing them as thinly disguised Satan worshippers, one of them set on a "Witches Island." The author Peter Levenda, who writes about CIA history, says this from his own reading of the books, though he does not name them. He sees it as a spy using fiction to go after the Kennedy family.
e-t-whittaker-s-1904-1905-papers-showing: The claim is that an English mathematician named E.T. Whittaker wrote two key papers in 1904 and 1905 showing that "scalar waves" can exist. These are said to be a type of wave unlike the ordinary radio waves first made by Heinrich Hertz, which is why they are called "non-Hertzian". Salvatore Pais, a Navy scientist with patents for unusual craft, sums up the papers himself and also mentions a writer named Tom Bearden. If true, physics would allow forms of energy beyond the ones in ordinary use.
eagle-lake-sphere-answers-sos-and-chases: In 1976, on Eagle Lake in Maine's Allagash Waterway, four men camping near Smith Brook saw a light they first took for the moon, a white circle the size of an aspirin, until it started to move; it is said to have answered their SOS signal and chased their canoe. Charlie Foltz, one of the four, describes the light, and Jim Weiner, another, says the sphere was right behind them and he remembers nothing more until the canoe reached the campsite shore. The other two were Jack Weiner and Chuck Rak, and the missing time is why the story is told as an alien abduction.
ear-sensation-logged-on-blog-before-the-: A former sergeant named Dan Sherman says he felt strange sensations in his ear and wrote them down on his blog before major earthquakes, once around September 2003 in connection with Japan and again before the great Indian Ocean earthquake near Indonesia. He tells it first-hand, pointing to his blog and to a 2006 update of his book Above Black as the record. Sherman, who says the NSA, a US intelligence agency, hired him to communicate with aliens, offers it as a sign that the sensations gave real warnings.
earl-of-elgin-confirms-james-bruce-was-a: The writer Graham Hancock says that in 1990, at the Broomhall estate in Scotland, the Earl of Elgin told him that the eighteenth-century Scottish traveller James Bruce was a Freemason, a member of the old secret brotherhood with its own rites: "dear boy, of course he was." Hancock says the Earl even named the lodge, Canongate Kilwinning Lodge No. 2 in Edinburgh, which Bruce belonged to. Hancock tells it as something he took part in while researching his book The Sign and the Seal, and it mattered to him because it tied Bruce's travels to the Freemasons.
earlier-undisclosed-events-before-wwii-1: There were events going back much further than the ones he can discuss, events he says he is not allowed to talk about, according to a guest named David Grusch. He tells Michels only that "there's some other stuff, too, that I can't talk about that was way before that," which would push the story back to around or before the Second World War.
earlier-weatherman-burned-by-tall-white-: In 1965 a military weatherman at Range Four, a test range in the Indian Springs Valley of Nevada, was burned when his shoulder came close to one of the beings Charles Hall calls the Tall Whites, very tall pale beings in suits. Hall, who says he later worked as a weatherman there himself and spent three years among these beings, says he saw the man's x-rays and photographs at the hospital at Nellis, an Air Force base in Nevada, which, if true, would mean the beings could physically harm people.
earliest-skinwalker-ufo-images-kept-with: Even the very first pictures of UFOs taken above Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property known for reports of strange events, since he took it over around 2016 still have their full metadata, the hidden data that records when and how a photo was taken, says Brandon Fugal, the ranch's owner. Fugal tells it first-hand, as proof that the images can be checked.
early-1960s-uap-event-filmed-at-a-milita: In the early 1960s, an event involving unidentified objects in the sky took place at a US military base, and there is evidence that recorded it happening. A physicist named Eric W. Davis tells this as something passed on to him, and ties it to George H. W. Bush, the former US president. If true, it would mean such a recording has existed inside the government for more than sixty years.
early-christian-libraries-discovered-in-: In the 1940s, libraries of early Christian writings were found, and they show that the first Christians were influenced by the Greek philosopher Plato, especially his Republic and its allegory of the cave, a story of prisoners who take shadows on a wall for reality. The religious studies scholar Diana Pasulka says this herself, without naming the finds, to show how early Christian ideas about other realms were shaped.
early-fbi-cia-army-documents-on-ufos-nea: Starting in 1945, when nuclear weapons arrived, thousands of government documents describe UFOs turning up in America's most sensitive airspace, especially around nuclear sites. Michels says this himself on two episodes, without naming a single file. He says the papers come from the FBI, the CIA and the Army's counterintelligence branch, and that one effort was even called Project Twinkle; if he is right, the government was quietly tracking strange craft near its bombs from the very start.
early-shuttle-crews-borrowed-yellow-u-2-: For the first space shuttle flights in 1981, the astronauts Young and Krippen had to go to Beale Air Force Base and borrow the yellow pressure suits worn by pilots of the U-2 and SR-71, two high-flying spy planes. The NASA doctor Greg Rogers tells this, passing on what he was told. It shows how much NASA borrowed from secret military flying in the early shuttle days.
earning-the-trust-of-the-space-kids: Greg Malatzi, a researcher making a film, says it took him about two years to earn the trust of a group he calls the "space kids" before they would talk to him on camera. He tells it from his own work on the interviews.
earth-s-rarity-and-galactic-pyramids: There are pyramids all over the galaxy, and they are power sources and places of healing, not tombs, says Steve Colbern, a scientist who studies objects said to be alien implants in human bodies. Colbern says "they told me" this, without saying on the show who told him, and he ties it to the idea that Earth is a rare place.
eben-alexander-near-death-experience-200: In 2008, a man named Eben Alexander says he had a near-death experience in which he felt an overarching, loving energy. He told the story in his book Proof of Heaven. David Grusch, a former intelligence officer who went public about secret government UFO programmes, brings it up with Michels and praises Alexander's "very interesting scientific outlook" on what happened to him.
ebner-effect-high-voltage-on-crops-1990: In Europe in the 1990s, something called the Ebner effect was said to show that putting crops and seeds in a high-voltage electric field changed how they grew. The researcher Dave Rossi brings it up in passing, without naming a source, saying "there was something called the Ebner effect, I believe in the 1990s." He offers it as an example of electric fields having odd effects on living things.
echo-flight-incident-1967: In 1967, at Echo Flight, a group of ten nuclear missiles at Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana, all ten missiles are said to have suddenly shut down while guards reported something strange overhead. A former Air Force officer named Robert Salas relays the account of the officer in charge, Walt Feele, who at first "couldn't believe what they were saying," before "all 10 of his missiles went down." Michels places it eight days before Salas's own similar incident and links it to later cases at Malmstrom. If true, it would mean something could switch off American nuclear weapons.
echo-flight-incident-and-the-boeing-sac-: In 1967, nuclear missiles at a group of launch sites called Echo Flight, at Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana, failed, and Michels says a report shows that something to do with UFOs was behind it. He describes a report by the aircraft and missile maker Boeing and the Strategic Air Command, the Air Force command in charge of nuclear bombers and missiles, in which they "tried to recreate the effect." Robert Salas, a former Air Force officer who took part in the missile events of that period, says that "Boeing also did a bench test on what's called a logic coupler," a part in the missiles' electronics, and he credits a man named James Klotz for this. In another episode, Michels says the command's own papers show it was "extremely puzzled" and had "no idea what was going on." To them, the point is that the people who built and ran the missiles could not find an ordinary cause.
ed-gets-cold-feet-before-ssci-testimony-: Around 2023, a witness known only as Ed was going to testify before the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence, the Senate panel that oversees US spy agencies, but he got cold feet just before. A researcher who goes by UAPGerb tells this, saying the UFO researcher Steven Greer did the right thing by trying to bring Ed in. He does not name a source for it.
ed-may-leads-stargate-research-in-its-fi: A researcher named Ed May is said to have run the research side of Stargate, a US government programme that studied whether people could use psychic means to spy on distant places, during its last ten years. The writer Eric Wargo tells this, without naming a source: May took over from the physicist Hal Puthoff and led the work until the programme was made public and, as Wargo puts it, "supposedly ended in 1995." The word "supposedly" hints that Wargo thinks the work may have gone on afterwards.
ed-may-s-decision-augmentation-theory: The writer Eric Wargo describes a theory from the psychic researcher Ed May called decision augmentation. It holds that good results in psychic experiments come from the researchers' own ability to sense the future, which nudges them to start an experiment at just the right moment. Wargo sums it up himself, and if true it would mean precognition, or knowing the future, quietly shapes the experiments meant to test it.
ed-may-worked-with-prince-hans-adam: A scientist named Ed May, linked to Stargate, a US government project that studied psychic abilities, is said to have worked with Hans-Adam II, the reigning prince of Liechtenstein. Michels mentions it in passing, saying May "talks about working with the Royal Prince of Liechtenstein." It would tie that psychic research to a European royal.
eddington-s-eclipse-confirms-general-rel: In 1919 the British astronomer Arthur Eddington watched a solar eclipse and measured how starlight bent as it passed the sun, which backed up Albert Einstein's new theory of gravity, called general relativity. A guest named Greg Rogers tells this, noting that "of all people it would take an enemy of Germany" to do the work that proved the German-born physicist right. He tells it to show how science can cross the lines drawn by war.
edgar-cayce-foundation-funded-zahi-hawas: The Edgar Cayce Foundation, a group built around the work of the psychic Edgar Cayce, reportedly paid for Zahi Hawass, the Egyptian archaeologist who later ran the Giza site. A researcher named Jay Anderson says this on the show without naming a source. If true, it would mean a group with mystical interests in Egypt helped shape one of its most powerful archaeologists.
edgar-fouche-s-1998-tr-3b-testimony-proj: A man named Edgar Fouche gave testimony in 1998 that centred on the TR-3B, a rumoured secret triangle-shaped aircraft, and in it he said many secret projects were moved out to Dugway Proving Ground, an Army test range in Utah. The online researcher known as UAPGerb points to this when he talks with Michels about how hidden programmes are run. He uses it as one more account placing such work at Dugway.
edgar-fouche-s-defense-advanced-research: S4, a secret site in Nevada, ran something called the Defense Advanced Research Center, according to a man named Edgar Fouché. An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb tells Michels about the claim and says a center by that name shows up as a proposal in a 1970s document from ARPA, the Pentagon's advanced research agency. He also names a man called Dan Burisch, and the point is that the paper would show the center was at least planned.
edgar-fouche-the-tr3b-timeline-from-prot: A secret triangular aircraft called the TR3B is said to have flown as test prototypes from the 1970s onward, with the first working models flying around in the 1990s, at places like the Navy's Patuxent River air station and Edwards Air Force Base in California. The source is a man named Edgar Fouche, who laid this out in a presentation at the 1998 International UFO Congress, and the researcher UAPGerb relays his timeline on Michels' show in 2026. If true, it would mean the US has long flown craft that people might mistake for UFOs.
edgar-mitchell-founds-the-institute-of-n: Edgar Mitchell, an astronaut who went to the Moon, went on to found the Institute of Noetic Sciences, a research institute devoted to the study of the mind. The scientist Rupert Sheldrake tells this on Michels's show and says he is himself a fellow of the institute.
edgar-mitchell-heard-about-roswell-1947: Edgar Mitchell, an Apollo astronaut who walked on the Moon, believed that an alien spacecraft crashed near Roswell, New Mexico, in 1947 and that the government recovered it. Michels says that as an astronaut Mitchell "heard all sorts of things about Roswell from people at all levels." A guest named Maaneli Derakhshani says Mitchell was "very clear" about this belief. An online researcher who goes by RedPandaKoala adds that the rocket scientist Wernher von Braun later told Mitchell that he could "corroborate what you were hearing back home about Roswell." If true, it would mean people at the top of the space programme knew of the crash.
edgar-mitchell-on-the-moon-landing-image: Edgar Mitchell, an astronaut who walked on the Moon in 1971, is said to have answered a question about the Moon landing pictures with "James, it wouldn't surprise me," adding that the astronauts used Hasselblad cameras, a make of film camera, with no viewfinders while wearing gardening gloves. The documentary filmmaker James Fox tells this, repeating what Mitchell said to him. Fox brings it up because it suggests that even an astronaut thought some of the famous pictures might not have been taken the way the public believes.
edgar-mitchell-s-apollo-14-esp-experimen: The Apollo 14 astronaut Edgar Mitchell is said to have run an experiment in extrasensory perception, sending thoughts by mind alone, during his 1971 trip to the Moon, and later to have started a society devoted to the study of consciousness. The Swedish UFO researcher Clas Svahn brings it up in passing, saying only that "it's an experiment with the Swedish guy."
edgar-mitchell-s-conversion-experience-o: On the way home from the Moon on Apollo 14, the 1971 lunar mission, the astronaut Edgar Mitchell had a sudden experience that changed his whole view of the world. Jesse Michels describes this himself in three episodes from 2022 to 2026, including one with the UFO filmmaker James Fox, who was Mitchell's friend. In one he calls it telepathic and parapsychological, something Mitchell was public about, and in another he says only that it felt like a conversion. If true, it would mean one of the few people to walk on the Moon came back convinced the mind reaches beyond the body.
edgar-mitchell-s-esp-experiment-in-space: On the Apollo 14 moon mission in 1971, the astronaut Edgar Mitchell is said to have run a test of ESP, meaning extrasensory perception, the claimed ability to send or receive information by mind alone, while he was in orbit. An online researcher who goes by RedPandaKoala tells it without naming a source, calling it "the first ever like psychic experiment in space," and links it to the card-guessing tests of the parapsychology researcher J.B. Rhine. It is told as a sign that serious people took psychic abilities seriously at the height of the space programme.
edgar-mitchell-s-esp-experiment-on-apoll: On the way to the Moon on Apollo 14 in 1971, the astronaut Edgar Mitchell is said to have run a private experiment in extrasensory perception, or ESP, the idea of sensing or sending information by mind alone, trying to send mental images of a set of cards back to people on Earth. Michels tells it, pointing to a 1971 New York Times interview with Mitchell as his source.
edgar-mitchell-s-last-filmed-interview-a: In his last filmed interview, given at his home around 2015 to 2016, the Apollo astronaut Edgar Mitchell said that a secret group was keeping UFO information from the public. The filmmaker Jeremy Corbell, who did the interview, says that is exactly what Mitchell told him, and that Mitchell also named the people he had talked with. Coming from a man who walked on the moon, it would mean the secret was confirmed by someone on the inside.
edgar-mitchell-s-psi-experiments-on-the-: Jesse Michels says that many astronauts practiced remote viewing, the attempt to see distant places or things with the mind alone. He says the Apollo 14 astronaut Edgar Mitchell is well known for doing such mind experiments during his 1971 trip to the moon. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, as a sign that the space program took the mind's powers seriously.
edgar-mitchell-s-ufo-squadron-over-germa: The astronaut Edgar Mitchell is said to have seen a whole squadron of UFOs on a training mission over Germany, over several days, flying in many different formations, and to have filmed them. According to the story, when he landed back in Washington a military plane landed right after him, the footage was taken away, and he never heard about it again. Michels tells this as something Mitchell said, and offers it as an example of evidence being quietly taken.
edgar-mitchell-said-no-astronaut-ever-sa: The astronaut Edgar Mitchell held that no astronaut ever saw a UFO in space. The Swedish UFO researcher Clas Svahn tells Michels this from his own talks with Mitchell, saying it was "the thing he was very adamant" about.
edgar-mitchell-speaks-out-on-ufos-1971: Edgar Mitchell, an astronaut who flew on Apollo 14, NASA's 1971 mission to the Moon, later went on to speak publicly about UFOs. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, and mentions Mitchell only briefly as an example of a respected figure who did just that. If true, it would mean someone who had walked on the Moon took the subject seriously in public.
edison-s-device-to-communicate-with-the-: The inventor Thomas Edison, near the end of his life in the 1920s, is said to have tried to build a machine for talking with the dead. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, in a 2025 episode about NASA, strange rituals and secret science. He uses it to show that even famous scientists reached toward the unseen.
editor-asks-avi-loeb-to-cut-alien-paragr: In 2025 a science journal editor told the astronomer Avi Loeb that his paper on 3I/ATLAS, an object passing through our solar system from outside it, was great but that he had to take out the final paragraph, the one raising the idea of aliens. Michael Shermer, a well-known skeptic, tells this, saying Loeb himself described it on a Zoom call. It is told as an example of how scientific journals handle talk of alien life.
editor-s-computer-hit-by-the-same-electr: In 2022, while Michels's video editor on the East Coast was cutting their film about Skinwalker Ranch, a ranch in Utah known for reports of strange events, his computer screen froze and went full of static, which it had never done before. Michels tells this himself, twice, as something his editor went through. He says it matched the electrical trouble that visitors to the ranch report, as if the effect followed the footage home.
edward-condon-atomic-insider-turned-ufo-: Michels tells, on his own account, how the physicist Edward Condon went from insider on the atomic bomb to the man who shut down UFO research. He says Condon studied in Göttingen, Germany, under the physicist Max Born, and worked with J. Robert Oppenheimer and General Leslie Groves on the wartime bomb project. Then, Michels says, he dropped out of sight until "he pops back up in 1966 and his clearance is mysteriously restored", and he was put on a panel that "deals a death blow to UFO research claiming it's all a waste of time and money". The point is that a man trusted with nuclear secrets ended up closing the door on UFOs. A 1943 document from the bomb laboratory, the Los Alamos Primer, confirms Condon was there at the start: its notes on the physicist Robert Serber's lectures "were written up by E. U. Condon", and it describes the goal as "a practical military weapon in the form of a bomb".
edward-teller-and-project-sundial-gigato: The physicist Edward Teller, the man behind the design of the hydrogen bomb, also reportedly worked on something called Project Sundial, a plan for a bomb with the force of a billion tons of explosive. A Navy scientist named Salvatore Pais brings this up, noting that the project is not secret, though he names no source. He tells it to show how far weapons research reached in the 1950s and 60s.
edward-teller-on-the-ufo-legacy-program: The claim is that the physicist Edward Teller, best known for his work on nuclear weapons, may have been one of the scientists in a secret long-running US UFO effort called the legacy program, if such a program exists. A guest named Max says he vaguely remembers other people suggesting this. He does not say who they were.
edwin-may-s-scientific-oversight-committ: Edwin May, the chief research physicist on Stargate, a US government programme that tested remote viewing, the claimed ability to describe faraway places with the mind alone, had to put together a committee of scientists to oversee the work. A researcher named Chris Ramsay tells this without naming a source, and he links it to the psychologists Daryl Bem, Philip Zimbardo and a scientist named Schwartz. The point of telling it is that the programme was checked by serious outside scientists, not run in secret on belief alone.
eeg-neurofeedback-chair-sessions-targeti: From about 2008 to 2010, at Baker Victory Services in Western New York, he was put through sessions in what he calls "the chair," brain-wave training that recorded his brain signals and aimed at the slow theta and fast gamma waves. That is what Jordan Jose says, a man who claims he was taken into a UFO program as a child. He speaks of it firsthand and says this is where many of his traumatic memories came back, which, if true, would mean such programs worked on children's minds.
eeg-shuts-down-inside-homestead-2-2020: A machine reading brain activity, called an EEG, is said to have shut down when a man walked into a building known as Homestead 2 on Skinwalker Ranch, a property in Utah, and come back on as soon as he walked out. Michels tells it himself, recalling the moment to his guest in a 2026 episode with the ranch's owner. He calls it "super strange," since it would mean something in that building can interfere with equipment.
effort-to-account-for-soviet-nukes-after: After the Soviet Union fell apart in 1991, the US government worked with the Russians in Moscow to track down every one of the old Soviet nuclear weapons, says Rolf Mowatt-Larssen, a former chief at the CIA, America's foreign spy agency. He tells it as someone who was there, and calls it "a heroic really heroic effort".
efim-liberman-s-research-on-cytoskeletal: A Soviet scientist named Efim Liberman was deeply interested in cytoskeletal learning, the idea that the tiny scaffolding inside cells helps the brain learn. Michels tells this himself, from his friends Daniil and David Liberman, Efim's sons, and says their father knew the physicist Roger Penrose or perhaps the anesthesiologist Stuart Hameroff, two men known for linking the brain to quantum physics. He brings it up as an early sign of the idea that the brain works at a quantum level.
eg-g-as-aec-doe-prime-contractor-running: A company called EG&G became the main contractor for the Atomic Energy Commission, the US agency that ran nuclear weapons work in the 1950s, at the Nevada Test Site, where those weapons were tested. It later filled the same role for the Department of Energy, the agency that took over that work. Michels says this himself, without naming a source, in an episode with a NASA doctor who says he saw a UFO in a secret hangar, to show who ran the secret desert sites.
eg-g-as-gatekeeper-of-area-51-1960: In the early 1960s, a company called EG&G, through a special projects division based in Las Vegas, was trusted to run the day-to-day business of Area 51, a secret military test site at Groom Lake in Nevada. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, and says the company handled screening of staff, access to the site, transport and daily operations. If true, a private contractor was the gatekeeper of one of the most secret places in the country.
eg-g-engineer-s-account-of-an-egg-shaped: A senior engineer at EG&G, a US defense contractor, described to a relative an egg-shaped craft about the size of an SUV that no one could open. Michels relays this in his episode with Jake Barber, a man who says he retrieved a UFO by helicopter, passing on what the engineer told a great uncle. If true, it would mean contractors held an object they could not get inside.
eg-g-interview-switched-mid-way-to-the-s: In 1988, Bob Lazar says, he went to a job interview at EG&G, a defense contractor in Las Vegas, and partway through they told him, "we actually have a different job that we're thinking of plugging you into now." Lazar, who tells it first-hand, says that other job was at S-4, the hidden site in Nevada where he says he went on to work.
egg-landing-in-a-brazilian-town-moment-o: Everyone in a small town in Brazil is said to have seen an egg-shaped object land, which seemed to give off something like ammonia and even seemed to kill a doctor. Michels retells it from a documentary called Moment of Contact, tied to a man named James Fox, as a case where a whole town shares one account.
egg-shaped-object-descends-in-the-kilo-a: In 1978 an object shaped like an egg went straight down to the ground in the "Kilo" area near the launch site called Kilo 10, part of the nuclear missile field run from Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota, says Mario Woods, an Air Force veteran who served there. Woods says he saw it himself and mentions a fellow airman named Mark Wade, telling it on an episode where veterans who say they were taken by aliens meet again 50 years later.
egg-shaped-tall-white-craft-using-dog-bo: Between 1965 and 1967, a man named Charles Hall says, tall white beings had a base at the north end of Indian Springs Valley in Nevada and used a spot called Dog Bone Lake as a landing field for their egg-shaped craft. Hall tells it as something he saw himself during three years he says he spent around these beings near a secret Air Force site, which, if true, would mean non-human visitors were living alongside the US military.
egg-video-as-helicopter-sling-load-2025: A 2025 video of an egg-shaped object, which the journalist Ross Coulthart and a man named Jake Barber present as a mysterious craft, may really show something hanging under a helicopter, according to the UFO skeptic Mick West. West says the object is probably bigger than it looks and might be a load being moved by helicopter. This is his own reading of the footage, and it would mean the video shows nothing unusual.
eglin-afb-diamond-formation-of-orbs-gaet: An aircrew at Eglin Air Force Base in Florida saw glowing orbs flying in a diamond-shaped formation, and when Matt Gaetz, a US congressman from Florida, tried to speak with that crew, he was turned away. This comes from a former intelligence officer named David Grusch, who passes on what Gaetz went through. If true, it would mean the military kept even a sitting member of Congress away from witnesses.
egyptian-authorities-board-up-the-paw-an: In the 1990s, Egyptian authorities are said to have covered the front of one of the Great Sphinx's paws at Giza with "literal boards" and blocked it off, and to have drilled holes that would mislead anyone looking. A researcher named Matt LaCroix tells this, linking it to radar scans said to show hollow spaces under the Sphinx. If true, it would mean officials hid whatever lies beneath the monument.
egyptian-decoration-at-the-mount-wilson-: The lodges where astronomers stayed at Mount Wilson Observatory, above Pasadena, California, were "reportedly decorated with Egyptian hieroglyphs and symbols." Michels tells it as something reported, linking it to the astronomer George Ellery Hale, in an episode about hidden pagan and ritual threads running through American space science.
egyptian-government-pumps-water-out-from: The Egyptian government has reportedly put in pumps near the Khafre Valley Temple, an ancient stone temple next to the Sphinx, to pump water out from under the Giza Plateau where the pyramids stand. A researcher named Jeffrey Drum says this without naming a source. He tells it as a sign that there is water and hidden space beneath the pyramids.
egyptian-priests-levitating-blocks-with-: Ancient Egyptian traditions are said to describe priests lifting the huge stone blocks of the Great Pyramid at Giza into the air, using sound to do it. The writer Graham Hancock, who writes about lost ancient civilisations, brings this up without naming the texts he means. If true, it would mean the builders had a technique that has since been lost.
egyptian-symbols-in-a-freemasonic-temple: Michels says he has been inside a temple of the Freemasons, an old fraternal society with secret rituals, in Washington DC, and that it is full of ancient Egyptian symbols. He tells this from his own visit, in passing, as a sign that old esoteric ideas sit close to the centre of American power.
eiffel-tower-pollution-prank-on-a-fellow: In the 1980s, inside a military remote viewing unit (a team that tried to describe faraway targets using only the mind), one viewer says he played a prank on a colleague by planting an image in his head before a session. Army sergeant Lyn Buchanan, who served in the unit, tells it as his own doing: he says he told the colleague, "Oh, by the way, your target today is probably not the Eiffel Tower," which would put the tower in the man's mind and spoil his reading.
eight-hour-read-ons-with-15-minutes-to-s: Dylan Borland, a man who says he worked at the defence company BAE Systems between 2015 and 2018, describes his first "read-ons", the briefings that let a worker into a secret programme. He says they lasted about eight hours and came with a stack of paper "like this thick" covered in sticky notes, and he tells it as someone who sat through them himself. The story's point is that he had only 15 minutes to sign at the end, which would mean people agree to strict secrecy without really being able to read what they sign.
eight-sided-great-pyramid-and-the-templa: The researcher Jay Anderson says the flag of the Knights Templar, a medieval order of crusader knights, is an eight-sided pyramid drawn flat, and that if you build it out in three dimensions you get the Great Pyramid of Giza. He draws the idea from the online commentator known as Dark Journalist and the author Joseph P. Farrell. If true, it would suggest the Templars held some secret knowledge about the pyramid.
einstein-letter-to-fdr-leads-to-the-manh: In 1939 Albert Einstein and another scientist wrote to President Franklin D. Roosevelt warning that Germany might build an atomic bomb, and this led to the Manhattan Project, America's secret wartime effort to build the bomb first. A former Air Force officer named Robert Salas tells this as background history, without naming a source, saying they wrote "about the possibility that Germany could build an atomic bomb" and admitting he cannot recall the other man's name. He tells it to set the scene for the nuclear age that UFOs are later said to take an interest in.
einstein-oppenheimer-letter-1940: There is a letter, supposedly written in the 1940s by the physicist Albert Einstein to J. Robert Oppenheimer, the scientist who led the building of the atomic bomb. The UFO historian Richard Dolan mentions it in passing and calls it "very interesting", but he does not say where it came from or what it says.
einstein-s-1923-paper-saying-general-rel: Albert Einstein, the physicist, is said to have written that his theory of gravity, general relativity, fits with the ether, an old idea of an invisible medium filling all of space. Michels recalls it as a paper from about 1923, and the Navy scientist Salvatore Pais dates it to 1921. The text itself, "Ether and the Theory of Relativity," is actually a lecture Einstein gave at the University of Leiden on May 5, 1920, and in it he says that "space is endowed with physical qualities; in this sense, therefore, there exists an ether," and that "space without ether is unthinkable."
einstein-s-cosmological-constant-and-cos: In 1917, Albert Einstein added a term to his equations, called the cosmological constant, that works like a cosmic antigravity, because he liked the idea of a universe that never expanded. The Harvard astronomer Avi Loeb tells this, explaining that a universe that never grew meant Einstein did not have to imagine what came before a beginning. He does not name a source.
einstein-s-deathbed-breakthrough-1955: There is a saying that when the physicist Albert Einstein was dying in Princeton, New Jersey, in 1955, he suddenly became ecstatic and began talking excitedly to his nurse in German, as if he had just made a breakthrough. The physicist John Brandenburg passes this on to Michels as something people say, not as something he saw. The story matters because the nurse did not speak German, so whatever Einstein may have worked out would have been lost.
eisenhower-aware-of-foo-fighters-1942: Dwight D. Eisenhower, the American general who later became president, knew about the foo fighters from 1942 to 1945. Foo fighters were the strange glowing objects that aircrews reported during the Second World War. The commentator Marik von Rennenkampff says this, without naming a source, during a debate on Michels's show with a UFO skeptic, as a sign that the issue reached the very top of the military that early.
eisenhower-era-peads-used-to-create-waiv: Under President Eisenhower in the 1950s, presidential emergency action documents, orders a president keeps ready for a national emergency, were used to set up waived special access programs, secret projects so sensitive they are exempt from the usual reporting, which left them free from oversight by Congress. The host says this in an episode with a guest named Eric W. Davis, whose account he is drawing on. If true, it would explain how secret projects could run for decades without lawmakers knowing.
eisenhower-era-presidential-emergency-ac: In the 1950s, President Dwight D. Eisenhower is said to have used secret orders called presidential emergency action directives, special White House instructions for emergencies, to cover the UFO subject. Eric W. Davis, a Pentagon scientist, says these orders "were instituted in the Eisenhower White House administration." He says they have since been used for many topics, but that he and a man named Jim Semivan know they were set up "for this topic." A guest named Grant Cameron also credits Semivan but does not name Eisenhower. He says this kind of document is "how it started, which means it's an executive program. The president is running the cover up." If so, the secrecy would come from the top of government, not from some lower office.
eisenhower-s-1954-treaty-with-the-greys: The story goes that in 1954 President Dwight Eisenhower made a secret treaty with the Grays, small grey-skinned beings from UFO lore, letting them collect biological samples and run medical experiments on Americans. Michels raises it several times as part of "the lore": he calls it the Greada treaty, says Eisenhower slipped away under the cover of a dentist visit in Palm Springs, and places the deal at Edwards Air Force Base in California. The philosopher Jason Jorjani tells a version in which Eisenhower first met the Nordics, tall human-looking beings from the same lore, and then the Grays, who "made him a better deal". The writer Peter Levenda mentions it in passing and more doubtfully, saying "Eisenhower or somebody" signed a contract with aliens in the 1950s. If true, the US government would have knowingly traded its own citizens' bodies for something from alien beings.
eisenhower-s-farewell-warning-about-the-: When President Dwight D. Eisenhower left office in January 1961, as John F. Kennedy came in, he gave a farewell address warning: "Beware of the military-industrial complex." A UFO researcher named Steven Greer cites that speech to Michels and says what he describes is "exactly" what Eisenhower warned about. For Greer, it shows a president saw the danger of an unaccountable power built from the military and its contractors.
eisenhower-s-granddaughter-is-an-abducte: A granddaughter of President Dwight Eisenhower, Laura Eisenhower, is described as an abductee, meaning someone who says she has been taken by non-human beings, and as deeply involved in the UFO subject. Michels brings this up himself, in passing, without naming a source. He raises it as a striking link between a former president's family and the topic.
eisenhower-s-meeting-with-ets-about-stop: President Dwight D. Eisenhower did meet with beings from another world in the mid-1950s, near Palm Springs, California, and the talk was about stopping the spread of nuclear weapons. That is the claim of Steven Greer, a UFO researcher, who says a series of reports from the French Ministry of Defense shows the meeting took place, though "it wasn't the mythology" people usually tell. If true, a US president would have been dealing directly with visitors over the bomb.
eisenhower-shown-five-spacecraft-at-edwa: The story goes that in the 1950s President Dwight D. Eisenhower vanished from public view for a day and was secretly taken to Edwards Air Force Base in California, where he was shown craft from another world. It is told by Charles Hall, a man who says he spent three years with tall white aliens at Area 51, a secret Air Force site in Nevada. Hall is repeating what others have told him, and he points to the television series Ancient Aliens. In his version, the official story was that Eisenhower was golfing in Palm Springs, and with no cameras and no press present he was shown five spacecraft sitting on the runway at Edwards. Michels tells it on his own in a later episode with an Air Force sergeant named Dan Sherman. He puts it in 1954, says the cover story was a dentist appointment rather than golf, and calls it a meeting without mentioning the five craft. If true, it would mean an American president was personally briefed on alien visitors seventy years ago.
elderly-widow-sees-a-ball-of-light-at-he: An elderly widow says she saw a ball of light go past her kitchen window. Chris Bledsoe, a man who says UFOs show up around him, passes on what she told him. He tells it as one more sighting of the lights connected to him.
eleanor-roosevelt-letter-to-oppenheimer-: Michels says rumors of UFOs over Los Alamos, the New Mexico laboratory where the atomic bomb was built, and over other nuclear sites spread so far that the former first lady Eleanor Roosevelt wrote to the physicist J. Robert Oppenheimer to ask about them. According to Michels, Oppenheimer wrote back to reassure her that they were only rumors, and his letter has been verified and is kept in the Library of Congress. Michels tells this himself, as a sign of how widely such sightings were talked about at the top in the late 1940s.
electrical-after-effects-of-the-encounte: After a strange encounter in 2019, a researcher's phone is said to have behaved oddly: even after he wiped it back to factory settings, it charged almost instantly for the first few days. The researcher, Deep Prasad, tells this as something that happened to him, as one of the after-effects of the experience. If true, it would suggest the encounter left some lasting electrical trace on the things around him.
electrodynamic-dust-shield-payload-teste: A device called the Electrodynamic Dust Shield, meant to keep moon dust off equipment, was landed on the Moon with nine units on board, a little over a year before he spoke. That is what Charles Buhler, a NASA engineer who worked on it, says. He tells it as proof the technology was tried on the lunar surface.
electronic-failures-near-the-baltic-sea-: Michels says that electronics fail and "the weirdest things happen" around a strange object lying on the floor of the Baltic Sea between Sweden and Finland. He tells this from his own trip there with a treasure hunter named Dennis Åsberg, who belongs to Ocean X, the diving team that found the object. If true, it would suggest the object still has some effect on the machines around it.
element-115-used-to-amplify-gravity: Element 115, a very heavy element made in laboratories, is said to have been used inside captured alien craft to boost their gravity effect. Steve Colbern, a scientist who studies objects said to be alien implants, repeats this from Bob Lazar, a man who has said he worked on alien craft at a secret site in Nevada. Colbern adds that he does not remember Lazar telling him this himself, only that it is Lazar's claim.
elena-hardy-finds-gli3-mutation-in-the-n: Genetic data from the small three-fingered mummies found near Nazca, Peru, shows a mutation in a gene called GLI3, according to the researcher Elena Hardy, who looked at the data herself in NCBI, a public US database of genetic information. She tells Michels that a similar mutation is linked in the scientific literature to polysyndactyly, a condition of extra or fused fingers and toes. That could offer an explanation for the bodies' unusual hands.
elephant-cage-hf-antennas-may-have-aided: Michels wonders whether the huge ring-shaped radio antennas known as "elephant cages", which pick up high-frequency signals at bases such as San Vito dei Normanni Air Station in Italy and Offutt Air Force Base in Nebraska, were tied to the signals a former sergeant named Dan Sherman says he was decoding for the National Security Agency, the US signals intelligence agency, in the early 1990s. Sherman describes that work in his book Above Black, which Michels draws on. Michels puts it as an open question of his own, not as something Sherman claims.
eleusinian-mysteries-and-earlier-minoan-: The Eleusinian mysteries, secret religious rituals of ancient Greece, may have grown out of much older forms among the earlier Minoan and Mycenaean peoples of the region. Michels brings this up himself, citing the writer Brian Muraresku and his book The Immortality Key. He raises it to suggest that these rituals carry knowledge from far older times.
eleusinian-mysteries-and-the-kykeon: For centuries, ancient Greeks are said to have gone to Eleusis, a town 13 miles northwest of Athens, for secret rites called the Eleusinian Mysteries, where they drank a potion called the kykeon. The writer Brian Muraresku argues in his book The Immortality Key that the drink probably held ergot, a fungus Jesse Michels describes as psychedelic and linked to LSD. Michels returns to this often. He calls Eleusis the spiritual capital of Greece and names Plato, Socrates and Alcibiades among those tied to it. He says the rites were secret on pain of death, and that initiates walked away thinking they were immortal, summed up by the saying "if you die before you die, you won't die when you die." In one episode he adds Muraresku's view that the rites go back to Egypt. In another he says the drink freed the soul so people could see other beings. The writer Graham Hancock tells it too, in his book Supernatural, saying every initiate was given the drink. The neuroscientist Andrew Gallimore also mentions the ergot preparation. If true, it would mean one of the West's great religious traditions was built on a psychedelic experience.
eleusinian-mysteries-as-near-death-ritua: The Eleusinian Mysteries, secret religious rites of ancient Greece held at Eleusis, may have worked by bringing people close to death. Michels puts this forward himself, without naming a source: he says these and similar rituals "involve the temporary killing of the physical body through a near-death experience," which would make them a deliberate way to reach experiences beyond the body.
eleusis-dmtx-retreat-and-research-center: In 2025, according to the neuroscientist Andrew Gallimore, his group was running DMTX, a way of keeping people in the state brought on by the powerful psychedelic DMT for longer, and was building a retreat and research center in the Caribbean nation of St Vincent and the Grenadines. Gallimore describes it as a project he is part of, and he mentions a group called New Nautics in connection with it.
elevator-descent-at-the-facility-1980: Randy Anderson, a man who says he was there himself, describes riding an elevator down inside a building at S4, a secret site in the Nevada desert, sometime in the 1980s. He says it was "the first odd thing": the ride felt like it went down much further than you would expect. If true, it would point to a facility buried deep underground.
elijah-calls-down-fire-against-the-pries: In the Bible, the prophet Elijah held a contest against the priests of Baal, a rival god, to see whose god would light a sacrifice, and he called down fire from the sky to win it. A researcher named Jeffrey Mishlove brings up the story, describing it as calling down lightning, to compare it with something similar he was discussing. He tells it as an example of a person seeming to command a force of nature.
elite-baal-cult-tied-to-the-epstein-mate: Some of the world's ruling elite are obsessed with Baal, an ancient god of the Middle East, and this shows in the files from the investigations into the wealthy financier Jeffrey Epstein. That is the view of a filmmaker named Tim Alberino, who offers it as his own reading without naming a source. If true, it would mean an old religious cult lives on among the powerful.
elizabeth-rauscher-s-oni-grant-and-her-b: The physicist Elizabeth Rauscher, who worked with the researcher Andrija Puharich, is said to have received a big grant from the Office of Naval Intelligence, the Navy's spy agency, sometime in the 1970s or early 1980s. The researcher Greg Malatzi says that after she died he searched for any papers about it, even sending someone through her large research archive at Berkeley, but they found nothing. To him, the missing papers suggest the Navy-funded work was kept out of the record.
elizabeth-targ-dies-of-the-glioblastoma-: The story is that Elizabeth Targ, a psychiatrist doing medical research on psychic healers, died in 2002 of glioblastoma, the same deadly brain cancer she had been studying with those healers. Jeffrey Mishlove, a researcher with a PhD in parapsychology, tells it, describing her as "doing brilliant medical research on psychic healers". He notes that she was the daughter of Russell Targ.
elizondo-confirms-hastings-ufos-and-nuke: Luis Elizondo, a former Pentagon official who worked on UFO matters, says the researcher Robert Hastings was right in his reporting on UFOs showing up at American nuclear missile sites, the subject of Hastings's work UFOs and Nukes. Speaking from his own government experience, Elizondo says "everything he was reporting we saw" and calls Hastings's conclusions "spot on". He adds that he could not say so while he was still in government. If true, the military itself has watched UFOs near nuclear weapons.
elizondo-directed-aatip-an-offshoot-of-a: A Pentagon official named Luis Elizondo was the director of AATIP, the Advanced Aerospace Threat Identification Program, a small Pentagon office that studied unexplained aerial reports, according to Jesse Michels. Michels says this office grew out of AAWSAP, the Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program, a larger defense study of the same subject. He gives this as background in his documentary about Elizondo, to show that Elizondo held an official role.
elizondo-in-gray-fox-and-jsoc-s-link-to-: Luis Elizondo, a former Pentagon intelligence official, was once a member of Gray Fox, which Michels describes as the US Army's intelligence support activity group, a secretive unit tied to the military's special operations command. Michels says this twice, both times passing on what he was told by Matthew Pines, a friend who later came on the show, and in one telling he places it in the 2000s. If true, it would put Elizondo inside the special operations world that some link to recovering crashed objects.
elizondo-met-edward-teller-on-an-air-flo: When he was about seven, Luis Elizondo, a former Pentagon intelligence official later known for his work on UFOs, says he was put on an Air Florida flight from Sarasota to Miami and ended up travelling with Edward Teller, the physicist known as the father of the hydrogen bomb. Elizondo tells it as his own memory, explaining that his father had friends in the government and placed him on the plane with Teller. He tells it as an early brush with the world of top-level weapons science he would later work near.
elizondo-neither-confirms-nor-denies-bei: At a 2024 hearing of the House Oversight Committee in Washington, a man named Luis Elizondo was asked whether he had been briefed into Immaculate Constellation, a secret UFO program named in a report brought out by the journalist Michael Shellenberger, and he answered that he could neither confirm nor deny it. Michels points to that answer as telling, since a flat denial would have been easy if no such program existed. Elizondo himself later recalls his words a little differently on the show: that he would not be authorised to confirm or deny the existence of any ongoing or past program.
elizondo-on-60-minutes-the-government-sa: The United States government has already admitted that UFOs are real, according to a former Pentagon official named Luis Elizondo, and Michels repeats the line on his show. It comes from a segment of the US television news programme 60 Minutes, aired on 16 May 2021, in which the journalist Bill Whitaker asks, "So what you are telling me is that UFOs, unidentified flying objects, are real?" and Elizondo answers: "The government has already stated for the record that they're real. I'm not telling you that. The United States government is telling you that."
elizondo-on-aliens-storing-messages-in-g: The idea is that anyone wanting to leave a message that truly lasts has only two choices: send it into deep space, where it will rarely meet anyone, or write it into biology and genetics. Jesse Michels passes this on as something a former Pentagon official named Luis Elizondo told him. If it were true, the message might already be inside living things on Earth.
elizondo-points-aaro-to-a-safe-drawer-th: Luis Elizondo, a former Pentagon official, once told investigators from the Pentagon's current office for unexplained aerial reports exactly where to look: a particular office, a particular safe, a particular safe drawer. When they opened it, according to the story, there was nothing there. Kurt McConnell, a Senate staffer, passes this on as an episode he heard about, not one he saw, and it matters because a full drawer would have been hard evidence of hidden material.
elizondo-regularly-sees-green-orbs-in-hi: Green balls of light regularly show up in Luis Elizondo's house, says Elizondo himself, a former Pentagon official, and Michels says it too. Elizondo says his wife, his kids and his neighbors saw them as well. He says the orbs began when he joined AATIP, a small Pentagon office that studied unexplained aerial reports, and that other people in that program had the same thing happen. If true, it would suggest that the work itself brought strange events into people's homes.
elizondo-s-book-blocked-from-a-lockheed-: According to Michels, the book by Luis Elizondo, a former Pentagon official, describes how Elizondo and his colleagues went to Lockheed Martin, the large American defense company, to try to get inside a secret program there, and were kept out. Michels brings it up from Elizondo's book during a conversation with another guest, giving no further detail of what the program was.
elizondo-s-idea-that-ufos-are-prepping-t: Luis Elizondo, whom Michels calls one of the first whistleblowers to go public about UFOs, in 2017, has in the past suggested that UFOs may be "prepping the battle space", that is, preparing the ground as if for a coming conflict. Michels repeats this himself, as something Elizondo has said, without pointing to where. If true, the objects would be doing something more purposeful and worrying than simply being seen.
elizondo-s-imminent-people-with-cherokee: Luis Elizondo, a former Pentagon official who ran a small office studying UFO reports, writes in his book Imminent that people with Cherokee blood and DNA seem to have more encounters with the phenomenon. The researcher Jason Simosa tells Michels "it's in there" when he talks about the book. If true, it would suggest these experiences run in some family lines.
elizondo-s-toy-in-the-sandbox-analogy-fo: Luis Elizondo, a former Pentagon official who speaks publicly about UFOs, compares a technology he says the US holds to a toy in a sandbox, and wonders aloud whether "the kids in the sandbox can play together," meaning whether it could be shared instead of fought over. The remark comes up on a later episode of Michels's show and is tied to a conversation with Michels.
elizondo-saw-jacobs-s-film-at-aatip-2010: Robert Jacobs, a man who has spoken about filming an object near a nuclear missile test, says Luis Elizondo told him he had seen that film while running AATIP, a small Pentagon office that studied unexplained aerial reports. Michels relays this second-hand, quoting Jacobs: "he verified when he was in charge of AATIP he saw my film, my account." If true, it would mean the Pentagon office knew about and kept Jacobs's footage.
elizondo-says-monsanto-linked-people-are: Some of the people working against Luis Elizondo, a former Pentagon official who speaks publicly about UFOs, are tied to Monsanto, the American chemical and farming company, according to what Elizondo told Jesse Michels. Michels passes this on in an episode with a guest named Brigham Buhler, and adds that there is an old link between Monsanto and Bechtel, a large engineering firm, and that these people may also have been involved in the UFO question. If true, it would tie big companies to whatever secrecy surrounds UFOs.
elizondo-time-is-not-a-luxury-that-we-ca: A former Pentagon official named Luis Elizondo says that the public can no longer wait to talk openly about unexplained objects in the sky. In his own words: "Time is not a luxury that we can afford. We the time has come. We need to start having the conversation collectively," a call for shared, public discussion of the subject.
