elizondo-was-nro-liaison-while-at-ttsa-2: Around 2017, while the former Pentagon official Luis Elizondo was working at To The Stars Academy, a private company that studied UFOs, he was also serving as a liaison to the National Reconnaissance Office, the US agency that runs spy satellites. This comes from a researcher who goes by the online name UAPGerb, who points to Elizondo's own CV as the source. If so, it would mean Elizondo kept an active tie to the intelligence world while working in the private UFO effort.
elizondo-won-t-confirm-or-deny-immaculat: Testifying before Congress in 2024, a former Pentagon intelligence officer named Luis Elizondo said he could neither confirm nor deny being briefed on Immaculate Constellation, said to be a secret Pentagon program that gathers UFO data. Michels tells this himself, dating the hearing to September 2024 and quoting Elizondo's refusal. He points to it because the dodge suggests the program exists and Elizondo knows about it.
elizondo-worked-with-grusch-in-a-scif: Luis Elizondo, a former Pentagon intelligence official, says he worked side by side with David Grusch, a former intelligence officer who later came forward as a UFO whistleblower, inside a SCIF, a sealed room for handling classified material. Elizondo says he was asked not to say where, but that Grusch "had every access that you needed to have and he saw the same information I did." He tells it to back up Grusch's account with his own.
ellsworth-inner-zone-alert-saucer-beams-: Mario Woods, a former security guard at Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota, says that one night he and his partner, Michael Johnson, found an object "the size of a Walmart building" hovering about ten feet over the blast door of a nuclear missile site called November 5. Woods tells it firsthand: he says he looked at his watch at 12:15 and next found it was after 6 a.m., with the two men and their truck moved miles away to a reservoir, the mud around the truck strangely warm on a freezing night, and his partner unresponsive. The researcher Robert Hastings and Michels also retell it, Michels once adding a report of a flying saucer sending "a beam of reddish light" down at the missile, though the tellers disagree on whether it happened in the 1960s or in 1977 or 1978, and on whether the men were moved five, eight and a half, or nine miles.
ellsworth-radar-jet-chase-and-bismarck-l: On 5 August 1953, Michels says, a trained civilian sky-watcher reported a light near Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota, setting off radar tracking, a jet chase and more lights seen over Bismarck, North Dakota; he tells it himself, crediting the files of Blue Book, the US Air Force's UFO study of the 1950s and 60s. The University of Colorado's 1968 UFO report, Scientific Study of Unidentified Flying Objects, covers the case in an analysis by the researcher Gordon D. Thayer, which says a volunteer of the Ground Observer Corps saw a stationary "red glowing light" near Blackhawk, South Dakota, and that the report was passed to the Rapid City filter center, not phoned in to the base, after which an F-84 fighter jet "chased" the object without gaining on it. Thayer concludes the pilot "was probably chasing a star," and puts the whole chain of sightings down to stars seen through a layer of warm air, at least one meteor and false radar echoes.
ellsworth-silo-abandoned-with-access-plu: In 1978, a security team at Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota is said to have left one of its underground nuclear missile silos with the access plug, the heavy hatch that seals it, standing open. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, in an episode about two Air Force veterans who say they were abducted the year before. He offers it as another strange event at the same missile field.
elon-musk-knows-ufo-secrets-but-can-t-sa: Elon Musk, head of the rocket company SpaceX, knows the truth about UFOs but cannot say it publicly, according to the comedian and podcaster Joe Rogan. Rogan says he talked this over a day earlier with someone he names only as Dan, on a podcast called Age of Disclosure, and his verdict was "of course he knows." The point is that someone running a space company would be told what is up there.
elon-musk-on-joe-rogan-denies-advanced-t: The tech businessman Elon Musk said on the podcast of Joe Rogan, a popular interviewer, that he has an all-access pass through Lockheed and Northrop, two big American defense and aerospace companies, and that "we don't have any of these technologies." Michels brings this up himself in a 2025 episode with Steven Greer, a man who says UFO secrets are kept by a global ring of insiders. Musk's words stand as a denial that hidden advanced craft exist.
elon-musk-on-legacy-programs-at-a-trump-: The tech billionaire Elon Musk was asked about legacy programs, meaning secret government projects said to hold advanced or unexplained technology, at a town hall while campaigning for Donald Trump in 2024. According to the analyst Matthew Pines, Musk answered that if the US government has interesting technology, it should make it available. Pines retells it from memory, as a sign that the subject was reaching powerful people.
elongated-skulls-without-a-sagittal-sutu: Elongated skulls are said to have been found inside the Hypogeum of Malta, an ancient underground burial chamber cut into the rock, and one of them is said to be on display in a museum in Valletta, the island's capital. Jay Anderson, a researcher of ancient sites, tells this as something he has seen for himself. The story's point is that these skulls look unlike ordinary human ones, lacking the seam that normally runs along the top of the skull, which would hint at an unusual people in Malta's distant past.
elvis-starr-s-memoir-tape-about-meeting-: There is a tape, recorded as Elvis Starr dictated his memoir in the 1970s, in which he says he met someone named Valerie Ransone in the White House. An unnamed researcher on the show mentions this without giving a source beyond the tape itself, putting it as "there's a tape of him saying, like, I met Valerie Ransone in the White House." It is told as evidence that this meeting really took place at the seat of the US government.
email-to-doty-about-who-wrote-serpo-2020: A researcher named Deep Prasad says that in 2020 he emailed Richard Doty, a former Air Force counterintelligence agent, about who had really written Project Serpo, a widely shared story about a supposed secret exchange of people with an alien world. Prasad had concluded more than one person was behind it, and he says Doty wrote back, "I tip my hat off to you for realizing there was more people involved," which would mean the story was a group effort.
email-to-nolan-about-a-glowing-object-th: Someone wrote to report a glowing object that dropped molten metal. A Stanford scientist named Garry Nolan, who studies metal said to come from such objects, says the email reached him in late 2021, a few weeks before he spoke with Michels. He brings it up as one of the newest reports sent to him, and it would mean more physical material to study.
emails-from-people-who-saw-cigar-shaped-: Since 2011, people have been sending emails and even paper letters to a Swedish treasure hunter named Dennis Asberg, saying they saw cigar-shaped objects crash into the water and into forests. Asberg says some of those who contacted him were former navy officers, though in one telling he speaks of cigars and forests and in the other of letters and navy men. He tells it as backing for his idea that more objects have come down than anyone admits.
embassy-correspondence-waiting-for-the-a: The claim is that in the 1950s, letters at the Canadian embassy in Washington included a document saying, in effect, "we're waiting for the Americans to make a statement" about UFOs. The researcher Grant Cameron tells this from the personal files of Wilbert B. Smith, a Canadian government engineer who studied UFOs, and also names Omond Solandt, a senior Canadian defence scientist. If true, Canada knew something and was leaving it to the United States to speak first.
emenegger-and-linda-moulton-howe-promise: In the 1970s and 80s, a filmmaker named Robert Emenegger and a journalist named Linda Moulton Howe each believed the government would give them real UFO footage, and each time it was pulled away before they got it. A guest named Bryce Zabel, talking about Hollywood and UFOs, tells this as part of a pattern of promises made and taken back. It would suggest someone in government was testing or teasing public disclosure through filmmakers.
emenegger-gave-a-copy-of-the-documentary: A filmmaker named Bob Emenegger, who made a documentary called UFOs Past Present and Future, is said to have given a copy of it to the film director Steven Spielberg in the mid-1970s, before Spielberg made Close Encounters of the Third Kind, his film about alien contact. A man named Grant Cameron repeats what Emenegger told him: "I gave a copy to Spielberg." Cameron tells it as a hint that Spielberg's film may have drawn on material the documentary carried.
emergency-conference-at-camp-hood-on-nuc: An emergency meeting about UFOs seen near nuclear sites was held at Camp Hood, an Army post in Texas, bringing together the Air Force's criminal and counterintelligence investigators, the Army's counterintelligence branch, and the FBI, the US federal police. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source or giving a date. If true, it would show that several security agencies treated the sightings as a serious threat.
emp-from-nuclear-blast-travels-through-d: The electromagnetic pulse from a nuclear explosion, the burst of energy that can knock out electronics, travels through more than one dimension. The musician Tom DeLonge says this is "the one thing we found out," passing on what he was told by people he does not name. If true, it would help explain why unexplained objects take an interest in nuclear weapons.
encyclopedia-galactica-alien-taxonomy-se: The congressman Eric Burlison says someone sent him both volumes of the Encyclopedia Galactica, a document laying out a classification of alien types. He tells it as something that happened to him, without saying who sent it, and if genuine it would mean someone wanted a member of Congress to have a catalogue of non-human beings.
energy-grid-like-structures-beneath-the-: Radar scans are said to show large built structures deep under the pyramids of Giza in Egypt, laid out like an energy grid. The scans were made by Filippo Biondi, an Italian radar scientist. He used a method called synthetic aperture radar Doppler tomography, a way of using radar from space to picture what lies below ground. Biondi says it himself: "We are counting at the moment four plus four tubes." He says they run down from the base of the pyramid to "something that is located at the bottom." He credits two colleagues, Corrado Malanga and Armando Mei. Michels returns to it often. He describes coiled columns or "eight pillars" under the chamber of the Khafre pyramid, and "a small city or energy grid" mapped with help from artificial intelligence. He links it to the writer Christopher Dunn. In one telling Michels dates the discovery to 2022 and asks why it is only coming out now. The podcaster Joe Rogan says the structures "might go as deep as 2 km." A researcher named Jay Anderson calls the underground signals "undeniable." If true, it would mean the pyramids sit on a buried machine far older and stranger than thought.
engineers-describe-xf-131-super-sentinel: In 1992, a man named Bill McDonald met four engineers in California's Mojave Desert, two from Northrop and two from Lockheed, both big aircraft makers. Tired of the secrecy around their work, they described to him a triangular craft called the XF-131 Super Sentinel, which he drew from their words. The craft was what is called an ARV, short for alien reproduction vehicle, meaning a human-built craft said to copy alien technology. The story is told by a researcher who goes by the online name UAPGerb, passing on McDonald's account, and it would mean such craft were really being built.
enhanced-pilot-photo-shows-slanted-hanga: An aerial photograph, taken by a pilot about 17 miles from Papoose Lake, a dry lake bed in the Nevada desert, is said to show slanted hangar doors once it is enhanced. Michels tells this in a 2026 episode about the time he spent with Bob Lazar, a man who has long claimed that secret work on alien craft happened at Papoose Lake. He describes a researcher named Luigi Vendittelli showing Lazar the high-quality photo, which would back up Lazar's account if the doors are real.
enoch-s-ascent-and-transformation-into-m: Enoch, a figure from ancient Jewish scripture, is said to have gone up to heaven and walked with God, and then turned into an angel called Metatron. Michels tells this from the Book of Enoch, an ancient religious text, in the translation by R. H. Charles. He brings it up as an example of a human being transformed by contact with the beings above.
enochian-tale-found-in-dead-sea-scroll-m: A researcher named Tim Alberino says the story told in the ancient Jewish text called the Book of Enoch, about angels and giants, does not appear only in that book. He says it also turns up in several of the Dead Sea Scrolls, the ancient manuscripts found in caves at Qumran, including the Book of Giants, and in texts such as the Book of Jubilees and the Genesis Apocryphon, which to him shows how old and widespread the tale is.
enrico-fermi-thinks-about-aliens-at-los-: The story is that Enrico Fermi, the physicist who helped lay the groundwork for splitting the atom, spent his spare time thinking about aliens while building the atomic bomb at Los Alamos, New Mexico, in the 1940s. Michels tells it to make the point that someone "as conventionally well regarded as it gets" took the question seriously. The Harvard astronomer Avi Loeb gives a more specific version: about 70 years ago Fermi went to lunch with colleagues and they talked about how likely it is that extraterrestrials are out there, though Loeb does not name the place. If true, the question of alien life would have been taken seriously by top scientists from the very start of the atomic age.
ent-specialists-find-otolith-damage-in-h: In most cases of Havana syndrome, the unexplained headaches and dizziness reported by US diplomats and spies, ear, nose and throat doctors reportedly found damage to the otolith, a tiny balance organ in the inner ear. A guest named Chris Gilbert says this without naming a source. If true, it would point to a real, physical injury behind the symptoms.
entities-based-on-the-moon-airdropping-t: Beings living on the Moon may have been dropping technology onto Earth "here and there" over time. Michels raises the idea as a question to his guest Randall Carlson, in an episode titled "The Moon Is An Alien Spaceship." He asks what such beings have been doing and suggests this as his own guess.
entity-pulls-him-out-of-his-body-and-sco: In 1970, while stationed in Germany and sunk in depression, Joe McMoneagle says he woke in the middle of the night to find an entity that "snatched me out of my body" and then scolded him until he snapped out of it. McMoneagle, who later served as an Army psychic spy, tells this as something that happened to him.
envelope-lettering-transferred-onto-deve: Steve Colbern, a scientist who studies objects people believe are alien implants in their bodies, says a doctor he names as Dr. builder once showed him one X-ray out of about 200. On it, he says, the lettering from the outside of the envelope that held the X-ray had somehow been transferred onto the developed film. Colbern tells it as something he saw with his own eyes, a sign that something unusual had been acting on the film.
epiphany-during-jean-houston-s-mystery-s: Jeffrey Mishlove, a researcher with a doctorate who studies psychic phenomena, says he once had a sudden experience of how God created the universe. He says it came while he was listening to a lecture at the "mystery school" run by the teacher Jean Houston, on The Cipher of Genesis, a book by Carlos Suarès about the Book of Genesis. Mishlove tells it as something that happened to him: "I got it. And I had the experience of how it happened."
epstein-as-the-front-for-a-project-or-sp: The idea is that the financier Jeffrey Epstein, with his private plane and island, was the public face of some kind of hidden project or special access program, the most tightly restricted kind of secret US government programme. A researcher named Eric Weinstein raises it in passing, without naming a source, while saying of another man that he does not think that man was the one running "the Jeffrey Epstein special access project or whatever it was." If true, it would mean Epstein's activities were part of something organised from above.
epstein-blackmail-file-on-senior-nationa: A very senior person in the US national security world was caught up with the financier Jeffrey Epstein, and is now kept on a short leash because a blackmail file exists on them. That's the claim of Steven Greer, a UFO activist, who presents it as something he was told and names no one. If true, it would mean someone high up in the government could be quietly controlled.
epstein-circle-s-gravity-interest-as-an-: The financier Jeffrey Epstein was fixated on physics research into defying gravity, and the researcher and philosopher Jason Jorjani suspects this was really a hunt for electrogravitics, the idea of controlling gravity with electricity, which he describes as what is believed to be the power and propulsion system of UFOs. On the show Jorjani tells Michels he "suspects" it, links it to an effect named after the inventor Thomas Townsend Brown, and says it is "all part of the UFO phenomenon that they're trying to crack." In his own essay Ocean Outlaw: A Portrait of Ghislaine Maxwell, about Epstein's associate Ghislaine Maxwell and published on 29 July 2025, he states it plainly as fact ("In other words, he was interested in electrogravitics") and does not mention Brown at all.
epstein-email-about-killing-pons-and-col: According to Jesse Michels, the financier Jeffrey Epstein bragged in one of his emails that he had "killed Pons" years before. Michels takes this to mean the chemists Stanley Pons and Martin Fleischmann, who in 1989 claimed results in cold fusion, meaning nuclear fusion at room temperature, and if he is right it would mean Epstein helped bury that work. Michels raises it himself across several episodes, quoting the emails without saying where he read them, and once adds, crediting the journalist Whitney Webb and her book One Nation Under Blackmail, that Epstein sold a piece of software tied to Sandia National Laboratories, a US nuclear weapons lab, that siphoned off American nuclear secrets.
epstein-files-show-interest-in-people-wi: The released records about the network around Jeffrey Epstein are said to show that it took an interest in people with psi abilities, meaning claimed powers of the mind, or with empathy or "consciousness abilities". Matthew Brown, introduced on the show as a Pentagon whistleblower, says this is "provably in the files", which would mean the network was looking for people with such gifts.
epstein-prison-cell-video-metadata-edite: The video from the jail cell where Jeffrey Epstein died in 2019, footage meant to show a suicide, had its metadata edited, the hidden file data that records how a video was made, probably with the editing program Adobe Premiere. Michels tells this himself, crediting a 2025 report in Wired, which he calls a fairly ordinary tech magazine. He raises it as a sign that the official account of the death may have been tampered with.
epstein-s-eugenics-plan-to-create-his-ow: Jeffrey Epstein, the financier, was obsessed with eugenics, the idea of breeding people for chosen traits, and wanted to create his own race, with his ranch in New Mexico as part of the picture. A guest named Jay Anderson says this, passing on what he heard from a witness named Juliet Byron. It is told as a clue to what Epstein was really after.
epstein-s-gravity-conference-and-submari: The financier Jeffrey Epstein took people down in submarines, the physicist Stephen Hawking among them, to study what were described as quantum gravitational anomalies in the Bahamas basin, the stretch of sea known as the Bermuda Triangle. A philosopher named Jason Jorjani tells Michels this, crediting others such as a researcher named Eric Weinstein, and if true it would suggest Epstein's circle was chasing ways to beat gravity. Jorjani's own article "Ocean Outlaw: A Portrait of Ghislaine Maxwell", published 29 July 2025, tells of a single dive in which Epstein's associate Ghislaine Maxwell piloted the "Atlantis" submarine that took Epstein and Hawking to the Bermuda Triangle seabed "to study quantum magnetic anomalies". That is magnetic, not gravitational, and the article does not name the Bahamas. It adds that Epstein's foundation sponsored a 2006 conference titled "Confronting Gravity" with top physicists from places like Caltech, MIT, Harvard and CERN.
epstein-s-gravity-conferences-casimir-ob: Jeffrey Epstein, the financier, is said to have been "obsessed" with the Casimir effect, a tiny force that appears between two very close metal plates in empty space, and, according to Michels, to have hosted gravity conferences and known about a physics theory of Michels's former colleague, the researcher Eric Weinstein. Michels tells this himself on two episodes, insisting that "this is all in the emails", meaning Epstein's leaked emails. In one of them he speaks only of the Casimir obsession, linking it to interest in new ways of propelling craft.
epstein-s-keycard-access-to-harvard-evol: The financier Jeffrey Epstein is said to have been involved in an evolutionary biology program at Harvard University and to have had a keycard to get into it. A philosopher named Jason Jorjani tells this, naming the evolutionary biologist Robert Trivers and the geneticist George Church in the same account. He raises it to suggest Epstein had close access to research on human evolution and genetics.
epstein-s-listening-post-at-one-brattle-: The financier Jeffrey Epstein had another "listening post", as the mathematician Eric Weinstein calls it, at One Brattle Square in Cambridge, Massachusetts, in the 2000s. Weinstein cites the released Epstein files for this and mentions the scientist Martin Nowak alongside it. The point, as he tells it, is that Epstein kept close watch on scientists in the Cambridge academic world.
epstein-s-obsession-with-gravity-propuls: The financier Jeffrey Epstein is said to have been obsessed with secret science, above all with gravity and new kinds of propulsion. According to Michels, Epstein flew physicists such as Kip Thorne, Stephen Hawking and Murray Gell-Mann out to his private island, and gave the scientist Lawrence Krauss about $250,000. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, calling it one of the lesser-known threads of the Epstein story.
epstein-s-zorro-ranch-near-los-alamos-ph: The financier Jeffrey Epstein is said to have set up his Zorro Ranch in New Mexico around 1993 so that he could be near retiring physicists from Los Alamos, the US nuclear weapons laboratory in that state. Michels raises it on four episodes and sources it to an interview Epstein gave the political strategist Steve Bannon near the end of his life, which Michels dates to 2019. Michels uses it to argue that security at the Department of Energy, the agency that runs the lab, was so lax that a private man could set out to get close to its scientists.
eric-bard-replicates-the-anomalies-with-: Brandon Fugal, the owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property known for reports of strange happenings, says a member of the research team there, Erik Bard, managed to reproduce some of the odd readings they had recorded. According to Fugal, Bard did it by focusing "intense electromagnetic force" with a neodymium magnet, a very strong permanent magnet, during work shown in the first season of the TV series The Secret of Skinwalker Ranch. If so, it would suggest the ranch's anomalies involve powerful magnetic effects.
eric-davis-at-closed-hearing-nhi-control: At a closed-door session of the US Congress in 2025, a witness named Eric W. Davis is said to have stated that "the NHI are controlling disclosure", meaning that non-human intelligences themselves decide how much the public learns about them. Michels tells this himself on two occasions; in one he places Davis at the closed session alongside Luis Elizondo, a former official Michels elsewhere calls a whistleblower, and a researcher named Avi Loeb. In the other he names no hearing or other witnesses and says it is his favorite line from Davis, though he disagrees with him about a figure named Townsend Brown. If true, the timing of any public revelation would be out of human hands.
eric-davis-calls-townsend-brown-a-phony-: The inventor Thomas Townsend Brown, known for claims that electricity could make objects move without propellers or rockets, was a phony, according to the physicist Eric W. Davis, who has worked on government UFO studies. Michels tells this himself, in a talk with the UFO activist Steven Greer, saying Davis contacted him directly to say so. It matters because Brown is often cited as an early pioneer of antigravity.
eric-davis-craft-defying-physics-but-no-: Eric Davis, a physicist who has worked on Pentagon studies of UFOs, is said to have described a secret programme with craft that "defy the laws of physics" but no physicists working on them. The mathematician Eric Weinstein repeats this as Davis's words. Michels repeats it twice in other episodes, once just saying there were no physicists on the programme, and once telling it as Davis's answer when asked directly whether any theoretical physicists were involved: "there none of them were." The point is that the people holding the strangest technology may not have the scientists needed to understand it.
eric-davis-denies-alien-reproduction-veh: The physicist Eric W. Davis says there are no American aircraft built by copying recovered alien craft, sometimes called alien reproduction vehicles. In his own words, there are "definitely no aircraft systems that have leveraged anything" and "there's been no one to one reproduction." The statement comes up in an episode with an online researcher who goes by UAPGerb, and it matters because it flatly denies one of the most persistent claims about secret UFO programmes.
eric-davis-dia-report-on-teleportation: The physicist Eric W. Davis wrote a report on teleportation for the Defense Intelligence Agency, the Pentagon's military intelligence service. Salvatore Pais, a Navy scientist who holds unusual patents, says he saw it among "one of those DIA reports" and calls it important, without saying more about its source. He brings it up because it supports his own ideas about advanced physics.
eric-davis-helped-write-a-book-for-bigel: While working on a Pentagon-funded programme that studied UFOs and other strange phenomena from 2008, run through the company of the aerospace businessman Robert Bigelow, the physicist Eric Davis is said to have been helping write a book for Bigelow at the same time. The claim comes from a speaker identified only as Jack, on an episode with the Navy scientist Salvatore Pais, who puts it simply: "Davis was helping write that book at the time." The book is not named. It is told to show how closely the government work and Bigelow's private projects ran together.
eric-davis-lied-to-uapgerb-about-alien-r: An online UFO researcher who goes by UAPGerb says that Eric Davis, a physicist who has worked on Pentagon UFO studies, lied to his face about whether the government has succeeded with technologies copied from alien craft and with alien reproduction vehicles, meaning human-built copies of them. UAPGerb tells it from his own dealings with Davis in the 2020s. If true, it would mean someone close to the programs is hiding how far they have got.
eric-davis-offers-full-testimony-for-bla: A Pentagon scientist named Eric W. Davis is said to have stated on camera that if he were given blanket immunity, meaning full legal protection from prosecution, he would tell everything he knows. A researcher named Eric Weinstein points to this, saying Davis is "on record" in the most recent film by James Fox. It would suggest Davis holds secrets he feels he cannot legally share.
eric-davis-s-notes-from-the-advanced-phy: The UFO researcher Grant Cameron says the physicist Eric W. Davis gave him his notes from the Advanced Physics Theoretical Working Group, a group that discussed unusual physics in the early 2000s. Cameron tells it first-hand and also mentions a person named Oke Shannon, and he treats the notes as an inside look at what such a group was weighing, tied to the papers of the astronaut Edgar Mitchell, including an alien autopsy document, and to an Army lab test of lift devices.
eric-davis-saw-classified-crash-retrieva: A craft that crashed was recovered along with alien bodies, according to the physicist Eric W. Davis, who says he has seen classified evidence of this crash recovery. He tells Michels he cannot say much more, only that 'there's a craft and there's alien bodies.' If true, it would mean the US government holds a downed non-human vehicle and its crew.
eric-davis-says-the-head-of-crash-retrie: The man who ran a secret program to recover crashed unknown craft refused to be interviewed, says Eric W. Davis, a researcher who was looking into such programs. Speaking on Michels's show in August 2026, Davis says he "would love to talk to the head of the crash retrieval program during that era, but he refused to talk to us," and he names Glenn Gaffney in the discussion. He tells it because, if such a program existed, its leader would hold the answers.
eric-davis-teleportation-study-for-mitre: A researcher named Eric W. Davis did a study on teleportation for the MITRE Corporation, a research company that works for the US government, in 2019. Michels tells this himself, saying a slide deck about the study was not exactly leaked but "kind of rediscovered". If true, it would show that the government was paying for research into teleportation only a few years ago.
eric-davis-writes-of-an-air-force-five-d: An Air Force study is said to have proposed that, if space and time are treated as having five dimensions instead of four, a link between electricity and gravity could be worked out to explain the Biefeld-Brown effect, a claimed push produced by high-voltage electrical devices. Michels reads this from the book Frontiers of Propulsion Science, quoting the writer Eric W. Davis, who he says "concedes" the point. In a later episode he reads from the same book again and names Marc Millis alongside Davis.
eric-haseltine-s-idea-of-a-massless-obje: An official named Eric Haseltine once asked whether the object Navy pilots met in 2004 near the aircraft carrier Nimitz, a white oval shape like a Tic Tac mint, might have no mass at all. He pointed to the basic physics rule that force equals mass times acceleration: something without mass could make sudden moves that no ordinary craft could. Jesse Michels relays the idea as something Haseltine brought up in his research, offering a way to explain how the object moved.
eric-hecker-raytheon-neutrino-system-und: A man named Eric Hecker, said to have worked for the defence contractor Raytheon, is reported to have described a neutrino system set up a mile under the ice at the South Pole. Neutrinos are tiny particles that pass through almost anything. The UFO researcher Steven Greer relays the story, saying Hecker "came forward" a couple of years ago about the system buried under the ice. A guest named Jay Anderson adds that Hecker noticed energy "being transferred from one area to another area where it wasn't supposed to be going." Jesse Michels also passes it on, calling it a neutrino emitter as well as a detector and linking it to the earthquake at Christchurch, New Zealand, which would mean a secret machine able to send energy through the Earth.
eric-hecker-s-childhood-involvement-with: A man named Eric Hecker says that as a child growing up on Long Island, New York, he was caught up in Stargate, the US government's secret programme for psychic spying. He tells it himself, describing it only as "a very peculiar history of nefarious activity" with the programme, on an episode about secret elite networks.
eric-henry-wang-s-name-on-dtic-engineeri: An engineer named Eric Henry Wang, who appears in UFO stories about Wright-Patterson Air Force Base in Ohio in the 1950s, was a real person, according to a researcher who goes by the online name UAPGerb. UAPGerb says you can find old engineering documents with Wang's name on them in the Defense Technical Information Center, the Pentagon's archive of technical reports. That would show at least that a figure from the stories really existed and did engineering work for the military.
eric-henry-wang-special-projects-at-wrig: Michels says a man named Eric Henry Wang ran special projects at Wright-Patterson, a US Air Force airfield, and was later moved to Kirtland Air Force Base in New Mexico, probably, Michels thinks, to work on exotic flight technology. In one telling he adds that in 1956 Wang's department was moved to the Sandia Laboratory complex at Kirtland, citing Wang's obituary in a mechanical engineering magazine and a writer named William Steinman. Michels raises it across several episodes, once alongside the inventor Viktor Schauberger, as a clue to where unusual flight research may have gone.
eric-lopes-and-the-second-capture-of-a-l: In Varginha, Brazil, in January 1996, two military police officers named Eric Lopes and Marco Eli Chereze are said to have captured a living, strange creature. It was the second such capture in the town. The UFO investigator James Fox describes Lopes as "the alleged driver during the second capture of one of the alive creatures." A documentary narrator, played in two episodes, places it on January 20, 1996. The narrator says that roughly three hours after a group of girls saw the creature, the two officers were driving down a road "on the lookout for something unusual when suddenly it runs right across their path." The tellers bring it up because, if true, it would mean authorities took a living non-human being into custody.
eric-lopes-refuses-to-talk-and-threatens: In Varginha, a town in Brazil where an extraterrestrial creature is said to have been seen and captured, a man named Eric Lopes refused to speak to a visiting film crew and threatened them, according to James Fox, who was there with the crew. Fox says that before Lopes threatened to shoot them, he said, "If you're here to talk about the ET, he won't talk." Fox tells it as a sign of how guarded people there still are about the case.
eric-lopes-went-into-hiding-marco-cherez: After a strange being was reportedly captured in Varginha, Brazil, in 1996, a driver named Eric Lopes who was involved went into hiding. A police officer named Marcos Charice, who is said to have handled the being while it was alive, died a couple of weeks later. The claim comes from the narrator of a documentary clip played on the show, and it would suggest that touching the creature was dangerous and that witnesses were afraid.
eric-walker-claimed-majestic-12-membersh: Eric A. Walker, a man connected to Penn State university, is said to have hinted that he belonged to Majestic 12, a secret US government group that some say was formed to handle crashed UFOs. According to Michels, Walker "seemed to claim" this in a conversation with a man named Henry Azadehdel. Michels brings it up in an episode with the UFO researcher Grant Cameron, whose work he draws on, and he leaves the details vague.
eric-walker-interview-what-do-you-know-a: In a 1987 phone interview, a man named Eric A. Walker, whom the researcher Grant Cameron describes as the head of the whole secret UFO program, cut off the person questioning him and asked, "What do you know about ESP?" ESP means sensing things beyond the normal senses, such as reading minds. When the person had no answer, Walker said that unless you understand how ESP works, "you will not be taken in by the control group," meaning the group said to run the secret. Cameron says he worked from the transcripts of these interviews, and he tells it as a sign that the secret is tied to the mind.
eric-walker-on-trw-board: The claim is that Dr. Eric A. Walker, a man named in UFO stories, sat on the board of directors of TRW, a large American defense and aerospace company, or even chaired it. A guest who goes by UAPGerb, an online researcher, says the UFO researcher Jacques Vallée has talked about this. Linking Walker to TRW would tie him to a major defense contractor.
eric-wang-s-secret-ufo-work-at-kirtland-: A man named Eric Henry Wang did secret UFO work at Kirtland Air Force Base in New Mexico in the 1950s and 1960s, according to his wife, Maria Wang. Jesse Michels tells how a researcher named Bill Steinman reached her, and she told him that her husband had worked there on "secret UFO related stuff." If true, it would place Wang inside a hidden government UFO effort.
eric-wargo-remote-viewing-as-precognitio: Remote viewing, the practice of trying to describe a distant or hidden place using only the mind, may really be precognition, a glimpse of one's own future, according to the writer Eric Wargo. Michels brings this up from Wargo's book Time Loops, where he says Wargo makes that argument.
eric-wargo-s-time-loops-theory-of-precog: A writer named Eric Wargo argues in his book Time Loops that people can sense events in their own future before they happen, and offers a theory of how: the brain works as a kind of hybrid of an ordinary and a quantum computer that can reach "future knowledge states". Michels brings up the book in several episodes, saying he had Wargo on his show, and in one he stresses instead Wargo's idea of the "long body", a person stretched out across time. If true, it would mean the future can leak back into the present mind.
eric-weinstein-joins-galileo-project-geo: A researcher named Eric Weinstein joined the Galileo Project, a Harvard-based effort to study UAP, the official term for unidentified objects in the sky, and he and a colleague sometimes speculate together about how such objects might work physically. This is told in Michels's episode on the Harvard study, in the words of a colleague of Weinstein's, around 2021 or 2022. It matters because it puts a well-known thinker on theoretical physics inside a scientific search for these objects.
eric-weinstein-s-secret-branch-of-physic: The mathematician Eric Weinstein has come to suspect that the United States ran a secret branch of physics from roughly the 1950s on. Michels tells this twice, describing what Weinstein believes rather than quoting him. In a 2024 episode he says Weinstein thinks physicists such as John Wheeler, Richard Feynman and Bryce DeWitt had far more to do with private aerospace companies "than actually met the eye." In another 2024 episode he adds the physicist Freeman Dyson to the list and speaks only of a "secret physics program," without the link to aerospace. If true, some of the best-known scientists of the century did hidden work for the weapons and aircraft industry.
erich-von-daniken-on-templar-secrets: Erich von Däniken, the Swiss author famous for arguing that ancient peoples were visited by beings from space, is said to have told the host that there are secrets about the Templars, the medieval Christian order of knights, that he cannot talk about. Michels tells this himself, as something von Däniken said to him when he asked about the order. If taken at face value, it suggests von Däniken believes he holds hidden knowledge about the Templars that he is bound to keep.
eridu-found-in-the-1800s-its-ziggurat-ne: Eridu, an ancient city in southern Iraq, was found in the 1800s, but diggers only excavated the main city, took its clay tablets to the British Museum, and never dug into its ziggurat, the great stepped temple tower. The researcher Matt LaCroix tells this as a summary, with an encyclopedia entry on Eridu credited behind it. He raises it because he thinks something important may still lie inside the unexcavated tower.
esa-scientists-recognize-tyler-at-the-va: Sometime in the 2010s, at the Vatican Observatory in Castel Gandolfo, Italy, scientists from the European Space Agency recognized a man she calls Tyler as soon as he was introduced by his real name, and "the whole place just erupted." The scholar Diana Pasulka says she was there, and names Guy Consolmagno as part of the story. Michels, retelling it, calls the man Tim Taylor and adds that this recognition got him led into the Vatican's archives, which would show how well known and trusted the man is in those circles.
esalen-contact-exercise-brings-blue-plas: In 2024, during a group exercise meant to make contact with something beyond ourselves at the Esalen Institute, a retreat center at Big Sur in California, blue glowing orbs rose out of the ocean and came within about 50 yards of the people there. Jordan Jose, who says he was taken into a UFO programme as a child, tells this as something he saw, calling them "plasma orbs." In a second telling he puts the group at about 30 people and stresses that they were "highly heart-centric," suggesting the group's state of mind drew the orbs in. He also mentions the journalist Ross Coulthart in telling it.
esgridge-s-poems-work-at-marshall-and-al: A co-host named Jack says an engineer named Richard Esgridge studied an idea called POEMS at NASA's Marshall Space Flight Center, a rocket research center, and that a scientist named Alzofon worked on approaches based on nucleonic spin, the spin of the particles in an atom's core. Jack says Alzofon talked these ideas over with the famous physicist Richard Feynman back in the 1930s. He tells it without naming a source, as part of a talk about unusual ways of moving craft.
esoteric-and-occult-imagery-on-nro-missi: The cloth patches made for launches by the National Reconnaissance Office, the US agency that runs spy satellites, are said to carry mystical and occult imagery. A researcher named Chris Ramsay says he looked into many of these mission patches himself and found them very interesting. He tells it as a hint that hidden beliefs run through secret parts of the government.
esp-tests-in-a-faraday-cage-at-the-round: In the early 1950s, at the Round Table Foundation, a private research group in Rockland, Maine, a researcher is said to have built a Faraday cage, a metal enclosure that blocks electric and radio signals, and run tests of ESP, the claimed ability to sense or send information by mind alone, inside it. The researcher Greg Malatzi tells this from his own understanding, without naming a source, calling it one of the first such tests "in a Faraday cage." The point of the cage was to rule out ordinary radio signals as the way any information got through.
esp-training-with-handler-meg-after-inte: Jordan Jose, a man who says he was taken into a secret UFO programme as a child, says that around 2008 to 2010 at Baker Victory Services, a children's service in Western New York, a team of interns was hired about two months after he arrived and worked only on him and his case. He says he was trained in ESP, meaning extrasensory perception, the supposed ability to sense things without the normal senses, under a handler he calls Meg. He tells it as his own experience, and if true it would mean a hidden programme was testing children for psychic abilities.
essa-truck-mechanic-repaired-damaged-sus: In 1996 the trucks at a Brazilian army school for sergeants, known as EsSA, needed major repairs to their suspensions, according to a man said to have been the base's truck mechanic. The documentary filmmaker James Fox says he had just spoken to this man, and he passes the account on. Fox raises it because damaged suspensions would suggest the trucks had carried something unusually heavy at that time.
estrada-cotton-joints-and-cyanoacrylate-: Small three-fingered bodies from Peru, presented by some as alien, were reportedly put together with cotton at the joints and held with cyanoacrylate, the chemical in super glue, which made them unusually hard. A researcher named Flavio Estrada says this from his own study of the figures, without naming another source. If true, it would mean the bodies were made by people.
ether-drift-detected-on-mount-wilson: An experiment on Mount Wilson in California is said to have picked up the Earth's motion through the ether, the invisible medium that older physics held fills all of space. The scientist Steve Colbern, who studies objects said to be alien implants in people, tells it from memory and gives the credit to a scientist he calls Milikin, saying the ether itself was not found directly, only the Earth's movement through it, and adding "I believe it was" about the place. If true, it would revive an idea that mainstream physics set aside.
ethiopian-churches-keep-the-book-of-enoc: The Book of Enoch, an ancient Jewish text left out of most Bibles, was taken into the holy scriptures of the Tewahedo Orthodox Christians and the Beta Israel Jewish community of Ethiopia around the 4th century AD. The filmmaker and researcher Tim Alberino tells Michels this, drawing on the book in the translation by R. H. Charles. He raises it to show that the book's stories, which matter to his interest in ancient giants, were long treated as sacred.
ets-arrived-en-masse-after-the-first-ato: After the first atomic bomb went off in 1945, extraterrestrials came to Earth in force and in large numbers, according to Steven Greer, a UFO disclosure campaigner. Greer states this as his own view and names no source. If true, it would mean nuclear weapons are what drew the visitors here.
ets-teleport-into-ce-5-circle: Extraterrestrials are said to have teleported right into the middle of groups gathered to contact them. Steven Greer, a former doctor who leads these gatherings, called CE-5, where people sit in a circle and try to invite contact with beings from elsewhere through meditation, tells it as something he and his groups experienced. If true, it would mean the beings answer such invitations in person.
ets-tell-government-leaders-to-develop-s: Aliens are said to have told government leaders that humanity must "develop spiritually" before they will share more technology or material with us. A guest named Dave Rossi, who says aliens taught him advanced physics, passes this on from stories he heard from the lawyer Dan Sheehan. If true, it would mean the holdup in contact is our own inner growth, not a lack of technology.
eugenicist-elites-become-the-nordics-189: The elites who backed eugenics, the movement to breed a 'better' human race, in America, Britain and Germany between about 1890 and 1939 went on to become the 'Nordics', the name UFO stories give to tall, fair, human-looking visitors. The writer and researcher Jason Jorjani puts this theory forward, naming the birth control campaigner Margaret Sanger among those involved and crediting a work called Closer Encounters. If true, it would mean some of the beings in UFO reports were linked to this human movement.
european-crash-retrieval-initiative-and-: A group called the European Crash Retrieval Initiative, run from Sweden, is looking into reports of crashed unknown craft in Europe, according to the astronomer Beatriz Villarroel, who is part of it along with Thomas Pinder and Alex Tal. She says they are working on an old unsolved case that she cannot describe, only calling it "super cool, super scary." She tells it as her own work, a sign that scientists in Europe are now chasing these cases too.
european-leader-confides-about-ufos-on-a: Sometime in the late 1990s an unnamed European leader went for a walk in a park with Kiran Ilum Xenov, a former president of a republic within Russia, and told him something very interesting about UFOs. Ilum Xenov tells it himself but does not say who the leader was or what he said. It matters because it would mean heads of state talk privately about these things.
european-research-council-s-10-million-p: A new mathematical approach to physics called positive geometries, tied to the physicist Nima Arkani-Hamed, has grown so big that the European Research Council, Europe's public science funding body, now has a 10 million euro programme for it. The scientist Donald Hoffman says so on the show. He brings it up as a sign that serious science is moving toward the idea that space and time are not the deepest layer of reality.
every-drilling-crew-suffers-equipment-fa: On the mesa at Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property famous for strange happenings, every drilling expert brought in to bore into the ground has had dramatic equipment failures, according to the ranch's owner. He tells it as something he has watched happen, and it feeds his claim that something lies hidden under the ranch.
every-recovered-craft-gets-a-reverse-eng: Every UFO the government recovers is said to get a copy: engineers build their own version to try to reproduce that specific craft and its technology. Michael Herrera, a man who says he saw a giant UFO in the Indonesian jungle, says this was relayed to him by people he does not name. If true, it would mean there is a human-built twin for each captured craft.
evidence-of-humans-in-the-americas-130-0: There is reportedly evidence of humans in the Americas as long as 130,000 years ago, ten times older than the usual date for when people first arrived there. The writer Graham Hancock says this without naming a source. If true, it would mean the history of people in the Americas is far older than taught.
ewen-cameron-examines-rudolf-hess-to-see: In England in the 1940s, the psychiatrist Ewen Cameron was brought in to examine Rudolf Hess, one of the top Nazi leaders. His job was to work out whether the prisoner really was Hess or a double. The author Peter Levenda tells this on Michels's show without naming a source. If the man was a double, the person in custody was not who the world believed he was.
exeter-wobbling-disc-1964: In 1964 in Exeter, New Hampshire, four people, two of them police officers, are said to have seen a large disc about 100 feet away and about 100 feet up, wobbling as it moved. Marik von Rennenkampff, a guest on the show, gives this as a short summary without naming his source, in an episode where Michels challenges the skeptic Mick West to a debate. He offers it as a case with several credible witnesses, police among them, seeing a craft up close.
exodus-details-written-by-someone-living: The details in the Exodus story, the Bible's account of the Israelites leaving Egypt, could only have been written by someone living in Egypt at that time. The researcher Luke Caverns makes this argument himself, without naming a source. If true, it would mean the story is an eyewitness-era record and not a later invention.
exodus-thrusters-weigh-less-on-a-scale-p: A NASA engineer named Charles Buhler, who works with a company called Exodus Propulsion, says the company's thrusters make objects lighter on a scale. In his words, "we put stuff on a scale and we turn it on, it gets lighter," and when it is flipped over, "it gets heavier." He says the work is going through peer review and a second patent application, which if it holds up would mean a working form of propulsion without fuel, close to antigravity.
exoprobe-telescope-network-to-find-and-r: The astronomer Beatriz Villarroel describes ExoProbe, her plan for a network of telescopes in New Mexico to search for an extraterrestrial probe, an alien-made device, in space near Earth. She says the hope is to then "pick up the object and bring it down to the earth", because she would like to bring down an actual alien probe. She speaks of it as her own project, which would give physical proof of alien visitors if it worked.
exorcist-boy-became-aerospace-engineer-a: The boy whose 1949 case was the basis for the film The Exorcist later grew up to become an aerospace engineer, and after his exorcism he urinated excessively. This comes from a religious studies scholar named Diana Pasulka, who passes on what she was told about the boy "who then turned out to be like an aerospace engineer." She tells it as one of the odd places where religion and UFO stories cross.
experiencers-account-of-breeding-experim: People who say they have met non-human beings, often called experiencers, describe those beings as running breeding experiments on humans for unknown reasons and passing on messages about the Earth's ecology. An engineer named Bob McGwier relays this, stressing that it is their story, not his. If true, it would mean someone is reshaping humans and trying to warn us about the planet.
experiment-current-induced-in-one-stone-: When voltage is induced and electric current sent into one stone of the kind used in ancient building, it is said to arc across into the next stone. Geoffrey Drumm, a researcher who argues that the pyramids were built to work as machines, says he and his team showed this by experiment, and in one telling he credits a collaborator named Ben. He tells it as evidence that the stones of ancient monuments could have carried electricity.
expired-first-patent-and-a-new-second-pa: The researcher Filippo Biondi, whose work is behind claims that a huge hidden energy grid lies beneath the pyramids of Egypt, admits that his first US patent has expired and says he now has a second one. He answers this himself, first-hand, after Flint Dibble raised the point in a video criticising him: "Yes, my initial patent at the moment is expired." The question matters because the patents are part of how Biondi's method is judged.
explorer-1-launched-on-imbolc-1958: Explorer 1, the first American satellite, was launched on January 31, 1958, a date Michels ties to Imbolc, an old Celtic festival held at the start of February. Michels tells this himself in an episode about pagan ritual in the space program. He notes that the satellite was built by JPL, a rocket laboratory in California, and suggests the timing was chosen to match the old calendar.
extended-state-dmt-trials-yield-encounte: In the 2020s, studies at Imperial College London and the University of California San Diego kept volunteers on DMT, a powerful psychedelic, for longer stretches than usual, and those volunteers are said to come back reporting meetings with thinking beings. The writer Graham Hancock describes these trials without naming a source, saying the volunteers "are all coming back with reports of encounters with sentient others," and ties them to the neuroscientist Andrew Gallimore and the researcher Rick Strassman. If true, it would suggest the drug opens onto a realm where other minds can be met.
extraction-shaft-under-the-queen-s-chamb: A shaft beneath the Queen's Chamber, one of the inner rooms of the Great Pyramid at Giza in Egypt, was part of a system of extraction shafts used to drain a "product solution" out of the pyramid. That is the theory of Jeffrey Drum, a researcher who says he has shown this in his own book. If right, it would mean the pyramid was a working plant that made something, not only a tomb.
extradition-fight-and-we-want-to-see-him: While Britain was deciding in the 2000s whether to send him to the United States for trial, Gary McKinnon, a hacker who says he found signs of a secret NASA space program, says an attaché at the US embassy in London, Ed Gibson, met his lawyer and said, "We want to see him fry." McKinnon takes it as a reference to the electric chair. He tells it to show how harshly he says the US wanted to punish him.
extraterrestrial-being-interviewed-behin: Sometime in the 1950s or 60s, a group was said to be taken to S4, a secret site linked to Area 51, the restricted Air Force base in Nevada. They went down several floors to a big room with a two-way mirror, and on the other side was a being from another world, which they interviewed. The lawyer Dan Sheehan tells Michels this, passing on what a man named Albert Stein told him, and he mentions card files kept from those S4 interviews.
eyewitness-accounts-of-nazi-nuclear-test: The claim is that near the end of the Second World War, around 1944 and 1945, Nazi Germany carried out what looked like nuclear tests, and that a second eyewitness describes one near the Thuringian Forest in central Germany. The researcher Jason Jorjani, who says he found Hitler's secret UFO program, sums this up himself. He relies on the book Critical Mass and on writers named Plimpton Hydrick and Farrell. If true, Germany would have tested nuclear devices before the American bomb.
ezekiel-s-visitors-appear-as-wheels-cove: In the Book of Ezekiel, part of the Bible, the prophet Ezekiel, living in Babylon, describes visitors who arrive as "interlocking wheels covered in eyes, wrapped in fire and storm". Michels retells the passage himself as a possible ancient description of encounters like those people report today.
f-86s-scrambled-to-chase-objects-away-fr: At Ellsworth, an Air Force base in South Dakota, F-86 fighter jets were sent up at least once or twice to chase unknown objects away from the runway and the pad where alert aircraft stood ready. Mario Woods, a former nuclear base guard, says this, passing on what he heard from a man named Chris Leato and adding that he thinks there are several reports of it. It is told to show that the objects were seen as a real threat near nuclear forces.
f-e-warren-missile-outage-blamed-on-a-ti: Michels says that in 2010 the nuclear missiles at F.E. Warren Air Force Base in Wyoming went offline for about an hour, 59 minutes by one account, and that staff on site linked the outage to an object flying in the local airspace, a Tic Tac, meaning a white oval shaped like the mint, though in one telling he calls it cigar-shaped. He credits the researcher Robert Hastings, author of the book UFOs and Nukes, who he says heard it through retired and serving missile technicians, as well as a Wired magazine article and a man named John Mills, and he adds that President Barack Obama was briefed. He pairs it with a 1967 case at Malmstrom in Montana as signs that unknown objects take an interest in nuclear weapons.
f-e-warren-witnesses-flagged-as-security: In the spring of 2011, airmen who had witnessed UFO events at F.E. Warren Air Force Base, a nuclear missile base in Wyoming, were each told during their exit interview from the Air Force that a note was being put in their files calling them a security risk. Robert Hastings, a researcher who studies UFOs seen near nuclear bases, tells this from what a witness named John Mills told him. He tells it as a sign that the Air Force wanted these witnesses kept quiet.
f-lee-bailey-on-the-cia-s-index-4-during: In 1973, during the Watergate scandal, the famous defense lawyer F. Lee Bailey was secretly on the CIA's "Index 4," according to the lawyer Dan Sheehan, who says he was close to the case of James McCord, one of the Watergate burglars. Sheehan says Bailey was one of four attorneys the CIA kept on retainer, which would mean the agency had a hand in McCord's defense. In one telling he says he learned this himself, and in another he credits two men, Andy Toney and William Johnstone Taylor, as his sources.
faa-supervisor-tracks-five-unknowns-near: Robert Hastings, a researcher who later wrote a book about UFOs at nuclear weapons sites, says that as a teenager working as a janitor at Malmstrom, a nuclear missile base in Montana where his father was stationed, he was called over to a radar screen and shown five "unknowns", the formal term for unidentified objects. He tells it firsthand, saying he saw "five blips in the sort of northeast quadrant" of the radar scope, and dates it to March 1967. Michels repeats it often as the start of Hastings's research, sometimes calling the man an air traffic supervisor from the FAA, the US agency that runs air traffic control, and sometimes a radar operator who took the 16-year-old under his wing.
fabio-furtado-sees-object-land-on-his-fa: In 1996 a strange object came down so low over a farm near Varginha, Brazil, that it seemed to be right over the farmer's house, according to the farmer, Fabio Furtado. The documentary filmmaker James Fox passes this on from talking with Furtado. It is one more witness who puts a craft over the area during the Varginha events that year.
face-and-five-sided-pyramid-at-cydonia-m: On a part of Mars called Cydonia Mensa there is a formation that looks like a face, and about five miles from it a five-sided pyramid, according to the physicist Dr. John Brandenburg, who sums this up from images dated to 1976 without naming a particular source. He says NASA, the US space agency, never shows the face and the pyramid side by side in its public photos "because it becomes obvious." If he is right, it would point to built structures on Mars and a space agency choosing not to draw attention to them.
facebook-page-leads-to-michael-johnson-2: In 2026 a fan of the show named Jason Miller sent the team a Facebook page that led them to Michael Johnson, a man in his seventies living in South Carolina. Michels tells this in an episode about Air Force veterans who say they were taken by aliens and who reunite 50 years later, as the way the show tracked Johnson down.
fail-safe-and-human-obsolescence-1963: The philosopher James Madden tells Michels about Fail-Safe, a film based on a novel of the same name, which he dates to around 1963 or 1964. He ties the story to the philosopher Günther Anders's idea that humans are becoming obsolete beside the machines they build. He brings it up as an early warning about people losing control to their own technology.
failing-cia-polygraphs-because-he-knew-t: A senior officer of the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency, says the agency at one point grew so paranoid that he could no longer pass a polygraph, the lie detector test officers must take. The officer, Rolf Mowatt-Larssen, tells this about himself, linking it to how much he knew. It suggests that knowing too much could itself make someone look suspect inside the agency.
fake-darpa-guest-exposed-by-an-email-fro: A guest named Michael, who claimed to be from DARPA, the US military's agency for advanced research, turned out never to have worked there. Jay Anderson, who had him on his own show, says DARPA's security manager emailed him after seeing the video: "I'm really sorry to email you, but we've just seen your video and this guy has never worked for DARPA." Anderson tells it firsthand as a warning about guests who claim inside credentials.
fake-military-ufo-letter-used-to-test-bi: Around 1979, the UFO researcher Bill Moore was tested with a fake military letter about UFOs, sent first to APRO, a civilian group that studied UFO reports, which passed it to him and told him to check it out. The writer Greg Bishop tells this, relaying what Moore himself said. It is told as the start of Moore being drawn into games played by people inside the military.
fake-videos-offered-to-james-fox: A documentary filmmaker named James Fox, who looks into UFO cases, has been offered many videos for sale that turned out not to be real. A Brazilian surgeon named Italo Venturelli tells Michels this, passing on what he knows of Fox's work in Brazil. He mentions it to show how much fake material circulates around such cases.
faked-gemini-spacewalk-photo-of-michael-: A photo said to show the astronaut Michael Collins on a spacewalk during Gemini, NASA's two-man spaceflight programme of the 1960s, is, in Jesse Michels's words, "verifiably fake." Michels says this himself in a conversation, calling it the Gemini 15 photo and crediting his guest with having pointed it out, as a sign that official space imagery cannot always be taken at face value.
falcon-and-the-mj-12-films-from-dia-humi: In the 1980s, a man known only as Falcon is said to have passed undeveloped film of the Majestic 12 papers, documents describing a secret UFO committee, to the TV producer Jaime Shandera and the researcher Bill Moore. The physicist Eric W. Davis tells this as a researcher, without naming his source. He says Falcon was an officer of the Defense Intelligence Agency, the US military's spy agency, sent to deal with the two men. He says the documents came from the "chop shop" of James Jesus Angleton, the CIA's mole hunter, which he calls a "document production factory". The researcher UAPGerb tells a simpler version. He says the papers first arrived in 1984 in a film canister sent to Shandera, and that they included a briefing paper for President Eisenhower. UAPGerb does not mention Falcon, the spy agency or Angleton. If Davis is right, the famous papers would have been made inside the intelligence world.
falcon-space-biefeld-brown-vacuum-test-r: In a test by a group called Falcon Space of the Biefeld-Brown effect, the claim that a high-voltage device can push itself along without a normal exhaust, a device in a sealed chamber spun one way, and then spun the other way as more and more air was pumped out. A researcher named David describes the test without naming a source, and mentions the writer Tim Ventura and a man named Mark in connection with it. The reversal matters because, if the push came only from moving air, it should simply fade in a near vacuum rather than change direction.
falsified-evidence-aimed-at-a-treason-de: Dylan Borland, a man who has come forward with claims about secret government UFO programmes, says that in 2025 someone falsified evidence to get him sentenced to death for treason and to bring espionage charges against others. He tells it as something done to him, in the words "they falsified evidence for me to go and get a death penalty for treason," and mentions the whistleblower David Grusch, a former intelligence officer, in the same account.
families-selected-for-the-program-by-dem: In the 1960s, families for a secret programme were picked partly by demographics, because planners knew a certain share of their children would want to join the military. Dan Sherman, a former Air Force sergeant, says an officer he calls Captain White told him this. If true, it would mean the programme was planned across generations, with children steered into military service.
faraday-cage-test-at-the-monroe-institut: Chris Bledsoe, a man who says UFOs show up around him and whom scientists have studied, says that in 2025 at the Monroe Institute in Virginia, a centre that studies the mind and consciousness, he was taken to the basement of the lab and put inside a Faraday cage, a metal enclosure that blocks outside radio and electrical signals. He tells it as something he went through himself, and mentions the retired Army officer John B. Alexander, the businessman Brandon Fugal and a Dr. Thompson in connection with the work. The point of such a test is to see what happens around him when all outside signals are shut out.
faraday-finds-that-magnetic-fields-chang: The scientist Michael Faraday is said to have found, through his experiments, that magnetic fields change the polarization of light, meaning the direction in which light waves vibrate. The scientist Rupert Sheldrake mentions this in passing, without naming a source. He brings it up as an example of a link between magnetism and light that experiment uncovered.
farmington-armada-1950: In 1950, the story goes, half the town of Farmington, New Mexico watched hundreds of silver discs swarm across the sky, an event later known as the Farmington Armada. Michels tells it himself, without naming a source, as part of a tour of the region. A witness who is not named, and who says they saw it, gives a slightly different picture: "The first day there were a few. The second day there were too many to count." So the witness describes it over two days, a handful of objects at first and then a sky full of them. The story matters to those who tell it because, if true, a whole town saw a mass of unknown craft at once.
farouk-el-baz-the-king-of-apollo-site-se: Farouk El-Baz, a scientist who oversaw moon science planning for NASA in the 1960s and helped choose where the Apollo missions to the moon would land, was nicknamed "the king" by the astronauts. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, and adds that El-Baz's father was a scholar of Egyptian religion. He raises it in an episode about pagan ritual and secret science at NASA, as a hint of ancient religion near the heart of the moon programme.
fascist-elite-preparing-a-thousand-year-: The claim is that the hundred years from 1945 to 2045 are a period of preparation, in which a fascist elite gets ready for a "thousand-year Reich", the never-ending empire Nazi Germany promised. The writer Jason Jorjani offers this as his own hypothesis. If true, Nazism did not end in 1945 but went quiet while it laid plans.
fast-walkers-code-word-for-ufos-in-space: The US military has its own name for unidentified objects moving in space: "fast walkers," according to the researcher Maaneli Derakhshani. He says the term is used by the US Space Force, by NORTHCOM (the military command that defends North America) and by NORAD (the joint US and Canadian air and space defence command), and he gives it without naming a source. If true, it would mean the military tracks such objects often enough to need a word for them.
fast-walkers-exempt-from-foia-defense-su: "Fast walkers", the name for fast-moving objects picked up by US military early-warning satellites high above the Earth, are said to be off limits to this day under the Freedom of Information Act, a US law that lets anyone request government records. Michels tells this himself and says a records researcher named John Greenewald Jr. tried to get such files and could not. If true, it would mean the government keeps these satellite sightings unusually secret.
fast-walkers-in-the-wikileaks-email-betw: An email published by Wikileaks, a website that puts out leaked documents, is said to show a man named Bob Fish writing to John Podesta, whose emails were in the leak, about "fast walkers", a term Michels ties to objects up near geostationary orbit, the high orbit where satellites hang over one spot. Michels brings this up himself on several episodes, without giving a source beyond the leak. He calls Fish an aerospace contractor who he thinks might have worked at a company called Aerospace Corporation in El Segundo, California, though once he calls him an IT contractor, and he dates the email to around 2015 or 2016. He raises it as a sign that UFO matters reached people close to the top of American politics.
fatal-aircraft-mishap-and-four-lost-hour: Greg Rogers, a doctor who served with a military unit called the Third Attack Battalion, says that while the unit was out in the field one of its pilots died in an aircraft accident. He tells it as something he went through himself, and links it to four hours that went missing and could not be accounted for.
father-k-takes-tyler-under-his-wing-in-r: On a visit to the Vatican around 2017, a priest known as Father K is said to have walked up to a man called Tyler, struck up a conversation, and at once decided to take him under his wing. The religion scholar Diana Pasulka, who studies beliefs about UFOs and was there on the trip, tells it as something she saw. She tells it as one of the odd, seemingly guided meetings that tie the Church to her research into UFOs and faith.
father-peter-rinaldi-s-meeting-on-the-sh: Sometime in the 1970s in New York, a priest named Father Peter Rinaldi, who knew the writer Whitley Strieber's wife Anne Strieber, called her and invited the couple to a meeting about the Shroud of Turin, a linen cloth said to carry the image of a crucified man. Strieber tells it as something that happened to him, as one of the odd turns that pulled him toward mysteries beyond ordinary life.
father-s-cylindrical-ufo-sighting: A cylinder-shaped UFO with a red light on its front was once seen over central California, according to the father of Steve Colbern, a scientist who studies objects said to be alien implants. Colbern tells it second-hand, as something his father told him he saw one time.
father-s-generation-called-ufos-at-nucle: In the 1950s and 60s, the people who worked on nuclear weapons tests saw unknown objects at the test sites and called them "tagalongs." The economist Pippa Malmgren says this, passing on what her father told her: "Dad said, yeah, we called it a tag along." If true, it would mean such sightings were common enough at nuclear tests to have a nickname.
father-s-racehorse-fixing-overheard-as-a: As a boy in the early 1970s, playing in the living room of the family home on Long Island, Bob Lazar says he overheard his father and other men deciding who was going to win a horse race. Lazar, best known for saying he worked on alien craft in Nevada, tells this as his own childhood memory of the races being fixed.
father-s-ship-crew-sees-an-object-leave-: An entire ship's crew of 29 or 30 men once watched something come up out of the ocean, rise into the sky and shoot away. Mario Woods, a former guard at a nuclear site, says his father, who is from Honduras and claims to have seen many strange things in the jungle and at sea, used to tell him this story often. It is told as one more account of objects that move between water and air.
fathers-of-the-space-programs-thought-th: The founders of the great space programmes all believed they were in touch with non-human beings: Jack Parsons, who founded the Jet Propulsion Laboratory, the American rocket lab, Konstantin Tsiolkovsky in Russia, and Wernher von Braun in Germany. Michels says this on several episodes, once crediting the religion scholar Diana Pasulka. Another time he softens it to Parsons only "implying" such contact, and on a third he names the German rocket pioneer Hermann Oberth and says Tsiolkovsky thought the beings were angels, which would mean space flight began partly as a spiritual quest.
fbi-agent-guy-hottel-investigates-condon: In the early 1950s an FBI field agent in Washington named Guy Hottel is said to have been building a dossier on the physicist Edward Condon, and Condon then lost his security clearance, which Michels calls "mysterious" and dates to 1953. Michels tells this himself across three episodes; in one he ties the loss to J. Robert Oppenheimer, the physicist who led the atomic bomb work, and to the Los Alamos Primer, the early lecture notes on how to build the bomb, rather than to Hottel's file.
fbi-briefing-to-congress-and-ongoing-fbi: A briefing that the FBI, the US federal police, gave to members of Congress in 2025 is said to have stunned the people who heard it. The FBI is also said to be running an ongoing investigation tied to a hidden government programme believed to hold UFO material. The Australian investigative journalist Ross Coulthart passes this on as something he was told. He urges people to keep an eye on the investigation and says he has dealt with some of the people on its team, which would mean federal police are now looking into the matter themselves.
fbi-calls-brigham-young-its-top-recruiti: The FBI, the US federal police and domestic intelligence agency, is said to have described Brigham Young University in Utah as its top source of recruits. The analyst Matthew Pines says this in passing, without naming where he heard it, as an example of which places feed people into the US security world.
fbi-document-calling-brown-the-navy-s-le: A file kept by the FBI, the US federal police agency, is said to describe the inventor Thomas Townsend Brown, known for work on what he hoped was antigravity, as knowing more about radar than anyone in the US Navy. Michels tells it himself in many episodes. He dates the file to the 1940s, at times to 1942 or 1943, and credits the researcher Paul Schatzkin with recently bringing it to light. In some tellings he adds that Brown's work made it into the B-2 stealth bomber and that the file says Brown was in charge of the Philadelphia Experiment, a rumoured wartime Navy test to make a ship invisible. He tells it to show that Brown was taken seriously at the very top of military science.
fbi-documents-tracking-puharich-s-moveme: Between 1970 and 1973, the FBI, America's federal police and domestic intelligence agency, is said to have kept close watch on a scientist named Andrija Puharich while he was in Israel, tracking all of his movements there. A researcher named Greg Malatzi says this on the show. He says the only thing his team could get was "this big chunk of FBI documents," obtained under the Freedom of Information Act, a US law that lets anyone request government records. If so, it would mean the government took a serious interest in what Puharich was doing abroad.
fbi-image-cheapening-of-jean-seberg-1970: Around 1970 the FBI, the US federal police, is said to have planted a false story in the Los Angeles Times, through the gossip columnist Joyce Haber, claiming that the Hollywood actress Jean Seberg's unborn baby was not her French husband's but a Black Panther activist's. A mathematician named Eric Weinstein tells this as the famous case of what the FBI called image cheapening, a way of ruining someone's reputation. He brings it up to show that agencies have used such tactics to discredit people.
fbi-memo-to-hoover-on-discs-and-balls-of: In 1949, according to Michels, a memo, now public, went to J. Edgar Hoover, director of the FBI, the US federal police, reporting "flying discs, flying saucers, and balls of fire" that were "considered Top Secret by Intelligence Officers of both the Army and Air Force," in connection with the Los Alamos nuclear weapons laboratory in New Mexico. Michels raises it as early evidence that UFOs were drawn to nuclear sites, and mentions it again in a later episode only as an FBI document on the link between UFOs and nuclear weapons.
fbi-records-on-karl-compton-destroyed-fo: The FBI's files on the physicist Karl Compton were destroyed, according to a reply from April 2014 to a request made by the records researcher John Greenewald Jr. under FOIA, a US law that lets anyone ask for government records. Michels reads out the reply himself: "records which may have been responsive to your request were destroyed August 30th, 2006." He raises it because Compton's records might have shed light on secret work tied to UFO material, and that trail now ends.
fbi-seizes-tesla-s-papers-after-his-deat: After the inventor Nikola Tesla died in 1943 at the New Yorker Hotel in New York, the FBI, the US federal police agency, is said to have come in, taken large numbers of his files and made them secret. Kurt McConnell, a former US Senate staffer, says that 'various accounts' tell it this way, without naming them. He raises it to suggest that some of Tesla's technology is still kept secret by the government.
fbi-von-braun-sent-classified-documents-: FBI documents, records of the US federal police agency, are said to show that the German rocket engineer Wernher von Braun was once caught sending classified documents to his former Nazi colleagues working in the Soviet Union, and that no disciplinary action seems ever to have been taken. Michels tells this himself in an episode about NASA, crediting it to those FBI files without quoting them. If true, it would suggest von Braun was protected from the usual consequences.
