fdr-letters-showing-awareness-of-the-phe: President Franklin D. Roosevelt, who led the United States through the 1940s, is said to have made statements or written letters showing he knew about UFOs. The researcher Richard Dolan says this on Michels' show, adding "I believe". He ties it to a set of papers known as the Majestic documents and names no other source. If true, it would mean the phenomenon reached the White House before the famous sightings of the late 1940s.
fdr-on-financial-interests-owning-americ: Franklin D. Roosevelt, the American president of the 1930s, is said to have written that financial interests had owned America since the days of Andrew Jackson, a president of a century earlier. The researcher Jason Simosa brings this up on the show. He says it came from "a conversation or letter" Roosevelt wrote, without naming the document or its date, and offers it as a hint that hidden money has long steered the country.
fdr-s-1937-desert-game-range-guarded-by-: The Desert Game Range in Nevada, around Sheep Peak, was set up under President Franklin D. Roosevelt in 1937, and was guarded by anti-aircraft guns, supposedly to protect the bighorn sheep. Charles Hall, a former military weatherman who says he spent three years with tall alien beings in that desert, tells it on the show and in his book Millennial Hospitality, citing park rangers. He takes it as a sign that the land was being guarded for some other reason.
fdr-s-foreknowledge-of-pearl-harbor-1941: The lawyer Dan Sheehan says that on the night before the Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor, Hawaii, on December 7, 1941, President Franklin D. Roosevelt sent a personal order for all the aircraft carriers to leave the harbor under cover of darkness. Sheehan passes this on as something he was told. If true, it would mean Roosevelt knew the attack was coming.
fdr-s-vatican-communications-via-envoy-m: President Franklin D. Roosevelt handled secret talks with the Vatican about a craft said to have crashed in Magenta, Italy, using his envoy to the Pope, Myron Taylor. Michels tells this himself, in his episode with Harald Malmgren, a former presidential advisor who says he handled UFO material. If true, the US and the Catholic Church would have been sharing knowledge of a crashed craft before the 1950s.
february-2026-white-sands-event-and-el-p: Something is said to have happened in February 2026 at White Sands, a military testing range in New Mexico, around the time the airspace over nearby El Paso, Texas was closed. Michels raises it only as a question, "what happened at White Sands in February of 2026?", which he puts to his guest Matthew Brown, described as a Pentagon whistleblower. Nothing more of the event is given.
february-event-a-tic-tac-uses-hills-to-h: At a February 2025 field event run by Skywatcher, a private company that tries to call in UFOs, an object shaped like a Tic Tac (a white oval, like the mint) is said to have used the hills to hide from the team's sensors. James Valor, a team member who was there, says this "object of the 2nd class" behaved in a way never seen before: "He actually used hills to hide from us and disappear from our main sensors." Another Skywatcher member who was there adds that on the fifth day the interference with their equipment went on for two hours. That member says an object shaped like a manta ray also hid behind the terrain, and credits a teammate named Jordan Jose. To the team, it suggests the objects know they are being watched and act on it.
feds-ransack-chuck-clark-s-place-1990: In the 1990s, federal agents ransacked the home of a man named Chuck Clark in Rachel, Nevada, the tiny town near the secret Area 51 air base. The documentary filmmaker James Fox tells this, naming the journalist George Knapp and Clark himself as his sources. It is told as a sign that the government was pressing people who watched the area.
felipe-vidal-santiago-and-the-umbrella-m: A Cuban exile named Felipe Vidal Santiago can be seen on the grassy knoll, the small slope in Dealey Plaza, Dallas, where President John F. Kennedy was shot in 1963, and he is tied to the so-called umbrella man standing there, according to the researcher Dan Sheehan. Sheehan says this without naming a source, telling Michels, "you see Felipe Vidal Santiago on the Grassy Knoll," and points to the House Select Committee, the congressional panel that looked again at the killing in the 1970s. He tells it as evidence that more people were involved in the shooting than the official account allows.
fellow-marine-refuses-to-come-forward-te: A fellow Marine who could back up Michael Herrera's story turned him down by text message, writing, "My family and military career far exceed anything you are asking of me." Herrera is a former Marine who says he saw a 300-foot UFO in the Indonesian jungle. Michels reads the texts himself on the episode with Herrera, as a sign of how hard it is to get other witnesses to speak.
felt-his-body-turn-to-stone-while-linked: Jordan Jose, a man who says he was taken into a secret UFO programme as a child, says that at an undisclosed place near directed energy weapons, which fire beams of energy rather than bullets, he was somehow linked to a craft when it was shot. He says that in that moment "it felt as if my body was actually turning to stone." He tells it as his own experience, which would mean people were being connected to craft as part of the programme.
felt-the-virgin-mary-s-presence-and-guid: In Portugal in 1998, a man says he felt the presence of the Virgin Mary, sensing her mind and thoughts though he had never met her. The man, Rolf Mowatt-Larssen, a former senior officer of the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency, tells it as his own experience and ties it to other things that happened to him. If true, it would be a personal spiritual contact of the kind he links to his wider strange experiences.
few-physicists-in-the-crash-retrieval-pr: A secret US program to recover crashed craft is said to have had very few physicists working on it. A NASA engineer named Charles Buhler brings this up, pointing out to Michels that Michels' own previous interview had made the point. If true, it would suggest the program lacked the scientists needed to understand what it found.
fewer-than-40-recovered-crashes-1930: The United States holds fewer than 40 crashed craft that are not of human make, according to Eric W. Davis, a physicist who has worked on Pentagon UFO studies, who says he knows the exact figure but it is classified. Michels later repeats it, crediting Davis or the physicist Hal Puthoff, as 10 to 40 craft kept in hangars across the country. If true, it would mean the government has quietly gathered dozens of such objects.
feynman-and-wheeler-s-1945-paper-on-time: In 1945 the physicists Richard Feynman and John Wheeler wrote a key paper on electromagnetism in which influences could run backward as well as forward in time. The biologist Rupert Sheldrake brings it up in passing, without naming the paper, as part of a theory he is laying out. He uses it to suggest that mainstream physics has already allowed for effects that do not only move forward in time.
feynman-s-any-questions-teaching-at-a-bu: The physicist Richard Feynman told a story called "Any Questions?" about having to travel to Buffalo, New York, while a physics professor at Cornell University, to teach at an aerospace company. A researcher named Eric Weinstein brings it up from Feynman's memoir books, Surely You're Joking, Mr. Feynman! and What Do You Care What Other People Think?, and ties it to patents Feynman held on nuclear technology. To Weinstein it shows how closely top physicists were tied to military industry.
ffrdc-spun-off-from-trw-as-principal-con: A single government-funded research center, run outside the government on its behalf, is said to have been the main contractor on work tied to recovered unknown technology for about 29 years, starting in the 1960s. The physicist Eric W. Davis passes this on from what he was told. He says the outfit started as a contractor not long after it was born, that it was a spin-off of TRW, an American defense and aerospace company, and that he will not name it. If true, one quiet organization would have held this work for nearly three decades.
fighter-jet-scrambled-and-possibly-fired: In 1952, when glowing lights were reported over Washington DC, an F-105 fighter jet was supposedly sent up to intercept them, and by one account its pilots may have been told to fire and may even have hit one. A former Pentagon official named Luis Elizondo repeats this from discussions he heard about the event, not as something he saw himself. If true, it would mean the military fired on unknown objects over the capital.
fighter-pilot-from-chile-meets-an-object: In the 1980s, a fighter pilot flying from Chile to Brazil is said to have met an object measured at 25,000 kilometres an hour, far faster than any known aircraft. The story is told by Aldo Rebelo, a former defense minister of Brazil, as one of the cases from his country he holds to be real.
fii-nocontract-marking-used-to-hide-ufo-: A records marking called FII NOCONTRACT is said to be a security tool used by the Department of Energy and its nuclear weapons arm, the National Nuclear Security Administration, to hide UFO programs inside national labs such as Sandia, Lawrence Livermore, Los Alamos and Oak Ridge. A researcher who goes by the online name UAPGerb puts this forward as his own belief, drawing on the UAP Disclosure Act, a proposed law on releasing government records about unidentified flying objects. If right, it would show where secret UFO work is kept.
files-show-george-joannides-lied-about-r: An intelligence officer named George Joannides ran a psychological warfare program out of a Miami station known as JM WAVE, and newly released files are said to prove he later lied about his part in it. The researcher Jeremy Riss says this, pointing to the JFK files, the government records on President John F. Kennedy's assassination. He raises it because it would mean an official misled investigators about work tied to the killing.
filippo-and-corrado-conclude-the-structu: Structures found deep beneath the Giza Plateau in Egypt were made by people and are not natural, according to Filippo Biondi, a researcher who studies what lies under the pyramids. Biondi says that he and a colleague he calls only Corrado both looked at the findings and "we agree that it is something that it is man-made." If true, it would mean a large built complex lies hidden under the pyramids.
final-casino-meeting-with-dennis-mariani: In 1989, in a Las Vegas casino, Bob Lazar is said to have had a strange last meeting with a man named Dennis Mariani, who would not look at him and then vanished. Lazar is a man who says he worked on alien spacecraft at a secret site in Nevada, and he tells it himself. He says he kept saying "Dennis, Dennis, I'm here, you know, what do you want?" but Mariani "never even looked up at me". Lazar walked over to his friend Gene Huff, and when they both turned around, "he was gone." A researcher named Luigi Vendittelli tells the same scene as Huff told it to him. In that version Mariani is a blonde, "military-looking guy" and Lazar talks to him while "the guy's not even looking at him." The scene is told as one of the odd moments around the time Lazar says he worked on the craft.
finding-the-tsar-s-submarine-som-and-que: Dennis Asberg, a Swedish treasure hunter who searches for wrecks in the Baltic Sea, says that in 2015 his team found the wreck of Som, a submarine of the Russian Tsar lost in Swedish waters in the early 1900s, working alongside a man named Peter Lindberg. He tells it firsthand, and says the find led to him being questioned in Stockholm by what he calls the Swedish "FBI", the country's security police.
fire-department-captures-screaming-being: In 1996, in the Brazilian town of Varginha, the local fire department is said to have caught a screaming, non-human being with a net, "like they would with a wild animal." The documentary filmmaker James Fox tells this from what witnesses told him during his investigation of the case. If true, it would mean ordinary local rescuers took a living creature into custody.
fireballs-seen-over-washington-dc-in-the: In the 1950s, glowing fireballs were seen flying over Washington DC, and Eric Haseltine says those sightings seem to have some credibility. Haseltine is a former official at the National Security Agency, the US electronic spying agency. He mentions the sightings in passing on Michels's show without naming a source, as one of the older cases he takes seriously.
first-agreements-with-the-tall-whites-sp: In the desert near Indian Springs, Nevada, in the mid-1960s, a young Air Force man says he made agreements with tall, pale beings he calls the tall whites: that when they came near him they would talk between themselves where he could hear, in English, and that he would sing to let them know he was coming. Charles Hall, who says he served there as a weather observer, tells it as his own experience. He tells it as the start of a working relationship with beings who, if he is right, lived beside a US military base.
first-allagash-sighting-sphere-of-light-: In 1976, at the Mud Pond campsite on Chamberlain Lake, along the Allagash Waterway, a wilderness canoe route in Maine, someone in another camping group called out "What the hell is that over there?", and across the lake was a sphere of light moving slowly, like a balloon, but into the wind. Charlie Foltz says he saw it himself, on a trip with a man named Jim Weiner. He tells it as the first of the strange sightings on that trip, which, if true, would point to an object moving under its own power.
first-captain-gives-economic-destabiliza: A former Air Force sergeant named Dan Sherman says that in the early 1990s the National Security Agency, the US government's code-breaking and eavesdropping agency, trained him to communicate with aliens. When he asked his first commanding captain why the whole thing was kept secret, the captain is said to have answered: economic destabilization. Michels retells this from Sherman's own account, which would mean officials feared the news itself would shake the economy.
first-cia-director-on-the-nicap-board-19: Roscoe Hillenkoetter, a Navy admiral who was the first director of the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency, is said to have sat on the board of directors of NICAP, a private civilian group that looked into UFO reports in the 1950s and 60s. The researcher Dylan Borland mentions this without naming a source. He tells it to show that a man from the top of US intelligence took part in a group pressing for answers on UFOs.
first-classified-tour-on-eleuthera-baham: In the 1960s, Joe McMoneagle, who later became an Army psychic spy, says his first classified posting was on Eleuthera, an island in the Bahamas, where the real work was hidden behind a cover story of air-sea rescue. He tells it as part of his own service history.
first-earth-battalion-sergeant-kills-a-g: A sergeant in the First Earth Battalion, an unusual US Army idea for training soldiers in mental and spiritual powers, is said to have killed a goat with his mind, then stolen a helicopter and disappeared. A former Army sergeant named Lyn Buchanan tells the story as it was passed on to him by an Army officer named Jim Channon, and adds that the man who killed the goat "experienced dying with the goat." If true, it would suggest that the mind can kill, and that doing so comes at a cost to the one who does it.
first-exodus-patent-and-a-possible-natio: A NASA engineer named Charles Buhler says the first patent for his company Exodus Propulsion's thruster may have been caught up in a national security review. He points to the Invention Secrecy Act of 1952, a US law that lets the government keep some inventions secret, and says "some patents apparently go through the Department of Defense," which would mean the military takes an interest in this kind of technology.
first-foo-fighter-reports-november-1944: The first reports of what came to be called foo fighters, unexplained objects seen in the sky, date to November 1944. A guest named Marik von Rennenkampff mentions this on Michels's show, marking it as the anniversary of those first reports. He brings it up to show how far back such sightings go.
first-goetheanum-burned-as-a-rival-to-na: The first Goetheanum, a building in Dornach, Switzerland, that served as headquarters for Anthroposophy, the spiritual movement founded by Rudolf Steiner, burned down in the 1920s. The writer Jason Jorjani says the Nazis burned it because they thought Anthroposophy "could really become a rival to Nazism". He tells it to show how seriously the Nazis took competing spiritual movements.
first-h-bomb-and-the-1952-dc-wave: Michels links the testing of the first hydrogen bomb in the Pacific in 1952 to a wave of UFO sightings over Washington, DC, that July. He raises it himself in a 2022 episode on UFOs and nuclear weapons, asking "What happened in 1952?" and answering with the DC sightings. The link would suggest the UFOs were reacting to the new bomb.
first-hypnotic-regression-tall-being-wor: Mario Woods, a former nuclear missile guard who says he was taken aboard a craft near a South Dakota missile site called November 5 in 1977, describes his first hypnotic regression, a session where hypnosis is used to try to bring back lost memories, which involved a man named Bob Upton. He says he recalled beings around him and that "the one that was messing with me was a very tall one." He tells it as his own memory, which if true would fill in what happened during the hours he says he lost.
first-intuitive-communication-received-i: Sometime around 1990, at an overseas base, an Air Force sergeant says he received his first message from non-human beings, picked up through intuition rather than radio, while working inside a communications van. Dan Sherman, who says the National Security Agency, the US agency that intercepts signals, hired him for this work, tells it as his own experience. He says that first message came a while after he started, and that once it did, "the ball started rolling."
first-mobile-phone-ufo-photo-matched-to-: In 2005, at a cottage in northern Sweden, someone took what is called the first mobile-phone photo of a UFO in Sweden, and the object in the picture was later matched to a military radar track. The Swedish UFO researcher Clas Svahn tells this from his own work on the case, though in one telling he puts the object over a lake rather than at the cottage. If the photo and the radar agree, something real was in the sky that night and both a phone and the military picked it up.
first-observation-of-the-force-laser-dis: In 2010, in a laboratory in Florida, a laser test that measures tiny movements showed a force predicted by a theory of his own, says Charles Buhler, an engineer the episode presents as a NASA chief. He was there for it, working with a colleague he calls Nathan and a scientist named Dr. Sid Clemens, and he calls it "the first time I witnessed it." He tells it to Michels as the start of the work he says led to a new kind of propulsion that pushes without throwing anything out the back.
first-peer-reviewed-paper-on-the-khufu-p: Filippo Biondi, a scientist who scans beneath the pyramids with satellite radar, says his team published its first peer-reviewed paper on the Great Pyramid of Khufu at Giza in 2021 or 2022, he does not remember which. The researcher Jeffrey Drum dates the paper to 2020 and gives its title, "Synthetic aperture radar Doppler tomography detects undiscovered high-resolution internal structures of the Great Pyramid of Giza." They raise it to show the radar work was checked by other scientists, which if it holds would give weight to claims of hidden structures inside the pyramid.
first-question-at-eg-g-was-about-john-le: When Bob Lazar sat down for a job interview at EG&G, a government contractor in Las Vegas, in 1988, the very first question he was asked may have been about a man he knew named John Lear. Lazar, who says he was hired that year for secret government work, tells this himself as something he went through. If true, it would mean his interviewers already knew who he spent time with before he walked in.
first-skywatcher-observation-class-1-tet: During a military war game in 2021, a team watching the sky recorded something they later rated as a first class sighting, a formation of objects they call a "tetra". James Valor of Skywatcher, a startup that says it can call up UFOs, tells this as one of their first observations and says he took part, and he mentions a person he calls only Mr. K. If it happened as he says, it would mean unknown objects showed up during a planned military exercise.
first-trip-to-egypt-and-inside-the-pyram: In late 2025, a scientist who studies scans of what lies under the Giza pyramids went to Egypt for the first time and went inside them. That scientist, Filippo Biondi, tells it himself, saying that "two weeks ago I went for the first time in Egypt." It counts because his claims about tunnels and shafts beneath the pyramids came before he had ever stood on the site.
first-ufo-recorded-within-a-week-of-the-: The first UFO ever recorded showed up within seven days of Trinity, the 1945 test of the first atomic bomb in New Mexico. Joe McMoneagle, who worked as an Army psychic spy, makes this claim without naming his source. It is told to suggest that UFOs are drawn to nuclear weapons.
first-videotaped-grusch-interview-at-bry: In 2023 the first filmed interview with David Grusch, a former intelligence officer who went public with claims about secret UFO programmes, was recorded at a house in Los Angeles, says Bryce Zabel, a Hollywood writer and producer who says it was his house and he was there. Zabel tells Michels that Grusch turned up "in cargo shorts and a t-shirt," and he names the Australian journalist Ross Coulthart and a man called Jared among the people involved. He tells it as an inside look at how one of the best-known UFO whistleblowers first went on camera.
first-voice-download-after-high-school-r: A man named Brent Friedman says that just after high school he heard a voice for the first time, and all it told him was "reality is subjective." Friedman tells it as his own experience, and says the message made no sense to him then. He presents it as the first of several messages that came to him this way.
fisherman-sees-an-orb-explode-off-ubatub: In 1957, a fisherman off Ubatuba on the coast of Brazil is said to have watched a glowing ball zigzag through the sky and then blow apart, and he gathered pieces that fell onto the beach and mailed them to a man named Ibrahim Sued. Michels tells it twice: first as one of the samples the Stanford scientist Garry Nolan studies, and later adding the zigzag flight, the mailing and a link to the researcher Jacques Vallée. If true, those fragments would be physical pieces of an unknown flying object.
fitness-beats-truth-theorem-in-evolution: A scientist named Don Hoffman says that he and his colleagues proved a theorem showing that evolution rewards usefulness, not accuracy: in his words, "the probability is zero that any sensory system has ever been shaped to see any true feature of objective reality." He tells it as his own research, built on evolutionary game theory, the mathematics of how strategies compete for survival, which goes back to Darwin and the biologist John Maynard Smith. If he is right, our senses show us a convenient interface rather than the world as it is, and things that are really there, aliens included, could go unseen.
fitts-sees-hud-s-unauditable-books-on-li: When a former official named Katherine Austin Fitz went to look at the accounts of the Department of Housing and Urban Development, the federal agency for housing, staff are said to have wheeled in library carts "one after another", stacked with disorganised papers, books that could not be audited. The UFO historian Richard Dolan tells this on Michels' show, repeating what Fitz told him and citing her work The Myth of the Rule of Law. He tells it to show how government money can vanish without a trace.
fitts-tells-tucker-carlson-the-money-goe: In a television interview, the talk show host Tucker Carlson is said to have asked Katherine Austin Fitz where huge sums of missing government money were going, and she answered: "Space." Michels tells his guest, the writer Richard Dolan, that in the same interview she sent Carlson to Dolan's work, saying "talk to Richard Dolan." Michels recounts this from memory, as support for the idea that hidden money pays for a secret space effort.
fitts-trillions-missing-from-dod-budget-: The claim is that trillions of dollars have gone missing from the budget of the Department of Defense and were quietly spent on secret projects. It comes from a woman named Catherine Austin Fitts, and Michels passes it on himself. An online researcher known as UAPGerb puts a figure on it: Fitts, he says, talks of "17 to 21 trillion" hidden in the secret US budget since the 1990s. The UFO historian Richard Dolan says Fitts told him that his idea of a "breakaway civilization" is "right on." By that he means a hidden group that has broken away from the rest of society, with advanced technology of its own. If true, it would mean huge sums of public money are paying for programs no one voted on.
five-executive-orders-given-to-the-presi: A UFO activist named Steven Greer says that in 2025 he drew up five executive orders, orders a president can sign on his own authority, for the president to sign. He shows them on the show, one page each, and says they are his way of getting the president to open up the government's UFO secrets.
five-transients-appearing-and-vanishing-: On 27 July 1952, five points of light are said to have appeared together in a narrow line on an old photographic plate from the Palomar Observatory in California, then vanished. The astronomer Beatriz Villarroel describes this from her own study of the plates. If they are real, they could be objects in orbit around Earth years before any human satellite.
five-uap-incidents-at-vandenberg-2003-20: Between 2003 and 2005 there were five sightings of UAP, short for unidentified anomalous phenomena, the government's term for UFOs, at Vandenberg Air Force Base in California, according to Jesse Michels. He says this himself, without naming a source, in an episode about a nuclear missile guard. It would mean unknown objects kept showing up at a base tied to missiles.
five-years-of-psychokinesis-experiments-: A research lab spent five years trying to prove psychokinesis, the idea that a mind can move or change physical things, and never managed to pin down what the mind was actually acting on, says Joe McMoneagle, who presents himself as having been part of the work. The episode presents him as a psychic who claims to see distant places with his mind, and he tells Michels "we did five years of experiments to prove psychokinesis." He does not name the lab or give dates.
flames-shoot-from-kuromanta-during-an-ex: During a dig at Kuromanta, a mountain in Akita, Japan, that some people call a pyramid, a thunderstorm broke out and the diggers looked up to see "flames shooting out of the top of the mountain." Geoffrey Drumm, a researcher who has his own theory about what pyramids were built for, tells this from a book on the excavation written by a man named Suzuki. Drumm gives no date for the book or the dig, and he tells it as a sign that the mountain works like a machine powered by energy.
fleeing-a-close-encounters-screening-in-: In 1977, watching the UFO film Close Encounters of the Third Kind at a theater on Main Street in Rapid City, South Dakota, Mario Woods, an Air Force veteran who once guarded nuclear weapons, got up, ran out and sat on the curb, because what he saw on screen "felt as if it was a direct replay" of what he had been through himself. Woods tells this on two episodes as part of his own account of being abducted, and the shorter version leaves out the curb and the replay.
flexner-report-reshapes-american-medicin: The Flexner Report, a study of American medical schools by the educator Abraham Flexner released in 1910, is said to have reshaped American medicine, with backing from the oil tycoon John D. Rockefeller and the steel tycoon Andrew Carnegie. Michels tells it himself, in an episode about the history of the drug industry.
flight-19-and-the-lost-pby-from-banana-r: In 1945 a Navy training flight called Flight 19 was lost off Florida, in the stretch of ocean known as the Bermuda Triangle, along with a PBY, a Navy flying boat, from Banana River Naval Air Station, the base later called Patrick Air Force Base. A former NASA doctor named Greg Rogers brings the story up and says he spoke to some of the men who were working in flight operations that day. He offers their memories as a firsthand link to one of the region's best-known disappearances.
flight-surgeon-gum-exam-burns-and-skin-s: A former Air Force nuclear weapons guard named Mario Woods says that in 1977, at Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota, a flight surgeon (a military doctor) examined him while agents of the Air Force Office of Special Investigations, the service's own investigators, looked on. Woods says the doctor checked his gums, pointed out burns above his right eye and on the back of his right hand, and clipped off a piece of skin, which he sealed in a corked tube and set on a tray. Woods tells this himself, in two separate conversations with Michels, as part of what he describes as an abduction, and if true it would mean the military took a close interest in what happened to him.
flight-with-jake-barber-over-a-lockheed-: A US congressman named Eric Burlison says that on a flight with a man named Jake Barber, they flew over a desert site near Burbank, California, run by Lockheed Martin, a big American aerospace and weapons company. He describes a bowl-shaped dip in the ground with a huge hangar door that looked plainly like the way into an underground building, and says a stream of white vans came racing out while they circled. He tells it as something he saw himself, as a sign of hidden work going on there.
flir-gimbal-and-gofast-navy-videos-2004: Three videos taken during US Navy encounters, known as FLIR (after the infrared camera that filmed it), Gimbal and GoFast, are said to show flying objects that the Pentagon says belong neither to the US nor to its rivals. Karl Nell, a former US Army officer, describes them in an official tone, saying the videos come from events in 2004 and 2015 and that the Pentagon "has asserted are not ours and are not our adversaries." If true, that would mean someone else is flying them.
flir1-object-may-be-a-balloon-2004: The object in FLIR1, a 2004 Navy video taken with a forward-looking infrared camera off Southern California, may simply be a balloon, according to the UFO skeptic Mick West. He makes the case from his own analysis of the footage, saying what it shows "of course suggests that what we're looking at is actually a balloon," while others link the same clip to a white oval object shaped like a Tic Tac mint. If he is right, one of the best-known military UFO videos would have an ordinary explanation.
flir1-video-leaked-on-a-german-server-be: A Navy video known as FLIR1, filmed through a jet's infrared targeting camera and showing an unexplained object, is said to have been online before 2017, posted on the forum site Reddit and even on a German server. Michels says this himself, without naming a source, as a sign the footage was circulating well before it became famous.
flood-dated-up-to-40-000-years-ago-from-: The great flood of ancient Mesopotamian stories could have happened as long as 40,000 years ago, according to a researcher named Matt LaCroix, who tells it without naming a source. He bases this on ice cores, long columns of ice drilled from Greenland and Antarctica that keep a record of past climate, and on earlier climate events that could have caused floods. If true, the flood memory would reach back far beyond the usual timeline of human civilisation.
florida-channel-wakes-up-with-an-unexpla: In the early 1970s a man in Florida who served as a channel, someone said to pass on messages from other beings, woke up to find a metal filling in his tooth that he never had before. A researcher named Greg Malatzi tells this from a book called The Stargate Conspiracy, in an account involving the medium Phyllis Schlemmer and the researcher Andrija Puharich. It is told as a sign that something had been done to the man in his sleep.
florida-coastline-extended-4050-miles-ea: About 14,000 years ago, the Florida coast near Miami is said to have reached 40 or 50 miles farther east than it does today, so where the beach is now there would have been forest. The researcher Randall Carlson says this himself, without naming a source. He tells it to show how much dry land the sea has since covered.
fluttering-leaf-reports-are-ours-1950: UFO reports describing a craft that moves like a fluttering leaf were, according to one man, American aircraft, not alien ones. Jan Lundquist relays this on Michels' documentary about the scientist Townsend Brown: Brown is said to have told a woman named Linda Brown to filter those reports out as she gathered UFO information, because "those are ours". If true, it would mean some sightings in the 1950s were secret US craft.
flying-craft-in-ancient-indian-texts: Ancient Indian sacred writings, such as the Bhagavad Gita and the Vedas, describe flying craft called vimanas, according to the UFO researcher Steven Greer. He agrees with this when it comes up, briefly and without naming a source, as a sign that such craft were known in the distant past.
flying-craft-through-the-mind-for-a-brai: Between 2008 and 2010, at a place called Baker Victory Services in western New York, a boy was used in work on a brain link for flying unidentified craft, because, he says, such craft are "not flown with joysticks. They're flown through the mind." That boy was Jordan Jose, who says a secret UFO program took him as a child, and he tells it from his own experience. If true, it would mean someone was training people to steer these craft by thought.
flying-lotus-attends-the-tridactyl-unvei: The hip hop artist Flying Lotus says he went to a presentation near his Los Angeles home about the "tridactyls," small bodies said to have three fingers and to come from somewhere other than Earth. He tells Michels the bodies themselves were not there: instead "they were showing the photos and the X-rays and all that stuff." He links the event to a man named Jaime Maussan, who put the bodies before the public, and he tells it as part of his own fascination with UFOs.
flying-saucer-observatory-detection-over: In 1954, in Ottawa, Canada, a small station built to detect flying saucers is said to have gone off when something flew right over it. It was part of Project Magnet, a Canadian government study of flying saucers linked to the engineer Wilbert B. Smith, and the story also involves a woman named Frances Swan. The researcher Grant Cameron says it happened a week after it was expected, on the 8th. He talked to one of the men who was in the building at the time, who said "all the bells went off". Cameron ties the episode to the end of Project Magnet.
fmri-study-of-brilliant-moves-in-the-gam: There is said to be a study in which a person's brain was watched in a brain scanner while they played Go, the ancient board game, to see what happens in the mind during a brilliant move. Michels brings it up himself, without naming the study or saying what it found. He mentions it in a talk about the mind and where flashes of insight come from.
foggy-night-encounter-with-a-scout-craft: Charles Hall, a former Air Force man who says he spent three years among tall white beings near Area 51, the secret Nevada test base, says that on a cold, snowy night in the 1960s he nearly died in thick fog in Indian Springs Valley, Nevada. He says a small scout craft flown by a young female being and some of her friends came to him, along with a larger deep-space craft and a craft flown by teenagers. He ties the story to a book, The Valley of the Grays, and tells it as part of his account of living alongside these beings.
foia-releases-of-thousands-of-ufo-pages-: From the 1970s into the early 1980s, requests under the Freedom of Information Act, a US law that lets anyone request government records, are said to have pried loose thousands of pages on UFOs: reports of failed military interceptions, memos from the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency, and investigations by the FBI, the federal police. The researcher Richard Dolan describes this wave of releases himself, without naming a particular source. In his telling, it showed the government had been taking UFOs far more seriously than it admitted.
foia-request-for-usaf-campinas-flight-re: In about 2022, a team led by James Fox asked the US Air Force for records of its flights connected to Campinas, a city in Brazil, starting from 1996. They used the Freedom of Information Act, a US law that lets anyone request government records, and the answer came back from the CIA, not the Air Force. Fox says he took part in this himself. He tells it because the CIA answering a question about Air Force flights suggests that something more than a routine flight happened there.
followed-by-a-12-year-old-tall-white-gir: A former airman named Charles Hall says that in 1965, while walking back to his barracks at Nellis Air Force Base in Nevada, he was followed by a young girl, about 12 years old, from the beings he calls the "tall whites." Hall tells this as his own experience, part of his account of spending three years in contact with tall, pale beings at the base. If true, it would mean these beings moved around freely near the people stationed there.
followed-during-his-clearance-and-told-g: In 1989, while he was being vetted for a security clearance in Las Vegas, Bob Lazar says someone was always parked outside his house, and he got scared and told his friend Gene Huff. Lazar, who says he worked on secret flying craft for the government, tells it himself as part of the story of how he came to go public.
followers-of-horus-secret-societies-pres: In ancient Egypt, groups known as the Followers of Horus were secret societies charged with keeping knowledge from what the Egyptians called the 'First Time', a lost early age, and passing it on to later generations. The writer Graham Hancock, who writes about lost ancient civilisations, sets out this idea, citing his co-author Robert Bauval and their book Talisman. If true, it would mean ancient wisdom was handed down in secret over thousands of years.
following-david-grusch-from-his-testimon: After a UFO whistleblower named David Grusch testified before Congress in 2023, Jesse Michels followed him from Capitol Hill back to Colorado and made a short documentary about him. Michels tells this himself as something he took part in, saying "we have the best time ever" making the film. He dates it a little differently from one telling to the next, once to the end of summer 2023 and once to September 2023.
following-the-second-van-to-noise-cancel: In 1991, near a National Security Agency training site in Linthicum, Maryland, a van he followed led to a company called Noise Cancellation Technology, says Dan Sherman. Sherman, a former Air Force sergeant who says the National Security Agency, the US spy agency for intercepted communications, hired him to talk with aliens, tells Michels he did the following himself. To him it hints at who was behind the program he says he was in.
foo-fighters-and-swedish-ghost-rockets-1: From 1942 to 1945, fighter pilots on both sides of the Second World War reported what looked like controlled balls of lightning, nicknamed foo fighters, and in 1946 Sweden saw its own wave of mystery objects called ghost rockets. Michels tells this himself across several episodes, citing the American air general James Doolittle and the Allied commander Dwight Eisenhower, though he places the lights variously over Europe, over Germany, or in Bavaria where he says they got in the way of Allied flights. He raises them as proof that strange objects were seen long before the modern UFO era.
foo-fighters-drawn-to-wwii-atomic-and-mi: The foo fighters, strange glowing lights that Allied airmen reported over southern Germany in 1944 and 1945, may have been drawn there by the war's atomic and military work, according to a former Pentagon intelligence official named Luis Elizondo. He offers this as his own reasoning, without naming a source: since unexplained craft seem "interested in nuclear capabilities and our military capabilities," he asks what was going on at the height of the war. If true, it would mean the interest in weapons sites goes back before the nuclear age began in earnest.
footage-of-the-varginha-alien-transport-: In 1996, in the town of Varginha in Brazil, a captured creature was reportedly moved from a military base into town and back again, and footage of that trip is said to exist. The UFO investigator James Fox describes this, passing on what he heard from a man named Marco and from a military source he calls "military X". If true, it would be filmed evidence of the Brazilian military moving a living non-human being.
football-field-sized-vehicles-moving-thr: Craft as big as a football field are said to be moving through the world's oceans at 500 knots, a speed far beyond any known submarine. The comedian and podcast host Joe Rogan repeats this on the show, crediting Marco Rubio, a senior US politician, who says it in a documentary film called The Age of Disclosure. The magician and YouTuber Chris Ramsay tells it differently. He credits Lue Elizondo, a former Pentagon official who ran a small office that studied unexplained aerial reports, with mentioning a giant underwater thing moving at 500 knots. Ramsay links it to an anonymous poster on 4chan, an online message board, known as the "4chan whistleblower", who he says described the same thing. Ramsay gives no size for the object. If true, it would mean huge unknown vehicles move under the sea faster than anything humans have built.
force-fields-bending-light-seen-in-the-n: Charles Hall, who says he spent three years with tall white aliens at Area 51, a secret US Air Force site in Nevada, says the force fields around such craft bend light, and that you can see this in the Navy's 2004 Tic Tac video, footage taken by Navy pilots of a white oval object shaped like the mint. He offers it as his own reading of the footage, which if true would tie the Navy video to the craft he says he knew.
ford-chooses-nazi-trucks-over-uk-engines: The Ford motor company once turned down a British request for engines because it was putting trucks for Nazi Germany first, according to the researcher Jason Simosa. He tells it without naming a source, quoting Ford as saying, "No, we're not going to do that. We're prioritizing the trucks for Nazi Germany." He raises it to show how closely a major American company was tied to the Nazi war effort.
ford-s-new-nsa-intelligence-system-1974: A former presidential advisor named Harald Malmgren says that in 1974 at the White House, President Gerald Ford asked him to arrange a new intelligence system with the National Security Agency, the US agency that intercepts and analyses communications. Malmgren tells this as something he was personally asked to do. If true, it would place him inside the president's intelligence planning at that time.
foreign-intelligence-attempts-to-penetra: Matthew Brown, who is described as a Pentagon whistleblower, says he has had moments that felt like foreign spies trying to break into his circle of contacts to pull information out of it and to send him threats. He tells it from his own experience, without saying when or where, as a sign of how much interest his work draws.
foreign-men-offer-luiza-cash-in-dollars-: A woman named Luiza, one of the people tied to the 1996 sightings of a strange creature in Varginha, Brazil, is said to have been offered money by foreign men to take back her story, cash in "American dollars in a briefcase." The documentary filmmaker James Fox passes this on from Luiza's own account. If true, it would mean someone from outside Brazil was working to silence the witnesses.
forensic-pathologists-with-physical-evid: In the Brazilian town of Varginha in 1996, a military police soldier named Marco Chereze is said to have grabbed a strange living creature and died weeks later, and doctors now say his autopsy turned up a very unusual bacteria. The documentary filmmaker James Fox, who has spent years investigating the Varginha case, told Michels in 2024 that two forensic pathologists, doctors who examine the dead to find the cause of death, had just come forward to him. Michels himself names the autopsy report on Chereze and says it shows bacteria in a soldier who died because he basically grabbed an alien being. He credits two doctors, one he calls Dr. Janini and one he calls Dr. Armando. That second doctor, Armando Fortunato, who performed the autopsy, came on the show and passed on what Dr. Janini had said only last year. In Fortunato's words, Janini said the bacteria from the lab samples was "not common in our country", was "extremely virulent" and fast-moving, and that he "did not rule out" that it "could be an alien bacterium." If that were so, it would be physical, medical evidence that a soldier touched something not from Earth.
formation-of-skywatcher-technologies-202: In 2025 a group of people who say they worked with a secret UFO program started a private company called Skywatcher Technologies. They say its aim is to call in unknown craft and record them. Jake Barber, a helicopter pilot who says he once helped carry a recovered UFO, says simply that it is "a company we formed." The researcher Matthew Pines, who also says he is part of it, explains that the team is using private money and the skills they picked up "from our aspects of engagement with the program" to gather enough evidence to convince more people the phenomenon is real. James Valor, another member, says the company was "created through UAP", meaning through the unexplained objects themselves. Michels, in his own telling, says Barber started the group after going public, that its purpose is summoning craft, and he also credits a man named James Fowler.
former-captain-introduces-new-ppd-contac: A former sergeant named Dan Sherman, who says the National Security Agency, the US government's electronic intelligence agency, hired him to communicate with aliens, says that sometime between 1990 and 1993 he was handed a new contact for that secret work. He tells it as something he lived: he was doing his regular job at a large base shared by several military services when the captain who had run him before, whom he calls Captain White, simply showed up at his workplace to make the introduction. It matters to his account because it shows the hidden programme running quietly inside an ordinary military posting.
former-darpa-man-s-hopeful-monsters-hybr: Michels says he met someone who used to work at DARPA, the Pentagon's advanced research agency, who told him about a project proposal for some kind of hybrid that he had submitted there. It drew on the work of the geneticist Richard Goldschmidt and his idea of "hopeful monsters." The man said he could talk about it only because the project was never approved and never went ahead.
former-dig-head-tells-congress-cia-spied: In 2026, a former official is said to have told Congress that the CIA spied on government whistleblowers, including people who had come forward about UFOs. The official had headed a group working under Tulsi Gabbard, the US intelligence chief. Jeremy Corbell, a filmmaker who investigates UFOs, relays it simply: "They found out the CIA was spying on the whistleblowers." He mentions names around the story, including Luis Elizondo, Jay Stratton and the reporter George Knapp. A guest named Dylan Borland names the man who testified as James Erdman III and says he spoke before the Senate. Borland says the testimony covered what was done to whistleblowers on UFOs and also on COVID and on "anomalous health incidents", the unexplained illnesses reported by some US officials, which would mean the agency watched people who tried to speak up.
former-dni-discusses-ufo-tracking-progra: A former director of national intelligence, the official who oversaw all American spy agencies, has openly talked about a program for tracking UFOs based at Area 51, the secret Air Force test site in Nevada. Michels says this himself, without naming the official, in an episode about the man Bob Lazar. He presents it as a sign that top officials now speak openly about such work.
former-employee-was-a-havana-syndrome-vi: One of the people hit by Havana syndrome, the unexplained headaches, dizziness and brain injuries reported by American officials abroad, once worked for him, says Eric Haseltine, whom the episode calls a former director at the National Security Agency, the US spy agency for intercepted communications. "One of them used to work for me. I know him extremely well," he tells Michels. He gives no name, place or date.
former-fortune-50-chairman-threatened-af: A UFO disclosure campaigner named Steven Greer says that in 2024 the retired chairman of a Fortune 50 company, meaning one of the fifty largest companies in the United States, approached his group with an offer to speak out. Greer says that as soon as the man did, an assassination team threatened to kill him, his whole family and his grandchildren. Greer tells this as something that happened to people he deals with directly, and if true it would mean powerful insiders are being silenced by force.
former-hells-angels-president-frozen-for: Brandon Fugal, the owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a ranch known for reports of strange events, says a man who had once led a large chapter of the Hells Angels motorcycle club was working there as security when he was left frozen, unable to move, for about ten minutes behind a building called Homestead 3. Fugal tells it as something that happened on his property, and as one of the ranch's unexplained effects on people.
former-ic-inspector-general-chuck-mccull: A man named Chuck McCullough, who has been involved in the UFO question, used to be the Inspector General of the Intelligence Community, the official watchdog who looks into wrongdoing across all the US spy agencies. Michels points this out himself, saying "people don't know" it, in an episode with a guest named Dylan Borland who says a top government official told him aliens run everything. The point is that someone this senior has taken the subject seriously.
former-lockheed-cia-contractor-eg-g-scie: In 2001, a man who had worked as a contractor for Lockheed, the aerospace company, and for the CIA, the US spy agency, went public saying Lockheed was working on UFO technology and that scientists hired through a contractor called EG&G were running the work in private labs in Utah. Michels tells this himself, without naming the man or a source. If true, it would mean recovered or alien-derived technology was being studied by private companies outside government sites.
former-mayor-admits-the-event-city-build: In Varginha, a town in Brazil where strange beings were reportedly seen in 1996, the former mayor is said to admit the event happened, and the town built a large model UFO statue to mark it. Michels tells this himself in a 2026 episode featuring a surgeon who says his hospital operated on an alien. He offers it as a sign that even local officials took the event seriously.
former-nsa-aaro-director-and-crowdsource: The Pentagon's office for studying unexplained objects in the sky, called AARO, is now led by a former official of the NSA, the US spy agency that collects electronic communications. Michels points this out himself while talking with his guest Dylan Borland. He suggests it fits a theory that the government releases small amounts of information so it can gather intelligence from the public's response.
former-nsa-research-director-never-saw-a: A former research director at the National Security Agency, the US spy agency that intercepts communications, says he never saw any program to take apart and copy recovered UFOs. Eric Haseltine says he "had access to a whole lot of stuff" and once, as a "super user," sat through a full day of briefings on the Pentagon's walled-off secret programs, "like Clockwork Orange where they clamped open my eyelids," and "there was nothing about UFOs in there." He tells it to weigh against claims that such programs are hidden inside the government.
former-police-chief-pedro-aguiar-says-he: In 1996, in the town of Varginha, Brazil, where many people say a strange creature was caught, the former local police chief Pedro Aguiar is said to have admitted that he took part in the operation and saw the creature under a tarp, perhaps only its lower half. The documentary filmmaker James Fox tells Michels this from his own interviews for his film Moment of Contact. Fox says Aguiar told them, once he felt more at ease, "I participated. I'm a witness." If true, it would add a police official to the many people who say something was really captured in Varginha.
former-politico-journalist-asks-brent-ab: A writer named Brent Friedman says that in November a journalist named Ben Schreckinger, who used to report for the news outlet Politico, came to him asking about a denial from John S. Herrington, a former US Secretary of Energy. Friedman tells Michels this happened to him directly. He does not spell out here exactly what Herrington denied, only that the denial drew a reporter's questions.
former-soldier-sees-triangle-take-off-at: In the mid 2010s a former Army soldier says he saw a triangle-shaped craft shoot off from an airstrip at Area 51, the secret Air Force test site in Nevada. A researcher who goes by the online name UAPGerb says he spoke with this man, who is not named. It is told as a hint that such craft are flown or tested there.
formula-given-to-brent-and-bryce-lost-fo: A man named Brent Friedman says that a stranger once handed him and his partner Bryce Zabel a formula, which they then lost for years, until his daughter found it around 2023 or 2024 in his garage in Washington. Friedman tells it first-hand: the paper had slipped out of its envelope, got damp, and stuck to the back of a book because of the envelope's glue. He tells it because finding the paper again let him go back to researching the formula.
forrestal-flown-to-hobe-sound-reported-b: In 1949 Forrestal, the US defense secretary, was flown to Hobe Sound in Florida, and there, it is said, he tried to hang himself with his belt. The researcher Richard Dolan, who writes about UFO history, tells this and is careful to mark it as hearsay ("he apparently, we're told"), pointing to an account tied to a man he calls William Manager. Dolan tells it as part of the story of Forrestal's breakdown and death, which he links to UFO secrecy.
forrestal-on-majestic-12-1947: James Forrestal, the first US Secretary of Defense, was supposedly a member of Majestic 12, a rumoured secret group of top officials said to have been set up around 1947 to handle UFO matters. Michels raises this himself, with the word "supposedly", while talking to Harald Malmgren, a former advisor to US presidents. If true, it would put UFO secrecy at the very top of the government.
forrestal-s-death-at-bethesda-1949: James Forrestal, the first US Secretary of Defense, died in 1949 after falling from a high window of the Navy hospital at Bethesda, Maryland, and some of the people telling the story say he was killed. Jesse Michels raises it in his own words on two occasions. Once he says Forrestal was "killed by gravity quote unquote," and another time he adds that his bathrobe was found tied to the radiator before he went out the window. The researcher Richard Dolan, speaking without naming a source, puts it flatly: "He was absolutely murdered." Dolan gives the night of May 21 into May 22 and the sixteenth floor, mocking the official account as Forrestal's "16th floor bungee jump out the window". He draws on Forrestal's own diaries and on people around him, including a man named Robert Lovett, a relative named Henry Forrestal and a priest called Father Sheehy. Dolan's episode is titled as the story of a defence secretary killed over UFOs, and if that were true, it would mean a top official died because of what he knew about them.
forrestal-s-limo-ride-with-symington-and: In 1949, after a ride in a limousine with an official named Steuart Simington, the Secretary of Defense James Forrestal is said to have been found in his office chair, staring at a blank wall and repeating one sentence: 'You are a loyal fellow.' The researcher Richard Dolan tells this without naming his source, in an episode that ties Forrestal's downfall and death to UFO secrets and that also mentions President Harry Truman. For Dolan, the scene shows a man under great strain in the weeks before he was pushed out.
forrestal-s-published-diaries-never-ment: James Forrestal, the first US Secretary of Defense, kept diaries that were published in two volumes after his death, and they are said never to mention UFOs. The researcher Richard Dolan points this out on an episode about Forrestal. He raises it because the silence matters to the claim that Forrestal knew about UFOs and that this was tied to his death.
forrestal-s-trips-to-paris-with-question: In the 1940s, James Forrestal, a top US defence official who became the country's first Secretary of Defense, is said to have travelled to Paris with questions and come back with answers. A former presidential advisor named Harold Malmgren says he found "several references" to these trips in records. He does not say what the questions were, but in this telling they hint at early secret contacts over the UFO subject.
forrestal-truman-meeting-dates-match-mj-: The claim is that the Majestic 12 papers, a set of documents describing a secret panel said to have handled crashed saucers, give dates for meetings between President Harry Truman and his Defense Secretary James Forrestal that match the days the two men really met. A researcher who goes by UAPGerb makes the point in passing, tying it to the Eisenhower briefing document, one of these papers presented as a briefing for President Eisenhower. Michels tells it in more detail himself. He describes a memo from Truman to Forrestal dated 24 September 1947, and he brings in the government scientist Vannevar Bush, the first meeting of the National Security Council, the president's top security body, and the UFO researcher Stanton Friedman. Both tell it for the same reason: if the dates line up, whoever wrote the papers knew the real schedules of the men at the top. The two tellers do not give the same detail, with Michels alone naming the September 1947 memo.
forrestal-unravels-says-he-is-followed-b: In Washington in 1948 and 1949, the US Defense Secretary James Forrestal began to fall apart, developing nervous tics and saying, "I'm being followed by strange foreign looking men," according to the UFO researcher Richard Dolan. Dolan tells it as part of the story of Forrestal's last months, naming the newspaper columnist Drew Pearson and Steuart Simington among the people around him. He brings it up as part of his argument that Forrestal's downfall and death were tied to UFO secrets.
fort-worth-general-orders-blanchard-it-s: In 1947 something crashed near the army air base at Roswell, New Mexico. According to this story, the base commander, Colonel Blanchard, then got "a very angry phone call" from a general at the big air base in Fort Worth, Texas, ordering him to say the wreck was a weather balloon. The scientist John Brandenburg tells it, passing on what Blanchard and Roswell veterans are said to have told people, and it would mean the balloon explanation was handed down from above rather than found on the ground.
fortune-10-scientist-with-free-energy-an: Steven Greer, a campaigner who says UFO secrets are held by a hidden group of powerful people, says that in 2025 a scientist from a Fortune 10 company, one of the ten largest companies in the United States, flew in to Los Angeles to meet him. Greer describes the man as a "super genius" who can build free-energy plasma devices and do teleportation. If true, it would mean technology far beyond anything public already sits inside big business.
fouche-and-the-tr3b-1970: Edgar Fouché, a man who presented himself as a UFO whistleblower, is said to have known about the TR-3B, a flying triangle supposedly built by copying alien technology. The online UFO researcher UAPGerb says Fouché learned of it from friends, including officials at the NSA, the US electronic spying agency. Michels says Fouché claimed to have been at Area 51, the secret Air Force test site in Nevada, himself. In Michels's version the TR-3A and TR-3B came from the defence company Northrop Grumman and ran on spinning mercury. If true, it would mean the US has flown craft built from technology that did not come from people.
fouche-saw-the-tr3b-twice-1990: A man named Edgar Fouche said he had seen the TR3B, a secret triangular aircraft people talk about, twice in the 1990s: once at Edwards Air Force Base in California and once somewhere else. A commentator who goes by UAPGerb repeats this, citing a talk Fouche gave at the 1998 International UFO Congress. If true, it would mean such a craft was flying at a US military base.
fouche-the-tr3b-uses-internal-mass-reduc: The TR3B, said to be a secret triangular US aircraft from the 1990s, does not use anti-gravity but "internal mass reduction," which supposedly cuts the craft's mass by about 89 percent. That was the view of a man named Edgar Fouche, who claimed inside knowledge of secret aircraft. An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb passes this on, saying Fouche "was adamant" about it. If true, it would mean the US built a craft that works by making itself almost weightless.
fouche-tr3b-program-led-by-nro-cia-and-n: The TR3B, a secret triangular aircraft rumoured to exist, was built under a program led by three US spy agencies: the National Reconnaissance Office, which runs spy satellites, the CIA, and the NSA, which handles electronic eavesdropping. That is what a man named Edgar Fouche said, as relayed by a researcher who goes by the online name UAPGerb. If true, it would mean spy agencies rather than the regular military ran the most secret aircraft work.
fouche-tr3b-propulsion-reverse-engineere: The engine of a secret aircraft called the TR3B was, by one account, copied from non-human technology at Sandia and Lawrence Livermore, two US national weapons laboratories. A researcher who goes by UAPGerb relays this from a man named Edgar Fouche. If true, it would mean government labs built working craft from recovered technology.
founders-of-washington-copied-egypt-with: The people who laid out Washington DC are said to have copied ancient Egypt on purpose, putting up obelisks as the Egyptians did, the same as was done in Central Park, France and England. Chris Bledsoe, a man who says UFOs show up around him, repeats this from a man named Robert Gilbert, who he says "explained to me what they knew and how the people that set Washington up, they did the same thing." If true, it would mean the capital was built on an old, deliberate design.
founding-myths-of-star-people-teaching-a: Nearly every culture's founding myth, Michels says, tells of people who came from the stars and taught humans how to farm. He says this himself, without naming any particular myth or source. If true, it would hint that ancient peoples everywhere remembered some contact with visitors from elsewhere.
founding-of-nasa-s-electrostatics-lab-by: NASA's lab for studying static electricity was started around 2000 by a physicist named Carlos Gier, after he spent a summer working at Kennedy Space Center in Florida. Charles Buhler, a NASA scientist who works in that lab, tells this as its origin story, the place where he says his team has since built a kind of propulsion that pushes without fuel.
founding-of-the-pear-lab-by-bob-jahn-197: A laboratory at Princeton University that studied parapsychology, the claimed powers of the mind, was founded in 1979 by Bob Jahn, then dean of the university's engineering school. Michels tells this himself in an episode about the CIA's psychic spy program. In a later episode he describes Jahn instead as a plasma physicist and propulsion engineer, gives no date, and draws on a book called Margins of Reality.
four-et-craft-appear-near-pensacola-1990: In the early 1990s, four alien craft are said to have suddenly appeared in the air near Pensacola, Florida, in front of a group of about 60 people spending a weekend on a beach. A UFO researcher named Steven Greer says he was there and that the group was "demonstrating" contact when the craft "just pop up right into right there"; in one telling he puts it in 1992. He says that afterward all kinds of people began coming to him, and that others knew about the event, which would mean such contact can be called up on purpose.
four-gliding-beings-in-uniforms-beside-t: In 1977, at a nuclear missile launch site called November-5 near Nisland, South Dakota, four beings in uniforms came toward him beside his truck, "just gliding across the ground" instead of walking, says Mario Woods, who was an Air Force guard at the site. He tells Michels this happened to him, as part of what he describes as an abduction. In a later episode he adds that three of them were small and one tall one stayed at the back.
four-hours-of-missing-time-and-crohn-s-d: A North Carolina man named Chris Bledsoe says that in 2007, near a river at Riverbank, North Carolina, he lost four hours he cannot account for, and came walking back to the river to find his son missing. Bledsoe tells this as his own experience and links it to the healing of his Crohn's disease, a long-term illness of the gut. If true, the encounter would have changed his body as well as his life.
four-plus-four-tubes-descending-beneath-: Filippo Biondi, a researcher who scans the ground with satellite radar, says his team has found four plus four, eight in all, tube-like shapes running down from the base of a pyramid at Giza in Egypt to something deeper below. He tells it as a result of his own scans, and if true it would mean large unknown structures lie under the pyramid.
four-psychic-groups-of-ets-friends-enemi: Aliens visiting Earth fall into four groups, according to a former Army sergeant and psychic spy named Lyn Buchanan: friends or enemies, each either more or less psychically gifted than humans. Buchanan says this came from his own work in the 1980s and a paper comparing human and alien psychic ability, and he tells Michels that 'the friends who are less or equal to us psychically come here for trade.' It is offered as a map of who is coming here and why.
four-rabbis-attempt-celestial-ascent: In an old Jewish tale known as the Pardes, or the orchard, four rabbis tried to rise up into the heavens, and only one came back alive with his mind intact. Michels tells it himself as a parable, in an episode with an MIT scientist about reality as a hologram. He uses it to show that ancient traditions warned how dangerous contact with higher realms could be.
four-star-general-from-the-clinton-admin: In the 1990s, a four-star general in President Bill Clinton's administration is said to have used his rank and authority to visit a secret program holding recovered crashed craft, and to have gotten inside. The physicist Eric W. Davis says he knows this general personally and relays what he was told. If true, it would mean that even top officials have to force their way in to see such a program.
four-star-general-says-mj-12-is-real: An unnamed four-star general, asked about the Majestic 12 documents, papers describing a secret group of officials said to handle the UFO question, is said to have answered that they are real, or that Majestic 12 itself is real. The researcher UAPGerb relays this on Michels' show in 2025 without naming the general. If true, it would mean a secret UFO control group existed at the top of the US government.
four-years-of-secret-funding-before-hist: The owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a property in Utah known for reports of strange events, says that from about 2016 he paid for a scientific investigation of the ranch and kept it completely secret and confidential for four years. He tells it as his own decision, saying he went public only after the History Channel, a US television network, persuaded him to. It would mean the work there began as a private, serious inquiry rather than as a television show.
fox-breaks-the-fife-symington-phoenix-li: Fife Symington, governor of Arizona at the time of the Phoenix Lights, a mass sighting of strange lights over Phoenix in 1997, was himself a witness, says the documentary filmmaker James Fox, who says he was the one who broke the story. Fox tells Michels that Symington looked into it and, speaking as a former Air Force pilot, said "that thing could not have been from here." In a later episode Fox adds that the governor's admission came about ten years after the sighting. If true, it would mean a sitting governor saw the lights and believed they were not man-made.
fox-concludes-there-were-more-beings-tha: There were many more strange beings around Varginha, Brazil in 1996 than the first reports said, with sightings continuing later on. That is the conclusion the documentary filmmaker James Fox says he is coming to after years of interviewing witnesses there. If so, the events were larger than the single creature first described.
fox-finds-marco-chereze-s-sister-marta: A man named James Fox, who went to Varginha, Brazil, to look into a story that the army there captured a live alien, says that after hours of knocking on doors he found the sister of a man named Marco Chereze, a woman named Marta Tavares. Fox tells this as something he did himself. Finding her mattered to him because she could speak for her brother's part in the story.
fox-interviewed-all-three-rendlesham-wit: James Fox, a filmmaker who investigates UFO reports, says he is the only person to have interviewed all three airmen, Jim Penniston, John Burroughs and a man named Cabansag, who went into the woods near a British air base called RAF Woodbridge in 1980 after strange lights were seen, an incident also linked to their officer Charles Halt. Fox tells it from his own interviews, which would make his account of that night the only one that hears from every man who was there.
fox-s-interview-with-edgar-mitchell-at-h: At his home in Florida, the Apollo astronaut Edgar Mitchell said on camera, "yes there have been ET visitation," meaning that beings from other worlds have come here. The UFO investigator James Fox tells this because he was the one who sat down and interviewed Mitchell there.
fox-s-investigation-of-the-varginha-cras: In 1996, according to the filmmaker James Fox, a UFO crashed near Varginha, a town in Brazil, and he says he travelled there five times over 12 years to look into it for his documentary film Moment of Contact. The journalist Michael Shellenberger says he later wrote the case up as a two-page spread in the New York Post newspaper, calling it "maybe the craziest of all the cases", and Michels himself brings it up, citing Fox's film. If true, it would be one of the best-witnessed crashes of a craft not made by people.
fox-s-vision-of-tim-coleman-keying-his-c: While editing his documentary Out of the Blue, the filmmaker James Fox says a picture suddenly came into his head of a man named Tim Coleman holding a key, "clear as day," scratching his car. Fox tells Michels this happened to him in the editing building, and he tells it as a moment of sensing something he had not seen with his eyes.
fox-sends-out-of-the-blue-to-all-535-mem: The documentary filmmaker James Fox says that around 2000 he personally handed out copies of his UFO documentary, Out of the Blue, to every member of the House and Senate, all 535 of them. He tells it as his own effort to put the subject in front of lawmakers in Washington, D.C., and get them to take it seriously.
fracking-oil-with-nuclear-weapons-in-the: John S. Herrington, a former US Secretary of Energy, says that under President Dwight D. Eisenhower in the 1950s the government was fracking oil with nuclear weapons, meaning it set off nuclear blasts underground to crack the rock and free the oil. He says it in passing as an example of how far that era's experiments went.
fractals-in-jackson-pollock-s-paintings-: The drip paintings of the American artist Jackson Pollock, made from the late 1940s on, are said to contain fractals, patterns that repeat the same shape at smaller and smaller scales, as found in nature. The philosopher Jason Jorjani raises this, telling the host to "go look this up" in a Scientific American magazine article called "Order in Pollock's Chaos," by the physicist Richard P. Taylor, and he also points to his own book Lovers of Sophia. He uses it to suggest that Pollock tapped into a hidden natural order without knowing it.
francis-crick-s-1973-directed-panspermia: In 1973, Francis Crick, the scientist who co-discovered the double helix shape of DNA, wrote a paper on directed panspermia: the idea that life on Earth was deliberately seeded from space by someone else. Michels tells this himself in several episodes, describing a paper on directed panspermia written in 1973. In one he also gives the year 1981 and calls Crick a former associate of his guest, the biologist Rupert Sheldrake. In another he gives no date and mentions no paper. The writer Graham Hancock tells it too, giving no source, and paints a vivid picture: a spaceship carrying bacteria that "collided with the early Earth" 3.9 billion years ago and "spilled out its contents." Hancock credits Crick's book Life Itself, published in 1981, and not just the earlier paper. The story gets told because if one of the founders of modern biology took the idea seriously, life's origins might lie beyond Earth.
franco-and-skorzeny-launch-saucer-shaped: In 1946, according to Spanish newspaper reports, the German wartime commando Otto Skorzeny was on Spain's Mediterranean coast with the Spanish dictator Francisco Franco, launching saucer-shaped rockets toward America. The philosopher Jason Jorjani tells Michels this, drawing on the writer Joseph P. Farrell's book Saucers, Swastikas and Psyops. If true, some early flying-saucer sightings could trace back to leftover Nazi technology.
frank-critzer-nazi-agent-killed-at-giant: The underground rooms beneath Giant Rock, a huge boulder in the California desert where George Van Tassel later lived and held UFO gatherings, are said to have first belonged to a Nazi named Frank Critzer, who was killed there. A philosopher named Jason Jorjani tells this, drawing on a work called Closer Encounters. He raises it to link a famous UFO site to a hidden Nazi past.
frank-drake-s-project-ozma-1961: In 1961, the astronomer Frank Drake began Project Ozma, which Michels calls "the first ever organized search for interstellar radio signals," meaning signals from other stars that might come from intelligent life. Michels tells this himself as background history in an episode with the astronomer Beatriz Villarroel about the search for signs of beings beyond Earth.
frank-tipler-s-rotating-disc-time-machin: A physicist named Frank Tipler is said to have worked out, in the 1970s, that a time machine could be a rapidly spinning ring, sphere or disc, which looks like a flying saucer. A researcher named Mike Masters tells it as the end of a line of work running back to Albert Einstein, a scientist named van Stockum and a mathematician named Kurt Gödel, with Tipler shrinking their ideas down to an object of finite size. Michels tells it too, calling Tipler a contemporary of the physicist John Wheeler and saying his "Tipler disc" took Gödel's time travel model and made it "a flying saucer." If true, UFOs could be time machines, perhaps built by humans from the future.
fravor-and-dietrich-disagree-on-how-long: Two Navy pilots who saw the same strange object off Southern California in 2004 do not agree on how long the encounter lasted. According to the UFO skeptic Mick West, the pilot Alex Dietrich says her part of it lasted only 8 to 10 seconds, from the moment they closed in on the object to the moment it flew away, a much shorter span than the version told by her fellow pilot David Fravor. West raises this on Michels's show to question how reliable the witness accounts are.
fravor-and-dietrich-saw-appendages-on-un: In 2004, off Southern California, Navy pilots met a white oval object, and the infrared camera video of it later showed small appendages sticking out of it, according to two of the pilots. Marik von Rennenkampff relays this on Michels' show: Commander David Fravor and Lieutenant Commander Alex Dietrich have said they saw these protrusions when they reviewed the tape filmed by a pilot named Chad Underwood. He raises it as a detail that a plain balloon or plane would not explain.
fravor-s-2004-nimitz-sighting-of-an-obje: In November 2004, off the coast of San Diego, a Navy fighter pilot named Commander David Fravor flew out from the group of ships around the aircraft carrier USS Nimitz to check on an object, and he describes "a small white tic tac object," a white oval shaped like the mint, "moving very abruptly over the water like a ping pong ball" before it "rapidly accelerated in front of us and disappeared." Michels comes back to this case again and again. He stresses Fravor's sense that the thing seemed "conscious and almost breathing" and "knew that he saw it." He also says it seemed to dip in and out of the water and was already waiting at the point Fravor was flying to next. Michels names other witnesses, including Chad Underwood, Kevin Day and Alex Dietrich, and says the ship USS Princeton picked it up on radar, a detail he credits to Luis Elizondo. He also notes that the story reached the public through Leslie Kean's 2017 New York Times article. Jacques Vallée, a veteran UFO researcher, asks why anything would let "11 F-18s," Navy fighter jets, chase it "all over the Pacific." Eric Haseltine, a former director of the National Security Agency, the US electronic spying agency, says "there's something real going on there" because of the many independent sensors and the reluctant people who saw it. If Fravor read it right, the object was not just fast but seemed to be aware of him.
fravor-s-joe-rogan-interview-draws-merri: The national security writer Marik von Rennenkampff says he was drawn into the UFO subject in late 2019 by an interview that David Fravor, a Navy fighter pilot and commander who reported chasing a strange object, gave on the show of the podcaster Joe Rogan. He tells it as his own starting point, showing how one pilot's public account pulled serious observers toward the topic.
fred-crisman-and-hunt-as-the-dallas-tram: A man named Fred Crisman is said to have been one of three tramps arrested in Dallas right after President John F. Kennedy was shot in 1963. Michels says some people think this, and adds that Crisman was also involved in the Maury Island incident of 1947, a reported UFO event around the time a man named Kenneth Arnold reported seeing his UFO.
