The author Peter Levenda, described as a CIA historian, says he can back it up and that a man named E. Howard Hunt may have been one of the tramps too. If true, it would tie early UFO stories to the Kennedy killing.
fred-darwin-s-list-of-a-high-level-flyin: A man named Fred Darwin wrote down a list of names, saying these men sat on a special committee on flying saucers at the highest level of the US defense research world in the late 1940s and early 1950s. Jesse Michels tells this himself, and the names he cites include the engineer Vannevar Bush and the mathematician John von Neumann. If true, it would mean top American scientists were quietly studying flying saucers.
fred-maywald-confirms-the-story-in-recor: The former Air Force officer Robert Salas says that in 1996 he finally reached his old commander, Fred Maywald, who confirmed the essentials of Salas's story of a 1967 night when a UFO shut down nuclear missiles in Montana. Salas says the call, recorded and posted on the website spiralgalaxy.org, also showed him he had been at Oscar Flight, one cluster of missile sites, rather than Echo Flight as he had thought. He tells it as a participant, and the call matters because it would back his account with a second officer's word.
fred-reed-s-letter-on-relandscaping-the-: After an alleged 1948 crash of a craft on a mesa in Hart Canyon near Aztec, New Mexico, a team is said to have come back "basically to relandscape the mesa," hiding any trace of what happened. Scott Ramsey, who has researched the crash story, says this comes from a letter by a man named Fred Reed dated March 27, 1999. It would mean someone worked to erase the site on purpose.
frederick-myers-and-the-society-for-psyc: In 1882, Frederick Myers of the Society for Psychical Research, an English group set up to study claims of the paranormal, is said to have introduced telepathy, mind-to-mind contact, as the way to explain strange experiences of knowing things one should not know. The researcher Eric Wargo describes this without naming a source, in an episode about prophetic dreams. He tells it to show that such experiences were long presumed to be telepathy, a view he questions.
frederick-valentich-disappearance-1978: A young pilot named Frederick Valentich disappeared in 1978 while flying his Cessna, a small private plane, over Bass Strait, the stretch of sea between mainland Australia and Tasmania. A guest named Ross Coulthart mentions it only in passing on the podcast, as something that had happened a few months before other events he was describing, which places it among the strange happenings of that time.
frederick-wolfe-german-pow-shot-at-fort-: A German soldier named Frederick Wolfe was held as a prisoner of war at Fort Knox, the army base in Kentucky, and was shot there. A former CIA officer named Rolf Mowatt-Larssen tells this as local lore of the base, without naming a source, saying Wolfe "was a German soldier who after World War II was sent to Fort Knox as a prisoner of war," though the story is placed in 1944.
free-edgar-mitchell-experiencer-study-hu: A large survey of people who report contact with non-human beings, run by a group called FREE and named for the astronaut Edgar Mitchell, is said to find that 52 percent of them met creatures that looked roughly human. Michels cites it himself across several episodes, at times saying "over 50%," describing the database as 5,000-plus abductees in the US, and also citing its findings on beings taking tissue samples. He raises it with Mike Masters, who argues in his book The Extratempestrial Model that the visitors may be humans from the future, and he tells it because so many humanlike beings would fit that idea.
free-energy-device-in-stan-meyer-s-archi: In a warehouse in Michigan holding the archive of an inventor named Stan Meyer, full of floppy disks and devices, there is said to be one machine "of great interest", a device for producing free energy. Steven Greer, a campaigner for UFO disclosure, tells this on Michels' show in 2025, repeating what his science advisor Dr. Ted Loder found when he visited, and points to a photo on the site dpiarchive.com. If true, it would mean such energy technology exists and has been sitting unused.
freeman-dyson-on-ida-advisory-board: A former intelligence contractor named Bob Maguire says that the physicist Freeman Dyson sat on the advisory board of the place where he worked, the Center for Communications Research in New Jersey, part of the Institute for Defense Analyses, a research group that works for the US government. Maguire tells this as a fact of his own workplace. He brings it up to show how well-known the minds around that work were.
freemasonry-descends-from-cathedral-buil: Modern Freemasonry, the secretive brotherhood organised in lodges, grew out of two older traditions that merged, according to the researcher Randall Carlson: the lodges of the guild builders who put up Europe's cathedrals, and the Knights Templar, a medieval order of warrior monks. Carlson gives this as his own summary, without naming a source. It matters to him because it would link the Masons to old building knowledge and to the Templars' secrets.
freescale-semiconductor-engineers-aboard: Among the passengers on MH370, a passenger plane that went missing in 2014, were 20 engineers from Freescale Semiconductor, a company that makes computer chips. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, in an episode about American scientists going missing. He raises it because, if it means anything, it would put a whole team of chip specialists in one vanished plane.
freezing-at-the-communion-cover-in-a-bar: John Blitch, a former scientist at DARPA, the Pentagon's advanced research agency, who says he was taken by an alien, recalls walking through a Barnes & Noble bookstore in a mall in the 1990s. He says he glanced at the wall to his right, saw Whitley Strieber's book Communion, a book about Strieber's own reported encounters with a staring alien face on its cover, and "froze in my tracks." Blitch tells it as his own experience, a jolt of recognition that fits his account of what happened to him.
freikorps-stahlhelm-militias-wearing-swa: Right after the First World War, in 1918 and 1919, armed volunteer militias in Germany known as the Freikorps were already wearing swastikas, and one group, the Stahlhelm, meaning "steel helmet", had the symbol painted on their helmets. A researcher named Peter Levenda tells this without naming a source. He tells it to show that the swastika was in use among German fighters before the Nazi party took it up.
french-1999-cometa-report-conclusions: The COMETA report was written in France in 1999 by a group of French experts, and according to a summary on the show it concluded that UFOs could be alien spacecraft, that there might be a base somewhere in our solar system, and that the United States was probably hiding information. The physicist Kevin Knuth gives this summary from memory, without quoting the report itself. If true, it would mean a serious French study had reached conclusions that the US has never admitted to.
french-bombing-of-the-greenpeace-boat-in: In 1985 a boat belonging to Greenpeace, the environmental campaign group, was blown up in Auckland Harbor in New Zealand by French intelligence, the agency known as the DGSE, in what the teller calls an intelligence operation "slap-bang in the middle of Auckland Harbor." The journalist Ross Coulthart brings it up on Michels' show as an example of what spy agencies are willing to do, even in a friendly country's harbor.
french-demonstrations-escalating-up-to-a: Around 1956 in France, people are said to have written to a man named Jacques Cornillon about a series of demonstrations, each time inviting someone of higher rank, until the guests reached officials in France's atomic energy body. The researcher Jan Lundquist describes these letters without naming where he saw them, in a documentary about the inventor Townsend Brown, who is said to have built flying craft early on. Lundquist tells it to show that the work drew interest at higher and higher levels of the French state.
french-farmer-meets-an-nhi-holding-a-tra: In France, the story goes, a trusted and respected farmer found a spaceship on his land, walked up to it, and found a non-human intelligence, meaning a being that is not human, standing there holding a tray full of soil samples. The journalist Michael Shellenberger tells it as a case he credits to the UFO researcher Jacques Vallée. If true, it would mean the visitors were collecting samples of the Earth.
frequent-ufo-sightings-in-alamogordo: Lyn Buchanan, a former Army sergeant, says he has seen many UFOs and that where he lives, in Alamogordo, New Mexico, people see them all the time. He tells it in passing, as his own experience of how common the sightings are there.
fresh-yellow-curb-lines-marking-the-kill: Three yellow lines were painted on the curb of Elm Street in Dallas the night before President John F. Kennedy was shot there in 1963, right where the shots struck, and a woman named Beverly Oliver was standing on one of them. The lawyer Dan Sheehan tells this, pointing to Oliver and to the Zapruder film, the home movie that caught the shooting. He tells it as a sign that the killing was planned in advance and the spot marked out.
freud-s-1895-dream-foreshadowing-his-ora: A famous dream the psychiatrist Sigmund Freud had in 1895 is said to foreshadow the mouth cancer he was found to have decades later. The researcher Eric Wargo makes this case, noting that Freud spent about 14 pages on the dream in his landmark book The Interpretation of Dreams. Wargo raises it as a sign that dreams can glimpse the future.
friedman-and-the-woods-authenticate-mj-1: Two papers, the Special Operations Manual and the Eisenhower briefing document, are said to come from Majestic 12, a supposed secret US group set up to handle crashed UFOs. A researcher who goes by UAPGerb says he follows the work of the UFO researcher Stanton Friedman, who "spent a bunch of time authenticating" both papers with Ryan Wood and Robert Wood. If the papers are real, they would show a hidden government UFO programme from the very start.
friend-abducted-by-grays-shows-delta-pat: A friend staying at Tim Alberino's house told him one day, "I forgot to tell you. They came and got me," meaning he had been taken by grays, the small grey-skinned beings of many abduction stories, and he showed marks on his body laid out in a triangle pattern. Alberino, a guest who also talks about a giant captured in Afghanistan, tells it as something he witnessed when his friend showed him the marks.
friend-dying-on-the-moon: A man is said to have watched, or known about, a friend of his dying on the Moon, which would mean people have been working there in secret. The Australian investigative journalist Ross Coulthart tells it from a conversation with an unnamed source he trusts, who he says "got very emotional" describing the friend's death.
friend-mike-secretly-watched-buer-and-dr: For years, a friend named Mike knew that Charles Buhler and Andrew Arjima were each working on the same propulsion idea separately, and never told either of them, says Buhler, an engineer the episode presents as a NASA chief. Buhler tells Michels he found this out around 2016 in Florida: "He knew about us working on this independently for years and never told us, never did."
friend-s-family-sees-the-same-beach-ligh: Around 2020 or 2021, a friend of a NASA engineer named Charles Buhler was out at the beach near Cocoa Beach, Florida, late one night with his family, and they saw the same strange lights Buhler had seen. Buhler passes on his friend's account and says he "thought was super cool" that someone else had seen them. To him, it backed up his own sighting.
friend-s-government-contact-warns-him-of: A friend of a filmmaker named Tim Alberino asked a government contact about the Kandahar giant, a story that US soldiers met and killed a giant near Kandahar, Afghanistan, and the contact's manner changed completely as he warned him off. Alberino relays this as what his friend told him. He tells it as a sign that the story touches something officials want kept quiet.
friend-s-medium-reading-channels-his-lat: A friend of Michels, whom he does not name, went to a medium, a person who claims to speak with the dead, and the medium at once began teasing him the way his late sister used to. Michels tells it as his friend's story in an episode about psychics and the afterlife with a guest named Jeffrey Mishlove. If true, it would suggest the sister was reaching out from beyond death.
friend-sees-a-black-pyramid-in-antarctic: A man who went to Antarctica, possibly to make a documentary, says he saw a kind of black pyramid there. Michels tells this himself, passing on what a friend of his told him. If true, it would hint at a structure hidden in the ice.
friend-sees-a-portal-open-in-the-sky-and: A man is said to have watched a portal open up in the sky and saucers fly out of it. The filmmaker Tim Alberino tells this about a friend of his, and says, "my friend saw this actually happen." He gives no time or place.
friend-spoke-to-amy-eskridge-hours-befor: A friend of a woman named Amy Eskridge, who died in Alabama in 2022, says he does not believe she killed herself. The friend, who is not named, says he spoke to her four hours before her death and that she told him again and again she was not going to commit suicide. He tells this from his own conversation with her, and if true it would cast doubt on how her death was explained.
friend-with-the-same-slit-in-his-eye-is-: The author Whitley Strieber says he has a friend in Marin County, California, who has the same odd slit in his eye that Strieber does. He adds that this friend is "one of the world's leading experts" on Konstantin Raudive, a man known for tape recordings he believed captured the voices of the dead. Strieber tells it as a strange link between himself and someone else drawn to the unexplained.
friends-lab-work-becomes-a-weapon-in-mon: Friends doing private lab work on advanced technology saw it turn into a weapon after only six or seven months of work. Dave Rossi, a guest who says aliens taught him advanced physics, tells this about mutual friends he does not name. He tells it to show how quickly this kind of research can become dangerous.
friends-turned-away-from-area-51: Friends who recently drove up to Area 51, a secret US military base in Nevada, just to look were stopped by soldiers and not let through. A Russian regional leader named Kiran Ilum Xenov tells this, passing on what his friends told him. He raises it as a sign of how closely the site is guarded.
friends-who-fought-the-cia-and-dni-inter: Dylan Borland, a man who speaks publicly about government secrecy over UFOs, says he has friends who fought the CIA and the office of the Director of National Intelligence, the head of all US spy agencies, from inside the government, telling them they could prove those agencies were lying, and then doing so. He tells it as something he knows from the people involved.
friends-working-on-antigravity-received-: Several friends of a guest named Kevin Knuth, whom the episode's title calls a whistleblower from NASA, the US space agency, are said to have worked on antigravity, meaning ways to cancel or push against gravity, and to have faced backlash for it. Michels raises this himself, reminding Knuth that he had said so on another podcast, the Danny Jones show. If true, it would suggest that research into such ideas is pushed back against.
friendship-with-robert-anton-wilson-and-: In 1970s Berkeley, California, Jeffrey Mishlove, a researcher with a doctorate who studies the mind and psychic claims, was friends with a man named Robert Anton Wilson, and he recalls that Wilson's "beautiful 15-year-old daughter was tragically murdered" there. Mishlove tells it first-hand, as a friend who was around at the time, and brings up the names Timothy Leary and Gabriel Kennedy, along with a book called Reality Is What You Can Get Away With.
fritz-haber-reverse-engineered-the-red-p: The German chemist Fritz Haber, who with Carl Bosch found a way to make ammonia from air, is said to have copied his method from the Red Pyramid in Egypt. The researcher Geoffrey Drumm puts this forward to Michels as his own idea. He points to a book about an Egyptian banker who paid for Haber's ammonia work, and to postcards Haber sent from Egypt. In a second moment he shows Haber's first apparatus next to the pyramid's three chambers to make the point that they match, this time without mentioning Bosch. If true, a modern chemical breakthrough would owe its design to an ancient building.
fugal-has-seen-ufos-in-the-air-himself: Brandon Fugal, the owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a property in Utah known for reports of strange events, says he has personally seen unidentified flying objects in the sky. He says it in passing, as a first-hand matter, "I've seen them myself in the air," without giving a time or place. It makes him a witness, not just the owner of a place where others report such things.
fulgurites-in-giza-iron-veins-as-evidenc: Samples taken from iron ore veins under the Giza plateau in Egypt are said to contain fulgurites, glassy tubes that form when strong electric current, like lightning, melts rock. A researcher named Jeffrey Drum says this is "evidence of high-voltage electric current distribution through these iron veins". If so, it would point to an ancient energy grid beneath the pyramids.
fungi-growing-on-the-iss-and-mir: Fungi have been found growing in space, on the International Space Station, the orbiting laboratory where astronauts live and work, and on Mir, the earlier Russian space station. Michels says this himself, without naming a source, in an episode about mushrooms. He offers it as a sign of how tough and far-reaching fungi can be.
fungi-on-the-iss-and-crick-s-directed-pa: Michels says fungi have been found on the International Space Station. He links this to Francis Crick, the scientist who co-discovered DNA's double helix, who argued that DNA could not have formed on Earth in 100 million years. Michels says Crick proposed in a paper he dates to 1973, and later in his book Life Itself, that a high-tech spaceship carrying blue-green algae, carbon dioxide, water and mushrooms might have been sent to seed life here, an idea Michels tells himself and connects to the astronomer Carl Sagan.
fused-silica-microspheres-from-fulgurite: Tiny glass beads, which he links to fulgurites, the glass that forms when lightning strikes sand, turn up at the Great Pyramid of Giza in Egypt, says Geoffrey Drumm, a researcher who has his own theory of what the pyramids were for. He shows Michels a photo of himself "down inside one of the boat pits adjacent to the great pyramid," the stone trenches beside the pyramid where ancient boats were buried. He offers the glass as a clue that great heat or electricity was at work there.
fusion-scientist-nuno-loureiro-shot-dead: A scientist named Nuno Loureiro, whom Michels calls the leading figure in magnetic reconnection, a process central to making nuclear fusion power work, was shot on December 15 at his home and died after surgery the next morning. Michels tells it himself across two episodes, naming the shooter as a man called Claudio Neves Valente and citing a US Department of Justice transcript of videos Valente made; he places the home in Brookline, Massachusetts in one telling and in Brooklyn, New York in another. Michels rejects the idea that the killing, which he mentions in the same breath as a man named Carl Grillmair, is a non-story, as part of a question about why top American scientists are dying or going missing.
fyodorov-s-russian-cosmism-and-resurrect: A Russian librarian and philosopher named Nikolai Fyodorov started a school of thought later called Russian Cosmism, which held that the real task of humanity and of Christianity was not to wait for the resurrection of the dead but to bring it about. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, as the starting point of a line of ideas he traces toward space science and its stranger beliefs.
gabinetto-rs33-and-its-nine-step-protoco: In 1933, the story goes, Italy's dictator Benito Mussolini set up a secret research group called Gabinetto RS33, with the radio pioneer Guglielmo Marconi as its president and the physicist Enrico Fermi as vice president, to study extraterrestrials. Michels says the group drew up a nine-step protocol for handling a reported crash near the town of Magenta and any later ones, and elsewhere calls it Italy's rumoured version of a secret US UFO control group. Michels says his main source is a prince who is Marconi's grandson, and that the grandson knew this through his family, not from documents. The grandson himself tells it as a study of UFO sightings near Varese in northern Italy, and in one retelling the founding is dated 1953 rather than 1933. If true, it would mean a European government was organising around UFOs years before any American programme.
gaffney-blocked-lockheed-to-bigelow-ufo-: In 2008 a CIA official named Glenn Gaffney is said to have personally stopped UFO material from being handed from Lockheed Martin, a large defense company, to Bigelow Aerospace, a private space company. Michels relays this from the journalist George Knapp. He says Knapp "even testified to Congress" that Gaffney "was personally responsible for blocking the transfer of UFO materials" between the two companies. A guest named Dylan Borland speaks of the same congressional hearing and names the man too, simply as "Glenn Gaffney, CIA", without a date or any details of the transfer. If it is true, a CIA official stepped in to keep recovered material inside a defense company and away from a private company that was studying it.
galileo-project-instruments-on-harvard-c: The Harvard astronomer Avi Loeb says he started the Galileo Project, an effort to gather new evidence about unexplained objects in the sky using the scientific method and without taking sides, and that by early 2022 more than a hundred scientists had joined and he was buying instruments to put on the roof of the Harvard College Observatory. Loeb tells this himself as its founder, saying thousands of people wrote to him wanting to help. Another guest, the researcher Eric Weinstein, mentions it only in passing as Loeb setting up his effort at Harvard.
galileo-project-monthly-meetings-2021: The Galileo Project, a scientific search for signs of alien technology led by the researcher Avi Loeb, holds team meetings on Zoom early each month, and the well-known skeptic Michael Shermer says he has been on that team since its first week and never misses one. Shermer tells it himself, to show that he takes part in the search even while doubting the claims.
gallaudet-briefs-the-japanese-diet-s-uap: Around 2024 or 2025, a retired US Navy admiral named Tim Gallaudet gave a presentation by video to a group of Japanese lawmakers in their parliament, called the Diet, who meet to study unidentified anomalous phenomena, the official term for UFOs. Gallaudet tells it himself, as the one who gave the talk, to show that interest in the subject reaches into other governments.
gallaudet-co-writes-the-bluegill-triple-: A retired Navy admiral named Tim Gallaudet says he helped write the report on Bluegill Triple Prime, a 1962 nuclear test. He says he wrote it with a man named Jeff Cruickshank. Gallaudet tells this himself, as someone who took part, and if it is true he knows first-hand what that report says.
gallaudet-sees-the-go-fast-video-on-the-: A retired Navy admiral named Tim Gallaudet says that in 2015, when he was a one-star admiral, he watched the Go Fast video on the Navy's classified computer network. That video is a Navy infrared recording of a small object racing low over the ocean, filmed during a training exercise off the US East Coast. Gallaudet tells it as something he saw himself, and he links it to a Navy fighter pilot named Ryan Graves, who flew in that exercise. The point of his story is that the video was being passed around inside the Navy long before anyone outside heard of it.
gallaudet-visits-skinwalker-ranch-with-b: A retired Navy admiral named Tim Gallaudet says he once spent a day at Skinwalker Ranch, a property in Utah known for reports of strange happenings, together with a businessman named Brandon Fugal. Gallaudet tells it himself, as someone who was there, and says only that "we had this great day together," without describing anything they saw.
gallimore-and-strassman-s-2015-extended-: In 2015, two researchers drew up a plan for what they called extended-state DMT, or DMTx. DMT is a powerful psychedelic substance, and the plan was a protocol for keeping a person in its state for longer. One of the two, the neuroscientist Andrew Gallimore, tells this first-hand. He says he wrote it with a fellow researcher named Rick Strassman, and he stresses that the work did not stop in 2015 and is still going on.
gallimore-s-laser-speckle-explanation-fo: A man named Danny says that shining lasers while on DMT, a powerful short-acting psychedelic, reveals a kind of code behind reality, and the neuroscientist Andrew Gallimore offers a plainer explanation. Gallimore says the grainy speckle pattern that laser light makes on the retina acts as "a sensory scaffold" around which, under DMT, a person sees complex forms. On his account, the "code" would come from the eye and the drug working together rather than from reality itself.
games-resume-after-the-dtra-contract-end: A former government contractor named Dylan Borland says that after his contract with the Defense Threat Reduction Agency, a Pentagon agency that deals with weapons of mass destruction, ended, the strange treatment he had faced before started again. He says that last June, while using his security clearance, he was asked to fill out an SF86, the standard form for a government security clearance, and his clearance was then left marked 'undefined'. He tells it as something that happened to him first-hand.
garrett-graff-s-ufo-debunking-book-after: A journalist named Garrett Graff put out a book simply called UFO, which the journalist Michael Shellenberger says came out earlier in 2024 and is "basically just a debunking" of the famous sightings. Shellenberger links the book to the Aspen Institute, a US policy organisation, and to a media executive named Vivian Schiller. He suggests the book followed an effort there to "pre-bunk" UFO stories, meaning to get the public to doubt them before they came out. If he is right, the debunking was planned ahead of time rather than reached independently.
garry-nolan-debunking-atacama-mummy: A Stanford scientist named Garry Nolan is said to have entered the UFO world by studying the Atacama mummy, a tiny mummified body found in Chile's Atacama Desert that some had called an alien, and debunking that claim. Michels points to it himself as the start of Nolan's path into the UFO subject. In the same episode he calls Nolan the man sitting on more UFO evidence than anyone alive.
garry-nolan-has-seen-little-people-and-a: A man named Garry Nolan, whose story is placed at Stanford, California, has seen some little people and has also seen a craft. That is what Jesse Michels says Nolan told him, and he passes it on second-hand without giving any detail of when or where. If true, it would mean Nolan saw both the beings and their vehicle himself.
garry-nolan-s-childhood-bedside-visitors: The Stanford professor Garry Nolan, a scientist, is said to have seen beings at the foot of his bed as a child. He called it not an abduction, and he remembers grey figures in his room. Michels tells this three times, passing on what Nolan has said: once he adds a saucer Nolan saw while on a paper route, and once he stresses that Nolan only uncovered these childhood memories later in life, after he took up the subject as a researcher. That would mean even a careful scientist came to the subject with experiences of his own.
garry-nolan-s-magnesium-bismuth-sample-f: A fisherman on a beach at Ubatuba, Brazil, is said to have watched an object explode, in 1957 by one account, and fragments of it later ended up in the Stanford laboratory of the scientist Garry Nolan, who studied them with mass spectrometry, a lab method that shows what a material is made of. Michels tells this himself across several episodes, saying the pieces were first mailed to the UFO researcher Jacques Vallée, that Nolan spoke about them on Joe Rogan's podcast, and in one episode that Nolan holds "this magnesium bismuth piece," a sample made of those two metals. Michels raises it as physical material that a working scientist can test, though in some tellings he gives the date and in others he does not, and only one mentions the metals.
gary-mckinnon-finds-a-list-of-off-planet: In 2001 or 2002, a British computer hacker named Gary McKinnon is said to have broken into US military computer systems from the UK and found a page listing officers who served off planet. Michels passes this on from what McKinnon told him, and if it were true it would point to a hidden space programme. In a 2024 episode Michels puts the list at 11 or 12 "off Planet officers", but in a 2026 episode he says there were 40 "non-terrestrial officers" and adds his own idea of a supply chain running in space.
gary-mckinnon-s-hack-and-the-tic-tac-ima: Around 2001, a British computer hacker named Gary McKinnon broke into computers at NASA's Johnson Space Center and saw an image of a UFO come up on his screen. McKinnon tells it himself, saying he was led there by a UFO whistleblower named Donna Hare, and describes "a big straight kind of silvery line" coming down, cigar-shaped, "what they now call a tic tac", meaning a white oval object shaped like the mint. Michels retells it several times, dating it anywhere from 2001 to 2003 and describing the object as orbiting Earth in deep space, which, if true, would mean NASA held images of unknown craft near the planet.
gary-nolan-presents-his-injury-research-: In 2016, on the night before a group visited a site in New Mexico, a scientist named Garry Nolan showed the others his research and photos on injuries, while everyone sat around having a beer. The religion scholar Diana Pasulka tells this as one of the people present, saying "Gary decided he was going to share his research with us and photos." She raises it because it shows serious researchers quietly sharing material of this kind among themselves.
gary-nolan-s-caudate-putamen-theories: The idea is that people with more densely packed nerve cells in the caudate nucleus and putamen, two linked structures deep in the brain, are more likely to see UFOs, and maybe also to be more "psychic", show stronger executive functioning, and pass the trait down in families. Michels raises it in several episodes, crediting a Stanford scientist named Garry Nolan, whom he calls both an immunologist and a microbiologist and also a friend. Michels presents Nolan's conclusions as working theories rather than settled findings, and in a later episode calls them studies. If true, it would point to a biological reason why some people have these experiences and others do not.
gary-nolan-s-cia-file-on-ufo-experiencer: A scientist named Garry Nolan is said to have been handed a file by the CIA, the US spy agency, and asked to study it, a file about people who say they had UFO encounters and about Havana syndrome, the strange injuries reported by US officials. Michels says Nolan told him this himself, mentioning he was "kind of given a file by the CIA and he was tasked with looking into this." It would mean the agency was quietly studying these cases.
gary-nolan-s-crash-retrieval-parts-from-: A Stanford professor named Garry Nolan says he has pieces of crashed UFOs, which he got from his friend Jacques Vallée, a researcher Michels calls the longtime godfather of UFO research. Michels says he has seen the parts himself: Nolan showed them to him in his lab. Michels describes them as magnesium-bismuth, and says Nolan suggested such materials might be used as tiny waveguides, parts that channel energy, for energy uses here on Earth.
gary-nolan-s-strontium-ufo-metamaterial-: One of the samples the scientist Garry Nolan keeps at his Stanford lab, which Nolan thinks might be UFO 'metamaterials', engineered materials from crashed craft, is said to contain strontium, a metal element. Michels says this himself, from memory and with an 'I believe', without naming a source. He brings it up because strontium came up in another context, and a match would link it to possible crash debris.
gary-s-biefeld-brown-ccto-experiments-in: Gary McKinnon, a British computer hacker, says that from about 2007 onward he has run his own experiments on the Biefeld-Brown effect, the idea that strong electric charges can make a device push itself along without propellant. He tells Michels he does all of it at home in the UK, "in a 10x 10t shed" in his garden.
gary-stearman-s-cessna-escorted-by-a-wal: A pilot named Gary Stearman was flying a Cessna, a small private plane, from Lubbock, Texas, to Dallas when, the story goes, a voice told him, "If you look to your left, you'll see a UFO," and a walnut-shaped object flew alongside him as an escort. The filmmaker Tim Alberino tells this as something Stearman himself told him, and gives no date.
gary-webb-and-cia-cocaine-in-the-inner-c: A man named Gary Webb knew that the CIA, the US spy agency, brought cocaine into poor Black neighbourhoods of American cities, in a story that runs from about 1980 to 2004. A guest named Kurt Metzger says this in passing while talking with the host, and he gives no more than that one line. He offers it as an example of a man who knew what the agency was doing.
garyaev-healing-people-in-wooden-pyramid: A Russian researcher named Peter Garyaev is said to have healed people by placing them inside wooden pyramids. The researcher Dave Rossi mentions this on Jesse Michels's show, drawing on the website for Garyaev's "linguistic wave genetics", Garyaev's idea that genes respond to waves and language. Rossi tells it as an example of healing through shape and structure rather than medicine.
gate-crashing-bobby-kennedy-s-funeral-at: In 1968 a young Peter Levenda, a writer the episode bills as a historian of the CIA, says he slipped uninvited into the funeral of the politician Bobby Kennedy at St. Patrick's Cathedral in New York. By his account, an official walked up and asked, "Russian Orthodox representatives?", and he answered, "No, Sloanic Orthodox representatives", which got him in among mourners such as Rose Kennedy and Jackie Onassis. Levenda tells it as his own adventure and points to a still photograph of the funeral procession.
gate-started-by-sidney-marland-in-1972-p: GATE, a US school program for gifted and talented children, was started in 1972 by an official named Sidney Marland, according to Michels, who says so himself in an episode about a guest who says he was taken into a UFO program as a child. Michels floats the idea that the program may have served as a funnel, picking out unusual children for secret government work, and he brings in the senator Frank Church alongside it; if true, a school program would have been a recruiting channel.
gate-testing-and-grooming-by-outside-psy: A man named Jordan Jose says that in 2004 or 2005, as a child in Springville, New York, he was tested by a gifted and talented education programme, sometimes called GATE or TAG. He says they gave him the Woodcock test of achievement, a standard school achievement test, and he ties this to outside psychologists picking him out and grooming him. Jose tells it as his own experience, in an interview about being taken into a secret UFO programme as a child, which he presents as the start of that story.
gauge-theory-economics-and-dale-jorgenso: The mathematician Eric Weinstein says that in the 1990s at Harvard, work he did with Pia Malaney applying gauge theory, a branch of mathematics used in physics, to economics was badly received by the economics department. He tells it from his own experience, singling out one man, Dale Jorgenson, then chairman of the department, as the chief opponent, and he names the politicians Bob Packwood and Daniel Patrick Moynihan in the story. He tells it as an example of how established institutions push back against unwelcome new ideas.
gauntlet-like-object-with-moving-hierogl: In 2014, at a Navy research base in Indiana called Naval Surface Warfare Center Crane, a man named Randy Anderson says he saw a glove-like object, like an armoured gauntlet, with a display above it where strange symbols appeared and moved. He tells it as his own experience, describing "a mirage type of effect" and "hieroglyphic symbols that I started to see appear." If true, it would mean the military holds technology nobody can explain.
gec-marconi-scientist-deaths-during-star: Between 1982 and 1990, 25 engineers and computer scientists working for GEC Marconi, a British defence electronics company, died one after another, all of them on some of Britain's most secret defence projects. These were the years of the American missile-defence plan nicknamed Star Wars. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, as part of an episode about scientists going missing, where a run of deaths like this would suggest a pattern rather than chance.
geller-2019-radio-interview-puharich-dru: According to a researcher named Greg Malatzi, the self-described psychic Uri Geller said on a radio show around 2019 that a researcher named Puharich, who worked with him in the 1970s, had experimented on him with mushrooms and hypnosis. Malatzi passes this on second-hand. It would mean that some of Geller's famous early experiences were shaped by drugs and hypnosis.
geller-bends-a-spoon-during-the-film-int: While a film crew was interviewing him, a man named Uri Geller bent a spoon in front of them. A researcher named Greg Malatzi says he was there for that interview, and he adds that he does not know how Geller did it.
geller-boards-a-landed-ufo-in-the-sinai-: Around 1971 or 1972, a UFO is said to have landed in the Sinai Desert, and Uri Geller, a performer famous for claiming psychic powers, went into a kind of trance, walked on board, and came back out holding a pen. The researcher Greg Malatzi sums up the story, which comes from a book about Geller by Andrija Puharich, the researcher who studied him. If true, Geller's powers would be tied to direct contact with a craft.
geller-teleported-from-new-york-city-to-: A man named Uri Geller was walking down a street in New York City, around 1973, and was teleported to Ossining, a town up the Hudson River in New York state. A researcher named Greg Malatzi tells it, giving the year as "1973, I think", and he ties it to a man named Andrija Puharich, who worked with Geller, and to a home movie Puharich shot on Super 8 film of a screened porch. If true, it would mean Geller's body moved miles in an instant.
gemini-11-object-flyover-and-battery-dra: During Gemini 11, a two-man NASA spaceflight in 1966, an unknown object is said to have passed the capsule while its batteries drained, first "Battery Charlie" and then "battery C". Michels reads this from the mission transcripts with the astronaut Pete Conrad and his crewmate, named only as Gordon, and later says he talked it over with a man named Kevin Knuth, coming away thinking "there was an actual UFO around Gemini 11 that caused this electromagnetic outage". In that later telling he also credits the online UFO commentator Chris Ramsay and points to a photo from NASA's archive.
gemini-7-frank-borman-s-bogey-at-10-o-cl: During the 1965 Gemini 7 flight, a two-man NASA mission in Earth orbit, astronaut Frank Borman reported a "bogey," pilot slang for an unknown object, high at his ten o'clock, separate from his rocket's booster, which he placed at two o'clock. Michels tells it from the flight audio, arguing in a debate with a skeptic that this shows Borman saw something he could not identify. In a later episode he ties the audio to a government release of files on unidentified anomalous phenomena, the official term for UFOs, by the Department of War, the new name for the US defence department.
gemini-ufo-audio-and-airbrushed-ufo-in-n: During Gemini, NASA's two-astronaut spaceflight program of the 1960s, there is said to be audio of a UFO, and a NASA textbook known as the Simpkinson textbook is said to show a UFO that was airbrushed. Michels tells this himself, crediting his friend Chris Ramsay, host of a show called Area 52, for bringing the textbook to light.
gene-cernan-s-flashes-and-blinking-objec: The astronaut Gene Cernan, the last man to walk on the moon in 1972, saw bizarre flashes and distant blinking objects in space, and was even hit by blinding flashes of light in the dark while he slept. Michels tells this himself, drawing on a release of UFO files by the US defense department. If true, it would mean strange things were seen even on the Apollo moon missions.
gene-roddenberry-channeling-session-with: Gene Roddenberry, the man Michels ties to Star Trek, is said to have sat in on sessions where a woman claimed beings were speaking through her. This was in Ossining, New York, sometime between 1973 and 1976. A researcher named Greg Malatzi says the group was Roddenberry, a man named Andrija Puharich, and Phyllis Schlemmer, a channeler, meaning someone who says other beings talk through her. Malatzi points to a tape of the session kept in Puharich's archive. Michels tells it differently, without a source and without Puharich: he says Roddenberry was inspired by Schlemmer, makes the link to Star Trek, and brings in the defense contractor EG&G. If true, it would mean a famous science fiction show grew partly out of claimed contact with non-human beings.
general-exon-held-a-roswell-body-like-a-: In 1947, after something came down near Roswell, New Mexico, an Air Force general named Arthur Exon is said to have held one of the bodies, which he likened to a big insect, when the debris and bodies were brought to Air Materiel Command, the Air Force's equipment and testing command at Wright Field in Ohio. The writer Whitley Strieber tells it, repeating what he says Exon told him. If true, it would mean bodies, not only wreckage, came out of Roswell.
general-moelner-the-secret-craft-filled-: A secret American aircraft was built only to fill a gap in spying from the air, and once it had done that job the military went back to using spy satellites. That is the account of a general named General Moelner, as passed on by the aviation journalist Nick Cook, who says he takes the general's advice at face value. If true, it would explain why such a craft could be built and then quietly retired.
general-muellner-s-retirement-day-interv: The writer Nick Cook says he interviewed General George Muellner, who ran research and development for the US Air Force, on the day Muellner retired in 1998, and asked him about Aurora, a secret American aircraft that was rumoured to exist. Cook tells this from his own experience and points to a documentary called Billion Dollar Secret. If the general said anything about Aurora, it would come from a man who was in a position to know about the Air Force's most secret aircraft.
general-neil-mccasland-goes-missing-2020: Neil McCasland, a retired senior US Air Force general, is said to have gone missing from his home in New Mexico. Jesse Michels tells it several times. He says McCasland once ran the Air Force's research laboratory at Wright-Patterson base and sat on the committee that oversees the most secret military programs. He also says McCasland was a source for the musician Tom DeLonge's Secret Machines books, which DeLonge calls fiction but Michels treats as disclosure. In one episode Michels sets the scene: a late Friday morning, February 27, 2026, on Quail Run Court in Albuquerque, below the Sandia Mountains. He draws on a 911 call recording and the local sheriff's office. The filmmaker Jeremy Corbell also brings it up, noting that a man "charged with protecting our national security" is missing. Michels raises it because a man with such secret knowledge vanishing would be strange.
general-roya-makes-him-a-warrant-officer: Between 1977 and 1979, at Army headquarters in the United States, a general he calls Roya told him, "I'm going to make you a warrant officer," a rank between enlisted soldiers and commissioned officers, and later made him a chief warrant officer. The former Army man Joe McMoneagle tells this about his own career, as part of how he came to be placed in the special work he did for the Army.
general-spaatz-flew-to-texas-during-rosw: During the 1947 Roswell affair, when a crashed object was recovered near Roswell, New Mexico, the senior Air Force general Carl Spaatz is said to have flown to Texas, where the recovered parts were supposedly taken before going on to Wright-Patterson, an Air Force base in Ohio. An online researcher who goes by RedPandaKoala tells this without naming a source, also mentioning the scientist John G. Trump. It is told as a sign that the recovery mattered to the very top of the military.
general-starbird-leaves-johnston-island-: In 1962, during Operation Dominic, a series of US nuclear weapons tests in the Pacific, General Alfred Starbird is said to have left Johnston Island, the small island used as a test base, at 4 a.m. on the night of Bluegill Triple Prime, one of the test shots. Michels tells this from the writings of a man named William Ogle, along with the logs of a navy ship, the USS Summit County, in an episode with a former presidential advisor about handling UFO material. He offers the sudden departure as a detail worth noticing.
general-stubblebine-recruits-buchanan-in: In the 1980s an Army general named Albert Stubblebine, who was hunting for soldiers with mind-over-matter talent, brought a sergeant named Lyn Buchanan to Fort Meade, an Army base in Maryland, to join a unit practising remote viewing, the claimed ability to describe distant places with the mind alone. Buchanan, telling Michels his own story, says Stubblebine got up in his face and asked, 'Did you kill my computers with your mind?' Buchanan also points to the book The Men Who Stare at Goats, which wrote about this world of Army psychic research.
general-stubblebine-s-2-billion-offer-19: A UFO campaigner named Steven Greer says that in 1992 a retired Army general named Albert Stubblebine offered him $2 billion, and Michels describes Stubblebine as first on the scene, seemingly trying to recruit Greer into a government programme. A researcher who goes by UAPGerb adds, citing a collection of documents and emails he calls the DPI archive, that the money was meant to buy Greer's organisation, known as CSETI, and fold it into Stubblebine's own work. Told this way, it suggests insiders wanted to bring Greer's efforts under their control.
general-tells-varginha-driver-what-he-sa: In 1996, around Varginha, a town in Brazil where many say a strange creature was captured by the military, a soldier says a general told him that what he had witnessed was "super natural". The soldier, who speaks only as "military X" and says he drove in the operation, tells it first-hand, and his account appears with the film Moment of Contact. If true, it would mean senior officers knew the event was something out of the ordinary.
generals-without-clearance-turned-away-a: In the 1990s, according to a former NASA doctor named Greg Rogers, three-star generals on vacation in Florida would sometimes drive up to the gate at Cape Canaveral Air Force Station and get turned away because they did not have the right clearance. Rogers says he saw this himself, and he tells it to show how tightly the base guarded access.
genesis-two-lights-matched-to-the-cosmic: The opening of the Book of Genesis, the story goes, describes two separate lights, and the second one matches the faint leftover glow of the early universe that astronomers call the cosmic microwave background. Greg Rogers, a former NASA doctor, offers this as his own reading, saying the moment "light returned to the universe" is "the light of the second day." If it holds, it would mean the ancient text echoes modern cosmology.
geomagnetic-anomalies-at-ufo-hotspots: Places famous for UFO reports always seem to have odd readings in the Earth's magnetic field, according to Michels, who points to Skinwalker Ranch, a ranch known for reports of strange happenings, and Mount Sangun Mori in Japan, near the Fukushima area and its civilian nuclear power network. Michels says this himself, without naming a source, as a pattern that might hint at why such things show up where they do.
george-ball-s-vietnam-memos-with-dismiss: A former presidential advisor named Harold Malmgren says that around 1968 and 1969 he went through the Nixon transition papers, the files passed on as Richard Nixon took over the White House. He says among them were letters from the diplomat George Ball "pleading" with the president to "downsize this whole Vietnam thing before it blows up in your face," with cover notes from Secretary of State Dean Rusk brushing them aside. Malmgren says he saw these himself, and if true they show clear warnings on Vietnam were dismissed at the top.
george-ellery-hale-s-inspiring-elf-or-sp: The astronomer George Ellery Hale said he got creative ideas from a being he described as an elf or a spirit, according to Jesse Michels. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, in an episode about NASA and the hidden side of science. It would mean some of science's great work was inspired by something beyond the human mind.
george-h-w-bush-as-cia-director-told-of-: When George H. W. Bush, later a US president, took over the CIA, the US spy agency, a briefer started describing a major UAP event (UAP means unidentified aerial phenomena, the official term for UFOs), and Bush said, "What are you talking about? I've never heard of this before." A scientist who has worked with the Pentagon, Eric W. Davis, says Bush told him this himself, and in a later episode Davis names the event as a landing at Holloman Air Force Base in New Mexico in April 1964, raised in Bush's very first briefing, though he says nothing there of Bush turning down film of it. Michels retells it second-hand from Davis, calls it the Holloman footage, and says Bush learned of it by accident, which would mean even the head of the CIA was kept in the dark.
george-h-w-bush-briefed-into-the-uap-rea: George H. W. Bush, the former US president, is said to have been told the truth about unidentified aerial phenomena, the government's term for UFOs. A former Pentagon official named Luis Elizondo says so plainly: Bush senior was briefed into the reality of these objects. The philosopher Jason Jorjani goes further. He says Bush had full access to the UFO file because he was briefed while he was deep inside the national security state. Jorjani ties this to Bush's part in finishing off the Soviet Union, and he brings in Bush's father, Prescott Bush. If true, at least one president knew everything the government knew.
george-h-w-bush-george-w-bush-and-cheney: George H.W. Bush, while he was director of the CIA in 1976, was allegedly told about a so-called legacy program, a secret effort said to hold recovered non-human craft, and later passed what he knew to his son George W. Bush, with Vice President Dick Cheney also said to have a role. Kurt McConnell, a former US Senate staffer, relays this as something he attributes to David Grusch, a former intelligence officer who has testified about such programs. If true, it would mean the secret ran through the CIA and the White House for decades.
george-h-w-bush-says-public-not-ready-fo: Former US president George H. W. Bush, at a campaign event for his son Jeb Bush's run for president around 2015 or 2016, started talking about how the American public is not ready for the truth about UFOs. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, and notes it was well off script for Bush; if true, it would hint that a former president knew something he felt the public could not handle.
george-hunt-williamson-as-adamski-s-hand: George Hunt Williamson, a figure around George Adamski, a man who claimed to meet beings from space in the 1950s, is said to have been a pseudonym for someone who acted as Adamski's handler and had earlier edited material for the Silver Shirts, a 1930s American political movement led by William Dudley Pelley. The philosopher Jason Jorjani lays this out on Michels' show in 2025 as his own research, citing publications named Valor and Closer Encounters. If true, it would mean early contact stories were shaped by people with political ties and hidden identities.
george-knapp-brings-back-russian-ufo-fil: After the Soviet Union fell in the early 1990s, the reporter George Knapp is said to have gone to Russia and brought back a large set of files on Soviet UFO activity. Michels mentions it in passing in a 2024 episode, saying Knapp "brought back all these files" about what Russia had been doing about UFOs. A researcher named Eric W. Davis tells the story at more length in another episode that year. Davis says that when the Soviet Union collapsed, the KGB, the Soviet secret police and spy service, opened its files. Knapp and others went in and found what Davis calls the "Thread Three" documents. According to Davis, these files show that the Soviets had their own crash retrievals, meaning they recovered crashed craft of unknown origin. If so, the United States would not be the only country holding such material. Neither man says he saw the files himself.
george-knapp-footage-off-baja-and-the-ta: The journalist George Knapp has interesting footage of strange things filmed around Baja, the long peninsula on Mexico's Pacific coast. That is how Michels puts it, crediting Knapp but not describing the footage. He adds that on the other side of Mexico, the Gulf city of Tampico seems to be a hotspot for sightings, which would mean the waters on both sides of the country draw this kind of activity.
george-knapp-says-harry-reid-read-hastin: Harry Reid, a powerful US senator, is said to have read Robert Hastings's book UFOs and Nukes, and it was one of the reasons he sought funding for a Pentagon-funded programme that studied UFOs. Hastings, a researcher who writes about UFOs near nuclear weapons sites, says the journalist George Knapp told him this in 2023, asking if he knew. If true, it would mean his book helped start the government's own UFO study.
george-knapp-urges-lazar-to-go-public-19: In Las Vegas in 1989, Bob Lazar, a man who says he saw secret craft while working for the government, was told by the local journalist George Knapp that going public was the only way to keep himself safe. Lazar tells this himself, quoting Knapp as saying, "you got to get the information out publicly because that's the only way". It is the start of how Lazar's story came to be broadcast.
george-smith-deciphers-the-tablets-start: A man named George Smith got hold of a set of ancient clay tablets, brought them back to the British Museum in London, and spent the next ten years studying them, starting with the Epic of Gilgamesh, an ancient poem from Mesopotamia. The researcher Matt LaCroix tells this in the 1870s setting without naming a source. He tells it because it is how these ancient texts first came to be read in the modern world.
george-trimble-s-1956-claim-on-cancellin: In 1956, according to Jesse Michels, an aviation executive named George S. Trimble of the Martin Corporation, an American aircraft maker, said: "We're already working on nuclear fuels and equipment to cancel out gravity." Michels says he found the quote in a 1956 article in Jane's Defense Weekly, a military trade publication, and brings it up as evidence that big aerospace firms were openly chasing anti-gravity technology in the 1950s.
george-w-bush-considered-ufo-disclosure-: President George W. Bush thought about publicly revealing what the government knows about UFOs, and discussed it with his national security adviser Stephen Hadley. Michels says this is now public knowledge through the physicist Hal Puthoff, a long-time researcher in this field, which would mean a sitting president seriously weighed telling the public.
george-w-bush-s-disclosure-net-assessmen: President George W. Bush's administration is said to have quietly studied whether to tell the public what the government knows about UFOs. Michels tells this several times, each time crediting a researcher named Hal Puthoff, who he says is on record about it. According to that account, Bush, Vice President Dick Cheney and national security adviser Stephen Hadley ran a kind of formal review of what disclosure would look like. In one telling Michels adds that the panel decided it was not worth it, and in another that those involved read The Three-Body Problem, a science fiction novel about contact with aliens, as part of the exercise, a detail he also links to Joe Rogan. A researcher guest on another episode says Puthoff himself was asked by the Bush administration to take part. It matters to the tellers because it would mean the White House took the question seriously enough to plan for it.
georges-st-pierre-s-ce5-sessions-bring-o: Georges St-Pierre, a famous fighter from the UFC, the biggest professional mixed martial arts league, says that when he holds CE5 sessions, group meditations meant to invite UFOs to appear, glowing orbs show up in the sky "a lot." Michels passes this on from a phone call he had with St-Pierre, as part of a point about how many people now report such sightings.
georgetown-pub-source-it-s-all-about-con: In a pub in the Georgetown neighbourhood of Washington, D.C., around 2018, one of the first things a source told Ross Coulthart, a guest who speaks of his own sources, was that the UFO subject is "all about consciousness". Coulthart tells it himself and does not name the source. He brings it up because it would mean the phenomenon is tied to the mind rather than only to machines.
georgia-power-only-his-house-lost-a-leg-: In 2017, a man named Mario Woods, a former guard at a nuclear weapons site, says his house in Georgia lost part of its electric power while no other house did. He says a supervisor at the power company Georgia Power told him, "you lit up our board downtown like the Fourth of July." Woods tells Michels this as part of his account of a UFO abduction, and he mentions photos of the transformer and the researcher Robert Hastings.
gerchsheimer-tricks-schauberger-into-sig: In 1957 a man named Carl Gerchsheimer is said to have tricked the Austrian inventor Viktor Schauberger into signing all his inventions and ideas over to the United States, after which they were labeled atomic energy research. Michels tells this himself, naming the writer Nick Cook among his sources, in a documentary about Townsend Brown, a scientist he says built UFOs for the CIA. If true, it would mean the US quietly took over an inventor's work and hid it under another name.
german-group-reproducing-the-effect-2020: A group in Germany is said to be reproducing a propulsion effect that a NASA scientist named Charles Buhler says his own team has achieved, thrust described in the episode as antigravity propulsion. Buhler says it himself: "There's another group I'm working with in Germany who's reproducing this." If so, the effect would not rest on his lab's results alone.
german-nuclear-tests-seen-over-the-balti: Nazi Germany carried out two nuclear weapons tests between late 1944 and early 1945, seen by eyewitnesses near the Baltic Sea, according to the researcher Jason Jorjani. He says "there are some eyewitness reports" of the tests but does not name them. If true, it would mean Germany had working atomic weapons before the war ended.
german-perforated-metal-found-at-roswell: A kind of perforated metal, meaning metal full of tiny holes, that Germany developed in the 1940s was later found at Roswell, the New Mexico town where a reported crash in 1947 became the most famous UFO story. The writer Jason Jorjani says this on Michels's show, drawing on the former Army officer Philip J. Corso. If it is true, it would link the Roswell debris to secret wartime German technology.
german-saucer-airframe-with-boundary-lay: In Germany, sometime in the 1930s or 40s, engineers are said to have come up with a saucer-shaped craft with suction vents all around its edge, meant to pull in the thin layer of air flowing over the surface. The researcher Jason Jorjani describes this without naming a source, in an episode about what he calls Hitler's secret UFO program. He tells it as evidence that Germany was working on real saucer-shaped aircraft.
german-silver-sighting-balloons-explain-: The shiny silver spheres that pilots reported during the Second World War may have been German balloons: in 1944 Germany was using metallic silver balloons as sighting balloons. Mick West, a well-known UFO skeptic, makes this point while debating Michels. He offers it as an ordinary explanation for sightings often counted as early UFOs.
german-submarine-carrying-uranium-to-jap: In 1945 a German submarine headed for Japan was stopped, and it carried uranium, engineers and parts in pieces, according to the writer Peter Levenda, who calls it "that famous submarine" without naming a source. He says J. Robert Oppenheimer, the scientist who led the American atomic bomb project, supposedly visited it at a crucial moment "because he couldn't figure out how to make the freaking bomb work." If true, it would mean Nazi materials and know-how helped finish the American bomb.
german-windhund-bomber-tracking-technolo: Germany had a piece of technology for tracking enemy bombers that went by the German name Windhund, meaning greyhound. A researcher named Nick Cook mentions it from memory ("I seem to remember"), without naming a source. He brings it up as one of the German wartime technical projects that he connects to stories of advanced craft.
gertrude-schmeidler-sheep-goat-studies-1: Gertrude Schmeidler, a parapsychologist, someone who studies claims of psychic ability, is said to have been active in the 1950s, 60s and 70s, and is known for 'sheep-goat' studies, which compared people who believe in psychic ability ('sheep') with people who doubt it ('goats'). The researcher Herb Metts names her without giving a source, in an episode about a psychic spy program run by the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency. He mentions her as part of the background of serious research into psychic ability.
getting-angry-fries-50-million-of-comput: In the 1980s, at a US military listening station in Augsburg, Germany, a former Army sergeant named Lyn Buchanan says that a moment of his own anger knocked out about $50 million worth of computers. He tells it as something he did himself: "the entire field station went down." He tells it as a sign that the mind can affect machines directly.
getting-bob-lazar-onto-joe-rogan-s-show-: In 2019, Bob Lazar, a man who says he once worked on alien craft at a secret Nevada site, was talked into going on the popular podcaster Joe Rogan's show over a speakerphone call. Jeremy Corbell says he took part. As he tells it, he called Lazar and said that he and his colleague George Knapp were coming out for a screening of their film in Michigan, and that was how the appearance was set up.
ghislaine-maxwell-s-swedish-male-aides-a: Ghislaine Maxwell, the associate of the financier Jeffrey Epstein, kept young live-in male aides at her townhouse on Manhattan's Upper East Side, and one of them found his hair being collected. A philosopher named Jason Jorjani tells Michels this, citing an article by a former Swedish aide, and if true it would point to an interest in these men's genetic material. Jorjani's own article "Ocean Outlaw: A Portrait of Ghislaine Maxwell", published 29 July 2025, says she chose men who were "almost exclusively blond, and blue-eyed", swapped them every three months on tourist visas, mostly from Sweden, and that the aide Rasmus Alpsjö "has reported that he noticed that his hair was being collected from his pillows and the bathroom he used", but it does not name or link the aide's article.
ghislaine-maxwell-s-terramar-project-as-: The TerraMar Project, an ocean group run by Ghislaine Maxwell, a long-time associate of the financier Jeffrey Epstein, was really an elite network of trading routes and shipping containers moving off the grid, to places like the waters near Antarctica, according to the researcher Jay Anderson. He says it was run by huge elites and ties it to the British businessman Richard Branson's island, passing this on from others. If true, the project would have been a hidden private network for the very rich.
ghost-murmur-quantum-sensor-detects-a-so: A sensor called Ghost Murmur, which uses quantum physics to pick up very faint signals, is said to have found a soldier who needed rescuing somewhere in the Middle East, possibly Iran or Afghanistan, by detecting his heartbeat. Michels tells this himself, linking it to Lockheed Martin, a large American weapons maker, and without naming his source. If true, it would mean such sensing has moved from theory into real rescue work.
giant-flown-to-a-base-in-qatar-2005: After US troops captured a giant about 12 feet tall in Afghanistan, its body was transferred to a military base in Qatar, around 2005. Tim Alberino, a documentary maker who tells the Afghanistan giant story, says this second-hand from what he was told. If true, it would mean the body was moved out of the country and kept by the military.
giant-found-dead-at-a-table-with-oysters: Sometime between 1978 and 1981, at Santa Anastasia in Sardinia, people opening a sealed tower are said to have found a giant sitting at a table, dead, with oysters in front of him. The filmmaker Tim Alberino passes this on from what he was told: "there was a giant seated at a table and he was dead."
giant-kills-a-recon-team-in-a-cave-and-i: In 2005, near Kandahar in Afghanistan, a giant humanoid is said to have killed a team of American scouts in a cave and was then shot dead by other soldiers. Tim Alberino passes this on from a man who says he was there. He describes the soldiers finding "this gigantic humanoid was eating on one of them." Michels retells it more briefly and gives no date or place: he says the man and his unit claim to have fought the giant in the caves, which the episode title puts at 12 feet tall. If true, it would mean giant beings are real and that the US military has killed one.
giant-progenitor-comet-behind-the-taurid: Some 25,000 to 30,000 years ago, a giant comet with a core perhaps 50 to 60 miles across was captured into an orbit inside Jupiter's, and its breakup is said to have created the Taurid meteor stream, a belt of debris that Earth passes through each year. The researcher Randall Carlson tells this, without naming a source, drawing on the astronomers Victor Clube and William Napier and on William Asher. If true, the debris from that comet could have struck Earth in prehistoric times.
giant-raccoons-and-the-toe-implant: Steve Colbern, a scientist who studies objects said to be alien implants in people's bodies, says that one night when he was alone at his house in Fillmore, California, he saw giant raccoons in his backyard. He tells it as his own strange experience, tied to an object found in his toe and to the work of a researcher of such implants named Roger Leir. For him it is part of what he takes as a sign of contact.
giant-skeletons-dug-up-in-excavations-of: The researcher Randall Carlson says that old accounts of digs into the great ancient earth mounds of the United States describe, over and over, giant human skeletons seven, eight and sometimes nine feet tall. He summarises this without naming a single source, pointing broadly to 19th-century archives, the records of the Bureau of American Ethnology, a US government office that studied Native American peoples, and early papers of the Smithsonian, the national museum, and he mentions the writer Graham Hancock. If true, it would suggest a lost chapter of the continent's ancient past.
giant-skull-carried-by-an-excavator-and-: Some time between 1978 and 1981, near Santa Anastasia on the Italian island of Sardinia, an excavator worker found a skull so large that he and his wife had to carry it together, and they brought it into the church. A guest named Tim Alberino tells it, passing on what he was told, without naming the man. He offers it as evidence that giants once lived there.
giants-driven-out-by-joshua-settle-on-sa: When the biblical leader Joshua conquered the land of Canaan, many of the giants who were not killed were driven out and ended up settling on the Mediterranean island of Sardinia. The researcher Tim Alberino puts this forward himself, reading it out of the Old Testament, saying he thinks Joshua "drove out a lot of the giants that weren't killed in the conquest." It would explain, in his view, where the giants of the Bible went.
gibbons-calls-in-pandolfi-to-brief-on-th: In the 1990s, President Clinton's science adviser John Gibbons called in a government scientist named Ron Pandolfi to give a briefing on the Rockefeller Initiative, a push tied to the Rockefeller name to get the White House to look into UFO matters such as the 1947 Roswell crash in New Mexico. The researcher Grant Cameron tells this, saying "this has been established that Ron was called to do the briefing." It matters because it would place UFO questions inside the White House at the time.
gifted-and-talented-programs-as-a-funnel: Michels says that school programmes for gifted and talented children seem to have acted as a funnel for recruiting young people into deeper, secret programmes that study psychic ability. He offers it partly as his own reading, and partly credits it to Jake Barber, a former helicopter pilot who says he retrieved a UFO, who went public about the gifted and talented programmes, and to two people named Jordan Jose and Julia Mosbury. If true, it would mean children were being picked out for this work through ordinary schools.
gifted-education-advisor-assigns-esp-cro: A researcher named Deep Prasad says that as a schoolboy, the teacher in charge of his gifted-students programme kept assigning him projects on ESP, meaning extrasensory perception, then on crop circles, the patterns flattened into farm fields, and then on stories of people taken by aliens. He tells it from his own memory, as an early nudge toward the subjects he later took up.
gifted-kids-program-with-esp-training-fr: As a boy near Vancouver, Canada, Deep Prasad was in a program for gifted children, and he says a teacher there named Miss Kaur got him to look into ESP. ESP, or extrasensory perception, is the idea that people can sense things without the ordinary senses. Prasad, now a researcher, tells this as something from his own childhood.
gillibrand-and-rubio-s-push-for-accounta: US senators such as Kirsten Gillibrand and Marco Rubio have spent recent years, it is said, not chasing public disclosure about UFOs but chasing accountability: finding out about "rogue programs" they never knew existed that were "controlling groundbreaking world shaking information." The analyst Matthew Pines gives this as his own reading of their motives, without naming a source. If true, it would mean Congress sees the issue mainly as hidden programmes slipping out of its oversight.
gimbal-j-hook-path-matches-aircrew-radar: In the Gimbal video, a 2015 Navy infrared recording of an object off Florida, the object is said to make a vertical U-turn, a "J hook path," that matches what the aircrew say the radar-tracked object did. The national security writer Marik von Rennenkampff makes this case from his own study of the footage, calling it "a spectacular match" with eyewitness accounts of a reversal of direction "with no radius of turn." If true, the video would back the pilots' account of a craft moving in ways no known aircraft can.
gimbal-object-flying-with-a-v-shaped-fle: The object in the Gimbal video, a 2015 Navy recording of an unidentified object off the US East Coast, may have been flying with a formation of other objects in a V shape, what the aircrew called "the fleet". A guest named Marik von Rennenkampff raises this in a debate with a skeptic, drawing on a man named Ryan Graves. If true, it would mean the object was not alone but part of a group.
gimbal-object-is-a-distant-jet-2015: The object in the Gimbal video, a 2015 Navy infrared clip filmed off Florida that former Navy fighter pilot Ryan Graves has spoken about, is a distant jet, says Mick West, a well-known UFO skeptic. He offers it as his own hypothesis from studying the video. If he is right, the famous clip shows an ordinary plane, not something unknown.
gimbal-object-wobbles-after-video-cuts-o: In the Gimbal video, a 2015 Navy infrared clip filmed off Florida showing an object that appears to rotate, the object is said to keep wobbling after the recording stops. The commentator Marik von Rennenkampff says this is according to the air crew, citing the Navy fighter pilot Ryan Graves. He brings it up because it would mean the object's motion was real and not just something the camera did.
gimbal-pilot-confirms-the-lns-radar-targ: In the Gimbal video, a 2015 Navy clip shot off the US East Coast by a fighter jet's infrared camera that shows an odd object rotating in flight, the pilots' voices on the audio are said to confirm the object was the jet's "LNS," meaning "launch and steering," the target the radar had locked onto. Marik von Rennenkampff, a guest arguing in a debate episode against the skeptic Mick West, makes this point from the video's own audio. If true, it means the object was tracked by radar too, not just a trick of the camera.
gimbal-radar-returns-as-interference-or-: The radar readings tied to the Gimbal video, a 2015 Navy recording of an unidentified object off the US East Coast, may have come from a distant jet, with the radar going wrong and making it look like something else. A UFO skeptic named Mick West says someone actually suggested this to him as a possibility, and he does not name the person. If true, it would mean the radar did not show anything strange after all.
gimbal-recorded-by-ryan-graves-squadron-: The Gimbal video, a 2015 Navy recording off Florida of an unexplained object that seems to rotate in the air, was filmed by the squadron of a Navy fighter pilot named Ryan Graves. The analyst Marik von Rennenkampff says so on Michels's show, calling it Graves's squadron, which he names as "VFA1, the Red Rippers" (the Navy fighter squadron VFA-11). It ties the famous video to a pilot who has spoken publicly about such sightings.
gimbal-rotation-is-a-camera-artifact-201: The skeptical investigator Mick West argues that the apparent rotation of the object in the Gimbal video, a 2015 Navy infrared clip filmed off Florida, is a camera artifact rather than a craft turning. He says it is an optical effect, such as glare, that seems to rotate because of a mechanism inside the camera system that turns the image to keep it level, and he also says the object's shape itself is a camera artifact. If he is right, the video would not show a strange craft moving at all.
gimbal-ufo-video-argument-between-marik-: Two men have been in a running public argument over the Gimbal video, a military video of an unidentified flying object: on one side Marik von Rennenkampff, on the other a man named Mick West. The journalist Michael Shellenberger mentions the dispute on Jesse Michels's show in November 2024, naming both men. He brings it up as an example of the fight over whether such videos show something truly unexplained.
gimbal-video-audio-a-whole-fleet-of-them: In the Gimbal video, a 2015 Navy infrared recording of an object off the US East Coast that seems to turn on its side as it flies, an unnamed member of the Navy aircrew can be heard saying, "there's a whole fleet of them. Look on ASA," meaning the radar display in the cockpit. The voice belongs to someone who was there that day. It suggests the crew were tracking a whole group of objects, and not just the one on camera.
girls-creature-and-hospital-being-were-t: In Varginha, Brazil, in 1996, the strange creature some girls said they saw and the being later said to be held in a hospital were, by this account, one and the same. The documentary filmmaker James Fox draws this conclusion from his own research and from people such as Italo Venturelli, a witness he cites: 'the capture occurred. It had to be the same being.' If true, it would mean a living creature was caught and taken into a hospital.
girls-on-horseback-turned-back-on-her-bi: On March 25, 1948, girls riding horses toward Hart Canyon outside Aztec, New Mexico, are said to have been stopped and sent back, on the same day a flying saucer reportedly came down there. Scott Ramsey, who has spent years interviewing people about the Aztec case, says one of the women told him this. When he asked how she could be sure of the date, she said: "Cuz it was my birthday." If true, it would put the crash and a guarded roadblock on a fixed day.
giza-mapped-to-orion-s-belt-around-10-60: The three great pyramids at Giza are said to be laid out to match the three stars of Orion's Belt, a line of stars in the constellation Orion. Michels says the layout "mapped fully" to the belt around 10,600 BC, when the sky shifted into that position. The writer Graham Hancock, known for his books on lost ancient civilizations, talks about the pyramids lining up with Orion's Belt without giving a date. He says the belt "has always, across many cultures, been the place of ascension of souls." If true, it would mean the builders laid out the ground to mirror the heavens.
giza-pink-granite-hauled-500-miles-from-: All the pink granite found across the Giza plateau in Egypt came from the Aswan quarry, about 500 miles to the south. A researcher named Matt LaCroix tells this. He uses it to show how far the builders moved huge blocks of stone, and how hard that would have been.
giza-pyramid-stones-may-have-been-mixed-: The stones of the pyramids at Giza in Egypt may not have been cut and hauled at all, but mixed and poured into place. A guest named Joe McMoneagle suggests this himself, without naming a source, and links it to a book called The Ultimate Time Machine. If true, it would change how the pyramids were built.
giza-wide-model-presented-at-the-malta-c: At a conference in Malta in 2024, researchers presented a model of the whole Giza plateau in Egypt showing underground vertical features linked to cube-shaped features beneath the pyramids and the Sphinx, according to the researcher Jeffrey Drum. Drum describes the model, which he ties to the radar researcher Filippo Biondi. If the features are real, there would be a large hidden structure under the pyramids, which Drum's episode frames as an energy grid.
glasnost-era-russian-crashed-craft-us-as: In the early days of glasnost, when the Soviet Union opened up and Russia and America were briefly friendly, Russia is said to have told America that it had a crashed craft, and an American astronaut was sent to help recover it. The Australian journalist Ross Coulthart tells it as a story that came up from his sources, without naming them. If true, the two rivals would have quietly cooperated on a crashed craft.
