glenn-gaffney-allegedly-blocked-ufo-mate: A former CIA official named Glenn Gaffney is said to have blocked a transfer of UFO material from the defence company Lockheed Martin to the space company Bigelow Aerospace. Michels tells this in 2026, saying a couple of people made the claim, one of them under oath in front of Congress. If true, it would mean crashed-craft material sits with private companies and officials decide who gets it.
glenn-gaffney-blocked-transfer-of-nhi-ma: In 2008 an official named Glenn Gaffney is said to have blocked the move of exotic technology of non-human origin, held at Lockheed Martin, the defense company, to Bigelow Aerospace, a private space company that was supposed to receive it. Michels tells this himself, saying there is congressional testimony about it and pointing to the first volume of a historical report from the Pentagon's current office for unexplained aerial reports.
glenn-gaffney-head-of-the-crash-retrieva: Eric W. Davis, a physicist who has worked on Pentagon studies of UFOs, says that Glenn Gaffney, who ran the CIA's science and technology branch from about 2008 to 2012, headed a programme to recover crashed craft in that period. Davis says he wanted to question him, but "he refused to talk to us".
glenn-gaffney-named-as-a-leader-of-the-l: Glenn Gaffney, who ran the science and technology branch of the CIA, the US spy agency, is said to have been one of the last leaders of the "legacy program", a supposed secret effort to hold and study crashed craft that are not of human make. Michels says this himself, telling it as something that "a lot of people" say, without naming them. If true, it would put a senior intelligence official at the head of that work.
glenn-gaffney-on-aaro-s-board-2020: Glenn Gaffney, who was the CIA's director of science and technology, sat on the board of AARO, the Pentagon office set up in the 2020s to investigate unexplained objects in the sky. Michels says this himself, without naming a source, in a conversation about how the Pentagon's UFO work is organised, as a sign of how closely the CIA is tied to that office.
glenn-gaffney-said-to-have-run-the-crash: Glenn Gaffney, once the CIA's director of science and technology, was rumoured to run the whole "legacy crash retrieval program", a supposed secret effort to recover and study crashed craft that are not man-made. Michels passes this on himself as a rumour, without naming who told it. If true, it would mean a senior CIA official ran the effort.
glenn-martin-company-employs-louis-witte: In the 1950s the aircraft maker Glenn Martin Company had a research unit, which Michels calls the Research Institute for Advanced Study, where the physicist Louis Witten, father of the physicist Edward Witten, worked on gravity, and some say anti-gravity, with ties to Wright Field, the Air Force base in Ohio later called Wright-Patterson. The mathematician Eric Weinstein brings it up with a hedge ("I believe"), adding Johns Hopkins University and names like the physicist Sheldon Glashow, while Michels states it flatly and links a Martin vice-president named George Trimble and the inventor Thomas Townsend Brown. Witten himself, in recorded interviews, says "the reason there was a laboratory at Wright Field was to find out what we were doing and to help us do it," and that he got a contract from them to study gravity, which he did "very happily," which would mean the military was quietly funding gravity research decades ago.
glimpsed-classified-uap-photos-via-colle: A former CIA contractor named Bob McGwier says that through colleagues in secret government work he got to see classified photos and other material showing that UAP, the government's term for unidentified aerial phenomena, are real. He tells it as something he saw himself: "photos and other things that said UAP are here."
global-crash-recovery-and-reverse-engine: There are programmes in other countries, outside the United States, that recover crashed unknown craft and try to work out how they function. Jake Barber, a former helicopter pilot who says he flew a UFO retrieval mission himself, passes this on second-hand. It would mean the United States is not the only country holding such craft.
global-ufo-nuclear-link-from-roswell-to-: UFOs are tied to nuclear sites around the world, from Roswell, New Mexico, where a crash many link to UFOs was reported in 1947 and which Michels calls the site of the largest nuclear stockpile of its day, to Fukushima in Japan and Chernobyl in Ukraine, both places of nuclear plant disasters. Michels lays out this connection himself, in his own framing of an episode with a former US Secretary of Energy, without naming a source. If true, it would mean whatever is behind UFOs takes a steady interest in human nuclear power.
glomar-explorer-possibly-dual-use-1974: There are rumours that the Glomar Explorer, a huge deep-sea ship built in 1974 for the Hughes Corporation and sent out into the Pacific, was really meant to go down to the seafloor and find strange objects, like a craft said to rest under the sea. Michels raises this himself, without naming a source, in two episodes. In one he only wonders aloud about the ship and the big company behind it. In the other he says plainly that the rumours have it searching for objects like the one his guest describes, which would mean a hidden purpose behind a famous ship.
glomar-explorer-recovers-a-sunken-soviet: In the 1970s, a huge corporation linked to the billionaire Howard Hughes, the Global Marine Corporation, used a ship called the Glomar Explorer to raise a sunken Soviet submarine from the floor of the Pacific Ocean. The UFO historian Richard Dolan tells this on Michels's show without naming a source and calls it an incredible feat. He uses it as an example of the kind of difficult recovery a big company could pull off.
glowing-disc-photographed-over-property-: In 2016, a glowing disc was photographed over Skinwalker Ranch, a property in Utah's Uinta Basin known for strange reports. The ranch's owner tells this as something he witnessed. He says the first image looked almost like the Millennium Falcon, the spaceship from Star Wars.
glowing-hole-in-bedroom-wall-and-electri: Mario Woods, a former guard at a nuclear weapons site, says that in 2017 a glowing hole about four and a half or five feet across appeared in the north wall of his bedroom at his home in Georgia, and the electricity failed. He tells it as something he saw himself, part of the strange experiences he links to being taken by unknown beings.
glowing-orb-ufos-at-pyramid-kuromanta-sh: At Kuromanta, a hill in Akita, Japan that some call a pyramid, glowing balls of light are said to appear, and old Japanese paintings are said to show them. The ancient-sites researcher Geoffrey Drumm tells this from his own research, without naming a particular painting. If true, it would mean the lights have been seen at the site for centuries.
glowing-red-metal-found-in-a-yard-under-: Some time in the 1990s in Zanesville, Ohio, a man saw something hovering over his house that went away as he drove up, and he found a piece of glowing red metal in his yard. A man named Chris Bledsoe, the subject of an episode about a man said to attract UFOs, says the man called him about it, and he passes it on second-hand without naming him. If true, it would mean the craft left something solid behind.
go-fast-email-deleted-under-the-spillage: An email carrying the "Go Fast" video, a 2015 Navy clip of a small object racing over the ocean, was deleted from Navy computer networks under the "spillage" rules, which are used to wipe secret material that ends up somewhere it should not be. A retired Navy admiral named Tim Gallaudet tells this, passing on what he says a Pentagon official named Jay Stratton told him: "when it was deleted they were still not sure whether it was adversary tech or or off-world." If true, it would mean the Navy erased the evidence before it knew whether the object was foreign or not from Earth at all.
go-fast-is-a-wind-blown-balloon-2015: The Go Fast video, a 2015 Navy recording off Jacksonville, Florida that seems to show a small object racing low over the ocean, probably shows nothing more than something like a balloon drifting with the wind. That is the view of Mick West, a well-known skeptic who analyses UFO videos, who says on Michels's show that his hypothesis is that it is "probably just a wind blown object like a balloon." If he is right, the object's apparent speed is an illusion of the camera angle.
go-fast-object-one-of-four-in-line-abrea: The object in Go Fast, a 2015 Navy video filmed off Jacksonville, Florida, that shows a small object skimming over the water, was one of four objects flying side by side, according to the Navy fighter pilot Ryan Graves, who tells it to Michels himself. The commentator Marik von Rennenkampff repeats the same point from Graves. The retired Navy admiral Tim Gallaudet goes further: he says the object was a sphere with no wings, steering surfaces or engines that moved as if under intelligent control, and he rejects the idea, raised by the head of the Pentagon's UFO office, Jon Kosloski, that it only looked fast because of the camera's angle.
go-fast-video-recorded-off-jacksonville-: In January 2015, Navy aircrew flying from the aircraft carrier USS Roosevelt, about 300 miles off the coast of Jacksonville, Florida, are said to have filmed a small object racing low over the ocean. The clip became known as the Go Fast video, named for how quickly the object seemed to move. Michels sets out the date and place himself, as background to a talk with a well-known UFO skeptic. The other telling comes from the aircrew themselves: their recorded cockpit voices are played, and one can be heard saying "Oh my gosh, dude. Wow." So one telling gives the host's account of when and where it happened, and the other gives the reaction of the people who saw it. It matters to the people who tell it because trained military crews, on their own instruments, recorded something they could not name.
gobekli-tepe-as-a-possible-origin-of-civ: Göbekli Tepe, an ancient site of huge carved stones in modern Turkey, is held up by some as a possible birthplace of civilization, older than Egypt. If that is right, people were building on a large scale far earlier than the usual story says. The podcaster Joe Rogan raises it, saying "a lot of people think" civilization may have started there rather than in Egypt. Michels returns to it in several episodes. In one he calls it a burial site "dating as far back as 9000 BC" and built from 50-ton blocks. In a debate with a skeptic he dates it to about 11,000 years ago and says it "rewrites the map" of how old human civilization is, crediting the writer Graham Hancock, his book Fingerprints of the Gods, and National Geographic. In another episode he describes a pattern where every 30 or 40 years a new find pushes the date back, and he suggests Göbekli Tepe may not even be the oldest such site.
gobekli-tepe-as-an-astronomical-calendar: Göbekli Tepe, an ancient site of carved stone pillars in Turkey, may have worked as a sky calendar, with pillars that are really pictures of star constellations. That is the reading of a researcher named Matt LaCroix, who gives it on Michels's show in 2024 without naming a source. If he is right, the people who built it were tracking the slow turning of the stars over very long ages.
gobekli-tepe-built-and-buried-by-survivo: Göbekli Tepe, a hill site in Turkey, holds what is called the oldest temple of giant standing stones, and the story goes that it was built and later buried by people who survived a great disaster. A researcher named Jay Anderson brings it up without naming a source. He says experts had put the area down to simple hunter-gatherers, and then this ancient temple site "pops up out of the ground", which in his telling suggests the past was more advanced than we were taught.
gobekli-tepe-chalices-and-burial-rituals: At Göbekli Tepe, an ancient site said to date back 12,000 years, just before people began farming, archaeologists are said to have dug up chalices tied to rituals, including burial rites. Michels takes this from a book called The Immortality Key by a writer named Brian Muraresku, as a hint that ritual drinks may be older than agriculture itself.
gobekli-tepe-datable-because-it-was-buri: Göbekli Tepe is an ancient stone site in Turkey, and the claim is that it could only be dated because the site is believed to have been buried. A researcher named Matt LaCroix says this in passing, without naming a source, in an episode about something large that he and Michels think happened around 12,000 BC. If he is right, the burial is the one thing that let anyone put an age on the place at all.
gobekli-tepe-pillar-43-as-a-sky-map-of-1: Pillar 43, a carved stone pillar at Göbekli Tepe, a very old ring of standing stones in Turkey, is said to be a map of the night sky as it looked at the summer solstice about 12,500 years ago. A researcher named Graham Hancock tells this without naming a source, calling it "very persuasively an astronomical diagram." If true, people that long ago were already carefully recording the stars.
god-s-divine-council-in-genesis-behold-m: In the Bible's book of Genesis, after the events in the Garden of Eden, God turns to a mysterious council of other beings in heaven and says, "Behold, man has become like us." The researcher Luke Caverns reads this from the text himself and says this divine council is very often overlooked. He points to it because it would suggest the Bible describes other heavenly beings alongside God.
goethe-s-merging-with-strasbourg-cathedr: The German poet Goethe is said to have had an experience of merging with Strasbourg Cathedral, feeling himself become one with the building. Michels tells this drawing on the thinker Rudolf Steiner and a work on Goethe's theory of knowledge, as an example of a way of knowing the world from the inside.
going-back-in-time-in-dreams-with-the-mo: In his dreams, a former CIA officer named Rolf Mowatt-Larssen says he went to a mountain with a group of monks and kept going back in time. He tells it himself, linking it to a figure named Harry Haller in his book, who told him that time is an illusion, and he says the dreams "proved it was an illusion cuz I kept going back in time."
going-public-with-the-find-through-expre: Dennis Asberg, a Swedish treasure hunter who says his team found a strange object on the seafloor, says that in 2011 he went public with the find by talking to a journalist at Expressen, which he calls "a big newspaper" in Stockholm. He tells it as his own decision, and it is how word of the object first got out.
gold-flown-to-geneva-and-gold-certificat: After the Second World War, between about 1947 and 1949, a large hoard of gold was flown out of Europe on US military transport planes and placed in the International Credit Bank in Geneva, Switzerland. Paper gold certificates were then issued against it and used to pay for secret operations against communism. A researcher named Dan Sheehan tells this on Michels's show in 2025, naming the intelligence chief Allen Dulles as part of it but no source for the account, which would mean a hidden fortune funded covert work outside normal government budgets.
golden-calcite-alabaster-altar-of-unknow: An ancient altar in the Lake Van region of Turkey is said to be carved from golden calcite alabaster, a soft, glowing yellow stone, and no one knows where the stone came from. The researcher Matt LaCroix says this to Jesse Michels while describing the site, without naming a source. If true, the stone's unknown origin would add to the mystery of who built the site and how.
golden-orb-escorted-by-helicopters-risin: A huge golden ball of light, pulsing and looking like glowing plasma, rose at 1:30 in the morning from behind Secret Mountain in Arizona with helicopters escorting it, according to the journalist Ross Coulthart, who says he watched it happen. He says he had been told that if he looked at that spot he would see such an orb, and "sure enough up comes this beautiful golden orb, gigantic." In one telling he names the helicopters as Black Hawks, dates it to 2025 and credits a researcher named Melinda Leslie with the tip. He tells it as evidence of a hidden UFO base there.
golf-ball-bounces-off-the-reactor-s-fiel: In the late 1980s, at a secret Nevada site called S4, a co-worker showed Bob Lazar the field around the power source of an alien craft, which Lazar calls the reactor. To show it off, the co-worker took a golf ball and tried to hit the reactor with it, and the ball bounced off the field and hit a ceiling tile. Lazar tells this first-hand and names Barry Castilio and Dennis Mariani in the telling. A former DARPA scientist named John Blitch passes on a version he heard from Lazar. DARPA is the Pentagon's advanced research agency. Blitch's version describes an object the size of a basketball or soccer ball that pushed things away, and it says nothing of a golf ball.
golf-ball-lands-on-frederick-wolfe-s-gra: Rolf Mowatt-Larssen, a former senior CIA officer, says that in 1976, playing golf at Fort Knox in Kentucky, his ball landed in a cemetery on the course, on a gravestone reading "Frederick Wolfe. German soldier died". He tells it as something he lived through, in an episode where he describes himself as a kind of time traveller, so the coincidence carries weight for him.
gorard-and-wolfram-hypergraph-physics-pr: In 2020 and 2021, a physicist named Jonathan Gorard, working with the scientist Stephen Wolfram, is said to have shown that simple networks of linked points, called hypergraphs, can produce both Einstein's theory of gravity and quantum mechanics. A guest named Matthew Pines relays this, calling it Gorard's "breakthrough result" and "really suggestive," linking it to Wolfram's book A New Kind of Science and to a researcher named Xerxes Arsiwalla. If it holds, the two great theories of physics could come from one deeper rule.
gorbachev-says-various-civilizations-hav: Mikhail Gorbachev, the last leader of the Soviet Union, is said to have said in the 1990s that "various civilizations" have made contact with people on Earth. Kiran Ilum Xenov, a former president of one of Russia's republics, who says he himself was taken by aliens in 1997, tells this from his own conversation with Gorbachev.
gordon-cooper-mercury-astronaut-among-pi: Gordon Cooper, one of the first American astronauts and one who spent more time in space than his peers, belongs on the list of pilots who saw UFOs. Michels brings him up himself, without naming a source, while talking with a former Navy fighter pilot, to show that such reports come from highly trained and credible flyers.
gordon-cooper-s-1957-craft-landing-on-ba: In 1957 a flying saucer is said to have passed right over a film crew at an air base, put down three small landing legs and landed on a dry lake bed. The astronaut and test pilot Gordon Cooper tells it himself in a clip shown on the episode. Separately, a man named Charlie Foltz repeats what he says Cooper told him in person: that a craft physically landed on the base while Cooper was there, which, if true, would mean a craft set down in plain view on a military base.
gordon-cooper-s-book-von-braun-worked-on: The rocket engineer Wernher von Braun is said to have told the astronaut Gordon Cooper that they "actually worked on UFO craft" in Nazi Germany. Robert Salas, a former Air Force officer, tells this on Michels' show in 2025, saying it is in a book Cooper wrote, whose title he does not give. If true, it would mean work on such craft began during the Second World War.
gordon-cooper-s-saucer-shaped-craft-flyi: The American pilot and astronaut Gordon Cooper says that in the 1950s he saw a group of craft flying in formation that, on a closer look, had no wings and were saucer shaped. He tells it as something he saw himself: "it turns out they didn't have wings. They were saucer shape." Coming from a trained pilot, it is offered as a sighting that ordinary aircraft cannot explain.
gordon-cooper-visits-puharich-s-ossining: The astronaut Gordon Cooper is said to have visited a lab run by a researcher named Puharich in Ossining, New York, during the 1970s. The researcher Greg Malatzi says Cooper went "many times" and wrote about it in his own book. According to Malatzi, Cooper describes seeing experiments with a Faraday cage, a metal enclosure that blocks electrical signals, and meeting the "space kids." An unnamed researcher guest on the same episode adds that a woman named Valerie Ransone brought Cooper there, in the late 1970s. The story matters to the tellers because it puts a famous astronaut inside a lab doing unusual contact experiments.
gordon-creighton-and-prince-philip-s-int: Steven Greer, a doctor who collects testimony from people claiming inside knowledge of UFOs, says he interviewed Gordon Creighton, a former British military intelligence man who published the UFO magazine Flying Saucer Review. According to Greer, Creighton's material "used to go over to the palace", and Prince Philip, the husband of the British queen, "was very keen on all of this", which would put UFO interest at the top of the British establishment.
gordon-gray-named-in-the-mj12-documents-: An official named Gordon Gray appears in the Majestic 12 papers, leaked documents that describe a top-secret research group President Truman is said to have set up around 1947 to deal with UFOs. The papers list Gray as one of the group's advisers. Michels points this out himself while asking whether a secret program to recover crashed craft existed, and whether Henry Kissinger oversaw it.
gordon-macdonald-said-the-moon-only-make: Gordon MacDonald, a space adviser to President Eisenhower, said the moon only makes sense if it is hollow, according to Jesse Michels. Michels repeats this in four episodes from his reading of MacDonald's work. He calls MacDonald Eisenhower's chief space adviser in one, places him at Columbia University in another, and in another leads into it with the claim that the moon rings like a bell when struck. If true, it would mean the moon may not be a natural body.
gordon-novel-prosecuted-for-burning-down: A man named Gordon Novel was arrested and prosecuted in New Orleans for burning down the office at 555 Camp Street, according to a researcher named Dan Sheehan, who tells it on two episodes without naming a source. Sheehan says the prosecutor was Jim Garrison, and he links that office to Lee Harvey Oswald, the man accused of killing President John F. Kennedy. In one of the two tellings he also names Guy Banister in connection with the office, and in the other he does not.
gordon-novel-shows-ufo-propulsion-drawin: In 1994, at a gathering called the International UFO Congress, a man named Gordon Novel walked up out of the crowd and offered drawings that he said explained how UFOs are propelled, according to the lawyer Dan Sheehan, who was there representing the Harvard psychiatrist John Mack. Sheehan tells it as his own encounter, recalling Novel saying "I've got all these drawings and stuff about the UFOs and how their propulsion system works."
gordon-novel-threatens-sheehan-and-is-la: A man named Gordon Novel once threatened Dan Sheehan, and was later hired by a man named John Alexander as an investigator for NIDS, the National Institute for Discovery Science, a private group that studied unexplained phenomena. Sheehan tells this from his own experience, and he points to the hiring as a surprising link between the two.
gorilla-masks-for-u-2-and-sr-71-test-pil: The test pilots who flew the secret U-2 and SR-71 spy planes were given gorilla masks. They were told to put a mask on if they ever flew close enough to an airliner for its pilot to make eye contact with them. A philosopher named Jason Jorjani tells this from the journalist Annie Jacobsen's book Area 51, and uses it to show how far the government went to hide its secret aircraft from witnesses.
gotthard-tunnel-proof-of-concept-scan-20: A 2024 scan of the Gotthard Tunnel, a very long railway tunnel through the Swiss Alps, is said to be the final proof that a scanning method linked to the researcher Filippo Biondi can see deep underground structures. The researcher Jeffrey Drum presents it as the test case, calling it "the final proof of concept, the Gotthard Tunnel," because the same method is used to claim that a vast energy network lies beneath the pyramids of Egypt.
government-air-to-air-flir-expert-s-emai: An analyst named Marik von Rennenkampff says a government expert on infrared targeting cameras looked at the Gimbal video. That is a Navy infrared clip, filmed off the US East Coast, of an object that seems to rotate. Von Rennenkampff reads out an email in which the expert writes that "the object in the video is definitely maneuvering causing the appearance of rotation." Elsewhere in the same debate he tells it differently, saying the expert called the video "bizarre" on a call, "I've never seen anything like this." He makes the point to Mick West, a UFO skeptic who argues the rotation comes from the camera, because if the expert is right, the object itself was moving.
government-background-check-on-harringto: Brent Friedman, who grew up in Walnut Creek, California, says that around 1980 his family was questioned by people from a government spy agency, "like NSA or like CIA", about a year before something to do with their neighbour John S. Herrington, a government official. Friedman tells it as a memory from his own family, read as a background check on the official's neighbours.
government-contracts-that-were-really-fo: Between 2021 and 2025, a startup that tries to call UFOs to appear says it received government contracts that were really for collecting data on these unexplained objects, though they were presented as war games. James Valor of that company, Skywatcher, says so from his own side of the deal, adding that "in the past we already received contracts from the government to collect data" on them, which would mean the government quietly pays private groups to gather UFO evidence.
government-crash-photos-that-faded-to-bl: After a craft is said to have crashed near Aztec, New Mexico, in 1948, there were two sets of photos, and the set the government took did not last, fading away to nothing. Scott Ramsey, a researcher of the Aztec crash, tells it, pointing back to the original story by a writer named Frank Scully. If true, it would help explain why no government pictures of the crash survive.
government-documents-describe-metallic-r: Between 1947 and 1952, US government documents described the objects people were seeing in the sky as metallic, reflective and flat on the bottom, Michels says in his own framing. He lists a 1947 memo known as the Twining memo, a 1948 analysis from Project Sign, an early Air Force study of the sightings, the CIA's analysis of UFOs flying over Washington, DC in 1952, and the analysis of Captain Edward J. Ruppelt, who led Blue Book, the US Air Force's UFO study of the 1950s and 60s. He points to them to show that officials themselves saw the objects as solid, built things.
government-getting-ahead-of-service-memb: The US government began talking about UFOs because so many service members were on the verge of saying, "I can't not tell them what I saw," and officials wanted to get ahead of them. The economist Tyler Cowen offers this as his reading of events, passing on what he has heard. If so, the openness came from pressure inside the ranks rather than a free choice.
government-gives-a-craft-to-industry-con: The government hands a recovered craft to an aerospace company and says, "Here's the craft. We want to know how it works." That is how the physicist and former Pentagon contractor Eric W. Davis says it works, according to two industry sources he does not name. He adds that the company gets a sole-source contract, one given to it without competition, with a set task: take the craft apart piece by piece, reverse engineer it, put it back together and try to make it work.
government-group-working-on-quantum-vacu: A group inside the US government is said to have been working since the 1990s on watching things through the quantum vacuum, the energy that physics says fills even empty space. Dave Rossi, a guest who says aliens taught him advanced physics, claims he knows this group. He says it twice in the same talk, and the second time he adds that the group has had "massive success" and that the technology is not a prototype but "established." If true, the government would have had a working tool like this for decades.
government-holds-close-range-cell-phone-: A man named Dylan Borland says the US government holds close-up cell phone videos of triangle-shaped craft, clear enough to end the debate about them "once and for all." He tells it as something he knows directly, though in another telling he only calls the videos classified, "undeniable," without saying who holds them or how close they were filmed.
government-knowledge-that-scalar-waves-a: The US government has known for years that certain "scalar" electromagnetic waves, a disputed kind of energy wave, can change how fast radioactive materials decay. Steve Colbern, a scientist who studies objects said to be alien implants in human bodies, says this, crediting the books of a writer named Tom Bearden. If true, it would mean the government holds a hidden way to change something physicists treat as fixed.
government-people-pushed-an-alien-narrat: Starting around 2007, Chris Bledsoe, a man who says UFOs appear around him, says government people tried to make him believe in flying saucers and little green men. He tells this from his own experience, and he suggests they were pushing that story on him from the very beginning.
government-psychic-programs-prompted-by-: The US government's programs in the 1950s that studied psychic abilities may have started because of what officials were learning about UFOs and beings from other worlds. That is the suspicion of Kurt McConnell, a former Senate staffer, who offers it on Michels's show in 2025 as his own guess rather than from a named source. If true, the mind research and the UFO research were tied together from the start.
government-published-propaganda-books-as: The US government secretly publishes books full of propaganda and places them on shelves next to books that hold real truth about UFOs, as part of what was called "a multi-billion dollar campaign to cover up the truth." The writer Brent Friedman says this was told to him directly by John S. Herrington, a former US Secretary of Energy. If true, it would mean much of the popular UFO literature was planted on purpose to confuse the public.
government-recruited-psi-capable-childre: For decades the US government is said to have searched the country for children with psi abilities, meaning supposed powers of the mind such as moving things by thought, and run parapsychology experiments on them. Michels tells this himself across several episodes, without naming a single source, and his versions differ: once he says the children were taken to national laboratories and names the Atomic Energy Commission, the US agency that ran nuclear work, and the Battelle Memorial Institute, a private research body; another time he ties it to gifted children's programs and to Stargate and Grill Flame, secret US psychic research programs, crediting the researchers Hal Puthoff and Russell Targ. If true, the government would have quietly treated children as test subjects for mind powers.
government-underfunding-meant-no-helicop: A spokesperson for Skywatcher, a startup that tries to call in UFOs (which officials call UAP, unidentified anomalous phenomena) and record them, says the government funded some of its observation events in the western United States between about 2020 and 2025 but never gave enough money, so there was no helicopter to chase what appeared. The company, linked to a man named Jake Barber, speaks of "our disappointment in the government" over "insufficient financing".
government-wanted-as-many-crashes-as-pos: The government wanted as many crashes of unknown craft as possible, so it could collect as much of their technology as it could. The physicist John Brandenburg says he heard accounts saying this, without naming who told him. If true, it would mean crashes were welcomed as a source of technology.
government-whistleblowers-claim-ufo-retr: Government insiders have come forward to say the United States has recovered UFOs, according to Michels. He says one of these whistleblowers has been a guest on his own show, and that it is "kind of hard to poke holes in his story." He brings it up himself, without naming the man, as a reason to take the question seriously.
governments-hide-the-bodies-for-cold-war: The governments that work hardest to hide strange finds are the ones doing the most reverse engineering, meaning taking unknown technology apart to learn how to copy it. That is the view of a researcher named David Ruiz, speaking in a talk about small three-fingered bodies said to have been found in Peru. He gives no source and ties this hiding to things that happened during the Cold War, which would mean such bodies are kept out of sight for their military value.
governor-richardson-on-looking-into-the-: Bill Richardson, a former governor of New Mexico, is said to have told the documentary filmmaker James Fox that one of the few things he did in his political career was look into UFOs, "particularly the Roswell crash," the reported 1947 crash of an unknown object near Roswell, New Mexico. Fox tells this as something Richardson said to him directly. It matters because it would mean a senior politician took the Roswell story seriously enough to investigate it himself.
gps-lost-over-the-object-on-the-stockhol: In 2025, while a Stockholm University ship passed over a strange object on the floor of the Baltic Sea, its satellite positioning system started failing. A treasure hunter named Dennis Asberg, whose team found the object, says he was aboard, and that a man he names only as Tomas told him, "Dennis, we have problems with the GPS function" just as they went over it. He tells it as a sign that the object itself may disturb equipment.
graham-hancock-on-joe-rogan-the-sarcopha: The stone box in the Great Pyramid of Giza, usually called a sarcophagus, may not be a coffin at all, but a place where people lay down to raise their consciousness. The writer Graham Hancock, known for his books on lost ancient civilisations, has suggested this on The Joe Rogan Experience, the podcast hosted by Joe Rogan. The researcher Luke Caverns passes this on to Michels as Hancock's changing view.
graham-hancock-s-first-article-on-the-ar: The writer Graham Hancock's very first piece of writing was an article about the Ark of the Covenant, the sacred chest described in the Bible. Michels says this is what Hancock told him when he interviewed him, and that he thinks the article was for a magazine. He brings it up as a sign of how early Hancock's interest in lost ancient mysteries began.
graham-hancock-s-lost-ice-age-civilizati: The writer Graham Hancock thinks ancient sites such as Göbekli Tepe, a very old stone temple site in Turkey, were built by a lost Ice Age people, "the Atlanteans or whoever." The skeptic Michael Shermer sums up Hancock's view, which Hancock set out in his book Fingerprints of the Gods, published in 1995. If true, civilization would be far older than the textbooks say.
graham-hancock-s-text-doubting-the-giza-: In 2025 the writer Graham Hancock said he did not trust the source behind a claim about radar scans of the Giza plateau, the site of Egypt's Great Pyramids. The scans were made with SAR, a kind of radar imaging, and the claim was tied to a researcher named Filippo Biondi. Michels says he texted Hancock about it, and Hancock replied: "I have no reason to believe that the source here is being honest."
graham-hancock-s-yage-experience-of-a-co: The writer Graham Hancock says that after drinking yage, a psychedelic plant brew from South America, he felt a presence with him that seemed to be communicating. He tells it as his own experience, describing "this sense of a presence and of communication," and offers it as a hint that such states put people in touch with some other intelligence.
graham-hancock-ties-cydonia-s-monoliths-: The worn-down monolith shapes seen in Cydonia, a region of Mars, may share symbolism with the ancient civilizations of Earth, according to the writer Graham Hancock in his book The Mars Mystery, from 1998. Michels brings it up from that book in an episode about whether Mars once had life.
grail-finds-large-lunar-caverns-and-lava: NASA has mapped what lies under the Moon's surface with a probe called GRAIL and found large caverns and lava tubes, which are long tunnels left behind by flowing lava. A researcher who is a guest on the episode, and is not named, says this without giving a source, in an episode about what NASA may be keeping quiet about the Moon. His point is that the Moon may hold large hollow spaces beneath its surface.
grandfather-s-name-carved-atop-the-great: The writer Graham Hancock says that when he climbed the Great Pyramid at Giza in Egypt with Santha Faiia, they found his grandfather's name carved in the stone: "P Hancock 5th of April 1916." Hancock says it was his grandfather Philip Hancock, and that his diaries back up the climb. Hancock has told the story more than once. In one version the name is on the top, and in another it is "one step down from the top" on the south side. He tells it as a family link to the place that sits at the centre of his life's work.
grandfather-s-radio-plays-on-wedding-day: The well-known skeptic Michael Shermer says that on his wedding day in 2014, an old radio that had belonged to his wife Jennifer's grandfather, and had long been silent, was found in a desk drawer playing romantic music, perfectly tuned. Shermer tells it first-hand and wrote about it in his column for the magazine Scientific American, as an odd moment even a skeptic could not easily explain. Michels, retelling it years earlier, remembered it differently, as a mechanical clock from her father that started playing on the wedding night.
grant-files-47-foias-at-midnight-on-janu: At one second after midnight on January 20, 2026, the UFO researcher Grant Cameron says he filed 47 requests at once under FOIA, a US law that lets anyone request government records. He tells it himself, and says the requests sought records of UFO briefings involving a former White House official named Reince Priebus, hoping new documents would come loose.
graves-s-congressional-uap-testimony-202: In 2023, the former Navy pilot Ryan Graves told a hearing of the US Congress that he had experienced advanced UAP firsthand. UAP, or unidentified anomalous phenomena, is the government's term for UFOs. Graves tells this himself, opening with his record: a former F-18 fighter pilot with ten years in the Navy. In the telling he also mentions a Navy fighter pilot named David Fravor and another witness, David Grusch.
graves-s-space-situational-awareness-cam: Ryan Graves, a former Navy fighter pilot who has spoken about pilots seeing UFOs, says he started a small company building what he calls "the next generation of space situational awareness cameras", meaning cameras that watch and track what is moving around the Earth in orbit. He tells it about his own work.
graves-speaks-out-because-colleagues-rep: A Navy fighter pilot named Ryan Graves says that when he went public in 2019 about unidentified objects seen by pilots, he did it only because his fellow aviators kept reporting them and getting no answers. He tells it about himself: "I did it simply because I was hearing that my colleagues were having no resolution to this issue." It frames his coming forward as a matter of flight safety and duty rather than publicity.
gravitec-vacuum-chamber-tests: A company called Gravitec is said to have achieved its effect inside a vacuum chamber, a sealed room with the air pumped out, and to have once worked as a contractor for NASA, the US space agency. Gary McKinnon, a British hacker known for breaking into NASA and US military computers, repeats this from a man he names only as Henrik, and gives no further detail on what exactly was done.
gravity-a-and-gravity-b-in-barry-s-lab-n: At S4, a secret site in Nevada where he says alien craft were studied in the late 1980s, a colleague named Barry Castilio is said to have had lab notes about two kinds of gravity, labelled gravity A and gravity B. Bob Lazar, who says he worked there, tells it, saying the notes showed "the direction they were going in at one time," though he does not know where the notes came from. It would show how the team thought the craft were powered.
gravity-researchers-went-dark-1950: In the 1950s, American scientists working on gravity suddenly went quiet. According to Bob Maguire, a former contractor for the CIA, the physicist Louis Witten never did anything more on gravity, and the inventor Thomas Townsend Brown went to work for the military and the defense industry and never published another thing about his work. Maguire says this on Michels's show without naming a source. If it is true, it would suggest that gravity research was moved into secret programs.
gravity-weakening-experiments-with-pulse: A physicist named John Brandenburg says he and colleagues ran experiments in which pulsing electromagnetic fields, the kind made by electricity and magnets, weakened gravity nearby by about one part in a thousand, an amount they could easily measure. He tells it as work he took part in, and if true it would point to a way of controlling gravity.
gray-encounter-in-catskills-cabin-with-m: The writer Whitley Strieber is said to have had an encounter with a gray, a small grey-skinned being, at his cabin in the Catskill mountains of New York in the 1980s, and to have seen "all these military and intelligence people standing around", including the CIA, watching. The philosopher Jason Jorjani relays this on Michels' show in 2025 from Strieber's own account, crediting his book Communion. If true, it would mean the government was present at, and perhaps behind, such encounters.
gray-pilot-explains-implants-as-broken-i: In the mid-1960s, somewhere off Earth, a gray alien pilot told Lyn Buchanan that the so-called implants people find in their bodies are the broken-off tips of instruments, used to make humans produce antibodies. Buchanan, a former Army sergeant, says he heard it first-hand. He quotes the being as saying: "we take one or two cells of our diseased tissue, put it on that tip and implant it into you, and you will start making antibodies."
gray-types-aboard-craft-and-coburn-s-han: Steve Colbern, a scientist who studies objects said to be alien implants, says he remembers being aboard a craft and seeing "mostly different types of grays", meaning small gray-skinned beings, among them one he treats as his own handler. He tells it as his own memory.
grays-as-biological-drones-1990: The small gray beings of UFO lore, known as grays, are biological drones, built living machines rather than independent beings, according to an anonymous self-described whistleblower who posted on 4chan, an anonymous online message board. The magician and video maker Chris Ramsay relays what that poster wrote in the thread. If true, it would mean someone else is behind the grays.
grays-moon-base: Small grey beings, known as grays, have a base on the Moon and "come and go at any time they want," according to Charles Hall. Hall says he spent three years at a Nevada military site with tall white aliens, and he passes this on as part of what he says he learned there, which would mean more than one kind of visitor is coming and going near Earth.
grays-rescued-orphaned-chinese-children-: Charles Hall, who says he spent three years among alien beings near Area 51, a secret military base in Nevada, says the beings had with them young Chinese people they had rescued, not abducted, after the children were orphaned. He tells it as something he saw himself in Indian Springs Valley, Nevada, in the 1960s, and as he tells it, the beings wanted to return these young people to human society. If true, it would mean the beings were caring for human children, not taking them.
grays-tall-whites-and-norwegians-arrived: Different kinds of aliens came to Earth at different points in the ice ages, according to Charles Hall, a man who says he spent three years among tall, white-skinned aliens while stationed at a military range in Nevada. Hall tells Jesse Michels he is "certain" that the small grey beings, known as the grays, "got here first" and were here before the last ice age, that the tall whites came second, and that a third group called the Norwegians arrived at yet another time. If he is right, several alien peoples would have been on Earth for longer than human history.
grays-that-handled-travis-walton-were-ro: Some of the grays, the small gray beings of many abduction stories, are not living creatures but robots built by the Nordics, tall human-looking beings described in some contact accounts, and these robots were the ones that handled Travis Walton during his reported 1975 encounter in Arizona. The researcher Jason Jorjani says this on Michels's show in 2025 without naming his source. If true, it would mean different kinds of visitors, some of them made by others.
grays-turning-into-owls-in-close-encount: There are cases where people say they saw grays, the small gray-skinned beings often described in alien encounter stories, turn into owls. A researcher named Jason Jorjani mentions this in passing, pointing to a researcher named Mike Cleland and a work called Closer Encounters. If true, it would suggest these beings can change the form in which they appear to people.
greada-treaty-eisenhower-agreement-1950: In the 1950s, President Dwight D. Eisenhower's government is said to have made a secret pact with non-human visitors, known as the Greada Treaty or the Eisenhower agreement. The researcher Tim Alberino says on Michels's show that he believes "the Greta contract was real, that it actually happened," without naming where he learned it. If true, it would mean the US government has dealt with visitors at the highest level for some seventy years.
great-falls-tribune-reports-of-strange-l: A former Air Force missile officer named Robert Salas says that in 1967, the same week a UFO was reported over his nuclear missile base near Great Falls, Montana, the local paper, the Great Falls Tribune, carried reports of strange lights in the sky. Salas tells this as part of his own account of a UFO he says shut down ten nuclear missiles, and he uses the newspaper reports as a sign that other people saw something too.
great-figures-he-met-said-we-are-not-alo: The president of a Russian republic, speaking to Jesse Michels in 2025, says that the greatest minds he met, "real geniuses", all told him that we are not alone in the universe. He names Pope John Paul II, the Dalai Lama, the Bulgarian seer Baba Vanga, the Indian guru Sai Baba, the American statesman Henry Kissinger and the Russian physicist Zhores Alferov. If he is right, some of the best-known figures of the last century privately believed in life beyond Earth.
great-pyramid-as-a-device-for-balancing-: The Great Pyramid of Giza in Egypt, along with other ancient structures, may have been built partly to balance the Earth's energy, not only as a tomb or monument. The researcher Matt LaCroix offers this as his own belief on Michels's show, drawing on the work of a writer on the pyramid named Christopher Dunn. If true, it would mean the ancient builders understood a kind of energy that we have since forgotten.
great-pyramid-as-a-giant-power-plant: The Great Pyramid at Giza in Egypt was not a tomb but a huge machine for making energy: that is the idea of Christopher Dunn, described on the show as a former aerospace engineer. Dunn tells it himself in two episodes. He says his first book, The Giza Power Plant, set out in 1998 what he thought the pyramid was: "a power plant," which he calls "an electron harvester." If he is right, the people who built it had energy technology far beyond what history credits them with. Others pass the idea along. The comedian and podcaster Joe Rogan mentions "the Christopher Dunn stuff" in passing. Jesse Michels brings it up several times, calling the pyramid an "energy generator" or "energy machine" and once applying the idea to the pyramids in general. A former nuclear site guard named Mario Woods gives his own version without naming Dunn: he thinks the pyramids were power generators sending power out worldwide.
great-pyramid-as-a-transmitter: The Great Pyramid at Giza in Egypt may have been a transmitter, sending signals to whoever its builders wanted to talk to. A researcher named Joe McMoneagle suggests this on the show without naming a source, in an episode where he also argues that Mars once had life. If it were true, the pyramid would be a communication device rather than only a tomb.
great-pyramid-built-over-hundreds-of-yea: The Great Pyramid of Giza was not built in the 23 years that the pharaoh Khufu reigned, but was more likely a project that took hundreds of years to finish. A researcher named Graham Hancock says this without naming a source, and he mentions the writer Robert Bauval alongside it. If true, the pyramid would be the work of many generations, and the usual story of who built it and when would have to change.
great-pyramid-chambers-aligned-to-sirius: The two main rooms inside the Great Pyramid of Giza, known as the King's Chamber and the Queen's Chamber, each point toward a different part of the sky, with the Queen's Chamber facing Sirius, the brightest star, and the design matching Sirius and the constellation Orion as they stood around 10,500 BC. A researcher named Matt LaCroix lays this out on Michels's show in 2024 without naming a source. If so, the pyramid would encode a date far older than the usual history gives it.
great-pyramid-sulfuric-acid-and-central-: The Great Pyramid of Giza in Egypt was a chemical plant that made sulfuric acid, a strong acid. That is the claim of a researcher named Geoffrey Drumm, who says the purpose of the pyramids was given to him by an alien. In his telling, the acid was carried into the middle pyramid of the three, where it reacted with salt to make hydrochloric acid, another strong acid. He gives no outside source.
greek-inventor-s-steam-sphere: An inventor in ancient Greece is said to have built a sphere driven by steam. Greg Rogers, who is introduced as a NASA doctor and who says he saw a UFO in a secret hangar, mentions it in passing without naming the inventor or a source. He brings it up as an example of advanced technology appearing far earlier than people expect.
greek-professor-says-the-delphic-women-w: At Delphi, the ancient Greek site of a famous oracle, women are said to have been possessed by the spirit of Zeus, the chief Greek god, as vapours rose from under the ground. A researcher named Luke Caverns tells this on the show, saying he has heard unnamed Greek professors describe it. If true, it would mean the oracle's trances were real possession, not only ritual.
green-fireballs-as-mothership-hypothesis: In the late 1940s, green fireballs that looked like meteors were seen over US nuclear sites, and Michels offers a hypothesis: a mothership waited outside the atmosphere and the green "meteorites" were tied to the UFOs seen near nuclear weapons. He puts this idea himself to the skeptic Mick West during a debate, drawing on the book UFOs and Nukes. If true, it would mean something was watching America's nuclear program from space.
green-object-over-savannah-river-site-en: In 1952, at the Savannah River Site, a US nuclear plant in South Carolina, an engineer named John Anderson and his colleagues were overtaken by a glowing green object, angular in shape, which darted back and forth at high speed and altitude with what was described as "phenomenal maneuverability." Michels reads this out himself, without naming the source, on an episode about UFOs watching nuclear sites, where it serves as an early case of such objects appearing over nuclear facilities.
green-orb-over-the-nevada-test-range-dur: During training on the Nevada test range, near the secret Air Force base known as Area 51, a green, glowing ball is said to have flown overhead and been seen by one of the trainees. Randy Anderson, a guest who says he saw alien technology at a military base, says it was his buddy who saw it. Later Michels adds that this colleague still works with Anderson at Area 51 and told him "yeah I saw that green orb that Randy talked about." Michels also mentions a DD214, the US military's discharge paper, as backing for Anderson's service.
green-triangles-near-lax-are-airliner-bo: The green triangle-shaped objects filmed near Los Angeles International Airport, which many shows present as unidentified craft, are in fact just airliners' lights blurred by the camera lens, according to the skeptic Michael Shermer. He says this in a debate with Michels, without pointing to a source, flatly calling the triangles "not" what the shows claim.
greenbrier-bunker-revealed-by-washington: Under Greenbrier in West Virginia, the story goes, there was a secret underground shelter where Congress would be taken in a nuclear war, and the public only learned of it in the 1990s when a newspaper broke the story. Bryce Zabel, a guest on an episode about Hollywood, the CIA and UFOs, tells it from memory and without a firm source: "we did not know about them until the Washington Post I think it was the Post that broke this story in the '9s about Greenbryer." He adds that "there's another one" too. The same words turn up in a later episode about a former US Secretary of Energy, credited there to Brent Friedman, a guest described as a journalist, who names the Washington Post's Greenbrier story as the source. Zabel brings it up to show that the government can keep large underground facilities hidden from everyone for decades.
greenstreet-of-the-new-york-post-dispute: Brandon Fugal, the owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property known for reports of strange events, says he was made to look like a liar about his meeting with a Pentagon official named Sean Kirkpatrick. In his words, "I was being made out to be the liar by Steven Greenstreet at the New York Post," a journalist at the newspaper who questioned Fugal's account. Fugal says he answered by posting photos of the meeting, as proof that it took place the way he said.
greenwald-foia-finds-ufo-references-in-o: A researcher named John Greenewald Jr. filed a request under FOIA, a US law that lets anyone request government records, and got back material showing many references to UFOs in the records of Barack Obama's presidency, from 2009 to 2017. A researcher named Jason Simosa recalls this from memory: he can't remember if it was 3,000 or 30,000, but thinks it was 30,000 mentions of UFOs, UAP (the government's term for unidentified aerial objects), and AATIP, a small Pentagon office that studied unexplained aerial reports. If true, it would mean the subject came up often at the highest level of government.
greenwald-s-foia-request-on-fast-walkers: A researcher named John Greenewald Jr., who runs an archive of government records called the Black Vault, is said to have asked for files on "fast walkers" and been turned down. He used FOIA, a US law that lets anyone request government records, and "fast walkers" is a military term for unexplained objects seen moving quickly through space. Michels says that when Greenewald tried, NORAD, the North American air defence command, answered that this was "very sensitive material." A guest named Maaneli Derakhshani says Greenewald asked the Space Force and the Department of Defense for all documents on both "fast walkers and slow walkers" and that the request was refused under an exemption. If true, the military would be keeping records of unexplained objects in space and declining to release them.
greer-assistant-and-congressman-develop-: A UFO researcher named Steven Greer says that he, his best friend and assistant at the time, and a member of Congress all got "aggressive metastatic cancers." Greer tells this himself, about people close to his UFO work, and if it were more than chance it would suggest those pushing on the subject were harmed.
greer-briefed-clinton-s-cia-director-199: Steven Greer, a campaigner who says UFO secrets are held by a hidden global group, says he personally briefed President Bill Clinton's director of the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency, on 13 December 1993 in Washington. He tells it as his own experience, part of a run of meetings he places in 1993, 1994 and 1995. If true, it would mean the UFO question reached the top of American intelligence in the early Clinton years.
greer-briefs-admiral-wilson-j2-1997: In 1997 a UFO disclosure campaigner named Steven Greer says he briefed Admiral Thomas Wilson, the head of intelligence for the Joint Staff (the top military advisers at the Pentagon), about UFOs. Greer tells Michels this himself, and ties it to a memo by the physicist Eric W. Davis that is said to record a later talk with Wilson about hidden UFO programmes. If true, it would mean the military's top intelligence officer was told about secret UFO work.
greer-calls-uapgerb-an-intelligence-asse: In 2024, the online UFO researcher known as UAPGerb says an unnamed Army public affairs contact told him, "I just talked to Greer and he said, 'You're an intelligence asset'", meaning someone working for spy agencies. UAPGerb tells it first-hand; Greer here is Steven Greer, a well-known campaigner for UFO disclosure, and the claim would cast doubt on UAPGerb's independence.
greer-contacted-by-a-cosmic-intelligence: Steven Greer, a well-known figure who holds public events about UFOs, says that at age 18 he was contacted by a kind of cosmic intelligence and told, in effect, to save the world, and he repeated this at his event in September 2024. A UFO researcher who goes by the name UAPGerb passes this along on Michels's show in 2025, as something Greer himself said in public. It is told as the root of Greer's sense of mission.
greer-gave-grusch-and-luna-an-unredacted: In 2023 or 2024 in Washington, Steven Greer, a doctor who has campaigned for decades to have UFO secrets made public, says he handed a hard drive of unredacted material to David Grusch and Anna Paulina Luna. Grusch is a former intelligence officer who told Congress that the government holds craft that are not human, and Luna is a member of Congress. Greer tells Michels he met and talked with both of them "and others" and said, "here's a hard drive," which suggests he was trying to hand his evidence straight to the people pushing for disclosure.
greer-passes-along-an-insider-s-contact-: After the former Marine Michael Herrera described a huge craft he says he saw in the Indonesian jungle, the UFO disclosure campaigner Steven Greer told him that a certain man "knows what you saw" and gave him that man's contact details. The man was Jake Barber, a former helicopter pilot who says he flew missions to recover crashed craft, and Herrera tells this from his own experience in 2023. It would mean insiders already knew about what Herrera saw.
greer-s-1993-95-recommendations-to-the-c: A UFO disclosure campaigner named Steven Greer says that between 1993 and 1995 he wrote a set of recommendations on UFO secrecy to President Bill Clinton's administration in Washington. He says they were the same recommendations he makes today. Greer tells this about his own work, as proof that he has been pressing the same case for decades.
greer-s-2001-national-press-club-whistle: In 2001, a UFO disclosure campaigner named Steven Greer hosted a panel of whistleblowers at the National Press Club, a press venue in Washington DC. The whistleblowers were people claiming inside knowledge of government UFO secrets, and a man named Mark McCandlish is named among them. A researcher who goes by the online name UAPGerb mentions the panel in passing, without naming a source, and points to a 2001 disclosure briefing document that went with it.
greer-s-ce5-coherent-thought-sequencing: Steven Greer, a UFO researcher, runs a practice called CE5, short for "close encounters of the fifth kind", in which people try to call in craft with their minds. According to Greer, the craft pick up "a directed coherent thought signal as clearly as a radio would pick up on an electromagnetic signal." Michels lays out Greer's idea in an episode about a UFO book he says the Pentagon tried to censor; if true, it would mean contact can be made by thought alone.
greer-s-claim-that-nimitz-objects-were-l: The strange objects that Navy pilots from the aircraft carrier Nimitz reported off San Diego in 2004 were, according to the UFO activist Steven Greer, secret projects of the defence company Lockheed Martin, run as "special access programs," the government's most tightly restricted classified projects. Michels passes on this claim as something Greer says publicly. If true, it would mean the objects were human-made aircraft, not anything unknown.
greer-s-groups-call-up-lights-on-a-nearb: Steven Greer, a UFO researcher who leads groups that try to make contact with craft, takes his groups to a beach about 40 minutes south of Cocoa Beach, Florida, to call up lights in the sky. Charles Buhler, an engineer presented on the show as a NASA scientist, says this, and notes it is almost the same beach where he himself has seen things. He tells it to suggest the spot is one where such lights keep turning up.
greer-s-iphone-hacked-and-threats-1991: A UFO campaigner named Steven Greer says that his iPhone was hacked and that he was threatened, just a week before he spoke with Jesse Michels in 2025. He tells it as something that happened to him, and adds that it was not the first time. He offers it as a sign that people are working to stop him from talking about UFO secrets.
greer-s-joe-rogan-episode-removed-for-sp: An episode of Joe Rogan's very popular podcast featuring Steven Greer was taken down around 2020, because Rogan had to remove it to get his money from Spotify, the streaming company that had signed his show. Greer, a researcher and campaigner on UFOs who was the guest on that episode, tells Michels this himself without naming a source. In his telling, it shows his message being pushed off the big platforms.
greer-s-near-death-experience-at-17-1972: Steven Greer, who argues that UFO secrets are held by a small global group, says that at 17, around 1972 in Charlotte, North Carolina, he fell very ill and had a near-death experience. He tells it as his own story, simply: "I got very sick. I had a near-death experience." He presents it as a turning point that shaped his later interest in consciousness and contact.
greer-says-the-octagon-craft-is-made-by-: An octagon-shaped craft that was retrieved, in a souped-up version, is built by Lockheed's Skunk Works, the secret design division of the aerospace company Lockheed, at a place given as "North Brumit". A witness who goes by the online name UAPGerb says this, repeating what he says a man named Steven Greer has said publicly about it. He says it to a fellow guest, Michael Herrera, who says he saw a 300-foot UFO in the Indonesian jungle, and if true it would mean the craft Herrera saw was a human-made machine.
greer-tells-fravor-the-tic-tac-was-a-sku: The Tic Tac, a white oval object shaped like the mint that Navy pilots met off California in 2004, is said to have been a human-made craft. On this telling, it came from Skunk Works, the secret aircraft design unit of the arms maker Lockheed. A guest named Steven Greer says he told this to David Fravor, the Navy commander who saw the object, some years ago. In his account, Fravor said it "had to be alien," and Greer replied, "Sir, with all due respect, that was how the Lockheed skunk works." Greer adds that such craft are kept hidden on purpose, because the builders "don't want the National Military Command structure to know" that something like what Fravor met "was ours." The journalist Ross Coulthart, without naming a source or mentioning Greer or Fravor, says, "I now know categorically that the Tic Tac is Lockheed Martin technology." If they are right, the most famous Navy sighting was a secret American aircraft.
greer-tells-rfk-jr-about-the-letter-at-s: Steven Greer, a campaigner who says UFO secrets are held by a hidden global group, says he once met Robert F. Kennedy Jr., son of the politician Robert F. Kennedy, in a crowd at Sundance in Utah. Greer says he told him briefly that he has a letter from his father about the UFO issue, dated a month before, in Greer's words, "they killed him." If true, it would suggest the elder Kennedy was looking into UFOs shortly before his death.
greer-warns-joe-firmage-at-mars-cafe-199: In the 1990s, at the Mars Cafe in the South of Market district of San Francisco, Steven Greer, a doctor who campaigns for UFO disclosure, says he met a wealthy man named Joe Firmage and warned him. Greer tells Michels that Firmage was "bait" because of his money, meaning that people who wanted to steer the UFO subject might use or target a rich newcomer.
greg-eghigian-researching-his-ufo-histor: A historian named Greg Eghigian spent a couple of weeks at a large UFO archive in Sweden while researching his book on the history of UFOs. That is according to a Swedish UFO researcher named Clas Svahn, who keeps the archive and hosted him there. Svahn mentions it to show that serious scholars come to use the collection.
grey-four-fingered-beings-with-a-wand-te: Charlie Foltz, one of the men involved in what is known as the Allagash abductions, says that in 1976, on the Allagash Waterway in Maine, he was taken by grey beings with four fingers who held a wand. He says they spoke to him silently, mind to mind: "I was told not to resist, not to fight. I wasn't in any danger. Just comply and everything will be all right." Foltz tells this as something that happened to him, and he points to a book about the case called The Allagash Abductions.
grinberg-and-puharich-meet-during-puhari: In the 1980s, the American researcher Andrija Puharich, who studied psychic phenomena, went into exile in Mexico after his house was burned. While he was there he met the Mexican brain scientist Jacobo Grinberg. An unnamed researcher who is a guest on Michels's show says this without naming a source, tying together two men who both worked at the edges of science.
grof-s-book-discarnate-aliens-would-show: If advanced beings exist that have no physical body, they might reach us in a form that looks like hallucination, according to an argument in one of the books of an author named Stanislav Grof (the transcript renders the name 'Grath'). The neuroscientist Andrew Gallimore brings this up on Michels's show in 2025, citing the book without naming it. If true, some visions might be real contact rather than tricks of the brain.
ground-penetrating-radar-finds-50-ft-rei: In 2025, a radar survey that looks under the ground found a 50-foot-wide structure of steel-reinforced concrete "literally just under the ground" beneath the road around Bradshaw Ranch near Sedona, Arizona. The Australian journalist Ross Coulthart tells this as someone who was there, saying a man he names only as Paul ran the scan. He tells it because it would point to a hidden underground site at a ranch long tied to UFO reports.
ground-penetrating-radar-finds-cut-voids: In the 1990s, scans with ground-penetrating radar and sonar under the Great Sphinx in Giza, Egypt, are said to have found hollow spaces cut into the rock with objects inside them. The researcher Matt LaCroix says he heard this over dinner from the geologist Robert Schoch, who told him he helped lead those underground readings. If true, it would mean there are hidden chambers beneath the Sphinx that have never been opened.
ground-radar-finds-debris-field-and-void: Ground-penetrating radar, which looks beneath the earth's surface, is said to have found a debris field of unusual material and empty spaces inside a mesa on Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property known for reports of strange happenings. The ranch's owner tells this himself, describing material that "does not fit" and is "unusual." If true, it would point to something buried in the mesa, which the episode frames as possibly a craft under the ranch.
grusch-and-the-legacy-reverse-engineerin: A former US intelligence official turned whistleblower named David Grusch may have come across a so-called legacy program, a long-running secret effort to study and copy recovered craft that are not of human make. Michels raises this himself, carefully saying Grusch may or may not have bumped into it. If true, it would mean such a program has run hidden inside the government for years.
grusch-approaches-knapp-and-corbell-at-a: The filmmaker Jeremy Corbell says that at an event in Rocket City, as Huntsville, Alabama is known, held by the SCU, a group of researchers who study unexplained aerial reports, David Grusch came up to him and the journalist George Knapp at a bar. Grusch is a former intelligence officer who filed a complaint with the inspector general of the intelligence community, the watchdog over US spy agencies, saying the government hides UFO programmes. Corbell tells it as something he was there for, with the scientist Garry Nolan also part of the story, and it marks how Grusch first reached the reporters who would help him go public.
grusch-asks-brent-to-help-bring-john-har: In the 2020s, David Grusch, a former intelligence officer who told Congress about hidden UFO programmes, asked the Hollywood screenwriter Brent Friedman to help get John S. Herrington, a former US Secretary of Energy, to come forward. Friedman tells this himself on the podcast: Grusch was asking, "could you help make this happen?" It matters because Friedman says Herrington once told him things about aliens, so a public statement from a former cabinet member would carry weight.
grusch-assigned-to-the-uap-task-force-20: A former intelligence officer named David Grusch says he was assigned in 2019 to the UAP Task Force, a Pentagon group set up to look into UAP, the government's term for UFOs. Grusch says the task force's director sent the request for him through an operations center. A physicist named Eric W. Davis, who says he knew the work at first hand, tells it a little differently: he says Grusch joined in 2020 to 2021 as the liaison from the National Reconnaissance Office, the US agency that runs spy satellites, and took his orders from a man named Jay Stratton. It matters because it would show that Grusch's later claims about hidden UFO programs come from inside the government's own inquiry.
grusch-blows-whistle-on-crash-retrieval-: A man named David Grusch, who worked with a Pentagon task force on unidentified flying objects, the UAPTF, looked into what that group had found and went further than anyone else on it. According to Michels, Grusch then blew the whistle: he says he thinks there has been a secret effort, lasting many decades, to recover crashed craft. Michels tells this himself, also naming a man called Jay Stratton as part of the background, and if true it would mean a long-hidden government programme.
grusch-colleague-finds-radar-data-on-big: A colleague of David Grusch, a former intelligence officer who became a UFO whistleblower, is said to have found military radar data showing an unexplained object pacing a nuclear warhead during the Big Sur incident, a 1964 missile test off California that was caught on film. Michels tells this as something an unnamed person told him. According to that person, Grusch knew of the film, and while he served on a Pentagon task force studying unexplained aerial objects he had a colleague search a military archive, and the colleague found radar data confirming the object. If true, it would back up the filmed event with official records.
grusch-dick-cheney-headed-the-ufo-progra: Dick Cheney, the former US vice president, is said to have been the head of the government's secret UFO program, according to David Grusch, a former US intelligence officer who went public as a whistleblower about such programs. Michels repeats this twice on the show, once noting that Cheney had just died, and once putting it as a question to a guest, a Pentagon scientist named Davis, framing Cheney as the program's last top man, until 2009.
grusch-disgruntled-insiders-inside-the-l: People working inside a secret, long-running government program that is said to hold recovered UFO material are deeply unhappy and want the whole thing brought out into the open. Michels says that David Grusch, a former intelligence officer who in 2023 told Congress about such a program, said this to him in their interview, which would mean the push for disclosure is coming partly from within.
grusch-dodges-the-question-about-agreeme: At his 2023 hearing before the US Congress, the former intelligence official and whistleblower David Grusch is said to have dodged a question about "agreements". The tellers do not spell out what the agreements were, only that the subject was too sensitive for him to answer. A researcher named Matthew Pines says Grusch "very pointedly dodged" the question under oath. A Pentagon whistleblower named Matthew Brown tells it the same way at second hand: Grusch was asked about agreements and said he could not give further detail. If true, it would hint that some arrangement exists that officials will only discuss behind closed doors.
grusch-files-ig-complaint-and-names-witn: In 2022, a whistleblower named David Grusch says he filed a complaint with an Inspector General, an internal government watchdog, and told it whom to interview, and that the investigators concluded, "Holy shit, this is credible". Grusch tells it himself, saying he vetted about 40 sources and made them sit for interviews; Michels says these were 40 people who handled exotic UFO material firsthand, though he names the intelligence community's watchdog rather than the Pentagon's. The former Pentagon official Luis Elizondo and the former Army man Dylan Borland repeat it second hand, Elizondo insisting the testimony is not all secondhand and Borland adding the complaint was found "urgent and credible".
grusch-gave-congress-locations-of-spacec: David Grusch, a former US intelligence officer turned whistleblower, is said to have told Congress exactly where to find hidden spacecraft, yet no subpoenas followed. The journalist Ross Coulthart, who has worked with Grusch's sources, says Grusch "gave them first hand direct information from his sources of where to look, where to find the spacecraft." A former Navy pilot named Ryan Graves remembers hearing Grusch offer at a hearing, "I can tell you the location. Let's get in a skiff," meaning a SCIF, a secure room for classified talks. Graves says nothing about subpoenas. If true, lawmakers were handed a lead to the craft and did not chase it.
grusch-gave-hundreds-of-pages-to-the-ici: In 2022, the story goes, David Grusch, a former intelligence officer, handed hundreds of pages of documents to the ICIG, the internal watchdog of the US spy agencies, laying out a long-running secret program that recovered crashed UFOs. Michels tells it many times. He says the inspector general at the time, Thomas Monheim, called the claims 'urgent and credible.' In one episode he puts the count at over a thousand pages, and elsewhere he calls the number 'presumed.' In another he tells it secondhand through someone named Omar, saying Grusch had hundreds of pages on a crash retrieval program running 'Sub Rosa,' meaning in secret. The online researcher UAPGerb says it may have been a thousand pages or more and complains that Monheim has since left and nothing has been done with them. To the tellers, it shows Grusch's claims were taken seriously by an official watchdog.
grusch-harassed-and-his-medical-file-lea: David Grusch is a former intelligence officer who filed a formal whistleblower complaint about hidden UFO programs. The story is that in 2022 and 2023 he was targeted for it: he was harassed, and his private medical file was leaked. The physicist Eric W. Davis says that both Grusch and his wife were "harassed and intimidated" by someone in the National Reconnaissance Office, the agency that runs US spy satellites. The filmmaker Jeremy Corbell passes on Grusch's own words about the condition named in that file, post-traumatic stress, which Grusch traces to "combat Afghanistan 2013." A Senate staffer named Kurt McConnell gives no details. He says some of what happened to Grusch has never been made public, and that people "went after him" because he went public. If true, it would mean the government punishes people who speak out about this subject.
grusch-harrington-holds-oral-history-of-: In 2026 David Grusch, a former US intelligence officer turned whistleblower, is said to have named John S. Herrington, a former US Secretary of Energy, as a key living witness to a stretch of history whose records have disappeared. Brent Friedman, a Hollywood writer, tells it twice on the show, saying they had identified Herrington as "a very important person who has oral history of a period where a bunch of documentation does not exist anymore." His writing partner Bryce Zabel adds that, according to Grusch, many documents from the years Herrington served in the Reagan administration have gone missing, and he mentions the House Oversight Committee, a committee of Congress. If true, Herrington's memory may be the only remaining record of what was hidden then.
grusch-has-no-information-on-lazar-1989: A UFO whistleblower named David Grusch, who testified before Congress in 2023, says he has nothing to back up Bob Lazar, a man who said in 1989 that he had worked on alien craft at a secret site in Nevada. Grusch tells Michels plainly, "I have no information on Bob Lazar," so Lazar's account gets no support from what Grusch learned.
grusch-hospitalization-and-retained-clea: Sometime in the 2010s, a UFO whistleblower named David Grusch is said to have had a mental health crisis, checked himself into a hospital, and still kept his security clearance, the government permission to see secret material. Mick West, a skeptic who studies UFO claims, tells it without naming a source, saying Grusch "had like, you know, psychotic episode and was voluntarily hospitalized and he kept his clearance". West raises it as something that bears on how Grusch's own claims should be weighed.
grusch-named-sarbacher-as-the-key-to-the: David Grusch, a former intelligence officer who in 2023 testified to Congress that the US secretly holds recovered craft, was asked whose work would let someone understand how that hidden program is built, and he answered: Robert Sarbacher, a scientist. Ammar Kandil, a guest who says he spoke with Grusch, relays this answer. If true, it would point to Sarbacher as a key figure in how the program was set up.
grusch-on-a-multi-decade-cold-war-with-a: The United States is in a decades-long hidden cold war with its rivals, most likely Russia and China, over crashed craft, according to David Grusch, a former intelligence officer who in 2023 told Congress the government holds such craft.
