The online researcher UAPGerb points to Grusch's 2023 interview with NewsNation, a US cable news channel, where he spoke of this. If true, the race for the craft would be an old, secret arms race.
grusch-on-asking-sarbacher-and-oppenheim: David Grusch, a former US intelligence officer who has given sworn testimony about UFOs, tells Michels that he suspects UFO matters were hidden away in the 1940s and 1950s by people at the top of American science. If he could, he says, he would ask Robert Sarbacher, a scientist who advised the government in those years, and the physicist J. Robert Oppenheimer "what was your thought process in the 40s and 50s you know squirreling this away". If he were right, the secrecy would go back to the first generation of nuclear-age scientists.
grusch-on-disclosing-the-biologic-side-2: David Grusch, a whistleblower who testified under oath to the US Congress in 2023 about hidden UFO programmes, says he deliberately touched on the most sensitive parts of the subject, including what he calls "the biologic side." He says he wanted to put enough out there so that the things that "really need to come out" would come out. He speaks of his own choices, and it matters because it implies the government holds biological evidence, not just craft.
grusch-on-jre-cia-psi-programs-as-a-key-: David Grusch, a former intelligence officer turned UFO whistleblower, is said to have suggested in 2024 that the CIA might have looked into psychic abilities as a way to unlock craft it has stored in a warehouse. A researcher who goes by the online name UAPGerb recalls this from Grusch's appearance on the Joe Rogan Experience, a popular podcast hosted by Joe Rogan. According to UAPGerb, the talk turned to remote viewing, the claimed ability to see distant places with the mind, and Grusch wondered whether such mind-based methods were being studied as a "key" to recovered objects.
grusch-on-sarbacher-s-role-in-standing-u: A physicist named Robert Sarbacher is said to have helped set up the secret government effort that handles recovered craft, sometime between the 1940s and the 1950s. The man who says so is David Grusch, a former US intelligence officer who became a whistleblower about that effort, and he says it only in passing: Sarbacher is "somebody purportedly involved in the stand-up of the stuff that I uncovered." If true, it would place the effort's beginnings in the years right after the Second World War.
grusch-on-sentient-plasmoid-life-2020: A former US intelligence officer turned whistleblower named David Grusch is said to have spoken, at a press event in Washington DC, about the idea of sentient plasmoid life: glowing balls of plasma, a charged gas, that might be alive and aware. Michels describes this himself while going over that event. He raises it as one of the stranger ideas Grusch put forward.
grusch-oppenheimer-helped-set-up-ufo-sec: The physicist J. Robert Oppenheimer, who led the building of the first atomic bomb in the 1940s, is said to have been involved in setting up the secret UFO work that David Grusch later uncovered. Grusch, a former intelligence officer who went public as a whistleblower, puts it this way: Oppenheimer was "somebody purportedly involved in the stand-up of the stuff that I uncovered." If true, UFO secrecy would date back to the same years and people as the atomic bomb.
grusch-oppenheimer-set-up-ufo-secrecy-19: The physicist J. Robert Oppenheimer, who led the building of the atomic bomb, and others of his time are said to have set up the secrecy around UFOs in the 1940s and 1950s. Michels raises this from David Grusch, a former intelligence official who has spoken publicly about UFOs, and says "if you believe David Grusch then they literally set up the secrecy." He also brings in the scientist Robert Sarbacher. If true, the cover-up would go back to the same men who built the bomb.
grusch-reprisals-at-the-nga-2020: A former US intelligence official turned whistleblower named David Grusch suffered serious reprisals and was dragged through the mud while working at the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency, the US agency that studies satellite imagery and maps. Michels says this himself in an episode criticising a Wall Street Journal article on UFOs, and adds that Grusch should receive a large check in the mail, meaning he deserves compensation for how he was treated.
grusch-s-40-witnesses-are-firsthand-and-: The roughly 40 witnesses David Grusch, a former intelligence officer who in 2023 told Congress the US secretly holds recovered craft, spoke to were all firsthand, but not one of them was a physicist. Eric W. Davis, a physicist who has worked on Pentagon studies of the subject, says this, adding that he and the mathematician Eric Weinstein talked about it for hours two years earlier. He raises it to suggest the witnesses may have seen things without the training to understand the science behind them.
grusch-s-alternative-timeline-view-of-th: The technology behind UFOs is not just a step ahead of ours but looks like it comes from "an alternative timeline", according to a whistleblower named David Grusch. Michels says Grusch told him this in an interview in 2023, saying that "if I were a betting man" that is how he would read it. Michels repeats it himself, as Grusch's own guess about what the craft might be.
grusch-s-claims-of-reverse-engineering-p: In 2023 a former US intelligence officer named David Grusch came forward and said the United States holds crashed craft that were not made by humans, and has secret programs that take them apart to learn how they work. Michels comes back to these claims in several episodes. He says Grusch spoke of a hidden crash retrieval and reverse engineering program running for 70 years or more, and he recalls Grusch at a public hearing in Congress, sitting beside pilots who described their own sightings, in a talk with the former Navy fighter pilot Ryan Graves. Speaking with a Senate staffer named Kirk McConnell, Michels adds that Grusch talked of "biologics," meaning bodies, kept with the craft in aerospace warehouses, and that he offered to give the warehouse addresses. The filmmaker Jeremy Corbell repeats Grusch's words himself: "Not only are UFOs real, but we are reverse engineering the craft. We've been exploiting the derivative technologies for decades." Corbell ties these claims to a complaint Grusch filed with the inspector general of the intelligence agencies, the official watchdog for spy agencies. If true, it would mean the government has kept physical proof of other beings hidden for most of a century.
grusch-s-ig-complaint-and-aoc-exchange-a: A witness named David Grusch is said to have handed hundreds of pages to Thomas Monheim, the Inspector General of the Intelligence Community, the official watchdog over US spy agencies, claiming there are covert programs taking apart and copying craft of unknown origin. The story, set in Washington between 2022 and 2023, also takes in an exchange with Congresswoman Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez about where such programs are located. Michels tells it in an episode with a NASA doctor, as backing for the idea that such programs exist.
grusch-s-irad-fraud-allegation-2023: David Grusch, a former intelligence officer who testified to Congress in 2023 about secret UFO programs, also made allegations of fraud tied to IRAD, the internal research and development money that defense companies spend and can bill back to the government. The allegation is raised only in passing, by an interviewer named Jack who asks the physicist Eric Davis about it on Michels' show, with nothing more said of what the fraud involved.
grusch-s-public-testimony-cleared-by-dop: When David Grusch, a former intelligence officer, testified to Congress in 2023 about secret programs holding non-human craft, everything he said in public had first been approved by the Pentagon's review office that clears what officials may say publicly, and the rest he gave in a closed, classified hearing. The physicist Eric W. Davis, who has worked on government UFO studies, says this on Michels's show, noting that what Grusch "was able to give was approved by the Department of Defense." The point is that his public words carried official clearance.
grusch-s-secondhand-spaceship-testimony-: When David Grusch, a witness who testified to the US Congress in 2023, said there were spaceships, he was only repeating what someone else told him, and that person may simply have seen a test drone and taken it for something else. That is the argument of Michael Shermer, presented as America's best-known skeptic, in a debate with Michels. He puts it as Grusch saying, "I talked to somebody who interacted with this spaceship. He told me it was a spaceship," and his point is that secondhand claims like this cannot prove anything.
grusch-s-terms-came-from-crash-retrieval: The terms that David Grusch, a former intelligence officer turned UFO whistleblower, uses are said to come from briefings he was given on a crash retrieval program, a claimed secret effort to recover crashed craft of non-human origin. The physicist Eric W. Davis says this, giving it as his own view of where Grusch heard the words. If so, it would mean Grusch was briefed directly on such a program.
grusch-s-testimony-prompts-rogers-to-com: Greg Rogers, a former NASA doctor who says he saw a UFO in a secret hangar, says the "real impetus" for him to go public came when David Grusch, a former intelligence officer, testified about UFOs before Congress in 2023. Rogers tells this about himself. It shows how one public hearing could push other insiders to speak.
grusch-s-witness-and-the-300-ft-triangle: Someone on their way to work, near Norfolk, Virginia, sometime in the 2010s, saw a huge triangle about 300 feet across. Michels says David Grusch, a former intelligence officer who has testified to Congress about UFOs, told him about this witness. If true, it would be a sighting of a very large craft over an ordinary commute.
grusch-says-cheney-was-the-last-at-the-t: Dick Cheney, the US vice president in the 2000s, was the last person at the top of the pyramid of an old secret government UFO programme, according to David Grusch, a former intelligence officer who has told Congress such programmes exist. Michels passes on what Grusch said. If true, oversight of the programme would have ended with Cheney.
grusch-says-he-knows-john-harrington-202: In 2023, at his house in Los Angeles, the television writer and producer Bryce Zabel says he asked David Grusch, a former intelligence officer who told Congress about hidden UFO programmes, whether he had heard of John S. Herrington, a former US Secretary of Energy. Zabel tells Michels that Grusch answered, "Oh, I know John Harrington," and he mentions the journalist Ross Coulthart in telling it. The point is that the man Zabel's circle connected to an alien story was already known to the people pushing for disclosure.
grusch-says-the-peruvian-skeletons-resem: David Grusch, a former intelligence officer who went public with claims about secret UFO programs, is said to have looked at strange three-fingered mummified bodies from Peru and said they resemble things he saw in classified settings. Michels says Grusch told him the skeletons Michels saw in Peru looked like what he had seen in secret. A congressman named Eric Burlison relays it more narrowly in 2025, saying Grusch found some of the mummies, by their physical build, "congruent with what he has seen in briefings in his former role." If true, it would tie the Peruvian bodies to beings the government already knows about.
grusch-sends-someone-to-interview-mccasl: A US congressman named Eric Burlison says that David Grusch, a former intelligence officer who has made public claims about hidden UFO programs, sent someone to interview a retired general named Neil McCasland. According to Burlison, speaking to Jesse Michels in 2026, the interviewer could not get much out of the general. It is told as part of the effort to find senior officers who might know what the government holds.
grusch-speaks-of-interdimensional-beings: At a 2023 hearing in the US Congress, the witness David Grusch is said to have used the phrase "interdimensional beings", and holography came up in the same discussion. A researcher named Eric Weinstein recalls this without naming a source, saying he believes Grusch used the phrase. It matters because it would mean ideas about beings from other dimensions were raised on the official record in front of lawmakers.
grusch-testifies-before-congress-2023: In the summer of 2023 a witness named David Grusch testified under oath before Congress in Washington about what he had found on hidden government UFO work. Jesse Michels comes back to it again and again across his episodes, and in one he gives the exact date, July 26, 2023. Michels says Grusch "explained to the world and to our system of government a host of staggering revelations", chief among them that the military has a program to recover crashed alien craft. If true, it would mean the US government has been holding non-human craft in secret. The UFO investigator James Fox also tells it, as someone who watched the testimony live on his phone. He describes Grusch testifying under oath "to a bipartisan group of lawmakers", meaning members of both parties. The tellers agree on the event and differ only in what they stress: the date, the oath, or the audience.
grusch-testimony-some-craft-were-gifted-: Some of the unknown craft the US government holds were given to it, not just found after crashes, according to Jesse Michels' reading of the 2023 testimony of a former intelligence officer named David Grusch. Michels gives this in his own words, saying it is one of the interesting points to come out of Grusch's account. If true, it would mean someone handed humans objects that give us a head start.
grusch-testimony-under-oath-and-inspecto: The story is that in 2023 David Grusch, a former US intelligence officer, gave sworn testimony to Congress and filed a complaint with the inspector general, an internal watchdog, about secret programmes that recover crashed craft. Michels says Grusch brought 40 firsthand whistleblowers to Thomas Monheim, the inspector general of the intelligence community, and that Monheim judged the complaint "urgent" and credible. Marik von Rennenkampff, a former Defense Department official, tells it as part of a wider pattern: firsthand people went to the inspector general, and Luis Elizondo, who once ran a small Pentagon office that studied UFO reports, went under oath to say, "Yes, we have crash retrieval programs." If true, the US government would be hiding recovered craft that are not of human making.
grusch-the-symbol-rate-is-too-slow: A former US intelligence official turned whistleblower named David Grusch told Michels, in an interview, that it is almost as if the symbol rate is too slow, meaning the speed at which information can pass is too low. Michels repeats the remark himself in an episode on consciousness and Plato's cave, the old story about mistaking shadows for reality, using it to suggest that human ways of communicating may be too slow to grasp what lies behind UFOs.
grusch-uses-the-data-to-find-40-witnesse: David Grusch, a former intelligence officer turned UFO whistleblower, is said to have used a store of collected data to track down 40 witnesses. The physicist Eric W. Davis says this, explaining that Grusch "ran with our data mine", meaning material Davis had gathered with a fellow physicist named Hal Puthoff. If true, it would mean Grusch's witness list grew out of their earlier work.
grush-tells-moskowitz-he-would-answer-on: At a 2023 hearing in the US Congress, the congressman Jared Moskowitz asked a whistleblower named David Grusch whether he had ever seen images from overhead collection, meaning spy satellites or aircraft, showing UFOs and UFO crashes. Grusch talked around the first question, then said of the second that he would have to answer it in the closed session, a private classified hearing. A UFO researcher who goes by UAPGerb recounts this exchange on Michels's show in 2026, which some read as a hint that such images exist.
guarded-portal-facility-under-forest-ser: "There is a portal in the United States," the story goes: a guarded facility at Bradshaw Ranch in Arizona, hidden behind the cover of the US Forest Service, the agency that manages national forests. The Australian investigative journalist Ross Coulthart passes this on from what he was told by a source he does not name.
guardians-of-the-ark-sicken-and-die: The writer Graham Hancock says that the monks appointed to guard the Ark of the Covenant, the sacred chest of the Bible said to be kept in a church in Aksum, Ethiopia, fall sick and die very quickly, living only about three years after they take the post. He tells it in one conversation as something he was told, and in a later one as what he learned from his own interviews, adding that the guardians develop cataracts. If true, it would hint that the object kept there is something physically dangerous.
gudea-of-sumer-given-temple-plans-in-a-d: An ancient king of Sumer, the early civilisation of what is now Iraq, is said to have written that in a dream he was given lapis lazuli, a deep blue stone, along with the plans for a temple. Michels brings this up himself, calling the king "Judaea" (the name in the record is Gudea), alongside other ancient rulers he names, Thutmose IV and Nebuchadnezzar. He tells it as an example of great buildings said to have been planned from visions.
guest-contacts-hal-puthoff-as-a-high-sch: A researcher who appeared on the show, and is not named, says that around 2002, while still in high school, he got in touch with the physicist Hal Puthoff. He tells it as his own experience, an early step into the subject that led to later research on the Moon and space secrets. It matters to him as the start of his link to a well-known figure in the field.
guest-interns-at-the-pear-lab-2003: Around 2003, an unnamed researcher who appears as a guest says they got in touch with the Princeton Engineering Anomalies Research lab, a Princeton University group that studied whether the human mind could affect machines and events, and went to intern there. The guest tells this from their own experience and names the lab's leaders, Brenda Dunne and Robert Jahn.
guest-s-attempt-to-show-aldrin-uap-image: A researcher named Maaneli Derakhshani says he tried to reach the astronaut Buzz Aldrin, who walked on the Moon, to show him unexplained objects he says he found in photographs from Apollo 11 and Apollo 17, two of NASA's Moon missions. He says he wrote through one of Aldrin's assistants at Buzz Aldrin Ventures, the astronaut's company, and got a polite reply. He tells it himself, as part of his case that the Moon missions caught things NASA has not explained.
guest-s-statistical-analysis-of-ganzfeld: In Ganzfeld trials, telepathy tests run from the 1970s in which one person, resting with their senses muted, tries to pick up an image another person is trying to send, the hit rate across the best-quality studies seems to be around 30 to 35 percent. A researcher who appears as a guest on Michels's show gives this figure, pointing to the work of a parapsychologist named Charles Honorton. The guest offers it as a sign that something beyond chance may be going on.
guest-saw-no-ufo-trace-among-stony-brook: From 2004 to 2008 a student at Stony Brook University in New York talked with nearly all its leading theoretical physicists and mathematicians and never saw "any hint or trace" of interest in UFOs. That student, the physicist Maaneli Derakhshani, says so from his own time there, at the university's physics institute and as president of the math club, and he mentions the mathematician Jim Simons. He tells it to push back on the idea that scientists there were tied to secret UFO work.
guest-shadowbanned-after-posting-photo-w: An unnamed researcher on the show says that when he posted a picture of himself with Robert Malone, a doctor known for public controversy, taken at a gathering called Heretic-con, he was "shadowbanned instantly" on X, the site once called Twitter, meaning his posts were quietly hidden from others. He tells it as something that happened to him in the 2020s. To him it shows how fast certain associations get suppressed online.
guide-s-son-claims-his-father-led-armstr: When the astronaut Neil Armstrong explored the Tayos Cave in Ecuador in 1975, his guide deliberately sent him the wrong way, so the expedition never found what it was looking for. Michels says he is in touch with the guide's son, who claims this. In one telling Michels names the son as his friend Luis Felipe San Salvador and adds that he says he knows the real location of the thing. If true, whatever was sought in the cave would still be there, and the family would know where.
gus-grissom-s-lemon-and-cia-on-the-launc: Before his death in 1967, the astronaut Gus Grissom is said to have hung a lemon on a coat hanger outside his Apollo spacecraft on the launch pad to protest how badly things were working. Joe Rogan, the comedian and podcast host, tells it at second hand, crediting sources that include Grissom's wife. According to Rogan, Grissom said, "We can't even communicate with the tower, how we're ever going to communicate when we're in space." Michels mentions it in passing and says Grissom died the next day. Both tell it as a sign that something about his death, and the programme around it, was wrong.
guthrie-law-article-finds-no-prosecution: A young lawyer named Dylan Guthrie wrote a legal article in the 2020s finding that no one has ever been prosecuted for disclosing classified information to Congress through secure channels. Kurt McConnell, a former US Senate staffer, brings up the piece, which he believes came out in the Harvard Law Review. It matters because it suggests insiders with UFO secrets could speak to Congress without fear of jail.
guy-banister-544-camp-street-and-the-fbi: Before he shot President Kennedy in 1963, Lee Harvey Oswald was working out of a building at 544 Camp Street in New Orleans, and that building was owned by Guy Banister, a prominent FBI man who, according to Michels, ran the bureau's UFO collection, the "real X-Files" that the television show was based on. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, in a conversation with Joe Rogan, as a link between the Kennedy killing and government UFO secrets.
guy-banister-reports-ufo-sightings-to-ho: In 1947, in the Pacific Northwest, a man named Guy Banister had the job of reporting UFO sightings back to J. Edgar Hoover, the head of the FBI, under an assignment called "special mission X". A researcher named Peter Levenda, presented on the show as a historian of the CIA, tells this without naming a source. If true, it would mean the FBI was quietly collecting UFO reports from the very start of the modern sightings.
gwynne-shotwell-s-special-launch-shoes-a: Gwynne Shotwell, the chief operating officer of the rocket company SpaceX, whom Michels says basically runs it now, has said she wears her special shoes on launch days. Michels brings this up himself, crediting something called Countdown to Launch, as an example of how even hard-nosed engineers keep small rituals.
h-g-wells-the-world-set-free-predicts-th: The novel The World Set Free, published in 1914 by the English writer H.G. Wells, describes the building of an atomic bomb, decades before one existed. A former Air Force missile officer named Robert Salas brings this up on the show, telling it from his own reading without naming another source. He raises it as an example of an idea seen long before it became real.
hahn-splits-the-atom-in-1938: In 1938 a German scientist named Otto Hahn did an experiment that was the first to split the atom, the discovery that later led to nuclear weapons. The former Air Force officer Robert Salas tells this from memory, calling Hahn "a Nazi scientist" and adding "I think" about the name, as background to his own story of nuclear missiles and UFOs.
haim-eshed-and-the-galactic-federation-2: In 2020 Haim Eshed, described on the show as the former head of Israel's equivalent of a space force, is said to have claimed in his autobiography that a Galactic Federation of aliens exists and that the United States and other nations are in direct contact with it. If true, it would be a senior official confirming secret contact with beings from elsewhere. Michels tells it several times and adds more each time: a secret space program, an underground base on Mars where American astronauts work with aliens, and "factions of aliens fighting each other." The filmmaker James Fox, without naming Eshed, stresses that heading Israel's space effort is "an extremely important position," which is why the claim carries weight. A guest named Chris Ramsay mentions Eshed's Galactic Federation as being "here to stop our nukes."
haim-eshed-claims-us-astronauts-and-alie: In 2020, Haim Eshed, the former head of the space office in Israel's defense ministry and in effect the father of the Israeli space programme, publicly said that American astronauts and alien representatives were working together at underground bases on Mars. Michels relays the claim himself in an episode about a hacker who says he found NASA's secret space programme. If true, it would mean a hidden human presence on Mars alongside aliens.
haim-eshed-s-galactic-federation-and-mar: A man from Israel named Haim Eshed has claimed that a galactic federation exists, and that there is a space program with people on Mars. Michels brings this up himself on the show, pointing to Eshed's own background as the reason the claim drew notice, since it would mean a hidden off-world program run alongside contact with other beings.
haitian-traditions-of-beings-among-us: In Haiti there are said to be old traditions of strange beings living among people, and of people seeing them. The religion scholar Diana Pasulka says a man emailed her about this. He told her that when he came to the United States he could hardly believe that people here had no belief in such things, given what he had seen back in Haiti.
hal-povenmire-s-visits-from-2008-and-his: A man named Hal Povenmire visited from 2008 on and, before he died in 2019, came to believe the phenomenon he had been studying was angelic. Chris Bledsoe, a man in Fayetteville, North Carolina, who says he has had repeated UFO encounters, relays what Povenmire told him. It matters because it shows someone close to the case seeing the visitors as spiritual rather than alien.
hal-puthoff-contacts-grant-cameron-about: A UFO researcher named Grant Cameron says the physicist Hal Puthoff suddenly got in touch with him about letters and photographs belonging to Arthur Lundahl, a government photo analyst. Cameron tells it as something that happened to him, and he sees it as a sign that people close to the government's UFO work took his research seriously.
hal-puthoff-on-rogan-us-holds-15-crashed: The United States holds about 15 crashed craft, the physicist Hal Puthoff is said to have told the podcaster Joe Rogan in 2025. Michels repeats this several times but gives the number differently, once as 12 to 15, once as 10 to 40, and once asks where Puthoff gets it; he also says Puthoff worked with President George W. Bush and his national security adviser Stephen Hadley on whether to make disclosures. If true, the government would hold a fleet of non-human craft.
hal-puthoff-ordered-copies-of-ufos-and-n: When the first edition of UFOs and Nukes came out, the physicist Hal Puthoff suddenly wrote to its author asking for four copies shipped overnight, to hand out to people in Washington. UFOs and Nukes is a book about unidentified craft seen near nuclear weapons sites, and the researcher Robert Hastings, who wrote it, tells this from his own experience. He tells it as a sign that his book was reaching people in government, years before a New York Times article in December 2017 revealed a secret Pentagon UFO study.
hal-puthoff-s-2004-white-house-conversat: In 2004, a conversation at the White House is said to have asked whether the American people were ready to be told the truth about UFOs. A former Pentagon intelligence official named Luis Elizondo brings it up, pointing to how the physicist Hal Puthoff had described it to Michels, and saying he could not believe Puthoff spoke about it publicly. If true, it would mean disclosure was weighed at the highest level of government twenty years ago.
hal-puthoff-s-medieval-levitating-secret: The UFO phenomenon might, by one idea, be the work of a medieval secret society that knows how to levitate and puts metal capsules around its members. Michels tells this as something the physicist Hal Puthoff said to him, apparently half in jest, while discussing what could lie behind the phenomenon. If true, it would mean the craft are human, not alien.
hal-puthoff-starts-the-government-s-psyc: In the 1970s, the story goes, a laser physicist named Hal Puthoff started the US government's psychic spy programme, an effort to use people with claimed psychic abilities to gather intelligence, at the Stanford Research Institute, a research centre in California. Michels tells it himself on several episodes, saying Puthoff "started the government's psychic spy program," that he "ran" it "for the CIA," the US foreign intelligence agency, and that he was "the founding architect of Stargate," the name of the programme. A Navy admiral named Tim Gallaudet calls Puthoff "a good friend and colleague" who has "shared extensively" about Stargate, runs it up to 1995, and names Paul Smith, Ingo Swann and Joe McMoneagle as people who took part. If true, the government would have spent decades taking psychic spying seriously.
hal-saflieni-hypogeum-oracle-room-tuned-: The Hal Saflieni Hypogeum, an ancient underground complex carved into rock in Malta, has a chamber called the Oracle Room that is "precision tuned to 111 hertz," a deep sound frequency, according to a guest named Jay Anderson. Anderson tells this as someone who has been there, and if it is true it would mean the ancient builders shaped the room on purpose to make sound resonate in it.
hal-warns-of-33-million-volts-2007: The craft or lights Chris Bledsoe encountered in North Carolina in 2007 carried something like 33 million volts. Bledsoe, who says he has had repeated UFO encounters, relays this from a man he calls Hal Pavvenmeer, who told him that people knew the voltage of one of these things. If true, the objects would hold enormous electrical power, dangerous to anyone near them.
haldi-as-celestial-intelligence-rather-t: Haldi, a god worshipped in ancient times around Lake Van in Turkey, is better understood as some kind of intelligence from the heavens than as a visiting alien of the kind ancient astronaut stories describe. A researcher named Matt LaCroix offers this view on Michels's show in 2024, as his own reading without a named source. It changes what the old gods would have been, if he is right.
haldi-relief-read-as-a-spearhead-sites-c: Near Lake Van in eastern Turkey there is an ancient carving known as the Haldi relief, and archaeologists read the object one figure passes in its hand as a spearhead. A researcher named Matt LaCroix describes this reading without naming a source, saying archaeologists "believe firmly" it is a weapon and so see the people as warlike. He adds that the old sites there are called fortresses, "kalesi" in Turkish, and he presents both readings as the experts' view, implying the carvings may mean something else.
half-of-a-ready-room-says-they-saw-the-c: A Navy fighter pilot named Ryan Graves says that after a New York Times article about these objects came out, he spoke to a group of pilots in a ready room, the room where a squadron meets for briefings, in a different region from the East Coast where he had flown. He says that when he asked, "about half the room raised their hand," saying they had seen "the cubes and spheres" too. Graves tells it as his own experience, and it would mean the sightings were common across squadrons, not limited to one.
hall-confirms-tall-white-restroom-visits: A former Air Force weather observer named Charles Hall says that tall, pale beings he calls the Tall Whites used the restroom in the operations building at Nellis Air Force Base in Nevada, around 1965. Another man had told him this, and Hall says he later learned at first hand that the man was telling the truth, on a day when his own work took him there. He tells it to back up his larger claim that he spent three years in contact with these beings near Area 51, the secret Nevada test site.
hall-photon-theory-copyrighted-1997-and-: Charles Hall, a man who says he spent three years among tall white aliens at an Air Force range in Nevada, says the craft he saw there going faster than light inspired a physics theory of his own about photons. Hall says he first copyrighted this theory in 1997. He lays it out in books he names, Beyond Relativity, Mirage Galaxies and Edges in Space, and Walking with the Tall Whites Aftermath.
hall-s-books-presented-to-pope-benedict-: The wife of Charles Hall, a former Air Force man who says he spent three years with tall white aliens at a secret Nevada base, says she took his first three books to Rome in the mid 2000s as a gift for Pope Benedict. She says the pope sent back a thank-you note, which is reproduced in Hall's fourth book.
hall-s-orders-said-he-could-never-be-bri: From 1965 to 1967, a former Air Force man named Charles Hall, who says he spent three years with tall white aliens at Indian Springs on Nellis Air Force Base in Nevada, was under orders saying he could never be briefed or debriefed, meaning never formally told the rules of a secret programme on entering or released from them on leaving. Hall tells it himself, saying "the reason is very simple," and he mentions a being he calls the Teacher, which suggests his work there sat outside any normal secret programme.
halloween-s-origins-linked-to-the-fall-t: The ancient roots of Halloween are tied to the Taurid meteor shower, a display of shooting stars that comes every autumn. A researcher named Randall Carlson draws this link on the show without naming a source. His point is that the holiday may preserve an old memory of things falling from the sky.
halls-of-amenti-ancient-library-under-th: Beneath the Great Sphinx at Giza in Egypt, the story goes, lies a hidden chamber holding an ancient library, a "hall of records." A guest named Matt LaCroix says "we're told by things like Edgar Cayce and others" that such a library was supposed to be under the Sphinx, Cayce being a man known for his visions. A researcher named Luke Caverns tells it as Cayce's own vision, dated to the 1940s, of a chamber whose records "tell the story of Atlantis," the legendary lost civilisation. If true, a written account of a forgotten world would be sitting under one of Egypt's best known monuments.
halt-hears-radio-reports-of-beams-into-w: During the 1980 sightings at RAF Bentwaters, an air base in England used by the US Air Force, the officer Charles Halt heard reports over his radio of an object hovering above the base's weapons storage area. Security police back at the storage area said the object was sending beams of light down into it. The researcher Robert Hastings, who studies UFOs seen near nuclear weapons sites, tells this on Michels's show without naming a source, as an example of UFOs taking an interest in nuclear weapons.
halt-memo-on-rendlesham-lights-1980: In 1980, a security patrol near a US air base in England is said to have seen strange lights coming down into the nearby Rendlesham Forest. Michels says an Air Force officer there, Lieutenant Colonel Charles Halt, set out the whole incident in a memo to the UK Ministry of Defence, the British government department in charge of the military. He brings it up as an official, signed account of something unexplained seen near a military base.
halton-arp-s-interacting-galaxies-with-d: The astronomer Halton Arp, famous in his field for a long time, found pairs of galaxies that seemed to be trading gas, which means they should be side by side, yet their redshifts, the shift in their light that astronomers use to judge distance, were completely different. The astronomer Beatriz Villarroel tells this on Michels's show in 2025 as a known episode in the field, without naming a source. If Arp was right, the usual way of measuring how far away galaxies are would be in question.
hameroff-s-view-of-microtubules-and-anes: An anesthesiologist named Stuart Hameroff noticed that when anesthesia shuts down microtubules, the tiny tube-like structures inside cells, the rest of the brain and body keep working normally but the person loses consciousness. Michels tells this himself in two episodes, tying it to a book by the writer Roger Penrose called The Emperor's New Mind. He raises it because, if true, it would point to microtubules as the place where consciousness is switched on and off.
hamlet-s-mill-on-ancient-knowledge-of-pr: Ancient peoples had "very ancient very early knowledge" of precession, the slow wobble of the Earth that shifts the stars over thousands of years, according to the book Hamlet's Mill, written in the 1960s by the historian of science Giorgio de Santillana of MIT and the scholar Hertha von Dechend of Frankfurt University. The writer Graham Hancock cites the book on Michels's show. If true, it would mean early cultures tracked the sky with far more skill than usually believed.
hancock-s-ayahuasca-alien-abduction-visi: The author Graham Hancock says that in 2003, after drinking ayahuasca, a psychedelic brew used by Amazon shamans, he had a vision outside a shaman's hut of being taken by aliens. He says he saw not one but several flying saucers above him, and the familiar alien face, heart-shaped with large dark eyes. He tells it as his own experience, and it raises the question of whether such visions touch something beyond the mind.
hancock-the-great-pyramid-was-not-a-tomb: The Great Pyramid at Giza in Egypt was not built as a tomb but as a kind of portal: that is what the author Graham Hancock told Jesse Michels, as Michels relays it on several episodes. Michels says he asked Hancock outright what the pyramids were for if not burial, and Hancock almost implied a stargate lined up with the stars of Orion's belt; another time Michels calls it a "celestial ascent chamber portal thing" and speaks of the pyramids in the plural. If true, the most famous monument on Earth would have had a purpose far stranger than the textbooks say.
hancockdibble-debate-and-the-shipwreck-d: In a 2024 debate between the writer Graham Hancock, who argues for a lost ancient civilization, and the archaeologist Flint Dibble, Dibble is said to have got all his shipwreck data completely wrong. Michels says this himself, telling listeners they can watch the debate and then fact-check Dibble. If true, it would weaken one of the arguments made against Hancock's ideas.
handoff-to-the-next-contact-by-a-call-on: In the early 1990s, at his first base after training, Dan Sherman, a former Air Force sergeant who says the National Security Agency (the US spy agency that listens to communications) hired him to talk with aliens, got a phone call in his dorm from his first contact officer, a Captain White. Sherman tells Michels that White gave him the name of the next person he would deal with and said he would meet that person at a set time, recognising him because "he would have his arms folded." Sherman tells it twice, and in one telling he places the base overseas in a warm climate and says he was briefed into the programme there; the story shows how, by his account, the secret programme passed him quietly from one handler to the next.
hannah-mcroberts-flying-saucer-photo-198: On October 8, 1981, a woman named Hannah McRoberts was out driving with her husband on Vancouver Island, Canada, and stopped near a well-known mountain, and that stop is where her photo of a flying saucer comes from. The researcher Clas Svahn tells it, passing on what McRoberts herself described and pointing to a collection he calls the Files of the Unexplained. He tells it because the photo would be a picture of a real saucer if it shows what it seems to.
hans-kammler-comes-to-the-us-1945: Hans Kammler, the Nazi officer in charge of Germany's most secret "wonder weapon" programmes, made his way to the United States after the war, according to Michels. He says "we now know" this, but tells it himself without naming a source. If true, it would mean the man behind Hitler's most secret weapons work ended up on the American side.
hans-kammler-s-skoda-works-saucer-projec: From 1942 to 1945, the story goes, Hans Kammler, an officer in the SS, the Nazi party's own armed force, ran a secret weapons unit called the Skoda Works, which is tied in the telling to German work on saucer-shaped craft. Michels brings this up himself, saying there is "real documented evidence" for it in a book by the writer Tom Agoston about Kammler and in US Air Force documents. In another episode he is more careful, saying Kammler "probably" ran it, calling it "the German Skunk Works" (after the American aircraft maker Lockheed's secret design shop), and pointing to the journalist Nick Cook's book The Hunt for Zero Point. If it is true, the Nazis were building secret advanced craft during the war.
hapgood-s-earth-crustal-displacement: The North Pole was once where Hudson Bay in Canada is today, because the Earth's outer crust slid as a whole across the planet and moved the poles. This is the idea of a writer named Charles Hapgood, known as earth crustal displacement, and the researcher Jason Jorjani sums it up for Michels without naming a further source. If true, lands such as Antarctica would once have sat in a warmer place, which would change how we read the deep past.
harassment-of-ufo-whistleblowers-2010: The scholar Diana Pasulka, who studies belief in UFOs, says she saw with her own eyes people who had come forward as UFO whistleblowers, insiders who speak out about secret programs, being harassed. She told Jesse Michels this in 2024, as something she witnessed over years of research. If true, it would mean someone is working to silence people who talk.
hard-drives-recovered-from-a-glacier-lak: A helicopter pilot named Jake Barber, who says he helped retrieve a UFO, says his team tracked down a person acting as their source, who led them high into the Sierra Nevada mountains of California to a glacier lake where hard drives were sealed in a steel container about 25 feet underwater. He tells it as an operation he took part in; in a later retelling he says the drives came from Toughbooks, rugged military laptops, and credits a man named Don Paul Bales. It is told as evidence that records tied to the secret retrievals were deliberately hidden.
hard-object-found-in-nostril-during-2001: Richard Barth, a former guard at a nuclear missile site who says he was taken by aliens, says that around 2001 he had nasal surgery for a deviated septum that made breathing hard, and a hard object was found in his nostril. He tells it as his own experience. He raises it because it might be a physical trace linked to his abduction.
harold-malmgren-nhi-track-the-frontier-o: Non-human intelligences are said to operate by watching the cutting edge of human invention, according to a presidential adviser named Harold Malmgren. Michels says Malmgren told him this himself, and describes him as an adviser who worked directly with Presidents Kennedy, Johnson, Nixon and Ford and who was briefed on UFOs. If true, it would mean whatever is visiting is drawn to wherever human technology is advancing fastest.
harold-malmgren-s-cia-connections-and-id: Michels argues that Harold Malmgren, a veteran Washington economic official he interviewed, had deep ties to the CIA from the 1960s on, with work at IDA, a defense research body, serving as a cover. As Michels tells it from his own interview, Malmgren said he was best friends with Tom Farmer, the CIA's general counsel, or chief lawyer, and he names others in that circle, such as Richard Bissell and Paul Mellon. Michels adds that he held Paul Mellon's walking stick for half the interview and mentions Malmgren's diary.
harold-malmgren-s-deathbed-account-of-na: A man named Harold Malmgren said near the end of his life that he was warned Naval Intelligence, the US Navy's spy service, would come asking about his study, would be impressed by how much he knew, and would "offer you special access" into secret work. Michels relays this as Malmgren's deathbed account, as a picture of how outsiders get pulled into hidden programs.
harold-malmgren-tweets-about-bissell-bri: Harold Malmgren, who advised Presidents Kennedy, Johnson, Nixon and Ford, has been posting online about things he learned in that role, including being briefed by Richard Bissell, a senior CIA official of that era. Michels tells this himself, drawing on Malmgren's own posts, to the UFO campaigner Steven Greer, as a sign that a high-level insider from the 1960s and 70s is now speaking about what he was told.
harrington-aliens-are-real-and-he-has-se: John S. Herrington, a US government official who later served as Secretary of Energy, once said privately: "Aliens are real. They're here and I've seen them." Brent Friedman, a Hollywood writer who says he was there, tells this from a conversation at the Herrington home around 1981. In one telling he places the home in Virginia; in another, the Washington DC area, saying it came out on the veranda after a couple of drinks and tying it to a briefing in West Virginia. If true, a senior official would have personally seen alien beings.
harrington-briefed-for-months-in-undergr: John S. Herrington, a former US Secretary of Energy, said he was briefed for months in an underground facility in West Virginia, and that seeing the aliens came only around day three. The Hollywood writer Brent Friedman tells it, repeating what he says Herrington told him, including the line: "No, Brent, you don't understand. That was like day three." If true, a cabinet member would have been shown far more than the public knows.
harrington-denies-brent-friedman-s-accou: John S. Herrington, a former US Secretary of Energy, flatly denies a story the Hollywood screenwriter Brent Friedman tells about him from around 1981, set between Walnut Creek, California and Washington. Herrington says on the podcast that the claim he told Friedman he had "been locked away for a month" and had "seen people from another planet" is "all a lie" and "total BS." This matters because Friedman's version would have a former cabinet member admitting to seeing aliens, and Herrington himself says it never happened.
harrington-has-seen-lasers-that-could-br: The US Secretary of Energy, John S. Herrington, says he has seen laser technology that could bring down almost anything. He says so from his own experience in office, speaking with Jesse Michels in 2026. It comes up as a hint at how far secret weapons work has gone, perhaps far enough to bring down unknown craft.
harrington-s-buck-slip-congratulating-br: A television writer named Brent Friedman says that in 1996, while working on Dark Skies, a TV series about a hidden UFO story, he got a buck slip, a short office note, from John S. Herrington, a former US Secretary of Energy. Friedman says the note read: "Hey Brent, you finally got your story out there. Congratulations." He tells it as his own experience, and in one telling he places it the week before a show he calls Sound, Light and Frequency premiered. The suggestion is that a senior official was hinting that the story was true.
harrington-s-contact-with-david-grusch-a: In 2023, a witness named David Grusch testified before the US Congress about secret government knowledge of UFOs, and he later wrote to a former US Secretary of Energy, John S. Herrington. Herrington tells Michels about it himself, saying Grusch sent him "a beautiful letter," a "long two-page letter." He brings it up to show that the man behind that testimony reached out to him directly.
harrington-s-fukushima-delegation-visit-: After the 2011 disaster at the Fukushima nuclear power plant in Japan, a delegation went to learn what had happened, and the man leading it told them that Fukushima "did not kill anybody." A former US Secretary of Energy named John S. Herrington tells this as someone who was with that delegation, and he uses it to argue that nuclear power is safer than people fear.
harrington-s-global-economy-reason-for-s: A former US Secretary of Energy named John S. Herrington is said to have explained UFO secrecy as a way to protect the global economy. A man named Brent Friedman relays what Herrington told him: that revealing the truth would take away people's reason for living their lives as they do, and then "everything falls apart and governments of the world will not be able to control the populace." It offers a reason, from a senior official, for why governments would keep such a secret.
harrington-tours-the-greenbrier-bunker-1: John S. Herrington, a former US Secretary of Energy, says that while in that job in the mid 1980s he toured the secret government bunker at the Greenbrier, a resort in West Virginia. He says he was there playing golf and went to see it. He tells it firsthand, as one of the hidden government places he saw from inside.
harry-reid-s-plan-for-a-billion-dollar-a: Harry Reid, the Nevada senator who led the US Senate, meant a Pentagon-funded study of unexplained aerial phenomena begun in 2008, the Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program, to grow into something like the Manhattan Project, the wartime crash effort that built the atomic bomb. That is the account of the physicist Eric W. Davis, who worked on the programme and says Reid saw the first funding as just a start, planning about a decade of work worth "a billion dollars maybe $2 billion." If so, the government came close to a huge, serious effort to study these objects.
harry-reid-s-request-for-sap-status-deni: The physicist Eric W. Davis says that in 2009, Senator Harry Reid wrote to the deputy secretary of defense, William Lynn, asking him to make the UFO research Davis was part of a special access program, which is the most tightly guarded kind of secret government project. Davis says Lynn turned the request down. He tells this as an insider, and he points to Reid's letter to Lynn. If true, it means the work was refused the extra secrecy and protection Reid wanted for it.
harry-reid-s-special-access-program-requ: Harry Reid, the US Senate majority leader, is said to have tried in 2009 to get UFO research made into a special access program, a tightly restricted kind of secret Pentagon project, and to have failed. According to the physicist Eric W. Davis, a former Pentagon contractor on UFO studies, the request was turned down by William Lynn, then Deputy Secretary of Defense. If true, even a powerful senator could not get that level of secrecy approved for the work.
harry-reid-the-ufo-information-is-alread: Harry Reid, the US Senate leader from Nevada, is said to have been asked by a journalist how a study of UFOs should start, and to have answered: "What are you talking about? It's all already there." The writer Peter Levenda repeats the exchange. If true, it would mean the government already holds the UFO information and does not need to go looking for it.
harry-rositzke-pulled-out-of-retirement-: A retired intelligence man named Harry Rositzke was brought back out of retirement to help run an unofficial operation against the Russians, the Chinese, or other rivals. A researcher named Greg Bishop tells this without naming a source, in an episode about a man he says was driven to madness by "aliens". Bishop also names the German spy chief Reinhard Gehlen in the same account, which would point to a secret operation running outside official channels.
harry-turner-investigates-uap-sightings-: A man named Harry Turner was invited to look into several sightings of UAP, unidentified anomalous phenomena, the official term for UFOs, at Maralinga in Australia, a remote site used for weapons tests, in the 1950s or 60s. Ross Coulthart, who has researched the subject, tells this without naming a source, and he also mentions the Australian UFO researcher Bill Chalker. If true, it would mean unexplained objects were being seen, and quietly investigated, at one of the country's most sensitive sites.
harry-turner-s-1971-australian-intellige: An Australian intelligence report from 1971 is said to show that the United States quietly studied UFOs and tried to learn how to control gravity in the 1950s. Jesse Michels brings it up again and again. He says it was written by Harry Turner, whom he calls the head of the nuclear division of the Joint Intelligence Organisation, an Australian spy agency he describes as "basically Australia's CIA", though once he says he is not sure of Turner's exact post. As Michels quotes it, the document reads: "A more astounding decision on the part of the US government was to allocate considerable funds to investigate gravity and a means of controlling gravity." According to Michels, it names famous physicists such as J. Robert Oppenheimer, Edward Teller and Freeman Dyson among the people involved, and it says Turner urged Australia to put more effort into UFO research. Michels also says it describes a research institute at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, run by a businessman named Agnew Bahnson, as an academic outpost of the CIA studying anti-gravity, and that it calls Blue Book, the US Air Force's UFO study of the 1950s and 60s, a public relations front. The researcher Ross Coulthart gives the date as 1972 and says the report covers the recovery of crashed craft and a UFO "flying squad". The researcher Eric Weinstein also cites it, and Michels says the UFO whistleblower David Grusch quotes it often. If it says what they say, a foreign ally was recording secret American work on gravity and UFOs decades ago.
harry-turner-ufo-obsessed-intelligence-c: Harry Turner, said to head the nuclear division of Australia's Joint Intelligence Organisation, the country's defence intelligence agency, was obsessed with UFOs. Michels says Turner's area covered the Woomera test range, a large Australian weapons testing site, and tells it himself without naming a source. He raises it as one more link between UFOs and nuclear sites, in an episode with the astronomer Beatriz Villarroel.
harvard-neuroscientist-s-telepathic-kids: Jesse Michels says he recently interviewed a Harvard brain scientist who is studying children said to be telepathic, able to read minds. He mentions it in passing in a 2025 conversation and does not name the scientist. It comes up as a sign that serious scientists are starting to test claims about the mind that most dismiss.
harvard-tried-to-get-rid-of-john-mack-wh: Harvard is said to have tried to push out John Mack, a psychiatry professor there, over his work with people who said they had met aliens. Luis Elizondo, a former Pentagon official, says he passes on that Mack fought back and won a legal case. The writer Whitley Strieber says Mack was invited to a meeting that was really an ambush, aimed at taking away his licence to practise psychiatry. The lawyer Dan Sheehan tells it as someone who took part: he says Mack called him when he faced a faculty committee and asked him to be his lawyer. To them it shows what a respected scientist risked by taking these stories seriously.
haseltine-s-novel-out-of-time-hiding-tru: A former director of research at the NSA, the US government's electronic spying agency, named Eric Haseltine wrote a book that Jesse Michels calls "fiction" in air quotes, a novel he thinks was titled Out of Time. Michels, who has interviewed Haseltine on his show, suggests the novel may carry real truths dressed up as a story, coming from someone with inside knowledge.
hastings-confessions-his-own-abduction-e: The researcher Robert Hastings, after writing UFOs and Nukes, a book about UFOs seen around nuclear weapons, wrote a further book called Confessions about his own experiences of being abducted by beings. Michels mentions this himself, in passing, while talking about Hastings' work.
hastings-did-not-systematically-ask-witn: Robert Hastings, a researcher who interviewed many military veterans about UFOs over nuclear sites, did not ask all of his witnesses whether they had seen beings as well as craft. Michels says he asked Hastings directly whether he had systematically put that question to everyone, and Hastings said, "No." It matters because more of those witnesses might have had close encounters than anyone knows.
hastings-s-nuclear-site-ufo-whistleblowe: More than 167 people who worked at nuclear sites across the United States have come forward to say they saw UFOs there, according to records gathered by a researcher named Robert Hastings. Michels raises this himself on his show in 2026, citing Hastings's collection as his data. Told this way, it would mean UFOs have taken a steady interest in American nuclear weapons.
hastings-s-phone-calls-followed-by-heavy: Mostly in February 1982, each time Robert Hastings, a researcher who looks into UFOs seen over nuclear weapons bases, finished a phone call with one of his sources, his phone would ring again within one to ten minutes, and on the line there was "nothing but heavy breathing." Hastings tells it himself, and if true it would mean someone was listening to his calls.
hatshepsut-s-obelisk-inscription-dedicat: An inscription on the obelisk of Hatshepsut, an ancient Egyptian queen who ruled as pharaoh, at the temple of Karnak dedicates the tall stone pillar to her father, the god Amun, and says she raised it using electrum, a natural mix of gold and silver. The researcher Luke Caverns says he has read the translated hieroglyphs and paraphrases them: "as for this obelisk I erected this from electrum." He raises it as a clue that the monument was once covered in precious metal.
haughton-mars-project-simulation-and-chr: John Blitch, a former scientist at DARPA, the Pentagon's research agency, says that in 2001 he took part in a pretend Mars mission at Haughton Crater on Devon Island, in the Arctic, where the team played at being Mars astronauts and he was "the robot guy." He says the stay included a lecture by the scientist Chris McKay. He tells it as his own experience, part of the background to the strange encounter he later describes.
havana-syndrome-as-pulsed-rf-directed-en: Havana syndrome, the unexplained illnesses reported by US officials, is said to be caused by beamed radio waves. A guest named Chris Gilbert says the current thinking is that it is radio frequency, microwave or directed energy, sent as a repeating train of very short pulses at very high peak power. Michels, on another episode, says that in the Havana syndrome cases the person is being wholly destabilized by microwaves essentially. If true, it would mean someone has a weapon that can harm people invisibly from a distance.
havana-syndrome-as-russian-attacks-since: Havana syndrome, the unexplained illness reported by US diplomats and spies, is said to have been caused by Russian attacks going back to the 1980s, according to a report by 60 Minutes, the American TV news program. Michels says the piece came out recently, made together with the German magazine Der Spiegel. Eric Haseltine, a former senior official at the NSA, the US electronic spying agency, recalls the program raising the stakes: "if it's the Russians doing it to us, that's an act of war." On another episode Michels says the CIA and the NSA blame Russia and microwave weapons, and places it in the last couple of years, without mentioning the 1980s or the program. It is told because if true it would mean a foreign power has been quietly attacking American officials for decades.
have-blue-prototype-owned-by-lockheed-sk: Have Blue, an early secret prototype of a stealth aircraft in the 1970s, is said to have belonged to Lockheed's Skunk Works, the company's secret advanced aircraft division, and not to the US Air Force, even though it carried Air Force markings. A NASA doctor named Greg Rogers says this, repeating what he was told. If true, it would show that secret aircraft can be privately owned while looking like military property.
hawara-labyrinth-and-the-2008-mataha-exp: Under Hawara in Egypt, home of a famous ancient building called the labyrinth, lies a hidden system of underground rooms, according to a researcher named Geoffrey Drumm. He says a 2008 survey he calls the Mataha expedition, linked to a researcher named Ben van Kerkwijk, scanned the site with ground-penetrating radar, a tool that sees below the surface. Drumm says they found "a huge slab, limestone slab" that is "not the floor, but actually the roof of this underground chamber system", which would mean much of the site is still unexcavated.
hawass-1992-speech-on-subterranean-labyr: In 1992, in a speech at a university in Cairo, the Egyptian archaeologist Zahi Hawass is said to have spoken of underground labyrinths beneath the Giza plateau, where the pyramids stand. A guest named Jay Anderson tells this on the show without naming a source. If true, it would mean that a senior figure in Egyptian archaeology once spoke openly of hidden passages under the pyramids.
hawkeye-360-searching-for-1-6-ghz-at-int: A company called Hawkeye 360, which picks up radio signals from space, has surely looked for signals at a radio frequency of 1.6 gigahertz at "interesting places," according to Bob Maguire, a former contractor for the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency. Maguire says he is "certain" of it but gives no source, and he raises it because a signal at that frequency could point to something unusual going on at those spots.
hawksbill-creek-agreement-and-devco-1950: Something happened in the Bahamas in the 1950s or 1960s, where a group of people struck a deal called the Hawksbill Creek agreement. The story also ties this to an outfit called Devco, about which the telling says nothing more. Jason Simosa, a researcher who also speaks as a witness, brings it up without naming a source, while arguing that the hiding of UFO knowledge leads back to one secret society.
headmaster-bans-louis-braille-s-books-at: At the first school for the blind in France, a new headmaster is said to have called the raised-dot reading system invented by Louis Braille pseudoscience and locked away all the braille books. Ky Dickens, who made a documentary about children said to read minds, tells this from the history of Louis Braille without naming a source. She gives it as an example of a real ability being dismissed as unreal by the people in charge.
heat-exchanger-and-extraction-shaft-hypo: The Great Pyramid of Giza may have been a machine, with a heat exchange system wrapping around its King's Chamber and above its long sloping hall called the Grand Gallery, and a shaft leading out of its Queen's Chamber to draw something out. A researcher named Jeffrey Drum describes this on Michels's show in 2026, drawing on the work of Filippo Biondi. If true, the pyramid would be part of an ancient energy system rather than only a tomb.
heavyweight-champion-on-cia-operations-i: In the late 1960s, at the Brotherhood Synagogue in Greenwich Village, New York, a man described as a heavyweight champion, named Andre Pinacio, talked to a group about running operations in Lebanon for the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency. Peter Levenda, a writer on the history of the occult and intelligence, tells Michels this as something he heard in person, and it shows how close spy work came to his own early life.
hedge-fund-recruits-memory-champion-nels: Around 2022, a hedge fund reached out to the memory champion Nelson Dellis through a Facebook group for memory enthusiasts and asked if he would be trained in remote viewing, the claimed ability to see distant or hidden things with the mind, so he could "remote view the stock market" for them. The magician Chris Ramsay tells Michels this, repeating what Dellis told him, and also names a man called Brett Stewart. If true, it would mean serious money people take remote viewing seriously enough to try it on markets.
hegel-s-philosophy-of-mind-on-the-parano: The German philosopher Hegel, best known for other works, wrote a book called Philosophy of Mind about the psyche, and it has long passages on the paranormal. The philosopher and researcher Jason Jorjani says this on the show, summarising it himself, and points to the scholar Glenn Alexander Magee, whose book Hegel and the Hermetic Tradition ties Hegel to older mystical thought. If so, one of the great names of Western philosophy took the paranormal seriously.
heifer-found-dead-with-ufo-shaped-object: A healthy two-year-old cow was found dead on Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property famous for strange reports, with no marks on its body, and cameras had caught an object above it. Michels tells it from the TV series The Secret of Skinwalker Ranch as one of the most disturbing things ever to happen there. The ranch's owner, Brandon Fugal, tells it at first hand, placing it in a field near the ranch's Homestead 1 and crediting a ranch worker named Thomas Winterton and a man named Caleb Benches. If true, something in the sky may have killed the animal.
heim-droscher-and-hauser-s-two-forms-of-: Gravity comes in two forms, according to a line of German theory that starts with the physicist Burkhard Heim and is carried on by two men Michels calls Rusher and Hauser, meaning Dröscher and Hauser. Michels brings this up himself in an episode with a guest who says aliens taught him advanced physics, pointing out that these Germans hold the same idea of two kinds of gravity. If true, a second kind of gravity could open a path to new ways of moving craft.
heisenberg-s-heavy-water-program-and-deu: Many of the rumours about how UFOs fly involve a reactor in the middle of the craft that runs on deuterium, a heavy kind of hydrogen. Put another way, a heavy-water engine. Michels says this himself, without naming a source, and ties it to the German physicist Werner Heisenberg's wartime heavy-water work in Nazi Germany in the 1940s. He also mentions the physicist Luis Walter Alvarez, suggesting that this old nuclear research might hold a clue to how such craft are powered.
heisenberg-s-team-calculates-the-fissile: In 1945, the German physicist Werner Heisenberg and his colleagues were secretly listened in on while held in the English countryside, and a wiretap transcript is said to show how fast they worked out the amount of fissile material, the nuclear fuel, used in the bomb dropped on Hiroshima. A researcher named Jason Jorjani brings this up on the show without naming a source, saying simply that "they overheard these guys." He tells it because, if true, it suggests the German team understood the bomb far better than they let on.
heisenberg-s-uranium-program-as-decoy-fo: The claim is that Nazi Germany's uranium enrichment program, run by the scientist Werner Heisenberg in the 1940s, was a red herring meant to draw attention away from a secret program that separated uranium by electromagnetic means. The researcher Jason Jorjani lays this out as the picture that "emerges," drawing on the writer Plimpton Hydrick's book Critical Mass and on a writer named Farrell. If true, Germany's real atomic work was hidden behind the program everyone was watching.
heiser-affirms-the-watchers-and-their-gi: The late Bible scholar Michael Heiser accepted the old story of the Watchers, fallen angels who are said to have fathered a race of giants, and the related tale of the Anakim, giants named in the Bible. A researcher named Tim Alberino says this, summarising Heiser's view as he understands it, with reference to Heiser's book The Unseen Realm and Alberino's own work Reversing Hermon. He tells it to show that a serious scholar treated the giants of scripture as real.
helen-mccall-s-sol-foundation-white-pape: A writer named Helen McCall is said to have written a white paper, a short policy report, for the Sol Foundation, a research group, on whether UAPs (unidentified anomalous phenomena, the official term for UFOs) could be a risk to financial stability. A researcher named Matthew Pines brings it up in passing, without saying more about what it found. He mentions it because, in his telling, it takes on exactly the question of what an official admission about UFOs could do to markets.
helicopter-chases-of-about-15-uap-in-60-: James Valor, of Skywatcher, a startup that says it can summon UFOs, says that in 2025 he chased about 15 unidentified objects by helicopter over roughly 60 days. He tells it as his own fieldwork: once something appears, the team gets into the helicopter and pursues it. It is offered as a sign that the objects can be called up and followed on purpose.
helicopter-freezes-mid-air-while-trying-: Skywatcher, a startup that says it can call up UFOs, says that in 2025 it sent a helicopter after a "tic-tac", a white oval object shaped like the mint, about 7 kilometres northwest of its site. A team member says that about half a mile away, the object "stopped moving" and froze in mid-air as the helicopter came near. He tells it as something the team saw, and if true it would mean the object reacted to being chased.
helicopter-harassment-after-aaro-testimo: After he gave testimony in April 2023 to the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office, the Pentagon office set up to investigate UFO reports, Michael Herrera, a man who says he saw a 300-foot craft in the Indonesian jungle, says helicopters began hovering over his house, over his father's home and over his business. Herrera tells this himself, and he presents it as pressure on him after he spoke to the government.
helicopter-recovery-of-the-20-foot-egg-2: A former helicopter pilot named Jake Barber says that he and his team picked up an egg-shaped craft, about 20 feet long, and carried it by helicopter out of the California desert. He tells it at first hand, saying they simply called it "the egg" because that is what it looked like. Jesse Michels repeats the story more than once and calls the egg extraterrestrial, and a congressman named Eric Burlison recalls Barber describing it, which would mean the US secretly recovers craft that are not man-made.
helicopters-escorting-ufos-into-mountain: Helicopters have been seen escorting some UFOs into the mountains, as if guiding them somewhere. Michels says this himself, without naming a source, on an episode with the owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a ranch known for reports of strange happenings, and takes it as a hint that someone on the ground knows where these objects go.
helicopters-vanish-into-a-pixelating-mou: In 2004, about five miles east of the town of Coyame in Mexico, helicopters are said to have flown straight into a mountainside that opened like a door: the rock began to pixelate, dissolving from three dimensions to two and then to nothing, as the aircraft slipped through and vanished "from one world into another." Michels narrates this scene from a book called Sentinels of Ether, citing a helicopter pilot named Jake Barber, and tells it as a sign that some craft may pass between our world and somewhere else.
hell-s-angels-chief-zapped-at-skinwalker: A leader of the Hell's Angels motorcycle club is said to have been "zapped" at Skinwalker Ranch, a property in Utah known for reports of strange events, and left paralyzed and catatonic on the spot. Michels mentions it only in passing and credits the story to a man named Brandon Fugal. If true, it would be one more case of the ranch physically harming the people who go there.
hells-angels-member-hospitalized-for-wee: A member of the Hells Angels motorcycle club is said to have checked himself into a hospital for weeks after a visit linked to a ranch famous for reports of strange events. Brandon Fugal, the owner of that ranch, known as Skinwalker Ranch, tells it on Jesse Michels's show, passing on what a witness named Erik Bard told him. He does not say exactly what happened on the visit, only that the man ended up in hospital for weeks, which would suggest the ranch's effects can follow people even after they leave.
helms-club-secret-consciousness-study-gr: For almost twenty years, a small group at the University of California, Irvine, met in secret to study consciousness, and Francis Crick, the scientist who discovered the structure of DNA, was one of them. The scientist Donald Hoffman tells this as a member himself. He says the group was called the Helms Club and that he spent a lot of time with Crick, which would mean one of the great names of biology quietly spent decades on the puzzle of the mind.
hemi-sync-paper-from-the-mid-1980s-1983: Michels says a paper from the CIA, the US spy agency, written in 1985 or 1986, describes Hemi-Sync, a technique for changing states of consciousness that the researcher Robert Monroe developed in Virginia. He says the paper came out through the Freedom of Information Act, a US law that lets anyone request government records, and that many people now cite it as a sign the government took such consciousness work seriously.
hennessy-claims-cheney-visited-s4-1993: A man named Derek Hennessy claimed he worked at S4, a reported secret site in the Nevada desert near Area 51 where alien craft are said to be studied, and that sometime in the mid-1990s Dick Cheney, the former US Secretary of Defense, came into S4. An online researcher of UAPs (unidentified anomalous phenomena, the official term for UFOs) who goes by UAPGerb repeats Hennessy's claim to Michels. If true, it would put a top US official inside the program.
henri-coanda-s-1936-saucer-patent-and-pr: A Romanian engineer named Henri Coanda is said to have held the first patent on a flying saucer, filed in 1936, and later to have worked with the Nazis after they took control of his world. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source beyond the patent. In one episode he gives the date as 1936, and in another he places it around 1937 and ties Coanda's ideas to the Avrocar, a saucer-shaped aircraft, rather than to Project Y, a later saucer-shaped aircraft project. If true, it would mean serious saucer designs were on paper more than a decade before the famous UFO reports of the late 1940s.
henri-coanda-s-patent-and-project-y-at-w: A Romanian scientist named Henri Coanda held a patent from 1936 on a flying design, and Michels says Coanda was in Vichy France, the part of France governed in step with the Nazis, where he was forced to work for them. Afterwards, Michels says, Coanda was taken to Wright-Patterson, a US Air Force base in Ohio, to work on Project Y, which Michels describes as an extension of the Avro car project, an effort to make flying saucers actually fly. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, as a sign that saucer-shaped craft were being built in secret.
henry-azadehdel-s-fraudulent-south-afric: A man named Henry Azadehdel is said to have put out fraudulent documents about South Africa. A UFO researcher named Clas Svahn, who is presented as holding a very large archive of UFO material, mentions it briefly without naming a source, and in passing speaks of Azadehdel publishing something about "silver diamonds". Svahn raises it as an example of faked papers that ended up in the UFO record.
henry-wallace-astors-and-duponts-fund-pu: In 1948 in Maine, a researcher of telepathy named Andrija Puharich says he was "unexpectedly put in contact with" Henry A. Wallace, who had been vice president under President Franklin Delano Roosevelt. The story, as it is filed, is that Wallace and members of the wealthy Astor and DuPont families went on to fund Puharich's telepathy research. Puharich tells it as his own experience, and it matters because it would put serious money and political names behind early mind-reading research.
hereticon-founder-s-startup-to-reverse-e: In 2022, at an event in Miami called Hereticon, one company founder was said to be trying to reverse engineer UFOs, meaning to work out how they are built, using quantum computing, a kind of computing based on quantum physics. Michels tells this himself during an episode with the economist Tyler Cowen. He calls the founder maybe "one of the most heretical thinkers here" but does not give a name.
hereticon-talk-flood-myths-rooted-in-rea: The flood stories told by peoples all over the world may go back to real floods, ones so huge they could be called biblical in scale. A researcher named Randall Carlson says this, recalling a talk at a conference called Hereticon, and he gives it as his own reading without naming a source. If he is right, those myths would be memories of real disasters, not just legends.
hermann-oberth-on-non-human-intelligence: Hermann Oberth, a German rocket pioneer and mentor to the rocket engineer Wernher von Braun, is said to have stated on record that beings from elsewhere helped humans build rockets to go to space. Michels tells this several times. In one episode he links it to a book called Secret Machines and says Oberth claimed non-human intelligence made the rockets possible. In another he quotes Oberth from interviews: "We cannot take all of the credit for our record advancements in certain scientific fields. We have been helped," and when asked by whom, "The people of the other worlds." Elsewhere Michels points to an audio recording of Oberth saying they "were aided and had help," and adds that Oberth gave a whole lecture on UFOs and that von Braun was inspired by the beings. A researcher named Jason Simosa puts it more vaguely, calling Oberth "the Nazi guy who claimed that they had relationship," without mentioning rockets. If true, the space age itself would owe something to non-human help.
hermann-oberth-on-video-about-ufos: The German scientist Hermann Oberth was once filmed talking about flying saucers. In a clip played on the show, Oberth says that so many witnesses have seen them that 'their existence cannot longer be denied,' and that he believes they 'come from another solar system.' Michels remembers the video a little differently in another episode, saying Oberth argued that the existence of UFOs should make anybody question reality.
hermann-oberth-s-1954-ufo-lecture-notes: In a 1954 lecture, the German rocket pioneer Hermann Oberth is said to have spoken about UFOs, unidentified flying objects, as real craft. The physicist Kevin Knuth, who appeared on an episode titled as a NASA whistleblower interview, says he owns Oberth's notes and lecture notes. According to Knuth, in those notes Oberth says he saw "numerous radar measurements of their speeds up to 19 km per second." Knuth also mentions Wernher von Braun, a fellow rocket scientist, alongside Oberth. Michels tells the lecture differently in another episode. In his version, Oberth argued that UFOs had been seen since at least the 1400s and believed they were flown by visitors from other worlds who were watching Earth's nuclear sites and military technology. Both tellers bring it up because a founding figure of rocket science seemed to take UFOs seriously.
herodotus-records-a-king-s-tomb-on-an-is: The ancient Greek historian Herodotus wrote that deep under Giza, in Egypt, there was the tomb of a great king set on an island surrounded by a lake of water. A researcher named Luke Caverns links this to the Osiris shaft, a deep underground shaft at Giza, saying "he records that down in the Osiris shaft there was the tomb of a great king".
