Caverns tells it as something he has read, without naming a source, as a sign that old accounts may describe real hidden chambers beneath the pyramids.
herodotus-takes-part-in-the-egyptian-mys: The ancient Greek historian Herodotus wrote about secret religious rites in Egypt, the so-called mystery cults, and openly wondered what went on in them. Then, while he was in Egypt, he was allowed to take part, and after that he never spoke of them again. The researcher Luke Caverns tells this, citing Herodotus himself, as a sign that the Egyptians guarded knowledge that outsiders were sworn to keep quiet about.
herrera-attends-greer-s-ce5-sessions: Michael Herrera, a guest who says he once saw a 300-foot UFO in the Indonesian jungle, says he has gone to several of the group sessions run by a UFO researcher named Steven Greer. In these sessions, which Greer calls CE5, people try to make contact with UFOs on purpose. Herrera brings it up himself as someone who took part, while talking with Jesse Michels about what Greer's effort is really for.
herrera-spoke-to-kirk-mcconnell-in-a-sci: Michael Herrera says he spoke with a man named Kirk McConnell in person, inside a SCIF, a sealed room in Washington used for talking about classified information. Herrera, who says on the show that he saw a 300-foot UFO in the Indonesian jungle, gives this as his own experience, saying simply "I talked to him in a skiff." He mentions it to show that he has been heard by people with security clearances.
herrera-testifies-at-greer-s-2023-nation: A man named Michael Herrera, who says he saw a 300-foot UFO in the Indonesian jungle, says he gave public testimony in 2023 at the National Press Club, a venue for press events in Washington DC. He says it was at an event put on by a UFO disclosure figure named Steven Greer. Herrera tells this as his own experience, and it marks the moment he took his account public.
hess-s-flight-to-britain-and-lifelong-qu: In 1941 Rudolf Hess, one of Adolf Hitler's top Nazi deputies, made a secret flight out of Germany that no one had approved and landed in a field in Britain, and he was then kept locked away for the rest of his life, until 1987. A researcher named Jason Jorjani tells this without naming a source, in a talk about what he calls Hitler's secret UFO program. He brings in Winston Churchill, Britain's wartime leader, and the story is told because Hess's lifelong isolation suggests he knew something that had to be kept quiet.
hessdalen-expedition-in-the-early-1980s: In the early 1980s a large expedition went to Hessdalen, a valley in Norway known for things seen in its sky, and managed to photograph them and once even pick them up on radar. The researcher Clas Svahn tells this as someone who was part of that joint Swedish and Norwegian effort, and if true it would mean whatever appears there is solid enough to be caught by cameras and instruments.
hidden-evaluation-run-during-the-q-cours: Randy Anderson, a former soldier who says he saw alien technology at a military base, says the Special Forces Qualification Course was more than it seemed. That course is the US Army's selection and training course for its Special Forces. He says that while he was going through it, the course was also secretly used to assess soldiers for another military unit ranked above those units. He tells it as someone who went through it, and it would mean some recruits were being quietly picked for a more secret outfit.
hidden-eye-patterns-on-product-packaging: Packaging can carry hidden eye-like patterns that catch a shopper's attention without being noticed as eyes, according to the cognitive scientist Don Hoffman. He says he has done this work himself with companies, making designs that read as "eye-like, but not obviously eye-like." He offers it as an example of how much our perception reacts to things we never consciously see.
hidden-f-117-stealth-fighter-line-in-the: In the 1980s, the first American fighter jet that radar could not detect, the F-117 stealth fighter, was being developed on Energy Department land in the Nevada desert, with its costs tucked inside the Energy Department's budget. That is what John S. Herrington, a former US Secretary of Energy, says from his own time in office, though he calls the plane "the F-17". If so, it shows how a secret military aircraft could be hidden inside a civilian department's books.
hidden-ufo-side-of-operation-paperclip: Operation Paperclip was the American effort after the Second World War to bring German scientists to the United States, and according to the former US intelligence officer David Grusch, it had a hidden second side that dealt seriously with UFOs. Grusch says much of it "dealt with the UFO, UAP issue in earnest" (UAP is the government's term for unidentified objects in the sky), and he ties this to the German rocket engineers Wernher von Braun and Arthur Rudolph. He passes this on as something he was told, not something he saw himself. If true, it would mean the US was working on the UFO question from the very start of the postwar era.
hidden-weapons-bunker-under-a-fake-gener: At a private facility belonging to Saddam Hussein, the former ruler of Iraq, what looked like a generator turned out to be hollow, and it tilted back to show steps leading down into a huge hidden weapons bunker. An Army sergeant named Lyn Buchanan tells this as something he took part in uncovering, describing the bunker as one 'you wouldn't believe.'
hieroglyphics-reported-at-historical-ufo: Several famous UFO cases are rumoured to have involved strange writing like hieroglyphics on the craft: Roswell, New Mexico, in 1947, the sighting by a man named Lonnie Zamora at Socorro, New Mexico, in 1964, and Kecksburg, Pennsylvania, in 1965. Michels lists these himself, calling them rumours and naming no source. He brings them up because the same markings turning up again and again would tie the cases together.
high-altitude-nuclear-tests-burned-holes: Michels says that nuclear bombs tested high in the sky in the 1950s and 60s would "just burn holes in the Van Allen belt," the band of charged particles that Earth's magnetic field holds in place far above the atmosphere. He says this himself, in passing, without naming a source. If true, it would mean these weapons tests did damage reaching all the way into near space.
high-definition-helicopter-video-of-orbs: A very clear video, filmed from a helicopter about 20 miles off the coast of Kuwait, is said to show a glowing ball rising out of the ocean and then being joined by a second one. The journalist Michael Shellenberger describes it on the show. He takes it from a report on a secret government program, said to be called Immaculate Constellation, that collected sightings like this, and if the report is right, the government holds high-quality footage of such objects that it has never released.
high-level-unnamed-source-corroborates-t: A high-level source, whom Jesse Michels does not name, is said to have backed up a number of details in the story of a man named Dan Sherman, whose account of secret government work Michels has covered. Michels says this himself, and in a later episode he says the source "basically corroborated Sherman's story", mentioning Sherman's DD214, the US military's discharge record, and a man he calls Dan Hog. If true, Sherman's account would have support from someone well placed inside the system.
high-ranking-nasa-official-tells-chris-h: Chris Bledsoe, a man who says UFOs show up around him and whom NASA has taken an interest in, says that in 2025 a high-ranking NASA official came up to him at the Capitol Hill Club, a private political club in Washington, DC. According to Bledsoe, the man gave him a big hug and said, "Chris, I'm a huge fan." Bledsoe tells it from his own experience, around the time of the congressional UFO hearings, as a sign that people high up in government take his story seriously.
high-school-seti-home-club-crunching-are: As a teenager, the pharmaceutical businessman Martin Shkreli started a high school club for SETI@home, a project that let home computers help sift data from the Arecibo radio telescope for signs of alien signals. He tells it himself: the club was about three people, and they all gave their computers' screen saver time to crunch the data. The project is placed between 1997 and 2009, and he brings it up as an early sign of his interest in life beyond Earth.
high-vacuum-dual-thruster-spinner-test-a: A new kind of thruster with no exhaust is said to have produced about 2.5 millinewtons of push, a tiny but measurable force, while spinning on a rig inside a vacuum chamber in Florida. The NASA engineer Charles Buhler, who ran the test, shows Michels a video of 'actual movement in vacuum using a dual thruster pack.' If true, it would mean a craft could move without throwing anything out behind it.
hike-up-stone-mountain-with-houston-2023: In 2023, while filming in Atlanta, the documentary maker Ky Dickens says she hiked up Stone Mountain in Georgia with Houston, one of the people in her film about children said to read minds. She adds that a doctor named Diane Powell came along too. Dickens tells it as something she took part in, a moment from making the film.
hikers-on-public-land-threatened-by-arme: Hikers walking on public parkland near Secret Mountain, outside Sedona, Arizona, say they were stopped by armed soldiers. The journalist Ross Coulthart says several people privately told him they met "men in uniform with automatic weapons, clearly highly trained elite soldiers," probably from the most elite special forces judging by how they moved. Michels retells it and places it in Coconino National Forest, adding that the men wore black uniforms with no insignia and carried M-16 rifles. If true, it would mean something secret is being guarded on land open to the public.
hikers-photograph-diamond-shaped-craft-m: Two people out hiking are said to have seen a large, diamond-shaped craft hovering, and to have photographed it, after which so-called men in black, mysterious visitors said to call on UFO witnesses, came after them. A UFO researcher named James Fox passes this on from what he was told, without giving a time or place. If true, it would mean the sighting drew attention from someone who wanted it kept quiet.
hikers-who-vanish-near-the-alien-bases-a: Hikers who go missing near Mount Nyangani in Zimbabwe and Mount Zeil in Australia, places he links to alien bases, are either killed or kept on as workers. An Army sergeant named Lyn Buchanan puts it bluntly: 'You see too much. You disappear.' If true, it would mean those disappearances are not accidents.
hill-at-hatshepsut-s-mortuary-temple-5-3: Near the mortuary temple of Hatshepsut, an ancient Egyptian queen, at Luxor, there is a hill that sits exactly 5,300 metres from the obelisks, the tall carved stone pillars, inside the Karnak temple complex. This comes from a researcher named Geoffrey Drumm, who calls it another of his "white horse hills" and gives the measurement without naming a source. He offers it as a sign that the old sites were laid out on purpose, at set distances from each other.
hillary-clinton-tells-kimmel-she-ll-get-: During her 2016 run for president, the politician Hillary Clinton was asked about UFOs by the late-night talk show host Jimmy Kimmel on his Los Angeles show, and she answered, "I'm going to get to the bottom of this." The UFO researcher Grant Cameron recounts the moment from memory on the show, without naming a source. He tells it as a sign that a leading candidate was ready to look into the subject in public.
hillary-s-presidential-run-timed-with-th: The timing of Hillary Clinton's run for president, says a man named Jake Barber, lines up with the setting up of AATIP, a small Pentagon office that studied unexplained aerial reports, and with what led to a New York Times article about it. Barber, who says he flew a helicopter to recover a UFO, tells Michels it is "probably no coincidence". If he is right, the opening up of the UFO subject between 2007 and 2017 was tied to politics at the top.
hillenkoetter-frustrated-at-being-kept-i: Roscoe Hillenkoetter, an early head of the CIA, was frustrated that he never got the proper information about Roswell, the reported 1947 crash of an object in the New Mexico desert. Michels says this himself, without naming a source, and mentions him alongside Donald Keyhoe, a writer on UFOs. If true, it would mean even a top intelligence chief was kept out of the loop.
hillenkoetter-leaves-nicap-as-hearings-l: Roscoe Hillenkoetter, a former head of the CIA, quit suddenly in 1962 from NICAP, a private group that pressed for open study of UFOs. According to the researcher Richard Dolan, he left at the very moment his friend Donald Keyhoe, a writer who led the group, was trying to get Congress to hold hearings on UFOs. Dolan tells it as a telling piece of timing, suggesting that pressure was put on the effort just as it might have reached Congress.
himmler-s-ahnenerbe-replacing-christiani: In 1930s Germany, Heinrich Himmler, head of the Nazi SS, ran an organization called the Ahnenerbe, meaning Ancestral Heritage, which aimed to replace Christianity with old Nordic rites. The writer Peter Levenda, who has researched the Nazis' occult interests, tells Michels that the Ahnenerbe was a real organization, without naming a source. It matters to him as a case of a state trying to rebuild belief around an invented ancient past.
historical-briefings-cut-off-in-the-earl: In the early 2010s, there was a push to stop giving the full history of a programme to the new people who took it over, so newcomers would no longer hear about what came before them. A researcher who goes by the online name UAPGerb says this on the podcast, passing on what a source told him, and places it around MITRE, a nonprofit that runs research for the US government. If true, it would explain how knowledge of secret UFO work could fade even inside the government.
hitchhiker-effect-at-fugal-s-home-dog-gr: Brandon Fugal, the owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a property known for reported strange happenings, says that in 2024 something seemed to follow him home from the ranch, which people call the "hitchhiker effect". He says his dog would get up around 3 a.m. and start growling and barking at something that wasn't there and couldn't be seen. Fugal tells it as something that happened in his own house, as a sign that whatever is at the ranch can travel with the people who go there.
hitchhiker-effect-at-thomas-winterton-s-: Strange things are said to have happened in the home of a man named Thomas Winterton after he came back from Skinwalker Ranch, a property where odd events are investigated, which people call the "hitchhiker effect": the idea that whatever is at the ranch can follow visitors home. Brandon Fugal, the owner of the ranch, passes this on from what Winterton told him, saying "Thomas has had things happen in his home upon returning from Skinwalker Ranch."
hitler-and-the-magenta-crash-nazi-saucer: A strange craft is said to have crashed in 1933 near Magenta, a town in Italy, and there are reports that the German dictator Adolf Hitler knew about it. There are also rumors that Nazi Germany tested saucer-shaped craft in what Michels calls "modern-day Czechoslovakia." Michels mentions both in passing in an episode about NASA, and he presents them as reports and rumors without naming a source.
hitler-orders-arrest-of-occultists-and-a: In 1941, after his deputy Rudolf Hess flew off on his own, Adolf Hitler is said to have ordered every occultist and astrologer in Germany arrested and sent to the camps. Peter Levenda, a researcher and writer on the occult, tells it in summary, and credits his book Unholy Alliance. If true, it would show how seriously the Nazi leadership took occult figures.
hitler-regime-support-for-zionist-revolu: In the years before and during the Second World War, Hitler's government in Germany gave some support to the Zionist movement, the campaign to found a Jewish state in what was then British-ruled Palestine. A Pentagon whistleblower named Matthew Brown says this in passing, without naming a source. He brings it up as an example of unlikely hidden alliances behind world events.
hitler-s-world-war-i-poems-to-odin-and-t: While serving as a soldier in the First World War, Adolf Hitler is said to have written poems to the old Norse gods Odin and Thor. An author named Peter Levenda, billed on the show as a CIA historian, agrees when Michels asks about it, and says the poems are reprinted in what he thinks is the historian John Toland's biography of Hitler. He tells it as a sign of Hitler's early pull toward pagan and occult ideas.
hittite-remains-in-underground-cities-sh: The underground cities at Derinkuyu in Turkey, a network of rooms and tunnels carved deep into the rock, show traces of the Hittites, an ancient people of the region, and of other early cultures that came later than the people who first dug them. That is how the researcher Matt LaCroix puts it, without naming a source. He tells it to suggest that later peoples moved into these tunnels and reused them, so the cities would be older than those who left their remains there.
hively-and-woodside-paper-on-extended-el: Two researchers, Lee Hively in Colorado Springs and a colleague named Woodside who Michels believes lives in Australia, have written a paper on extended electrodynamics, a proposed widening of the standard theory of electricity and magnetism. Michels brings up the paper himself in a talk with the mathematician Eric Weinstein and a Pentagon scientist, as possible new physics, without saying much about what it contains.
hjalmar-schacht-advises-sukarno-on-a-rev: Hjalmar Schacht, a banker who had served as Nazi Germany's economics minister, went to Indonesia after being cleared in Germany's postwar purge of Nazis and met its leader Sukarno. There, the researcher Peter Levenda says, Schacht told Sukarno he had to build an "Islamic crescent" to hold back Chinese communism. Levenda tells it, without naming a source, as an example of former Nazi figures shaping world politics after the war.
hmnzs-southland-followed-by-an-800-foot-: In the 1980s a New Zealand navy ship, the HMNZS Southland, was followed at sea by an underwater object about 800 feet long. A former NASA scientist named Kevin Knuth mentions it without naming a source, calling it a USO, short for unidentified submerged object, a UFO found in water. He tells it as one example of strange objects seen around ships.
hms-blonde-orange-sphere-rises-from-the-: At 3:30 in the morning on August 12, 1825, the night watch on HMS Blonde, a British Royal Navy ship sailing near the Cook Islands in the South Pacific, is said to have seen an orange ball of light rise out of the ocean. The researcher Richard Dolan tells this, drawing on the diary of a man aboard named Andrew Bloxom, written in 1825, which records that the watch "reported this orange spherical object rise from the ocean". Dolan brings it up to show that sightings like this go back about 200 years.
ho-chi-minh-s-letter-to-the-us-president: In the years after 1945, the Vietnamese leader Ho Chi Minh is said to have sent an impassioned letter to the American president, with a copy of Vietnam's new national constitution, which was identical to the American one. Joe McMoneagle, a guest known for remote viewing, the claimed skill of perceiving distant things with the mind, passes this on as something he was told. He tells it to suggest that the later war between the two countries need not have happened.
hoagland-and-flynn-hold-joint-conference: Richard Hoagland, a writer known for claiming there are ruins on the surface of Mars, held a series of conferences together with another writer named David Flynn. A researcher named Tim Alberino mentions this in passing, without naming a source, while talking about the people who promoted the idea of ancient structures on Mars.
hockey-puck-devices-on-the-shins-1976: In 1976, near Allagash, Maine, a man named Jim Weiner says he was taken aboard a craft, where a being with long, thin, jointed arms held up something that looked like a flattened hockey puck. According to Weiner, who tells it as his own experience, the beings put one of these on the outside of each of his shins, and then he could not move his legs. He describes being terrified, and the detail matters to him as a sign of how he was held still.
hoffman-at-mit-studying-under-marvin-min: The guest, a scientist named Hoffman, was at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology right when the field of artificial intelligence was starting, and studied under Marvin Minsky, one of its pioneers. Michels says this to his guest at the start of their talk, calling it amazing and also naming the linguist Noam Chomsky. He brings it up because it gives Hoffman's ideas about the mind and intelligence a starting point at the very birth of the field.
hoffman-s-dmt-research-collaboration-wit: The scientist Donald Hoffman, who argues that our brains evolved to hide much of reality from us, says he is working with a researcher named Gallimore on DMT, a powerful psychedelic drug. Hoffman mentions the collaboration himself, in 2026, as part of his search for what lies beyond ordinary perception.
hoffman-s-team-of-mathematicians-working: In 2026 the scientist Donald Hoffman says he is putting together a team of mathematicians to work on a set of conjectures, unproven mathematical claims, that he and his colleagues have already published openly. Hoffman tells this about his own work, as part of his effort to build a mathematical theory of reality that goes beyond what our senses show us.
hofmann-grof-and-ruck-s-reported-plan-fo: Michels says that three men who studied psychedelic drugs wanted to create "a new Eleusis": the chemist Albert Hofmann, who discovered LSD, the psychiatrist Stanislav Grof, and the scholar Carl Ruck. Eleusis was the site of a secret religious rite in ancient Greece, so the idea would be to bring back something like that sacred ceremony in modern form. Michels tells it himself, without naming a source, and adds that "maybe this is a rumor."
holloman-afb-landing-footage-that-allan-: In 1964, three flying saucers are said to have come in over Holloman Air Force Base in New Mexico: two peeled away, one landed, a door opened and beings stepped out, all of it caught on film. The filmmaker James Fox tells it from what Allan Sandler, a man who says he saw the footage, told him: "it might have been a training video I don't know but it was real flying saucers." In another episode Fox puts it flatly: "No question about it. Three came in over the base. Two peeled away. One came down and landed." Sandler himself, speaking on the show, describes one round, wobbly craft that landed, "and a door opened and guys come out looking like they were outer space guys". He dates it to 1971, not 1964. The scientist Eric W. Davis adds that it set down on the tarmac near a hangar and that a very tall being who looked Northern European came down a ramp. He says the film was kept from Blue Book, the US Air Force's UFO study of the 1950s and 60s, and from its adviser, the astronomer J. Allen Hynek. The researcher Grant Cameron, going on the word of the producer Robert Emenegger, dates it to May 1971. The tellers also point to the film UFOs Past Present and Future and to articles by the writer Coral Lorenzen. If true, the military would have filmed a planned meeting with visitors.
holloman-footage-debunked-as-an-f-4-1970: Film said to show a UFO landing at Holloman Air Force Base in New Mexico in the 1970s has, according to later accounts, turned out to show an ordinary military plane. The footage appears in a documentary called UFOs: Past, Present and Future. Michels says so in a 2025 episode with the writer Greg Bishop: there is "a little bit of footage", and it "has now been debunked as an F4", meaning an F-4, a US military fighter jet. An unnamed documentary narrator, played in a 2026 episode with the researcher Grant Cameron, tells how this came to light. The narrator says a newer high-definition DVD release of the film, from around 2024 or 2025, was "a gamechanger". Skipping ahead to the landing footage, the narrator was "momentarily stunned by what that extra detail revealed." In that telling the object is simply a plane, not an F-4 by name. Either way, the claim matters because the landing film had long been offered as evidence of a meeting at a US base.
homeless-man-says-look-up-and-corbell-se: The filmmaker Jeremy Corbell says that a homeless man once walked up to him and said, "Look up," and when he did, he saw a globe in the sky. Corbell tells it as his own experience and puts it in 2013, though the record files it under 2004. He shares it as something few people know about him, a moment that pointed him toward the subject.
homestead-3-that-people-refuse-to-enter-: On Skinwalker Ranch, a property known for reports of strange events, there is an old building called Homestead 3 that some people will not walk into. Brandon Fugal, the businessman who owns the ranch, says it is "the oldest structure on the property" and that some visitors refuse to enter it, and he names a woman called Kristen and the musician Trent Reznor in connection with the place. He tells it from his own time owning the ranch, from about 2016 on, as a sign that the building gives people a feeling they cannot shake.
honeymoon-photos-labelled-grand-central-: A man named Chris Bledsoe, who says he attracts UFOs and has been studied by NASA, says his honeymoon photos from New York around 1982 are labelled "Grand Central Station", but that if you search today the place is called Grand Central Terminal. He offers it as a Mandela effect, the idea that many people remember something differently from how the record now shows it, and tells it from his own photos.
hooded-figures-spraying-plague-from-land: In medieval Europe, outbreaks of plague are said to have begun only after hooded figures landed in the fields in strange objects, stepped out, and walked around with what looked like spray cans, and this sight is said to be where the image of the Grim Reaper with his scythe comes from. A researcher named Jason Jorjani tells this from the work of an author named William Bramley, who wrote the book The Gods of Eden. If true, it would mean the plague was spread on purpose by visitors from elsewhere.
hooked-on-ufos-by-chariots-of-the-gods-1: Greg Rogers, a doctor billed as a NASA doctor who says he saw a UFO in a secret hangar, says he got hooked on UFOs in 1969, as he recalls it, when he read Chariots of the Gods, a book by the writer Erich von Däniken. He tells it as the start of his own lifelong interest.
hoover-handwritten-note-army-grabbed-rec: In 1947, the FBI director J. Edgar Hoover wrote by hand on a bureau memo that "we must insist upon full access to discs recovered," and complained that "the Army grabbed it and wouldn't let the bureau have it for cursory examination." The UFO researcher and filmmaker James Fox points to the note, which also appears in his work Out of the Blue. He reads it as proof that a disc was recovered and that the Army kept it even from the FBI.
hoover-letter-calling-condon-a-russian-s: Around 1949, J. Edgar Hoover, head of the FBI, is said to have written a letter to Congress calling the physicist Edward Condon a Russian spy. Robert Salas, a former Air Force missile officer, tells it from the record as he remembers it, saying "I believe it was" Hoover who wrote to Congress, and he raises it because Condon later led the government-funded study of UFOs, which would cast that study in a different light.
hoover-letters-deny-fbi-jurisdiction-ove: Between the 1940s and the 1950s, J. Edgar Hoover, head of the FBI, the US federal police agency, is said to have written several letters stating that "the investigation of unidentified flying objects is not and never has been within the jurisdiction of the FBI." Michels tells this himself, crediting the documentary Out of the Blue and its filmmaker James Fox, and raises it as a question of which part of government, if any, was really handling the subject.
hopi-ant-people-as-a-global-subterranean: There may be a species that lives underground all over the world, and the Hopi, a Native American people linked to Arizona, have a legend about "ant people" that would fit it. Michels raises this while discussing strange three-fingered figures found in Peru, and he credits the idea to a Chilean researcher named David Velasco, who he says "speculates" about it. If it were true, legends from very different places would be describing the same hidden beings.
hopi-ant-people-emerging-from-undergroun: Among the Hopi, a Native American people, there are stories of "ant people" who came up from under the ground to help humans in times of great trouble and strife. A guest named Jay Anderson brings this up as one of several tribal stories of helpers from below, the kind that some read as memories of other beings living among us.
hornig-guards-the-trinity-bomb-the-night: On the night before Trinity, the first atomic bomb test in New Mexico in 1945, the physicist J. Robert Oppenheimer, who led the bomb project, is said to have handed a weapon to a young scientist named Donald Hornig and told him to guard the bomb in its tower through a storm. A former NASA scientist named Kevin Knuth tells it from what Hornig himself told him. It is told as a firsthand link to the start of the nuclear age.
hospital-reprimands-italo-for-filming-th: In 2023 a surgeon named Italo Venturelli took a man named James Fox into the maternity ward of the regional hospital in Varginha, Brazil, to film the room where, he says, the being treated there was kept, and afterwards the hospital banned him from filming inside. Venturelli tells this himself and says the ban was fair, since he had already done the filming.
hospital-staff-now-say-the-room-was-lock: In 1996 in Varginha, a town in Brazil where some say a strange creature was captured and taken to hospital, staff at the regional hospital now say a room there really was locked that day. The surgeon Italo Venturelli, who worked at that hospital, says that when he raises it with colleagues today, many tell him "the room was really locked, that this really happened here" and recall details of what they saw. If true, it would back the claim that something unusual was held at the hospital.
hospital-wing-closed-because-of-the-crea: In 1996, in the Brazilian town of Varginha, where a strange living being was reportedly captured, a wing of the local hospital is said to have been shut for weeks because the smell left by the creature was so strong. The documentary filmmaker and UFO investigator James Fox passes this on from what he was told, and has told it twice on the show. The first time he says only that "they had to close that wing in the hospital for like weeks," and the second time he names the Hospital Regional and places the stench in the room where X-rays of the being were taken. If true, it would mean the being was physically handled and examined inside a real hospital.
host-attended-the-congressional-uap-hear: Jesse Michels says he was in the room in 2023 for the US congressional hearing on UAP, the government's term for UFOs. At that hearing, a former intelligence officer named David Grusch and others testified under oath about what the government knows. Michels mentions it himself while talking with a guest named Matthew Pines, recalling what it felt like to be there.
host-discussed-precognition-hypothesis-w: Jesse Michels says he once talked over the idea of precognition, sensing the future before it happens, with Hal Puthoff, the man who ran Stargate, the CIA's psychic research programme. Michels tells this himself, in a conversation with the writer Eric Wargo about prophetic dreams. He raises it because it would mean someone who led the government's own psychic research took the idea seriously.
host-has-seen-jacobs-dd214-1964: Jesse Michels says he has seen the DD214, the US military's discharge record, of a former Air Force man named Bob Jacobs. He says it shows Jacobs "definitely worked at Vandenberg," the California air base where Jacobs places a 1964 Atlas rocket launch that he says was scrubbed from the records. Michels tells this himself, to back up Jacobs against a Wall Street Journal report he criticises.
host-s-dream-of-flea-texting-him: Michels once dreamed that Flea, the famous bass player, was texting him. He tells this himself, as a passing personal story, on an episode about a government official's claims, and he gives no date and does not say what the texts said.
host-s-father-dreamed-of-an-earthquake-o: Jesse Michels's father kept dreaming of an earthquake on January 17th, before the Northridge earthquake struck Los Angeles. Michels relays this from his father, who, Michels says, writes about it in the book The Tools. If true, the dreams would be a glimpse of an event before it happened.
host-s-frightening-month-after-visiting-: Jesse Michels says that after he visited Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah ranch known for strange happenings, he had a strange month and that things there "instilled fear in me". He tells it himself, from his own experience. In a later retelling he says he went at the most egotistical time of his life and calls the month afterwards simply not a great one, rather than frightening.
host-s-mars-ufo-photo-tweet-turns-out-to: Michels once posted a picture on Twitter that seemed to show a UFO on the surface of Mars, and it turned out to be a rock. He tells this on himself, briefly, in an episode with a guest named Luke Caverns, calling it "this little um picture of like a UFO on Mars or whatever."
host-s-own-ayahuasca-experience: Michels says he has taken ayahuasca, a plant brew known for producing strong visions, once, but has never taken DMT, a powerful psychedelic compound. He mentions it about himself while talking with the neuroscientist Andrew Gallimore, who studies DMT and the worlds people report seeing on it.
host-s-own-two-ufo-sightings-2020: Jesse Michels says he saw two UFOs himself in 2020, and after that he became obsessed with the subject. He says it in passing, as his own experience, while talking with a treasure hunter named Dennis Asberg, to explain how he got into all this.
host-s-reading-of-majestic-as-a-continui: "Majestic" or "Majestic 12" is a name said to belong to a secret group of officials that managed the UFO question in the 1950s. Michels suggests it may really have been one of the committees set up to keep the government running through a catastrophe, which is called continuity of government. Talking with a former presidential advisor named Harold Malmgren, he says such committees "have gone by many names. 5412, the 303 committee, the committee of 40." In a later episode Michels credits the idea to a former Army officer named John B. Alexander instead, who told him that Majestic 12 and similar elite groups around UFOs are "almost euphemisms for continuity of government programs". If that reading is right, the UFO question would have been handled inside the government's most protected emergency planning.
host-s-talk-with-former-skunk-works-head: In 2024 Jesse Michels says he spoke with a man who used to head revolutionary technology at Skunk Works, the secret advanced aircraft division of the company Lockheed. Michels tells this himself, without naming the man, across two episodes. In one he adds that he feels free to mention it because the man is on record as believing in this kind of thing, meaning that the mind can affect matter.
host-s-trifield-meter-drained-at-skinwal: At Skinwalker Ranch, a famous paranormal hotspot in Utah's Uintah Basin, Jesse Michels says a trifield meter, a handheld device that measures electromagnetic fields and radiation, went off just before his group left: it had a full battery, was flashing, and then was dead. Michels tells it himself as something he saw, on several occasions. In one telling he dates the visit to 2022 and also mentions smelling sulfur, and in another he says the meter went off because of high gamma radiation, rather than describing it draining.
host-sees-two-metallic-orbs-during-holot: Michels says he once saw two metallic orbs while doing holotropic breathwork, a practice of deep, fast breathing meant to bring on altered states, with a friend in Silver Lake, California. He tells it about himself, offering it as his own brush with the kind of experience his guest describes.
host-smelled-sulfur-at-skinwalker-ranch-: Jesse Michels says that when he visited Skinwalker Ranch, a property known for reported strange happenings, around 2022, he smelled sulfur and felt he had to get out of there. He has told it himself on several episodes. In one he adds that a dark month followed the visit, and in another he says a gas monitor picked up nothing and jokingly blames a "dragon".
hostile-telepaths-encountered-on-mars: If you travel to Mars with the mind, the first thing you meet is a group of five telepaths who are "not exactly welcoming." So says Jeffrey Mishlove, a researcher with a doctorate in parapsychology, the study of psychic abilities, who passes it on without naming where it comes from. If true, it would mean minds of some kind dwell on Mars and can be reached by mental travel alone.
hosting-the-mind-s-ear-on-kpfa-radio-197: In the 1970s a Berkeley radio station called KPFA, part of the listener-funded Pacifica network, offered a young Jeffrey Mishlove his own show. Mishlove, a psychologist who went on to study psychic phenomena, remembers being told: "We have a slot for you every Tuesday and Thursday at noon. We'd like you to host this interview show called The Mind's Ear." He tells it as the start of his work interviewing people about the mind and consciousness, which led him to people like Robert Monroe, a researcher of out-of-body experiences.
houdin-s-theory-that-the-great-pyramid-w: The Great Pyramid of Giza in Egypt was built from the inside out, with the stone blocks hauled up a ramp that spirals inside the pyramid itself, according to the French architect Jean-Pierre Houdin. Michels brings up Houdin's idea himself on several episodes, once saying it gained new interest after the ScanPyramids project, a scanning survey of the pyramid, found unexplained empty spaces inside it, and another time pairing it with talk that the pyramid may be older than thought. He calls Houdin one of the leading researchers on how the pyramid was built.
house-sized-tall-white-deep-spacecraft-s: In the 1960s in Indian Springs Valley, Nevada, a man named Charles Hall, who says he spent three years near pale, tall beings he calls the Tall Whites, says he personally saw one of their deep-space craft up close. He describes it as a bit longer and wider than a house and about half again as high. Hall tells it as his own sighting, and if true it would mean such craft landed on American soil.
houston-answers-a-question-his-mother-as: A mother named Katie, from Atlanta, Georgia, says she asked her son Houston a question silently, only in her head, and he answered it. She tells it as something she saw herself, on an episode about children said to be able to read minds, and if true it would mean he picked up her thought without any words.
houston-finds-crystal-dice-hidden-for-a-: A boy named Houston in Atlanta, Georgia, is said to have come home from school and found crystal dice that had been hidden away as a gift for a son-in-law, because he could hear or feel their energy. Ky Dickens, who made a documentary about nonspeaking children said to read minds, tells it from what the family, through a woman named Katie, told her. If true, it would mean the boy sensed objects he had no ordinary way to know about.
houston-finds-hidden-stones-and-senses-t: A mother named Katie says that her son Houston, one of the children in the Telepathy Tapes, found three stones that had been hidden and could sense their energy. The Telepathy Tapes is a documentary about children who cannot speak and are said to read minds. She says that a little later she found he had lined the three stones up on his bedside table in his room in Atlanta, Georgia. Katie tells it as someone who was there, as a sign the boy can perceive things he was never shown.
houston-names-the-hill-a-telepathic-chat: A young non-speaking person named Houston is said to have coined the name "the Hill" for a kind of telepathic chat room, a place in the mind where people who cannot speak tune in and talk with one another. The documentary filmmaker Ky Dickens, who made a series called The Telepathy Tapes about non-speaking people said to read minds, relays this from what Houston and others named Akil, John Paul and Libby told her in Atlanta around 2023. If true, it would mean these people share a hidden way of communicating with each other.
houston-says-mama-i-love-you-the-day-bef: The day before Thanksgiving in Atlanta, a 17-year-old boy named Houston said "Mama, I love you", and his mother had never once heard him say her name before. His mother, Katie, tells it herself in an episode about the Telepathy Tapes, a documentary by Ky Dickens about children who are said to read minds. She says she was shocked, which for her marks a son who had never said those words finding them at last.
houston-sends-ky-images-at-night-about-t: The documentary maker Ky Dickens says that in 2024 she wrote to a woman named Katie to ask whether Houston, one of the people in her film about children said to read minds, was sending her images at night about the movie. She says Katie asked Houston, and he answered yes, he does send Ky images. Dickens tells it as her own experience, and it would suggest a mind-to-mind link at a distance.
houston-spells-out-a-text-message-he-nev: A mother named Katie, from Atlanta, Georgia, says someone sent her a text message that her son Houston never saw, and he then spelled out exactly what it said. She tells it as something she witnessed, on an episode about children said to be able to read minds, and if true it would mean he got the words without seeing them.
how-roger-leer-began-removing-alien-impl: A podiatrist named Roger Leir, a foot doctor with a deep interest in UFOs, is said to have started removing alien implants (small objects some people believe aliens placed in their bodies) after a man named Daryl Sims urged him to look into them at a UFO conference. A scientist named Steve Colbern, who studies such objects, tells this from what Leir told him, calling Leir "the most knowledgeable ufologist I've ever met."
how-the-atlantis-story-passed-from-solon: The story of Atlantis, the lost island civilization, is said to have come from Egyptian priests to Solon, a lawmaker of ancient Athens, then passed from Solon to Dropides, to Critias the Elder, and to Critias the Younger, who told it at a gathering with Socrates that the philosopher Plato wrote down. The researcher Randall Carlson traces this chain for Michels from memory, without naming a source. If the chain holds, Plato's Atlantis would be a handed-down record, not just a made-up tale.
howard-hughes-and-the-mormon-mafia-1950: Howard Hughes, the billionaire aviator and industrialist, ran his business empire through senior managers and handlers who were mostly members of the Mormon church, a group people called the "Mormon mafia". A researcher named Matthew Pines says this without naming a source. He raises it to show how closely a small, tight-knit circle was tied to Hughes's corporate and aerospace work.
howard-hughes-brought-to-the-bahamas: At some point the billionaire Howard Hughes was suddenly brought down to an island in the Bahamas, according to the researcher Jason Simosa. Simosa mentions it in passing, without a source, as one piece of a larger web he sees linking UFO secrecy to a small group of powerful people. He gives no date and no further detail.
howard-hughes-s-undisclosed-sensitive-pr: The billionaire aviator and industrialist Howard Hughes was working on "a couple other extraordinarily sensitive programs" for the US government in the decades after the war, beyond the ones that are known. The lawyer Dan Sheehan says so in passing and does not say what the programs were. He brings it up to suggest Hughes was tied into secret government work deeper than the public knows.
howard-hughes-visiting-george-van-tassel: In the 1950s, the rich aviator Howard Hughes is said to have landed on a private airstrip at Giant Rock, a spot in the California desert, to visit its owner George Van Tassel, a man known for UFO gatherings there, and to eat his wife's cooking. The philosopher Jason Jorjani tells this in passing, without naming a source, and credits a book called Closer Encounters. It would place a powerful businessman close to the early UFO scene.
howard-morland-reconstructs-the-teller-u: In 1979 a writer for The Progressive magazine named Howard Morland was given an assignment: with no knowledge of physics, see if he could work out the secret design of the hydrogen bomb, known as the Teller-Ulam design. The researcher Eric Weinstein tells the story without naming a source, setting it against the Atomic Energy Acts of 1946 and 1954, US laws that made nuclear knowledge secret. He uses it to show how far government secrecy over physics can reach, and how an outsider can still piece it together.
huge-glowing-craft-over-the-november-5-m: Mario Woods, an Air Force veteran, says that in 1977 a huge glowing craft hung over a nuclear missile launch site called November 5. The site belonged to Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota. He says the thing was so wide it stretched past the fence line around the site. Woods tells it as someone who was there, with a fellow airman named Michael Johnson, and it would mean an unknown craft had come right up to American nuclear weapons.
huge-unidentified-underwater-craft-promp: According to a former president of one of Russia's republics, "very large unidentified underwater craft were discovered and cited in the Pacific Ocean," and similar sightings came from the Baltic Sea, the North Sea and the Atlantic. He tells Michels that these finds led the defence officials of the United States, Britain and the Soviet Union to get in touch with one another, which would mean the rival powers treated the craft as a shared problem.
hugh-angleton-in-italy-during-the-1933-m: Michels says that Hugh Angleton, the father of James Jesus Angleton, who later ran spy-hunting for the CIA, was stationed in Italy in 1933, when an unknown craft is said to have crashed near the town of Magenta. Michels raises this himself, without naming a source, and calls it "really crazy." The point would be that the Angleton family was close to one of the earliest reported crashes of a craft not made by people.
hugh-everett-s-multiverse-theory-and-his: The physicist Hugh Everett, who came up with the "many worlds" theory (the idea that every possible outcome plays out in its own separate universe), is said to have gone on to work for the Pentagon, the US Department of Defense, on game theory for the American nuclear weapons programme. Michels tells this himself in two episodes, without naming a source, and also mentions the physicists John Wheeler and Bryce DeWitt alongside Everett. He brings it up to show how closely the deepest ideas in physics were tied to military work.
hughes-aircraft-builds-the-glomar-explor: In the 1970s the American aerospace company Hughes Aircraft built the Glomar Explorer, a ship made for recovering things from the deep ocean floor. Michels brings it up himself, without naming a source, in an episode about two days he spent with Bob Lazar. He gives it as an example of the kind of hidden project a private company can build in secret.
human-abduction-squads-made-to-look-like: A UFO activist named Steven Greer says people came to him who had flown man-made craft, and others who had served on human abduction squads dressed up to look like aliens. He says he debriefed the very people running this human abduction program, and adds that its cases were fed to the well-known abduction researchers David Jacobs, Budd Hopkins and John Mack. If true, it would mean some reported alien abductions were staged by people, not by visitors from elsewhere.
human-bottleneck-reset-event-70-000-year: About 70,000 years ago, human numbers crashed so low that our genes still show it, and some people see this as one of several "reset events" in human history. A speaker identified only as Jack raises it without naming a source, saying "we know genomically there was a bottleneck", meaning a narrow squeeze in the population. If true, it would mean human history may have been wiped back and restarted more than once.
human-civilization-as-a-cargo-cult-from-: All of human society may be a cargo cult, a group copying the visits of an advanced outsider it does not understand, left over from some ancient meeting with beings from elsewhere. The author Peter Levenda gives this as the starting idea behind Sekret Machines: Gods, a book project he worked on with the musician Tom DeLonge, saying "our entire society is a cargo cult because everything we're trying to do" goes back to that contact. If true, it would mean much of what humans build is an imitation of visitors.
humanoid-figure-emerges-from-fog-and-abd: In 1964, at a Minuteman nuclear missile site called D5 on Vandenberg Air Force Base in California, a missile guard named Richard Barth says he saw a shadow in the fog, and then a man or humanlike figure stepped out of it and took him away. Barth tells it as his own experience: he says the being apologised and explained that they had to have access to the site, that he felt both terror and love, and that it was too vivid and real for anyone to have staged it. He says he never told anyone on the base because the beings had somehow conditioned or hypnotised him not to.
humans-and-aliens-working-side-by-side-a: Humans and aliens are said to work side by side at Mount Zeil, a mountain in Australia. A former Army sergeant named Lyn Buchanan repeats this from what others told him, saying he has "heard that from people who absolutely know for sure," though he does not name them.
humans-as-slave-workers-in-eden: In the Garden of Eden, humans were slave workers tilling the fields for the gods without knowing it, and their nakedness was the sign of it, since in the ancient world being naked marked slave labour. The philosopher and researcher Jason Jorjani gives this reading of the Bible's Book of Genesis himself, without naming a source. If true, the story of the fall would be a story of servants leaving their masters.
hume-center-funded-by-former-cia-s-t-off: The Hume Center at Virginia Tech in Blacksburg, Virginia, was funded by Ted Hume, a former science and technology officer at the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency, and his wife. That is what a researcher named Bob McGwier, who worked with the CIA as a contractor, says: Hume left the agency, started a company that did well, sold it, and put some of the money back into the center.
humming-three-phase-power-boxes-feeding-: At Bradshaw Ranch, a property near Sedona, Arizona, a man named Paul heard a humming, kicked a bush aside and found a huge three-phase power box, the heavy-duty kind of electrical supply used for big machinery, with a cable running into the ground. Ross Coulthart, who says he has located a UFO base in Arizona, repeats this from Paul in 2025, as a sign that something is being powered underground there.
hundreds-of-maltese-skulls-vanish-after-: On the island of Malta, hundreds of unusual skulls were found, the man who found them then died mysteriously, someone from the Smithsonian, the big American museum and research institution, took over, and all the skulls vanished. A guest named Jay Anderson repeats this as something he heard from Maltese locals. If true, it would mean strange remains were found and quietly taken out of sight.
hundredth-monkey-effect-on-japanese-isla: The hundredth monkey effect is the idea that once enough animals in one group learn a new habit, it suddenly appears in others they never meet, and it is said to come from a kind of monkey living on islands in Japan, kept apart by the water. A guest named Randy Anderson, who says he saw alien technology on a military base, brings it up from what he was told, unsure of the details. He uses it to suggest that minds may be linked in ways that do not need contact.
hunt-s-deathbed-confession-of-a-conspira: As he was dying, a man named E. Howard Hunt claimed there had been a conspiracy to kill President John F. Kennedy in 1963, and that he had known about it. A historian named Peter Levenda repeats this without naming a source. If true, it would mean the assassination was a planned plot that insiders knew about.
hunters-report-total-silence-just-before: Hunters who came back from the wilderness after a companion vanished say that just before he disappeared there was no sound at all, total silence. The researcher Jason Jorjani relays this from David Pitus and his Missing 411 series about people who disappear in wild places, giving the example of someone saying, right before Charlie disappeared, there was no sound. The silence is told as a sign that something out of the ordinary was at work.
hvt-escort-of-sealed-mystery-boxes-on-cl: Jake Barber, a helicopter pilot who says he once flew to retrieve a UFO, says that in the 1990s he escorted secret cargo on classified flights. The military called this cargo "high-value targets". He says that most of the time these were sealed containers that the crews called "mystery boxes", and they were never told what was inside. Barber tells it as his own experience, as part of how he came to carry things he was not meant to know about.
hybrid-woman-with-skateboard-in-the-groc: In 2024, in a grocery store near Santa Monica, the writer Whitley Strieber says he passed a woman with a skateboard and knew at once that she was "one of them", meaning, in his account, a being that is part human and part alien. He says that as she walked in ahead of him he was hit by a brilliant sudden feeling of recognition. He tells it as proof, if true, that such beings live quietly among ordinary people.
hydraulic-water-locks-used-to-float-bloc: Some researchers have proposed that the builders of the Great Pyramid at Giza used a system of water locks, like those on a canal, to float the huge stone blocks up into the pyramid. The researcher Jeffrey Drum explains this idea, which he covered in a 2021 video, without naming who first proposed it, and says certain features could be "remnants or vestiges" of that lock system. In one telling he ties these features to radar scans taken from satellites, and in another he simply calls them possible remains of the locks.
hyman-s-government-commissioned-report-c: A researcher named Ray Hyman had written a report for the government, two decades before the events Michels is discussing, that was harshly critical of Uri Geller, the famous psychic. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, while talking about government interest in psychic abilities. He uses it to show that Hyman was already a known sceptic of psychic claims before his later role.
hynek-1966-article-on-ufos-over-minot-mi: An article written in 1966 by the well-known astronomer J. Allen Hynek is said to report UFOs floating around nuclear missiles at Minot Air Force Base in North Dakota. Michels says Hynek wrote it while running Project Blue Book, the US Air Force's official UFO study of the 1950s and 60s, and that his guest, the researcher Robert Hastings, came across it by chance. Michels tells it as the starting point of the idea that UFOs take an interest in nuclear weapons.
hynek-and-vallee-s-invisible-college-and: The UFO researchers J. Allen Hynek and Jacques Vallée called their private group of fellow investigators the Invisible College, and Michels says the name was a tongue-in-cheek nod to the Invisible College of the scientist Robert Boyle, a circle from around the start of the Enlightenment. Michels tells this himself, drawing on a book by the historian Frances Yates about how the Rosicrucians, a secretive mystical movement, fed into the birth of modern science. He brings it up to suggest that UFO research sits in a long line of half-hidden groups pursuing knowledge at the edge of science and mysticism.
hynek-at-project-blue-book-opposed-then-: Michels says that J. Allen Hynek, the astronomer who advised Project Blue Book, the US Air Force's UFO study of the 1950s and 60s, at first argued against UFO reports but later took all of that back and "kind of repented for the fact that he was opposed." Michels tells this himself, without naming a source. It matters because it would mean the Air Force's own scientist changed his mind about the subject.
hynek-delivers-a-prepared-computer-to-be: Around 1980, the astronomer J. Allen Hynek is said to have turned up at the door of Paul Benowitz, a man in Albuquerque, New Mexico, who was picking up signals he thought were alien, with a fully built computer and the words, "This will help you with the signals." A writer named Greg Bishop tells this from what a UFO researcher named Bill Moore told him. If true, it would mean a well-known scientist was quietly helping, or steering, Benowitz's work.
hynek-gave-spielberg-alien-drawings-for-: The astronomer J. Allen Hynek, a scientist long tied to UFO research, is said to have given the film director Steven Spielberg a set of drawings of alien beings to use for the special effects in his UFO film Close Encounters. The UFO researcher Budd Hopkins says this without naming a source. He says the drawings date back to the late 1960s and early 1970s and look very much like other drawings he was discussing, which would mean the film's aliens were modelled on what witnesses had described.
hynek-provided-bennewitz-s-computer-doty: The astronomer J. Allen Hynek, Michels says, gave a computer to Paul Bennewitz, an Albuquerque man who believed he was picking up alien signals in the 1980s. Michels adds that Bennewitz was being fed false information as a psychological operation by an Air Force officer named Rick Doty. Michels tells this himself as something he had just learned, without naming a source, and it would tie a well-known scientist to a government deception campaign.
hynek-s-swamp-gas-explanation-1960: In the 1960s the astronomer J. Allen Hynek, who advised the US Air Force's UFO study of the 1950s and 60s, was the one who came up with the "swamp gas" explanation: the idea that lights people reported came from gas rising off a marsh. The UFO skeptic Mick West points this out in passing, as a reminder of who was behind one of the best-known official explanations for a sighting.
hynek-says-he-played-a-part-in-the-blue-: The astronomer J. Allen Hynek, who worked on Blue Book, the US Air Force's UFO study of the 1950s and 60s, is said to have admitted later that he "played a part in the cover up." Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, in an episode about an astronomer who tracks UFOs. If true, it would mean that someone inside the official study helped hide what it found.
hypnosis-with-dr-michael-o-connell-train: Around 2007 in the Carolinas, a man named Chris Bledsoe, who says he attracts UFOs, says he went through hypnosis to recover a stretch of time, with help from a doctor named Michael O'Connell, who he says was trained by a researcher named John Mack. Bledsoe tells it himself, describing "a doctor from Harvard helping me", as the way he came to remember what had happened to him.
hypnotic-regression-reveals-mental-conta: A hypnosis session held at a beach in Brazil is said to have brought back a witness's memory of reaching out to a creature at a crash site near the town of Varginha in 1996. The creature supposedly spoke into the witness's mind: "Calm down. Everything is fine. Go away. It's dangerous for you here." The session used regression hypnosis, a method that tries to recover buried memories, and it was filmed. A man named Carlos de Souza tells this on Michels's episode about an alien said to have been treated in a Brazilian hospital, reading from the recording. He says he believes it "because I saw the tape", which, if true, would mean the creature talked to people without speaking aloud.
hypothetical-nuclear-principle-electroma: Dylan Borland, who says a top government official told him aliens run everything, puts forward a 'hypothetically': a power source that is electromagnetic, probably works on nuclear principles, and gives off energy whose load cannot be controlled. He offers it as a what-if, drawing on people he names only as Towns and Brown, to suggest how such a device might behave and why it could be hard to handle.
i-81-corridor-ufo-flaps: A stretch of Virginia, Maryland and Pennsylvania has had waves of UFO sightings for decades, according to the researcher Dylan Borland. He calls it the I-81 corridor, after the interstate highway, and says it runs from Navy and Air Force country around Norfolk and Langley up past Winchester to Harrisburg, and also takes in Washington DC and Pax River, a Navy flight test base in Maryland. Borland gives no single source but points to the TV series Unsolved Mysteries, and he says he hates to call these sightings "flaps", the word for a burst of reports.
i-beams-with-hieroglyphics-told-at-the-r: After the reported 1947 crash of a flying object near Roswell, New Mexico, everything was said to have been flown out, including metal I-beams marked with hieroglyph-like writing and a number of plates. A physicist named John Brandenburg says he heard this at a conference called Reminiscences of Roswell, from surviving officers and from the daughters of the local sheriff. If true, it would mean the wreckage was not of human making.
ian-fleming-s-mi6-mission-to-evacuate-ma: Ian Fleming, who later wrote the James Bond novels, was an agent of MI6, Britain's foreign intelligence service, and his specific mission at the end of the Second World War in 1945 was to help Martin Bormann, Hitler's top aide, escape to Argentina. The researcher Jason Jorjani tells Michels this without naming a source. If true, it would mean Britain secretly helped a leading Nazi flee.
ian-stevenson-s-reincarnation-cases-at-t: A researcher named Ian Stevenson is said to have spent decades at the University of Virginia, from about the 1960s, collecting cases of young children who spontaneously remembered past lives. The philosopher Jason Jorjani describes "hundreds and hundreds" of such cases and calls the work "extremely rigorous." A documentary filmmaker named Ky Dickens adds a story from Stevenson's fieldwork in India: when he said he was trying to prove past lives, locals asked why he was bothering, since they already knew it was real. They raise it because, if true, it would suggest something of a person survives death.
iarpa-request-to-study-crispr-cas9-dna-d: Bob Maguire, a contractor who worked for the CIA, says that around 2013 or 2014 he was asked to look into storing information inside DNA. The method was CRISPR-Cas9, a tool for editing genes. He says the request came from IARPA, the US intelligence agencies' research funding office, while he was at the Hume Center, a research center at Virginia Tech. He adds that IARPA was then run by Stacy Dixon, who later became deputy director of national intelligence, the second-highest official over US spy agencies.
iblis-refuses-to-bow-to-adam: In Islamic tradition, Iblis, the devil figure, refused to bow before Adam, the first man that God had created. A researcher named Jason Jorjani retells this old story without naming a source, as part of a wider talk about myths of rebellious beings who stand apart from humanity.
ice-age-crustal-rebound-as-the-cause-of-: When ice ages come and go quickly, the weight of ice building up or melting over places like Hudson Bay and northwestern Europe could shake the Earth's outer shell loose enough to slide, moving whole continents relative to the poles. The researcher Randall Carlson offers this as his own view, building on the writer Charles Hapgood and a talk he gave on Atlantis, saying rapid glaciation or deglaciation "induces a tremendous amount of instability in the Earth's crust." If true, it would mean the poles can shift fast enough to remake the world within human memory.
ice-age-gray-farm-and-granary-with-13-tu: Back in the ice age, a race of gray aliens is said to have run a farm in an L-shaped desert valley in central Nevada, with thirteen tunnels cut into the mountain on the valley's west side for use as a granary. Charles Hall tells this. He says he spent three years with tall white aliens at Area 51, the secret US Air Force base in Nevada, and he speaks of the valley as a place he knows himself. If true, it would mean aliens farmed in the American desert long before people wrote history.
ice-age-sahara-as-origin-of-egyptian-civ: The roots of ancient Egyptian civilization may lie in the Sahara Desert during the Ice Age, back when the region was very different from today. A researcher named Graham Hancock puts this forward as his own view, without naming a source, saying that anyone looking for Egypt's origins will "have to start looking at what the Sahara was doing during the Ice Age." If he is right, Egypt's beginnings would be much older than usually thought.
icecube-as-a-two-way-device-earthquake-g: IceCube, a large detector buried in the ice of Antarctica that catches tiny particles called neutrinos, is said by some to be a two-way machine that can also send energy out, even as a kind of earthquake weapon, with a link drawn to Christchurch, New Zealand. A researcher named Jay Anderson relays this as the claim of a man named Eric Hecker, saying Hecker has found documents that "insinuate it's a two-way device" able to emit energy. Michels tells it directly as Hecker's claim that there are neutrino detectors and emitters at the South Pole. If true, it would mean a science station hides a weapon.
icig-hinted-to-brown-that-humans-are-not: A Pentagon whistleblower named Matthew Brown says that staff at the Intelligence Community Inspector General, the watchdog office that takes complaints from inside the US spy agencies, hinted to him personally that humans are not the ones in charge. Brown tells it as something that happened to him, and says he wants to stay respectful toward the office even as he says "the ICIG did it with me," which would mean the people officially charged with checking the agencies had passed him that idea.
icig-hints-that-humans-are-not-in-charge: A guest named Dylan Borland says that the Intelligence Community Inspector General, the internal watchdog office for the US spy agencies, strongly hinted to him in the 2020s that humans are not the ones in charge, which would mean an official source was quietly pointing at a non-human power. Borland says the office "extremely hinted at it." In a second telling he stresses that it happened to him in person: "the ICI did it with me personally."
idea-for-directed-energy-ufo-shootdowns-: The idea of shooting down UFOs with directed energy, meaning focused beams of energy, is said to have come to the CIA (the US spy agency) and the Atomic Energy Commission (the US body that ran nuclear research after the war) from an alien being that survived the 1947 crash near Roswell, New Mexico. Jesse Michels relays this himself, saying a presidential advisor named Harald Malmgren told it to Pippa Malmgren on his deathbed and off the record. If true, it would mean a surviving being gave the US the very idea of how to bring its kind down.
ignored-idea-to-carry-the-space-shuttle-: In 1972, when NASA was first planning the Space Shuttle, someone proposed carrying the shuttle on the back of a Boeing 747 jumbo jet, and the idea was brushed aside at first. Greg Rogers, a former NASA doctor, tells this from his own time around the agency as an example of how good ideas and bad ideas get sorted, and how a good one can be ignored.
igy-listening-posts-for-u-2-overflights-: In 1957 the inventor Townsend Brown, described as a scientist who worked with the CIA, used a worldwide science project called the International Geophysical Year as cover to travel and set up listening posts for the U-2, an American spy plane flying over the Soviet Union. A researcher named Jan Lundquist tells this without naming a source. It would mean a public science program quietly served secret spying work.
illuminati-poster-in-the-dupont-circle-h: In the 1970s, while doing research at the National Archives, the US government's main store of official records, Peter Levenda checked into a hotel at Dupont Circle in Washington, DC. He says that when he carried his suitcase in, he found a huge poster on the wall that someone had left behind: the eye in the pyramid, a symbol often tied to the Illuminati, a secret society of legend. Levenda, whom the episode bills as a CIA historian, tells it himself on the podcast as an odd sign that met him on that trip.
immaculate-constellation-answers-to-the-: A former Pentagon official turned whistleblower named Matthew Brown says that a secret programme called Immaculate Constellation answers in the end to the National Security Council, the White House body that advises the president on security. In his words, it "appears that the cognizant authority," the place where the buck stops, is in that council. If so, oversight of the programme would sit at the very top of government.
immaculate-constellation-as-quarantine-o: Immaculate Constellation, the name given to a reported secret US government programme, may exist to quarantine communications, keeping certain information sealed off, including about crashed UFOs if there are any. Michels puts this forward himself, as his own reasoning in a conversation, not as something he was told. If so, the programme's job would be to keep such secrets from spreading.
immaculate-constellation-hub-at-schrieve: Schriever Air Force Base in Colorado is said to be at least one hub of Immaculate Constellation, a secret program that gathers imagery and data on unidentified flying objects. A former Pentagon official named Matthew Brown says a capabilities briefing on the program points toward the base, which would place a hidden UFO program inside an ordinary military site.
immaculate-constellation-report-describe: In 2024, a report on something called Immaculate Constellation described a secret US government programme for gathering data on UAPs, the official term for UFOs. The journalist Michael Shellenberger, who released the report, says it shows that "a very large strategic intelligence project" exists to evaluate this information. Michels describes it a bit differently: as a 12-page report on what seemed to be an unacknowledged special access programme, a secret project whose existence the government does not admit, put out around the time Shellenberger testified before Congress.
immaculate-constellation-rotating-triang: Slowly rotating triangles were seen over the area watched by Indo-Pacific Command, the US military's command for the Pacific and Asia, according to a document called Immaculate Constellation that the researcher known as UAPGerb attributes to a man named Matthew Brown. UAPGerb, summarising the document, elsewhere describes them as equilateral triangles with three lights over Chinese territory, and calls them adversarial "alien reproduction vehicles", meaning craft built by a rival nation in imitation of alien ones. If true, a foreign power would be flying such craft and the US military would know it.
immaculate-constellation-search-spike-an: Michels says that searches for "Immaculate Constellation", the name of a reported secret government UFO program, spiked online around August or September 2023, when a whistleblower witness named David Grusch came forward, and that this spike was later removed from Google Trends, Google's public record of what people search for. He tells it himself, linking it to the journalist Michael Shellenberger's testimony about the program at a November 2024 congressional hearing and to a man named Rob Jones, as a hint that someone wanted the program's name kept quiet.
immaculate-constellation-usap-managed-by: The story is about Immaculate Constellation, said to be an unacknowledged special access program, meaning a secret US government program whose existence is not officially admitted, which supposedly gathers UFO data. The journalist Michael Shellenberger, who published a report on the program in 2024, says that after it came out he was told the program was "managed by the Department of Defense but held at the White House." In other words, the Pentagon ran it day to day, but it sat under the President's own house. A Pentagon whistleblower named Matthew Brown tells it differently, passing on what he was told. He says the program is "ran out of and owned by the National Security Council," the President's own security staff at the White House, rather than managed by the Pentagon. Brown also calls it an old mission that started well before 2017. Both accounts come from unnamed sources speaking to the tellers, and if either is right, it would mean the secret UFO effort reaches all the way to the White House.
immaculate-constellation-usap-set-up-in-: A highly secret Pentagon program called Immaculate Constellation was set up in 2017 as a reaction to events that year, and its job is to cut out satellite and other overhead data that may show UFOs and lock it away in older secret programs, one of which he calls MCOM. This comes from an online researcher who goes by UAPGerb, who explains it without naming a source. If true, it would mean the government is actively hiding its best images of unexplained objects.
imminent-names-bae-systems-as-an-inherit: The defense company BAE Systems is named as one of the firms that inherited UFO technology, according to Imminent, a book by Luis Elizondo, a former Pentagon intelligence official. Michels passes this on from his own reading of the book, as a pointer to where recovered technology might have ended up in private industry in the United States or Britain.
immune-collapse-and-treatment-at-brooke-: The writer Whitley Strieber says that in 1952 his immune system collapsed and he ended up being treated at Brooke General Hospital, a military hospital in San Antonio, Texas. He tells it as something that happened to him, and he points to an old school report card from that time as a record of it.
imperial-college-extended-the-dmt-state-: Researchers at Imperial College, a university in London, are said to have found a way to keep people in the state brought on by DMT, a powerful psychedelic drug whose effects normally last only minutes, for much longer, around 30 minutes. The neuroscientist Andrew Gallimore says Imperial College, with the researcher Chris Timmermann, picked up the idea and built a much better method, and that every subject in the trials got through it without serious problems. The writer Graham Hancock says they can keep people in the state for an hour. Michels describes the work as Gallimore and Imperial College mapping the spirit world, which is what it would mean to its believers if true.
implant-from-a-va-surgeon-moving-under-t: A small object taken out of a US veteran's body was, according to the pathologist who examined it, "moving under the microscope under its own metabolism," as if it were alive. A former Pentagon official named Luis Elizondo tells this to Michels as something he knows about directly, saying a surgeon at the Department of Veterans Affairs, the US agency that runs hospitals for former soldiers, removed it from a veteran who said he had had a close encounter with a UAP, the government's term for a UFO. If true, the object would be living material connected to such an encounter.
implant-indications-and-alien-dyes-found: A scientist named Steve Colbern, who studies what he says are alien implants in human bodies, says he found signs of implants in a man named Eric Mitchell. He adds that he and Mitchell recently found what he calls dyes on them, which he takes as more evidence that something foreign was placed in the body. Colbern tells it as his own work: "I saw some indications of implants."
implant-paper-rejected-by-journal-of-sci: Steve Colbern, a scientist who has analysed small objects said to be alien implants taken from people's bodies, says he and Roger Leir, a doctor who removed such objects, wrote a paper and tried to publish it in the Journal of Scientific Exploration, a journal for studies on unusual subjects, and it was rejected. Colbern tells it as something he lived through, as an example of how hard it was to get the work taken seriously.
implant-purpose-and-bloodline-hybrid-pro: Steve Colbern, a scientist who studies objects people say were planted in their bodies by aliens, says his understanding is that one such implant was a medical monitoring device. He tells Michels it seemed built to track things like blood sugar and body temperature, which, if true, would mean someone was keeping watch on the health of the person who carried it.
implant-starts-working-after-anne-s-deat: The writer Whitley Strieber says that after his wife Anne Strieber died in 2015, a small object he believes was implanted in his body began to work, and sent him words that slowed down and spelled out "it's me." He tells it as something he lived through himself. If true, it would mean his wife was reaching him after death through that implant.
implant-tracking-patent: A former CIA contractor named Bob McGwier says he wrote a patent that explains how implants in people could be tracked, and that this is how aliens would find such beacons anywhere on Earth. He tells it on the show as his own work. He says: "I didn't believe these stories at all about these implants and them being tracking until I wrote the patent that tells you how they do it." The implants he means are devices that some people say were placed in their bodies during alien encounters. In a second remark in the same conversation, he ties the patent to a name he gives as Hawkeye 360. He says that is "how the aliens would find these beacons all over the planet." Both mentions come from McGwier himself, and no outside record of the patent is given. He tells it because, to him, the patent made the implant stories technically believable.
implants-emitted-radio-signals-during-ja: Objects removed from people's bodies, which some believe are alien implants, began giving off radio signals while a Japanese TV show was filming them. A scientist named Steve Colbern, who studies these suspected implants, says he was there and doing the filming himself. If true, the objects would be active devices sending signals, not just bits of debris.
implants-from-roger-leir-s-surgeries-one: The writer Whitley Strieber, who says he has met aliens, says that in the 1990s he looked at objects taken out of people by a doctor named Roger Leir, who did surgeries to remove them. Strieber says one was remarkable: while it sat at the C2 vertebra in a person's neck, the second bone of the spine, "it was emitting a radio signal," which would suggest a working device rather than a stray fragment.
implants-modulating-gene-expression-thro: The small implants found inside the three-fingered bodies said to come from Nazca, Peru, might be steering the beings' genes through electrical signals, shaping them into what they are.
