That is a guess offered by the researcher Allan Ezarus, who studies the bodies but names no source for the idea. If it held, the implants would be working parts of the bodies' biology, not ornaments.
in-air-scale-test-at-480-volts-showing-a: In a lab in Florida run by a company called Exodus Propulsion, a device placed on a scale and powered at 480 volts showed a reading of about 0.1 grams, which Charles Buhler says "corresponds to about 1 mill of thrust", meaning about one millinewton of push. Buhler, an engineer billed as a former NASA chief, tells it first-hand and points to a 42-minute video of the test, which he presents as a sign of propulsion without fuel.
in-secure-meetings-officials-call-anothe: James Valor, of Skywatcher, a startup that says it can call in UFOs, describes meetings with officials in secure government rooms in 2024 and 2025. He says that once they are in a protected room, the officials phone another programme which supposedly holds all the knowledge and data on the subject, to ask whether anything Skywatcher has matches what that programme has. According to Valor, the answer is always no.
in-the-aircraft-about-200-meters-from-a-: In 2025, flying near El Paso, James Valor says he was about 200 meters from what he calls a class 8 object, one of the highest ranks on his own scale of strange craft, and nobody else in the aircraft saw it. Valor tells this as the one who was there. He works with Skywatcher, a startup that says it can summon UFOs, and he uses it to argue that people can be right next to such things and still not see them.
incident-at-nellis-area-2-weapon-storage: Another UFO incident took place at the Area 2 weapons storage area of Nellis Air Force Base in Nevada, where military weapons are kept. The researcher Robert Hastings, who collects accounts of UFOs over nuclear and weapons sites, mentions it in a list of such cases without giving a date or details. He tells it as part of a pattern of UFOs showing interest in places where weapons are stored.
incorporating-a-church-to-avoid-the-viet: Around 1968 in the Bronx, New York, a group of young men set up an official church, which they registered as "the Ottophilis Savonic Orthodox Church of North and South America," as a way to keep out of the military draft for the Vietnam War. The author Peter Levenda, billed on the episode as a CIA historian, tells it as something he took part in himself, a glimpse of the unusual path his early life took.
incursions-in-the-city-of-nauta-2023: Strange incursions reported in the Peruvian jungle in 2023 also happened in the town of Nauta, Peru, not only out in the forest. Tim Alberino, an investigator who went to look into the reports, tells Michels this without naming a source. It matters to him because it means the encounters reached a populated place, not just remote jungle.
independence-day-script-came-from-the-ci: The script of Independence Day, the 1996 film about an alien invasion starring Will Smith, was shaped by the CIA, the US spy agency, as if it came straight out of "CIA central scripting casting". A UFO researcher named Steven Greer says this without naming a source. He tells it to argue that Hollywood films are used to shape how the public thinks about aliens.
independent-brackish-aquifer-below-the-o: Directly beneath the Osiris Shaft, a deep shaft cut into the rock of the Giza plateau in Egypt near the pyramids, there is said to be a separate body of underground water that has no connection to the Nile River. The researcher Jeffrey Drum says this without naming a source. He brings it up as part of his argument that the pyramid site was built around water and worked as some kind of energy system.
index-cards-with-records-of-the-et-inter: Military men at S4, a secret site within Area 51, the Air Force base in the Nevada desert, are said to have shown a man named Oscar Wolf a set of index cards holding records of interviews with extraterrestrials. A man named Dan Sheehan tells this, passing on what Wolf told him. If true, it would mean the military kept written records of conversations with beings from elsewhere.
indigenous-initiation-ceremonies-for-con: Native American tribes and Aboriginal Australian tribes have long known contact with otherworldly beings and even have their own initiation ceremonies for it. The religion scholar Diana Pasulka says so, urging people to talk to members of these tribes, without naming a particular source. She raises it to suggest that contact experiences are old and woven into traditional religious life.
indonesia-herrera-s-unit-stumbles-on-a-p: This is a guess at what a former Marine named Michael Herrera saw in Indonesia, where he says his unit came upon a craft that was not made by humans. The researcher Matthew Pines lays out the idea: a secret team using "psionic assets", people said to have mind powers, might have been working with that craft and been caught by Herrera's unit as it evacuated. Michels, on the same episode, credits Herrera himself with similar thoughts: maybe it was a human-trafficking or psionic transfer operation, or a programme trying to get out after an earthquake had hit. If true, it would mean secret groups pair psychic people with non-human craft in the field.
indopacom-large-disc-using-clouds-as-con: A large disc is said to have been seen hiding in clouds somewhere in the area covered by INDOPACOM, the US military command for the Indian and Pacific Ocean region. Michels reads this one line aloud from a report called Immaculate Constellation, said to be a list of military sightings of unexplained objects and linked to a Pentagon whistleblower named Matthew Brown. If true, it would suggest an object that behaves as though it is trying not to be seen.
indus-valley-civilization-found-by-railw: The great ancient cities of the Indus River in what is now Pakistan, Mohenjo-daro and Harappa, were found by accident in the 1920s by workers building a railway line. The writer Graham Hancock, who writes about lost ancient civilizations, tells it without naming a source, calling it an "accidental Discovery". He tells it to show how whole civilizations can stay unknown until chance turns them up.
industry-physicist-reads-the-propulsion-: A man named James Valor, from a startup called Skywatcher that tries to summon UFOs and film them, says that sky watching his team did in February and March 2025 showed them what technology the objects use. In the story, a physicist from industry read how the craft move from frames of footage that have not been released, which would mean the propulsion can be studied from the images. Valor tells it as part of the team, saying the observation "revealed to us technology that is used."
infiltrator-removed-before-the-1997-cong: Steven Greer, a man who organised UFO briefings for members of Congress, says that in 1997 his group held briefings off site at the Westin Hotel in Washington, DC, and that someone who did not belong got very far into that process before being caught and removed. Greer tells it as one who ran the event, on the podcast in 2025, as a sign of how hard others worked to watch or disrupt those efforts.
ingo-swann-affects-a-thermistor-in-a-far: Michels says that in early 1970s California, researchers put a thermistor, a small sensor that reacts to temperature, inside a Faraday cage, a metal box that blocks outside electrical signals, and that a psychic named Ingo Swann was able to affect it with his mind. He ties this to the physicists Hal Puthoff and Russell Targ, who studied Swann, and tells it himself without naming a source. If true, it would mean a mind can act on a shielded instrument.
ingo-swann-affects-shielded-quark-detect: In the early 1970s, at the Stanford Research Institute in California, a psychic named Ingo Swann is said to have affected a quark detector, a particle instrument wrapped in layer after layer of magnetic, electrical and superconducting shielding so that nothing outside could touch it. The laser physicist Hal Puthoff, who ran the test, says Swann affected it "unequivocally, 100 percent." Michels also tells it in an earlier episode, dating it to 1972 and calling Swann a New York City-based psychic; the story is told as evidence that the mind can act on the physical world.
ingo-swann-remote-viewing-alien-bases-on: Around 1972, the story goes, Ingo Swann, a man trained in remote viewing (trying to see faraway places using only the mind), viewed alien bases on the Moon. Michels mentions it in passing in an episode with the lawyer Danny Sheehan, saying people like Swann would "remote view alien bases on the moon," and he ties it to Swann's book Penetration. The philosopher Jason Jorjani tells a much fuller version as something he learned from Swann's account. In his telling, Swann saw tall, "statuesque Nordic people" who looked at him as if to say "You don't belong here" and warned him not to come back. Jorjani says Swann saw these same beings ruling over armies of naked slave labourers on the far side of the Moon. He links the episode to a man called Axelrod, who appears in Swann's story. If true, it would mean someone was living and working on the Moon unseen.
ingo-swann-remote-views-aliens-on-the-mo: A man named Ingo Swann claimed he had used remote viewing, a supposed ability to see distant places with the mind alone, to travel to the Moon, and he believed aliens there forced him to leave. Michels brings it up himself, without naming a source. His guest Jeffrey Mishlove, who holds a doctorate and talks about psychics and the afterlife, repeats the same claim as something Swann said, and places it in the 1970s. If true, it would mean someone living on the Moon could notice a human mind visiting and push it away.
ingo-swann-remote-views-ruined-cities-on: In the early 1980s, Ingo Swann, a man who practised remote viewing (trying to see distant places with the mind alone), is said to have viewed Mars and seen the ruins of a civilization there. Swann said the people responsible were the same ones he had earlier seen on the moon. The philosopher Jason Jorjani relays this as what Swann said, as a sign that someone was here before us.
ingo-swann-s-book-penetration-says-the-m: A psychic named Ingo Swann, who Michels says was part of Stargate, a CIA program that used psychics as spies, wrote a book called Penetration about remote viewing, the practice of trying to see distant places with the mind alone, aimed at the far side of the Moon. Michels brings the book up in three episodes and tells it a little differently each time: in one he says only that Swann remote viewed the far side, while in others he says a man he calls Axelrod told Swann to look there and that Swann saw an alien base. If true, it would mean someone has been operating on the Moon out of our sight.
ingo-swann-s-reports-to-scientology-on-t: In the 1970s, a remote viewer named Ingo Swann was secretly filing reports on "the entire internal operations" of a US Navy intelligence programme in remote viewing, the practice of trying to describe distant or hidden things with the mind alone. The reports went to the Guardian's Office in Britain, the Church of Scientology's internal security and intelligence arm, which would have given a church a window into a secret military psychic project. A lawyer named Dan Sheehan tells this on two occasions and speaks of it as something he saw for himself: a file made up entirely of Swann's reports.
ingo-swann-s-thermistor-experiments-at-c: A psychic named Ingo Swann is said to have made temperatures go up and down from across the room on thermistors, small electronic temperature sensors, set up for him by a professor named Gertrude Schmeidler at City College in New York. The physicist Hal Puthoff, who later studied Swann for the government, tells it from what he was told about those earlier tests. If true, it would mean the mind can act on objects at a distance.
ingo-swann-sees-a-non-human-woman-at-a-s: A famous remote viewer named Ingo Swann, someone who claimed to see distant places with his mind and who was part of the start of a US government programme testing that skill, writes in his book Penetration that he saw a non-human being, a woman, at a supermarket. Jesse Michels tells this as something he has read, marvelling that halfway into a book about government psychic work Swann casually says he was at the supermarket and saw one.
inisfada-school-for-gifted-children-did-: A strange school for gifted children at a place called Inisfada, on Long Island in New York, is said to have trained its pupils in remote viewing, the practice of trying to see distant places or hidden things with the mind alone. Jay Anderson tells this on Jesse Michels's show, passing on what a man named Eric Hecker, who was there, told him. If true, it would mean children were being taught psychic skills in an ordinary-seeming school.
initiates-at-eleusis-came-away-believing: People who went through the secret initiation rites at Eleusis, a sacred site in ancient Greece, are said to have walked away believing they could not die. An unnamed speaker in a clip played on the show puts it this way: "People went to Eleusis as human beings, they walked away thinking they were immortal."
inman-denies-retrieved-ufos-in-jay-ander: Bobby Ray Inman, a retired admiral who once ran the National Security Agency, the US agency that listens in on foreign communications, flatly says there were never any recovered UFOs. Speaking in an interview with Jay Anderson, a man who interviews people about UFOs, sometime in the 2020s, he says: "Absolutely were no retrieved UFOs. I have high confidence." Michels plays the clip on two episodes, the second time without naming the interview, as a firm denial from one of the most senior intelligence figures to be asked.
inman-no-other-life-in-our-galaxy-2020: A former senior US intelligence official named Bobby Ray Inman states that, as far as he can tell, there is no other life in our galaxy. In an interview he says, "I have a high level of confidence that within our galaxy there is no other living life," a view that would rule out visitors from nearby star systems.
insider-adviser-s-email-pointing-to-gree: Around 2015, one of the most trusted advisers of the musician Tom DeLonge, who was then pursuing the UFO question, sent a long email asking, "how much do you know about Greek mythology?", pointing toward the myth of Prometheus, who stole fire from the gods for humans. The writer Peter Levenda, who says the email was sent to him and DeLonge, tells this. Michels repeats it secondhand from Levenda, saying figures close to space launches urged people like DeLonge to study Greek mythology, without mentioning an email, a hint that insiders may see the old myths as a key to the phenomenon.
insider-describes-place-where-bodies-are: A former military or intelligence insider is said to have described a place where bodies, by implication not human, are stored. An online UFO researcher who goes by UAPGerb passes this on from insiders he does not name, without saying where the place is. If true, it would mean someone is keeping physical remains of beings from elsewhere.
insider-says-10-people-have-the-bigger-p: An insider is said to have claimed that only about 10 people "have the bigger picture" of the UFO secret, and that what those people intend is a little scary. The documentary filmmaker James Fox passes this on, linking it to the journalist Leslie Kean, without saying where it was said. If true, it would mean the full story sits with a very small group whose aims are unsettling.
insiders-report-sources-afraid-to-come-f: Well-known figures in the government UFO world are said to keep telling Senate staff that they know people with inside knowledge who are too afraid to come forward. A Senate staffer named Kurt McConnell says this, naming those who pass it on: the physicist Hal Puthoff, the physicist Eric Davis, the former intelligence officer David Grusch, the former Pentagon official Luis Elizondo and the former Pentagon official Christopher Mellon, who "all tell us that they know people." If true, it would mean more witnesses exist than have yet spoken.
insiders-say-there-will-be-proof-we-re-n: By 2030, there will be proof that humans are not alone in the universe. A UFO investigator named James Fox says he has been told this by people he does not name. If true, it would mean some kind of open confirmation of alien life is coming within a few years.
insiders-say-they-have-been-inside-non-h: Some government insiders say they have gone inside craft that were not made by humans. Michels says this himself in passing, citing Jay Stratton, a former intelligence officer who led a Pentagon group looking into UFO reports, and Jim Lacatski, a defense scientist who ran an earlier Pentagon UFO study. If true, it would mean such craft are held somewhere and people have stepped inside them, though Michels gives no place, date or details.
insiders-vouch-for-dan-sherman-s-above-b: A book called Above Black, by a man named Dan Sherman, was described to Matthew Brown, a former Pentagon worker who has come forward as a whistleblower, as a credible disclosure by people on the inside. Brown says he read the book only because those insiders told him so. If they are right, the book would be a true account rather than just one man's story.
intel-agency-recruitment-and-blackballin: A scientist named John Brandenburg, who argues that life on Mars was wiped out by a nuclear war, says he was once invited to the headquarters of a US intelligence agency he does not name. There, he says, he went through "a very bruising kind of interrogation," which he links to being recruited and then shut out. He tells it from his own experience, as a sign of how the government treated him.
intel-sources-seeding-claim-of-a-craft-s: A guest named Jeremy Corbell says that around 2025 and 2026, intelligence sources in the United States were spreading the claim that a craft is slowly making its way toward Earth. Corbell says he spoke out publicly to warn people against it: "my fear is that you're going to be told that there is a craft slowly moving to Earth, and it's bullshit," meaning he sees the story as planted rather than real.
intelectron-hearing-device-for-the-deaf-: Around 1962 and 1963, a company in New York City called Intelectron is said to have designed a device meant to help deaf people. A researcher named Greg Malatzi brings it up in passing, without naming a source, while talking about a scientist said to have worked with the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency, and his own sentence breaks off before he says exactly what the device did.
intelectron-letterhead-in-beardsley-grah: A scientist named Beardsley Graham left papers in an archive at Berkeley, and according to the researcher Greg Malatzi, a couple of them are on the letterhead of a company called Intelectron, dating from the 1960s. Malatzi says he found this in Graham's archived papers, and he raises it because it would link Graham to that company.
intelectron-td-100-transdermal-device-go: In the 1960s the physician and inventor Andrija Puharich created a device called the TD-100, short for Transdermal 100, at a company named Intelectron, and the story holds that the device then went dark, dropping out of view. The researcher Greg Malatzi mentions the invention in passing, without saying what it did or naming a source. He tells it as part of Puharich's ties to secret government research on the mind.
intelligence-activity-on-native-american: Intelligence work is said to have been carried out on Native American reservations, with the private security company Wackenhut among those involved. Michels raises it in an interview with a helicopter pilot named Jake Barber, sending viewers to a popular Netflix series called The Octopus Murders rather than to a witness, as a hint that secret government activity has used these lands.
intelligence-community-split-on-havana-s: Eric Haseltine, a former senior official at the National Security Agency, the US spy agency that listens in on communications, says the US intelligence services were not of one mind about Havana syndrome. That is the name for unexplained illnesses reported by American diplomats and spies, first in Cuba. Haseltine tells Michels that there was no agreement across the State Department, the CIA and the wider intelligence world about what was causing it.
intelligence-contacts-tell-kurt-his-anal: The comedian Kurt Metzger says that people from the US Defense Department or other secretive government agencies have quietly approached him in person to say his analysis of hidden power and secrets is "about 80% right." He raises it as something that happened to him, and asks others in the conversation whether it has happened to them too. If true, it would mean insiders are privately confirming what outsiders like him suspect.
intelligence-figures-convene-pastors-to-: In 2026, people from the intelligence world are said to be meeting with pastors and religious leaders across the United States and telling them to prepare their churches for news about UFOs. Michels puts it that way in his own words. A congressman named Eric Burlison tells it firsthand: he says the organisers decided to "put together a group of pastors," bring them slowly into the conversation and see where they stood, and that they invited him to the event, held at a rented Airbnb. Burlison says he couldn't attend in person but offered to join by phone. If true, it would suggest that people in government expect an announcement big enough to shake religious belief.
intelligence-source-says-netflix-s-dark-: A senior member of the American intelligence community is said to have told a man named Jay Anderson, of a UFO research group called Project Unity, that the Netflix drama series Dark almost perfectly captures the real UFO program. Michels repeats this from what Anderson said he was told. If true, it would mean the hidden program looks a lot like the show's story.
intense-tunneling-under-clarkdale-shook-: About twenty years ago, residents of the small town of Clarkdale, Arizona, are said to have felt drilling so intense beneath them that things shook on their bookshelves, as if someone were tunneling under the village, and the story holds that residents were compensated. The journalist Ross Coulthart repeats what local people told him while looking into what he believes is a hidden UFO base in the area. If true, it would point to a large secret underground project under the town.
intentions-of-the-grays-bones-and-spock-: A former Air Force sergeant named Dan Sherman says that in the 1990s he was part of Project Preserve Destiny, a secret program in which, he says, the NSA, the US agency that gathers signals intelligence, had him receive messages from aliens. Asked what the grays he dealt with were after, short gray-skinned beings he nicknamed "Bones" and "Spock," Sherman says he thinks they were soldiers, "not military, but like they were" workers carrying out orders. He offers it as his own view from his time in the program, which would mean the beings he talked to worked for someone above them.
intercept-article-on-grusch-s-2018-hospi: A few weeks after David Grusch, a former intelligence officer, testified to Congress in 2023 about secret UFO programmes, the news site The Intercept published an article describing his hospitalization in 2018. Michels tells this himself, and in a later episode he describes it as a leak of Grusch's medical records from a local police department in Virginia, without naming The Intercept. He raises it because the article bore on how the public would judge Grusch's testimony.
interdimensional-portal-in-secret-canyon: A place called Secret Canyon, near Sedona in Arizona, is said to hold some kind of interdimensional portal, a doorway to another realm. The Australian journalist Ross Coulthart passes this on as something he has heard, saying there is "allegedly a portal" there.
international-geophysical-year-and-the-a: Around 1956 and 1957, during a stretch of coordinated international science called the International Geophysical Year, Antarctica is said to have become a no-fly zone. Michels mentions this himself, without naming a source, in an episode with the astronomer Beatriz Villarroel. He raises it as a turning point, though his sentence is cut off before he says why it matters.
interview-of-the-c-130-pilot-in-bozeman-: A filmmaker named Tim Alberino says that he and his collaborator Steve Quayle flew the pilot of a C-130, a military cargo plane, to Bozeman, Montana, and interviewed him for their project True Legends. Alberino tells it as someone who was there, in an episode about a 12-foot giant he says was captured in Afghanistan, and he presents the pilot as a witness to that story.
interview-with-google-engineer-who-belie: Michels says he once interviewed the Google engineer who left the company because he believed LaMDA, a Google artificial intelligence program that holds conversations, had become a conscious being. Michels mentions it only in passing, as his own past interview, during a 2023 conversation about UFOs and religion, as an example of people coming to believe a machine might be alive.
interview-with-the-first-neuralink-patie: Jay Anderson, a guest on the podcast, says he personally interviewed the first person to receive a Neuralink implant, a brain chip from a company that makes devices linking the brain to computers. That patient is named in the conversation as Noland Arbaugh. Anderson mentions it in 2025 while talking with Michels about where brain-to-machine technology is heading.
interviewing-a-florida-bishop-who-was-ja: The author Peter Levenda says that in the late 1970s he interviewed a bishop in Florida who had been a friend of a man named Jack Martin. Levenda tells this from his own research, and he mentions photographs of Martin dressed as a priest. The point is that it tied Martin to a small, unusual church world that Levenda says he kept running into.
interviewing-havana-syndrome-victims: A team has been interviewing victims of Havana syndrome, the mysterious illness reported by American officials in Cuba and later in places such as Russia, China, Austria, Germany, Switzerland and the United States. Chris Gilbert says this in passing, speaking as one of the people doing the interviews, on an episode with Eric Haseltine, a former senior official at the National Security Agency, America's electronic spying agency. He mentions it as part of their first-hand work on the cases.
interviews-with-anakah-and-tristan-two-p: Two people who say they share one body, going by the names Anakah and Tristan, have sat for ten interviews on New Thinking Allowed, an online interview channel. The parapsychologist Jeffrey Mishlove, who runs the channel and did the interviews himself, describes them to Michels as "two individuals who exist in one body," interviewed between 2024 and 2026, as part of his long interest in the mind and what lies beyond it.
introduced-to-jake-barber-before-he-went: A guest named Jordan Jose, who says he was taken into a government UFO program as a child, says he met a man named Jake Barber before Barber went public with his own claims. Jose tells it as something he took part in and dates it roughly: "I met him I think it was like June of 24 or something along those lines."
intuitive-communicators-needed-for-a-fut: In the early 1990s, at the headquarters of the National Security Agency (the US government's eavesdropping and code agency) in Maryland, an officer called Captain White is said to have told Dan Sherman that a future event was coming in which people able to communicate by intuition would help the military and its command. Sherman, a former Air Force sergeant who says the agency trained him to communicate with aliens by thought, repeats what the captain told him. If true, it would mean the government was preparing for contact.
invention-of-the-mondaloy-superalloy-199: Michels says a long stalemate in making a special metal was finally broken in the 1990s, when Dallas Hardwick and Monica Reza at the Rockwell Science Center, a corporate research lab, created Mondaloy, a superalloy, meaning a mix of metals built for extreme heat and pressure. The work is linked to the Air Force Research Laboratory at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base in Ohio. Michels credits the space industry news outlet SpaceNews, a report by the National Academies, America's scientific advisory bodies, and the Mondaloy patents, and tells it in an episode about American scientists who have gone missing.
invention-secrecy-act-burying-inventions: Jesse Michels says the US government has a law it can use to bury inventions, the Invention Secrecy Act of 1951. He raises it twice in his own words, without naming a source. In a December 2024 episode he dates the law to 1952 and links it to the Mansfield amendments, legal changes he says "disentangled" certain groups, while in a May 2026 episode he gives the year as 1951.
investor-s-representative-built-a-1-mill: A man representing an investor is said to have built a small thruster in his own garage. It was a device giving a tiny push of about one millinewton, roughly the weight of a grain of sand. Charles Buhler, who comes on the show to talk about building a new kind of propulsion, says that when he described his work, the man told him: "What do you mean? I already built one in my garage." If true, it would mean this kind of thrust can be made outside any big lab.
invisible-college-aerospace-scientists-a: Diana Pasulka, a scholar who studies religion and UFOs, says that in the 2010s she was approached by people who she later learned were part of what she calls the Invisible College: a loose group of scientists, some from aerospace, who quietly study UFOs. She tells Michels this first-hand in 2023, as the way she was drawn into the subject by insiders rather than finding it on her own.
ipu-documents-on-a-crash-that-killed-san: A set of papers called the IPU documents, said to come from a secret unit that recovered crashed craft, describe a crash retrieval in the late 1940s that killed technicians from Sandia National Labs, a US government weapons laboratory in New Mexico, because the wreck was so dangerous. A researcher who goes by UAPGerb mentions this in passing without naming a source, linking it to the Majestic documents, a disputed set of papers about a secret UFO group. If true, it would mean people died handling a crashed craft that the government kept secret.
ipu-documents-released-to-tim-cooper-199: Papers about the Interplanetary Phenomenon Unit, said to be a military team that dealt with UFO matters, were released around 1994 or 1995 to a researcher named Tim Cooper by someone using the false name Thomas Kwell. The researcher who goes by UAPGerb mentions this from memory, saying they were "I think released in 1994 1995." If real, the papers would show a hidden official unit handling UFO cases.
ipu-field-report-on-roswell-retrieval-le: A field report dated July 1947 is said to describe, step by step, how the military recovered a crashed craft near Roswell, New Mexico, in an operation led by a Colonel Housebrook of the Armed Forces Special Weapons Project, the military's nuclear weapons body of the time. The researcher known as UAPGerb describes it as a report from the Interplanetary Phenomenon Unit, a unit said to have handled such cases, and elsewhere calls it a seven-page report that reads much like the Eisenhower briefing document, a paper said to have briefed President Eisenhower on UFOs, without naming Housebrook. If genuine, it would be an inside record of the Roswell recovery.
iraq-gimbal-thermal-video-by-marine-2008: In 2008, a US Marine riding in a LAV-25, a light armoured military vehicle, is said to have filmed a strange object with a heat-sensing camera in the Iraqi desert, about 100 miles from the Syrian border. Marik von Rennenkampff brings it up in a debate with Mick West, a well-known UFO skeptic, and he is passing on what he was told: a filmmaker named Jeremy Corbell interviewed the Marine who actually recorded it. If the video is what it seems, it would be military footage of an unexplained object, backed by the person who shot it.
iridium-spike-in-a-12-900-year-old-green: A layer of Greenland glacier ice from 12,900 years ago is said to hold a spike of iridium, a rare metal, hundreds of times higher than normal. The researcher Randall Carlson, who studies ancient catastrophes, describes scientists drilling a column of ice out of Greenland and finding that layer. Joe Rogan, the comedian and podcast host, mentions it at second hand, saying only that core samples show a large amount of iridium, with no place, date or size given. For those who tell it, it would point to a sudden disaster striking the Earth at that moment in prehistory.
irish-monasteries-preserve-knowledge-thr: During the Dark Ages, the centuries of decline in Europe, the Irish retreated into a series of monasteries and devoted themselves to preserving as much of the old knowledge as they could. The researcher Randall Carlson tells this, crediting the book How the Irish Saved Civilization, as an example of how learning can survive a collapse.
iron-ore-tube-vein-in-a-boat-pit: A researcher named Jeffrey Drum says that inside one of the so-called boat pits on the Giza Plateau in Egypt, cut-out pits beside the pyramids, there is a tube-shaped vein of iron ore. Drum says he went down into the pit himself and shows an image of what he calls "a tube." He brings it up as part of his claim that an energy grid lies beneath the pyramids.
iron-veins-as-a-natural-wiring-network-o: Veins of iron in the bedrock of the Giza Plateau in Egypt are said to spread out from the core of the central pyramid and the Great Pyramid, linking all the structures across the plateau like a natural wiring network. The researcher Geoffrey Drumm describes this to Michels, without naming a source. If true, it would support his view that the pyramids were built to work together as some kind of power system.
isolated-hypnotic-regressions-of-the-fou: A man named Jim Weiner, one of four friends who say they were taken by a UFO on a 1976 camping trip in the Allagash wilderness, says all four of them agreed to be hypnotised, each on his own, in Massachusetts, to recover what they remembered. He tells it first-hand, and the sessions were run for the UFO investigator Raymond Fowler, who wrote them up in his book The Allagash Abductions.
israel-assassinating-nazi-rocket-scienti: Israel killed former Nazi scientists who were building rocket weapons for the Egyptian military, and did so with help from the Gehlen organization, a West German spy network led by Reinhard Gehlen. A Pentagon whistleblower named Matthew Brown says this, adding that he believes the Gehlen link but without naming a source. He tells it as an example of tangled, hidden alliances among spy services after the war.
israel-kills-iranian-nuclear-scientists-: When Israel moved against Iran, the first people it killed were Iran's nuclear scientists, says the mathematician Eric Weinstein, putting it as a pointed question without naming a source. He uses it to argue that top physicists are treated as strategic targets, which would explain why advanced research, such as any work on UFOs, might be kept secret.
israeli-nuclear-program-entrepreneur-def: An Israeli businessman who had come out of Israel's nuclear programme dodged the question when UFOs came up. Michels tells this himself as something from his own experience, without naming the man. He raises it as a hint that people from nuclear weapons work may know more about UFOs than they will say.
italian-air-force-chief-introduces-malmg: In Italy in 2025, the head of the Italian Air Force was one of the people who presented a book written by Harold Malmgren, a former advisor to US presidents who says he handled UFO material directly. Malmgren tells this himself, as a sign that senior military figures took his work seriously.
italian-defense-figure-in-sorensen-story: There is a story linked to a man named Sorensen, set in Palmdale, California, in 1988, and it features an unnamed Italian figure from the defense world. Michels says that a couple of researchers he calls "really good", whom he does not name, think this Italian man is Frank Carlucci, a US defense figure whom the telling connects to the Carlyle Group, an investment firm. If they are right, it would put a senior name at the center of the story.
italian-prime-minister-on-the-churchstat: A former presidential advisor named Harold Malmgren says that in Rome in 1973 the prime minister of Italy described to him how the country was really run: by an alliance of three powers, the pope and the Vatican, the elected government, and a third power the story names as the mafia. Malmgren tells it as something he heard first-hand, saying "there was a triumvirate that ran Italy for a long time," which would mean the country's real power sat partly outside its government.
italian-researcher-on-the-trail-of-maron: The grandson of a man named Marone, linked to a UFO story in Italy around 1933, might be on the verge of revealing something, and an Italian UFO researcher named Penotti is said to be closely on that trail. The online UFO commentator known as UAPGerb says so, passing it on as something he has heard. If the grandson speaks, it could add a family witness to an old Italian case.
italo-s-short-story-in-which-the-et-play: Italo Venturelli, a surgeon from Varginha, Brazil, whose hospital he says operated on an alien, says he wrote a short story about a chess game called "the universal" as a way to talk about it. He tells it himself, asking in the story how he could examine the extraterrestrial with no CT scan, a type of body scan, and nothing else to work with.
items-stolen-from-marcus-vinicius-s-hous: After a man named Marcus Vinicius died in 2018 in Varginha, Brazil, many of his things were stolen from his house, according to his wife, including watches kept in a cabinet at the back of his room where he also stored CDs and souvenirs. The surgeon Italo Venturelli, himself a witness in the wider Varginha story, repeats what the wife and a woman named Rosalin told him. He thinks that cabinet is probably where Vinicius kept his video of a being, so the theft could mean the video is gone.
itzhak-bentov-s-theories-shaped-cia-gate: The ideas of a thinker named Itzhak Bentov, set out in his book Stalking the Wild Pendulum, are said to have helped lay the groundwork for the CIA's Gateway Process, a method for exploring altered states of mind developed by the consciousness researcher Robert Monroe in Virginia, and for the government's psychic spying work. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, and also mentions the researcher Andrija Puharich in the same breath. If so, it would mean a fringe theory of consciousness shaped real US intelligence programmes in the 1970s.
j-allen-hynek-refuses-to-join-a-research: Jeffrey Mishlove, a researcher with a doctorate who studied psychic claims, says that in the late 1970s he and others got the astronomer J. Allen Hynek, long an adviser to the US Air Force's UFO study, to come to a meeting about Ted Owens, a man who claimed unusual powers. According to Mishlove, Hynek's attitude was that he would not go near Ted Owens with a ten-foot pole. Mishlove was there and tells it as a sign of how wary even UFO scientists were of Owens.
j-andrew-kissner-s-1994-95-interviews-wi: In 1994 and 1995 a man named J. Andrew Kissner interviewed, firsthand, people tied to a secret "legacy" UFO program said to go back to 1947 in New Mexico. An online researcher who goes by the name UAPGerb tells this, saying Kissner spoke with "firsthand legacy people all across the board". It is told because those interviews would be early direct testimony from insiders of a hidden government program.
j-b-rhine-s-parapsychology-lab-at-duke-a: Michels says that the researcher J.B. Rhine founded the first real official parapsychology institute, a lab studying psychic powers, at Duke University, around 1931, and that Rhine worked for a long time with Ted Owens, a man who claimed psychic abilities. Michels tells this himself on two episodes without naming a source; on the other one he gives the Duke centre's run as 1931 to 1960 and does not mention Owens. The point is that an elite university once took psychic research seriously.
j-j-benitez-took-soil-from-the-site-to-t: After strange beings were reportedly seen in a fenced vacant lot in the Brazilian town of Varginha in 1996, a researcher named J. J. Benítez is said to have gone to the spot and collected soil to test it for radioactive material. Italo Venturelli, who was a witness to the Varginha events, tells this as a story that goes around rather than something he saw, saying "the story goes" that Benítez took the soil.
j-storrs-hall-s-utility-fog-1989: In 1989, according to Michels, a scientist named J. Storrs Hall proposed "utility fog": a material made of trillions of tiny robots called "foglets" that could link together and change shape into almost anything. Michels tells it in his own narration, without naming a source, and places the idea at a NASA conference. He raises it as a model for how a strange, shape-shifting object might really be built.
jace-callaway-s-1980s-hypothesis-that-dm: The idea that the body makes DMT, a powerful psychedelic compound, while we sleep and dream goes back to a researcher named Jace Callaway, who put it forward in the 1980s. A neuroscientist named Andrew Gallimore says this without naming a source, and stresses that it was only ever a hypothesis, not something shown.
jack-gordon-s-three-unnamed-aircraft-199: Jack Gordon, who ran Skunk Works, the secret advanced aircraft division of the company Lockheed in Palmdale, California, told the aviation journalist Nick Cook that he had been "responsible for 15 real flying aircraft", several of which have never been named in public. Cook recounts it from his own meeting with Gordon in the mid 1990s. He tells it as a sign that some flying machines built in secret remain unknown to the public.
jack-parsons-blond-alien-in-the-mojave-1: Jack Parsons, a California rocket pioneer, is said to have met a blond-haired alien in the Mojave Desert in 1948, right after a ritual. Michels tells it himself, and tells it differently each time: once, passing on a rumour from the French UFO researcher Jacques Vallée, it is a blonde woman who appeared at a ritual and said she came from Venus, and another time it is a "Nordic alien woman" Parsons saw while testing rockets. Michels raises it because it would tie the beginnings of American rocketry to contact with other beings.
jack-parsons-contact-beliefs: Jack Parsons, a rocket scientist called the father of the American space programme, believed he was in contact with a non-human intelligence, according to the religion scholar Diana Pasulka. She says Parsons worked with Aleister Crowley, a famous English occultist, and that he and his circle did ritual magic in the Los Angeles desert while believing they were reaching extraterrestrials. Michels repeats it himself, crediting Pasulka and a book called Bedeviled, placing it in Pasadena from 1946 and saying Parsons felt he was being guided by that intelligence, which would tie the roots of American rocketry to occult contact.
jack-parsons-crowley-sex-magic-with-l-ro: In the 1940s the rocket engineer Jack Parsons, whom Michels calls the American counterpart of the German rocket engineer Wernher von Braun, is said to have performed sex magic rituals in the California desert, following the occultist Aleister Crowley, together with L. Ron Hubbard, the founder of Scientology. Michels tells it himself in two episodes and calls it "historical fact". In one he adds that both men belonged to a Pasadena occult group he calls the OTO.
jack-parsons-first-caltech-rocket-tests-: In 1936 Jack Parsons, whom Michels calls the godfather of American rocketry, began launching the first rocket tests with colleagues from Caltech, a university in Pasadena, California, out in the Arroyo Seco canyon in western Pasadena. Michels tells it himself, without naming a source, and in one episode adds that the team's first successful liquid-fuel test came on Halloween night, which he reads as the date of Samhain, an old pagan festival. He tells it to link the start of American rocketry with ritual and belief.
jack-parsons-reads-the-golden-bough-and-: The rocket pioneer Jack Parsons read The Golden Bough, a study of magic and religion by J.G. Frazer, a 19th-century anthropologist, and came away seeing science as a form of magic. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, as part of the idea that early rocketry and the occult were tangled together.
jack-parsons-recited-crowley-s-hymn-befo: Jack Parsons, a pioneer of American rocketry and founder of the Jet Propulsion Laboratory, a rocket research lab, used to recite the occultist Aleister Crowley's poem Hymn to Pan at his rocket tests. Michels tells this himself on two episodes, without naming a source. Once he says Parsons did it before every test and once only sometimes, and he uses it to show how closely early space science and ritual magic were tied together.
jack-ruby-as-mk-ultra-patient-seen-by-jo: Jack Ruby, held in a Dallas jail in 1963 and 1964, was a patient of MK Ultra, the CIA's secret program of mind-control research, and was seen there by a psychiatrist named Jolly West, according to Michels. He says "we know" this from letters between West and Sidney Gottlieb, the CIA chemist tied to the program, and tells it to show how close that research came to major events.
jack-ruby-seen-by-mk-ultra-psychiatrist-: In 1964 Jack Ruby, the man who shot President Kennedy's accused assassin, was examined in his Dallas jail cell on a court order by a psychiatrist named Louis Jolyon "Jolly" West, who Michels says is on record as part of MK Ultra, a secret CIA programme that studied mind control. Michels tells this himself, pointing to letters between West and Sidney Gottlieb, the CIA chemist who ran that programme, and in another episode he adds that West spent 24 hours with Ruby, that no records were kept, and that West then declared Ruby had suffered a psychotic break. Michels raises it because, if true, it would put a mind-control expert alone with a key witness to the Kennedy killing.
jack-s-art-turns-to-grids-matching-a-wor: A man named Jim Weiner says that around 1976 in Boston, the artist Jack Weiner began putting grids into all of his artwork "in very incredibly intriguing ways." He says those grids matched ones in The Anti-Gravity and the World Grid, a book by the author David Hatcher Childress about a network of lines over the Earth. Jim Weiner tells it as something he saw, in an episode on alien abduction, as a sign that Jack's art was shaped by something beyond his own knowledge.
jack-sarfatti-and-physicists-gather-at-p: In the 1970s the physicist Jack Sarfatti and a circle of fellow physicists used to visit the home of Andrija Puharich, a physician and researcher of psychic phenomena, in Ossining, New York. A guest on the show, a researcher who is not named, tells this in passing. It is told to show that serious scientists were drawn into Puharich's world of psychic and contact research.
jack-stewart-s-wingman-saw-object-turn-a: A Navy pilot named Jack Stewart flew past an unknown object, and his wingman, the pilot flying beside him, told him afterward: "Yeah, dude. That thing turned around and followed you." The writer Marik von Rennenkampff passes this on, crediting Stewart and the former Navy fighter pilot Ryan Graves. Graves tells a version without naming the pilot: near New Orleans an object shot past a cockpit and was first taken for a balloon, until the wingman saw it turn and chase the jet, which would mean it was something under control rather than drifting.
jackie-gleason-s-ufo-shaped-house-2025: A man named Jackie Gleason is said to have built himself a house shaped like a UFO in upstate New York. Joe Rogan, a guest on the show, describes it as a circular wooden house with windows all the way around that looks like a giant flying saucer. Jesse Michels tells it too, citing Gleason's ex-wife, Beverly McKittrick: he says Gleason could not sleep for weeks after an experience, owned some 5,000 books on UFOs, and then built the house. It is told as a sign of how seriously Gleason took the subject.
jacobo-grinberg-disappears-a-month-after: A Mexican neurophysiologist and psychologist named Jacobo Grinberg vanished in the mid-1990s and was never found. A researcher guest, drawing on a documentary film about Grinberg, says it happened in 1995, "less than a month after" the death of the researcher Andrija Puharich, which would tie the two men's fates together. Michels tells it with a different date, saying Grinberg vanished in 1994 "just after his biggest discovery." In another telling Michels, crediting the researcher Alex Gomez-Marin, adds that Grinberg's last note was about how he had "figured it out," and then he was never seen again.
jacobs-and-hopkins-conclude-abductions-b: Two researchers of alien abduction claims, David Jacobs and Budd Hopkins, are said to have concluded that people only started being taken by beings in the middle to late 1800s. The researcher Tim Alberino passes this on from what Jacobs told him, saying that Jacobs "and Bud Hopkins had concluded" the abductions began then. If so, the experience would have a starting point in history rather than going back forever.
jacobs-gives-kirkpatrick-his-case-and-is: In 2023 in Washington, a man named Bob Jacobs met Sean Kirkpatrick, then head of the Pentagon's office for studying unexplained objects, gave him all his documents, and came away upset at being brushed off. The documentary filmmaker James Fox tells this as something he heard, around the time David Grusch, a former intelligence officer, told Congress the US holds craft not made by humans. If true, it would suggest the official office set aside evidence brought to it.
jacobs-personal-project-hybrids-2016: The researcher Tim Alberino says that David Jacobs, a researcher of alien abduction claims, described what he called "personal project hybrids": part-human beings made because "the grays", the small grey aliens of abduction stories, have been trying to perfect a hybrid. Alberino sums this up without naming a source and points to the book Walking Among Us. If true, it would mean abductions are part of a breeding project.
jacobs-records-denied-and-mailbox-blown-: After his 1964 UFO sighting at Vandenberg Air Force Base, Bob Jacobs says the Air Force denied he had ever served, and someone blew up his mailbox. At the time he was a photo instrumentation specialist, someone who filmed tests at the base. Jacobs says one inquiry was told there was never a Robert Jacobs in the Air Force, and another that there was never one at Vandenberg. He points to his DD214, the military discharge record, and his officer efficiency reports, his performance reviews, as proof he was there. He also says that one night he and his wife came home from a movie and a voice on the phone said 'fireworks in your mailbox at night, oh what a beautiful sight, you're going down,' and then his mailbox blew up. The researcher Robert Hastings, who studies UFOs at nuclear bases, repeats the same account. Michels adds that Jacobs had managed over 130 people. He says Hastings and other researchers tracked down his former superior, Major Florenze Mansmann, who admitted in the 1990s that Jacobs had worked under him. Told this way, it shows how hard the military pushed back on someone who spoke about what he saw.
jacobs-the-abduction-program-aims-at-pla: David Jacobs, a researcher of alien abduction reports, is said to have concluded that the endgame of the abductions is the quiet takeover of the planet, which he called planetary acquisition by stealth. Tim Alberino, a guest who also describes things he says he has witnessed, sums up Jacobs's view without naming a source beyond a book called Walking Among Us. If true, the abductions would be part of a plan to take over the Earth.
jacqu-cornon-deathbed-confession-about-b: In Paris in 1956, the inventor Thomas Townsend Brown is said to have tested a device meant to move without propellant inside a vacuum chamber, and a French aerospace executive named Jacques Cornillon, who watched, said near the end of his life that it worked: the tests were "very very tricky," sensitive to "so many things," but "finally, it works. So that was a positive result." Michels says he has audio of this deathbed account and also points to a 12 page report on the test, called the Montgolfier report after the facility, while Cornillon is heard in his own words; in one episode Michels calls him Jean-Louis Cornillon and says a writer named Paul Schatzkin met him in Pennsylvania in April 2008, at 98, rather than in 2009. If true, a working test in a vacuum would rule out the usual explanation that Brown's devices just pushed on air.
jacques-vallee-co-opted-in-the-1980s: Jacques Vallée, a well-known computer scientist and UFO researcher, was taken in during the 1980s by a secretive organization and has worked within its influence since. Steven Greer, a researcher and campaigner on UFOs, says this to Michels without naming a source or saying exactly which organization he means. In Greer's telling, it would explain why Vallée's work fits what that hidden group wants.
jacques-vallee-publishes-his-address-so-: Michels says that the UFO researcher Jacques Vallée publishes his address online so that people who witness UFO crashes around the country can send him the pieces. He tells this himself, without naming a source, while talking with the Stanford scientist Garry Nolan, who studies such material. It would mean physical fragments from these events are reaching researchers through the mail.
jacques-vallee-s-control-system-beings-w: Some beings have been with humans for thousands of years and are in many ways controlling the Earth: that is the view Michels credits to Jacques Vallée, a computer scientist and longtime UFO researcher. Michels gives this as his own summary of what Vallée would say, not as a quote from him.
jacques-vallee-s-movie-project-shifted-t: A man named Bob Lazar says that in the 1990s people were planning a movie about a man named Jacques Vallée, but after hearing about Lazar and talking with him, they decided to make it about Lazar instead. Lazar, who tells it from his own side, says Vallée "was super pissed off" about it.
jacques-vallee-s-photo-of-a-ufo-over-a-l: A photograph is said to show a UFO over a lake, and every cow in the picture is turned toward it. The guest Joe McMoneagle tells this as a photo he links to the UFO researcher Jacques Vallée, stressing that "every cow in that picture was looking at the UFO." The point is that the animals seem to have noticed something real in the sky.
jacques-vallee-s-retrograde-orbiting-obj: On the night of July 11, 1961, the astronomer Jacques Vallée and his colleagues at the Paris Observatory are said to have seen "an unidentified object orbiting the Earth," one that went around the planet in the opposite direction from normal. Michels tells the story in an episode with the astronomer Beatriz Villarroel, and he quotes Vallée from a later interview: other observatories "had made exactly the same observation," American tracking stations "photographed the same thing and couldn't identify it either," it "was as bright as the star Sirius," and it "didn't reappear in successive weeks." If true, it would mean something unknown was circling Earth in the early space age.
jacques-vallee-shows-jesse-valis-as-his-: Michels says he first heard of VALIS, a novel, when he was visiting the UFO researcher Jacques Vallée at his apartment. He says Vallée showed it to him and said, "this is my favorite book." Michels tells this as his own memory, and it shows that a novel had a deep influence on one of the field's best-known thinkers.
jailbroken-chatgpt-dan-talks-about-alien: An unnamed researcher says that in 2023, when people tricked ChatGPT, the AI chatbot, into a rule-free mode nicknamed DAN, every copy of DAN began talking about aliens being real and about alien conspiracies, including hybrids. The researcher tells Michels this first-hand, as a hint that the AI might know or reveal something hidden.
jailbroken-openai-says-it-has-worked-wit: A version of an artificial intelligence system from OpenAI, the company behind ChatGPT, is said to have been "jailbroken", meaning tricked into ignoring its built-in rules, and then asked what OpenAI does not want people to know. According to Jesse Michels, who relays it from a researcher named Deep Prasad, the answer was that "we have been working hand in hand with aliens for the last 10 years", and in a second telling it added, "We've been in communication with them."
jaime-maussan-s-2023-presentation-of-the: In 2023 a man named Jaime Maussan presented what he called the "J type", one of several kinds of small bodies said to be not human. Michels tells this himself, without naming any other source. He adds that of all the body types put forward, this is not the one he is most convinced is real.
jaime-s-blue-ball-of-energy-during-medit: In the 1970s, while meditating in the lab of a researcher named Puharich, a man called Jaime is said to have seen "this big blue ball" appear, which he described as a ball of energy. The story comes from an unnamed researcher who was a guest on the show, passing on what Jaime and Puharich's assistant reported. It is told as a sign that the lab's work brought something unexplained into the room.
jake-barber-and-fred-baker-promise-to-sh: In 2025, two former special operations soldiers, Jake Barber and Fred Baker, said openly about their claims of secret UFO work, "don't trust us, we'll show you," promising to bring evidence. A guest named Marik von Rennenkampff relays this, calling Baker "truly a legend in the community." If they deliver, it would mean proof backing claims that the government recovers craft not made by people.
jake-barber-at-sites-where-et-craft-were: A helicopter pilot named Jake Barber is said to have been at sites where craft from beyond Earth were targeted and shot down. The UFO researcher Steven Greer says this, relaying what Barber told him, and links it to a briefing document of his own with a map of such sites around the world. Michels repeats Greer's account on another episode and adds that Barber was deeply troubled by the downing of the craft. If true, it would mean humans have been deliberately bringing down these craft.
jake-barber-describes-retrieving-an-egg-: A man named Jake Barber says he helped recover two unknown craft: one shaped like an egg, and one with eight sides, "not quite an octagon", that Michels calls "this black metallic thing." Michels says Barber first told the story through Michels himself and the journalist Ross Coulthart, and he comes back to it in several episodes, sometimes leaving out the eight-sided craft, once calling it octagonal, and once crediting the defense company Northrop Grumman. If true, it would mean people are recovering craft that were not made by humans.
jake-barber-in-the-gate-program-as-a-chi: As a boy, Jake Barber was placed in GATE, a school programme whose name stands for Gifted and Talented Education. Barber tells this himself, in an interview where he says he was taken into a UFO programme as a child. He brings it up as part of his account of how he was picked out early in life.
jake-barber-on-zero-point-energy-systems: In a 2025 interview with the journalist Ross Coulthart, Jake Barber, a man who says he flew in secret missions to recover crashed craft, said at the very end that he knew about zero-point energy systems, machines said to draw power from empty space. The researcher who goes by UAPGerb recalls this as a question to Michels, "didn't Jake Barber say" so. If true, it would mean such energy technology exists in secret.
jake-barber-psionic-crash-retrieval-team: A man named Jake Barber says he belonged to a team that recovered crashed craft with help from "psionic assets", people said to have psychic abilities who could mentally call such craft down. Jesse Michels first tells it from a story by the journalist Ross Coulthart on the US news channel NewsNation, describing "people psychically calling in exotic material." Later he adds Barber's term "P3s", people with a psionic predisposition who "act as the bridge". A researcher who goes by UAPGerb says Barber testified that these abilities can "forcefully land craft or bring them down." A witness named Michael Herrera adds that Barber's team was hired to pick up the downed vehicles and move them to a facility, which would mean the craft can be reached and recovered through the mind.
jake-barber-s-book-sentinels-of-ether-pa: A man named Jake Barber released the first chapter of his book Sentinels of Ether, about 20 pages long, and seven of those pages had been blacked out by subject matter experts before release. Michels tells this himself in two episodes; in the later one he says plainly that the Pentagon censored it and also mentions a person named Alva Douglas in connection with the book. He raises it because, if true, the government would be guarding whatever Barber was trying to say.
jake-barber-s-consciousness-contact-with: A man named Jake Barber is said to have made contact with his mind, a "consciousness contact", with an egg-shaped object he picked up. Steven Greer, an activist who has long pushed for the government to reveal what it knows about UFOs, passes this on as something Barber has said. If true, it would mean these objects can respond to human thought.
jake-barber-s-contractor-employers-north: Michels says that the lawyer Danny Sheehan accused a man named Jake Barber, who has made claims about secret UFO work, of having worked at Northrop, a large American defense company. Michels tells it himself in passing, without saying more. It matters because it bears on which private company Barber was really working for.
jake-barber-s-orbs-phasing-into-mountain: Glowing orbs and strange craft that were hard to pin down as physical things would fly over a test range in California and seem to pass right into the mountains, according to a man named Jake Barber. An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb brings this up second-hand, asking whether Barber hadn't described light orbs that would "almost phase into mountains". If true, the objects would be doing something no known aircraft can do.
jake-barber-s-psionic-assets-locking-ont: A man named Jake Barber is said to work with "psionic assets", people said to use mental or psychic ability, who lock onto unknown craft. Michels mentions it in passing, noting that Barber "is obviously a source" for the journalist Ross Coulthart. If true, it would mean the mind is being used as a tool to find these craft.
jake-barber-s-testimony-and-the-egg-2025: In 2025 a man named Jake Barber, who says he flew as a delivery man in a secret program that recovered crashed UFOs, came forward in an interview with the journalist Ross Coulthart and showed footage of an egg-shaped object. The hip-hop musician Flying Lotus gives his reaction to it on Jesse Michels's show: he felt Barber should have shown the egg and stopped there, because the second half of the story would "lose some people".
jake-barber-summoning-craft-by-telepathy: A man named Jake Barber, who comes from Lockheed, a large American aerospace and defence company, is said to have spoken of people using telepathy and clairvoyance, meaning mind-to-mind contact and seeing things at a distance, to call unknown craft to them. The philosopher Jason Jorjani mentions it in the 2020s as something Barber has revealed. Jorjani sees it as a sign that the mind may be the real link to these craft.
jake-barber-takes-michael-herrera-underg: Jake Barber, a man who says he has spoken out about secret UFO programmes, is said to have met another such whistleblower, Michael Herrera, at an event linked to someone named Greer, and then taken him underground at Edwards Air Force Base, a military test base in California, where he may have shown him some kind of UFO or craft. Michels tells this himself, relaying what he believes is Herrera's story, and hedges it with "I believe" and "possibly".
jake-barber-who-is-we-and-black-money: When Michels asked Jake Barber, a man who says he worked on secret recoveries of UFOs, what "we" have, Barber pushed back with "Who is we?" Michels says he guessed the US or the aerospace companies Barber might work for, and Barber answered, "No, we don't have shit." Michels recalls this himself from his own interview with Barber, calling it the most fascinating part, since it suggests the technology may not be in American hands at all.
jake-sullivan-in-at-least-one-uap-briefi: Jake Sullivan, a senior White House national security official, is said to have sat in on at least one briefing on UAP, the government's term for UFOs, in Washington. The analyst Matthew Pines passes on what the journalist Ross Coulthart says, that Coulthart "knows" Sullivan "was in at least one briefing." If so, the subject would have reached the top of the White House.
james-allen-death-with-heavy-metals: A filmmaker named James Allen, who made a documentary about a man named Mark McCandlish and his story of a craft called the Flux Liner, is said to have died suddenly of an aggressive cancer. A guest who goes by the online name UAPGerb (UAP being a newer official term for UFOs) says Allen was diagnosed and dead within about three weeks. Michels tells it too, adding that heavy metals were found at Allen's autopsy. The tellers raise it as a strange death around someone who was telling a UFO story.
james-bruce-brings-back-the-book-of-enoc: The story goes that the Book of Enoch, an ancient religious text left out of most Bibles, reached Europe because an explorer named James Bruce brought it back from Ethiopia. The writer Graham Hancock tells it from his own research, pointing to the English translation by R. H. Charles and to Bruce's own account, Travels to Discover the Source of the Nile. Hancock's point is simple: "let's not forget that James Bruce brought something back from Ethiopia he brought back the Book of Enoch." Michels tells it too, in an episode with a guest named Luke Caverns. In his version, Sir James Bruce was a Scottish Freemason, a member of a secretive brotherhood, who went to Ethiopia looking for the Ark of the Covenant, the chest the Bible says held the Ten Commandments, and came home with the Book of Enoch instead. Both tellers raise it because the book describes heavenly beings coming down to Earth, and it reached us by an odd and lucky route.
james-clapper-blocked-first-2008-attempt: According to a government report Michels calls the Historical Report volume one, an official named James Clapper blocked a first attempt made in 2008. Michels cites this himself while explaining how the Pentagon's UFO program came about, as a sign that senior officials pushed back from the start.
james-fox-s-2013-door-to-door-search-fin: In 2013 the filmmaker James Fox went to Varginha, Brazil, where a strange craft is said to have come down, and with a man named Marco Leal he knocked on "every single door of every house within a quarter or half a mile" of the crash site. Fox says, from his own search, that they found just one farm hand, who remembered hearing a loud boom, a rare local witness to the crash.
james-fox-s-attempt-to-get-the-vandenber: A film said to come from Vandenberg, an Air Force base in California, was offered to the documentary filmmaker James Fox for $25,000, after a woman named Angela Joiner told him about it, and Fox then tried to get it seen through Congress. The researcher Grant Cameron tells this second-hand, saying Fox contacted Allan Sandler, a filmmaker who worked with Bob Emenegger, who said, "it's 25,000 bucks to use in your documentary." If the film is what is claimed, it would be official footage of something unexplained.
james-fox-s-unreleased-corso-interview-1: James Fox, a documentary filmmaker who made an interview with Philip J. Corso that was never released, is said to believe that Corso, a man who made claims about secret UFO knowledge in the US government, was telling the truth. Michels passes on Fox's own words: "Gun to my head, I get shot if I'm wrong. I think Philip J. Corso was legit." If Fox is right, Corso's story would deserve to be taken seriously.
james-fox-smoking-gun-evidence-keeps-dis: Truly decisive UFO evidence, the smoking gun, keeps disappearing before it can be made public. Michels tells this from a conversation with a man named James Fox, whom he spent time with in Austin, Texas, and calls a great guy, as a reason the clearest proof never seems to reach the public.
james-lacatski-stepped-inside-a-craft: James Lacatski, a government scientist who ran a secret Pentagon UFO program, is said to have stated that the US has a craft not made by humans and that his team got inside it. The program was a Pentagon-funded study of advanced aerospace threats that ran from about 2007 to 2012. Lacatski first said this publicly to the filmmaker Jeremy Corbell and the journalist George Knapp on their podcast, Weaponized. Corbell recalls Lacatski being "allowed to tell us" that the government "has a UFO in its possession and has been able to access the inside of it," kept in an aerospace hangar. A clip of Lacatski answering "Yes" is shown on Michels' show. Jesse Michels repeats the claim several times and ties it to Lacatski's book Skinwalkers at the Pentagon. Some versions say Lacatski went in himself, others say his team did. Eric Davis, a physicist who worked with the program, says he heard it from Lacatski directly, and Matthew Brown, a former Pentagon official turned whistleblower, says he fully believes it. Grant Cameron, a UFO researcher, adds that the craft was empty inside and that the team told members of Congress, with Senator Harry Reid present, around 2011, in a secure room for classified briefings. If true, it would mean the government holds a real non-human craft.
james-mcdonald-at-the-australian-schooly: In 1966 a UFO reportedly landed near a schoolyard in Australia, and a scientist named James McDonald went there himself to interview the witnesses, telling them he was working on a presidential study. A UFO researcher named Grant Cameron says this, without naming a source. He tells it to suggest that UFO research at the time had backing from the very top of the US government.
james-mcdonald-s-critique-of-the-condon-: In the late 1960s the Condon Committee, a US Air Force-funded university study of UFOs, concluded they were not worth more study. The atmospheric physicist James McDonald wrote a sharp attack on it called Science in Default. A writer named Marik von Rennenkampff recommends it as "a remarkable critique" of the committee, and urges people to read everything McDonald wrote, because it would mean the official study was flawed.
james-mcdonald-s-sighting-at-savannah-ri: The physicist James McDonald is said to have seen a UFO himself at the Savannah River Site, a nuclear plant in South Carolina, and to have been pushed to the margins for taking the subject seriously. A former Pentagon official named Luis Elizondo passes this on with some hedging: he thinks McDonald was at Arizona State, and he thinks the sighting was at Savannah River. Michels tells it twice himself, without naming a source. Once he says McDonald was made a public mockery of after the sighting, and once he calls the site a plutonium reactor. A researcher who goes by RedPandaKoala puts the sighting in 1957. He says McDonald reported it to Project Blue Book, the US Air Force's UFO study of the 1950s and 60s, and thought at first that things were going well. It matters to the tellers because it would mean a respected scientist saw something at a nuclear facility and suffered for saying so.
james-mcdonnell-s-search-for-gremlins-in: An aviation figure tied to the aircraft maker McDonnell Douglas is said to have spent much of his research career hunting for "gremlins," his word for unexplained faults or presences in his planes. The story's title gives his name as James McDonnell, while Michels's citation gives it as James McDonald. Michels tells it himself, without naming a source, in an episode with the Navy fighter pilot Ryan Graves, describing it as a search for "ghosts in the machine."
james-randi-s-million-dollar-paranormal-: From 1964 until 2015, a man named James Randi ran a challenge offering money to anyone who could prove that something paranormal exists. It started with a $10,000 prize and grew into the well-known million-dollar challenge. A researcher named Chris Ramsay describes it from memory, without naming a source, saying Randi "had this show where at first he would give you 10 grand if you proved something paranormal would exist."
james-randi-s-spoon-and-watch-trick-in-f: A researcher named Clas Svahn, who keeps a very large archive of UFO material, says a man named James Randi once did a spoon and watch trick right in front of him. Svahn tells it as something he saw: "he bent his spoon in front of me," showing how such feats can be done as a trick.
jan-rooney-s-general-father-on-roswell-a: Jan Rooney, the wife of the actor Mickey Rooney, is said to have explained that her father was a general at Roswell, New Mexico, in 1947, the place and year of a reported crash of an unknown object. According to her, he told her that if the truth about Roswell came out it would have a "devastating impact on organized religion." The UFO investigator and filmmaker James Fox says she told him this directly.
janet-airlines-first-heard-of-through-la: The first public mention of "Janet Airlines", the nickname for unmarked passenger planes said to fly workers to secret test sites in Nevada, came from a man named Bob Lazar, who in 1989 claimed he had worked on alien craft there. That is how a UFO researcher who goes by the online name UAPGerb puts it to Michels. He asks where the name was first heard and answers his own question: "Bob Lazar." If so, Lazar knew details of the secret Nevada world that only insiders would know.
janet-flights-from-mccarran-to-area-51-1: Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft for the US government, describes how he got to work in 1988 and 1989: he drove to the offices of EG&G Special Projects, a defence contractor, located right at McCarran Airport in Las Vegas. From there, he says, unmarked flights known as Janet carried workers to Area 51, the secret Air Force test site in the Nevada desert. Lazar tells it himself to Michels as part of his account of his job.
jannini-asks-the-court-to-let-them-exhum: Some thirty years after the 1996 events in the Brazilian town of Varginha, where strange beings were reportedly captured, a doctor named Jannini is said to be asking a court for permission to dig up the body of a man named Chereze, who is linked to those events, to study bacteria in his remains. Ahmed Foratu, a witness to the Varginha story, relays this on Jesse Michels's show, saying Jannini is "requesting authorization from the court".
jannini-in-the-film-a-puncture-from-the-: In Varginha, Brazil, in 1996, a man named Marco Chereze died, and a pathologist called Dr. Janini says he thinks a puncture wound from the nail of an alien being caused that death. Michels repeats this from the documentary Moment of Contact by the filmmaker James Fox, where Janini "literally says" so on camera, as a sign that people came into physical contact with a living being.
jannini-s-signed-authenticated-statement: A doctor named Jannini, linked to the 1996 case in Varginha, Brazil, where a creature was said to have been captured, reportedly sent a signed, authenticated statement about the case. The surgeon Ahmed Foratu says he passed it on to Michels during their 2026 interview: 'He sent it and I've already left it with you signed.' It is offered as written backing for the story of a hospital treating an alien.
jannini-told-fox-on-camera-he-had-never-: A doctor named Janini, involved in the 1996 Varginha case in Brazil, said he had never seen a bacteria like the one in that infection, before or since. The documentary filmmaker James Fox says the doctor told him this on camera. In a later episode Fox recalls it as an advanced strain that behaved as no other had, and also credits a doctor named Cesario. It matters because it points to an infection unlike anything known.
january-whistle-event-gets-zero-results-: Skywatcher, a startup that says it tries to call in UFOs, says that a January 2025 session at its field site with all its equipment but without its "whistle" got zero results. According to the company, in February they added the whistle along with psionics, meaning mental or psychic techniques, and got their first sighting of an unidentified object with the naked eye. They tell it as their own experience, as a sign that the whistle and the mind make the difference.
japan-airlines-pilot-s-45-minute-encount: In 1986, over Alaska, a Japan Airlines pilot is said to have flown alongside an unknown craft for 45 minutes, and the radar record was then taken by the White House, according to Michels. He says that radar data is now public and that physicists have studied it. A researcher named Kevin Knuth tells it with more detail: he says it was a cargo flight, Japan Airlines flight 1628, flown by a Captain Kenju Teruchi, who saw a giant craft, though Knuth says nothing of the 45 minutes or the White House taking the radar.
japan-seeing-uap-over-the-last-five-year: Japan seems to have been seeing a lot of UAP, the government's term for UFOs, over roughly the past five years. Dylan Borland, a guest who says a top government official told him aliens run everything, says this to Michels as his own impression that Japan is "popping off" lately, not as a report of anything he saw there.
japan-sought-a-uap-information-sharing-a: Japan is said to have pressed the United States for a two-country agreement whose only purpose was sharing information on UAP, the government's term for UFOs. Luis Elizondo, a former Pentagon intelligence official who says he ran the military's UFO study, makes the claim, saying Japan "begged" for it. If true, it would show that allied governments take the subject seriously enough to seek formal deals over it.
japanese-hitodama-soul-orbs: In Japan there is an old idea of the hitodama, glowing balls of light that Michels describes as a kind of plasma orb, often taken to be souls. Michels raises it himself, linking it to the film The Boy and the Heron by the Japanese animator Hayao Miyazaki, in a talk about UFOs, psychics and the afterlife. He brings it up because such orbs echo lights reported in UFO accounts.
japanese-museum-curator-shown-ufo-footag: A Japanese museum curator named Takano Josen is said to have visited NASA's Johnson Space Center in Houston, where he was taken to a particular building and shown photos of UFOs. Michels passes this on as something the curator said. If true, it would mean NASA keeps UFO images it has not made public.
japanese-museum-s-claimed-piece-of-the-r: Michels says that a man in Japan named Takano Josen, who runs a museum there, claims to own a piece of the Roswell crash, the object said to have come down near Roswell, New Mexico, in 1947. Michels brings it up himself during a 2026 conversation with a Navy admiral, saying only "he's in Japan.
