joseph-mcmoneagle-awarded-the-legion-of-: Joseph McMoneagle, a man who worked as a "remote viewer" for the US government (someone said to describe faraway places and things using only the mind), is said to have won the Legion of Merit, a high US military award, for over 200 instances of this work. Michels says this himself, without naming a source, as evidence that the government took such abilities seriously.
joseph-mcmoneagle-given-legion-of-merit-: A soldier named Joseph McMoneagle is said to have received the Legion of Merit, a US military medal for exceptional service, for his work in remote viewing. Remote viewing is the practice of trying to describe distant places or hidden things using only the mind. Michels tells this himself on three different episodes and notes that McMoneagle was once his guest. In those episodes he calls McMoneagle "remote viewer number one" and "one of the best remote viewers," and in one of them he places the work between the 1970s and the 1990s. He tells it as a sign that the US Army took the practice seriously enough to honour it.
joseph-mcmoneagle-s-remote-viewing-of-so: A man named Joe McMoneagle used "remote viewing", the claimed ability to see far-off places with the mind alone, to find Soviet nuclear bases and foresee key events, according to Jesse Michels. Michels adds that McMoneagle even helped find James Dozier, an American general kidnapped in Italy. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, as a sign that this kind of mind-sight worked well enough for real intelligence jobs.
joseph-of-arimathea-brings-the-grail-to-: According to legend, Joseph of Arimathea, the follower of Jesus said to have carried the Holy Grail, came to Glastonbury in England and met a pagan chieftain called Arviragus. Arviragus granted him 120 hides of land (a hide being an old measure of farmland) as a sacred precinct, where Joseph built the first Christian church. The researcher Randall Carlson retells this as a legend, without naming a source, as part of his account of Glastonbury as a sacred site.
joseph-of-copertino-levitating-during-ma: Joseph of Copertino was a Franciscan friar in 17th century Italy who had ecstatic visions from childhood, and many people saw him float off the ground while taking part in Mass. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, as an example of a strange event recorded in religious history.
joseph-of-copertino-s-levitation-records: There are written records of Joseph of Copertino, an Italian saint said to have risen into the air, and the religion scholar Diana Pasulka says she has them and has been reading them. She calls them "pretty intense," bringing them up while talking about how much data she has looked at, with a mention of Hal Puthoff, a physicist who has studied the paranormal. If the records hold, they would be an old, written account of a man seen floating.
joseph-smith-possibly-killed-by-governme: Joseph Smith, the founder of the Mormon church, "actually may have been assassinated by agents of the government," according to the national security analyst Matthew Pines. He tells Michels this in connection with the 1840s and Deseret, the name the early Mormons gave to the state they hoped to found in what is now Utah. He offers no named source, and the claim would mean the government saw Smith's movement as a threat worth killing over.
josiah-describes-author-max-davis-s-popp: A boy named Josiah is said to have described the house of an author, Max Davis, with its popping noises, and a barn nearby, without being told about them. His mother tells it as someone who was there, and she recalls Josiah asking: "are you a barn man Max, like there's animals or there's a farm by you". She tells it on an episode about the Telepathy Tapes, a documentary on children said to read minds, as a sign that her son picked up details he had no ordinary way to know.
josiah-knows-about-max-s-mixtape-and-pri: A nonspeaking boy named Josiah, one of the children in The Telepathy Tapes, a documentary about children said to read minds, is said to have known private things about a man named Max Davis. According to the documentary maker Ky Dickens, Josiah wrote "your music is being banded together", which she ties to a mixtape Davis was making, and "you love your sacred time at the motel", which she ties to a private beach motel he loves on the Gulf of Mexico coast. If true, it would mean the boy picked up things he had no ordinary way to know.
josiah-knows-about-max-s-nap-and-the-fir: A boy named Josiah, one of the children said in the documentary The Telepathy Tapes to read minds, knew things about a writer named Max Davis that he had no ordinary way of knowing: the day after Davis took a nap, Josiah wrote to him "I hope your nap was nice", and he also knew about a chapter of Davis's called "First Fruits". The filmmaker Ky Dickens tells this, passing on what was told to her. If true, it would point to a child picking up someone's thoughts or doings from a distance.
josiah-knows-max-went-into-the-woods-to-: A boy named Josiah, who is among the non-speaking children featured in a documentary about telepathy, is said to have known, without being told, that a man named Max Davis had gone into the woods to pray the night before. The documentary maker Ky Dickens, who made the series The Telepathy Tapes, relays it as an example of these children seeming to read other people's minds.
josiah-says-auntie-told-an-angel-to-tell: A boy named Josiah says his late great-aunt, whom he calls Auntie and who died at 89, told an angel to pass a message on to him. His mother tells it as something she saw unfold herself, repeating his own words: "Auntie told an angel to tell me." She tells it on an episode about children said to read minds, because if true it would mean a child getting word from a dead relative.
journalist-threatened-with-arrest-at-the: In 1996, a journalist looking into the Varginha case, a Brazilian story of a creature said to have been captured by the army, says he was threatened with arrest while reporting at an army sergeants' school in the town of Três Corações. The journalist, who is not named, tells it first-hand and says that he had never been arrested for doing his job, "neither before nor after this case." He tells it because a threat like that would suggest the army had something about the case it wanted kept quiet.
journalists-on-cia-payroll-operation-moc: In the 1960s many American journalists were secretly paid by the CIA, the US spy agency, in what is known as Operation Mockingbird, and their names and what they were paid are now known. A man named Jeremy Corbell tells Michels this as something he has heard. He brings it up to show that the press could be shaped by the agency.
jp-cahn-s-10-000-offer-to-scully-1950: In San Francisco in 1950, a journalist named JP Cahn is said to have offered the writer Frank Scully $10,000 for the rights to his story of crashed flying saucers, and Scully turned him down. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, in an episode about claims that alien bodies were recovered from a crash.
jp-morgan-funds-tesla-s-wardenclyffe-wir: The inventor Nikola Tesla is said to have got money from the banker J.P. Morgan for experiments at Wardenclyffe, his research site in New York, on sending power through the air without wires. Michels tells this himself in two episodes without naming a source. In one he calls it wireless energy transmission, and in the other "wireless instantaneous transmission". He tells it as an example of Tesla's work that he believes was ahead of its time and may still be hidden.
jpl-counter-clerk-hands-over-negatives-o: Sometime in the 1980s, a counter clerk at the Jet Propulsion Laboratory, a space research laboratory in California, handed over photographic negatives from the mapping of Mars and said, "oh this is the old city on Mars." Joe McMoneagle, who says he was the one standing at that counter, tells it to Michels. If it happened as he says, it would mean that staff at the lab casually treated a city on Mars as known.
jpl-manager-life-on-mars-means-death-for: Managers at the Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Pasadena, the NASA lab that builds and flies space probes, were once talking about finding life on Mars, and one of them scolded the rest: "Don't you realize that life on Mars means death for JPL?" Michels passes this on as something the writer Whitley Strieber told. The point of the story is that the lab itself might have a reason not to find life there.
jpl-viking-mission-lead-believed-there-w: The man in charge of the Viking missions, NASA's 1970s landers sent to Mars, firmly believes there was evidence of life on Mars, Jesse Michels says. The man worked at JPL, NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory, which builds and runs its robot space probes. Michels says only that he has "heard" this, without naming the man or a source. If true, a scientist who led the search would believe it found life on another world.
jsoc-crash-retrievals-and-knights-of-mal: A modern head of the Joint Special Operations Command, the US military command over its most elite special forces units, General Stanley McChrystal, is said to belong to the Knights of Malta, an old Catholic order of knights, and so are many of the command's own members. Michels raises this in an episode with a former presidential advisor, crediting the investigative journalist Seymour Hersh. It matters to him because this same command comes up in talk of secret recoveries of crashed craft, and the claim would tie that work to a private religious order.
jude-quotes-the-book-of-enoch: The Letter of Jude, a short book of the Bible's New Testament, takes words word for word from the Book of Enoch, an ancient Jewish text left out of most Bibles. Tim Alberino, a filmmaker and researcher, says this on the show in his own summary. It matters because it would show that early Christians treated Enoch as scripture.
julian-jaynes-bicameral-mind-theory-a-sh: A Yale professor named Julian Jaynes argued that human consciousness changed after about 1000 BC, moving away from what he called a "bicameral," or two-chambered, mind. Michels brings it up himself with a guest, naming Jaynes's book The Origin of Consciousness in the Breakdown of the Bicameral Mind, as a way to think about how ancient people may have experienced the world differently.
julius-evola-stayed-with-the-ss-to-the-e: According to the writer Peter Levenda, a man named Julius Evola stayed with the SS, Nazi Germany's elite force, until the end of the Second World War. Levenda says the SS gave Evola access to its libraries and let him use them. Levenda tells this to Michels without naming a source, as a sign of how close Evola was to the Nazi inner circle.
junior-hicks-files-on-uinta-basin-ufo-si: A local man named Junior Hicks kept detailed files on hundreds of UFO sightings in Utah's Uinta Basin, going back to 1950. Brandon Fugal, the owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a property in that basin known for strange reports, passes this on, along with the names of Thomas Winterton, a witness, and Jim Morse, and a book called The Utah UFO Display. He tells it to show that the area's strange activity goes back decades.
kabbalists-meet-the-dalai-lama: When the Dalai Lama, the spiritual leader of Tibetan Buddhism, met a group of Kabbalists, Jewish mystics, the two sides are said to have found a lot in common. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, and he tells it two different ways. Once he says the Dalai Lama was surprised that Kabbalist meditation and prayer looked strikingly like Buddhist meditation. Another time he says they talked about non-human intelligences and the colors linked to them, which would mean two old traditions describe the same unseen beings.
kafka-s-trial-as-a-description-of-a-spec: The philosopher Jason Jorjani reads The Trial, a novel by the Prague writer Franz Kafka about a man caught in a court he cannot see, as a picture of a ghostly bureaucracy of angels that governs human lives. He says he set this out in an essay in his own collection Lovers of Sophia, drawing also on Kafka's private writings known as the Blue Octavo Notebooks. He offers it as his own interpretation, without citing anyone else.
kafsokalyvia-skete-maximus-the-flying-mo: Kafsokalyvia is a skete, a small monks' settlement, on Mount Athos in Greece, and it is named for a saint remembered as Maximus, a "flying monk" who burned his huts, worked miracles and was seen flying. A visitor named Ralph Larson tells this from what a young monk who looked after the skete told him during his trip there in 2005. It is told as local lore of a holy man who could fly.
kaikoura-ufo-incident-1978: In 1978 there was "a really big UFO incident" at Kaikoura, a place on the east coast of New Zealand's South Island. The researcher Ross Coulthart brings it up from memory, without naming a source. He says it happened when he was 16 and treats it as a major case from his youth.
kakino-stone-circle-with-magnetic-anomal: At Kakino in Japan, a stone circle on a steep hillside is said to show the same magnetic oddities caused by lightning that are found at other ancient sites. Geoffrey Drumm, a researcher who says he has seen these sites, tells it without naming a source. He brings it up as a sign that ancient builders chose or used places where lightning left a mark on the rock.
kalmykian-president-s-debrief-with-kissi: The president of Kalmykia, a small republic inside Russia, says he once sat down with two famous statesmen to talk about his own encounter with aliens. They were Henry Kissinger, the former US Secretary of State, and Mikhail Gorbachev, the last leader of the Soviet Union. The president, named Kiran Ilum Xenov, tells this himself. He sets it in the late 1990s, in a sauna at his home in Moscow. He says Kissinger suddenly asked him, "Well, how was it?" Gorbachev, sitting beside Kissinger, then said, "Come on, Henry, tell him. You should tell him everything." From their talk, Xenov says, he understood that Kissinger was "very familiar with the materials" on UFOs held by the US President's office, the CIA or NASA. Michels also tells the story, passing on what the president told him: that he met Gorbachev and Kissinger and was asked how it had been. If true, it would mean that men at the very top of both superpowers knew about such encounters.
kammler-black-world-program-in-nazi-germ: Nazi Germany is said to have run a secret advanced weapons effort under Hans Kammler, a general in the SS, the Nazi party's elite force. Michels passes on "rumors" that Kammler's people were doing "black world nuclear stuff," meaning hidden, off-the-books nuclear work. The researcher Nick Cook describes it as "a special projects office run by SS General Hans Kammler," called the Kammlerstab, active from 1942 to 1945 in Czechoslovakia and Poland, and he does not stress nuclear work. In a later episode Michels also calls it the Kammler Stab and talks about scientists there working on new kinds of propulsion. If true, it would mean the Nazis had a hidden technology program bigger than the known record shows.
kammler-negotiating-with-the-western-all: Hans Kammler, the SS general who ran Nazi Germany's secret weapons projects, is said to have been negotiating with the Western Allies before the end of the war in 1945. The aviation journalist Nick Cook tells Michels there was "quite a bit of evidence" for this, without naming it. If true, Kammler may have traded Germany's most advanced technology to the Americans or British in exchange for his own escape.
kammler-s-flying-saucer-work-and-die-glo: At a site in what was then Czechoslovakia, now part of Poland, the Nazi official Hans Kammler was rumoured to be building flying saucers. Michels calls Kammler the most ruthless Nazi, the man running the most secret technology projects, and names the site as "Commto". The story is tied to Die Glocke, German for "the Bell", a secret Nazi device people talk about. Michels tells it himself as a rumour, without naming a source.
kammlerstab-nazi-tech-transfer-to-wright: During the Second World War there was a secret weapons facility in Czechoslovakia, which Michels places in modern-day Poland, run by an SS officer named Hans Kammler, and its technology is said to have passed afterward to Wright Field, the US Army Air Forces research base in Ohio. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, in an episode asking whether the physicist Robert Oppenheimer worked on UFOs. If true, it would mean early American work on strange craft drew on captured Nazi research.
kansas-k9-trooper-drone-swarm-2019: Around 2019 or 2020, a police dog handler with the Kansas state troopers is said to have had a group of drones fly right over his head. Marik von Rennenkampff, a writer on national security, brings up the case, credited to someone named Doug Johnson, during a debate with a UFO skeptic. He uses it as an example of unexplained objects seen by trained officials.
kant-suppressed-swedenborg-s-disturbing-: The philosopher Jason Jorjani says that the German philosopher Immanuel Kant, who lived in Königsberg, Prussia, deliberately pushed aside the writings of Emanuel Swedenborg, a mystic who wrote about the spirit world in books such as Arcana Coelestia (Secrets of Heaven). According to Jorjani, Kant admitted he did this because Swedenborg's material was "so disturbing that it would destabilize society, including on a political level". Jorjani gives this as his own summary without naming a source, though he links it to Kant's book Groundwork of the Metaphysics of Morals and to his own book Prometheus and Atlas.
kardashev-scale-1964: In 1964 a Russian astronomer named Nikolai Kardashev proposed a way to rank civilizations by how much energy they can use, up to tapping the power of an entire star. A guest named Karl Nell explains this, without naming a source, saying it came at a time when optical and radio astronomy were opening new ways to look for other civilizations.
karen-an-experiencer-who-threw-lamps-at-: A woman named Karen, one of the people who said they had been visited by non-human beings, used to fight back by throwing things at them, even lamps. The lawyer Dan Sheehan tells this from his time around John Mack, a Harvard psychiatrist who studied people reporting alien abductions, as a sign that not everyone took these encounters quietly.
karen-gallaudet-s-remote-viewing-trainin: Karen Gallaudet, the wife of a retired Navy admiral named Tim Gallaudet, has been trained in remote viewing, the practice of trying to describe distant places or hidden things using only the mind, by a teacher named Paul Smith. Tim Gallaudet says she took one basic course and then finished the advanced course, traveling to Smith's place in Cedar City, Utah for it, sometime in the last couple of years. He tells it as something close to home that shows his family takes the practice seriously.
karen-silkwood-and-the-missing-plutonium: In 1974, according to Dan Sheehan, a worker at a nuclear fuel plant in Oklahoma named Karen Silkwood discovered that 40 pounds of 98 percent bomb-grade plutonium was missing from the facility. Sheehan tells it as someone who was involved in the matter himself, and he ties it to a CIA officer named Theodore Shackley and a reporter named David Burnham. If true, it would mean that enough material for nuclear weapons had quietly gone missing.
karl-compton-recruits-teenage-malmgren-t: Harold Malmgren, who later advised American presidents, says that around 1950, as a teenager, he was brought to a mansion near Cambridge, Massachusetts to meet the physicist Karl Compton of MIT, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. He says that after two hours Compton told his father, "I want to take this boy out of your school," and have him enroll at MIT that September. Malmgren tells it as his own experience, explaining how he was picked out young for elite science circles.
karl-maria-wiligut-himmler-s-ss-seer-of-: In 1930s Nazi Germany, a man named Karl Maria Wiligut claimed he had a photographic memory of the distant past "when there were only Nordics on the planet," and he became a source of ideas for Heinrich Himmler, head of the SS, the Nazi party's elite guard. The researcher Peter Levenda tells this without naming a source. If true, it would mean Nazi beliefs about race came in part from one man's claimed memories of a lost age.
karl-nell-on-a-reverse-engineering-arms-: The United States is said to be in a secret race with Russia and China to take apart and copy captured UFOs, a process called reverse engineering. The claim comes from Karl Nell, who helped found Army Futures Command, the US Army's modernisation headquarters, in remarks published by The Debrief, an online news site. Michels repeats it several times, calling Nell his friend and saying that if Nell is right, the race is going on right now. In one telling Michels calls it a sub rosa, or hidden, conflict that has been going on for decades, and he mentions it alongside David Grusch, a former intelligence officer who has said the government holds such craft. An online researcher who goes by the name UAPGerb also cites Nell, though without the race. In his version Nell says the US actively has craft and is working out how to run their systems. All tellers are passing on what Nell said, not anything they saw. If true, it would mean these craft are real and that rival nations are fighting quietly to master them.
karl-nell-s-revised-kardashev-scale-2023: An Army officer named Karl Nell has proposed his own version of the Kardashev scale, a way of ranking civilizations by how much energy they can harness. Michels brings this up himself in passing. He describes Nell as someone who helped set up Army Futures Command, the Army's command for modernizing its forces, and who served on the UAP task force, a Pentagon group that studied unidentified anomalous phenomena, the official term for UFOs. He adds that Nell publicly defended a man named David Grusch "as soon as he came out" with his claims, but he does not say what Nell's revised scale actually contains.
karl-nell-says-disclosure-is-dead-2017: Karl Nell, a retired Army colonel who has spoken in favor of the government revealing what it knows about UFOs, recently went on a podcast and said "disclosure is dead." Michels passes this on himself, as something Nell said in public. It matters because it would mean one of the push's own backers no longer expects the government to reveal what it knows.
karl-wolfe-run-over-before-disclosure-wa: Just as the wave of so-called disclosure, the public release of government UFO information, began in 2017 and 2018, a man named Karl Wolfe was run over by a vehicle, the same way the researcher John Mack had been. The researcher Jason Jorjani makes this link, suggesting that people tied to the subject die in suspiciously similar ways.
karl-wolfe-sees-photos-of-a-lunar-megali: In the 1960s, a technician named Karl Wolfe is said to have been shown photographs of a huge city of giant stone structures on the far side of the Moon. The philosopher Jason Jorjani tells it, relaying Wolfe's own account: while repairing a machine at a facility of the NSA, the US electronic spying agency, Wolfe was shown mosaic photographs, pieced together from Moon-mapping missions, showing "a huge megalithic city on the dark side of the moon." Jorjani adds that Ingo Swann, known for remote viewing, the claimed ability to see distant places with the mind, confirmed it. John Blitch, a scientist who worked for DARPA, the Pentagon's research agency, tells it too, also from Wolfe. In his version it happened at Langley, a Virginia base, and they were described as "huge structures" rather than a city. If true, it would mean someone built on the Moon before us and the government kept the pictures quiet.
karla-turner-allegedly-killed-by-a-cia-c: A woman named Karla Turner, who died in the 1990s at age 48, officially of cancer, was really killed, possibly by a weapon of the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency, that makes a death look like cancer. A researcher named Jason Jorjani says he believes this, without naming a source, saying she "supposedly died of cancer at the age of 48." If true, it would mean someone was silenced on purpose.
karla-turner-and-her-family-as-alien-and: The researcher and author Karla Turner, who wrote the books Taken and Into the Fringe, was herself an abductee, and so was her family, taken both by aliens and, it is said, in military abductions, known as MILABs, in which humans in uniform seize abductees. The filmmaker Tim Alberino tells this, setting her beside other abduction researchers such as Budd Hopkins and the hypnotherapist Barbara Bartholic, and says that being an abductee herself is what made Turner unique.
karla-turner-s-abductees-describe-a-cont: People who said they had been abducted by aliens told the writer Karla Turner in the 1990s that humans live inside a control system run from a metallic sphere just beyond the Earth, which the story takes to be the Moon. The researcher Jason Jorjani repeats this from Turner's work, linking it to the writer Robert Monroe and his book Far Journeys. If true, something off-world would be steering human life.
karla-turner-s-husband-abducted-by-the-m: The husband of Karla Turner, a writer who researched alien abductions, was "abducted by elements of the military," according to the filmmaker Tim Alberino. He tells Michels this in passing, without saying where he learned it. If true, it would mean some abductions blamed on aliens involve human soldiers.
karst-cave-and-tunnel-system-venting-hyd: A scientific paper is said to show that a karst system under the Giza Plateau in Egypt, home of the great pyramids, is the source of hydrogen sulfide gas rising from the ground. Karst means a network of caves and tunnels worn into limestone. A researcher, named Jeffrey Drum in one episode and Geoffrey Drumm in another, describes the paper on an episode about an energy grid he believes lies beneath the pyramids. In the later episode he reads out its full title: "The development of sulfuric acid speleogenetic deposits within cavernous Middle Eocene beds and inference on hydrocarbon gas seepages, Giza Pyramids Plateau, Egypt." That title speaks of seeping hydrocarbon gas, and the first telling speaks of hydrogen sulfide. He tells it because underground gas and tunnels would fit his idea that the pyramids were built to use something coming up from below.
kary-mullis-saw-an-alien: Kary Mullis, the scientist who invented PCR, a lab method for copying DNA that won him a Nobel Prize, is said to have had an encounter with an alien, waking up in a shed and speaking with some kind of being. Jesse Michels brings this up himself on more than one episode, once simply saying Mullis saw an alien and once calling it an abduction, while admitting he does not remember the exact details. He tells it to show that even a celebrated scientist reported such an experience.
kecksburg-craft-was-bell-shaped-1965: In 1965 something is said to have crashed near Kecksburg, a small town in Pennsylvania. Jesse Michels says a recent film got it wrong by showing a flying saucer, because the object was really shaped like a bell or an acorn. Michels makes the point himself, without naming a source, to set the record of the crash straight as he understands it.
kecksburg-crash-and-eric-walker-connecti: Eric Walker, a former president of Penn State University, is said to have been present at the 1965 crash of an unknown object at Kecksburg, a small town in Pennsylvania. Jesse Michels returns to this link several times. He says Walker was "supposedly" there. He also says the people at the site reported that a civilian was in charge, and that this civilian was likely Walker, who he calls an alleged member of Majestic 12, a rumoured secret committee said to govern the UFO matter. A researcher who goes by the online name UAPGerb says Walker made the claim himself, in meetings with the researchers William Steinman and Henry Azadehdel. The researcher Grant Cameron says he was part of it. He says he had someone call Walker back to ask whether he had been at Kecksburg, and Walker answered, "I was there. So what?" If true, it would place a senior university figure with possible ties to a secret UFO group at a crash site.
kecksburg-crash-witnesses-saw-people-in-: When something is said to have crashed near Kecksburg, Pennsylvania, in 1965, every witness at the scene reportedly saw people in what they called "moon suits." A researcher who goes by the name UAPGerb brings this up without naming a source. He uses it to suggest that a trained crew in protective gear was sent to recover whatever had come down.
kecksburg-object-1965: In 1965, "something very bizarre came down" at Kecksburg, a town in Pennsylvania. The researcher Richard Dolan says he does not think it was a Soviet satellite, and he names no source in the telling. If he is right, the object that fell there was something stranger than any known spacecraft.
keeping-the-beings-out-of-the-official-r: In 1977 at Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota, a nuclear weapons guard named Mario Woods says he saw beings during an encounter he describes as an abduction, but he kept them out of his official report. He says that if he had reported the beings, he would have been removed right away from the Personnel Reliability Program, the screening that clears people to work around nuclear weapons. So in his account, the official record leaves out what he says he saw.
kelly-johnson-s-ufo-sighting: Kelly Johnson, an aircraft engineer who led Skunk Works, the secret aircraft design shop of the company Lockheed, is said to have watched a strange black object in the sky. Michels reads from an account that says that at about 5 p.m. Johnson was looking out a large west-facing window at the sunset when "he watched this black thing." A commentator named Marik von Rennenkampff, calling Johnson the best-known aeronautical engineer in American history, says Johnson saw the object from his ranch in Southern California near the Channel Islands, that a Lockheed crew saw it too, and that it was elliptical. They tell it because a witness of Johnson's standing is hard to wave away.
ken-farley-s-description-of-the-craft-s-: Ken Farley, a witness to a craft said to have come down in 1948 in Hart Canyon near Aztec, New Mexico, could still describe it in perfect detail years later, and at the end he added that "three brass or copper or gold lines" ran all the way around its center section. Scott Ramsey, a researcher who has spent years investigating the Aztec case, tells Michels this as what Farley said, and he also names a man called Doug Noland in connection with the account. It is one of several witness memories Ramsey offers as signs that a real craft lay in that canyon.
ken-farley-struck-with-a-rifle-butt-1948: In 1948, after a flying saucer is said to have come down in Hart Canyon near Aztec, New Mexico, a local man named Ken Farley was hit in the gut with the butt of a gun for the way he was talking about it. Scott Ramsey, a researcher who has spent years on the Aztec crash, relays this as something he heard about Farley. If true, it would mean people at the scene were forced to keep quiet.
ken-johnston-told-to-destroy-anomalous-a: A NASA worker named Ken Johnston Sr. was told to destroy a batch of early photo negatives from the Apollo moon missions because they showed things "not supposed to be there", and he quietly saved some of them. The physicist Maaneli Derakhshani passes this on from what Johnston said, adding that NASA did not want the images released. If true, it would mean the space agency hid strange things in its own moon photos.
ken-shoulders-ceramic-puncture-experimen: The engineer Ken Shoulders once ran an experiment where electrical pulses fired into a piece of ceramic did not break it but punched tiny holes through it, something ordinary electricity should not do. A guest named Dave Rossi describes it from memory, without a source, and asks to be corrected if he has it wrong. He brings it up as a hint of strange physics that might help explain how UFOs work.
kennedy-delegation-tours-western-nuclear: After the Cuban missile crisis of 1962, President John F. Kennedy led a group on a tour of Los Alamos and other nuclear sites in the western United States. A former Senate staffer named Kurt McConnell tells Michels this, crediting the researcher Jeff Cruickshank, who listed who went: Kennedy and Vice President Lyndon B. Johnson, along with names such as the national security adviser McGeorge Bundy and the Air Force general Curtis LeMay. McConnell raises it because a trip of such senior people to these sites suggests they were being shown something important.
kennedy-proposes-a-joint-soviet-us-space: In 1963 President John F. Kennedy is said to have proposed to the Soviet leader Nikita Khrushchev that the United States and the Soviet Union run a joint space program. A researcher named Dan Sheehan tells this without naming a source, at first slipping and saying Gorbachev before correcting himself, as part of his case that Kennedy was moving toward openness on things others wanted kept secret.
kennedy-s-orange-bowl-promise-to-cuban-e: In 1962 President John F. Kennedy went to the Orange Bowl stadium in Miami and held a large gathering where he made a promise to Cuban exiles, people who had fled Cuba. The researcher Dan Sheehan tells this without naming a source and does not spell out the promise in his words. He brings it up as part of a story about what Kennedy knew and promised in his last years.
kennedy-s-silver-certificates-on-june-5-: President John F. Kennedy is said to have done something odd in June 1963: ordering the printing of silver certificates, a kind of paper money backed by silver. The lawyer Dan Sheehan brings it up, mentioning the film director Oliver Stone, and admits he has never quite figured out why Kennedy did it, telling it among other hints that Kennedy was acting on secrets in his last months.
kenneth-arnold-s-1947-craft-matched-hort: The objects that the pilot Kenneth Arnold reported seeing in the sky in 1947, a sighting that started the modern UFO era, had the same design as the flying-wing aircraft built by the Horten brothers, two German designers of the Nazi era. The writer Peter Levenda tells Michels this, saying it was "the same design without him knowing at the time." If so, what Arnold saw may have been a craft built from German wartime designs.
kenneth-arnold-s-paranormal-experiences-: Kenneth Arnold, the pilot whose 1947 sighting of strange flying objects over the United States started the modern UFO era, is said to have had mysterious paranormal experiences after that first sighting. The parapsychologist Jeffrey Mishlove says this, believing that Arnold's daughter has written a book about it. If so, the first famous UFO witness also met the strange events that later witnesses often report.
kenneth-arnold-sighting-1947: In 1947 a pilot named Kenneth Arnold reported a group of strange craft racing through the sky in the Pacific Northwest, and his sighting is said to have started the modern UFO era. A former US intelligence officer named David Grusch says Arnold was searching for a downed cargo plane near Mount Rainier, two months before the reported crash at Roswell, New Mexico. A physicist named John Brandenburg adds that soon afterward such craft were being seen all over the country. The author Peter Levenda instead places the flight in the Rockies and stresses the craft's impossible speeds. A man named Chris Bledsoe, who says he attracts UFOs, describes about half a dozen chevrons moving freely and links them to the phrase "flying saucers"; Jesse Michels says the objects were really crescents and that the word "saucer" came from Arnold's description.
kent-selin-sees-flux-liner-over-edwards-: A man named Kent Selin is said to have seen a craft called the flux liner, described as a human-built flying saucer, over Edwards Air Force Base in California in the 1970s. The researcher who goes by UAPGerb tells this second-hand, through the aerospace illustrator Mark McCandlish, who talked to Selin, and it would mean such a craft was flying in the open decades ago.
kentucky-farm-case-behind-night-skies-an: A case from a Kentucky farm, where a family is said to have found an alien and hidden it in their barn, was the starting point for a film called Night Skies, which the director Steven Spielberg was developing as a producer. As the story is filed, that project is linked to his later alien film E.T. An unnamed guest tells this in the same words on two of Michels's episodes about Hollywood and UFOs, and doesn't say where he heard it.
kevin-day-radar-objects-at-28-000-ft-mat: During a 2004 Navy encounter with unknown objects off Southern California, a man named Kevin Day reported that the objects were at 28,000 feet, and according to the story, the data backs up that height. A guest named Marik von Rennenkampff repeats Day's account on an episode about challenging the skeptic Mick West to a debate: "Kevin Day said that these objects were at 28,000 ft." He also mentions a man named Chad Underwood, who filmed the event with an infrared camera. Matching the reported height in the data would mean the objects were real things high in the sky, not tricks of the camera.
keyhoe-air-force-tracked-two-unknown-sat: In 1953, before any country had launched a satellite, the US Air Force was tracking two unknown artificial satellites circling the Earth 400 and 600 miles up. Michels repeats this from the UFO writer Donald Keyhoe, calling it astonishing, because it would mean something man-made but not human was in orbit years before Sputnik.
kgb-department-researching-unknown-flyin: In Soviet times, a special department inside the KGB, the Soviet secret police and spy service, studied unknown objects, both ones that flew and ones under water. Kiran Ilum Xenov, a former president of a Russian republic who says aliens took him in 1997, relays this from what was shown to the country's leader, and he links it to Mikhail Gorbachev, the last Soviet leader. If true, it would mean the Soviet state had its own secret UFO study.
khafre-research-project-proposal-to-the-: A team led by Filippo Biondi, a scientist who used radar from satellites to scan beneath the pyramids of Giza in Egypt, is preparing a proposal to the Egyptian government for the Khafre Research Project, a study of the second great pyramid at Giza, together with the University of Ferrara in Italy and collaborators Armando Mei and Corrado Malanga. Biondi describes it himself across two appearances, first hoping the project can be "at the center" of the work, and later saying the plan is to clear shafts filled with debris using robots and to submit the proposal "these weeks." If it went ahead, it would let researchers check in person what the scans seem to show under the pyramid.
khafre-research-project-used-a-low-incid: Scanning the Khafre pyramid at Giza in Egypt from satellite radar, the team aimed their beams at a low angle, according to the radar researcher Filippo Biondi, who worked on the project in the 2020s. He says, "For the Khafre research project, we used a low incidence angle." He explains it as part of how they say they found tube-like structures deep beneath the pyramid, which would mean far more lies underground than anyone knew.
khafre-substructure-tubes-about-20-m-wid: Beneath the pyramid of Khafre, the second great pyramid at Giza in Egypt, there are said to be "huge tubes descending approximately for more than 1 km having a diameter of approximately 20 m." Filippo Biondi, a researcher who reads radar scans of the ground, says this from his own 2025 work on the site. If true, it would mean a vast built structure lies deep under the pyramid.
khufu-cartouche-allegedly-painted-by-vys: The name of the pharaoh Khufu, painted inside the Great Pyramid of Giza in Egypt in a cartouche (an oval frame around a royal name), may have been painted there in the 1830s by Howard Vyse, the explorer who said he found it. Jay Anderson, a guest who calls himself a witness on other matters, tells this without naming a source and cannot quite remember the name ("Voss or Vas something"). He says the explorer was working for the British Museum, was running out of money and time, and then "suddenly finds the signatures of Kufu written in very suspicious ochre." If true, the main evidence that the pyramid belongs to Khufu would be in doubt.
khufu-project-scan-shows-a-network-of-tu: The scientist Filippo Biondi says his scans beneath a pyramid at Giza, Egypt, show a network of tunnels deep underground. He hopes that one day someone could go down a shaft and reach one of the horizontal tunnels, which would mean an unknown structure lies under the monuments. In a later episode he talks about a new scan of Khufu, the Great Pyramid, and stresses that it was not meant to repeat his team's 2020 work but to see what lies deep below it.
killeen-base-emergency-meeting-1949: In 1949, after several sightings over Killeen Base at Camp Hood in Texas, which Michels says held America's largest store of nuclear weapons at the time, an emergency meeting about UFOs and nukes was reportedly held there. Michels tells it himself, citing Air Force documents from 1949 and the writer Robert Hastings, author of the book UFOs and Nukes. He says the Army's counter-intelligence corps, the FBI, the Office of Naval Intelligence and the CIA were all present, though in one telling he is unsure of the year. He raises it as evidence that the government was worried early on that UFOs were watching its nuclear weapons.
killing-of-caltech-astronomer-carl-grill: On February 16, 2026, in Llano in California's Antelope Valley, the astronomer Carl Grillmair, who worked at Caltech (a university in Pasadena) and JPL (NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory), met what Michels calls a tragic and suspicious end. Michels points out that this was about 30 miles northeast of Waterman Mountain, where another colleague, Monica Resza, had disappeared. He tells it himself, drawing on someone named Freddy Snyder, in an episode about top American scientists going missing, as though the two cases might be part of a pattern.
killing-of-thule-society-members-april-1: On April 30, 1919, in Munich, Germany, members of a group called the Thule Society were killed in what is described as an assassination. A researcher named Peter Levenda mentions it in passing, giving the date himself but no source.
kim-peek-s-brain-anatomy-and-his-recall-: Kim Peek, an American man famous for remembering the contents of some 12,000 books, was not autistic as many people believed, according to a researcher named Diane Powell. She says he actually had hydrocephalus, a condition he was born with in which the body cannot properly handle the fluid that surrounds the brain and spinal cord. Powell gives this as a summary, without naming a source, while discussing how unusual brains might explain unusual mental abilities.
king-charles-mountbatten-and-savile-s-bl: King Charles, his great-uncle Lord Mountbatten, and the British television presenter Jimmy Savile are said to have spent time together in the 1970s and 1980s and to have had special black berets made for themselves. The comedian Kurt Metzger repeats this as something he was told, in a conversation about Jeffrey Epstein and a secret network of the powerful.
king-frederick-shelters-hermetic-thinker: A European king named Frederick, who ruled lands in Bohemia and the Palatinate, is said to have sheltered a group of mystical and heretical thinkers, among them the English magician and scholar John Dee, his partner Edward Kelley, and possibly the philosopher Giordano Bruno. Michels takes this from the book The Rosicrucian Enlightenment by the historian Frances Yates, and adds, hedging with "I think", that when war came the philosopher René Descartes fought on the opposing side. He tells it to suggest that the rise of modern rational thought was bound up with a clash against these mystical circles.
kingman-1953-crash-arthur-stansel-sees-s: In 1953 near Kingman, Arizona, an engineer named Arthur Stansel Jr. was sent to a crash to work out how fast the craft hit the ground, and the researcher known online as UAPGerb says that inside a makeshift tent Stansel saw "a tiny little brownish being, possibly charred and mangled," while Michels, crediting the researcher Bill Steinman, who found Stansel's name in records, puts the body at about four feet and ties it to Wright Field, an Air Force base in Ohio, and to a scientist there named Eric Henry Wang. Stansel himself, speaking on the show, tells it more cautiously: he says they were told it was a secret test vehicle and he accepted it was "probably some United States government vehicle, a highly classified vehicle." If the tent story is true, it would mean the government recovered a crashed craft with a non-human body on board.
kingman-craft-held-by-lockheed-in-a-ware: A craft said to have been recovered near Kingman, Arizona, is supposedly kept in a warehouse by Lockheed, a big American aerospace company, and is described as a beautiful thing with no seams and no rivets. Michels tells this himself, loosely ("some warehouse or whatever"), without naming a source. If true, a private company would be holding a craft no human seems to have built.
kingman-crash-survivor-went-to-the-back-: After a craft is said to have crashed near Kingman, Arizona, one of the beings on board survived, and she went back inside the craft and stayed in the back. Charles Hall, a former Air Force weather observer, tells this as the Kingman sheriff's own words to him, which would mean a local lawman saw a living crash survivor.
kingman-crash-was-the-one-they-walked-aw: A UFO crash said to have happened near Kingman, Arizona, was 'the one they walked away from', according to a remark by an insider at a showing of the documentary maker James Fox's film at the SOL conference, a UFO research gathering. The UFO researcher Grant Cameron tells it from a woman he is in contact with, who was sitting next to one of the main people there, a man Cameron won't name; when the Kingman crash came up on screen, the man said, 'That's not right. That's not right. That was that crash.' If true, it would mean someone with inside knowledge holds a different version of that crash than the one shown.
kirk-mcconnell-and-extended-electrodynam: A Senate staffer named Kurt McConnell, who worked for the Senate Armed Services Committee, the group of senators that oversees the military, "knows all about extended electrodynamics", according to Jesse Michels. That is an idea that goes beyond standard physics of electricity and magnetism, which some link to how unexplained craft might fly. Michels says McConnell worked under Jack Reid, the senator from Rhode Island, and tells this himself without naming a source, hinting that such physics is understood inside Congress.
kirk-mcconnell-confirms-blue-on-blue-fir: A man named Kurt McConnell, linked in the story to the Senate Armed Services Committee and to Senator Kirsten Gillibrand, is said to have confirmed at a gathering called SOL that he had heard of a blue-on-blue firefight, meaning a fight between teams on the same side, and of humans being carried in craft built by copying non-human technology. A guest who goes by the name UAPGerb tells this, without naming a source, saying McConnell was asked about both by a couple of people and answered yes to each.
kirkpatrick-dodged-a-meeting-with-borlan: In 2023, Sean Kirkpatrick, then head of AARO, the Pentagon office that looks into unexplained things in the sky, is said to have avoided a meeting he was meant to have with Dylan Borland. Borland tells it himself: he was told to go and talk to Kirkpatrick, and in his words, Kirkpatrick "ducked me". Borland, who says a top government official told him aliens run everything, tells it as a sign the office did not want to hear what he had to say.
kirkpatrick-leaves-aaro-for-oak-ridge-20: The story is that Sean Kirkpatrick, who led AARO, the Pentagon's current office for investigating unexplained aerial reports, went to work for Oak Ridge National Laboratory in Tennessee, a government science lab, after he left. A Senate staffer named Kurt McConnell, who says he was close to it, explains that the contract for AARO's advisory group "was let through Oak Ridge," and that Kirkpatrick, once retired from government, now works "with and for Oak Ridge under contract." An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb says Kirkpatrick "ran off to Oak Ridge" and tells listeners to look at Oak Ridge's ties to FFRDCs, privately run research centres paid for by the government. UAPGerb sums it up without naming a source, while McConnell speaks as someone who saw the arrangement. They tell it because, if these links mean what they suspect, the man in charge of the official UFO office was tied to the same private research world that critics say hides UFO material.
kirkpatrick-lobbied-against-the-uap-disc: A Pentagon official named Sean Kirkpatrick lobbied against the UAP Disclosure Act, a proposed law that would push the US government to release what it knows about unidentified aerial phenomena, the official term for UFOs. Michels says this himself in a 2025 episode, without naming a source, and hopes Kirkpatrick will not oppose the bill again when it next comes to a vote, since he sees the bill as a path to openness.
kirkpatrick-metallic-orbs-worldwide-said: Sean Kirkpatrick, the first director of the Pentagon's office for investigating UFO reports, is said to have told NASA's public UFO panel in 2023 that "we're seeing metallic orbs making very interesting apparent maneuvers all over the world." The writer Marik von Rennenkampff, a former government analyst, quotes those words on the show while debating a skeptic. He cites them because they would mean the top official on the subject admitted to unexplained objects seen worldwide.
kirkpatrick-s-aaro-denied-the-herrera-in: Sean Kirkpatrick was the first head of the Pentagon office set up to investigate unexplained sightings. While that office denied a sighting reported by a former serviceman named Michael Herrera, Kirkpatrick is said to have admitted in private, to members of the Senate Intelligence Committee, that it happened "exactly as reported by Michael Herrera." Jake Barber, a former military helicopter pilot who says he once carried a recovered UFO with his helicopter, tells Michels he knows this "for a fact" and adds that Kirkpatrick also confirmed Barber's own additions to the story. If true, the official denial and the private admission would contradict each other.
kirkpatrick-tells-gillibrand-s-committee: In April 2023, according to the researcher Robert Hastings, Sean Kirkpatrick, who then led the Pentagon's office for unexplained aerial reports, told a Senate committee led by Senator Kirsten Gillibrand that there was no evidence of craft from other worlds. Hastings, who studies UFO reports at nuclear weapons bases, brings it up on his own without naming a source, and calls that hearing the high point of the government's denials, which matters because it pushes back on what witnesses say they have seen.
kirtland-security-meeting-with-benowitz-: In 1980, Paul Bennewitz, a New Mexico man convinced he was picking up signs of alien activity, presented what he had to a meeting at Kirtland Air Force Base. People kept walking out, saying "oh, that's not ours," until only three or four were left. The writer Greg Bishop tells this from what Tom Deuley, who was there, told him. The point would be that each group in the room was checking whether the strange things were its own secret projects.
kissinger-among-the-first-cic-officers-i: In 1945 Henry Kissinger, who later became a top US diplomat, was one of the first officers to move into the barracks at Oberammergau, a town in Bavaria in southern Germany. He was there with the Counter Intelligence Corps, the US Army's spy-catching branch. Michels tells this himself in an episode that asks whether Kissinger oversaw a program to recover crashed UFOs. He brings it up to place Kissinger in intelligence work early in his career.
kissinger-consults-for-the-psychological: In 1951, 1952 and again in 1955, Henry Kissinger, who later became a top American diplomat, worked as a consultant for the Psychological Strategy Board, a Washington body that coordinated US psychological warfare, and for the board that replaced it, the Operations Coordinating Board. Michels tells this himself, mentioning the board's official Gordon Gray, in an episode that asks whether Kissinger oversaw a secret programme for recovering crashed UFOs.
kissinger-directs-the-cfr-study-group-on: In 1955 the future statesman Henry Kissinger was invited to lead a study group on nuclear war and foreign policy at the Council on Foreign Relations, a private New York foreign policy club, work that led to his book Nuclear Weapons and Foreign Policy. Michels tells this himself, naming the physicist J. Robert Oppenheimer and the atomic energy official Gordon Dean in connection with it, in an episode asking whether Kissinger also oversaw a program to recover crashed UFOs.
kissinger-dobrynin-transcript-on-microwa: A recently declassified transcript from the 1970s, from talks between the US and the Soviet Union on limiting nuclear arms and easing tensions, shows the US official Henry Kissinger raising with the Soviet ambassador Anatoly Dobrynin the microwave beams aimed at the US Embassy in Moscow, with the US diplomat Walter Stoessel also named. Michels brings it up himself, citing the document, as proof that energy weapons were a live concern between the two powers.
kissinger-in-army-counterintelligence-te: Henry Kissinger, who later became a top American statesman, is said to have served in the 1940s as a US Army counterintelligence officer whose job included recovering enemy technology in Europe. Michels states this himself in passing, without naming a source. It would mean that a future power broker had early, hands-on experience with secret technology.
kissinger-involved-in-ufo-matters: Henry Kissinger, the former US Secretary of State, was involved in the government's handling of UFOs, Michels says. He tells this himself, in a conversation with the comedian and podcaster Joe Rogan, saying he has uncovered a lot about it, but he gives no source or details. If true, it would put UFO secrecy in the hands of the most senior figures in American foreign policy.
kissinger-letter-to-nixon-on-prisoners-p: A former Army intelligence officer and psychic spy named Joe McMoneagle says he once saw a letter from Henry Kissinger, then a top adviser to President Richard Nixon, telling Nixon he would not go back to negotiate for any more prisoners of war. McMoneagle tells it first-hand as evidence that American prisoners were left behind in Laos and Cambodia during the Vietnam War era, around 1970 to 1973.
kissinger-on-the-303-committee-overseein: The 303 Committee was a secret US group, drawn from several agencies, that oversaw all covert operations, and the statesman Henry Kissinger was part of it, says Jesse Michels. Michels lays this out himself, without naming a source, in an episode asking whether Kissinger oversaw a program to recover crashed UFOs. If so, Kissinger would have sat where such a secret program could be run.
kissinger-s-1977-moon-dust-telegram-to-o: In January 1977, just before leaving office, Henry Kissinger, then the US Secretary of State, is said to have sent a telegram to the US embassy in Ottawa asking for a report on "possible returned space objects." Michels tells this himself, citing the telegram, which carried the subject line Moon Dust, the name of a US government effort to recover objects that fell from space. He raises it because, if true, it would tie one of America's top officials to that recovery work.
kissinger-s-harvard-career-as-cover-for-: Henry Kissinger's career as a Harvard academic in the 1950s was only a cover for deeper intelligence work: advising Majestic 12, a rumored secret group said to handle crashed UFOs, through a specialized think tank called PI40. Michels lays this out himself in an episode asking whether Kissinger oversaw a program to retrieve crashed UFOs, without naming a source.
kissinger-studied-under-thomas-schelling: Henry Kissinger, who later became a top American diplomat, studied at Harvard under the economist and strategist Thomas Schelling. The story also holds that Schelling later tried to intervene with him at the White House, though the telling gives no details of that. Michels mentions it himself, in passing, without naming a source.
kissner-tells-steven-schiff-who-launches: In 1995, a New Mexico state representative named J. Andrew Kissner allegedly told another New Mexico representative, Steven Schiff, what he knew, and Schiff then launched an inquiry by the GAO, the investigative office of the US Congress, into records about Roswell, the 1947 New Mexico crash that some say involved a flying saucer. A researcher who goes by UAPGerb tells this, crediting the GAO's Roswell audit, as the spark that put Congress itself on the trail.
kit-green-and-eric-walker-both-tied-to-g: Two men later linked to UFO matters, Kit Green and Eric Walker, were both involved with the Glomar Explorer, a ship used in a secret US government deep-sea recovery operation in the 1970s, according to a UFO researcher named Grant Cameron. Cameron says that when Green read Walker's biography, he turned to the researcher Jacques Vallée and said, in effect, have you seen this man's background, it is unbelievable. Cameron tells it without naming a source, as a hint that the same small circle of people kept turning up in secret projects.
kit-green-and-garry-nolan-study-biologic: Kit Green, a medical scientist who worked with the CIA, and Garry Nolan, a Stanford biologist, have studied the bodily effects on people who saw or met UFOs, including what looks like electromagnetic radiation damage. Michels mentions it himself in passing, calling it "CIA spooky stuff," without naming a study, as a sign that these encounters might leave physical traces.
kit-green-could-not-get-read-into-the-au: Kit Green, a scientist who worked with the CIA, is said to have been let in on most of a secret government UFO programme in the 2000s but could never get cleared for the part dealing with autopsies, presumably of non-human bodies. The UFO researcher Grant Cameron tells it as a story he heard, and it would mean that part was guarded even from well-placed insiders.
kit-green-kicked-out-of-eric-walker-s-of: The researcher Kit Green is said to have been thrown out of the office of Eric Walker, the president of Penn State University, after asking him about UFOs. Michels mentions the episode in passing. The UFO researcher Grant Cameron tells it in more detail, relaying it from the published diaries of the UFO researcher Jacques Vallée, called Forbidden Science. In Cameron's version, set in the 1980s, Walker "just blew up" and started yelling, telling Green he did not have to tell him anything. The story is told because it suggests Walker knew secrets about UFOs that he was guarding.
kit-green-knew-ransone-but-refuses-to-ta: Kit Green, a former CIA scientist, is said to have known a woman named Valerie Ransone well during the 1970s and early 1980s, yet refuses to speak about her. An unnamed researcher who appears on the show tells this from his own dealings, saying "he knew Ransone really well." The silence matters to the teller because Green could confirm parts of her story if he chose.
kit-green-ran-the-cia-s-weird-desk: A man named Kit Green ran the CIA's so-called "weird desk" for a long time, Jesse Michels says, meaning the spot at America's foreign spy agency that handled strange subjects. Michels says this himself, without naming a source, while talking with the owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property famous for odd events. It would mean the CIA kept someone on hand just for the unexplained.
kit-green-s-cia-files-on-ufo-related-inj: A CIA scientist named Kit Green held agency files on the biological effects suffered by people who had encounters with UFOs, and those files were handed to the scientist Garry Nolan around the mid-2010s. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, as the starting point for Nolan's own study of people harmed in such encounters.
klaus-fuchs-atomic-espionage-1941: Klaus Fuchs was a scientist who stole American atomic bomb secrets while working at Los Alamos, the New Mexico lab where the bomb was built, from 1941 to 1950. Michels mentions it in passing, without naming a source, in an episode with a guest named Dave Rossi. He uses Fuchs as a comparison, wondering aloud who might be "the next Klaus Fuchs" for today's secrets.
klippenstein-admits-dod-and-ic-tipped-hi: In 2023, according to Michels, the journalist Ken Klippenstein admitted on Breaking Points, a news show hosted by Saagar Enjeti and Krystal Ball, that the Defense Department and the US intelligence agencies had basically tipped him off on his story about David Grusch, a former intelligence officer who came forward that year with claims about hidden UFO programmes. Michels tells this himself from memory of the show. If true, it would mean government insiders were shaping how the Grusch story reached the public.
knapp-and-corbell-broke-the-fravor-tic-t: A filmmaker named Jeremy Corbell says that he and a Las Vegas journalist named George Knapp were the first to tell the story of a Navy fighter pilot named David Fravor. Fravor's story is about the Tic Tac, a white oval object shaped like the mint. Corbell says the two of them told it "quietly on the radio twice" before the New York Times article of 2017 made it famous. If that is right, the story was public before the newspaper that is usually credited with breaking it.
knapp-puts-lazar-on-air-and-it-goes-vira: In Las Vegas in 1989, the reporter George Knapp is said to have phoned a man named John Lear and told him, "I'm missing a guest on tonight's show." That gap went to Bob Lazar, a man who said he had worked on alien craft in the Nevada desert. His appearance spread far and wide. The UFO researcher Grant Cameron tells this to Michels without naming a source, as the moment Lazar's story reached the public.
knew-bigelow-at-the-rockefeller-ranch-19: The UFO researcher Steven Greer says he knew the businessman Robert Bigelow in 1993 at the JY Ranch in Wyoming, owned by the wealthy philanthropist Laurance Rockefeller. Greer tells it from his own experience, while counting Bigelow as "one of those" people in a group he is describing.
knuth-sees-something-fall-into-the-sea-t: In 2021, looking through night-vision goggles off Laguna Beach, California, the physicist Kevin Knuth says he saw something fall from the sky and hit the water. Knuth, who has worked with NASA, tells it as his own sighting: "I actually saw something fall and hit the water in infrared." He offers it as a firsthand case of an unexplained object he saw with his own eyes.
kobitz-shown-an-atomically-bonded-bulkhe: A man named Nat Kobitz is said to have been led into an underground room at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base in Ohio, under heavy guard, and shown a piece of a bulkhead, a structural wall from a craft, that was bonded at the atomic level. Ross Coulthart tells it as something Kobitz described to him personally: he was "shown what he described to me as the piece of a bulkhead." Michels later repeats Coulthart's account in a different way, without the bulkhead: Kobitz, dying of cancer, said he had seen UFO technology at the base. If true, it would mean the base holds material from craft that humans did not build.
kobitz-us-recovered-multiple-craft-inclu: The United States recovered several crashed craft not built by people, among them the ones said to have fallen at Roswell and Aztec in New Mexico and at Kingman in Arizona. The Australian journalist Ross Coulthart says a man named Nat Kobitz told him this, and that Kobitz had himself been told it, so it comes to us at second hand twice over. If true, it would mean these crashes were real and more than one craft is held.
kohler-refuses-to-name-his-sources-1950: In 1950, at the radio station KMYR in Denver, Colorado, a man named George Kohler refused to say who had given him a story he was spreading. In his own recorded words, played on the episode, the information "was told to me as a story," but the names of the people he got it from were entrusted to him in confidence. His silence is why the source of his story could never be checked.
kohler-secretly-records-the-osi-intervie: In 1950 a man named George Kohler was questioned by the Air Force Office of Special Investigations at a Denver radio station, KMYR, and as they walked into the recording room he told the technician, "Record this." The researcher Scott Ramsey tells this, crediting the recording itself, in which men named Hansen and Unger also figure. If the recording exists as he describes, it would preserve exactly what investigators asked Kohler about a crash story at the time.
kona-blue: Kona Blue is said to be the name of a planned secret US government program about unidentified flying objects, whose existence came out when an internal slide presentation was made public. Jesse Michels brings it up in his own words while talking with a guest. He says it was "released I think by accident" and calls it "like a UAP program of some sort", UAP being the government's term for unidentified aerial phenomena. A fuller account comes from an online researcher who goes by UAPGerb, speaking without naming a source. He dates it to 2010 and calls it a "failed prospective special access program", meaning a proposed program with very tightly restricted access that never got started. He credits AARO, the Pentagon office that now studies unexplained aerial reports, with releasing the slide deck. He also names three people tied to it: Glenn Gaffney, Robert Cardio and Rob Jones. The tellers raise it because a proposal like that would show that people inside government once tried to set up a formal secret UFO effort.
kona-blue-documents-admit-capability-to-: Papers from Kona Blue, a proposed US government programme on UFOs, admit that the government can give people false memories, tamper with their brains and make them do things, all without drugs. That is how Dylan Borland, a former Air Force man who speaks about secret UFO matters, describes the documents. If true, it would mean the government holds the power to rewrite what a person remembers.
kona-blue-materials-were-kingman-1953-wr: The material meant for Kona Blue, a proposed secret government programme of that name for handling recovered unexplained craft, is said to have included wreckage from a 1953 crash near Kingman, Arizona. The researcher who goes by UAPGerb says he has heard this himself, crediting a person named Jim Ryder, and it would tie a modern programme to a crash from seventy years earlier.
konrad-zuse-s-calculating-space-and-nucl: The German thinker Konrad Zuse, in his work Rechnender Raum, or Calculating Space, held that the universe works like a computation, and he thought this could be tested in extremely chaotic events such as a nuclear bomb going off. The researcher Jason Jorjani tells this without naming a source beyond Zuse himself, and writes about it on his online newsletter under the title Nuking the Matrix. If true, reality would be a kind of computer that could be caught glitching.
konstantin-meyl-s-extended-electrodynami: A scientist named Konstantin Meyl, working in the Black Forest of Germany, is said to be studying an extended version of electrodynamics, the physics of electricity and magnetism, by testing it on plants. Michels brings this up himself on three different episodes without naming a source. In one he calls it "scalar waves," a proposed kind of energy wave, that can make flowers grow in beautiful ways, and links the idea to the 19th-century physicists James Clerk Maxwell and Oliver Heaviside; in another he stresses scalar waves and resonance with DNA rather than the plants.
kordylewski-clouds-and-1920s-long-delay-: Radio signals sent in the early 1920s are said to have come back to Earth after a strange delay, and these "long delay echoes" may have bounced off Kordylewski clouds, which are faint clouds of plasma sitting at Lagrangian points, spots in space where the pull of two bodies balances out. Michels takes the idea from the author Robert Temple, who sets it out in his book The New Science of Heaven and in a research paper. Michels does not place the clouds the same way each time: in one episode they lie between the Earth and the Sun, and in another at a balance point between the Earth and the Moon.
kordylewski-clouds-as-possible-conscious: Out at the L5 point, a spot in space where the pull of Earth and Moon balance so things can collect, there are two faint clouds called Kordylewski clouds, each roughly nine times as large as Earth, and they may be conscious beings made of plasma, a charged gas. The parapsychologist Jeffrey Mishlove tells this from the writer Robert Temple's book A New Science of Heaven. If true, there would be living minds of enormous size close to our planet.
korean-man-s-ayahuasca-sessions-in-peru-: In 2024 a Korean man drinking ayahuasca in Peru had what he called a full-blown alien experience. Ayahuasca is a psychedelic brew used in Amazon ceremonies. During it, he said, he was taken away by a being he described as "the alien scientist." The neuroscientist Andrew Gallimore, who studies the psychedelic DMT, tells Michels what the man told him, as an example of how these substances can seem to open contact with alien beings.
kosloski-hearing-firsthand-witnesses-of-: At a 2024 Senate hearing, Jon Kosloski, head of the Pentagon office that looks into unexplained objects in the sky and sea, said at least two people with firsthand knowledge of secret programs on such objects, programs never reported to Congress, had come to his office. The commentator Marik von Rennenkampff relays this from the hearing, where Senator Kirsten Gillibrand was asking questions. If it holds, it would mean the government's own UFO office has heard from insiders about hidden programs.
kripal-s-levitation-talk-to-lockheed-eng: Jeffrey Kripal, a professor of religion at Rice University, was once invited to give a private talk on a single subject, levitation, to top engineers at Lockheed, the American aerospace company whose secret research division is called Skunk Works. Jesse Michels passes this on from what Kripal said on another podcast, hosted by Danny Jones: the invitation came from Charles Chase, who ran Lockheed's revolutionary projects group. It is told because it would mean serious aircraft engineers were interested in accounts of people floating in the air.
kryptos-conundrum-an-intelligence-commit: A document Michels calls the Kryptos Conundrum, which he links to a former CIA officer named Chase Brandon, describes a secret intelligence committee that manages humanity's future, and the beings behind it are said to "paranormally show up to everybody on the committee like independently and coordinate them together." Michels tells this himself in two episodes. In the later one he adds a detail: the committee had "a crystal tablet that gave them access to reading future timelines," which would mean someone outside humanity is steering events and letting a small group see what is coming.
kuber-lada-and-friends-meet-military-blo: Seven days after a witness saw something crash near the town of Varginha, Brazil, in 1996, a man named Kuber Lada was leaving a gym with several friends when they saw two military trucks driving into town. The documentary filmmaker James Fox tells this on Michels' show, passing on what Lada told him. It is one of many accounts from Varginha that, if true, would mean the army moved in to collect a living being that was not human.
kubrick-on-the-2001-monolith-1969: The director Stanley Kubrick said in a 1969 interview that seeing the monolith in his film 2001: A Space Odyssey as an alien object is the most superficial way to read the film. The monolith is the tall black slab at the centre of the story, which he made with the writer Arthur C. Clarke, author of the novel. Michels brings up the interview himself, as a hint that the film was about something deeper than aliens.
kumamoto-university-researchers-saw-ligh: Stones on Oshidoishi Hill in Japan are said to have been struck by lightning again and again, and researchers from Kumamoto University are said to have seen it happen several times. A researcher named Geoffrey Drumm tells this on the show. He says the Kumamoto team "actually witnessed these things being struck by lightning on multiple occasions." When he describes the stone itself, he says "the scarring pock marks and melted top of this stone are a result of lightning strikes," and he does not mention the university witnesses there. If true, the marks on the stones would come from lightning, not from tools or weather.
kuramanta-pyramid-built-on-geothermal-ho: A pyramid in Japan that he calls Kuramanta was built right on top of a hot spring, says the pyramid researcher Geoffrey Drumm, so that natural heat and sulfur gas rise up into the structure. Drumm gives it as an example without naming a source, as part of his argument that pyramids were placed on purpose to use energy coming out of the ground.
kuromanta-pyramid-documented-red-granite: Kuromanta, a hill in Akita, Japan, is said to be a real man-made pyramid, documented by archaeologists, with red granite chambers inside that were found with ground-penetrating radar, a tool that maps what lies under the surface. Geoffrey Drumm, a researcher who says he has seen the site, tells it and names someone called Suzuki in connection with it. He calls the chambers reaction chambers, as part of his idea that pyramids were built as machines.
kurt-russell-saw-the-phoenix-lights-whil: In 1997 the actor Kurt Russell is said to have seen the Phoenix Lights, a famous display of strange lights over Phoenix, Arizona, while he was flying his own plane. Jesse Michels mentions it in passing, saying Russell claimed the thing was so big "he could have landed his airplane on it." The UFO investigator James Fox tells it more fully in a later episode, giving Russell's account in Russell's own voice. In that version Russell is coming in to Phoenix and sees "a bank of lights, six lights in the shape of a triangle," passing right over the airport. Why it matters to the tellers is that a well-known pilot, not just people on the ground, says he saw the object up close from the air. The two versions differ on detail: one stresses the size, the other the six lights in a triangle.
kurt-s-forgotten-childhood-in-gifted-and: The comedian Kurt Metzger says he was placed in a gifted and talented program as a child in New Jersey, but has no memory of it at all: "I don't remember a single part of it." He tells it about himself on an episode about secret programs, where a blank like that hints that something was done to him he cannot recall.
kutu-cuthah-entrance-to-the-underworld-i: An ancient place called Kutu, or Cuthah, was supposed to be the entrance to the underworld, and it still exists today in Iraq, at a site called Tell Ibrahim south-east of Baghdad. The researcher Peter Levenda says this without naming a source, linking it to the Necronomicon, a book of occult spells and lore. If he is right, a real spot on the map was once treated as a doorway to the land of the dead.
ky-dickens-controlled-telepathy-tests-wi: In 2023 the documentary filmmaker Ky Dickens says she brought a young girl named Mia up from Mexico and rented a house in Glendale, California, to run controlled tests of whether Mia could read minds. Dickens says most of the family spoke no English, except Mia's aunt Sophia, and a researcher named Diane Powell was also part of the story. Dickens took part herself and tells it as evidence that some children can pick up others' thoughts.
kyle-sends-whole-sensory-experiences-tel: A person in England named Kyle is said to send whole experiences by telepathy, mind to mind, so that the receiver gets not just a message but the smells and feelings that come with it. Ky Dickens, the maker of a documentary about telepathy called The Telepathy Tapes, tells this on the podcast, passing on what Kyle and Kyle's mother told her. If true, it would mean thoughts can be shared as full sensory scenes, not only as words.
l-espresso-article-on-project-preserve-d: In the summer of 2025, the Italian magazine L'Espresso published an article that, according to Jesse Michels, drew on a confidential source and claimed that President Donald Trump was taking control of special access programs, the Pentagon's most tightly restricted secret projects, away from the Pentagon. Michels tells it himself in two episodes. In one he dates the article to July 2025 and says it discusses something called Project Preserve Destiny. In the other he leaves that name out and dwells on the struggle over the secret programs, which would matter because it would put the White House in charge of whatever those programs hold.
la-danta-and-el-tigre-oldest-maya-pyrami: La Danta and El Tigre, two huge pyramids at El Mirador, an ancient Maya city in the jungle of Guatemala, are among the very oldest pyramids the Maya built, according to Luke Caverns, a researcher of ancient sites who says he has been there. He calls La Danta "the first known pyramid." He brings it up as part of his case that the pyramids are older and stranger than people usually think.
lab-finds-unknown-chemical-burning-in-so: Soil and a tree at a site near Varginha, Brazil, where a strange craft is said to have come down in 1996, were burned by chemical products that a lab could not identify, according to results relayed by Carlos de Souza, a guest on an episode about the case. He says a researcher named Claudia Kovu took samples to the lab, and months later reported that "the burning of the soil in the tree was caused by chemical products and that they were unknown." De Souza passes it on from Kovu, also pointing to home-movie film shot on Super 8 cameras, as evidence that something out of the ordinary touched down there.
lab-nine-tapes-of-remote-viewing-targets: In the 1970s, the story goes, sessions at Lab Nine, a research house in Ossining, New York, run by the researcher Andrija Puharich, were taped. On some tapes the questions are about spying by remote viewing, the practice of trying to see distant places with the mind alone. A researcher named Greg Malatzi, who has studied the tapes, says some ask things like "what time is the best to remove you the Kremlin so we can get into it." The Kremlin is the seat of the Russian government. Another researcher on the same episode, who is not named, gives a different example: a question asking for the code name used by Russian guerrilla soldiers. They tell it because the questions sound like intelligence work, which would tie Puharich's sessions to government spying.
lab-retest-of-the-marble-finds-no-iridiu: A small marble from a site said to be a UFO crash, which an earlier scan had read as about 40 percent iridium, a very heavy rare metal, did not hold up when retested. Matthew Zodakis says he ran the test himself in his own lab and found the piece "nowhere near dense enough for a heavy metal like iridium." His result cuts against the earlier claim that the marble was an unusual metal object.
