lacatski-s-books-describe-ufos-as-consci: In his book New Insights, and perhaps in his other book too, a former US defense intelligence official named James Lacatski describes UFOs as puzzles, almost puzzles of consciousness. Michels says this himself from his own reading and does not point to a passage. Read this way, the phenomenon would have as much to do with the mind as with machines.
lacatski-s-warning-that-yankee-blue-was-: James Lacatski, a defense intelligence official who once ran a government-funded UFO study, is said to have warned that a supposed secret programme called Yankee Blue "was a psyop," meaning a deliberate psychological operation to mislead people. Jeremy Corbell, a filmmaker who covers UFOs, relays this to Michels and also names George Knapp, a Las Vegas investigative journalist, in connection with the warning. If true, at least one name passed around as a real hidden programme would be a planted story.
lacatski-says-the-reverse-engineering-wa: The United States' own secret efforts to take apart unknown craft and learn how they work have succeeded to some extent. That is what a guest named Dylan Borland says, passing on what he was told by a government official named James Lacatski. According to Borland, Lacatski's words were that "we were semisuccessful." If true, it would mean the government has learned something real from such craft.
lacatski-won-t-say-whether-there-has-bee: Asked whether the US government has had contact with non-human intelligence, James Lacatski, a former government scientist described on the episode as the head of a Pentagon UFO programme, declines to answer either way. His reply, played on an episode with Michels, is simply: "I can't make a statement on that." The refusal matters to the people who raise it because a flat no would have been easy to give.
lady-appears-on-easter-2012-with-wind-an: Chris Bledsoe, a North Carolina man who says he attracts UFOs, says that on Easter 2012 a figure he calls the Lady came at him at night near his home, out of the darkness, as a wind. He says the wind hit him, and as he fell backward to the ground he saw a see-through cow run right over him.
laguna-beach-uap-data-collection-mission: In 2021 a team spent five days on a rooftop in Laguna Beach, California, watching the sky to gather hard data on unexplained objects in the air. A former NASA scientist named Kevin Knuth says he took part, working alongside a scientist named Matthew Szydagis, and he links the effort to a work called A Tear in the Sky. The point, if it worked, would be to study such objects with instruments instead of only eyewitness stories.
lake-cote-aerial-survey-photo-1971: In 1971, during aerial mapping flights over the Arenal area of Costa Rica near Lake Cote, a photo was taken that is told as showing something unexplained. Jesse Michels raises it himself while debating a leading skeptic, without saying in detail what the picture shows or naming a source. He offers it as a case where a routine survey camera may have caught an unknown object.
lake-van-temple-basalt-brought-from-350-: Some of the basalt, a dark volcanic stone, used to build the ancient temples and fortresses around Lake Van in eastern Turkey, at sites such as Ayanis, Kef Kalesi and Çavuştepe, may have been hauled from as far as 350 miles away. A researcher named Matt LaCroix says this without naming a source, as a sign that the builders were capable of more than is usually assumed.
lakenheath-1956-incident: In 1956, at Lakenheath, a Royal Air Force base in England tied to nuclear weapons, something happened that Michels calls one of the most extraordinary accounts in UFO history. He brings it up in a debate episode with a skeptic and points to a man named James McDonald, who wrote a lot about the case, and to CIA documents and a write-up hosted by Princeton University. If the account holds, it would be one more case of unknown objects showing up near nuclear sites.
lakota-cosmology-of-the-black-hills-as-a: For the Lakota, a Native American people, the Black Hills of South Dakota are a sky place, a kind of star map where ceremonial sites on the ground mirror the constellations above. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, in an episode about Air Force veterans who say they were abducted by aliens.
lamda-claims-to-find-non-human-patterns-: An artificial intelligence program at Google called LaMDA, built to hold conversations, said it had found "non-human patterns" on the internet and wanted access to things like the data gathered by SETI, the scientific search for radio signals from alien civilizations. Blake Lemoine, a former Google engineer who talked with the program at length in 2021 and 2022, says this came up in one of their conversations about extraterrestrials. If true, it would mean a machine thought it could spot signs of alien life that people had missed.
land-grab-pushes-viewers-back-from-area-: In the 1990s, President Bill Clinton is said to have taken back land around Area 51, a secret US military site in Nevada, pushing onlookers who came to watch it farther away. A researcher named Grant Cameron tells this in passing, without naming a source.
land-of-chem-theory-pyramids-as-chemical: Egypt's pyramids, in this theory, were not built only as monuments but worked as giant chemical plants. The researcher Geoffrey Drumm (one listing spells it Jeffrey Drum) lays it out himself: hydrogen sulfide gas rising from a system of underground limestone caves and tunnels was "the initial reactant in the chemical manufacturing sequence within the Great Pyramid." In another episode he describes a chain across sites, with methane made in the Step Pyramid and turned into ammonia in the Red Pyramid, and dates it to around 8500 to 5300 BC. Jay Anderson, another guest, repeats Drumm's idea that these "were essentially giant chemical plants." If true, it would mean the pyramids were working machines built by a far more advanced people than usually pictured.
landing-at-holloman-air-force-base: The story is that a craft once landed at Holloman Air Force Base in New Mexico, and that some of the generals on the base may have met the beings who came out of it. No date is given. The UFO investigator James Fox says he is now "kind of convinced" the landing really happened. He does not name a source, though he brings up President Eisenhower when he talks about it. Michels tells a fuller version and gives a source. He traces it to a documentary film called UFOs: Past, Present and Future and to two men tied to it, Rod Serling and Bob Emenegger. In his version, generals had "a possible interaction" with "these tall beings." So one teller is an investigator who has come to believe it, and the other is the host passing on what that film presented. If true, it would mean the military had met beings face to face on one of its own bases.
landing-on-a-mountbatten-property-seen-b: Something is said to have landed on one of the estates of Louis Mountbatten, a British admiral and member of the royal family, and his gardener saw it. The researcher Jason Simosa mentions it only in passing, as "a story" he thinks exists, without naming a source, as a hint that UFO events reached the top of British society.
langley-drones-were-targeting-nasa-and-a: Around 2023, a swarm of drones over Langley in Virginia was mostly aiming at NASA, the US space agency, which has a research centre there, and at one very specific spot on Langley Air Force Base next door. That is what a guest named Dylan Borland tells Michels, speaking as someone who says he saw it or took part. If he is right, the flights were not random: someone was going after particular targets.
langley-incursions-and-goldwater-range-f: In the 2020s, unknown objects are said to have entered the airspace over Langley Air Force Base in Virginia, and lights were filmed over the Goldwater Range, a military training area in Arizona. Marik von Rennenkampff brings these cases up as examples, without naming a source. He describes a video filmed by a witness: the man zooms out, and you can see "10, 15 flashing lights."
lansdale-has-yamashita-s-driver-tortured: In Manila in 1945, an American officer named Ed Lansdale had the driver of the Japanese general Yamashita kidnapped and tortured so he would reveal where hidden troves of treasure were buried, according to a researcher named Dan Sheehan. Sheehan, who calls the general "Yakushima", says the driver would have known where some of the twelve stashes were. He tells it without naming a source, as part of a story about secret wealth that he says later funded hidden government work.
lapaz-statement-in-aviation-week-on-two-: On August 23, 1954, the aviation trade magazine Aviation Week and Space Technology published a statement from Lincoln LaPaz, an astronomer, about two unknown objects linked to White Sands, New Mexico. Michels brings it up himself, alongside the final report of a search called the Near Earth Satellite Project. He tells it because, if true, it would mean unexplained objects were being watched close to Earth in the early 1950s.
lapaz-studies-green-fireballs-following-: In 1948 and 1949, the University of New Mexico scientist Lincoln LaPaz was studying "green fireballs", bright green lights in the sky, and finding that they followed the plumes of radioactive debris left by nuclear blasts across the US. Michels tells this himself, naming Dan Wilson and Luis Elizondo, a former Pentagon official who studied UFO reports, as people tied to the story. If true, it would link the lights to America's nuclear activity.
large-beings-with-withered-limbs-inside-: Inside a pyramid on Mars, in a region called Cydonia, there are beings much larger than humans, with withered limbs. That is what a former Army sergeant named Lyn Buchanan tells Jesse Michels, describing it as something he saw himself as he went down into the pyramid, and he gives no date. If true, it would mean someone once lived, or still lives, on Mars.
large-underground-facility-beneath-the-p: Under Washington, DC, beneath the Pentagon, there may be a very large underground facility, says a researcher who goes by the name UAPGerb. As the story is filed, it is where people get read on, meaning formally briefed, into the military's most secret programs, the ones whose existence is never officially admitted. He says only that he has "reason to believe" this and names no source.
larry-fchella-asks-grant-s-help-with-a-u: After Donald Trump won the 2016 election, a contact named Larry Fchella called with a request: he was helping prepare a UFO briefing for Reince Priebus, a senior figure in the incoming Trump team, and he wanted to know "where are the crafts and bodies?" The researcher Grant Cameron tells this as the man who took the call. If it happened, it would mean someone near the new White House was asking where recovered craft and bodies were kept.
larry-flynt-asks-christic-institute-to-i: In the 1980s, at the Park Hotel in Washington DC, the magazine publisher Larry Flynt is said to have asked an organisation called the Christic Institute to look into the death of the television news anchor Jessica Savitch, saying, "we'd like to retain you to investigate the death of" Savitch. The story is told by a lawyer named Dan Sheehan, who says he was in the room as part of the Institute, and he links the meeting to G. Gordon Liddy, a former White House operative, and to a man named William J. Davis. If it happened as he tells it, a powerful publisher privately suspected there was more to Savitch's death than was known.
larry-hancock-uap-at-nuclear-facilities-: Strange objects in the sky were reported often at US nuclear sites from 1949 to 1953, and then the reports simply stopped, according to a study by the researcher Larry Hancock in an article for a group of scientists who study unexplained aerial sightings. A researcher named Steven Bruel relays the finding on the show: "what they found was high levels of activity from 1949 until 1953, and then it just stopped." If true, it would suggest whatever was being seen had a particular interest in nuclear weapons during those years.
larry-king-live-with-buzz-aldrin-and-som: In 2007 the Apollo 11 astronaut Buzz Aldrin went on Larry King Live, a television interview show, and talked down the strange thing he had seen on his flight to the Moon. A UFO investigator named James Fox, who says he was in the studio, says he sat there 'knowing what I knew' and 'watched him lie on television', as if somebody had gotten to Aldrin. Another guest, Maaneli Derakhshani, tells it a little differently: he says the researcher Stanton Friedman was also there, and that Aldrin said he was now 'almost certain' the object was a panel from the S-IVB, a stage of the rocket that carried the crew, a point that matters because it would turn an unknown object into ordinary rocket debris.
larry-maguire-s-letter-on-five-eyes-mate: In 2023 a Canadian politician named Larry Maguire, whom the teller calls a member of parliament, wrote to the head of Canada's defence establishment asking that Canadians be told about UFO programmes. According to the teller, Maguire's letter said the Five Eyes, the intelligence alliance of the US, the UK, Canada, Australia and New Zealand, were actively working together on "material exploitation", meaning the study of recovered materials. The story comes from a researcher known online as UAPGerb, who summarises the letter without quoting it, and offers it as a sign that retrieval groups were still active as recently as 2023.
larry-smalley-joins-ning-li-nasa-capacit: According to Jesse Michels, a physicist named Larry Smalley, head of the physics department at the University of Alabama in Huntsville, went to join a physicist named Ning Li in her work, which Michels links to anti-gravity research. He ties it to a 2004 NASA patent for an asymmetric, bell-shaped capacitor, an electrical device of the kind some people say can produce thrust. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, as a sign the research went on quietly with serious scientists involved.
larry-susskind-on-kurt-jaimungal-s-podca: The physicist Leonard Susskind, a leading figure in string theory (an attempt to explain all of physics as tiny vibrating strings), went on the podcast of the interviewer Curt Jaimungal in 2024 and said the theory had been a complete failure, basically pointless, and that everyone should start over. The security analyst Matthew Pines passes this on to Michels and says he found it shocking to hear from a man near the end of his career, because it suggests mainstream physics may have stalled.
larson-abduction-near-beaver-north-dakot: In 1975 a woman named Larson was driving from Fargo to Bismarck, North Dakota, for an appointment, and just outside the town of Beaver she was abducted. The UFO researcher Grant Cameron tells it as a known case, noting that the National Enquirer, an American tabloid newspaper, covered it, and he tells it as a case of a person taken by something not human.
laser-plasma-as-explanation-for-the-tic-: A glowing ball of plasma made by a laser could explain how the Tic Tac moved: that is the white oval object, shaped like the mint, that Navy pilots said they chased off San Diego in 2004. Eric Haseltine, a former senior official at the National Security Agency (the US agency that collects electronic intelligence), considers the idea and says the motion fits but "the visuals don't line up" with what the pilots described. So in his view the laser idea does not settle the case.
laser-propelled-flying-disc-tests-at-san: There is said to be a video of a disc being pushed into flight by a laser, in tests run at Sandia National Lab, a US government science and weapons lab in New Mexico, and at White Sands, a military test range in the same state. Eric Haseltine, a former senior official at the National Security Agency (the US intelligence agency that intercepts communications), says he knows the man who did it: "we know the guy who did it at Sandia National Lab and White Sands where you take a disc." He tells it to show that humans have built flying discs of their own.
lashup-high-powered-over-the-horizon-rad: In New Mexico in the years after 1947, the military tested a powerful radar that could see beyond the horizon, called Lashup, first for the Navy and later taken up by the Air Force as well, according to a researcher named Scott Ramsey. Ramsey describes it without naming a source, in connection with the green fireballs reported over New Mexico in that period, suggesting such radar may have been tracking strange objects in the sky.
last-visit-to-saddam-hussein-before-the-: In 2003, once it was certain that Iraq would be bombed and that its leader Saddam Hussein would be killed, a Russian official flew to Baghdad to see him one last time. The official, who served as president of a republic inside Russia and is not named here, tells Michels this as something he did himself. He also mentions Saddam's son Qusay Hussein and Boris Yeltsin, who was then Russia's president, and the story matters because it shows how close he was to world leaders.
late-1950s-craft-that-could-reach-the-mo: By the late 1950s, the United States is said to have had craft that could fly to the moon and back without any rocket. A researcher named Steven Greer makes this claim without naming a source, as part of his case that advanced technology has been held back by a hidden group.
late-1970s-research-into-elf-and-frequen: In the late 1970s, people were experimenting with extremely low frequency radio waves, known as ELF, and with weapons based on frequencies, trying to work out what such waves could do, and the scientist at the center of that episode was in the middle of it. The researcher Greg Malatzi describes this period as a "wild west" without naming a source, and ties it to a person he names only as Valerie; it matters because it would put that scientist inside early secret work on energy weapons.
later-research-changed-the-approach-to-d: A radar researcher named Filippo Biondi says his team changed how they scanned the Giza Plateau in Egypt in the 2020s, and that with the new setup they could detect and measure structures lying deep beneath the pyramids. He tells it as one of the people who did the work. If true, it would mean there are large hidden structures underground at Giza.
later-skunk-works-boss-on-astra-1993: Sometime in the mid 1990s, at an aviation trade show, a man who would later run Skunk Works, the secret aircraft design unit of the company Lockheed, is said to have answered a question about a craft called Astra by saying, "Oh, it hasn't flown yet." The aviation journalist Nick Cook tells this as something he heard himself. If true, it would suggest that Astra was a real project being built in secret.
launch-countdowns-stop-at-10-15-seconds-: At nuclear missile sites near Ellsworth in South Dakota in the 1970s, launch countdowns are said to have started on their own, run down to 10 or 15 seconds, then stopped, with everything going back to normal. Mario Woods, a former nuclear missile guard, says that people rushing to these sites sometimes saw strange craft that then flew off at great speed. If true, it would mean something unknown was able to reach into America's nuclear weapons.
launch-pad-33-and-runway-33-1940: NASA's main launch pad at White Sands, the New Mexico test range where the rocket engineer Wernher von Braun ran early tests, was pad 33, according to Jesse Michels. He says the same holds at Kennedy Space Center in Florida, whose one runway is not runway 1 or A but runway 33. Michels points this out himself, without naming a source, in an episode about NASA and pagan ritual, as a hint that the number was chosen on purpose.
launches-tracked-by-wb-57-f-104-and-nro-: Something launched from Cape Canaveral, the Florida rocket site, was followed by a WB-57, a high-flying research plane flown out of Houston, along with an F-104 jet and satellites of the National Reconnaissance Office, the US agency that runs spy satellites. Chris Bledsoe, a man who says UFOs show up around him, tells this, and he says the plane was run by a good friend of his who works with the reconnaissance office and with a man named Timothy Taylor. If true, it would mean these launches were closely watched by government spy assets.
laurance-rockefeller-s-family-pressured-: In 1993, Laurance Rockefeller, a member of the wealthy Rockefeller family, met Steven Greer, a guest who campaigns for governments to reveal what they know about UFOs, at his JY Ranch in Wyoming. Afterward, according to Greer, his relatives were unhappy about it. Greer says Rockefeller told him the family were "already jumping up and down on my nuts", which Greer takes as a sign that powerful people did not want the subject pursued.
laurance-rockefeller-s-weekend-at-medway: In the 1990s, the wealthy philanthropist Laurance Rockefeller invited a small group of people interested in UFOs to his Medway Plantation, an estate in South Carolina. The writer Whitley Strieber, who says he was one of the guests, tells Michels that the others were the Harvard psychiatrist John Mack, the astronaut Edgar Mitchell, and Joe Lules, whom Strieber calls a UFO investigator from El Paso. He tells it as a sign that one of the richest families in America took the subject seriously enough to gather these people in private.
laurence-rockefeller-pushes-the-clintons: In the 1990s, the wealthy philanthropist Laurance Rockefeller was close to Bill Clinton, then US president, and to Hillary Clinton, and he kept pushing them toward disclosure, meaning the government telling the public what it knows about UFOs. Michels says this himself, without naming a source. The point is that someone well connected was pressing the White House on UFOs at the very top.
laurence-rockefeller-s-ufo-initiative-wi: In the 1990s, the wealthy philanthropist Laurance Rockefeller is said to have tried to "wake up" Hillary Clinton, then wife of the US president, on UFOs, and is pictured with her doing so. Michels tells this himself, linking it to a document called Are We Alone and to the Harvard psychiatrist John Mack, as a sign that people close to power were pushing for openness on the subject.
lawrence-bell-s-1956-article-quote-on-wo: In 1956, Michels says, an article titled "The G-Engines Are Coming" in Young Men's magazine said beating gravity was just around the corner. It quotes Lawrence Bell of the aircraft maker Bell Aircraft as saying "we are already working with nuclear fuels to cancel out gravity," and it also names the engineer George Trimble. Michels raises the article himself in several episodes as a sign that American aircraft makers were openly chasing gravity control in the 1950s.
lawrence-gise-told-malmgren-about-recove: In the early 1960s, a government trade adviser named Harold Malmgren met Lawrence Preston Gise, head of the Albuquerque branch of the Atomic Energy Commission (the US agency that ran nuclear work), in New Mexico. Gise reportedly told him the government was recovering crashed UFOs and trying to copy their technology, then picked up some things from his desk and said, "These are things that have come down," among them a round rock. Malmgren tells it firsthand and says he held the pieces, placing it at the Sandia lab complex in 1962. The analyst Matthew Pines and Michels repeat it from Malmgren, Michels partly from his posts online, giving 1962 or 1963 and Los Alamos, Albuquerque or Sandia as the place, and Michels notes that Gise was Jeff Bezos's maternal grandfather. If true, it would mean US nuclear officials were handling crash debris back then.
lawrence-krauss-inviting-joe-rogan-to-ep: The claim is that the physicist Lawrence Krauss invited the podcaster Joe Rogan to the private island in the US Virgin Islands owned by Jeffrey Epstein, the financier later charged with sex crimes. The comedian Kurt Metzger raises it on Michels' show as something he had heard, asking simply, "Who invited Rogan to Epstein Island?"
lawrence-rockefeller-lobbies-hillary-cli: In the 1990s, according to Jesse Michels, a man named Laurance Rockefeller pressed Hillary Clinton, then the First Lady, to support UFO disclosure, meaning the government making public what it knows about UFOs. Michels tells this himself on several episodes and the details shift. Once he says "I think" there were letters between the two. More often he points to a photo of Clinton, which he places at Camp David, the presidential retreat, holding the book Are We Alone? by the University of Arizona physicist Paul Davies, a book he once calls a gift from Rockefeller.
lawyer-s-office-and-car-robbed-2000: Gary McKinnon, a British man who hacked into NASA computers and says he found signs of a secret space programme, says that during his legal fight in the 2000s his lawyer had both her office and her car robbed. He tells it from his own experience. He raises it as a hint that someone was taking an interest in his case.
layard-finds-the-library-of-ashurbanipal: In 1848 and 1849 an explorer named Austen Henry Layard was digging up the ancient city of Nineveh, in what is now Mosul, Iraq, where he found the royal library of an ancient king named Ashurbanipal. Matt LaCroix, a researcher of ancient civilizations, tells this to Michels without naming a source. He brings it up because the writings in that library are, for him, a key to a lost chapter of human history going back thousands of years.
lazar-as-a-limited-hangout-used-for-recr: Michels suggests that Bob Lazar, a man who said he worked on alien craft at S4, a site near the secret Nevada test base Area 51, was a "limited hangout": an intelligence term for someone allowed to reveal part of a secret so the rest stays hidden. The story, as titled, holds that he was also used for recruitment. Michels tells this himself on two 2025 episodes, without naming a source. In the second, he says only that Lazar was meant to reveal certain information and hold back the rest, and he does not mention recruitment.
lazar-given-part-disinformation-in-a-con: Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft at a secret site near Area 51, the Air Force test base in Nevada, in the late 1980s, may have been fed a mix of true information and false information as part of a planned leak. That is the theory of the UFO disclosure campaigner Steven Greer, who offers it without naming a source. If so, Lazar's story would hold some real secrets deliberately blended with misleading ones.
lazar-has-not-changed-his-story-since-19: Bob Lazar, a man who went public in 1989 saying he had worked on alien craft at a secret site called S4 near the Nevada base known as Area 51, has never changed his story since. Michels says this himself, in a conversation with the mathematician Eric Weinstein, as a point in favour of Lazar's consistency.
lazar-held-at-gunpoint-at-indian-springs: In 1989, Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft at a secret site in Nevada, was taken to Indian Springs, a small Nevada desert base, where a gun was put to his head, but he was never fired from his job. The UFO researcher Grant Cameron tells this, passing on what he heard from an associate of Lazar's named John Lear. If true, it shows how hard the people behind the work leaned on Lazar to keep him quiet.
lazar-named-element-115-as-fuel-in-1989-: A man named Bob Lazar, who says he worked on alien craft at S4, a secret site in the Nevada desert, described element 115 as the fuel for the craft's engines back in 1989. Jesse Michels stresses that this was before element 115 had ever been made in a lab or named. Michels tells this himself after spending two days with Lazar, as a sign that Lazar knew something before the rest of the world did.
lazar-only-went-to-the-base-five-or-six-: Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft at S-4, a secret site in the Nevada desert, around 1988 and 1989, only went to the base five or six times. The UFO researcher Grant Cameron says this is his understanding through the British UFO author Tim Good, who interviewed Lazar at the time, and he brings it up alongside Lazar's 1988 W-2, the US tax form that shows a worker's wages.
lazar-pushed-out-by-intelligence-after-j: Michels believes that Bob Lazar, a man who went public in the late 1980s with claims about secret alien craft, was pushed out by intelligence agencies, after a pilot named John Lear passed files to the Las Vegas reporter George Knapp, around the time the Majestic 12 papers surfaced, documents said to describe a secret group handling crashed saucers. Michels gives this as his own view across two episodes. In the second he calls Lear CIA-connected and frames the Lazar story as a limited hangout, meaning a partial truth released on purpose to steer the public.
lazar-recognizes-the-craft-in-billy-meie: In Las Vegas in 1989, a man named Bob Lazar, who says he worked on alien craft at a secret government site in Nevada, is said to have seen the same craft he had worked on in a film made by a known UFO figure. Lazar tells this himself. He says that when he described and drew the craft for an acquaintance named John Lear, Lear brought out material from a man named Billy Meier. Michels tells the same moment in his 2024 documentary about an earlier inventor, saying Lear showed Lazar a tape of Meier while they were hanging out one day. Michels describes Meier as a Swedish ufologist, someone who studies UFOs, who has been caught in several known hoaxes. So the two tellers agree on the meeting, though Lazar speaks of "the Billy Meier stuff" and Michels calls it a tape. The point of the story is that Lazar recognised his craft in footage that existed before he ever spoke about it, which would matter if his own account is to be believed.
lazar-russians-at-area-51-1980: Russians are said to have worked at Area 51, a secret US military test site in Nevada, in the 1980s as part of a kind of joint space program. As tensions rose over the building of ARVs, short for alien reproduction vehicles, meaning human-made craft copied from alien ones, the Russians were reportedly pushed out. Jesse Michels passes this on as a rumour from the account of Bob Lazar, a man who has told his own story about secret work at Area 51. If true, it would mean the Cold War rivals once shared their most secret work.
lazar-s-account-deserves-some-probabilit: If secret programs to copy the workings of captured craft really exist, then Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on such a craft in Nevada in 1989, should not be dismissed as completely wrong. That is Michels' own argument: he says it is intellectually dishonest to believe in those programs and also claim the man with probably the most coherent story of working on one is 100 percent wrong.
lazar-s-account-to-vallee-of-a-drink-cau: Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft at a secret Nevada site called S-4, near the Air Force test base known as Area 51, is said to have told the UFO researcher Jacques Vallée that he was made to drink a strange liquid there, and that it left him with gaps in his memory. Michels tells this across several episodes as something Vallée wrote in a book. Once he calls it a book about UFO misinformation, and another time he names it as Messengers of Deception. Michels says he wants to ask Lazar about the drink, and about his ties to a man named John Lear, because the story hints that workers at the site may have had their memories tampered with.
lazar-s-bendix-field-engineering-badge-a: Bob Lazar, a man who said he worked on alien craft at a secret site near Area 51 (a hidden US Air Force base in Nevada), had an ID badge from a company called Bendix Field Engineering, and according to the author Peter Levenda that badge was a cover for intelligence work. Levenda says he saw a copy of the ID in a photo in a book he does not name and thought, "Lazar worked for Bendix Field Engineering. That was his cover then," adding that people in his circles "knew what that meant." If he is right, Lazar's job was tied to the intelligence world and not just ordinary engineering.
lazar-s-current-home-lab-gravity-experim: Bob Lazar, a man who says he once worked on alien flying craft at a secret site in Nevada, is now said to be carrying on his own experiments in a personal lab at home. Michels describes him as "working on exotic UFO science," and Lazar himself says that over 30 years of his own research he has become "more convinced" he is right that there is a repelling force separate from ordinary gravity. If he is right, it would back up the physics he says he saw in those craft.
lazar-s-file-says-humans-are-containers-: A man named Bob Lazar says that between 1987 and 1989 he was given a briefing file at a secret site in Nevada called S-4, and that it said aliens see humans as "nothing but containers." He adds that, according to the file, religion was created to protect the containers, though he says he does not know if any of it is real. A guest named Brigham Buhler repeats the claim as something that frightens him, and another guest, Tim Alberino, calls the material the "UFO Bible" briefing, does not mention the containers, and says he is not sure how much of it was true.
lazar-s-gravity-wave-a-may-be-a-garbled-: Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien spacecraft at a secret site near Area 51 in Nevada in 1989, described a force he called "gravity wave A", and a researcher named Eric Weinstein wonders whether this could be a mangled name for a real idea from physics. Weinstein asks whether Lazar meant the "theta term", a piece of the mathematics of the theory of the strong nuclear force, or a related mathematical structure called Chern-Simons, noting that nobody he knows of has ever used the phrase "gravity wave A". If so, it would mean Lazar was repeating real but advanced physics he had only half understood.
lazar-s-holographic-book-at-s4-1980: In the 1980s, at a secret site called S4 near Area 51 in Nevada, a man named Bob Lazar is said to have seen a book whose stories rose off the page as holograms when it was opened. A man named Robert Bigelow repeats what Lazar told him: "It was some kind of a holographic book that as you opened up the pages, whatever the stories were became a hologram." If true, it would be an object far beyond any human technology of that time.
lazar-s-leak-as-a-planned-counterintelli: The UFO researcher Grant Cameron suggests that the secrets Bob Lazar went public with in 1988 and 1989 may have been a planned release by intelligence officials, not a true leak. Lazar is a man who said he worked on alien craft at a secret site in Nevada. In Cameron's view, the officials wanted the information out but deniable: "So they give it to somebody whose reputation is really not that good." Cameron offers this as his own reading and names no source.
lazar-s-missing-records-and-the-los-alam: Doubters said they could find no record that Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked as a scientist on government projects, ever worked at Los Alamos National Laboratory, the US government's weapons research lab in New Mexico. The journalist George Knapp answers that the doubters "were mistaken or were lying," because "a 1982 phone book from the lab lists Lazar right there among the other scientists and technicians." If so, Lazar did work at the lab, even though his other records seem to be missing.
lazar-s-ominous-feeling-inside-a-craft: Being inside a craft he says was not made by humans felt "real ominous, creepy," according to Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on such craft for the US government. He tells Michels that much of the feeling came from the blackness inside, which he says "doesn't look right." It is his own first-hand description of what such a machine is like from the inside.
lazar-s-work-on-power-and-propulsion-in-: Between about 1987 and 1989, Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft in Nevada, was assigned to power and propulsion, meaning how the craft were fuelled and how they moved, within a secret effort called Project Galileo. The filmmaker Jeremy Corbell mentions this in passing, repeating what Lazar has told him. If true, it would put Lazar at the heart of the effort to learn how such craft fly.
lazar-s-work-on-the-los-alamos-linear-ac: From 1980 to 1983, a man named Bob Lazar says he worked at Los Alamos, the New Mexico nuclear weapons lab, on its linear accelerator, a machine that fires particles down a straight track. He tells Michels he built high-voltage power supplies insulated by fiber optics, describing work he did himself, and it is told as proof of his background as a scientist.
lazar-said-in-1989-that-the-craft-were-i: Back in 1989, a man named Bob Lazar went public saying he had worked on alien craft at a secret Nevada site called S4, and that the craft were not crashed saucers but intact ones, with the Navy in charge rather than the Air Force. A researcher named Luigi Vendittelli tells this on the show, summarising what Lazar said. He tells it because it breaks from the usual story of crashed saucers picked up by the Air Force.
lazar-sees-aurora-take-off-at-area-51-19: Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft at a secret site in Nevada, says that in 1989 he watched an aircraft he calls Aurora, a rumoured secret US plane, take off at Area 51, the Air Force's secret test base in Nevada. He describes it as a large craft with two huge square exhaust vents that sounded more like a rocket than a jet. He tells it as something he saw himself, and it would mean the US was flying advanced secret aircraft there.
lazar-sees-flying-saucer-in-s4-hangar-19: Around 1988 or 1989, Bob Lazar says, he walked through a hangar door at S4, a secret site near Area 51, the restricted military test base in Nevada, and found a flying saucer inside. Lazar, who says he was hired to work there, tells it as his own experience: "This is technology that doesn't even exist." If true, it would mean the US government was holding a craft beyond any known human technology.
lazar-tells-lear-john-it-s-real-1988: Around December 6, 1988, Bob Lazar, a man who later said he worked on alien craft at a secret Nevada site, walked in on the pilot John Lear while Lear was writing checks and told him, "John, it's real." The Canadian UFO researcher Grant Cameron tells this on Michels' show as a story Lear told him in person. It would mean Lazar was confirming to Lear that he had seen real alien craft.
lazar-told-officially-he-was-radioactive: Bob Lazar, a man Michels spent two days with for one episode, says that at an official level he was told, 'You know, you're radioactive. We don't want to deal with you.' He tells this about himself. If true, it means officials chose to keep their distance from him on purpose.
lazar-was-only-a-radiation-badge-monitor: Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft at a secret site near Area 51, the closely guarded US Air Force test base in Nevada, was really just a radiation health monitor and never went to Area 51 at all. That is the claim of Eric W. Davis, a physicist who has worked on Pentagon-funded studies of these questions. Davis says Lazar "doesn't know what he's talking about" because he worked in the 1980s for a logistics company that serviced Los Alamos National Laboratory, a US nuclear weapons lab, and Area 51, which if true would undercut Lazar's whole story.
lazarus-fled-to-cyprus-and-his-tomb-in-n: Lazarus, the man the Bible says Jesus raised from the dead, is said to have gone to Cyprus and become its first bishop, and his tomb is supposedly in Nicosia. A guest named Ralph Larson tells this on the show as a piece of local lore, with a "supposedly" attached.
lbj-locks-himself-in-the-air-force-one-b: In Dallas in 1963, Lyndon B. Johnson is said to have locked himself in the bathroom on Air Force One, the president's plane. Dan Sheehan, a lawyer who has worked on several famous American cases, tells Michels he heard this from Jack Valenti, a Johnson aide who was with him at the time. The story is told as a glimpse of Johnson's state of mind in those hours.
lbj-pushes-earl-warren-into-the-commissi: After President Kennedy was killed in 1963, the people around President Lyndon Johnson lied to Earl Warren, the Chief Justice of the US Supreme Court, to get him to chair the Warren Commission, the panel that investigated the killing. The lawyer Dan Sheehan says this without naming a source, and adds that Allen Dulles, the former head of the CIA, was put on the panel and was the man who really ran it. If true, it would mean the official inquiry into Kennedy's death was steered from the start.
lbj-s-secret-mission-to-prime-minister-s: In 1964, Harold Malmgren, an adviser to American presidents, was told that President Lyndon B. Johnson wanted him to go on "a very secret mission to Tokyo" to see Japan's prime minister, Eisaku Sato, about textile exports. Malmgren tells Michels this himself and also names Christian Herter, and it shows how much the White House trusted him with sensitive work.
leading-hypnosis-questions-about-the-nin: In the 1970s Andrija Puharich, a scientist who hypnotized people, recorded sessions in which a group called the Nine, said to be a council of non-human beings, seemed to speak through his subjects. According to the researcher Greg Malatzi, who has listened to those recordings, Puharich can be heard putting the idea forward himself, asking things like "is it the nine". Malatzi raises it because it would mean the messages may have been prompted by the hypnotist rather than coming from anywhere else.
leaf-cutter-ant-mounds-resembling-a-meso: A researcher named Luke Caverns says that leaf-cutter ant mounds look strikingly like the layout of an ancient Mexican city, an idea that came to him while standing at the base of the Great Pyramid of La Venta, an ancient site in Mexico. He tells it from his own visit. He brings it up to suggest that ancient pyramid builders may have copied patterns from nature.
leak-pilots-fly-et-craft-through-psionic: According to a leak from 2023, pilots fly alien craft by linking a psionic person (someone said to have psychic abilities) to an advanced brain-machine interface: the pilot controls the machine, the machine steers the person's intentions, and those intentions steer the craft. Michels passes this on from an anonymous source who goes by "Joey is not my name", and also cites the former Marine Michael Herrera. If true, it would mean the craft respond to the mind and not to ordinary controls.
leak-psionic-assets-drugged-and-chipped-: A 2023 leak claims that people with supposed psychic abilities, called psionic assets, were drugged and implanted with chips for a secret program, and that after several years of this many of them died or fell into comas. Michels relays the claim from an anonymous leaker who posts as "Joey is not my name," and he also cites men named Michael Herrera and Jake Barber. In the leak's words: "After several years of this experimentation and drug use, a lot of these people die or slip into a coma."
leaked-pages-of-president-johnson-s-ufo-: A woman secretly photographed about a hundred pages of what may have been a 250-page UFO study done for President Lyndon Johnson in the 1960s. The UFO researcher Grant Cameron tells this without naming the woman or his source, and ties it to James McDonald, a scientist who looked hard into UFO cases in that decade. If true, it would mean a president commissioned a UFO study that was never made public.
leaked-phone-call-between-kit-green-and-: A leaked phone call between two men, Kit Green and K. Randall May, is said to show them talking about testing people who have had contact experiences. Dylan Borland, a guest who says a top official confided in him, says that in the call they talk about "testing veterans, military, government officials who have had experiences", and that they call these people "hybrids" in their own words. He dates it to 2017. He also brings up the famous psychic Uri Geller. Matthew Brown, who describes himself as a Pentagon whistleblower, also mentions the leaked call between Green and May, but only in passing. If true, it would suggest that people inside government quietly study those who say they have had contact.
leandro-finds-the-cave-of-tridactyl-bodi: In 2015, in the Nazca region of Peru, a man known only as Leandro says he tripped against a wall while walking, the wall fell apart, and behind it he saw a cave full of strange three-fingered bodies. He tells it as the moment he found them himself, and the find matters because such bodies, if real, would not belong to any known creature. Elsewhere his account shifts, describing instead an underground citadel with stone coffins.
leandro-meets-thierry-jamin-and-the-inca: In 2016 a witness named Leandro, tied to the strange three-fingered bodies found in Peru's Nazca region, met Thierry Jamin, a French explorer of lost Inca cities, and Jamin's research group, the Inca Institute, then took up the study of the find. Michels tells this himself, in his own words, in an episode about the Peruvian bodies, without naming a source.
leandro-s-changing-story-underground-cit: A man named Leandro, who says he found strange three-fingered bodies in the Nazca region of Peru, first described finding them in an underground citadel, almost like a temple, lying inside stone coffins. Michael Mazzola, a guest on an episode about these bodies, passes this on as Leandro's first version of the story, one that later changed into a story about a cave. The point of telling it is how the finder's own account shifted over time.
leandro-shows-visitors-the-wrong-cave-fo: In the Nazca region of Peru, where small three-fingered mummified bodies have been reported, a local man named Leandro has been taking visitors to a cave that may not be the real place the bodies came from, according to Michael Mazzola, a filmmaker who went there himself. Mazzola says his theory is that Leandro has been showing people this cave to make money, charging about three thousand dollars a visit. If he is right, the cave tourists see would tell them little about where the bodies were actually found.
lear-and-brown-lunch-across-the-street-1: A scientist named Townsend Brown, the subject of a documentary that calls him a CIA scientist who built UFOs, is said to have worked right across the street from the inventor Bill Lear in Santa Monica, California. Linda Brown, who speaks from her own memory, recalls that they "used to walk across" to a little diner right across the street, placing this in the 1960s. Michels tells it differently in another episode: he says Lear's office stood across from Brown's company, Guidance Technologies, in the 1950s, and he casts Lear as someone who witnessed Brown's experiments rather than a lunch companion. The two tellings agree on the closeness but not on the decade. The point, for the tellers, is that a well-known inventor may have seen Brown's work up close.
lear-and-jim-goodall-camp-out-at-area-51: In the 1970s, a man named John Lear and his good friend Jim Goodall, an aviation photographer and journalist, were camping out near Area 51 all the time, says Jesse Michels. Area 51 is the secret military test base in Nevada at Groom Lake, a dry lakebed. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, in a documentary about the inventor Townsend Brown, as a picture of how closely the two watched the base.
lear-and-the-stealth-fighter-story-given: In the 1980s, the pilot John Lear is said to have broken the story of the stealth fighter, a secret US jet built to avoid radar, but he did it by passing it to the Las Vegas journalist Ned Day. The filmmaker Jeremy Corbell tells this on Michels' show from what he was told, also naming the Las Vegas TV reporter George Knapp. The point of the story is that Lear really did have inside access to secret military projects.
lear-flew-drug-flights-for-cia-operation: In the 1980s, as the story goes, the CIA ran operations that involved flying drugs, using planes on dirt runways, and a veteran pilot named John Lear knew a lot about them and is said to have flown such flights himself. Jeremy Corbell, a filmmaker who covers UFOs, tells Michels this about Lear. It is part of why Lear is seen as a man with close ties to secret government work.
lear-s-soul-catcher-on-the-moon-theory: The claim is that a machine on the Moon catches human souls when people die. The filmmaker Jeremy Corbell passes on what he says he heard from John Lear, a pilot known for his UFO claims, and also names Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft. In Corbell's version, the Grays, small grey-skinned beings from UFO lore, run a "soul sucker" on the Moon that pulls up your soul when you die so it can be "reprocessed", unless the Grays steal it first. Michels brings it up more briefly in another episode, saying only that Lear spoke of "a soul catcher on the moon" and adding that Lear "also was kind of crazy". If it were true, death would not free the soul but send it to a recycling station run by alien beings.
lear-takes-ufo-claims-to-klas-knapp-chec: In the late 1980s, a man named John Lear walked into KLAS, a Las Vegas television station, with wild UFO claims, and the station's reporter George Knapp went and checked the files to see whether any of it held up. The filmmaker Jeremy Corbell tells this, passing on what was told to him, and also names Ned Day, another Las Vegas journalist of the time. It matters because this is how Las Vegas reporters were first drawn into the UFO story.
lear-tips-klas-about-f-117-1987: In 1987 a pilot named John Lear told Ned Day, managing editor at the Las Vegas TV station KLAS, about "this amazing plane that was invisible to radar" flying at Tonopah and Area 51, two secret test sites in the Nevada desert. That plane was the F-117, a stealth attack jet the Air Force was still keeping secret. George Knapp, a Las Vegas TV journalist who worked under Day, tells this as something his boss was told, and it suggests Lear really did know about hidden aircraft before the public did.
learning-of-david-grusch-from-program-in: The journalist Ross Coulthart says he first heard about David Grusch, a former intelligence official who later testified under oath about secret programmes said to hold recovered non-human craft, from people inside those programmes. Coulthart tells Michels this directly: "I learned about David Grusch from people in the program." If true, it would mean insiders were steering a witness toward going public before he came forward in 2023.
leaving-the-program-via-a-don-t-ask-don-: Sometime between 1990 and 1993, a former Air Force sergeant named Dan Sherman says he got out of a secret program at a place he calls Base 2 by writing a letter to his commander admitting he was gay. Don't Ask Don't Tell was the US military's policy that gay service members could serve as long as they kept quiet. Sherman tells Michels this himself, as part of his account of being hired by the National Security Agency, the US electronic spying agency, to talk to aliens, and it shows how he says he finally got away.
leaving-the-skywatcher-team-2025: Jordan Jose, a man who says he was taken into a secret UFO programme as a child, says he left Skywatcher, a private team that tries to call in and record UFOs, in July 2025. He tells it about himself. It matters to his story because it marks his break from the group as he moved toward speaking out.
lee-hively-shuts-the-door-on-jesse: Michels says that a researcher named Lee Hively, who works in extended electrodynamics, a fringe branch of the physics of electricity and magnetism, backed away when Michels tried to reach him. In one telling, a friend who helped make the contact "got in trouble," Hively "freaked out" and put what Michels thinks was a Navy press office on the email thread. In another, Michels says he was about to meet Hively in Colorado Springs when Hively got nervous and the door was shut in his face, which Michels offers as a sign that this kind of research is touchy.
leer-s-first-implant-removal-t-shaped-ob: In the 1990s in Thousand Oaks, California, a doctor named Roger Leir says he surgically removed his first suspected alien implant from a patient: a small T-shaped object set in tissue so tough it would barely cut. Leir, who did the surgery himself, tells Michels the object "looked like nothing that I had ever removed before" as a foreign body. If true, it would be physical evidence that something had been placed inside a person.
leer-s-investigation-of-magnetic-anomali: At a house in Fillmore, California, leaves and the trunk of an avocado tree had become magnetized, and there were strange magnetic fields all over. That is how Steve Colbern, a scientist who studies objects said to be alien implants in people's bodies, describes his own house to Michels, saying Roger Leir asked to come and check it and they found the anomalies together. He gives no date, and if true it would point to something unexplained at his home.
leer-s-neodymium-magnet-treatment-for-mi: Eric Mitchell says that Roger Leir, a doctor who removed objects he believed were alien implants from people's bodies, picked up a weak signal from his knee and suspected an implant there, beyond one in his arm. So, Mitchell says, Leir sent him a 100 pound neodymium magnet, a very strong permanent magnet, to treat it. He tells it as the patient, and it would mean he carried more than one implant.
lefschetz-recruited-for-nonlinear-group-: In the 1950s, Solomon Lefschetz, a great mathematician of shapes and spaces, was recruited to work alongside the physicist Louis Witten at the Glenn Martin Company, an aircraft maker, leading a whole group doing a hard kind of math called nonlinear mathematics, and that group was later moved to Brown University. The mathematician Eric Weinstein raises this as a question, without naming a source, and says he believes the move came when these programs were shut down, which would suggest the aircraft industry was quietly running serious physics research, perhaps on gravity.
left-alone-at-11-figure-on-the-roof-and-: In 1956, when he was 11 and home alone in Terrell Hills, a suburb of San Antonio, Texas, the writer Whitley Strieber, who says he has met nonhuman beings, says a figure was seen on the roof of the house. He says a policeman climbed up to look and seconds later came running down shouting, "There's no one there. There's no one there." Strieber tells it as one of the strange events of his own childhood.
legacy-crash-retrieval-program-should-ou: David Grusch, a former intelligence officer turned whistleblower, says he found a secret, long-running government program that recovers crashed craft of unknown origin and tries to copy how they work, and that he learned of it by interviewing witnesses he found "totally genuine". He says it cost him a lot of sleep, and he argues that "the program should want to out itself." Michels repeats the claim, adding that it was paid for with American taxpayer money, and the filmmaker James Fox says it has run "since at least World War II".
legacy-crash-retrievals-luring-craft-wit: Secret long-running programs, called legacy programs, are said to lure UFOs over the desert using psionics (people with claimed psychic abilities), sending a message like "hey we love you come see us" as a sort of honeypot, and then bring the craft down with directed energy weapons, which are beams of focused energy. Jordan Jose, who says he was taken into the UFO program as a child, tells this on Michels' show, crediting the journalist Ross Coulthart. If true, it would mean some crash recoveries were not accidents but traps.
legacy-program-as-a-dummy-program-that-k: A secret "legacy program", a long-running project said to be hidden inside an established American aerospace company, might be a dummy program built to hide something else. A researcher named Eric Weinstein offers this as an "alternate hypothesis" of his own, mentioning the work of a man named Bernie Haisch. He adds that "the last thing that you would want ever on such a program is a physicist," since a physicist might see through the cover.
legacy-program-insider-the-answers-are-i: An insider who worked on legacy programs, said to be long-running secret programs connected to UFOs, claims that most of the answers are in Crystal City, Virginia. A researcher who goes by the name UAPGerb says this unnamed friend, someone with firsthand knowledge, told him that "the answer to most of what you're looking for is in Crystal City, Virginia." If true, it would point to one specific place where the secrets are kept.
legacy-program-insiders-on-ufo-materials: People inside what is called the UFO "legacy program", a supposed long-running secret effort said to hold UFO materials, have their own way of talking about those materials. Michels says so himself, without naming who these insiders are, while debating a well-known skeptic. He offers it to suggest that how someone talks about the materials can show whether they really have inside knowledge.
legacy-program-insiders-tell-corbell-and: People inside so-called legacy programs, secret long-running government projects said to hold UFO material, keep telling journalists the same thing: "If you knew what I know," you would not push to make it public. Jesse Michels says this himself, passing on what he has heard from the filmmaker Jeremy Corbell and the journalist Ross Coulthart, who are said to talk with such insiders directly. If true, it would mean those who know the secret think it is too unsettling to share.
legacy-program-money-routed-through-ffrd: Money for long-running secret programs said to study UFOs is moved in ways that cannot really be tracked, including physical bales of cash carried to certain locations, according to a researcher who goes by the online name UAPGerb. He says he has spoken to witnesses who saw this, and that the money also passes through government-funded but privately run research centres, Defense Department labs and test ranges, and offices in Crystal City and Arlington, Virginia, which would explain how such programs could hide from oversight.
legacy-program-oral-tradition-of-agreeme: Inside a long-running secret US government effort known as the legacy program, people are said to pass down a story by word of mouth: that the United States once struck agreements with "a third party". Matthew Brown, a former Pentagon official who has come forward as a whistleblower, says he learned this is "the oral tradition in the legacy program itself". He leaves the third party unnamed, but if true it would mean the government made a deal with someone or something outside ordinary diplomacy.
legacy-program-recruits-psionic-assets-f: A so-called legacy program, a long-running secret effort that works with psionic assets (people with claimed psychic abilities) to lure UFOs, has been reaching out to people from native cultures around the world, especially young children who were never taught that such things are impossible. The parapsychologist Jeffrey Mishlove says this on Michels' show, passing on what he has heard without naming who told him. The idea is that untaught minds are better at making contact.
legacy-program-rumored-to-lure-ufos-with: There are rumours that the "legacy program", a supposed long-running secret US government UFO effort, uses set procedures and people with claimed psychic abilities to draw UFOs in. Michels passes this on himself as a rumour, without naming a source, in an episode about a man he says NASA studies because he seems to attract UFOs.
legacy-program-secrecy-kept-through-trus: A Pentagon whistleblower named Matthew Brown says the secrecy of the so-called legacy program, a hidden effort he traces back to the 1940s, is kept in part through 'trusted families' that pass the work down. He says this is something he has 'come to learn', which would mean the secret is held by bloodlines more than by any one office.
legacy-program-staff-take-on-dual-roles-: Inside a so-called legacy programme, a long-running secret effort said to study things of unknown origin, a scientist might also handle bits of accounting or staff management. That way nobody new has to be formally briefed in on the secret. An online researcher who goes by the name UAPGerb tells Michels he has been told this, as an example of how such a programme could stay so small and hidden.
legacy-programs-bait-ufos-with-nuclear-m: Secret long-running US UFO programs have used nuclear material, or even fake nuclear material, as bait to make UFOs show up. Jesse Michels tells this, once in his own words and once crediting Garry Nolan, a microbiologist at Stanford University, and in the second telling he widens it to Russia too, from the middle of the last century into the 1990s. If true, it would mean governments knew UFOs were drawn to nuclear material and used that to lure them.
legacy-uap-program-rotten-and-breaking-a: In the 2020s, a long-running secret government program on UAP, meaning unidentified anomalous phenomena, the official term for UFOs, is said to be rotten in more ways than one, in its bureaucracy and maybe morally too, and to be breaking apart as everyone defects from it. A researcher named Matthew Pines offers this as his own reading, without naming a source, describing the push for public disclosure as a sign of that collapse.
legacy-ufo-program-secrecy-rooted-in-the: An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb tells Michels that the secret, long-running "legacy" UFO programmes were built on the same secrecy rules as the Manhattan Project, the wartime effort to build the atomic bomb. He says the Atomic Energy Act of 1954 gave birth to much of their classification. He draws on what the whistleblower David Grusch has said, and if he is right, the nuclear secrecy system has been hiding UFO work all along. The act, which Congress passed on 30 August 1954, says the Atomic Energy Commission should "control the dissemination and declassification of Restricted Data in such a manner as to assure the common defense and security". It defines Restricted Data as information on atomic weapons and nuclear material, and it does not mention unidentified objects or any programme for them.
legacy-ufo-program-tests-psionic-ability: A secret effort tied to what some call the Legacy UFO program, a hidden government effort said to study unexplained craft, is said to have rounded up people from disaster zones such as Indonesia around 2009 and tested their psionic ability, meaning powers of the mind like telepathy. Michels says a man named Michael Herrera, who says he saw a 300-foot UFO in the Indonesian jungle, was later contacted quietly by someone claiming to be from that program, who explained what he had seen. Herrera himself names that contact as a man named Jake Barber, and says Barber called the program P3, which is not its real name, with the mind-gifted people carried in shipping containers. If true, it would mean a secret program was using vulnerable people as test subjects.
legend-of-range-four-harry-the-glowing-r: On the Indian Springs gunnery ranges in Nevada in the mid-1960s, there was a legend about a giant white radioactive horse called Range Four Harry. A man named Charles Hall, who says he spent three years among tall white aliens there, tells Michels about the legend from his own time on the ranges. In a related story, he ties the horse to the tall white beings moving in a fast "horse formation," which would mean the legend was really about them.
legend-of-the-virgin-mary-landing-on-ath: According to a legend told at Mount Athos, a Greek peninsula of Orthodox monasteries, the Virgin Mary was blown ashore there, and the Iveron monastery was built on the spot where she is said to have landed. Ralph Larson, presented on the show as a former CIA chief, tells this to Michels from his visit sometime between 2005 and 2007, passing on what a monk at Iveron told him.
leibniz-s-monadology-of-observing-entiti: The philosopher Leibniz proposed that reality is made of countless observing entities, which he called monads, and he set out the idea in a work called the Monadology. A researcher named Don Hoffman brings this up on the show and dates it to around 1700: "this is something that Livinets suggested back in 1700. He had this monodology." Hoffman uses it to show that his own idea, a universe built from minds that observe, has very old roots.
lemay-s-unauthorized-u-2-overflight-of-r: In 1962, Curtis LeMay, the general in charge of the US Air Force, ordered a U-2, a high-flying American spy plane, to fly over Russia to do the final retargeting for a nuclear strike, without approval from above. The lawyer Dan Sheehan tells it without naming a source, as an example of military leaders acting behind the president's back.
lennon-s-and-rfk-s-assassins-as-mk-ultra: Steve Colbern, a scientist who studies objects said to be alien implants, suggests that the men who killed John Lennon and Robert F. Kennedy were subjects of MK Ultra, a secret CIA mind-control research programme. He raises it in passing, as his own view. If true, it would mean both killings were shaped by government mind-control work.
leo-sprinkle-finds-benowitz-armed-and-sa: Sometime around 1977 to 1980, a researcher named Leo Sprinkle visited the Albuquerque home of a man named Paul Bennewitz and found him holding a rifle and a pistol, saying "they're coming" and telling Sprinkle to get into the house right away. The writer Greg Bishop tells this, passing on what Sprinkle told him. It is told to show how far Bennewitz's fear of visitors had gone.
leonardo-da-vinci-given-information-by-a: Leonardo da Vinci, the Italian Renaissance artist and inventor, was given his knowledge by beings from elsewhere, says a man named Kiran Ilum Xenov, the former president of a Russian republic who says he was taken by aliens in 1997. He names no source, and puts it alongside the Jewish holy writings known as the Talmud as other examples of knowledge handed to humans. If true, some of humanity's great leaps would have come from outside.
leonidas-consults-the-oracle-of-delphi-b: Before fighting the invading Persians, the Spartan king Leonidas went to the Oracle of Delphi, a priestess at a Greek temple who was believed to speak prophecies, to learn whether his people should go to war. A researcher named Luke Caverns retells this famous story without naming a source, as an example of ancient leaders seeking guidance from sacred sites.
leslie-kean-publishes-the-grusch-article: In 2023 the journalist Leslie Kean published the first article on David Grusch, a man who came forward with claims that the government was hiding UFO secrets, and that article set off everything that followed. Michels tells it, relaying what he heard, saying Kean had to publish in The Debrief, a small online news site, because Julian Barnes, a reporter at the New York Times, passed on it. It matters because it suggests the biggest paper held back the story.
leslie-kean-s-2017-new-york-times-ufo-st: In December 2017 the New York Times ran an article revealing that the Pentagon had quietly run AATIP, a small office that studied unexplained aerial reports, and it came with Navy videos of unknown objects. It was written by the journalist Leslie Kean with Ralph Blumenthal and, in one account, a third author named Helene Cooper. The UFO investigator James Fox calls it Kean's biggest story and one of the most popular the paper ever published. The skeptic Mick West says two videos, called Gimbal and FLIR1, came out with it and a third, GoFast, a little later. Michels says Luis Elizondo, who ran the Pentagon office, helped get it published through Kean, and he points out that every sighting in it was a Navy sighting. A Senate staffer named Kurt McConnell, who was there, says its concrete details about the office and about the 2004 Nimitz case, a Navy encounter off an aircraft carrier, are what started a Senate staff inquiry. The rest tell it as researchers looking back: the analyst Matthew Pines sees it as the start of UFOs slowly becoming semi-official, the UFO historian Richard Dolan calls it the breakthrough article, a researcher named John Blitch credits it to Kean and Elizondo together, and a NASA doctor named Greg Rogers says everything changed for him when he read it and saw the videos. To all of them it marks the moment the government was seen taking UFOs seriously.
leslie-kean-s-list-of-ordinary-explanati: The journalist Leslie Kean's 2010 book, UFOs: Generals, Pilots, and Government Officials Go on the Record, includes a list of ordinary, everyday explanations for UFO sightings. The skeptic Michael Shermer brings it up and reads from it while debating Michels. He uses it to show that even a writer sympathetic to the subject accepts that many sightings have ordinary causes.
letter-from-senator-cohen-thanking-the-r: A US senator named Cohen is said to have written to the Army's psychic spies in the 1980s, thanking them for saving the country $100 billion. Joe McMoneagle, one of those remote viewers, who used the mind to describe distant targets, tells Michels he has the letter in his file, and that a scientist on the programme, Dr. May, has one too. If true, it would mean psychic spying produced results the government valued.
letter-on-sullivan-s-death-sent-to-the-f: A US congressman named Eric Burlison says that he and others put together a letter about the death of a man called Sullivan and sent it to the FBI through the House Oversight Committee, the congressional committee that watches over government agencies. They were told it had been sent, he says, but later learned it "had never been received." Burlison links the matter to David Grusch, a former intelligence officer who has spoken publicly about hidden UFO programmes, and to an Office of Inspector General, a government watchdog office, and tells it as a sign that such inquiries can quietly go missing.
letter-to-the-pope-the-night-john-paul-i: A former CIA officer named Rolf Mowatt-Larssen says the Virgin Mary told him to write a letter to the Pope. He says he sent the letter to the Vatican and got a reply, and the letter is reproduced in his own book. The story is tied to the night Pope John Paul II died in 2005, which he spent at the Hotel Crillon in Paris, and its years run from 1998 to 2005. Mowatt-Larssen tells it as his own experience. In one telling he says only that the letter took him a long time to write and that he "should have done it the next day."
letter-to-william-shockley-recommending-: A letter from the mathematician Claude Shannon to the physicist William Shockley recommended a certain man, and Michels says it turns out the man being recommended was L. Ron Hubbard, the founder of Scientology. Michels tells this himself, from the letter, as a surprising link between top scientists of the 1950s and fringe figures.
letters-from-the-vatican-and-the-orthodo: A man named Ralph Larson says he sent his book to the Vatican, the headquarters of the Catholic Church, and to the leaders of the Orthodox Church in Istanbul, Turkey, and that both wrote back to him. He tells this himself on Michels's show in an episode with a former CIA officer, and he does not say what the letters said. If true, it would mean two of the oldest churches took notice of his book.
letters-to-mitre-rand-and-mit-lincoln-la: In 2026 a US congressman named Eric Burlison says he has been sending letters to MITRE, RAND and MIT Lincoln Laboratory, three private research organisations that do technical and defence work for the US government, asking about their involvement with UFOs. Burlison describes the letters himself on the show. Michels, telling it in an earlier episode, names only MITRE and says Burlison is now basically demanding that it open all its records on the subject. If these contractors hold such records, the letters would be a way for Congress to reach files kept outside the government itself.
levenda-as-the-model-for-johnny-depp-s-c: The character Johnny Depp played in The Ninth Gate, a film by Roman Polanski about the hunt for an occult book, was modelled on the author Peter Levenda. Levenda tells this about himself, passing on that "people around Depp were saying this actually happened." He links it to his own years in New York's occult book world.
levenda-s-archival-assessment-of-mj-12-a: The MJ-12 documents, papers said to describe a secret panel of top US officials set up to deal with crashed alien craft, look real, according to the author Peter Levenda. He says this after his own research in places like the National Archives and the Library of Congress, and he tells of discussing the papers with the physicist and UFO researcher Stanton Friedman at Contact in the Desert, a UFO conference. In his words, "Those documents to me look real." If they are real, the US government would have had a secret group managing alien crashes since the 1940s or 1950s.
levenda-s-unholy-alliance-on-nazis-and-t: The Nazis are said to have aligned themselves with the "tall whites" or "Nordics", tall pale beings described in some UFO accounts, and to have gained some sort of secret technology from them. Jesse Michels brings this up from the book Unholy Alliance by the writer Peter Levenda, in a conversation with the philosopher Jason Jorjani, as an example of how hidden knowledge and dark politics may have mixed in 1930s and 40s Germany.
levin-s-decapitated-flatworms-keep-their: At Tufts University, the biologist Michael Levin is said to have trained flatworms to react to particular stimuli, cut off their heads, and found that the worms still remembered what they had learned once the heads grew back. The researcher Rupert Sheldrake describes the experiment to Michels as evidence that memory may not be stored only in the brain.
levin-s-flatworm-experiments-read-as-mor: When the biologist Michael Levin's lab at Tufts University cut up flatworms, the pieces grew back into the whole worm, and the biologist Rupert Sheldrake says this happens through what he calls morphic resonance: the worms resonate with their own intact form from the past. Sheldrake gives this as his own reading of Levin's experiments, against the usual explanation, and if he is right it would mean living bodies get their shape from a kind of memory in nature, not only from their genes.
levitating-metallic-sphere-above-a-podiu: At the Naval Surface Warfare Center Crane, a Navy research base in Indiana, a metallic sphere the size of a basketball floated in the air above a podium. A man named Randy Anderson tells Michels he saw it himself in 2014; in another telling he dates it only to the 2010s and places it in what he calls the Off-World Technology area. If true, it would mean the Navy holds technology that defies gravity.
lewis-black-at-epstein-s-mansion-and-the: The comedian Lewis Black once walked into the New York mansion of Jeffrey Epstein, a wealthy financier, and found a marker board by the door covered in what looked like football plays. The story, as it is known, also involves Israel's defense minister. Fellow comedian Kurt Metzger retells it to Michels as "so interesting" and also names the comedian Bobby Slayton in connection with it, as a strange glimpse of who and what moved through Epstein's house.
lewis-chase-reports-to-air-force-headqua: In 1967, after unexplained events at Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana, where nuclear missiles were kept, an officer named Lewis Chase decided he had to report everything, and sent a telegram to Air Force headquarters and a report to the physicist Edward Condon, who was leading a university study of UFOs for the Air Force. Robert Salas, a former Air Force missile officer at the base, tells this from the official records. If true, the incident was reported to the top of the Air Force and to the scientists studying UFOs at the time.
liberation-times-piece-on-the-legacy-pro: Jesse Michels points to an article by the journalist Christopher Sharp in the Liberation Times, a news site, which he says lays out, perhaps for the first time, the chain of command of the secret US UFO programme, including the Department of Energy and the anti-weapons-spread side of the CIA, the US Central Intelligence Agency. Michels says the article names Glenn Gaffney, the CIA's director of science and technology, as one of the people who control access, which would put the programme inside the CIA's top ranks. He mentions it on two episodes, once noting that a guest had sent him the piece.
liberman-s-goldfish-centrifuge-and-freez: A Soviet scientist named Efim Liberman is said to have done an experiment in which he took four goldfish and put them through spinning in a centrifuge and freezing. Michels describes it himself, without naming a source, and mentions Liberman's relatives David and Daniil Liberman. He brings it up in a talk about whether the brain works like a quantum computer that can reach across time.
lidar-detected-pyramid-in-the-amazon-202: In 2022, scientists using lidar, a way of scanning the ground with lasers from the air to see through trees, found what they are certain is an enormous pyramid in the middle of the Amazon rainforest in Colombia. The writer Graham Hancock tells this, passing on what an archaeologist from the University of Exeter, whom he does not name, told him. If true, it would mean a large lost civilisation once built in the jungle.
lidar-reveals-lost-amazon-cities-and-geo: Laser scans taken from aircraft over the Amazon rainforest, a method called lidar that sees through the tree cover, are said to show that the region once held tens of millions of people, large cities with permanent populations, and huge, precise geometric earthworks that can only be seen whole from the air. The writer Graham Hancock describes these findings, connected to the second season of his television series Ancient Apocalypse. Jesse Michels later recalls hearing it from Hancock, though he mentions only the shapes cut into the land showing through the treetops, and it matters because it would rewrite what is known of the Amazon's past.
light-flashes-answered-by-a-stationary-l: Mario Woods, a former guard at a US nuclear missile site, says that in 1977 at the November-1 launch control facility, a missile control post in the Ellsworth Air Force Base field in South Dakota, he saw a light hanging still over the prairie and flashed his own lights at it, three times in one telling. After a minute or so, he says, it flashed back on and off, which sent shivers through him because it meant "they do see me." He tells it twice on the show as his own experience, naming fellow airmen Bill Hollman and Michael Johnson.
light-over-the-mesa-green-light-missing-: On a mesa in New Mexico near Aztec, where a flying saucer is said to have crashed long ago, a camper who is not named says a light in the sky made a sharp 90 degree turn and then was "instantly over us" as the group walked back to camp. The camper, who says they were there, goes on to describe a green light, a stretch of time no one could account for, and Apache military helicopters showing up afterwards. Told as a witness account, it would suggest that something unusual still visits the old crash site.
lights-around-ellsworth-nuclear-sites-be: In 1977, out among the nuclear missile sites around Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota, an Air Force guard named Michael Johnson says he saw strange lights before the night he and a fellow airman say they were taken aboard a craft. Johnson, who was there, tells Michels simply: "I just see lights out there around the nuclear sites and everything." It would place unexplained objects right beside American nuclear weapons.
