lights-filmed-near-brunswick-nuclear-pla: In 2024, lights were filmed in the sky right next to the Brunswick nuclear plant, run by the power company Duke Energy in Southport, North Carolina. Michels brings it up himself as an example of strange objects showing up near nuclear sites. Later he calls it "UAP activity", using the newer official term for UFOs, and credits a well-known UFO skeptic named Mick West for pinning down which facility it was.
lights-on-a-road-stretch-at-mattibu-gotl: On Gotland, an island in Sweden, there is a place called Mattibu where people go to a certain stretch of road to watch for lights that wander along it. The Swedish UFO researcher Clas Svahn tells Michels about the spot as local lore, with no date, as an example of places where odd lights keep being reported.
lilli-hornig-s-los-alamos-typing-intervi: When the chemist Lilli Hornig arrived at Los Alamos, the New Mexico laboratory where the atomic bomb was built in the 1940s, her job interviewers asked how fast she could type, and she answered, "They don't teach typing at Harvard." The physicist Kevin Knuth passes this on as something Hornig herself told him, and he tells it to show how a trained woman scientist was taken for a typist.
limestone-cube-erosion-study-on-the-smit: A freshly cut cube of limestone was once placed on the roof of the Smithsonian Institution, the US national museum in Washington, and its wearing away was measured over many decades. The researcher Randall Carlson describes this study without naming where it was published. He brings it up as a way to judge how fast stone erodes, and so how old weathered ancient stonework might be.
lincoln-lapaz-studies-green-fireballs-19: Starting in 1948, a meteor expert at the University of New Mexico named Lincoln LaPaz is said to have studied green fireballs in the sky that kept showing up near nuclear sites and nuclear test blasts. Michels tells this himself on several episodes. Once he credits it to the book UFOs and Nukes by a researcher named Robert Hastings, adds that Edward J. Ruppelt, then head of Blue Book (the US Air Force's UFO study of the 1950s and 60s), also recorded the fireballs, and calls them "intelligently moving". If true, it would mean something unexplained was paying attention to America's earliest nuclear work.
lincoln-s-niagara-speech-on-the-giants-w: Abraham Lincoln, the American president, is said to have written a speech praising Niagara Falls in which he spoke of an ancient race of giants. A researcher named Tim Alberino quotes it from memory without naming where he found it: "The eyes of that ancient species of giants whose bones fill the mounds of America have gazed upon Niagara as ours do." Alberino brings it up because, if Lincoln wrote it, it would show that talk of giant bones in America's ancient earth mounds was taken seriously in his time.
linda-bradshaw-saw-and-photographed-port: A portal is said to exist on Bradshaw Ranch near Sedona, Arizona, and the ranch's former owner, a woman named Linda Bradshaw, is said to have seen it and taken photographs of it. The Australian journalist Ross Coulthart tells this, passing on what Bradshaw reported. If true, the ranch would be a place where something opens onto somewhere else.
linda-brown-s-2014-review-of-tim-taylor-: Linda Brown, daughter of the inventor Thomas Townsend Brown, reviewed Launch Fever, an autobiography that a man named Tim Taylor published in March 2003, long before anyone knew who Taylor was. Michels tells it himself as a sign of an early tie between the Brown family and Taylor. In one telling he dates the review to 2014. In another he says only that she posted it on Amazon before Taylor became known.
linda-brown-sees-a-100-000-check-from-th: Linda Brown, the daughter of Townsend Brown, a scientist Michels links to early secret work on flying-saucer-like craft, remembers seeing a check for $100,000 from her father's foundation to Stanford while visiting him in Atherton, California, in the 1970s. Michels passes on her memory. It is told as a sign that Brown's research was being funded at a major research institution.
linda-jones-and-grass-growing-rapidly-wh: A woman named Linda Jones in Manchester, England, was running with her children away from a UFO when the grass began growing rapidly under her feet, according to a researcher named Mike Masters. Masters tells it without naming a source, as a sign that time itself may behave strangely near these objects, which fits his idea that the visitors are humans from the future.
linda-tripp-placed-beside-monica-lewinsk: The UFO researcher and activist Steven Greer claims that Linda Tripp was an Army intelligence and NSA person, NSA being the National Security Agency, the US government's eavesdropping and code-breaking agency, and that she was deliberately put right beside Monica Lewinsky, the young White House staffer at the centre of the 1990s scandal over President Bill Clinton. In Greer's telling the whole affair was set up: when Clinton was asked about it he lied under oath, and that led to his impeachment. Greer gives no source for this, and when he tells the setup a second time he talks only about the lie and the impeachment and leaves Tripp out, but the point either way is that Clinton was deliberately brought down.
little-a-le-inn-we-made-a-digital-copy-2: At the Little A'Le'Inn, a small roadside inn in the desert town of Rachel, Nevada, a woman told a UFO investigator named James Fox, in 2023, that of course they had made a digital copy of a VHS tape recorded by a man named Chuck Clark. Fox tells it first-hand, saying she answered him, "you think we're that stupid," which suggests the footage on the tape was guarded and kept safe in more than one form.
little-glowing-glass-like-being-with-a-t: Chris Bledsoe, a North Carolina man who says he attracts UFOs, says that in 2007, in the woods near his house, he met a small glowing being that looked like it was made of glass and bore a triangle. He tells it as the person who saw it. He gives it as part of his account of contact with non-human beings.
little-progress-reverse-engineering-reco: Whatever craft the United States has recovered since around 1947, it has not done much with them, like a caveman holding a USB drive. Michels offers this as his own opinion, not citing anyone, meaning that even if the objects exist, the technology may be far beyond our ability to understand it.
little-sophia-doll-used-to-map-children-: A doll called Little Sophia was, in this story, handed to children in Africa as a way to map their brains, sold under the idea of getting kids to think about science and technology. Kurt Metzger, a guest on an episode about the financier Jeffrey Epstein, tells it as something he was told by someone else, calling it "this ass doll" meant "to make him think about STEM", a term for science, technology, engineering and maths. He brings it up as a sign of hidden projects aimed at children's minds.
livelsberger-email-gives-area-51-coordin: A strange email that Michels attributes to a man named Matthew Livelsberger gives map coordinates for what it calls America's "gravitic propulsion" operations center, meaning craft moved by controlling gravity, and the coordinates point to Area 51, a secret military test site in Nevada. Michels brings up the 2025 email himself, without saying where he got it. He raises it as a hint that such technology exists and is kept at that base.
livermore-s-nuclear-pumped-space-laser-l: In the 1980s, scientists at Lawrence Livermore Laboratory, a US government weapons lab, are said to have worked on a space weapon, called Excalibur, that would set off a nuclear explosion in space and focus its energy through "a lens about the size of your thumbnail." John S. Herrington, who was US Secretary of Energy at the time, tells it from his own experience, saying the physicist Edward Teller "sat on my couch with me one afternoon" at the Department of Energy and showed him the lens. He offers it as a glimpse of how far secret government science reached.
living-at-arthur-young-s-institute-for-t: In the 1970s a man named Arthur Young 'showed up' in the life of the parapsychology researcher Jeffrey Mishlove and invited him to live at the Institute for the Study of Consciousness, a center Young had set up in Berkeley, California. Mishlove tells this from his own life, as the place where his work on the mind took shape.
living-crystal-orb-shown-in-psychologist: In 2008, in a local psychologist's office in Western New York, a boy was shown a crystal orb with a clear shell whose inside seemed alive. Jordan Jose, who says he was taken into a secret UFO program as a child, tells Michels he saw it himself. If true, it would mean someone was showing children strange living technology.
living-reptilians-from-a-crash-were-shot: Living reptile-like beings were taken from a crashed craft and then killed, according to an unnamed speaker in a clip played on the show. The speaker passes this on from someone else, and when asked what happened to the living reptilians from the crash, answers that they were deceased: "They were killed." If true, it would mean live non-human beings were recovered and deliberately put to death.
lizard-dna-sequences-pulled-for-the-hill: Martin Shkreli, a former drug company executive, says that in 2017, as a joke about the claim that Hillary Clinton was a "lizard person", an idea pushed by the British writer David Icke, he offered a bounty for her hair. To play it up, he says, he went to BLAST, a gene-sequence database run by the US government's National Institutes of Health, and pulled out lizard DNA sequences. He tells it as the one who did it.
lk-99-room-temperature-superconductor-pa: In 2023 a team in South Korea published papers on LK-99, a material they said was a superconductor at room temperature, meaning it carries electricity with no resistance and needs no extreme cooling. A guest named Jack says the team was so sure of its result that it put out one paper with six authors and a second with only three, because a Nobel Prize can be shared by at most three people. He tells it, from memory and without a source, as an example of how confident the researchers were.
local-name-of-the-nazca-region-meaning-a: The old local name of the Nazca region in Peru is said to translate as "laboratory for insemination and hybridization". Michels raises it in a 2025 episode with the guests Jay Anderson and Kurt Metzger, crediting a book from 2006 that he does not name. If true, it would suggest that the people who once lived there linked the place to the making of mixed or hybrid beings. The researcher and explorer Thierry Jamin, who studies the three-fingered mummies found in Peru, tells it in another 2025 episode with a different source and date. He credits "a little book published in 2004 by a local author from Nazca" that described various sites around Nazca. In Jamin's telling the name also takes in cloning. So the two tellers agree on the meaning but not on the book's date: Michels says 2006 and Jamin says 2004.
local-tribal-people-told-not-to-look-tow: For generations, members of the local tribe on the Ute Ouray reservation in Utah have been told not even to look in the direction of a nearby ranch famous for reports of strange happenings. Brandon Fugal, the businessman who owns the ranch, passes this on as what he says the tribe's people told him around 2016, and he offers it as a sign that the land was feared long before anyone studied it.
locked-car-found-open-repeatedly-fear-of: Around 1989 in Las Vegas, Bob Lazar says his locked car kept being found open, so often that he and a friend feared someone had planted a bomb in it. Lazar is a man who says he worked on alien craft for the US government. He tells it himself: "we would lock it and test the door and because it had happened before and go, 'All right, it's locked.'" He says the car was open again later anyway. The friend was Mario Woods. A researcher named Luigi Vendittelli passes on what Woods told him. Woods said he was with Lazar all the time and "we were scared that something was going to blow up." Woods said he was going through such hard times that he didn't care. He told Lazar to stay back and started the car himself. The story is told as a sign that someone was watching and pressuring Lazar after he spoke out.
lockheed-divests-a-craft-which-may-end-u: A recovered craft once held by Lockheed Martin, the big American defense contractor, was eventually passed on by the company and may now sit with a firm that has offices at Picatinny Arsenal, an army site in New Jersey. Jesse Michels credits the research to his friend Rob Jones, and links the handover to an investment firm he calls Veritas Capital. Jones, a researcher, tells it himself on two episodes and names the company now holding "that material" as one that sounds like Peraton, which would mean a private contractor today has custody of the object.
lockheed-engineer-this-is-what-you-learn: An engineer at Lockheed, the American aerospace company, is said to have told someone asking about UFOs, "you're not supposed to learn about this. This is what you learn about when you die." The writer Peter Levenda tells it, taken from a book by a man named John B. Alexander, and says it was not Lockheed's Ben Rich, who was more open on the subject, but another man who was against talking. It suggests insiders treated the subject as off limits for life.
lockheed-executive-admitted-to-fravor-th: A UFO researcher named Steven Greer says that an executive at Lockheed, a major American aircraft and weapons maker, recently admitted to the Navy fighter pilot David Fravor that the Tic Tac belonged to the company. The Tic Tac is the white oval object, shaped like the mint, that Fravor reported chasing. Greer is passing on what he says Fravor was told. If true, it would mean the most famous Navy UFO sighting was a secret human-made craft.
lockheed-martin-coherent-matter-wave-bea: The defense company Lockheed Martin holds a patent for something called a coherent matter wave beam, according to a guest named Dave Rossi, who describes it without pointing to the document itself. He says the patent makes use of the Aharonov-Bohm effect, an effect in quantum physics. Rossi raises it as a sign that a major weapons maker is working on very unusual physics.
lockheed-martin-divesting-ufo-material-t: In 2008, according to the journalist George Knapp, the defence contractor Lockheed Martin made a deal to hand over strange material it had kept at a facility in California to a company run by the businessman Robert Bigelow. Knapp says he confirmed on the record that Bigelow and a colleague from a Pentagon-funded study of unexplained phenomena met Lockheed's senior executives to work out the deal, and that the material "was not made here." Michels repeats the claim, noting that Knapp has said it before Congress, because it would mean a major contractor was holding material from somewhere other than Earth.
lockheed-martin-vp-tried-to-bring-the-cr: Around 2008 to 2010, a vice president of Lockheed Martin, the large US defence company, is said to have tried to move craft and hardware the company obtained long ago "out the back door", meaning out of secret hands and into the open. The filmmaker Jeremy Corbell tells this, repeating what he says he learned from people involved in a government-funded study of the subject. If true, it would mean a major defence contractor holds unknown craft.
lockheed-s-quantum-magnetometer-modelled: Around 2016, the American aerospace company Lockheed is said to have studied how birds such as robins sense the earth's magnetic field, through a protein called cry4, and to have copied that physics in a quantum sensor it calls the dark ice magnetometer. A researcher named Deep Prasad tells this without naming a source, as an example of engineers learning from nature at the quantum level.
lockheed-skunk-works-and-the-ufo-topic-b: Ben Rich, president of Skunk Works, the most secretive division of the arms maker Lockheed Martin, used to call UFOs "unfunded opportunities," according to Michels. He ties this to emails from 2016 and 2017 published by WikiLeaks, a site that releases leaked documents, which involve the Skunk Works executive Rob Weiss and the musician Tom DeLonge, who was pushing for UFO disclosure. Michels tells it himself as a sign that the company took the subject seriously.
lockheed-skunk-works-response-to-grusch-: In 2023, after a former intelligence officer named David Grusch testified about UAPs (unidentified anomalous phenomena, the government's term for UFOs), the defense company Lockheed Martin answered that "questions about UAPs are best answered by the federal government." The response was tied to Skunk Works, Lockheed's secret advanced aircraft division. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, and calls the reply "pretty telling", because he hears it as a company declining to deny any part in the matter.
lockheed-ttsa-and-killing-the-schumer-bi: Robert Weiss, director of Skunk Works, the secret aircraft division of the defence company Lockheed, was connected to Tom DeLonge, a rock musician, and his UFO research company To The Stars Academy, set up in 2017. Michels offers this as his own theory, without naming a source, and ties it to a later fight over a proposed law from Senator Chuck Schumer to release government UFO records, naming the congressman Mike Turner. It would suggest the defence industry had a hand in how UFO secrets were handled.
lockheed-vp-jim-ryder-the-veil-thinning-: Jim Ryder, a vice president of space systems at the aerospace and defence company Lockheed Martin, is said to have claimed that "the veil is thinning," the old idea that the barrier between our world and some other realm is wearing away, and that this is literally the Earth's magnetosphere, the magnetic field that shields the planet, which is weakening right now. A member of the show's crew, who is not named, repeats what he says Ryder said, which would turn a mystical phrase into a physical event.
loeb-s-artificial-light-sail-theory-of-o: The Harvard scientist Avi Loeb argues that 'Oumuamua, an object that passed through our solar system from interstellar space in 2017, may be an artificial light sail: a thin, built sheet pushed along by sunlight. On two visits years apart, Loeb says that every natural explanation put forward for its odd behaviour "invoked a rock of a type that we've never seen before", which to him makes a made object the simpler answer; he credits the case to his book Extraterrestrial. If he is right, it would be a piece of alien technology seen passing by Earth.
logan-paul-offers-chuck-clark-100-000-fo: The internet celebrity Logan Paul offered a man named Chuck Clark, in remote Arizona, 100,000 dollars for a VHS tape he holds, and Clark turned him down. The UFO filmmaker James Fox tells this from what he was told. It shows how much the tape is thought to be worth, and how firmly Clark keeps it.
logger-saw-the-same-craft-in-the-area-19: In the 1970s, a logger working near the Allagash Waterway, a stretch of wilderness rivers in Maine, is said to have seen the same craft that others reported in that area. A guest named Charlie Foltz, who presents himself as a witness to events there, passes on the logger's account second-hand. He tells it because a separate witness would back up what he and others say they saw.
london-bridge-at-lake-havasu-has-childre: London Bridge, the old bridge moved from England to Lake Havasu, Arizona, in the 1960s, is said to have children walled up inside it, and that this is why it was brought over. A guest named Kurt Metzger tells this, passing on what a man named Nathan Reynolds told him, and adds that the Knights of Columbus, a Catholic men's organization, hold the controlling interest. If true, it would make the bridge a hidden site of a dark crime.
london-drought-and-mishlove-s-first-meet: In the summer of 1976, during a drought in London, a man named Ted Owens was asked to end the drought, and was then invited to a conference at the University of London sponsored by the Paris Science Foundation. The parapsychologist Jeffrey Mishlove tells it first hand, because that conference is where he met Owens and became his friend. He tells it as the start of his own time with a man said to have unusual powers, a story he connects to an article in Psychic magazine.
long-delay-echoes-behind-sagan-s-contact: In the 1920s and 30s, when radio was new, operators are said to have heard long delay echoes: their own signals coming back after a strange pause. Michels tells this himself and suggests that the astronomer Carl Sagan was thinking of these echoes in his novel Contact, about a signal from space. If he is right, it would mean Sagan saw in them a possible hint of someone out there answering.
long-delay-echoes-rise-when-earth-moon-l: Radio operators have sometimes heard their own signals come back seconds after sending them. These are called long delay echoes, and one study supposedly found more of them whenever a certain point in space was above the horizon. That point is the Earth-Moon L5 point, a spot along the Moon's orbit where an object can stay parked because the pulls of Earth and Moon balance out. Michels mentions the study without naming it, and it matters because it would hint that something sitting there is bouncing the signals back.
long-delay-radio-echoes-heard-by-norwegi: In 1927, shortwave radio operators in Norway began to notice something odd: radio signals seemed to come back as echoes after a long delay. Michels tells this himself and cites a man named Karl Stormer in the story. He brings it up in an episode with the astronomer Beatriz Villarroel about the idea that many unknown objects may be circling Earth, where strange echoes like these could hint at something out in space.
long-distance-healing-in-australia-over-: Chris Bledsoe, a man who says he has had many UFO encounters, says he has seen people healed from far away, including someone in Australia, over the phone. He tells it as something he has witnessed himself, saying, "I've seen it too many times." If true, it would mean healing can work at a distance, with no one in the room.
long-island-crash-near-moriches-bay-1989: Something is said to have crashed near Moriches Bay on Long Island, New York, in about 1989. The UFO historian Richard Dolan brings it up only briefly, without naming a source and unsure of the year ("I think it was supposed to be 1989"), as one more case of a craft said to have come down and been recovered.
lonnie-zamora-never-the-same-after-socor: The wife of Lonnie Zamora, the police officer who reported an encounter at Socorro, New Mexico, in 1964, is said to have told the documentary filmmaker James Fox: "I don't know what happened when he looked at that creature, but he was never the same." Fox recalls her saying this to him in person, and he tells it to show that whatever Zamora saw changed him for good.
lonnie-zamora-s-socorro-landing-1964: On April 24th, 1964, the story goes, a police officer named Lonnie Zamora in Socorro, New Mexico, saw an egg-shaped craft land, and afterwards found burnt plants on the ground where it had been. The documentary maker James Fox has investigated the case himself. He leans on the investigator Ray Stanford and on Stanford's account, Socorro Saucer in a Pentagon Pantry, and he also mentions the astronomer J. Allen Hynek. Fox goes further than most: he says Zamora "locked eyes with one of these beings." Michels brings the case up in several episodes in his own words. He calls Zamora "this police officer" who "sees this egg actually land, sees burnt vegetation in the area," and in another episode he says the craft "allegedly had little legs." If it is true, it is a landing seen up close by a police officer, with marks left on the ground.
lonnie-zamora-sighting-near-nuclear-site: In 1964 a police officer named Lonnie Zamora reported a strange craft near Socorro, New Mexico, and Michels says the spot was only a couple of miles from sensitive nuclear sites. He raises it himself, without naming a source, in a debate with a skeptic, as part of a pattern of sightings near nuclear facilities, which would suggest the craft take an interest in nuclear weapons.
looking-for-city-lights-on-proxima-b-202: The Harvard astronomer Avi Loeb says that in 2021 he wrote a paper with a Stanford undergraduate arguing that the James Webb Space Telescope, a large new space telescope, could look for city lights on the dark side of Proxima b, a planet circling the star nearest to our Sun. Loeb describes his own work. If such lights were found, it would point to a civilization living there.
lookout-mountain-cia-facility-in-laurel-: Lookout Mountain, in the Laurel Canyon area of Los Angeles, is said to have been a facility of the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency, tied to a long story of drugs, government, the Vietnam War and spying in the 1960s. A researcher named Eric Weinstein says this, agreeing with a point the host had made ("as you point out"), and names no other source.
lookout-mountain-laboratory-as-manhattan: Lookout Mountain Laboratory, a secretive facility in Laurel Canyon in Los Angeles, was the film laboratory for the Manhattan Project, the American wartime effort to build the atomic bomb, according to a researcher named Paul Schatzkin. He says this has only come out as more information has been released, though he does not name what was released, and it would mean the site's ties to secret government work go back to the war years.
loose-stone-samples-tested-in-israel-tur: In 2012, loose stones taken from the Baltic Sea anomaly, a strange shape on the floor of the Baltic Sea, were tested in Israel and found to be basalt, a volcanic rock. A treasure hunter named Dennis Asberg, who was involved in exploring the site, relays the result as he was told it: "basalt, volcanic stones they found." The finding matters because it bears on what the object on the seafloor is made of.
looting-at-eridu-and-the-campaign-to-sav: Eridu, an ancient city site in southern Iraq, is being stripped by looters, according to Matt LaCroix, a writer who researches ancient civilisations. LaCroix says he found many photographs, taken over the last ten years, of locals going into the site and pillaging it, and he tells it as the start of an effort to save the place before what it holds about the distant past is lost.
lore-of-lockheed-and-northrop-crash-retr: There is a lot of lore, Michels says, that aerospace companies like Lockheed and Northrop have recovered crashed UFOs without proper supervision or oversight from the government. He offers this himself as background in an episode with a former head of the National Security Agency, the US spy agency for communications, and names no source. If true, private companies would hold such material out of the public's and the government's reach.
lorentz-regauging-of-maxwell-s-quaternio: In the early 1900s, the physicist Hendrik Lorentz is said to have carried out what Dave Rossi calls a "symmetrical regauging" of James Clerk Maxwell's equations of electricity and magnetism. Maxwell had written those equations in quaternions, a four-part kind of number, and in Rossi's account Lorentz reworked them into a simpler form. Rossi, a man who says aliens taught him advanced physics, tells this to Michels without naming a source, as a point where he believes part of Maxwell's original physics was lost.
lorie-barnes-visited-by-blue-dwarfs-whil: In 1954, a woman named Lorie Barnes was visited by small blue beings while she was pregnant, and they told her: "We're interested in the girl child you're carrying." The writer Whitley Strieber, known for his accounts of his own encounters with such beings, passes on the story as she told it to him. He tells it as an example of visitors taking an interest in particular families across generations.
los-alamos-disinformation-as-a-model-for: During the 1940s, the secret lab at Los Alamos, New Mexico, where the atomic bomb was built, made misleading filings so that no one would learn that plutonium and uranium were the two radioactive elements it was focused on. The mathematician Eric Weinstein tells this without naming a source, linking it to the chemist Harold Urey, as a model for how secret programs today may hide what they are really working on.
los-alamos-hiring-during-a-nuclear-arms-: Los Alamos, the New Mexico weapons laboratory, is said to be hiring hard in the 2020s because, in the words of a woman the writer Greg Bishop quotes, "There's a huge nuclear arms race going on right now, and they're building bombs like mad." Bishop passes on what she told him and does not name her, and he tells it as a sign of how busy the bomb work has become again.
los-alamos-insider-surfaces-that-solid-o: An insider at Los Alamos, the US nuclear weapons laboratory in New Mexico, is said to have described metal surfaces that could be worked so that solid things could be passed through them, in or out. Mario Woods, an Air Force veteran who speaks of being abducted, repeats this as something an unnamed insider told him, in the context of studying recovered craft. If true, it would mean the lab handles materials that behave like nothing ordinary metal can.
los-alamos-insider-their-propulsion-syst: Someone connected to Los Alamos, the US government weapons laboratory in New Mexico, is said to have claimed that the engines of non-human craft are not built but grown. A guest named Mario Woods relays this from a man he does not name, quoting him as saying: "Their propulsion systems are not built. They're grown." If true, it would mean the craft are made by something closer to biology than to engineering.
los-alamos-tiger-team-security-test-fail: Around 1990, a so-called tiger team, a group sent in to test security by trying to break through it, came to Los Alamos, the US nuclear weapons laboratory in New Mexico, and the lab "failed so horribly". Bob Lazar, a man known for claims that he worked on secret government projects, tells it as something he was told. It would mean that one of the country's most sensitive sites had weak defences.
los-alamos-working-group-concludes-ufos-: A working group at Los Alamos National Laboratory, the US government's nuclear weapons laboratory in New Mexico, is said to have decided sometime in the 2000s that UFOs are interdimensional objects "coming down into a lower dimensional plane." A guest named Jay Anderson tells this second-hand, as something a man he names as Oke Shannon told him, and he ties the idea to Flatland, a book about creatures living in a flat, two-dimensional world. If true, it would mean government scientists had decided these objects come from outside our ordinary three dimensions.
los-alamosbattelle-nitinol-contract-of-1: In 1949 Los Alamos, the US nuclear weapons laboratory in New Mexico, signed a contract with the Battelle Memorial Institute, a private research institute, tied to work on Nitinol, a nickel and titanium metal that springs back to its original shape. Michels says this himself, without naming the document's wording, and calls it some of the most interesting evidence he has found for Roswell, the reported 1947 crash of an unknown craft in New Mexico, because shape-recovering metal is said to have been found in the debris.
loss-of-the-marine-sulphur-queen-1963: The Marine Sulphur Queen, a ship that left port in Port Arthur, Texas, sank and was lost at sea in 1963. Mario Woods, a former guard at a nuclear site, tells Michels it was the first ship he ever set foot on, as a boy of five, which ties him personally to a well-known sea mystery.
lost-hiker-meets-a-woman-who-went-missin: A hiker lost in a forest in the United States is said to have met a woman whose description matched someone who had gone missing in that same place a decade or more earlier. The researcher Jason Jorjani tells it on the show, passing on what a man named David Pitus told him, and ties it to Missing 411, a collection of cases about people who vanish in the wild. If it were true, it would mean some people who disappear out there do not simply die but turn up somewhere, years later.
lost-submarines-like-the-uss-connecticut: Michels says in passing that there have been a lot of lost submarines, and he gives the USS Connecticut, a US Navy submarine, as an example of a case where "we don't really know what happened." He tells it himself, without naming a source, as a hint that strange things go on in the deep ocean.
lot-s-angelic-visitors-extract-him-befor: In the Bible, angels come to the city of Sodom to lead a man named Lot and his family out before the city is destroyed. A researcher named Tim Alberino tells it on the show, saying that Abraham's nephew Lot "encounters angelic beings who come to extract him and his family before the destruction of Sodom." Michels tells it himself in shorter form: "Two angels walk into Sodom the night before the fire falls." He gives the number and the timing but does not mention the rescue. The King James Bible, published in 1611, tells it in Genesis 19: "there came two angels to Sodom at even," they say "the LORD hath sent us to destroy it," and in the morning they took Lot, his wife and his two daughters by the hand "and set him without the city." Then "the LORD rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah brimstone and fire from the LORD out of heaven." On the show it is told as an ancient account of nonhuman visitors stepping into human affairs.
lou-baldin-s-day-aboard-a-ship-with-milt: A man named Lou Baldin says that in a park near where he lived, sometime in the 2000s, he was paralyzed and floated up into a ship, where he spent a day with a being called Milton. The UFO researcher Richard Dolan passes this on from what Baldin told it, and points to Baldin's account, A Day with an Extraterrestrial, as where it is set down. Dolan's words for it: "He's floated, levitated into a ship."
lou-baldin-s-in-league-with-a-ufo-1947: A man named Lou Baldin wrote a book called In League with a UFO, which the UFO historian Richard Dolan says came out in the mid 1990s. Dolan mentions the book in passing, without naming any other source, as one man's written account of his own UFO experiences, and he says little more about what is in it.
lou-elizondo-told-kirkpatrick-where-the-: A secret film said to show a UFO shooting down a dummy nuclear warhead during a missile test off Big Sur, on the California coast, in the 1960s is said to have been seen by Lue Elizondo, a former Pentagon official who ran a small office that studied unexplained aerial reports. A researcher of UFO sightings at nuclear bases named Robert Hastings gives the fullest version. He says a Senate staffer named Kurt McConnell emailed him to say he had driven Elizondo to his interview with AARO, the Pentagon's current UFO office. On the way back, McConnell wrote, Elizondo said he had told Sean Kirkpatrick, the head of that office, that he had seen the Big Sur film. Michels repeats the core of it twice, simply saying Elizondo says he has seen the video, without the drive or Kirkpatrick. Every teller is passing on what Elizondo is said to have said. If true, it would mean the film still exists inside the government and that officials were told about it.
low-s-handwritten-note-hippler-blames-em: In 1967, Robert Low, a leader of the Condon Committee, a government-funded UFO study of the late 1960s, wrote a handwritten note saying that an Air Force colonel named Robert Hippler had told him the missile shutdowns of that period were caused by EMP, a burst of energy from a nuclear blast that can knock out electronics. Robert Salas, a former Air Force officer who was involved in the missile events, describes the note, saying Low "talked to" Hippler and Hippler "told him" this. He also credits Roy Craig, who worked on the study. Michels comes to the same claim through a 2025 Wall Street Journal article, which he says quotes Hippler blaming "EMP fallout from a nuclear detonation." For Salas, the note matters because it shows how officials explained the shutdowns at the time.
luc-montagnier-on-electromagnetic-inform: Near the end of his life, the French Nobel Prize winner Luc Montagnier said that electromagnetism plays an important part in how information is carried and passed along within DNA. Michels brings this up himself, without naming a source, in a conversation about synchronicities and prophetic dreams.
lucille-ball-hears-the-radio-through-a-t: The actress Lucille Ball said that after getting a tooth filling she began hearing radio music in her head while driving. In a clip played on the show, she says it was around World War Two near a radio station in Los Angeles: she first thought her car radio was on, then realised the music was coming from her mouth, and she credits the comedian Buster Keaton in the story. Michels repeats it twice, citing The Telepathy Tapes, a documentary series about children said to read minds, and adds that she was on an overpass, as a sign that the body can pick up signals.
luckman-book-s-alien-drawing-matches-a-b: A drawing of an alien in a 1970s book called UFOs: Past, Present and Future, made by Bob Emenegger and Allan Sandler, is said to match an old image held in the British Museum in London. The researcher Grant Cameron repeats this from a man named Michael Luckman, and says he has sent Michels the British Museum photo, which shows "exactly the being" that was drawn. If true, it would mean the book's alien was modelled on something far older.
lue-elizondo-s-book-on-anti-gravity-bubb: A book by Lue Elizondo, a former Pentagon official who ran a small office that studied unexplained aerial reports, is said to explain why UFOs come in the shapes they do: they would carry some kind of anti-gravity device. A US congressman named Eric Burlison says the book describes it this way, so that the shapes "seem to make sense" once you picture a device that cancels gravity around the craft. A former scientist with DARPA, the Pentagon's advanced research agency, named John Blitch, also points to the book. He says it shows a "warp bubble", a pocket of bent space around a craft, which Elizondo had discussed with a physicist named Hal Puthoff. Both men are summarising the book from their own reading, not from anything they saw. The idea matters because it would offer a physical reason for the odd forms witnesses report.
lue-elizondo-s-superiors-who-saw-the-phe: Some of the bosses of Luis Elizondo, a man who worked in a small Pentagon office that studied unexplained aerial reports, are said to have seen the UFO phenomenon as demonic. The account comes from a former nuclear security guard named Mario Woods, who says he found the passage in Elizondo's own book: "I found the part where he talks about some of his superiors where they had this demonic" view. If true, it would mean that people high in the Pentagon read the phenomenon in religious terms.
luigi-s-company-attacked-court-demand-fo: Luigi Vendittelli, a researcher from Montreal who has worked with Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft for the US government, says that in the 2020s his company was "attacked ferociously for over a year and a half" until it fell to zero. He says that along the way a court document demanded his communications with Lazar. Vendittelli tells it as his own experience, a sign to him that being close to Lazar drew hostile attention.
luis-alvarez-muon-scan-of-khafre-pyramid: In the 1960s, the story goes, the physicist Luis Walter Alvarez, a senior figure in the Manhattan Project, the US wartime programme that built the atomic bomb, took a team to Egypt to scan the inside of a pyramid at Giza using muons, particles from space that pass through stone and can reveal hidden rooms. The researcher Luke Caverns says the team scanned the Khafre pyramid, the second great pyramid at Giza, in the 60s. Michels tells it himself on two episodes, once saying Alvarez, who is shown in the film Oppenheimer, x-rayed the pyramids in the 50s, and once dating it to the 70s, without naming which pyramid. It is told as the first serious attempt to look for hidden chambers inside the pyramids.
luke-s-theory-old-kingdom-pharaohs-were-: The kings of Egypt's early Old Kingdom period were never buried in their pyramids at Giza; their real tombs lie in the south, near the ancient site of Abydos. That is the theory of a researcher who calls himself Luke Caverns, who gives no source but says a later pharaoh, Amenemhat III, seems to have known this. If right, it would mean the pyramids were built for some purpose other than tombs.
luke-s-visit-down-the-osiris-shaft: A pyramid researcher named Luke Caverns says he went down the Osiris shaft, a deep underground passage beneath the causeway at the Giza pyramids in Egypt, where, as he puts it, "it drops down." He tells it as his own visit, made with a guide who goes by the name Land of Kem and showed him around. He brings it up as part of his case that the pyramids are not what people think.
lunar-dust-prevented-a-fourth-eva-for-ap: Moon dust caused the Apollo astronauts so much trouble that they could not manage a fourth EVA, a walk outside the spacecraft on the Moon's surface, according to a NASA engineer named Charles Buhler. He mentions it in passing on the program that landed Americans on the Moon between 1969 and 1972, as a sign of how hard the dust is to deal with.
lunar-laser-reflectors-1969: Equipment left on the Moon by astronauts between 1969 and 1972 can still be reached by lasers fired from Earth, according to a man named only as Ben, whose words are passed on by a guest named James Fox. Fox quotes him as saying "we can put a laser on some of the things that we left on the surface of the moon." It is told as evidence that the Moon landings left real, checkable traces behind.
lunar-layers-are-inverted-like-an-excava: The claim is that the moon's lower layers of sediment are newer than the layers above them, the reverse of what you would expect, and that this pattern looks like an excavation site, as if someone had dug material up and piled it back in reverse order. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, in an episode built around the idea that the moon could be an artificial object.
lunar-mascons-forced-apollo-orbit-correc: The Apollo spacecraft, which carried NASA's astronauts to the Moon, ran into trouble while orbiting the Moon and preparing to land, according to a researcher who appears as a guest without being named. The story behind it is that patches of unusually dense material under the lunar surface, called mascons, pulled unevenly on the craft and forced corrections to their orbits, which the guest raises as a sign the Moon's interior is stranger than expected.
lunar-transient-phenomena-outgassing-and: Strange short-lived events have been seen on the Moon for centuries, from gas venting out of the surface to unexplained lights. These are known as lunar transient phenomena. The researcher Randall Carlson describes them in a 2025 episode. He says there are "hundreds of examples of the moon outgassing carbon dioxide, outgassing water vapor, things like that." If true, it would mean the Moon is less dead and unchanging than people usually picture it. An unnamed researcher in a 2026 episode tells it from another angle. That guest says NASA, the US space agency, keeps "this archive of transient lunar phenomena dating back hundreds of years", gathered from amateur and professional astronomers on Earth. In that guest's version many of the reports cluster around Aristarchus, a bright crater on the Moon. Neither teller says he saw these events himself.
lunch-with-stubblebine-about-buchanan-s-: Sometime in the 1980s, an Army sergeant named Lyn Buchanan says he was out at lunch with Albert Stubblebine, an Army general he calls Bert, when the general asked him straight out: "What is your clearance?" Buchanan tells this first-hand to Michels as the moment that drew him into secret work beyond his security level, the kind of work that led him to say he once operated a UFO with his mind.
lunch-with-von-daniken-attended-by-joe-r: Jesse Michels once set up a lunch with the writer Erich von Däniken, and the podcaster Joe Rogan came to it. Michels mentions this himself, as something he took part in, in a 2022 episode about mushrooms. He says nothing more about what was said at the table.
lundahl-s-cuban-missile-crisis-briefing-: In 1962, during the Cuban missile crisis, the standoff over Soviet missiles in Cuba, a man named Arthur Lundahl is said to have briefed President John F. Kennedy at the White House, and to have received an award from Kennedy for that work. A researcher named Grant Cameron mentions this briefly, without naming a source.
lyn-buchanan-army-psychic-spy-behind-the: The character Cassidy in The Men Who Stare at Goats, a story about the US Army's psychic soldiers, is based on a real man named Lyn Buchanan, according to Jesse Michels. Michels describes Buchanan as a famous Army psychic spy and remote viewer, meaning someone trained to describe faraway places or targets using only the mind. Michels says he had just interviewed Buchanan himself, and he names a man called Albert Stubblebine alongside him, which would mean the Army really did run psychics as spies.
lyn-buchanan-brought-to-an-underground-s: A man named Lyn Buchanan was reportedly taken to a deep underground facility in California where a collision between an airliner and a UFO had been rebuilt piece by piece, the way the FAA, the US agency that oversees air travel, rebuilds crashed planes to study them. The philosopher Jason Jorjani tells this, passing on what Buchanan said. If true, it would mean a passenger plane once hit an unknown craft and the wreckage was kept secret.
lyn-buchanan-met-by-three-nordic-men-at-: Lyn Buchanan, a man who trained as a remote viewer (someone taught to try to see distant places with the mind alone), says he was confronted by three men at a diner where he eats regularly, men described as "Nordic," the tall, fair-haired visitors of UFO lore. The philosopher Jason Jorjani relays this as what Buchanan told him, as if beings like these were checking up on people who do that kind of work.
lyn-buchanan-met-with-an-alien-as-a-remo: Lyn Buchanan, a remote viewer for the US Army, meaning someone trained to try to see distant places with the mind alone, is said to have met with an alien, probably on a military base. Greg Bishop, a guest who says he has known Buchanan for a long time, tells it as something Buchanan told him personally "eight or nine years ago", around 2016. If true, it would mean military psychic programmes put people face to face with non-human beings.
lynda-bird-johnson-says-lbj-valued-georg: President Lyndon Johnson greatly valued the advice of a man named George Ball in the 1960s, according to Johnson's daughter, Lynda Bird Johnson. A former presidential advisor named Harold Malmgren repeats what she told him: "I know this by his daughter... that he really valued George Ball." Malmgren uses it to show who had the president's ear in that period.
macarthur-s-1955-west-point-interplaneta: In a 1955 speech at West Point, the US Army's officer academy, General Douglas MacArthur is said to have told the cadets: "The next war will be an interplanetary war." Michels quotes this himself in his narration, without naming a source. If MacArthur said it, one of America's best-known generals was talking openly about a threat from beyond Earth.
machine-based-and-person-based-uap-summo: There are two ways to call in unidentified flying craft, one that uses a machine and one that relies on a person, and both have been shown to work, according to Jake Barber, a helicopter pilot who says he flew a recovered UFO. Barber speaks as someone involved in the work, saying these are "two types of summoning that can be done that we've proven works and we're still working with." If true, it would mean people can deliberately make such craft appear.
mack-and-sheehan-s-plan-to-train-repeat-: Around 2004 at Harvard, a Harvard professor named John Mack and a lawyer named Dan Sheehan set out to train people who said they were taken by aliens again and again, so they could handle those meetings better. Sheehan tells it as someone who took part. He says he was legal counsel to Mack's group, the Program for Extraordinary Experience Research, and that the plan used holotropic breathing, a fast, deep breathing method meant to bring on altered states. In another telling he leaves out the breathing and stresses teaching these people to question the beings who took them, which would mean treating the encounters as real conversations.
mack-s-mother-sends-him-to-bud-hopkins-1: The Harvard psychiatrist John Mack, who became known for studying people who said they had been abducted by aliens, got into the subject because his mother sent him to talk to Budd Hopkins, an artist who researched abduction accounts. The lawyer Dan Sheehan, who knew Mack, passes on this account of how Mack's work began. He tells it to explain how a respected academic came to take the subject seriously.
mack-used-grof-s-holotropic-breathwork-t: In the 1990s, John Mack, a researcher who worked with people saying they had been taken by aliens, reportedly used a method called holotropic breathwork to help them remember what happened. Holotropic breathwork is a deep, fast breathing technique for reaching altered states, developed by a researcher named Stanislav Grof. Michels describes this himself, without naming a source.
madden-s-turn-to-ufos-2017-openness-and-: The philosopher James Madden says that, like a lot of people, he got hooked on UFOs around 2017, when 'suddenly it was okay to talk about this.' He says that in the summer of 2021 he was watching The X-Files, a TV series about government agents chasing the paranormal, with his kids just as 'the big first Pentagon press conference' on the subject happened, a story he says he always tells to mark when the topic became real for him.
maeterlinck-s-the-cloud-that-lifted-fore: The author and researcher Peter Levenda says that a play called The Cloud That Lifted, by the Belgian writer Maurice Maeterlinck, seems to foretell the 1963 killing of President Kennedy in Dallas, and that its story touches Lee Harvey Oswald, the man accused of the shooting. Levenda links it to the same writer's better-known work The Blue Bird, saying "the same guy who wrote that wrote a play called The Cloud That Lifted," and he tells it as his own summary without naming a source. If true, it would mean a writer saw the event in advance.
mafia-enforcement-in-malmgren-s-rhode-is: When Harold Malmgren was a boy in Rhode Island in the 1940s, around Providence and Narragansett Bay, mob enforcers were part of daily life. Malmgren, a former presidential adviser, says he saw it himself: a couple of men would walk in, grab someone, take him outside and beat him badly. He tells it with a laugh in a 2025 interview, as a picture of the rough world he grew up in.
magellan-radar-finds-metallic-snow-on-ve: In the 1990s Magellan, a NASA space probe that mapped the surface of Venus with radar, found what looked like metallic snow on the planet's mountaintops. The physicist Kevin Knuth, who calls himself a former NASA insider, tells it from his own time there: "I was at NASA when the Magellan probe was mapping Venus using radar." He brings it up as an example of a strange finding from NASA's own data.
magenta-case-mussolini-s-rs33-investigat: In 1933, near Magenta in Italy, a craft is said to have crashed, and the Italian dictator Benito Mussolini first thought it was an advanced Nazi, British or American aircraft, while his own secret investigation team, called RS33, became convinced it was not human technology and likely worked with the Nazis on it. The online researcher who goes by UAPGerb tells it without naming a source, mentioning David Grusch, a former intelligence officer who spoke about crash recoveries before Congress, and it matters because it would put the first recovery of such a craft years before the war.
magenta-craft-as-a-trigger-for-the-axis-: A strange craft said to have come down near Magenta, in Italy, around 1933 may have helped push Italy and Germany into the alliance later known as the Axis, the pact behind their side in the Second World War. Harald Malmgren, a former presidential advisor, raises this as an open question rather than a claim, wondering aloud whether the craft drove that decision, which would mean a UFO helped shape the war.
magenta-craft-taken-to-nazi-germany-1930: A craft the tellers call the Magenta craft is said to have been taken to Nazi Germany and studied there. A former Air Force officer named Robert Salas says it is reasonable to think the craft went to Germany, where studies were done on it. Michels raises it as a question, not a claim: pointing to photos of sites in Czechoslovakia and Poland and a ring-shaped test structure he says looks like it could hold an acorn-shaped object, he asks whether the Nazis were testing the Magenta craft there. If true, it would mean Nazi scientists had a strange craft to learn from.
magonia-people-arrested-at-lyon-agobard-: In medieval Lyon, in France, people said to have come from Magonia, a legendary land in the clouds whose sky ships were spoken of in folklore, were arrested, and a bishop named Agobard argued that the whole thing could not possibly be real, according to the philosopher Jason Jorjani. Jorjani tells it without naming a source, linking it to the researcher Jacques Vallée, who has written about Magonia, and casts Agobard as an early rationalist explaining away what may have been encounters like modern UFO reports.
maguire-saw-a-ufo: A CIA contractor named Bob Maguire says he once saw a UFO himself, and that after it he "couldn't go back" to his old way of seeing things. He gives no time or place for the sighting. He tells it as the moment that changed his outlook.
maison-rouge-meeting-1944: In 1944, the senior Nazi official Martin Bormann is said to have gathered the leaders of German industry for a very secret meeting in Paris, at a place called the Maison Rouge. The rooms were swept beforehand so that no one could listen in. The researcher Jason Simosa tells this, linking it to the writer Peter Levenda. If it happened as told, Nazi leaders and big business were making plans together in secret as the war turned against them.
majestic-12-1940: Majestic 12, or MJ-12, is described in disputed papers as a secret committee that dealt with the UFO question in the 1940s and 1950s, said to include figures such as the Air Force general Nathan Twining, the defense chief James Forrestal and the government science chief Vannevar Bush. Michels brings it up himself as a reported committee, because if real it would mean the highest levels of government were handling UFOs in secret.
majestic-12-as-a-cover-for-continuity-of: Majestic 12, the supposed secret committee said to have handled UFO matters from the late 1940s, was basically just a cover for continuity of government programs, the secret plans to keep the government running after a nuclear war or other disaster. Michels says that the retired Army colonel John B. Alexander admitted this to him at one point, which would make the famous UFO group a front for something else entirely.
majestic-12-briefing-document-1952: A secret paper is said to have briefed Dwight Eisenhower, then president-elect, in 1952 that a flying saucer had crashed and the government had its wreckage. Michels tells it himself, calling it "easily the most controversial" document "in UFO circles" and describing it as "supposedly a briefing document prepared in 1952". The paper is tied to Majestic 12, said to be a secret group of officials set up under President Harry Truman to handle the matter. In another telling Michels relays the view of the UFO researcher Stanton Friedman: if it is a "legitimate document", it shows first "that a flying saucer crashed" and second "that the wreckage was recovered". That version stretches from 1947 onward and names a man named Donald Menzel as a rumored member of the group. A researcher who goes by the online name UAPGerb also tells it, saying "I'm particularly fond of the Eisenhower briefing document." He places it between 1947 and 1952 and links it to Truman, Eisenhower, the defense official James Forrestal and a man named Walter B. Smith.
majestic-12-committee: There is a rumour in UFO circles of a secret committee called the Majestic 12, said to have been set up by President Harry Truman in 1947 to deal with the question of beings from other worlds. Michels tells it himself across several episodes, always as an allegation. He credits papers known as the MJ12 documents, names the engineer Vannevar Bush, the official Gordon Gray, the astronomer Donald Menzel, President Eisenhower and the general Nathan Twining as members or links, and describes the group as scientists, military and intelligence officials who advised the president directly on UFOs. In one episode he calls the committee fictitious.
majestic-12-maji-named-in-an-nro-documen: A UFO researcher named Steven Greer says the secret group that handles UFO matters used to be called Majestic 12, and that the last name he can pin down for it is "Maji" or "Magic", taken from a 1990s document of the NRO, the US agency that runs spy satellites. Greer summarises this himself and does not show the document. If true, it would mean a hidden UFO group still existed under a new name decades later.
majestic-documents-curated-by-ryan-and-b: A large set of papers known as the Majestic documents, said to describe secret US government work on UFOs from the 1940s to the 1960s, has been gathered and studied by two men named Ryan Wood and Bob Wood. A researcher named Richard Dolan, speaking from his own reading rather than a named source, describes going through them "page after page" and calls them "extremely sophisticated, frankly." He brings it up because, if real, the papers would be an inside record of a hidden UFO programme.
major-murphy-tells-vallee-about-1943-sau: A man called Major Murphy is said to have told Jacques Vallée, a UFO researcher, in an account in Vallée's book Messengers of Deception, that someone may have been experimenting with saucer technology as early as 1943, and that its "real advantage wasn't its flight capabilities, but its psychotronic effect", meaning its power over people's minds. The researcher Jason Simosa summarises this from the book. If true, it would mean such craft were developed as tools for affecting how people think.
malign-swarm-like-nhi-in-delonge-s-books: Several sources are said to describe a harmful, swarm-like kind of non-human intelligence, which people in this field shorten to NHI. The researcher Matthew Pines points, without a specific source, to the books of Tom DeLonge, to hints from Luis Elizondo, a public voice on government UFO work, and to a book called the Cryptoterrestrial Conundrum, saying they all deal with "the bad NHI or the malign." If true, it would mean not everything behind these encounters is friendly.
malmgren-at-the-ida-interviewed-by-the-h: Michels says that a man named Malmgren was part of the Institute for Defense Analyses, a research group that advises the US Defense Department, early in its history, at a time when the engineer Eric A. Walker chaired it. Michels says this himself, in an episode with the researcher Grant Cameron, adding that he had the privilege of interviewing Malmgren. He raises it to tie Walker, a figure often linked to stories of secret UFO work, to someone Michels has spoken with directly.
malmgren-diaries-record-meetings-with-ri: The private diaries of a man named Harold Malmgren record many meetings between him and another man, Richard Bissell. The journalist Ross Coulthart says on Michels's show in June 2025 that he has seen the diaries himself, and that they are now "in a safe place and they're backed up, so don't mess with them." He brings them up as written proof that the two men met often.
malmgren-goes-public-that-nhi-are-real-2: Harald Malmgren, a former adviser to US presidents, is said to have gone public in 2024 "saying NHI are real. We have their stuff," NHI meaning non-human intelligence. The security analyst Matthew Pines relays Malmgren's statement, which would mean a senior insider is saying the government holds material from non-human beings.
malmgren-helped-shoichiro-toyoda-set-up-: Harald Malmgren, a former advisor to American presidents, is said to have helped Shoichiro Toyoda, the head of the carmaker Toyota, set up Toyota's headquarters in Kentucky in the 1980s. Michels relays this as something Malmgren talked about with him, as a mark of how close Malmgren was to the centres of power, which matters because Malmgren also says he handled UFO material directly.
malmgren-introduced-to-putin-at-an-arran: Harold Malmgren, a former presidential adviser, says he was personally introduced to Vladimir Putin, the future Russian leader, before Putin was widely known. Malmgren says the person who set it up looked for him, found him in a crowd and brought him over. In one version he names that person as the Russian official Yevgeny Primakov and places the meeting in St. Petersburg in 1992. There he says Primakov told him: "This man is rising. He will soon be very important to Russia. You should know him." Malmgren tells it in a 2025 interview, as a sign of how close he was to powerful people.
malmgren-investigates-for-kennedy-admini: In 1962, a man named Harold Malmgren was looking into something for President John F. Kennedy's administration. As part of that, Malmgren is said to have visited Lawrence Preston Gise, the Albuquerque director of the Atomic Energy Commission, the US agency then in charge of nuclear work, and the maternal grandfather of Amazon founder Jeff Bezos. Michels tells this himself in an episode with a former Senate staffer named Kirk McConnell. He uses it to tie a White House inquiry to the nuclear world in New Mexico.
malmgren-links-his-life-and-his-knowledg: Harold Malmgren, a former advisor to US presidents, says that looking back on his life, including things he knew and said as a young man around MIT, the Massachusetts university, in the 1950s, the only explanation he can find is time travel. He says he has "thought about this many many times and the answer is yes," pointing to how freely he spoke to an MIT professor: "I didn't have the slightest inhibition." If true, it would mean his knowledge came from somewhere outside ordinary time.
malmgren-on-his-deathbed-cia-and-the-maj: A man named Harold Malmgren, speaking from a hospital bed near the end of his life, told Michels that the CIA had started tracking him, putting his name in a file, and that "the Majestic" did too. The Majestic is a rumoured secret group said to handle UFO matters at the top of the US government. Michels tells it as something he heard from Malmgren directly, and it would mean such a group kept watch on people from the 1950s on.
malmgren-on-office-of-naval-intelligence: The Office of Naval Intelligence, the US Navy's intelligence service, knew more about UFOs than any other part of the government, according to Harold Malmgren, a former advisor to American presidents, as Jesse Michels repeats him on several episodes. Michels says Malmgren kept stressing that the office knew "way more than meets the eye," in one telling calling it the "deepest" core of the secret, and in another saying "that's where all the secrets are kept." If true, it would point to the Navy as the centre of what the government knows.
malmgren-on-the-secret-committee-1940: A man named Harold Malmgren, before he died, is said to have spoken of a secret committee, linked to the early years of UFO secrecy in the 1940s and 50s, and to have said someone was on that committee's radar and may even have worked with it. Michels passes this on from Malmgren. It is told as support for the idea that a small hidden group managed the UFO secret from the start.
malmgren-ran-sub-four-minute-miles-after: Harald Malmgren, a former presidential adviser, was one of the first people on Earth to run a mile in under four minutes after the British runner Roger Bannister first did it in the 1950s. Michels says the two of them talked about this, and he tells it to show how remarkable a man Malmgren is.
malmgren-read-into-legacy-uap-retrieval-: A former US trade official named Harold Malmgren claimed that he was told about a long-running secret programme for recovering crashed UFOs (the government now calls them UAP, unidentified anomalous phenomena), and that the man who told him was Richard Bissell, a senior CIA official who, by this account, founded Area 51, the secret test base in the Nevada desert. The journalist Ross Coulthart relays this from Malmgren's own diaries, where he says Bissell is the key figure behind Malmgren's claim. If true, it would put the existence of such a programme in the mouth of one of the CIA's own senior men.
malmgren-s-ida-job-as-cover-for-nsc-work: An economist and government adviser named Harold Malmgren is said to have described his job at the Institute for Defense Analyses, a federally funded research center that worked for the Pentagon, as "actually a cover" for work he was doing for the National Security Council, the president's top security staff, and for the president himself. Michels repeats this from Malmgren's own words in two episodes. In the first he puts it as a straight cover and mentions a CIA official named Richard Bissell. In the second he calls it an unofficial cover. The point is that research institutes like this one could hide secret government work.
malmgren-s-ida-work-a-cover-for-the-nsc-: A former Washington official named Harold Malmgren is said to have stated, in a 2024 interview given before he spoke with Michels, that his job at the Institute for Defense Analyses, a defense research group, was really a cover for work he did for the National Security Council, the president's own security staff in the White House. Michels reports this himself, and ties it to Malmgren's diaries and to the CIA official Richard Bissell. It matters because it would place Malmgren closer to secret 1960s decision-making than his public job suggests.
malmgren-s-research-on-thomas-townsend-b: A former presidential advisor named Harald Malmgren is said to have been deep into research on Thomas Townsend Brown, an inventor of the mid-1900s who worked on anti-gravity. Michels relays this from what Malmgren told him. It matters because it would tie a high-level government insider to the hunt for craft that defy gravity.
malmgren-s-two-unherd-essays-on-putin-20: Harald Malmgren, a former advisor to American presidents, wrote two essays about the Russian leader Vladimir Putin for UnHerd, an online magazine, in 2022. Malmgren mentions them himself on the show ("I wrote two essays about Putin"). He uses them as a sign of how closely he followed world affairs.
malmgren-saw-video-of-the-roswell-being-: Harold Malmgren, a former advisor to American presidents, is said to have seen film of a living creature from Roswell, New Mexico, where a craft is said to have crashed in 1947, being interviewed. Jesse Michels repeats this on several episodes as something Malmgren told his daughter Pippa Malmgren, in one version on his deathbed, saying "he saw the video of this creature being interviewed." In some tellings Michels links the footage to an X-ray weapon and to Bluegill Triple Prime, a 1962 nuclear test. If true, it would mean at least one being survived the crash and was questioned on camera.
malmgren-sent-into-the-tank-to-stall-cur: During the Cuban missile crisis of 1962, a young aide named Harold Malmgren, then about 26 or 27, says he was sent by President John F. Kennedy into "the tank," the Pentagon's secure meeting room for the top generals, to stall Curtis LeMay, the Air Force's commanding general, who was pressing for a nuclear strike. Malmgren, later a presidential adviser, tells Michels himself that he argued it was madness, because "if you hit Moscow, there's no one to talk to," and he names Defense Secretary Robert McNamara and the White House adviser McGeorge Bundy as being there. A commentator named Matthew Pines, who relays what Malmgren told him, tells it twice on the show, once as Kennedy telling Malmgren to "stall him out" and once just as holding LeMay back from possibly launching nuclear weapons.
malmgren-tracked-by-majestic-12-guardian: Harald Malmgren, who later advised several US presidents on trade, says that as a young man in the 1950s his name went into secret lists of talent kept not only by the CIA, the US spy agency, but by "the Majestic," a group he calls guardians who took it on themselves to protect the world's secrets. In his own interview he ties this to the day he met Karl Compton, the president of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, and also mentions Christian Herter, then a senior US statesman. When Michels retells it in a later episode, he says the flagging followed a letter Malmgren wrote to the Atomic Energy Commission, the agency then in charge of nuclear work, which would mean a hidden body was watching for gifted young people from the start.
malmgren-tracked-by-majestic-guardians: Harold Malmgren, a former presidential adviser, says he was watched not only by the CIA, the US spy agency, but also by what he calls "Majestic". He describes this as a group of "guardians" who see their job as protecting the world. He speaks of it as something that happened to him, in a 2026 episode, and if true it would mean a hidden group beyond the normal agencies keeps watch over people who know about UFO matters.
malmgren-tweet-on-bluegill-tests-and-jfk: A former US government official named Harold Malmgren posted on social media that he was "now reconstructing my personal interactions with Los Alamos", the New Mexico nuclear weapons laboratory, during the Bluegill tests of 1961 and 1962. He describes these as tests of intercepting long-range nuclear missiles, and mentions President John F. Kennedy's visit to Los Alamos in November 1962. Michels reads the post aloud as a hint that Malmgren was close to nuclear secrets of that era, in an episode about reports of unknown craft watching nuclear sites.
malmstrom-afb-disc-wobbling-on-edge: At Malmstrom Air Force Base, home to nuclear missiles, a border patrol officer saw a metallic disc, "wobbling on its edge," in his own quoted words, about 30 feet wide and 100 feet away. The writer Marik von Rennenkampff tells it without naming a source, as one of many cases of strange craft showing up near nuclear weapons.
malmstrom-missiles-disabled-by-red-glowi: On March 24, 1967, at Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana, a glowing red object is said to have hung over a nuclear missile site while the ten missiles under one underground crew shut down one after another. If true, it would mean something unknown could switch off American nuclear weapons at will. The man at the centre of it is Robert Salas, then a young Air Force officer on duty in the buried launch control centre for a group of missiles called Oscar Flight, and he tells it himself on the show. Guards on the surface phoned to say strange lights were moving oddly in the sky. Then, he says, "before I could tell them about the phone calls, we get a big horn go off," as the first missile went from green, ready, to red, unable to launch, and he names his commander, Fred Meiwald, as there with him. Salas says all ten went into a "no-go" state; Michels, who has met him and returns to the case again and again, once puts it at nine of ten. Another witness, Bob Jameson, describes a wall of status lights where "all 10 missiles were off alert. All red," and the lawyer Dan Sheehan says the base commander, Arie Arnoldson, filed a UFO report with the North American air defence command. Michels credits the researcher Robert Hastings, who gathered such cases in his book UFOs and Nukes and held a 2010 press conference with six Air Force witnesses, Salas first among them.
malta-foundation-with-a-solar-power-stat: A research foundation is being set up on the island of Malta, with a rented site, a solar power station already installed, and plans for a data center full of GPUs, the powerful chips used for heavy computing. Filippo Biondi, a researcher who claims to have found huge structures beneath the pyramids of Egypt, describes it as his own project in the 2020s: "We have rented a nice place where we have installed it a solar power station." It is meant to give his work its own computing power.
maltese-legend-of-giants-building-the-te: Local legends on Malta, a small island nation in the Mediterranean that has very old stone temples, say giants once lived on the islands and helped build those temples. A researcher of ancient sites named Jay Anderson, who has been to Malta, repeats the legend as he heard it there. He tells it as a hint that the temple builders may not have been ordinary people.
man-abducted-off-a-downtown-street-in-co: In 1976 a man walking through downtown Concord, California, at four in the morning said he had been abducted right off the street, even though he had no interest in UFOs. The parapsychologist Jeffrey Mishlove says he and his colleagues interviewed the man, and he tells it among stories linked to Ted Owens, a self-described psychic whom Mishlove studied, with a police report also part of his account.
man-in-a-black-duster-carrying-the-mothm: In a movie-theater parking lot in Los Angeles, a man in a long black coat appeared holding a copy of The Mothman Prophecies, a book about strange sightings and a winged creature. A Hollywood screenwriter and producer named Bryce Zabel says he saw it himself, together with a colleague named Brent Friedman. He tells it as an odd encounter that seemed to echo the strange-visitor stories in the book itself.
man-made-craft-rising-from-desert-openin: A UFO activist named Steven Greer says he has flown over desert sites where human-made craft rise up out of openings in the ground. He tells it as something he saw. In one telling he names the place as the Lockheed Skunk Works site, the secret aircraft design branch of the aerospace company Lockheed, and says he filmed it by iPhone from a helicopter around 2023. If true, it would mean some craft taken for UFOs are secret human-built machines.
man-made-ufo-down-in-russia: A man-made UFO, meaning a craft built by people rather than visitors, is said to have come down in Russia. Steven Greer, a UFO researcher who argues that UFO secrets are held by a global group of insiders, says the crash was "confirmed recently" to him by a special operations team, a unit of elite soldiers he does not name further. If true, it would mean human-built craft of this kind are already flying, and crashing.
man-who-says-he-was-in-the-gate-program: A young man claims he was part of something he called the GATE program, a programme the telling does not explain. A researcher named Greg Malatzi says he spoke with him and will not give his name: "I talked to a kid who claimed he was part of the GATE program." Malatzi mentions it as a lead suggesting the programme exists and that people inside it are talking.
managed-disclosure-campaign-that-began-i: Since 2017, according to a guest who goes by the name UAPGerb, there has been a carefully managed campaign to slowly reveal what the government knows about UFOs. UAPGerb says that Karl Nell, a figure in the public debate on government UFO secrecy, has called this campaign dead, and he disagrees "quite a bit". He thinks it is still running, which would mean the drip of revelations is planned rather than accidental.
manchester-airport-orb-2024: An orb was seen at Manchester Airport in England in June 2024. Michels reads this out from a caption, "Manchester airport June 2024 sighting," while showing footage to the UFO skeptic Mick West in a debate, offering it as a case for West to explain.
manchester-orb-sized-at-24-inches-at-mos: A glowing ball seen in the sky near Manchester Airport in England in 2024 was, at most, about 24 inches across. That is the finding of Mick West, a researcher known as a UFO skeptic, who says on the show that he and others built a detailed 3D model of the scene from the exact viewpoints and the available data. If he is right, the object was something small, not a large craft.
mandela-effect-remembered-death-of-nelso: The Mandela effect is the name for a memory that a large group of people share. It comes from the many people who remember Nelson Mandela, the South African freedom leader, dying in prison in the 1980s. Michels explains the term himself in an episode about the idea that our universe is a kind of hologram.
manhattan-project-as-original-ufo-legacy: There are rumors that the Manhattan Project, the US wartime program of the 1940s that built the atomic bomb, was the first secret program for handling UFOs and their technology. Michels mentions these rumors himself, without saying where they come from. If true, the secret structures built for the bomb would be where the UFO secret began.
manhattan-project-as-the-first-blue-book: The Manhattan Project, America's secret 1940s effort to build the atomic bomb, is said to have been the first government UFO program, long before Blue Book, the US Air Force's UFO study of the 1950s and 60s. David Grusch, a former intelligence official who has come forward about hidden UFO programs, tells Michels that some of his own colleagues had grandparents who were the people handling UFO reports inside the Manhattan Project. In a later episode Michels repeats that Grusch told him, during a car ride in Washington, that the Manhattan Project was basically the original UFO program, which, if true, would put the start of official UFO secrecy at the birth of the bomb.
manipulated-ellsworth-document-traced-to: There is a supposed Air Force document saying that on November 16, 1977, guards at a missile site called L9, near Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota, were attacked with a beam by aliens. The UFO historian Richard Dolan mentions it in passing, saying it is a document "which has been manipulated" and that it was traced back to Richard Doty, a former Air Force investigator. Michels covers it in more detail in an episode with Air Force veterans who say they were abducted. He gives the date and the L9 site, and he credits the UFO researcher Brad Sparks for work on the case. He also passes on a chain of reports: according to the physicist and UFO researcher Bruce Maccabee, the researcher Bill Moore said that Doty confessed to forging the Ellsworth document. So the tellers differ on how far it goes, from a document that was altered to an outright forgery. It matters because a fake official record can steer UFO research the wrong way for years.
mansmann-letters-describe-domed-disc-on-: A film shot at Vandenberg Air Force Base in California in 1964 showed a disc-shaped object with a dome, according to private letters written by a man named Florenze Mansmann, who had studied the film. The researcher Robert Hastings, who writes about UFOs seen over nuclear weapons sites, says Mansmann went through the film frame by frame with a loupe, a small magnifying lens, and by the mid-1980s was writing to a man named Robert Jacobs that "what I saw with the magnifier was a disc-shaped object with a dome." If true, it would mean a military camera caught a built craft on film.
