manson-modeled-his-life-on-heinlein-s-st: The cult leader Charles Manson, according to Jesse Michels, carried around the novel Stranger in a Strange Land by the science fiction writer Robert Heinlein and modelled his life on it in 1960s California. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, and names the psychiatrist Jolly West alongside it, as part of a wider picture he draws of hidden hands shaping the violence and counterculture of that era.
mantell-s-plane-disintegrated-by-magneti: The plane of a pilot named Thomas Mantell, who went down near Fort Knox, Kentucky, in 1948, did not blow up and crash but "disintegrated", according to Silas Newton, a man whose recorded words are heard in the episode, who blames magnetism. Newton is passing on what he says the account of the crash stated. If true, it would mean the plane was torn apart by some unknown force.
mantis-being-at-the-bedside-tears-flesh-: In 1995, at his home near Denver, Colorado, a being shaped like a praying mantis stood by the bed of John Blitch, a scientist who worked for the Pentagon's advanced research agency. Blitch says he saw it himself: its 'triangle face opens up and these jaws' appear, and it tore flesh to show him that the body is only a container for the soul.
manuel-caceres-knockoff-figure-confused-: One of the three-fingered figures linked to the so-called Nazca bodies, small mummified bodies from Peru that some claim are not human, was really a knockoff souvenir, Michels says: a local journalist named Manuel Caceres made it as merchandise. Michels quotes a Peruvian forensic archaeologist named Flavio Estrada calling it "fake. It's craftsmanship constructed, built," and in a later episode he describes such wooden figurines as "confiscated at the Lima Airport in 2023," which, in his telling, is how the knockoff got mixed up with the bodies themselves.
many-uap-sightings-off-the-coast-of-san-: Many sightings of UAPs, the government's term for unidentified aerial phenomena, happen off the coast of San Diego, California. The economist Tyler Cowen says this to Michels, passing on what he has been told, as he talks about where the reports cluster. If true, it would point to one stretch of sea as a hot spot for these sightings.
map-of-key-black-sites-in-greer-s-brief: The UFO campaigner Steven Greer says a document he calls "the brief" holds a map showing "where all the key black sites are," meaning the secret facilities where, he says, this hidden work goes on. Greer describes the document himself as something he has in hand. If true, it would point to where the secrets are kept.
marble-from-crash-site-tests-about-40-ir: A small marble found at the site near Aztec, New Mexico, where a flying saucer is said to have crashed, reportedly came back from an X-ray fluorescence test, a scan that reads which elements are in a material, as close to 40 percent iridium, a rare metal. Michels tells this from the work of the researchers Scott Ramsey and Suzanne Ramsey, who studied the site, and calls the result "very anomalous", since that much iridium would be hard to explain for an ordinary object.
marcel-s-son-handled-the-roswell-materia: In 1947 an Army intelligence officer named Jesse Marcel Sr. is said to have held wreckage from a crash near Roswell, New Mexico, and taken some of it home, where his son, Jesse Marcel Jr., later an Air Force flight surgeon, played with it. Michels tells this more than once, passing on the son's account; once he calls the material a kind of memory metal that fits the father's own description, and once he stresses that the father held it in his hands. If true, it would mean strange material from Roswell was handled by an ordinary family.
marcker-s-general-electric-experiment-te: A scientist named Marcker is said to have run an experiment at General Electric, the large American engineering company, built to test whether spacetime, the combined fabric of space and time, has torsion, a kind of built-in twist. A researcher named Eric W. Davis brings it up on the podcast without naming a source and praises the setup as "very well designed". He tells it because a real test of torsion would bear on whether such exotic physics can be checked in a lab.
marco-chereze-dies-after-handling-the-va: Marco Chereze, a soldier in the Brazilian town of Varginha, is said to have died in 1996 after catching and holding a strange creature that was covered in an oily, greasy substance. Michels tells this himself on three episodes: in one he credits Chereze's family, who say to this day that the being caused his illness and that near the end he kept worrying he was sick because he had held it. In another, crediting a man named Armando Fortunato, he says Chereze died from a puncture wound from the being.
marco-leal-re-interviews-carlos-about-25: Around 2021 in São Paulo, Brazil, a man named Marco Leal interviewed the surgeon Carlos de Souza again, about 25 years after first hearing his story, and found it had not changed at all. De Souza, who says his hospital once operated on an alien, recalls Leal telling him: "Your account is exactly the same as the one you gave 25 years ago. Identical. Not a single detail has changed." De Souza tells it in a 2026 interview as a sign that his memory has stayed steady.
marco-rubio-s-attempt-to-approach-harrin: About five or six years ago, around 2020, the US senator Marco Rubio is said to have tried to approach a government official named John S. Herrington about UFO matters and to have been shut down. Brent Friedman, a guest on the show, tells it as something passed along to him, with the whistleblower David Grusch among those he cites, and it would suggest that even a senior senator could not get answers.
marco-rubio-s-ssci-staff-seek-whistleblo: Since 2017, the story goes, Marco Rubio, a US senator, has been quietly interested in UFOs and has had his staff look for whistleblowers. That staff sat on the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence, the Senate panel that oversees the spy agencies. A UFO researcher who goes by UAPGerb says this is long known among people deep in the subject, without naming a source, and tells it as a sign that a powerful senator took the topic seriously.
marconi-believed-the-magenta-craft-non-h: In the 1930s an unusual craft was reportedly connected to Magenta, Italy, and Guglielmo Marconi, the Italian radio pioneer, is said to have truly believed it might not have been made by humans. Michels says this himself, pointing to "some documents" and later confirmations from Marconi's family that he does not name. If true, it would mean one of the great scientists of his time took the idea of a non-human craft seriously.
marconi-radar-and-the-italian-crash: The idea here is that an unexplained crash may not have happened only at Cape Girardeau, in Missouri, but perhaps in Italy as well, and that Guglielmo Marconi, the Italian radio pioneer, was involved. John Blitch, a guest on the show who calls himself a witness to strange events, raises this in passing without naming a source and gives no further details. If it were true, crash stories would reach back into Italy and into the work of one of radio's founders.
marconi-s-grandson-tells-oggi-about-the-: The grandson of Guglielmo Marconi, the Italian inventor of radio, is said to have told Oggi, an Italian gossip magazine, that his grandfather "had a lot to do with the UFO and ET issue" in the 1930s, when Benito Mussolini ruled Italy. Michels tells this himself, pointing to a video of the interview that he says anyone can watch. If true, it would place official interest in UFOs in Italy before the Second World War.
marconi-s-transatlantic-radio-experiment: The radio pioneer Guglielmo Marconi's first signal across the Atlantic, sent between Newfoundland and Cornwall in 1901, worked almost by luck: his radio waves bounced off the ionosphere, a layer of charged gas high in the atmosphere, and came back down to the receiver, just as the physicist James Clerk Maxwell's theory of electromagnetic waves allowed. That is how a scientist named Filippo Biondi, who scans beneath the pyramids with radar, explains it, without naming a source. Michels later passes the story on from Biondi, calling Marconi ignorant in a useful way, someone who simply tried it across the ocean when others would not have bothered.
marcos-obtains-two-troves-through-tortur: The Philippine leader Ferdinand Marcos, working with a military officer named Colonel Ver, is said to have gotten hold of two hidden troves by torturing people, sometime between 1970 and 1989. A researcher named Dan Sheehan says so in passing, "Marcos got two of them", without naming a source or saying more about what the troves held.
marcus-vinicius-s-chain-smoking-after-th: After the events of 1996 in Varginha, a town in Brazil where a creature was said to have been brought to a hospital, a man named Marcos Vinícius was so shaken that he began chain smoking. The surgeon Italo Venturelli, who says his hospital was involved, tells this as someone who knew him: "He even began smoking more. He'd smoke all day." He offers it as a sign of how deeply the episode affected those close to it.
marcus-vinicius-s-video-of-the-being-sho: In Varginha, Brazil, a doctor named Marcos Vinícius had a video of the being said to have been treated at the town's regional hospital in 1996, and he showed it to many people at his house. The surgeon Italo Venturelli, who worked at that hospital, says visitors would come in, sit on the sofa, and watch it on his colleague's computer, which he thinks played it from a CD, sometimes over and over. If true, footage of the creature was passed around town among people who saw it with their own eyes.
maria-farmer-mural-showing-epstein-in-a-: A guest named Jay Anderson describes a mural called The Elite, painted by the artist Maria Farmer, which he says shows Ghislaine Maxwell, the financier Jeffrey Epstein's associate, as a dragon biting a child in half. In the same picture, he says, an antenna flies a flag of the FBI, the US federal police agency, with a flying saucer hanging off the top and Epstein's face in its window. Anderson relays this from Farmer's work, calling it "all very nasty stuff."
maria-s-finger-bones-tested-in-sri-lanka: Two finger bones from Maria, one of the small three-fingered bodies from Peru that some call the M types, were genetically tested in Sri Lanka, and one is said to have come back male and the other female. Michels passes this on from the UFO researcher Steve Mera, who told him about the tests. If true, the mismatched results would raise questions about whether the body is a single being at all.
maria-wang-says-her-husband-reported-dir: A woman named Maria Wang said that her husband, who worked in the 1950s at Wright-Patterson, an Air Force base in Ohio, reported directly to Henry Kissinger, the man who later became US Secretary of State. Michels passes this on from what she said, in an episode asking whether Kissinger oversaw a program to recover crashed UFOs, which is what it would hint at if true.
marilyn-monroe-rumor-that-jfk-spilled-uf: According to a rumor, the actress Marilyn Monroe said that President John F. Kennedy told her some UFO-related secrets. Michels brings it up himself, without naming a source, in a conversation with the podcaster Joe Rogan. If true, it would mean a president knew about UFOs and talked about them in private.
marine-claims-he-was-on-the-usaf-flight-: An anonymous US Marine claims he was on board a US Air Force flight out of Campinas, Brazil, in 1996, as part of the operation the episode covers, in which the army is said to have captured a live alien. The UFO investigator James Fox relays this from an email the Marine sent him, quoting him as saying, "I was on the flight." If true, it would place the US military directly in the Brazilian case.
marine-squadron-commander-saw-the-churni: In 2004, off the coast of Southern California, a commander of a Marine Corps squadron who happened to be flying by also saw the churning white water on the ocean surface, the same disturbance that Navy pilots linked to the Tic Tac, a white oval object shaped like the mint. The writer Marik von Rennenkampff brings this up, naming the commander, a little unsure, as Kurth. It matters because it would add another trained witness to the Navy pilots' story.
mariner-4-photographs-a-barren-mars-1965: In 1965 the space probe Mariner 4 photographed Mars up close, and its pictures showed a planet that looked inactive, barren and lifeless. Michels tells this himself, drawing on the Mariner 4 photographs, in an episode about whether Mars once had life. He brings it up because those pictures ended many people's hopes of finding a living Mars.
mariner-9-s-inca-city-ruins-near-the-mar: In 1972 a NASA space probe called Mariner 9, which orbited Mars, sent back pictures near the planet's south pole of what looked like ancient ruins, and the team informally nicknamed the spot the "Incan City". Michels tells this himself, pointing to the probe's photographs, as a hint that Mars may once have had life or builders.
mario-finds-his-right-b-52-pilot-glove-m: In 1977, an Air Force veteran named Mario Woods says he checked his bag at home near Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota and found his left B-52 bomber pilot glove there but the right one gone. He tells it as something that happened to him, and he ties it to what he and a fellow airman, Michael Johnson, say happened to them that night: a taking by aliens.
mario-keeps-the-beings-out-of-his-debrie: In 1977, at Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota, an Air Force airman named Mario Woods says he left out of his official debriefing that he had seen non-human beings. He tells Michels that had he said he saw these beings, he would have lost his clearance under the Personnel Reliability Program, the screening that decides who is fit to work around nuclear weapons. If true, it suggests that the rules themselves pushed service members to keep such sightings off the record.
mario-s-childhood-sightings-of-craft: Mario Woods says he has been seeing strange craft since he was a boy. Woods is an Air Force veteran who says he was abducted by aliens, and he tells this himself in a 2026 episode. He is careful to say that he saw their craft, not the beings themselves.
mario-s-doe-clearance-delays-and-repress: In 1978 a former airman named Mario Woods, who says he was abducted by aliens while in the Air Force, pushed the memory of that experience down because he was waiting on a security clearance from the US Department of Energy, the agency that runs nuclear sites such as Oak Ridge and Los Alamos. Woods tells it himself: "I had to repress this because my first clearance took over 8 months to obtain." He gives it to explain why he stayed silent for so long.
mario-s-earlier-hypnotic-regression-trig: An Air Force veteran named Mario Woods, who says he was abducted by aliens, once went through hypnotic regression, a session using hypnosis to bring back buried memories, and reliving the experience was so traumatic that it threw his heart into atrial fibrillation, an irregular heartbeat. Michels tells this himself in an episode reuniting veterans who say they were abducted together, as a sign of how real the memory felt to Woods.
mario-s-glove-seen-on-the-shiny-floor-of: An Air Force veteran named Michael Johnson says that in 1977, after a night in the missile fields around Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota, he remembers lying down somewhere and seeing a glove on "a real shiny floor, nothing like the inside of that truck." He tells it as his own memory of being aboard a craft. The glove, he suggests, was the one his fellow airman Mario Woods later found missing, which would tie both men's accounts to the same place.
mario-s-regression-a-device-pushed-into-: Under hypnosis, an Air Force veteran named Mario Woods recalls that during a 1977 abduction aboard a craft, one of the beings bent his wrist backwards and pushed a device down into it. Woods, telling Michels what he says happened to him, puts it this way: "he bends my wrist backwards and he goes down into my wrist with it." If true, he was implanted or examined by whoever took him.
mario-s-regression-because-he-s-here-197: During a regression, a session meant to bring back buried memories, Mario Woods recalled being on board a craft in 1977 and hearing a small being say plainly, "Because he's here." Woods, an Air Force veteran who says he was abducted, tells this himself in a 2026 episode where he reunites with others from that time. The story is tied to a man named Michael Johnson, whom Woods links to that remark.
mario-woods-abduction-at-ellsworth-afb: In 1977, a man named Mario Woods, stationed at Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota, was taken by something unknown along with his partner, Michael Johnson, according to Michels, who has told the story on several episodes. Michels draws on Woods himself, on the researcher Robert Hastings's book UFOs and Nukes, and on a man named Richard Doty. In his telling, the abduction came back to Woods under hypnosis, and the details include a signal exchange, at least five missing hours, a truck at a dam, mud in a frozen field, burns a doctor found, a single glove, drawings of the craft, and Woods waking up nine miles away. Michels says he later brought the two men back together for an interview, which would matter because it would be two serving airmen recalling the same abduction.
mario-woods-becomes-obsessed-with-pyrami: After an alien abduction he says he lived through at Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota in 1977, a young airman named Mario Woods became obsessed with drawing pyramids. Woods tells it himself: other airmen at the missile field laughed at him because he would sit in the day room drawing pyramids with "a weird top on it and little sparks coming out of it," which he now calls "an Atlantean pyramid," after the legendary lost city of Atlantis. Michels also mentions Woods and the Ellsworth abduction of 1977 in another episode, repeating what Woods told him. The drawings are told as a lasting mark the experience left on him.
mario-woods-debriefed-and-found-with-cir: In the 1960s, a man named Mario Woods, who guarded nuclear missiles at Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota, is said to have been taken by aliens and then examined at the base hospital. A researcher named Robert Hastings, who studies UFO reports around nuclear bases, passes on what Woods told him. According to Hastings, the doctor found a round wound or dent with a small dimple in the centre, on Woods's forehead and on his ankle. Michels tells it too, also from Woods's account, and adds that Woods held a Q clearance, a high security clearance for nuclear work, and guarded ICBMs, long-range nuclear missiles. In Michels's version a doctor checked Woods's teeth, and he says nothing of the wounds. If true, it would mean something was taking a close interest in the men who guard America's nuclear weapons.
mario-woods-reports-the-incident-to-aaro: An Air Force veteran named Mario Woods says he reported his 1977 alien encounter to AARO, the Pentagon office set up to look into UFO reports, in March 2023, but the office never followed up, and his fellow airman Michael Johnson was never found by them. Woods tells it first-hand on two episodes. In one he adds that the interview ran four hours and nineteen minutes and was not recorded. He tells it to show that the office did not take witnesses like him seriously.
mark-felt-pushes-to-investigate-the-mexi: In 1972, a senior FBI official named Mark Felt is said to have insisted on flying to Mexico City the very next morning to look into a bank account there, one tied to money under investigation. A researcher named Dan Sheehan tells this on the show without naming a source, and he places Felt alongside his FBI superior, a man named Pat Gray. Sheehan tells it to suggest the bank account was a lead that someone inside the Bureau badly wanted followed.
mark-felt-s-biography-nixon-shown-covert: President Richard Nixon is said to have been shown some secret, highly specialised technology, according to a book about the former FBI official Mark Felt. Michels brings this up in three episodes, always hedging with "I think". He calls the book a biography in two of them and an autobiography in the third, and once he names the reporter Bob Woodward alongside Felt. If true, it would mean a sitting president was let in on hidden technology.
mark-mccandlish-s-alien-reproduction-veh: A man named Mark McCandlish described what he called alien reproduction vehicles: working craft, built by humans, that copy technology taken from alien ones. Michels mentions this in passing, relaying McCandlish's account as a sign that, in his words, "we have workable craft."
mark-twain-predicts-his-death-with-halle: The novelist Mark Twain was born on November 30, 1835, just as Halley's Comet, which passes Earth about every 75 years, was going by, and he often said he expected to "go out with the comet" when it came back. According to Michels, he died in 1910, just as he predicted. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, as an example of people seeming to sense the future.
mars-destroyed-by-a-cme-and-plasma-event: The claim is that Mars was wrecked by a huge burst of charged gas thrown off by the sun, called a coronal mass ejection, along with electrical plasma events, and that these are tied to Valles Marineris, the planet's giant canyon system. A researcher named Matt LaCroix puts this forward as his own view, without naming a source: once something "then weakens," he says, "I believe that is what caused the entire destruction of Mars." If he is right, a planet could be stripped by the sun in a single disaster.
mars-global-surveyor-image-of-a-square-s: In 2001 the Mars Global Surveyor, a NASA spacecraft that orbited Mars, took a photo of a square structure on the planet that looks man-made, and the picture has only now gone mainstream. Michels tells this himself on two episodes. He says his friend Chris Ramsay, who makes UFO videos, posted the photo, the podcaster Joe Rogan reshared it, and it has been "verified at the highest levels", a claim that would point to something artificial on Mars.
mars-global-surveyor-images-of-possible-: Some pictures taken by Mars Global Surveyor, a spacecraft from NASA (the US space agency) that circled Mars from the late 1990s into the mid 2000s, show shapes that might be the fossil skeletons of large living things. That is the claim of a researcher named Maaneli Derakhshani, who raises it on Jesse Michels's show without pointing to a particular study. He says there are "a number of these images" that look like they "could well be" fossils of big creatures, which would mean Mars once had large life.
mars-investigation-at-sri-just-down-the-: The Mars scientist John Brandenburg says that in the 1980s a study of possible signs of past life on Mars was run at SRI, the Stanford Research Institute in California. He says they 'found out later' that the government's remote viewing program, an effort to test whether people could describe distant places with the mind, 'was just down the hall' from the Mars study's headquarters, which he tells as a hint the two were linked.
martial-arts-programs-that-train-people-: Some martial arts programs, it is said, train students to know when someone is looking at them from behind. A researcher named Rupert Sheldrake mentions this without naming a particular school or source. He raises it because, if people can learn that sense, it would suggest that being stared at is something a person can actually feel.
martian-meteorite-alh84001-with-possible: Scientists found a rock from Mars in Antarctica that may hold traces of ancient bacteria. Jesse Michels says they found it in 1984 and gave it the code name ALH84001. If those traces are fossils, they would be signs of past life on another planet. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source. On another episode he recalls that in the 1990s President Bill Clinton made a speech about the meteorite. A researcher named John Brandenburg, who argues that Mars once had life, also talks about it. He confirms that ALH84001 was found in Antarctica but places the find in the 1990s, not 1984. The two tellers agree on the rock and where it was found, and both bring it up as a piece of evidence for life on Mars.
martian-scout-ship-finds-a-volatile-prim: Long ago, a group of beings from Mars is said to have been sent out in a craft to scout a new world they might live on, and to have found a young, unstable Earth. The philosopher Jason Jorjani relays this story from Joe McMoneagle, a remote viewer, someone who says he can see distant places and times with the mind. If true, it would mean humans' story is bound up with visitors from Mars.
martian-survivors-fled-and-some-may-have: Joe McMoneagle, a researcher, believes there were once people on Mars who got stranded there and tried to survive by going into hibernation, and the story holds that some survivors fled and may have reached Earth. He gives it as his own view, with no source named. If true, it would mean some of Earth's past is tied to a lost people from Mars.
martians-attacked-from-space: The idea is that Mars was once home to living beings, and that something happened there which looks as if "they were attacked from space by somebody else." A researcher named John Brandenburg says this on an episode about his view that life on Mars was destroyed by nuclear war, and he names no source. If true, it would mean Mars once had a civilisation that someone else destroyed.
martians-built-the-moon-as-a-transport-a: The philosopher Jason Jorjani suggests that people living on Mars probably built the Moon, for two purposes: to carry things across space and to reshape Earth so it could support life. He offers this as his own reading, drawing on Joe McMoneagle, a man known for remote viewing, the practice of trying to perceive distant places with the mind, and on a work called Closer Encounters; if true, the Moon would be a made object rather than a natural one.
martin-cannon-s-the-controllers-and-john: A book called The Controllers, by a writer named Martin Cannon, argues that some alien abductions were faked, and Michels says a man named John B. Alexander "threatened him when he wrote this book." Michels tells this himself and does not say where he heard of the threat. In other tellings he describes the book's contents: Cannon writes about MK Ultra, the CIA's secret mind-control research programme, and a related effort he calls MK-Often, says implants were involved, and suggests the alien abduction story was used "as a smoke screen for MK Ultra." A researcher named Greg Malatzi summarises the book the same way, as being about "the fabrication of alien abductions," without mentioning any threat. If the book is right, some abduction reports would be cover for human experiments, and the threat story would suggest someone did not want that said. The tellers agree on the book's thesis, but only Michels, in one telling, brings up Alexander's threat.
martin-gardner-finds-his-own-lost-book: Martin Gardner, a writer on mathematics and puzzles, was once browsing in a used bookstore when he came across a familiar title, and it turned out to be a lost book of his own. Michael Shermer, a researcher billed on the show as America's top skeptic, tells this without naming his source. He mentions it alongside the statisticians Persi Diaconis and Frederick Mosteller, as an example of how a striking coincidence can happen by plain chance.
mary-k-sturdivant-as-lockheed-insider-wh: A person named Mary K. Sturdivant is suggested to have been an insider at Lockheed Martin, a big American defense contractor, who helped shut down Kona Blue, a proposed government program tied to the study of UFOs, in the years between 2006 and 2021. A researcher who goes by UAPGerb raises this as a possibility, not a finding, saying there "may have been a conflict of interest" inside the company. If true, it would mean a private contractor helped stop the government from taking on the subject.
mary-magdalene-lands-at-marseille-merovi: According to some old traditions, Mary Magdalene, the follower of Jesus named in the Gospels, sailed with Joseph of Arimathea, the man who in the Gospels buried Jesus, and came ashore at the spot that is now Marseille, in southern France. The researcher Randall Carlson passes this on as tradition, without naming a source. The story matters to those who tell it because it is linked to the idea of a sacred bloodline running into the Merovingians, an early line of French kings.
mary-s-mosaic-mary-pinchot-meyer-and-jfk: A book called Mary's Mosaic is about Mary Pinchot Meyer, a Washington woman close to President John F. Kennedy in the 1960s and once married to the CIA officer Cord Meyer. Michels brings the book up himself in an episode on Kennedy and UFOs, saying only that he thinks that is its title, as a source on what Kennedy may have known.
masonic-and-zodiac-symbolism-in-nasa: Some say the US space agency NASA is full of hidden symbols from Freemasonry, a fraternal order with its own secret signs, and from the zodiac. The researcher Luis Elizondo makes the point without naming a source: "look at Launchpad 33 I mean everything is Masonic," he says, and adds that the Apollo moon missions follow "the zodiac signs." Jesse Michels returns to the idea in his own words, crediting a writer named Richard Hoagland and his book Dark Mission. He goes further and speaks of the idea that there are "cult rituals" behind the space program, again pointing to Launchpad 33. The claim matters to the tellers because it would mean the space program was shaped by a hidden belief system the public was never told about.
mass-of-online-prophecies-of-9-11-2001: The claim is that there were a great many predictions, or prophecies, of the September 11, 2001 attacks on New York posted before they happened. A researcher who writes about prophetic dreams, Eric Wargo, says "there's a million" of them, without naming any one source. If so, it would suggest that people sense major events before they happen.
mass-sighting-near-hometown-explained-as: Near Mariestad, Sweden, many people once reported a big sighting in the sky that was later explained as the planet Jupiter. The Swedish UFO researcher Clas Svahn, who says he was there and part of it, tells it in a 2026 episode. He describes it only as "this huge observation" near his hometown.
massive-cme-event-during-the-older-dryas: During the Older Dryas, a cold spell near the end of the last ice age, the Earth was hit by a huge burst of charged material from the sun, known as a coronal mass ejection, and it was bigger than anything seen in modern human history. A researcher named Matt LaCroix says so, pointing to ice cores drilled in Antarctica but naming no particular study. If true, it would mean a solar catastrophe struck the ancient world around 12,000 BC.
masters-childhood-precognition-of-a-gray: At eight years old, Mike Masters, a researcher who argues that aliens may be humans from the future, had what he now understands as a moment of precognition, seeing something before it happened, in which he pictured a gray alien. Masters tells it himself, saying that moment is how he "got into this." It is the starting point of his lifelong interest in the subject.
masters-face-to-face-contact-with-future: A researcher named Mike Masters, who argues that the visitors are humans from the future, says that in 2022 at a conference hotel in Phoenix, Arizona, two such beings approached him face to face. He tells it as his own experience: one pulled a chair up so close that his knee pressed into Masters' crotch. If true, it would mean these future humans walk among us and seek people out.
matching-puncture-marks-examined-by-dr-m: In 2019 on St. Simons Island, Georgia, puncture marks on the body of someone who reports being taken by non-human beings were examined by a doctor named Dr Margo, who is said to have found them "exactly the same depth" and the same size. Mario Woods, a former guard at a nuclear site who describes his own abduction, relays what the doctor told him. The matching marks are offered as physical evidence that something was done to him.
material-found-buried-deep-in-rocks-at-t: In 2016, at a place in New Mexico said to be the site of a UFO crash, a small group dug and found material buried far down beneath rocks, according to Diana Pasulka, a professor of religious studies who says she was there. She says they did find things, but they were not easy to find: if they had been planted, they were placed under rocks that looked like they had sat there for a hundred years. She tells it as a reason to doubt that the material was simply put there recently.
materials-scientist-the-metal-acts-like-: A materials scientist, working somewhere around Silicon Valley and NASA in the 2020s, is said to have described an unusual metal as acting "much like an animal", always seeking energy and seeking to connect. Chris Bledsoe, a man who says he attracts UFOs and who has been studied by NASA, repeats the words as he heard them from the scientist, whom he does not name.
mathematician-sees-dmt-entities-solving-: A mathematician named Andress is said to have seen beings, while on DMT, a very strong psychedelic drug, solve the four color theorem, a hard maths problem about colouring any map with four colours so no neighbours match, in under a second, over and over. The neuroscientist Andrew Gallimore tells this as what the mathematician reported to him. To Gallimore it suggests the beings met on DMT have minds far beyond ours.
matt-bell-funds-robots-to-drill-the-quee: Matt Bell, from a show called the Limitless podcast, is said to be paying for robots that will explore the narrow shafts running out of the Queen's Chamber, a room inside the Great Pyramid at Giza in Egypt, and drill through a small door that blocks the northern shaft, in 2026. A researcher named Jeffrey Drum tells this on the podcast without naming a source. What sits behind that door has long been an open question, so the work could show what the shafts were for.
matt-gaetz-constituent-describes-similar: A constituent of the congressman Matt Gaetz is said to have come into his office and described something very like other accounts of people with psychic abilities being carried as cargo. Michels tells this as something Gaetz recounted on a live Twitter audio chat, and he raises it as a sign that such stories reach elected officials from more than one direction.
matthew-bevan-s-1990s-hacks: A British hacker named Matthew Bevan is said to have broken into US government computers, including those of the US Department of Energy, back in the 1990s. Gary McKinnon, a hacker who says he found signs of a secret space program in NASA systems, mentions Bevan as someone who did this before him. It is told to show McKinnon was not the first to go looking.
matthew-brown-amentum-hangars-at-pax-riv: Hangars at Naval Air Station Patuxent River, a Navy base in Maryland, owned by a company called Amentum are said to hold anomalous material. The online researcher UAPGerb tells Michels that the Pentagon whistleblower Matthew Brown said so, and Brown himself reads out his post on X, the social media site, of 6 June 2025, telling the businessman Elon Musk it "shouldn't be an issue for you to get a tour of the special project hangars owned by @amentum_corp (and other fun spaces). Make sure to look up!" The post does not say what the hangars hold; that they house anomalous material is how the tellers read it.
matthew-brown-discovers-immaculate-const: A former government official named Matthew Brown is said to have found a secret document called Immaculate Constellation that had been wrongly uploaded to IntelLink, a shared computer network used by US intelligence agencies, sometime in the 2020s. Jeremy Corbell, who reports on UFOs, passes this on from Brown, and Michels adds, crediting Corbell and the journalist George Knapp, that the document talks about transmedium objects, meaning UFOs that move in and out of the water. If true, it would mean the government keeps a record of such craft that it has never made public.
matthew-brown-prison-planet-humans-captu: A man named Matthew Brown is said to have claimed that there is a god, but that Earth is a kind of prison planet and humans are, in effect, captured by certain beings. Michels relays this himself on a 2025 episode as something Brown told him.
matthew-brown-s-view-of-humans-as-a-reso: A former government official named Matthew Brown is said to have stated that people may be a resource for non-human intelligence, meaning beings not from humanity. Michels brings this up twice, recalling it from an interview Brown gave the filmmaker Jeremy Corbell on Corbell's show Weaponized, and adds that Brown was smeared by the Office of the Director of National Intelligence, which oversees US spy agencies. If true, it would mean someone inside government believes humans are being used by something else.
matthew-brown-s-wmd-corruption-whistlebl: A State Department official named Matthew Brown is said to have also blown the whistle on corruption involving WMDs, weapons of mass destruction, his area of expertise, in the 2020s. The filmmaker Jeremy Corbell says so, passing on what he knows of Brown. It is told to show Brown has spoken out on serious matters beyond UFOs.
matthew-brown-snuck-into-secret-congress: Sometime between 2024 and 2026, the filmmaker Jeremy Corbell says he quietly brought a man named Matthew Brown into a secret briefing in Washington with three members of Congress. Corbell says all three lawmakers had agreed to meet when he asked. He tells it himself, as the person who arranged it, in a 2026 episode.
matthew-brown-uncovers-immaculate-conste: A man named Matthew Brown says that in 2024 he figured out a secret program called Immaculate Constellation, said to gather government records of unexplained flying objects, and that Luis Elizondo, a former Pentagon official who worked on such reports, was tied to it by name. Michels passes on what Brown told him, calling it "maybe the weirdest, most interesting thing." He adds that Elizondo then testified alongside the journalist Michael Shellenberger and said he could neither confirm nor deny whether he had been let in on the program, a story that also touches the filmmaker Jeremy Corbell.
matthew-brown-white-house-ai-timeline-ma: The White House is said to have a special artificial intelligence system that manages, or predicts, the course of future events. Michels repeats this from a Pentagon whistleblower named Matthew Brown, first calling it an AI timeline management system and later describing it as an AI able to accurately predict a range of future events, which would mean the government can see what is coming.
matthew-sullivan-s-death-and-his-legacy-: A man named Matthew Sullivan is said to have worked inside a secret "legacy program," a long-running hidden effort to recover and study unknown craft, and to have handled such craft directly before he died. Congressman Eric Burlison says he was told Sullivan "was in the legacy program, had firsthand experience with craft," naming the whistleblower David Grusch and a man named Jake Barber in the same breath. Jeremy Corbell, who makes films on the subject, says Sullivan "had direct hands-on with the craft" and was set to testify to Congress in private about two weeks before he died. Corbell says the FBI is looking into whether the death was suspicious, and mentions a letter from members of Congress and the intelligence community's inspector general, its internal watchdog. The tellers differ on the timing, with Burlison's account set around 2023 and Corbell's in 2025 or 2026. It is told because, if true, a would-be witness died just before he could speak.
maurice-hill-s-jellyfish-shaped-ufo-1973: Around 1973 or 1974, in the Washington DC area, a groundskeeper named Maurice Hill says he had a close-up encounter with a UFO shaped like a jellyfish. Michels tells this in his documentary about Lue Elizondo, passing on what he heard Hill say about his own encounter. He offers it as one of the up-close accounts that drew people into the subject.
maurice-hill-witnessed-the-1952-washingt: A man named Maurice Hill was living in Washington DC in 1952, when strange objects were reported flying over the city and the Capitol, a famous UFO episode, and he is said to have witnessed it. Luis Elizondo, a former Pentagon official who ran a small office there that studied unexplained aerial reports, introduces Hill on camera and passes on what Hill told him.
maury-island-incident-slag-rains-onto-a-: In 1947 a man sitting in a boat in Puget Sound, near Maury Island in Washington State, is said to have seen several UFOs fly overhead, one of them seemingly in trouble, which then rained shards of metal or slag all over his boat. The writer and researcher Peter Levenda retells it without naming a source, and ties it to a man named Fred Crisman. It is told as an early case where a UFO supposedly left physical debris behind.
maussan-sues-the-peruvian-government-for: Jaime Maussan, a man who has championed the strange three-fingered bodies found in Peru, says he sued the Peruvian government for 300 million dollars over its handling of them, sometime in 2024 or 2025. Maussan says it himself: "I put a lawsuit against them for $300 million." A journalist named Pavel also tells it, without giving a figure, saying the lawsuit "forced the Peruvian Ministry of Culture and the Peruvian government to take this a little more seriously." If so, the case pushed officials to look harder at the bodies.
max-davis-s-first-skeptical-reaction-to-: A man named Max Davis says that when messages first came from Josiah, a boy featured in a documentary about children said to read minds, his doubt was so strong it made someone cry. He tells it as his own memory and calls himself a skeptic. He presents it as how his involvement began, before he came to see things differently.
maxwell-and-epstein-meet-castro-for-perm: Maxwell, whom the teller calls Glenn Maxwell, is said to have gone to Cuba with the financier Jeffrey Epstein to meet Fidel Castro, Cuba's longtime leader, and ask permission to dive on an underwater site there. The philosopher Jason Jorjani tells this as something he had heard, placing it after the site "disappears from the media". If true, it would tie Epstein's circle to a secret interest in what lies on that site.
maxwell-sells-promis-software-to-sandia-: The story goes that in the 1980s the British media owner Robert Maxwell sold a computer program called Promis, a piece of data-tracking software, to Sandia Labs, a US government weapons laboratory in New Mexico. A researcher named Jason Simosa, who also counts himself a witness, tells it without naming a source: "So, he sold that to Sandia Labs." He tells it because it would put a foreign businessman's software inside one of America's most secret labs.
mayan-flood-legend-of-atlan-and-tulan: According to a researcher named Jason Jorjani, the Maya of ancient Central America told of a homeland lost to a great flood, and they had two names for it: Atlan and Tulan. Jorjani tells this on Michels's show, crediting the idea to the writer Graham Hancock. He brings it up because "Atlan" sounds so much like Atlantis, the sunken island of legend, as if the two traditions might remember the same place.
mayor-earl-cabell-brother-charles-cabell: Michels points out that the mayor of Dallas when President Kennedy was shot there was Earl Cabell, and that Cabell's brother, Charles Cabell, was the CIA's number two at the time of the Bay of Pigs, the failed 1961 invasion of Cuba backed by the United States. Michels raises this himself, in an episode on Kennedy's death, as a possible link between the CIA and the city that planned Kennedy's motorcade route.
mccasland-and-monica-reza-cases-possibly: The case of a general named Neil McCasland seems eerily, possibly connected to that of a woman named Monica Reza. Michels raises this himself, in an episode about top American scientists who have gone missing, without saying how the two might be linked.
mccasland-as-pentagon-director-of-specia: From June 2009 to May 2011, an Air Force officer named Neil McCasland is said to have been director of special programs in the Pentagon office that buys weapons and technology for the military. That put him over special access programs, the most secret and tightly restricted military projects. Michels tells this himself in an episode about missing scientists, citing McCasland's official Air Force biography, Pentagon training papers and Wikipedia, as a way of showing how close McCasland stood to the government's most hidden work.
mccasland-buys-a-medical-kit-at-rei-befo: Before he went missing in New Mexico in 2026, a retired Air Force general named Neil McCasland is said to have stopped at REI, an outdoor gear store, and bought a medical kit. Eric Burlison, a US congressman, passes this on as "the latest information" he has about the disappearance, a detail that would suggest McCasland was preparing to be out on his own.
mccasland-delonge-contacts-as-a-disclosu: The filmmaker Jeremy Corbell argues that the contacts in 2015 and 2016 between Neil McCasland, a senior Air Force officer, and the musician Tom DeLonge were an organised effort, an "op" in his word, by people inside the system trying to get UFO information out, and that it was meant to prepare the ground for a presidency of the politician Hillary Clinton. Corbell says "op" is not meant as an insult: "there were people trying to get [ __ ] out." He points to an email published by WikiLeaks, a site that posts leaked documents, and to the journalist George Knapp, and if he is right, a planned release of UFO secrets was tied to the 2016 election.
mccasland-s-elephant-remark-to-delonge-2: Around 2015 or 2016, the retired Air Force general Neil McCasland is said to have told the musician Tom DeLonge, after their first phone call, that he worried DeLonge might find a group of people stumbling around an elephant. The researcher Jason Simosa relays the remark, which he reads as a hint that a hidden group was circling a huge secret about UFOs without fully grasping it.
mccasland-s-wife-tweets-about-alien-abdu: After a man named McCasland vanished in New Mexico, his wife reportedly posted on Twitter that maybe the best explanation was that an alien had abducted him from a mother ship, "although no mother ship has been found in the local area." Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, and reads the post as a pointed, sarcastic remark from someone close to the case.
mcconnell-invites-kirkpatrick-to-senate-: A Senate staffer named Kirk McConnell, who worked for the Senate committee that oversees the military, says he regularly invited Sean Kirkpatrick, head of the Pentagon's office for investigating UFO reports, to sit in on his interviews with Navy pilots and scientists, and to a briefing by Brandon Fugal, a businessman who owns a ranch known for strange events. McConnell tells Michels this first-hand: "I invited him with some regularity to sit in on our interviews." The point is that the official in charge was shown the same witnesses Congress heard.
mccord-s-letter-to-judge-sirica-1973: A lawyer named Dan Sheehan says that in 1973 James McCord, one of the men caught in the Watergate break-in, grew angry that he and the others were being sold down the river and wrote a letter to John Sirica, the judge hearing the case. Sheehan, who says he was close to it through his office, tells it as the moment that cracked the cover-up open.
mcculloch-letters-urging-cia-and-navy-to: Letters kept in a Northwestern University archive show the scientist Warren S. McCulloch writing to the CIA, the US spy agency, and to the Navy, urging them to look into Andrija Puharich, a researcher of psychic abilities. The researcher Greg Malatzi describes these letters, and also mentions the writer Annie Jacobsen in connection with them. They matter because they would show government agencies being steered toward Puharich's work early on.
mccullough-on-the-phone-they-did-it-not-: A man named Chuck McCullough is said to have told Dylan Borland on the phone, in 2025, "Well, they did it. The whistleblowers didn't", pinning some wrongdoing on others rather than on the people who had come forward. Borland, a man who has spoken out about secret UFO programs and says false evidence was built against him, tells it himself, also naming the filmmaker Jeremy Corbell in connection with the call.
mcdonald-confronts-hynek-over-the-swamp-: In the 1960s, the story goes, a physicist named James McDonald went to the astronomer J. Allen Hynek and angrily told him he was taking part in a cover-up of UFO sightings. Michels tells it himself, without naming a source. In his version, McDonald, whom he calls a serious physicist, tells Hynek that what people saw in Michigan was not swamp gas, which was the explanation Hynek had given for a wave of sightings there. A researcher who goes by RedPandaKoala tells it too, also without a source, and says McDonald was furious and told Hynek that what he was doing to science was horrible. In RedPandaKoala's version, this confrontation is a big part of why Hynek later changed his stance and came clean about UFOs.
mcdonald-mocked-in-congressional-hearing: After a 1966 wave of UFO sightings in Michigan, a scientist named James McDonald who took UFOs seriously was, it is said, mocked in a hearing of the US Congress, with a congressman making fun of his interest and the whole room laughing. A researcher who goes by RedPandaKoala tells it as a well-known episode, without naming a source, as an example of how hard it was to raise the subject in public.
mcdonnell-douglas-parapsychology-lab-197: The aerospace company McDonnell Douglas ran a program studying psychic phenomena at Washington University in St. Louis. Michels brings this up himself in three episodes without naming a source. In one he says James McDonnell, the company's founder, set up the institute in the 1960s and was close to Bob Jahn, a Princeton dean of engineering who went on to start a Princeton lab studying anomalies of the mind. It would mean a major weapons maker took the paranormal seriously.
mcdonnell-instructs-staff-to-study-ufos: James McDonnell, head of the aircraft maker McDonnell Douglas, is said to have told his company to study UFOs. The aviation journalist Nick Cook says there are declassified company papers that show McDonnell giving that instruction, though he does not quote them. If true, it would mean a major plane builder took UFOs seriously enough to put its own staff on them.
mckenna-brothers-weeks-long-mushroom-tri: In the 1970s, the brothers Terence McKenna and Dennis McKenna, both famous for writing about psychedelic drugs, took mushroom trips in the Amazon that lasted for weeks. Michels says that during these trips they would "download and channel things," meaning they felt they were receiving ideas from beyond themselves. He tells it himself, without naming a source.
mckenna-stone-ape-theory-consciousness-f: The idea is that human consciousness began when our primate ancestors found and ate mind-altering mushrooms. It comes from the writer Terence McKenna, and people call it the stoned ape theory. A researcher named Jeffrey Mishlove, who holds a doctorate, sums it up this way: consciousness itself developed when our ancestors discovered these mushrooms. Michels describes McKenna's version himself. A couple of million years ago in Africa, he says, hunter-gatherer bands had to follow animal dung to find their prey. In another episode he says the theory could explain why skull size doubled between Homo habilis, an early human species, and modern humans. The writer Graham Hancock names McKenna's book Food of the Gods as one of the first books to set it out. If it were true, a plant would have helped make us human.
mckinnon-on-why-he-scanned-us-military-n: Around 2000 to 2002, a British computer hacker named Gary McKinnon read a book from the Disclosure Project, a campaign led by Steven Greer and his team to gather testimony on hidden UFO knowledge, and decided to run what he calls "a light scan on American military networks" from his girlfriend's aunt's house in London. McKinnon tells Michels this himself. He says that by using accounts with blank passwords he got into networks at the National Security Agency at Fort Meade, the Defense Information Systems Agency, the Department of Defense, and the Army, Navy and Air Force, something he now calls "mad" but says felt at the time like "a playful idea" to see whether the book's claims held up.
mckinnon-s-hard-drives-seized-by-office-: When the British computer hacker Gary McKinnon was arrested in 2002, all his data went to the Office of Naval Intelligence, the US Navy's intelligence service, and he says they still hold his hard drives. McKinnon, who says he found signs of a secret NASA space program, tells it himself in a 2026 episode. He says he has tried for years to get them back and was told: "No, it's still an ongoing investigation. You can't touch it."
mckinnon-s-left-heel-puncture-experience: One night around 2006 a man named Gary McKinnon, known as a hacker who broke into NASA computers, woke to a sharp pain and found two perfectly round holes in his left heel. McKinnon tells it himself: "There were two perfectly circular holes, both about five millimeters in diameter." In another telling he dates it to 2005, places it in a small first-floor rented room, and adds that bumps appeared later that he suspected were an implant. He tells it as a sign that something was done to him in his sleep.
mcminnville-photo-string-revealed-at-fre: The McMinnville photos, two famous 1950 pictures of a saucer-shaped object over a farm in McMinnville, Oregon, are said to have been shown at a conference in France to have a string in them, suggesting the object was hanging from something. A researcher named Clas Svahn mentions this only in passing, saying it came out at "this conference in France a couple" of years back, without naming who presented it. If it holds, one of the best-known UFO photographs would show a small model hung from a line.
mcminnville-trent-photos-1950: In 1950, Paul Trent and Evelyn Trent, whom Michels calls "hapless farmers", took photos of what they said was a UFO near their farm in McMinnville, Oregon. Michels tells this himself and says the case is "unfalsifiable in either direction": no one can prove it real or fake. Another time he mentions it without naming the Trents, grouping it with another case he calls Lake Cote and saying that in both "we have video."
mcmoneagle-remote-views-a-submarine-bein: In 1979, the story goes, a soldier named Joe McMoneagle was asked to describe a sealed building at a Russian shipyard on the White Sea using remote viewing alone. Remote viewing is a practice, once studied by the US government, of trying to see distant places with the mind. He described a huge new nuclear submarine being built inside. Michels tells it twice, once with the 1979 date and once from his own interview with McMoneagle, where he puts it in "78 or 79" and does not name the shipyard. McMoneagle tells it himself: "what I got was a really unique submarine." In his version the site is north of the Arctic Circle, the submarine is called TK-089, his report went to the National Security Council and to Robert Gates, a senior intelligence official, and the submarine was confirmed 114 days later. If it is true, it would mean the mind can gather real intelligence across great distances.
mcmoneagle-s-cia-mars-remote-viewing-mar: In 1984, according to the philosopher Jason Jorjani, a remote viewer named Joe McMoneagle, someone said to describe distant places using only his mind, was tasked by the CIA at the Monroe Institute, a Virginia centre for consciousness research, to view Mars a million years ago. McMoneagle tells it himself and says he saw pyramids and dying people, "just really big people," about 12 feet tall, though he gives no date or CIA link. Michels repeats it on several episodes, adding that the full session transcript has been declassified and that contacts at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory sent McMoneagle photos, which would suggest Mars once held human-like life.
mcmoneagle-s-cia-remote-viewing-of-mars-: A man named Joe McMoneagle was, according to Michels, tasked by the CIA to remote view Mars as it was a million years ago, remote viewing being the claimed skill of describing faraway places or times with the mind alone, and he described giant beings there. Michels brings this up himself, mentioning that McMoneagle told it on the show of a podcaster named Shawn Ryan, in an episode about claims of giants.
mcmoneagle-s-jpl-correspondence-and-life: It is an open secret at the Jet Propulsion Laboratory, NASA's space research center in Pasadena, California, that there was once life on Mars, according to what Michels says Joe McMoneagle, a man known for remote viewing, the practice of trying to perceive distant places with the mind, implied to him. Michels relays this himself in a 2025 episode about life on Mars, and if true it would mean space scientists quietly know more than they say.
mcmoneagle-s-legion-of-merit-for-remote-: Joseph McMoneagle, a government "remote viewer" (someone said to see distant places with the mind alone), is said to have won the Legion of Merit, a high US military award, for more than 200 cases where he helped gather intelligence, including hostage cases and sketching nuclear sites. Michels says this himself, without naming a source, on an episode with a Navy scientist, as a sign that the US military found the work useful.
mcmoneagle-s-pentagon-remote-viewing-of-: A man named Joe McMoneagle, working at the Pentagon, is said to have used remote viewing, the practice of trying to see distant places with the mind alone, and seen a UFO hovering over a nuclear missile. Robert Hastings, a researcher who studies UFOs at nuclear bases, passes this on from McMoneagle. If true, it would add to claims that UFOs watch nuclear weapons.
mcmoneagle-tasked-to-remote-view-mars-a-: In the 1980s, a man named Joe McMoneagle, who worked in a US government psychic spy program, is said to have been given coordinates and asked to remote view, that is, to perceive a distant place with the mind alone, the planet Mars as it was a million years in the past. Michels tells it himself and says the tasking is now public and declassified, which, if so, would mean the government took the idea of ancient Mars seriously enough to send a psychic there.
mcmoneagle-tells-jesse-that-humans-may-b: Humans may be slowly turning into the alien beings, or being nudged by them to become like them, according to Joe McMoneagle, a remote viewer, someone trained to try to see distant things with the mind. Michels says McMoneagle told him this on a phone call, putting it as "we might be turning into these ETs". If true, the visitors would be our own future, or a shape we are being led toward.
mechanical-watch-stopped-by-the-emitter-: Between 1987 and 1989, at S4, a secret site in Nevada, a mechanical watch is said to have simply stopped near an emitter, a device Bob Lazar says came from an alien craft he worked on there. The researcher Luigi Vendittelli repeats this from Lazar after spending two days with him, as an example of the strange effects the device is said to have had.
medications-and-diagnoses-cleared-within: A man named Jordan Jose, who says he was taken by a secret UFO program as a child, says that around 2010 to 2011, in Springville, New York, he came off his medications and within a year 'was released from every single' psychological diagnosis. He tells it about himself, as a sign that what he went through was not mental illness.
medieval-angel-hierarchy-guiding-stars-a: In the Middle Ages, the story goes, Christian thinkers believed each star and planet was alive and intelligent and had its own guiding angel. The biologist Rupert Sheldrake describes this view, linking it to the medieval theologian Thomas Aquinas, the early Christian writer known as Dionysius the Areopagite, and the ancient Syrian philosopher Iamblichus, though he names no particular text. He brings it up because it shows that a living, minded cosmos was once the mainstream view.
medieval-paintings-with-ufo-like-objects: Some medieval European paintings show a thing in the sky that looks a bit like a UFO. Michael Shermer, a researcher billed on the show as America's top skeptic, brings this up dismissively ("whatever") while talking about the UFO researcher Jacques Vallée and the religion scholar Jeffrey Kripal, who see such images as signs that the phenomenon goes far back in history.
medvedev-april-fool-s-interview-on-russi: Dmitry Medvedev, a top Russian leader, was once asked about UFOs in an interview on April Fool's Day, and the interviewer expected him to joke. Instead, Michels says, Medvedev answered, "Oh yeah, no, we have an extensive file about this stuff." Michels tells it himself twice. The second time he guesses Medvedev may have been president then, places it in roughly the 2010s, and connects it to nuclear codes, taking it as a sign that Russia keeps its own UFO records.
meeting-a-real-recluse-on-the-second-ath: On his second visit to Mount Athos, a Greek mountain of monasteries, around 2005, Ralph Larson says he met a real hermit who gave him a book. Larson, the guest on a 2026 episode titled after a CIA chief who calls himself a time traveler, tells it himself. He says the two had a tremendous conversation about the end of the world.
meeting-archbishop-marcinkus-at-the-vati: In 1973 Harold Malmgren, a former advisor to US presidents, met Archbishop Paul Marcinkus, the churchman who ran the Vatican's bank, and was told the church already knew all about him. Malmgren tells it himself: the archbishop said, "we know about you from your boyhood with a lot of our associates in the mafia." He tells it to show how closely powerful hidden networks had followed him since childhood.
meeting-bob-lazar-and-george-knapp-at-th: An author known as a CIA historian, Peter Levenda, says he met Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft at a secret Nevada base, for the first time when their project began, around 2017 to 2019, together with the Las Vegas TV journalist George Knapp. Levenda tells it as something he was there for, marking the start of his work with both men.
meeting-edward-teller-before-his-los-ala: In 1982, while working at Los Alamos National Laboratory, the US nuclear weapons lab in New Mexico, Bob Lazar says he met the physicist Edward Teller, known as a father of the hydrogen bomb. Lazar, who later said he worked on alien craft at a secret site in Nevada, tells Michels that the local paper had run a front-page story that day on a jet-powered car he built, and that Teller happened to be giving a speech at Los Alamos the same day. He tells it as how he first crossed paths with Teller, a link that matters to his later account of how he got his job.
meeting-eric-davis-hal-puthoff-and-sonny: While in graduate school working on pulsed fusion, a kind of nuclear energy research, a man named Jack says he went to a conference to present and was introduced to three physicists: Eric Davis, Hal Puthoff and Harold "Sonny" White. Jack tells it himself on a 2025 episode with the Navy scientist Salvatore Pais. He brings it up to explain how he came to know these people.
meeting-jeffrey-epstein-a-constructed-pe: The researcher Eric Weinstein says he met Jeffrey Epstein once, for about an hour, and came away thinking Epstein was a "constructed" person, someone whose identity had been built for a purpose. Weinstein tells it from his own experience: "he was an absolutely terrifying person to encounter." He offers it as a hint that Epstein was not what he appeared to be.
meeting-john-lear-through-gene-huff-s-ap: In 1980s Las Vegas, Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft at a secret Nevada base, met the aviator John Lear through a friend named Gene Huff, a property appraiser. Lazar tells it himself: Huff was doing the appraisal on Lear's house, and Lazar went along. It is how he tells the start of his ties to the circle that would later bring his story out.
meeting-lab-partner-barry-earlier-teams-: In 1988 and 1989, at a secret Nevada site he calls S-4, a man named Bob Lazar says he met his lab partner, a man known only as Barry, and found that the scientists there before him were already quite comfortable around the alien craft they studied. Lazar, who says he worked there, tells Michels that "these guys had reached a point where it was nonchalant." It would mean the work had been going on long before he arrived.
meeting-spielberg-about-a-video-game-in-: In 1996, during a dispute, a Hollywood writer named Bryce Zabel went to Amblin, the film director Steven Spielberg's company in Los Angeles, to meet Spielberg about a video game. Zabel tells it as something he lived through: he sat waiting in Spielberg's office, and Spielberg came in, shook his hand and said, "Great to see you again."
meeting-steven-greer-at-a-boulder-book-s: At a book signing in Boulder, Colorado, in 2018, the UFO researcher Steven Greer is said to have stood up, handed over his card and said, "Don't tell anybody this information." The man who got the card tells it himself: Michael Herrera, who says he once saw a huge craft, about 300 feet long, in the Indonesian jungle. He tells it to Michels as a sign that the people who heard his account early on wanted it kept quiet.
meeting-the-bali-bombing-leader-who-beli: An author and historian named Peter Levenda says he met the man who planned the 2002 Bali bombings, a terror attack in Indonesia, and that this man believed in The Protocols of the Elders of Zion, a text that claims to reveal a secret Jewish plan to rule the world. Levenda tells it first-hand, as proof that such writings still drive real violence.
meeting-the-virgin-mary-in-a-paris-hotel: In 1998, in a Paris hotel, a CIA officer is said to have seen the Virgin Mary appear in the air in front of him. He is Rolf Mowatt-Larssen, a former senior CIA officer, and he tells it himself on the show: he was in Paris on a CIA work trip, "doing actually Russian things," when, after a dream, "off the ground was the full image of the Virgin Mary," standing right across from him. He says she told him to write to the Pope. Coming back to it later in the same conversation, he adds something he says he forgot the first time: at the end she told him, "We will meet again." He also brings up the Catholic monk and writer Thomas Merton. If true, it would be a religious vision granted to a working intelligence officer.
meeting-whitley-strieber-in-politically-: The skeptic Michael Shermer says that in the 1990s he met the writer Whitley Strieber, author of Communion, a book about Strieber's reported meetings with strange beings, in the green room of Politically Incorrect, the TV talk show hosted by Bill Maher. Shermer tells it as his own memory, in a debate about UFOs where he also brings up Budd Hopkins, a man who collected accounts of people who said they were taken by aliens.
meeting-with-grusch-while-he-was-underco: Steven Greer, a UFO researcher, says he met David Grusch, an intelligence officer who later went public about secret UFO programmes, while Grusch was still working undercover and nobody knew who he was. Greer tells this as something he took part in himself, on Jesse Michels's show in 2025. He adds that Grusch's bosses were the people he was passing information to, which would mean Greer had been feeding the same officials who later saw Grusch come forward.
megalithic-architecture-on-mars-seen-by-: Joe McMoneagle and Ingo Swann were remote viewers, people who took part in experiments where they tried to describe faraway places using only the mind. They are said to have seen buildings on Mars in a style matching the largest ancient stone monuments on Earth. The philosopher Jason Jorjani passes this on, also naming a man called Karl Wolfe. He tells it because it would link the giant stone ruins on Earth to a builder that also built on Mars.
meidum-pyramid-as-collapsed-test-structu: The pyramid at Meidum, near the Faiyum oasis in Egypt, was, according to a pyramid researcher named Geoffrey Drumm, a test build meant to model the same physics and chemistry as the Red Pyramid, another ancient Egyptian pyramid, and it suffered "a catastrophic collapse." Drumm gives this as his own reading without naming a source. If he is right, the pyramids were built as working machines, with Meidum as a failed early try.
meier-introducing-nordics-to-arab-leader: In the 1970s a man named Billy Meier, said to be working at the time as a kind of super spy in the Middle East, is claimed to have introduced Arab leaders to tall, very good-looking beings of human appearance, which UFO lore calls Nordics. The philosopher Jason Jorjani repeats this from people who say they were involved with Meier in those years, as written up in a work called Closer Encounters. If true, it would mean such beings dealt directly with world leaders.
melissa-s-ball-of-light-from-john-mack-s: A woman called Melissa, in her early twenties, saw a ball of light come through the sliding doors of her apartment, bounce around the room, go down the hall and into another room. Michels brings it up from Abduction, a 1994 book by John Mack, a psychiatrist who studied people reporting encounters with alien beings. He tells it to show that such visits of strange lights carry on into modern times, in a conversation about UFOs and religion.
memory-floods-back-two-weeks-later-lost-: Richard Barth, a guard at nuclear missile sites at Vandenberg Air Force Base in California, says that in 1964, about two weeks after a strange night, he woke up paralyzed and 'got flooded with this whole experience,' and knew 'it wasn't a dream.' He says there is a gap in his memory from about 2 a.m. to dawn, and that about 20 years later a friend from that night turned down hypnosis meant to recover the lost time, crediting a man named Lonnie and the researcher Robert Hastings for that detail.
men-from-a-twin-study-institute-try-to-t: Sometime between 1957 and 1959, near Allentown, Pennsylvania, two men came to the house of a boy named Jim Weiner and his twin brother Jack Weiner. They asked to speak to the parents, said they came from an institute somewhere that studied twins, and said they wanted to take the two boys away to study them. Jim Weiner tells this from his own childhood memory, as part of a wider story of abduction experiences, which would mean someone was taking an interest in the twins from a very early age.
men-in-black-at-point-pleasant-during-ke: In 1966 and 1967, while the writer John Keel was investigating the Mothman, a winged creature reported around the town of Point Pleasant, mysterious "men in black" would suddenly appear outside the local newspaper office. The researcher Jason Jorjani tells this in passing, without naming a source. It is told as a sign that someone was watching the strange events in the town.
men-in-black-confront-carlos-de-souza-at: In 1996, near the Brazilian city of Varginha, where witnesses say a strange craft crashed and living creatures were captured, a witness named Carlos de Souza says he stopped at a gas station to pull himself together and was approached by men from an unmarked vehicle who already knew who he was. Carlos tells it himself: one of them pointed a finger in his face and said, "Just a word of advice. You didn't see anything. You don't know anything." The filmmaker James Fox, who investigated the Varginha case, retells it from what Carlos told him, but mentions only the unmarked vehicle, not the warning. If true, it would mean someone was working quickly to silence people who saw the crash.
men-in-black-interrogation-about-the-con: Lyn Buchanan, a former Army sergeant, says that in the late 1980s at the Defense Intelligence Agency, the US military's intelligence service, he was questioned by mysterious men about a control panel, the kind of thing he connects to operating a UFO. He tells it as something that happened to him, and mentions a colleague named Ed Dames. Buchanan says that when he gave his answer, a man sitting off to the side slapped his leg and said, "So that's it," as if Buchanan had solved something they had been stuck on.
men-in-black-on-ashaway-road-1990: In 1990, around the time of the first Gulf War, the author Peter Levenda says he had an encounter with Men in Black, the dark-suited strangers said to appear around people connected to UFO matters, on Ashaway Road in Rhode Island, where he was living. Levenda tells it himself as something that happened to him, and in the same telling he brings up the rocket engineer Wernher von Braun. For Levenda it is a sign that someone was watching him.
men-in-black-seen-by-trick-or-treaters-1: Sometime between 1983 and 1986 in southeast New York, children out trick-or-treating are said to have met two strange men dressed in 1920s clothes, who told them that if they ever saw something weird, they should close their eyes and tell it to land. Charles Buhler, an engineer who has worked with NASA, tells the story as something passed on to him, in the tradition of the so-called men in black who are said to appear around UFO sightings.
men-in-suits-arrive-by-helicopter-and-ta: In 2004, after the Navy's encounter with the Tic Tac (a white oval object, shaped like the mint), men in suits are said to have landed by helicopter on the USS Princeton, a Navy warship, and taken all its radar data. A defense writer named Marik von Rennenkampff tells this, passing on, with an "I think", what sailors aboard said, including a sailor named Gary Voorhis. If true, it would mean someone moved fast to take the evidence.
men-in-suits-visit-puharich-at-intelectr: On the day President John F. Kennedy was assassinated in 1963, men in suits are said to have walked into the New York offices of Intelectron, a company linked to the researcher Puharich, and gone into his office. The researcher Greg Malatzi says a woman named Melanie, who worked there at the time, told him this, a detail that would tie Puharich to people in government on a fateful day.
menzel-deletes-harvard-observatory-data-: Starting in 1953, the astronomer Donald Menzel is said to have deleted a great deal of sky data from the Harvard Observatory. Jesse Michels brings this up from what he heard from the astronomer Beatriz Villarroel, whom he calls Swedish. If true, it would mean records that might have shown unusual things in the sky were removed.
menzel-protege-lewis-branscomb-restores-: In the 1960s, a man named Lewis Branscomb, a protégé of the astronomer Donald Menzel, gave the scientist Edward Condon back his security clearance, and Condon then led the Condon Committee, an official study of UFOs, which Michels calls a hit job on the subject. According to Michels, that study killed Blue Book, the US Air Force's UFO study of the 1950s and 60s. He tells this himself, without naming a source, implying the clearance was a reward for burying the UFO question.
menzel-s-name-in-the-majestic-12-documen: The astronomer Donald Menzel, best known publicly as a UFO skeptic, is named in the Majestic 12 documents. These papers claim to describe a secret group set up to study UFOs, unidentified flying objects. The astronomer Beatriz Villarroel brings this up without naming a source. She describes looking into Menzel and "suddenly" finding his name "is famous for the so-called MJ12." Michels tells it in another episode. He says Menzel was named as a member of President Harry Truman's top secret UFO research panel in the late 1940s. Both tell it because it would mean a leading public debunker was secretly on the inside.
menzel-stops-the-harvard-sky-survey-in-1: In 1953, the story goes, the Harvard astronomer Donald Menzel stopped Harvard's famous sky survey, a long-running photographic watch over the whole sky. The astronomer Beatriz Villarroel tells it on two episodes without naming a source, and in one adds that the survey had run since the late 1800s and stayed halted from 1953 to 1967, about 15 years. It matters to her because it would leave a gap in the sky record just when many unexplained sightings were being reported.
menzel-the-objects-are-not-unidentified-: In the 1950s an astronomer named Donald Menzel argued that the flying objects people were reporting were not unidentified at all. In his own words, played on the podcast: "First of all, the objects are not unidentified. We know what they are." His view was that ordinary explanations account for the sightings, so there would be no mystery left to study.
merkavah-mystics-chariot-practice-on-yom: Every year on Yom Kippur, the Jewish Day of Atonement, certain groups of Jewish mystics carry out what they call "descending the chariot", a visionary journey from the Merkavah tradition, an old Jewish practice built around visions of God's heavenly chariot. A writer on secret and occult history named Peter Levenda describes this, without naming a source, as proof that such a journey of the mind is possible.
message-board-post-claiming-puharich-nev: Around 1995 someone on an online message board claimed that Andrija Puharich, a researcher of psychic phenomena, never died but was taken in by the government. An unnamed researcher on Michels's show says he came across the post himself, quoting it as saying 'I know for a fact that Puharich never died.' It is told as one of the strange rumours around Puharich's life.
message-do-not-fear-mario-woods-heard-fr: A former guard at a nuclear weapons base named Mario Woods says that during an encounter with beings in South Dakota he kept hearing the words "do not fear" over and over, a message he felt travel through his body like a vibration or a hiss, as if telepathic. He tells it himself across several conversations with Michels, and the details shift: in some he places it on November 5, 1977, at Ellsworth Air Force Base, an Air Force base in South Dakota, rather than in the 1960s, and in one he adds that he recognized the voice and remarks on its accent. If true, it would suggest the beings tried to calm the people they took.
messengers-of-deception-mass-appearance-: The book Messengers of Deception, published in 1979 by the UFO researcher Jacques Vallée, is said to argue that if UFOs suddenly appeared in large numbers around the world, UFO cults could blossom while trust in governments collapsed. The researcher Jason Simosa summarises the book's argument on the show, as a warning of how such an event might be used to shape society.
messerschmitt-s-1952-interview-with-a-fr: Michels says that in 1952 the German aircraft designer Messerschmitt told a French newspaper that UFOs seen in the sky were probably craft he had designed, built through a project linked to a man named Habermohl and at the Škoda Works factory under a man named Hans Kammler. Michels tells this himself, from that interview, as a possible earthly origin for some saucer sightings.
metal-bb-blown-out-of-nose-1964: In 1964, a man named Richard Barth, a former guard at a nuclear missile site who says he was abducted by aliens, says he blew a small metal ball out of his nose. He tells it himself: he had a sinus problem and "a BB came out, little round ball with a flat side on it."
