A researcher on the same episode, not named, adds that it was not copper but looked "chrome plated or something". That researcher puts it years after Barth's childhood and suggests it was an implant. If so, it would be physical proof left behind by an abduction.
metal-detector-search-finds-the-crash-si: When a metal detector search was made in 2025 at the spot near Varginha, Brazil, where a UFO is said to have crashed, the ground turned out to be all dug up. The documentary filmmaker James Fox, who was there, says the man searching with him told him, "Man, this whole area has been all upturned," which would suggest someone got to the site first and took away what was there.
metal-factory-worker-hears-radio-station: In the 1950s or 60s a man who worked with metal is said to have heard voices that turned out to be a radio station, picked up through metal dust lodged in his teeth. The story comes from the work of Andrija Puharich, a scientist who studied the mind and later psychic claims. The researcher Greg Malatzi tells it from the writer Annie Jacobsen's account, calling it Puharich's first "aha moment": a mental patient who said he heard voices was in fact receiving New York's WOR radio station. Jesse Michels tells it several times, crediting Puharich and once a documentary about him. In his versions the man worked in a metal mill or sawmill and fine metal got into his teeth, and Michels does not name the station. Once he links it to the idea that thoughts might be sent by very low frequency radio waves. The tellers raise it because it suggests the body could receive signals directly, which Puharich took as a clue to telepathy.
metal-found-near-the-serpent-mound-area-: A piece of strange metal is said to have been found near the Serpent Mound in Ohio, an ancient Native American earthwork built in the shape of a snake, which is described as a place of unusual activity. Chris Bledsoe, a man who says he attracts UFOs and who has been studied by NASA scientists, tells it as something passed to him by a man named Timothy Taylor. Bledsoe brings it up because the spot near the mound would link the metal to a known hot spot of strange events.
metal-ore-veins-with-rare-earths-gold-an: Veins of iron ore running through the bedrock under the Giza Plateau in Egypt, where the great pyramids stand, are said to be full of precious metals and rare elements. To the man telling it, this is a clue to what the pyramids were really for. The researcher Geoffrey Drumm makes the claim, saying he has chemical analysis data showing these mineral deposits are "permeated with rare earth elements, gold, silver." In a second telling in the same episode he adds electrum, a natural mix of gold and silver, and says the samples hold "everything that you could think of." In a later episode, where he says an alien told him the pyramids' true purpose, he speaks more loosely of "valuable metal deposits." Platinum, named in some versions of the claim, does not appear in his quoted words. All of this rests on Drumm's own account of the analysis, and Michels hosts both conversations.
metaverse-as-answer-to-the-fermi-paradox: When the metaverse, a plan for shared virtual worlds, was announced in 2021, a Harvard researcher named Avi Loeb says he realised it might solve the Fermi paradox, the puzzle, named for the physicist Enrico Fermi, of why we see no sign of alien civilizations if they should be common. His thought, offered as his own idea, is that advanced civilizations may retreat into virtual worlds and stop reaching out into space.
methane-detected-in-the-martian-atmosphe: In 2003, methane, a gas that living things can produce, was detected in the atmosphere of Mars. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, as support for the idea that life on Mars is "a distinct possibility."
mexican-congress-hearing-on-peruvian-ali: In 2023, according to Michels, Mexico's Congress in Mexico City held a session about mummies from Peru that were presented as aliens. Michels mentions it only in passing, without naming a source, as something that happened the day after another UFO event. It shows the subject reaching a national lawmaking body.
mexico-city-bank-money-in-bernard-barker: The cash found in the pocket of a man named Bernard Barker, arrested in 1972, came from a Mexico City bank account belonging to a lawyer whose name sounds like "Agario", and that money, the story goes, traces back to money skimmed from casinos. A researcher named Dan Sheehan tells this without naming a source, and he ties the account to the New Orleans crime boss Carlos Marcello and to an assassination. If true, it would join a 1972 political scandal to organised crime money going back to the early 1960s.
mh370-orb-videos-and-ashton-forbes-s-tel: MH370, a Malaysian airliner that vanished in 2014 in a story CNN covered for three months, is said by a researcher named Ashton Forbes to appear in videos being circled by three glowing orbs over the Nicobar Islands. Forbes, who began posting about it on Twitter, claims the orbs were man-made, fusion-powered plasma that opened a spinning wormhole and teleported the plane westward out of the sky. Michels tells this himself in several episodes, repeating Forbes's claim, which would mean secret human technology far beyond anything known.
mh370-videos-teaser-2014: Some videos tied to MH370, the civilian airliner that vanished over Southeast Asia in 2014, are said to show the plane simply disappearing. Michels raises the videos with Salvatore Pais, a Navy scientist who holds patents on unusual physics. Pais says that when he watched them and saw "that thing open up", he recognised what he calls the Pais effect, the physics described in his own work. If he is right, the plane's disappearance would be tied to technology like the one he patented.
mia-s-diary-says-she-can-read-minds-then: A girl named Mia in Monterrey, Mexico, is said to have written in her diary that she could read her parents' minds, and in fact everybody's mind, and was then tested at home during the COVID pandemic, between 2020 and 2022. The story is told by Ky Dickens, a filmmaker behind a documentary about telepathy in children, who relays what she was told about the diary and the home tests. If true, it would point to a child reading thoughts.
mica-under-the-teotihuacan-pyramids-as-t: The claim is that huge sheets of mica, a thin, glassy mineral, were brought to the Pyramid of the Sun at Teotihuacan, the ancient city in Mexico, from two to three thousand miles away in South America, and that this hints at some technology. Jim Weiner, a guest who speaks as a witness to abduction experiences, raises it as a question without naming a source: why would anyone haul it that far? If there was a reason, the pyramid would be more than a monument.
mice-inheriting-fear-of-acetophenone: Mice taught to fear acetophenone, a chemical with a sweet smell, are said to have passed that fear on to their offspring, who had never been taught it. The biologist Rupert Sheldrake describes this study from a US university, noting it was published in the journal Nature under a title about inheriting the fear of fathers, and he raises it because it would mean learned memories can be inherited.
michael-aquino-s-ceremony-at-wewelsburg-: A man named Michael Aquino is said to have held some kind of satanic ceremony in the 1980s at Wewelsburg Castle in Germany, the castle used by the SS, the Nazi elite guard. The researcher Peter Levenda tells this himself, pointing to a book called Unholy Alliance. It is told as a sign of a link between modern occult groups and Nazi ritual sites.
michael-aquino-says-mj-meant-non-human-b: The letters "MJ", which appear in the MJ12 documents, papers describing a supposed secret group that handled the UFO matter, were used inside US Space Command as a label for non-human living beings, according to a man named Michael Aquino. The writer Peter Levenda, who studies the history of intelligence agencies, repeats what Aquino told him: "Oh yeah, MJ, we had that in... Space Command. We use that for non-terrestrial biologics." If true, it would tie those papers to a real military code for beings not from Earth.
michael-collins-said-no-stars-visible-co: After the 1969 Apollo 11 Moon mission, the astronaut Michael Collins is said to have told a press conference that the crew could not see any stars, while his own later book describes it differently. Michels tells this himself, comparing the press conference with Collins's book, which he does not name. He raises it because, if the two accounts clash, it would raise questions about what the astronauts were saying in public.
michael-confirms-the-ufo-in-the-first-ph: An Air Force veteran named Michael Johnson, in his first phone call with his old fellow guard Mario Woods in decades, confirmed that they both saw a UFO at the November 5 missile site near Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota in 1977. Johnson, who was there, tells Michels: "It was big though. I remember. We saw it. It was white." Two witnesses agreeing after nearly 50 years is why the call matters to them.
michael-driven-back-to-base-by-a-sergean: After a strange incident in 1977 in the missile field of Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota, a former Air Force man named Michael Johnson says his next memory is riding back with a sergeant. Johnson tells it himself, and the gap would mean part of that night is missing from his memory.
michael-eisner-rejects-the-plasma-firewo: Eric Haseltine, a former senior official at the National Security Agency (the US agency that intercepts communications) who earlier worked at Walt Disney Imagineering, the company's design and engineering arm, says he once showed a kind of plasma fireworks, displays made from glowing electrically charged gas, to Disney's chief executive, Michael Eisner. According to Haseltine, who was there, Eisner's answer was simply, "Oh, we're not going to do this."
michael-half-recognizes-doty-from-a-phot: Michael Johnson, a former Air Force man who says he and a fellow guard were taken by aliens at a nuclear missile site at Ellsworth Air Force Base, South Dakota, in 1977, says he half recognizes Richard Doty, a former Air Force special agent, from a photo. Johnson says it himself on Michels's show: "I can't picture him, but I see a guy like him," hinting that someone like Doty may have been around after the incident.
michael-herrera-s-2009-indonesia-encount: In 2009 a Marine unit headed to the Philippines was diverted to western Sumatra in Indonesia, aboard the USS Denver, a Navy ship, as part of what was called Operation Katana. A former Marine named Michael Herrera, who says he was there, says they came upon a huge black craft in the jungle, about 300 feet across, which he describes as having a pyramid-like top with vents at the corners. Others retelling it call it eight-sided and 'blacker than black'. Herrera says a team of about eight American operators in all black, with advanced M4 rifles, rangefinders and body scanners, disarmed the Marines, held them at gunpoint, and talked about whether to 'smoke' them. He says trucks were loaded onto a floating platform and the craft 'rose up past the treetops and then it shot off' toward the ocean, and that the Marines were sworn to secrecy. Michels retells it on several episodes, guessing the team might have been a paramilitary unit of the Department of Energy, the agency that runs America's nuclear work. A researcher who goes by UAPGerb and the researcher Tim Alberino relay it from Herrera, Alberino casting it as human trafficking, and Herrera links it to the craft that Jake Barber, a helicopter pilot, says he lifted, only far bigger. If true, it would mean a secret American team flies a craft like this.
michael-in-a-capsule-with-floating-objec: A former Air Force man named Michael Johnson says that in 1977, near the missile field of Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota, he found himself in an empty space, "a capsule or something", where things were floating around him, and that he bumped into a fellow airman named Mario Woods lying on a table. Johnson tells it as his own experience aboard what he takes to be a craft, which would mean the two men were taken together.
michael-is-put-in-a-machine-like-a-showe: An Air Force veteran named Michael Johnson says that in 1977, at Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota, he was put into a machine that was "like a shower stall." He tells it himself, as part of his account of being abducted by beings while serving there, in a conversation where he reunites with others who say the same happened to them.
michael-johnson-s-visit-and-matching-dra: In 1977, at the Hanes Way Apartments in Rapid City, South Dakota, two Air Force men found that their memories of a strange encounter matched: a craft, a black sphere bouncing up and down in front of their vehicle, a smell, and a voice saying "do not fear". A former nuclear-weapons guard named Mario Woods says his fellow airman Michael Johnson came to see him and had seen and heard every bit of it, and their drawings of the craft matched. Johnson tells it himself, decades later, stressing that he said "I want to write it down before I forget."
michael-johnson-vanishes-with-no-records: After the night in 1977 when two Air Force guards say they were taken by aliens at a missile site near Rapid City, South Dakota, one of them, Michael Johnson, disappeared from the other's life with no records left behind. Mario Woods, a former nuclear weapons guard and the other man, tells it himself: after a final conversation where they agreed on what had happened, "that was the last time I ever saw him," which would suggest someone moved Johnson out of sight.
michael-kratsios-statement-on-manipulati: In 2025 Michael Kratsios, a senior White House science and technology adviser, made a statement that Michels quotes as saying "Our technologies permit us to manipulate time and space. They leave distance annihilated." Michels raises it himself as a sign that people at the top of the US government may be hinting at far more advanced technology than the public knows about.
michael-levin-frog-embryo-in-a-faraday-c: A frog embryo kept in a Faraday cage, a metal enclosure that blocks all outside electric and magnetic signals, will not grow correctly, according to work Michels credits to the scientist Michael Levin at Tufts University. Michels tells it himself twice, and the second time he adds that an embryo placed next to a Wi-Fi router does not grow normally either, which suggests to him that living things depend on electrical fields to take shape.
michael-levin-s-planaria-regeneration-an: A scientist named Mike Levin works with planaria, tiny flatworms that reproduce by cutting themselves in half, with each half growing back into a whole worm. His experiments look at the weak electrical signals in their bodies that seem to guide this regrowth. The account comes from another scientist, Donald Hoffman, who sums up Levin's work on Michels's show and calls it "wonderful." Hoffman uses it to suggest that living bodies are shaped by something more than their genes.
michael-made-to-undress-for-examination-: In 1977 at Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota, after an experience he and other airmen describe as an alien abduction, an Air Force airman named Michael Johnson says base staff made him undress and examined him. He tells Michels he had to be in a room, undressed, with a bunch of men, and he tells it as evidence that the military took what happened to them seriously enough to check their bodies.
michael-s-article-15-discharge-and-coded: An Air Force veteran named Michael Johnson says that around 1977 or 1978 at Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota he was given an Article 15, a form of military punishment, and yet was let go with an honorable discharge, with his record marked in a coded way. He tells it first hand on an episode where veterans who say aliens took them meet again 50 years later. To him the mismatch suggests the military was handling his case in a special way.
michael-s-fight-with-a-sergeant-at-a-mis: A former Air Force man named Michael Johnson remembers getting into a fight with a sergeant at one of the missile sites around Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota in 1977. He tells it himself, as one of the scattered memories from the time of the strange events he describes there.
michael-s-medical-exam-and-injection-sod: An Air Force veteran named Michael Johnson says that in 1977, at the medical facility of Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota, he was examined and injected in the vein with something, which the story names as sodium pentothal, a sedative drug. He tells it himself, saying only that he remembers "they shot something in me, in my vein," as part of his account of an abduction while he served at the base and what followed it.
michael-s-own-memory-frozen-at-the-wheel: Michael Johnson, a former Air Force guard, says that one night in 1977 at a nuclear missile site known as November 5, part of Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota, he froze at the wheel while a big bright light came close in front of him and his partner Mario Woods, then pulled back. He tells it as his own memory, adding that he saw blurry shapes like humans, the kind of detail that would mean the two men were visited by beings and not just a light.
michael-s-regression-procedures-on-board: Under hypnosis with a hypnotherapist named Yvonne Smith, an Air Force veteran named Michael Johnson recalls being aboard a craft in 1977 and undergoing procedures, with needles and something like "a cold blade" slicing his back. Johnson tells Michels about it himself. In another moment of the same session he puts it as fear rather than feeling: "they're going to take specimens or something, they're going to insert something in me." If true, he was the subject of medical work by non-human beings.
michael-s-regression-three-creatures-in-: A former Air Force man named Michael Johnson says that in 1977, at a missile site called November 5 near Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota, three creatures stood in front of his truck: "Three creatures I never seen out of this whole world was in front of me." He recalled this decades later under hypnotic regression, a way of trying to recover buried memories, in a session guided by a hypnotist named Yvonne Smith. If true, it would mean beings that are not from this world met Air Force men at a nuclear missile site.
michael-s-right-arm-weak-since-the-abduc: Right after he says he was abducted in 1977, at Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota, an Air Force man named Michael Johnson noticed that his right arm was sore, and it has been weak ever since. Michels tells this in his own narration of an episode where Air Force veterans who say they were abducted meet again 50 years later. He offers the arm as a lasting physical mark of the event.
michael-s-son-thinks-he-was-dropped-off-: In 1977 a man named Michael, one of a group of Air Force veterans who say they were abducted by aliens, was later dropped off somewhere, and his son thinks that place may have been Area 51, the secret Air Force test site in Nevada. Michels passes on the son's view himself, which, if right, would tie the abduction to the US military.
michael-s-strange-sightings-in-missouri-: An Air Force veteran named Michael Johnson, who says he was abducted by beings while serving at a South Dakota air base in 1977, says he has also seen "strange occurrences" in Missouri, in the Ozarks hill country and in Texas. He mentions them himself in passing, without describing what he saw or when.
michael-sees-football-field-sized-octago: A witness known only as Michael is said to have seen a huge eight-sided craft, as big as a football field, meant for moving humans somewhere else. An online UFO commentator who goes by UAPGerb passes this on from Michael. If true, it would mean there are plans, and craft, to relocate people.
michael-shermer-on-the-white-house-uap-s: In a debate with Michael Shermer, a well-known skeptic and researcher, Michels brings up a White House science advisory committee on UAPs (unidentified anomalous phenomena, the government's term for UFOs). He says someone with connections to people in government, a person he calls Avi, could be part of it. Michels raises this himself, without naming a source, to argue that serious scientists are taking the subject on.
michael-talbot-dies-of-the-leukemia-he-w: The writer Michael Talbot, author of the book The Holographic Universe, had once written a vampire novel in which vampirism was a rare form of leukemia, a blood cancer. Then, in 1992, he died of a rare form of leukemia himself. This comes from Jeffrey Mishlove, a researcher with a doctorate who studies psychic claims and who says he visited Talbot in hospital before he died, and who tells it as a strange irony, as if the novel had foreseen its author's death.
michael-wonders-who-built-the-pyramids-a: An Air Force veteran named Michael, who says he was abducted by aliens, wonders aloud who built the Egyptian pyramids and how the great standing stones of England got where they are. He asks this during a reunion with fellow veterans on Michels' show, as someone who suspects people alone may not have done it.
michele-sindona-s-money-laundering-opera: A financier named Michele Sindona is said to have run, from around 1964, what one teller calls the world's biggest money laundering operation ever, moving about 200 billion dollars. A researcher named Jason Simosa repeats the figure from the author Paul Williams. He brings it up as part of a larger story linking hidden money to secret power.
michels-s-own-sighting-at-the-start-of-h: Jesse Michels says he has seen something strange in the sky himself, and that it happened right when he was starting his show. He brings it up only in passing, without saying what it looked like, where or when, as a way of telling a guest that he too has had an experience like theirs.
michelson-morley-ether-experiments-1890: In the 1890s, by Michels' dating, the scientists Michelson and Morley ran a set of light experiments to detect the ether, an invisible medium once thought to carry light through space. Michels tells this himself while talking with the biologist Rupert Sheldrake, as an example of an experiment that shook up established science.
michigan-swamp-gas-case: The researcher Marik von Rennenkampff brings up the Michigan sightings that were famously explained away as "swamp gas", gas rising from marshes, and says that in such cases you also see large disc-like objects. He mentions it in passing, without a source, during a debate with a UFO skeptic. He raises it as an example of a sighting whose official explanation does not fit what was reported.
mick-s-2017-metabunk-post-calls-the-diet: On December 30, 2017, the skeptic Mick West wrote a post on Metabunk, an online forum he runs to debunk strange claims, in a thread about the Navy's infrared video of the Tic Tac, a white oval object shaped like the mint. In the post he called laughable an interview with Navy commander Alex Dietrich, one of the pilots who said she saw the object. The interview had been put out by To The Stars Academy, a company set up to research UFOs. The writer Marik von Rennenkampff reads West's own post back to him during a debate, to press him on how he dismissed a witness's account.
mick-s-analysis-flir1-object-is-a-distan: The FLIR1 video, a 2004 Navy infrared camera recording from off Southern California, shows an object that seems to zip off the screen, which many found amazing; the skeptic Mick West argues the object is a distant aircraft and the zip is only the camera moving. West makes the case himself in a debate with Michels. His opponent, Marik von Rennenkampff, describes West's analysis a little differently, as saying the object is probably an airliner 50 to 100 miles away, without mentioning the camera movement.
mick-west-sees-a-wingless-plane-fuselage: The UFO skeptic Mick West says that once, on a flight down to Los Angeles, he himself saw what looked like the body of a plane with no wings. He tells it to show how an ordinary aircraft can look like something strange from the wrong angle.
mick-west-tic-tac-video-zoom-change-2004: The famous Tic Tac video, filmed in 2004 by Navy jets from the aircraft carrier USS Nimitz and showing a white oval object shaped like the mint, may show a camera zoom change rather than the object itself doing something strange. The skeptic Michael Shermer relays this from Mick West, another skeptic who studies UFO videos, who points out that the screen reads "zoom 1.0" on its vertical axis. If West is right, part of what looks odd in the footage would come from the camera, not the object.
mickelsen-safeguard-abm-site-and-the-197: The story is that in February 1975 the Mickelsen Safeguard site opened near Nekoma, North Dakota, the only working anti-ballistic missile base in the United States, built to shoot down incoming nuclear missiles, and that a wave of UFO sightings followed that year. The UFO researcher Grant Cameron tells it without naming a source. He links the two because it would suggest the objects were drawn to America's newest nuclear defences.
microwave-cannons-used-to-bring-down-cra: Michels says that people tied to Jake Barber, a man linked to "psionics" (the claimed use of mind powers), and to Northrop Grumman, a large American weapons maker, have a lot of microwave cannons. He raises it himself to suggest those weapons could be used to bring down unknown craft.
mid-1950s-aerospace-propulsion-breakthro: In the mid-1950s, the aircraft maker Martin Aircraft, and maybe other companies, made a breakthrough in aircraft propulsion, and people there said they could be making these new craft on an assembly line within three years. The philosopher Jason Jorjani says this on the show as something "we know", without naming his source. If true, it would mean advanced propulsion was within reach of American industry seventy years ago.
mike-masters-abductees-sanitize-before-b: In many abduction cases studied by a researcher named Mike Masters, the abductees had to clean themselves by showering or doing chemical rinses before they were taken onto the alien craft. Michels repeats this from Masters' work, which supports Masters' idea that the visitors are time travellers from our own future, careful about contamination.
mike-masters-theory-that-ufos-are-time-t: An evolutionary biologist at Montana Tech, a university in Montana, named Mike Masters argues that UFOs may be humans traveling back from the future. Michels brings him up in a conversation, mentioning his books Identified Flying Objects and Extempore. The writer Eric Wargo, in a separate episode, says the real core of the phenomenon "very likely involves time traveling humans," going further than Michels in backing the idea. Both are passing on Masters's ideas rather than any event they saw. If true, the visitors would not be aliens at all but our own descendants.
mike-mcconnell-as-dan-burisch-s-godfathe: Mike McConnell, a former top US intelligence official, is said to have been the godfather of Dan Burisch, a man known for claims about secret alien-related research. Michels mentions this as one of several odd stories around Burisch, passing on what he has heard, including from Brian Jackson, and it would link Burisch to the highest levels of intelligence.
mike-mcconnell-linked-to-s4-area-51-via-: Michels suggests that a man named Mike McConnell, who later led the NSA, the US eavesdropping and code-breaking agency, was involved in work at S4, a secret site said to sit near Area 51, the classified Air Force base in Nevada. He links McConnell to the story of a man named Dan Burisch, who claims to have worked there, and mentions a pilot named John Lear. Michels offers this as his own guess while talking to Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft at S4, and adds that he thinks Burisch's story "holds up a lot less" than Lazar's.
mike-turner-and-aerospace-donors-removed: In 2023 a congressman named Mike Turner, backed by aerospace company donors, is said to have helped remove a clause from a proposed law that would have let the government take control of any UFO material held by private companies, a legal power called eminent domain. Michels offers this himself as his own "understanding of the behind the scenes," also naming Mike Johnson, the Speaker of the House. If true, it would mean companies kept the power to hold such material away from public control.
mike-turner-wright-patterson-donors-and-: Congressman Mike Turner represents the Ohio district home to Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, which Michels calls the center of UFO legend and of efforts to copy recovered craft, going back to the reported 1947 crash at Roswell, New Mexico. Michels says Turner's top donors include Boeing and Lockheed, both big aircraft and weapons makers. He tells it himself as background to a 2023 fight in Congress over an eminent domain clause, a rule that would let the government take private property, suggesting Turner's ties to these companies shaped that fight.
milab-abductee-meets-a-nordic-on-a-milit: A woman who said she had been taken by the military, not only by aliens, said she met a "Nordic" on a military base. A Nordic is a tall, fair, human-looking being in abduction lore. She asked it whether its kind were involved with "the grace", most likely meaning the Greys, the small grey beings of those same stories, and it answered "by degrees." The researcher Tim Alberino retells this from the work of a researcher named Karla Turner and her book Taken. If true, it would mean the military and different kinds of beings work together.
military-abductions-of-abductees-after-g: Some people who say they were taken by gray aliens, the small gray-skinned beings of many abduction accounts, also say that after they were returned home the military showed up and took them again, to Air Force bases and underground bases in the US. A researcher named Tim Alberino retells this, drawing on the work of an abduction researcher named Karla Turner. If true, it would mean the military knows about the abductions and follows up on them.
military-base-calls-a-witness-after-the-: Around 2021 or 2022 in Brazil, a UFO investigator and filmmaker named James Fox interviewed a witness on camera, and right afterward the local military base phoned that same man. Fox tells it as something he was there for, and it would suggest the military was watching who talked to him.
military-convoy-cordons-the-crash-site-a: In 1996, near the Brazilian city of Varginha, close to an army training school, a witness named Carlos de Souza says he drove toward the site where a strange craft had come down and met a military convoy coming at his car as soldiers sealed off the area. He tells it himself, and in a later conversation adds that one soldier stepped back, raised his gun, cocked it and pointed it at his head. If true, it would mean the army moved fast to control a crash site and keep onlookers away.
military-driver-sees-non-human-creature-: A military driver, not named and called only "military X", says that in 1996 at Humanitas Hospital in Varginha, Brazil, he saw a non-human creature with skin that was "very oily" and had "a sort of silicone-like texture." He tells it as an eyewitness, in connection with the documentary Moment of Contact, and it belongs to the wider Varginha story of a craft said to have crashed there and a living being said to have been captured and taken to hospital.
military-helicopters-following-researche: Researchers at the spot in Hart Canyon, near Aztec, New Mexico, where a UFO is said to have crashed, say they have been followed by military helicopters. Scott Ramsey, a researcher of the case, says an earlier researcher named Bill Steinman claimed this happened to him a couple of times in the 1980s as he drove away, and that it happened to Ramsey's own group once while they were putting up a plaque at the site, as if the military still keeps watch over the place.
military-members-saw-football-field-size: Some US military members say that on their drive to work they saw huge triangular craft, the size of a football field, hovering right over them. David Grusch, a former intelligence officer who later became a whistleblower, tells Michels he interviewed these people himself while looking into such reports. He calls what they saw "some really profound stuff."
military-officer-briefs-gaetz-on-hybrid-: A senior military officer once walked into the office of the congressman Matt Gaetz and told him about hybrids, according to Gaetz. The story comes second-hand from Congressman Eric Burlison, who says Gaetz told him about the visit but never gave the officer's rank. If true, it would mean someone in uniform was briefing lawmakers on human and non-human hybrid programmes.
military-officers-who-reported-ufos-were: High-ranking military officers who had reported UFOs were sent for psychiatric exams to John Mack, whom the teller describes as the head of clinical psychiatry at Harvard, and these cases are said to be what first drew Mack into looking at the subject. The lawyer Dan Sheehan tells this on the show, passing on what Mack himself told him. If true, it would mean the military was quietly treating its own witnesses as psychiatric cases.
military-officials-approach-sandler-and-: In the early 1970s, the story goes, US military officials asked two documentary makers, Allan Sandler and Robert Emenegger, to make a film about UFOs, and offered them real military footage for it. A researcher who goes by UAPGerb says two officials approached them and said they could use footage from Holloman, an Air Force base, in which a craft is said to land. Michels, in his own framing, says Emenegger was in touch with Norton Air Force Base and that when he went there "everybody there is talking to him about UFOs." He ties this to their film UFOs: Past, Present and Future, and mentions the astronomer J. Allen Hynek and the television writer Rod Serling. The UFO researcher Grant Cameron, passing on what Emenegger told him, puts the meeting at Norton around 1973 rather than 1971. He names a man named Paul Shartle, a Colonel Coleman, and H.R. Haldeman, a senior aide in the White House, and says the officials asked for "this other documentary on UFOs, but we'd like you to hide it below the other eight documentaries." If it is true, the military wanted to release UFO material to the public quietly, through filmmakers.
military-trying-to-contact-ufos-with-fig: In the 1950s, the story goes, the American military tried to signal UFOs by flashing lights from fighter jets, as an attempt at contact. A researcher named Grant Cameron brings it up as "a story back in the '50s", without naming where it comes from. If true, it would mean the military was not just chasing these objects but trying to talk to them.
military-video-of-instantaneous-accelera: A military video shows an object that accelerates instantly while a weapons system has a firm, weapons-grade lock on it, and an analysis of its dive has since come out. Jeremy Corbell, a filmmaker who reports on UFOs, says he and George Knapp, a Las Vegas TV journalist, obtained the video and released it themselves. If it is what he says, the military recorded a craft moving in ways no known aircraft can.
military-x-everything-started-at-my-farm: In 1996, people near the town of Varginha in Brazil said a strange creature had been caught and taken away by the military. According to a documentary filmmaker named James Fox, a military source he calls only "military X" told him that everything in the case "started at my farm". Fox says he heard this himself while making his film Moment of Contact. If it is true, the source would place the start of the military operation on his own land.
minas-gerais-as-the-centre-of-brazil-s-u: The Brazilian state of Minas Gerais is said to be the centre of the country's UFO activity, and the reason given is its rare elements and minerals. A researcher who is not named in the episode says this, passing on a view he heard from others: "For us, there's a close relationship between the UFO phenomenon and those rare elements, minerals in the whole state." If true, it would mean whatever is behind the sightings is drawn to what lies in the ground.
mind-lamp-turns-green-during-the-episode: During a 2021 episode filmed in Princeton, New Jersey, the people on the show tried to make a "mind lamp" turn green, and it did so on the first try, within the first 30 seconds. Michels describes this himself, citing a researcher named Herb Metts, in an episode about the CIA's program to use psychics as spies. Michels works out the odds as a 2% chance of that happening by luck, which would point to the mind having some effect on the lamp.
minister-joe-s-special-needs-youth-group: In 2023 a minister named Joe, who runs a youth group for children with special needs at a large church, said some of the children in his group were talking about "the hill." The documentary filmmaker Ky Dickens, who made a film about children who seem to read minds, repeats what the minister told her. She tells it because it suggests the children share an experience that nobody taught them.
ministry-of-culture-raids-a-press-confer: Peru's Ministry of Culture is said to have raided a press conference about mummified three-fingered bodies found in Peru, going after a woman named Joyce Mantilla who was involved in presenting them. Michels tells this himself, without giving details, pointing to it as an example of how hard Peruvian officials pushed back against the people promoting the bodies.
minot-afb-all-ten-missiles-down-after-uf: In 1966, at Minot Air Force Base in North Dakota, all ten nuclear missiles in one group are said to have shut down after a UFO appeared nearby. A former Air Force officer named Robert Salas tells this on the show and says it comes from another witness who came forward, a man named David Schindele. If true, it would mean something unknown could switch off American nuclear weapons.
minot-afb-radar-reviewed-by-kevin-knuth-: In 1968, at Minot Air Force Base, a US military base in North Dakota, an unknown object was reportedly caught on radar, and Michels says physicists have since gone over that radar record. He brings it up in a debate with a skeptic and names the physicist Kevin Knuth as one of the people who reviewed it. He tells it as a case that rests on more than eyewitness accounts. A researcher who goes by the online name UAPGerb, speaking without naming a source, tells the same base's story differently: a bomber, which he calls a B-2, met a saucer that flew around it. He gives no year and says nothing about the radar or Knuth.
minot-launch-signal-stopped-by-inhibit-s: In 1966 at Minot Air Force Base in North Dakota, the story goes, a missile officer named Captain David Sher saw a launch indicator come on at his post, and the launch was stopped by an inhibit switch, a safety control that blocks a missile from firing. Michels tells this himself, citing a phone interview that Robert Hastings, a researcher who studies UFOs at nuclear bases, did with Sher. It is told as part of a pattern of strange events at nuclear missile sites, which would mean something was tampering with the weapons.
minuteman-silos-on-black-hills-land-guar: According to Jesse Michels, 150 silos for Minuteman nuclear missiles were sunk into land in the Black Hills of South Dakota that had been promised to the Great Sioux Nation by the Fort Laramie Treaty of 1868, an agreement between the United States and Sioux tribes. Michels says this himself, without naming a source, while telling a story about Air Force veterans, as a reminder of whose land these weapons sit on.
miracle-of-fatima-mass-sighting-1917: In 1917 in Fatima, Portugal, a huge crowd is said to have seen something strange in the sky. Michels tells it as three orphans being given a prophecy that the Virgin Mary would come, and then lights appearing in the sky in front of a hundred or more people. The researcher Jason Simosa says the clouds parted and a thing appeared that lawyers, doctors and other serious witnesses described as a silvery disc. The skeptic Michael Shermer mentions it in passing as the Miracle of Fatima, with a crowd of 50,000 or 70,000. People bring it up because, if true, it would be a religious miracle seen by many people at once that sounds a lot like a UFO.
misawa-disc-flips-on-its-edge-1952: In 1952, during a training exercise at Misawa in Japan, a pilot practising intercepts saw a disc rise up to his plane and flip onto its edge. A commentator named Marik von Rennenkampff tells this, without naming a source, as one of the cases he puts forward in a debate with the skeptic Mick West.
mishlove-s-accredited-doctorate-in-parap: In the 1970s at the University of California, Berkeley, Jeffrey Mishlove earned a doctorate in parapsychology, the study of psychic abilities and similar effects, according to Mishlove himself. He tells Michels he thinks he is the only person in the world ever to hold an accredited doctoral diploma that says parapsychology right on it. He tells it to show that a major university once formally recognised the field.
mishlove-s-eleven-year-study-of-ted-owen: A researcher of psychic abilities with a PhD, Jeffrey Mishlove, says he worked with Ted Owens, a man who claimed psychic powers, for eleven years, from 1976 until Owens died in 1987. Mishlove tells it first-hand, naming the physicists Hal Puthoff and Russell Targ, who studied psychic claims, and the archive on Owens he kept. The study was meant to test whether Owens's claimed powers were real.
mishlove-s-prize-winning-bigelow-essay-o: In 2021 the businessman Robert Bigelow held an essay contest through his Bigelow Institute, asking for "the strongest evidence that human consciousness will survive permanent bodily death," and the parapsychologist Jeffrey Mishlove says his entry won a prize. Mishlove tells it himself, as someone who wrote one of the winning essays arguing that the mind lives on after death.
mishlove-s-remote-viewing-trial-at-sri-1: In February 1976 a researcher named Jeffrey Mishlove was invited to the Stanford Research Institute, a research lab in California, to try remote viewing, the practice of describing a far-off place using only the mind. Mishlove says he took part in a trial there run by the physicists Hal Puthoff and Russell Targ and that it was "very successful", which would mean the mind can perceive places it cannot see.
missile-fields-as-the-obvious-place-for-: If something non-human has been watching humanity's most powerful weapons since the end of the Second World War, then the nuclear missile fields of South Dakota and Montana are "not a strange place to find them at all. They are the obvious place." Michels puts this forward himself, as his own framing, in an episode where Air Force veterans who say they were abducted by aliens meet again fifty years later. If he is right, sightings around missile bases would be watchers checking on our weapons, not chance.
missing-411-national-park-disappearances: A researcher named David Pitus, author of the Missing 411 books about people who vanish in US national parks, is said to have found that the same areas where people go missing are places where people also report seeing UFOs, a link tied to a work called Closer Encounters and to FBI files said to be hidden. The writer Jason Jorjani repeats this from Pitus's work, as a hint that the disappearances and the sightings may be connected.
missing-and-dead-scientists-loureiro-gil: A handful of scientists and officials tied to advanced research are said to have gone missing or died. Among them are a man named Nuno Loureiro, who in Michels's words "basically ran MIT's plasma fusion lab" (MIT is a leading American university, and plasma fusion is research into power from superheated gas), a man named Carl Gilmore linked to Caltech, another top American university, and a man named Neil McCasland linked to Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, a US Air Force base. Michels raises these as "cases people are talking about" while speaking with the researcher Jeffrey Mishlove, without naming a source or saying more about what happened to each, and the point of raising them is that such losses might be connected rather than chance.
missing-fetus-syndrome-grays-take-back-h: In what is called missing fetus syndrome, women are said to become pregnant with a part-human, part-alien child, and then gray aliens, the small gray-skinned beings of many abduction stories, "come and get the fetus" before birth. A researcher named Tim Alberino describes this without naming a source, as a sign that aliens are breeding hybrids.
missing-time-on-drive-home-from-college: Bob Maguire, a former contractor for the CIA, says that on a drive home from college, about two and a half hours in, he and his companion suddenly found themselves in the middle of nowhere, with no idea where they were or how they got there. He tells it as his own experience, saying their watches showed they had somehow lost an hour and a half, which he calls "a classic example of missing time," the kind of memory gap people link to being taken by aliens.
missing-time-waking-up-by-a-reservoir-da: In 1977, two Air Force men named Mario Woods and Michael Johnson are said to have come to in their truck with "missing time", meaning a stretch of time they could not account for. The truck was parked behind the wall of a reservoir dam near a town called Newell, South Dakota, "more than 8 miles from their post." Michels tells this himself in an episode where the two veterans meet again fifty years later, and he offers it as part of an account that, if true, would mean they were taken by something not human.
mission-control-split-between-nasa-and-t: Mission control at Cape Canaveral, the Florida launch site, is split in two, according to a man named Chris Bledsoe who says he attracts UFOs and was shown around: NASA staff sit at the consoles on one side, and on the other side "it's exactly the same, but it's all Air Force people." Bledsoe, who says he saw it himself, mentions a man named Timothy Taylor as part of the visit. He tells it to Michels as a sign that the military quietly sits alongside the space agency.
mission-to-recover-panasonic-toughbooks-: A former military helicopter pilot named Jake Barber says he took part in a mission to recover Panasonic Toughbooks, rugged laptops, believed to hold sensitive information about the retrieval of crashed UFOs. He says the laptops were brought back to a facility in the California desert, and he tells it first-hand as part of his account of secret crash-retrieval work.
misty-echo-test-portal-and-dan-burisch-s: A patch made for Misty Echo, an underground test at the Nevada Test Site in 1988, appears to show a portal underground, Michels says. He tells this himself, crediting the YouTuber Chris Ramsay with tweeting the patch, and says it would explain the story of Dan Burisch, a man who claims to have worked at S4, a secret site near the Area 51 air base in Nevada also tied to the whistleblower Bob Lazar.
mit-dream-implantation-technology: The Massachusetts Institute of Technology, known as MIT, is said to have published technical applications on implanting dreams in people's minds, including from a distance. Matthew Brown, described in the episode as a Pentagon whistleblower, mentions this twice and frames it as recent, public work anyone can look up, which would mean such mind-influencing technology is already being developed openly.
mit-ion-plane-credits-obscure-1920s-scie: In 2018 MIT, the engineering university in Massachusetts, flew a model "ion plane", an aircraft pushed along by electrically charged air with no moving parts. The researcher Jan Lundquist points to it in a documentary episode about the inventor Townsend Brown, without naming a source, and the story ties the work back to an obscure scientist of the 1920s. It is told as proof that an old, overlooked idea about silent propulsion actually works.
mitchell-and-uri-geller-svahn-meets-gell: A UFO researcher named Clas Svahn says he talked a lot with the astronaut Edgar Mitchell about Mitchell's meeting with Uri Geller, a performer who claimed psychic powers, and that Svahn met Geller himself as well. Svahn tells it from his own conversations, without much detail of what passed between them.
mitchell-confessed-blue-orbs-to-the-spac: The Apollo 14 astronaut Edgar Mitchell is said to have privately admitted that during his 1971 moon landing, he and his crew saw blue, orb-like lights following them from the lunar surface. The physicist Maaneli Derakhshani relays this from In Plain Sight, a book by the journalist Ross Coulthart, which quotes an unnamed source called "the Spaceman" who was a close friend of Mitchell's. If true, it would mean astronauts saw something unexplained on the moon and kept quiet.
mitchellhoagland-debate-on-coast-to-coas: The story is that in the 1990s the Apollo astronaut Edgar Mitchell and Richard Hoagland, a writer on space mysteries, had a long debate on Coast to Coast AM, the late-night radio show hosted by Art Bell. A guest named Maaneli Derakhshani mentions it in passing, without naming a source, on an episode about secrets of the Moon. He brings it up as a moment when an astronaut publicly argued over claims about the Moon.
mithras-liturgy-ascent-through-seven-hea: In the Mithras Liturgy, an ancient religious text found among the Greek Magical Papyri, a collection of spells and rites written on papyrus in the Greek and Roman world, a person being initiated uses breathing techniques, visualisations, chants and ceremonies to rise up through seven heavens. Michels tells this himself, citing the texts, as an ancient example of a practice for leaving ordinary reality.
mitre-as-the-place-to-look-for-the-legac: A man named Jordan Jose, who says he was taken into a secret UFO program as a child, says that anyone looking for the "legacy program", a long-running hidden government effort around non-human craft, should look at MITRE, a US nonprofit that runs government-funded research centers. He gives it as advice from his own experience, saying, "if you want to look at legacy program stuff, I'd look at MITER."
mitre-funded-papers-detecting-gravitons-: Research papers paid for by the MITRE Corporation, a US research company that works on government contracts, are said to show that gravitons, the particles thought to carry gravity, could be detected near Earth's atmosphere, at both very high and extremely low frequencies. The researcher Dave Rossi says this, dating the papers to some 20 or 25 years back, without naming the papers themselves. If true, it would mean gravity-related physics was being probed in private far earlier than people assume.
mj-12-burned-memo-on-lancer-1963: A document called the burned memo, one of the Majestic papers said to come from a secret group overseeing UFO matters, is claimed to describe "Lancer," the code name for President John F. Kennedy, around 1963. The researcher Richard Dolan brings it up without naming where it came from, as part of his account of Kennedy and the UFO secret. If true, it would tie Kennedy's fate to that secret group.
mj-12-document-cardinal-spellman-given-a: One of the Majestic 12 papers, documents said to come from a secret group set up to handle crashed saucers, reportedly states that the Catholic cardinal Francis Spellman was given access to the materials from Roswell, the 1947 crash in New Mexico. Michels mentions this document himself, in passing. If genuine, it would mean a senior churchman was let into the most closely held secret of the day.
mj-12-documents-surface-in-1984-sent-fro: A set of papers known as the MJ-12 documents, said to describe a secret group of officials handling UFO matters, first turned up in 1984 and were probably mailed from somewhere near Kirtland Air Force Base in New Mexico. The researcher Richard Dolan says this on Jesse Michels's show, summarising it without naming a source. If he is right, it would point to the papers coming from people close to a military base rather than from an outsider.
mj-12-papers-judged-compelling-but-not-c: In the 1980s a set of papers known as MJ-12 surfaced, said to describe a secret government group handling crashed UFOs, along with a supposed memo briefing President Eisenhower on it, and the researcher who first put them out judged them only "compelling but not conclusive." The writer Greg Bishop tells this, relaying what the researcher Bill Moore said when he released his report on them in a book called The MJ-12 Papers. The point is that even the man who brought the papers to light did not claim they were proven real.
mj-12-scientists-really-were-involved-19: The scientists named in the Majestic 12 papers really were involved in secret UFO work in the years after 1947, says the author Whitley Strieber. Majestic 12 is a set of documents said to describe a secret group of scientists and officials who handled UFO matters. Strieber pushes back on the view that a UFO researcher named Stanton Friedman "made the whole thing up," says "That's not true. They were involved," and names the mathematician John von Neumann among them, though he does not say how he knows.
mj12-document-jfk-asks-dulles-for-a-revi: A document from the MJ12 papers, a disputed set of papers said to describe a secret US group handling UFO matters, which leaked in 1995, is said to record a top secret request from President John F. Kennedy to Allen Dulles, then head of the CIA, dated 28 June 1961. Michels raises it after it was discussed on the news channel NewsNation by the journalist Ross Coulthart and a former Australian intelligence officer named Jeff Cruickshank, and Coulthart, speaking on the show, stresses that the MJ12 files are "very disputed" and points to Dulles's own diary, released in 2022 among the Kennedy files, for that same date. If the date checks out, it would lend the disputed papers some weight.
mj12-memos-reference-cic-involvement-at-: Leaked papers said to come from MJ12, a supposed secret US committee set up to handle crashed UFOs, refer to the Counter Intelligence Corps, a US Army security unit, investigating UFOs in the 1940s, including the reported crash near Roswell, New Mexico. Michels states this himself, as support for the idea that a hidden government group managed recovered craft.
mk-monarch-acknowledged: A secret programme called MK Monarch, which the teller treats as real, has now been officially acknowledged, according to Kurt Metzger, a guest on the show. Metzger says he got this from a friend he names only as Emma, who made an episode about MK Monarch on her YouTube show, Imagination Podcast, and he says he sent Michels the link.
mk-ultra-bluebird-artichoke-and-occult-r: In the 1950s and 60s, US government mind-control projects run by the CIA, the American spy agency, under names like MK Ultra, Bluebird and Artichoke, were also studying the occult, meaning magic and hidden spiritual traditions. That is what a researcher and author named Peter Levenda says on Michels's show, speaking without citing a document. "They were looking at occult systems," he says, which would mean the government took magic seriously as a tool.
mk-ultra-born-of-mind-control-race-fears: MK Ultra, a secret US government program of mind-control experiments that ran from the 1950s into the 1970s, grew, it is said, out of fear that America was losing a race to the Russians over mind control. The skeptic Michael Shermer says this on the podcast without naming a source, to explain why the government put money into such strange research.
mk-ultra-lsd-dosing-death-at-new-york-ho: In the 1950s a man who went to a New York City hospital for counseling was, after about two days, dosed with 'a huge mass of LSD without telling him,' because the hospital was running MK Ultra experiments, a CIA program that tested mind-altering drugs on people, and the man died. The lawyer Dan Sheehan tells this, and says the death was covered up with help from Jacob Javits, a New York politician, and Warren Burger, a lawyer who later became Chief Justice.
mk-ultra-purpose-lsd-as-interrogation-tr: MK Ultra, a secret US government program of the 1950s and 60s that tested drugs such as LSD on people, was really aimed at turning LSD into a truth serum for interrogations, according to a researcher named Dan Sheehan. He explains the thinking without naming a source: if you dose someone with LSD, it dissolves "the boundaries of their concept structures", so the person might no longer hold back what they know. If so, the program's goal was breaking down a prisoner's guard, not mind expansion.
mk-ultra-remote-viewing-and-ufos-under-o: The CIA's mind-control experiments known as MK Ultra, the government's work on remote viewing (trying to see distant places with the mind alone), and the study of UFOs all sat under one umbrella, according to the researcher Dylan Borland, who gives this as his own reading without a named source. He ties in the Pentagon scientist James Lacatski and the book Skinwalkers at the Pentagon as part of the same web. If true, it would mean these strange-seeming programmes were one effort, not separate oddities.
mlk-essay-on-mystery-religions-and-chris: Martin Luther King Jr., the American civil rights leader, wrote a little-known essay called "The Influence of the Mystery Religions on Christianity," about the secret initiation cults of the ancient Mediterranean world and what early Christianity took from them. Jesse Michels brings it up himself during a talk about the roots of Christian stories and the Gospel of John. He raises it because, if King was right, some of Christianity's stories would be borrowed from older pagan rites.
modern-4602d-personnel-attend-ramsay-lec: A researcher named Scott Ramsey, who studies a reported crash of a craft with alien bodies, says that present-day people linked to the 4602D, a 1950s Air Force intelligence unit that looked into UFO reports, came to one of his lectures. He says it happened in Denver, Colorado, and tells it as something he saw, which would mean the military still pays attention to his work.
moment-of-contact-the-varginha-witnesses: In 1996, people in the town of Varginha in Brazil said they met strange beings, and the filmmaker James Fox tells their stories in his documentary Moment of Contact. Michels praises the film himself on two episodes, saying this isn't some official US government story and the witnesses aren't lying. He also says the Varginha beings had three fingers, which he links to three-fingered bodies found in Peru.
monk-timotheus-says-other-monks-have-see: In 1991, at the Dionysiou monastery on Mount Athos, a Greek peninsula full of Orthodox monasteries, a monk named Timotheus is said to have told a visitor that other monks had seen "the light of the Virgin Mary" moving down the mountain. He added that the visitor might have seen it too. Ralph Larson tells this as the visitor himself, passing on what the monk said to him.
monsanto-chemicals-sprayed-in-vietnam-ca: The chemical company Monsanto shipped its chemicals to Vietnam and other poor countries with weak safety rules, where they were sprayed on crops and "started creating birth defects," according to Brigham Buhler, a businessman who speaks out against the drug industry. He tells it on Michels's show to argue that big companies have pushed harm onto people with little protection.
monsanto-pays-agent-orange-veterans-comp: In the mid 1980s, the chemical company Monsanto was made to pay millions of dollars to war veterans who had been exposed to Agent Orange, which Michels calls a highly toxic chemical. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, in an episode about the dark history of the drug and chemical industry, as an example of a company paying for harm it did to people.
montagnier-dna-water-teleportation-confi: Luc Montagnier, a Nobel Prize-winning virologist, wrote a paper claiming that the signal of DNA could be passed into water at a distance, a kind of teleportation. A man named Dave Rossi says he has seen it confirmed in private lab experiments that he watched himself. If so, it would mean the paper's strange result holds up.
montauk-experiments-1950: Some kind of machinery was found at Montauk, a town at the tip of Long Island, New York, where people say secret experiments were run between the 1950s and the 1960s. Michels brings this up from a book he can't quite place, saying only that the author was "Preston something," meaning the writer Preston Nichols, and that he believes the machinery was really there. He tells it because, if it were true, it would mean strange government work went on in that spot.
montauk-experiments-behind-stranger-thin: Secret experiments are said to have been carried out at Montauk, on the tip of Long Island in New York, and these are said to be the inspiration for Stranger Things, a television series about hidden government experiments. Michels tells this himself, saying that "even the makers of Stranger Things" say the show is based on them and that it is "pretty well established that there were some experiments in Montauk," though he does not say what the experiments were or name where he learned it.
months-of-swarms-over-navy-ships-off-sou: In 2019, swarms of unknown objects are said to have flown over US Navy ships off the Channel Islands and the Southern California coast, again and again for five or six months. A guest named Marik von Rennenkampff passes this on from the journalists Jeremy Corbell and George Knapp. Corbell himself, on a later episode, says the swarms held about 100 objects, which he calls UAP (the government's term for UFOs), and that some were shaped like pyramids. If true, it would mean unknown craft were watching Navy warships for months at a stretch.
montserrat-scanned-and-found-to-carry-a-: In Peru, one of the mummified three-fingered bodies, known as Montserrat, is said to have been scanned and found to be pregnant, carrying a three-fingered fetus. Michels tells this himself from his visit, describing being shown the recording of the scan at "the exact moment they discovered that she was pregnant," which, if real, would suggest these bodies were living, reproducing beings.
moon-dust-document-fireball-and-silent-a: A declassified document from Moon Dust, a US government effort to recover objects that fell from the sky, describes a fireball in Bolivia followed by sightings of silent aircraft near the crash site. Michels tells this himself, citing the document, as a sign that the US was quietly tracking and retrieving unexplained crashes abroad.
moon-dust-document-spherical-objects-rec: A declassified government document is said to describe the recovery of round, ball-shaped objects from farmland in New Zealand. Michels tells this himself, as one of the documents tied to Moon Dust, a US government effort to recover objects that fell from space. He raises it because, if true, it would show that effort reaching far beyond America.
moon-ruins-at-33-in-the-disney-von-braun: In one of the 1950s space exploration films that Walt Disney's studio made with the rocket engineer Wernher von Braun, astronauts reach the far side of the Moon for the first time, and a radar engineer shouts that some kind of radiation is being picked up at 33°. Michels tells this himself, describing the scene as a find of ruins on the Moon, and reads the number 33 as a hidden symbol slipped into the film.
moon-s-two-moments-of-inertia-suggest-it: The idea is that the Moon's mass is spread in an odd way, giving it two different measures of how it resists spinning, called moments of inertia, and that this may mean it was deliberately built or reshaped. The researcher Randall Carlson offers this as his own view, without naming a source: "I am willing to consider that the moon has been geoengineered." If true, someone would have engineered the Moon itself.
moore-benowitz-operation-as-a-24-hour-st: A man named Bill Moore is said to have described the operation around a man named Benowitz, based near Kirtland Air Force Base in New Mexico between about 1970 and 1983, as something like a stage play running 24 hours a day. A guest named Greg Bishop passes this on from Moore, telling Michels to "imagine the Benowitz operation as a 24-hour long stage play." The point is that what Benowitz saw and heard may have been staged for him on purpose.
moore-hands-aquarius-document-to-benowit: In 1981 a UFO researcher named Bill Moore is said to have taken Paul Bennewitz, an Albuquerque man who believed he was picking up alien signals, into a supply closet in Bennewitz's office, turned the radio up, and handed him a paper about a secret government UFO project called Aquarius, saying: "I was told to give this to you. Take it with a grain of salt." The writer Greg Bishop tells this as he heard it, and it matters because it suggests someone was feeding Bennewitz official-looking UFO papers on purpose.
moore-photographs-documents-in-an-upstat: In the early 1980s the UFO researcher Bill Moore was told to go to a hotel room in upstate New York, where, the story goes, he photographed documents he was being shown. The writer Greg Bishop tells this on the show, repeating what Moore himself said happened. It matters because it suggests someone was deliberately feeding Moore papers to spread.
more-crash-retrievals-in-the-ocean-than-: More crashed unknown craft have been recovered from the ocean than from anywhere else, according to a claim passed on by Tim Gallaudet, a retired top Navy admiral. Gallaudet says he is repeating the researcher Eric W. Davis, who in his words "has said there are more crash retrieval operations that have been occurred in the ocean than elsewhere." If true, the seas would be the main place where such recoveries happen.
more-detailed-image-based-communications: Dan Sherman, a former Air Force sergeant who says the National Security Agency, the US spy agency for communications, hired him to talk to aliens, says that between 1990 and 1993, at a place he calls Base 2, the messages he received in his mind turned into detailed pictures with feeling in them. He says they were "very like pictures, images" and "much more colorful," showing things like rockets and troop movements, which would mean the contact had grown richer than simple words.
more-than-one-non-human-species-not-all-: In 1964 at Vandenberg Air Force Base in California, a guard at a nuclear missile site named Richard Barth says he learned from beings who took him that there is more than one non-human species, and that not all of them are as benevolent as the ones he met. Barth tells it as part of his own abduction experience. If true, it would mean that whatever is visiting does not all share the same intentions toward people.
morgan-and-townsend-brown-s-conversation: In a man named Morgan's office, the inventor Thomas Townsend Brown, whom Michels calls a scientist who worked with the CIA, the US spy agency, once asked: "What if we had the ability to time travel?" He added that he believed it would happen in their lifetime. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, as a sign of how far Brown's thinking reached.
morgan-robertson-s-wreck-of-the-titan-fo: The American writer Morgan Robertson published a short novel in 1898 called Futility, or the Wreck of the Titan, about the Titan, the largest liner ever built, which hits an iceberg in the North Atlantic on an April night and sinks, years before the real Titanic did the same. The book calls its ship "practically unsinkable" and says she "carried as few boats as would satisfy the laws." The text quoted here comes from a 1912 edition, so the 1898 wording may differ. Michels brings it up several times as a possible case of seeing the future, once placing the book vaguely in the early 20th century, about ten years before the Titanic. A writer on precognition named Eric Wargo tells it too, citing his book Time Loops.
morgan-says-brown-was-cia-research-1950: The work of Townsend Brown, a scientist who is said to have built flying-saucer-like devices from the 1950s on, was "basically CIA research," meaning it was secretly backed by the CIA, the US spy agency. Jan Lundquist passes this on in a documentary about Brown on Michels's show. She says a person named Morgan told it to Paul Schatzkin, a writer who has researched Brown's life. If true, Brown's strange experiments were government-backed spy work.
mork-mindy-white-egg-as-a-hint-of-hidden: The 1970s television comedy Mork & Mindy, in which the actor Robin Williams played an alien who flew to Earth in a white egg, may have been a hint of secret knowledge, according to Jake Barber, a helicopter pilot who says he once carried a UFO. Barber points out that the white egg was shown in the preview and was part of every episode. To him it suggests someone behind the show knew what real craft look like.
mormonism-as-a-ufo-religion-joseph-smith: Mormonism is, when you look into it, "kind of a UFO religion": its founder, Joseph Smith, reported contacts with beings and knowledge handed to him in the United States between the 1820s and 1840s. The researcher Matthew Pines makes this point on the show, without naming a source. His point is that a major American religion may have started with the same kind of encounters people now call UFO experiences.
morphologies-of-the-peruvian-mummies: The small mummified bodies from Peru that some people say are not human fall into three body types, called the J types, the S types and the M types. Michels names these types himself, in passing and without naming a source, and says nothing more about what sets each one apart.
moses-burning-bush-as-a-plasmoid: Michels suggests that the biblical story of Moses speaking to a burning bush could have been a plasmoid, a glowing mass of electrically charged gas, and so a kind of modern UFO encounter. He draws the idea from the writer Robert Temple's book A New Science of Heaven, as a way of reading old religious visions as the same thing people now report.
most-hessdalen-residents-report-experien: In Hessdalen, a valley in Norway, a very large share of the people who live there, "upwards of 80, 85, 90%", have experienced strange things. Michels says this himself from what he found there, which would make the valley a place where odd events are part of ordinary life.
mosul-dam-turbine-proof-of-concept-scan-: A team scanned the Mosul Dam in Iraq in 2024 to show that their method could see inside large structures, according to a researcher named Jeffrey Drum. He calls it "another proof of concept" and links it to the work of Filippo Biondi, but names no other source. He brings it up in a talk about scans of the Egyptian pyramids, because if the method works on a dam, it might also show what lies beneath the pyramids.
mother-ayahuasca-gives-hancock-a-novel-s: In 2006, over five sessions drinking ayahuasca, a plant brew that causes visions, in Brazil, the writer Graham Hancock says he was "literally given the entire plot of a novel". He tells it first-hand, crediting the spirit he calls Mother Ayahuasca, and ties it to his novel Entangled. If true, it would mean the visions came from an intelligence outside his own mind.
mother-faking-telepathy-on-danny-jones-s: A mother who appeared on the podcast of the host Danny Jones, as part of claims linked to The Telepathy Tapes, a series about children said to read minds, was clearly peeking past her blindfold, according to Michels. He tells this himself, saying some of the people involved are, he thinks, faking things, which he calls unfortunate.
mother-s-apparition-in-the-kitchen: A former guard at a nuclear weapons base named Mario Woods says that, in Tampa, Florida, his mother appeared standing in the kitchen during a lightning storm. He tells it himself, as something his family talked about, alongside his other accounts of strange experiences.
mother-s-earlier-sightings-in-rocky-moun: The mother of Mario Woods, a former guard at a nuclear site who says he was abducted by a UFO, told him she had seen strange things herself as a child growing up in Rocky Mount, North Carolina. Woods says she said only that much and never explained what she had seen. He tells it to suggest that these encounters might run in his family.
mothership-at-langley-incursion-per-chri: During the 2023 incursions over Langley Air Force Base in Hampton, Virginia, small saucers were seen flying out of a larger mothership, according to Chris Mellon, a former deputy assistant secretary of defense for intelligence under Presidents Clinton and Bush. Michels passes this on from Mellon, calling it the Hampton Air Force Base incursion. If true, it would mean unknown craft were operating in coordinated groups over a US military base.
motion-sciences-anti-gravity-effort-debu: In 2010 a project called Motion Sciences tried to build an anti-gravity device in a hangar at the Provo airport in Utah, and it was shown not to work. The owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property known for strange happenings, tells it as someone who was involved, saying the scientists Hal Puthoff and Kit Green sat on its science advisory board, so even serious names backed an effort that came to nothing.
mount-athos-dedicated-to-mary-and-closed: Mount Athos, a mountain in Greece that is home to monks, is said to be given over entirely to Mary, the mother of Jesus, and for that reason women still may not set foot on it to this day. A guest named Ralph Larson says so in passing, on an episode about a former CIA man who calls himself a time traveler.
mount-kailash-as-an-energy-vortex-where-: Mount Kailash, a sacred mountain, is described as a kind of energy vortex, a place where the body itself seems to change: the spiritual teacher Michels calls Sod Guru reportedly said his fingernails grew faster while he was on the mountain. Michels repeats this himself, as something Sod Guru said, offering it as an example of a place with unusual power.
mount-nemrut-near-lake-van-erupted-at-en: Mount Nemrut, a volcano southwest of Lake Van in Turkey, last exploded at the end of the last ice age, during the Younger and Older Dryas, two sudden cold spells of that time. The researcher Matt LaCroix says this without naming a source, in a talk about something big happening around 12,000 BC. He tells it as part of the case that the end of the ice age was a time of violent upheaval.
mount-nyangani-as-a-ufo-repair-facility: Mount Nyangani, a mountain in Zimbabwe, is a repair facility for UFOs, according to a former Army sergeant named Lyn Buchanan. He speaks from his own experience and says that what he "found out about that one was that it seems to be a repair facility." If he is right, the mountain would be a place where unknown craft go to be fixed.
mount-shasta-portal-opening-and-the-10-f: In 2014, a portal is said to have opened at Mount Shasta, a mountain in northern California, and someone who was there describes seeing a ten-foot-tall man wearing boots. This comes from the UFO researcher Grant Cameron, who says that in 2015 he interviewed almost everyone who had been at the portal and asked them what they saw. He names no single witness, and if the account were true it would mean people met a giant being face to face.
mount-st-helens-observers-killed-by-heat: When the volcano Mount St Helens in Washington State erupted in 1980, people watching from 5 to 10 miles away were killed by the heat, says Matt LaCroix, a researcher of ancient history. He points to documentaries about the eruption as his source. He brings it up to show how far a disaster's deadly heat can reach, in a talk about a disaster he believes struck the world around 12,000 BC.
mount-wilson-cover-up-buried-fried-serve: At a Mount Wilson property linked to Robert Bigelow, a businessman who owned it, there was a cover-up around 1996: buried computer servers that had been "fried" and a hidden rail system, along with signs of activity older than the official story. That account comes from the owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a property known for strange reports, who says he uncovered this evidence himself and told it in an episode billed as him breaking his silence. If true, it would mean someone worked to hide what had gone on at the site.
mount-zeil-as-an-alien-port-of-entry-to-: Mount Zeil, a mountain in northern Australia, is described as "sort of a port of entry to the earth" where friendly visitors from elsewhere arrive. The claim comes from Lyn Buchanan, a former Army sergeant who worked as a remote viewer, meaning someone trained to try to describe distant places by the mind alone. He links the idea to Pat Price, another remote viewer, and if it were true it would mean there is a known landing spot for friendly beings on Earth.
mountain-bike-ride-with-missing-time-at-: On a mountain bike ride in 1995 at Daniels Park, a burial ground south-southwest of Denver, Colorado, at least five hours went missing that no one could account for. That is what John Blitch says, a scientist the episode describes as having worked for DARPA, the Pentagon's advanced research agency, and he tells it as the man it happened to. He says he had been on the skeptical side until this ride, and it is what turned him toward believing he had been taken by something not human.
mountain-bike-sabotage-after-senate-brie: About three weeks after he briefed people in the US Senate in 2023, someone sawed through the bolt that holds the seat on his mountain bike. That is the account of Steven Greer, a guest who argues on the show that UFO secrets are held by a small global group, and he tells it as something that happened to him. He offers it as a sign that someone wanted to harm or frighten him for speaking out.
mountains-as-possible-non-human-no-go-zo: Certain mountains, such as Mount Shasta in California, Secret Mountain in Arizona and Mount Inyangani in Zimbabwe, are said to be places where glowing balls of light and craft are seen flying straight into the mountain. Michels raises this himself, without naming a source, in a conversation with a Pentagon whistleblower named Matthew Brown, offering these peaks as possible places that non-human beings keep for themselves and where people are not meant to go.
mountains-worldwide-as-possible-alien-ba: The idea here is that certain mountains around the world might hide alien bases. Michels raises it in a conversation with the owner of a ranch known for strange sightings, listing peaks like Mount Zeil in Australia and Mount Hayes in Alaska, and the story also places Mount Perdido and Mount Shasta in the same list. He gives no source and no detail beyond the names of the mountains.
moving-boulders-of-the-mojave-racetrack: In the Mojave Desert there is a place called the racetrack, where boulders are said to move across the ground on their own. A professional skeptic named Michael Shermer mentions "the story of the moving boulders" in passing, without saying more about it or naming a source.
moving-the-sine-wave-by-mentally-humming: A former Air Force sergeant named Dan Sherman says that between 1990 and 1993, at a hidden facility near the National Security Agency, the US spy agency that listens to signals, in Maryland, he learned to move a wave line on a screen just by humming a tone in his head. He tells it first hand, saying that when he saw the wave move "it came into focus," as part of his account, told in a book called Above Black, of being trained to talk to aliens with his mind.
