mr-d-s-signal-discovery-for-locating-uap: A member of a startup called Skywatcher, which says it can call up UFOs, known only as Mr. D, found a way to pick up signals from the objects and work out where they were in the sky. That is how James Valor of Skywatcher tells it, as someone who took part in the work between 2021 and 2025. He also says government radar was seeing the same unidentified anomalous phenomena, the government's term for UFOs, but never told Skywatcher, which would mean officials were tracking what the startup was drawing in.
mr-x-s-work-on-exotic-vacuum-objects-and: An unnamed man known only as Mr. X is said to have done a great deal of work around 2020 and 2021 on what he calls exotic vacuum objects, strange glowing forms thought to come out of empty space, and on plasma, a glowing electrically charged gas, that seems to organize itself. A guest named Jay Anderson tells this from what he knows of Mr. X, saying he is not a government man but "really is a savant" who simply does not want to be named.
mris-of-ufo-contact-dod-and-intelligence: Brain scans of people who had run-ins with UFOs reportedly showed an unusual, larger region deep in the brain called the caudate-putamen. The Stanford scientist Garry Nolan says that sometime in the 2010s he was shown MRI scans of these people, who were Pentagon and intelligence staff, and later puts it more cautiously as an area that seemed "disturbed" or "different". Michels repeats it as a what-if about fighter pilots who see UFOs, since it could hint that some people are wired to notice or attract such encounters.
muldoon-americans-wanted-kaikoura-shut-d: Robert Muldoon, New Zealand's prime minister around the time of the 1978 Kaikoura UFO sightings off that country's coast, once chuckled and let slip that "the Americans wanted that one shut down pretty quickly." The Australian journalist Ross Coulthart tells this, recalling what Muldoon said to him. If true, it would mean the United States pressed another government to quiet a UFO case.
multi-billion-dollar-propaganda-book-cam: A government official named John S. Herrington is said to have pointed to a shelf of books around 1981 and said that right beside the real ones sat "the books that we publish full of propaganda," part of "a multi-billion dollar campaign to cover up the truth." Brent Friedman, a guest on an episode about Hollywood and the CIA, repeats what he says Herrington told him. If true, it would mean the government paid to fill bookshops with false stories.
multi-sensor-corroboration-of-uap-satell: Some UFO sightings in the United States are backed up by satellites, radar, people who saw them, and heat readings, all at once, and "it's all totally consistent," according to the economist Tyler Cowen. He tells it to Michels in 2022 as something he has heard from others, not something he saw himself. If true, these objects are not just tricks of one camera or one pair of eyes.
multiple-high-clearance-sources-say-uap-: Over roughly a year, the economist Tyler Cowen says, a number of people holding very high security clearances told him that UAP, the government's term for UFOs, are a real phenomenon. Cowen stresses that these sources were completely separate from one another and that their clearances were "very, very high." If true, it would mean people inside secret government circles take the subject seriously.
mummified-pharaohs-in-the-cairo-museum-w: In the national museum in Cairo, Egypt, some of the mummified pharaohs look very short, says Michels. He says their skulls were clearly reshaped on purpose, which he takes as an attempt to look like their gods, and that they end up looking like gray aliens, the big-headed figures of UFO lore. Michels tells this himself as something seen at the museum, without naming a source, in an episode about the pyramids.
muon-detected-big-void-to-be-excavated-i: Inside the Great Pyramid at Giza in Egypt there is a large empty space, called the Big Void, found by tracking muons, tiny particles from space that pass through rock. A researcher named Jeffrey Drum says it is to be dug into in 2026 by the ScanPyramids team, a scanning project, with the approval of Egypt's Ministry of Antiquities, the government office in charge of ancient sites. He gives no source beyond naming those groups, and he presents it as the moment the hidden space would finally be opened and checked.
muon-team-may-have-mistaken-the-grand-ga: The "Big Void" found inside Egypt's Great Pyramid by the ScanPyramids team, who scanned it with muons (particles from space that pass through stone), may really be the floor of the Grand Gallery, the pyramid's tall inner passage, according to the radar researcher Filippo Biondi, who offers this as his own reading of the team's paper. At another point he describes the void only as running parallel to the Grand Gallery and talks about muon scans failing in general. If he is right, the famous hidden chamber would be a misreading of a known space.
musgrave-saw-snake-like-things-writhing-: A space shuttle pilot named Musgrave is said to have seen things like snakes writhing in space while in orbit. The space shuttle was NASA's reusable spacecraft, and NASA is the US space agency. The story comes up on an episode billed as a NASA whistleblower talk, where the guest Kevin Knuth passes it on as something Musgrave described, and Michels repeats it in almost the same words. Neither gives a date or any more detail about what the shapes were. If true, it would mean astronauts have seen living-looking things outside the spacecraft.
musha-s-ex-honda-team-and-capacitors-in-: A team of researchers in Japan, possibly people who came out of the carmaker Honda, is said to have worked on capacitors, devices that store electric charge, placed in transmission oil as part of work on propulsion without wings or rockets. Michels mentions it himself in an episode about antigravity propulsion, saying he believes the lead scientist is named Musha and making clear he is unsure of the details.
mushrooms-tell-mckenna-about-hyperlight-: The writer Terence McKenna said that during a mushroom trip, the mushrooms spoke to him and told him that "within my memory exist the blueprints for hyper light drives," meaning ships that travel faster than light. Michels brings this up himself on three occasions, the first time reading from McKenna's book True Hallucinations, where McKenna tries to set down what the mushrooms were telling him. His later retellings shift a little: once he speaks of blueprints and names no book, and once he places the message on a two-week trip in the Amazon, saying the mushroom held the knowledge in its memory. The point of telling it is that the mushrooms might be something like an alien mind holding knowledge beyond ours.
musk-and-mike-griffin-go-to-russia-for-r: In the early 2000s, the entrepreneur Elon Musk and an aerospace engineer named Mike Griffin are said to have travelled together to Russia, where they "actually find the rocket engines" Musk was looking for. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, as part of the early story of Musk's push into building rockets.
mussolini-asks-hitler-about-the-magenta-: In 1933, the story goes, an unknown flying object crashed near Magenta in Italy, and the Italian dictator Benito Mussolini went to the German leader Adolf Hitler about it. Michels tells it twice, calling it a rumour. In one telling it is a kind of partnership between the two, and in the other Mussolini simply asks the Nazis, "Is this yours?" If true, it would put a crashed craft in fascist hands more than a decade before the Second World War ended.
myles-standish-recalculates-and-dismisse: In the 1990s, the story goes, NASA announced it had found signs of an extra planet at the edge of the solar system, a "Planet 10", until an astronomer named Myles Standish redid the maths and said, in effect, "we made a mistake, forget about it." A researcher named Matt LaCroix tells this twice in the same conversation, without naming a source, adding the second time that NASA had first announced it publicly. He tells it to suggest a real discovery may have been quietly waved away.
myrna-hansen-hypnotic-regression-and-und: Around 1980 near Albuquerque, New Mexico, a woman named Myrna Hansen said she had been abducted and taken to an underground facility. Her memories came out under hypnosis, with the psychologist Leo Sprinkle. The researcher Greg Bishop tells it as part of the story of Paul Bennewitz, an Albuquerque businessman she came to visit at his house to talk about her abduction, and in Bishop's telling her account fed the idea of hidden underground bases.
mysterious-death-of-pat-price-1975: A man named Pat Price, part of the psychic research circle around the researcher Hal Puthoff, died in 1975 in a way that people who were there describe differently from the published account. Lyn Buchanan, a former Army sergeant from the same world, passes on what he heard from them: the death came in Washington DC, an unmarked ambulance was involved, and years later the head of security said, "Pat Price died and we haven't heard from him since." Buchanan tells it to suggest the official story of the death is not the whole story.
mysterious-jungle-sickness-and-deafness-: On a 2024 trip to Tikal, a jungle site of ancient ruins in Guatemala, a researcher named Luke Caverns says he came down with a mysterious sickness. He tells it as something that happened to him, and he says that by the end of the trip he was 75 percent deaf in each ear.
mysterious-man-plays-ransone-a-metallic-: In Houston in the early 1970s, a mysterious man is said to have put a cassette tape into a car player for a woman named Valerie Ransone, and out came a metallic voice presented as an alien's. An unnamed researcher on the show retells this from Ransone's own interview on the Eyes on Cinema YouTube channel. If true, it would mean someone was handing out recordings of alien contact.
mystery-airship-phenomenon-1807: At one point in history, people in the United States and Europe began reporting strange airships in the sky, at a time when no such craft should have existed. A researcher named Tim Alberino mentions this "mystery airship phenomenon" on Michels's show, crediting the UFO historian Richard Dolan. He brings it up as something that appeared "suddenly at the same time" as other odd events he is describing, as if they were linked.
mystery-schools-aim-to-recover-the-lost-: The secret groups known as mystery schools, which pass down hidden spiritual knowledge, have one main goal: "to recover the lost knowledge of the gods from Mars," according to the filmmaker Tim Alberino. He gives this as his own reading. He draws on the writer David Flynn, on Cydonia, a region of Mars where some people see a face and pyramids in photos, and on Elon Musk's plans to go to Mars, which suggests he sees the push to reach Mars as tied to that old aim.
name-dennis-mariani-confirmed-by-someone: Michels says he knows of one case where someone at the Nevada Test Site, the US government's nuclear testing ground in the Nevada desert, confirmed the name Dennis Mariani, a name that is part of the story of Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft at a secret site there in the late 1980s. Michels tells this himself without saying who that person was. If true, it would back up one detail of Lazar's account.
nanosims-analysis-finds-anomalous-magnes: Some metal fragments known as the Ubatuba fragments, which are said to come from a UFO, were tested at Stanford University, and one of them came back strange: "The magnesium ratios were way off." Magnesium comes in a few natural forms of slightly different weight, and the claim is that the mix of those forms in this piece did not match what is normally found, which would hint that the metal was not made in the ordinary way. The Stanford scientist Garry Nolan tells this himself as one of the people who ran the test. He describes the machine as a highly sensitive mass spectrometer, an instrument that sorts atoms by weight.
narmer-palette-shows-egypt-existed-befor: The Narmer Palette, an ancient carved Egyptian slab, is said to mark the start of Egypt's age of kings by showing the reunification of Upper and Lower Egypt, which implies an Egypt existed before that joining. A researcher named Geoffrey Drumm makes this point in his own summary, without naming a source, calling the reunification "the hallmark of the beginning of the dynastic period" as shown on the palette. He raises it to argue that Egyptian civilization is older than the usual starting point.
narrator-clip-the-channeler-s-second-tra: In Washington in 1959, a channeler, a person who claims to speak for other beings while in a trance, is said to have gone into a second trance in front of a man the clip calls Friend. An unnamed narrator describes it in a clip played on the show, without naming a source: "He sat for several minutes and then appeared in a deep trance with his Adam's apple moving up and down rapidly." It comes up in an episode with the UFO researcher Grant Cameron about the man who once headed the government's UFO program, as a sign that official investigators sat in on such sessions.
nasa-3i-atlas-press-conference-2025: In 2025 NASA, the US space agency, held a press conference about 3I/ATLAS, an object passing through our solar system from outside it, and Michels calls it an "idiotic press conference about manipulation." He says this himself, on an episode about a NASA insider who says the agency hides UFO data, and he points to the Harvard astronomer Avi Loeb, who had raised questions about the object. For Michels, the press conference is a sign that NASA steers how such findings get told to the public.
nasa-administrator-isaacman-says-some-ca: Jared Isaacman, the current head of NASA, the US space agency, is said to have admitted that some UFO sightings remain unexplained. Michels raises this twice, and in the second telling says it came after the Department of War's first release of UFO files, which centred on space missions and astronaut encounters, and that Isaacman denied anything about reverse engineering craft or confirmed alien bodies. Michels calls it a big shift for an official of that rank.
nasa-announcement-of-planet-x-planet-10-: NASA is said to have once announced the discovery of an unknown planet beyond the known ones, calling it Planet X or Planet 10. Matt LaCroix, a writer on ancient civilizations, says on the show that he believes this was a real announcement, placing it in the 1990s. He brings it up because a hidden distant planet would fit his account of ancient catastrophes.
nasa-announcement-of-possible-life-on-ma: NASA recently announced that it had found some sort of life on Mars, according to Dan Sherman, a former Air Force sergeant who says the National Security Agency, the US agency for intercepting communications, hired him to speak with aliens. Sherman mentions the announcement in passing as something NASA said. If true, it would be the first official word of life beyond Earth.
nasa-assessor-baron-killed-by-train-500-: In 1967 a man named Thomas Baron, hired by NASA, the US space agency, to judge how likely its programme was to succeed, was killed by a train, and his 500-page report then vanished. That is how Joe Rogan, a guest on the show, tells it, passing on Baron's story as he heard it. Rogan tells it to suggest that someone who had written a damning report was silenced and the report buried.
nasa-attempt-to-read-the-ramey-memo-with: In the early 2000s, a team at NASA's Intelligent Systems Division is said to have written computer programs to read the Ramey memo, a blurry paper held by an Army general named Roger Ramey in a 1947 photo taken after the Roswell UFO reports. Kevin Knuth, a former NASA scientist who was on the team, tells Michels: 'we actually wrote the algorithms to actually read this memo.' If the memo could be read, it might say what was really recovered at Roswell.
nasa-dart-mission-hits-dimorphos-2022: In 2022 a NASA spacecraft, sent on a mission called DART, is said to have deliberately crashed into Dimorphos, a small moon circling an asteroid called Didymos, to show that humans could push an asteroid off course and keep it from hitting Earth. Michels brings this up himself in two conversations, once with the author Graham Hancock in 2022, where he describes it as a programme "aimed to prove that humans can deflect asteroids" and places it across 2021 and 2022, and again with the researcher Randall Carlson in 2025, where he recalls it as "a spacecraft knocking into" the little moon. He tells it as something he looked into, and it matters to him because it suggests people now have a way to defend the planet from space rocks.
nasa-department-of-war-special-investiga: In 2026 NASA released an image from Apollo 17, the last crewed Moon landing, showing lights, and the note next to it said that "the department of war and NASA have opened a special investigation for this particular image." A guest named Maaneli Derakhshani says this, pointing to the first batch of NASA's released files on UAP, the government's term for UFOs, with the Department of War being the Pentagon under its new name. If true, the space agency and the military are formally looking into something seen on the Moon.
nasa-didn-t-want-to-talk-after-news-call: Something Chris Bledsoe, a man who says UFOs appear around him, mentioned in public around 2024 caught the attention of a news outlet, which then called NASA, the US space agency, and NASA's reaction was, in effect, "God, we don't want to talk about this." Bledsoe tells it second-hand, as what he heard from a friend in the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency, in Washington. To him it suggests the agency knows of his case but would rather stay quiet.
nasa-director-wrote-psychic-spy-manual-f: A director at NASA, the US space agency, is said to have written a manual on psychic spying for the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency. Michels says this himself, hedging as he goes, naming the man as Steven Hubbard "I believe" and giving no source. If true, it would tie the space agency to the government's interest in using the mind to spy.
nasa-eagle-works-engineer-s-casimir-effe: An engineer from Eagle Works, a small NASA lab that tested unusual propulsion ideas, claims to have powered a little microchip with 1.5 kilovolts drawn from the Casimir effect, a tiny force that appears out of empty space between very close surfaces. Michels repeats the engineer's claim himself, without naming the engineer. If true, it would mean usable energy pulled from empty space.
nasa-electrostatics-lab-measures-thrust-: A NASA electrostatics lab in Florida, near Kennedy Space Center, has been measuring thrust from electrically charged devices in high vacuum, testing "almost every day, probably every other day" since 2020. That is what the engineer Charles Buhler says, as someone who runs the tests, building on ideas from the inventor Thomas Townsend Brown. If true, it would point to a way of pushing a craft without burning fuel.
nasa-electrostatics-scientist-charles-bu: A NASA scientist who works on electrostatics, the study of electric charges at rest, named Charles Buhler, is said to insist that an effect he studied really works, and keeps working even in a vacuum, where there is no air to push against. Michels relays this as Buhler's own claim, in an episode about a hacker who says he found a secret NASA space program. If true, it would mean the effect cannot be explained away as air currents.
nasa-employee-wrote-a-cia-remote-viewing: Someone working at NASA, the US space agency, wrote a training manual for the CIA, the US spy agency, on remote viewing, the practice of trying to see distant places or objects with the mind alone. The scientist Kevin Knuth, who says NASA holds back UFO data, mentions this on the show without naming the person. If true, it would mean the space agency and the spy agency shared work on psychic spying.
nasa-experiment-tardigrades-survive-18-m: Tardigrades, tiny water-dwelling animals, survived 18 months in the vacuum of space in a NASA experiment outside the International Space Station, according to a guest named Dr. Gilbert. He says it without naming a source. It is told to show how tough life can be, and so how life might travel between worlds.
nasa-flight-surgeon-on-apollo-astronauts: In 2008 a NASA doctor told John Blitch that other astronauts from the Apollo moon missions had shunned Edgar Mitchell, an Apollo astronaut who walked on the moon. Blitch, a former scientist at a Pentagon research agency, says he heard this while diving with the doctor at Aquarius, an underwater research base off Key Largo, Florida, and he keeps the doctor's name to himself. The point is that Mitchell was pushed out by his own peers.
nasa-langley-staff-tag-puzzles-and-hiero: Staff at NASA Langley, a NASA research center in Virginia, have been tagging puzzles, hieroglyphs, rocks and formations on Google Maps. That is the account of Dylan Borland, a former Air Force intelligence specialist. He says he took screenshots of these tags years ago, about three years before, including labyrinths and pyramids marked at Langley's hypersonic facilities complex, which tests very high-speed flight. He says the tags were later removed. He suggests they are hidden messages from people working inside.
nasa-mission-controller-tells-of-space-p: People in what is called a secret space programme, a supposed hidden space effort outside the public one, honour unseen "sponsors" in Latin from the second century, according to a NASA mission controller named Timothy Taylor. Michels passes this on second-hand from the scholar Diana Pasulka, who writes about her conversations with Taylor. Told this way, the story hints that such a programme answers to something old and not human.
nasa-mission-controller-tim-taylor-s-adv: A NASA mission controller named Timothy Taylor told Michels that, to make a rocket work, "you have to think about what they want", and Michels understood "they" to mean non-human intelligence. Michels tells it first-hand; in a later telling he says it came on a FaceTime call and links it to American Cosmic, a book by the religion scholar Diana Pasulka about belief in alien contact among scientists. The hint would be that some space technology depends on the wishes of beings that are not human.
nasa-mission-controller-tim-taylor-says-: A NASA mission controller named Timothy Taylor is said to have revealed that astronauts see unexplained things in space. Michels passes this on from a book called American Cosmic, noting that Taylor has since "been outed" by name. If true, it would mean the space agency's own people know of sightings that are not made public.
nasa-moon-pigeons-report-1970: In the early 1970s NASA published a report called Moon Pigeons, according to the researcher Maaneli Derakhshani, who mentions it in passing without saying what it contains. He brings it up as evidence that NASA took odd lunar matters seriously enough to write about them.
nasa-moon-program-development-at-langley: In the 1960s, the work that got NASA, the US space agency, into space and toward the Moon was done at Langley Air Force Base in Virginia, including the work on pressurization, meaning how to keep air inside a spacecraft or suit. Dylan Borland, a guest who served in the Air Force, says this in passing and names no source. He brings it up to show how much of the space effort was centred at that one base.
nasa-operator-disconnects-gary-during-ha: While breaking into US government computers around 2001 and 2002, a British hacker named Gary McKinnon says someone on the other end caught him in the act. He recalls a person who "right clicked the LAN icon and disconnected me", meaning they cut his network connection by hand, and he is sure that was NASA, the US space agency. He tells it as his own experience, as proof that someone inside was watching what he was doing.
nasa-people-invite-him-to-lunch-during-a: Sometime between 1997 and 1999, during a visit to the US Congress, a member of the Russian Parliament named Kiran Ilum Xenov says he got a phone call from people who said they were from NASA, the US space agency. He tells it himself: they said they had heard about a public statement he had made and wanted to meet, and they invited him to lunch. He tells it as a sign that his account had reached people inside the American government.
nasa-people-study-the-phenomenon-and-tra: People from NASA, the US space agency, study the strange events around him and travel with him, says Chris Bledsoe, a man who says UFOs show up around him. Speaking of his own life since about 2007, he names two men he works with, Hal Pavvenmeer and Timothy Taylor, and says, "there are a lot of other NASA guys that I'm currently talking with." If true, it would mean people at the space agency take his experiences seriously enough to follow them up.
nasa-program-with-psychic-kids-in-florid: In the late 1960s, the story goes, NASA, the US space agency, ran some kind of programme in Florida that worked with children thought to have psychic gifts. A researcher named Greg Malatzi says he has "heard a lot about" it, describing "somewhere in Florida" "a NASA thing with kids," though he passes it on second-hand. A guest named Jay Anderson, appearing as a witness, mentions it in a single line, "NASA had the star kids," and gives no place or date. If it were true, the space agency would have been quietly studying children for unusual mental abilities.
nasa-representative-4-000-recorded-cases: Someone from NASA, the US space agency, is said to have stated around 1997 or 1998 that "we officially record about 4,000 cases a year" of people seeing unidentified objects such as saucers. Kiran Ilum Xenov, called the president of a Russian republic in the episode's title, says this is what the NASA man told him in conversation. If true, the agency would be quietly keeping count of thousands of sightings.
nasa-s-higher-resolution-mars-images-rel: After a public uproar over photos of Cydonia, a region of Mars, NASA, the US space agency, released a second, sharper set of images to calm things down. Tim Alberino, a guest on the show, says this in passing without naming a source. In his telling, the sharper pictures were put out to quiet the firestorm, not just to share new data.
nasa-s-innovative-propulsion-program-fun: The story is that NASA, the US space agency, has quietly paid for research into warp drive, an idea for crossing space faster than normal by bending space itself. A former intelligence official named Eric Haseltine talks about NASA's "innovative propulsion program," which he calls "fantastic." He does not say where his knowledge comes from, though he connects it to a work called The Shadow of Time. Michels tells his own version without naming a source. He says a man named Miguel Alcubierre came up with a theoretical model for such a drive, and that NASA has been studying it for years. He names Harold "Sonny" White, who he says has done interesting work on it at NASA. Neither man gives details of the program itself, such as its budget or what it built. The two tellers are independent, a former official and the host. If true, it would mean the government takes faster-than-light travel seriously enough to pay for it.
nasa-space-force-track-uncorrelated-targ: NASA tracks "uncorrelated targets," objects in space that do not match anything on the lists of known satellites and debris, "all the time." Jesse Michels tells this himself in 2026, saying he heard it from someone who works at NASA now and whom he does not name. He raises it alongside the work of the astronomer Beatriz Villarroel, and if true, it means unknown objects are being tracked quietly and not made public.
nasa-telepathy-experiments-and-remote-vi: In the 1960s the US space agency NASA is said to have run telepathy experiments, and the researcher Andrija Puharich claimed they sent remote viewers, people who try to see distant places with the mind alone, to the moon. The researcher Greg Malatzi tells this, pointing to newspaper articles and to Puharich's NASA contracts. If true, it would mean the space agency took mind powers seriously.
nasa-tries-to-replicate-podkletnov-s-wei: In the mid-1990s, NASA, the US space agency, is said to have tried to reproduce an effect reported by a Russian named Yevgeny Podkletnov, who was working at the University of Tampere in Finland, where objects appeared to lose some of their weight. A researcher named Nick Cook tells this without naming a source. He says NASA "had exhibited, weirdly, an interest in anti-gravity" after those reports, which would mean the agency took the idea of beating gravity seriously.
nasp-as-cover-program-for-aurora-1980: A US project from the 1980s and 1990s to build a plane that could fly into space, known as NASP, is said to have really been a cover for a secret aircraft called Aurora. The writer Nick Cook tells this as the belief of a man named Bill Sweetman, saying "Bill became convinced that NASP was actually a cover program for Aurora." If so, the public project would have hidden a more advanced one.
nat-kobitz-as-coulthart-s-original-navy-: A senior Navy scientist named Nat Kobitz is said to have been the first insider source of the journalist Ross Coulthart, the person who "really brought him down the rabbit hole" of UFO secrets. Michels mentions this himself, without naming where he learned it, while talking about Hollywood, the CIA and UFOs, and it matters because it would mean Coulthart's reporting began with a figure from inside the Navy's own science world.
nat-kobitz-confirms-being-read-into-a-ua: Nat Kobitz, a former senior US Navy research official, confirmed that he had been "read in", meaning formally given access, to a secret programme on unidentified aerial phenomena (the government's term for UFOs) and alien technology. The journalist Ross Coulthart tells this, describing how he put the question to Kobitz directly. If true, it would mean such a programme existed and real officials were cleared into it.
nathan-twining-reference-in-disclosure-d: A film called Disclosure Day, which Michels discusses in an episode about Steven Spielberg and Hollywood, nods to Nathan Twining, an Air Force general who in 1947 headed Air Materiel Command, the Army Air Forces' aircraft development and testing command. Twining signed the Twining memo, "AMC Opinion Concerning 'Flying Discs'," written on September 23, 1947, and Michels notes he was rumored to belong to Majestic 12, a supposed secret group of twelve officials handling UFO matters that is described in a set of disputed documents. Michels tells this himself, pointing to the line that "12 people are missing," as a hint that the film is drawing on real UFO history.
national-archives-extends-the-deadline-f: The National Archives, the US government agency that keeps federal records, gave an extension to the end of September 2025 for releasing its records on UAP, the government's term for UFOs. The lawyer Dan Sheehan says this in passing, as someone following the release closely. The date matters to him because it is when more of the hidden files are supposed to come out.
national-archives-photos-of-eg-g-sandia-: Photographs kept in the National Archives, the US government's records store, are said to show underground operations at the Nevada Test Site, the government's desert testing ground, run by the contractor EG&G and the Sandia weapons laboratory. A researcher who goes by UAPGerb describes the set himself, saying the photos range "from 1972 to at that time 1992 before Martin Marietta purchased Sandia back in 1993," Martin Marietta being a defence company. He raises them as a record of secret work going on beneath the test range.
national-geographic-double-blind-remote-: In a test filmed for National Geographic, the former Army remote viewer Joe McMoneagle says he described a hidden target that turned out to be the end of the Dumbarton Bridge, which crosses San Francisco Bay. Remote viewing means trying to describe a distant place by the mind alone, and the test was double-blind, so neither he nor the person with him knew the target. McMoneagle tells it as something he took part in, with a man he calls Ed, as evidence that the skill works under strict conditions.
national-security-act-passed-weeks-after: The National Security Act of 1947, the law that reorganised America's military and intelligence agencies, came in September 1947, just weeks after the reported crash of something near Roswell, New Mexico, that July. Michels points out the timing himself, giving the dates from memory, as a hint that the crash may have shaped how the government set up its secret agencies.
national-underwater-reconnaissance-offic: The United States is said to have a secret office for spying under the sea, called the National Underwater Reconnaissance Office, or NURO. A researcher who goes by UAPGerb says it was set up in 1969 and has still never been officially disclosed. Jesse Michels mentions it twice. Once he calls it the underwater "little brother" of the National Reconnaissance Office, the US spy agency for reconnaissance, and says it is now public but little is known about it. The other time he credits a man named Bob Ballard with founding it, and he gives no founding date either time. If true, it would mean the government quietly set up a programme to watch the oceans decades ago.
nato-warships-around-the-expedition-2011: During a 2011 dive expedition to a strange object on the floor of the Baltic Sea, warships from NATO, the Western military alliance, gathered around the team's boat. A treasure hunter named Dennis Asberg, who led the expedition and was there, says the ships were French, German, American and British, which he takes as a sign that militaries were paying close attention to what his team had found.
navair-high-energy-electromagnetic-field: A Navy team ran an experiment with a high energy electromagnetic field generator at NAVAIR, the Navy's air systems research and engineering command, to test what Salvatore Pais calls the Pais effect. Pais, a Navy scientist known for patents that read like UFO technology, says he worked on it himself. He says they could not get an electrical charge above ten to the minus eight units, when they needed at least one to show the effect is real.
navajo-curse-legend-of-skinwalker-ranch: Skinwalker Ranch, a property in Utah's Uinta Basin known for reports of strange happenings, is said to sit on cursed ground. Michels tells the legend himself on several episodes: in the 19th century, around the Civil War, the Ute tribe sided with the US government against the Navajo, and the Navajo, beaten and feeling betrayed, cursed the land with skinwalkers, shape-shifting figures of Navajo lore. In a later telling he leaves out the Navajo story and says instead that the Ute won't even talk about the place, calling it cursed ground and the path of the Skinwalker, and that on the ranch drones malfunction, helicopters lose power and equipment dies. Brandon Fugal, the ranch's owner, repeats the legend as he was told it, saying the Navajo were driven away and cursed the property. The legend is offered as old roots for the strange things reported there.
navajo-skinwalker-lore-matches-ranch-act: The old Navajo stories of skinwalkers, shape-shifting figures from Navajo tradition, talk about glowing objects. Those are much like what people report at Skinwalker Ranch, a property named after the legend and known for strange happenings. Michels says he found this himself while doing a little Googling, and raises it as a hint that the activity at the ranch may be very old.
naval-intelligence-as-a-major-funder-of-: Naval Intelligence, the US Navy's intelligence service, was at one point a big funder of Andrija Puharich, a doctor who researched psychic phenomena, from the 1950s right into the early 1980s. A researcher named Greg Malatzi says this as something "we know", without naming a source. If true, it would mean the Navy was paying for decades of research into the paranormal.
naval-intelligence-commander-s-email-uap: Unidentified objects are said to be seen in the ocean more than anywhere else, going in and out of the water in five to seven areas of the world. A retired Navy admiral named Tim Gallaudet says this was in an email he received from a naval intelligence commander. Later in the same talk he goes further and calls these "undersea bases possibly," which, if true, would mean something has made a home under the sea.
naval-intelligence-sphere-program-for-vi: Someone who says he worked in naval intelligence, the Navy's spy branch, claims he was part of a secret program that used a sphere to see into other timelines, as a tool for "remote viewing," the practice of trying to see faraway things with the mind alone. The online UFO researcher who goes by UAPGerb passes on this claim from a source he does not name, and calls it only a claim. He says the sphere was like one described by a man named Randy Anderson.
navy-astronomer-measures-wobbling-disc-1: In New Mexico, one of the US Navy's top astronomers watched a wobbling disc in the sky and measured it, according to the researcher Marik von Rennenkampff. He points to the source as a well-known Life magazine article from 1947. He brings it up to show that trained scientists were reporting these objects from the very start.
navy-aviators-privately-report-regular-s: Navy pilots at a US Navy base said in private that they were "seeing uh phenomena that they couldn't understand on a very regular basis," including near misses, but were not talking about it openly. That account comes from a man named Dr. Gilbert, who says the pilots told him and his colleagues this directly, speaking in an episode with a former director of the National Security Agency, the US spy agency for signals and communications. If true, it would mean strange encounters were common and kept quiet inside the military.
navy-cia-tug-of-war-over-the-nuro-1969: Until 1972, the US Navy and the CIA, America's foreign intelligence agency, are said to have fought over who would control the NURO, a secret office whose control was in dispute. On the CIA side the fight was led by its science and technology branch. An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb tells this without naming a source and mentions Bobby Ray Inman, a senior US intelligence official, as he sketches who held power over secret programs in those years.
navy-commander-george-hoover-on-roswell-: The beings found in the crash near Roswell, New Mexico, in 1947, the event the military first announced as a recovered flying disc, were time-traveling humans, according to a Navy commander named George Hoover, who Michels says held a top secret clearance for most of his life. Michels tells this himself, saying Hoover admitted it, without saying where or to whom. If true, the so-called aliens would be our own descendants.
navy-gave-pais-crash-material-for-his-pa: Salvatore Pais, a Navy scientist known for filing unusual patents for exotic craft, was likely given crashed UFO material by the Navy and worked out the equations behind it for his patents, according to Bob Maguire, a CIA contractor. Maguire says plainly he is guessing and names no source. If true, the patents would be a public trace of reverse-engineered technology.
navy-gun-camera-videos-off-san-diego: Videos from US Navy gun cameras, the targeting cameras on fighter jets, showed an object off San Diego traveling at what looked like warp speed and then diving into the ocean. John S. Herrington, a former US Secretary of Energy, tells Michels he saw this on television, so he is describing the footage as a viewer rather than from inside the government. He raises it as the kind of thing that made him take the subject seriously.
navy-has-no-original-flir1-tape-only-the: The US military does not have the original of the FLIR1 video, a 2004 infrared clip from a Navy fighter jet's camera showing an odd white object. Instead, the copy the Navy released is the same one that had been leaked online on a German file-sharing server, according to Mick West, a well-known UFO skeptic. West gives this as his own reading of the record, and he tells it because it raises doubts about where the famous video came from and whether it is complete.
navy-intelligence-visits-frances-swan-19: In 1954, Navy intelligence officers are said to have taken notice of a woman named Frances Swan in Eliot, Maine, and gone to visit her. A researcher named Grant Cameron tells this in his own summary, pointing to a record about her from the FBI, the US federal police, and Navy intelligence. If true, it would show the military took a private woman's claims seriously enough to look into them in person.
navy-misidentifications-a-jet-called-a-d: Trained lookouts on a US Navy ship, a group nicknamed the Snoopy team, mistook stars for drones, and a jet was also called a drone, in 2019. A skeptic named Mick West, who studies UFO videos, says this without naming a source, to argue that even trained military observers can misread ordinary things in the sky.
navy-overcharging-for-parts-1980: In the 1980s and 1990s, the US Navy was charged far too much for parts, according to a guest who goes by the online name UAPGerb. He offers it as "a really interesting example" without naming a source, in a talk about how Pentagon money is handled. The point is that a budget can carry costs that hide where the money really goes.
navy-patent-for-laser-drawn-plasma-decoy: The US Navy holds a patent for using lasers to draw glowing plasma shapes in the sky, such as the shape of an airplane, to fool incoming missiles, according to Eric Haseltine, a former research director at the National Security Agency, the US agency for intercepting communications. He raises it as something he found out about, suggesting some strange sightings could be military decoys.
navy-pilots-interviewed-including-fravor: A former US Senate staffer named Kurt McConnell says he and his colleagues interviewed a string of Navy pilots about unexplained objects. Among them they tracked down the Navy pilots David Fravor and Alex Dietrich, who in 2004 had flown in the Tic Tac episode, where pilots off the US coast reported a white oval object shaped like the mint. McConnell tells it as part of his own work, which shows that Senate staff were taking the pilots' accounts seriously.
navy-recovering-non-human-craft-from-the: The US Navy is said to be recovering "crafts of non-human origin" from the bottom of the oceans all over the world. Michels says this himself, without naming a source, in an episode about the two days he spent with Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft in Nevada. If true, it would mean such craft are being found and quietly collected at sea, not only on land.
navy-says-brown-s-work-still-classified: According to Jesse Michels, when Linda Brown, daughter of the scientist Townsend Brown, and his biographer Paul Schatzkin asked the US Navy for his records, the Navy was uncooperative at first; in one telling Michels says Schatzkin used the Freedom of Information Act, a US law that lets anyone request government records, and the Navy acted as if it had never heard of a man by that name. In another episode Michels gives it only as his own belief that Brown's work, which he links to anti-gravity, is likely still classified by the Navy today, which would mean the research mattered more than the official silence suggests.
navy-seal-finds-a-black-octagonal-struct: A Navy SEAL, a US special forces sailor, is said to have found a "highly polished black stone octagonal structure" standing about 18 feet out of the ice near McMurdo, the main US research station in Antarctica. The philosopher Jason Jorjani passes this on from the researcher Linda Moulton Howe, who told the story. If true, something built by someone would be sitting under the Antarctic ice.
navy-secretary-kimball-and-admiral-radfo: In 1950, on a flight from California to Hawaii, an unknown object is said to have circled two planes: one carrying Dan Kimball, the Secretary of the Navy, and one carrying the admiral Arthur Radford. A guest named Richard Dolan tells it to Michels, passing on an account he credits to a man named Donald Kho. If true, it would mean the Navy's own top leaders had a close encounter of their own.
nazca-and-paracas-cranial-elongation-rit: The Nazca and Paracas, ancient peoples of southern Peru, are said to have practised rituals that reshaped and lengthened the skull. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, as one of the customs of those cultures, in an episode about strange three-fingered bodies found in Peru, where it bears on whether odd-looking remains from the region could be explained by such human practices.
nazca-lines-made-to-be-seen-from-the-sky: The Nazca Lines, huge figures and lines drawn into the desert ground in southern Peru, are said to make sense only when seen from the air. Michels says this himself, without naming a source: the figures "only make sense 150 to 500 m in the air, which is far higher than any of the closest vantage points on the ground." He raises it because it would suggest whoever made them meant them to be seen from the sky.
nazi-aneutronic-fusion-bomb-traded-away-: The researcher Jason Jorjani suggests that in 1944 and 1945 the Nazis may have developed a kind of fusion bomb that gives off almost no radiation, so powerful that "atom bombs would be like matches" next to it. The story holds that this weapon was traded away in exchange for amnesty after the war. Jorjani lays it out as a theory, without naming a source, and if true it would mean the Allies quietly inherited a weapon beyond the atom bomb.
nazi-antarctica-expedition-1938: Nazi Germany sent an expedition to Antarctica in the late 1930s, and it is told as part of the larger story of what the Nazis may have been looking for far from Europe. The researcher Jason Jorjani, a guest who talks about what he calls Hitler's secret UFO programme, brings it up without naming a source. He calls it the German Antarctic Expedition of 1937 or 1938 and adds that it dropped swastika flags over the ice. Michels raises it himself in a separate episode with Peter Levenda, a guest billed as a CIA historian, and says simply that the expedition "was very real."
nazi-bell-propulsion-research-at-the-sko: During the 1940s, Nazi Germany is said to have run advanced propulsion research, linked to a device known as the Bell, at the Skoda Works, a large industrial plant just outside Prague, under the SS general Hans Kammler. The researcher Jason Jorjani tells it as a summary of what he has read, drawing on books such as The Hunt for Zero Point and Closer Encounters and on the writers Nick Cook, Igor Witkowski and Joseph P. Farrell. If true, it would mean the Nazis were working on exotic flying technology near the end of the war.
nazi-bell-scientists-killed-1940: The story goes that in the 1940s Nazi Germany secretly built a strange device called the Bell, somewhere in Germany or Czechoslovakia, and that it was deadly to the people who worked on it. The UFO historian Richard Dolan tells it from the British journalist Nick Cook's book The Hunt for Zero Point. Dolan says the claim is that a group of around 60 scientists was involved, that many of them died from the effects of the device, and that the rest were executed at the end of the war so they could not talk. The researcher Jason Jorjani, in an episode about what he calls Hitler's secret UFO program, describes something else about the device. He says plants placed around the Bell would turn to mulch, and he speaks of a "first team" of workers. Jorjani does not give the figure of 60 or say that the survivors were killed. The tellers raise it because it suggests the Nazis had a power far beyond the science of their day.
nazi-disc-shaped-craft-projects-miethe-s: In the 1940s in Nazi Germany, several men are said to have worked on separate attempts to build flying craft shaped like discs. The researcher Jason Simosa names Richard Miethe, Rudolf Schriever and a man called Lutzow, and says four or five others also claimed to have worked on such projects. He gives no source, and he raises it because it would mean people were building saucer-shaped craft on Earth before the modern UFO era.
nazi-discs-brought-to-us-via-operation-p: In the 1940s the United States took disc-shaped craft and other material out of Nazi Germany and shipped it home through Operation Paperclip, the postwar American effort that brought German scientists and technology to the US. That is the claim of Michael Herrera, a man who says he saw a 300-foot UFO in the Indonesian jungle. He mentions it in passing, as an example of where secret American craft might have come from.
nazi-enriched-uranium-sent-to-the-us-by-: In 1945, the story goes, a deal was struck with the Nazis to send the United States, by submarine, the nuclear material that ended up in the bombs dropped on Hiroshima and Nagasaki. A researcher named Jason Jorjani gives this as a summary, crediting it to a writer named Plimpton Hydrick and his book Critical Mass, about a deal made with the SS, the Nazi party's own armed and security force. If true, it would mean America's first atomic bombs relied partly on German uranium.
nazi-expeditions-searching-for-atlantis-: In the 1930s and 40s, members of the SS, the elite Nazi organisation, went on expeditions through Peru, Nepal and Tibet looking for traces of Atlantis, the sunken island of legend. A researcher named Jay Anderson says this on Michels's show. He says there are photographs of the Nazis with high lamas, Tibetan Buddhist teachers, with swastikas in the background, which would show how seriously the Nazis took ancient myths.
nazi-expeditions-to-the-himalayas-in-sea: In the 1930s and 1940s, Nazi Germany sent expeditions to the Himalayas to hunt for evidence of myths about an ancient "Aryan" master race. A former Senate staffer named Kurt McConnell tells this, saying he thinks it was the writer Igor Witkowski who described those expeditions. He brings it up as part of a wider story about secret Nazi research.
nazi-flying-saucers-attempted-but-not-ac: Nazi Germany certainly tried to build flying saucers, but it never actually had the technology, according to Luis Elizondo, a former Pentagon intelligence official. He speaks from general knowledge, without naming a source, pointing to known wartime experiments and to the "foo fighters", glowing objects that pilots reported in the skies over Bavaria during the Second World War. His point is that these sightings cannot simply be explained as secret Nazi craft.
nazi-memorabilia-at-paperclip-facilities: Swastikas and other Nazi objects were reportedly on open display at some of the sites, such as Fort Bliss in Texas and White Sands in New Mexico, where Operation Paperclip put its scientists to work. Paperclip was the US programme that brought German scientists to America after the Second World War. Michels tells this himself as something reported, without naming a source, to show how openly those scientists' past was tolerated.
nazi-missions-to-antarctica: The Nazis are said to have been fascinated by Antarctica and to have sent several missions there. Luis Elizondo, a former Pentagon intelligence official, says this in passing, with no date and no source. He mentions it as one more sign of how far the Nazis' interests reached.
nazi-occult-documents-found-in-a-cave-19: In 1945, near the end of the Second World War, American forces are said to have found a hidden stash of Nazi documents in a cave in southern Germany, among them records of real occult projects run by the Nazi state. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, in an episode on secret science and the American space agency, NASA.
nazi-submarine-traffic-intercepted-near-: Around 1946, Nazi German submarines were picked up travelling to Argentina, near the southern region of Patagonia. The philosopher Jason Jorjani says this on the show without saying who intercepted them or where he learned it. If true, it would mean Nazi submarines were still running secret trips to South America after the war.
nct-s-darpa-contract-and-military-ties-a: In June 1991, the Washington Post reported that a company called Noise Cancellation Technologies, based in Linthicum, Maryland, won a $210,000 research contract from DARPA, the Pentagon's agency for advanced research. Michels brings this up himself, along with a Navy research bulletin and the company's own website, in an episode about a sergeant named Dan Sherman, who says the NSA (the US agency for intercepting communications) hired him to speak to aliens. Michels uses the company's military ties as a way to back up parts of Sherman's story.
near-death-experience-after-poisoning-ou: In 1970, after being poisoned in Austria, a guest named Joe McMoneagle says he was delivered dead on arrival to a clinic in Germany, at a town he names as Passau, and had no heartbeat for almost 40 minutes. He tells it as his own experience: while he was gone, he says, he traveled outside his body and saw a white light.
near-death-experiencers-describe-living-: People who nearly died and say they visited another realm describe buildings there that seem alive, with doors that open as if made of molten metal, according to the UFO researcher Grant Cameron. He says he has collected such accounts himself: "I've got a whole list of maybe 20 so far." He names no single source, and he treats the shared detail as a sign that these people may be describing a real place.
nearly-2-000-experimental-variations-tra: A team at a Florida company called Exodus Propulsion Technologies, which works on a new kind of propulsion, has tried close to 2,000 versions of its experiment. Charles Buhler, who does this work himself, says that he and a colleague, Andrew Arjima, have been "keeping track" of every variation since around 2016. He gives the number to show how long and how carefully they have been testing the effect.
neighbor-moved-to-roswell-to-see-ufos: A man moved to Roswell, the New Mexico town long tied to UFO stories, because he wanted to be close to the sightings, and he claimed he did see something there. An unnamed audience member at an event around an interview with the whistleblower David Grusch tells this about a neighbour of his, passing on what the neighbour told him.
neighbor-saw-backyard-lit-up-like-a-holl: In 2017, at his home in Georgia, a neighbor told Mario Woods, a veteran who says he has had encounters of his own, that his backyard had been "lit up like a Hollywood set or something." Woods repeats what the neighbor told him. He offers it as an outside witness to strange lights at his house.
neighboring-farmer-s-house-shook-at-5-a-: In 1996, near Varginha in Brazil, where a craft and strange creatures are said to have come down, a farmer living close to the crash site says his whole house shook at five in the morning and soldiers told his family to stay inside. Carlos de Souza tells this on the show, drawing on filmed interviews made by a woman named Claudia Kovu, in which the farmer says: "Of course I did. My entire house shook." It matters because it would place a crash and a military operation at that farm on that morning.
neil-armstrong-discusses-a-ufo-research-: In the early 1970s the astronaut Neil Armstrong, the first man on the Moon, asked to sit with the astronomer J. Allen Hynek, who had advised the US Air Force on UFOs, and his family, and the two talked seriously about starting a new UFO research group. That is told by Hynek's son, who says he was there. If true, it would mean one of the most famous astronauts took UFOs seriously enough to want to study them.
neil-armstrong-s-1975-tayos-cave-expedit: After walking on the moon in 1969, the astronaut Neil Armstrong is said to have gone to the Tayos cave in Ecuador, at the edge of the Amazon, which was rumoured to hold ancient alien metal objects and a kind of hidden library. Michels tells this himself in several episodes, usually putting it in 1975 (once in 1976), saying Armstrong brought a film crew from the BBC, the British broadcaster, and linking the cave to Erich von Däniken, a writer of ancient-alien theories, and his book Chariots of the Gods. Michels finds it striking that the first man on the moon made this his next trip.
neil-armstrong-s-truth-s-protective-laye: Neil Armstrong, the first man to walk on the moon, once gave a speech saying "There are great ideas undiscovered. Breakthroughs available to those who can remove one of truth's protective layers," and these words get quoted as a hint that hidden truths are out there. Michels remembers it as a speech from the 1980s, when Armstrong was getting a medal. The comedian and podcaster Joe Rogan, repeating the story on the show, puts it 25 years after the moon landing, at an anniversary event for the brightest high school students, and a later episode plays the line and places it at the White House in 1994.
neil-armstrong-said-to-have-seen-ufos-on: Neil Armstrong, the astronaut who first walked on the Moon in 1969, is said to have seen UFOs while he was there and to have come back to Earth "super scared." Michels repeats this himself as a story that goes around, without naming a source, and if true it would mean the first Moon landing had company.
neil-armstrong-seemed-scared-at-his-spee: In 1969, about three weeks after coming back from the Moon, the astronaut Neil Armstrong gave a speech, the first man to walk on the Moon talking about "a big step for mankind". Michels says Armstrong looked scared and sheepish while he spoke. Michels describes this himself, without naming a source, as a hint that Armstrong may have seen something up there that troubled him.
neil-armstrong-we-were-told-not-to-come-: The astronaut Neil Armstrong is said to have told people in Washington DC, sometime in the 1970s, that "we were told not to come back to the moon." Michels repeats this as one of several "apocryphal stories" about Armstrong, without saying who heard it. A scientist named Steve Colbern, who studies objects said to be alien implants in human bodies, tells it a little differently: he says Armstrong was overheard saying it at a party, and that the warning came from the grays, the small grey beings of many alien accounts. If true, it would mean the moon landings were cut short by someone other than us.
nellis-object-as-balloons-drifting-in-th: A 1994 video from the Nellis and Tonopah range, a military testing area in Nevada, shows an unexplained object, and the UFO skeptic Mick West says he thinks it is just a balloon or a bunch of balloons floating in the wind. He gives this as his own reading of the footage in a debate with Michels. If he is right, the video shows nothing unusual.
nellis-range-face-to-face-encounter-1994: A man named Jason Sands says that in August 1994, at the Nellis testing range, a military area in Nevada, he came face to face with someone in a military outfit who, by his account, did not look human. The documentary filmmaker James Fox tells the story, which Sands gave as part of Fox's film project The Program. Fox mentions it several times in one conversation, at one point just thanking Sands "for including that encounter in Nellis," and at another describing "a guy dressed in you know military outfit that clearly according to him did not appear to be human." Michels also repeats it in a later episode, from Sands and Fox, though his version calls the being a blue alien and gives no date. If true, it would mean a non-human being was working inside a US military site.
nematode-revived-after-46-000-years-in-s: In 2023 it was reported that a nematode, a tiny worm, had been brought back to life after 46,000 years frozen in the permafrost of Siberia, the ground in the far north of Russia that stays frozen all year. A guest called Dr. Gilbert mentions the report without saying where it appeared. He brings it up to show how long life can survive in a frozen state.
network-of-underground-tunnels-beneath-t: Beneath the Giza Plateau in Egypt, where the great pyramids stand, there is said to be "something like a network of underground tunnels." The scientist Filippo Biondi, who scanned the ground there with radar in 2025 alongside his colleague Armando Mei, says the scans came back as "a mess" of echoes from underground. He tells it as his own finding, which would mean there are large hidden structures under the pyramids.
neuralink-implant-immune-reaction-2024: The first patient to get a brain implant from Neuralink, Elon Musk's company that puts chips in the brain, a man Michels calls Nolan Arba, may have needed his device adjusted after it first worked, because of an immune reaction, Michels says. He tells this himself, hedging that this is what he believes, without naming a source, in an episode about implants found in human bodies.
neurologist-steers-jim-toward-john-mack-: In 1976, while a patient in a Boston hospital connected to Harvard Medical School, a man named Jim Weiner says a neurologist, named in the telling as Jonathan Silverman, came into his room and pointed him toward people who studied UFOs. Weiner tells it as his own story: the doctor told him about Raymond Fowler, a UFO investigator who would be speaking at a conference at a Marriott hotel, and also steered him toward a man named John Mack. He tells it as the moment a medical doctor took his strange experience seriously enough to send him to these researchers.
neurotypical-woman-with-a-head-injury-re: A woman without autism who suffered a head injury is said to be able to reach the same inner "space" that autistic people who cannot speak are able to touch. Ky Dickens, maker of the documentary series The Telepathy Tapes, relays this from that project. If true, it would suggest the telepathy she studies is not limited to autistic people.
nevada-test-fallout-theory-dismissed-as-: One idea holds that fallout from weapons testing in Nevada explains the strange events on a ranch in Utah, and Brandon Fugal, the owner of that ranch, known as Skinwalker Ranch for its many odd reports, talks about it. He grants that "some of the testing in Nevada could have" played a part, but in the end he treats the theory as having no real basis, which would leave the ranch's events unexplained.
never-before-seen-footage-of-a-ufo-at-ar: There is said to be legendary footage, never shown before, of a UFO at Area 51, a secret US Air Force test site in the Nevada desert. Michels announces it himself, without saying where it came from, in an episode built around two days he spent with Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft near the site.
new-data-show-the-object-separated-from-: New 2025 data on a strange object lying on the floor of the Baltic Sea show that it seems to be separated from the seabed beneath it. The treasure hunter Dennis Asberg, whose team found and surveys the object, says so, putting it carefully: "It looks like it's separated from the bottom. That's what I can say." If true, it would suggest the object is something sitting on the seafloor rather than a natural part of it.
new-hoffmanlevin-collaboration-on-recurs: The cognitive scientist Donald Hoffman says he and the biologist Mike Levin are just starting to work together in 2026. Their shared interest is a piece of mathematics Hoffman calls "recursive trace logic", and they plan to hire a junior researcher to work on it. Hoffman tells it as his own news, and it matters to him because it would join his theories of the mind with Levin's work in biology.
new-jersey-and-uk-base-drone-sightings-2: In late 2024, strange flying objects were reported hovering over sensitive military sites in New Jersey and over bases in the United Kingdom. Michels tells it as proof that UFO interest in nuclear sites is ongoing, and, crediting the researcher Robert Hastings, names Picatinny Arsenal in New Jersey, the Lakenheath base in England, the Salem nuclear power plant in New Jersey and a power plant at Brunswick in North Carolina. A commentator named Marik von Rennenkampff stresses how serious the response was, with the FBI and the FAA, the US aviation authority, involved, drone flight bans in place and the governor engaged. The skeptic Michael Shermer calls it "the New Jersey swarm" and places it during Donald Trump's autumn 2024 campaign, while a former presidential advisor named Harald Malmgren says, "We have unidentified objects flying all over the United States."
new-jersey-drone-flap-and-objects-emergi: In 2024 swarms of unexplained drones were reported over New Jersey, and some witnesses said they saw them rising out of the sea off the coast. Jesse Michels tells this himself on several episodes. He says there were sightings of these objects "emerging from the water." He quotes Donald Trump on the Jersey drones: "These are coming out of the water. We know where the garage is." He says a local sheriff also reported that they came out of the water, and he points to a Rolling Stone article on the New Jersey drones. To Michels this suggests the objects may have a base under the ocean. A researcher and historian named Richard Dolan gives a matching account, also without naming a source. He mentions reports of the objects "supposedly coming out of the water" and adds that they were said to have harassed US Coast Guard ships.
new-jersey-drone-flap-and-the-disclosure: The wave of drone and UFO sightings over New Jersey in November 2024 may be linked to the filming of Disclosure Day, a film by Steven Spielberg, in the same state. Jesse Michels passes on this idea from his friend Chris Ramsay, who runs a show called Area 52, saying the film was shot in New Jersey in late 2024. In a later episode Michels tells it a little differently, saying production started in February 2025, a few months after the sightings, and naming Morris County and an Army base called Picatinny Arsenal.
new-nautics-and-university-of-florida-pr: A team at the University of Florida has been hired to develop ways to "hack" the brain's own supply of DMT, a powerful psychedelic substance the body makes naturally in small amounts. The neuroscientist Andrew Gallimore says so as one of the people behind the project, which he says runs through a company called New Nautics and is known as EDMTX. The aim, as he describes it, is to reach on purpose the strange realm that people report on DMT.
new-parapsychology-degree-program-at-the: A school called the California Institute for Human Science now offers a doctoral and a master's degree that can specialise in parapsychology, the study of claimed psychic abilities. Jeffrey Mishlove, a guest with a doctorate who talks about psychics, UFOs and the afterlife, says in 2026 that he just helped create the programme. For him it marks the field gaining a place in formal higher education.
new-start-treaty-to-reduce-nuclear-weapo: In 2010, while Barack Obama was president, the United States signed a treaty with Russia called New START, to cut the number of nuclear weapons each side keeps ready for use. A former Air Force officer named Robert Salas mentions it from memory, first calling it by the name of an earlier arms deal and then correcting himself, as part of his account of what has happened to America's nuclear missiles.
new-tall-white-arrivals-come-too-close-a: One night in 1965, about a week after the full moon, a group of newly arrived tall white beings came too close to a man working out on Range Three, a stretch of test range in Indian Springs Valley, Nevada. Charles Hall tells this as his own experience, from the three years he says he spent around these beings, whom he calls Tall White aliens, while stationed in the Nevada desert. If true, it would mean non-human visitors lived alongside US military staff there.
new-zealand-archives-reveal-kaikoura-cov: Government files released by New Zealand around 2011 shed light on the 1978 Kaikoura sightings, lights seen and filmed off New Zealand's coast, including the official explanation that the lights were squid fishing boats, which he presents as a cover-up. The journalist Ross Coulthart says he discovered this archive release himself while researching the case. If so, the official story about Kaikoura would have been shaped to explain the sightings away.
newgrange-curbstone-with-perplexing-symb: Outside Newgrange, an ancient stone tomb in Ireland, there is a large curbstone carved with many puzzling symbols. A researcher of ancient sites named Geoffrey Drumm, who says he has been there himself, describes it as part of his search for the hidden purpose of such monuments.
newly-found-mysterious-sites-in-eastern-: In eastern Turkey, in the Ararat region that was once part of Armenia, there are said to be very mysterious ancient sites that had only just been found. The researcher Matt LaCroix, who writes about lost ancient history, says he "stumbled across" them himself. He tells it because such sites could point to a forgotten chapter of human history.
news-clip-victory-learning-center-employ: A local news report says three employees at the Victory Learning Center, a school in Lackawanna, New York, were put on leave over claims that they physically mistreated students. The unnamed reporter attributes this to OLV Human Services, the organization that runs the center. Jesse Michels plays the clip in an interview with a man who says he was taken into a UFO program as a child, as an outside record touching the place in his story.
news-report-of-the-oklahoma-city-bombing: In 1995, a huge car bomb went off outside a large federal building in downtown Oklahoma City. It wrecked the building and killed children, federal workers, soldiers and civilians. These words come from a clip of an unnamed news reporter that was played during an episode about a scientist who studies objects he says were implanted in people's bodies.
news-report-survivors-of-the-plane-crash: An unnamed news reporter, standing at Jamaica Hospital in New York, says the hospital has "received 14 survivors from the plane crash." The clip is played in an episode with the writer Jason Jorjani, and the reporter is describing what the hospital itself has said.
newsnation-finds-nothing-in-the-vatican-: According to the skeptic Michael Shermer, the American cable news network NewsNation went to the Vatican and searched its files over a claim tied to 1933, and "couldn't find anything." Shermer gives this as a summary, without naming a source. He brings it up to argue that the Vatican holds no record backing the story.
newsnation-slide-showing-a-doe-gravity-p: A slide shown by NewsNation, a US television news channel that Michels says covers UFOs a lot, is said to tie a patient to "advanced gravity propulsion research" at the Department of Energy, the US government department that runs much of the country's nuclear and energy research. According to Michels, the patient had damage to the brain's white matter, the kind of bodily harm he compares to Havana syndrome, the name given to mysterious injuries reported by US officials. Michels describes the slide himself in two episodes, in 2024 and 2026, the first time while discussing the journalist Ross Coulthart and the researcher Eric Weinstein, as a hint that such research could hurt the people near it.
newton-and-gebauer-framed-in-fraud-trial: Two men, Silas Newton and Leo GeBauer, are said to have been treated unfairly and set up in a 1950s fraud trial in Colorado over a doodlebug, a gadget said to find oil or minerals underground. A researcher who goes by UAPGerb praises the author William Steinman, whose book on the reported saucer crash case known as Aztec draws on Colorado court records. In UAPGerb's account, Steinman went through those records and found how unfairly the two men were attacked. He also brings in the government scientist Vannevar Bush. A researcher named Scott Ramsey puts the trial in Denver in 1953 and names a Herman Flader. He says the case went through seven judges, and each one refused to hear it. Ramsey also mentions the writer Frank Scully. The point of telling it is that if the two men were framed, the saucer story tied to them looks less like a con.
newton-diaries-sarbacher-tells-wilbur-sm: In 1950, a man named Robert Sarbacher is said to have told Wilbert B. Smith, a Canadian radio engineer who led Canada's first government project on UFOs, that flying saucers were real, top secret, and studied by the US government through a group led by a man named Vannevar Bush. A researcher who goes by the online name UAPGerb tells this twice, summarising without naming a single direct source. In one telling he says it comes from the diaries of a man named Silas Newton, and in the other from a 1950 memo of Canada's Department of Transport and a book called The Flying Saucer Conspiracy, also mentioning a writer named Frank Scully.
newton-saucer-settled-gently-within-500-: Around 1948 to 1950, a round object that had "already been identified as being a flying saucer" is said to have "settled gently to Earth" somewhere within 500 miles of Denver, Colorado. A man named Silas Newton tells this as something he knew of directly. If true, it would mean an intact craft came down and was recovered in the American West.
next-30-years-a-danger-time-in-the-tauri: The next 30 years are a dangerous time for Earth as it passes through the Taurid stream, a band of comet debris the planet crosses every year, according to scientists from a team called the Comet Research Group. The writer Graham Hancock passes this on from that group and from one of its scientists, Allen West. If they are right, Earth could face a serious impact from that debris within a generation.
nhi-communication-ci-wizards-are-messing: Someone is said to have made contact with a non-human intelligence, asked it something like what was going on or why it was here, and got the answer that "CI wizards are messing with the timeline." A guest named Matthew Pines passes this on second-hand, from what he was told. He tells it twice, and once the phrase comes out as "CIA wizards", meaning the US spy agency, rather than "CI", a common short form for counterintelligence.
nhi-component-to-the-new-jersey-drone-fl: The wave of mysterious drone sightings over New Jersey in 2024 had, mixed in with other things, an NHI component, meaning non-human intelligence. Jake Barber, who says he once carried a recovered UFO with his helicopter, gives this as his own view rather than something he saw. If true, some of what people saw over New Jersey would not have been made by people.
nhi-testing-us-at-missile-fields: Non-human intelligences, beings that are not from Earth, are testing humanity when they show up at nuclear missile sites, according to a Navy scientist named Salvatore Pais, who holds patents for unusual craft designs. He gives no source and states it as obvious: "Of course, they're testing us." If true, the visits would be deliberate probes of our most dangerous weapons.
nhtcu-meets-oni-doj-extradition-threat-o: After he was caught, the British hacker Gary McKinnon says Britain's national cyber crime police unit met in Washington in 2002 with the Office of Naval Intelligence, the US Navy's spy service, and the US Department of Justice. That November, he says, the Americans threatened to have him sent to the US for trial, where on paper he faced 70 years in jail. McKinnon tells it as his own experience, to show how seriously the US took what he had found.
nicap-s-founding-as-a-possible-link-to-t: Around 1956, the same time as a break or cutoff that comes up in his talk with the astronomer Beatriz Villarroel, a group called NICAP was founded, which Michels calls "the first civilian UFO research program," meaning a private group of citizens studying UFO reports. Michels raises the timing himself, without a source, as a possible link between that cutoff and the start of public UFO research.
nick-cook-rebuffed-by-a-scared-george-tr: When the aviation journalist Nick Cook tried to meet George Trimble, a long-retired aerospace man then in his eighties, through a friend at the aircraft maker Lockheed Martin, Trimble refused to talk. Michels tells it in 2023 citing Cook, and Cook tells it himself in 2024, saying Trimble was "really quite spooked" at the idea of speaking to him and naming the Martin company alongside Lockheed. They tell it because Trimble's fear hints he knew about secret work on antigravity flight.
nick-cook-s-search-for-1950s-gravity-res: In the 1950s there was said to be a burst of research into controlling gravity, which then vanished and went nowhere. Michels tells this himself, drawing on The Hunt for Zero Point, a book by Nick Cook, an aviation journalist at Jane's Defence Weekly, a British military trade magazine, whom Michels calls hard-headed and who he says stumbled onto the research. If true, it would suggest the work was hidden away rather than abandoned.
nick-pope-s-death-from-cancer-2020: Nick Pope, a British figure well known for talking about UFOs, died of cancer just a short while ago, according to the skeptic Michael Shermer, who mentions it in passing during a debate with the host. Shermer brings it up while speaking of Pope's wife, a woman named Elizabeth Weiss, and names no source for it.
nids-study-correlating-triangle-sighting: A study by NIDS, a private group that looked into unexplained phenomena, is said to have matched reports of triangle-shaped craft to the locations of US naval bases. Matthew Brown, called a Pentagon whistleblower in the episode's title, mentions it as a "famous" study from what he thinks was the late 1990s or early 2000s. If so, it would tie the triangles to the Navy.
night-aircraft-spotting-with-lear-outsid: In the 1980s, a man named Bob Lazar, who says he worked on unknown craft in the Nevada desert, says he went out at night with a companion named John Lear to watch for aircraft. He tells it from his own memory: they were "out in the desert in the middle of the night with binoculars and stuff" outside the small Nevada town of Tonopah, hoping to see secret or unusual flying things.
night-intrusion-at-the-cabin-when-the-im: One night in 1989 at his cabin in upstate New York, the writer Whitley Strieber says he turned and saw a woman already standing near the foot of the bed with a man beside her, while a male voice in the backyard said "Condition red." Strieber, who says he has met aliens, tells this as the night an implant was put in his body. If true, it would mean beings, or people working with them, came into his home to do it.
night-meeting-with-military-x-about-the-: To learn about a 1996 military operation in Varginha, a town in Brazil where a strange creature was reportedly captured, the UFO documentary filmmaker James Fox says he drove about four hours into the night, north of the town. There he met a man he calls only "military X", a source with ties to the operation. Fox tells it as his own trip, since a military insider would back up what townspeople said they saw.
night-meeting-with-puthoff-and-hameroff-: In 2026, Michels says that just the night before he had been in a room with a researcher named Hal Puthoff and the scientist Stuart Hameroff. He tells it himself, as someone who was there, and explains that Hameroff is behind a theory called orchestrated objective reduction, which holds that consciousness comes from quantum effects inside microtubules, tiny tube-like structures within brain cells.
night-of-shifting-timelines-in-an-la-air: During a strange night in a rented Airbnb home in Los Angeles around 2024 or 2025, a man heard a voice speak the word "Timelines" while he showered.
