Brent Friedman, a guest on an episode about Hollywood and UFOs, says it happened to him: he was repeating a calming mantra to himself and trying to wind down when the voice spoke. He tells it as part of a night when he felt timelines were shifting around him.
night-scarb-s-measurements-of-the-osiris: Measurements from a 2024 scan of the Osiris shaft, a deep underground shaft near the pyramids at Giza in Egypt, are said not to match the shaft's known layout, with the signals in the scan turning up in the wrong places. The researcher Jeffrey Drum says the measurements were made by an online channel called Night Scarb and shows them as backing his case. If true, it would mean there is more under Giza than the known shaft.
night-sky-suddenly-bright-in-the-brookha: Around 7 one November evening in 1992 in Brookhaven, Long Island, New York, the dark night sky suddenly became brighter than it is in daytime. That account comes from an unnamed witness in a clip Michels plays, who says they saw it. The sudden light is the start of what is called the Brookhaven incident.
night-visitors-in-the-twins-childhood-ho: In the 1950s, in their childhood home near Allentown, Pennsylvania, twin brothers say they would wake at night to find "something pulling the covers off our beds." Jim Weiner, who has spoken publicly about alien abduction experiences with his twin Jack Weiner, tells it as something the two of them lived through in their shared bedroom. He tells it because it suggests their strange encounters began long before adulthood.
nightly-3-a-m-wake-ups-and-communing-201: The writer Whitley Strieber says that from 2015 to 2020 the beings he says he is in contact with "woke me up religiously every night" around 3 a.m., and that he spent those hours communing with them. He tells it first hand, linking it to his work The Hidden Garden, as proof of an ongoing bond with visitors he says live among us.
nile-freshwater-mussels-found-120150-ft-: Shells of freshwater mussels and remains of other Nile animals have been found 120 to 150 feet above the level where the Nile floods today. A researcher named Randall Carlson says so on Michels's show, without naming where the finding comes from. If true, it would mean the river once ran far higher, likely in some huge ancient flood.
nimitz-encounter-as-multisensory-evidenc: In 2004, off the coast of San Diego, ships and jets of a group led by the aircraft carrier USS Nimitz tracked a white oval object shaped like a Tic Tac mint. Michels says it was seen on radar, by eyewitnesses including the Navy pilot David Fravor, and on infrared camera footage that was later released, with 11 or 12 witnesses over three days. Michels makes this case himself in several episodes, holding it up as some of the strongest UFO evidence because so many different kinds of sensors caught it at once.
nimitz-tic-tac-acceleration-and-power-es: In 2004, off Southern California, near the aircraft carrier USS Nimitz, a white oval object shaped like a Tic Tac mint is said to have dropped from 28,000 feet to sea level in a fraction of a second. A researcher named Kevin Knuth gives his team's estimate, garbled in speech as "7.5 seconds or so, 78 seconds", without naming a source. He uses the figure to work out how fast the object sped up and how much power that would take, far beyond any known aircraft.
nimitz-tic-tac-incident-2004: In 2004, off San Diego, Navy pilots from the aircraft carrier Nimitz, among them a fighter pilot named David Fravor, reported a "Tic Tac", a white oval object shaped like the mint. Michels brings it up twice in his own words, calling it one of the "holy grail events" of the subject, the case on which many people rest their belief that UFOs are real. In one telling he adds that the film director Steven Spielberg cites the case as what renewed his own interest in UFOs.
nina-kulagina-stops-the-hearts-of-animal: After the Soviets picked up research into mind powers, they had a woman named Nina Kulagina who could stop the hearts of rats, rabbits and other animals, according to a former Army sergeant named Lyn Buchanan. Buchanan, who calls her "Nina Cologa", tells it without naming a source. He brings it up as a sign of how far Soviet work on psychic powers is said to have gone.
nine-craft-seen-through-the-open-hangar-: Around 1988 or 1989, at S-4, which he describes as a secret site in the Nevada desert, a man named Bob Lazar says he looked down through open hangar bay doors and saw a row of flying craft, nine of them. Lazar tells it as something he saw himself, and in a second telling says "nine for sure," adding that he can only speak to what he saw with his own eyes. If true, it would mean the US government was holding a whole fleet of such craft.
nine-dr-g-scientists-traced-to-bush-s-os: The researcher Scott Ramsey says he and his colleagues traced nine of the unnamed scientists behind a book called Behind the Flying Saucers, known in the book as "Dr. G," to the circle of Vannevar Bush. Bush was the engineer who ran the Office of Scientific Research and Development, the US government's wartime science agency in the 1940s. Ramsey says they went "down each division" of Bush's group and recognised name after name, among them Richard C. Tolman, Eugene McDermott and Cecil Howard Green, which he takes as a sign that the book's sources were real wartime insiders.
nine-page-pentagon-uap-report-2021: In June 2021 the Pentagon put out a short report on unexplained objects in the sky, which the government calls UAP, short for unidentified aerial phenomena. Jesse Michels dates it to June 25, 2021, and says it acknowledged "the existence of objects in our sky that we cannot explain." The mathematician Eric Weinstein talks about it in two episodes as a reader of the report. He says it ran to nine pages, six of them relevant, and was written to be "as dull as is humanly possible about the most exciting thing that you could possibly imagine." To him that meant one of two things: either the Pentagon was running a psychological operation, or people inside it believe almost for certain that Earth has been visited by beings from elsewhere. In a later episode he credits the report to the office that oversees US intelligence agencies and reads it differently, as a fight between two authors. He says he could hear one voice that "wanted to disclose more and one that said over my dead body."
nine-vanishing-transients-on-1950s-plate: Nine points of light that show up on photographs of the night sky from the 1950s were later gone, and when the world's largest optical telescope looked at those spots, nothing was there. The astronomer Beatriz Villarroel, who led the work, says the objects appear on plates from the Palomar Sky Survey, a mid-century photographic map of the sky, and not in a star catalogue kept by the US Navy, and that a friend pointed the 10.4 metre Gran Telescopio Canarias in the Canary Islands at eight or nine of the positions and found "nothing left." If true, something bright sat in the sky in the 1950s and then disappeared.
ning-li-and-podkletnov-rotating-supercon: Two scientists spun superconductors, materials that carry electricity with no resistance when very cold: a physicist named Ning Li worked with a rotating disc of a ceramic superconductor called YBCO, and a scientist named Eugene Podkletnov also used rotating superconductors. Michels names this work himself, without naming a source, in a talk with a Navy scientist about patents for unusual craft, as earlier examples of experiments along the same lines.
ning-li-and-smalley-took-400-000-in-army: Two physicists at the University of Alabama in Huntsville, Ning Li and Larry Smalley, took $400,000 from the Army Research Laboratory, the US Army's main research lab, and produced nothing for it, according to Eric W. Davis, a physicist who has worked on government-funded studies of advanced propulsion. Davis tells Michels that "they didn't deliver anything for that money," a claim that casts doubt on their gravity research, and he names a colleague, Travis Taylor, in the same account.
ning-li-email-intercepted-by-west-point-: In the early 2000s, emails from a scientist named Ning Li are said to have been intercepted by an internet address belonging to West Point, the US Army's military academy, after which she was never heard from again. A guest named Dave Rossi tells this from what he knows about her. The suggestion is that the military quietly took over her work.
ning-li-last-seen-at-mitre-anti-gravity-: A researcher named Ning Li, who worked on anti-gravity, is said to have made her last public, on-record appearance in 2003 at a conference about anti-gravity held by MITRE, a research company near Washington that does work for the US government. Michels says this himself on two separate episodes, without naming a source. He brings it up because, in his telling, she went quiet after that, which would suggest her work was taken out of public view.
ning-li-s-disappearance-after-breakthrou: The story is that a Chinese-born physicist named Ning Li did breakthrough work on anti-gravity in the United States, somewhere between the 1990s and 2000s, and then vanished. The researcher Matthew Pines cites her as one of several people doing "breakthrough research on the margins" who then go "poof, they disappear". The comedian and podcaster Joe Rogan, in a clip played on another episode, tells it more loosely as the story of a Chinese scientist working on anti-gravity who vanished, without naming her. If true, it would suggest that people who get close to such technology are taken out of public view.
ning-li-s-gravito-magnetic-research-move: In the 1990s, the physicist Ning Li is said to have left her job at the University of Alabama in Huntsville to work full-time at Redstone Arsenal, a US Army base in Alabama, on research into gravity and magnetism so sensitive that it effectively vanished from public view. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, and mentions her colleagues Larry Smalley and Douglas Torr. In a second episode he adds that in 2014 she was hit by a car on the University of Alabama campus and was left with permanent brain damage, and he follows her story up to 2021.
ning-li-s-last-talk-was-at-a-mitre-confe: A scientist named Ning Li is said to have given her last public talk at a conference held by MITRE, a research organisation that does work for the US government, before she "kind of went into the black," meaning she disappeared into secret government work. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, and it matters because it would suggest her research was taken behind closed doors.
ning-li-s-spinning-superconductors-nasa-: The physicist Ning Li claimed that spinning superconductors, materials that carry electricity with no resistance, produced an unusual effect, but when NASA, the US space agency, tried to reproduce it, they did not see the effect. Charles Buhler, presented on the show as a NASA figure working on new propulsion, tells this from memory and hedges ("someone, I think NASA"). He brings it up as an example of a claimed gravity-related breakthrough that did not hold up when others tested it.
ning-li-s-superconductor-antigravity-wor: In the 1990s, a physicist named Ning Li at the University of Alabama in Huntsville studied whether superconductors, materials that carry electricity with no resistance, could make objects lighter. Michels tells this on two episodes. In one, he places her under a researcher named Larry Smalley. In the other, he says she published results with a colleague named Douglas Torr, showing the masses she tested lost between 0.5% and 2.1% of their weight over several trials. If it held up, it would be a step toward antigravity.
ning-li-superconductor-gravity-shielding: A physicist named Ning Li, working at the University of Alabama in Huntsville and later through her own company, Anti-gravity LLC, is said to have spun superconductors (materials that carry electricity with no loss when kept very cold) very fast and found that things above them weighed less, which she explained as tiny particles of gravity, called gravitons, creating a kind of gravity shield. Michels brings this up several times, putting it in the early 2000s and linking it to ceramic superconductors described in a book by James Lacatski, while Li herself, speaking firsthand, says "nobody found any mistake in my calculation." If it held up, it would point to a way of weakening gravity in the lab.
nitinol-developed-from-the-roswell-crash: A metal called nitinol was developed from material recovered after the 1947 crash near Roswell, New Mexico, which some say was an alien craft, according to the UFO researcher Grant Cameron. He mentions it in passing and sounds unsure ("I think was something developed from the Roswell crash"), naming no source. If true, an everyday modern material would have come from crash debris.
nixon-calls-hughes-to-set-up-a-castro-as: Around 1960, Richard Nixon, later president, is said to have called the businessman Howard Hughes to arrange a plot to kill the Cuban leader Fidel Castro, which then ran through Hughes's aide Robert Maheu to the gangsters Johnny Roselli and Sam Giancana. A lawyer named Dan Sheehan tells it, saying it all came straight from Santo Trafficante Jr., a man he says was a client of the firm where he worked. Sheehan tells it on two episodes, and in one he adds more names, Sheffield Edwards and Paul Helliwell, a meeting at the Fontainebleau Hotel, and a unit he calls the S Force.
nixon-ended-the-apollo-program-and-scrap: President Richard Nixon pulled the plug on Apollo, NASA's program that landed men on the Moon, and the giant Saturn rockets that carried them were scrapped, because the Vietnam War was costing the country so much money. The researcher Randall Carlson offers this as "the more prosaic explanation", without naming a source, in a conversation about stranger reasons the Moon trips might have stopped. It is the ordinary account he sets beside the unusual ones.
nixon-haldeman-smoking-gun-tape-1972: A 1972 recording from President Richard Nixon's White House, known as the Smoking Gun tape because it caught the cover-up of the Watergate break-in on tape, has Nixon's chief of staff H.R. Haldeman walk in and say, as the lawyer and investigator Dan Sheehan quotes it, "Mr President, I think we've got a problem here." Sheehan, summarising the tape without naming where he got his reading, places the conversation on 21 June and ties it to figures including the intelligence chief Richard Helms. He uses it to show how the people at the top handled the scandal behind closed doors.
nixon-headed-the-5412-committee-under-ei: Richard Nixon, while vice president under President Dwight D. Eisenhower in the 1950s, also headed the 5412 committee, which Michels describes as a plan for keeping the government running in a catastrophe. Michels says this himself, hedging with "I believe" and naming no source, while talking about how deep Nixon's ties to secret government projects went.
nixon-on-whether-the-cia-conspired-to-re: Richard Nixon, the former US president, was asked whether the CIA, America's foreign spy agency, worked to push him out of office. In a recording Michels plays, Nixon says he doesn't know, that "many people think so," but that he found it hard to understand why the CIA, "which apparently had advanced knowledge of the break-in," meaning the 1972 burglary behind the Watergate scandal that brought down his presidency, never told him. If the CIA did know in advance, it would raise the question of whether the agency let his downfall happen.
nixon-s-1960-assassination-team-killed-j: Dan Sheehan, the guest, says that an assassination team that Richard Nixon set up in 1960 was the same team that killed President John F. Kennedy in Dallas in 1963. Sheehan passes this on from others, naming Santo Trafficante Jr., Andy Toney and William Johnstone Taylor among the people behind it. If true, a plan made inside the government would have been turned on a sitting president.
nixon-s-filing-cabinet-folder-of-alien-b: Richard Nixon, the US president, kept a folder in his filing cabinet holding photographs of dead alien bodies, and people would be shown those pictures, according to the UFO researcher Grant Cameron. Cameron tells it as a story that went around and says he believes it is true. If it were, it would mean a sitting president had seen physical proof of alien bodies.
nixon-sets-up-operation-40-after-castro-: Around 1959, after Fidel Castro, the new revolutionary leader of Cuba, refused his terms, Richard Nixon, then Vice President, is said to have set up a secret operation first called Operation 40. The lawyer Dan Sheehan tells this without naming a source and links it to the mob boss Santo Trafficante Jr. He tells it as the start of a covert group he connects to later events, including the killing of President John F. Kennedy.
nixon-shows-brezhnev-a-folder-moon-fligh: At a US-Soviet summit in the early 1970s, President Richard Nixon is said to have opened a small folder about UFOs and shown it to the Soviet leader Leonid Brezhnev, and the American moon flights stopped soon after. The story comes from Kiran Ilum Xenov, a former president of one of Russia's republics, in a December 2025 episode. He passes it on second-hand and links it to the last Soviet leader, Mikhail Gorbachev. Xenov says that after the others had left the room, the American president "had a small folder like this that he opened and showed" to Brezhnev. He adds that Yuri Andropov, a senior Soviet official, was present. In the same episode Michels repeats the point in his own words. He describes Nixon giving the Soviet Union information in the 1970s about what the CIA, the US spy agency, and the White House knew about UFOs and aliens. Michels does not mention the folder or the end of the moon flights. If true, it would mean the two Cold War rivals quietly shared their UFO secrets at the highest level.
nixon-takes-jackie-gleason-to-homestead-: One night in the 1970s, President Richard Nixon is said to have turned up at the home of the comedian Jackie Gleason and taken him to Homestead Air Force Base in Florida to see secret UFO material. Michels calls it a "famous story" and gives the year as 1973. Elsewhere he says Nixon may have been drunk and came with no Secret Service guards. The comedian and podcaster Joe Rogan, citing a magazine article, says Gleason saw a crashed UFO and "biological alien bodies that were in freezers," and became a UFO fan after that. The story goes back to Gleason's ex-wife, Beverly McKittrick, in an interview with the National Enquirer, a tabloid newspaper, in 1983. The writer Bryce Zabel and the researcher Grant Cameron both name her as the source. Cameron says she told it this way: either Gleason was out "fooling around with women" or it really happened, because he came home badly shaken. Michels also cites a book called The Great One. If true, a sitting president would have shown alien remains to a TV star.
nixon-used-malmgren-to-check-kissinger-1: President Richard Nixon used an adviser named Harold Malmgren to keep watch on his top foreign policy aide Henry Kissinger, to make sure Kissinger was not going off on his own in negotiations. A researcher named Matthew Pines says so, without naming a source, in two conversations with Michels; in the second, about whether Kissinger oversaw a secret program to recover crashed craft, he places it in 1971 to 1974 rather than starting in 1969.
nixonford-era-decision-to-privatize-the-: Under Presidents Nixon and Ford, between 1969 and 1977, a decision is said to have been made to hand the government's long-running secret UFO effort, which insiders call the legacy program, over to private companies. A Pentagon whistleblower named Matthew Brown passes this on as "legacy program lore" that has since leaked out from people he has heard from. If true, it would explain why the material sits outside normal government oversight.
nnsa-officials-attend-sol-foundation-ufo: Officials from the National Nuclear Security Administration, the US agency that looks after the country's nuclear weapons, showed up at a gathering of the Sol Foundation, a Stanford group dedicated to UFO research. Michels tells this himself, as something he saw while he was there. He brings it up as a sign that people in the nuclear world are paying attention to UFOs.
nnsa-reply-to-foia-request-on-starfish-p: Someone, described by Michels as an anonymous person, used the Freedom of Information Act, a US law that lets anyone request government records, to ask the National Nuclear Security Administration, the US agency that runs the country's nuclear weapons, for every record about UFOs (and related terms like UAP, the government's newer word for them) connected to Starfish Prime, a series of US nuclear tests. Michels tells this himself across three episodes and quotes the agency's reply of June 2022: "It was determined that an additional review of your case by the subject matter expert with jurisdiction regarding responsive records was required." To him, the reply suggests such records exist, since otherwise there would be nothing for an expert to review.
no-american-flag-on-the-sport-model-1988: A craft called the sport model, kept at a secret Nevada site called S-4, is said to have carried no American flag. Bob Lazar, who says he worked there in 1988 and 1989 studying craft that did not come from Earth, says he noticed this on his very first day inside. He tells it as something he saw himself, because a missing flag would suggest the craft was not built by the US.
no-column-supports-the-craft-s-53-ft-flo: Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft in 1988 and 1989 at a secret site in Nevada called S-4, is said to have seen no column holding up the 53-foot-wide floor of one craft when he peeked into its bottom level. A researcher named Luigi Vendittelli, who spent two days with Lazar, makes the point from Lazar's account. He says there is nothing "supporting" that floor, which would point to building methods unlike ours.
no-footage-until-the-lady-allowed-filmin: From 2007 to 2012, a North Carolina man named Chris Bledsoe says he went out every night behind his house with a camera trying to film the strange lights he was seeing, and got nothing at all. He tells it as his own experience: he wanted proof to save himself from the doubts of his community, and he says footage only came once a being he calls "the Lady" allowed it to be filmed.
no-loose-nuke-nest-and-fbi-wmd-staff-sta: Whatever was happening over New Jersey in 2024, it was not a lost nuclear weapon, according to Jake Barber, a former military helicopter pilot who says he flew a UFO retrieval. He says he knows this for certain because he knows people on NEST, a federal team that searches for loose nuclear material, and staff in the FBI's weapons of mass destruction section, and they stayed home in New Jersey with their families instead of fleeing. To him that rules out a nuclear threat as the explanation.
no-physicists-on-nasa-s-follow-up-uap-st: When NASA, the US space agency, ran its own study of UAP, the government's term for UFOs, in 2023 and 2024, there were no physicists on the follow-up team, says Charles Buhler, a NASA engineer. He speaks as someone who was there: "my wife and I were approached to help with the UAP. NASA was doing their own UAP thing." His point is that a study of strange flying objects left out the very scientists best placed to explain how they might move.
no-physicists-on-the-claimed-crash-retri: The researcher Eric Weinstein asks whether two things are linked: physics has made no progress beyond its two great theories, the standard model of particles and Einstein's general relativity, and there are no physicists on the claimed secret programme to recover crashed unknown craft. He puts it as a question to a Pentagon scientist, drawing no source. If they are two sides of one coin, it would mean the secrecy around UFOs has held back physics itself.
no-real-physicists-on-the-program: The physicist Eric W. Davis says that the government UFO programme he was talking about had no real physicist on it: nobody with a doctorate in applied or theoretical physics. He tells it to suggest the people studying the material were not equipped to understand it.
no-reverse-engineering-success-after-eig: A secret effort to copy technology from recovered non-human craft, running from the 1940s on, never worked, according to a senior vice president at an American aerospace company. The Pentagon scientist Eric W. Davis says he interviewed this man for years, before and after he retired, and that the executive "confirmed that there was no success in the reverse engineering program after eight decades." In Davis's telling, the program exists but "just didn't go anywhere."
no-transient-nuclear-test-matches-after-: Old sky photographs from the Palomar Observatory in California show brief flashes of light, called transients, and some of them line up in time with nuclear bomb tests. The last such match is said to fall on 17 March 1956. The researcher Steven Bruel gives the date without naming a source, and it matters because a link to nuclear tests would hint that the flashes were tied to events on Earth.
no-writings-in-the-great-pyramid: There is no writing anywhere inside the Great Pyramid of Giza in Egypt, according to a researcher named Matt LaCroix. He says this on Michels's show without citing a source. He raises it because a monument that big with no inscriptions makes him question who built it and when.
noah-rodek-s-foia-on-project-preserve-de: An independent researcher named Noah Hradek used the Freedom of Information Act, a US law that lets anyone request government records, to ask the Air Force about Project Preserve Destiny. That is the program a former sergeant named Dan Sherman says recruited him to communicate with aliens. Michels tells this across several episodes. He says the Air Force passed the request on to the NSA, the US agency that intercepts communications, and he reads from the Air Force's reply: "Good afternoon. This letter is in final response to your 27th of July, 2023 Freedom of Information Act request." To Michels, the handoff to the NSA suggests the program is real.
non-disclosure-agreement-incident-made-c: Mario Woods, a former guard of nuclear weapons at Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota who says he was abducted by a UFO, says that in 1977, after his incident, a man named Jack Reed walked over and handed another piece of paper across as Woods's own paper was being set down: a non-disclosure agreement, a pledge to keep quiet. Woods says the whole incident was then made classified, and also names a Colonel Spraker as part of the scene. He tells it as something he went through himself, as evidence that the Air Force wanted the event kept secret.
non-human-biologics-recovered-with-crash: Some people claim that a secret US program has recovered crashed craft that are not of human make, and that bodies or other biological remains, called "biologics", came with some of them. David Grusch, who has gone public about these programs, says it most strongly, repeating what he says he was told by people "with direct knowledge" who are still in the program. In a clip from his testimony to Congress, he says those remains were judged to be non-human. He adds that he already said so in a TV interview with the news channel NewsNation. Jake Barber, a helicopter pilot who says he carried a recovered UFO, says there are "reports that we do have biologics in storage and we just don't know what that is." The UFO reporter Jeremy Corbell says he has heard the same, "mostly autopsy reports." Neither Barber nor Corbell ties the remains to a particular crash. If true, it would mean the government holds the bodies of whoever flew these craft.
non-human-biologics-stored-at-institutio: Biological remains that are not human are said to be kept at various institutions. A guest named Brigham Buhler tells this second-hand, saying he heard it in a documentary but does not remember which one or who said it.
non-operational-emp-testing-at-samso-and: Tests are said to have been run on the same kind of nuclear missile equipment Robert Salas worked with, using EMP, a sudden burst of electromagnetic energy, but at test sites rather than live bases: the Space and Missile Systems Organization, an Air Force unit in San Bernardino, and Hill Air Force Base in Utah. Salas, a former Air Force officer, summarises this from a book called The Faded Giant by a writer he names as James Clattz. It bears on whether such a burst, and not something unknown, could explain missiles shutting down.
non-verbal-amazon-tribes-and-their-ancie: There are tribes in the Amazon rainforest who don't speak, and who send information to each other by telepathy, meaning mind to mind, using what they call "the ancient language." Michels tells this himself without naming a source, first on an episode about a documentary on children said to read minds, where he says the tribes "apparently" exist, and later as plain fact. He brings it up as a sign that telepathy might be a real, older way for people to communicate.
nordic-alien-on-orcas-island: A man says he once met a tall, fair being, the kind UFO lore calls a "Nordic alien," on Orcas Island in Washington State. He is Brent Friedman, a Hollywood writer and one of the creators of the UFO television series Dark Skies, and he tells Michels he saw it himself. He says it happened on a friend's 20-acre property: suddenly a figure was there who looked "like a Scandinavian male model," and it spoke to him without moving its mouth, which would mean a human-looking visitor that talks mind to mind.
nordics-from-mars-caused-the-extinction-: One idea holds that the Nordics, tall human-looking beings, came here from Mars and "were responsible for the extinction of the dinosaurs." The philosopher Jason Jorjani lays out this theory, drawing on a work called Closer Encounters. If true, it would mean human-looking beings were on Earth long before people.
norseen-report-under-nasa-weather-contra: Researcher John Norseen's report on a brain-computer link for pilot cockpits was paid for under a government contract numbered N66001, a contract this story connects to NASA weather work run through a Navy systems center in San Diego. Michels says this himself, based on Norseen's own citation of the report. He brings it up to show that the mind-control research was hidden under an unrelated contract.
norseen-s-not-heard-nor-seen-email-and-d: In the early 2000s John Norseen, a defense researcher linked to the Naval War College in Newport, sent an email signed "John not heard nor seen." About two weeks later, the story goes, he was found dead in a motel room, possibly in Tennessee. A man named Jim Weiner, who tells of his own alien abduction, says he was in contact with Norseen. He tells it across two episodes and credits a man named Ed. Told this way, the timing makes the death look like more than chance.
norsine-at-allagash-in-august-1976-runni: A man named John Norsine claims he was at the Allagash Waterway in Maine in August 1976 running what he called a "TTR," a "tag trace retrieve exercise with a subcutaneous device": a tracking chip placed under the skin. Charlie Foltz, a witness to the strange events at the Allagash that summer, repeats what Norsine told him. If true, part of what happened there would have been a human operation.
norsine-denies-a-government-cover-story-: A man named John Norsine, linked to an alien abduction case in Newport, Rhode Island, flatly denied that the abduction was a government cover story. Jim Weiner, who tells the abduction story, says he put the question to Norsine, who simply said "No," and Weiner says Norsine believed what he said. This matters to Weiner because it counts against the idea that the event was staged by the government.
norsine-s-bioenergetics-work-with-duncan: A man named John Norsine is said to have worked with a man named Duncan Laurie in Jamestown, Rhode Island, on bioenergetics, the study of energy in living things. A witness named Jim Weiner mentions it second-hand, from what he was told, and in the moment he only gets as far as saying John was working with him on it, so what they actually did goes unsaid.
north-american-indian-legends-of-six-fin: Native American peoples had legends of red-haired giants with six fingers, according to a researcher named Tim Alberino. He says this twice in one episode without naming a source, and the second time he leaves out the six fingers. He brings it up as support for his claim that giants once lived, and that one was even captured in Afghanistan.
north-sea-oil-rig-engineer-sighting-in-j: In 1989 an engineer on a North Sea oil rig named Chris Gibson is said to have looked up and seen a black, dart-like, arrow-shaped craft. The journalist Nick Cook tells it as a story he ran in Jane's Defence Weekly, a military trade magazine, and credits an aviation writer named Bill Sweetman with the account. If true, it would point to a secret aircraft flying over the North Sea at the time.
north-sentinel-island-analogy-for-hidden: India looks after North Sentinel Island, a small island in the Indian Ocean, but never lands there, so the people living on it would have no sign of the outside world that knows all about them. The mathematician Eric Weinstein offers this as his own comparison: the islanders would face their own Fermi paradox, the puzzle of why, if others are out there, we see no sign of them. He uses it to suggest that non-human beings could be watching Earth while choosing to stay away.
northcom-jellyfish-uap-crosses-us-mexico: A jellyfish-shaped unidentified object is said to have crossed the US-Mexico border, in a case logged by NORTHCOM, the US military command that defends North America. Michels raises it himself in an episode with a Pentagon whistleblower named Matthew Brown, crediting a report he calls Immaculate Constellation.
northern-lights-seen-as-far-south-as-lon: In 2024 the northern lights, the glowing night sky usually seen only near the poles, were seen as far south as London. The scientist Rupert Sheldrake mentions it from what others told him, adding that he did not see them himself "cuz it was cloudy."
northern-sweden-police-investigator-of-t: During the 1940s wave of ghost rockets, strange rocket-like objects reported in the skies over Sweden, a policeman far up in northern Sweden is said to have looked into the sightings. The Swedish UFO researcher Clas Svahn mentions him only briefly and gives no name or details. He brings it up as one of the early official efforts to look into the sightings.
northrop-grumman-area-51-arv-story-calle: An unnamed insider called it "all myth" that the defense company Northrop Grumman, or anyone at Area 51, the secret Air Force test site in Nevada, has an ARV, meaning a human-built copy of an alien craft. The Pentagon scientist Eric W. Davis says he asked the man directly and got that answer. It bears on stories like that of Bob Lazar, a man who has claimed he worked on alien craft near Area 51.
northrop-grumman-s-corporate-security-as: Northrop Grumman, a large American defence contractor, seems to have been given the authority some time ago to enforce the secrecy of classified programmes through its own corporate security guards. This comes from Matthew Brown, a Pentagon whistleblower who speaks as someone who saw it from the inside, in his interview with Jesse Michels. If true, it would mean a private company, not the government, is policing who learns what about some secret programmes.
northrop-paper-vanishes-b-2-electrostati: A 1968 paper by the American aircraft maker Northrop on using electric charge to help planes fly is said to have later vanished from an aeronautics journal, and the idea is said to live on in the wings of the B-2 stealth bomber. Michels tells this from the work of the writer Nick Cook and his book The Hunt for Zero Point, saying a researcher named Dan Marcas went looking for the paper and "found that it had totally vanished." Cook himself, on the show, recalls such papers but places them in the early 1960s and is unsure of the date, linking them to the electric-propulsion work of a scientist named Thomas Townsend Brown.
northwest-airlines-pilot-s-telepathic-en: A former airline pilot, who James Fox thinks flew for Northwest Airlines, is said to have had an encounter in Arizona in which something reached him by telepathy, meaning mind to mind without spoken words. The UFO investigator James Fox tells it from his own interview with the pilot, though he gives no date or details of what passed between them. If true, it would mean a trained aviator says he was contacted directly by whatever he met.
norwegian-farmer-sees-a-craft-hovering-b: A farmer in Norway is said to have seen a craft hovering right around his house. Michels tells this himself, as something the farmer told him when they talked on a trip to Norway, and he gives no more detail.
norwegians-with-24-teeth-want-to-build-c: A group of beings he calls the Norwegians, who have 24 teeth, could only repair their craft once they reached Earth, at least in 1965, and they wanted to work with the American government to build craft here. Charles Hall, a whistleblower who says he spent three years with tall white aliens at Area 51, the secret US Air Force base in Nevada, tells this as something he learned firsthand. If true, it would mean an alien group sought a joint building programme with the United States.
nova-scotia-navy-divers-see-occupants-be: In 1960, off Nova Scotia in Canada, Navy divers are said to have seen the occupants of two flying saucers standing outside their craft on the seabed, and even to have filmed them, during an operation the tellers call Sweep Clear Five. A retired US Navy admiral named Tim Gallaudet passes this on from the researchers Chris Styles and Brian Fitzpatrick, who looked into the case. If true, it would mean military divers met visitors face to face under the ocean.
november-1975-helicopter-near-miss-with-: On November 7, 1975, a helicopter pilot near the border between Sweden and Norway nearly collided with a "ghost rocket", the Swedish name for unexplained rocket-like objects in the sky, according to Clas Svahn, a Swedish UFO researcher. Svahn relays what the pilot told him: he was flying 20 metres over the treetops, on a moonlit night, over snow. Svahn says he has been hunting the files of a joint military, customs and police operation from that period, which were sealed until 2040, and that he "just the other day got the clearance" to have them released.
nrl-s-1952-appraisal-of-brown-s-device-m: A 1952 assessment of the experiments of Thomas Townsend Brown, an inventor who worked on devices meant to fly by electrical forces, has gone missing from the Naval Research Laboratory, the US Navy's science lab, which did the study. Michels says that Tom Valone of the Integrity Research Institute went looking for the paper, titled "TT Brown electrogravity device", and was told the lab no longer had it. He tells it as a sign that Navy interest in Brown's work was hidden away.
nro-corona-satellites-immediately-imagin: As soon as America's spy satellites went up under President Eisenhower, they started picking up lots of pictures and signals of UFOs. That is the theory offered by an online researcher who goes by UAPGerb. He says it began once the National Reconnaissance Office, the US agency that runs spy satellites, took over Corona, the first US photo-spy satellite program, and the later Keyhole satellites. He presents it as "a theory that could be constructed", not a documented fact, but if true it would mean the government has had orbital evidence of UFOs since the late 1950s.
nro-founded-for-reconnaissance-in-denied: The National Reconnaissance Office, the American agency that runs the country's spy satellites, was set up to gather intelligence over "denied airspaces", meaning Soviet territory where American planes could not fly openly, according to a researcher who goes by the name UAPGerb. He gives the reason in his own summary, naming no source: the US knew a nuclear war with the Soviets "would lead to mutually assured destruction," so it needed to see inside the Soviet Union without fighting. He tells it to Michels while explaining how he thinks the Pentagon's UFO work is organised.
nro-neutrino-detectors-used-to-target-an: The National Reconnaissance Office, the US agency that runs spy satellites, is said to have fitted satellites with detectors for neutrinos, tiny particles that pass through almost anything, so it could pick up the signature of alien spacecraft and "knock them down." This comes from the UFO disclosure campaigner Steven Greer, who tells it on Michels's show as something only insiders knew, without naming his source, and if true it would mean the government has been secretly shooting down visiting craft.
nro-nga-senate-and-gao-audit-over-carryo: In 1994 and 1995, two US spy agencies were investigated by the Senate and by the Government Accountability Office, the auditing office of Congress, over roughly 3.2 billion dollars in misused "carryover funds", money left over from one year and carried into the next. The agencies are the National Reconnaissance Office, which runs spy satellites, and the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency, which handles maps and imagery. A researcher who goes by the name UAPGerb tells this to Michels without naming a source, in a talk about how a hidden UFO program might be paid for, and cites the former intelligence official David Grusch.
nro-program-b-ground-element-at-pine-gap: In the 1980s, a secret branch of the National Reconnaissance Office, the US agency that runs spy satellites, is said to have set up its ground station at Pine Gap, a remote listening base in the Australian outback. The researcher who goes by UAPGerb says this on the show: "the ground element of NRO program B was established at Pine Gap, Australia." He names a figure called R. Evans Heinman alongside the claim, and if it were true it would place this hidden unit's work on Australian soil.
nro-sentient-program-integrated-with-imm: A program called Sentient at the National Reconnaissance Office, the US agency that runs spy satellites, is said to have been joined up with Immaculate Constellation, which he describes as a secret effort to gather UFO data. Matthew Brown, a former Pentagon official turned whistleblower, says that to his understanding Sentient came online after Immaculate Constellation already existed and was then integrated with it. If true, it would tie the satellite agency's systems to hidden UFO tracking.
nrol-16-on-walpurgisnacht-matching-a-nec: A secret US spy satellite launch called NROL-16 went up at 12:50 a.m. on April 30, 2005, which Michels says is the same day as Walpurgisnacht, a European night traditionally linked to witches. Michels tells it himself, citing a former intelligence officer named John Ramirez, and ties the date to a ritual in the Necronomicon, a book of occult spells, as a sign that the space program has a hidden ritual side.
nsa-certificate-for-ea280-electronics-in: Michels shows a certificate he says the National Security Agency, the US spy agency for intercepted signals, gave to an Air Force sergeant named Dan Sherman for completing its EA280 intermediate electronics intelligence collection and analysis course. Michels presents the document himself as proof of Sherman's training, in an episode where Sherman says the agency hired him to communicate with aliens.
nsa-glomar-response-cites-executive-orde: In 2023 the NSA, the US agency that intercepts communications, answered a researcher's records request about UFOs by refusing to say whether any records even exist, a kind of reply known as a Glomar response. Jesse Michels reads it on the show: the request was filed by a researcher named Noah Hradek under the US law that lets anyone ask for government records, and the reply cites Executive Order 13526, a presidential order on classified information, saying that "the fact of the existence or non-existence of the material you request is a currently improperly classified matter." Michels raises it as a sign the agency is guarding something on the subject.
nsa-may-have-tracked-sherman-since-child: A former Air Force sergeant named Dan Sherman, who says the NSA, the US agency that intercepts and handles signals and communications, hired him to communicate with aliens, believes the agency may have been watching him long before that. As Michels puts it, narrating Sherman's view, "the NSA may even have tracked him since childhood into his young adulthood and military service." If true, it would mean Sherman was picked out for the work years in advance.
nsa-personnel-attend-ramsay-lecture: People from the National Security Agency, the US spy agency that listens in on communications, are said to have turned up at a public lecture in Baltimore, Maryland. Scott Ramsey, a researcher who studies a reported UFO crash said to have left alien bodies, tells Michels this happened at one of his own talks, saying "we similarly had something like that happen in Baltimore too." He gives it as a sign that intelligence agencies keep an eye on his work.
nsa-purges-borland-s-jwics-document-data: In 2024, Dylan Borland says, he had a large saved collection of documents, briefings and private messages on JWICS, a classified US intelligence computer network, and the National Security Agency, the US electronic intelligence agency, wiped it. Borland tells Michels this as something that happened to him. He tells it as a sign that someone was working to remove material he had collected.
nsa-source-at-collusion-meetings-with-a-: A man working for the NSA, the US agency that intercepts communications, sat in meetings with senior executives of a major tech and telecommunications company where, in effect, the two sides were colluding. Steven Greer, a UFO researcher and activist, says this man is his source and relays what he was told. Greer offers it as a sign that government secrecy reaches into private industry.
nsa-treat-men-in-black-unit: The NSA, the US agency that intercepts communications, supposedly had a "men in black" unit, a team that quietly deals with UFO witnesses and evidence, called the Tactical Reconnaissance Engineering Assessment Search Team, created by a man named Albert Stubblebine. An online UFO researcher who goes by UAPGerb tells this, drawing on emails from what he calls the DPI archive and on names such as Edgar Fouche and Hans-Adam II. If true, it would mean a real government team exists to handle UFO matters out of sight.
nsa-utah-data-center-code-named-bumblehi: Around 2005 the National Security Agency, the US agency that intercepts communications, built what was then the largest single data center in Utah, and its now declassified code name was Bumblehive. A researcher named Matthew Pines tells this, without naming a source, as a code name he finds interesting.
nsc-study-on-disclosure-of-recovered-cra: There was reportedly a study, ordered by the National Security Council, the White House's top security advisers, under President George W. Bush, asking whether the time had come for "disclosure" of recovered craft. The former Senate staffer Kirk McConnell relays it, citing Sean Kirkpatrick, who once led the Pentagon office for unexplained aerial reports, and linking the study to a Pentagon think tank called the Office of Net Assessment. If true, it would mean the White House seriously weighed telling the public about such craft.
nsf-and-nasa-co-sponsor-extended-electro: The National Science Foundation, the US government agency that funds science, and NASA co-sponsored a podcast in which highly credentialed scientists and engineers said they were looking into extended electrodynamics, an idea for stretching the standard theory of electricity and magnetism. Michels tells this himself without naming the podcast, as a sign that mainstream science is now taking up ideas from the fringe.
nsf-gulfstream-v-surveys-over-the-triang: The owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property known for strange reports, says that a $50 million Gulfstream V jet belonging to the National Science Foundation, the US government's science funding agency, flew over a part of the ranch called the triangle. The owner tells this as a witness, speaking to Jesse Michels, and offers it as a sign of how seriously the place is being studied.
nttr-retrieval-insider-describes-a-crack: A member of a crash retrieval team, a group said to recover downed craft, reportedly described a cracked egg-shaped craft on the Nevada Test and Training Range, a huge military range in Nevada, whose skin was made of layers "like a Russian nesting doll." A guest who goes by UAPGerb passes this on from the unnamed team member. In a second telling he leaves out the layers and adds that the egg had a crew of grays, the small grey-skinned beings of many abduction stories.
nuclear-assets-of-the-29th-guards-missil: Near the Siberian city of Irkutsk in Russia sits the 29th Guards Missile Division, which Michels says is and long has been a live force of nuclear-armed intercontinental ballistic missiles, the long-range kind, carried on mobile launchers. He states it as known fact, drawing on someone named Stephen Pearson, in an episode about strange three-fingered bodies from Peru, to point out that the place in question sits beside serious nuclear weapons.
nuclear-posture-review-and-the-motive-to: The military is said to have had a reason to discredit people who saw UFOs near nuclear weapons, because its own policy treats those weapons as everything. Robert Salas, a former Air Force officer, makes this case from the Nuclear Posture Review, a Pentagon document that sets out US nuclear policy, quoting it as saying "nuclear deterrence is the backbone the basis of our national security." In his view, anything that made the weapons look vulnerable would be pushed down.
nuclear-powered-airplane-in-an-idaho-fal: An airplane powered by nuclear energy sits in a hangar in Idaho Falls, Idaho, according to John S. Herrington, a former US Secretary of Energy. He puts it to Michels as a question, "Jesse, this goes back decades. If I told you there is an airplane powered by nuclear power sitting in a hanger in Idaho Falls, would you believe me?", and when he repeats it he credits the aviator and industrialist Howard Hughes. He raises it to show that the government has long held technology the public would find hard to believe.
nuclear-silo-shutdowns-and-anti-nuclear-: UFOs are said to have shut down nuclear missiles in their underground launch sites, and people who report contact often describe being warned that humanity will destroy itself in a nuclear war. Michels raises this in a conversation with a Navy scientist named Salvatore Pais, drawing on the work of a researcher named Robert Hastings, and he offers it as a sign that whatever is behind the phenomenon is especially concerned with nuclear weapons.
nuclear-systems-kept-archaic-so-they-can: America's nuclear weapons systems are deliberately kept on old, outdated technology because old systems are harder to hack, according to Michael Herrera, a man who says he saw a huge UFO in the Indonesian jungle. Herrera says he learned this personally, around 2017, and links it to NORAD, the US and Canadian command that watches North American airspace, and to secret military sites. If true, it would mean the oldest-looking parts of the nuclear system are old on purpose, as a defence.
nuclear-test-sites-with-marines-dug-in-n: In the 1950s, at the Nevada Test Site where the US exploded nuclear bombs, the military is said to have set off blasts with Marines dug in "right next to where the explosions were going off." Randy Anderson, a guest who says he saw alien technology at a military base, tells this himself. He offers it as an example of how far the military would go in testing on its own people.
nuclear-weapons-aboard-the-nimitz-group-: In 2004, when Navy pilots with the Nimitz carrier strike group, a fleet built around the aircraft carrier USS Nimitz, reported a strange object off California, the ships likely had tactical nuclear weapons on board, Michels says. He tells this himself, linking it to the work of the researcher Robert Hastings and his book UFOs and Nukes, which argues UFOs show special interest in nuclear weapons, and if true that interest would explain why the object appeared there.
nukes-used-to-bring-down-ufos: The military has used nuclear weapons to bring UFOs down, according to the musician Tom DeLonge. The claim comes second-hand from a researcher who goes by the online name RedPandaKoala, who mentions it on the show as something DeLonge has said. If true, it would mean there have been armed clashes with these craft that the public never heard about.
number-137-in-the-proportions-of-the-sec: The number 137, which the physicists Richard Feynman and Leon Lederman wrote about as a puzzling constant of nature, also turns up in the proportions of the second pyramid at Giza, the one built for the pharaoh Khafre. So says a researcher named Armando Mei, who tells Michels that the listener "surely haven't failed to notice the correspondence." He offers it as his own reading, without naming a source, and the point would be that the pyramid's builders knew something of the physics behind that number.
numbers-spoken-from-television-sets-1960: In the 1960s in the United States, some people said they heard numbers being spoken straight at them out of their television sets. The philosopher Jason Jorjani brings this up on the show without naming a source, and says these cases were reported by the writer John Keel, who collected strange encounters from that period. Told this way, it suggests something odd was trying to reach people through their own household devices.
nuraghe-towers-buried-as-if-by-a-tidal-w: The nuraghe, ancient stone towers on the island of Sardinia, were at some point buried all at once, according to a researcher named Tim Alberino. He says they "were suddenly covered in earth, almost like a tidal wave had swept across the island," and he gives no source or date for it. If true, it would point to a sudden disaster that swept over the whole island.
nuro-finding-things-on-the-seafloor: A little-known secret US office that works on the ocean floor, called NURO, is said to be finding things down there. When Michels puts it to John S. Herrington, a former US Secretary of Energy, that "it seems like they might be finding things on the seafloor," Herrington answers: "Yep. They are." He gives no details, but the brief confirmation hints that unexplained objects may be turning up under the sea.
nurse-says-she-was-there-1996: In 1996, in the Brazilian town of Varginha, where many people say a strange creature was caught and taken to hospital, a nurse is said to have told interviewers she knew what happened because she was there herself. James Fox, who was interviewing witnesses there, tells it: when they asked how she knew, she was shaking, and she said, "Cuz I was there." If true, she would be a direct witness from inside the hospital.
nurse-says-the-wright-patterson-craft-ca: A nurse is said to have claimed that a crashed craft held at Wright Patterson, an Air Force base in Dayton, Ohio, came from Aztec, a town in New Mexico where a saucer is said to have come down. Scott Ramsey, who researches the Aztec crash, repeats what the nurse said, and says this is how they "found out it came from Aztec." If true, it would link the Aztec crash to the military.
nurse-speaks-for-first-time-in-virginia: A nurse at a hospital in Virginia, who had worked under a surgeon named Amar, spoke for the first time about a non-human "being" said to have been treated there. Michels raises it himself while interviewing the surgeon, saying "for the first time, she started to speak about this being." If true, it would back up the surgeon's account that his hospital operated on an alien.
nurses-and-radiology-technician-also-wit: In 1996 at the Regional Hospital in Varginha, Brazil, where a strange being is said to have been brought in, nurses and a radiology technician are said to have seen something too, the technician describing a closed box. The surgeon Italo Venturelli tells this from what those staff said, telling Michels "many people say they saw it." It is one of many accounts claiming a non-human creature was taken to that hospital.
o-reilly-brown-inventions-handed-to-cons: A few of the inventions of a scientist named Townsend Brown are said to have been handed to other groups, with a consortium, a group of companies working together, seemingly involved. Michels relays this from a person named O'Reilly, alongside a writer named Paul Schatzkin, in his documentary on Brown. If true, it would mean Brown's work went on in private hands.
oak-ridge-magnesium-bismuth-technical-do: In the 1950s, Oak Ridge, a US government nuclear research laboratory in Tennessee, is said to have produced a technical document that talks about the metals magnesium and bismuth. Michels tells this himself, without naming the document, while talking about government records on UFOs. He raises it because, if true, it would suggest the laboratory was studying the same metals linked to UFO stories.
oak-ridge-visit-arranged-by-howard-baker: Sometime between the 1970s and the 1980s, a senior government adviser says he was sent to spend time at Oak Ridge, the US government nuclear research laboratory in Tennessee, on a visit arranged through Howard Baker, a senator from Tennessee. The adviser is Harald Malmgren, who worked as an adviser to presidents and says he handled UFO material directly, and he tells Michels he went himself: "I went to go up to Oak Ridge and spend some time with them." He brings it up as part of how he came close to the government's handling of unexplained material.
obama-administration-s-ufo-answers-then-: Around 2012, the administration of US President Barack Obama was asked whether the government investigates UFOs and gave no real answer, though Obama himself later spoke about UFOs on a late-night TV show. The story comes from an online researcher who goes by RedPandaKoala, speaking on Michels's show from memory. He says the question "was just kind of like left off," a sign of how the government once dodged the subject.
obama-at-a-campfire-tells-eddie-vedder-t: Former President Barack Obama, drunk around a campfire, is said to have told Eddie Vedder, lead singer of the band Pearl Jam, who asked what was really going on, to "read the three-body problem," a science fiction novel about alien contact. Michels tells this twice, once as something Vedder passed on and once in his own narration. If true, it would hint that a president knew more about aliens than he could say.
obama-on-james-corden-about-unidentified: In 2021 the former US president Barack Obama said on television that there are objects in the sky that nobody can identify. Michels recalls him saying it on the talk show of the TV host James Corden, and in another episode Obama's own words are played: "There's footage and records of objects in the skies that we don't know exactly what they are." Coming from a former president, it is told as a sign that the question is taken seriously at the very top.
obama-on-jimmy-kimmel-says-the-aliens-wo: Former US president Barack Obama, appearing on Jimmy Kimmel's late-night TV talk show, joked that "the aliens won't let it happen" when asked about revealing what the government knows about UFOs. The comedian Kurt Metzger brings it up from memory, saying Obama did it "with a smile but what are you really saying." He reads the joke as a hint that something real lay behind it.
obama-s-area-51-remark-later-walked-back: In 2026, the story goes, the former US president Barack Obama said something about Area 51, a secret military base in Nevada, and alien beings kept underground there, and then took it back. Michels mentions it himself in passing, without a source, and says Obama sort of walked his statement back. Bryce Zabel, a guest talking about Hollywood's ties to the CIA, also tells it without naming a source. He says Obama had to take the remark back the very next day, and that Donald Trump, the sitting president, took the bait.
obama-s-betty-and-barney-hill-documentar: Former president Barack Obama is said to have a quiet interest in UFOs. Jesse Michels points to two things: Obama's production company taking on a project about Betty and Barney Hill, a couple who said they were abducted in 1961 in what Michels calls the first such case in the US, and Obama visiting the set of Disclosure Day, the director Steven Spielberg's UFO film. Michels tells this himself across several episodes. He calls the project sometimes a documentary and sometimes a movie, and says sometimes that Obama is making it and sometimes only that he thought about it. In one episode he calls it "predictive programming," the idea that films prepare the public for things to come. In another he cites Spielberg speaking openly on Michelle Obama's podcast. Brent Friedman, a television writer, recalls the Obamas announcing a Betty and Barney movie that was later dropped, and notes that he had put a scene about the Hills in the pilot of Dark Skies, a 1990s TV series. Michels raises it as a sign that Obama may know more than he says.
obama-says-on-a-podcast-that-aliens-are-: Former US president Barack Obama is said to have answered a podcast host's question about aliens by saying, "Yeah, I think aliens are real." In a clip shown on the show, Obama adds that he hasn't seen them and that they are not being kept at Area 51, the secret Air Force base in Nevada. The skeptic writer Michael Shermer says this remark set off a release of government UFO files, while Michels frames it as Obama provoking Donald Trump.
obama-shuts-down-a-putin-back-channel-th: In 2009, the Russian leader Vladimir Putin is said to have tried to set up a private diplomatic channel through Harald Malmgren, a former adviser to American presidents, and President Barack Obama is said to have shut the idea down. Michels tells it as something he and Malmgren had talked about off camera. It suggests Malmgren was trusted at the highest levels long after leaving office.
obamatrump-exchange-over-ufos-2026: Aldo Rebelo, a former defence minister of Brazil, tells Michels that the UFO question became controversial again recently because of what he calls "a dialogue, let's call it a dialogue," between former US President Barack Obama and President Donald Trump. He brings it up as a sign that the subject has reached the highest level of American politics, though he gives no details of what the two men said.
oberth-and-von-braun-s-neopagan-rituals-: In Nazi Germany's rocket and space programme of the 1930s and 40s, says Michels, the rocket pioneer Hermann Oberth went through strange neo-pagan rituals, meaning revived pre-Christian religious ceremonies. Oberth was the mentor of the rocket engineer Wernher von Braun. Michels tells this on three episodes without naming a source. In two of them he names only von Braun as the one going through the rituals, and once adds that von Braun was believed to be a Freemason, a member of a secretive fraternal order. He raises it to suggest that the early space age had an occult side.
object-abroad-too-large-to-move: Somewhere outside the United States there is an object so large that it cannot be moved, according to Congressman Eric Burlison. He says this is what he has been told, framing it as "reportedly" and naming no source or place. If true, it would mean a crashed or buried craft is too big to be taken away and is being kept where it lies.
object-appears-beside-the-atlas-8f-reent: In 1962, during a missile test from Cape Canaveral in Florida, an unknown object is said to have appeared next to a reentry vehicle, the part of a missile that falls back through the atmosphere, as it flew. Michels describes test footage in which, at the 4 minute 40 second mark, an object "appears to phase itself into existence" alongside the vehicle while it travels at 20,000 feet per second, about eighteen times the speed of sound, and he credits a postflight report by the US Air Force and NASA, the US space agency. A former Senate staffer named Kurt McConnell tells the same story, naming the vehicle as the Mark V built by a company called AVCO and dating the test to September 19, 1962. McConnell says the official report to the Defense Department states that "objects of unknown origin and identity were tracking or pacing" the vehicle, and he points to declassified test video. The two tellers differ on the name of the vehicle but agree on what was seen. If true, it would mean something kept pace with one of the fastest objects humans could launch at the time.
object-came-out-of-the-water-and-zapped-: In 2024, one of the unexplained objects is said to have come up out of the water and "zapped" or hit a person. A guest named Matthew Pines says he heard this at a meeting with unnamed people in the intelligence side of the US Department of Defense. He tells it twice, once saying "zapped" and once only "hit", and if true it would mean these objects can harm people.
object-inside-the-mesa-at-skinwalker-ran: Something large and metallic is said to be buried deep inside a mesa, a flat-topped hill, at Skinwalker Ranch, a property in Utah known for strange reports. Michels tells it on two episodes. In one, he says a scientific team used soil resistivity and ground-penetrating radar, both ways of looking underground without digging, and found a big metal object about 400 feet below the mesa, crediting the work to people named Aaron Blunt and Ravi Chandran. In another, he says such objects have been located but are hard to pull out, "like they have a life of their own," and points to Secrets of Skinwalker Ranch, a television series about the property. The ranch's owner, speaking firsthand on an episode where he breaks his silence, tells it differently. He says engineered, manufactured material has in fact been extracted "from hundreds of feet within the mesa." If it were true, it would mean something made by someone was placed deep underground long ago.
object-shot-down-over-alaska-said-to-hav: An object shot down over Alaska in 2023 put itself back together and was seen flying over Canada, according to things Michels says he heard. Michels tells this himself as hearsay, without naming who told him. If true, it would mean the object was no ordinary balloon or drone.
objects-on-radar-and-seen-by-airmen-over: In 1967, objects showed up on radar at Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana, a base for nuclear missiles, and airmen at the base saw them with their own eyes. Robert Salas, a former Air Force officer who served there, tells it as reports that came in at the time, citing an officer named Lewis Chase. He raises it because it would mean the unknown objects were watched closely around America's nuclear weapons.
objects-over-ellsworth-runway-weapons-st: Between about 1957 and 1959, unknown objects are said to have come down the runway at Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota and over its weapons storage area and its B-52 alert pad, where nuclear bombers stood ready. Mario Woods, an Air Force veteran, says he heard about "four or five other cases" like this, at the base and out in the missile fields. If true, these objects were taking an interest in American nuclear forces.
occult-history-in-nasa-and-launch-pad-ch: NASA, the US space agency, is said to have a lot of hidden occult history, with some mission names and the choice of launch pad 33 picked on purpose for symbolic reasons. An unnamed guest says this on an episode featuring a guest known as RedPandaKoala, calling those choices "very deliberate."
occult-minded-nazis-brought-in-through-p: After the Second World War, Germans with an interest in the occult were brought to the United States through Operation Paperclip and Operation Overcast, US programmes that recruited German scientists from 1945, and they went on to run the American space programme. That is what a researcher named Chris Ramsay says on the show, summing it up without naming a source. If true, it would mean the US space effort was shaped from the start by men with Nazi pasts and mystical beliefs.
ocean-shells-on-the-eridu-ziggurat-summi: Ocean shells still lie on top of the ziggurat, a stepped temple tower, at Eridu, an ancient city in southern Iraq, according to a researcher named Matt LaCroix, who says he identified them himself. He tells Michels the shells point to a flood coming in from the sea, out of the Persian Gulf, and he raises it while arguing that something huge happened to the world around 12,000 BC.
oceanographer-says-the-objects-are-under: In 2025 an unnamed oceanographer, a scientist who studies the sea, is said to have revealed that the unexplained objects come from under the sea or under the ground, and belong to neither China nor the United States. A former presidential advisor named Harald Malmgren passes this on as something revealed in the days before the interview. If true, it would put the objects' origin on Earth, but not with any known country.
odlum-investment-guidance-technologies-s: An inventor named Townsend Brown, who worked on using electric fields to lift or push aircraft, suddenly shut down his company, Guidance Technologies, in the fall of 1967 without explaining why, saying only that he got no results. Michels tells this himself, adding that just three months later the aircraft maker Northrop, which he ties to the financier Floyd Odlum, wrote a 1968 paper saying it was investing in that same kind of research. In one telling he also points to a report in the magazine Aviation Week about the B-2 stealth bomber. He tells it to suggest that Brown's work did not end but went secret.
odlum-s-open-ended-payments-to-the-brown: In the 1960s, a wealthy businessman named Floyd Odlum pressed her family into signing an open-ended contract with her father, according to Linda Brown, who tells it as someone who lived through it. She speaks on Jesse Michels's episode with the writer Nick Cook about antigravity craft, and says Odlum "did force" the signing. The point of the story is that a powerful backer kept her father's work tied to him with no end date.
odni-claim-that-dylan-borland-drew-a-sen: Word came from the Office of the Director of National Intelligence, the office that oversees US spy agencies, that a UFO whistleblower named Dylan Borland had drawn a fourth drawing, of a sensor system. The filmmaker Jeremy Corbell says he heard this straight from that office. Borland himself tells it differently, saying the drawing was faked, tied to a report by the Pentagon's UFO office, and that he has text messages to prove it.
odni-duplicated-borland-s-phone-2025: Dylan Borland, a man who has come forward to speak about secret government UFO programmes, says that in 2025 the Office of the Director of National Intelligence, the office that oversees America's spy agencies, copied his phone. He tells it himself: "I know I'm tapped. I mean they duplicated my phone." If true, it would mean he was being watched by his own government around the time of the congressional hearings on UFOs.
odni-interested-in-how-borland-tracked-s: Investigators at the office that oversees all US spy agencies, and at that office's internal watchdog, wanted to know how he tracked search-and-rescue missions, says Dylan Borland, a former intelligence analyst, about events from 2023 to 2025. He says he could read the satellite pictures and intercepted signals behind such a mission: "I know a search and rescue tasker with imagery and sigint when I see it and I know what is our guys and what isn't." He tells it because, as he presents it, some of those rescues were not for our own aircraft.
odni-nine-month-operation-against-whistl: The Office of the Director of National Intelligence, the US office that oversees all the spy agencies, is said to have run a nine-month operation aimed at UFO whistleblowers and journalists around 2025 and 2026. Jeremy Corbell, who reports on UFOs and tells it as something he knows first-hand, says flatly to Michels, "ODNI ran an operation for 9 months." He ties it to the journalist George Knapp, the whistleblowers Dylan Borland and Matthew Brown, the intelligence chief Tulsi Gabbard and a group he calls the Directors Initiative Group, and tells it as proof that the government watched the people pushing for UFO disclosure.
odni-tells-corbell-that-borland-told-the: Dylan Borland, a former intelligence official, is said to have told the Inspector General of the Intelligence Community, a watchdog Corbell calls "the police of the intelligence agencies," that a secret UFO program exists and is "called Rubik's Cube." The filmmaker Jeremy Corbell says he heard this in the 2020s from someone at the Office of the Director of National Intelligence, which oversees America's spy agencies, and once describes that person as a lead of the office's "Director's Initiative" group. He tells it twice, naming the program in one telling and the group lead's role in the other.
odyssey-systems-data-management-platform: Around 2008 to 2010, some of the computer systems a secret programme used to manage its data came from Odyssey Systems, a defence contracting firm, with MITRE, a government research contractor, also named. Jordan Jose, who says he was taken into a UFO programme as a child, tells this to Jesse Michels as something he saw himself. He offers it as a concrete detail of how the programme ran day to day.
oechsler-on-the-news-inman-convinced-him: A UFO researcher named Bob Oechsler said in a news clip that a retired Navy admiral named Bobby Ray Inman had convinced him that certain craft were not built with human technology. Oechsler's words, shown on the show, were that Inman "convinced me that uh these vehicles were uh not manufactured by human technology," which for him was "pretty conclusive." He is repeating what he says Inman told him sometime between 1989 and 1999, and if true it would mean a senior military figure privately confirmed non-human craft.
oedipus-fulfills-the-prophecy-by-fleeing: In the old Greek story, a prophecy says that a young prince of Thebes will grow up to kill his father and marry his mother, and in running from that fate he makes it come true. The writer Eric Wargo, who studies dreams that seem to foresee the future, retells it to Michels and points to Sigmund Freud, the founder of psychoanalysis, as a reader of the tale, to show how a vision of the future can bring itself about.
off-base-doctor-asks-had-they-let-you-se: A doctor near Wright-Patterson Air Force Base in Ohio once asked John Blitch, out of the blue, "had they let you see the alien bodies yet." Blitch, a former scientist at DARPA, the Pentagon's advanced research agency, says this happened to him and gives no date. If true, it would suggest that people living around the base took for granted that alien bodies were kept there.
off-planet-pin-given-at-cape-canaveral-2: Sometime between 2007 and 2010, at Cape Canaveral, the Florida rocket launch site, a famous person whom "everybody has read about" gave Chris Bledsoe a pin described as having come from off the planet. Bledsoe, a man NASA has studied because he says he attracts UFOs, tells this himself and declines to name the giver, though the story's notes link it to a man named Timothy Taylor. He tells it as a sign of quiet contact with people inside the space world.
off-record-source-the-sun-as-a-portal-to: The idea is that the sun may work as a kind of portal, a doorway to other star systems. Michels passes it on from a conversation with a source he does not name, during his episode with Dan Sherman, a former Army sergeant who says the National Security Agency, the US agency that intercepts communications, hired him to talk with aliens. According to Michels, this source compared the sun to a portal to other stars, which would mean our own star could be a route for travel across space.
office-of-naval-intelligence-man-offers-: In the mid-1990s, while they were making Dark Skies, a TV series about a hidden government UFO cover-up, its creators say a man from the Office of Naval Intelligence, the US Navy's spy service, came to them in Los Angeles with a deal, and they turned it down. Brent Friedman, one of the show's creators, tells Michels he was in the room, along with his writing partner Bryce Zabel. He says the man was "so abusive to us in the conference room" and that, under the deal, this man would effectively have become their boss, which suggests the military wanted a hand in how UFOs were shown on screen.
office-of-naval-intelligence-reports-tim: The Office of Naval Intelligence, the US Navy's intelligence branch, wrote up reports on strange objects, Michels says, and a retired Navy admiral and ocean scientist named Tim Gallaudet speaks often about unidentified objects seen moving underwater. Michels mentions this himself in passing, as a sign that the Navy has taken such underwater sightings seriously.
officer-points-to-his-phone-when-giants-: When the subject of giants came up, a military officer silently pointed at his phone, as if to warn that someone might be listening. Tim Alberino, a researcher who claims a 12-foot giant was captured in Afghanistan, tells Jesse Michels he saw this himself. He offers it as a sign that the topic is watched and sensitive.
officers-keep-saying-don-t-worry-about-m: In 1977 at Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota, a nuclear weapons guard named Mario Woods kept asking his superiors what had happened to a fellow guard, Michael Johnson, and kept being told, "don't worry about Michael Johnson, he's fine." Woods tells this himself, as part of his account of being taken during a UFO encounter, and he names a Colonel Spraker among the officers involved. If true, it would mean the Air Force was keeping quiet about what happened to the men that night.
officials-asked-whether-he-had-a-mental-: When Dylan Borland, a man who says a top government official told him aliens run everything, came forward with his story, officials are said to have been "very interested" in whether he had a mental connection to "the triangle," the triangle-shaped craft at the centre of his account. Borland tells this himself. It suggests the officials thought a witness might be linked to such a craft by the mind and not only by sight.
officials-deny-such-a-craft-in-inventory: When government officials said in recent years that the US had "never had a craft like that in our inventory," one man says he knew otherwise because he had seen it. He is Greg Rogers, a doctor who worked with NASA, and he tells Michels he saw such a craft in a secret hangar. He recalls sitting and listening to the denial thinking, "What are you talking about? I saw it," which would mean officials were denying something real.
officials-endorse-a-multi-generational-c: Past directors of the CIA, the US spy agency, along with members of Congress and whistleblowers from several agencies, are said to have backed the idea of a secret program, running for decades and across generations, that recovers crashed UFOs and tries to copy how they work. Michels says this himself, as a summary of what he has seen, in an episode about the time he spent with Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft. If true, it would mean the claim is supported by people inside government, not only by outsiders.
