officials-evasive-on-crash-materials-of-: When officials in the United States are asked whether the government holds materials of unknown origin, the kind said to come from crashed craft, they give a wishy-washy answer and avoid saying no. The author Peter Levenda says this on the show, explaining that he was told "by way of omission": what the officials left unsaid was the answer. If true, it would hint that such materials are held and that officials will not deny it.
officials-say-the-lady-s-dates-and-symbo: A man named Chris Bledsoe says he is given dates and symbols by a figure he calls the Lady, and some officials suggest that these match things they already watch and have seen from other trusted sources. Michels tells this himself, without naming the officials, and sets it around 2007 in the United States. If true, it would mean Bledsoe's messages line up with what the government is already tracking.
offworld-technology-sign-on-the-wall-at-: In 2014, at Crane, a Navy weapons and research center in Indiana, a man walked into an area where a sign on the wall read "offworld technology". Randy Anderson tells Jesse Michels he saw the sign himself, in an episode about alien technology he says he witnessed at a military base. If true, it would mean the Navy keeps a labelled area for technology not made on Earth.
oil-and-gas-company-drills-beside-the-me: Just as drilling was going on at a mesa on Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property famous for reports of strange events, an oil and gas company suddenly showed up on the ranch's northern border and, in the owner's words, "ramrods permits through" to drill next door. The ranch's owner tells this himself, giving no date. If true, it would suggest someone else wanted to get at whatever lies under that spot.
oke-shannon-discussed-on-classified-serv: In 2024, something called Oke Shannon was a big topic on the US government's top secret computer network, says Dylan Borland, a former intelligence analyst who says he saw it himself. In his words, "Oak Shannon was a massive conversation on the classified servers." He does not explain here what Oke Shannon is, but he tells it to show that insiders were talking about it in secret.
oke-shannon-s-1985-bdm-physics-working-g: Notes written in 1985 by a man named Oke Shannon, from a working group on advanced theoretical physics at the defence company BDM International in McLean, Virginia, are said to contain the line "ask Don Kerr for funding" in a discussion of programmes to study recovered UFOs and copy how they work. The researcher UAPGerb describes the notes himself, without naming who passed them to him, and names Donald Kerr as the man to be asked for money. If true, it would put a real funding contact behind talk of such programmes in the mid 1980s.
oki-shannon-on-building-an-anti-gravity-: A man named Oke Shannon, whom Michels ties to Los Alamos National Laboratory, the US government's weapons research lab in New Mexico, is said to have backed a theory by a man named Ferris Williams as the way to beat gravity. Michels quotes him in an episode on early secret work on flying craft: "If we were to build an anti-gravitational device, it would be built on the principles involved in William's theory." He offers it as a sign that serious lab scientists took the idea of a machine that cancels gravity seriously.
old-agreement-with-non-human-beings-from: A former Pentagon official turned whistleblower named Matthew Brown says that a very old agreement was reached with non-human beings sometime in the era of Presidents Harry Truman and Dwight Eisenhower, roughly 1945 to 1961. He passes this on as something he was told rather than something he saw, and says it shaped "the nature of at least one very old agreement." If true, it would mean the US government struck a deal with non-human beings decades ago.
old-maps-show-antarctica-as-two-islands: Old world maps known as the Piri Reis map and the Oronteus Finaeus map include one that shows Antarctica as two islands lying very close together. The researcher Jason Jorjani brings this up on the show without naming a source. If true, it would mean the old mapmakers knew something about the land under Antarctica's ice.
older-bae-archives-colleague-with-ts-sci: A former worker at BAE, a large defense company, says an older colleague in its archives department, who held a top-level security clearance known as TS/SCI and later moved into the intelligence agencies as a government employee, gave him a warning. Dylan Borland tells this to Michels as something that happened to him directly. He tells it as a sign that people with deep clearances knew he was close to something sensitive.
older-pilots-private-ufo-stories: According to a fighter pilot named Ryan Graves, older military pilots who have flown for a long time all seem to have their own UFO story, one they tell you only once they have had a few drinks. Graves says this on Michels' show as something he picked up from those pilots over the years, not as one particular sighting. If true, it would mean strange encounters are common among pilots but rarely spoken about in the open.
oliver-reiser-s-tone-theory-and-letters-: A philosopher at the University of Pittsburgh named Oliver Reiser held a theory of the universe built on tones, set out in his work Cosmic Humanism, and traded dozens of letters with the scientist Puharich in the 1960s and 70s. An unnamed researcher on the show tells this in his own summary, also bringing in Albert Einstein, saying Puharich "knew this guy. They exchanged like dozens and dozens of letters." It matters to the story of Puharich's own ideas about contact with other beings.
oliver-sacks-autistic-twins-who-traded-s: Twin brothers who were autistic and lived in an institution are said to have played a game of saying large prime numbers, up to six digits, back and forth to each other. The researcher Diane Powell repeats this as a case report by the neurologist Oliver Sacks, linking it to his book Awakenings. If true, it would suggest the twins shared knowledge in a way no one could explain.
one-in-four-ellsworth-missile-security-p: Among the security police who guarded nuclear missiles at Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota in the 1970s, roughly one in four has probably seen something strange in the night sky. That is the estimate of Mario Woods, a former nuclear missile guard who served there and speaks from his own time on the job. If he is right, odd lights over American nuclear weapons were a common sight for the men watching them.
one-of-grusch-s-40-witnesses-died-at-a-c: One of the roughly 40 witnesses behind David Grusch, a former intelligence officer who went public with claims that the US holds crashed craft not made by humans, has since died. A helicopter pilot named Jake Barber, who says he flew a UFO recovery himself, tells Michels this and adds that the man's death was "quite conveniently timed" for anyone who might have had a hand in it. He does not say who or how, but the hint is that a witness may have been silenced.
one-to-two-craft-brought-down-per-year-a: At some secret military facilities, known as black sites, one or two unknown craft are brought down every year. The commentator who goes by UAPGerb, who says he has seen strange craft himself, passes this on as a claim made by the UFO researcher Steven Greer and others. If true, it would mean crashes and captures of such craft are routine rather than rare.
ongoing-arrangement-with-pilots-of-the-b: The US government may have some kind of deal with whoever flies the black triangles, large dark triangle-shaped craft that people report seeing in the sky, and may also have built its own copy. Matthew Brown, a former Pentagon official turned whistleblower, puts it as "an exchange or some sort of arrangement with whatever is piloting" them. If true, it would mean the government is in an ongoing relationship with non-human pilots.
ongoing-hybrid-program-semen-extraction-: The claim is that people taken by aliens have semen extracted from them, as part of an ongoing programme to breed human and alien hybrids. The parapsychologist Jeffrey Mishlove raises it, pointing to the writer Whitley Strieber as one of those who "talk about you know semen extraction taking place during alien abductions." If true, it would mean abductions serve a deliberate breeding effort.
ongoing-psionic-operation-in-the-pentago: The claim is that the Pentagon, the headquarters of the US military, is still running an operation that uses psionics, meaning mind powers such as sensing or influencing things at a distance. The journalist Ross Coulthart says he has spoken to people who confirmed that this psionic operation is still going on, though he does not name them. If true, it would mean the military still treats mental powers as a working tool.
onion-effect-gray-project-hidden-inside-: Between 1990 and 1993, a secret effort called the gray project was hidden inside a regular secret, or black, project, so that only a few people in the black project knew the gray one existed, like the layers of an onion. Dan Sherman, a former Air Force sergeant who says the National Security Agency, the US spy agency for intercepted signals, hired him to communicate with aliens, tells this to Jesse Michels. He says an officer named Captain White explained the layering to him, telling him others would cover the cover work but "I'm going to talk to you about the gray project." The story places the briefing at agency headquarters in Maryland, while Sherman in one telling puts it in a communications van at an overseas post. If true, it would show how a programme could stay hidden even from people working right beside it.
online-whistleblower-nhi-live-and-build-: There are five to seven places in the world's oceans where unexplained craft are seen going in and out of the water, and, according to an online whistleblower who calls himself Condor Man, these are where non-human intelligences live and build their own craft. A retired Navy admiral named Tim Gallaudet passes this on, repeating the statements Condor Man made online rather than anything he saw himself. If true, the oceans would hold the home bases of whatever is behind these sightings.
only-about-150-of-40-000-ashurbanipal-ta: Of the roughly 40,000 clay tablets from the library of Ashurbanipal, an ancient Assyrian king, found at Nineveh in what is now Iraq, only about 150 have been translated, according to the researcher Matt LaCroix. The tablets are written in cuneiform, the wedge-shaped writing of ancient Mesopotamia. LaCroix mentions this himself, without naming a source, to suggest that most of what the ancients wrote down is still unread.
only-minuteman-launched-from-a-silo-at-n: Only one missile ever flew out of the ground in the Minuteman program, the US land-based nuclear missile force, and it happened in the 1960s at a launch site called November 2 in South Dakota's Ellsworth missile field, where it flew for about five seconds. A former nuclear missile guard named Mario Woods says so. He was stationed at November 2 years later, so he passes it on as the history of his own post, not as something he saw.
onr-studies-of-a-sixth-sense-2011: In 2011 and 2012, the US Navy published studies on whether people have a sixth sense, according to the researcher who goes by UAPGerb. He says the studies came from the Office of Naval Research, the Navy's science office, and he does not name the papers. If true, it would mean the military was taking human intuition seriously as something to study.
operation-40-becomes-operation-mongoose-: In the early 1960s, a covert group called Operation 40 was turned into Operation Mongoose, a secret campaign against Cuba, run from a large station on the University of Miami campus called JM WAVE. The lawyer Dan Sheehan says this on the show without naming a source. He tells it as part of the story of President John F. Kennedy and the Soviet leader Nikita Khrushchev, saying the change was only a renaming and the same operation went on under a new name.
operation-bluebird-as-the-first-mkultra-: Operation Bluebird, a CIA program that ran from about 1950 to 1953, is described as the first version of MKUltra, the CIA's later program of mind-control experiments. Michels calls it pre-MKUltra in a conversation with the writer Peter Levenda, and in that exchange it is agreed that it was in effect the first MKUltra. The point is that the CIA's mind-control work began earlier than its best-known name suggests.
operation-castle-sailors-see-discs-over-: During Operation Castle, a 1954 series of American hydrogen bomb tests in the Marshall Islands in the Pacific, sailors on several ships saw disc-shaped or round objects hovering over their vessels, according to a researcher named Robert Hastings. Hastings says he found these sailors and that they described "very brief but clearly sightings" of the objects. He tells it to Michels as part of his long-held claim that UFOs keep watch on nuclear weapons.
operation-highjump-1946: In 1946 the United States Navy sent a huge expedition of ships to Antarctica, an effort known as Operation Highjump and linked to the explorer Richard Byrd. The philosopher Jason Jorjani tells it on the show without naming a source, saying the Navy did it "for whatever reason". He raises it because, if the purpose was not what was said, the trip may have been about something hidden in the far south.
operation-highjump-and-byrd-s-statement-: After Operation Highjump, a large US Navy expedition to Antarctica in 1946 and 1947, its leader, the polar explorer Admiral Richard Byrd, made a statement that some people read as a hint about flying saucers. The philosopher Jason Jorjani says that in a port in Chile, Byrd told the Chilean press "we needed to prepare for a third World War in which aircraft could cross from pole to pole at tremendous speeds." Jorjani cites Chilean press clippings. The UFO historian Richard Dolan has read it differently: "I read Bird's full statement that he gave and if you really read the whole thing I don't think he's really talking about flying saucers." So the two agree there was a statement, but not on what it meant. If Jorjani's reading is right, the expedition met something in Antarctica that worried the Navy.
operation-highjump-laser-shooting-discs: Around 1946 and 1947, Admiral Richard Byrd, a US Navy polar explorer, led Operation Highjump, a big naval expedition down the coast of Argentina toward Antarctica. According to Michels, the fleet reportedly met flying discs that shot at them with lasers. Michels tells it twice without naming a source. The second time he gives the fleet's size as about 70 ships, 33 aircraft and nearly 5,000 men, and ties it to James Forrestal, the US Navy's top civilian official of the time.
operation-moonwatch-and-its-36-ufo-repor: Operation Moonwatch was a 1950s sky-watching programme run from Harvard by the astronomer Fred Whipple, with about a dozen tracking stations around the world, and according to the astronomer Beatriz Villarroel it logged 36 UFO reports. She says J. Allen Hynek, an astronomer who later advised the Air Force on UFOs, helped Whipple run it, and that the researcher Jacques Vallée found those reports, which her own team is now going through. She tells it as background to her research, and it would mean trained observers in a scientific programme recorded unexplained sightings.
operation-overlord-with-bodyguard-and-fo: In 1944 the Allies made one real invasion and faked another, according to a researcher named Eric Weinstein. He says Operation Overlord, the D-Day landing on the beaches of Normandy, was the real thing, while Operations Bodyguard and Fortitude were made-up plans meant to make the enemy think an invasion of Norway was coming: "we never actually invaded Norway as we said we were going to do." He uses it as an example of how a government can run a true story and a false one side by side.
operation-paperclip-scientists-in-the-ch: In the 1950s, scientists brought to America under Operation Paperclip, the US programme that brought German scientists over after the Second World War, apparently lived in Terrell Hills, the San Antonio, Texas, neighbourhood where the writer Whitley Strieber grew up. Strieber, who says he has met aliens, tells it about his own childhood and credits the author Peter Levenda for the point. If true, it would place him as a boy right beside the men of a secret postwar programme.
operation-prato-as-an-official-armed-for: In 1977, Brazil's armed forces ran an official operation, called Operation Prato, to watch strange phenomena in the sky over the state of Pará in northern Brazil. Aldo Rebelo, a former Brazilian defense minister, confirms it: "The operation took place. It was an official operation led by the armed forces." Coming from him, it means the Brazilian state itself treated the sightings as real enough to investigate.
operation-snow-white-scientology-infiltr: In the 1970s, in a plan called Operation Snow White, the Church of Scientology infiltrated several US government agencies, among them the tax agency known as the IRS and the CIA, the country's foreign spy agency. A researcher named Jay Anderson brings it up, without naming a source, describing it as a huge infiltration.
oppenheimer-created-the-classification-c: The claim is that J. Robert Oppenheimer, the physicist who led America's wartime atomic bomb project, was the one who created the secrecy rules that came to cover UFOs. It comes from David Grusch, a former intelligence officer who has testified that the US hides UFO material, and he says it in his own interview with Michels. Michels then repeats it on several later episodes: sometimes he says Oppenheimer set up the secrecy with the Atomic Energy Commission, the US agency in charge of nuclear work, and sometimes he names a scientist called Robert Sarbacher as a co-founder, once putting it in 1954. If true, it would mean UFO secrecy was built into the same system that guarded the bomb.
oppenheimer-first-nuclear-weapon-in-mode: J. Robert Oppenheimer, the physicist who led the building of the first atomic bomb in 1945, was supposedly asked by a student how it felt to make the first nuclear weapon, and answered that he was the first "in modern history." Jesse Michels tells this himself on two episodes and calls it apocryphal, a rumor. In one he ties the answer to the Bhagavad Gita and the Vedas, old Hindu scriptures that he says describe weapons of death, which would hint that ancient people knew such weapons.
oppenheimer-on-the-aztec-crash-retrieval: A book by a writer named William Steinman, UFO Crash at Aztec, says that a craft crashed near Aztec, New Mexico, in 1948 and that the physicist J. Robert Oppenheimer, who led the building of the atomic bomb, was part of the team that recovered it. Jesse Michels brings this up from the book in a conversation with a guest, as a claim that the top scientists of the day were drawn into secret crash recoveries.
oppenheimer-recalls-the-trinity-test-and: Watching the first atomic bomb test, at the Trinity site in New Mexico in 1945, the physicist J. Robert Oppenheimer recalls thinking of a line from the Hindu scripture the Bhagavad Gita: "Now I am become death, the destroyer of worlds." His own recorded words are played on the show. Oppenheimer does not say which translation he followed; in Edwin Arnold's 1885 English version, the god Krishna's words at that verse are "Thou seest Me as Time who kills, Time who brings all to doom."
oppenheimer-s-gita-quote-originally-i-am: The famous line that J. Robert Oppenheimer, the physicist who led the building of the first atomic bomb, took from the Hindu scripture the Bhagavad Gita, "I am death, the destroyer of worlds", originally read "I am time, the destroyer of worlds". A guest named Dave Rossi tells Michels he read this, and it would mean the scripture speaks of time itself as the destroyer. He does not say which translation he read; in Edwin Arnold's 1885 English translation, The Song Celestial, the god Krishna says at chapter 11, verse 32, "Thou seest Me as Time who kills, Time who brings all to doom", which speaks of Time, though in other words.
oppenheimer-s-late-speech-on-abolishing-: In one of his last speeches to his scientists, J. Robert Oppenheimer, the physicist who led the building of the first atomic bomb, is said to have told them that they could not afford to believe nuclear weapons can't be abolished. A former Air Force missile officer named Robert Salas, who says a UFO once shut down ten of the nuclear missiles in his care, quotes the line to Michels. He uses it to back his case that the world must get rid of nuclear weapons.
oppenheimer-set-up-ufo-secrecy-1940: The claim is that J. Robert Oppenheimer, the physicist who led the Manhattan Project (the secret US effort to build the atomic bomb during the Second World War), set up the government's secrecy around UFOs. Michels says a man he calls only Rush told him this on the record in an interview. A researcher named Bob Maguire offers it as his own belief, without naming a source: Oppenheimer and others from the Manhattan Project were, in his words, "the original secret keepers." If true, UFO secrecy would go back to the same people who kept the bomb secret, starting in the 1940s and 1950s.
oracle-at-delphi-as-a-burning-methane-se: The oracle at Delphi, the place in ancient Greece where a priestess gave prophecies, was really "a burning methane seep," a spot where natural gas leaked out of the ground and burned. That is the view of a researcher named Geoffrey Drumm, who states it to Michels in passing without naming a source. If true, the famous holy site would have been built around a natural gas vent.
orang-pendek-and-surviving-flores-homini: In the forests of Indonesia, people speak of the Orang Pendek, a short, upright, ape-like creature, and some wonder whether it could be a surviving relative of the small early humans whose remains were found on the island of Flores. Jesse Michels raises this himself, as something people speculate about, without naming a source. If true, it would mean another kind of human lived on into recent times.
orange-moved-by-psychokinesis-in-a-vivid: In a vivid dream set in his family's drawing room, an orange suddenly moved eight to ten inches as if something had pushed it. Deep Prasad, a researcher who argues on the show that artificial intelligence is alien technology, says it happened to him. He tells it as an experience of psychokinesis, moving objects with the mind.
orange-orb-lands-near-an-open-minot-miss: Sometime between 1966 and 1968, an orange glowing ball came over Minot Air Force Base in North Dakota, a nuclear missile base, hovered, and came down near a missile silo that was open, with a man on the ground "screaming like it's landing." The documentary filmmaker James Fox tells it from his own research for his film The Phenomenon. It is told as a case of an unknown object taking close interest in nuclear weapons.
orange-reddish-wobbling-ufos-around-area: Orange-reddish UFOs are said to have been flying around Area 51, a secret US Air Force test site in Nevada, since the 1980s and 1990s, wobbling at low altitude as if riding on a wave. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, in an episode about the time he spent with Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft near the site.
orb-and-tall-glowing-figure-filmed-at-a-: During a healing session for a cancer patient at his home in North Carolina, around 2013 to 2015, a glowing ball of light and a tall glowing figure are said to have been caught on video. Chris Bledsoe, a man who says UFOs appear around him and whom NASA scientists have studied, tells Michels he was there and that the footage shows it: "all of a sudden in the video, you'll see an orb appear. It comes zooming right up to me." He offers it as evidence that the lights he sees are tied to healing.
orb-as-ancient-relic-compared-with-salva: A man named Jordan Jose, who says he was taken into a secret UFO program as a child, suggests that a mysterious orb he heard described as a 'relic' may not come from non-human beings or a crash at all, but may have been on Earth for a very long time. He compares it to Salvator Mundi, the painting attributed to Leonardo da Vinci of Christ holding a clear orb.
orb-flies-figure-eights-over-the-capitol: In 2025, after a congressional hearing on unexplained flying objects, a glowing orb appeared and flew figure-eights over the Capitol and the White House for 45 minutes, as a group watched from a platform at the Library of Congress. Chris Bledsoe, a North Carolina man who says he attracts UFOs, tells Jesse Michels he was there, naming Congresswoman Anna Paulina Luna and Congressman Eric Burlison among those around the hearing. He offers it as a sighting over the seat of government itself.
orb-photo-showing-chris-s-lost-child: Chris Bledsoe, a North Carolina man who says he draws UFOs to him and whom NASA has studied, says he took a picture of a lone glowing ball of light and found a child in it. He tells it himself: he and his wife lost one of their children, and he was outside thinking about that son when "this lonely orb" came, and the photo showed "a child." If true, it would mean the lights he sees are tied to his lost son.
orbs-appearing-inside-bledsoe-s-house-20: Since about 2007, glowing balls of light, or orbs, are said to have shown up "just about every day" inside a family home in North Carolina, hovering over chairs and flying through the rooms. Chris Bledsoe, a man who says he attracts UFOs and whose experiences have drawn interest from NASA, tells this about his own house. If true, it would mean the phenomenon follows one person into his everyday life.
orbs-rise-out-of-the-sea-for-danny-jones: In 2025 at Indian Rocks Beach in Florida, two glowing orbs are said to have risen up out of the sea when asked to, and were filmed by Danny Jones, who hosts another podcast. Chris Bledsoe, a man who says UFOs appear around him, tells Michels he was the one who asked: "it comes up out of the sea. And suddenly, here it came. Two of them." He tells it as proof the lights answer him on request.
orbs-seen-during-sky-observing-at-bledso: While watching the sky at the North Carolina home of Chris Bledsoe, a man who says he attracts UFOs, a massive, very bright orb "flashed into existence" just above the trees about 300 to 400 meters away. Bob McGwier, an engineer described on the episode as a CIA contractor, tells Jesse Michels he saw it himself, with Bledsoe, his son Ryan Bledsoe and the writer Richard Dolan named in the account. He offers it as a trained observer's own sighting.
orbs-seen-with-unmarked-black-helicopter: At Skinwalker Ranch, a property in Utah known for reports of strange events, glowing orbs are said to be seen, sometimes along with unmarked black helicopters. Michels mentions this himself while talking with the ranch's owner, without giving a date or a source. If true, it would hint that someone official is watching the orbs too.
orbs-summoned-to-hover-over-jay-anderson: Jay Anderson, a guest on the show, says he went into a meditative state and asked for something to appear, float down and hover over his house, and that glowing balls of light did. He tells it himself, giving no date. If true, it would mean these lights can be called by the mind.
origin-of-adjustment-team-philip-k-dick-: The science fiction writer Philip K. Dick got the idea for his story Adjustment Team, later made into the film The Adjustment Bureau, after the pull chain on his bathroom light seemed to have turned into a wall switch, as though reality had been quietly changed. A researcher named Riz Virk tells this second-hand, from what Dick's wife Tessa Dick told him: "he went into the bathroom and there was a light that he had turned on and off many times." Virk tells it as a hint that the world might be a kind of simulation that can be edited.
origins-of-the-us-remote-viewing-program: In the 1960s and 70s, the story goes, the US government started a programme in remote viewing, the practice of trying to describe faraway places or things using only the mind, built around researchers named Hal Puthoff and Russell Targ. Lyn Buchanan, a former Army sergeant who later served in it, says they brought in a man named Ingo Swann, who developed a method called controlled remote viewing, and that the unit had already existed for ten years before he arrived. A guest named Dan Sheehan names Puthoff and Targ too, but pairs them with a man named Pat Price rather than Swann and calls it the entire psychic programme. Told this way, it means the US government took psychic abilities seriously enough to fund them.
orion-and-osiris-symbolism-in-the-apollo: The patch of Apollo, NASA's 1960s programme to land people on the Moon, hides the constellation Orion behind its letter A, with the A's crossbar deliberately lined up with Orion's belt, Michels says. He tells this himself in an episode on pagan ritual at NASA, reading it as a nod to Osiris, the Egyptian god tied to Orion.
orion-correlation-theory-1994: The Orion correlation theory holds that the great pyramids on the Giza Plateau in Egypt are laid out to match the stars of Orion's belt. The writer Graham Hancock credits it to the author Robert Bauval, saying he came up with it in 1994 in his book The Orion Mystery, published that year. The researcher Geoffrey Drumm also brings it up. He says some of these structures "are connected to Orion's belt" and adds "I think that's true," but does not name Bauval or give a date. The theory is told because, if right, it would mean the pyramid builders planned their monuments around the sky.
osap-at-skinwalker-ranch-and-the-hitchhi: From about 2007 to 2012, a government-funded program studied strange events at Skinwalker Ranch, a property in Utah, and its researchers later reported strange effects they called the "hitchhiker effect". Michels tells this himself. He says the program, called OSAP, ran under the protection of Senator Harry Reid, and that its people dug holes and looked into exotic weapons on the ranch. In another episode he calls it AATIP, a small Pentagon office that studied unexplained aerial reports, led by Luis Elizondo. He adds that because Bigelow Aerospace, a private company owned by the billionaire contractor Robert Bigelow, ran the work, its data is classified and cannot be requested under FOIA, a US law that lets anyone request government records. He also credits the journalist Leslie Kean's 2017 article with bringing it to light. Retired Navy admiral Tim Gallaudet says the Defense Intelligence Agency, a military spy agency, paid for about two years of research at the ranch, citing George Knapp and Colm Kelleher. The ranch's current owner, Brandon Fugal, calls it a Pentagon black-budget program that brought together dozens of government scientists and ended in 2013, not 2012. He points to Kelleher and Knapp's book Skinwalkers at the Pentagon as the record. If true, it would mean the government quietly paid scientists to study a haunted-seeming ranch for years.
oscar-wolf-s-project-blue-book-special-u: While Project Blue Book, the US Air Force's UFO study of the 1950s and 60s, told the public that sightings were swamp gas or misidentified birds, there were in fact over 700 real sightings kept apart. The lawyer Dan Sheehan tells Michels this, relaying a man who worked on Blue Book: in one episode he names him as Oscar Wolf, and in another as Albert Stein, an Army clerk typist assigned to the project, and if true it would mean the public study was a front. The Air Force's own fact sheet of January 1985 says "a total of 12, 618 sightings were reported to Project BLUE BOOK. Of these 701 remain 'Unidentified,'" but says nothing of a special unit for them.
oscar-wolfe-deathbed-interview-about-s4-: A dying man named Oscar Wolfe gave an interview about S4, a secret site near Area 51 in Nevada, where he said he had seen an autopsy film of a gray alien. The filmmaker Jeremy Corbell says he brought in the UFO historian Richard Dolan to interview Wolfe "as he was dying on like I think it was like a dialysis machine." Corbell points to Wolfe's DD-214s, the US military's discharge papers, as backing for his service record.
osireion-built-to-tap-the-water-table: The Osireion, an ancient stone structure at Abydos in Egypt, was cut out of the bedrock and built to reach straight down into the groundwater beneath it, according to a researcher named Jeffrey Drum. He tells Michels this without naming a source, as part of his case that the old Egyptian sites were built around water and energy.
osiris-myth-as-preserving-antediluvian-k: The researcher Tim Alberino reads the ancient Egyptian myth of the god Osiris, whose story reaches the Phoenician port of Byblos, as a coded record of knowledge saved from a world that existed before the great flood. In his words, the myth shows "an ark floating on the water with a body of knowledge inside of it from the anti-dolivian world," meaning the world before the flood. He offers this as his own interpretation, and if right it would mean the myth preserves memory of a lost earlier civilisation.
osiris-shaft-water-samples-tested-with-t: Water taken from the Osiris Shaft, a deep flooded shaft beneath the Giza plateau near the pyramids, is said to have been sampled and lab tested. Jeffrey Drum, a researcher who argues the pyramids once worked as a kind of energy system, tells Michels he took part himself, testing the water with an archaeological group called the Osirion 7 mission, alongside Jim Westerman, to find "the source of the water within the Osirion," an ancient underground temple in Egypt. He uses the results to support his idea that water played a part in how the pyramids worked.
oslo-peace-process-dinner-clinton-presse: At a dinner in the royal castle in Oslo, Norway, around 1998, President Bill Clinton urged the Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat, "Take the deal, Yasser. Take the deal. It's your last best chance for peace," with Israeli leader Ehud Barak and Vladimir Putin also part of the scene. Rolf Mowatt-Larssen, a former CIA officer, tells Jesse Michels he was there and also shares his first impression of Putin. He tells it as a first-hand view of a turning point in Middle East peace talks.
osmium-and-cadmium-implants-in-the-m-typ: Some of the small three-fingered bodies said to come from Nazca, Peru, a group called the "M-types", are said to carry metal implants. Michels says this himself in an episode about the bodies, without naming a source: "These metal implants contain osmium and cadmium, which are extremely rare earth metals." He raises it because such metals would be hard to explain in an ancient or faked body.
oss-project-mcgregor-moves-italian-ufo-t: Near the end of the Second World War, American agents went after advanced technology in northern Italy, including a craft rumored to have crashed near the town of Magenta, and by 1945 that craft was reportedly moved to Wright-Patterson Air Force Base in Ohio for study. Michels tells this himself, saying the work was done by the Office of Strategic Services, America's wartime spy agency, under a secret effort called Project McGregor. In a later episode he tells it more loosely, saying only that a craft crashed in Italy before any of the American cases and passed into US hands, with no agency, project, date or destination named. If true, the US would have held a crashed craft before the famous American crash stories of 1947.
oswald-at-atsugi-u-2-base-1950: Lee Harvey Oswald, the man accused of killing President John F. Kennedy, served in the 1950s at Atsugi, a base in Japan where the CIA ran its U-2 spy plane program. A researcher named Dan Sheehan says this without naming a source. If true, it would tie Oswald to one of the CIA's most secret projects years before the killing.
oswald-could-not-have-fired-all-the-shot: Lee Harvey Oswald, the man accused of killing President John F. Kennedy in Dallas in 1963, could not have fired as many shots as were fired that day. That is what a guest named Dan Sheehan says on Michels's show. Sheehan goes further and says, "I do know who did kill him," meaning others were involved in the killing.
oswald-infiltrates-free-cuba-group-and-i: In New Orleans in 1963, Lee Harvey Oswald, the man accused of killing President John F. Kennedy later that year, worked his way inside a Free Cuba group, a movement opposed to Cuba's government, and was then arrested on the street. A researcher named Dan Sheehan tells Michels this from his own knowledge, without naming a source: "He infiltrated the group. That was when he got arrested on the street, remember?" Sheehan raises it as a sign that Oswald was working for someone rather than acting alone.
oswald-s-attempted-call-to-nags-head-196: Lee Harvey Oswald, the man accused of killing President John F. Kennedy in Dallas in 1963, is said to have tried to place a telephone call to Nags Head, a town in North Carolina, asking the operator for the call. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, in an episode about Kennedy and UFOs with the lawyer Danny Sheehan. The point of telling it is that the call hints Oswald had connections he was trying to reach.
oswald-s-fair-play-for-cuba-leaflets-car: In New Orleans in 1963, according to the author and researcher Peter Levenda, the leaflets that Lee Harvey Oswald, the man accused of killing President Kennedy that year, handed out for Fair Play for Cuba, a group that supported Fidel Castro's Cuba, were stamped with an address on Camp Street. Levenda says it was the same address, 544 Camp Street, used by a man named Guy Banister, and he tells it as a fact from his own research without naming a source. The point is that it would tie Oswald to Banister's circle rather than leaving him a lone pro-Cuba activist.
oswald-s-planned-role-and-the-killing-of: In Dallas in 1963, the plan was for Lee Harvey Oswald, the man accused of shooting President John F. Kennedy, to take his shot, run away, and then be killed by J. D. Tippit, a Dallas police officer who was himself shot dead that day. A lawyer named Dan Sheehan lays out this account to Michels as something he was told, not something he saw. If true, Oswald was meant to be silenced and Tippit was part of the plot rather than a random victim.
oswald-trained-by-oni-part-of-private-fi: Lee Harvey Oswald, the man accused of killing President John F. Kennedy in 1963, was trained not by the CIA but by the Office of Naval Intelligence, the US Navy's spy service, and was part of a privately run intelligence operation in the field, according to a researcher named Dan Sheehan. Sheehan tells this without naming a source, and ties it to figures such as the businessman William D. Pawley, a man named Hunt, the general Charles Willoughby and Guy Banister of New Orleans. If true, it would mean Oswald was working inside a hidden network rather than acting alone.
other-remote-viewing-teams-trained-by-pa: There were rumours that remote viewing, the claimed skill of seeing far-off places with the mind alone, was taught to more teams than the one people know about. A speaker named only as Jack raises this on an episode with the Navy scientist Salvatore Pais. He says Pat Price and Joe McMoneagle, two of the best-known remote viewers, were rumoured to have trained other teams besides the one linked to the physicist Hal Puthoff. If true, the psychic spying work would have been bigger than the record shows.
other-ufo-nuclear-witnesses: Many people besides Robert Salas say they saw UFOs interfere with nuclear weapons, among them men named Dave Chandel and Walter Feel. Salas, a former Air Force officer who says a UFO shut down the nuclear missiles he oversaw, makes the point to Michels so that his own account does not stand alone.
otto-skorzeny-in-the-same-building-as-ru: In Spain, the American writer Robert Ruark and his associate Ricardo Sicre lived in the same building as Otto Skorzeny, a former Nazi commando officer. Jason Simosa, a researcher, says this on the show without naming a source, and he tells it as a revealing link between these men.
otto-skorzeny-s-ratline-used-knights-of-: The lawyer Dan Sheehan says that Otto Skorzeny, a Nazi commando officer, ran the "rat line," the secret escape route that smuggled Nazis out of Europe after the Second World War, and that the people moved along it carried passports from the Knights of Malta, an old Catholic order of knights. Sheehan passes this on as something he learned from others, and it would tie a respected religious order to the escape of Nazis.
otto-skorzeny-working-with-the-mossad-19: Otto Skorzeny, a Nazi commando officer in the Second World War, was working with the Mossad, Israel's foreign spy service, in the early 1970s, according to a researcher named Jason Jorjani. He says it to Michels as a plain statement, without naming a source, in a conversation about what he calls Hitler's secret UFO programme, and it would mean former Nazis kept working with intelligence services long after the war.
ouija-board-warning-of-an-aboriginal-upr: Sometime between 1963 and 1966 in New York, a Ouija board, a lettered board used to try to receive messages from spirits, warned of an Aboriginal uprising in Australia outside Perth, and the warning was taken to the Australian consulate. The author Peter Levenda tells it as something he took part in, saying the message "was very specific." If true, it would mean the board gave detailed news about events on the other side of the world.
outer-limits-episode-premiered-before-th: The Outer Limits, a science fiction TV show on CBS, is said to have aired its first episode about 11 days before Betty and Barney Hill had the experience they later described as being abducted by aliens. Michels takes this from American Cosmic, a book by the writer Diana Pasulka, and raises it in two episodes. Its point is that a TV show may have shaped one of the most famous abduction stories.
oval-office-briefing-on-zarqawi-camp-bef: In 2003, before the US invaded Iraq, a CIA officer stood in the Oval Office and told President George W. Bush, "We know where he is. He's in this camp in northeast Iraq," speaking of the militant Abu Musab al-Zarqawi. Rolf Mowatt-Larssen, a former senior CIA official, says he gave that briefing himself, with CIA director George Tenet also part of the story. He tells it to show that the US knew where Zarqawi was before the war began.
over-30-000-nuraghe-towers-on-sardinia: The island of Sardinia once held more than 30,000 nuraghe, ancient round stone towers. A researcher named Tim Alberino says this to Michels without naming a source, as a sign of how large and busy the ancient world that built them must have been.
over-a-hundred-crash-retrieval-cases-in-: A researcher who goes by UAPGerb says that a book called Majic Eyes Only, by the writer Ryan S. Wood, lists more than a hundred cases of UFO crash retrieval, meaning the recovery of crashed craft. UAPGerb calls it a fantastic book and points to it in passing, without going through the cases. If those cases hold up, crashed craft would be far from a one-off event.
overseas-prospecting-for-psionic-assets: Secret operations abroad are said to search for "psionic assets", people believed to have psychic abilities, who are "highly coveted". Jake Barber, a former military helicopter pilot who says he flew a recovered UFO, claims these operations run "OCONUS", military shorthand for outside the continental United States. Michael Herrera, who says he saw a huge craft in the Indonesian jungle, passes on Barber's claim that the people are screened from poor countries. Michels says it can happen in disaster zones and "in some not so ethical ways." Steven Greer, an activist for UFO disclosure, calls it trafficking, places it in Indonesia, and says the people are taken to hidden sites to be screened and tested, which would mean human beings are being collected for their minds.
overwhelming-evidence-of-subsidence-on-t: The floor of the Atlantic Ocean shows overwhelming evidence of major sinking, most of it along the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, the long underwater mountain chain running down the middle of the ocean. The researcher Randall Carlson says this himself, without naming a source, and ties it to the dialogues of the ancient Greek philosopher Plato, the Timaeus and the Critias, which tell of the sunken island of Atlantis. If he is right, the old story of a land that sank into the Atlantic would have real geology behind it.
owens-168-demonstrations-over-20-years-1: A man named Ted Owens is said to have carried out 168 demonstrations of powers he claimed to have, over about 20 years from around 1960, and about two thirds of them "worked out the way he said they would." The parapsychologist Jeffrey Mishlove, who keeps his own files on Owens, gives these figures. If they hold, Owens could make things happen by predicting or calling for them.
owens-approaches-puthoff-and-targ-at-sri: In the 1970s, the physicists Hal Puthoff and Russell Targ were testing psychic abilities at the Stanford Research Institute, a research lab in California, with the Israeli performer Uri Geller, and a self-proclaimed psychic named Ted Owens wrote to them offering himself instead. According to the parapsychologist Jeffrey Mishlove, who relays the story, Owens asked "why are you wasting time with him? I'm the world's greatest subject," and the scientists turned him away. Mishlove tells it as part of Owens' strange history with official psychic research.
owens-brain-operated-on-beside-a-circle-: A man named Ted Owens, who claimed psychic powers, said that one day while driving on a highway in Texas he suddenly found himself standing on the road beside his car or truck, which was surrounded by a whole circle of tarantula spiders, and the story goes that his brain had been operated on there. The parapsychologist Jeffrey Mishlove, who holds a PhD and studies psychic claims, tells it as Owens told it to him, adding "as I recall" about the details. To Owens it would mark the moment unseen beings changed him.
owens-declares-war-on-the-us-government-: Between about 1980 and 1983, a self-proclaimed psychic named Ted Owens announced, "I'm declaring war against the United States government," and soon after came reports of poltergeist attacks, unexplained disturbances, on Navy ships and nuclear power plants. Jeffrey Mishlove, a researcher of psychic claims who knew Owens, tells this and says he would receive newspaper clippings of those attacks. The suggestion is that Owens could cause such events with his mind.
owens-extorts-sports-team-owners-and-a-s: Ted Owens, a man who claimed psychic powers, is said to have asked owners of major league sports teams for money to "protect" their teams. A researcher named Jeffrey Mishlove, who holds a doctorate, tells this without naming a source. He says that when one owner went back on the promise, a suicide followed, which would suggest Owens believed, or wanted others to believe, his powers could do real harm.
owens-predicts-end-of-california-drought: In 1976, while California was in a bad drought, a self-described psychic named Ted Owens is said to have told the researchers Hal Puthoff and Russell Targ, "I'm going to end this drought, and it's going to happen within a couple of days," with strange weather and UFOs to follow. The researcher Jeffrey Mishlove tells it from Puthoff and Targ's files on Owens. If true, it would show a man claiming to command the weather on demand.
owens-space-intelligences-mantid-like-be: Ted Owens, a man who claimed psychic powers from about the 1960s to the 1980s, said he got those powers from insect-like beings in a huge invisible UFO hovering over the Earth. The parapsychologist Jeffrey Mishlove repeats Owens' own words: he used psychokinesis, the supposed power to move things with the mind, and sent "telepathic messages to my friends, the space intelligences", and "they do it". The philosopher Jason Jorjani tells the same story in another episode and adds that Owens named the mantis-like beings "Twitter and Tweeter" and placed them in a saucer. If true, a human being would have had direct mental contact with alien beings who acted on his requests.
owens-summons-lightning-near-the-camden-: In the 1960s in Philadelphia, Ted Owens, a man who claimed psychic powers, pointed his finger at the Camden Bridge, and within moments lightning struck nearby, not on the bridge but close to it. Jeffrey Mishlove, a researcher of psychic abilities, relays this from a sworn statement by a witness named Sydney Margolies, and also cites the books How to Contact Space People and The PK Man. If true, it would mean Owens could call up weather with his mind.
owens-takes-an-eagles-fullback-out-of-a-: A man named Ted Owens, who claimed psychic powers, is said to have told a sports writer in the middle of a Philadelphia Eagles football game, "I'm going to take out this player," after which a fullback was taken out of the game. The parapsychologist Jeffrey Mishlove relays the story, crediting the sports writer's newspaper article. If true, it would mean Owens could affect events with his mind.
owens-three-ufo-sighting-experiment-arou: In 1976, a man named Ted Owens, who claimed he could call up UFOs with his mind, is said to have promised to "create three UFO sightings within a 90-day period within a 100 miles of San Francisco," with San Diego used as a comparison area. Jeffrey Mishlove, a researcher with a doctorate in parapsychology, the study of psychic claims, tells Michels he took part in setting up the test. If it worked, it would mean a person could summon UFOs on demand.
owens-tries-to-sway-football-games-while: A self-proclaimed psychic named Ted Owens would sit in his living room smoking cigars and drinking whiskey, with two or three televisions showing football games, and try to change how the games turned out with his mind while drunk. The parapsychologist Jeffrey Mishlove tells this as something he learned about Owens, set in the 1970s and 1980s, as a picture of how Owens tested his claimed powers.
owner-s-own-physical-impact-hitchhiker-e: Whatever goes on at Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property known for strange reports, has had a very real physical effect on people's lives, including the owner's own, sometimes described as something following people home. The ranch's owner says so to Jesse Michels, speaking from personal experience. The point is that the place's effects do not stay on the ranch.
p3-operators-as-interfaces-to-et-vehicle: According to Steven Greer, a longtime UFO activist, there are people called P3 operators who go through hard training so they can act almost like a human link between the people who control them and alien vehicles. Greer says he is passing on what Jake Barber, a man who has spoken publicly about secret UFO work, described. If true, it would mean humans are trained to connect directly with craft from elsewhere.
pablo-amaringo-on-flying-saucers-as-spir: The Peruvian painter and former shaman Pablo Amaringo told the writer Graham Hancock, matter-of-factly, that the flying saucers in his visions were "vehicles for entering and leaving the spirit world." Hancock, who writes about lost civilisations and altered states, relays this on two episodes from his meeting with Amaringo in the Peruvian Amazon, around 2005, and credits his book Supernatural. In the later episode he dates it more loosely and also credits a book called Visionary. If true, it would tie UFOs to the spirit visions of Amazon shamans.
pacaccini-says-he-saw-35-second-video-of: A Brazilian investigator named Vitorio Pacaccini says that in 1996, in Brazil, he "saw with my own eyes an alien creature kept in captivity" in a 35-second military video. He tells it first hand, on an episode about a creature said to have been caught by the army and taken to a hospital, and if true it would mean the military held a living alien.
pacaccini-shot-at-and-disappears-for-20-: In 1996, Vitorio Pacaccini, a Brazilian researcher looking into the case of a creature said to have been captured by soldiers in the town of Varginha, was shot at, and the story goes that he then dropped out of sight for some twenty years. Pacaccini says it himself: on the road between Varginha and Três Corações, two shots hit his back bumper, and he knew from the noise it was gunfire. The documentary filmmaker James Fox repeats that Pacaccini "was shot at," as a sign of the danger around people who dug into the case.
pais-agrees-his-devices-facilitate-vacuu: The unusual inventions of Salvatore Pais, a Navy scientist known for patents on exotic devices including rumored "free energy" machines, are said not to make energy themselves but to tap the energy thought to fill empty space, which physicists call vacuum energy. Dave Rossi, a guest who says aliens taught him advanced physics, tells Michels he put this idea to Pais himself and that Pais agreed. If true, such devices would draw on a nearly endless source of power rather than produce it.
pais-inspired-by-steven-greer-documentar: A Navy scientist named Salvatore Pais, known for patents on unusual flying craft, says a lot of what inspired him "was done by Dr. Steven Greer". Greer is a campaigner who wants UFO secrets made public, and the work Pais means is his documentaries Close Encounters of the Fifth Kind and Unacknowledged. Pais says this himself to Michels, and it would mean that UFO films helped shape his work on Navy patents.
pais-on-theory-of-everything-plasma-as-d: Effects such as reducing an object's mass and its resistance to motion might be produced not with solid materials but with plasmas, the electrically charged gas found in lightning and stars. An engineer named Dave Rossi says this is what Salvatore Pais, a Navy scientist known for unusual patents, meant when he appeared on Theory of Everything, a physics podcast hosted by Curt Jaimungal. Rossi offers it as his own reading of Pais, "not to speak for him", and if right it would point to how advanced craft could move as they are said to.
pais-patent-test-at-pax-river-had-no-def: In 2025, the military admitted it had tested one of the unusual craft patents filed by Navy engineer Salvatore Pais, he believes the antigravity one, at Patuxent River, a Navy air base in Maryland, but got no definitive results. Congressman Eric Burlison tells Jesse Michels he heard this directly, with Jon Kosloski, head of the Pentagon's office for unexplained aerial reports, named in the account. It matters because it would mean the Navy actually tried to build what the patents describe.
pais-s-career-at-navy-programs-and-space: Salvatore Pais, a Navy scientist who holds patents for craft that sound like UFOs, says he worked for Strategic Systems Programs, the Navy office for submarine-launched nuclear missiles, at the Washington Navy Yard and then moved to the Space Force, the US military branch for space. He tells this about his own career, giving no dates. It matters because it places the man behind those patents inside serious defence work.
pais-stops-jesse-s-questions-in-motel-in: During an interview in a motel near Pax River, a Navy air base in Maryland, a Navy scientist named Salvatore Pais is said to have cut off Michels's questions once they reached a certain level of the science. Michels recalls Pais telling him to stop asking, and Pais himself tells it in his own words: "We'll not touch on that. Leave it there, Jesse. Trust me on that," naming the fifth dimension as the topic he would not discuss, which suggests the subject is sensitive.
pais-told-ashton-forbes-that-the-mh370-o: Videos said to show glowing orbs around Malaysia Airlines flight MH370, the airliner that vanished in 2014, show the Pais effect in action, according to the Navy scientist Salvatore Pais, whose name is on the effect, a physics idea from his patents. Pais tells Michels he said so to a researcher named Ashton Forbes in 2023, on Forbes's first podcast appearance, on the Hard Truths podcast: 'I told him this is the Pais.' If true, it would tie the plane's disappearance to advanced physics of the kind Pais describes.
pakistani-gunsmith-who-hammers-out-aks-f: Just across the Afghan border in Pakistan, a man living in a mud hut makes working AK assault rifles by hammering scrap metal from aircraft on a granite rock. Joe McMoneagle, a former Army remote viewer, someone trained to describe distant places by mind alone, tells the story as something he was told. He uses it to show how much skill can exist far from modern factories.
palermo-stone-shows-pre-dynastic-egyptia: A pyramid researcher named Geoffrey Drumm says the Palermo Stone, an ancient Egyptian stone slab carved with records of early kings, shows that Egyptian civilisation goes back far before the age of the pharaohs. He hedges a little, saying "I believe it's the Polarmo stone," and offers it from his own reading without naming a source. If he is right, Egypt's civilisation would be much older than the usual history allows.
palomar-transients-missing-in-earth-s-sh: Old sky photographs taken at Palomar Observatory near San Diego between 1949 and 1957 show brief points of light that appear and vanish. According to the astronomer Beatriz Villarroel, those points are strangely scarce in the part of the sky that falls in Earth's shadow. That would fit objects in orbit that flash only when sunlight hits them, before any satellites were launched. Villarroel works on this through VASCO, a project that compares old sky photographs with modern ones. She says that when her team checked a sample of these lights gathered by the Spanish Virtual Observatory, "We get a huge deficit" in the shadow. She places the effect at geosynchronous distance (the height where an orbiting object keeps pace with Earth's spin) and credits a researcher named Guy Nir. Michels later repeats her finding in another episode, describing objects that seemed absent "on the dark side of the Earth" where the sun should not light them.
pamela-fails-her-trust-test-while-about-: One night in the mid 1960s, in the desert ranges of Indian Springs Valley, Nevada, near an ammunition bunker, a being called Pamela failed a test of trust while about 70 small scout craft watched, says Charles Hall, a man who says he spent three years living alongside tall white aliens at a secret Air Force base. He tells it as something he saw: "On that night, she failed the test."
pan-starrs-discovers-oumuamua-2017: In 2017, the Pan-STARRS telescope in Hawaii spotted a fast-moving object passing through space, later named 'Oumuamua. Michels tells this himself in an episode with the Harvard researcher Avi Loeb, and in a later episode he calls it the first interstellar object ever seen visiting our solar system, citing Loeb. It matters because an object from outside our solar system is very rare, and some ask what it might be.
pandolfi-email-senators-let-him-carry-th: In an email, a CIA scientist named Ron Pandolfi is said to have written that senators and congressmen keep asking questions about UFOs without realising the real issue is not the material itself but access to it, that you can get into a lot of trouble, and that when he tells the senators this "they just let me carry the keys." The UFO researcher Grant Cameron says he has this email, and he quotes it from memory without showing it. If true, it would mean one official, not Congress, holds the keys to what is known.
pandolfi-going-to-los-alamos-to-talk-to-: Around 1991, Ron Pandolfi, a scientist at the CIA, the US spy agency, is said to have told people at a meeting that he was going to Los Alamos, the New Mexico nuclear weapons laboratory, that week to talk to a live alien. The UFO researcher Grant Cameron relays this, as something passed on to him, in a story that also involves the researchers Dan Smith and John B. Alexander. If true, it would mean a living non-human being was held at a government lab.
pandolfi-s-teenage-metallurgical-analysi: Ron Pandolfi is said to have studied, as a teenager, the metal of a piece his father gave him, which came from the work of the Glomar Explorer, a deep-sea recovery ship his father was involved with. The UFO researcher Grant Cameron repeats this as a story Pandolfi told, and calls it "another story" in passing. If true, an odd piece from a secret recovery would have passed through a family's hands.
pandolfi-s-uncle-a-founding-member-of-th: A researcher named Jason Simosa says that a request for information was shut down by a Dr. Pandolfi, and that this man's uncle, Louis Pandolfi, was a founding member of the OSS, the American wartime spy agency that came before the CIA. Simosa relays this from others, citing the researcher Jacques Vallée and the interviewer Danny Jones, and he raises it to suggest family ties running deep into the intelligence world behind the people who guard UFO secrets.
pandolfi-steers-clinton-toward-a-maccabe: In the 1990s, Ron Pandolfi, a scientist at the CIA, the US spy agency, told President Bill Clinton he should be briefed on UFOs by a physicist named Bruce Maccabee. Maccabee had written a book about UFOs and the FBI, the US federal police. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, as part of his account of the Clinton White House looking into UFOs.
panelists-claiming-trade-agreements-with: A writer named Peter Levenda, whom the episode's title calls a CIA historian, says he once sat on a conference panel with men who insisted that humanity already has trade agreements with other planets, with goods going back and forth. He tells it as something he heard himself, as an example of the kinds of claims he has met on the UFO speaking circuit.
pantex-diamond-shaped-ufo-in-2015: In 2015 a diamond-shaped UFO is said to have appeared at Pantex, the plant in Texas where America's nuclear weapons are assembled. Michels mentions it himself, citing a release of government files under a law he calls the PURSUE act. It adds to the idea that unexplained objects turn up at nuclear sites.
paper-great-pyramid-concentrates-electri: Geoffrey Drumm, a researcher who studies the pyramids, says a scientific paper came out some time ago showing that the Great Pyramid of Giza in Egypt can store and concentrate electric fields right around the King's Chamber, a granite room deep inside it. Drumm brings up the paper from memory and does not give its authors or date. If true, it would suggest the pyramid was built to do something with energy, not only to serve as a tomb.
paper-on-the-moon-s-effect-on-lightning: A scientific paper called "The moon effect on lightning" is said to show that the moon affects how lightning behaves on Earth. The researcher Geoffrey Drumm, who studies the pyramids, brings up the paper on the show, naming it but not its authors. He uses it to support his idea that the moon plays a part in the electrical workings of the Earth.
paper-on-why-ufos-appear-near-nuclear-si: A former Army sergeant and remote viewer named Lyn Buchanan says he wrote a paper on why UFOs show up near nuclear sites such as Chernobyl. His answer is disturbances in spacetime. He says that if he is right, the reason they appear "has nothing to do with" the usual idea that they are interested in the weapons themselves.
paperclip-and-the-gehlen-network-as-a-ho: Operation Paperclip, the postwar US program that brought German scientists to America, and the absorption of the spy network of the German general Reinhard Gehlen into US intelligence were really a "homecoming", as if Nazi Germany had been set up as a field laboratory for highly unethical work. A philosopher and researcher named Jason Jorjani puts this forward as his own reading, naming no source, in a conversation about what he calls Hitler's secret UFO program.
paperclip-scientists-confirm-german-ufo-: In the 1960s, German scientists brought to America after the war under Operation Paperclip, a US programme that recruited experts from Nazi Germany, are said to have told astronauts at weekend meetings that Germany had worked on UFO-like craft. Robert Salas, a former Air Force officer, passes it on from what he was told: "other of the paperclip scientists from Nazi Germany confirmed this." If true, it would mean the astronauts heard it from the scientists themselves.
paperclip-scientists-in-new-mexico-mail-: In the late 1940s, scientists brought to New Mexico under Operation Paperclip, the American programme that recruited German scientists after the Second World War, went into nearby towns and mailed letters to Germany, which were then carried by courier to colleagues held in the Soviet Union. A researcher and author named Peter Levenda tells Michels this without naming a source. If true, it would mean American secrets had a quiet path straight to the Soviets.
paperclip-scientists-split-between-redst: After the Second World War, the German scientists brought to America under Operation Paperclip, a US programme that recruited former Nazi experts, were split in two, according to a former Pentagon official named Matthew Brown. He says the ones who were Nazis "in name only" settled around Redstone Arsenal, an Army rocket base in Huntsville, Alabama, while "the true believers" went to Los Alamos, the New Mexico weapons laboratory. Brown tells this without naming a source and links the split to later contact events, as if each group had a different role in them.
paperclip-scientists-work-on-the-magenta: After the war, some of the top German scientists who had worked for the Nazis were brought to Wright-Patterson Air Force Base in Dayton, Ohio, and put to work on the craft said to have crashed at Magenta in Italy. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, tying it to Operation Paperclip, the postwar program that brought German scientists to the United States. If true, the first American study of such a craft would have leaned on German expertise.
papoose-lake-map-altered-eight-days-afte: Government geological maps of Groom Lake and Papoose Lake, dry lake beds on the Nevada Test Site, were modified on May 23, 1989, which a researcher named Luigi Vendittelli points out was exactly eight days after Bob Lazar went public. Lazar is a man who in 1989 claimed he had worked on alien craft near Papoose Lake. Vendittelli says he found the date stamped on the US Department of the Interior maps himself, and if the timing is not chance it would mean the government changed its maps in response to Lazar's story.
paralysis-a-shimmering-object-golden-sym: A man says he once found he could not move, then saw a shimmering object appear, take full shape and touch him, giving him what he calls 'a true download' of knowledge. The researcher Deep Prasad tells this from his own experience. He says he moved his eyes left and right hoping the thing would go away, and when he looked back it had fully appeared, with 'the most enchanting and beautiful golden symbols' dancing at its center. In another part of the same episode, the guest places it in a 30th-floor condo in Toronto in 2019. He describes the shape as a visor that turned out to belong to a whole being, with face, suit and helmet. He adds that when unmasked, the beings looked like the Peruvian mummies, small bodies some people present as non-human. Only the man it happened to tells it, in a single episode. To him it was contact with something not human.
paranormal-activity-in-towns-after-nucle: After the 1945 Trinity test in New Mexico, the first atomic bomb explosion, people in nearby towns reported devils chasing them and all sorts of paranormal activity. Michels tells this himself without naming a source, first on an episode with the UFO researcher Jacques Vallee, and later he names Roswell too, the New Mexico town linked to a reported 1947 crash. He uses it to suggest that nuclear blasts may stir up strange happenings.
parapsychology-master-s-program-at-john-: Around 1980, John F. Kennedy University in California offered a master's degree in parapsychology, the study of things like telepathy and psychic ability. Jeffrey Mishlove, a PhD who says he taught there at the time, mentions it in passing. He tells it as part of his own background, showing that a university once treated the subject as a field of graduate study.
parapsychology-programs-at-elite-us-univ: Several top American universities once had research programs in parapsychology, the study of psychic abilities: the Rhine Center linked to Duke, a lab at Princeton, and SRI, a research institute connected to Stanford. Michels tells this himself in two episodes, and in the later one he adds that these programs concluded there seems to be a "constricted present", meaning the present moment is not as sharply cut off from the future as we assume. It is told to show that serious institutions took such questions seriously.
parents-see-a-hooded-being-in-their-bedr: One night in the 1950s, near Allentown, Pennsylvania, a couple are said to have seen a hooded being standing in their bedroom. Their son, Jim Weiner, who has his own account of being taken by aliens, says he never knew about it until Ray Fowler, a UFO investigator, interviewed his mother. It would suggest such visits ran in the family.
parsons-and-hubbard-s-babylon-working-19: In 1946 in Pasadena, the rocket scientist Jack Parsons and L. Ron Hubbard, the man who later founded Scientology, carried out a magic ritual called the Babylon Working, an attempt to summon a divine female figure known as Babylon. Michels tells it himself, linking it to the English occultist Aleister Crowley and his novel Moonchild, as part of a case that occult practice was tangled up in the early American space program.
parsons-crater-and-jack-parsons-laborato: The rocket pioneer Jack Parsons is said to be honoured in two ways: a crater on the Moon bears his name, and at JPL, the Jet Propulsion Laboratory, NASA's rocket and spacecraft centre in Pasadena, California, "some insiders still call it Jack Parsons Laboratory." Michels says this himself, without naming a source, as a sign of how central Parsons was to American rocketry.
parsons-death-in-a-home-lab-explosion-19: In 1952 the rocket scientist Jack Parsons died in an explosion in his home laboratory in Pasadena, which was officially ruled an accident with volatile chemicals, though some found the circumstances suspicious. Michels tells this himself, without naming who those doubters were. The story is told because, if the death was no accident, it would cast a shadow over an early pioneer of American rocketry.
parsons-invokes-bartzabel-against-hubbar: In 1946, the rocket engineer and occultist Jack Parsons is said to have been so furious with L. Ron Hubbard, the man who later founded Scientology, that he tried a magical counterattack: in a Miami hotel room he called on Bartzabel, the spirit of the planet Mars in ritual magic. Michels tells the story himself, without naming a source, in an episode on NASA, pagan rituals and secret science.
parsons-past-life-regression-as-simon-th: The American rocket engineer Jack Parsons is said to have gone through a past-life regression, a practice of recalling supposed earlier lives, and found that he had been Simon the Sorcerer, an ancient magician figure. Michels tells this himself, and in another episode places it in the OTO, an occult society linked to the English occultist Aleister Crowley, where he says such regressions were done. It is told as part of the strange link between early rocketry and the occult.
part-of-a-program-shut-down-as-demonic-t: Part of a secret US government research programme was once shut down because some people felt American taxpayers' money should not pay for chasing "demonic technology". The physicist Hal Puthoff, who has worked on government studies of unexplained phenomena, says this on Michels's show from his own experience inside the work. He does not say which programme it was or when it happened, but if true it would mean religious objections have shaped what the government is willing to study.
parthian-feudal-houses-rule-iran-for-ove: The Parthians, an ancient dynasty, ruled Iran directly for 400 years, and their noble families kept power there for more than a thousand years in all. A researcher named Jason Jorjani says this, opening with "So, get this." He means it to show how long one ruling bloodline held on behind the scenes.
party-crasher-jc-knows-the-unaired-dark-: In 1996, a stranger calling himself JC is said to have turned up at a party at the Los Angeles home of Bryce Zabel, co-creator of Dark Skies, a TV series about a government cover-up of aliens. He claimed to have seen the show's first episode before it aired. Zabel tells it himself: JC wanted "to congratulate me on a successful show" and said, "You guys got a lot right." Brent Friedman, a writer on the series who was there, adds that JC said he was from the Office of Naval Intelligence, the Navy's spy service, and offered them access to information if they would help with a "slow drip disclosure program," a gradual release of the truth about aliens to the public. If true, a military intelligence office was trying to use Hollywood to prepare people for that truth.
parviz-jafari-s-1976-tehran-ufo-encounte: An Iranian fighter pilot named Parviz Jafari is said to have had a dramatic UFO encounter over Tehran in the mid 1970s while flying an F-4 Phantom jet, a case also studied by the Defense Intelligence Agency, a US military spy office. The UFO investigator James Fox says he met Jafari himself, through the writer Leslie Kean, and dates it to around 1975, while Michels later retells it from Fox as a 1979 case in which the pilot fired at the object. If true, it would be a military pilot facing an object he could not stop.
pascagoula-abduction-near-a-nuclear-sub-: In 1973 two men, Charles Hickson and Calvin Parker, said they were taken by aliens while fishing near Pascagoula, Mississippi, examined, and then let go. Jesse Michels brings the case up several times. In one telling he credits a researcher named Luigi Vendittelli with pointing out that Pascagoula was where the Navy built nuclear submarines, though there he puts the town in Missouri, and in another he dates it to 1974. The researcher Richard Dolan also tells it, saying the men were abducted off the Mississippi coast, without mentioning the shipyard. Michels raises it as one of many UFO stories said to cluster around nuclear sites.
passing-massive-body-rearranged-the-plan: Long ago, a huge object passed through our solar system, and its gravity shifted the planets and stripped away Mars's air. A guest named Joe McMoneagle offers this idea on Michels's show, without naming a source. If true, it would explain how Mars could once have held life and then lost it.
past-experimental-interbreeding-between-: Aliens and humans have interbred in the past as an experiment. Dan Sherman, a former Air Force sergeant who says the NSA, the US government's signals intelligence agency, hired him around 1990 to 1993 to communicate with aliens, says he got that impression from those communications. If true, some humans would carry the results of earlier alien breeding experiments.
past-extraterrestrial-presence-on-the-mo: Beings from elsewhere were once present on the Moon and on Mars, says a guest identified only as Max, who calls this "the inference to the best explanation of this cumulative data." He gives it to Michels as his own conclusion from the evidence taken together, without naming a source, in an episode about what he sees as a secret kept by NASA, the US space agency.
pastor-apologizes-for-misattributing-the: A pastor publicly apologized in 2026 for saying that a US congressman named Eric Burlison held the view that all UFO encounters are demons, according to Burlison himself. Burlison, who took part in the events around the US government's UFO hearings that year, says the pastor came out afterwards and said Burlison never said this. He tells it to correct the record about what he believes.
pasulka-and-the-vatican-archives: The religious studies professor Diana Pasulka has visited the Vatican archives, the Catholic Church's private collection of records, and speaks with conviction that the Church knows more about UFOs than it lets on. Michels brings this up himself, without naming a source, while listing people who might hold pieces of the hidden story.
pasulka-and-vallee-aliens-as-the-modern-: The idea is that the aliens people report today are the modern version of what earlier ages called angels and demons. Michels says two people hold this view: a religious studies professor named Diana Pasulka and a French UFO researcher named Jacques Vallée. If they are right, UFO sightings would belong to a very old human story rather than a new one.
pasulka-finds-space-program-records-clas: When she began her research in 2012, Diana Pasulka, an academic who studies religion and belief in UFOs, says she did the usual scholarly search for records on the space programme and saw right away how much of it was classified. She tells this from her own experience. She raises it because it suggests that much of what she set out to study was kept out of public view from the start.
pasulka-meets-garry-nolan-and-sees-his-i: Around 2014, the religious studies professor Diana Pasulka met a scientist named Garry Nolan, and he showed her his own research into injuries. Pasulka tells this from her own memory, saying Nolan had been recruited into the same circle of UFO research at about the same time she was. It matters to the story because it places two serious academics being drawn into this work early on.
pasulka-meets-tyler-and-begins-an-emerge: A man named Tyler, said to belong to a secret tradition of people who quietly know about UFOs, met a scholar and the two began working together, opening up "a transparency that we've never seen before." Diana Pasulka, a professor who studies religion and UFOs, tells this about her own meeting with Tyler over the years from about 2010. She presents it as a rare case of the hidden side sharing what it knows.
pasulka-s-encounters-source-daughter-of-: One source in Encounters, a 2023 book by the writer Diana Pasulka, was the daughter of a man Pasulka believed worked in a secret space program, meaning a hidden government space effort. The daughter said her father kept using the word "simulacra", meaning copies that stand in for something real, at lunch with his colleagues. Michels repeats this from the book in an episode about whether we live in a hologram, and says it always gives him chills.
pasulka-s-research-on-historical-angelic: While researching Heaven Can Wait, her 2014 book on Purgatory, a religious studies professor named Diana Pasulka of the University of North Carolina Wilmington began documenting dozens of historical cases of nuns, priests, brothers and saints, Francis of Assisi among them, who reported direct contact with God or angels. Michels tells this himself, describing some of those accounts as resembling modern alien abduction stories, which would tie religious visions to UFO experience.
pat-price-remote-views-a-file-inside-a-c: In the 1970s Pat Price, a remote viewer, meaning someone who tried to see distant places with the mind alone, is said to have described a file inside a top-security CIA facility in the United States. A lawyer named Dan Sheehan tells it, saying "it's a top CIA security facility", and links it to the researcher Russell Targ and to reports written by another remote viewer, Ingo Swann. If true, it would mean secrets could be read from afar without entering the building.
