pat-price-remote-views-denied-soviet-sit: In the early 1970s, a psychic named Pat Price, working in a US government programme on remote viewing, meaning the claimed ability to describe distant places using only the mind, is said to have described secret Soviet sites accurately, including machinery, a big tower and large steel spheres. Joe McMoneagle, an Army officer who later became a remote viewer in the same programme, tells this as something he learned about Price's work. If true, it would mean the mind can gather spy information from places no one could visit.
pat-price-remote-views-underground-base-: In 1973, a psychic spy named Pat Price is said to have used remote viewing, an attempt to see distant places with the mind alone, to describe a huge underground base inside Mount Hayes in Alaska, with advanced technology, control consoles and staff who looked military. Michels tells this himself, saying it happened in a remote viewing programme run by the CIA, the US Central Intelligence Agency, and that Price named three more bases: Mount Perdido in Spain, Mount Inyangani in Zimbabwe and Mount Ziel in Australia. A former Army sergeant named Lyn Buchanan, who joined the unit later, repeats what he heard: that Price saw four alien bases, in work he calls Project 8200, done before he arrived. In other episodes Michels says the work was run by a man named Skip Atwater, and calls the bases alien, though he tells it with less certainty there. If true, it would mean hidden bases, possibly not human, sit inside mountains around the world.
pat-price-remotely-reads-a-file-inside-a: In the 1970s, a man named Pat Price is said to have become so good at remote viewing, the practice of trying to describe a faraway place with the mind alone, that he could describe a secret government site he had never seen. A guest named Dan Sheehan tells it from a file he says he saw, crediting it alongside Russell Targ and Ingo Swann and a document he calls the "Ingo Swann file." In his telling, Price was given "the exact longitude and latitude" of a top-security facility of the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency, and was able to read a file inside it. A guest named Joe McMoneagle tells it differently, passing on what Targ and Hal Puthoff told him. He says Price was sent to describe "this old Cabin in the Woods" but instead "described a clandestine site" close by. To both tellers, this would mean the mind can reach places that walls and secrecy are meant to keep shut.
pat-price-s-death-linked-to-psychokinesi: Pat Price, a man who took part in US government psychic research in the 1970s, died because he was recruited into a secret program on psychokinesis, moving things with the mind, given certain operations, and came to have serious moral doubts about them. The philosopher Jason Jorjani offers this as his own reading of events, not as something he witnessed. If true, it would mean the program was willing to silence its own people.
patents-for-a-memory-erasing-neuralizer-: A man named Chris Bledsoe, who says UFOs come to him and that NASA studies him, says he has seen US patents for technology that can wipe memories, like the "neuralizer" gadget from the Men in Black films. He tells it first hand, saying he "learned some stuff on that," as a hint that such memory-erasing tools are real.
path-of-souls-the-soul-s-leap-to-orion-a: The writer Graham Hancock says that peoples across North, Central and South America shared a belief called the path of souls, in which the soul at death leaps to the constellation Orion and then travels along the Milky Way. He tells it from his own research, which he also presented in his television series Ancient Apocalypse, and he raises it because a shared belief across so many places would point to a common ancient source.
pathologist-attributes-infection-to-the-: In Varginha, Brazil, in 1996, a man named Marco Chereze died of an infection that, according to people involved, came from a scratch by the claw of a strange being captured in the town. A doctor named Armando, who says he took part, points to Chereze's autopsy report and describes "a very distinct and deliberate scratch" on his skin. A surgeon named Ahmed Foratu, whose hospital he says operated on the being, gives this as the second of two explanations: that Chereze "contracted the infection from a scratch, from contact with an extraterrestrial being." He credits Dr. Jannini and Italo Venturelli with the idea. If true, a human would have died from contact with a living non-human creature.
patient-17-s-implant-cut-from-his-leg-an: A man known only as Patient 17 had a small object, said to be an alien implant, cut out of his leg, and it was then tested for zinc-64, a particular form of the element zinc, according to Jeremy Corbell, a maker of UFO documentaries who says he watched it being removed. Corbell calls the case terrifying and says the man only told him his story after Corbell had seen the removal. He links it to the work of Roger Leir, a surgeon who removed such objects, and of Jacques Vallée, a computer scientist and longtime UFO researcher.
patrick-afb-helicopter-flies-out-to-the-: Off Cocoa Beach, Florida, in 2013, a helicopter from Patrick Air Force Base, a nearby US Air Force base, flew out toward a strange light the witnesses were watching. Charles Buhler, a NASA engineer who says he saw it himself, tells it. To him the helicopter going out to it shows the military also noticed the light and took it seriously.
patrick-jackson-s-theory-of-spheres-as-a: The idea is that mysterious spheres seen in the sky are part of a worldwide defense system set up by an alien civilization to keep the bad guys away from Earth. Ross Coulthart, an Australian investigative journalist, relays this as the theory of a man named Patrick Jackson. If true, it would mean someone out there is protecting the planet rather than threatening it.
patton-s-army-rushes-to-pilsen-before-be: Near the end of the Second World War in 1945, the army of the American general Patton is said to have raced to Pilsen, a city in Czechoslovakia, before heading for Berlin. A researcher named Jason Simosa says it, calling the choice "very interesting." He hints that something at Pilsen mattered more to the Americans than the German capital.
paul-eluard-s-mantis-collection-and-cail: The French poet Paul Éluard, one of the founders of surrealism, an art movement built on dreams and the unconscious, kept a huge collection of praying mantises in his home. The philosopher Jason Jorjani tells this on the show without naming a source, linking it to Éluard's friend, the writer Roger Caillois, who studied folklore about the mantis. Jorjani brings it up as a sign that these early surrealists were deeply taken with the mantis.
paul-feyerabend-s-astrology-chart-and-hi: In the 1970s, when a group of scientists put out a public statement condemning astrology, the philosopher of science Paul Feyerabend rebuked them, and when he published his book Against Method he put an astrology chart on its back page. The parapsychology researcher Jeffrey Mishlove tells this as an example of a serious thinker refusing to let scientists dismiss a subject they had not studied.
paul-hellyer-briefed-by-greer-press-conf: Paul Hellyer, a former Canadian minister of defence, is said to have come forward publicly about UFOs in the 2000s, partly because of Steven Greer, an American activist who campaigns for UFO disclosure. Greer tells this himself. He says he was "one of the reasons why he came out publicly" and that the two of them held a press conference together in Toronto. In the same conversation, Greer also mentions The Day After Roswell, a book by Philip Corso, a former Army officer. Charlie Foltz, a man who says he was abducted, also recalls Hellyer coming forward to describe UFOs, though he calls Hellyer Canada's prime minister and says nothing of Greer or Toronto. The story matters because a senior Western defence official speaking out lends weight to the subject.
paul-hellyer-dying-canadian-emergency-ma: A dying man who had headed Canada's emergency management office is said to have confessed that he was taken to Langley, Virginia, home of the CIA, the US spy agency, where he "signed my life away", and then flown to Area 51, a secret US military base in Nevada, where he sat inside a craft. Grant Cameron, a UFO researcher, relays this from Paul Hellyer, a former Canadian defence minister, who heard the confession. If true, it would mean the US held a craft and showed it to a senior Canadian official under oath of secrecy.
paul-mccartney-s-flaming-pie-dream-and-t: Paul McCartney, one of the Beatles, is said to have had a dream about a flaming pie, a vision tied to the story of how the band got its name. Michels brings it up himself, from memory and without naming a source. He tells it as an example of an idea arriving through a dream or vision.
paul-mellon-brought-back-a-nazi-flying-d: Near the end of the Second World War, around 1945, a man named Paul Mellon is said to have seen a German flying disc, a saucer-shaped craft, in a hangar, and in some versions to have stood on it or brought it back, together with the American intelligence man Allen Dulles. The source is Mellon's grandson, John Warner IV, who says his grandfather told him himself, in one version over a third martini; Warner tells it on the show, and Michels and the UFO researcher Steven Greer repeat it. The tellers disagree on the details: Greer says Mellon admitted going to get a Nazi disc, Warner says only that they saw one in a hangar, and Michels places it at Pilsen in what is now the Czech Republic, sometimes in 1944, with the two men on a tech retrieval mission, which would mean American officials recovered such a craft before 1947.
paul-mellon-s-family-and-support-for-fas: In the 1930s and early 1940s, a wealthy American named Paul Mellon, or his family, is said to have been a huge supporter of Adolf Hitler and fascism, along with the carmaker Henry Ford and Watson, the head of the computer company IBM. Steven Greer, a guest who argues that UFO secrets are held by a global ruling circle, repeats this from a man named John Warner IV, who he says told him directly. If it were true, some of the great American fortunes of that era would have backed fascism, which feeds Greer's picture of who holds the secrets.
paul-mellon-s-walking-stick: Harold Malmgren, an economist who advised several US presidents and says he handled UFO material himself, recalls being shown a walking stick in Virginia and being told it belonged to Paul Mellon, a very wealthy American banker's son and art collector. Malmgren repeats only what he was told, and gives nothing more about why the stick mattered.
paul-muller-confiscates-and-destroys-val: In the early 1960s, a young French scientist named Jacques Vallée, working at an observatory in France, recorded tracking data on a tape of an object in the sky, and his boss there, an astronomer named Paul Muller, is said to have taken the tape the next morning and destroyed it. Michels tells this himself, in the words "Muller, who behaved like a petty army officer, simply confiscated the tape and destroyed it," without naming a source, in an episode with the astronomer Beatriz Villarroel. It is told as an early case of scientists throwing away evidence of unknown objects.
paul-s-ascent-to-the-third-heaven: The Apostle Paul, the early Christian leader, is said to have described his own rise into the heavens, to what he called the third heaven. Michels tells this himself, citing Paul's letter known as Second Corinthians in the Bible, and says some scholars think Paul knew of ancient practices of journeying up to the heavens. If true, it would mean such mystical journeys were part of Christianity from its very beginning.
paul-s-merkabah-conversion: The Apostle Paul, the early Christian leader who began by persecuting Christians, "wanting Christians to die," was turned around by a merkabah experience, a vision of the kind Jewish mystics describe as seeing God's heavenly chariot. That is how the researcher Diana Pasulka tells it to Michels, stressing that the vision "happened just spontaneously to him" and was not something he sought. She uses it to link old religious visions to modern encounters with strange beings.
paul-smith-remote-views-the-uss-stark-at: In 1987, during the war between Iran and Iraq, a man named Paul Smith says he was given a target in a US government psychic spy program and began, in his words, "describing this vessel, which reminded me of an American destroyer." He ties this to the attack on the USS Stark, an American Navy warship hit in the Persian Gulf that year. Smith tells it as his own session in remote viewing, the practice of trying to describe a distant place or event with the mind alone. He names a colleague, Skip Atwater, and points to the Washington Post for the record, and if it is true, a psychic picked up a real attack from far away.
paul-thigpen-s-path-from-the-woo-to-cath: A man named Paul Thigpen ran into what people call "the woo", strange paranormal experiences, and that pushed him to search for the truth, a search that ended with him becoming Catholic. A guest named Dylan Borland passes this on as Thigpen's own story, as an example of how such encounters can lead a person toward religion.
paula-harris-gets-an-audrey-call-about-c: A woman named Paola Harris was looking at Crestone, a small town in Colorado, and thinking to herself how beautiful it was and that she would like to go. Just then the phone rang. It was someone named Audrey, who told her not to worry, she would go back. The researcher Grant Cameron passes this on as something Harris told him, and he mentions the campaigner Steven Greer alongside it. It is told as a call that seemed to answer a thought Harris had never said out loud.
paulina-zelitsky-s-sunken-city-off-cuba-: A researcher named Paulina Zelitsky, who reported finding a sunken city on the seabed off western Cuba, is said to have gone to Mexico in the early 2010s to look into a link between the two places, and there to have been arrested, badly intimidated by the authorities and sent back to Canada. The philosopher Jason Jorjani tells this on the show as something passed on from Zelitsky's own account, and he also brings up the magazine National Geographic in connection with it. Told this way, it suggests someone did not want that link looked into.
pax-river-facility-for-lockheed-to-bigel: A congressman named Eric Burlison says that in 2025 he stood on site at Naval Air Station Patuxent River in Maryland, known as Pax River, and saw the facility that was meant to receive a transfer from the defense company Lockheed Martin to Bigelow Aerospace, a company owned by a businessman named Robert Bigelow. If true, it would point to some hidden holding passing from one company to another. Burlison tells it first-hand on the show, Michels later repeats him as saying that if a craft were stored anywhere it would be at Pax River, and a Pentagon whistleblower named Matthew Brown adds that Burlison got a tour but was shown nothing resembling technology of unknown origin.
paynter-lands-at-the-wrong-airport-on-th: In 1974, a man named Bill Paynter, flying to Chico, California, landed at the wrong airport. John S. Herrington, a former US Secretary of Energy, tells this as something he was part of, and says it plainly: "Painter has landed at the wrong airport." He gives it as one moment in a longer account of his own.
pdni-memo-waives-uap-ndas-2026: In 2026, the second-ranking official in US intelligence, a man named Aaron Lucas, is said to have sent out a memo, by the president's order, saying that anyone with knowledge of unidentified flying objects who had signed a nondisclosure agreement, a contract promising secrecy, would be released from it. A retired Navy admiral named Tim Gallaudet tells it as recent news, saying "the NDAs will be waived," which would free insiders to speak openly.
pearly-white-saucer-seen-on-closed-circu: In 1992 a pearly white saucer about 20 feet across showed up on a closed-circuit video feed at Cape Canaveral, the Florida rocket launch base, says Greg Rogers, a NASA doctor who says he saw it himself. He describes it this way: "there's a saucer 20 ft across. It was sort of like a modified egg." If true, an unknown craft was being watched at one of the country's main launch sites.
pendulums-are-the-most-common-artifact-i: Chris Bledsoe, a man who says UFOs have been drawn to him for years, says that when people dig in the soil of Egypt, the most common ancient object they find is the pendulum, a weight hung on a cord. He passes it on from a teacher named Robert Gilbert. If true, it would hint that the ancient Egyptians used pendulums for some important everyday purpose.
penetration-appeared-without-swann-ever-: Ingo Swann was a psychic who worked in American government research on remote viewing, the practice of trying to describe distant places by mind alone. In 1998 he published a book called Penetration, and according to Joe McMoneagle, it took even those close to him by surprise. McMoneagle, a remote viewer who worked in the same field and knew Swann, says on the show that the book "came right out of the clear blue" and that Swann "never spoke a word of it" beforehand.
penkovsky-papers-a-nazi-psychic-unit-tak: Adolf Hitler had a psychic unit in Germany, which the Soviets later took over, according to reading material in Russian credited to a Soviet colonel named Igor Pinkovski. Lyn Buchanan, a former US Army sergeant who worked as a psychic spy, says he read this himself while learning Russian at a language school in Monterey, California, and that it said Hitler "had a unit called Dr. Grunbomb". If true, it would mean psychic spying passed from the Nazis to the Soviets.
penniston-given-sodium-pentothal-in-inte: Jim Penniston, a witness to strange events at a Royal Air Force base in England called Bentwaters around 1980, said he was later given a drug, something like sodium pentothal (a drug sometimes called truth serum), and then questioned. The researcher Robert Hastings, who studies UFO reports at nuclear bases, passes this on as what Penniston told him. Michels speaks of the same case, known as the Rendlesham Forest case, and of its witnesses in general rather than of Penniston by name. If true, it would mean the military drugged its own men to find out what they had seen.
penniston-s-career-stalled-after-rendles: A US Air Force airman named Jim Penniston, a witness to the 1980 UFO sighting in Rendlesham Forest in England, is said to have never reached the rank he probably could have because he was a witness. Michels raises this himself in a talk with the UFO investigator James Fox, without giving a source. If true, it would mean speaking up about a sighting can quietly cost a military career.
penniston-s-sphere-of-influence-near-the: Near the craft reported in Rendlesham Forest in England in 1980, a US airman named Jim Penniston said he entered what he called a "sphere of influence", where walking felt like moving through water. A researcher named Mike Masters repeats this on the show without naming a source. It is told as a sign that the object changed the space around it.
penniston-touches-craft-and-receives-bin: In 1980, in Rendlesham Forest in England, a man named Jim Penniston says he touched an unknown craft and found its surface smooth like glass, with strange symbols carved on its side that looked like hieroglyphs. After touching it, he says, a flood of binary code, the ones and zeros that computers use, came into his mind by telepathy. Michels relays Penniston's account in an episode about UFOs and nuclear bases. If true, it would mean the craft passed a message straight into a witness's head.
pentagon-confirms-navy-thermal-footage: A piece of thermal camera footage, filmed in heat-sensing infrared, shows an unexplained object, and according to Jeremy Corbell, a filmmaker who reports on UFOs, the Pentagon has "confirmed" that "it is actual Navy filmed footage." Corbell says this in an episode about the physicist J. Robert Oppenheimer. If he is right, the US military has admitted the video is real and its own.
pentagon-press-release-denying-the-kanda: The Kandahar giant story says American troops in Afghanistan fought and captured a twelve-foot giant near the city of Kandahar. A guest named Tim Alberino, who discusses the story with Jesse Michels, says he saw something that looked like an official Pentagon press release saying "the Kandahar giant story is not true." He brings it up as a sign that the military took notice of the tale, though he does not say when the release appeared.
pentagon-records-of-ufo-detections-and-t: The Pentagon is said to hold hundreds of cases where UFOs were picked up by cameras, radar and heat-sensing infrared sensors, and from those records the Department of Defense is said to have set out five "observable" traits that come up again and again. Michels says this himself in an episode with a young physicist, citing the researcher Eric Weinstein, and he does not list the five traits there. He raises it as the starting point for anyone trying to work out how such craft might fly.
pentagon-review-of-the-ornl-report-on-ar: In August 2024, a group met in a Pentagon conference room to read a full 90-page materials analysis from Oak Ridge National Laboratory, a US government research lab, on a set of metal fragments known as "Art's Parts", and found nothing there. A scientist named Eric W. Davis says he was in the room with his colleague Hal Puthoff and read the report himself. If he is right, the lab's tests on these much-discussed fragments turned up nothing out of the ordinary.
pentagon-says-only-three-uap-videos-exis: After some military videos of UAP, short for unidentified anomalous phenomena, the official term for UFOs, were released, the Pentagon said there were no more videos beyond those three, and then another branch of the military admitted it had more. The journalist Michael Shellenberger tells this, crediting John Greenewald Jr., a researcher who collects government records. If true, it would mean the Pentagon's answer did not cover everything the military held.
people-across-varginha-report-seeing-spa: People all over the Brazilian city of Varginha say they have seen spaceships, according to Ahmed Foratu, a guest who speaks as a witness on an episode about a hospital said to have operated on an alien. "If you walk throughout the city," he tells Michels, "there are always reports of people who have seen spaceships." He passes this on as what he has heard from people around town, and if it is true, sightings there are an ordinary part of local life rather than a single event.
people-missing-from-native-cultures-trac: People sometimes go mysteriously missing from native communities, Michels says, and he knows someone who studies this by looking through census records. He tells it himself as something he has heard, without naming the researcher, in a conversation about psychic experiences and the unexplained.
people-who-say-they-worked-on-recovered-: There are people who say they worked on crashed craft of unknown origin recovered by the US government, or at least saw them. Kevin Knuth, a guest billed in his episode as a whistleblower from NASA, the US space agency, says he has met such people himself, though he does not name them or say what they told him beyond that claim. If they were right, the government would be holding and studying such craft.
people-who-spoke-out-on-the-program-have: People who were coming forward to talk about a secret program that recovers crashed UFOs have died, according to Jake Barber, a former helicopter pilot who says he flew a UFO out of a crash site himself. Barber says this from the inside, as someone who works for and with the groups involved. In a second remark he goes further: he says he knows for a fact that leaders within those groups have called for "wet works", a slang term for killings. If true, it would mean people are being silenced for speaking out.
percival-lowell-s-martian-irrigation-can: The astronomer Percival Lowell went so far as to claim that some of the dark areas and lines seen on Mars were irrigation canals built on purpose by a Martian civilization. Michels tells this himself, as part of the history of ideas about life on Mars, without naming a source. If Lowell had been right, Mars would once have held intelligent builders.
perelman-s-unspoken-unified-theory: Grigori Perelman, a Russian mathematician who lives quietly and refuses public honours, is said to claim he has a unified theory, an explanation tying all of physics together, but will not talk about it. Michels brings this up himself as something he has heard, hedging with "I think he claims." If true, a major key to the universe would be sitting unspoken with one man.
person-harmed-when-the-gauntlet-object-w: Someone may have been hurt while recovering an unusual object he calls "the gauntlet", according to Randy Anderson, a man who says he saw what he believed was alien technology at a military base, the Naval Surface Warfare Center Crane in Indiana, around 2014. Anderson says this came up while he was there; he does not say he saw the harm himself, only that "somebody was potentially harmed in the retrieval of that item". If true, it would mean the object was dangerous to handle.
peru-bill-banning-study-of-ancient-biolo: In 2025, Peru put forward a bill that would forbid the study of ancient biological specimens, meaning very old remains of living things. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, and guesses it was probably a response to a video his own show had made, which would mean his work had reached lawmakers in another country.
peruvian-face-peeler-alien-attacks-2023: In 2023, villagers in San Antonio de Pintoyaku, a remote place in the Alto Nanay region of the Peruvian Amazon, said they were being attacked at night by beings some called aliens and others called "pelacaras", which means "face peelers". The filmmaker and researcher Tim Alberino tells this, partly from what a man he names only as Doug told him, and says the raids always began after dark with two small flying saucers hovering in the air, followed by armoured attackers on hoverboards. If true, it would be a recent, violent encounter with something not human.
peruvian-government-shifts-to-tacit-endo: The Peruvian government was dead set against the case of the strange three-fingered bodies found in Peru, until September 2024, when it began quietly backing research at the University of Ica that might show the bodies are real. Michels says so himself, citing a man named David Ruiz, whom he counts as a witness. If true, it would mean Peru's officials went from dismissing the bodies to taking them seriously.
peruvian-tribe-warns-that-the-undergroun: A tribe in Peru warns that the "ant people", beings said to live underground, are sinister and best left alone. In the tribe's words, as a guest named Jay Anderson repeats them from what he was told: "Don't mess with it."
peruvian-tridactyl-mummies-scanned-2025: In 2025, Michels says, he went to Peru and watched mummified bodies with three fingers and three toes being scanned, and came back saying "I just might have seen a dead alien" and that it "broke my brain a little bit." He tells it as something he saw himself, alongside the fellow witnesses Michael Mazzola and Ammar Kandil and a man named Brigham Buhler. He adds that forensic experts say the skulls show no sign of the head-binding rituals you would expect from the people of the region.
pete-worden-connected-tom-delonge-and-ge: Pete Worden, a former senior NASA official, is said to have introduced the musician Tom DeLonge, who later took up UFO research, to the retired Air Force general Neil McCasland, sometime in the 2010s. Michels says this himself, adding that it is public information. It is told to show how a space official helped link a celebrity UFO effort with a senior military figure.
pete-worden-knows-more-about-nasa-ufo-kn: A guest named Maaneli Derakhshani says he has heard that certain people, among them a man named Pete Worden, know a lot more than is public about what NASA, the US space agency, knows about UFOs. He passes this on as something others told him, without saying who, and if true it would mean the space agency holds UFO knowledge it has not shared.
peter-garyaev-s-retracted-nobel-nominati: A Russian researcher named Peter Garyaev, linked to an idea called linguistic wave genetics, is said to have been nominated for the Nobel Prize, the top award in science, in 2019 or 2020, only for the nomination to be withdrawn, and he later died, in the teller's words, "I believe, under mysterious circumstances." Dave Rossi, a guest who says he was taught advanced physics by non-human beings, tells this as a researcher summarising, crediting a website on linguistic wave genetics rather than any person. He raises it as a sign that this kind of work gets pushed aside.
peter-jennings-ufo-special-cut-by-90-fol: In 2005, a television special on UFOs presented by the ABC news anchor Peter Jennings went on air with most of its material cut out, according to a researcher named Jason Jorjani. He says "what they aired excluded 90% of the material," and the story as he tells it ends with Jennings's death soon after. If true, it would mean much of what the program found was held back from viewers.
peter-thiel-almost-intercepted-over-ener: Steven Greer, a longtime UFO activist, says the tech investor Peter Thiel was nearly intercepted, or stopped, because of his interest in a secret energy technology. Greer says he got a warning from a senior insider in a group he calls the MOCI, which he does not spell out here, and quietly passed it on to the mathematician Eric Weinstein. If true, it would mean powerful people are watched and blocked when they get near hidden energy secrets.
peter-thiel-on-joe-rogan-aliens-must-be-: In 2024 the investor Peter Thiel went on The Joe Rogan Experience, the talk show hosted by Joe Rogan, and spent about half the conversation on aliens. Thiel argued there that if aliens are real, they must be something like angels or demons, and he cited the work of the religion scholar Diana Pasulka. Michels told Pasulka about it on his show in December 2024, saying it had happened a month earlier. In a later episode Thiel's reasoning is given in his own words, with no date and no mention of Pasulka: "If you have faster than light travel, there's something really crazy that has to be true on a cultural, political, social level."
peterson-and-cia-director-woolsey-invite: In the early 1990s, a man named John Peterson and his wife, along with James Woolsey, then director of the CIA, and his wife, are said to have invited Steven Greer, a doctor who campaigns for the release of UFO secrets, to dinner near Washington. The UFO historian Richard Dolan tells this as something he heard from the people involved. If true, it would mean the head of the CIA was quietly sitting down with a leading UFO campaigner.
peterson-offered-to-show-fitts-a-ufo-if-: In 1998, a man named John Peterson, connected to a place called the Arlington Institute, is said to have promised to show a researcher named Katherine Austin Fitz a UFO if she would stop her research. Michels tells this himself, in an episode with the guest Richard Dolan, as something passed on from people involved, and he also names a woman called Linda Thompson in connection with it. If true, it would mean someone was offering a look at a UFO as a bargain to make an inquiry go away.
phantom-radar-contact-near-the-anomaly-2: In 2011, at the site of a strange object on the floor of the Baltic Sea, a radar showed something about 150 meters from the dive boat, but when the crew looked, nothing was there and they were alone. Dennis Asberg, a Swedish treasure hunter whose team found the object, says he saw it himself, and a man named Peter Lindberg is part of the telling. He tells it as one of several odd events around the expedition.
pharaoh-s-soul-guided-through-seven-pala: In the Pyramid Texts, the oldest religious writings of ancient Egypt, priests lead the soul of the pharaoh, Egypt's king, through seven "areet", a word Michels says also means palaces. Michels tells this himself, dating the texts to 2400 BC, in an episode about the idea that we live in a hologram. He raises it to show that the image of seven palaces goes back to the very oldest scripture we have.
pharaoh-statues-of-past-and-future-outsi: Outside the California headquarters of SAIC, a large US defense contractor, there are said to be two pharaoh statues, one standing for the past and one for the future. Jay Anderson, a researcher of UFO history, says the musician Tom DeLonge, who in 2017 was promoting his UFO research company, told people about the statues back then. It is told as a hint that the contractor sees itself as a keeper of hidden, ancient knowledge.
phenomena-seen-everywhere-near-sensitive: Someone once told the researcher Eric Weinstein that he did not need the government to show him anything about these mysterious objects. In Weinstein's retelling, the advice was: "You can just go up and look for yourself," because if you get close to sensitive sites, you will "see these things everywhere."
phenomena-showing-up-around-nuclear-base: Unexplained objects keep showing up around nuclear weapons bases. A writer on lost ancient civilisations named Graham Hancock mentions this in passing, without naming a source or a base, and simply calls it interesting.
phenomenon-lines-up-in-triangles-or-thre: Unexplained lights in the sky always try to line up in a triangle or in groups of three, according to Chris Bledsoe, a man who says UFOs appear around him and who has been studied by NASA scientists. Bledsoe says he has many videos of this from his skywatching nights, starting around 2012, and tells Michels he will see it for himself if they go out watching together.
philadelphia-experiment-actually-happene: The Philadelphia Experiment, a well-known story that the US Navy made a ship vanish or teleport in Philadelphia during the Second World War, actually took place in Rhode Island, and Philadelphia was only "the cover story," according to a researcher named Steven Greer. Greer tells Michels this while citing a man named Bob Beckwith. Others tell the same old story as a ship teleportation or as a cover for a nuclear accident.
philadelphia-experiment-and-townsend-bro: The story goes that the Navy ran a real secret project in 1943 around Philadelphia and Norfolk, Virginia, which became famous as the Philadelphia Experiment, and that a scientist named Thomas Townsend Brown ran it and had a nervous breakdown around that time. Michels tells this himself across several episodes, at times citing a 1943 FBI file on Brown (the FBI is the US federal police agency) and the researcher Bill Moore. In one episode he says Brown told his friend Josh Reynolds late in life that the experiment "did happen, its events were just greatly exaggerated." In other episodes he leaves that remark out and simply says Brown led it, which, if true, would mean a real wartime programme sits under the popular legend.
philadelphia-experiment-as-cover-for-nuc: The Philadelphia Experiment, the famous tale that the US Navy made a warship vanish in 1943, may have been a cover story for an accident: a turbine blew up and sailors were sprayed with a radioactive fluid, hexafluoride. A researcher named Jan Lundquist tells Michels this without naming a source, in a film about the inventor Townsend Brown, which would mean the strange legend hid an ordinary but deadly mishap.
philadelphia-experiment-sailors-stuck-in: There is a rumor that some of the people caught up in the Philadelphia Experiment, a secret experiment said to have taken place in Philadelphia in 1943, ended up stuck inside walls, their bodies merged with solid matter. Dave Rossi, a guest who says aliens taught him advanced physics, repeats this rumor as something he has heard. He explains it as "temporal displacement", meaning people shifted out of place in time and space, which would mean the experiment did far more than anyone has admitted.
philadelphia-experiment-ship-teleportati: The story known as the Philadelphia Experiment holds that, sometime in the 1940s, a Navy ship with its crew still aboard was teleported from a port in Philadelphia to a port in Norfolk, Virginia. Michels tells it himself, and he tells it in two ways. Once he calls it a clearly bogus disinformation campaign and connects it to a man named Thomas Townsend Brown. Another time he simply calls it a rumour and traces it to Bill Moore, Carlos Allende and Morris Jessup and to a book titled The Philadelphia Experiment, without calling it disinformation.
philip-corso-sees-a-roswell-body-at-fort: An Army officer named Philip J. Corso said that in 1947 at Fort Riley, an Army base in Kansas, he opened up the caskets that had been shipped there and saw a body from Roswell, the New Mexico site of a reported crashed craft. The documentary filmmaker James Fox relays this from Corso's book The Day After Roswell. If true, it would mean the military recovered non-human bodies from that crash.
philip-k-dick-s-1974-dream-precognizing-: In 1974 the science fiction writer Philip K. Dick is said to have dreamed of being shown a brownie scored around its edges by a fork, which was somehow a relief map, years before Steven Spielberg's 1977 film Close Encounters of the Third Kind. The researcher Eric Wargo tells this from Dick's letters, also linking it to the abductee Betty Hill. If true, it would mean Dick dreamed parts of the film before it was made.
philip-k-dick-s-metz-speech-claiming-the: The science fiction writer Philip K. Dick is said to have told an audience that the world of one of his novels was a real timeline, and that we live in a programmed reality. He said it in a speech in Metz, France, in 1977, under the title If You Find This World Bad, You Should See Some of the Others. Michels remembers the title loosely, and in one episode he dates the speech to 1976 or 1977. A researcher named Riz Virk quotes its best-known line, "We are living in a computer-programmed reality," and Dick's added point that the only clue we get is when some variable is changed and our reality is altered. Virk says Dick came to believe that The Man in the High Castle, his novel about Germany and Japan winning World War II that later became a well-known series, was a real timeline and not just imagined. Dick also believed, Virk says, that the simulators reran history on another timeline because they liked this one better. Michels tells it the same way in another episode: the novel was actually a real timeline. If true, history could be rewritten from outside, with only small changes left behind as clues.
philippine-senate-blue-ribbon-commission: At the end of World War II, a general is said to have buried 176 hoards of treasure across the Philippines, and the Blue Ribbon Commission, an investigating body of the Philippine Senate in Manila, was later given the job of finding them. Dan Sheehan, a guest on an episode about UFOs and President Kennedy, tells this as passed on to him by a Senator Pimentel and a Mr. Ayala; he calls the general "Yakushima", while the people he cites name him as General Yamashita. The story matters to him because hidden wartime gold of that size could pay for secret work outside public view.
phobos-monolith-and-the-proposed-nasa-sa: NASA has photographed a monolith, a tall standing block, on Phobos, one of the moons of Mars, according to a researcher who appears as a guest. He links the object to the astronaut Buzz Aldrin and to a NASA mission that was proposed to bring back samples from that moon. If true, the object would be something worth going to Phobos to look at up close.
phoenician-masons-build-solomon-s-temple: The temple of the Bible's King Solomon in Jerusalem was built by Phoenicians, a seafaring people of the ancient Near East: Hiram, king of their city of Tyre, and his master craftsman, Hiram Abiff. A researcher named Tim Alberino tells this on Michels's show, calling Hiram Abiff the king's "premier artificer" and saying, "that's who built the temple."
phoenicians-crossed-the-atlantic-and-min: The Phoenicians, an ancient seafaring people of the eastern Mediterranean, crossed the Atlantic and mined copper around the Great Lakes of North America, says a researcher named Tim Alberino. He gives it to Michels as his own belief ("I think they crossed the Atlantic"), without naming a source, and if true it would mean people from the old world reached America long before Columbus.
phoenix-lights-boomerang-craft-1997: In 1997 a huge boomerang-shaped craft was seen over Phoenix, Arizona, an event known as the Phoenix Lights. A UFO researcher named James Fox mentions it on the show in passing, without naming a source, calling the Phoenix case "pretty phenomenal". He brings it up as one of the strongest mass sightings he knows.
phoenix-lights-boomerang-over-the-hospic: On March 13, 1997, in Arizona, a huge boomerang-shaped craft passed over a group of hospice workers, during the night of sightings known as the Phoenix Lights. James Fox, a UFO investigator and filmmaker, says he interviewed these workers in the 1990s and relays what they told him. In one retelling he adds that there were five of them, that they simply sat and watched it, and that it took about five minutes to pass overhead because it was so large. He tells it as evidence of an enormous craft seen up close by ordinary people.
phoenix-lights-footage-taken-by-fake-bar: On the night of the Phoenix Lights in 1997, when many people in Phoenix, Arizona saw huge lights in the sky, two men in suits are said to have pulled up in an unmarked government car, posed as staff of a city councilwoman named Frances Emma Barwood, and took away footage of the event. The filmmaker James Fox tells this as what Barwood told him. If true, it would mean government agents moved quickly to collect evidence of the sighting.
phone-call-to-bobby-ray-inman-about-puha: A researcher named Greg Malatzi says he phoned Bobby Ray Inman, a former senior US intelligence chief, and asked him straight out whether he knew two men, a researcher named Andrija Puharich and another named Bob Beck. Malatzi says these two were working in the 1970s with the "space kids", children said to have psychic contact with beings from elsewhere, and that Inman was friendly but said he had never heard either name. Malatzi raises it because a link between those men and intelligence leaders would tie that psychic work to the government.
phone-call-with-rep-mike-gallagher-and-i: In 2024, after a single phone call with Mike Gallagher, a Republican member of the US House of Representatives, Eric W. Davis was interviewed by staff of a House subcommittee, a small panel of lawmakers. Davis, a physicist who has worked on government UFO studies, tells this himself, and says Gallagher represented a district in Wyoming. It shows Congress quietly taking his knowledge seriously.
phone-tapping-audits-and-unmarked-cars-a: After word leaked out in 1996 that a São Paulo hospital in Brazil had operated on an alien, the surgeon involved found his phone being listened to, faced audits and saw unmarked cars around him, according to the surgeon himself, Carlos de Souza. He says that every time he picked up the phone, there was someone on the other end listening. He tells it as a sign that someone powerful wanted to watch or silence him.
phone-won-t-power-off-during-interview-2: During an interview in the UK in 2026, Jesse Michels says his phone would not switch off, and he filmed his finger pressing the power button to prove it. He tells this himself, as something that happened to him while talking with Gary McKinnon, a British hacker who says he found signs of a secret space programme in NASA computers. Michels presents it as a strange glitch worth documenting given who he was talking to.
photo-from-scotland-shown-in-fox-s-film: A documentary by the UFO filmmaker James Fox shows what Michels calls an incredible photo taken in Scotland. Michels mentions it in passing while talking with Fox, as one of the strongest pieces of evidence in the film, but says nothing more about what the photo shows.
photo-of-jolly-west-on-the-set-of-2001-1: There is said to be a photograph of the psychiatrist Jolly West on the set of 2001: A Space Odyssey, the space film shot in the 1960s. Michels brings it up in passing while talking with his guest, crediting the point to another podcaster named Danny Jones. He raises it because it would tie a man linked to the intelligence world to one of the great films about contact with something beyond Earth.
photographs-of-alien-objects-on-mars-inc: Joe McMoneagle, who worked as a psychic spy for the US Army, says he has around sixty photographs of things on Mars that are "clearly alien", among them an object shaped like a square. He tells this on Michels's show about his own collection. If true, it would mean something built by a non-human intelligence sits on Mars.
photographs-of-ed-lansdale-in-dealey-pla: Photographs show Ed Lansdale, a US military intelligence officer, in Dealey Plaza in Dallas, the square where President Kennedy was shot in 1963, according to a researcher named Dan Sheehan. Sheehan says the pictures show Lansdale "sitting right there," and that Lansdale's own wife identified him in them. If true, it would put an intelligence man at the scene of the killing.
photographs-of-hal-puthoff-s-layered-mag: A guest named Dan Sheehan says he has seen photographs of a piece of layered metal, made of magnesium and bismuth, that a man named Hal Puthoff had. Sheehan tells it first-hand on the show, as something he looked at himself, offering the photos as a sign that such a sample really exists.
photographs-of-rip-robertson-in-dealey-p: Photographs show a man named Rip Robertson standing in Dealey Plaza in Dallas in 1963, where President Kennedy was shot. That is the claim of a researcher named Dan Sheehan, who calls Robertson "the field operations commander for the S force", a unit he does not explain further. Sheehan points to the photos as putting this operative at the scene. In one of his two mentions he also places another man, Ed Lansdale, there beside Robertson.
photographs-of-underground-treasure-cave: A vast treasure trove is said to have been hidden in an underground cavern in the Philippines around 1945, and the lawyer Dan Sheehan says he has seen photographs of it. He describes the cavern as looking "like a football stadium down underneath the ground." If his account is right, a huge wartime treasure store sat hidden beneath the islands.
photos-of-kirkpatrick-meeting-with-brand: There are photos of Sean Kirkpatrick, the Pentagon official who led its UFO office, sitting in a meeting with Brandon Fugal, the owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah ranch known for strange reports. Michels raises it himself: "you have pictures of him in like a meeting with Brandon Fugal." Fugal, who was there, tells it more fully, saying Kirkpatrick sat "right across from me" for two and a half hours in a confidential briefing in April 2018. It matters because it would show a top official took a close look at the ranch.
photos-of-tim-taylor-at-bledsoe-children: There are said to be photos of a man named Timothy Taylor at the children's football games of a man named Chris Bledsoe. A researcher who goes by the name UAPGerb raises this only in passing, as a question to Michels, and does not say where the photos come from. If it holds, it would suggest a personal tie between the two men.
phyllis-schlemmer-channels-the-nine-eart: A woman named Phyllis Schlemmer is said to have received messages from a group of beings called "the Nine", and Michels thinks one of those messages was that Earth is a bottleneck of consciousness. He brings this up himself, citing her book The Only Planet of Choice, which he describes as channelled, meaning written down as messages passed on from those beings. In another episode he links her to a man named Andrija Puharich and says she was in contact with the Nine, but does not mention the bottleneck idea.
phyllis-schlemmer-says-puharich-used-the: A woman named Phyllis Schlemmer, who worked with the researcher Andrija Puharich in the 1970s, is quoted as saying he used a device called the TD 100 machine on her all the time, and that she never knew or questioned what it did. An unnamed researcher on the show relays her words, which would mean Puharich was running some kind of machine on the people he worked with.
physicist-friend-sees-boulder-pushed-int: At the site in New Mexico where a craft is said to have crashed near Roswell in 1947, a boulder appears to have been shoved into what was probably a young tree at the time. Michels says he went to the site and saw this himself. He offers it as possible physical trace of a heavy impact there.
pictures-mailed-to-sagan-never-arrived-1: Pictures sent to the famous astronomer Carl Sagan at Cornell University in the 1980s never reached him, according to John Brandenburg, a physicist who argues that Mars once had life. Brandenburg says he later asked Sagan what he thought of the pictures, and Sagan answered, "I never got them." He tells it as a hint that the material was stopped before it could reach Sagan.
pills-handed-out-during-intuitive-commun: Between about 1990 and 1993, at an undisclosed site near the headquarters of the National Security Agency, the US government's electronic spying agency, in Maryland, trainees in a programme for intuitive, mind-to-mind communication were told they would take some pills. Dan Sherman, a former Air Force sergeant who says he was recruited to communicate with aliens this way, tells it from his own experience. He says an officer he names as Captain White told him about the pills, which suggests the programme used drugs to help the training.
pilot-compatibility-with-different-class: A man named Jordan Jose says that as a child, between 2008 and 2010 at Baker Victory Services, a children's care facility in New York, he was part of a programme that matched people as "pilots" with different kinds of UAP, the government's term for unidentified flying objects. He tells it from his own experience, saying a person "might work very well with object A but I can't work with object B or C." If true, it would mean someone was testing which humans could control which unknown craft.
pilot-photo-of-arv-over-provo-1960: In the 1960s, a pilot named Harvey is said to have photographed a craft over Provo, Utah, close to Dugway Proving Ground, a military testing range, and the craft is taken to be an ARV, short for alien reproduction vehicle, meaning a human-built copy of a non-human craft. The guest UAPGerb, an online researcher who argues that Utah is the new Area 51 (the secret Nevada air base), says the image belongs to a man named Mark McCandlish, and admits he cannot quite remember the pilot's full name. If true, it would put such man-made copies in the air over Utah decades ago.
pilot-vouches-for-marzulli-s-source-usin: A pilot who had a story to tell is said to have kept certain details secret on purpose, so he could test anyone who later came forward with more, and when a source of L.A. Marzulli, an author who writes about giants and the supernatural, came forward, the pilot said that man was telling the truth. Tim Alberino, a filmmaker who investigates claims of giants, relays this as it was told to him, naming Marzulli and the author Steve Quayle. It would mean the source's account was confirmed by someone who knew facts no one else had.
pilot-who-flew-the-gold-out-is-still-ali: The commander and pilot who flew a load of gold out, in a story set around 1945, is still alive, according to a researcher named Dan Sheehan. Sheehan says this in passing to Jesse Michels and names no source. He does not say where the gold went or why, only that the man who flew it could still speak to what happened.
piloting-uap-orbs-by-moving-consciousnes: Between 2008 and 2010, at a place called Baker Victory Services in New York, a boy was asked in a lab to fly glowing orbs, or UAP (the government's term for unidentified flying objects), by moving his consciousness into them. Jordan Jose, who says a secret UFO programme took him as a child, tells it as something he did himself. If true, it would mean such craft can be steered by the mind.
pilots-mistaking-u-2-and-sr-71-for-ufos-: In the 1950s and 60s, airline pilots flying at 35,000 feet reported UFOs streaking above them at several times their speed and height, and these were really the U-2 and SR-71, secret high-flying US spy planes the pilots did not know existed. The skeptic writer Michael Shermer tells this to Michels without naming a source, in a debate, as a plain explanation for many sightings of that era.
pilots-report-uaps-emerging-from-the-dip: Navy pilots in the 2010s reported UAPs, the official term for unidentified flying objects, coming out of something called "the Dipper" and even dogfighting near it in orbit. Michels gives this as something said by the Navy pilot Ryan Graves, whom he calls "very humble in his claims", in an episode about NASA and UFOs.
pilots-seeing-uap-at-lemoore-fallon-and-: Navy pilots are running into UAP, the government's term for unexplained objects in the sky, not only off Virginia Beach and the California coast but further inland too, at the big Navy training ranges at Lemoore and Fallon and at Pax River, where the Navy trains its test pilots. Ryan Graves, a former Navy fighter pilot, passes this on from what other pilots have told him. It would mean the sightings are not tied to one base but turn up across the Navy's training areas.
pines-judges-barber-credible-as-a-delive: A man named Jake Barber, who has said he flew helicopters in a secret government program that recovers crashed craft of unknown origin, is judged by the guest Matthew Pines to be "extremely credible", with real professional credentials and "entirely truthful" about his experiences. Pines, speaking with Michels in 2025, stresses that Barber was essentially "a delivery guy": a helicopter pilot who knows what he saw and carried, but not someone told the bigger picture. That framing would mean Barber's account is real but limited to his own small part.
pines-speculates-the-psionic-programs-us: The idea is that secret programs which train people in psionics, meaning mind powers such as telepathy, find recruits in three ways: they look for people born with a natural gift, they track family lines that may carry it, and they give children mixes of drugs as part of their training. A researcher named Matthew Pines puts this forward as his own guess, without naming a source. If he were right, it would mean these abilities are being bred and trained in people from childhood.
pioneer-mission-tenth-planet-covered-up-: The claim is that NASA's Pioneer probes, sent to the outer solar system, found a tenth planet four to five times larger than Earth, and that this was covered up. Michels repeats it from Matt LaCroix, a writer on ancient history, and in another episode he mentions, more cautiously, a possible scrubbing of Pioneer data, tied to the astronomers Thomas Van Flandern and Robert Harrington. If true, it would mean a giant world sits at the edge of our solar system without the public being told.
piri-reis-map-showing-antarctica: An old map known as the Piri Reis map, according to Jesse Michels, shows parts of Antarctica without ice, looking tropical. Michels mentions it himself while talking with others, along with another old map called the Oronteus Finaeus map, and links the idea to the writer Graham Hancock. The point is that if the map is read this way, someone mapped Antarctica before it was covered in ice, long before any known civilization could have.
pla-rocket-force-purges-and-a-possible-h: China's leadership under Xi Jinping has purged people from the country's rocket forces, the branch of its military that runs its missiles, in the last few years, and this could point to a hidden Chinese programme. The researcher Matthew Pines raises this on the show without naming a source, and offers the purges as a hint that China may have secret work of its own on unexplained craft.
pla-s-ufo-report-tracking-system: China's army, the People's Liberation Army, is very sophisticated at tracking UFO reports, according to a researcher named Richard Dolan. Dolan says this in summary to Michels without naming a source. If so, it would mean China's military takes these sightings seriously enough to follow them closely.
plains-of-san-agustin-saucer-crash-with-: In early July 1947 a flying saucer is said to have crashed on the Plains of San Agustin in New Mexico, with dead aliens aboard and one alive. A scientist named John Brandenburg tells it from what he has heard. He says that "roughly the morning of 4th of July an object crashed on the plains of San Augustine", about 100 miles from Roswell, the New Mexico town tied to a famous crash story of that summer. A man named Charles Hall, who says he spent three years among tall white aliens at Area 51, a secret Air Force site in Nevada, also brings it up. He speaks only of a lone craft that was "in deep trouble" over the plains in 1947 and says nothing of alien bodies. If true, it would mean more than one craft came down in New Mexico that summer.
plan-for-oswald-to-fire-a-deliberate-mis: The plan in Dallas in 1963, according to a researcher named Dan Sheehan, was to coax Lee Harvey Oswald, the man later accused of killing President Kennedy, into taking a shot at the president's motorcade without hitting anybody, so the attack could be blamed on Cuba. Sheehan tells this without naming a source and connects it to the later killing of a Dallas police officer named J. D. Tippit. If true, it would mean the shooting began as a staged provocation that went further than planned.
plan-to-move-the-program-to-kwajalein-so: The secret program studying alien craft at a site called S4 in the Nevada desert would ideally have moved to the South Pacific, perhaps to Kwajalein, a remote island, but the cost made it impossible, according to Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked at S4 in 1989. Lazar says this is what the people running the program told him, which would explain why such work was done in Nevada at all.
planck-joked-planck-length-would-be-best: After the physicist Max Planck found what is now called the Planck length, the shortest length in physics, he thought it would be the best way to talk to aliens, precisely because it is the shortest length there is. A guest named David Grusch says this in passing, as something he heard about Planck.
plane-carrying-maury-island-slag-explode: In 1947, in Washington State, two military officers are said to have collected slag, a rough metal residue, linked to a reported incident at Maury Island. They got back on their plane to fly to their base, and the plane exploded in midair, killing them both. The researcher Peter Levenda tells this without naming a source, in a story tied to a man named Fred Crisman, and it is told because it suggests that the material, or the people carrying it, mattered to someone.
planned-double-blind-dna-test-of-the-per: The bodies said to come from Peru, which are shown in a documentary called This Is Not a Hoax, were due to be DNA tested in 2025 by independent aerospace contractors, using a double-blind setup in which the testers do not know which sample is which, "so no cheating allowed." Michels mentions the plan in passing, naming Michael Mazzola and Jaime Maussan in connection with it, and does not say who the contractors are. If such a test went ahead, it would be an outside check on whether the bodies are what their promoters say they are.
planned-film-tests-of-telepathy-and-of-c: In 2025, a documentary team planned to film tests in which two or three non-speakers, people with autism who do not talk, would sit in different places and communicate with each other through what they call "the hill", a kind of shared telepathic meeting place. Ky Dickens, the filmmaker behind a documentary series called The Telepathy Tapes, describes the plan as her own work in progress. If it worked, it would show these people sharing thoughts without speech or contact.
planned-live-demo-at-electrostatic-socie: A NASA engineer named Charles Buhler says he will give a live demonstration of his propulsion device, which the episode presents as a form of antigravity, at a conference of the Electrostatic Society of America, a professional group for researchers who study static electricity. He tells Michels his lab is in Cocoa Beach, Florida, and that he will show it working there in person. If it works as he says, it would be a public demonstration of a new way to move things without ordinary thrust.
planned-move-to-a-boarding-facility-in-e: Around 2010, a boy was due to be sent to a facility in eastern New York to live there full-time as part of a secret UFO programme. Jordan Jose says this happened to him, as someone who says he was taken into that programme as a child. If true, it would mean the programme recruited and housed children.
planned-public-uap-summoning-demonstrati: A public demonstration of calling down UFOs, which the government now calls unidentified anomalous phenomena, was planned for the first half of 2025, according to Jake Barber, a former helicopter pilot who says he once carried a recovered craft. Barber told Michels in January 2025 that his group hoped to do it within months, which would show the phenomenon could be summoned on demand. More than a year later, Michels himself said that Barber apparently "didn't land another egg," meaning an egg-shaped craft, as he had predicted.
planned-wrightsville-beach-skywatch-broa: Chris Bledsoe, a man who says he attracts UFOs and whom NASA has studied, says he planned a skywatch, a group night of watching the sky for craft, on the beach at Wrightsville Beach, North Carolina, in 2025. About 40 people were to take part, and he says it would be broadcast through a group he calls the World Forum. He tells it as his own upcoming event, meant to let others witness what he says he sees.
plaque-at-hospital-regional-marking-the-: In the Brazilian town of Varginha, where people say strange beings were seen and one was taken to a hospital in 1996, the Hospital Regional is said to have a plaque marking the path the creature took. The UFO documentary filmmaker James Fox says he has been there and seen it: a "big plaque out front," and from the reception you learn the being was "brought around the back." For Fox, the plaque shows that the town treats the event as part of its own history.
plasma-balls-turning-into-solid-objects-: People who say they were part of a so-called UFO legacy program, a supposed secret government effort to recover and study unknown craft, describe balls of plasma, glowing electrified gas, that seem to draw together, go still, turn into solid objects and come down out of the sky once they are summoned. Michels sums up these testimonies himself, without naming who gave them, in a conversation with the parapsychology researcher Jeffrey Mishlove about UFOs, psychics and the afterlife.
plasma-compression-fusion-device-paper-c: A paper on a "plasma compression fusion device," a design for producing energy by squeezing superheated gas, is being cited by important research teams in China, according to its author. Salvatore Pais, a Navy scientist known for patents on unusual craft, says this himself, adding that the latest citation came that year, 2025, in an IEEE journal on cybernetics (IEEE being a large professional body for engineers). He tells it as a sign that his ideas are being taken seriously abroad.
plasma-orbs-seen-around-the-nasa-space-s: People on and around NASA's space shuttle, flown from 1981 to 2011, are said to have described glowing balls of plasma near the craft in orbit. Michels raises this himself as a question to an MIT scientist, without naming who saw them. It is brought up as a possible sign of strange phenomena in space.
plato-s-atlantis-date-matches-the-end-of: The ancient Greek philosopher Plato dates the sinking of Atlantis, an island said to have vanished into the sea, to 9,000 years before the Athenian lawmaker Solon heard the tale in Egypt. The researcher Randall Carlson tells Michels that Solon's visit came around 600 BC, which puts the date near 9600 BC, the end of the last ice age, and Michels, crediting Carlson and the writer Graham Hancock, goes further on later shows: he says the flood that ended the ice age, which he calls Meltwater Pulse 1B, is what drowned Atlantis. In Plato's dialogues the Timaeus and Critias, read in Benjamin Jowett's translation, an Egyptian priest tells Solon of "your citizens of 9000 years ago" and says that "afterwards there occurred violent earthquakes and floods" in which Atlantis "disappeared in the depths of the sea," but the texts give no date BC and say nothing of an ice age, and in the Critias the nine thousand years run back from Critias's own day, with "many great deluges" along the way rather than a single flood.
plato-s-atlantis-located-in-antarctica: Plato's Atlantis lay on the coast of Antarctica, by the "world ocean" where the Pacific, Atlantic and Indian Oceans meet. A philosopher named Jason Jorjani puts this to Michels as his reading of Plato's dialogues the Timaeus and the Critias, and if true it would put the lost civilisation under the southern ice. In Benjamin Jowett's English translation of the Timaeus, the power of Atlantis "came forth out of the Atlantic Ocean" from an island "in front of the straits which are by you called the Pillars of Heracles", the ancient name for the mouth of the Mediterranean, beyond which lay "the opposite continent which surrounded the true ocean"; the text names no southern continent and no meeting of three oceans.
plato-s-cave-someone-outside-the-cave-pu: In the ancient Greek philosopher Plato's book The Republic, people trapped in a cave mistake shadows for reality until one is led out into the light, and the philosopher James Madden argues that for anyone to be led out, "there has to be somebody outside of the cave" pulling us through toward enlightenment. Madden offers this as his own reading of Plato and of Plato's teacher Socrates, in an episode linking the cave to UFOs and consciousness. If he is right, waking up would never be something people do alone, but something done to them from outside.
plato-s-myth-of-er: In the Republic, the ancient Greek philosopher Plato tells the Myth of Er, about a soldier who dies in battle and then returns to tell what he saw beyond death. The religious studies scholar Diana Pasulka calls it one of the earliest recorded near-death experiences, "the soldier who dies in battle and has a near-death experience." The philosopher James Madden tells it too, as a reader of Plato. He describes Er as "a virtuous person" who "dies in battle for the city," and does not frame it as a near-death experience. Both bring it up on Jesse Michels's show to suggest that accounts of consciousness surviving death are very old. The two differ only in how they frame Er: as an early case of a modern experience, or as a moral tale about a good man.
plato-took-ergot-at-eleusis: The Greek philosopher Plato, the author of The Republic, is said to have gone to Eleusis in Greece and been tripping on ergot there. Ergot is a fungus that grows on grain and can cause visions. Michels says this himself in a conversation about the psychedelic drug DMT, without naming a source, and it would mean that drug visions may have shaped one of the founders of Western thought.
plutarch-names-sonchis-priest-at-sais: The ancient Greek writer Plutarch is said to name a particular elder priest, Sonchis, at the Temple of Sais in Egypt. A researcher named Matt LaCroix tells this twice in the same episode, drawing on Plutarch's Lives. The first time he simply says Plutarch describes "a very specific elder priest" at the temple named Sonchis. The second time he goes further: Sonchis was the one who "had all the knowledge," the other priests supported him, and he was the source who passed the story of Atlantis, a lost island civilization, to the Athenian lawmaker Solon, whose account the philosopher Plato later wrote down. No other teller adds to it. If true, the Atlantis story would trace back to a named, real person rather than a vague legend.
podcast-with-doty-where-mario-confronts-: Mario Woods, an Air Force veteran who says he was taken by aliens, went on a podcast with Richard Doty, a former Air Force intelligence agent, and tried to question him. Woods says Doty was so protected by the hosts that it was hard to get a straight answer out of any of them. Michels tells it differently, saying Doty "kind of doubled down" on his account of a case known as the L9 incident.
podesta-emails-and-the-delongemccaslandw: Hacked emails from 2015 and 2016 are said to show a rock musician, Tom DeLonge, working with a senior political adviser, John Podesta, on a UFO project with top defence figures. The researcher Jason Simosa says the emails, leaked after Podesta's account was hacked, held about 35 messages between DeLonge and Podesta's team. He says they show a meeting with Podesta, DeLonge, a retired Air Force general named Neil McCasland, someone named Michael Carey, and Robert Weiss, president of Skunk Works, a secret aircraft design unit. The researcher Grant Cameron calls Podesta, McCasland and Weiss "the three kings" whom the leak exposed. Jay Anderson, released through WikiLeaks, says DeLonge wrote that he wanted young people to be "more pro-military, more pro-government", tying it to DeLonge's book series Sekret Machines. The researcher RedPandaKoala quotes DeLonge as wanting "the government to come off as cool". To these tellers the emails suggest powerful people were behind efforts to shape what the public hears about UFOs.
podesta-emails-hillary-clinton-s-seven-y: In the Podesta emails, messages from John Podesta, the chairman of Hillary Clinton's 2016 presidential campaign, which were leaked and published in 2016, there is said to be talk of a seven-year plan to promote UFO material. The UFO researcher Grant Cameron says Podesta wanted the talk show host Jimmy Kimmel to ask Clinton about aliens when she went on his show, but Kimmel did not ask the UFO question. Cameron, summarising the emails without quoting them, dates the appearance to November 2015 and adds that she was furious. To him it shows a presidential campaign planning to bring UFOs into the open.
podesta-staffer-mentions-the-ufo-project: In 2015, a staffer writing to a Washington political figure named John Podesta suggested a certain person for something called "the UFO project". Podesta was then at the Center for American Progress, a think tank in Washington. A researcher named Jason Simosa reads it from a set of Podesta's emails, quoting the staffer: "John, maybe we should consider this individual for the UFO project." If true, it would mean a UFO effort was being discussed in Washington's political circles.
podkletnov-rumored-to-work-for-an-americ: A researcher named Eugene Podkletnov was, at one point, said to be working for an American contractor. Salvatore Pais, a Navy scientist who holds patents on unusual craft designs, says only that he was once told this, without saying by whom, and if true it would put Podkletnov's work in American hands.
podkletnov-s-father-a-soviet-agent-retri: The father of Eugene Podkletnov, a Russian scientist, is said to have been a Soviet counterintelligence agent who was sent, in the 1940s, to recover many of the files of Viktor Schauberger, an Austrian inventor whose papers ended up in Germany. Michels tells this on the podcast, passing on what Podkletnov said to the journalist Nick Cook, as Cook gives it in his book The Hunt for Zero Point: "my father was a Soviet agent and he was actually counterintel and he was tasked with retrieving a lot of Shaburgger's files." If true, it would mean the Soviets went looking for Schauberger's unusual ideas after the war.
podkletnov-s-father-retrieved-schauberge: The father of a scientist named Eugene Podkletnov is said to have been a Soviet agent who recovered the files of the inventor Viktor Schauberger, around the 1940s. Michels says this himself, in an episode with a guest named Dave Rossi, without naming a source. If true, it would link Podkletnov's own work to Schauberger's ideas through his family.
podkletnov-s-gravity-shielding-and-a-sch: In the 1990s, a researcher named Eugene Podkletnov at the University of Tampere in Finland claimed that objects lost some of their weight when placed near spinning superconductors, which are materials that carry electricity with no resistance. Michels brings this up himself on his podcast, crediting the book The Hunt for Zero Point by the writer Nick Cook, and places Podkletnov in a line of earlier work that runs back through the figure Viktor Schauberger and Soviet research. If the claim held, it would mean a step toward shielding against gravity.
podkletnov-s-impulse-gravitational-gener: A Russian scientist named Eugene Podkletnov is said to have built an "impulse gravitational generator," a machine meant to throw out a pulse of gravity-like force. Salvatore Pais, a Navy scientist who holds patents on unusual craft designs, brings it up without naming a source. He frames it with care: "if it's true that he has made this," then Podkletnov "has hit on something," which would mean gravity can be produced and controlled by a machine.
point-dume-alien-base-erased-from-maps: Off Point Dume in Malibu, California, there is said to be an alien base that was erased from maps. Michels mentions it in passing in conversation, without saying who erased it or where the claim comes from. If true, it would mean something under the sea there is being hidden on purpose.
point-mugu-missile-base-near-oxnard: A military base called Point Mugu, near the town of Oxnard in California, was once a very important place, according to Steve Colbern, a scientist who studies objects he believes are alien implants in human bodies. Colbern mentions the base in passing while talking with Michels, from his own knowledge of the area, and names no source.
police-explain-the-attacks-as-river-mine: In 2023, police in San Antonio de Pintoyaku, a village in Peru where people reported being attacked by strange beings sometimes called "face peelers", are said to have concluded that the villagers were being assaulted by river miners using jetpack technology. Tim Alberino, a filmmaker guest, passes this on from a person named Talia. The police explanation stands against the villagers' own talk of alien attackers.
polish-magical-working-animating-a-golem: A woman at a party in New York is said to have told the writer Whitley Strieber that in the 1930s she took part in a magical ritual in Poland to bring a golem to life, a creature of clay from Jewish folklore, and that the story then turned to Nazi tanks. Strieber relays it as what she told him, and the tale also touches on China and the American general Joseph Stilwell. If true, it would mean ritual magic was being used in the run-up to the Second World War.
polished-marble-found-at-the-crash-site-: In 1999, at Hart Canyon near Aztec, New Mexico, where a flying saucer carrying alien bodies is said to have crashed, the researchers Scott Ramsey and Suzanne Ramsey are said to have found what looks like a small polished marble, "totally out of place." Michels tells this himself in an episode about the Aztec crash. It is offered as a physical trace that might back up the crash story.
polygraph-question-about-loyalty-to-a-no: Sometime around 2020 to 2022, one or two new questions were added to the lie-detector screening for people tied to the UAP Task Force, a Pentagon group set up to study unexplained aerial reports. According to what a guest named Matthew Pines says he was told, the questions asked whether a person had any relationship with, or loyalty to, "any non-human faction". If true, it would mean officials took seriously the idea that their own people might be in contact with something not human.
polygraph-with-flashing-images-and-air-h: He was given a lie detector test while a computer flashed pictures at him and air horns blasted, says Dylan Borland, a former intelligence analyst who says it happened to him. In his words, "I get hooked onto this polygraph machine and there's a computer where they're flashing images and air horns." He tells it as an example of the harsh treatment he says people like him faced.
polymeropoulos-feels-betrayed-by-the-cia: A former CIA officer named Marc Polymeropoulos still loves the agency but feels it has betrayed him. That is how Eric Haseltine, a former senior official at the National Security Agency (the US spy agency for intercepted communications), sums up what Polymeropoulos said on a segment of 60 Minutes, the American TV news programme, about Havana syndrome, the mysterious illnesses reported by US officials. Haseltine passes it on as something Polymeropoulos 'said very well', a sign of how some officers feel about how the CIA handled their case.
pompeo-i-saw-the-ufo-files-too: Mike Pompeo, a former director of the CIA, the US spy agency, is said to have dropped an odd remark about secret UFO files while being asked about something else. Michels brings it up in 2023, calling it a "very weird non-sequitur." Pompeo had been asked why nearly 5,000 files on the killing of President John F. Kennedy, known as the JFK files, still had not been released. The journalist Michael Shellenberger tells the same moment and names the interviewer as a commentator called Judge Napolitano. In his telling, Pompeo said no, they could not release them because some of the people are still alive, and then added that he had seen the UAP files as well, UAP being the government's term for UFOs. Both are describing a public interview they watched. It catches attention because it would suggest a top official has seen hidden UFO records and links them in his mind to other secrets.
pons-and-fleischmann-cold-fusion-rumor-1: There is said to be a rumor that the chemists Stanley Pons and Martin Fleischmann were right after all, and that a breakthrough in cold fusion, nuclear energy made at room temperature, may have happened in the 1990s or 2000s. Michels raises this himself as a rumor, asking about it in an episode with a Secretary of Energy. If true, it would mean a huge energy breakthrough was kept quiet.
pope-francis-message-and-vatican-paintin: Pope Francis is said to have sent word that the Church knows the glowing orbs people report are angels, and the Vatican is said to hold paintings showing orbs alongside angels. Chris Bledsoe, a man who says he has had many encounters with UFOs, tells this as a message passed to him by Diana Pasulka, a professor who studies religion: "she said to tell me that they know that they're angels." If true, it would mean the Vatican reads these lights in religious terms.
pope-john-paul-ii-we-are-not-alone-1994: Pope John Paul II told a visiting leader in 1994 that "we are not alone" in the universe, according to Kiran Ilum Xenov, the former president of a Russian republic, who says he met the pope himself. Xenov, who also says aliens took him in 1997, says he did not quite understand the pope's words at the time. He tells it because, read later, it would mean the head of the Catholic Church knew of life beyond Earth.
