pope-john-xxiii-to-broker-the-warhead-de: In 1963, the Soviet leader Nikita Khrushchev is said to have proposed that Pope John XXIII act as go-between in a deal with the United States, so that each side could check the other was not only taking apart its nuclear warheads but actually destroying them. Dan Sheehan, a guest on an episode about UFOs and President Kennedy, tells this as something passed on to him, and he ties it to the headquarters of the Jesuits, a Catholic religious order. If true, Kennedy and Khrushchev would have been far closer to real nuclear disarmament than the public knew.
pope-pius-xii-informs-allies-of-the-craf: Pope Pius XII, head of the Catholic Church during the Second World War, quietly told the Allies that a crashed craft existed and where it was kept. Michels says this was the object said to have crashed near Magenta, Italy. He tells it twice without naming a source. The second time he adds that it was probably kept at the Soratte bunker, an underground shelter outside Rome, and that the news went through the Pope to US President Franklin D. Roosevelt. If true, it would mean the Vatican and the US knew of a crashed craft before Roswell.
porch-insight-the-big-bang-as-a-ripple-i: Sitting on his screened porch, a former CIA officer named Rolf Mowatt-Larssen says he pictured the Big Bang for the first time and saw it as a ripple inside a universe that was otherwise at rest. He tells this as his own insight, drawing on thinkers such as Thomas Aquinas, Gottfried Leibniz and Albert Einstein, and offers it as a way to explain where the Virgin Mary came from.
portage-county-police-chase: Police officers in Portage County, Ohio, chased a large, metallic, disc-shaped object for 90 minutes and over 86 miles. The writer Marik von Rennenkampff tells this to Michels without naming a source or a date, in a debate with a skeptic, as a case that is hard to explain away.
portal-or-wormhole-theory-for-the-ranch-: The idea is that Skinwalker Ranch, a property in Utah long known for reports of strange lights and events, may hold a portal or wormhole, a shortcut through space. Brandon Fugal, the businessman who owns the ranch, says this is speculation by a scientist he calls Dr. Taylor and others who study the place. If true, it would explain the ranch's strange events as things coming through from somewhere else.
portland-police-see-nine-discs-1947: In July 1947 in Portland, Oregon, five police officers saw a total of nine discs flying in different directions. A guest named Marik von Rennenkampff tells this from the raw reports of Project Sign, the US Air Force's first study of UFO sightings in the late 1940s, and offers it as a case seen by several trained witnesses.
poseidon-temple-on-little-st-james-and-a: The financier Jeffrey Epstein, the story goes, built a temple to Poseidon, the Greek sea god, on his private island, Little St. James, and laid out a maze at his New Mexico property, Zorro Ranch, in the shape of the lost city of Atlantis. The philosopher Jason Jorjani tells it, passing on what an online commentator called Dark Journalist found. He says Poseidon was Epstein's "patron deity," and that "on Zoro Ranch, where the breeding program was, he had a labyrinth in the shape of the ground plan of Atlantis." That plan is the one the Greek philosopher Plato describes in his dialogues Timaeus and Critias. Michels, in his own framing in another episode, is vaguer: on the island Epstein "built a temple with a cult symbology." He does not name Poseidon or mention the ranch. They tell it because, if true, it would point to some private belief system behind Epstein's world.
possible-mixing-of-us-secret-technology-: Michels wonders whether part of what came out in a 2017 New York Times article about the Pentagon and UFOs was really secret American technology mixed in with the unexplained sightings. He raises it himself, as a question, in an episode about Hollywood, the CIA and UFOs. If so, some of what the public took as unknown objects would be the country's own hidden aircraft.
post-assassination-letters-telling-ruth-: After President John F. Kennedy was killed in 1963, Ruth Paine, a woman connected to the accused assassin Lee Harvey Oswald, was told in letters to keep quiet about him, according to the researcher Peter Levenda. He says the letters came from her mother-in-law, Ruth Forbes Paine Young, the wife of Arthur Young, and sums up their message as "ix nay on the Oswald gay", pig Latin for "don't talk about Oswald". Levenda cites the letters between the two women, which went between Pennsylvania and Texas in 1963 and 1964, and if he is right, Paine's own family was trying to control what she said about Oswald.
post-malone-s-security-detail-sees-a-spe: The singer Post Malone once visited Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property known for reports of strange happenings, and his heavily armed security team is said to have seen a ghostly figure dart through a house on the ranch called Homestead 2 and up through the roof. Brandon Fugal, who showed Michels around the ranch in 2022, tells it as something the visitors reported to him rather than something he saw. For him it is one more case of trained, sober people meeting something on the ranch they could not explain.
post-war-nazi-network-die-spinne-in-the-: The philosopher Jason Jorjani argues that after the Second World War there was an international Nazi network, which some call Die Spinne, German for "the spider", operating in the Arab world. He says he lays this out in his book Closer Encounters, building on research by the author Joseph Farrell. If true, it would mean Nazi influence carried on quietly long after the war ended.
postwar-secrecy-shaped-by-war-of-the-wor: After the Second World War, the theory goes, officials kept UFO matters secret partly because they remembered the panic over The War of the Worlds. That was Orson Welles's radio drama of a Martian invasion, which some listeners took for real news. A former Senate staffer named Kurt McConnell puts it this way: in the postwar years "we were barely a decade removed from Orson Wells War of the Worlds event. I think that was in 1938." John S. Herrington, a former US Secretary of Energy, says the same thing from his time in government: "Orson Wells broadcast war of the world and the country went nuts." Both tell it to explain why leaders might have feared how the public would react to news of UFOs.
potassium-chloride-suicide-plan-2008: In 2008, in Britain, Gary McKinnon, a hacker who says he broke into NASA computers, bought potassium chloride, one of the three chemicals used in lethal injections, planning to take his own life. McKinnon tells this himself, about the pressure he was under at the time. It shows how much the case against him weighed on him.
ppd-shut-down-and-possibly-reborn-as-oth: PPD, the secret programme in which he says he was trained to communicate with aliens, has been shut down and may live on under other names. Dan Sherman, a former Air Force sergeant who says the NSA, the US signals intelligence agency, hired him for that work in the early 1990s, says he is "pretty sure" it ended, and a man named Scott Andrews is part of the telling. It would mean the work carried on in other, hidden programmes.
prayer-breakfasts-and-doug-coe: Powerful people in Washington are said to gather at prayer breakfasts, meetings where officials pray and talk together, and a man named Doug Coe is said to have been behind them. Michels tells it himself, without naming a source. He says Coe was one of the leaders of a group called the Family in the 1980s, and that every president had to attend his prayer breakfast. Peter Levenda, a researcher billed as a CIA historian, also brings it up without a source: "they had prayer breakfasts and that kind of thing," he says, and they get together and talk, and he names Coe. It is told as a sign that a quiet private network had a way into the highest offices in the country.
prayer-to-reach-rock-musicians-answered-: Chris Bledsoe, a man who says UFOs appear around him and who has been studied by NASA scientists, says he prayed to reach certain rock musicians and the prayer was answered with phone calls. He names the rock stars Sammy Hagar, Kirk Hammett, Robert Plant and Fred Durst, and says that last year on his birthday he got a call out of the blue from Hagar's wife. He tells it as one of the strange, answered requests that run through his life.
pre-adamic-cosmic-war-wipes-out-the-civi: In a war fought across the solar system before the time of Adam, the first man in the Bible, a civilization living on Mars was destroyed. That is how a researcher named Tim Alberino tells it to Michels, drawing on a writer named David Flynn and on works called Cydonia and Birthright, and in his words "the civilization on Mars was eviscerated." If true, it would mean Mars once held a civilization that was lost in an ancient cosmic conflict.
pre-dynastic-maadi-lion-cult-around-the-: The suggestion is that the Sphinx, the huge stone lion with a human head at Giza in Egypt, may have been the god of the Maadi, a people who lived around Giza before Egypt's kings began their rule. A researcher named Luke Caverns says he has always thought this was perfectly possible, and he mentions a man named Robert Schoch along the way. If so, the Sphinx would be older than the usual story of the pharaohs.
pre-war-ig-farbenstandard-oil-monopoly-a: In the 1930s, before the Second World War, the German chemical company IG Farben and the American oil company Standard Oil are said to have made a deal that gave each of them a monopoly in its own field. A researcher named Jason Simosa says this without naming a source, and in the same breath he mentions the Rockefeller family and a man named Schroeder. If true, it would mean an American firm and a German one had split up markets between them on the eve of the war.
preacher-solon-brown-sees-beings-in-the-: In 1948, at Hart Canyon near Aztec, New Mexico, where a saucer is said to have come down, a preacher named Solon Brown later said he saw a few beings inside the craft, maybe three, slumped over some kind of table or panel. Michels tells this himself, repeating what Brown said years afterward. If true, it would be an eyewitness account of the crew of a crashed craft.
precognitive-dream-of-the-focus-magazine: In 1972, in married student housing in Berkeley, California, a man dreamed of a magazine lying on his living room floor, and the next day he found it there just as he had dreamed it. The man is Jeffrey Mishlove, a researcher of psychic experience with a PhD, who tells it as his own experience: "there in the middle of the living room floor, just as I had dreamt, was a magazine. I picked it up. It was called Focus." Focus was the magazine of KQED, a public broadcaster in the San Francisco area, and Mishlove brings in the writer Eric Wargo as he tells it as a dream that saw the future, which would mean the mind can sometimes know what has not happened yet.
predecessor-killed-when-a-running-reacto: In 1988 at the Nevada Test Site, the government's nuclear testing ground, workers cut into a strange reactor while it was running, and it exploded and killed the man doing the work. That is the story of Bob Lazar, a man who says he was hired to study recovered alien technology, and who says he was brought in to replace the man who died. A Navy scientist named Salvatore Pais also repeats Lazar's account and says the tool was a blowtorch.
predicted-extraction-shaft-beneath-the-r: There should be an extraction shaft running down from below the last inner room of the Red Pyramid, an ancient pyramid at Dahshur in Egypt, according to a researcher named Geoffrey Drumm, who says an alien told him the true purpose of the pyramids. Drumm calls that room the "final synthesis chamber" and makes the prediction from his own theory of what the pyramids were for. If such a shaft were found, it would support his idea that the pyramids worked as a kind of production plant.
predicted-hidden-anticamera-linking-the-: Inside the Great Pyramid at Giza in Egypt, a hidden antechamber sits off the north corridor and leads to the Grand Gallery, the large sloping passage in the pyramid, and on to the Big Void, a large empty space found inside the structure, according to a researcher named Filippo Biondi. He puts it simply: "that chamber goes directly to the Grand Gallery." Biondi offers this as a prediction from his own work, without naming another source, and it would mean the pyramid has connected rooms no one has yet entered.
predicted-ufo-hovers-over-puharich-famil: Sometime between 1987 and 1989 in North Carolina, a huge object is said to have hovered silently over a family gathering of Andy Puharich, a scientist said to have tried to contact an alien council, after he had predicted it would appear. The researcher Greg Malatzi relays it from what a cousin of Puharich told him, saying Puharich's son and "two or three of the cousins all saw this huge thing," and links it to a family video. If true, it would mean a UFO came when it was called.
predicting-three-orange-orbs-at-9-45-at-: At Contact in the Desert, a UFO gathering near Palm Springs, California, in 2025, Chris Bledsoe, a man who says he attracts UFOs and whom NASA has studied, says he told the whole group ahead of time that at 9:45 three orange orbs would appear beneath the clouds. He tells it as his own experience. If true, it would mean he could predict the appearances in advance.
premonition-dream-of-friends-2-a-m-arres: When he was about 18 or 19, the researcher Randall Carlson says, he was asleep at home and had an intense dream that his best friend from high school and the friend's older brother were in trouble and had been "busted", that is, arrested, around 2 a.m. Carlson tells this as his own experience, and offers it as a sign that the mind can sense events at a distance.
premonition-of-the-dc-metro-red-line-fir: A premonition is said to have come true "on the 89th day," when a deadly fire broke out on the red line of the Washington DC subway, the Metro. Luis Elizondo, who once ran a small Pentagon office that studied unexplained aerial reports, tells this about himself, mentioning the physicist Hal Puthoff in connection with it. If true, it would suggest that some people can sense events before they happen.
preparata-and-del-giudice-worked-with-fl: Two scientists at the University of Milan in Italy, Giuliano Preparata and Emilio Del Giudice, are said to have worked with Martin Fleischmann and Stanley Pons on cold fusion, the idea of getting nuclear fusion energy at room temperature, over a span from about 1980 to 2015. A researcher named Filippo Biondi says so, without naming a source. He brings it up to show the serious scientific background of the people he connects to his own work.
presidency-cut-out-of-the-loop-under-eis: In the 1950s, under President Dwight D. Eisenhower, the presidency was cut out of the secret about unexplained craft. The researcher Steven Greer calls this "the decapitation of the presidency" and tells it without naming a source. He adds that Richard Nixon, Eisenhower's vice president and the chairman of the space council, a White House body for space policy, was "part of the team that betrayed Eisenhower." If true, it would mean that since then the people holding the secret have answered to no president.
president-of-kalmykia-abducted-by-aliens: A man named Kanan Il Yum Xenov, the president of Kalmykia, a Buddhist republic in Russia that borders Dagestan, says he was taken by aliens, or invited onto a spaceship, while he was the sitting president. Michels says he interviewed the man himself and tells the story twice, once giving the year as 1997. If true, it would mean a serving head of a region had such an encounter.
presidential-advisor-held-ufo-material-f: Near the end of his life, the presidential adviser Harold Malmgren said he had held pieces of a UFO that came down from a high-altitude nuclear test in the Marshall Islands, Pacific islands where the US tested atomic weapons. Michels tells it from his own show's interview with Malmgren. He first dates it to late 1963, then in later episodes names the test as Bluegill Triple Prime in 1962, credits a man named Lawrence Preston Gise, and mentions Sandia, a US nuclear weapons laboratory complex.
presidential-ufo-briefings-nixon-to-bush: US presidents Nixon, Carter, Reagan and Bush all seem to have been briefed on UFOs, but Bill Clinton was not, according to a researcher named Jason Simosa. Simosa tells Michels it is "pretty demonstrable" that Clinton never got such a briefing, covering roughly 1969 to 1993, though he names no source. If true, it would mean the secret was kept from at least one sitting president.
presidents-look-into-ufos-and-find-nothi: Each new president, Bill Clinton, Barack Obama and Donald Trump among them, comes into office vowing to find out what is going on with UFOs, and comes away with nothing. The skeptic writer Michael Shermer says this to Michels without naming a source, as a sign that there is no hidden secret to find.
presidents-not-told-unless-like-bush-41-: Most American presidents are never told about the government's secret UFO work, the claim goes, unless they once ran the CIA, as George H. W. Bush did before he became the 41st president. A former US intelligence officer named David Grusch says this to Jesse Michels in a 2023 interview: unless you are "Bush 41", he says, "you probably don't even know." If true, it would mean the programs are hidden even from the people who are supposed to command them.
presocratic-cave-rituals: The Greek thinkers before Socrates are said to have practiced rituals in caves, which Michels describes as sensory deprivation and as older than the Eleusinian mysteries, the famous secret Greek initiation rites. Michels tells this as something he has read in the writer Peter Kingsley, and in one episode also credits the German philosopher Martin Heidegger. It is told to suggest that early Western philosophy grew out of altered states of mind.
price-and-mcmoneagle-find-aliens-and-hum: Inside Mount Hayes, a mountain in Alaska, aliens and humans were said to be working side by side at a kind of intelligence-gathering post. A former Army sergeant named Lyn Buchanan says this was found by two men he names, Pat Price and Joe McMoneagle, and he repeats what they found rather than anything he saw himself. No date is given. If true, it would mean a hidden base shared by people and beings from elsewhere.
priest-tells-vallee-to-burn-an-ibm-circu: A Catholic priest in France once looked at a circuit card from an IBM computer and told the person showing it, "My son, burn it, it is from the Devil," according to Jacques Vallée, a computer scientist and longtime UFO researcher who was there for the story in the 1950s or 60s and links it to someone he calls Michelle. Vallée tells it to show how new technology can look like something evil or otherworldly to people who are not ready for it.
primakov-proposes-that-the-svr-keep-araf: In Moscow in 1993, the head of Russia's foreign spy service, the SVR, a man named Yevgeny Primakov, is said to have offered the CIA a deal to protect the Middle East peace process. Russia's spies would keep the Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat alive, and America's spies would keep the Israeli prime minister Yitzhak Rabin alive: "Our goal will be to keep Arafat alive. Your goal will be to keep Rabin alive." A former senior CIA officer named Rolf Mowatt-Larssen tells this as something Primakov said to him directly. If it is true, it shows two rival spy services quietly working side by side.
prince-hans-adam-expects-jesus-on-a-flyi: Hans-Adam II, the reigning prince of Liechtenstein, a small country in Europe, is said to believe that Jesus will return on a flying saucer. Michels says this himself, in an episode about secret societies and UFOs, without naming a source. He raises it as an example of powerful people mixing religion with belief in UFOs.
prince-hans-adam-gathered-the-roswell-wi: Hans-Adam II, the reigning prince of the small European country of Liechtenstein, is said to have gathered together all of the witnesses to the 1947 Roswell crash in New Mexico. Michels tells this himself, once crediting it to John Brandenburg, a scientist he interviewed. In a later episode he links it to the writer Whitley Strieber instead and gives no time. If true, a European head of state would have taken a private hand in the Roswell story.
prince-hans-adam-of-liechtenstein-s-lett: Prince Hans-Adam II, the ruler of the small European country of Liechtenstein, is said to have written a thoughtful letter in reply to someone Michels calls Max, saying that proof of these matters always slipped through his fingers. Michels tells it as something he heard secondhand, with the researcher Maaneli Derakhshani and the physicist Hal Puthoff named alongside it, in an episode about Hollywood, the CIA and UFOs. It would suggest that even a reigning prince looked into the subject and came up empty-handed.
princeton-anomalies-research-lab: Princeton University is said to have had a lab devoted to researching anomalies, unexplained effects that science usually sets aside. Michels names it only in passing, himself, in a talk with the writer Eric Wargo about synchronicities and prophetic dreams. It is mentioned to show that a major university studied such questions.
princeton-parapsychology-lab-studied-uri: In the 1970s, a lab at Princeton that studied claimed mind powers is said to have studied Uri Geller, a performer who said he had psychic abilities. He was brought there by Andrija Puharich, a researcher who promoted him. Michels mentions it only in passing, without naming a source, as part of a wider web of government and fringe science work in that decade.
princeton-pear-lab-and-the-global-consci: Machines that spit out random numbers, run by a Princeton University research group, are said to have shown their biggest spike ever on September 11, 2001, and another at the death of Bob Jahn, the engineer who led the Princeton Engineering Anomalies Research lab. Michels tells this himself, tying it to that lab and to the Global Consciousness Project, which watches such machines around the world, without naming a further source. If true, it would suggest that human minds, in moments of shared shock, can nudge physical chance.
princeton-pear-lab-random-event-generato: At a Princeton lab that studied odd mental effects, known as PEAR, researchers ran machines called random event generators, which spit out random numbers, to see whether people's minds could nudge the results, and they reportedly found a pattern called the "rebound effect". Jesse Michels tells this several times, from a mentor named John Valentino who he says helped run the lab under its head, Bob Jahn. In other tellings Michels calls it a "skewing effect" with "a ton of corroborated evidence", or stresses how a focused, coherent observer shifts the numbers, which would suggest the mind can touch the physical world.
princeton-random-event-generators-affect: At a Princeton University lab that tested whether the mind can affect machines, the story goes, people found that how warm and open-hearted a person is tracks how well they can sway a random event generator, a device that churns out random results like electronic coin flips. Michels tells this in a 2025 episode, passing on what an unnamed friend from that lab told him, who called it a "dirty little secret" that is "well known" among researchers of these machines. If true, it would tie the heart, not just willpower, to the mind's reach over matter.
princeton-studies-of-geller: A man named Geller was studied by researchers at Princeton University in New Jersey, and there are papers about it, according to Michels. He mentions it in passing, citing a friend at the Princeton parapsychology lab (a lab that studied claimed psychic abilities), and says "they even have like some papers where they studied him at Princeton."
priscilla-mcmillan-revealed-as-cia-asset: A writer named Priscilla McMillan, who interviewed Lee Harvey Oswald, the man accused of killing President John F. Kennedy, while he was in Russia, was secretly working for the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency. That is the claim of a researcher named Jeremy Riss, who says McMillan also befriended Oswald's wife, Marina Oswald, and wrote her life story for her, and calls her "a witting CIA asset", meaning she knew she was serving the agency. Riss names no single source but points to the JFK files, the government records on the Kennedy killing. If he is right, the agency had someone close to Oswald and his wife between 1959 and 1963.
private-contractor-and-jsoc-team-exchang: There is a rumour that two teams sent to recover the same crashed object fired on each other at the crash site: a private military team hired by Lockheed Martin, the large aerospace and defence company, and a team from JSOC, the US military's command for its elite special forces. A guest host named Jack tells it first, as a story he has heard, saying a contractor team "contracted by locky Martin" and a JSOC team were both sent out to the same crash. Jesse Michels repeats it later as a rumour of "a dog fight" between the two retrieval teams. He dates it to 2004, places it at Coyame in Mexico, and ties it to Sentinels of Ether, a work linked to a man named Jake Barber. If it were true, it would mean crashed objects are valuable enough that rival American teams would fight over them.
private-jsoc-veteran-team-behind-herrera: The claim is that one private team, made of veterans of the Joint Special Operations Command, the unit that runs America's elite special forces, was behind the recoveries of unexplained craft described by two men, Michael Herrera and Jake Barber, around 2009. A researcher who goes by the name UAPGerb says it seems the team Herrera dealt with is the same one Barber knows, without naming a source. If true, it would mean such recoveries are run by one hidden private group rather than separate units.
private-lab-effects-verified-by-others: Dave Rossi, a man who says aliens taught him advanced physics, says he has seen things in private laboratories that are "undeniable" and that other people in those facilities have verified. He tells this from his own experience but does not say which labs or what exactly he saw. He raises it to argue that the effects he describes are real and confirmed by more than one person.
private-sector-companies-with-wet-works-: Some private companies are said to have people inside them who would use "kinetic activity", meaning physical violence, against others. This is what spy slang calls "wet works". A US congressman named Eric Burlison says that whistleblowers who spoke to him between 2023 and 2025 all gave him much the same warning. Among them were a former intelligence officer named David Grusch and another whistleblower named Jake Barber. If it is true, people who speak out about secret UFO programs could be in real danger.
prodigy-spotted-at-age-12-or-13-and-recr: A boy named Harold Malmgren was supposedly picked out as a prodigy at 12 or 13 and recruited by the president of MIT, a leading American technical university, with Rensselaer and Yale also part of the story. The researcher Matthew Pines tells it without naming a source, and also mentions the mathematician James Simons. He uses it as an example of how gifted young people were found early and drawn into elite science.
professor-s-friends-at-malmstrom-ufos-di: At Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana, UFOs fly over nuclear missile sites and shut the missiles down, according to friends of the professor Kevin Knuth who work at the base. Knuth passes on what they told him: "they have problems with UFOs flying over nuclear missile sites and disabling nuclear missiles." If that is true, something unknown can switch off American nuclear weapons.
program-reported-by-shellenberger-that-u: A secret program is said to use artificial intelligence to pick out UAP, the government's term for UFOs, and possibly ARVs too, meaning human-built craft said to copy alien designs. A guest named Matthew Pines brings it up, crediting the journalist Michael Shellenberger, who wrote about the program and who, Pines says, might testify to Congress about it the following week. If true, it would mean the government is quietly running organised, high-tech tracking of these objects.
program-traced-to-dachau-vanished-childr: A secret program involving children who vanished, which he links to the gas chambers, began in the Nazi camps such as Dachau in the 1940s, according to Whitley Strieber, a man who says he has met aliens living among us. Strieber offers this to Michels as his own belief ("I think it started in the camps") without naming a source. He does not spell out the program in detail, but if he is right it would trace its roots back to Nazi Germany.
programs-call-psionic-operators-pink-ass: Some secret government UFO programs are said to call their "psionic operators", people who are supposed to use mental abilities to reach or guide unknown craft, by the nickname "pink assets." Michael Herrera, a former Marine who says he saw a 300-foot UFO in the Indonesian jungle, tells Michels in 2025 that this was "communicated to me" by a man named Jake Barber, who has made his own claims about these programs. If true, it would mean such programs treat mind abilities as a real working tool.
programs-for-summoning-ufos-such-as-skyw: There are said to be efforts to call UFOs to appear on purpose, such as Skywatchers, which Michels describes as a modern version of this, and he suggests the US government has been doing the same thing for a while inside special access programs, its most restricted secret projects. Michels says this himself, without naming a source, in an episode about secret societies and the UFO cover-up. If true, it would mean contact has been sought deliberately, not just waited for.
project-a119-to-set-off-a-nuclear-blast-: In 1958, according to Michels, the US Air Force ran a top secret plan called Project A119 to set off a nuclear bomb on the Moon as a show of force against the Soviet Union, and the astronomer Carl Sagan worked on it as a secret consultant. Michels raises it himself in several episodes, calling it a documented Air Force project, and once he places it at Kirtland Air Force Base, a US Air Force base. Other times he dates it more loosely to the late 1950s and names no base, and he brings it up to show that Sagan, a public voice of scientific caution, had worked inside secret military projects.
project-aquarius-document-said-to-be-rea: A paper known as the Aquarius document, said to describe a secret US government UFO project and dated to 1977, is real, according to a man named Alonzo McDonald. The physicist Eric W. Davis, who has worked on government-funded studies of unexplained aerial reports, says he has seen the document himself and that McDonald told him the people long accused of faking it, the UFO writer Bill Moore and a man named Rick Doty, "had nothing to do with anything." If so, it would mean a paper many dismissed as made up came from inside the government.
project-atom-in-serpo-matches-ttsa-s-ato: A secret program called Project Atom is said to have run at Los Alamos, the US nuclear weapons laboratory in New Mexico, studying nuclear radiation and the radiation properties of materials taken from crashed alien spacecraft. A researcher named Deep Prasad describes it this way and draws the name from the Project Serpo papers, an account that circulated online about a supposed exchange of people between the United States and an alien world. He links it to a project of the same name around 2013 to 2016 tied to the musician Tom DeLonge and the physicist Hal Puthoff, which, if the match holds, would suggest the Serpo story and their work point to the same real program.
project-blue-beam-conspiracy-theory: There is an idea called Project Blue Beam, and Jesse Michels brings it up himself, calling it a conspiracy theory. He raises it in a conversation with a man named Jake Barber, who says he retrieved a UFO with his helicopter, but in this passage Michels names the idea without saying what it claims.
project-blue-book-and-the-condon-study-1: The Air Force's UFO study of the 1950s and 60s, Project Blue Book, is said to have commissioned a University of Colorado study led by the physicist Edward Condon, a veteran of the Manhattan Project that built the atomic bomb, who wrote the study's conclusion before it was finished and bragged about it. The former official Karl Nell tells this on the show, and the same words appear again in another episode framed by the host, without the bragging. The Condon report, published on 31 October 1968, says the Air Force Office of Scientific Research asked the university to take on the project, but it says nothing about when its conclusions were written, while a 1985 Air Force fact sheet says the report was the basis for ending UFO investigations.
project-blue-book-and-the-pentagon-repor: The findings of Project Blue Book, the US Air Force's UFO study of the 1950s and 60s, and those of the Pentagon's recent report on unexplained aerial sightings do not fit together, so either the government lied then in saying there was nothing to see or is lying now. A researcher named Eric Weinstein makes this argument to Michels, and if he is right one of the two official accounts is false. The Air Force's fact sheet on Blue Book, from January 1985, concludes that no UFO it studied posed a threat to national security, that nothing pointed to technology beyond present science, and that there was "no evidence indicating that sightings categorized as 'unidentified' are extraterrestrial vehicles."
project-galileo-briefing-and-its-two-dir: Around 1988 and 1989, Bob Lazar says, he was given a briefing on Project Galileo at S-4, a secret site in Nevada where he says he worked on craft not built by humans, and that "Galileo dealt with the propulsion system of the craft." Lazar tells Michels this himself and also mentions a second briefing, on a Project Looking Glass. If true, it would mean the government ran named projects to study how such craft move.
project-orion-nuclear-propulsion-1950: In the 1950s and 60s, according to Jesse Michels, the United States had a plan called Project Orion to drive spacecraft with nuclear power. He says the Air Force general Curtis LeMay wanted it and the physicist Freeman Dyson worked on it, but President John F. Kennedy was strongly against it, so it was dropped. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, as an example of bold propulsion work that was cut short.
project-pandora-and-soviet-radio-frequen: Starting in the 1960s, the US ran a study called Project Pandora into Soviet weapons that used radio waves, according to a researcher named Greg Malatzi. He tells it without naming a source and is unsure of the date, saying it "started in I think that the '60s". He raises it as part of a wider story of secret government research into the mind and strange phenomena.
project-preserve-destiny-code-name-staun: In 1991, at a training site in Maryland run by the NSA, America's signals-spying agency, a former Air Force sergeant named Dan Sherman says he was given the code name "Staunch 118" for a secret programme called Project Preserve Destiny. Sherman tells this from his own experience, saying the agency hired him to communicate with aliens. If true, it would mean the government ran a programme for talking with non-human beings.
project-preserve-destiny-mother-abducted: A man named Dan Sherman says that while his mother was pregnant with him she was abducted by aliens and her unborn child was genetically altered, as part of what he was told was a secret effort called Project Preserve Destiny. Michels passes this on from Sherman's own account, tied to a book called Above Black, setting it in the United States in the 1990s. If true, it would mean a hidden government program was tracking and shaping people from before birth.
project-serpo-book-built-on-puthoff-s-sp: The book about Project Serpo, a story that began circulating in 2005 about a secret exchange in which Americans supposedly visited an alien world, is said to lean entirely on the ideas of a physicist named Hal Puthoff. His idea, "spacetime metric engineering", holds that space and time themselves could be reshaped to make travel possible. A researcher and quantum computing entrepreneur named Deep Prasad says the book "completely integrates" this physics, which would tie the Serpo tale to serious-sounding science.
project-serpo-exchange-program-1947: After the 1947 crash at Roswell, New Mexico, the United States is said to have recovered a living alien, an "EBE" or extraterrestrial biological entity, and then to have taken part in an exchange programme in which Americans were sent to the alien's home planet, called Serpo. An unnamed researcher who appears on the show describes this from the Project Serpo papers, documents tied to the physicist Hal Puthoff, the former Air Force intelligence agent Richard Doty and the Defense Intelligence Agency, the Pentagon's military spy service. If true, it would mean humans have already visited another world.
project-serpo-exchange-program-1970: Under a story called Project Serpo, aliens from a planet named Serpo are said to have sent some of their own to Earth in the 1970s, while humans were sent to their star system in an exchange. The researcher Greg Bishop summarises it, tying it to a man named Rick Doty and to a set of leaked papers known as the Serpo leak, which if true would mean a secret swap of people between two worlds.
project-sidekick-briefing-on-the-craft-a: A man named Bob Lazar, who says he worked on a craft at a secret site in Nevada called S-4 around 1988 and 1989, says he read a briefing for something called Project Sidekick, which dealt with the craft's potential as a weapon, a particle beam weapon. In his words, "Sidekick was the weapon potential of the craft." He tells it on the show as someone who says he saw the briefing himself, and if true it would mean officials were studying the craft as a possible weapon.
project-sidekick-directed-energy-weapon-: In the 1980s, at a secret site in the Nevada desert known as S4, there was a project called Sidekick, and it was a weapon, said to be one that fires a beam of energy. That is the claim of Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked at S4 himself. He mentions it only in passing, as "project sidekick which is a weapon", next to the other work he describes there.
project-sign-1948-report-on-common-shape: One of the first reports of Project Sign, the US Air Force's earliest UFO study, is said to have found in late 1948 that the shapes people reported most often were silver discs, spheres and balls of fire. The commentator Marik von Rennenkampff brings this up in a 2025 debate episode with Michels, summarising from memory ("I think it was late 48") and pointing to records gathered by the archivist John Greenewald Jr. He raises it to show that the same kinds of objects have been reported since the very start of official interest.
project-sign-estimate-burned-by-vandenbe: In the late 1940s, staff at Project Sign, the US Air Force's first UFO study, based at Wright Field in Ohio, are said to have written a top-secret report concluding that UFOs were craft from another world. The report was called the Estimate of the Situation, and the story goes that the Air Force general Hoyt Vandenberg killed it. Jesse Michels tells it in his own words, dating the report to 1949. Robert Salas, a former Air Force officer, tells it too, but dates it to 1948 and says Vandenberg rejected the report rather than burning it. Salas insists "it was a real document," and adds that it "was seen by Ruppelt." That is Edward Ruppelt, who later ran the Air Force's UFO study. Salas cites Ruppelt's book, The Report on Unidentified Flying Objects, as his source. If true, it would mean Air Force investigators concluded early on that UFOs were extraterrestrial and that the conclusion was buried from the top.
project-starlight-and-the-2001-national-: Starting in 1993, a private effort code-named Project Starlight gathered material on UFOs, and in 2001 it went public at an event at the National Press Club, a journalists' venue in Washington, D.C. Steven Greer, who says he led it, tells Michels this himself and says 800 million people saw that event. He tells it as the moment the effort stopped being private and went out to the world.
project-twinkle-green-fireballs-over-new: In the late 1940s and 1950s, people in New Mexico reported strange green fireballs crossing the sky, and the government set up an investigation called Project Twinkle to find out what they were. An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb describes it as an investigation run by the "Z division" of Sandia, a nuclear weapons laboratory in New Mexico. Michels tells it in two episodes and calls it an Air Force project. He says it was led by Lincoln LaPaz, a meteor expert at the University of New Mexico, who began to track the green fireballs. In one telling Michels points to FBI documents about the fireballs. In an episode with the astronomer Beatriz Villarroel, he says the fireballs showed up across American nuclear sites, naming Los Alamos, where the atomic bomb was built, and Holloman Air Force Base. The tellers raise it because something unexplained seemed drawn to the country's most sensitive nuclear sites just as the bomb age began.
project-unity-flagged-by-the-dod-as-a-ru: Jay Anderson, who runs a platform called Project Unity, says he was told that the US Department of Defense had flagged him as "a Russian disinformation platform", meaning a channel spreading Russian propaganda. He does not say who told him or when, and he jokes that "they're still letting me in the country."
prometheus-chained-in-the-caucasus-by-ze: In the old Greek myth, Prometheus is punished by Zeus, king of the gods, by being chained in the Caucasus mountains while his liver is eaten. A researcher named Jason Jorjani retells this, naming a source rendered as Escalas, as part of a larger argument about knowledge given to humans and the price paid for it.
prometheus-system-brain-neural-interface: Between about 2008 and 2010, at a children's services center called Baker Victory Services in New York, researchers were reportedly recording a psychic child's brain waves to build what was called the Prometheus system. In his words, "what they were trying to do is build a brain neural interface," meaning a link between a brain and a machine. The account comes from Jordan Jose, a man who says he was that child and was taken into a secret program, and if it were true it would mean children's minds were being used to build hidden technology.
promise-of-new-sar-scans-of-khafre-to-de: More radar scans of the pyramid of Khafre, one of the great pyramids at Giza in Egypt, are promised for 2026, with the aim of finding a hidden space called the Belzoni chamber. The promise comes from a radar researcher named Filippo Biondi, whose team uses satellite radar imaging (known as SAR) to look beneath the ground. "I ensure you that more scans will be done on the Khafre in order to find something to detect Belzoni," he tells Michels, a sign he expects the chamber to show up.
proof-of-concept-scans-of-known-structur: A scanning technology linked to the researcher Filippo Biondi correctly picked out known structures inside modern buildings, such as a laboratory in Italy called Gran Sasso, and also a deep shaft in Egypt known as the Osiris Shaft, according to a researcher named Jeffrey Drum. Drum tells Michels this as a test run, done in the 2020s, which showed the method works before it was used beneath the Egyptian pyramids. If the test holds, it would give weight to what the same scans later seemed to show under the pyramids.
prophet-predicting-trump-being-shot-in-t: A self-proclaimed prophet is said to have foretold that Donald Trump would be shot in the ear, and even to have named the ear that was later hit in the 2024 attempt on his life. Michels mentions this in passing, without naming the prophet or a source, during a conversation with the writer Peter Levenda about whether something might be steering human timelines. If true, it would suggest that some people can see events before they happen.
prophet-yahweh-summons-a-ufo-for-a-las-v: Around 2005, a Las Vegas man who called himself Prophet Yahweh and said he could call down UFOs dared a local TV crew to watch him do it. They met him at a park, he told them to keep their eyes on the sky, and according to the story something strange appeared, which the crew filmed and showed on the evening news. Jeffrey Mishlove, a researcher of psychic phenomena with a PhD, tells it as something he heard about, and it would suggest such sightings can sometimes be called up by a person.
propheta-s-letters-to-jim-garrison-in-th: In the 1960s, the leader of a small church in the Bronx, a man called Propheta, is said to have written to Jim Garrison, the New Orleans district attorney who investigated President Kennedy's assassination. Propheta was asking about Jack Martin, a man caught up in Garrison's investigation: "When you're finished with Jack Martin, can you send him back to us?" A writer on occult and secret history named Peter Levenda describes the letters, which he says sit in Garrison's correspondence files. If true, they link a figure in the Kennedy case to a strange little church.
proposals-to-shoot-at-craft-bledsoe-call: A man named Chris Bledsoe, who says he can draw unexplained craft down from the sky, says someone once proposed that if he got one to come down, they could shoot at it. Bledsoe tells this himself on the show, and says his answer was "absolutely not." If true, it would mean someone was ready to fire on a craft he believes he can summon.
proposed-experiment-testing-penrose-grav: In 2024 an experiment was proposed, called the G experiment, to test the physicist Roger Penrose's idea that gravity is what makes quantum states collapse into one definite outcome: it would take two tiny crystals and link them magnetically in a quantum way. The analyst Matthew Pines brings it up, mentioning Penrose and Stuart Hameroff, a scientist who worked with Penrose on these ideas. It matters because it would put a long-argued theory to a real test.
proteomics-shows-a-j-type-head-is-alpaca: Bone from the skull of one of the strange three-fingered mummies found in Peru, a type called a J-type head, turned out to be alpaca bone, according to an anonymous expert in proteomics, the study of proteins used here to tell which species a bone came from. The expert says they ran all the bone samples from the skull through their analysis pipeline and 'they all came back identified as alpaca bone', and points to a paper in the journal Nature on identifying ancient bones and to scans showing a likeness to an alpaca's braincase. If right, the head would be made from animal remains, not some unknown being.
protesters-against-the-white-train-and-t: During the 1980s, much of the job of a senior official named John S. Herrington was taken up with protesters, he says. He served as US Secretary of Energy, and he describes them as people trying to stop a train he calls the white train or trying to get onto the nuclear test site in Nevada. He tells this from his own time in office, and it gives a picture of the pressures on the man in charge of that nuclear work.
protocols-of-the-elders-of-zion-as-a-rus: The Protocols of the Elders of Zion, a document claiming to reveal a secret Jewish plan to rule the world, was a fake made up by the Russian secret police under the Tsar, before the Soviet Union existed. That is how Peter Levenda, an author who writes about occult history and secret societies, describes it to Michels in 2025, saying "we know it was a hoax." He tells it as an example of how a secret agency can invent a story that shapes what millions believe.
prussian-school-system-designed-for-cont: The school system of Prussia, an old German kingdom, was built to control its people, and it worked so well that other countries sent visitors to learn how it was done. That is how a comedian named Kurt Metzger tells it, calling it "the Prussian miracle" and imagining the visitors asking, "How did you get such control over your citizens?" He offers it as a way of saying that modern schooling, including in the United States, was shaped for obedience more than learning.
psionic-asset-recruited-through-the-gate: The government is said to have found people with claimed psychic abilities, which it calls "psionic assets", through the GATE program, the name used in American schools for gifted-and-talented classes. Michels says that the day before, he had interviewed one such person who was recruited this way. He does not name the person. If true, it would mean schoolchildren were being screened for psychic talent.
psionic-asset-tested-with-sphere-that-ca: A "psionic asset," meaning a person said to be used by the government for psychic abilities, was tested with a sphere that came off a craft. Michels says he had just interviewed this person, named Ry, who told him this story, and he mentions it in passing on an episode about a scientist from the Pentagon's research agency who says he was taken by an alien. If true, it would tie psychic people to objects from unknown craft.
psionic-assets-in-faraday-cage-work-suit: A man named Jake Barber, who says he flew helicopters to recover unidentified craft, says his team treats a 'psionic asset', a person trained in remote viewing (trying to perceive distant things with the mind), as one more measuring instrument in the field. He says they put that person in their work suite, which he likens to a Faraday cage, a metal enclosure that blocks radio signals, and use them as a 'sixth, 7th, eighth piece of equipment.' Michels later repeats Barber's account in his own words, saying the government uses such people to summon UFOs 'into people's sort of field of consciousness,' and suggests the wording should change. If true, it would mean the government pairs trained minds with its sensors to call these objects in.
psionic-assets-used-to-summon-craft-give: Some people with claimed psychic powers are said to be used in a secret US effort to summon unknown craft, and they are said to be treated badly and given cocktails of drugs so they can do the job. A researcher who goes by UAPGerb says there is historical testimony to this, and that the treatment could put these people in danger or even kill them. Michels tells it too. He calls these people "P3 assets" and traces the account to Michael Herrera, a guest who says he saw a huge craft in the Indonesian jungle. Michels says that when they first interviewed Herrera in early summer 2024, what Herrera knew was that these people were treated like garbage and drugged so they could connect with the craft.
psionic-pipeline-feeding-the-uap-legacy-: Jordan Jose, a man who says he was taken into a secret program as a child, says that around 2008 to 2010 in western New York he was placed in "a psionic development pipeline for legacy program development." By this he means a track for training psychic, mind-based abilities in children, meant to feed a long-running hidden government effort on unidentified flying objects. If true, it would mean that effort was quietly recruiting and shaping gifted children.
psionic-program-some-assets-are-abductee: A man named Tim Alberino says he was told that a programme studying psychic abilities knew "for a fact" that some of its own people were abductees, meaning people who say they were taken by non-human beings. Alberino repeats this as something said to him directly. If true, it would mean the people running such work believed abductions were real and were using those who had been through them.
psionic-shortcuts-tested-on-program-memb: A secret program has tested "cheats", meaning shortcuts to psionic abilities (powers of the mind), on its own members, and some of them, children included, have been harmed by it. That is the claim of Jake Barber, a guest who says he used his helicopter to retrieve a UFO, and he repeats it as something he was told: "some of the cheats that have been experimented with are things that have not fared well for those involved in the program including children."
psionics-as-part-of-the-cold-war-retriev: Psionics, the study and use of mind powers, was part of a Cold War program to recover crashed objects and copy their technology, according to the researcher Matthew Pines. He tells Michels this without naming a source, which, if true, would tie research on the mind directly to the hunt for non-human craft.
psionics-detect-nhi-at-sedona-base: A hidden base near Sedona, Arizona is alleged to be linked to non-human intelligence, meaning beings that are not human, and people with claimed mental sensing powers say they have felt that presence there. The Australian investigative journalist Ross Coulthart tells Michels this in 2025, saying "there are allegations that that base is NHI" and that people "who are psionic" told him they detected it in that area. If true, it would place a non-human presence at a specific site in the United States.
psionics-team-at-work-on-the-night-of-th: On a night in 2014 in the California desert, when an eight-sided craft was being recovered, a psionics team was also at work. Psionics means using the mind to sense or affect things at a distance. This comes from a helicopter pilot named Jake Barber, who says he took part in the recovery himself and tells Michels plainly that "there was a psionics team working that night", which, if true, would mean mind-based methods were part of how such craft are brought in.
psychiatric-patient-picking-up-radio-sig: A psychiatrist named Diane Powell recalls a patient she saw almost 30 years earlier who said she was picking up radio signals through a dental filling. Powell tells it from her own practice, as a case she treated herself.
psychic-locates-a-crashed-plane-in-zaire: The CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency, is said to have asked a psychic to help find a missing government plane that went down in Zaire, a country in central Africa, without the president of the day knowing about it. Michels tells it himself as something former President Jimmy Carter revealed in 1995. If true, it would mean the agency took psychic powers seriously enough to use them on a real search.
psychic-medium-explains-the-voice-in-the: A voice that Brent Friedman says he heard during a frightening encounter with what he calls a witch, in a bungalow in Los Angeles, was his guardian angel speaking to him. That is how a psychic medium friend of his, whom he does not name, explained it, and Friedman, who says he lived through the encounter, repeats her words: "that was your guardian angel or your higher self or whatever you want to call it talking to you."
psychic-predicts-orbs-over-the-ocean-at-: In the early 1950s, a psychic is said to have predicted when glowing orbs would show up at the Round Table Foundation, a research group on the coast of Maine run by a doctor and psychic researcher named Andrija Puharich. The psychic would call out a time, like "11:00, you know, tonight", and the group would go outside and see an orb. A researcher named Greg Malatzi tells this from Puharich's own journals. If true, it would point to a link between the mind and these lights.
psychological-strategy-board-as-source-o: Much of the early lore about aliens came out of a small circle of people around the Psychological Strategy Board, a body under President Eisenhower in the 1950s that oversaw military psychological operations. That is how Michels puts it, in his own framing and without naming a source. He says the circle included the officials Gordon Gray and Charles Douglas Jackson, and Philip J. Corso, who he says sat on the board. If he is right, some of the best-known alien stories may have started among people whose job was shaping what the public believed.
ptolemy-on-the-soul-s-ascension-through-: The ancient astronomer Ptolemy is said to have written that the soul rises after death along a path through Orion's Belt, the row of three bright stars in the constellation Orion. Michels raises this himself, without naming the work, while talking with the writer Graham Hancock about the idea that the Great Pyramid was built as a gateway for consciousness. If so, it would tie the old Egyptian focus on Orion to a belief about where souls go.
pub-dedicated-to-the-gravity-research-fo: In New Hampshire there is said to be a pub dedicated to the Gravity Research Foundation, a group the businessman Roger Babson set up to study gravity and ways to overcome it. Michels brings it up himself while talking with Ryan Graves, a former Navy fighter pilot who saw UFOs, noting that Graves lives close to the pub.
publication-of-the-necronomicon-financed: The Necronomicon, a book presented as a collection of ancient magical texts, got into print in New York in the mid 1970s with money from a man named Larry Barnes, according to Peter Levenda, a writer on occult history who took part in the project. Levenda says the work involved Barnes and a New York occult bookseller named Herman Slater, and that "by December of 77 there was a completed actual book for sale."
puharich-as-the-earlier-stage-of-the-res: Jordan Jose, a man who says he went through a secret psychic research program as a child around 2010, believes an earlier researcher named Puharich, active in upstate New York from the 1970s, laid the groundwork for it. In Jose's words, Puharich "likely championed the earlier iteration of research that I later experienced." Jose offers this as his own theory, and it would tie his experience to a line of psychic research going back decades.
puharich-asks-for-his-papers-to-be-taken: A scientist named Puharich, the subject of an episode about a CIA scientist said to have contacted an alien council, reportedly asked in the 1990s that the papers in his house be taken away, saying "I don't trust giving them my children." A researcher on the show repeats this as it was told to them by Puharich's assistant. It is told because it suggests Puharich thought his papers held something worth keeping safe.
puharich-courted-by-dark-occult-groups: The researcher Andrija Puharich, the subject of an episode calling him a CIA scientist who contacted an alien council, said he was always being approached by what he called dark occult groups. The researcher Greg Malatzi tells this from a lecture Puharich gave late in his life, which would mean secretive groups were trying to draw him in.
puharich-delgado-correspondence-1960: Letters are said to survive between Andrija Puharich, a doctor who studied psychic abilities, and the scientist Jose Delgado, written to each other during the 1960s. The researcher Greg Malatzi tells Michels in a 2026 episode about Puharich that "we found letters between the two of them" from that time. He raises them as evidence that Puharich was in touch with other scientists at the edge of mainstream research.
puharich-first-announces-his-geller-work: In 1972 a researcher named Andrija Puharich made his first public announcement about his work with a man named Uri Geller, at a conference at Zellerbach Auditorium in Berkeley, California. Jeffrey Mishlove, who holds a doctorate and studies psychic claims, tells this as the person who sponsored that conference, and says 1,800 people came. He tells it as the moment this work first went public.
puharich-found-dead-at-the-bottom-of-the: Andrija Puharich, a scientist who is said to have worked for the CIA, the US spy agency, and to have contacted an alien council, was found dead at the bottom of the stairs in his house in 1995, having fallen. An unnamed researcher who was a guest on the show tells this, without naming a source.
puharich-helped-find-psi-children-in-the: In the 1970s and 1980s, children with supposed psychic powers were sought out in the United States and Britain, and a researcher of psychic phenomena named Andrija Puharich is said to have helped find them. A researcher named Greg Malatzi says Puharich spoke of it openly, quoting him as saying, "I helped locate these kids." If true, it would mean someone was quietly gathering gifted children for study.
puharich-hypnotizes-geller-in-israel-and: Around 1970 or 1971 in Israel, a researcher named Andrija Puharich hypnotised a young man named Uri Geller, and a group of beings calling themselves "the Nine" began speaking through him. This all happened before Puharich brought Geller to the United States. A researcher named Greg Malatzi tells it from Puharich's own book about Geller and from Puharich's tape recordings, and he also mentions a Dr. Vinod. The story matters because it is said to be the start of a scientist's contact with what he took to be an alien council.
puharich-jokes-on-tape-about-being-a-dou: On a tape recording, a doctor and psychic researcher named Andrija Puharich is said to joke that he was a double agent for Israel: "Oh, I'm a double agent." A researcher named Greg Malatzi, who has gone through Puharich's papers and tapes, describes the moment. If there was truth behind the joke, Puharich was serving more than one country's spy services.
puharich-letter-admits-israeli-us-mind-c: A scientist named Andrija Puharich is said to have admitted, in a letter to his bookkeeper and confidant, that he took part in a joint Israeli and American mind control program at Aberdeen Proving Grounds, a US Army test site in Maryland. The researcher Greg Malatzi describes the letter in summary, without naming where he saw it. If true, it would tie Puharich to secret government work on the mind.
puharich-meditates-in-airports-the-nine-: A scientist named Puharich, who Michels's episode title describes as having worked with the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency, is said to have stopped at airports in the 1970s to meditate, believing it would help bring about world peace. Michels tells it himself, without naming a source, and says Puharich believed that the Nine, a council of beings he thought he was in contact with, would speak to him through his watch.
puharich-recruited-into-the-army-special: Puharich, the scientist at the centre of an episode about a man said to have contacted an alien council, was recruited into the Army Specialized Training Program, an Army scheme that sent recruits to study at universities. The researcher Greg Malatzi says this without naming a source and places it at Northwestern University in Chicago around 1947, as an early sign of Puharich's ties to the military.
puharich-s-assistant-says-he-created-the: A former assistant to Andrija Puharich, a doctor who studied psychic phenomena, says Puharich used flashing lights and similar tricks to create "the UFO experience" for the people around him: "That stuff was all created, she says." An unnamed researcher on the podcast passes this on from a tape recording made around 1994 by the writer Dick Russell. If true, it would mean some of the contact experiences tied to Puharich were staged.
puharich-s-journal-lists-the-names-of-th: In one of his journals, Andrija Puharich, a doctor who studied psychic abilities, is said to have written down the names of all the children, known as the "space kids", that he was working with in the 1970s. An unnamed researcher says this in a 2026 episode with Michels about Puharich, telling it as something found in his own papers. It would mean the group of children was real and recorded at the time, not just remembered later.
puharich-s-journal-records-a-day-with-to: Andrija Puharich, the scientist at the centre of the episode, wrote in his private journals of meeting a man named Thomas Townsend Brown in Washington, DC, in 1953 and spending the day with him. A researcher on the show, who is not named, mentions this from the journals, to the laughter of the room, as a sign that the two men's paths crossed.
puharich-s-journal-records-a-meeting-wit: In the 1950s, a doctor and psychic researcher named Andrija Puharich is said to have met Allen Dulles, who ran the CIA during that decade. An unnamed researcher who has studied Puharich's journals says they record the meeting: "He met with Dulles." If true, it would put Puharich's psychic research in direct contact with the head of American intelligence.
puharich-s-lecture-admitting-work-for-th: Around 1995, at conferences on psychic phenomena, a scientist named Andrija Puharich gave a lecture saying he had worked for the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency, and that his boss was directly involved in its hypnosis and mind manipulation work. An unnamed researcher retells this to Michels, quoting Puharich as saying, "I worked for this part of the CIA." If true, it would tie Puharich's later claims of contact with an alien council to US intelligence.
puharich-s-legal-pad-elf-emitter-in-his-: In 1994 or 1995, someone put a device that gave off ELF, or extremely low frequency, radio waves inside the television of the scientist Andrija Puharich, so that "when he would turn on the TV, he would get hit by this." An unnamed researcher on the episode tells it from Puharich's own handwritten notes on a legal pad. If true, it would mean Puharich was being secretly targeted in his own home.
puharich-s-prosthetic-finger-with-an-elf: In the 1970s the inventor and researcher Andrija Puharich said he had built an artificial finger carrying a chip that gave off a set extremely low frequency, or ELF, a kind of very slow radio wave. An unnamed guest on the show repeats this, saying Puharich describes it "in his own words". It is told as an example of Puharich using these frequencies to affect the human body.
puharich-s-theory-in-beyond-telepathy-of: In his book Beyond Telepathy, published in the 1960s, the psychic researcher Andrija Puharich put forward a theory that for receiving kinds of extrasensory perception, meaning picking up information without the normal senses, it helps to be relaxed, as opposed to an aroused, keyed-up state. Jeffrey Mishlove, a parapsychology researcher with a PhD, describes the book to Michels in 2026. If the theory holds, a person's state of mind would decide which psychic abilities work best.
puharich-s-upstate-new-york-camp-channel: Andrija Puharich, a scientist the host calls a CIA contractor, is said to have run a camp in upstate New York, often placed in the town of Ossining, where he gathered children he believed were strongly telepathic, his "space kids", to channel the Nine, a council of alien beings; he is also said to have brought the psychic Uri Geller over from Israel, and Michels mentions a book he believes Puharich wrote, The Sacred Mushroom. Michels returns to this again and again, at times adding that the channelling took place in Faraday cages, metal enclosures that block radio signals, in the 1970s, at times linking it to MK-Ultra, the CIA's old mind-control research, and once pointing to a work called The Mind Traveler. A researcher named Greg Malatzi tells it as well, placing the camp in Ossining in 1973 and 1974 and saying Puharich hypnotized the children so the Nine could speak through them, which would mean a spy agency contractor was trying to talk to aliens through children.
puharich-s-wife-s-suicide-1957: In the late 1950s, the scientist Andrija Puharich learned that his wife Jenny had taken her own life, and the news came in what he calls "a grim call from Jenny's father." The episode presents Puharich as a researcher with CIA ties, and the words are his own, a first-hand account of a painful turn in the life of a man later known for claiming contact with otherworldly beings.
puharich-says-his-boss-ran-hypnosis-and-: A researcher named Andrija Puharich is said to have admitted that he worked on a programme whose boss "did all research with hypnosis and mind manipulation." The researcher Greg Malatzi repeats this as Puharich's own words, without naming where they come from. If true, it would tie Puharich to official research into controlling the mind.
puharich-witnesses-ufos-alongside-uri-ge: In the 1970s, Andrija Puharich, a researcher of psychic phenomena, is said to have seen UFOs himself while working with Uri Geller, the Israeli performer famous for claiming to bend spoons with his mind. A parapsychologist named Jeffrey Mishlove repeats this, saying Puharich also witnessed strange meaningful coincidences around Geller. If true, it would tie psychic powers and UFOs together in one person's direct experience.
puppet-masters-in-plato-s-cave-omitted-f: A religion scholar named Diana Pasulka wrote that when she taught her students Plato's Cave, the old Greek story of prisoners who take shadows on a wall for the real world, she left out one part: the puppet masters who make the shadows. Michels brings this up from her book Encounters, from 2023, which he says is her latest. It matters because it hints that someone may be shaping what people are allowed to see.
pure-iron-pillar-of-delhi: An iron pillar standing in the middle of Delhi, India, is still standing after all these centuries, according to Kiran Ilum Xenov, whom the episode presents as the president of a Russian republic and who says aliens took him in 1997. He brings it up with Michels as an example of ancient work that has lasted, alongside other old structures that "still stand", without naming a source.
purple-aura-above-treetops-and-bledsoe-s: At the North Carolina home of Chris Bledsoe, a man known for reported encounters, a guest named Bob McGwier says he saw a 'purple aura that looked like purple glowy smoke right above the treetops.' McGwier tells it as a witness who was there, and the story ends with Bledsoe saying 'they're gone now,' as if he could tell the visitors had left.
purple-lady-seen-on-first-dmt-trip: The comedian Kurt Metzger says that the first time he took DMT, a powerful psychedelic drug, he saw a figure he calls the Purple Lady. He tells it as his own experience, in passing, during a conversation with the host about hidden powers and otherworldly beings, hinting that the figure he met may be something real.
pursue-file-law-enforcement-officers-rep: A government report among the PURSUE files, a set of released UFO records, describes law enforcement officers at a national security site in the western United States who had many encounters with glowing orbs, including what they called a mothership orb that launched other orbs from it. Tim Gallaudet, a retired Navy rear admiral, describes this report on the show as one that "came out" recently. If accurate, it would mean guards at a sensitive site met objects that behave like a fleet.
push-for-the-uap-disclosure-act-in-the-n: Congressman Eric Burlison tells Michels that he, along with fellow House members Tim Burchett and Anna Paulina Luna, tried to put the wording of the UAP Disclosure Act into the National Defense Authorization Act, the yearly law that sets military spending ("UAP" is the government's term for UFOs). If it had passed, the government would have been bound to release its UFO records. He does not say which version he means. The 2023 version was a Senate amendment that Senator Chuck Schumer submitted on 13 July 2023 to that year's defence bill, and it was "ordered to lie on the table". Burlison is talking about the House side, which that text does not cover.
puthoff-and-davis-describe-how-the-legac: To join the "legacy program", a supposed long-running secret effort to study crashed or recovered craft, a person is said to first have to apply for a job at one of the big aerospace companies thought to be part of it. An unnamed researcher says this is what he was told by two physicists, Hal Puthoff and Eric W. Davis. If true, these companies would be the front door to the program.
puthoff-and-davis-never-shown-aaro-notes: Two scientists, Harold Puthoff and Eric W. Davis, met with AARO, the Pentagon office set up in 2022 to look into unexplained sightings, and to this day have never been shown the notes taken at those meetings. A former Senate staffer named Kurt McConnell says so, passing it on as something he knows of the two men, which would mean the office kept its own record of their accounts out of their sight.
puthoff-and-green-introduce-owner-to-big: Around 2016, two men named Hal Puthoff and Kit Green reached out to the man who now owns Skinwalker Ranch, a property where strange events are said to happen, and arranged for him to meet Robert Bigelow. The owner tells this himself, saying he is thankful they trusted him with the chance to meet "Mr. Bigelow." He tells it as the start of his own path into the ranch.
puthoff-floats-a-joint-space-program-202: Hal Puthoff, a physicist long tied to government studies of psychic and UFO topics, is said to have suggested that a secret space program might be run jointly by humans and non-human beings. An online UFO researcher who goes by UAPGerb tells Michels in 2025 that he asked Puthoff whether the program was "the NHI program or is it our program", and Puthoff answered, "what if it's a joint space program." If true, it would mean humans and non-humans are already working together.
puthoff-green-davis-email-chain-on-alien: In 2001 and 2002, the physicist Hal Puthoff, the physician Kit Green and the physicist Eric Davis traded emails about the Santilli alien autopsy film, a widely circulated film said to show doctors cutting open an alien body. In that exchange, according to an online researcher who goes by UAPGerb and who describes the email chain without saying where it came from, Green said he had seen different pictures of an alien autopsy. If true, it would mean Green saw autopsy images apart from that film.
puthoff-head-of-stargate-and-leader-on-u: Jesse Michels points out that the physicist Hal Puthoff, a leading voice on how UFOs might move, was once head of Stargate, which Michels describes as the CIA's psychic spy programme (the CIA being the US foreign intelligence agency). Michels says this himself, without naming a source, to tie the study of the mind and the study of UFO propulsion together through one man.
puthoff-later-briefs-grusch-s-group: A team working with a former intelligence officer turned whistleblower named David Grusch is said to have finally got a meeting with a physicist named Hal Puthoff. Puthoff then briefed them on what he knew. A physicist and longtime Puthoff colleague named Eric W. Davis tells this as something he heard about. If true, Puthoff's knowledge fed into Grusch's claims.
puthoff-met-townsend-brown: The physicist Hal Puthoff is said to have once met Thomas Townsend Brown, an inventor. Chris Bledsoe, a man who says he has had many encounters with UFOs, says Puthoff told him so himself: "he told me he met him." It is told as a link between two men known in circles that study strange propulsion.
puthoff-mk-ultra-and-the-remote-viewing-: The physicist Hal Puthoff worked on both UFOs and research into the mind, and in that world MK Ultra, the CIA's mind-control experiments with drugs, was the weapon side, while remote viewing, the effort to see distant places with the mind alone, was the spycraft side. The researcher Matthew Pines lays this out for Michels without naming a source, linking the UFO and mind programs through one man.
puthoff-s-article-on-the-stargate-and-sc: In the 1970s, the story goes, the Defense Intelligence Agency and the CIA paid for psychic spying projects called Scanate and Stargate. These used remote viewing, the claimed ability to describe distant places with the mind alone. The work was based at the Stanford Research Institute in California, with the physicists Hal Puthoff and Russell Targ, and the story also involves the spoon-bending performer Uri Geller and his critic, the magician James Randi. An unnamed researcher who appears as a guest brings it up by showing an article they wrote about the programmes, drawing on what Puthoff and the others have said, and also cites a work called Mind at Large.
puthoff-s-cia-psychic-spy-program-and-re: Starting in the 1970s, the CIA (the US foreign intelligence agency) ran a psychic spy program built on remote viewing, the claimed ability to describe distant places using only the mind. According to Michels, the scientist Hal Puthoff ran that program. Michels says many of its remote viewers reported seeing beings in different places, and that one viewer, Ingo Swann, saw them on the far side of the Moon. He also names another viewer, Joe McMoneagle. The researcher Peter Levenda, without naming a source, puts the weight somewhere else: the tests at SRI, the California research institute where the work was done, showed statistical improvements in results, and Swann did what Levenda calls tremendous work there.
puthoff-s-earthtech-papers-as-a-guide: The physicist Hal Puthoff has posted a full set of research papers on the website of EarthTech, his research group, and one man says those papers served as his mentor. Dave Rossi, who says aliens taught him advanced physics, tells Michels in 2025 that Puthoff's work is "absolutely fascinating" and "acted as a mentor-type guide to me." He tells it to explain how he made sense of the physics he says he received.
puthoff-s-extended-electrodynamics-model: The physicist Hal Puthoff is said to have a theory he calls extended electrodynamics, and it might explain psychic and even alien communication. The theory is built on vector and scalar potentials, quantities that sit underneath ordinary electric and magnetic fields. Michels says Puthoff told him directly, when asked point blank, that he does think psychic communication happens along these lines, a field where Puthoff holds patents. Michels also says Puthoff has discussed the model in public. One discussion was on a podcast with Anna Brady-Estevez, where Puthoff talked about work with Josephson junctions, tiny superconducting electronic parts, and Michels credits Lewis Darro and Larry Forsley alongside him. Another, he says, was a podcast with the National Science Foundation, a US science funding agency, co-sponsored by NASA, where Faraday-chamber experiments come up. A Senate staffer named Kurt McConnell describes the model as a physics explanation for telepathy that Puthoff and others are working on. If it held up, mind-to-mind contact, even with other beings, would have a basis in physics.
puthoff-s-paper-on-ultraterrestrials-sur: The beings behind UFOs may not be from space at all but survivors of an earlier civilization on Earth that was wiped out in a cataclysm, a group the physicist Hal Puthoff calls ultraterrestrials. Michels passes this on twice from Puthoff: once he says Puthoff wrote a paper on beings that could have died off in a catastrophe, and once he calls it the ultraterrestrial hypothesis, dating that civilization to before the Ice Age, without mentioning a paper. If true, the visitors would be old neighbors rather than newcomers.
puthoff-s-polarizable-vacuum-approach-to: The physicist Hal Puthoff says he has a way of describing gravity as empty space changing its properties, which he calls the polarizable vacuum approach, and that in a paper he published in a physics journal it reproduces "all of the tests of general relativity," Einstein's theory of gravity. A Navy scientist named Salvatore Pais, who holds patents on unusual craft, praises the same work on another episode, naming the journal as Physical Review and calling the gravity paper "deserving of a Nobel prize." If it holds, gravity could be treated as something engineers might one day adjust.
