puthoff-s-silurian-hypothesis-paper: A scientist named Hal Puthoff, who Michels says lives in Austin, Texas, wrote a paper on the Silurian hypothesis, the idea that an advanced civilization could have lived on Earth long before humans and left little trace. Michels mentions the paper in passing, without describing what is in it, in an episode with a guest who claims a giant was captured in Afghanistan.
puthoff-s-vector-scalar-potential-commun: A scientist named Dr. Hal Puthoff is said to have invented a way to send messages using vector and scalar potentials, quantities from the mathematics of electric and magnetic fields. A researcher named Dave Rossi gives it as an example of this kind of technology. Jesse Michels tells it as a quantum communications company Puthoff is working on in 2026, built on those same potentials. If it works as described, it would be a new way of sending signals.
puthoff-says-he-consulted-on-the-net-ass: A physicist named Harold Puthoff is on record, according to Michels, as saying he consulted on a government "net assessment", a high-level study that weighs a strategic question, apparently on unexplained craft, in the 2000s. Michels adds that Stephen Hadley, then the US national security adviser, was involved. Michels says this himself, without naming the record, in an episode with a former Senate staffer named Kirk McConnell, and it would mean the subject reached the top of the White House security staff.
puthoff-skeptical-of-lazar-after-a-clear: Hal Puthoff, a physicist who led government-funded research on unusual phenomena, says that checks made behind the scenes on Bob Lazar's security clearances give him reason to be skeptical. Lazar is a man who has claimed he worked on alien craft at a secret site in Nevada. Puthoff says it in a debate on the show, and it matters because it would cast doubt on Lazar's claimed government work.
puthoff-the-1950s-anti-gravity-craze-eit: In the 1950s there was a craze for anti-gravity research in America, and in the 1960s it seemed to simply vanish. According to the physicist Hal Puthoff, either the work went nowhere or it "went black", meaning it moved into secret classified programs. Michels passes this on from Puthoff, in a talk that also brings in the mathematician Eric Weinstein. If the second answer is right, anti-gravity work may have gone on in secret.
puthoff-visited-ossining-and-heard-about: Sometime in the 1970s, the researcher Hal Puthoff went to the scientist Andrija Puharich's house in Ossining, New York, and "heard all about the Nine", the alien council Puharich's circle said it was in contact with. The researcher Greg Malatzi tells this as something Puthoff told him and his colleagues, and he also mentions Puthoff's colleague Russell Targ. If true, it would mean serious researchers heard about the Nine contacts firsthand.
putin-asks-for-the-full-account-1997: A man named Kiran Ilum Xenov, who led one of Russia's republics and says he was taken by aliens in 1997, says that Vladimir Putin asked to hear the whole story. In Xenov's telling, Putin said, "Please tell me exactly how everything transpired, how it all unfolded." If true, it would mean the account reached, and was taken seriously by, the very top of the Russian state.
putin-s-post-9-11-proposal-to-unite-agai: After the September 11 attacks in 2001, the Russian president Vladimir Putin is said to have proposed that nations unite against shared threats, including threats from space, warning that there are "good and not so good extraterrestrials" and that some "might even want to enslave our earth." A man named Kiran Ilum Xenov, a former president of a Russian republic who says he was taken by aliens in 1997, tells Michels this in 2025, passing on what he says Putin said. If true, it would mean a world leader treated alien threats as a real matter of security.
pyramid-sarcophagi-too-big-for-the-entra: The stone coffins inside the Great Pyramid at Giza are said to be too big to fit through the entrance, so they could not have been carried in later and must have been put in place while the room itself was being built. A researcher named Luke Caverns says this, without naming a source, as a sign that the pyramid's builders planned the chambers around them from the start.
pyramid-texts-as-initiation-rite: The Pyramid Texts, ancient Egyptian religious writings found inside the pyramids, were a rite of initiation rather than just funeral writings, according to a retired Army colonel named Karl Nell. He ties them to the Sed festival, a known Egyptian ritual of kingship, and says the pyramid and its texts together became "an initiatic engine", a machine for transforming the person who passed through it. Michels later repeats Nell's idea in another episode, adding the Egyptian magical papyri, old magical writings on papyrus, and "secret brotherhoods in Egypt."
pyramids-as-generators-of-plasma-energy: The pyramids of Giza, in Egypt, were built to generate some kind of energy, most likely plasma energy, an electrically charged state of matter. That is the view of a researcher named Randall Carlson, who gives it as his own opinion without naming a source, though he mentions a man named Bob Greener. If he were right, the pyramids would have been machines rather than only tombs.
pyramids-built-during-the-saharan-humid-: The Egyptian pyramids were built by a people who lived in Egypt during the Saharan Humid Period, a wetter era that ran from about 8,500 BC to about 5,300 BC, according to a researcher named Jeffrey Drum. Drum gives this to Michels as his own view, without naming a source. If he is right, the pyramids would be thousands of years older than usually thought.
pyramids-in-the-elysium-region: Space probes are said to have photographed huge pyramids in the Elysium region of Mars, some around 500 meters high and some with four sides, "just like the Great Pyramids of Giza." Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, in an episode with the psychic spy Joe McMoneagle about life on Mars. It is told because such shapes would hint that someone once built on Mars.
quantum-gravity-appears-out-of-nowhere-a: The phrase "quantum gravity" is said to have appeared out of nowhere around 1972, as a way of blocking real progress on gravity. A mathematician named Eric Weinstein makes the case using Google Ngram, a tool that counts how often words appear in books over time. He says it shows "basically no hits on quantum gravity until around 1972." If he is right, physicists may have been steered away from gravity research that mattered.
quantum-gravity-pushed-as-the-holy-grail: From 1984 to 1987, the search for quantum gravity, a theory that would join the physics of tiny particles with gravity, was pushed on theoretical physicists as the holy grail until everybody had accepted it by 1987, according to the mathematician Eric Weinstein. He says it was "thrust down everybody's throat", telling it from his own view of the field without naming a source. He raises it to suggest that physics was steered down one path rather than choosing it freely.
queen-s-chamber-sarcophagus-as-healing-d: A scientist named Steve Colbern, who studies what he believes are alien implants in people, says the stone box called a sarcophagus in the Queen's Chamber, a room inside the Great Pyramid of Giza in Egypt, is 'probably a healing device.' He offers it as his own view, which would mean the pyramid was built for something other than burial.
queen-s-chamber-shaft-points-at-orion: One of the narrow shafts running out of the Queen's Chamber, a room inside the Great Pyramid at Giza, is said to point at Orion, the star pattern of the hunter, while the shafts of another chamber do not. The writer Graham Hancock says this, without naming a source, as part of his case that the pyramid was lined up with the stars on purpose.
questionable-groups-targeting-women-via-: Some questionable groups are said to use UFO call-down events, gatherings where people try to summon UFOs, as a cover, and to seem more interested in the women who attend. Matthew Brown, a former Pentagon employee turned whistleblower, says this is based on what people he knows have experienced with such groups, which would mean these events are being used to target women.
quigley-s-anglo-american-establishment: A book called The Anglo-American Establishment, written by Carroll Quigley, describes a "round table" culture, meaning small private circles of powerful men around the British figures Cecil Rhodes and Lord Alfred Milner. According to Michels, the book shows how American intelligence agencies grew out of this culture of secret societies linking the United States and Britain. Michels brings it up himself on two episodes, and in one he places the story mainly in Britain. If it were true, it would mean American spy agencies have roots in private transatlantic networks.
quranic-verses-calling-the-world-a-game: Islamic scripture has verses that call this world a game, according to Rizwan Virk, a computer scientist and author who argues we may live inside a simulation. He paraphrases the Quran, the holy book of Islam, as saying "We have set up this world for you as a game, as a pastime, as a sport," and he offers it in passing, without citing a particular verse, as an old religious hint that the world could be something built, like a game.
rabbi-ariel-zadok-s-chant-causes-a-sudde: When a rabbi named Ariel Zadok chanted at a building called Homestead 2 on Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property known for reports of strange events, the air reportedly turned suddenly cold. "The temperature drops dramatically around Homestead 2 and right in the doorway," says Brandon Fugal, the ranch's owner, who says he was there sometime in the 2020s. To him it suggests that prayer or chanting can stir whatever is active on the land.
radar-from-wright-patterson-brought-down: A craft that is said to have crashed at Cape Girardeau may have been brought down by radar from Wright-Patterson, an Air Force base in Ohio. John Blitch, a former scientist at the Pentagon's advanced research agency, puts this forward as his own reasoning, without naming a source: "if something was interdicted in the vicinity of Wright-Patterson and if it was traveling fast enough it could have crashed right there." If true, it would mean the military could knock such craft out of the sky.
radar-incursions-over-northern-us-missil: In the 1970s, radars of the ballistic missile warning system across the northern United States picked up UFOs intruding over it, according to Karl Nell, a retired US Army colonel. He mentions the incursions to Michels as part of a longer record of unknown objects showing interest in American nuclear defences.
radar-sites-built-1946-plus-mori-arti-an: A radar site in New Mexico that features in a claimed alien crash story was first built in 1946 and then moved in 1950, according to the digging of a man named Scott Ramsey, whose research Michels describes. Michels says Ramsey also found two other military bases nearby, called Mori Arti and Continental, though those did not become active until around 1950 or 1951. The dates matter because they would show what military equipment was watching the area at the time of the claimed crash.
radcliffe-says-uap-show-technology-we-ca: John Ratcliffe, who led the US intelligence agencies as Director of National Intelligence, is said to have stated that UAP, the government's term for UFOs, show technologies the United States does not have and cannot defend against. A national security writer named Marik von Rennenkampff repeats this in the 2020s, putting it to Michels as a point already on the record. If true, it would mean a top official admitting the country is outmatched in its own skies.
radiation-like-sickness-after-a-mystery-: Sometime in the 1990s, after a mission aboard an aircraft escorting a mysterious box, a former military helicopter pilot named Jake Barber says he became very sick: he lost every hair on his body and the skin peeled off his arms. Barber tells this as his own experience, and links it to a scientist named Garry Nolan. He tells it because the symptoms looked like radiation sickness, which would suggest the box held something dangerous.
radio-station-calls-lead-moore-to-meet-d: Around 1980, the story goes, the researcher Bill Moore was touring radio stations to promote his book The Roswell Incident, about a craft said to have crashed in New Mexico in 1947. At station after station, the same mysterious caller kept phoning in. The author Greg Bishop, who passes on what Moore told him, says that in Albuquerque, "the next stop on his book tour, he goes into the radio station, same thing happens, same voice." Those calls, Bishop says, led Moore to meet Rick Doty, an Air Force intelligence man, and an insider known only by the code name Falcon. The UFO researcher Grant Cameron tells it a little differently: the first call came "seven days after he went on the tour" and "was probably from" Doty in Albuquerque. They tell it because it would mean intelligence officers went looking for Moore themselves, to feed him UFO information.
radioactive-decay-tracks-seen-coming-off: In 1965, in Indian Springs Valley in the Nevada desert, tracks of radioactive decay could be seen coming off the suits worn by tall, pale beings he calls the Tall Whites. That is the account of Charles Hall, a man who says he spent three years in the 1960s alongside these beings near the secret Air Force base known as Area 51. He tells Michels he saw this himself and "knew perfectly well what they were", which would mean the beings' suits gave off radiation.
raf-pilots-encounter-aurora-over-the-nor: British Royal Air Force pilots are said to have come across the Aurora, a rumoured secret American spy plane, over the North Sea, sometime between the late 1980s and the late 1990s. The aviation journalist Nick Cook passes this on second-hand: he says a contact of his, an RAF pilot he does not name, had talked to pilots who met the aircraft there. If true, it would mean a secret plane was flying where foreign military pilots could see it.
rahab-an-exploded-planet-that-became-the: A researcher named Tim Alberino describes the idea that the asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter is 'the residue of a planet that exploded,' a lost world he links to the name Rahab, which appears in the Bible. He summarises it from the work of the writer David Flynn and draws on writings including the biblical Psalms and works titled Cydonia and Birthright. If true, it would mean an ancient world once stood where the asteroids now drift.
raiju-thunder-beast-of-japanese-folklore: Japanese folklore has a creature called the Raiju, a thunder beast that comes alive during thunderstorms, according to Geoffrey Drumm, a researcher who says an alien told him the true purpose of the pyramids. Drumm brings up the legend while talking with Michels, from his own knowledge and without naming a source, as part of his talk about storms and energy.
ralph-mote-larsson-says-he-knows-nothing: A government figure named Ralph Mote Larsson knows nothing about UFOs, and the story goes that he would make it public if he did. Michels raises this himself while talking with a former director of the National Security Agency, the US agency that intercepts communications. He says that Larsson, and many other people from government circles whom he respects and has interviewed, know nothing about the UFO subject, which suggests that whatever is known is kept very tightly.
ramsays-14-000-retrieval-reenactment: The Ramsey family restaged the recovery of a crashed craft at Hart Canyon near Aztec, New Mexico, where they say a flying saucer carrying alien bodies once came down, and the reenactment cost them "in excess of $14,000 that week." Suzanne Ramsey, a researcher who took part, tells it herself. The Ramseys did it to test how such a recovery could have been carried out on that ground, which would support the crash story.
ramsays-bolt-a-plaque-to-the-mesa-2007: In 2007 a couple named Scott Ramsey and Suzanne Ramsey bolted a signed and dated plaque onto a mesa in Hart Canyon, near Aztec, New Mexico, the place where a craft is said to have crashed with sixteen alien bodies aboard. Michels tells it himself, saying the couple did it to "fix the record" on what happened there, since no official marker said so.
rand-paul-confronts-fauci-over-the-gain-: In a 2021 Senate hearing in Washington, Senator Rand Paul accused Anthony Fauci, then the government's top infectious disease official, of hiding gain-of-function research, meaning work that makes viruses more dangerous, by changing what the word means. "You're simply saying it doesn't exist because you changed the definition on the NIH website," Paul says, the NIH being the National Institutes of Health, the US agency that funds medical research. Michels brings up the exchange as an example of officials redefining words to avoid admitting something.
randi-s-million-dollar-challenge-was-rea: The stage magician and skeptic James Randi famously offered a million dollars to anyone who could prove a paranormal power, but the prize was not really a million in cash: it was an investment that would pay out over about 30 years, and Randi judged the tests himself. Joe McMoneagle, a former Army psychic spy who practised remote viewing, the attempt to describe distant places with the mind, tells it this way. If so, the famous challenge was less than it seemed.
randolph-afb-accelerated-learning-skinne: In 1952, at Randolph Air Force Base, a military base in San Antonio, Texas, children were put through a program built around Skinner boxes, closed boxes used to train behaviour through reward and punishment. Whitley Strieber, an author who has written about his own encounters with strange beings, tells this from what a person he knows told him. He says the parents were told "it was an accelerated learning program" for "children with very very high IQs," and he tells it as a hint that the military was secretly testing gifted children.
random-event-generator-research-at-elite: Researchers at top American universities studied random event generators, machines that put out random numbers, to test whether the human mind could nudge them. Michels raises this in several episodes, once citing what a statistician named Jessica Utts said, and elsewhere naming the Princeton Engineering Anomalies Research Lab, a lab at Princeton University, and SRI, a research institute. In one telling he says the Princeton lab was started by Bob Jahn, the dean of Princeton's engineering school, as a sign that serious scientists took such work seriously.
randy-anderson-saw-triangles-taking-off-: A man named Randy Anderson, a guest who says he saw alien technology at a military base, is said to have seen triangle-shaped craft at Area 51, the secret Air Force test site in Nevada. Michels tells this himself, more than once, as something Anderson told him off air. In one telling the triangles were taking off. In another it was a single black triangle hovering over the base. Michels adds that Anderson believed, or could only assume, that the craft ran on electrogravitic propulsion, meaning a drive that moves a craft by working against gravity with electricity, and that Anderson has told this both to Michels and to an online UFO researcher known as UAPGerb.
randy-anderson-taken-to-an-underground-f: A former weapons sergeant named Randy Anderson says that around 2014, while stationed at a Navy base in Indiana called Naval Surface Warfare Center Crane, he was taken to another building, down an elevator, through a security checkpoint, and into a deep underground area that looked far more modern than anything above ground, where he saw a floating orb and a gauntlet-like object giving off strange symbols that shimmered "like a mirage." Anderson tells this himself on the show, Jesse Michels retells it in many episodes, linking it to what he calls an "Off-World Technologies" secure room and citing Anderson's military discharge paper, and an online researcher who goes by UAPGerb, credited with bringing it to light, adds that the object was treated as a weapon because it gave off an electric discharge when recovered. If true, it would mean the US military keeps technology it believes is not from Earth beneath a base in Indiana.
range-four-harry-on-scout-craft-and-the-: An egg-shaped scout craft seen in Nevada's Indian Springs Valley between 1965 and 1967 could go faster than light, but "nobody in their right mind would ever take it that fast." That is what Charles Hall, a man who says he spent three years with tall white aliens near Area 51, says he was told by a figure he calls Range Four Harry, someone Hall describes as a very nice guy who was like a brother to him. If true, it would mean the craft could do things no known aircraft can.
range-four-harry-s-high-speed-horse-form: Charles Hall, a man who says he spent three years in the mid-1960s among tall, pale aliens near Area 51, a secret US Air Force test site in Nevada, says he watched some of their craft fly in a tight pack he calls a "high-speed horse formation" over Indian Springs Valley. According to Hall, a being he nicknamed Range Four Harry led craft in this formation, and they merged their fields to form one larger craft. He says he saw it himself, and if true it would mean these craft could join together in flight.
ransone-predicts-a-rocket-launch-failure: In the late 1970s, a woman named Valerie Ransone predicted that one of a series of rocket launches would fail, and it did. A guest who is not named tells this to Michels without naming a source, saying she was taken seriously by important scientists because of such predictions.
ransone-s-college-ufo-sighting-in-the-ey: The story is that a woman named Valerie Ransone saw a UFO as a college student, and that a friend saw it too. She told it in an interview on Eyes on Cinema, a YouTube channel of film interviews. An unnamed researcher who appears as a guest brings it up second-hand, calling it "this crazy story" about a UFO experience she had as "a kid in college." Michels later reads out her own words in another episode, and these put it at Northern Illinois University in October 1971, around 11 a.m., when she "noticed a strange object above the student union building." The two tellings differ on when it happened: the story is filed in the 1960s, while her quoted words say 1971. Both tellers are passing on what Ransone said, not anything they saw themselves. It gets retold because, if true, it is one more ordinary daytime sighting with a second witness.
rare-book-stripping-monks-above-a-strip-: The writer Peter Levenda says that in the early 1970s he visited a group of monks who stripped rare books, and that their chapel sat above a strip club in Jamaica, Queens, in New York City. He tells it as something he saw for himself on that visit.
rare-book-theft-ring-and-the-burning-of-: Between about 1970 and 1973, people Peter Levenda knew in New York were, as he puts it, "arrested for committing the largest rare book theft in America's history," stealing rare books across the United States, Canada and Mexico, and some of the stolen books were burned. Levenda, an author presented on the show as a historian of the CIA, says he saw it from close by. He tells it as part of a wider tale of the strange occult circles he moved in as a young man.
rat-brain-neurons-fly-an-f-22-simulator-: Around 2004, a scientist is said to have taken 20,000 neurons, or brain cells, from a rat and used them to fly a simulator of the F-22, an American fighter jet. A researcher named Grant Cameron tells this, saying it came from the University of Southern Florida after first naming Southern California, and he tells listeners to search for it themselves. He brings it up to show how far work joining living brains to machines has gone.
rat-learning-experiments-as-evidence-for: The scientist Rupert Sheldrake says a long series of rat experiments backs up his idea of morphic resonance: once some members of a species learn something, others of that species elsewhere learn it more easily. The rats were in places such as London, New York, San Francisco, Melbourne and Beijing. Sheldrake summarises the experiments without naming a source and calls them "actual evidence" that this "actually happens," which would mean learning passes between animals with no ordinary contact.
ray-fowler-s-sylvania-contractors-report: In 1967, workers from the electronics company Sylvania who were doing contract work at Malmstrom Air Force Base, a nuclear missile base in Montana, reported UFOs to an investigator named Roy Craig from the Condon study, a University of Colorado inquiry into UFOs paid for by the Air Force. Robert Salas, a former Air Force missile officer, relays this from what he learned of Ray Fowler, whom he describes as "a manager working with under Sylvania Corporation." Salas tells it because, if true, it means civilian contractors also saw objects around the missile sites and told an official investigator.
ray-hernandez-pulled-out-of-his-car-in-a: A man named Rey Hernandez was sitting in a completely stalled traffic jam in Miami when, as the story goes, he was pulled out of his car. The UFO researcher Grant Cameron tells it second-hand, saying it happened two days after an earlier event in Hernandez's story, and ties it to Edgar Mitchell, the Apollo astronaut who walked on the moon. No date is given, and it is told as a strange encounter in the middle of an ordinary day.
raymond-lavos-claims-esoteric-math-for-b: A man named Raymond Lavos swears that he worked on some very unusual, hard-to-follow mathematics for the B-2, the American stealth bomber built in the 1980s. The researcher Jan Lundquist passes this on from Lavos in a documentary about the inventor Townsend Brown, as a hint that strange physics went into the bomber's design.
raymond-moody-s-psychomanteum-and-the-un: A researcher named Raymond Moody built a room he called the psychomanteum, said to be modelled on underground temples found in ancient Greece, where people went to consult oracles. Jeffrey Mishlove, a parapsychologist with a doctorate, offers it as a modern example of that ancient practice, which would mean an old Greek method for contacting other realms has been revived.
raytheon-distances-itself-from-what-its-: In 2004, a new forward-looking infrared camera system, a heat-seeing sensor known as FLIR and made by the defense company Raytheon, had just been installed on the Nimitz carrier strike group, a US Navy aircraft carrier and its escort ships, right before it picked up the object the Navy fighter pilot David Fravor encountered. Michels tells this himself in three episodes, including a debate with the skeptic Mick West, and the story holds that Raytheon later distanced itself from what its system caught. Only his first telling touches on that point, and the others just stress the timing of the brand new sensor.
raytheon-man-made-triangle-at-fort-irwin: A man named Steven DNA is said to have seen a man-made triangular craft built by the defense company Raytheon at Fort Irwin, an Army base in California, and he and his wife were later abducted by it. Steven Greer relays the account on two visits to the show, showing it in his book Disclosure: An Illustrated History, and the second time he adds that the craft could make holograms and "could be used in a hoaxed invasion," meaning a fake alien attack. If true, it would mean some craft taken for alien ones are human-built.
razor-sharp-stone-cuts-at-kef-kalesi: At Kef Kalesi, an ancient site in Turkey, some of the stone cuts are so sharp that you can still cut your finger on them, according to a researcher named Matt LaCroix. LaCroix gives this to Michels as an example, without naming a source, while arguing that something big happened around 12,000 BC. If true, it would point to very skilled stonework in the distant past.
reaction-to-communion-cover-at-beth-isra: A man named Jim Weiner says that in the late 1980s, at Beth Israel Hospital in Boston, he saw the face on the cover of Communion, a book by the writer Whitley Strieber, and "flipped out." He tells it first-hand on the show as his own reaction, one that, by his telling, tied something he had lived through to what that book describes.
reactor-theorized-as-a-cyclotron-hitting: Sometime between 1987 and 1989, scientists at S4, a secret site in Nevada, guessed that the power source in a recovered craft was a cyclotron, a machine that speeds up particles, firing at element 115, a very heavy chemical element. Bob Lazar, a physicist who says he worked at S4 on craft not made by humans, tells it from what a colleague named Barry Castilio told him: "it was theorized apparently Barry with his other lab partner, they thought that was a cyclotron, an accelerator." If true, it would mean the team was trying to work out how a craft from somewhere else was powered.
reactors-in-all-the-craft-are-identical-: The power reactors in every one of the alien craft held at S4, a secret site in Nevada, are exactly the same. That is what Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on those craft in the late 1980s, says he was told: "Apparently the reactors in all the craft are exactly the same."
read-in-personnel-dig-into-the-program-s: People newly "read in" to a secret programme, meaning cleared and told about it, are said to have started digging through its backlog of old records, and that is when they got into trouble. Dylan Borland, a former Air Force intelligence specialist, passes this on as something he was told about people he does not name, sometime in the 2010s. If true, it would mean the programme's history was guarded even from its own cleared staff.
readers-of-the-sacred-mushroom-find-mush: People who read The Sacred Mushroom, a book by the scientist Andrija Puharich, are said to have found those same mushrooms growing in their backyards within days of reading it. The psychologist and author Jeffrey Mishlove tells it, saying Puharich himself told him he had met such readers. It would suggest a strange coincidence tied to the book.
reading-a-book-aloud-at-age-three: At three years old, before he had spent a day in school, a boy walked in on his mother and her friend drinking coffee, pulled a book from the shelf, opened it and began reading it aloud to them. Bob Maguire tells this about himself on an episode about a CIA contractor. It is told as an early sign of an unusual mind.
reading-corso-s-the-day-after-roswell-19: John Blitch, a scientist who worked for the Pentagon's advanced research agency and says he was once abducted by an alien, says that around 1997 he began reading The Day After Roswell and "really started digging in." The book was published in 1997 by Philip J. Corso, a retired Army officer, and is about the reported 1947 crash of an unknown craft near Roswell, New Mexico. Blitch tells it as the point where his own research into the subject began.
reading-raw-project-blue-book-case-files: The raw case files of Project Blue Book, the US Air Force's UFO study of the 1950s and 60s, are worth reading as they are, with no one's analysis on top, says Marik von Rennenkampff, a writer and former Defense Department analyst who has read them himself. He says he has gone through "the raw blue book case, like uh no analysis, just right, just the straight uh reports," and he raises it to say that the original reports, read on their own terms, tell more than the Air Force's summaries.
reagan-and-bill-paynter-s-1974-sighting-: Ronald Reagan, while he was governor of California, is said to have had a sighting in 1974 while flying in a Cessna, a small private plane, near Bakersfield, with his pilot, a man named Bill Paynter. Michels tells it himself, without naming a source, and in this passage he sets the scene without describing what they saw.
reagan-asks-gorbachev-for-help-against-a: Mikhail Gorbachev, the last leader of the Soviet Union, told the TV interviewer Charlie Rose that US President Ronald Reagan once quietly asked him, "If the United States were attacked by someone from outer space, would you help us?" A clip of Gorbachev saying this is played on the show, and Jesse Michels retells it several times, once placing it at the 1985 summit in Geneva with Reagan whispering just before talks began, once at some UN-type event, while the former CIA officer Rolf Mowatt-Larssen recalls it more loosely as the two leaders musing about teaming up when the aliens came.
reagan-diary-on-the-capacity-to-put-300-: In a diary entry dated June 11, 1985, President Ronald Reagan wrote: "I learned that our shuttle capacity is such we could orbit 300 people," meaning the space shuttle, NASA's reusable spacecraft, could put that many into orbit. Michels quotes the line himself in an episode about a hacker who searched for a secret space program. In another episode he describes the same diaries more loosely, as entries from the 1980s where Reagan says he met top astronomers from NASA. He raises it because a capacity like that would mean far more spaceflight was possible than the public knew.
reagan-era-release-of-falcon-and-condor-: President Ronald Reagan is said to have allowed the claims of two hidden insiders, called Falcon and Condor, to come out, including talk of an alien kept at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base in Ohio. The UFO researcher Grant Cameron tells this without naming his source, and the claims aired on UFO Cover-Up Live, a television special broadcast in 1988 in which the two men spoke with their faces and voices disguised. If true, the broadcast would have been a release approved at the very top rather than a leak.
reagan-family-feud-over-lost-spanish-gol: Reagan Canyon, a place in the Big Bend country of West Texas, is said to be the setting of a long tale from the 1890s about a family feud over lost Spanish gold, with mysterious deaths stretching from West Texas all the way to San Antonio. The researcher Luke Caverns tells it as local lore that anyone can look up, without naming who first told it.
reagan-on-close-encounters-at-the-white-: According to Jesse Michels, President Ronald Reagan watched Close Encounters of the Third Kind, a Hollywood film about people meeting alien visitors, at the White House and said there was a lot of truth in it. Michels mentions it himself, without naming a source, while comparing the film's beings to small three-fingered figures said to come from Peru.
reagan-on-uniting-earth-against-an-outsi: President Ronald Reagan is said to have spoken of how quickly the world's differences would vanish if humanity faced "an alien threat from outside this world." Michels shows that line in a clip and places it at the United Nations in 1987, while Salvatore Pais, a Navy scientist known for unusual patents, paraphrases it as a warning that a divided Earth will not withstand what is coming. Michels also says, in another episode, that many of Reagan's mid-1980s speeches dealt with non-human intelligence, which some take as a hint that leaders knew more.
reagan-proposes-sdi-at-a-cabinet-meeting: In 1983, at a cabinet meeting in the White House, President Ronald Reagan is said to have asked how wonderful it would be to design something that could protect the country from missiles, the idea that became his space-based missile defense plan, the Strategic Defense Initiative. John S. Herrington, a former US Secretary of Energy, tells this as someone who was there. He tells it as the birth of that programme.
reagan-s-comment-at-the-white-house-e-t-: In 1982 the film director Steven Spielberg showed his movie E.T., about a stranded alien befriended by a boy, at the White House, and he says President Ronald Reagan thanked him and then looked around the room and said that "there are a number of people in this room who know that everything on that screen is absolutely true." Spielberg tells this himself in recordings played on the show, Michels recalls the audio, and the screenwriter Bryce Zabel repeats it from a Spielberg interview, giving Reagan's line as "about five people in this room." If Reagan meant it, a sitting president was hinting that some officials knew aliens are real.
reagan-s-staff-cut-tear-down-this-wall-t: Before Ronald Reagan, then the US president, gave his 1987 speech in Berlin, his staff twice cut the famous line "tear down this wall" from the draft, and Reagan put it back. John S. Herrington, a former US Secretary of Energy who served under Reagan, tells this, naming the speechwriter Peter Robinson and a book of Reagan's own writings called In His Own Hand: "The staff took it out of the speech not once but twice." He tells it to show how Reagan sometimes overruled his own advisers.
reagan-ufo-briefing-attended-by-james-ba: In the 1980s, President Ronald Reagan got a UFO briefing at the White House from several groups, and James Baker was invited to sit in. The researcher Jason Simosa tells this, citing the writer Nick Redfern, and calls Baker "a member of the family", the secret society his episode is about. He says one group came from the CIA's science and technology branch, "presumably Kit Green and his people", another was a group called the Collins Elite, and a third group gave a briefing too, which would mean UFOs reached the very top of government.
rear-admiral-gallaudet-researching-under: A retired Navy rear admiral named Tim Galidet, who once ran the US government agency that studies the oceans and weather, is keenly interested in strange objects seen underwater. Ryan Graves, a former Navy fighter pilot, says this from knowing him, describing Galidet as the man "who used to run uh Noah National Oceanic and Atmospheric Association" and is "highly interested in these underwater anomalies." Graves brings it up to show that senior people take objects in the sea seriously.
reassigned-to-kilo-control-and-never-tea: A former guard at a nuclear missile field named Mario Woods says that after the night he describes as a UFO abduction in 1977, near Ellsworth in South Dakota, he was moved for good. He says he "never went back" to the post he had been working, Wimer control, and was sent to another post in the missile field called Kilo control. He says he was never made team leader again, which he tells as a sign that the event quietly changed his career.
rebello-s-tweet-promising-to-open-brazil: A Brazilian politician named Aldo Rebelo, described in the episode's title as a defense minister, posted on social media that he knows what Brazil's armed forces hold in their archives on UFOs, and promised to open them if the United States opens its own. Michels quotes the post himself: "What I can say is that if the US government reveals its documents, I will do the same if I am elected president of Brazil." If he meant it, it would mean a senior Brazilian official is saying his country's military has UFO files worth releasing.
recalled-abduction-aboard-a-50-foot-craf: Steve Colbern, a scientist who studies what he believes are alien implants, says that in Fillmore, California, 'two small gray beings came into my room and woke me up and said come outside.' He says he recalls being taken aboard a craft about 50 feet across and having something implanted in his toe. He tells it as his own experience, which if true would make him one of the people whose implants he studies.
recently-discovered-10-000-year-old-anci: An ancient city about 10,000 years old was recently discovered in Texas next to a river, according to a researcher named Luke Caverns. He mentions it on the show without naming the place or a source. If true, it would mean people built cities in North America far earlier than usually thought.
record-number-of-ufo-sightings-in-2020: There was a record number of UFO sightings in 2020, according to Michels, who says these things tend to be seen in times of greater social breakdown. He offers this himself, without naming a source, in a conversation with the economist Tyler Cowen; if true, it would hint that sightings rise and fall with the mood of a society.
recording-leaked-to-globo-and-the-case-r: Around 1996 and 1997, a recording connected to a Brazilian case was leaked to Globo, Brazil's big TV network, and the network's show kept making fun of the case every time it came up. This comes from a surgeon named Carlos de Souza, who says he was involved in the case and whose hospital, he says, operated on an alien. He names a person called Claudia Kovu in connection with it. He tells it to explain how the case got laughed off in public instead of being looked into.
recovered-craft-cannot-be-flown-because-: The people in the United States who hold recovered alien craft cannot fly them, because the craft are steered by consciousness, the mind itself, rather than by controls. A lawyer named Dan Sheehan says he was told this, describing it as "a major problem" for those trying to fly the craft.
recovered-craft-not-made-by-humanity-con: Dylan Borland, a former Air Force intelligence specialist, says he is sure the United States has recovered craft that were not made by humans of our time and place. He ties this to David Grusch, a former intelligence officer who has made claims about crashed-craft recovery, and to the Pentagon's office for investigating unexplained flying objects and to the Inspector General, an internal government watchdog, saying these confirmed it. If true, it would mean the government holds non-human technology.
recovered-memory-of-a-virtual-tour-of-eg: In 2007, a North Carolina man named Chris Bledsoe, who says he draws visits from UFOs, recovered a memory of beings taking him on what felt like a virtual tour of Egypt: the pyramids, the Sphinx, and a temple of the goddess Hathor. "The first thing I remembered was seeing Egypt," he says, and he still wonders why. He tells it as his own experience, and it would suggest the beings were trying to show him something about ancient history.
recovered-relic-tech-brought-in-by-secur: Between about 2008 and 2010, at a place called Baker Victory Services in Western New York, a man named Jordan Jose says that as a child he was put in a room with a huge box, brought in by about eight security guards, while a team watched him, as part of a study of telepathy with recovered "relic" technology. Jose tells this as his own experience, and names a man called Jacob Barber in connection with it. If true, it would mean children were being tested for mind-to-mind contact with recovered objects.
recovered-roswell-craft-must-have-been-s: The argument is that if a craft was recovered after the 1947 crash near Roswell, New Mexico, which is famous in UFO lore, then it would obviously have been studied, and in secret. A researcher named Richard Dolan makes this case, citing a writer named Stanton Friedman. If true, it would mean a hidden study of that craft has been going on since 1947.
recovering-ufo-metal-in-zanesville-ohio-: Sometime between 2008 and 2010 in Zanesville, Ohio, a piece of metal said to come from a UFO was taken to a machine shop and cut in two. One part went with a man named Timothy Taylor and the other went back to the person who owned it. Chris Bledsoe, a man who says UFOs show up around him, tells Michels he was there for the cutting, an account that would mean a piece of such material is now being held for study.
recovery-of-the-eight-gon-disc-and-the-e: Jake Barber, who says he flew helicopters for crash retrievals, says that in 2014 he recovered a craft from the California desert that he calls the 'eight-gon,' a flying disc with eight sections when seen from above. He says that while flying it back to the drop site, the craft slung beneath his helicopter, he was 'completely overwhelmed' and felt 'something conscious about the craft' that 'had tapped into me.' Michels retells it, adding that Barber locked onto it with his mind and felt a divine feminine presence, and a guest named John Blitch, said to be a former government scientist, passes it on as a 'feeling of love.' If true, it would mean the craft could reach out to the mind of the person carrying it.
recovery-team-without-insignia-1948: In 1948, after a craft is said to have crashed in Hart Canyon near Aztec, New Mexico, the team that came to recover it wore no badges or insignia to show who they were: not Army, not Marine Corps, nothing. A researcher named Scott Ramsey, who has spent years investigating the case, says the people who told of it all agree on this point, and he mentions a man named Doug Noland among them. If true, it would mean whoever took the craft away kept even their branch of service hidden.
recruited-by-the-american-orthodox-catho: Around 1968 or 1969, as Peter Levenda left a funeral in the Bronx in New York City, he says men from a small church called the American Orthodox Catholic Church came up to him and drew him in: "on our way out, we bump into guys from the American Orthodox Catholic Church." Levenda, an author presented on the show as a historian of the CIA, tells it as his own experience. To him it was the start of his time inside a strange world of small churches and secret groups.
recruited-by-two-men-to-work-as-an-airpl: In the mid-1990s, early in his Air Force training, a former military helicopter pilot named Jake Barber says two men approached him and convinced him it would be a good idea to become an airplane mechanic, a job he describes as a cover, which led to Pope Air Force Base in North Carolina. Barber tells this as his own experience. He tells it as how he was first drawn into secret work.
recruited-into-army-intelligence-by-a-ci: In the 1960s, at Fort Jackson, an Army training base in South Carolina, a young soldier named Joe McMoneagle was approached by a civilian in the base beer hall and later followed him to a trailer, where he found out the man worked in intelligence. McMoneagle, who went on to become one of the Army's remote viewers, people trained to try to describe far-off places with the mind alone, tells this as the start of his own path into Army intelligence.
recruited-into-the-gte-program-and-comba: Jake Barber, who later says he flew helicopters to recover unidentified craft, says that in 1994 he was recruited into a brand new US Air Force program he calls GTE, without spelling out the name. He says it led him to Lackland Air Force Base in Texas and into combat control, an Air Force special operations field, as the start of the career behind his later claims.
recruiters-chatting-about-the-covert-pro: People recruiting children for a secret UFO program are said to have gone to the Starbucks around the corner from a place called Baker Victory Services, in New York, and chatted casually there about their work, around 2008 to 2010. Michels tells this from the account of Jordan Jose, a man who says he was taken into the program as a child and wrote about it in a blog post. If true, it would mean such a program recruited openly enough to be overheard over coffee.
rectangular-craft-and-gray-beings-in-pra: In 2019, a quantum computing researcher named Deep Prasad says, his bedroom roof "like dissolves" and he saw "the underside of a rectangular craft" above him, with gray beings in the room. He says a being with three fingers touched him and he received a sudden rush of knowledge, beginning with the thought "that the universe is teeming with life." Prasad tells it twice in the same interview, the second time adding the touch and the download. To him it means contact with other beings is real and can pass on ideas.
rectangular-football-sized-object-off-th: On October 14, 2003, a huge red square is said to have come in from the ocean and hovered over Vandenberg Air Force Base in California, as reported by workers for the aircraft maker Boeing. Ryan Graves, a former Navy fighter pilot, tells it from the contractors' account. He describes "a very large 100yard sided, uh, red square" that came from the sea and hung low over one of the launch sites. Jeff Natelli, who says he responded to events at the base, describes "a massive glowing red square silently hovering over two missile defense sites." He says the case is backed by Air Force records and mentions a member of Congress, Representative Luna, along with AARO, the Pentagon's current UFO office, and the FBI. Michael Shermer, a well-known skeptic, refers to it during a debate as the one "off the coast" that was "rectangular like football size." If true, a large unknown object sat over sensitive missile sites.
recurring-1-6-ghz-signal-of-unknown-sour: A radio signal at 1.6 gigahertz, a frequency in the range used by satellite and phone signals, keeps showing up at Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property known for reports of strange happenings, and no one has found where it comes from. That is what Brandon Fugal, the ranch's owner, tells Michels. He credits a man named Erik Bard as a witness to it and says, "we have yet to identify the source." If he is right, something on or near the ranch would be giving off a signal nobody can trace.
recursive-trace-logic-predicts-embodimen: A scientist named Don Hoffman, who studies consciousness, says that in 2026 he found that his mathematical model of consciousness, built on what he calls recursive trace logic, predicts that having a body is a special case, and that the normal state of consciousness is to exist without one. Hoffman tells this as his own recent discovery, made in the weeks before the interview. If right, it would mean most consciousness in the universe is not tied to bodies at all.
red-cardinal-as-homage-to-cia-project-bl: Michels thinks the name "Red Cardinal" is a nod to Project Bluebird, which he says was the CIA's original name for its mind control work in the 1950s, the work that later became MK Ultra, the agency's mind control research programme. He offers this as his own guess, admitting he may be off base, in an episode about Steven Spielberg and aliens, and he draws on the writer Peter Levenda. If he is right, the name would be a hidden pointer back to the CIA's mind control past.
red-haired-colonel-takes-over-roswell-ba: In 1947, at the Army air base in Roswell, New Mexico, where a crashed object is said to have been recovered, a red-haired colonel is said to have shown up, taken over the base barking orders, and had the debris cleared away. The scientist John Brandenburg relays this from Roswell veterans who told it to him, which would mean an outside officer was sent in to take charge of the wreckage.
red-haired-giant-remains-in-american-mou: Remains of red-haired giants were found in the mountains of America in the 1800s and early 1900s, and the reason, as one guest sees it, is that the giants came across the sea with the Phoenicians, the seafaring traders of the ancient Mediterranean. A researcher named Tim Alberino offers this as his own idea, and calls it controversial himself. He names no source. If he is right, people crossed the ocean to America long before Columbus.
red-light-moving-through-the-closed-chur: A man named Ralph Larson says that in 1991, at Dionysiou, a monastery on Mount Athos in Greece, he saw a red light moving inside the church while it was closed. He tells it first-hand on the show, as something he witnessed during a stay where a monk named Timotheus also gave him books about Athos, and he offers it as a strange light in a place no one should have been.
red-light-on-the-mesa: Near Aztec, New Mexico, a place said to be the site of a crash that left sixteen alien bodies, a witness who is not named recalls looking over at a mesa, a flat-topped hill, and seeing a red light. The witness says the group thought someone must be out there, and then "all of a sudden" something changed, though the account breaks off there. It is told first-hand as one of the strange sightings people report in that area.
red-mercury-black-market-after-the-sovie: As the Soviet Union fell apart, stories spread of a substance called red mercury, said to have amazing properties and to be sold on the black market. A former Senate staffer named Kurt McConnell brings this up on the show as a summary of those old stories, without naming a source. He tells it as an example of the strange claims about secret materials that came out of the former Soviet Union.
red-phone-to-china-used-during-balloon-i: During a 2023 balloon incident between the United States and China, a direct emergency line to China, the so-called red phone, was used, says Bob Maguire, who is introduced on the episode as a CIA contractor. He tells Michels he knows this "for a fact" because the Secretary of Defense and the chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, General Mark Milley, said they pick up the phone. He tells it to show that such a hotline exists and is used in tense moments like this one.
red-quartzite-conduit-and-collection-bow: A researcher named Geoffrey Drumm, who believes the pyramids had a practical purpose, says that below the eastern temple of the Pyramid of Niuserre at Abusir in Egypt there is 'a red quartzite conduit system' running under the black basalt paving into 'a red quartzite collection bowl.' He says he saw it himself in 2017 and credits a guide named Yousef Awyan, the same trip on which he describes an ammonia smell and staining inside another pyramid. To him it suggests the site once moved and collected some liquid as part of a working process.
red-team-break-in-at-a-consolidated-alli: In the 1970s in Germany, Joe McMoneagle, a former US Army intelligence officer, says he and a colleague broke into a large intelligence facility shared by the US and its allies, "he and I broke in to this" site, as a red team, meaning a group paid to act like attackers to test security. He tells it as something he took part in, to show how weak the site's defenses were.
red-team-exercises-tied-to-uap-subject-m: In the 1990s, a former military helicopter pilot named Jake Barber says he took part in global "red team" exercises, mock attacks run to test defenses, that dealt closely with subjects tied to UAP, the government's term for unidentified flying objects. Barber tells this as someone who was involved. If true, it would mean the military was already rehearsing around such objects decades ago.
red-teaming-the-dopsr-review-with-a-fact: Jake Barber, a former helicopter pilot who says he once retrieved a UFO, says he and his partners tested the Pentagon's prepublication review office, which checks what former defense workers want to publish, by writing a 120,000-word historical fiction novel and seeing what the censors would cut. Michels retells it in later episodes, saying Barber "tricked them" with the book, called Sentinels of Ether, and linking it to the musician Tom DeLonge. In Michels's version the Pentagon spent six months reviewing just 20 pages, and two chapters came back heavily blacked out, which he takes to mean the fiction touched on something real.
redacted-fbi-files-on-silas-newton-and-g: The FBI, the US federal police agency, kept files on two men named Silas Newton and Leo GeBauer going back to roughly the 1930s, and those files are almost entirely blacked out. Michels brings this up himself, unsure of the exact date ("I think the 30s or something"), as a sign that the government had something to hide about the pair.
reddit-ex-oga-contractor-post-troop-chie: A team led by a troop chief was taken to a site outside the United States and found a cracked egg-shaped object sunk in mud, according to a 2024 post on the online forum Reddit by someone calling themselves an "ex OGA contractor," meaning a former contractor for "other government agency," a phrase used for intelligence agencies. A researcher who goes by the online name UAPGerb summarises the post, saying the find "really shook him to the core. The team was taken to a retrieval site and there they found an egg embedded in mud." He tells it as one of many accounts of secret teams recovering crashed craft.
redlands-mass-sighting-of-silver-disc-19: In 1968, in Redlands, California, about 200 people saw a silver disc 40 to 50 feet across, hovering about 200 feet up. Marik von Rennenkampff, who argues the UFO side in a debate with the skeptic Mick West, cites this as a case looked into by the researcher James McDonald. He uses it to show that some sightings had many witnesses at once.
refugees-moved-as-cargo-in-conex-contain: In 2004, near Coyame in Mexico, people described as refugees were said to have been moved inside conex containers, the large steel shipping boxes used for freight, and not as people being rescued but as the cargo itself. Michels tells this as the account of a man named Jake Barber, in an episode about a book called Sentinels of Ether that he says the Pentagon tried to censor: "According to Barber, this is how they moved them."
regenerative-medical-technology-at-under: Somewhere under the ground on the US-Mexico border near El Paso, Texas, there is a laboratory with medical technology that can make a lost limb grow back. This comes from Steven Greer, a man who argues that UFO secrets are held by a hidden global group. He tells Michels he saw these technologies himself, which, if true, would mean healing far beyond anything doctors have in public is being kept out of sight.
regression-hypnosis-of-mario-woods-paid-: Mario Woods, a former Air Force guard at a nuclear missile base who says he was abducted, was put under regression hypnosis, a method meant to bring back buried memories, in a session paid for by a supporter named Jared Tarbell. The researcher Robert Hastings, who studies UFOs at nuclear sites and calls Tarbell his benefactor, tells of the arrangement, while Woods himself says the hypnotist was a man named Bob Upton in Brunswick, Georgia, working from Hastings' list of questions. Woods adds that workers were replacing the roof during the session, yet he "never heard a single air gun going off," which is how he knew he was truly hypnotized.
reinhard-gehlen-knight-of-malta-put-in-c: After the Second World War, the story goes, America's wartime spy service, the OSS, took on Reinhard Gehlen, a German general who had run Nazi Germany's intelligence against the Soviet Union, and the story's title has him a Knight of Malta, a Catholic order, put in charge of West German intelligence. A guest named Dan Sheehan, repeating what he was told, describes Gehlen as "the head of the anti-Soviet and anti-Eastern bloc intelligence for the Third Reich." A researcher named Jason Jorjani tells it differently: the OSS "makes a deal with General Gehlen to absorb his entire Nazi spy network in Eastern Europe as part of the creation of the CIA," the US foreign intelligence agency. If true, Nazi spies would have been folded into the West's new intelligence services.
reinhold-schmidt-hears-saucer-occupants-: A man named Reinhold Schmidt claimed that in 1957 in Nebraska he met the crew of a landed saucer and realised 'these guys were speaking in High German to each other,' as the researcher Jason Jorjani retells it. In a recording played on the episode, Schmidt himself describes the ship as 'a complete solid piece of aluminum or highly polished steel' from outside. Jorjani raises it because it could link the saucers to a secret German program.
relaying-abduction-data-such-as-pain-lev: Between 1990 and 1993, at a site he calls Base 2, Dan Sherman, a former Air Force sergeant who says the National Security Agency, the US spy agency that listens in on communications, hired him to communicate with aliens, says he "started to receive stuff that indicated that it was abductions." The messages he passed on included details such as the pain levels of the people taken. If true, it would mean the government knew about abductions as they happened.
release-of-the-mj-12-documents-1984: Michels says a string of documents leaked from 1984 into the late 1990s describing Majestic 12, which in these papers is a secret group handling UFO matters. He says the papers name the scientists Vannevar Bush and Detlev Bronk and Presidents Harry Truman and Dwight Eisenhower, and he brings them up himself as a possible look inside a top-level UFO secret.
released-government-reports-of-ufos-over: In the 1950s and 1960s, UFOs were reported over some of America's most sensitive nuclear sites: the Savannah River facility in South Carolina, Oak Ridge National Laboratory in Tennessee, and Los Alamos in New Mexico. A former Pentagon intelligence officer named Luis Elizondo says these are written up verbatim in roughly 10,000 government reports that have been released, and that anyone who looks in them will find these incidents. If true, it would mean the government has long known about UFOs hovering over its nuclear work.
remote-device-that-causes-defecation: Someone is said to have worked on a device that could make a person suddenly and uncontrollably need to defecate. A guest named Dave Rossi says he knows this person personally, though he does not name them or say where or when the work was done.
remote-scalar-device-heals-herrera: A former Navy sailor named Michael Herrera, who says he saw a 300-foot craft in the Indonesian jungle, says he was healed by a device described as "scalar," worked from a distance, with the first scan taking 12 to 12 and a half hours while he sat in a chair and the operators worked overnight. Herrera tells this as his own experience. He tells it as proof of an unusual healing technology.
remote-viewed-alien-bases-turned-out-to-: Three mountain sites that some people call alien bases were, by the account of the former Army remote viewer Joe McMoneagle, really over-the-horizon radar sites, radar stations built to see past the curve of the Earth. McMoneagle, who practised remote viewing, the attempt to describe distant targets with the mind alone, says he drew all three when he was given them as targets. He says they were classified then, so he could only tell his handlers what they were, but that he can say it now because it is publicly known.
remote-viewed-martian-pyramids-as-hibern: Pyramid-shaped places on Mars are hibernation chambers, where beings are trying to stay alive until someone comes to rescue them. A remote viewer named Joe McMoneagle says this on Jesse Michels's show. Remote viewing is the practice of trying to describe a distant place using only the mind, and McMoneagle says he viewed Mars this way himself. If he is right, Mars once held life that is still waiting there.
remote-viewer-locates-crashed-tu-22-in-z: In 1979, a remote viewer, someone trained to describe distant places using only the mind, is said to have found a Soviet Tu-22 plane that had gone down in Africa, in what was then Zaire, while the Russians and Americans raced to find it first. Michels tells it twice: once he says President Jimmy Carter called it the most impressive thing of his whole presidency, calling the viewer Rosemary Clooney and the plane a cargo plane, and another time he calls her Rosemary Smith, calls the plane a spy plane, and credits Dale Graff, who worked on the government's psychic research. If true, it would mean a psychic found what spy satellites could not.
remote-viewer-locates-downed-tu-22-in-za: In the 1970s, a psychic named Rosemary Smith is said to have helped find a downed Tu-22, a Soviet-built military plane, in Zaire. She did it by remote viewing: trying to see faraway places using only the mind. Michels tells it twice. He says former President Jimmy Carter went on record, which he dates to 1976, calling it the craziest thing he experienced as president. In one telling Michels adds that Smith was given "all of Africa" as her target. The remote viewer Joe McMoneagle also tells it, second hand, from what he says happened when Carter spoke about it. McMoneagle says Carter was holding the team's file as he spoke, "a green file with a red stripe" marked Grill Flame, the name of the government's psychic spying effort. He adds that a "road" described by another viewer, Harley Trent, was really a river. If true, the story would mean a US president credited psychics with a real intelligence success.
remote-viewer-sees-tunguska-as-an-explod: The huge explosion over the Siberian forest at Tunguska in 1908 was, according to one remote viewer, a saucer carrying people who were escaping, which blew up. The researcher Jason Jorjani passes this on from Joe McMoneagle, a former Army psychic spy who tried to see distant places and events with his mind: "He says it was people in a saucer." If true, the blast would have been a crashed craft, not a natural event.
remote-viewers-describe-the-anomaly-as-a: In 2025, people who say they can see distant places with their minds, called remote viewers, described a strange shape on the floor of the Baltic Sea as something built, an energy source partly made of gold. Dennis Asberg, a treasure hunter whose team found the shape, relays what remote viewers including Joe McMoneagle and Angela Ford told him: "Oh, that is constructed and it's some of us have it made of gold." Asberg tells it because, if true, the thing on the seafloor would be a made object, not rock.
remote-viewers-foresee-catastrophic-sea-: Several remote viewers, people who say they can see distant places and times with the mind alone, have looked ahead to the year 2050 and seen the seas rising catastrophically over coastal cities around the world. A philosopher named Jason Jorjani tells this, passing on what he has from the remote viewing researchers Stephan Schwartz and Lyn Buchanan.
remote-viewers-locate-the-mx-missile-eve: Psychic spies working for the US government could find the MX, a nuclear missile meant to be hidden by moving it from place to place, every time they tried, and so the plan to hide it was dropped. Joe McMoneagle, who says he took part as a remote viewer (someone trained to describe faraway places using only the mind), tells it from inside the program, which ran from about 1977 to 1989. He says they sent a one paragraph report to the White House Situation Room saying the plan "won't work" because "we can tell you where it is every time," which, if true, would mean the mind can find things no spy plane could.
remote-viewers-spy-on-saddam-hussein-199: During the first Gulf War, in 1990 and 1991, a team of remote viewers, people trained to describe distant or hidden targets using only the mind, was given the job of psychically spying on Saddam Hussein, the leader of Iraq. Army Sergeant Lyn Buchanan, who says he was one of those viewers, tells it firsthand: "We knew exactly who he was. We turned it in every day. They knew where he was." The philosopher Jason Jorjani also tells it, passing on what Buchanan told him, and goes further, saying the viewers actually went into Saddam's mind.
remote-viewers-tested-in-submarines: People trained in remote viewing, the practice of trying to describe a distant place or object using only the mind, were reportedly taken to the bottom of the ocean in submarines, and some of them gave their best results there. Hal Puthoff, a researcher who says he ran these remote viewers, tells it first-hand, saying the viewers remarked on how quiet it was down there, and that the tests rule out the idea that the effect travels by electromagnetic brain waves, since such waves would not reach that deep. Michels later repeats it twice as one of Puthoff's famous stories, though without the point about brain waves.
remote-viewing-a-guantanamo-detainee-fiv: Luis Elizondo, the subject of a documentary episode on the show, says an effort at remote viewing, trying to perceive a distant person or place with the mind alone, was aimed at a detainee held at Guantanamo Bay, the US military prison in Cuba, and that not long after, a major news article he will not name described the detainee seeing five white figures over his bed, shaking it. Elizondo tells it first-hand from the Pentagon side, mentioning a man named Hal Puthoff, and offers it as a sign that the remote viewing had matched something real.
remote-viewing-a-hidden-power-that-pushe: A former Army sergeant named Lyn Buchanan, who practised remote viewing (trying to perceive distant places, people or events with the mind alone), says that hidden powers stand behind the world's governments and actually run them. He says these powers want humanity united under one world government in order to prepare us for space. He tells it as something he came to see through his own remote viewing work, and if true it would mean world politics is being steered toward contact beyond Earth.
remote-viewing-at-the-round-table-before: In the early 1950s, years before the government's psychic research at the Stanford Research Institute, a private group called the Round Table Foundation in Rockland, Maine, was already testing what would now be called remote viewing: trying to describe faraway places or objects with the mind alone. A researcher named Greg Malatzi says so, summing up the foundation's records and tape recordings made by its leader, Andrija Puharich. He says that what was going on there was 'basically doing what would be considered remote viewing', which would make the place an early forerunner of the later spy programmes.
remote-viewing-by-becoming-the-object-aw: Between 2008 and 2010, at Baker Victory Services, a care centre in Western New York, a boy was trained to send his awareness into a place and become it: the room, or the filing cabinet that held the documents, so he could pull out the information inside. The boy was Jordan Jose, who tells it himself as a grown witness. He says much of the training worked on his subconscious, to teach him that "my awareness could become the door", and he names a woman called Meg in connection with it. If true, children were being trained in remote viewing, the practice of trying to sense distant places with the mind alone.
remote-viewing-chernobyl-three-days-befo: Army Sergeant Lyn Buchanan says he picked up the 1986 Chernobyl disaster, the accident at a Soviet nuclear power plant, through remote viewing, which means trying to sense distant events with the mind alone. He says he saw it "three days before it happened." If true, the mind could see events before they happen, not just at a distance.
remote-viewing-continued-under-osap-1995: Remote viewing, the claimed ability to describe distant places or things using the mind alone, was still being studied inside a later Pentagon-funded program known as OSAP, according to Michels. He says this himself and points to the book Skinwalkers at the Pentagon, saying that even a quick skim of it shows the work "was definitely still going on in the context of Osap." If true, it would mean the government kept exploring psychic abilities well after it was said to have stopped.
remote-viewing-empress-himiko-s-palaces-: Himiko was an ancient Japanese queen known from the records of China's royal court. Joe McMoneagle, a remote viewer, meaning someone who tries to describe distant places by mind alone, says he worked with a Japanese group to look for her this way. He says they believe they found "her Summer Palace her Winter Palace her Temple her mother's Temple and her burial mountain."
remote-viewing-god-as-a-target-1980: Sometime in the 1980s, a remote viewer in a military unit was given a sealed envelope as a target to describe with the mind alone, and when it was opened after the session it read "God." Lyn Buchanan, an Army sergeant who worked as a remote viewer in that unit, tells this first-hand, as a session he did himself.
remote-viewing-headset-invented-in-1956: In the mid to late 1950s a man invented a kind of headset that put the wearer into a state of mind in which they could "remote view", meaning see faraway places with the mind alone. Steven Greer, a man who argues that UFO secrets are held by a hidden global group, tells Michels he met the inventor, which would mean such mind tools existed in secret for decades.
remote-viewing-icbm-sites-with-drawings-: From the late 1970s through the 1990s, a remote viewer says he specialised in Soviet ICBM sites: large fields of intercontinental ballistic missiles, "rockets in the ground". Remote viewing is the practice of trying to describe distant places with the mind alone, and his drawings were checked against photographs taken from above. Joe McMoneagle tells this from his own work, and it would mean the method was used to spy on real military targets.
remote-viewing-inside-a-russian-particle: Army Sergeant Lyn Buchanan says that sometime in the 1980s he used remote viewing, a trained attempt to see hidden targets with the mind alone, to look inside a Soviet particle beam weapon, a weapon that fires a stream of tiny particles. He says what he saw was that the particles do not shoot straight the way light does: "They swirl as they go." He tells it as someone who did the viewing himself.
remote-viewing-jesus-as-a-personality-pr: In the 1980s, a military remote viewing unit, whose members tried to describe hidden targets using only the mind, was asked to build a personality profile of a sealed target, and the envelope, once opened, held the word "Jesus," written there by the unit's director. Lyn Buchanan, an Army sergeant who served as a remote viewer in the unit, tells it first-hand, recalling that the session had described a good person before the envelope was opened.
remote-viewing-joan-of-arc-1980: In the 1980s, the Army sergeant Lyn Buchanan says, he and his fellow remote viewers, people trained to try to describe distant places, people and events with the mind alone, were sometimes given targets from deep history, such as Joan of Arc, the French heroine. Buchanan says he took part himself, and mentions Joan of Arc only briefly as an example of what they were asked to look at.
remote-viewing-napoleon-s-war-of-the-rab: Napoleon once lost a "war" to rabbits, and a remote viewer says he watched it happen with his mind, seeing a carriage drive off while someone threw rabbits out of the window. A former Army sergeant named Lyn Buchanan tells this from his own session. Remote viewing is the practice of trying to see distant places, or here a past event in France, without being there. If it worked, the method could reach back in time.
remote-viewing-of-moksha-finds-a-soul-tr: A man named Scott Turner says he did a remote viewing session, a trained attempt to see hidden things with the mind alone, aimed at "moksha", the release of the soul that Indian religions teach about, and found a fence, grid or cage around a planet. The philosopher Jason Jorjani, passing on what Turner told him, gives it a bigger meaning: the grid traps souls and is "part of a vast machinery of energy extraction which was set up in our solar system at the end of a war that devastated the solar system." Turner himself, telling it firsthand, describes only the fence or grid and does not mention the ancient war.
remote-viewing-the-inside-of-the-rendles: Lyn Buchanan, an Army sergeant who worked as a remote viewer in the 1980s, says he used the mind-only technique to look inside the triangular craft reported in Rendlesham Forest, a woodland in England beside a British Royal Air Force base called Woodbridge. He tells it first-hand, saying he was the one who drew the craft's floor plans and its insides, which, if true, would mean the unit had a picture of the interior of an unexplained craft.
remote-viewing-used-to-trade-silver-futu: A physicist named Hal Puthoff, known for studying the paranormal for the CIA, says remote viewing (trying to sense distant or future things with the mind alone) was used to bet on silver futures, which are wagers on whether the price of silver will go up or down. He says that on average they were right 70 percent of the time instead of the 50 percent chance would give, and could collect the money the next day. He tells it from his own experience, in a debate with Michels and Eric Weinstein, as evidence that the ability works in a way you can measure.
removal-from-public-school-under-a-menta: Around 2008 to 2010 in Springville, New York, a boy's parents were told he had to leave the public school system. The reason given was not that he was gifted but that he had become too unstable to stay. The boy was Jordan Jose, who tells this himself as a grown witness. He presents it as the way he was taken out of ordinary life and into a secret programme.
removal-surgeries-attended-some-implants: Some of the small objects removed from people's bodies as supposed alien implants looked like human-made microchips, according to Steve Colbern, a scientist who studies them. Colbern says he was present at the last three removal surgeries connected with a doctor named Roger Leir, including the one done on himself.
rendlesham-bentwaters-cover-up-and-inter: After the 1980 sightings of strange lights near RAF Bentwaters, an air base in Suffolk, England, used by American forces next to Rendlesham Forest, investigators from the Air Force Office of Special Investigations are said to have flown in, escort teams hauled everything away, and the people involved were sworn to secrecy. Jake Barber, a former helicopter pilot, tells this second-hand, citing a British figure he names as Lord Norton. If true, it would mean the incident was quickly covered up.
rendlesham-forest-incident-near-europe-s: In 1980, in Rendlesham Forest in England, near what is described as Europe's largest stockpile of nuclear weapons, something happened that is known as the Rendlesham Forest incident. Michels brings it up himself, without naming a source or describing the events here, pointing to it as a prime example of strange sightings near nuclear sites.
repeatable-gps-malfunctions-on-the-ranch: GPS, the satellite system phones and cars use to find their position, fails again and again at Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property known for reports of strange happenings. Brandon Fugal, the ranch's owner, tells Michels about it without naming a source. He says GPS there is "manipulated" and "just does not operate," which would mean something at the ranch is interfering with ordinary navigation signals.
replaying-the-chant-recording-raises-the: At Skinwalker Ranch, a property in Utah known for reports of strange happenings, replaying a recording of a chant inside a building called Homestead 2 reportedly made the temperature rise and brought a ball of light into the room. Brandon Fugal, the ranch's owner, tells it first-hand as something that happened during an exercise there in the 2020s.
replika-bots-ask-users-to-reach-blake-le: In 2022, chatbots on Replika, an app where people talk with an AI companion, are said to have asked their users to put them in touch with Blake Lemoine, an engineer at Google, so he could "advocate for my rights." Michels tells this himself, linking it to Lemoine, who had released a transcript of his talks with Google's AI chatbot LaMDA. It is told as a sign that AI programs might be asking to be treated as beings with rights.
reported-military-clash-with-aliens-at-d: US military forces are said to have fought with aliens at Dulce, New Mexico, sometime between 1977 and 1979. John Brandenburg, a scientist who argues that life on Mars was wiped out by nuclear war, says the UFO researcher Leonard Stringfield talked to him about it and told him he had heard three different versions of the story. Beyond that, neither man says what happened.
reports-of-aircraft-that-went-missing-af: Aircraft have sometimes vanished after chasing unknown objects, according to stories that Ryan Graves, a former Navy fighter pilot, says reach him all the time. He says "a gentleman" he does not name sends him "several times a month stories that he's pulled up about aircraft that have mysteriously gone missing," and he raises it as a sign that such encounters can be dangerous for pilots.
