reptilians-as-dinosaur-hybrids-made-by-t: The reptile-like beings of alien lore, called reptilians, were supposedly made by the Nordics, tall human-looking aliens, who genetically mixed dinosaurs with themselves to create a slave race. The philosopher Jason Jorjani lays this out, drawing on a work he credits called Closer Encounters, and puts it as a question: why not take dinosaurs and hybridize them? If true, it would make one kind of alien the creation of another.
republican-politician-angered-by-argenti: Around 1945, an American Republican politician, a very conservative right-wing man, is said to have become furious when he found out that Argentina was protecting Nazi war criminals who had fled there after the war. The author Peter Levenda tells this without naming the man, drawing on the books Secret Machines War and The Hitler Legacy, as part of a larger story about Nazis and their secrets escaping to South America.
request-to-bring-harrington-to-testify-t: In 2025, David Grusch, a former intelligence officer who has made claims about crashed-craft recovery, is said to have sought help getting an official named John Harrington to Washington to possibly testify to the House Oversight Committee, a committee of the US Congress. The television writer Bryce Zabel tells this as something he took part in: he says the journalist Ross Coulthart called him and asked him to ask a man named Brent to help bring Harrington to Washington.
research-report-on-three-ways-to-read-th: One of the first pieces of research Bryce Zabel and his collaborators got back on a certain formula was a report of about 20 pages that broke it into three main ways to interpret it. Zabel, a guest on an episode about Hollywood, the CIA and UFOs, describes the report himself, without naming who wrote it, as an early attempt to make sense of what the formula meant.
researcher-chris-evans-dies-on-the-day-h: A researcher named Chris Evans died on the very day he was coming to meet the Ramseys, according to Scott Ramsey, a UFO crash researcher who tells it of his own family and his wife Susanna. Ramsey says Evans died in 2005 on a bridge in West Virginia and points to a West Virginia Highway Patrol report on it. He also mentions a woman named Alice Scully in telling it, and raises the death as one of the strange turns in his research.
researcher-forwards-an-alleged-ransone-e: A researcher who is not named on the show says that, sometime between 2010 and 2021, another man forwarded him an email said to be from a woman named Valerie Ransone, and then the man disappeared from contact. The researcher tells it as something that happened to him: "he forwards me an email, which is allegedly from Valerie." He tells it as part of a wider story about a government scientist said to have been in contact with an alien council.
researcher-friend-in-touch-with-eric-hen: A man named Eric Henry Wang, linked to Wright-Patterson Air Force Base in Ohio in the 1950s, really existed, says Jesse Michels, who tells this from what a researcher friend he does not name told him. Michels says "I could say definitively he was real cuz I have a researcher friend who's in touch with his daughter now," and he offers it to show that a figure from these old stories was a real person.
researcher-s-archive-destroyed-by-his-wi: After the death of a Brazilian researcher who had gathered material on a case from 1996, his widow is said to have destroyed his files, while his daughter, Claudia Kovu, kept part of them. Carlos de Souza, a surgeon interviewed on the podcast, passes on what Kovu herself says: "her stepmother destroyed all the material and she still has a part of the material." If so, some of the record of the case may still survive with her.
researchers-measure-energy-fields-at-pyr: Researchers are said to have measured energy fields at ancient pyramids and stone sites in Mexico and Central America, Europe and Egypt, and found that seeds kept there grew far better. Jim Weiner, a researcher of such sites, says from a book he calls Seeds of Knowledge, Stones of Power that they found "they increase yield per acre like three to five times." The pyramid researcher Geoffrey Drumm credits the same work to John Burke and his book, which he calls Seed of Knowledge, Stone of Plenty. Drumm says the fields were recorded with electrostatic voltmeters, instruments that measure static electric charge, and that they showed a positive charge on the ground at stone circles. He also names the researcher Hugh Newman. The tellers raise it because, if true, it would mean these ancient sites were built to do something practical, such as boost farming.
researchers-question-dr-eric-walker-abou: UFO researchers are said to have walked into the Penn State University office of an engineer named Eric A. Walker and asked him outright what he knew about UFOs. Michels tells it as "do you know anything about the UFO stuff," set in the 1980s. A researcher who goes by UAPGerb says Walker admitted he knew about Majestic 12, an alleged secret committee set up to handle crashed UFOs. Walker said he had known about the group for 40 years. UAPGerb credits the UFO researcher William Steinman, and also names Henry Azadehdel. In one version he names the questioner as Styon and says Walker answered with a Don Quixote impersonation. Grant Cameron, a UFO researcher, says he was there himself, which he puts about 30 years ago. He says that when talk turned to the committee, Walker cut the questioner off and asked, "What do you know about ESP?" ESP is extra-sensory perception, sensing things without the normal senses. Cameron says the man had no answer. Cameron also says they asked Walker whether there had ever been communication, adding "we promise not to tell." The story matters because it suggests a well-placed scientist knew of a secret UFO group and tied it to the mind.
resolute-sentinel-joint-exercise-in-peru: A 2023 military exercise in Peru called Resolute Sentinel may have been a cover for something else, according to a researcher named Tim Alberino. He describes it as a joint exercise that involved "basically every military agency", and he raises it as a possible screen for some other operation, though he names no source. If he were right, a public training event would have hidden a secret mission.
resorts-international-intertel-and-donal: A paint company, the Merry Carter Paint Company, is said to have turned into a casino business called Resorts International, which then had a subsidiary running a private intelligence network called Intertel, short for International Intelligence Incorporated. A researcher named Jason Simosa tells this without naming a source, and in one telling he links it to Donald Trump. In another he credits a man named Meyer Lansky instead, places it on Paradise Island in the Bahamas in the 1960s and 1970s, and leaves Trump out.
respected-business-leader-receives-downl: A highly credible man, a respected business leader, says he receives what he calls "downloads", knowledge that seems to arrive in his mind from outside. Eric Burlison, a member of the US Congress, tells Michels this person was brought to him and that he found him believable, which would mean serious people report getting information this way.
restoring-seti-budget-and-closed-door-se: In 1977, after Congress cut funding for SETI, the scientific search for signals from alien civilisations, a group lobbied members of the House of Representatives and got the money put back. A guest named Dan Sheehan says he took part, going round to members of Congress with others, including the former astronaut Rusty Schweickart, and he also mentions a congressional researcher named Marcia Smith. The story's title also links this to a closed-door seminar for SETI scientists at the Jet Propulsion Laboratory, NASA's space research centre. It would mean people inside Washington were quietly backing the search for alien life.
restroom-in-the-back-of-the-alien-craft: An alien craft kept at Area 51, a secret US Air Force test site in the Nevada desert, had a restroom in the back. A man named Charles Hall says so, telling it as something he saw himself: "In the back of that craft was a restroom." If true, it would suggest the beings flying it had bodily needs much like ours.
retired-navy-pilot-s-family-sees-lights-: The family of a retired Navy pilot living in Pacific Palisades, California, have seen several white lights flying in formation over the channel off the coast, which they took to be under "intelligent control." A retired Navy admiral named Tim Gallaudet relays what the family told him, calling the lights UAP, the official term for unidentified flying objects.
retired-titan-iv-rockets-at-wright-patte: Once their last launch was done in 2005, the remaining Titan IV rockets, large US Air Force launch rockets, were retired and sent to museums. Michels says this himself, without naming a source, in an episode about NASA and UFOs. One went to the National Museum of the US Air Force at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, and the story places another at McMinnville, Oregon.
retired-usaf-colonel-david-flies-a-craft: A retired US Air Force colonel named David, living in Orange County, California, is said to have told a story of suddenly finding himself on board a craft and flying it. The UFO researcher Grant Cameron passes on what David told him, without giving a date.
retrieval-team-members-found-living-ets-: Men who served on secret teams that recover crashed craft are said to have met living beings from elsewhere, and every one of them described those beings as very peaceful, very enlightened and very kind. Steven Greer, a doctor who campaigns for the release of UFO secrets, says he has been meeting such men since the early 1990s and has never heard otherwise, and he mentions Jake Barber, a helicopter pilot who says he took part in one recovery. If true, it would mean those who saw the beings up close found nothing hostile in them.
retrieval-teams-for-crashed-triangular-c: Special teams have gone out to recover crashed triangle-shaped craft, according to Steven Greer, a doctor and activist who campaigns for the government to reveal what it knows about UFOs. Greer says he knows "two different people who've been on the retrieval teams of the triangular ones," but he does not name them, and he tells it as proof that such craft are being collected in secret.
retrieved-craft-revealed-unknown-propuls: Studying recovered craft taught the US that kinds of propulsion exist that no one had ever imagined. That is how Harold Malmgren, a former advisor to US presidents, puts it, pointing to the account of Philip J. Corso, an Army officer who wrote about handling such material: "some types of propulsion for example exist that we did never, never envision." If true, it would mean the craft gave the country a real leap in technology.
return-to-athos-with-a-month-long-visa-v: In 2005, Ralph Larson, a former CIA officer, says he went back to Mount Athos, a mountain in Greece home to Orthodox monasteries, with a month-long permit to stay, which he arranged through the head of the CIA's office in Athens, an old friend he does not name. He tells it first-hand, as part of a trip that took him to Saint Anne's skete, a small community of monks on the mountain.
return-to-november-5-for-documentary-fil: Mario Woods, a former guard at US nuclear missile sites who says he was abducted by a UFO on a November 5 long ago, returned in the 2020s to the spot on Orman Road near New Underwood, South Dakota, to film a documentary. Woods says that as he got out of the vehicle and walked toward the site, "that feeling came over me, I about went to my knees." He tells it as his own experience, a sign of how strongly the place still affects him.
reuters-story-quoting-flavio-estrada-tha: The Nazca mummies, three-fingered bodies from Peru that some people put forward as possibly not human, are said in a news report to be "dolls made from animal bones from this planet joined together with modern synthetic glue." Michels reads this out on his show, quoting an article from the news agency Reuters in early 2024 in which a man named Flavio Estrada gave that judgment. Michels brings it up as the main argument against the bodies being anything unearthly.
revelation-of-the-echelon-surveillance-s: In the 1990s, the Australian journalist Ross Coulthart says he was the first to reveal Echelon, a system for spying on communications run by Five Eyes, the intelligence alliance of five English-speaking countries including Australia. Coulthart tells it first-hand as one of the biggest stories of his time reporting in Australia. He raises it to show he has broken real secret-government stories before.
reverse-engineered-craft-flown-only-with: There are stories, Michels says, of a secret program copying recovered non-human craft in which the only way to fly the craft is with your mind. He brings it up in passing, as something he has heard from others he does not name, in an episode with the researcher Tim Alberino; if true, it would mean the craft respond to thought rather than controls.
reverse-engineering-achieved-propulsion-: Secret efforts to copy recovered craft are said to have learned enough to build working propulsion and "beamed power", meaning energy sent through the air so a device does not need its own power source on board. Matthew Brown, who has come forward as a Pentagon whistleblower, says this on the show, and if true it would mean the government has technology far beyond what the public knows.
reverse-engineering-of-a-laser-weapon-fr: Someone is said to have worked on taking apart and copying a laser weapon system recovered from a downed Russian craft. Michels describes it as "a downed Russian asset" while talking with Jeremy Corbell, a filmmaker who reports on UFOs. Corbell, citing sources he does not name here, goes further and calls the object a downed Russian "NHI spaceship," NHI meaning non-human intelligence. If true, it would mean Russia had a non-human craft and the US learned weapons technology from it.
reverse-engineering-run-out-of-national-: Work on taking apart and copying non-human technology is said to be ongoing and run out of the US national laboratories. Matthew Brown, a former Pentagon official turned whistleblower, says so partly from what he was told, adding that the national labs are where samples of exotic technologies are stored. If true, it would place any recovered material inside the government's own research labs.
review-panel-removed-from-the-uap-disclo: The independent review board meant to oversee the release of UFO records was cut from the first version of the UAP Disclosure Act, says Ryan Graves, a former Navy fighter pilot, who calls it his "biggest disappointment" ("UAP" is the government's term for UFOs). The board matters because it would have pushed the records out. The bill as Senator Chuck Schumer submitted it on 13 July 2023 did create an "Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Records Review Board" as an independent agency. It was to have nine citizens appointed by the President with the Senate's consent, charged with the "public disclosure of government records relating to unidentified anomalous phenomena".
rfk-jr-says-thane-eugene-cesar-killed-hi: Robert F. Kennedy Jr., son of the senator Robert F. Kennedy who was shot dead in Los Angeles in 1968, is said to believe his father was not killed by Sirhan Sirhan, the man convicted of it, but shot from behind by Thane Eugene Cesar, whom Michels describes as a security guard at Skunk Works, the secret aircraft division of the company Lockheed. Michels tells this himself several times, saying he has talked to the son about it at length. In one telling Sirhan may also have fired but Cesar shot from the back, and some tellings bring in Bob Maheu, a fixer for the billionaire Howard Hughes. If true, it would mean the killing was not the work of one man.
ribicoff-mission-on-soviet-jewish-emigra: In the 1970s, a US official worked with Senators Abe Ribicoff and Jake Javits on letting Jews leave the Soviet Union, and was sent to Jerusalem to be briefed by Israel's intelligence services, Mossad (its foreign spy agency) and Shin Bet (its domestic security service). The man is Harold Malmgren, a former presidential adviser, who tells it from his own career. He tells it to show how close he was to sensitive government work.
richard-bar-abducted-at-vandenberg-1964: In September 1964, a missile security officer named Richard Barth was guarding a missile station at Vandenberg Air Force Base in California when, Michels says, he was taken aboard a craft with four alien beings. Michels says he interviewed Barth himself, and Barth tells it firsthand: he was terrified, then everything went blank, and "I come to and I'm inside this it's a circular room." Michels tells it as one of several strange events at the base that same month.
richard-bissell-briefed-malmgren-private: Harold Malmgren, an adviser to presidents Kennedy, Johnson, Nixon and Ford, says Richard Bissell, a senior CIA official whom Michels calls the founder of Area 51, the secret US test site, privately briefed him on "otherworld technologies" the government had been trying to recover and understand, opening with the words "there are things you need to know." Malmgren tells it first-hand and adds that these forces were beyond the CIA's knowledge or control and may have interfered with its work with private industry, while the analyst Matthew Pines, the researcher UAPGerb and Michels repeat it, Michels saying he has seen Malmgren's diary, thinks it genuine, and finds Bissell all over it. The tellers date it variously to 1962, 1963, the 1960s or about 1973, and Michels says it covered past crash retrievals, including a 1933 case he calls Magenta; if true, it would mean the CIA knew of non-human technology decades ago.
richard-bissell-sets-up-area-51-for-u-2-: In 1955, a CIA official named Richard Bissell is said to have set up Area 51, a secret base in the Nevada desert, to test the U-2, a high-flying American spy plane. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, in an episode with the philosopher Jason Jorjani. He gives it as the origin of a base later tied to many UFO stories.
richard-dolan-men-in-black-as-nhi-counte: The men in black, figures said to visit and frighten people who have seen UFOs, may be a kind of counterintelligence working on behalf of non-human intelligence, meaning the aliens themselves, according to the researcher Richard Dolan. Michels passes on Dolan's view in his own words. If true, it would mean these visitors protect the aliens' secrets rather than any government's.
richard-doty-as-air-force-counterintelli: Richard Doty, a man said to have worked in Air Force counterintelligence, the branch that guards against spies, comes up when Jesse Michels starts to explain who Doty turned out to be, though his sentence trails off before he says it. Michels names him alongside two other figures from UFO circles, John Lear and Bill Cooper, and gives no further detail.
richard-doty-describes-his-role-as-an-af: Richard Doty says that in the 1970s and 1980s he was a counterintelligence officer for the Air Force Office of Special Investigations, the Air Force's own investigative and counterintelligence service. He says this himself on the show, "I was a Counter Intelligence officer for the Air Force Office of Special Investigations," to explain the position from which he says he dealt with UFO matters.
richard-doty-s-father-involved-in-area-5: The father of a man named Richard Doty was "deeply involved in Area 51 and with UFOs", Area 51 being a secret US military test site in Nevada, according to the researcher Richard Dolan, who says he got this from Doty but admits he does not know all the details. Michels later repeats it to another guest, the writer Greg Bishop, saying only that Doty's father worked at Area 51 and that Dolan told him so. If true, it would mean Doty's ties to secret UFO matters went back to his own family.
richard-foch-saw-vault-documents-dating-: The United States learned to control gravity in October 1954, according to documents a man named Richard Foch is said to have seen in a vault, linked to the Naval Research Laboratory, the Navy's science lab. Steven Greer, an activist who campaigns for UFO secrets to be made public, tells it from what Foch told him: "Rick had been in the vault and saw the documents for the date we mastered gravity control and it was October 1954." Michael Herrera, a former Marine who says he saw a huge craft in Indonesia, repeats it only through Greer, speaking of "one of his teammates" without naming Foch or giving the month, and both tell it to suggest a secret technology far beyond anything made public.
richard-hoagland-s-dark-mission-2007: NASA, the US space agency, is said to be run partly like an occult, ritual-driven organisation with a hidden history. That claim comes from Dark Mission: The Secret History of NASA, a book by the writer Richard Hoagland, published in 2007. Michels brings the book up in two episodes about life on Mars, admits it is very controversial, and says Hoagland made claims like those discussed with his guests.
richard-miethe-joins-avro-project-with-j: A German aircraft engineer named Richard Miethe, said to have worked on Nazi flying-disc projects, ended up in Canada in the 1950s on a saucer-shaped aircraft project, the Avrocar, led by an engineer named John Frost. Michels tells this himself across three episodes: in one he says the project was British-linked and run in partnership with the American CIA, the US spy agency; in another he says Miethe was the man captured by an American inventor and CIA-linked scientist named Townsend Brown, and does not mention the CIA's role; in a third he calls Miethe's work on it only speculation. If true, it would mean wartime German disc know-how passed into Western secret programs.
richard-sauder-s-book-on-deep-undergroun: Michels says underground military bases exist across the United States, called DUMBs, short for deep underground military bases, and that a writer named Richard Sauder wrote a book about them that he recommends. He brings it up himself on two episodes. In one, with a journalist who says he located a UFO base in Arizona, Michels says the book backs up that claim, though there he gives the author's name as Larry Sanders.
richard-thompson-s-alien-identities-on-t: The philosopher Jason Jorjani says a writer named Richard Thompson wrote a fine UFO book, which he thinks is called Alien Identities, that looks closely at the Ramayana and the Mahabharata, two ancient Hindu epics, and their gods, the devas, as possible accounts of visitors. Jorjani brings it up on the show from his own reading, alongside the work of a writer named Michael Cremo, author of Forbidden Archaeology.
rick-doty-s-later-claims-of-alien-races-: After being caught up in an old saga of UFO deception, a former Air Force man named Rick Doty came out saying "I am now on the side of the truth," and began telling people on UFO Twitter and on Gaia, a streaming service for paranormal shows, that there are this many alien races and that certain crashes really happened. Michels tells this himself on an episode with the writer Greg Bishop, who wrote about a man driven to breakdown by such stories. He tells it to show how hard it is to know what to make of Doty's later claims.
rick-doty-sent-to-collect-the-witnesses-: In 1977, after a missile security team at Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota said they had a strange encounter, a man named Rick Doty was sent to the base flight surgeon's office to pick up the team members' medical records. A former Air Force security guard named Mario Woods, one of that team, says so, passing on what he was later told, and also names a fellow team member, Michael Johnson. Woods raises it because it suggests someone was quietly gathering information on the men afterwards.
rick-strassman-s-dmt-study-with-60-volun: In the early 1990s a researcher named Rick Strassman gave DMT, a powerful psychedelic drug, to 60 volunteers, and many described experiences like alien abductions. The neuroscientist Andrew Gallimore describes the study without citing a source, calling it "a much larger study" than earlier work, and in another part of the talk he places it in "room 531" of the University of New Mexico hospital, with no count or details of what was reported. Gallimore tells it to suggest that DMT opens a door to a realm where such beings are met.
rickover-and-the-atomic-energy-commissio: The Atomic Energy Commission, the government body that ran America's atomic work after the war, did not come under the Department of Energy until 1976, according to John S. Herrington, a former US Secretary of Energy. He says this while talking about Hyman Rickover, and a book titled Underway My Way is credited alongside it. The point bears on which agency was responsible for what in those years.
rickover-tells-townsend-brown-the-navy-a: The inventor Thomas Townsend Brown is said to have gone to Hyman Rickover, the admiral who founded and ran the American nuclear navy, and been told to stop wasting his time because the Navy had "already figured this stuff out back then." Michels tells it himself, naming the researcher Paul LaViolette among his sources. If true, it would mean the Navy had quietly solved the kind of advanced propulsion Brown was working on.
rickover-tells-townsend-brown-the-navy-i: At some point between the 1950s and early 1960s, the researcher Thomas Townsend Brown brought his work to Hyman Rickover, a senior US Navy figure, and Rickover told him not to bother. Michels tells it himself, without naming a source, and quotes Rickover as saying, in effect, "don't waste your time, we're already on it, we know all about this." If true, it would mean the Navy was already quietly working on whatever Brown was offering.
riding-the-l-1011-jump-seat-posing-as-fa: In the 1980s, a man named Bob Lazar says, he rode in the spare cockpit seat of an L-1011, a large passenger jet, on a flight from Las Vegas to Minneapolis, passed off as an inspector from the Federal Aviation Administration, the US agency that oversees flying. He says his friend John Lear, who was flying the plane, would tell the co-pilot and flight engineer, "Hey, this guy's from the FAA, so he's just going to be observing us." Lazar tells it first-hand to Michels, as a story from the days when he first got to know Lear.
ringing-green-light-and-out-of-body-feel: While being questioned at a missile site in South Dakota, a nuclear weapons guard went to the restroom and suddenly heard a ringing in his ears "as if somebody struck a Liberty Bell right next to my head", then saw a green light and felt he had left his body. The guard, a former Air Force man named Mario Woods, tells it himself on three episodes and names a Master Sergeant Gray in it. The story places it in the 1960s, but in two tellings Woods dates it to November 1977 at a launch control site called November-1, and one of those leaves out the green light. He tells it as part of an alien abduction.
rite-of-incubation-in-the-giants-tombs: The giants' tombs, ancient stone tombs on the Italian island of Sardinia, were built so that people could perform what is called the rite of incubation, a practice of sleeping in a sacred place to receive dreams or visions. That is what the researcher Tim Alberino tells Michels. He says the archaeological community already knows this, though he names no source, and he raises it as a clue to what the tombs were really for.
rob-reinhardt-s-recent-visit-to-atlanta-: A friend of the researcher Randall Carlson, a man named Rob Reinhardt, recently visited a place Carlson calls "Atlanta", apparently meaning Atlantis, the legendary sunken island. Carlson mentions it only in passing, and his remark breaks off before he says where the place was or what Reinhardt found there.
robert-bigelow-s-plan-to-hire-the-guest-: Robert Bigelow, a businessman who ran his own aerospace company, Bigelow Aerospace, once planned to hire Steve Colbern, a scientist who studies objects said to be alien implants. Colbern says so himself, adding that the job fell through, just as another opportunity had: "that also fell through."
robert-f-kennedy-s-1968-letter-to-a-ufo-: The senator Robert F. Kennedy is said to have written a letter in 1968 to a UFO researcher with a group called the Amalgamated Flying Saucer Clubs of America, dated one month before he was killed. The UFO researcher Steven Greer brings up the letter without naming where he got it, and his phrase "before they killed him" suggests he links Kennedy's interest in UFOs to his death.
robert-goddard-rocket-testing-at-roswell: An American rocket pioneer named Robert Goddard had just been testing rockets right at Roswell, New Mexico, according to Michels, who describes them as V2 rockets, the German wartime missile. He says this himself, without naming a source, as a reason Roswell, the town later famous for a reported 1947 saucer crash, was already a place of secret aerospace work.
robert-hastings-7-or-8-of-167-nuclear-wi: Out of 167 military witnesses who saw UFOs around US nuclear weapons sites, mostly in the 1960s, about seven or eight are said to have had close encounters where they saw beings or were abducted. Michels relays this from a conversation with the researcher Robert Hastings, author of the book UFOs and Nukes: Michels asked how many had seen beings, and Hastings answered, "like seven or eight out of the 167." In an earlier episode Michels mentions the same 167 witnesses without that count, describing them as security staff for long-range nuclear missiles and radar operators. A former nuclear missile guard named Richard Barth, who says he was abducted himself, gives the book's count as "like 169 accounts" and puts the close encounters at eight. The tellers differ slightly on the numbers. If true, a small group of nuclear base personnel met the beings, not just the craft.
robert-hastings-exposes-bill-moore-s-int: In the late 1980s, a UFO researcher named Bill Moore was brought down after his links to intelligence agencies came out, and the person most responsible was another researcher, Robert Hastings. The UFO historian Richard Dolan gives this as his own opinion and names no source, though he points to the journals of MUFON, a civilian UFO research group, as the record. If he is right, it would mean one of the field's own researchers exposed a colleague who had been working with the intelligence world.
robert-hastings-feels-subliminally-guide: Robert Hastings, who wrote the book UFOs and Nukes, says he feels he is being subliminally guided, nudged without knowing it, toward disclosure, the public revealing of what is known about UFOs. A guest named Mike Masters passes this on in 2023, saying he had been "on the phone yesterday" with Hastings. If true, it would suggest some unseen influence steering people who work on the subject.
robert-hastings-interviews-on-ufos-at-nu: UFOs are said to have shown up again and again at American nuclear weapons bases, according to a book called UFOs and Nukes by the journalist Robert Hastings. Michels returns to it more than any other source and calls Hastings a friend. He says Hastings spent a lifetime interviewing about 167 military men: launch officers for long-range nuclear missiles, maintenance crews, security guards and radar operators. Many held Q clearances, a high US security clearance for nuclear work, and some signed sworn statements. In Michels' telling, the witnesses describe Tic Tacs (white ovals shaped like the mint), saucers and orbs over bases such as Malmstrom and F. E. Warren. They say missiles were shut down and tampered with, and objects were even seen in the plumes of atmospheric nuclear tests. In other episodes he widens it to bases abroad, including Rendlesham Forest in England in 1980. His numbers vary, from over 60 to almost 170, and he says Hastings once emailed to correct him: only 12 to 15 were radar operators, and the rest were missile security staff. A scientist from the Pentagon's advanced research agency, John Blitch, also calls the book powerful. The tellers point to it because so many trusted nuclear workers telling the same story would suggest something is watching the weapons.
robert-hastings-nasal-implant-and-blood-: Robert Hastings, the writer of UFOs and Nukes, a book about UFOs seen at nuclear weapons sites, is himself someone who says he has had UFO experiences, and in another book, Confessions, he writes of an implant in his nose and of waking up with blood on his pillow. Michels tells this himself, from Hastings' book, in an episode about a nuclear missile guard who says he was abducted by aliens.
robert-jameson-s-targeting-team-called-i: In 1967, at Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana, a group of nuclear missiles known as Oscar Flight is said to have dropped off alert, meaning they could no longer launch, and a missile targeting team under a man named Robert Jameson was called in to get them working again. The account comes from Robert Salas, a former Air Force officer, who passes on what Jameson told him, starting with Jameson's words, "I got a call saying a missile went off alert in Oscar flight." It is told as part of the larger claim that something shut down American nuclear weapons that year.
robert-lovett-s-memo-to-truman-leading-t: In the 1940s a Washington official named Robert Lovett is said to have written the first memo to President Harry Truman urging that something like the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency, be set up. The lawyer and researcher Dan Sheehan says this on the show, without naming where he learned it, and gives little more of the memo than its opening plea that "we've got to" act. He brings it up as part of the agency's beginnings, which would matter for his wider story about secrecy.
robert-low-memo-on-condon-study-1966: In 1966 or 1967, Robert Low, the second in charge of the Condon Committee, a University of Colorado study of UFOs paid for by the Air Force, wrote a memo about how the study would be run. Robert Salas, a former Air Force missile officer, brings it up as "a famous letter" and memo by Low, pointing to it as a sign that the study's outcome was shaped from the start.
robert-maxwell-and-nazi-tech-transfer: Robert Maxwell, a British publisher, is said both to have helped invent scientific peer review, the system where experts check each other's work before it is published, and to have been in charge of the handover of Nazi technology. Michels says this himself, without naming a source, in an episode with Tim Alberino, a man who claims a giant was captured in Afghanistan.
robert-maxwell-gatekeeping-science-via-p: Robert Maxwell, the father of Ghislaine Maxwell, was secretly an agent for British intelligence (MI6), Soviet intelligence (the KGB) and Israeli intelligence (the Mossad), and he used his control of Pergamon Press, a publisher of scientific journals, to keep groundbreaking discoveries away from the public. That is what the researcher and philosopher Jason Jorjani tells Michels, without naming where he learned it. He makes the same case in his own essay Ocean Outlaw: A Portrait of Ghislaine Maxwell, published on 29 July 2025, which says Maxwell worked "as a double agent for both MI6 and the KGB" before being recruited by the Mossad in the late 1970s, and that "as a gatekeeper, he selectively suppressed or sequestered" revolutionary research, "including defense-related research with military applications."
robert-maxwell-interrogated-nazi-scienti: Robert Maxwell, whom Michels calls a man of British foreign intelligence, is said to have interrogated Nazi scientists after the Second World War, something Michels says hardly anybody knows. Michels raises this himself on two episodes. In the second, with a guest named Matthew Brown, he adds that Maxwell later came to own Pergamon Press, a publishing house, and credits the writer Whitney Webb's book One Nation Under Blackmail, which would tie Maxwell to the handling of German wartime science.
robert-maxwell-owned-the-national-enquir: Robert Maxwell, a media owner and the father of Ghislaine Maxwell, owned the National Enquirer, an American tabloid newspaper, and Michels suggests this was a way to shape how UFOs were covered in the 1980s. Michels raises it himself, in a talk with the filmmaker James Fox, without naming a source, as part of a picture in which UFO news was flooded and steered rather than simply kept secret.
robert-maxwell-promis-software-sold-to-n: Jesse Michels says that the British publisher Robert Maxwell, whom he calls closely tied to the financier Jeffrey Epstein, sold a piece of software called PROMIS to US national laboratories, the government's big science and weapons research centres. Michels raises it himself, as a question to Bill Richardson, a former US Secretary of Energy, asking whether he knew of it; if true, it would mean software from a well-connected outsider sat inside sensitive labs.
robert-monroe-invites-mishlove-to-join-h: In the 1970s, Robert Monroe, a man who ran his own program exploring consciousness, invited the young Jeffrey Mishlove to join it, but Mishlove turned it down because he was already studying at Berkeley. Mishlove, who went on to earn a doctorate in the study of the mind and psychic matters, tells this first-hand.
robert-monroe-the-world-is-mined-for-loo: Robert Monroe, a writer on out-of-body experiences, taught that the Earth is a kind of farm, mined for "loosh," an energy given off by human emotion. Michels mentions it in passing, saying Monroe "talks about the world being kind of mined for luch." The philosopher Jason Jorjani gives more, citing Monroe's book Far Journeys, which he places in 1985: "we're in a louch farm," he says, and "humans are being deliberately subjected to conditions that create extreme emotional states." If true, it would mean human suffering is being harvested on purpose by something else. Jorjani names the book, while Michels does not.
robert-sarbacher-and-ufo-secrecy-through: A scientist named Robert Sarbacher is said to have built the secrecy around UFOs in the 1950s by using the Atomic Energy Act of 1954, a US law that put nuclear matters under strict secrecy, and he was a close confidant of a man named Thomas Townsend Brown. Michels passes this on from David Grusch, a witness who has spoken publicly about hidden UFO programmes. If true, it would mean the law that guards nuclear secrets also became a way to hide UFO material.
robert-sarbacher-liaison-with-australian: In the 1950s, a scientist named Robert Sarbacher was involved in liaison work with Australian scientists, according to a researcher named Ross Coulthart. Coulthart says only that Sarbacher "was definitely involved in liaison," and gives no further detail or source. It matters because it would place Sarbacher in contact across national lines in the years when governments were looking into UFOs.
robert-schoch-s-solar-flare-and-lichtenb: A researcher named Robert Schoch thinks the Giza plateau, the site of the great pyramids in Egypt, was once hit by a solar flare, a huge burst of energy from the sun. The idea ties to Lichtenberg figures, the branching tree-like marks that electrical discharges such as lightning leave behind. Geoffrey Drumm, a guest who studies the purpose of the pyramids, passes it on as what Schoch believes, and if true it would mean the site carries the scars of a great electrical event.
robert-temple-s-conversation-with-a-fema: A man named Robert Temple is said to have been on a flight to Singapore when what he called a plasma being, a living thing made of glowing charged gas, came into the airplane, and he had a long conversation with her. Jeffrey Mishlove, who holds a PhD and studies psychics and the afterlife, passes this on as something Temple described to him: "a plasma being entered the airplane and he had a lengthy conversation with her." If true, it would mean that such beings can come among us and speak with people.
robert-temple-s-living-plasma-thesis-and: A writer named Robert Temple, in a book called The New Science of Heaven, argues that plasma, the glowing electrically charged state of matter, is the basic substance of the universe and that it is alive. Michels recommends the book himself as a great one on two occasions. The second time he brings it up while talking with a man named Adam Curry about experiments with plasmoids, small balls of plasma, and what he calls a plasma front, rather than the living-universe idea.
roberto-pinotti-s-book-and-the-1933-blac: In 1933, according to the Italian researcher Roberto Pinotti, Italy's Fascist government sent out telegrams ordering the press to say nothing about an unknown aircraft said to have landed in the country. Pinotti quotes one: "by the personal order of Il Duce," meaning the dictator Benito Mussolini, "absolutely no mention is to be made of the alleged landing of an unknown aircraft on national soil," and he links it to the Stefani agency, the news agency of the time. Michels brings it up as the subject of a book Pinotti wrote, as a sign that a government was hiding such a landing long before the modern UFO era.
robertson-panel-adopts-a-policy-of-ridic: In 1953 a group of scientists brought together by the CIA, known as the Robertson panel after its chair Howard P. Robertson, adopted a policy of ridiculing UFOs, Michels says, telling it himself. The panel's report, written by the CIA's Office of Scientific Intelligence and dated 16 February 1953, never uses the word ridicule: it recommends an education program with two aims, "training and 'debunking'," carried out through "television, motion pictures, and popular articles" built on puzzling cases that were later explained. It also asks the security agencies to strip UFOs of "the aura of mystery they have unfortunately acquired," arguing this would make the public less open to hostile propaganda.
robertson-panel-aim-to-debunk-sightings-: The Robertson Panel, a group of scientists the CIA called together in January 1953 to review UFO reports, set out in papers kept secret at the time that the explicit aim of Project Blue Book, the Air Force's UFO study, was to throw the public off and to downplay, suppress and explain away sightings. Michels tells this himself, elsewhere giving fear of mass hysteria as the reason, crediting the physicist Hal Puthoff, and saying the panel's leader, the physicist Howard P. Robertson, created Blue Book's mandate; if true, the public study was built to mislead. The panel's report, written by the CIA's Office of Scientific Intelligence and dated 16 February 1953, does recommend a "debunking" aim to reduce public interest in "flying saucers" and lists the public's openness "to mass hysteria" among the dangers, but it states no motive of Blue Book's own, and Blue Book was already running when the panel met.
robertson-panel-directive-to-watch-and-i: A 1953 CIA panel of scientists, the Robertson Panel, is said to have directed that civilian UFO groups be watched and infiltrated. Robert Salas, a former Air Force officer, tells Michels the directive was "let's keep an eye on UFO groups," pointing to the panel's report of 16 February 1953. That report says such groups, naming the Civilian Flying Saucer Investigators and the Aerial Phenomena Research Organization, "should be watched because of their potentially great influence on mass thinking" and that "the possible use of such groups for subversive purposes should be kept in mind"; it does not say they should be infiltrated.
robertson-panel-recommends-downplaying-u: In 1952 and 1953 a panel of academics led by a Caltech physicist named Howard P. Robertson concluded that the US government should systematically downplay UFOs, through the media, movies and other means. Michels tells this himself in two episodes, without naming a document; in the second he adds that the panel feared that if the public learned the truth it would set off mass hysteria. If so, it would mean the official dismissal of UFOs was a deliberate policy from early on.
rock-formation-like-a-second-sphinx-head: On the southeast side of the Giza plateau in Egypt, near the pyramid of an ancient queen called Khentkawes and the tombs of the pyramid workers, there is a piece of limestone worn away so strangely that, when you walk up to it, it looks like the back of a second Sphinx head. Luke Caverns, a researcher who studies the pyramids, tells Michels he has seen it, a sight that would hint the plateau holds more carved figures than the famous one.
rockefeller-files-correspondence-routed-: In the 1990s, letters between the wealthy philanthropist Laurance Rockefeller and the president's science adviser are said to have passed through the mailbox of Hillary Clinton, then the First Lady. The researcher Grant Cameron says he found this in two puzzling documents among the Rockefeller files, papers from Rockefeller's contacts with the Clinton White House, one of which said all the mail going each way went through her mailbox. If so, it would put the First Lady at the centre of those exchanges.
rockefeller-funding-intercepted-by-cia-n: In the 1990s, money that the wealthy Laurance Rockefeller meant to give to UFO disclosure work was intercepted by people on his own team who were secretly CIA officers under "nonofficial cover", meaning they posed as private citizens. A UFO researcher named Steven Greer tells this from his own dealings with Rockefeller. If true, the CIA was quietly steering private efforts to reveal UFO secrets.
rockefeller-pressure-leads-the-clinton-a: In the 1990s, the wealthy philanthropist Laurance Rockefeller pushed President Bill Clinton's White House to look into the Roswell case, a reported 1947 crash in New Mexico that many believe involved a UFO. The documentary filmmaker James Fox tells it, passing on what he heard from John Podesta, a senior Clinton aide, and pointing to a briefing paper Rockefeller prepared. According to Podesta, Clinton "was not happy with the answers they were getting. They were getting the runaround," which would mean even a president could not get straight answers about Roswell.
rockefeller-s-panel-meets-at-quantico-19: In 1955, a panel led by Nelson Rockefeller, then an adviser to President Dwight Eisenhower, is said to have first met at Quantico, a Marine Corps base in Virginia, to draft reports for Eisenhower. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, in an episode asking whether Henry Kissinger, who later became Secretary of State, oversaw a program recovering crashed UFOs. In his telling, the group was an early link between these men and the secret UFO question.
rockefeller-serves-breakfast-and-vows-to: In the 1990s, the billionaire Laurance Rockefeller hosted the UFO abduction researchers Budd Hopkins, David Jacobs and John Mack at his house, served them breakfast himself 'like a butler', and told them: 'I'm going to get disclosure', meaning he would get the government to reveal what it knows about UFOs. The UFO researcher Grant Cameron tells it as a story Hopkins told him, adding that the guests found it odd to be fed by a billionaire. Cameron links it to the Rockefeller Initiative, Rockefeller's push for UFO openness, documented in government files released under FOIA, a US law that lets anyone request government records.
rockefellers-fund-greer-mack-and-the-pri: In the 1990s the Rockefeller family, and Laurance Rockefeller in particular, is said to have paid for early UFO research, funding the UFO activist Steven Greer and the psychiatrist John Mack, who studied people reporting alien contact. Michels tells this himself on three episodes, without naming a source; once he adds that they funded a parapsychology lab at Princeton that studied mind over matter, and once he leaves the lab out and names the writer Whitley Strieber among those connected. If true, it would mean one of America's richest families was quietly backing the field.
rod-serling-s-film-and-the-footage-edwar: The filmmaker Rod Serling, who Michels says was his father's godfather, made a 1974 film called UFOs Past, Present and Future, and Michels believes Edwards Air Force Base, a military air base in California, contacted Serling and promised him footage of a UFO. Michels tells this himself, from memory, in an episode with a scientist who claims life on Mars was destroyed by nuclear war. If true, it would mean the Air Force itself offered UFO film to a public documentary.
roddenberry-s-script-the-nine-1970: The television writer Gene Roddenberry is said to have written a script called The Nine, which the story places in the 1970s. A researcher named Greg Malatzi mentions it in passing on the show, without naming a source and without saying what the script contains. He raises it alongside other stories about secret government work of that decade, as a sign that those ideas were reaching popular entertainment.
rodent-microdialysis-studies-show-dmt-le: Laboratory studies are said to have measured DMT, a powerful psychedelic chemical the body makes on its own, in the brains of living rats, and found that the levels rise sharply as the animal dies. The neuroscientist Andrew Gallimore describes these experiments without naming the study. If it holds, the brain may flood itself with a psychedelic at the moment of death.
rodri-castle-sees-a-giant-triangle-and-b: In 1997, during Hunter Warrior, a military exercise testing new ways of fighting, a man named Rodri Castle, who worked on Harrier jump jets as an aviation technician, was sent to check on some unauthorised flares and is said to have found a massive triangle-shaped craft guarded by a "black team", an armed security squad, who held him at gunpoint. An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb repeats Castle's account, and in a second version, naming him Roger Castle, he places it in Nevada, says Castle was 150 feet from a giant rotating triangle, and likens it to the TR-3B, a rumoured secret triangular aircraft. Told this way, it would point to a hidden program flying craft far beyond what the public knows.
rodriguez-paper-proposing-to-test-dmt-en: In the early 2000s a man named Rodriguez is said to have published a paper proposing a test for the beings people report meeting on DMT, a strong psychedelic drug: ask them to break a large number into its prime factors, a sum too hard for a person to do in their head. The neuroscientist Andrew Gallimore describes the paper to Michels without giving its title or where it appeared. If the beings could answer, it would suggest they are more than the user's own mind.
rogan-backlash-over-malone-and-mcculloug: In 2022 the popular podcaster Joe Rogan faced a public backlash because he had two guests, Robert Malone and Peter McCullough, on his show. Michels brings this up himself, without naming a source, in an episode with a whistleblower, as an example of how much trouble comes from giving a platform to unpopular voices.
rogan-s-first-5-meo-dmt-experience: The first time Joe Rogan, the comedian and podcast host, took 5-MeO-DMT, a very strong psychedelic drug, he was sure it had killed him. Rogan tells it himself: "I thought it was dead for sure... there's no way this is real."
rogan-s-offline-explanation-of-lazar-s-d: Bob Lazar, a man who says he once worked on alien craft for the US government, has long faced questions because records of his time at MIT, a university in Massachusetts, cannot be found. Michels says that the podcaster Joe Rogan, whenever Lazar comes up, says he could explain "offline" something that would make the deleted MIT records make sense. Michels passes this on second-hand, and Rogan's explanation itself is never given.
rogan-s-possible-childhood-sighting: The podcaster Joe Rogan says he thought he might have seen a UFO when he was young, though he now thinks it was probably a fighter jet. He tells it himself, wishing he had a sighting of his own.
rogan-s-reading-on-project-blue-book-hyn: Joe Rogan tells Michels that he "got really into" Project Blue Book, the US Air Force's UFO study of the 1950s and 60s, and read a lot about the scientist J. Allen Hynek, the Army officer Philip J. Corso, and Roswell, New Mexico, where a UFO crash is said to have happened in 1947. He brings it up to explain where his own interest in the subject came from.
rogan-s-vivid-dream-of-slender-pinkish-h: In 2025 the comedian and podcaster Joe Rogan had a vivid dream in which very slender, tall, humanlike beings talked to him, beings that were not gray but "kind of like pinkish like us." Rogan tells it himself and returns to it more than once in the conversation, adding that his feeling was that "someone was trying to get me used to this," meaning used to contact.
roger-leir-s-implant-extractions: Roger Leir, a surgeon, is said to have removed small objects from people's bodies that were believed to be implants, things put there by non-human beings. The researcher Tim Alberino tells it second-hand: he says his colleague and friend Ellie Marculli worked with Leir and was in the room when some of these implants were taken out.
roger-leir-s-licence-targeted: Authorities went after the professional licence of a man named Roger Leir in California, the same way the author Whitley Strieber says they went after him. Strieber tells this, saying "Roger Lear had the same thing happen. They went after him." He tells it as a sign that people who speak about alien contact are punished.
roger-leir-s-tapes-and-book-doctors-tele: In 1996, in the Brazilian town of Varginha where a strange creature was reportedly captured, two doctors at Humanitas Hospital are said to have met with a doctor named Roger Leir and told him about a creature they had treated and that communicated with them by telepathy. The UFO investigator James Fox tells it from Leir's taped interviews and his book on the case, saying Leir "describes a meeting with these two doctors at a hospital." On a later episode Fox adds that this part appears in the book but not in the tapes.
roger-leir-s-video-of-a-craft-with-grays: A man named Roger Leir is said to have had a video, filmed over the ocean near Lebanon or Turkey, of what looks like a craft with grays, the small gray-skinned beings of UFO lore, visible inside it. Tim Alberino, a guest who researches giants and the unexplained, passes this on from what Leir told him. If the video showed what he describes, it would be footage of beings inside a craft.
rogers-book-we-got-it-from-them-2025: Greg Rogers, a doctor who has worked with NASA and says he saw a UFO in a secret hangar, says he wrote a book in 2025 about what he witnessed. He tells it in connection with Contact in the Desert, a UFO gathering, and jokes that, "to be really ingenious," he called it We Got It From Them, meaning the technology came from non-human makers.
rogers-craft-as-human-built-but-aerodyna: Greg Rogers, a NASA doctor who says he saw a strange craft in a secret hangar around 2000, believes what he saw was built by humans, even though its shape seemed to make no sense for flying. He tells it first-hand, as his own reading of the craft.
rogers-egg-craft-resembles-lazar-s-sport: An egg-shaped craft that Greg Rogers, a doctor who worked with NASA, says he saw in a secret hangar looked very much like the "sport model." That is the name Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft at a secret Nevada site called S-4 near Area 51, gave to a saucer he describes. Rogers makes the comparison himself on the show, saying the craft he describes "would be very much like his sports model." If true, it would mean two people separately saw the same kind of craft.
rogue-elements-of-us-government-managing: Some parts of the US government have gone "sort of rogue" and run their own secret programs on UAP, the government's term for UFOs, working with defence companies such as the aerospace firm Lockheed. A commentator named Matthew Pines says this is how he reads the claims of David Grusch, a whistleblower who came forward about such programs. If true, it would mean these programs operate outside the normal control of elected government.
roman-gods-on-mission-patches-for-our-sp: A researcher who is not named says he once asked someone at NASA, the US space agency, why its mission patches, the cloth badges made for each flight, show Roman gods and use Latin phrases, when nobody up in space is going to read Latin. He says the answer was "Our sponsors." He tells it as a conversation he had himself, and if taken at face value it would hint that the space programme answers to someone beyond the public.
romans-say-phoenicians-sacrificed-childr: The Phoenicians, an ancient seafaring people whose reach included the island of Sardinia, sacrificed their children to a god called Molech, at least according to Roman accounts. A researcher named Tim Alberino brings this up when describing their rites, citing the Romans without naming any particular text.
ron-evans-and-bae-s-project-greenglow-an: BAE Systems, a big British defence company, had an anti-gravity research effort called Project Greenglow, and a man there named Dr. Ron Evans talked about it publicly. Michels tells this himself and adds that Evans went further and wrote a book about the project.
ron-hell-maria-is-a-natural-asian-africa: Maria, one of the small three-fingered mummified bodies said to come from Peru, is a natural hybrid, not an alien or an engineered being, according to a researcher named David Ron Hell. He offers this as his own hypothesis, tying her origins to Asia, Africa and South America, without naming a source.
ron-johnson-sees-his-lost-dog-s-fate-in-: A man named Ron Johnson says he finally learned what happened to his dog, which vanished around 1972, by watching the dog's life play out in a crystal. In the crystal he saw a neighbour come, shoot the dog, throw it in the back of a pickup and dump it at the town dump. The UFO researcher Grant Cameron tells this as something Johnson told him.
ron-johnson-sees-the-milky-way-from-a-di: A man named Ron Johnson is said to have been asked by the beings he met, "Ron, where would you like to go?", and to have answered that he would like to see the Milky Way, our galaxy, from a distance. The researcher Grant Cameron relays this as something Johnson told, and it would mean non-human beings offered a person a trip far beyond Earth.
ron-pandolfi-breakthrough-into-the-next-: A CIA man named Ron Pandolfi, said to have been at the agency since 1984 and rumoured to brief presidents, once said there had been "a breakthrough" in going "into the next world", and that next time a man named John went to the desert, several of them would go there and come back. A UFO researcher named Grant Cameron tells this, saying he met Pandolfi and later found a tape of the remarks online. Cameron says Pandolfi did not know the tape would become public and believes he was talking about portals. If true, the government had found a way to cross into another realm.
ron-pandolfi-links-the-jasons-and-the-uf: A man named Ron Pandolfi seems to be part of the JASON group, a circle of top scientists who advise the US government, and yet also turns up again and again in the world of UFO research, according to Michels. He says this himself, without naming a source, in a conversation with the mathematician Eric Weinstein, as a sign that elite government science and the UFO question may be quietly connected.
ron-s-visits-to-the-spirit-world-with-el: A man in Utah known only as Ron says a being called Elby took him to the spirit world three times, and his story also involves a crystal table. The UFO researcher Grant Cameron repeats it as Ron told it to him, without giving more detail about what Ron saw there.
ronald-moultrie-scrubbed-battelle-board-: Ronald Moultrie, a senior Pentagon intelligence official who set up the offices under which AARO, the Pentagon office that now investigates UFO reports, was created, is said to have also sat on the board of the Battelle Memorial Institute, a research organisation, and to have deleted that role from his LinkedIn profile, his public online résumé. An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb points this out from the profile itself, without naming another source. He raises it to suggest a quiet link between the people overseeing UFO investigations and an outside research contractor.
ronald-richter-s-fusion-project-in-baril: Between about 1947 and 1951, a German scientist named Ronald Richter set up a project in Bariloche, Argentina, to make fusion, the energy process that powers the sun. The philosopher and researcher Jason Jorjani tells this without naming a source. He says Richter was promising nuclear weapons to Argentina's leader, Juan Perón, and that this is why intelligence agents, whom he calls "the IA," went down there.
rongorongo-and-nazca-lines-as-depictions: Rongorongo, marks on Easter Island long thought to be a form of writing, and the Nazca lines, giant drawings on the ground in Peru, are said to be pictures of plasma discharges, glowing electrical bursts in the sky. The researcher Matt LaCroix relays it from the researcher Robert Schoch, author of the book Forgotten Civilizations, and his wife Katie, who looked at the rongorongo marks on Easter Island. If true, it would mean ancient people were recording a sky event, not words.
room-of-antiques-with-a-singer-sewing-ma: In 1977, near a nuclear missile site in South Dakota known as November 5, Mario Woods, then a young Air Force guard, says he was taken aboard a craft and shown a room full of old things, including a sewing table with a Singer sewing machine and a round window. Woods tells it himself and has made drawings of it, and he adds that a small being led him there and "just allowed me to be there and to look." He says the objects looked like the ones in his childhood home in Port Arthur, Texas.
rosemary-smith-remote-views-a-downed-tu-: During Jimmy Carter's presidency, a woman named Rosemary Smith is said to have used remote viewing, a claimed ability to see distant places with the mind alone, to find a Soviet Tu-22 plane that had crashed in Zaire, drawing a circle of about three square miles on a map that held the wreck. Carter himself is heard saying "we located the plane where she said it was," the only inexplicable thing he ever experienced, and Michels retells it on several episodes. Paul Smith, a former Army remote viewer, tells it secondhand from Dale Graff, who worked on the government's psychic spying effort, and dates it to 1979.
ross-coulthart-gets-brent-to-name-harrin: Around 2019 or 2020, the journalist Ross Coulthart got Brent Friedman on camera and pushed him until he named a man called Harrington. Friedman tells it himself, recalling that Coulthart "got me on camera and just pushed me." It comes up on an episode about a former US Secretary of Energy speaking about UFOs.
ross-coulthart-s-investigation-at-bradsh: At Bradshaw Ranch near Sedona, Arizona, a place known for UFO sightings, unknown craft are said to fly in and out of a nearby peak called Secret Mountain, a story looked into by the investigative journalist Ross Coulthart. Michels brings it up in several episodes, drawing on Coulthart's work and a work called Sentinels of Ether; at one point he calls them craft that move between air and ground, "going in and out of the mountain," and compares the site to Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property famous for strange events, while elsewhere he adds that the US government took over the site, "a move that raised some eyebrows," and speaks of armed guards. If true, it would mean something is hidden inside the mountain.
ross-coulthart-says-on-need-to-know-that: In 2025, the journalist Ross Coulthart said on his show Need to Know that the Tic Tac, a white oval object shaped like the mint that Navy pilots reported seeing, is technology made by Lockheed Martin, the American defense contractor. His on-air partner, the writer Bryce Zabel, says he was there and quotes him as saying, "I can now state categorically that the tic tac is Lockheed Martin technology." A clip of Coulthart himself has him say "I now know categorically," a claim that would make the object human-made.
rossi-devices-and-ring-superconductor-ex: Between 2021 and 2024, Dave Rossi, a guest who says advanced physics came to him from aliens, built a handful of devices, including experiments with rings of superconductor, a material that carries electricity with no resistance. He tells it first-hand, saying the devices showed interesting effects that seemed to back up theories discussed by the researchers Hal Puthoff and Eric W. Davis, which would mean those theories of exotic propulsion can be tested at the bench.
roswell-as-home-of-the-509th-atomic-bomb: Roswell, New Mexico, the town tied to a famous 1947 crash story, was also home to the 509th, the US bomber unit that carried atomic bombs. Several people tell it that way to suggest that whatever came down there may have been drawn to the nuclear weapons. A guest named Marik von Rennenkampff calls it "the first bomber squadron" of its kind in the US. The researcher RedPandaKoala adds that this was the unit that dropped the bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki, and the scientist John Brandenburg goes further, saying all the nuclear weapons on Earth were stored at Roswell. Jesse Michels says in his own words that Roswell held "the only American nuclear stockpile at the time" and names the officers involved: Jesse Marcel Sr., Walter Haut, William Blanchard and Roger Ramey. Another time he names Curtis LeMay as the unit's leader and asks a guest whether something happened at Roswell.
roswell-bodies-kept-on-ice-at-wright-pat: Bodies from the 1947 crash near Roswell, New Mexico, where many say a strange craft came down, were flown to Wright-Patterson, an Air Force base in Ohio, and kept on ice. An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb mentions this to Michels in passing, as something known "historically," without naming a source. If true, the military would have held the remains of whoever was aboard the craft.
roswell-boulder-split-and-memory-metal-1: Something came down near Roswell, New Mexico, in 1947 and left a "memory metal," a material said to spring back to its shape, and Michels says he believes this basic story. He says it himself, once in a debate with a skeptic and once with another guest, and he says he trusts two men from the Roswell base, Jesse Marcel Sr., whom he at one point calls an Air Force flight surgeon, and Walter Haut. In one telling he adds that the material was taken to Wright Field, an Air Force base in Ohio.
roswell-corona-crash-confirmed-via-ed-mi: The 1947 crash near Roswell, New Mexico, which the scientist Eric W. Davis prefers to call the Corona crash after the nearby ranch, was a real crash and not a Mogul balloon, a secret Army balloon project, according to what Davis says he was told. Davis, a scientist who has advised the Pentagon, says he got this through the Apollo astronaut Ed Mitchell, after Pentagon briefings by Steven Greer, an activist whose Disclosure Project pushed for UFO secrets to be released. He says a Navy admiral named Thomas R. Wilson came back and confirmed the crash had happened, which, if true, would mean the official balloon explanation is wrong.
roswell-craft-said-to-have-been-brought-: The object that came down near Roswell, New Mexico, in 1947, which the military first announced as a flying disc, is said in some early accounts to have been struck by lightning and crashed. Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft at a secret site in Nevada, mentions this in passing as one of the stories that went around before later explanations, a version that would make the crash an accident of weather.
roswell-crash-and-stringfield-s-marcel-i: In 1947 something was said to have crashed near Roswell, New Mexico, and a UFO researcher named Leonard Stringfield was among the very first to interview Jesse Marcel Senior, a military officer tied to that story, and to publish the interview. A researcher named Richard Dolan tells this while going over the history, without naming a source. If so, Stringfield helped bring a key Roswell witness to the public.
roswell-crash-as-exotic-human-technology: The object that people say crashed near Roswell, New Mexico, in 1947 may have been advanced human technology and not something from elsewhere. That is the view of Peter Levenda, a researcher and author, who offers it as a possibility without naming a source. He links the idea to Secret Machines, a book series he worked on. If he is right, the most famous UFO crash story would be about a secret human aircraft.
roswell-crash-caused-by-radio-signatures: The craft said to have crashed near Roswell, New Mexico in 1947 came down, in one telling, because clashing radio signals confused its navigation. An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb passes this on from a man named Philip J. Corso, who, he says, described the crash as "due to kind of conflicting radio signatures messing with craft navigation." If true, it would mean our own radio and radar equipment could bring such a craft down.
roswell-crash-debris-retrieved-by-mac-br: In 1947, the story goes, a rancher named Mac Brazel found strange crash debris on his land near Roswell, New Mexico. Michels tells this himself, and the physicist John Brandenburg passes on what Roswell veterans said: Brazel took the wreckage into town, showed it to the sheriff, and was told to "take it to the base." A researcher named Luigi Vendittelli adds that the debris was spread all over the ranch, and that a pod with beings inside was found about two miles away by hikers who had children with them. The journalist Michael Shellenberger asks whether one craft or two came down, and whether radar brought them down. The researcher Robert Hastings notes that Roswell was then the only nuclear bomber base in the world, and he points to a new book by the author Luis Elizondo that calls it a real UFO crash. Michels says that he personally thinks what happened there "was otherworldly," which would mean the military recovered a craft that was not made by humans.
roswell-crash-test-dummy-and-project-mog: The official explanations for the 1947 crash near Roswell, New Mexico, namely that people saw bluish crash test dummies or debris from Project Mogul, a secret military balloon project, do not fit, because both of those happened later, according to Michels. He says this himself, without naming a source. If he is right, the explanations could not account for what was found in 1947.
roswell-date-of-july-7-1947-in-the-brief: A former CIA officer named Ralph Moat Larson once had a dream in which, he says, he downloaded a string of numbers, including 747, and Jesse Michels wonders whether that number points to July 7, 1947, a date tied to the reported crash of an unknown craft near Roswell, New Mexico. Michels raises it himself while interviewing Larson, noting that the date appears in a book, and asking whether it connects to his '747' download. In a later episode Michels retells it secondhand, describing the download as a dream full of numbers and pointing to Larson's book A State of Mind: Faith and the CIA. If the link held, the dream would be pointing at the Roswell event.
roswell-debris-swapped-for-the-ramey-pho: After the 1947 crash near Roswell, New Mexico, which the military first announced as a recovered flying disc, the wreckage shown to the press in photos with a general named Ramey may not have been the real debris but a swapped-in substitute. A researcher named Kevin Knuth says he finds the swap the more likely story, pointing to the claim tied to Jesse Marcel Sr., the officer who handled the original debris. If true, the real material was hidden from the start.
roswell-flying-disc-announcement-then-re: In July 1947 a flying disc is said to have come down near Roswell, New Mexico, and the military airfield there, Roswell Army Air Field, published a press release saying it had a flying disc and then took it back. Michels tells this himself while debating a well-known skeptic, saying the airfield retracted the announcement "in a panic", which he raises as a sign that the first official word was the true one.
roswell-held-the-most-us-nukes-in-1947: Jesse Michels says that in 1947, when something was said to have crashed near Roswell, New Mexico, the base there held more US nuclear bombs than anywhere else in the country. Michels states this himself, without naming a source, as a reason the crash might matter: whatever came down did so beside the nation's largest store of nuclear weapons.
roswell-ignored-until-berlitz-s-1980-boo: The skeptic writer Michael Shermer says the Roswell story, about something said to have crashed near Roswell, New Mexico, in 1947, was not a big deal for over thirty years. In his telling, it only "became a thing" in 1980, when the writer Charles Berlitz published his book The Roswell Incident, and the UFO researcher Stanton Friedman and others took it up. Shermer offers this as his own summary, to suggest the story grew from books rather than from 1947 itself.
roswell-material-as-seed-for-an-exotic-a: Whatever was recovered from the reported 1947 crash at Roswell, New Mexico, is said to have become the seed of a secret research program at the Air Force Research Lab at Wright-Patterson, an Air Force base in Ohio, working on exotic materials. Michels presents this himself as "the theory", without naming who holds it, in an episode about missing American scientists; if true, it would mean crash debris fed decades of hidden military research.
roswell-operators-part-of-the-craft-s-gu: The beings who flew the craft said to have crashed near Roswell, New Mexico, in 1947 were supposedly part of the craft's own guidance system, not just its pilots. An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb says this comes from interviews with a man named Philip J. Corso, who "said that the operators of specifically the Roswell craft were part of the guidance system." If true, the craft and its crew would have worked together as one machine.
roswell-s-shifting-official-stories-incl: The official story of what crashed near Roswell, New Mexico, in 1947 is said to have changed so many times that it is laughable, with one version even involving children with progeria, a rare disease of rapid aging. Michels says this himself, without naming a source, in an episode about Hollywood, the CIA and UFOs. To him the changing stories suggest the government has never told it straight.
roswell-style-seeding-of-our-internet-te: Much of our internet technology may have been dropped on us by outside beings, the same way people claim technology came from the 1947 crash at Roswell, New Mexico, and its purpose would be to keep us constantly distracted. Michels floats this himself, in an episode with a guest named Randall Carlson, without naming a source.
roswell-technologies-per-corso-were-germ: The technologies that the Army officer Philip J. Corso said came from the craft that crashed at Roswell, New Mexico, as told in his book The Day After Roswell, were all invented by the Germans in the 1940s. A researcher named Jason Jorjani says so, citing a writer named Joseph P. Farrell, whose work Saucer Swastikas and SCOPS, Jorjani says, "provides documentation" for every one. If true, it would mean that technology credited to a crashed alien craft had a human, German origin.
roswell-the-world-s-only-nuclear-bomber-: In 1947 something came down near Roswell, New Mexico, and it was later explained away as a balloon. The point of this story is that the men at Roswell were hardly people who would mistake a balloon for a flying saucer. Bryce Zabel, a guest on an episode about Hollywood and UFOs, says without naming a source that the people at Roswell were "the only people running a nuclear bomber base in the world in 1947." Michels makes the same point himself, a little differently: Roswell "wasn't a random desert," he says, but "the largest concentration of nuclear weapons in the world at the time." Both tell it because if those men really couldn't tell a saucer from a balloon, that would be hard to believe.
roswell-was-a-nazi-staged-event-1947: The 1947 crash near Roswell, New Mexico, where many say a strange craft came down, was staged by the Nazis to create a crisis. The philosopher Jason Jorjani tells Michels this, saying "they staged an event." He draws on the account of a former US Army officer named Philip J. Corso. If true, Roswell would have been a planned human operation, not an accident.
roswell-witnesses-describe-non-human-bei: In 1947, after a craft is said to have crashed near Roswell, New Mexico, people there described a strange being with three or four fingers and toes coming out of it, and said it was clearly not human. Michels says this himself, without naming the witnesses, in a conversation with the writer Peter Levenda. If true, it would mean that what came down at Roswell carried someone who was not from here.
roswell-witnesses-describe-threats-made-: In 1947 in Roswell, New Mexico, where a crashed object was said to have been recovered, local people were threatened to keep quiet, told that "they'll be picking your bones out of the desert." James Fox, a UFO investigator and filmmaker, tells Michels that men who were there told him this was what had been said to them at the time. If true, it would mean the military forced silence about what came down.
roswell-wreckage-in-the-hangar-had-the-b: Wreckage said to come from the 1947 crash near Roswell, New Mexico, where many believe an alien craft came down, was kept in a hangar, with a bathroom on the other side. A man named Charles Hall, who says he spent three years among tall white aliens at Area 51, a secret US Air Force site in Nevada, tells it as something he saw. Asked what it was like, he said only that "that wreckage had the bathroom on the other side", suggesting he was close to it.
roswell-wreckage-rumoured-at-wright-patt: The wreckage of a flying saucer or disc said to have crashed near Roswell, New Mexico, in 1947 is rumoured to have been taken to a lab at Wright-Patterson, an Air Force base in Ohio, and Michels notes that Neil McCasland, an Air Force general, later ran that very lab. Michels tells this himself across several episodes: once he adds Fort Worth as a stop on the route, once he calls the base, also home to Project Blue Book (the US Air Force's UFO study of the 1950s and 60s), the alleged home of the debris, and once he credits the musician Tom DeLonge and his book Secret Machines, saying the Air Force's work on studying captured foreign hardware ended up with the Roswell pieces, "if you believe the lore." If true, it would put a crashed craft in the hands of one specific government lab.
round-table-foundation-elf-research-pene: A researcher named Andrija Puharich, working through a private research group called the Round Table Foundation from the late 1950s, is said to have found an extremely low radio frequency that could get through the walls of a Faraday cage, a metal enclosure built to block radio signals. A researcher named Greg Malatzi tells this without naming a source. If it were true, a shield thought to cut off all such signals could be passed through.
round-table-foundation-funded-by-army-na: Around 1949 and 1950, a small research group in Rockland, Maine, called the Round Table Foundation is said to have drawn money from the US Army, the Navy and the CIA, the country's foreign intelligence agency, all flocking to fund the man running it. The researcher Greg Malatzi tells this, pointing to letters from those agencies to the foundation, and it would mean the military and spies were backing its unusual research very early on.
