rov-camera-and-lights-fail-at-the-object: In 2011, when a team dove on a strange object lying on the floor of the Baltic Sea, their equipment failed: the remote-controlled underwater vehicle, its camera and its lights all stopped working. Dennis Asberg, the treasure hunter whose team found the object, says this happened while he was there: "the camera stops working, the light stops working."
rov-image-shows-a-straight-wall-on-the-a: In 2025, pictures from an underwater robot sent to the Baltic Sea anomaly, a strange object lying on the floor of the Baltic Sea, reportedly showed a straight wall on it. Dennis Asberg, a treasure hunter whose team found the object, tells it first-hand and judges the wall to be at least 30 meters long, with the whole object about 60 meters, which to him suggests something more than a natural rock.
roy-craig-interview-with-lewis-chase-who: In 1967 an investigator named Roy Craig recorded an interview with Lieutenant Colonel Lewis D. Chase, chief of the operations division at Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana, a nuclear missile base, and Chase denied knowing anything about the UFO events there. Robert Salas, a former Air Force officer who says a UFO shut down ten nuclear missiles, plays the tape, which opens: "The following interview conducted by Roy Craig is with Lieutenant Colonel Lewis D. Chase." Salas brings it up because the denial sits against what he says happened.
royal-raymond-rife-s-microscope-and-freq: In the 1930s an inventor named Royal Raymond Rife claimed to have built a microscope so powerful it could watch live viruses, work said to have been pushed aside along with his frequency machine. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, in an episode with a pharmacy businessman named Brigham Buhler about the drug industry's past; if true, it would mean a major medical tool was lost or buried.
royal-tomb-theory-and-the-lack-of-mummie: Most experts on ancient Egypt hold that the Great Pyramid at Giza was built around 2500 BC as the tomb of the pharaoh Khufu, and the pyramid beside it as the tomb of his son, the pharaoh Khafre. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, and adds that no confirmed mummy or burial of either king has ever been found inside the pyramids. He raises it because, if the tombs were never there, the pyramids may have been built for some purpose other than burial.
rubik-and-jabs-reanalyse-the-michelson-m: The Michelson-Morley experiment, a famous physics test that looked for an invisible 'ether' thought to carry light and is remembered for finding nothing, may in fact have found a small effect after all. That is what a biophysicist named Beverly Rubik and a physicist named Harry Jabs argued in a paper after going back over the original data, according to the psychiatrist and researcher Diane Powell, who summarises it without naming the paper. If they are right, a result taught as a clean 'no' would need a second look.
rubio-credible-witnesses-with-high-clear: The US politician Marco Rubio is said to have stated, on camera and more than once, that the people who have come to him about UFOs are credible, hold high security clearances and high positions, and fear for their lives. A writer named Marik von Rennenkampff passes this on, saying Rubio "said that on camera." If true, it would mean serious insiders believe it is dangerous to speak about what they know.
rubio-s-2020-intelligence-committee-prov: In 2020, the senator Marco Rubio is said to have slipped a provision about unexplained aerial sightings into the written instructions of the Senate's intelligence committee, the 2020 Senate Intelligence Committee report language. The writer Marik von Rennenkampff tells this from his own reading, without naming a source, while challenging the UFO skeptic Mick West over a tweet about it. He raises it to show that Congress was quietly pressing the government on the subject.
rubio-things-flying-over-nuclear-sites: Marco Rubio, the US Secretary of State, is said to have been asked which conspiracy he believes in most and to have answered, "There are things flying with impunity around our nuclear sites." Michels relays the exchange himself, taking it as close to an admission from a top official that unknown objects fly freely over America's nuclear facilities.
rudolf-hess-s-telepathy-experiments-and-: Rudolf Hess, Hitler's deputy who flew to Britain in 1941 and was held prisoner there, believed he was in telepathic contact with his wife from his cell, and experiments in telepathy were run on him. A researcher named Peter Levenda tells this without naming a source, as part of a wider story that Hess's flight was itself timed by astrology.
rudolf-hess-sent-to-antarctica-1938: One of the main men Nazi Germany sent toward Antarctica around 1938 and 1939 was Rudolf Hess, a senior Nazi leader, according to the writer Jason Jorjani. Jorjani gives this as his own summary, crediting a work called Hess and the Penguins, while talking about Nazi Germany's interest in the frozen continent, which would put a top party figure at the heart of that expedition.
ruins-of-an-ancient-civilization-at-cydo: There are said to be ruins of an ancient civilization on Mars, in a region called Cydonia, left by an extraterrestrial people who once lived there. The filmmaker Tim Alberino says this, drawing on the researchers David Flynn, Richard Hoagland and Michael Heiser and his own film Birthright, and adds that he expects this truth about Mars to be revealed within our lifetime.
rumored-crash-in-chinese-territory: Something unknown is rumoured to have crashed on Chinese soil, and the Russians, not the Chinese, may have ended up with it. The author Peter Levenda says he heard these rumours over years of doing business with the Chinese government, adding, "I think the Russians got it though." If true, it would mean the US is not the only country to have recovered such a craft.
rumored-dod-hybrid-program-using-non-hum: Rumors have reached the US Congress of a secret project inside the Department of Defense, the US military's headquarters department, that mixes human genes with what is described as "non-human genetic material". The words come from Lauren Boebert, a US congresswoman, heard on a November 2024 episode with the journalist Michael Shellenberger. She passes it on as a rumor that has come "up to the hill", and if it were true it would mean the military was quietly working on human and non-human hybrids.
rumored-tunnels-and-cave-system-under-me: There are rumours of a cave system and tunnels running under the mesa at Skinwalker Ranch, a property in Utah famous for reports of strange events. The ranch's current owner tells this on the show, saying the rumours go back to earlier owners' time on the ranch and even, as he puts it, back to the Mayans. If true, it would mean something hidden lies beneath the land itself.
rumors-about-area-51-at-the-energy-depar: In the 1980s the US Energy Department is said to have heard many rumors about what was going on at Area 51, a secret test site in Nevada. John S. Herrington, who served as Secretary of Energy, recalls this himself, describing Area 51 as "a very highly classified area with a lot of projects that are highly classified."
rumors-of-elites-having-out-of-body-expe: Jesse Michels asks a guest whether he has heard rumours that powerful people today spend time inside the granite chambers of some pyramids, seeking out-of-body experiences. He raises it himself as a question, without naming a source, and gives no further detail.
rumors-of-luring-uap-with-nuclear-materi: There are rumours that the US might be setting traps for UAP, the government's term for unidentified flying objects, by trying to lure them in with nuclear material. The economist Tyler Cowen raises this in 2022 as something he has heard, not something he knows, and it would mean the government is actively trying to catch these objects.
rumour-that-the-giant-ended-up-at-wright: According to a rumour, a giant said to have been captured in Afghanistan around 2005 was later taken to Wright-Patterson, a US Air Force base in Ohio. Tim Alberino, who tells the giant story as someone close to it, passes this on as something another person told him. If it were true, the base would be holding the body of a creature that should not exist.
rumoured-2027-arrival-clock: A rumour has gone around that "they", meaning visitors from elsewhere, will openly show up in 2027, as if on a countdown. A commentator named Matthew Pines says he has heard this, that "word got around that they're going to come up and show up in 2027", but that he does not believe it. If true, it would mean a public arrival is only a short time away.
rumoured-badlands-incident-in-which-two-: Two military security policemen guarding nuclear missiles were found out of their vehicle, and reportedly unclothed, near the Badlands of South Dakota, in the area of a missile unit called the 66th, according to rumours from around 1977. A former nuclear missile guard named Mario Woods says he heard these rumours about events from years before he arrived, and gives no more detail. He tells it alongside his own account of strange happenings at the missile sites.
rumoured-deep-underground-military-bases: There are rumours of deep underground military bases stretching from Edwards and Nellis, two US Air Force bases in the western desert, to Peterson in Colorado and the Cheyenne Mountain Complex, the mountain bunker in Colorado that houses NORAD, the North American Aerospace Defense Command. Michels brings this up himself as rumour, without naming a source, in an episode about a government research scientist who says he was abducted. If true, it would mean the military keeps hidden facilities far below some of its best-known bases.
rumoured-jfk-joint-space-program-with-th: President John F. Kennedy is said to have wanted to share what the US knew about UFOs with the Soviet Union in the early 1960s. Jesse Michels raises it as a rumor that Kennedy wanted a joint space program with the Soviets, using UFOs as "a unifying, you know, rallying cry." Harold Malmgren, who served as an adviser to Presidents Kennedy, Johnson, Nixon and Ford, answers on the same episode as someone inside government at the time. He says Kennedy "expressed verbally to a number of the senior people his desire to share our knowledge of UFOs with Russia" and that this "caused alarm." Malmgren speaks of sharing knowledge rather than a joint space program, and ties it to the Soviet leader Nikita Khrushchev. The tellers raise it because, if true, it would mean a president was ready to open the UFO secret to America's main rival, and that some of his own officials feared it.
rumoured-mormon-connection-to-the-ufo-le: There are rumours, Michels says, that the Mormon church is tied to the UFO legacy program, the supposed long-running secret government effort around UFOs, and that Brigham Young University, the church's university in Utah, could be a feeder that sends people into it. He passes this on as rumour and does not name a source. If it were true, a religious community and its university would be quietly helping to staff one of the most secret projects there is.
rumsfeld-admits-trillions-missing-in-aud: The day before the September 11 attacks in 2001, Defense Secretary Donald Rumsfeld is said to have admitted publicly that the Pentagon could not account for trillions of dollars. The journalist Ross Coulthart says he dug up Rumsfeld's own speech while writing his book, and that in it Rumsfeld "admitted that there was something" wrong with the money. The researcher Richard Dolan tells it too, working from Pentagon records and the reporting of others. He says the figure was first "2.3 trillion dollars in unaccounted expenditures" and kept being revised. Dolan places the accounting before the House committee that oversees the military over 2001 and 2002, and credits Dov Zakheim and Catherine Austin Fitts, people who dealt with or wrote about the missing money. The tellers raise it because hidden money of that size could, in their view, fund secret programs, including UFO work, out of sight of Congress.
ruppelt-in-look-magazine-on-sightings-at: In 1952, the Air Force's chief UFO investigator, Captain Edward J. Ruppelt, was quoted saying that "many of the sightings reported had originated at one atomic weapons related site or another all around the country." The quote comes from a 1952 Look magazine article called "The Hunt for the Flying Saucer," which Michels reads out in two episodes, one of them about UFOs and nuclear bases. It matters because it would mean the Air Force's own investigator saw a link between sightings and nuclear weapons sites as early as 1952.
ruppelt-pressured-to-debunk-his-own-book: Edward J. Ruppelt, who had led the US Air Force's UFO study in the early 1950s, is said to have been pressured into debunking his own book, The Report on Unidentified Flying Objects, published in 1956. The researcher Richard Dolan says this without naming a source, and if true it would mean the man who wrote the inside account was pushed to take it back.
ruppelt-s-account-of-early-ufo-hypothese: In the early years of UFO sightings after 1947, US officials worked through a list of explanations: were the objects human, Russian, or somehow Nazi technology? That is how the researcher Jason Simosa sums up the book written by Edward J. Ruppelt, an Air Force officer who studied the reports in that period. He brings it up to show how seriously the government once weighed who might be behind the objects.
ruppelt-s-book-reports-metallic-spheres-: In the 1950s, metallic spheres flying in formation were reported, according to the book The Report on Unidentified Flying Objects, published in 1956 by Edward J. Ruppelt, the Air Force captain who was first director of Blue Book, the US Air Force's UFO study of the 1950s and 60s. A writer named Marik von Rennenkampff points listeners to the book, saying "if you read" Ruppelt you will find such cases. He raises it to show that the Air Force's own investigator recorded reports that are hard to explain away.
ruppelt-s-serious-cases-cluster-near-nuc: Most of the UFO sightings that Edward J. Ruppelt took seriously happened near sensitive nuclear sites in the United States, Michels says, pointing to Ruppelt's book The Report on Unidentified Flying Objects, an account of the Air Force's UFO investigations of the 1950s. Michels makes the point himself during a debate with a skeptic named Mick West, who had cited the same book. He raises it to suggest the objects show a particular interest in nuclear weapons.
ruppelt-s-study-of-sightings-near-nuclea: Edward J. Ruppelt, who led the US Air Force's early study of UFO reports, is said to have looked into sightings around American nuclear sites in a study that ran from 1947 to 1952, and then to have written a book about it in 1956. Michels brings this up himself, without naming the book, in a 2025 episode where the skeptic Mick West is challenged to a debate. He offers it as early official evidence that UFOs took an interest in nuclear sites.
russell-targ-coming-around-to-remote-vie: A physicist named Russell Targ, known for studying remote viewing (the practice of trying to describe faraway places or hidden targets with the mind alone), is said to have come around to the idea that it really works by seeing the future. A writer on precognition named Eric Wargo says this to Michels as his own impression, without naming a source. If so, a leading figure in the field would be treating remote viewing as a glimpse ahead in time rather than across space.
russell-targ-saw-real-miracles-while-wor: Russell Targ, a researcher, is said to have worked as a stage magician when he was young and to have seen "actual miracles" happen during that time, beyond the tricks. The magician Chris Ramsay tells this as something Targ himself mentioned, as a hint that real wonders can show up alongside stage illusion.
russia-and-china-retrieval-teams-and-the: Russia and China are said to have their own teams that recover crashed craft of non-human intelligence, and their own technology copied from those craft, roughly on par with what the US has. Michael Herrera, a former Marine who says he saw a huge UFO in Indonesia, relays this as something he was told, and it would mean the race to recover such craft is not America's alone.
russia-used-nuclear-material-to-bait-ufo: In Russia, the claim goes, nuclear material was used as bait to draw UFOs in. Michels mentions it in passing while talking with the UFO investigator James Fox, prefaced with "apparently" and without naming a source or a date. It would mean the craft are drawn to nuclear material, and that someone tried to use that on purpose.
russian-admiral-the-phenomenon-s-reality: In 1990s Russia, a Russian admiral told the filmmaker James Fox, through his interpreter, that if Fox had come to ask whether the UFO phenomenon was real, "the door is right over there." Fox, who has spent years investigating UFOs for documentaries, tells it as something he sat through himself, as a sign that senior Russian military men took the phenomenon's reality as settled.
russian-deception-as-source-of-some-uap: Some UFO sightings are said to be the work of deliberate Russian deception. Eric Haseltine, a former senior official at the National Security Agency, the US signals-intelligence agency, says the Russians in particular do a lot of this, and mentions the World War Two general George Patton in the discussion. If true, some reports would be staged tricks by a rival rather than anything unknown.
russian-dna-phantom-experiments-1990: In the 1990s, Russian scientists are said to have described something strange in what were called the "DNA phantom" experiments. Michels mentions this himself, without naming a source, in an episode on UFOs and the history of human experiments by drug companies, and calls it "even more bizarre" than what came before. In this line he gives the name of the experiments and nothing more about what was found.
russian-earthquake-weapons-could-set-off: Russia has weapons that can cause earthquakes, and could use them to set off one at Yellowstone, the huge volcanic park in the western United States. A former Army sergeant named Lyn Buchanan says this to Michels without naming a source. He says such a quake would "wipe out the center US."
russian-general-alexeyev-in-german-magaz: A Russian general named Vasily Alexeyev is said to have stated, in a German magazine in 2000, that UFOs would appear whenever sensitive scientific technology was being moved. Michels mentions this in passing on two episodes without naming the magazine. In one he gives only the general and the year, and in the other only the claim. He raises it as a sign that a senior Russian officer, too, had linked UFOs to secret technology.
russian-high-school-taught-moon-landing-: A friend of Jesse Michels who grew up in Russia told him that in Russian high school they were taught the American moon landing was faked. Michels repeats this himself, in a conversation about Joe Rogan's views, as a sign of how widely that doubt has spread.
russian-intelligence-sends-an-armed-team: During the 1993 attempt to overthrow Boris Yeltsin, then Russia's president, Russian intelligence is said to have sent a team of heavily armed men to keep American spies at the ambassador's residence in Moscow from being captured. A former CIA officer named Rolf Mowatt-Larssen, who was there, says his Russian counterpart called it "very extraordinary circumstances" and offered the guards. He mentions the US ambassador of the time, Tom Pickering. If true, it shows the two rival services working together at a moment of real danger.
russian-officials-studying-ufos: Russian officials have said publicly that their country has people studying UFOs. Robert Salas, a former Air Force officer, passes this on, quoting them as saying, "Yeah, we we've got people studying the UFO questions." If true, it would mean the interest in UFOs is not just an American one.
russian-snow-alien-body-found-in-siberia: In 2011, Michels says, two Russian men named Timur and Kirill came across an alien body in the snowy woods of Siberia, one month after a UFO was seen over the same region around the city of Irkutsk. Michels tells it himself on two episodes in 2025. In the later one he gives no year and credits the story to someone he names only as Marshall rather than to the two men who found it. If true, it would be physical remains of a non-human being.
russian-triangle-event-as-pre-arranged-m: Matthew Brown, introduced on the episode as a Pentagon whistleblower, believes that an event in 2018 over the Pacific Ocean off Kamchatka in eastern Russia, which he calls the Russian triangle event, was not a chance encounter. He tells Michels, "I've come to believe that that was some sort of pre-arranged meeting um for whatever purpose," a meeting or handover that, if he is right, someone had planned in advance.
russians-beaming-negative-mental-energy-: The Russians would beam negative mental energy at their opponents during chess matches, trying to throw them off with the mind alone. This comes from Eric Haseltine, a former official at the National Security Agency, the US spy agency that intercepts communications, who mentions it in passing without saying where he heard it. It would mean a state took the idea of mental influence seriously enough to use it in competition.
ruth-paine-and-marina-find-the-walker-no: After President Kennedy was killed in 1963, and after the FBI had already searched the home thoroughly, Ruth Paine and Marina Oswald, the wife of the accused killer Lee Harvey Oswald, are said to have come forward with a newly found note he had left for Marina. The note was tied to Edwin Walker, a retired general Oswald was accused of trying to shoot. The lawyer and researcher Dan Sheehan tells this without naming a source, and raises it to suggest the note's late discovery was suspicious.
ruth-paine-at-naushon-island-retreat-wit: Ruth Paine, a figure in the story of President Kennedy's assassination, is said to have spent the summer of 1963 on Naushon Island, near Martha's Vineyard in Massachusetts, a retreat linked to the Forbes family, in the company of Mary Bancroft, the mistress of former CIA director Allen Dulles. A researcher named Dan Sheehan confirms this on the show without naming a source. He tells it to suggest a link between Paine and the circle around Dulles.
ruth-paine-houses-lee-harvey-oswald-and-: In 1963 a woman named Ruth Paine took Lee Harvey Oswald, the man accused of killing President John F. Kennedy, and his wife Marina Oswald into her house in Texas. The writer Peter Levenda, billed on the show as a historian of the CIA, tells it without naming a source, and simply says the Oswalds were living with Ruth Paine in that house. Michels brings it up too, while tracing family ties among people he links to the CIA. He says he thinks Ruth Paine was the daughter of a woman he is discussing, and that she is the one who took in Oswald. Both tell it because they see the Oswalds' hosts as part of a wider web of connections behind the Kennedy killing.
ruth-paine-s-sister-works-for-the-cia-pa: In 1963 a woman named Ruth Paine brought Lee Harvey Oswald, the man accused of killing President Kennedy, and his wife Marina Oswald to Dallas, and Paine's sister worked for the CIA, the US spy agency. The researcher Dan Sheehan tells this without naming a source ("Turns out her sister works for the CIA") and traces the story through Virginia, New Orleans and Dallas. If true, it would tie the spy agency to the people around Oswald just before the killing.
ryan-graves-says-go-fast-was-recorded-by: One of the Navy videos of unexplained objects that the New York Times made public in 2017 was recorded in 2015 off Jacksonville, Florida, by a close friend of the Navy fighter pilot Ryan Graves, Graves says. He tells it first-hand: he first saw the video in a classified setting and says "my very good buddy" recorded it, though he won't name the friend or say which video it was. Michels later repeats it, saying Graves, who also testified under oath to Congress, "kind of admitted" the video known as Go Fast, which shows a small object moving fast over the ocean, was filmed by a buddy of his. That would put a real pilot he knows behind one of the famous clips.
s-4-facility-hand-scanner-corridor-and-n: A secret site called S-4, near Papoose Lake in the Nevada desert, had a hand scanner controlling access, a corridor, and nine hangars, according to a man named Bob Lazar, who says he worked there in 1988 and 1989. Lazar describes it to Michels as something he saw himself ("And there were nine hangars") and mentions a man named Dennis Mariani in connection with it. If true, it would describe a hidden base the public was never told about.
s-force-triangular-fire-team-trained-on-: Between about 1960 and 1963, a group Dan Sheehan calls "S force" set up a training base on a Mexican ranch owned by the Texas oilman Clint Murchison Jr. There, he says, a three-person team practiced shooting a moving target from three different spots at once, a setup he connects to Fort Huachuca, an Army base in Arizona. Sheehan, a lawyer, tells Michels this without naming a source, and he ties it to a CIA man named Carl Jenkins and the mob boss Santo Trafficante Jr. He raises it because it would point to a plan behind the killing of President John F. Kennedy.
s4-imagery-covered-up-on-google-earth-pr: Satellite images of S4, a secret site in Nevada tied to the claims of a man named Bob Lazar, are said to have been covered up on Google Earth, the online map of satellite photos. Michels says the data shows "stuff they tried to cover up on Google Earth," and credits a documentary called Project Gravitar. An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb relays the work of another researcher, Luigi Vendittelli, who he says "painstakingly" tries to show how foliage was rearranged around S4 sites, which he places near Papoose Lake. In a later episode Michels explains that Vendittelli used Google Earth's older archived images to find a 2022 picture of the area taken before the site was blurred, showing vehicle tracks around S4. The tellers differ on details but all point to the same researcher and documentary. If true, it would suggest someone is hiding activity at the place Lazar describes.
s4-project-directives-duplicate-propulsi: In 1988 and 1989, the work at S4, a secret site in the Nevada desert, had two standing orders: first, copy the craft's propulsion system "at any cost", and second, find a way to disable that system from a distance, also at any cost. That is how Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked at S4, describes it to Jesse Michels from his own time there. If true, it would mean the goal was both to copy the technology and to be able to defend against it.
sac-telegram-on-echo-flight-demands-boei: After a group of nuclear missiles called Echo Flight shut down at Malmstrom Air Force Base in 1967, Strategic Air Command, the Air Force command in charge of nuclear missiles and bombers, is said to have sent a telegram demanding that the company Boeing investigate. Robert Salas, a former Air Force officer, says this telegram was "one of the documents we received from the air force" about the shutdown. To him it shows the military took the event seriously at the highest level.
sagan-and-shklovskii-s-intelligent-life-: The American astronomer Carl Sagan co-wrote a book called Intelligent Life in the Universe with the Soviet scientist Iosif Shklovsky in the 1960s, a joint work across the Cold War divide about life beyond Earth. The philosopher Jason Jorjani brings up the book in passing, without naming a source.
sagan-bumped-up-against-the-ufo-program: The astronomer Carl Sagan may have run into a secret government UFO program and been told he needed to make changes, according to a researcher named Bob Maguire. Maguire says plainly that he does not know this as a fact and offers it as his own belief. If so, it would mean one of the best-known public voices on space was steered by people who knew more.
sagan-in-venus-anomaly-meeting-with-whit: A man named Bob Maguire, a contractor for the CIA, says he walked into a meeting about something strange found on Venus and knew why he was there: in the room sat the astronomer Carl Sagan, "maybe the most famous venusian planet scientist that ever lived." Michels repeats a version he heard, in which the meeting included the White House science adviser, while Maguire himself places it in the office of the chief scientist at the National Security Agency, the US government's electronic spying agency, during the Clinton years, as a meeting about passing technology on. Told either way, it would mean a top scientist was quietly brought in on an unexplained finding.
sagan-s-1963-paper-estimating-et-visitat: The astronomer Carl Sagan published a technical paper in 1963 that used the Drake equation, a formula for estimating how many advanced civilizations might exist in our galaxy, to work out how many there probably are, and the paper is said to consider alien visits to Earth and bases on the Moon. A researcher named Maaneli Derakhshani describes it on the show, without quoting it directly, to show that a mainstream scientist once took such ideas seriously.
sagan-s-1975-paper-on-detecting-artifici: The astronomer Carl Sagan wrote a paper in 1975 about how to find signs of technologically advanced life on other planets by looking for artificial structures on their surfaces. The researcher Maaneli Derakhshani brings it up without giving more detail of the source. He uses it to argue that looking for built structures on other worlds was a serious scientific idea.
sagan-s-early-diaries-about-ufos-1950: The astronomer Carl Sagan, Michels says, wrote about UFOs all the time in his early diaries, written roughly in the 1950s and 60s. Michels says this himself on two episodes, once mentioning the astronomer J. Allen Hynek alongside Sagan, and he does not quote the diaries. If true, it would show that a scientist known for doubting UFOs privately took a close interest in them.
sagan-s-nsa-contractor-green-badge: The astronomer Carl Sagan is said to have carried a contractor's badge at the National Security Agency, the US government's code-breaking and eavesdropping agency. A former CIA contractor named Bob Maguire says he saw it himself: a green contractor badge with Sagan's photo, the kind "you don't get if you're casual". It would mean Sagan did real, ongoing work for the agency.
sagan-whispers-keep-up-the-great-work-to: The astronomer Carl Sagan is said to have walked up to Richard Hoagland, a man known for claims about NASA and the Moon, at a hearing. Sagan put a hand on his shoulder, whispered "Keep up the great work" in his ear and walked off. A guest named Maaneli Derakhshani tells this second-hand, as something Hoagland told him, and it would suggest that Sagan quietly backed work he did not support in public.
sagancarlotto-correspondence-on-the-face: In the 1980s there were letters with Mark Carlotto, one of the early researchers of the Face on Mars, a hill in the Cydonia region of Mars that looks like a face in spacecraft photos. The letters showed interest in analyses of the face by the astronomer Carl Sagan. A researcher named Maaneli Derakhshani tells Michels this without naming a source, and he brings in the NASA scientist Gerald Soffen too. He raises it because it would mean well-known scientists took the face more seriously than they let on in public.
sages-helped-by-the-gods-founded-a-new-c: Around Lake Van, in eastern Turkey, a group of very wise sages, who were "literally being helped by the gods" as the old accounts put it, built something new there, a fresh start for civilization. A researcher named Matt LaCroix tells this in his own words and does not name the texts he draws on. If true, it would point to a lost chapter of early human history guided from outside.
saic-as-contractor-for-psionic-testing-n: According to Jesse Michels, a person he calls only Sammy believes that SAIC, a large US defence contractor, was the company doing psionic testing, meaning tests of mind powers, for the government. Michels passes this on secondhand, noting that SAIC sits right next to Naval Surface Warfare Center Crane, a Navy research base in Indiana, and he names the physicist James Woodward in the same breath.
saic-connection-to-crane: SAIC, a large American defense contractor, is said to have done work connected to Crane, a US Navy research base in Indiana. Michels raises this himself in an episode with a guest who says he saw alien technology at a military base, and credits the digging to an online researcher who goes by "UAP Gerb" (UAP being the government's term for UFOs). He says this researcher has turned up "a lot of research" on the link, which would tie a private contractor to the base at the centre of the guest's story.
saic-exotic-science-and-stargate-links: A company called SAIC (Science Applications International Corporation), based in Reston, Virginia, has openly studied unusual science such as exotic propulsion, anti-gravity and energy beams, and seems to have worked hand in hand with Stargate, the psychic spying programme of the CIA, the US Central Intelligence Agency. Michels says this in two episodes, calling it public information, and in the later one says SAIC inherited the CIA's remote viewing work (attempts to see distant places with the mind) and that Bobby Ray Inman, a man he says sat on the company's board, linked it to possible recovery of crashed UFOs. If so, a private contractor would sit at the meeting point of psychic research and UFO secrets.
sal-pais-applauds-rossi-s-panel-example-: About two summers before this conversation, around 2023, a scientist named Salvatore Pais started clapping when a guest named Dave Rossi gave a certain physics example on a panel they shared. Rossi tells this as something he was part of, saying he "used this exact example and Sal Pais started basically clapping." He brings it up as a sign that a serious scientist backed his line of thinking.
salas-rebuts-the-emp-explanation-1967: The 1967 shutdown of nuclear missiles at Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana was explained in the Wall Street Journal as caused by an electromagnetic pulse, a burst of energy that can knock out electronics, but Robert Salas, a former Air Force officer who was there, rejects that. Michels quotes Salas's reply: "it would have been irresponsible and unthinkable for the U.S. Air Force to jeopardize the operational status of these weapons." If Salas is right, the shutdown still has no ordinary explanation.
salas-s-14-point-wsj-rebuttal-2025: A former Air Force officer named Robert Salas says that in 2025 he wrote a rebuttal listing 14 reasons why an EMP test, a burst of electromagnetic energy that can knock out electronics, "couldn't have been" what shut down his nuclear missiles. He was answering a Wall Street Journal article in which the Pentagon office that studies unexplained aerial reports gave the test as the explanation. Salas, who says a UFO shut down the missiles while he was on duty, tells this himself to Michels, and he is pushing back on the official account of his own story.
salas-s-2-5-hour-aaro-interview: A former Air Force officer named Robert Salas, who says a UFO once shut down ten nuclear missiles, says he sat with AARO, the Pentagon office that now studies unexplained aerial reports, for two and a half hours to lay out his case. He tells Michels he also handed them documents to back up what he said, which matters to him because it means the office had his evidence firsthand.
salty-liquid-water-on-the-martian-surfac: In 2015, researchers claimed to have found firm evidence of salty liquid water flowing on the surface of Mars, and Michels says the news "stunned the world". He tells it himself, without naming a source, on a 2025 episode with the remote viewer Joe McMoneagle about whether Mars once had life. He raises it because liquid water would make past or present life on Mars more plausible.
salvatore-pais-filed-patents-at-pax-rive: A Navy scientist named Salvatore Pais filed patents for unusual technologies, including a craft that reduces its own inertial mass and a machine that makes high-frequency gravitational waves, while working at Naval Air Station Patuxent River, a Navy test base in Maryland known as Pax River. The researcher UAPGerb says that is where he filed them. Michels dates the patents to 2018 and says they contain basically everything you would need to build a UFO, while Pais himself says he filed five applications, of which three became patents, and that the two rejected ones were the most ordinary.
salvatore-pais-inertial-mass-reduction-p: In 2016, according to Michels, the US Navy filed a patent naming an inventor called Salvatore Pais for what it titled a "craft using an inertial mass reduction device", meaning a vehicle meant to act as if it had far less mass so it could move in ways normal aircraft cannot. Michels tells this himself, in an episode about a UFO book the Pentagon is said to have tried to censor, as a sign that the Navy was working on technology like the kind people describe in UFOs.
same-distances-encoded-at-roman-sites: The same distances, 5,300 meters and 2,300 meters, are said to be built into Roman sites and into hillsides laid out like the White Horse Hills of Wiltshire, England, where huge horse figures are cut into the chalk. A researcher named Geoffrey Drumm says this without naming a source. He takes it as a sign that one shared system of measurement links ancient sites across the world.
same-words-do-not-fear-recalled-by-both-: Two Air Force men, Mario Woods and Michael Johnson, say they were abducted in 1977 near Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota, and each recalled the same three words, "Do not fear." Michels tells it himself, describing it as two men in two rooms, hours apart, out of earshot of each other, with the story placing those sessions under hypnosis. In a later episode he says instead that they heard the words over and over before the abduction, and does not mention hypnosis. If the accounts match without either man hearing the other, it would point to a shared real experience.
sami-shaman-s-amanita-muscaria-winter-so: Among the Sami, the native people of Lapland in the far north of Europe, a shaman or healer is said to have travelled with reindeer at the winter solstice to gather fly agaric, the red and white mushroom known as Amanita muscaria, and then dried it over a fireplace. A mushroom writer and entrepreneur named Tero Isokauppila tells this to Michels as lore from the region, without naming a source. It is told as an old ritual use of the mushroom in the far north.
sammaciccia-s-guess-about-ss-eugenics-pr: The SS, the Nazi elite force, ran eugenics programs, attempts to breed "better" humans, and rumor has it these went on in secret in underground sites after the war. The philosopher Jason Jorjani tells Michels this was the guess of Bruno Sammaciccia, an Italian man who said he had contact with strange beings in the 1950s. Jorjani says the idea "occurred" to Sammaciccia as a way to explain what he had met.
sammy-hagar-s-love-walks-in-lyrics-came-: The rock singer Sammy Hagar does not know where the words of his 1986 song Love Walks In came from, according to Chris Bledsoe, a man who says UFOs appear around him. Bledsoe says Hagar told him this personally, and he tells it as an example of ideas arriving from somewhere outside the person.
samples-from-the-baltic-sea-anomaly-test: In 2011 and 2012, divers took samples from the material lying on top of a strange round shape on the floor of the Baltic Sea, and the tests showed it was burned organic matter of natural origin. Dennis Asberg, a Swedish treasure hunter whose team found the shape, tells Michels this himself and notes the samples were not taken from the object itself. The burned material matters because it would suggest something very hot once happened there.
san-jose-woman-s-disc-that-was-bigger-in: A woman in San Jose, California, is said to have seen a big disc over her house, and once inside it found it far larger than it looked, like walking into a movie theater, where a being led her up a staircase. The computer scientist and longtime UFO researcher Jacques Vallée tells it from his case files, and Michels retells it citing him, adding the movie theater detail, while Vallée in a later episode adds the being and the staircase.
sandia-history-lists-kissinger-as-a-semi: A redacted internal history of Sandia Laboratories, a US nuclear weapons laboratory at Kirtland Air Force Base in New Mexico, names Henry Kissinger, the future American statesman, as one of the experts at seminars held there. Michels reads from it himself: "Carter organized interdisciplinary seminars featuring noted international experts and specialists, one of them, Henry Kissinger," Carter being a man named Don Carter. Michels raises it while asking whether Kissinger oversaw a program to recover crashed UFOs, since it would place him at a key nuclear site early on.
santa-anastasia-excavation-yields-giant-: During a dig at the Church of Santa Anastasia on the island of Sardinia, around 1978 to 1981, the bones of giants are said to have come out of the ground, entire skeletons, which were then kept in the church. Tim Alberino, a guest who researches giant lore, passes this on from what he was told by someone connected to the site. If true, it would mean whole giant human skeletons were found and stored there.
santa-claus-tradition-traced-back-to-the: The Santa Claus tradition can be traced back to the Sami, the reindeer-herding people of Lapland in the far north of Europe, according to a guest named Tero Isokauppila. He follows the custom backwards: it reached New York through the Dutch, who had their own version called Sinterklaas, and before that ran through Germany, Italy and Turkey. He tells it as his own reading of the routes, with no named source.
sar-doppler-tomography-paper-on-vesuvius: A scientist named Filippo Biondi, known on the show for scanning beneath the pyramids, says that in 2019 he wrote a paper with the National Research Council of Italy on what lies under Mount Vesuvius near Naples, using a method that turns satellite radar signals into images of what is underground. He tells it first-hand, calling it "a very very nice paper," as an earlier test of the same technique he later used elsewhere.
sar-doppler-tomography-research-started-: A team studying the pyramids of Giza in Egypt began in 2018 to use satellite radar to build pictures of what lies under the ground, a method called radar Doppler tomography. Filippo Biondi, a researcher who led the work, says they started about two years before publishing their papers and have now been at it six or seven years. He tells it as background to his claim of large structures hidden beneath the pyramids.
sar-scan-shows-shaft-system-coming-out-o: A 2020 radar scan of the Great Pyramid of Giza in Egypt is said to show a system of shafts running down out of the floor of the Queen's Chamber, one of the rooms deep inside the pyramid. The scan comes from a 2020 paper by Filippo Biondi and a colleague named Corrado. It used satellite radar, a method that bounces radio signals off a target to build a picture of what lies beneath the surface. A researcher named Jeffrey Drum describes the result on the show, summarising the paper. If he is right, it would mean there are hidden structures under the pyramid's known rooms.
sar-team-detects-the-big-void-in-a-trans: A team scanning the Great Pyramid of Giza in Egypt with satellite radar, which builds pictures of hidden structures from radar echoes, says it found the Big Void, a large empty space inside the pyramid, lying crosswise from east to west. A researcher named Filippo Biondi says this, describing work he took part in with a colleague he calls Corrado: "we have detected the big void also." In a second telling Biondi stresses that "these are not simulated data," adds that they also picked up the Grand Gallery, the long sloping passage inside the pyramid, and dates the work to 2018 to 2020.
sar-tomography-detects-king-s-chamber-re: A 2020 scientific paper, linked to the researcher Filippo Biondi, used satellite radar scans, a method called SAR Doppler tomography, to look inside the Great Pyramid of Giza and is said to have picked up the King's Chamber, the stone beams above it, and the stone box called the sarcophagus. The researcher Jeffrey Drum walks through the images on the show, explaining that "the red is indicating a very strong vibrational signature from inside of the structure." He offers it as proof the method can see known rooms, so its other findings should be taken seriously, though a related account says the scan missed the King's Chamber.
sar-tomography-mapping-of-the-gran-sasso: Researchers are said to have used SAR tomography, a radar imaging method meant to see beneath the ground, to map the Gran Sasso Laboratory in Italy, which lies about 1.4 kilometers inside a mountain. A researcher named Jay Anderson brings this up, crediting the work to a researcher named Filippo Biondi. He offers it as a test showing that the method can find deep hidden structures.
sarbacher-craft-at-wright-patterson-take: A scientist named Robert Sarbacher is said to have claimed that a craft was being held at Wright-Patterson, an Air Force base in Ohio, and that it was taken over by something called "the Anderson trust", a story also tied to a figure from MIT, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, named Karl Compton. Michels tells this himself, passing on what he says Sarbacher said, in an episode about a government research scientist who says he was abducted. If true, it would mean a recovered craft passed out of military hands into a private or academic group.
sarbacher-involved-in-standing-up-the-pr: A man named Robert Sarbacher is said to have helped set up the secret government UFO programme that a former intelligence officer turned whistleblower, David Grusch, says he uncovered. Grusch passes this on as something he was told, calling Sarbacher someone "purportedly involved in the stand up" of it. Michels tells it a little differently: relaying Grusch, he puts the start of UFO secrecy in 1954 and ties it to the atomic physicist J. Robert Oppenheimer and an inventor named Thomas Townsend Brown, which, if true, would place the secrecy's roots with some of the biggest names in American science.
sarbacher-karl-compton-briefed-on-ufo-te: In 1950, the story goes, Karl Compton, the president of MIT (the Massachusetts Institute of Technology), was briefed on UFO technology at Wright Field, an Air Force base in Ohio. Michels says the scientist Robert Sarbacher told this to Stanton Friedman, a nuclear engineer and UFO researcher. In another episode Michels repeats it more loosely, without a source, a date or Compton's name: an MIT president was rumoured to have been shown the craft itself. If true, it would mean one of the country's top scientists was let in on recovered UFO technology.
sarbacher-known-to-australian-nuclear-en: In the 1950s, it is said, nuclear engineers in Australia knew of the American scientist Robert Sarbacher, with a link to Woomera, a weapons test site in the Australian outback. Michels mentions it only in passing, on a 2025 episode with the writer Whitley Strieber. He says the Australian journalist Ross Coulthart has "interesting data points" about these engineers, and he raises it as backing for Sarbacher's place in the UFO story, without giving the details.
sarbacher-picks-up-townsend-brown-after-: Jesse Michels says that in 1956 the inventor Thomas Townsend Brown ran an experiment in Paris showing that the Biefeld-Brown effect, a push produced by high-voltage electricity, works even in a vacuum, hinting at a link between electromagnetism and gravity. When Brown came back to the US, Michels says, he was picked up in a black Cadillac by Robert Sarbacher, a government scientist. Michels tells it himself, without naming a source, as a sign that officials quietly took an interest in work that might lead to anti-gravity.
sarbacher-put-cameras-on-modified-v2-roc: A scientist named Robert Sarbacher is said to have put cameras on modified V2 rockets, the German missiles the US took over after the Second World War, to try to photograph UFOs. Michels tells it in two episodes: in one he quotes Sarbacher's son, who he says has gone on record that "my father told me" this, and in the other he tells it in a passage about the inventor Thomas Townsend Brown, without citing the son. If true, it would mean American scientists were actively hunting UFOs with rocket cameras in the years after 1947.
sarbacher-s-letter-to-william-steinman-1: Late in his life, the physicist Robert Sarbacher is said to have admitted in writing that the rumours of crashed UFOs were "substantially correct." Jesse Michels tells this in several episodes. He describes Sarbacher as a student of Einstein and a famed Harvard physicist who wrote to a UFO researcher named William Steinman, around 1987 by Michels' dating. In Michels' account, Steinman wrote first to ask whether there really was a UFO program, and Sarbacher replied that the scientists Vannevar Bush, John von Neumann and J. Robert Oppenheimer were involved. Michels also says Sarbacher worked under Bush and was a close colleague of the inventor Thomas Townsend Brown. He sometimes speaks of a single letter and sometimes of several. A UFO researcher named Grant Cameron tells it a little differently: he cites a 1983 taped conversation with Sarbacher rather than a letter, credits the UFO researcher Stan Friedman, and says Sarbacher was invited to a briefing on a crash at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base in 1950. If true, it would mean some of America's leading wartime scientists were quietly studying crashed craft.
sarbacher-s-secret-atomic-lab-in-washing: In the 1950s, a scientist named Robert Sarbacher ran a secret atomic lab at a house in Washington DC. The researcher Jan Lundquist says a newspaper reported that Sarbacher had asked to renew a permit "to pursue atomic research at this residential address," though Lundquist does not name the paper. He offers it as a sign of hidden research going on in plain sight.
sarbacher-said-von-neumann-was-directly-: The American scientist Robert Sarbacher is said to have claimed that the mathematician John von Neumann was directly involved in the government's secret handling of UFOs in the 1950s. Michels mentions this in a single line while talking with the author Whitley Strieber, and he does not say where Sarbacher said it. If true, it would place one of the century's great minds inside the secret.
sarbacher-tells-strieber-about-battelle-: Sometime in the 1980s, a scientist named Robert Sarbacher described in detail the materials he had been working on at the Battelle Memorial Institute, a private research institute, according to a man named Whitley Strieber, who says he spoke with him by phone. Strieber tells Michels that a contact named only as Sam passed him Sarbacher's number and called back to say Sarbacher was "very eager to talk". If true, it would mean someone inside that research work was willing to talk openly about unusual materials.
sardinian-elders-dug-up-giant-bones-with: Older people on the Italian island of Sardinia say that in the middle of the twentieth century they dug up, with their own hands, the bones of giants, buried with jewellery. The filmmaker Tim Alberino says he interviewed dozens of these people himself for a work called True Legends, in which the author Steve Quayle also appears. If true, it would mean a race of very large humans once lived there.
sardinians-said-to-descend-from-giants: Some people on Sardinia, the Italian island in the Mediterranean, say they are descended from giants. Tim Alberino, a guest who hunts for evidence of ancient giants, passes this on as what some of the islanders themselves say, as part of his case that giants once lived.
sarfatti-s-claimed-non-human-intelligenc: A man named Jack Sarfatti is said to have claimed, about fifty years ago in the 1970s, that he had an experience with a UFO or with some non-human intelligence, and to have worked on the problem ever since. A guest named Bob Maguire mentions this in passing, relaying what Sarfatti himself has claimed.
sarfatti-s-navy-friend-and-the-living-cr: At a Navy facility on the US East Coast, a recovered craft is said to have resisted every attempt to get inside it, because the craft is alive, conscious, and "got an attitude": unless you "vibrate at the right level," you cannot get in. The UFO researcher Grant Cameron relays this from the physicist Jack Sarfatti, who in turn heard it from a friend in the Navy. If true, it would mean such craft are living things, not just machines.
sars-spike-protein-modification-proposal: In 2017, Michels says, EcoHealth Alliance, a US nonprofit research group, sent DARPA, the Pentagon's advanced research agency, a proposal to change a SARS virus so that its spike protein could attach to ACE2, a receptor on human cells, and when DARPA turned it down the work moved to the Wuhan Institute of Virology in China. Michels tells it himself on a 2025 episode with Brigham Buhler, naming Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and the US health official Anthony Fauci, and draws on no named document. He raises it as a sign that the research behind the COVID virus may have been planned in the open and then moved abroad.
satan-and-his-angels-cast-down-to-earth-: Long ago, before Adam, the first man in the Bible, Satan and his angels came to Earth or were thrown down to it after a battle in the heavens. The researcher Tim Alberino tells Michels this as his own reading, without naming a source. He says they arrived "a long time ago after that cosmic battle."
satellite-mistaken-for-object-near-jupit: About a year before the conversation, people on the social media site X got excited about a strange object they thought was circling Jupiter or Saturn, when it was really a satellite going around the Earth. That is how Michael Shermer, a well-known skeptic who studies why people believe unusual things, tells it from what he saw posted, as an example of how easily ordinary objects in the sky get mistaken for something extraordinary.
satellites-shake-over-roraima-s-rare-ear: American satellites that scan the planet for minerals are said to shake violently, "almost to the point of dropping," when they pass over Roraima, a state in northern Brazil, because the signal from the rare earths in its ground is so strong. Rare earths are scarce metals used in modern electronics. Aldo Rebelo, a former Brazilian defence minister, passes this on as something that "is believed," a way of saying how rich and strategically important that land would be.
saucer-as-contractor-owned-prototype-wit: A saucer-shaped craft Greg Rogers says he saw in a hangar at Cape Canaveral Air Force Station in Florida in 1992 was, he believes, a prototype owned by a private defense company, not by the Air Force. Rogers, a NASA doctor, saw it himself and describes it hooked up to cables and hoses. If he is right, such craft are being built and kept by companies, outside the military's own records.
saucers-fly-on-magnetic-lines-of-force-1: Flying saucers move by riding magnetic lines of force, according to a man named Silas Newton, speaking at the University of Denver in Colorado in 1950. In his own words, heard on the episode, "That ship and the others that are flying fly on magnetic lines of force." If true, it would mean someone had studied a real craft closely enough to know how it flew.
saudi-pilots-filmed-orbs-2024: In 2024, two pilots flying over Saudi Arabia are said to have seen, and filmed, some striking glowing orbs. Michels mentions it himself, saying it happened about a week earlier, during an episode about the former Pentagon UFO investigator Lue Elizondo, with no source named and few details given.
saul-on-the-road-to-damascus-blinded-by-: The bright light that blinded Saul on the road to Damascus, in the Bible's Book of Acts, was really an orb, a glowing ball of light. Chris Bledsoe, a man who says UFOs are drawn to him and whom NASA has studied, says so as his own reading of the passage, with no other source. If he is right, one of the best-known conversions in Christian scripture would be an early sighting of the same lights he says he sees.
saw-sharper-uap-video-on-the-inside-than: A Pentagon whistleblower named Matthew Brown says that inside the government he saw videos of unidentified flying objects that ranged in quality, some sharper and clearer about what the object was than the footage released to the public. He tells Michels this from his own work around 2018, and it would mean the public has seen only the blurrier end of what exists.
scalar-treatment-cures-herrera-s-dog-s-b: A man named Michael Herrera, who says he once saw a 300-foot UFO in the Indonesian jungle, says a treatment he calls scalar cured his dog. He says the dog had been diagnosed with a mass in its bladder that vets thought was cancer, and that this treatment was used on him. Herrera tells it as his own experience, as proof that the technology heals.
scandinavian-ghost-rockets-that-hit-wate: In the 1940s, rocket- and cigar-shaped objects called "ghost rockets" were reported over Norway and Sweden, and they are said never to have landed or crashed on the ground, always plunging into water instead. Michels tells this himself in two episodes, once in passing and once in more detail, where he speaks of at least 1,400 documented sightings and says the Swedish government even formed a special military unit to deal with them. He raises it because objects that only ever came down in water would point to something linked to the sea.
scandinavian-ufos-come-down-only-in-wate: In 1946, when many strange objects were reported over Sweden and Norway, not a single one is said to have crashed on land: the ones that came down all went into water. A Swedish UFO researcher named Clas Svahn points this out, stressing that it is important, while summing up the cases he has studied. The pattern, if real, would suggest the objects behaved in a deliberate way rather than falling at random.
scanpyramids-project-uses-muons-to-find-: Since 2015 a research effort called the ScanPyramids project has been looking for hidden empty spaces inside the pyramids at Giza in Egypt. It does this by using muons, tiny particles that rain down on Earth from space and pass through stone. The researcher Filippo Biondi, who has scanned beneath the pyramids himself by other means, describes it in a December 2025 episode. He says ScanPyramids "is using muons which are sub particles that are emitted from the universe." By measuring how many of these particles get through the stone, the team can spot hollow areas. The researcher Jeffrey Drum tells more about the project in a 2026 episode and cites the team's published paper on its muon work. Drum says the scientists work with "a Japanese team that's been sponsoring and providing the funding for all of this", together with Egypt's Ministry of Antiquities, the government office that oversees ancient sites. The project is brought up because it shows that the pyramids may still hold rooms nobody has entered.
scans-show-a-second-grand-gallery-inside: Scans of the Great Pyramid in Egypt are said to show what looks like a second Grand Gallery, a copy of the tall sloping passage inside, sitting above the first one. The writer Graham Hancock mentions this without naming a source. He sees it as a sign that the pyramid still hides large unknown spaces.
schauberger-devices-that-reportedly-took: In the 1940s, in Austria and Czechoslovakia, an inventor named Viktor Schauberger supposedly built machines that "reportedly took off" and flew. The researcher Nick Cook passes this on without a source, calling them "pretty arcane stories." If true, it would mean flying machines of an unusual kind were being built during that decade.
schauberger-s-propulsion-work-taken-to-b: An inventor named Viktor Schauberger was tricked by the US Army Counter Intelligence Corps, an Army intelligence unit, into handing over all his work on unusual ways of propelling craft, and that work ended up at Brookhaven National Laboratory, a US government research lab. Michels tells this in passing, pointing listeners to the website of the writer Nick Cook as his source. If true, it would mean exotic propulsion ideas from Europe quietly entered American government science.
schauberger-s-wartime-diary-matches-the-: Viktor Schauberger was an Austrian inventor who worked on unusual flight technology during the Second World War, and his wartime diary is said to line up with the secret sites run by Hans Kammler, the Nazi officer in charge of hidden weapons projects. The British aviation journalist Nick Cook says he went to visit the Schauberger family, who "opened up their files, the family files," and that the diary placed Schauberger at sites such as Jablonec, in what was then Czechoslovakia, between 1942 and 1945. To Cook this ties Schauberger to the Nazis' most secret advanced aircraft research.
schauberger-taken-by-ss-to-secret-work-1: In 1941 an officer of the SS, the Nazi elite force, approached the Austrian inventor Viktor Schauberger, and after that his life went completely silent. Michels tells this himself in a documentary about the inventor Townsend Brown, drawing on a letter Schauberger wrote to his son Walter Schauberger. The suggestion is that Schauberger was taken into secret wartime work for the Nazis.
schindele-red-glowing-object-over-minot-: A retired US Air Force captain named David Schindele remembers starting his shift at Minot Air Force Base in North Dakota in 1966 and hearing reports of a bright red glowing object hovering over the base. Michels relays Schindele's account in an episode about UFOs seen over nuclear weapons bases, where it serves as one example of such objects watching those sites.
schliemann-finds-troy: Troy, the city of Homer's ancient poems, was long dismissed as myth until Heinrich Schliemann, a German businessman, took the old stories seriously and found it in Anatolia, in modern Turkey. Michels tells this himself on four episodes, giving the date as 1871 in one, "the 1870s" in another and simply the late 19th century in a third, and naming Herodotus in one telling and Thucydides in another as the ancient historians who guided Schliemann. He uses it to argue that legends of lost places and lost history can turn out to be true.
schriever-disc-test-flight-in-prague-194: Jesse Michels says that a German technician named Rudolf Schriever claimed to have worked in Prague on a disc-shaped aircraft that first flew in February 1945, climbing to 40,000 feet in three minutes. Michels says Schriever was recruited by Hans Kammler, a Nazi officer in charge of secret weapons, and tells it himself, without naming a source, as a hint that disc-shaped craft may have wartime human roots.
schriever-s-1944-disc-flight: A German technician named Rudolf Schriever is said to have claimed that a disc-shaped craft he worked on during the Second World War flew and climbed to 40,000 feet within minutes. Michels tells this himself in two episodes, passing on Schriever's claim: in one he puts the flight in 1944, and in the other, a documentary about the inventor Thomas Townsend Brown, he places it in Prague in February 1945 and says the climb took three minutes. If true, it would mean Nazi Germany flew a working flying disc before the war ended.
schrodinger-s-1944-what-is-life-lectures: The idea is that living things are drawn toward order and that cells act with goals and intentions. Michels says the physicist Erwin Schrödinger theorized this in his 1944 lecture series What is Life?, and that the biologist Michael Levin at Tufts University is finding it now, that "biological cells have clear goals and intentions." Michels offers this himself as part of an argument that purpose runs deep in nature.
schrodinger-s-what-is-life-and-aperiodic: The physicist Erwin Schrödinger, in a book called What Is Life?, which Michels dates to 1944, wrote about "aperiodic crystals" in living cells. These are orderly structures whose pattern does not simply repeat. Michels says himself that Schrödinger saw them in DNA as important containers of information, and he brings it up twice as an early scientist's hint that life carries information in unusual ways.
schumer-amendment-to-ndaa-gutted-mike-tu: In 2023, an amendment by Senator Chuck Schumer to the National Defense Authorization Act, the yearly law that sets US military spending, was almost entirely stripped out, and the congressman Mike Turner played a part in that. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, as proof of how hard it is to get the government to release what it knows about UFOs.
schumer-s-64-page-uap-amendment-2023: In 2023 the Senate's majority leader, Chuck Schumer, put forward a long piece of draft law that speaks openly of "non-human intelligence", of recovered technologies of unknown origin and of biological evidence. Several guests tell Michels about it as a sign that people at the top of Congress take crashed craft seriously. The text is the Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Disclosure Act of 2023 ("unidentified anomalous phenomena", or UAP, is the government's term for UFOs). Schumer submitted it on 13 July 2023 as an amendment to the Senate's yearly defence spending bill, for himself and Senators Mike Rounds, Marco Rubio, Kirsten Gillibrand, Todd Young and Martin Heinrich. It defines non-human intelligence as "any sentient intelligent non-human lifeform regardless of nature or ultimate origin", and it describes a "legacy program", meaning long-running secret efforts "to collect, exploit, or reverse engineer technologies of unknown origin or examine biological evidence of living or deceased non-human intelligence". David Grusch, a former intelligence official turned whistleblower, says Schumer "was compelled" to write a "64 page amendment" about non-human technology and recoveries. The researcher Matthew Pines and Karl Nell, a retired Army colonel, focus on who sponsored it, and Nell says its message was that Congress is not being told the truth. The writer Marik von Rennenkampff says it mentions non-human intelligence 22 times, Michels himself says 65 times counting UAP, and the lawyer Dan Sheehan says the law, signed by the president, orders every military service to gather its UFO records going back to 1945. In the official record of Congress the amendment actually fills seven pages and uses the phrase "non-human intelligence" 24 times.
scientific-breakthroughs-as-divine-inspi: Michels suggests that some of science's great breakthroughs may have arrived like inspiration from outside, almost downloaded. His examples are Albert Einstein working out the photoelectric effect (how light knocks electrons out of metal) while bored at his desk in the Swiss patent office, the physicist Wolfgang Pauli dreaming up the structure of the hydrogen atom, Werner Heisenberg finding his matrix mathematics on the island of Helgoland, and Paul Dirac staring into a fire in Cambridge before writing his famous equation. He offers this as his own idea, and in a later episode credits the writer Jimena Canales for it, leaves out Einstein and Pauli, and adds Niels Bohr and René Descartes, which takes the pattern back to the 1600s.
scientific-engineering-institute-passes-: The CIA's Scientific Engineering Institute, a research body tied to the US spy agency, was quietly moved into private hands in the late 1970s, Michels says, passing first to the drug company Searle and then, by the mid 1980s, to the chemical company Monsanto. He tells it himself, without naming a source, on a 2025 episode with Brigham Buhler about drug companies and human experiments, and names the politician Donald Rumsfeld in connection with it. He raises it as a sign that secret government science can live on inside private companies.
scientist-x-lecture-at-university-of-den: On March 8, 1950, a man named Silas Newton stood up at the University of Denver in Colorado and gave a lecture as the mysterious "Scientist X." Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, in an episode about a crash in which sixteen alien bodies are said to have been found. In that episode the lecture is part of how the crashed craft story first reached the public.
scientists-find-traces-of-underground-dw: Scientists who study caves and rocks are said to have found traces of beings living underground in the mountains of the Caucasus, India, Tibet and the Altai. The teller is a former president of one of Russia's republics, who says he knows these scientists and repeats what they told him while travelling with them. He gives no more detail of what the traces were.
scientists-limited-to-20-minutes-inside-: After a craft reportedly came down in 1948 in Hart Canyon near Aztec, New Mexico, the scientists who went inside it could only stay a short time. Michels says they could not stay longer than 20 minutes at a time "because some negative energy overcomes them." Scott Ramsey, who has looked into the Aztec site with his family, tells it at second hand. He says a man told him what a woman had told that man: that scientists who stayed inside any longer "would come out sick." If true, it would mean the craft gave off something that harmed the people studying it.
scientology-belief-in-a-pleiadian-zeta-r: The Church of Scientology, a religion founded in the United States, believes a great war is going on between humanlike people from the Pleiades, a cluster of stars, and reptilian beings from Zeta Reticuli, a nearby star system. The lawyer Dan Sheehan tells Michels this on two episodes, once in 2024 and again in 2025, using nearly the same words each time. He presents it as what the church believes and names no source for it.
scientology-flies-sheehan-to-florida-to-: In the 1970s the Church of Scientology flew a lawyer named Dan Sheehan to Clearwater, Florida, to try to recruit him as a lawyer for its founder, L. Ron Hubbard. Sheehan says this happened to him, and remembers the church's "big blue cube", a huge blue building. He mentions the Guardian's Office, the church's in-house arm that dealt with legal and security matters, as part of the approach.
scientology-s-claim-to-sovereign-status-: The Church of Scientology, a religious movement in the United States, believed it was entitled to be treated as a sovereign entity, like a country of its own, because the Catholic Church was, according to a lawyer named Dan Sheehan. Sheehan, who says he dealt with this firsthand, ties that claim to the group's Fair Game program, its policy toward people it saw as opponents.
scientology-s-surveillance-file-on-sheeh: In the 1970s, the Church of Scientology, a religious movement founded by L. Ron Hubbard and based in Clearwater, Florida, kept a surveillance file on the lawyer Dan Sheehan, he says, with "pictures of me" in it. Sheehan tells this himself, saying he saw the file, and he mentions the lawyer Mark Lane in the same account. It would mean the church was watching him closely while he dealt with it.
scif-meeting-with-aaro-head-jon-kosloski: The documentary filmmaker James Fox says he met Jon Kosloski, head of a Pentagon office set up to look into unexplained sightings, in a secure room for classified talks near the Pentagon, sometime in the 2020s. Fox, who made the film The Phenomenon, tells it as his own meeting and says Kosloski told him, "You know, James, I can't part my hair without the approval of the DoD," meaning the Department of Defense, which Fox offers as a sign of how little the office head could say on his own.
scif-meeting-with-congressional-staffers: On March 3, 2023, a man named Dylan Borland says he sat with congressional staffers in a SCIF, a secure room built for classified conversations. He tells Michels he had been put in touch with Congress a few days earlier, part of the same wave of insiders who came forward to lawmakers about UFOs that year.
scif-world-map-briefing-on-borderless-co: Inside a SCIF, a sealed and guarded room where secret government briefings are held, there was a map on the wall showing a hidden organisation that does not follow national borders. Steven Greer, a man who argues that UFO secrets are held by a hidden global group, tells Michels he was in the room himself, which would mean the people keeping these secrets work across countries rather than for any one government.
scott-andrews-taken-to-space-command-as-: A man named Scott Andrews is said to have been taken as a child to an Air Force base with a space command centre, the part of the military that watches over space, to do "intuitive communications with aliens," meaning contact by mind rather than by machine. Michels passes this on from Andrews himself, in a conversation about a former Army sergeant named Dan Sherman who says a government spy agency hired him for similar work. If true, it would mean the military used gifted children as go-betweens with non-human beings.
scott-crane-meets-eric-walker-of-majesti: A man named Scott Crane is said to have met a man named Eric Walker, whom he believed belonged to Majestic 12, a rumoured secret group of officials and scientists said to manage the UFO question. Michels tells this himself in an episode with the writer Peter Levenda, and adds that Crane then converted to Christianity, became "hardcore Christian" and "forgot about the whole thing." If true, it would mean a person had direct contact with a member of that secret group and then walked away from it.
scott-kelly-s-tomcat-ufo-was-a-bart-simp: A "UFO" seen from a Navy fighter jet off Virginia Beach in the 1990s turned out to be a Bart Simpson balloon. Scott Kelly, a former Navy pilot who was flying the plane, an F-14 Tomcat, says the radar officer in his back seat was convinced they had flown past a UFO. He tells it to show how ordinary things can fool trained crews.
scott-overhears-navajo-men-talk-of-the-o: In 1988 in Farmington, New Mexico, a man named Scott Ramsey says he overheard some Navajo men, from the Native American people of that region, talking about a "crash site." Ramsey says he pressed them on it and they told him, "Oh, it's an old wives tale. Who knows? UFO crashed out there. Late 40s, early 50s." He tells it as the first hint that led him toward a possible crash of an unknown craft in the area.
scout-craft-powering-up-and-accelerating: Between 1965 and 1967, in the Indian Springs Valley in Nevada, small scout craft would power up and shoot off at 8,000 to 12,000 miles per hour, according to a man named Charles Hall, who says he spent three years near tall white beings at a Nevada base. He tells Michels he watched this himself, but only from a distance, because "if you get too close the fields will burn you like a microwave".
scu-study-of-ufos-at-nuclear-sites-1940: UFOs were seen watching US nuclear sites, as far back as the 1940s, and a group called SCU, a coalition of scientists who study UFO reports, did a study on it. Kevin Knuth, a former NASA scientist, mentions the study in passing without going into its findings. If the pattern holds, it would suggest the objects take a particular interest in nuclear weapons.
scully-meets-a-scientist-in-the-mojave-1: Around 1949, a writer named Frank Scully is said to have met a scientist in the Mojave Desert who told him a remarkable story about the recovery of a crashed flying saucer. The men involved were named Silas Newton and Leo Gaybower, and Scully later wrote the story up in his book Behind the Flying Saucers. A researcher named Scott Ramsey tells it on the show as a summary, presenting it as one of the earliest accounts of a saucer being recovered.
scully-says-dr-g-is-no-longer-available-: In 1950, the writer Frank Scully was asked to bring forward a scientist he called Dr. G, and he answered, "Oh, that won't be possible... He's no longer available." A researcher named Scott Ramsey tells this as happening around a Chicago radio station, and links the story to a physicist named John Torrance Tate. Ramsey raises it because it suggests the scientist behind Scully's crashed-saucer claims was being kept out of sight.
sdi-as-a-back-door-to-fund-uap-programs-: The Strategic Defense Initiative, President Ronald Reagan's 1983 plan for a space-based missile shield, likely served as a back door to fund programs on UAP, the government's term for UFOs, and to "act offensively against UAP", according to a researcher who goes by the online name UAPGerb. He says it once as his own view and once as something unnamed sources told him during his projects. If so, a famous defence programme would have doubled as cover for secret work against unknown craft.
sdi-brilliant-pebbles-as-a-black-budget-: The Strategic Defense Initiative, the 1980s American plan for missile defense in space nicknamed Star Wars, and its Brilliant Pebbles part, were a front: an expensive project whose money mostly went into secret black-budget projects. That is what a UFO researcher named Steven Greer says, without naming a source. If true, a famous public defense program was used to hide money for secret work.
sea-supply-corporation-heroin-profits-fu: In the 1950s, a company called the Sea Supply Corporation, with offices in Havana and Miami, is said to have used profits from heroin to pay for weapons for the Kuomintang, the Chinese Nationalist party. A lawyer named Dan Sheehan tells this to Michels without naming a source, and he links it to an intelligence officer named Paul Helliwell, a mob boss named Santo Trafficante Jr., a businessman and diplomat named William D. Pawley, and a writer and diplomat named Clare Boothe Luce. If true, it would mean drug money was quietly funding a foreign war.
seal-beach-weapons-station-sightings-200: In March 2009, local media reported several UFO sightings near the Seal Beach Naval Weapons Station in Orange County, California, near a set of bunkers that the teller says held nuclear weapons. The researcher Robert Hastings, who studies UFO reports at nuclear sites, tells it from those news reports and from what local civilians said, as one more case of UFOs showing up where nuclear weapons are kept.
sealed-needle-in-tube-device-moves-3-4-f: A guest named Charles Buhler says that in 2016, in his lab, a device made of a needle sealed inside a tube rose three to four feet into the air when he turned up his power supply. He tells it first-hand on the show, mentioning a colleague named Andrew Arjima and videos posted on a website called Exodus, as evidence of a push that works without any fuel or moving parts.
sean-kirkpatrick-s-aaro-as-a-debunking-e: Michels suggests that the Pentagon's UFO investigation office of the 2020s, known as AARO, was probably a fake hit job on UFOs, an effort to explain them away. He points to its head, Sean Kirkpatrick, who he says has long ties to the Department of Energy, the US agency that runs the nation's nuclear weapons labs, and who worked at Oak Ridge, one of those government labs. Michels says this himself, without naming a source, as a reason to distrust the office's findings.
sean-kirkpatrick-s-background-at-brookha: Sean Kirkpatrick, who led the Pentagon's UFO investigation office, once worked at Brookhaven Lab in New York and at Oak Ridge National Laboratory in Tennessee, which Michels calls a "clear atomic site".
