Michels points this out himself on a 2024 episode with the researcher Robert Hastings about UFOs and nuclear bases. He raises it to suggest that the man in charge of the official inquiry had close ties to the nuclear world where many sightings are said to happen.
sean-ryan-threatened-after-the-herrera-i: After a man named Shawn Ryan, who runs his own interview show, had a guest named Michael Herrera on in 2023 to talk about UFOs, Ryan was threatened. That is the account of Steven Greer, a researcher who has long said the government hides what it knows about UFOs. He mentions it in passing, without naming a source, as an example of what happens to people who speak out.
search-for-a-metal-tablet-given-to-a-boy: In the north of Sweden, a man said that as a young boy he was given a metal tablet by aliens, and researchers went up there to look for it. The Swedish UFO researcher Clas Svahn tells this, passing on what the man told them, as one of the cases he has followed in person. If the tablet were found, it would be a physical object from an encounter.
search-for-the-missing-team-brought-in-s: In 1977, when a missile security team from Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota went missing in the missile field, the base did not only search for them itself: it asked for outside help, and two sheriff's deputies from the nearby town of Sturgis and one state trooper were sent out. A former Air Force security guard named Mario Woods, who was on that team, says he only learned this in 2021, from what others told him, naming a fellow team member, Steve Colbern, and a man called Kellogg. In a later retelling he credits a Meade County sheriff's dispatch log for it and names the town of Newell. He tells it because it suggests the team really was missing long enough for an official search.
search-of-marcus-vinicius-s-house-and-co: In 2018, the house of a man named Marcus Vinicius in Varginha, Brazil, was searched from top to bottom for his video tape, and his computer was taken to a warehouse in São Paulo. A surgeon named Italo Venturelli tells this as he heard it from a man named James Fox, who went there himself: "They searched his whole house." It is told because the tape was believed to hold something people wanted found or kept hidden.
searching-for-a-ufo-that-landed-and-sank: Somewhere in Norway, according to witnesses, a UFO landed and then sank into the water. Michels says he himself took part in a search for it, along with his guest, and mentions it briefly as one of the places they have looked for physical evidence.
second-alien-communicator-nicknamed-bone: Between 1990 and 1993 a former Air Force sergeant named Dan Sherman says he was trained by the National Security Agency, the US code-breaking agency, to receive messages from aliens by thought. He says there was a second alien he talked with, a different one from the first, nicknamed Bones, at a site he calls Base 2. He tells it as his own experience.
second-century-latin-inscribed-on-rocket: Old Latin, from the second century, is said to have been written on some space missions, on the rockets themselves. Jesse Michels repeats this twice as something said by Diana Pasulka, a professor who studies religion and UFO belief; once he places it on the rocket's fairing, the shell that covers the nose of the rocket. If true, it would hint at old religious or esoteric ideas tucked inside modern spaceflight.
second-craft-near-skinwalker-ranch-shoot: Near Skinwalker Ranch, a property in Utah known for reports of strange happenings, a craft is said to have shot straight into a mountain, as if the rock were a doorway. A man named Robert Bigelow describes it as the second such case, after another craft did the same thing. Michels relays Bigelow's account in an episode about a UFO book he says the Pentagon tried to censor.
second-face-found-in-utopia-1980: A second site with faces sits in Utopia, a region of Mars that was once on the shore of an ancient ocean, according to a scientist named John Brandenburg, who says he found it himself in the 1980s. He says there are two faces there, and one looks like the same face seen at Cydonia, another Martian region known for a face-like formation, but "inside a helmet." If true, it would point to someone having once built things on Mars.
second-giza-scan-paper-under-peer-review: Filippo Biondi, a scientist who used radar scans to look beneath the Khafre pyramid at Giza in Egypt, says in 2025 that his team is preparing a second paper on what they found. "In this moment we are working on a scientific paper," he says, describing it as under review by other scientists before publication.
second-marine-squadmate-reaches-out-via-: In 2024 a second man from Michael Herrera's old Marine unit reached out to him through LinkedIn, the professional networking site, according to Herrera, a former Marine who says he saw a 300-foot UFO in the Indonesian jungle. Herrera shares their messages, in which the squadmate writes: "Keep the faith. there is nothing, no borders lines that they won't cross." For Herrera, the contact supports his account and warns of how far those hiding it will go.
second-meeting-implants-not-ganglion-199: In 1996, at the Los Angeles offices of Dark Skies, a television series about UFOs, a second meeting with outside visitors turned on the idea of alien implants, something technological, rather than an earlier idea involving a ganglion, a cluster of nerve cells. A television writer named Bryce Zabel tells Michels this as someone who was in the room, naming the visitors only as JC and "the captain".
second-night-at-carman-ping-pong-ball-ob: In 1975, near Carman in Manitoba, Canada, a researcher named Grant Cameron says he watched an object on a second night of sightings that went "boom boom boom," jumping around the sky, and that people called it the ping pong ball. He says that as it flew away that night he decided to find out what was going on, a search that led him from the Canadian government to a man named Eric A. Walker, whom Cameron calls the head of the whole UFO programme. Cameron tells it more than once in the same interview, sometimes only as the moment the object flew away, as the start of his life's work.
second-regression-michael-lying-opposite: In 1977, aboard a craft near a South Dakota nuclear missile site called November 5, a guard named Mario Woods says he lay across from his fellow guard Michael Johnson with a small being standing between them. Woods says he learned this in his second session of regression, a kind of hypnosis meant to bring back lost memories, led by the hypnotherapist Yvonne Smith. It is part of his account of being taken by beings while guarding nuclear weapons.
second-silent-object-seen-by-three-witne: In 2016, a few weeks after a first strange object, a second object with a different shape was seen at Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property known for odd reports, and it made no sound at all. The ranch's owner tells this, saying the witnesses were three of his staff: his ranch security man and surveyor, and his caretakers at the time. He presents it as one of the events behind his belief that something unusual is at the ranch.
second-voice-download-you-have-everythin: A Hollywood writer named Brent Friedman says that the second time a message, which he calls a "download," came into his mind, it told him: "you have everything you need." Friedman tells it as something he experienced himself, one of a series of such messages.
secrecy-briefing-at-kilo-control-and-ost: In 1977, after an incident in the missile field at Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota, an airman named Mario Woods says he was sent to Kilo control, a launch control post there, and given "a real strict briefing" about secrecy by a Master Sergeant Gray, and was shunned afterward. Woods, an Air Force veteran who says he was abducted by aliens, tells Michels this from his own experience, also naming a Colonel Spraker.
secret-electrogravitic-propulsion-progra: The US is said to have run secret projects on electrogravitic propulsion, a way of moving craft by using electricity to work against gravity. Matthew Brown, a former Pentagon official turned whistleblower, names it in passing, "Electromagnetic. Electrogravitic," and ties it to Thomas Townsend Brown, an inventor who worked on the idea. If true, it would mean such hidden propulsion has been under study for years.
secret-kennedy-khrushchev-letters-on-des: In 1963 the American president John F. Kennedy is said to have started secretly exchanging letters with the Soviet leader Nikita Khrushchev about destroying their nuclear warheads, passing them through a go-between named Norman Cousins. A researcher named Dan Sheehan tells this without naming a source, in a conversation linking Kennedy to the UFO secret. If true, it would mean Kennedy was quietly working toward ending the nuclear arms race behind his own government's back.
secret-machines-adviser-genocides-may-be: In the non-fiction Secret Machines books, written by the researcher Peter Levenda and the musician Tom DeLonge, one of their advisers is said to have told them outright that "genocides may be a function of the phenomenon," meaning whatever is behind UFOs, and that "it may be trying to eliminate certain genetic strands for its own purposes." A researcher named Jason Simosa points this out on the show from his reading of the books. He names advisers called McCasland and General Hayden among the people involved, but does not say which one said it. If true, the phenomenon would be shaping human history through mass killing.
secret-pentagon-program-to-build-weapons: Inside a small Pentagon office that studied unexplained aerial reports, there was a deeper, "Above Top Secret" part whose real aim was to build an advanced weapon system from technology recovered from crashed UFOs. A researcher named Dan Sheehan says this, and says a former Pentagon official named Luis Elizondo was involved in that program, though Sheehan gives no source. If true, the US military would hold and be trying to copy craft not made by humans.
secret-radiation-testing-of-animals-afte: The Australian journalist Ross Coulthart says that early in his digging through the Australian government archives he found documents showing that animals were secretly tested for leftover radiation from the nuclear tests carried out in the Pacific in the 1950s and 60s. He tells it as one of his first finds showing the government doing things in secret.
secret-service-guarded-the-dying-von-neu: When the mathematician John von Neumann was dying in 1957, Secret Service agents (the federal agency that protects the president) were reportedly posted outside his room at a naval hospital because officials were afraid of what he might say. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, first in one episode and again more than a year later. The second time he hedges, saying he believes it was a Navy hospital in Maryland. A researcher named Deep Prasad tells it the same way, also without a source, though he does not say it was a naval hospital. The point of telling it is that von Neumann seemed to know secrets the government did not want him to let slip at the end.
secret-space-program-friend-s-father-s-s: In her book Encounters, Diana Pasulka, a scholar of religion who writes about UFO belief, interviews a friend who was said to be part of one of the secret American space programs, much like a man called Tyler in her earlier book American Cosmic. The story is about a joke the friend's father made about a "simulacrum," though Michels, who tells it himself from Pasulka's book, gives no more detail. He brings it up as a sign that people tied to hidden space programs talk to her openly.
secret-ufo-briefings-of-the-trump-camp-b: In 2024, before Donald Trump's team came into government, its people are said to have received several secret briefings about UFOs. A guest named Ross Coulthart says this, and points to Donald Trump Jr., the president's son, as someone who has been briefed by a number of people. If true, it would mean the incoming administration was told about UFOs before taking office.
secret-us-air-force-plane-landed-without: In 1996, a US Air Force plane is said to have landed in Varginha, a town in Brazil, on a secret mission, without the Brazilian government's permission. The documentary filmmaker James Fox relays this from someone who told him, in an episode about a Brazilian hospital said to have operated on an alien, as a sign that the US was quietly involved.
secret-us-fundamental-physics-research-a: Since the Second World War, the US government is said to have run secret research into the basic laws of physics. Matthew Pines, an analyst, says on the show that it is "very clear" to him the government has been doing this, without naming a source. James Valor, who works with a startup that tries to call UFOs into view, agrees with the thinker Eric Weinstein. He says the government probably has "top secret physics, knowledge and science" going back at least to the end of the war. Both give it as their view, not as something they saw. If true, it would mean there is a hidden science far ahead of what the public knows.
secretive-spy-vs-spy-meetings-with-gary-: Between 2021 and 2024 there were secretive, "spy vs. spy" style meetings involving a man named Garry Nolan and staff from the US Congress, with others named Alex and Jake Barber also in the picture. James Valor, of Skywatcher, a startup that says it tries to call up UFOs, tells Michels he took part and once met Nolan in a way that "honestly, he felt very inconvenient." The story matters because it suggests the people chasing this subject watch and test one another in private.
security-guard-george-frozen-and-later-h: In 2016 a security guard named George on Skinwalker Ranch, a property in Utah known for strange reports, is said to have frozen in place on a mesa and later ended up in a hospital in Las Vegas. Brandon Fugal, who runs the ranch and was there that night, says George told him that when the others jumped out of the truck he stood up, "was frozen, I couldn't move, and everything went black." Fugal tells it as one of the ranch's direct harms to people.
seeing-a-tag-along-object: An unnamed speaker in a clip played on the episode says they saw an object that they call a "tag along." They tell it as something they saw themselves, but the clip gives no place or date.
seeing-a-ufo-while-remote-viewing-mount-: An Army sergeant named Lyn Buchanan says he saw a UFO, not in a hangar but at Mount Zeal in Australia, while remote viewing, which is the practice of trying to perceive faraway places with the mind alone. He tells Michels this from his own sessions, and if true it would mean the method could pick up such craft out in the open.
seeing-tall-white-children-in-the-indian: In the mid-1960s, Charles Hall says, children of tall, pale aliens would come into his barracks at Indian Springs, Nevada, and he would get up and see them playing. Hall, who says he spent three years among these beings near Area 51, a secret US Air Force test site, tells it as his own experience, adding that at first he thought he must be short on vitamins.
selective-service-chief-russians-moving-: In 1968, the head of the Selective Service in New York, the office that ran the military draft, is said to have told Peter Levenda, an author and historian, that the Russians were sneaking spies into the United States through Orthodox churches. Levenda relays that warning, and in a second telling speaks as if from his own knowledge, naming the church at 97th Street and Fifth Avenue, which answered to Moscow, as "the one they were running agents through". If true, it means Soviet spies used a church as cover in Manhattan.
selectively-visible-lights-over-valley-o: A bright white light hovered over a valley 5 or 10 miles away while a scientist named Steve Colbern drove with his son on Highway 40 toward their old vacation place in Bullhead City, Arizona, in a remote area. Colbern, who studies objects said to be alien implants in human bodies, tells this as something he saw himself, and he also names someone called Garrett. The story's point is that the lights seemed visible only to some people, not to everyone.
self-designed-doctorate-in-parapsycholog: In the 1970s, a student named Jeffrey Mishlove designed his own doctoral program at the University of California, Berkeley, and seven years later earned a doctorate in parapsychology, the study of psychic abilities. Mishlove tells Michels this about himself, and it means a major university once granted a degree in the field.
semivan-and-kit-green-question-tom-delon: Around 2015, two intelligence insiders, a former CIA officer named Jim Semivan and a CIA scientist named Kit Green, are said to have sat the rock musician Tom DeLonge down in a hotel room and asked him where he was getting his information about UFOs. The researcher Grant Cameron tells this to Michels without naming a source. The point of the story is that people inside government wanted to know how an outsider had come by what he knew.
semivan-on-a-non-state-intelligence-netw: Emails leaked in 2016, during the presidential race between Hillary Clinton and Donald Trump, were leaked by an intelligence network that belongs to no government. That is what a retired intelligence officer named Jim Semivan says, according to the researcher Jason Simosa, who repeats it without naming a source. If true, it would mean a private spy network could steer events as big as an election.
senate-armed-services-staff-on-admiral-w: Staff on the Senate Armed Services Committee, the Senate committee that oversees the military, are said to have confirmed things about a Navy admiral named Thomas R. Wilson and his connection to UFO craft that were being reverse engineered, meaning taken apart to copy their technology. The UFO investigator James Fox says he talked to some of those staff members himself about Wilson and reverse-engineered UFOs. Michels tells it differently, passing on someone who says, "I talked to the people that subpoenaed him." In Michels's version Wilson was legally ordered, in the 2020s, to appear in a SCIF, a sealed room for classified conversations. If true, it would mean Congress has pressed a senior officer about hidden craft programmes.
senate-findings-that-uap-records-were-wr: Proposed US Senate legislation from 2023 on UAP, short for unidentified anomalous phenomena, the government's term for UFOs, is said to state that "credible evidence indicates that relevant UAP records have been inappropriately classified and withheld" from elected officials in both Congress and the executive branch. A researcher named Matthew Pines summarises these findings himself. If true, it would mean the Senate is on record saying UFO files were kept even from the people meant to oversee them.
senate-intelligence-scif-meeting-and-bla: After a classified meeting with the Senate Intelligence Committee, its main investigator is said to have been harassed by military helicopters flying over his home. Steven Greer, an activist for UFO disclosure, says he took part in the meeting. It was held in a secure room for classified briefings, around 2022, in a period when Senator Marco Rubio was involved with the committee. Greer says that within a day or two, the investigator had "two Blackhawks over his house, unmarked." Ross Coulthart, an Australian journalist, tells it differently, through Jake Barber, a man who has come forward with UFO claims. In Coulthart's version, the staffer asked Barber to help with security because "somebody from the Defense Department is ordering helicopters" over his home. He places it in 2024 or 2025 rather than 2022. If true, it would mean parts of the military were intimidating the people investigating them.
senate-language-on-historical-exotic-tec: Wording put out by the US Senate around 2023 says that, to avoid being surprised by foreign technology, the government 'must broaden awareness of historical exotic technology antecedents previously provided by the federal government for research and development purposes.' The analyst Matthew Pines quotes this language and ties it to talk that such material ended up with Lockheed, the big aerospace defense company, sometimes described as sitting in Lockheed's basement. Read his way, it would mean the government once handed unusual technology to private companies to study.
senate-staff-meet-mellon-puthoff-davis-t: In 2017 and 2018, a US Senate staff member named Kurt McConnell says, he and his colleagues met in Washington with a group of people tied to UFO research. He names Chris Mellon, Luis Elizondo, the physicists Harold Puthoff and Eric W. Davis, the people who had worked on Skinwalker Ranch (a property in Utah studied for strange events), Brandon Fugal, and the Navy pilots David Fravor and Alex Dietrich, who reported the Tic Tac, a white oval object shaped like the mint. McConnell tells it first-hand, as the way the subject came to Congress's attention.
senate-to-pass-the-64-page-uap-disclosur: A lawyer named Dan Sheehan says that the US Senate is "going to pass the 64-page bill again," meaning the UAP Disclosure Act, a proposed law to force the release of government records on UAP, the government's term for UFOs. He talks about it in 2025 as someone involved in the push, and names Senators Mike Rounds and Chuck Schumer, Marco Rubio and the congressman Dan Crenshaw. If he is right, lawmakers would try a second time to make the government open its UFO files.
senator-claiborne-pell-part-of-the-cabal: Claiborne Pell, a United States senator, was secretly part of what the researcher Steven Greer calls a cabal: a hidden group that he says controls UFO secrets. Greer says he found this out only after Pell died, and he gives no source. If true, it would mean someone inside the Senate itself belonged to the group keeping the secret.
senator-cussed-out-by-curtis-lemay-over-: Senator Barry Goldwater said that he once asked General Curtis LeMay, a top Air Force commander, to let him see a secret room at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base in Ohio, and that LeMay cursed him out for asking. The story comes from a recording of Goldwater himself that Michels plays in many episodes: "I called Curtis LeMay and I said, General, I know we have a room at Wright-Patterson where you put all this secret stuff. Can I go in there?" Goldwater goes on: "I've never heard him get mad, but he got mad in hell at me," and LeMay told him never to ask that question again. Michels, in his own words, says the place was called the "Blue Room" and places it in the 1960s or 70s. In one episode the same account is credited to Harald Malmgren, a former presidential adviser, as his own experience. The story is told because it suggests even a senior senator was kept away from whatever the base was holding.
senator-gillibrand-s-uap-legislation-gil: Between 2020 and 2023, Senator Kirsten Gillibrand of New York worked with Senator Marco Rubio on some of the first changes to US law dealing with UAP, the government's term for UFOs. Those changes are known as the Gillibrand-Rubio amendments. A guest named Matthew Pines points out that Gillibrand is also one of the main senators behind laws friendly to cryptocurrency, through a bill she wrote with Senator Lummis. He treats the overlap as a telling coincidence.
senator-inouye-on-a-shadow-government-du: During the 1980s Senate hearings into secret US arms deals known as Iran-Contra, US senator Daniel Inouye is said to have warned that there exists a shadow or secret government sitting above the US government. A UFO researcher named Steven Greer repeats this warning, without pointing to a record of it. He uses it to suggest that real power lies outside elected officials.
senator-reid-they-re-shutting-down-our-n: Around 2019, Harry Reid, the former Senate leader, is said to have answered at once, when asked what worried him most about UFOs, that "they're shutting down our nukes". James Fox, a filmmaker who investigates UFOs, says he asked Reid the question himself and Reid replied without a pause. Fox links it to the work of the researcher Robert Hastings, who collected reports of UFOs disabling nuclear missiles.
senator-ted-stevens-foo-fighter-encounte: Ted Stevens, a Second World War pilot who later became a senator from Alaska, is said to have had wartime encounters with foo fighters, the strange glowing objects that Allied aircrews reported following their planes over Europe. Luis Elizondo, who once ran AATIP, a small Pentagon office that studied unexplained aerial reports, calls Stevens one of the founders of his programme and says Stevens "himself admitted he had encounters with Foo Fighters during the war." A researcher named Marik von Rennenkampff speaks of a single foo fighter sighting. He ties it to Stevens later sponsoring UFO research with Senator Harry Reid through OSAP, the Pentagon study that came before AATIP. Michels says Stevens saw a UFO, "I think, in World War II," which would mean one of the men who started the government's UFO study had a reason of his own to care.
senior-ge-scalar-physicist-at-greer-s-20: A senior physicist from General Electric, the big American industrial company, spoke at a 2023 conference held just before a news event at the National Press Club in Washington DC, a well-known hall for press events, according to a UFO researcher named Steven Greer, who organised both. Greer says the physicist worked on what he calls scalar physics. He mentions that a man named Michael Herrera spoke at the Press Club event, and he brings the scientist up as an insider backing his claims.
senior-intelligence-official-and-his-wif: A very senior American intelligence official and his wife are said to have been taken by non-human beings. Jesse Michels says he knows, as an anecdote, of "one extremely senior intelligence official who had a pretty gnarly abduction experience along with his wife," without naming him. The author Peter Levenda names the man as Jim Semivan, a former CIA officer, and says Semivan talks openly about a kind of abduction experience. Bob McGwier, a former government contractor, also names Semivan, and describes beings that appeared in his room at home with his wife present, experiences he calls not pleasant rather than an abduction. If true, it would mean such encounters reach people deep inside the intelligence world.
senior-navy-sources-say-the-greys-geneti: The greys, small grey-skinned beings described in many alien abduction stories, are said to have been collecting human genetic material, and that collection may now have ended. Michels says he heard this from some senior, impressive people in the Navy, whom he does not name. He mentions it as a hint that abductions may have stopped.
senior-nsa-official-blocks-a-finding-fro: In the 2000s, a senior official at the NSA, the US agency that intercepts communications, stopped a team from telling President Bush about something they had discovered, saying "Nope, I'm not going to let you do that." Eric Haseltine, a former NSA official, tells Michels this from his own time there, as an example of how findings can be kept from reaching the very top.
senior-vp-material-scientist-no-physicis: Sometime in the 2010s, a senior vice president at an old, established aerospace company, a materials scientist, said his company's work on recovered crashed craft had never had a single physicist on it. Eric W. Davis, a scientist who has worked for the Pentagon, tells Michels he asked the man where his physicists were and was told: "we don't have any. We never did," because the company was only allowed to keep about a handful of people on the work. Davis also says from his own contact that he knew of five such people at that company, met two of them, and saw one routinely through a Pentagon study he calls OSAP; one, a woman, was a mathematician working as chief of security. If true, it would mean the craft were handled by a tiny team with no one trained to understand how they work.
sensory-deprivation-training-as-sac-s-ba: The writer on occult history Peter Levenda argues that sensory deprivation training, where people are cut off from sight, sound and touch, gave Strategic Air Command a back door into studying the paranormal between the 1950s and the 1970s. Strategic Air Command was the US Air Force branch that ran the nuclear bombers. Levenda gives this as his own reading, without naming a source, and calls it the "back door at SAC" for looking into "paranormal phenomena and occultism".
sent-to-sri-to-assess-the-gondola-wish-p: In 1978 Joe McMoneagle, an Army intelligence soldier, says he was sent to the Stanford Research Institute, a research lab in California, to judge an Army project called Gondola Wish, which was testing whether people could spy using the mind alone, and then was put on the project himself. He says a general he calls General Roya had learned the project was starting at Fort Meade, an Army base in Maryland, and was nervous about it. McMoneagle tells it as how he became one of the Army's psychic spies.
sentinels-of-ether-reverse-engineered-cr: Craft rebuilt from recovered unknown vehicles can only be flown, Michels says, if "psionic assets", people with psychic abilities, lock in on them from the ground. He says this himself, crediting a work called Sentinels of Ether and citing a man named Jake Barber, in an episode with a guest who says he was taken into the UFO programme as a child. If true, mind and machine would have to work together for these craft to fly.
september-1993-meeting-with-wright-patte: In September 1993, a UFO researcher named Steven Greer says, he met at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base in Ohio with the colonel in charge of operations for an Air Force intelligence center there that studies foreign aircraft and technology. Greer tells it as a meeting he was at himself, recalling something that "Colonel Canola" said to him, and he also names an "Admiral Kramer" in connection with it. Greer gives no more detail of what was said, but tells the story as evidence that senior officers were involved in the subject.
serapeum-granite-boxes-found-blown-apart: The Serapeum, an underground tomb complex at Saqqara in Egypt full of huge granite boxes, is said to hold many boxes that were found "blown up," as if "a lot of energy had surged through" them. The researcher Matt LaCroix tells this without naming a source. He suggests it points to some powerful force or lost technology in the ancient past.
sergeant-larson-s-onion-speech-on-secrec: A former sergeant named Dan Sherman, who says a US intelligence agency trained him to receive messages from aliens, says that in the early 1990s at an overseas base, a Sergeant Larson gave his group "the onion thing," a talk on secrecy as layer upon layer, during their "black introduction," the briefing that brought them into a secret program. Sherman tells it first-hand on the show and in his book Above Black, as part of how he was told the program was hidden.
serpo-alien-language-decoded-from-a-live: An alien language is said to have been decoded over one to three decades by scientists working with a live EBE, short for extraterrestrial biological entity, meaning a living alien, recovered from the crash near Roswell, New Mexico, in 1947. The account comes from Project Serpo, a story about a secret exchange with aliens, and the researcher Deep Prasad summarises it without naming a further source. If true, it would mean the government had a working alien language from a living survivor.
sethite-theory-adopted-by-jews-and-by-th: An old reading of Genesis 6, the Bible passage where the "sons of God" have children with human women, says those sons of God were simply noble men from the family line of Seth, a son of Adam. Tim Alberino, a guest who researches the giants of ancient lore, says this reading was taken up by Jewish teachers and then by the Christian church through Augustine, the early church thinker. He tells it in his own summary to show how the passage came to be read as being about ordinary humans.
seven-government-attempts-to-seize-the-b: In the 2020s, Peruvian authorities came seven times, with police and a prosecutor, trying to take away the strange three-fingered bodies kept at the University of Ica in Peru, according to a man named Martin Alacrone, who says he saw this. He tells Michels the story, also naming a Roger Zuniga, and it would mean the government wanted the bodies out of the researchers' hands.
several-such-sites-around-the-world: There are said to be several sites like this one around the world, including in Southeast Asia and Mexico. A guest named Michael Herrera, who says he saw a 300-foot UFO in the Indonesian jungle, repeats this on the show and credits it to a man named Jake Barber.
shaft-and-chamber-system-found-under-the: Early excavators of the Great Pyramid at Giza in Egypt found a pit in the Queen's Chamber, one of the pyramid's inner rooms, filled with rubble and dirt, and below it a system of shafts and chambers that was later sealed. That is the account of a researcher named Jeffrey Drum, who points to the original excavation reports from the 1800s and early 1900s, though in one telling he gives no date and does not say the pit was sealed. He tells it as evidence that something lies hidden beneath the chamber.
shafts-below-the-sphinx-admitted-by-zahi: There are said to be shafts and chambers beneath the Sphinx in Giza, Egypt, and even Zahi Hawass, whom Jesse Michels calls Egypt's Minister of Culture and a well-known skeptic, is said to have admitted it. Michels tells this several times: once he says Hawass acknowledged three separate tunnels linked to the Sphinx, and another time he says Hawass debated those who claimed such chambers and tried to suppress the information, yet admitted some exist and even went down into some himself. A researcher named Matt LaCroix tells it differently, crediting a survey by Robert Schoch that found hollow spaces and saying there are four entrances under the Sphinx, one beneath its left paw. If true, it would mean there is more hidden under the monument than is officially described.
shah-bought-laser-isotope-enrichment-tec: In 1970 the Shah, who then ruled Iran, bought technology from Switzerland that uses lasers to enrich nuclear fuel by separating out different forms of uranium. The researcher Jason Jorjani tells this without naming a source and calls it amazing, because it would mean Iran got hold of very advanced nuclear methods that early.
shallow-lunar-craters-with-a-hard-convex: The craters on the Moon are all only a few miles deep, and none is ever more than five or six miles deep, as if something hard below the surface stopped them. A philosopher named Jason Jorjani makes this point himself, without naming a source. He raises it because it would hint that the Moon has a hard shell under its surface.
shamans-accounts-of-little-men-out-of-a-: Shamans in places like the Pacific and Siberia have long described "little men who came out of a big light", according to the computer scientist and UFO researcher Jacques Vallée. He recalls a shaman telling him this fifty years ago, and ties it to his book Passport to Magonia, which compares modern UFO stories with old folklore. The point is that today's encounters may echo far older ones.
shane-freaks-shown-a-sphere: An old military veteran named Shane Freaks says he was shown a sphere, the kind of round unexplained object often reported in UFO cases. Michels passes this on from what Freaks said in a discussion on the social media site Twitter. If true, it would mean such objects are being shown to people inside the military.
shard-thousands-of-feet-tall-beside-a-ma: A giant shard of rock or structure, thousands of feet tall, is said to stand beside an impact crater on Mars. Joe McMoneagle, a remote viewer who tries to describe distant places by mind alone, says he saw it in photo negatives from the mapping of Mars by NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory. "That's not a pyramid, that's a shard," he says, as part of his case that Mars once had life.
sheehan-as-counsel-to-disclosure-project: A lawyer named Dan Sheehan says that for twenty years he was the legal counsel for the Disclosure Project, a group that gathered witnesses to push the US government to release what it knows about UFOs, and that he also represented the psychiatrist John Mack and attended what he calls "the peer group." Sheehan says this himself on Michels's show, as someone who took part, and he raises it to say that Luis Elizondo, a former Pentagon official involved in UFO matters, knew perfectly well who Sheehan was and what he had done.
sheehan-gets-access-to-every-internal-sc: In the 1970s the lawyer Dan Sheehan says he refused to meet L. Ron Hubbard, the founder of the Church of Scientology, unless he was first given access to "every single document anywhere in the world" in the church's internal files. Sheehan tells it himself, saying this included the files of the Guardian's Office, the church's internal security and legal arm, and he names Hubbard's wife Mary Sue Hubbard in the account. It would mean an outsider saw the church's most private records.
sheehan-gets-an-injunction-against-the-s: Sometime in the 1970s, a lawyer named Dan Sheehan says, he stopped a grand jury's subpoenas against the Church of Scientology. A grand jury is a panel that weighs criminal charges, and a subpoena is an order to hand over evidence or testify. Sheehan tells Michels he did it himself: he went up to New York, where he was allowed to practise in the federal court for the Southern District, and "got an injunction shutting them down," an injunction being a court order to stop. If true, it shows how much one lawyer could do against a federal investigation.
sheehan-represented-john-mack-and-vetted: A lawyer named Dan Sheehan says he was the legal representative for the Harvard psychiatrist John Mack for about ten years, starting around 1990. Mack worked with "experiencers," people who say they have had contact with alien beings. Sheehan tells Michels that during those years he met dozens of the people Mack had worked with, which means he saw the people behind Mack's cases for himself.
sheehan-s-account-of-james-mccord-and-th: In 1972 burglars broke into the Democratic Party's national offices at the Watergate building in Washington, and the lawyer Dan Sheehan says they were there to bug Larry O'Brien, the party chairman, because O'Brien had earlier been the main Washington lobbyist for the billionaire Howard Hughes. According to Sheehan, President Richard Nixon was terrified of this and wanted to learn whether O'Brien knew about a secret Hughes operation and might use it, so he ordered the phone tapped and the office bugged. Sheehan tells this on two episodes without naming a source, and Michels repeats it twice, adding that the burglar James McCord, a former CIA security man, "wasn't clued in" on why, and once describing O'Brien as running George McGovern's campaign.
sheehan-visits-ingo-swann-at-his-new-yor: Sometime in the 1970s, a man named Ingo Swann took his visitor all the way upstairs and out onto the roof of his New York apartment building. The visitor was Dan Sheehan, a guest on an episode about UFOs and President John F. Kennedy, and he tells it as his own memory: "I went to see him at his apartment in New York and we go all the way upstairs up onto the roof." He does not say in these words what happened up there.
sheffield-edwards-gives-the-green-light-: In 1960, at a meeting at the Fontainebleau Hotel in Miami, a man going by the code name "Mr. Ed" is said to have arrived and given the go-ahead, and he was Sheffield Edwards. The lawyer Dan Sheehan tells it second-hand, naming as the others involved Bob Maheu and the crime figures Santo Trafficante Jr., Johnny Roselli and Sam Giancana. He tells it as part of a wider story about secret government dealings tied to President Kennedy's killing.
sheldrake-s-crystals-growing-faster-afte: Crystals are said to form more easily each time they are made: a new chemical compound may be hard to crystallize at first, but the more often it is done, the easier it gets, anywhere in the world. The biologist Rupert Sheldrake gives this himself on an earlier episode as part of his idea that nature builds habits, while Michels later puts it more loosely, as a crystal lattice in a petri dish that grows slowly the first time and much faster after. If true, it would mean nature has a kind of memory.
sheldrake-s-paper-is-the-sun-conscious: A scientist named Rupert Sheldrake wrote a paper called "Is the Sun Conscious?", which asks whether the sun and the stars might have minds of their own. He says it was published in the Journal of Consciousness Studies, an academic journal, and that the paper is fairly recent even though he has been interested in the idea for a long time. A researcher named James Madden also brings it up, calling it "this really interesting paper".
sheldrake-s-plant-research-at-an-agricul: Before his better-known work, the scientist Rupert Sheldrake spent years in India at a farming research institute, breeding better chickpeas and pigeon peas. Sheldrake tells this about himself to Jesse Michels as part of his own life story, which shows him grounded in practical plant science.
sheldrake-s-ted-talk-censored-and-taken-: Jesse Michels says that in 2013 a TED Talk, one of the popular short lectures from the TED conference, given by the biologist Rupert Sheldrake was censored and taken off YouTube. Michels states this himself, without naming a source, while introducing Sheldrake as a scientist pushed aside for ideas outside the mainstream.
sherman-accounts-of-orbs-and-giant-wolf-: In the 1990s, the Shermans, a family who lived on Skinwalker Ranch in Utah, a property known for reports of strange happenings, are said to have seen glowing orbs of light moving toward an area called Dry Gulch Creek. They also told of giant wolf-like creatures heading toward the same spot and then vanishing. The ranch's current owner, Brandon Fugal, passes on these stories from the family to show that one part of the ranch has long drawn strange things.
sherman-family-haunted-off-the-ranch-199: In the 1990s, a family named the Shermans took over Skinwalker Ranch, a property in Utah known for strange events, and were, as the story goes, haunted off the land. Michels tells this himself in an episode about his own visit to the ranch, saying the family met glowing orbs, UFOs and skinwalkers (shape-shifting creatures from Navajo lore), and were even rushed by an oversized wolf walking on two legs that they said survived a close-range shotgun blast. The story is told as the reason the ranch became famous.
sherman-on-affecting-the-sine-wave-at-wi: In the 1990s, at a complex of the National Security Agency in Maryland (the agency that runs US electronic spying), a man named Dan Sherman says he could change the movement of a sine wave, a smooth repeating line on a signal display, using only his mind. Sherman, who says he was taken into a secret UFO programme as a child, tells Michels this from his own experience: "I could definitely affect the motion and I could do it just at will." If true, it would mean a person's mind could act directly on a signal.
sherman-s-base-photo-identified-as-san-v: Michels says that he and his researcher took a photo of a base printed in Above Black, a book by a former sergeant named Dan Sherman, ran a reverse image search on it, which matches a picture against others online, and found it was San Vito dei Normanni in southern Italy. Michels tells it on the show as his own find, and Sherman, sitting with him, confirms it was one of the bases where he was stationed in the 1990s, which would place his story at a real site.
sherman-s-mother-abducted-and-fetus-gene: In 1963, while she was pregnant with him, Dan Sherman's mother was abducted again by aliens who carried out "genetic management" on the unborn baby, according to Sherman. Sherman, a former Air Force sergeant who says the National Security Agency hired him to communicate with aliens, says he was told this by a man he calls Captain White. If true, it would explain why he says he was chosen for that work.
sherman-s-sine-wave-tone-training-1990: In the early 1990s, a man named Dan Sherman, whom the episode calls a CIA scientist who contacted an alien council, was trained using a pure musical tone. He tells Michels about it first-hand: his trainer said, "I'm going to play a tone, and I want you to mentally hum that tone." Sherman tells it as the first step in learning to communicate with his mind alone.
shermans-direwolf-survives-a-12-gauge-sh: In the mid-1990s, the Sherman family, who then owned Skinwalker Ranch in Utah, a ranch known for strange reports, said a huge wolf-like animal attacked their prized cattle and survived being shot with a 12-gauge shotgun. Brandon Fugal, the ranch's current owner, repeats the story, citing a report in the Utah newspaper Deseret News by a reporter named Zack Van Eyk. If it happened, the animal was something no ordinary wolf could be.
shermer-s-1983-alien-abduction-experienc: Michael Shermer, a well-known skeptic and researcher, says he himself had what felt like an alien abduction in 1983. He says it happened while he was riding a lonely rural highway near Haigler, Nebraska, during the Race Across America, a nonstop cross-country bicycle race, and that he described it at the time in an interview for ABC's Wide World of Sports, a television sports show. He tells it as a first-hand example of how such an experience can feel real.
shirley-maclaine-s-going-within-meeting-: The actress Shirley MacLaine wrote a book called Going Within in which she describes being in a government office in Washington, DC, with Senator Claiborne Pell, the abduction researcher Budd Hopkins and a prince, Hans-Adam II. Michels tells this himself from his memory of the book, without quoting it. He brings it up because it would put a sitting senator, a royal and a UFO researcher together in one room in the capital.
shoemaker-levy-9-breaks-apart-and-strike: In 1994 a comet called Shoemaker-Levy 9 broke into pieces and slammed into the planet Jupiter. The researcher Randall Carlson, who studies ancient catastrophes, tells it without naming a source. He says 21 pieces struck Jupiter in what he thinks was the second week of July 1994. Michels mentions it himself in an episode with Graham Hancock, saying only that it collided with Jupiter in 1994. It comes up as proof, in our own time, that big objects from space really do hit planets.
short-strange-looking-police-officer-esc: In 1977, on restricted government land in Nevada, a short police officer with a puffy face and a hat like the one worn by the cartoon character Deputy Dawg walked a man named Michael off the property. Michael, an Air Force veteran who says he was abducted, tells it as something he lived through. It belongs to his larger story of a trucker's UFO sighting and lost time on a drive from Texas to that Nevada land, and he tells it because the officer seemed strange to him.
shroud-of-turin-dating-tested-later-repa: The Shroud of Turin, a linen cloth kept in Italy that many believe wrapped the body of Jesus, is said to have been dated using pieces of later repair cloth, which were "much younger than the original." The researcher Randall Carlson tells this without naming a source, saying the cloth had several repair jobs over the centuries. If true, it would mean the test that made the shroud look young was measuring the patches, not the original.
shurmer-and-avi-loeb-s-alien-bet-with-th: The professional skeptic Michael Shermer says he and the Harvard-style researcher Avi Loeb, a scientist who argues for looking for alien technology, have made a $1,000 bet about aliens, set through a group called the Long Now Foundation and tied to the year 2030. Shermer tells this himself, as one of the two people who made the bet, though he gives few details of the terms beyond the stakes.
shuruppak-excavation-finds-a-flood-layer: When archaeologists dug at Shuruppak, an ancient city in what is now Iraq, they found a layer of flood mud about four feet thick lying right on top of it, as recorded in a 1931 excavation report from the Penn Museum, a university museum in Philadelphia. The researcher Matt LaCroix tells this, and in another moment calls Shuruppak one of the oldest cities on Earth, sealed and buried by the flood, without mentioning the report. He tells it as evidence that a great flood really did bury the earliest cities.
sidney-sheldon-s-novel-about-a-crashed-s: The bestselling novelist Sidney Sheldon is said to have known something about real UFOs but never dared to say so publicly, so he wrote a novel, which the teller calls The Doomsday Project, about a crashed saucer in Italy seen by the passengers of a tour bus. The lawyer Dan Sheehan tells this, passing on what he heard through the television producers Bill Todman Jr. and Bill Todman Sr., and calls the book "a hypothetical." If so, the novel would be a true story dressed up as fiction.
sighting-map-clusters-around-trinity-sit: When UFO sightings from the 1940s and 1950s are put on a map, they cluster around Trinity Site in New Mexico, where the first atomic bomb was tested, says the documentary filmmaker James Fox, who worked on this for his film The Phenomenon. Fox says "the proximity to Trinity site was unbelievable," and he credits the filmmaker Lance Mungia and the nuclear UFO researcher Robert Hastings in telling it. If true, it would suggest the phenomenon took a special interest in atomic weapons.
sightings-at-los-alamos-from-1948: Unexplained objects were being seen over Los Alamos, the New Mexico laboratory where the first atomic bombs were built, as early as about 1948. A researcher who goes by the online name RedPandaKoala says so, without naming a source, as part of a wider claim that UFOs show up around nuclear sites.
signals-beamed-into-benowitz-s-computer-: In the early 1980s in Albuquerque, New Mexico, signals are said to have been beamed into the computer of a man named Benowitz from across the street. A writer named Greg Bishop says it may have happened and that he heard it from a UFO researcher named Bill Moore. Bishop tells it in an episode about how supposed alien contact drove Benowitz to madness.
signed-copy-of-alien-conspiracy-2004: Jesse Michels says he got hold of a copy of a book called Alien Conspiracy and found, on its first page, a signature from a man named Chris Evans, dated December 1, 2004. Michels tells it himself, as something he found, and brings it up as a clue linking Evans to the story of crashed craft and bodies that his episode is about.
silas-newton-speech-beings-interested-in: In a speech given in 1950, a man named Silas Newton said that visiting beings were taking a close interest in America's nuclear work: "Unquestionably, they are interested in our atomic research." His words come up in an episode about a reported crash of a craft with alien bodies on board. If he was right, it would mean beings from elsewhere were watching the atomic programme.
silent-black-triangles-over-aboriginal-c: People in Aboriginal communities in the Australian Outback have described silent black triangles flying over their homes, according to the Australian journalist Ross Coulthart. He relays this from people who told him, as part of his search for hidden UFO activity.
silent-triangle-ufo-in-florida-2019: In 2019 in Florida, a silent triangle with lights on it passed overhead, according to the author Peter Levenda, whom the episode calls a CIA historian. Levenda says he saw it himself, along with a man he names only as Tom, and he recalls thinking, "I'm looking at a triangle with the lights."
silver-bridge-collapse-drowning-victims-: When the Silver Bridge at Point Pleasant collapsed in 1967, some people drowning in the river are said to have heard voices calling out numbers, like "number 3,486", and "wake up, wake up", and then came back to life. A philosopher named Jason Jorjani tells this, drawing on the writer John Keel, and places the bridge in Pennsylvania. He tells it as a sign of strange outside forces around the disaster.
silver-disc-above-the-mesa-darts-away-20: In 2016, Brandon Fugal, the owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property known for strange reports, says he saw a silver-gray disc hanging in the air about a hundred feet above a mesa on the ranch, and it then darted away. He tells it himself across two episodes, years apart. In the first he says the disc was 'just sitting there suspended in the air' right in front of them. In the later one he calls it a physical flying saucer seen in broad daylight, and he credits a man named Erik Bard, who was with him. He says it was his first sighting and turned him 'from being a skeptic to an experiencer within a matter of minutes.' Only Fugal tells it, as the man who saw it. If true, it would mean a solid craft showed itself openly over the ranch.
silver-sky-memo-given-to-moore-as-a-test: A UFO researcher named Bill Moore was handed a document called the Silver Sky memo, supposedly about a secret project named Silver Sky in New Mexico, but when he checked it out he found it was false, apparently given to him as a test. The writer Greg Bishop tells this, passing on what Moore told him: Moore 'went and checked it out and found out that was BS too'. It matters because it suggests people were feeding fake documents to UFO researchers to see what they would do with them.
silver-snake-comes-out-of-the-burnt-tree: A silver snake came out of a burnt tree in his backyard in North Carolina, says Chris Bledsoe, a man who says UFOs seem to be drawn to him. He tells it as something he saw himself: "all of a sudden, this snake comes out of the tree. This silver snake."
silver-surfer-video-bill-nye-s-brine-shr: In 2008, over Santa Monica, California, the filmmaker Jeremy Corbell says he saw something in the sky he could not identify, filmed it, posted the footage, and named it the Silver Surfer. Corbell tells this as the person who shot it, and the story as he tells it also involves the television science educator Bill Nye offering an explanation involving brine shrimp, and a later claim that it was a Red Bull skydiver, which Corbell treats as explanations to be knocked down.
similar-incursions-at-norfolk-naval-base: Unknown objects are said to have entered restricted airspace at Norfolk Naval Base in Virginia and over Washington, DC, much like the ones Navy pilots met off the East Coast. The former Navy fighter pilot Ryan Graves passes this on as something he was told. If true, it would mean these objects were showing up over a major Navy base and the capital itself.
similar-structures-under-menkaure-2-2-an: The hidden structures found under Khafre, one of the three great pyramids at Giza in Egypt, turn up under the smaller pyramid of Menkaure too, two pairs of them, and one more under the Sphinx. That is what the scientist Filippo Biondi says. He scanned the ground beneath the pyramids himself and tells Michels, about the 2025 work, "we found the same thing also in Menkaure and also under the Sphinx." If true, it would point to one planned network of buildings underground across the whole site.
simon-magus-levitating-and-peter-and-pau: In an old Christian legend, a magician named Simon Magus uses black magic to float in the air, and then meets the apostles Peter and Paul. Michels brings it up himself, calling it a biblical story, while talking with a guest about hidden forces in history. He tells it as an ancient account of a man defying gravity.
simone-s-belief-that-ai-is-the-current-r: A woman called Simone believes we are living, quite literally, in a time of revelation, and that what is being revealed is artificial intelligence. Diana Pasulka, a professor who studies religion and UFO belief, describes her this way and says she gives Simone a whole chapter in her book Encounters.
simons-engineered-stony-brook-joint-mana: The researcher Matthew Pines says that Stony Brook University teamed up with the Battelle Memorial Institute, a private research organisation, to run Brookhaven National Laboratory, a US government research lab on Long Island. He says the partnership was "personally engineered" by Jim Simons, the mathematician and hedge fund founder, and he names no source for it. He raises it to show how much quiet influence Simons had over American science.
simons-foundation-head-david-spergel-cha: In 2022 NASA, the US space agency, set up an independent panel to study UAP, or unidentified anomalous phenomena, the official term for UFOs. The man chosen to lead it was the scientist David Spergel, who also headed the Simons Foundation, the science charity of the billionaire Jim Simons. The analyst Matthew Pines lays this out in a 2024 episode: Spergel "was tapped to be the chair of the NASA UAP working group", and the same account appears again in a 2025 episode. Michels returns to it in at least four episodes. In one he puts it as a question, asking whether the panel's leader "might have any ties to Jim Simons", and he credits the researcher Eric Weinstein for drawing his attention to the link. In other episodes Michels adds that Simons founded Renaissance Technologies, an investment firm, and calls Spergel Simons' "principal scientific advisor". The tellers raise the point because, if the link matters, the panel may not have been as independent as it was presented. None of them goes further than pointing out the connection.
simons-if-you-knew-how-he-actually-made-: The investor Jim Simons once suggested that the way a famously successful money-maker really earned his fortune would be a letdown, according to the researcher Eric Weinstein, who says he was there. Weinstein tells Michels that Simons took a drag on his cigarette, paused for a long time, and said, "Eric, if you knew how he actually made money, you'd be so disappointed." Michels repeats the story in a later episode as something Weinstein told him, without the cigarette, and puts the line as "you'd be disappointed if you knew how we made our money." The two use it to suggest that well-known success stories may hide a less impressive or less visible source.
simosa-s-conversion-to-and-departure-fro: Growing up in England, Jason Simosa, a researcher, became a Christian at 19 "kind of out of nowhere," in his words, and later left the faith. He tells it about himself, as part of the personal path that led him to the subjects he now studies.
simpkinson-gemini-11-ufo-lithograph-like: A printed picture from Gemini 11, a NASA space flight of 1966, that shows a UFO over Earth was likely a mock-up, because the original photo shows no UFO at all. A scientist named Kevin Knuth says a researcher named Ed Wilson found that original in the University of Arizona archives, among the files of a man named Scott Simkinson: it "shows Earth with that cloud pattern in the background, and there's no UFO there." It is told to show how a famous space UFO image may have been made up.
simpkinson-s-nasa-files-auctioned-and-bo: The NASA files of a man named Scott Simkinson are said to have gone up for public auction after he and a woman named Emily Erdle had both died. A man named Ed Wilson bought them and found a lithograph, a kind of printed picture, among the papers. A guest named Kevin Knuth tells the story as a summary, as the way the picture came to light.
sir-peter-horsley-approached-by-nordics-: In the 1950s a British air force officer named Sir Peter Horsley is said to have been approached by two "Nordics", tall humanlike beings, called Miss Markham and Mr. Janus, who invited him to a fireside chat. The philosopher Jason Jorjani tells this from a book called Closer Encounters. He brings it up as an example of aliens quietly making contact with powerful people.
sirhan-sirhan-as-an-mk-ultra-subject-lin: Sirhan Sirhan, the man who shot Robert F. Kennedy in 1968, was himself a subject of MK Ultra, the CIA's secret mind-control program, Michels says, because he had spent time with a hypnotist named William Joseph Bryan; on the episode Michels calls him "William Jennings Brian". The story is tied to the Santa Anita racetrack in California. Michels tells it himself on a 2024 episode, and if true it would mean the killer had been shaped by the government's mind-control work.
sirhan-sirhan-s-diary-before-the-rfk-sho: Sirhan Sirhan, the man who shot the politician Robert F. Kennedy, known as RFK, in Los Angeles in 1968, is said to have written in his diary just before the shooting. Michels mentions the diary himself, in an episode about a CIA scientist said to have contacted an alien council, though in the words given he does not say what was written in it.
sirius-program: A former Pentagon official turned whistleblower named Matthew Brown mentions a program called Sirius in a post he wrote to the billionaire Elon Musk on the social network X. On the show he says only that "Sirius is a star," and gives no more about what the program is or does.
sister-maria-s-flame-in-the-convent-cell: A young nun named Sister Maria was sleeping in her small cell in a Catholic convent when she woke up to see a shining object, like a flame, come out of the wall and hover above her. Michels tells it in an episode about UFOs and religion and puts it in the late 1800s, while the story itself is dated 1807 to 1809. He tells it to show that encounters like this have long been part of religious experience.
site-in-texas-that-teaches-blindfolded-s: There is said to be a place in Texas that teaches people to develop senses beyond the usual ones, such as sensing things while blindfolded. Michels mentions this himself, unsure of the details ("I think a site in Texas"), in an episode with the biologist Rupert Sheldrake. He brings it up as a sign that such abilities might be trained.
sitting-beside-arthur-c-clarke-at-the-20: At the 1968 London premiere of 2001: A Space Odyssey, the science-fiction film directed by Stanley Kubrick, the writer Whitley Strieber ended up sitting next to Arthur C. Clarke, the author whose short story The Sentinel the film grew out of. Strieber tells it as something that happened to him, and he also mentions a man named Mike Smith.
six-fingered-diorite-hand-found-at-shuru: At Shuruppak, an ancient Sumerian city in what is now Iraq, digging in 1931 is said to have found a hand carved from diorite, one of the hardest stones on Earth, with six fingers. The researcher Matt LaCroix tells this, crediting the excavation report of the Penn Museum, the University of Pennsylvania's museum, which dug the site. If true, it would raise the question of why ancient carvers showed a six-fingered hand in such hard stone.
six-of-knapp-s-corroborating-witnesses-w: In Las Vegas in 1989, six people who could back up the story of Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft for the government, are said to have each got a phone call threatening them, and none of them ever went public. A researcher named Luigi Vendittelli says the Las Vegas television journalist George Knapp told him this. If true, it would mean someone worked to keep support for Lazar's claims from coming out.
six-tons-of-missing-fissionable-material: After the 1986 disaster at Chernobyl, a nuclear power plant in the Soviet Union, six tons of fissionable material, the kind of nuclear fuel that can sustain a chain reaction, went missing from the plant. A former Army sergeant named Lyn Buchanan tells this to Jesse Michels and stresses that the material was stored at the plant, not inside the reactors. If true, it would mean a large amount of nuclear material was unaccounted for.
size-of-the-pyramid-at-el-mirador-2024: The pyramid at El Mirador, an ancient ruined site in the jungle of Guatemala, is so big that you can walk on it for minutes without knowing, says a researcher named Luke Caverns. He went there in 2024 and tells Michels he realised that "for the last 5 minutes I was walking on the pyramid straight." He tells it to show how huge and overgrown these old buildings are.
skeptic-carl-pflock-s-only-visit-to-the-: Only one skeptic has ever visited Hart Canyon near Aztec, New Mexico, where, as the episode tells it, a craft carrying sixteen alien bodies came down. That skeptic was the writer Carl Pflock, and he came only because Scott Ramsey drove him there. Ramsey tells Michels first-hand that he walked Pflock around the site, even though Pflock lived only two hours away, and he uses this to say that doubters rarely take the trouble to look.
skeptical-cinematographer-michael-convin: In 2023 in Glendale, California, a cinematographer named Michael watched tests of Mia, a child said to be able to read minds, and says they convinced him. The tests were filmed for The Telepathy Tapes, a documentary by the filmmaker Ky Dickens about children who are said to share thoughts without speaking. Michael, who says he was there, explains that he is "generally a skeptic in my life for most things," but after seeing this, "it's hard for me to not believe this stuff."
skeptical-finnish-rov-team-calls-it-man-: In 2019, a doubtful Finnish team sent a remote-controlled underwater robot down to a strange object found on the floor of the Baltic Sea. According to the treasure hunter Dennis Asberg, who found the object, their operator said, "This must be man-made. This is constructed," and likened it to a power line. Asberg tells the story to show that even doubters saw it as something built rather than natural rock.
skiers-in-antarctica-evacuated-by-black-: Michels says that skiers who were supposedly exploring Antarctica just for sport have had black helicopters come down on them. He tells this himself, without naming a source or saying when it happened. The point, if true, is that someone is guarding parts of the frozen continent from visitors.
skinny-bob-video-dismissed-as-cgi-2020: The hip hop artist Flying Lotus says the Skinny Bob video, a clip passed around in online UFO circles on Twitter, now called X, is "clearly CGI," meaning made with computer graphics. He gives this as his own judgment from watching it, setting it aside as something not to take seriously.
skinwalker-ranch-camera-dismantled-betwe: At Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property known for reports of strange happenings, a camera on a pole was taken apart between one frame and the next: in that short gap, someone cut its wires and pulled all the duct tape off the pole. The philosopher Jason Jorjani tells this without naming a source and links it to John B. Alexander, a retired Army officer who looked into the ranch. He tells it as a sign that something there acts faster than any person could.
skinwalker-ranch-cattle-mutilations-and-: Skinwalker Ranch, a property in Utah, is said to be a place where the family who once lived there saw many mutilated cattle and all kinds of other strange events. Then Robert Bigelow, a businessman deeply interested in UFOs, bought it in the 1990s, and Michels says it became a site for experiments where odd electromagnetic effects show up on the ground. Michels tells this himself on a 2022 episode where the mathematician Eric Weinstein debates the physicist Hal Puthoff.
skinwalker-ranch-freaky-stories: Skinwalker Ranch, a property in Utah, is a very freaky place, and a lot of freaky stories come out of it. That is how the journalist Michael Shellenberger describes it in passing, without telling any one story.
skinwalkers-at-the-pentagon-on-aatip-and: The book Skinwalkers at the Pentagon describes AATIP, a small Pentagon office that studied unexplained aerial reports and dates to around 2007, along with a second program alongside it. Michels says he was just reading the book and that it looks like remote viewing, the claimed ability to sense distant places with the mind alone, was "sort of again revived" by these programs. If so, it would mean the Pentagon's UFO work also took mind-based methods seriously.
skip-atwater-s-contact-in-australia-sees: A man working in Australia near Mount Zeil, a mountain in the centre of the country, is said to have called it the most boring job he ever had, if it weren't for all the UFOs going in and out of the mountain. The former Army sergeant Lyn Buchanan tells this second-hand, as something passed on by his associate Skip Atwater about a contact of his, suggesting the mountain may hold some kind of base.
skorzeny-shown-a-demonstration-of-the-be: In 1944 Otto Skorzeny, whom the researcher Jason Jorjani calls Nazi Germany's master of psychological warfare and special operations, went to the Skoda Works, an arms factory, and was supposedly given a demonstration of the Bell, a secret craft the Nazis are said to have been building. Jorjani tells this without naming a source. If true, it would put a top Nazi commander in front of a working version of the craft.
skunk-works-advisors-to-secret-machines-: Several senior figures from Skunk Works, the secret aircraft design division of the company Lockheed, named Robert Weiss, Steve Justice and Eric Schrock, along with Neil McCasland, a commander of the Air Force Research Laboratory, all advised a 2016 project called Secret Machines. Michels says so himself in an episode on NASA and UFOs. Secret Machines was a project of the musician Tom DeLonge and the writer Peter Levenda, so this would tie top military aerospace people to a popular UFO project.
sky-elements-drones-fall-from-the-sky-ov: Between 2023 and 2025, a fleet of drones flown by a drone outfit called Sky Elements began acting strangely over a part of Skinwalker Ranch known as the East Field, or the triangle, and then dropped "like bricks from the sky". The story comes from Brandon Fugal, the owner of the ranch, who says he was there for it. To him it suggests that something on the property interferes with machines.
sky-ship-with-glowing-sails-snags-a-lond: In the early 1800s a sailing ship with glowing sails is said to have flown over London, dropped an anchor, snagged a chimney and broken its top off. Chris Bledsoe, a man who says UFOs appear around him, tells this as a story he once read, without naming where. If true, it would be a very old report of a craft in the sky that touched something on the ground.
sky-watcher-operators-differ-from-legacy: The team at Sky Watcher, a group run by a man named Jake Barber, does not do what the older secret government UFO programs do; its operators work in a completely different way. Michael Herrera, who says he saw a huge craft in the Indonesian jungle, passes this on from what Barber has told him. It matters because it sets Barber's team apart from the hidden programs it might otherwise be compared to.
skywatcher-s-government-funded-uap-obser: From about 2020 to 2025, a speaker from Skywatcher, a startup that says it can call UFOs to appear, says the company ran sky-watching events paid for by the government. The events were meant to see UAP, the official term for unidentified objects in the sky. In a garbled passage the speaker tells Michels that for about four and a half years there was "no psionics," meaning no attempt to use the mind to draw the objects in, and mentions "eight classes" of something linked to it. The point seems to be that the sightings did not depend on mental methods.
skywatcher-s-jordan-psionic-mind-meld-wi: A witness named Jordan Jose, who is tied to a UFO-hunting effort called Skywatcher, is said to describe flying these craft by the mind alone: a mind meld with a craft that is itself conscious, with control modules that a person in effect takes over. A guest named Matthew Pines passes this on as what Jose has said explicitly, in an episode about psionics, the idea of using the mind to act on things. If true, it would mean the craft are steered by thought rather than by hands on controls.
skywatcher-s-mechanical-and-human-dog-wh: Jesse Michels describes a method used by Skywatcher, a private group trying to draw out UFOs, as pairing a "mechanical dog whistle", a device meant to call the craft, with a "human dog whistle", a person meant to call them with the mind. He tells it himself, crediting the idea to Jake Barber, a former military helicopter pilot linked to the group; if true, it would mean UFOs can be summoned on purpose.
skywatcher-sees-orange-orbs-over-picatin: In 2024, while people across New Jersey were reporting strange drones in the night sky, orange balls of light appeared over Picatinny Arsenal, a military base in the state. Jake Barber, a helicopter pilot who says he once carried a UFO with his helicopter, tells Michels that he and his team arrived on their first night and within 30 minutes saw "all these orange orbs come into existence right over" the base.
skywatcher-sessions-psionic-calls-brough: In 2024 and 2025, field sessions run by Skywatcher, a group that tries to call in unidentified flying objects, got friendly objects when they reached out with the mind alone and aggressive ones when they used a mechanical device they called a dog whistle. Jordan Jose, who says he was taken into a UFO program as a child, says he took part, and that "every time we did elicit a response," the mind-only calls brought a phenomenon that was "highly benign." If true, it would mean the way you call these things changes how they behave.
slime-mold-out-designs-the-japanese-subw: Slime mold, a simple living thing with no brain, can work out a more efficient route than Japan's real subway system if you lay out food in the shape of that network. That is how Tero Isokauppila, a guest who talks about mushrooms and fungi, tells it to Jesse Michels, passing it on as something he was told rather than something he did. If it holds, it suggests that even very simple life can solve hard design problems.
slow-acceptance-of-gobekli-tepe-1960: Göbekli Tepe, an ancient site of carved stone pillars in Turkey, is said to have taken mainstream archaeology 15 years to accept after the archaeologist Klaus Schmidt began digging it in 1994. Michels says this himself, without naming a source, in an episode about strange three-fingered bodies found in Peru. He uses it to suggest that experts can be slow to accept findings that upset their picture of the past.
small-ancient-cities-in-the-united-state: There are small ancient cities in the United States that have never been discovered, in places such as Florida, Georgia, South Carolina, Alabama and West Texas, according to a researcher named Luke Caverns. He tells this from his own exploring and points to the archaeologist Ed Barnhart, and if true it would mean the country's deep past is far larger than anyone has mapped.
small-grays-and-a-tall-gray-during-mario: Mario Woods, a former guard at a nuclear missile base, says he was taken aboard a craft in South Dakota and saw beings there. He says they looked like "the small Grays," the gray-skinned, big-eyed beings of many abduction stories, with a taller gray one standing behind them, like the figure on the cover of Communion, the writer Whitley Strieber's book about his own encounters. Woods tells it in two episodes, and the dates differ: one telling places it in the 1960s, the other in 1977, around November 5.
small-helicopter-circles-the-crash-site-: In 1948, in Hart Canyon near Aztec, New Mexico, where a disc is said to have crashed, a very small helicopter is said to have suddenly appeared, circled the crash site, and then flown off to the northeast. Scott Ramsey, who has spent years gathering accounts of the Aztec crash, tells it second-hand: he says a man named Ken Farley was the first to tell him about the helicopter, and he also names a man named Doug Noland among his sources. If true, it would mean someone with an aircraft reached the site quickly, as though they already knew about the crash.
smith-propulsion-paper-sent-to-vannevar-: In the 1950s a Canadian named Wilbert B. Smith wrote a paper on how unknown craft might be propelled, and it was passed to Vannevar Bush, a top American government science adviser, for his view. The UFO researcher Grant Cameron says this comes from Smith's personal files, where Smith writes, in Cameron's words, that the UFO writer Donald Keyhoe "took the document on the propulsion to Vannevar Bush and we're waiting for his opinion." If true, it would show such ideas reaching the very top of American science at the time.
smith-s-memo-to-the-psb-on-1-500-ufo-rep: In 1952 an official named Walter B. Smith sent a CIA memo to the head of the Psychological Strategy Board, a Washington body that worked on psychological strategy, noting that more than 1,500 UFO reports had been logged. Michels cites the memo himself, as one of several documents showing how seriously the government was taking the sightings.
smithsonian-digs-up-giant-bones-in-ameri: The researcher Tim Alberino says that the Smithsonian Institution, the US national museum and research body, dug up the bones of giants in the mountains of America. In the same conversation he points to the Smithsonian's own annual reports, saying they record very unusual skeletal remains, many of them very large, though there he does not say they came from mountains. If true, it would mean a respected public institution once found and wrote down evidence of giant humans.
smoke-but-no-flame-at-darpa-and-afrl-wri: A scientist named John Blitch says that in his years at DARPA, the Pentagon's agency for advanced research, and at the Air Force Research Laboratory at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base in Ohio, he found lots of hints about UFOs but no hard proof. He served three years at Wright-Patterson and tells Michels there was "a lot of smoke but no flame that I personally observed." Coming from an insider who also says a being abducted him, it means the rumours reached those places but he never saw what was behind them.
smyslov-s-alien-chess-vision-before-the-: The chess grandmaster Vasily Smyslov is said to have seen an alien appear before him in a German hotel room in the 1970s, while he was preparing for a match against the player Robert Hübner. Kiran Ilum Xenov, a former president of one of Russia's republics, tells the story in a December 2025 episode. He passes on what he heard about Smyslov and his wife, Nadezhda Smyslova, and points to Smyslov's own records of the game. According to Xenov, Smyslov was working out his moves when "an alien appeared right before him." If true, it would mean an outside intelligence stepped into a top-level chess game. Michels retells the story in a January 2026 episode with a surgeon, crediting Xenov but not naming the player. In his version, one of the greatest chess players was playing through a simulation before a big tournament, "the moves made themselves", and the player put this down to some kind of alien help. So the two tellings differ: Xenov has an alien appearing, and Michels has the moves playing on their own.
snow-would-not-settle-on-the-saucer-airm: At a crashed saucer said to have come down in Hart Canyon near Aztec, New Mexico, in 1948, snow reportedly blew across the site and piled up on the ground and rocks but vanished as soon as it touched the craft, so none built up on it. Michels tells this as he narrates the crash story, and he credits the detail to a young airman on perimeter security named Donald Bass. It suggests the object was giving off heat or some other energy.
snowden-s-revelations-about-bullrun-and-: The 2013 leaks by Edward Snowden, a former US intelligence contractor, showed that American spy agencies had "back doors" into technology through programs called Bullrun and PRISM, Michels says, and he does not believe this happened without Google and Apple knowing.
