strieber-s-childhood-mind-control-camp-a: As a boy in the 1950s, Whitley Strieber, a writer who says he has met alien beings, was sent to a summer camp at Randolph Air Force Base near his home in Texas. Strieber alleges that there he was put through physical torture and mind-control experiments. The philosopher Jason Jorjani retells Strieber's own account, which would mean the military tested such things on children.
strieber-s-meeting-with-james-jesus-angl: The writer Whitley Strieber, known for his account of being taken by alien beings, is said to have once met James Jesus Angleton, the longtime head of counterintelligence at the CIA, America's spy agency. Michels mentions it in passing, saying Strieber told him so on the podcast, but he gives no details of what was said at the meeting.
strieber-s-written-account-to-sarbacher-: In 1986, the author Whitley Strieber, who wrote the book Communion about his own encounters, says a man in Florida named Robert Sarbacher asked him to write out his whole experience. Strieber says he wrote it at his cabin in upstate New York and shipped it, and the next morning the delivery driver called to say, "We can't deliver it. The recipient has expired." Strieber tells this firsthand, sometimes stressing only that Sarbacher wanted it all written down, while Michels, repeating Strieber later, puts it as Sarbacher dying just before the two were about to meet.
strieber-taken-to-a-school-for-special-c: In the 1950s, a boy named Whitley Strieber was taken from Randolph Air Force Base, a US Air Force base, to a school for special children in Baja California, Mexico. The researcher and philosopher Jason Jorjani tells this, passing on what Strieber himself told him. If true, it would mean the military was moving certain children to a special school in secret.
strieber-writes-to-warn-against-the-oxfo: In 1988 the author Whitley Strieber, who says he has met aliens, wrote to a priest named Father Raldi warning him not to let scientists at Oxford carbon-date the Shroud of Turin, a linen cloth some believe wrapped the body of Jesus. Strieber tells Jesse Michels he warned that the scientists would defend their way of thinking and "lie without knowing it". He says that is what happened: they dated the shroud to the Middle Ages and, in his words, destroyed the research.
string-theory-as-an-intentional-dead-end: String theory, a branch of physics that tries to explain everything as tiny vibrating strings, may have been pushed on purpose as a dead end, to keep physicists away from dangerous work. Michels puts the question himself, asking whether the theory, which the physicist Ed Witten worked on, is "intentionally a bridge to nowhere." A mathematician named Eric Weinstein makes it his own claim, calling it a possible "blocking mechanism" and tying it to an account he attributes to Andreessen and Horowitz about classified physics, and naming Witten and the physicist Brian Greene.
stringfield-files-on-headband-transceive: In some cases where crashed UFOs were said to be recovered, witnesses reportedly described the crews wearing a kind of headband, possibly a radio-like headband transceiver, along with cutaway drawings of the craft. The claim comes from the crash retrieval status reports, a series of seven reports that the UFO researcher Leonard Stringfield put out from Cincinnati, Ohio, between 1970 and 1989. A guest who goes by the online name UAPGerb brings it up on Michels' show, saying that the researcher Michael Schratt found many such mentions in those files. If true, it would hint at how the operators flew or communicated with their craft.
stringfield-s-investigations-into-crash-: A man named Stringfield is said to have done a huge number of investigations into crash retrievals, meaning the alleged recovery of crashed unknown craft by the US government. The journalist Michael Shellenberger mentions him in passing during an episode about a secret UFO program. He brings it up as an example of earlier digging into this kind of story.
sts-124-bolt-in-the-payload-bay-was-the-: Something that looked like a stray bolt floating in the cargo bay of a Space Shuttle in 2008 turned out to be the International Space Station seen in the distance. Scott Kelly passes on the story from his brother Mark Kelly, a former astronaut with NASA, the US space agency, and now a US senator, who commanded that shuttle flight, known as STS-124. He tells it on an episode where Michels debates a skeptic, as an example of a strange sight in space with an ordinary answer.
sts-48-and-sts-80-shuttle-uap-videos-199: Two videos filmed from the space shuttle are said to show unexplained objects in orbit, one from the STS-48 mission in 1991 and one from the STS-80 mission in 1996. A guest named Maaneli Derakhshani names both cases, mentioning a man named James Oberg, in an episode about NASA and the Moon. Another guest, identified only as Max, refers back to the same two shuttle cases in passing, without years. They come up as possible evidence of unknown things seen by NASA's own cameras in space.
stubblebine-s-effort-to-cognitively-enha: In the 1980s Albert Stubblebine, the general who headed the US Army's intelligence and security command, wanted to "cognitively enhance soldiers", making their minds sharper and stronger. The online researcher who goes by UAPGerb mentions this to Michels in passing, without naming a source. He raises it as an example of the military taking unusual mental abilities seriously.
student-vanishes-on-mountain-excursion-i: A group of students went on an excursion in the mountains of Minas Gerais, a state in Brazil, and one of the girls wandered away from the group for a while and simply vanished. Aldo Rebelo, who is presented on the show as a Brazilian defense minister, calls it a very well-known event and says it was reported in the local press. He brings it up as one of the strange Brazilian cases that would point to something unexplained if it happened as described.
sturgis-led-raid-sinks-a-russian-ship-ma: In 1962, a man named Frank Sturgis, who worked with anti-Castro forces, is said to have led Cuban exiles in a raid on Cuba that sank a Russian ship, after which US marshals burned their base on No Name Key, a small island in Florida. A lawyer named Dan Sheehan tells this to Michels without naming a source, and he ties it to Robert F. Kennedy, then the US Attorney General. If true, it would show the US government shutting down its own Cuban raiders after they went too far.
sub-bottom-profiling-shows-the-layers-un: Around 2025, a team looked beneath a strange round object on the floor of the Baltic Sea using sub-bottom profiling, a kind of sonar that sees into the layers under the seabed. The treasure hunter Dennis Asberg, who found the object, mentions it only briefly and confirms that the profiling was done. It ties to his claim that new data show the object sits apart from the seabed under it.
submarine-crew-showed-the-doctor-the-son: A doctor named Greg Rogers, who worked with NASA (the US space agency), says that while he was aboard a US Navy submarine the crew took him into the sonar room, where sailors listen for sounds and objects underwater. Rogers tells this from his own experience as part of the story of what he says he learned and saw while working with the military.
submarines-take-evasive-action-from-fast: Several US Navy submarine crew members say they suddenly found an object under the water closing in on them fast. The account comes from Tim Gallaudet, a retired Navy admiral, who says two officers and one enlisted sailor came to him separately with these reports. If true, it would mean something unknown moves through the ocean quickly enough to alarm a submarine crew.
substack-article-on-the-boxer-upsets-the: The writer Peter Levenda says he wrote an article about a particular event involving a boxer, and that it upset people in the wrestling world. He posted it on his Substack, an online newsletter he says he had not touched in about a year, and he tells the story himself as its author.
subterranean-chamber-as-giza-s-original-: The chamber cut into the rock about 100 feet straight down beneath the Great Pyramid in Egypt may be the original sacred site at Giza, older than the pyramid above it. The writer Graham Hancock says he thinks so, giving it as his own view. A researcher named Luke Caverns repeats it from Hancock's appearance on Joe Rogan's interview show, adding that Hancock believes most of the pyramid was built under the pharaoh Khufu but wonders if that underground level came from an earlier time.
sudden-mastery-of-morse-code-under-threa: In the 1960s, at an Army intelligence school, a soldier facing the threat of being shipped to Vietnam suddenly mastered Morse code, the system of sending letters as dots and dashes, jumping through speeds from 10 up to 22 words a minute in about two hours. The soldier was Joe McMoneagle, later known for psychic spying work, and he tells it himself, saying "something popped in my head" that day. He offers it as an early sign of an unusual ability in his mind.
sufi-imam-jinn-change-physical-scripture: A Sufi imam, a teacher in the mystical branch of Islam, is said to have explained why Muslims still memorise the Quran word for word even though it has long been written down: beings that live outside our space and time can go back and change physical objects, but they are not allowed to change our memory. Rizwan Virk, a guest the episode presents as an MIT scientist, passes this on from an imam he does not name. He offers it as a hint that reality may work like a simulation that can be edited.
suicide-stand-down-in-the-drone-program-: In 2013, according to a guest named Dylan Borland, the US Air Force's drone program called a suicide stand-down, a pause in normal work after suicides among its people. Borland says people from the program called him and told him, "Yo, we had a suicide standown." He tells it as something those callers passed on to him, as a sign of the strain inside the program.
suited-beings-on-a-scrap-metal-train-car: In October 1971, a woman bicycling through a small city in central Sweden saw something she kept to herself for decades: beings in suits on a train car loaded with scrap metal. Clas Svahn, a Swedish researcher who collects UFO reports, says she wrote him a letter and then told him, the night before, the first time she had shared it outside her family. He passes on her story as she told it to him.
sumer-over-12-000-years-old-based-on-geo: Sumer, the early civilisation of what is now Iraq, goes back well over 12,000 years, according to a researcher named Matt LaCroix, who bases this on how its sites line up with measurements of the Earth's shape. He says that great age is why the Sumerians "essentially invented everything". He gives it as his own view, without naming a source.
sumerian-accounts-of-civilizations-from-: The Sumerians, an ancient people of Mesopotamia, are said to have spoken of civilizations that existed before there was a moon in the sky. Michels says this himself, without naming a source, on an episode with a guest named Randall Carlson titled around the idea that the moon is an alien spaceship. If true, it would mean the moon arrived within human memory.
sumerian-anunnaki-engineered-a-slave-rac: In the myths of Sumer, the ancient civilization of Mesopotamia, the gods called the Anunnaki are said to have made humans as workers, and some modern writers read this as genetic engineering by visitors. The philosopher Jason Jorjani puts it this way: "the Sumerian myths tell us that when the Anunnaki engineered a slave race on Earth." He draws on the writer Zecharia Sitchin, who read these ancient texts this way. Jeffrey Mishlove, a researcher of the mind with a doctorate, sums up Sitchin more softly. He says Sitchin "suggests that the ancient gods, the Anunnaki, performed genetic experiments on our primate ancestors," and does not mention slaves. If it were true, humans would have been designed by beings from somewhere else.
sumerian-astronomical-knowledge: The buildings of Sumer, one of the earliest civilisations, in ancient Mesopotamia, show a surprisingly early knowledge of astronomy. Michels says this himself, without naming a source, in a conversation about Harvard studying UFOs. He offers it as a hint that ancient peoples knew more about the sky than expected.
sumerian-flood-story-as-the-source-of-no: A researcher named Matt LaCroix says on the show that the flood stories of ancient Mesopotamia, in the Epic of Gilgamesh and the older poem Atrahasis, are "almost identical to Genesis," which would make them the source of Noah's ark. In E. A. Wallis Budge's 1920 translation of the epic's eleventh tablet, the survivor Utnapishtim is told to "throw down the house, build a ship," loads it with grain, cattle and craftsmen, rides out a storm until "the mountain of Nisir held the ship," and then sends out a dove, a swallow and a raven, which "came not back." The epic names neither Noah nor Genesis: the comparison is LaCroix's own.
sumerian-god-who-emerged-from-the-water-: The myths of Sumer, the ancient civilisation of what is now Iraq, tell of a god who landed in the river outside Sumer, came up out of "a vehicle of some kind", and taught people the arts of civilisation. Peter Levenda, a writer on occult history, retells this from the myths themselves. He brings it up because, read literally, it sounds like a visitor from somewhere else teaching early humans.
sumerian-king-list-with-kings-ruling-ten: An ancient record from Sumer, in old Mesopotamia, known as the Sumerian King List, names kings who are said to have ruled for 40,000 years or more. The comedian and podcaster Joe Rogan raises it with Michels as something he has been told, saying that eight kings are recorded and that some of them were real people. If the list is taken at its word, people once lived and reigned for spans far beyond any human lifetime.
summoning-and-piloting-uap-through-medit: People can go into a meditative state and summon UAP, the government's term for UFOs, and perhaps even guide them. Jake Barber, a former military helicopter pilot who says he took part in this kind of work, insists that this ability "is real".
summoning-demonstrations-for-the-aaro-di: A private team says it is showing the new head of the Pentagon's UFO office, known as AARO, how it calls up unexplained craft. Jake Barber, a former helicopter pilot who says he once carried away a UFO, describes it from inside the effort: "We're doing demonstrations for the new director," he says, adding that the office is "fully privy" and has "seen our videos." If true, it would mean the government is watching attempts to summon these objects on purpose.
summoning-team-present-the-night-of-the-: A former military helicopter pilot named Jake Barber, who says he helped retrieve an egg-shaped craft in the California desert in 2014, says another team was there that night. According to Barber, that team handled what he calls the summoning part of data collection, meaning efforts to call such craft to appear. He says he was there himself; if true, it would mean someone was deliberately trying to bring these objects in as part of an organised effort.
summoning-the-egg-in-daylight-after-leav: In 2024, out in the desert and in daylight, a former helicopter pilot named Jake Barber says he called up "the egg", the egg-shaped craft he says he once lifted for a secret retrieval programme, and watched it fly by "in dead silence", turn and come in to land behind a house before vanishing. Barber tells it as his own experience after leaving the programme, naming Garry Nolan as a witness and mentioning the Pentagon's current UFO office, known as AARO. If true, it would mean such craft respond to human call.
sun-angle-3d-reconstruction-of-the-flir1: The object in FLIR1, a 2004 infrared video filmed from a Navy jet off Southern California, can be rebuilt in three dimensions using the angle of the sun. Marik von Rennenkampff, who argues the UFO side in a debate with the skeptic Mick West, says that by working out which way the pilot, Chad Underwood, was flying and where the sun stood, around 320 to 330 degrees, "give or take," you can work out the object's true shape. He offers this as his own analysis to push back against readings that the object was something ordinary.
sun-is-400-times-larger-and-400-times-fa: The sun is 400 times larger than the moon and also 400 times farther away, so the two look about the same size in our sky. The researcher Randall Carlson points this out without naming a source, in a conversation that asks whether the moon could be something other than natural.
suppressed-childhood-memories-resurface-: Around late 2022 and early 2023, a man named Jordan Jose says ordinary triggers in daily life made him "unravel," and memories of a childhood he had never recalled came back as flashbacks like those of post-traumatic stress, memories he ties to being taken into a UFO program as a boy. Jose tells this about himself, and in one telling says it came over about two months in 2023 as a crisis, so that he woke up remembering "an entire childhood" he had forgotten.
surgical-animal-mutilation-with-no-blood: Near Aztec, New Mexico, a farm animal is said to have been found with parts of its body cut away as cleanly as surgery and no blood anywhere. Two locals tell it on an episode about an alleged crash of a craft with alien bodies near the town. An unnamed resident says it "looked like a surgeon had taken it off. No, but no blood." An unnamed rancher places it on the Archuleta Ranch and says "the ears and eyes were still intact," but the rest "looked like a surgeon had taken it off." They tell it as one more strange thing in a place they tie to the crash.
surrealist-founders-occult-seances-and-b: The founders of surrealism, the French art movement of the 1920s, were constantly doing occult rituals, including long séances, even before the movement had its name. A philosopher named Jason Jorjani says this, naming the poet André Breton, who wrote a 1922 article, along with the painter Max Ernst and the poet Paul Éluard, though he gives no source. If true, one of the great modern art movements grew partly out of attempts to contact spirits.
survey-finding-only-about-30-of-physicis: A recent survey found that only about 30 percent of physicists still hold to the standard model, the accepted mainstream theory in their field. Jeffrey Mishlove, a parapsychologist and longtime interviewer, cites this to Michels without naming the survey. He uses it to suggest that mainstream science is less settled than it looks.
susan-clancy-s-harvard-study-of-abductee: In the 2000s a Harvard psychology researcher named Susan Clancy did a doctoral study of people who said they had been abducted by aliens, and she later wrote a book about it called Abducted. The researcher and well-known skeptic Michael Shermer mentions her work in passing while debating Michels, summarising it from memory. He uses it as a psychologist's look at why people come to believe they were taken.
susan-gough-by-kirkpatrick-s-side-at-geo: At a 2023 event at George Mason University in Virginia, the Pentagon spokesperson Susan Gough reportedly never left the side of Sean Kirkpatrick, then head of the Pentagon's UFO office. The defense writer Marik von Rennenkampff says he was there and met Kirkpatrick, and that Gough "was attached at his hip, would not leave." He tells it to suggest the Pentagon was keeping a close watch on what Kirkpatrick said.
susan-gough-refuses-to-amend-statement-t: In the 2020s, a Pentagon spokesperson named Susan Gough is said to have refused a request to widen her statement that there were no extraterrestrials so that it also covered "non-human intelligence," a broader term for any intelligent beings that are not human. The online researcher UAPGerb tells this without naming a source, saying the request came from someone using FOIA, a US law that lets anyone request government records. He suggests her refusal leaves room for beings that the narrow word "extraterrestrial" would not cover.
susan-gough-s-psychological-operations-r: The Wall Street Journal article "The Pentagon Disinformation That Fueled America's UFO Mythology," published in 2025, relies on Susan Gough as one of its main sources. Michels says, citing her own LinkedIn profile and independent sources, that she held a lead role in the psychological operations practice at Booz Allen Hamilton, a defense consulting firm that does this work for the Department of Defense. Psychological operations means military work meant to shape what people believe, so Michels raises it to suggest the article itself may be shaping opinion rather than simply reporting.
susan-gough-says-gimbal-is-not-a-trainin: The Gimbal video, Navy footage of a strange object filmed by a fighter jet's targeting camera off Florida in 2015, is not a training video, according to a Pentagon spokesperson named Susan Gough. The UFO skeptic Mick West says he asked Gough directly, and she told him it was not a training video. It matters because it rules out one ordinary explanation for where the footage came from.
susan-mccasland-accepted-a-calendar-invi: A woman named Susan McCasland is said to have accepted a Google calendar invite for a meeting between the rock musician Tom DeLonge and John Podesta, a senior Washington political adviser, around 2015 or 2016. Michels points to this himself, citing the Podesta emails, messages from Podesta's account that were published by WikiLeaks, a website that releases leaked documents, where he says "a calendar notification shows that Susan herself accepted a Google calendar invite for something called a Dong Podesta meeting." He raises it as a sign that the McCasland household was tied into DeLonge's private push to get officials talking about UFOs.
susan-mccasland-s-911-call-about-her-hus: In 2026, in Albuquerque, New Mexico, a woman named Susan McCasland called 911, the US emergency number, about her missing husband and told them, "I have some indication that he must have planned not to be found." Her own words come from the recording of that call. The story is told in an episode about top American scientists who have gone missing.
susan-mccasland-s-facebook-statement-on-: In 2026 a woman named Susan McCasland posted a statement on Facebook that, as Michels reads it out, says a man named Neil "does not have any special knowledge about the ET bodies and debris from the Roswell crash stored at Wright Pat." Roswell refers to a reported 1947 crash, and Wright-Patterson is an Air Force base in Ohio. Michels quotes it himself, and the wording seems to take for granted that alien bodies and wreckage are kept there.
susi-temples-no-longer-face-east-west-im: In eastern Turkey there are old temples of a type called Susi temples, whose openings were built to face only the rising or setting sun, east or west, but today they no longer line up and sit offset. The researcher Matt LaCroix tells this without naming a source, and treats the offset as a dating clue: it would mean the Earth's axis has shifted since the temples were built.
suspected-spook-at-the-hotel-during-the-: While Michels and a friend named Chris Ramsay were in Washington for the congressional hearings on UFOs, a man Michels calls "just straight up spook", meaning an intelligence agent, came up to them. Michels tells this from his own experience, a few weeks after it happened, in a conversation with the writer Whitley Strieber, as a sign that people working on the subject are being watched.
suzanne-s-mother-moves-the-family-to-azt: A woman named Suzanne grew up near Aztec, New Mexico, because her mother was obsessed with UFOs and moved the whole family there from South Dakota after reading Behind the Flying Saucers. That was the first book about a flying saucer said to have crashed at Aztec, and it was written by Frank Scully, a columnist for the show-business paper Variety. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, as background to Suzanne's story and as a sign of how far the Aztec tale reached: the family settled in Flora Vista, a suburb of Aztec.
swedenborg-s-visits-to-other-planets: The Swedish mystic Emanuel Swedenborg, whom Michels places in the 17th century, said he went to other planets and came back to tell about it. Michels mentions it in passing, without a source, as an older example of people claiming to travel beyond Earth by the mind.
swedish-1970s-ufo-photographers-admitted: A Swedish researcher named Clas Svahn, who has spent decades collecting UFO reports and evidence, says he tracked down every Swedish photographer who took a UFO photo in the 1970s, and that they admitted the pictures were faked. The one exception, he says, is a man named Christ Sunstrom, who still stands by his photo. Svahn tells this as his own investigation, to show how few classic photos survive close checking.
swedish-ghost-rockets-and-doolittle-s-in: In 1946 and 1947, according to Michels, more than a thousand sightings of so-called ghost rockets were reported over Sweden, objects that looked like modified V2s, the German rockets of the Second World War. He says it is not disputed that Dwight D. Eisenhower, the American general and later president, sent General James Doolittle to investigate. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, on an episode with a former Senate staffer named Kirk McConnell, as an early case the US government took seriously.
swedish-navy-ship-heads-straight-for-the: In 2011, while a treasure-hunting team was diving on a strange object found on the floor of the Baltic Sea, a navy ship, taken to be Swedish, appeared in the distance and headed straight for their boat. An unnamed crew member who was on board tells this, on an episode with the treasure hunter Dennis Asberg, saying "suddenly we saw" the ship "heading directly on us". It is told as one of several strange events around the site that suggested official interest in the find.
swedish-security-service-calls-him-in-ov: In 2015, after a Swedish treasure-hunting diver named Dennis Asberg found an object on the seafloor that he likens to a UFO, Sweden's security service called him in. Asberg tells Jesse Michels he got the call once he was home, from what he describes as Sweden's version of the FBI, the US federal police. It suggests the authorities took his find seriously.
sweep-and-the-1964-money-funnel-in-sekre: Around 1964, hundreds of billions of dollars were secretly moved into a huge hidden underground effort, according to the researcher Jason Simosa. He gives this as a summary on Michels' show and credits it to Sekret Machines, a series of books tied to the musician and UFO researcher Tom DeLonge, without naming any other source. If it were true, it would point to a vast secret budget behind UFO work going back to the 1960s.
swirling-storm-cloud-over-the-lot-betwee: In 2013 in Fort Collins, Colorado, a swirling storm cloud is said to have hung over the empty lot between two houses, looking like "a miniature hurricane." John Blitch, a scientist who worked for the Pentagon's research agency, says he saw it with his neighbor, a man named Andy. He ties it to his account of being taken by strange beings.
switching-astronaut-chem-lights-from-red: A doctor named Greg Rogers, who worked with NASA (the US space agency) at Kennedy Space Center in Florida around 1989 to 1991, says it took him a year and a half to get NASA to switch the glow sticks carried for astronauts from red to green. He tells it from his own experience and mentions a Colonel Shokitis in the story, as an example of how slowly the agency changed its ways.
sybil-leek-and-the-occult-side-of-mk-ult: A woman named Sybil Leek, known for her ties to the occult, was openly involved with Operation Often, a CIA effort that looked into the occult alongside MK-Ultra, the agency's mind-control research of the 1950s to 1970s. The writer Peter Levenda says this came out later, without naming his source. It would mean the CIA's mind-control work reached into witchcraft and the supernatural.
sycamore-knoll-undersea-base-claim-rejec: There is a claim that aliens keep a base under the sea at Sycamore Knoll, an underwater hill off Point Dume on the Southern California coast, and on this podcast it is turned down. Tim Gallaudet, a retired Navy admiral, says it plainly: "There was no alien base there." He mentions the idea as it appears in the book Undersea UFO Base by a writer named Preston Dennett. Michels says he looked into it himself with a man named Will O'Brien, going through a survey made by an underwater rover. "We did the research and we're like I don't think there's anything," he says. Both tell it to set aside this one spot, even as they discuss unexplained things in the ocean.
symbols-aboard-the-craft-and-the-gray-al: Aboard a craft over Fillmore, California, there were symbols, and three orange circles set in an equilateral triangle stand for the "gray alliance", a grouping of seven species of the small grey-skinned beings of UFO lore. This comes from Steve Colbern, a scientist who studies objects said to be alien implants in people, who says he was there, and who adds that he was "led to believe" what the symbol means.
synctext-message-how-long-will-you-be-do: While visiting the Baltic Sea anomaly, a strange formation on the floor of the Baltic Sea, in a spot with no phone reception, Michels says his phone got a text through the messaging app Synctext that asked: "How long will you be down here for?" He tells this as something that happened to him on the same trip when equipment failed, and says everyone who was with him will back up the story. If true, someone or something knew where he was and could reach him where no signal should get through.
synesthete-watson-who-saw-and-felt-taste: A man named Watson is said to have seen things every time he tasted something, so that a flavour came with images as well. The cognitive scientist Don Hoffman tells this to Michels from memory, unsure of the name and without giving a source, as a case of synesthesia, where the senses blend. He uses it to show that the brain can build very different pictures of the world from the same inputs.
szydagis-tests-alleged-crash-debris-with: A physicist at the University at Albany named Matthew Szydagis has been studying pieces of debris said to come from crashes of unknown craft, testing them with neutron activation, a lab method that fires neutrons at a sample to find out what elements it contains. His colleague, the researcher Kevin Knuth, whom the episode presents as a NASA whistleblower, mentions this work in passing to Jesse Michels without going into results. If such material ever showed something unusual, it would be physical evidence rather than testimony.
t-pillar-at-cavustepe-visited-with-rober: At Çavuştepe in Turkey there is a T-shaped stone pillar made of basalt, of the kind found at very old sites in the region. Matt LaCroix, a researcher of ancient sites, says he went there recently with a group that included Robert Schoch, a geologist who studies ancient monuments, and he shows a picture of Schoch standing by the stone. He brings it up as part of his case that a lost early civilisation once existed.
t-pillar-design-on-the-gate-of-the-sun: A T-shaped pillar design is carved on the back of the Gate of the Sun, a stone gateway at the ancient site of Tiwanaku in Bolivia. The researcher Matt LaCroix points this out on the podcast without naming a source. He says it shows "the same concept of the three doorways" that he sees at other ancient sites, which would suggest a shared idea linking cultures far apart.
t-t-brown-apparatus-left-in-the-eureka-g: A group in Eureka, California called the Borderland Society, which had ties to the inventor Thomas Townsend Brown, still had some of Brown's apparatus sitting in a garage. Brown was known for electrical devices said to work against gravity. A UFO researcher named Clas Svahn says he saw it himself but could not bring it away with him.
t-townsend-brown-s-high-voltage-capacito: A mid-century American inventor named Thomas Townsend Brown, Michels says, found a way to move things that went beyond burning fuel, using high-voltage capacitors, devices that store electric charge. In one episode Michels puts it outright: he has "uncovered an absurd amount of information" leading him to believe Brown "essentially discovered anti-gravity in the 1950s." Michels returns to this himself across several episodes, from his own research, as a lost key to new kinds of flight.
table-levitation-at-family-seances-1965: As children in the Bronx, New York, in the mid-1960s, a family is said to have held seances where the table rose off the floor. The author Peter Levenda says he was there, recalling that "we actually had paranormal phenomenon" as kids. In another moment he describes it differently, as the table knocking rather than lifting, and gives no time or place. He tells it as his own early brush with the unexplained.
tablets-detailing-construction-of-the-fl: Ancient clay tablets from Mesopotamia, the old land between the Tigris and Euphrates rivers, are said to describe in close detail how the boat that survived the great flood was built, down to how much pitch to use and what kind of wood. The researcher Matt LaCroix sums this up on Michels' show without naming a particular tablet, saying the detail is all there for anyone who reads them. He raises it as a sign that the flood story preserves a real memory.
tactical-plan-to-stand-down-the-covert-o: Steven Greer, who argues that UFO secrets are held by a hidden global group, says a tactical plan to make that secret organisation stand down is already in place. Speaking in 2025, he tells Michels it has been in place for about a year and a half to two years. If true, it would mean someone is actively moving to dismantle the group he says hides the secret.
tae-technologiestrump-media-merger-annou: A merger between TAE Technologies, a company working on fusion energy, and Trump Media, the media company tied to President Donald Trump, was announced on December 18, 2025, just two days after the death of a scientist named Loureiro on December 16, Michels points out. He tells it himself, without naming a source, in an episode about top American scientists going missing. He raises the timing as a coincidence worth noticing, hinting the two events may be linked.
tag-17-dead-end-corridor-behind-the-nort: A radar scan of the Great Pyramid in Egypt is said to have found, in 2020, a dead-end corridor hidden behind the chevrons, the big angled stone blocks set into the pyramid's north face, a feature the scanning team labelled Tag 17. The researcher Jeffrey Drum says the team, whose work he links to a radar researcher named Filippo Biondi, detected it in 2020 and has since gone inside it with a tiny camera, and he offers this as proof that the scans can find real hidden spaces.
tag-along-object-follows-the-incoming-mi: In 1962, during Bluegill Triple Prime, an American high-altitude nuclear test over the Pacific near Johnston Island, an object showed up on the tracking screen and "tagged along following the incoming missile down." Harold Malmgren, an adviser to presidents in the 1960s, says he saw this in the test's report, and he places it among officials such as President John F. Kennedy, his advisers McGeorge Bundy and Robert McNamara, John McNaughton and Lyndon B. Johnson. If true, something unknown was shadowing a US nuclear test.
takano-josen-met-hermann-oberth-and-disc: A Japanese man named Takano Josen says he met Hermann Oberth, the German rocket pioneer, and that the two talked openly about UFOs, with Oberth saying he "truly respected the beings actually riding in UFOs." Michels says he met Takano on a trip to Japan and relays the story, and Takano also tells it himself on the same episode. If true, it would mean one of the founders of rocketry took the visitors seriously.
taken-aboard-a-spacecraft-from-his-mosco: In 1997, in his top-floor apartment in Moscow, a man named Kiran Ilum Xenov, presented on the show as the president of a Russian republic, says he felt something calling him, went to the window, and saw "something like a translucent pipe glowing," made of some kind of matter, before being taken aboard a spacecraft. Xenov tells this as his own experience, and if true it would be a first-hand account of being taken by beings from a craft.
taken-in-broad-daylight-in-2007: A North Carolina man named Chris Bledsoe, author of the book UFO of God, says that in 2007, near the Cape Fear River in North Carolina, beings came and took him in broad daylight. He tells it as something that happened to him: "Then they came and they took me." If true, it would mean such abductions do not only happen in the dark.
taken-off-mountain-bike-and-out-of-bed-b: Beings he calls "the veterinarians" are said to come and "pluck us out of our bed, play with us," and to have taken one man off his mountain bike and out of his own bed. That man is John Blitch, a scientist who worked for the Pentagon's research agency, telling it as something that happened to him. He links it to a hurricane-like cloud over his house, which he says the beings used as cover to land.
taken-unknowingly-to-the-hangar-building: A doctor named Greg Rogers, who worked with NASA (the US space agency), says he was once taken to a secret hangar building without knowing where he was going. His escort from EG&G, a private contractor that worked at secret government sites, knew he was headed to that building that day, he says. Rogers tells this firsthand as the lead-up to what he says he saw inside: a UFO.
taking-george-knapp-through-los-alamos-1: In 1989, Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft for the government, says he took the Las Vegas TV reporter George Knapp through Los Alamos, the government's nuclear weapons laboratory in New Mexico, where Knapp filmed everything and spoke to people Lazar worked with. Lazar tells it himself, admitting it "was not all 100% legal", and says they rode right into the experimental areas, where he told Knapp, "George, this is my desk." He offers it as proof that he really worked there.
talbert-newspaper-series-on-1950s-aerosp: In the 1950s, the story goes, a newspaper series reported that several big aerospace companies had suddenly become interested in anti-gravity, meaning ways to cancel or control gravity for flight. Michels gives the record: an article by Anel Talbert in the New York Herald Tribune in November 1955, titled 'Conquest of gravity aim of top scientists in United States.' He ties it to Gordon Gray, then president of the University of North Carolina. The physicist Hal Puthoff remembers it as a series in the Miami Herald and other papers, 'probably' from the 1950s, and links it to the physicist Bryce DeWitt. The physicist John Brandenburg tells it in nearly the same words, spells the author Talbot, and connects it to an essay DeWitt wrote for the Gravity Research Foundation, a group that ran essay prizes on gravity. The philosopher Jason Jorjani does not name the author but says the articles quoted the chairmen of the aircraft makers Martin, Lear and Convair, and that the firms said they had cracked anti-gravity. He takes this from a book called Closer Encounters. If true, it would mean the aircraft industry was quietly working on gravity control decades ago.
tall-white-children-s-play-saucer-1960: In the Indian Springs Valley in Nevada in the 1960s, tall, white-skinned aliens kept a small saucer for their children to take out to a play area, a craft not built to fly faster than light. Charles Hall, a man who calls himself a whistleblower and says he spent three years with these beings near Area 51, a secret US Air Force test site, tells Jesse Michels he saw it himself. If true, it would mean whole alien families living near a US base.
tall-white-deep-spacecraft-schedules-and: Tall, pale beings that Charles Hall calls the Tall Whites kept flight schedules for their deep-space craft, and the longest he saw was five years, for craft he was told came straight from their home planet. Hall, a man who says he spent three years around these beings in the mid-1960s in Indian Springs Valley, Nevada, near Area 51, tells Michels this from what he saw and what he says he was told. If true, it would mean regular traffic between Earth and another world.
tall-white-electronics-that-read-and-imp: Tall, pale beings at a Nevada air base in the mid-1960s are said to have had electronics that could read a person's thoughts and plant thoughts in their mind. Charles Hall, a former Air Force man who says he spent three years among these beings, which he calls the Tall Whites, tells it first-hand. Their devices, he says, can "put thoughts in the conscious part of their mind by electronic means."
tall-white-in-an-orcas-pub-asks-what-it-: In a pub on Orcas Island, in Washington State, a very tall, pale stranger of the kind some people call a "Tall White", meaning a type of alien said to look almost human, is said to have asked a local what it is like to live here, and when the local misunderstood, he answered, "No, on Earth." Brent Friedman, a guest on an episode about Hollywood and the CIA, tells it as something an unnamed friend on the island told him. If true, it would mean such beings walk among people unnoticed.
tall-white-underground-facilities-and-ha: In the 1960s, according to a man named Charles Hall, who says he spent three years with tall, white-skinned aliens near Area 51, a secret US Air Force test site in Nevada, these beings lived in underground facilities at the north end of Nevada's Indian Springs Valley, complete with hangars for their craft. Michels lays out Hall's claim in his own words on an episode with Hall. He notes that it closely resembles the story of Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft at a secret Nevada site.
tall-whites-came-in-the-last-ice-age-to-: Charles Hall, who says he spent three years living alongside tall, pale, human-like aliens he calls the tall whites at Area 51, a secret Air Force test site in Nevada, says these beings first came to Earth in the middle of the last ice age. He says they came for the same reason the US keeps a base on the Pacific island of Guam: Earth is a handy stopping point on their travels. Hall tells it as something he learned from his own time with them.
tall-whites-gated-compound-on-orcas-reac: The story goes that the "tall whites", tall pale beings who come up in UFO lore, have a gated compound on Orcas Island, and that people get there by an unmarked black helicopter. Brent Friedman, a guest on an episode about Hollywood, the CIA and UFOs, says a friend of his on Orcas Island told him this: "they have a compound on the Orcus Island." If true, beings that are not human would be living in a guarded place in plain sight.
tall-whites-in-suits-forming-a-high-spee: In the mid 1960s, on the Air Force ranges at Indian Springs, Nevada, tall pale beings known as the "tall whites" would switch on their suits out in the desert, and the force fields around the suits merged so that, from a quarter mile away, "you would swear there was a giant white floating horse coming at you." This is told by Charles Hall, a former Air Force man who says he spent three years among these beings and saw it himself. It is offered as the origin of a local legend of a glowing horse.
tall-whites-mistaken-for-ancient-egyptia: In the 1960s, some of the men working alongside Charles Hall in Indian Springs Valley, Nevada, saw the tall pale beings he calls the Tall Whites and took them for ancient Egyptians who had somehow got into the valley, become trapped there, and were still writing in their own hieroglyphics. Hall, a former Air Force weather observer who says he spent three years among these beings near Area 51, tells this on two episodes as something his fellow rangemen believed. He tells it because the beings looked human enough to be mistaken for an ancient people.
tall-whites-playing-airplanes-on-the-ind: On summer nights in the mid-1960s, tall, pale beings are said to have played on the runways of Indian Springs Air Base, a small base in the Nevada desert. Charles Hall, a former Air Force man who says he spent three years among the beings he calls the Tall Whites, says he watched them himself. "I used to watch them play at the runways," he says, as part of his account of living alongside them.
tall-whites-posing-as-charlie-hall-and-h: Charles Hall, who says he spent three years with tall, pale, human-like aliens he calls the tall whites, says that in the 1960s some of them passed as humans to visit Lawrence Livermore Laboratory, a US government weapons research lab in California. According to Hall, one went by the name Charlie Hall, and a female tall white named Pamela pretended to be his wife so they could go in and talk to the scientists. If true, it would mean aliens were quietly mixing with top American scientists.
tall-whites-say-dominant-species-kill-of: In the 1960s near Indian Springs, Nevada, a man named Charles Hall says he dealt with tall, pale beings he called the Tall Whites, and that they told him they are not here to save anyone. According to Hall, they found it odd that humans ride horses and live alongside other creatures, because on most civilized worlds the dominant species kills off anything that could threaten it. A guest named Kurt Metzger repeats this on Michels' show as what Hall said, as a warning about what such visitors might want.
tall-whites-two-month-trip-to-a-star-nea: In late summer 1965, the tall pale beings called the "tall whites" made a round trip of about six weeks to two months to a star near Arcturus, a bright star far from Earth, which means their craft must travel faster than light. Charles Hall, a former Air Force man who says he worked alongside these beings at Indian Springs, Nevada, tells this from his own experience, naming figures he calls the Teacher and the Tour Guide.
tapes-mention-coupling-to-the-computer-d: Many of the recorded sessions held by a scientist named Andrija Puharich in the 1970s mention coupling to a computer data bank. An unnamed researcher on the episode sums up the tapes this way, without quoting a specific one. The phrase hints that whatever spoke through the sessions described linking up with some kind of stored store of knowledge.
tapes-of-puharich-meditating-in-the-king: There are said to be tape recordings of Andrija Puharich, a scientist the episode's title calls a CIA scientist who made contact with an alien council, meditating inside the King's Chamber, a granite room deep inside the Great Pyramid of Egypt. Both tellings come from a single episode, about Puharich, where researchers talk about what they have found. A researcher named Greg Malatzi says, "We have tape recordings of him meditating in the King's Chamber." Another guest, whose name is not given, adds the year: "in '76," and the host answers "What?" in surprise. The story fits with other 1970s accounts of scientific work inside the pyramid. It matters because it would show Puharich trying to reach other beings from inside one of the world's most mysterious buildings.
tara-swart-s-husband-s-death-and-doves: After the husband of the neuroscientist Tara Swart died in unfortunate circumstances, a flock of doves is said to have appeared at her house. Michels mentions this briefly and with some hedging ("I think") during a conversation about other topics, and he presents it as a story Swart has told. He offers it as a possible sign from the dead.
targ-and-puthoff-publish-in-nature-and-w: Two scientists, Russell Targ and Dr. Hal Puthoff, wrote an article in Nature, the science journal, and then a book called Mind-Reach, according to Joe McMoneagle, who worked as a remote viewer, a person trained to describe distant places using the mind alone. McMoneagle puts the article in 1972 and says he thinks "it was called nature magazine," relaying it as part of how that research became known.
tate-s-post-trip-talk-on-solved-energy-1: In 1948 the University of Minnesota physicist John Torrance Tate is said to have come back from a trip to the American Southwest and said, "I saw while on this trip, we will never have to worry about energy. That's already been figured out." The researcher Scott Ramsey tells this, crediting Tate's archived records and linking the trip to Vannevar Bush, the top US government science administrator of the era. Ramsey raises it as a hint that Tate had seen technology recovered from a crashed craft.
tate-s-sealed-archive-at-university-of-m: A sealed collection of papers belonging to a man named John Torrance Tate, covering roughly 1948 to 1950, is said to sit in the University of Minnesota archives in Minneapolis. A researcher named Scott Ramsey says he and his team flew to Minneapolis and got a meeting with the archive to see those records, and he mentions the electronics company Texas Instruments alongside Tate. Ramsey treats the papers as possible evidence for the crash story he is researching.
taylor-flying-cargo-jets-between-florida: Timothy Taylor, a man said to attract UFOs and the subject of one of Michels's episodes, once flew cargo jets back and forth between Florida and Nassau, the capital of the Bahamas. Michels says Taylor writes about this himself in Launch Fever, his biography. He brings it up as part of Taylor's background as a working pilot.
taylor-hospitalized-with-injuries-from-r: A man named Travis Taylor, who has worked at Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah ranch known for reports of strange happenings, is said to have ended up in hospital with injuries from what goes on there, and to have had strange things follow him after he left. The ranch's owner tells this on Michels' show, passing on what happened to Taylor, as a sign that whatever is at the ranch can harm people.
taylor-next-rocket-science-advance-will-: A rocket scientist named Timothy Taylor once told the religious studies scholar Diana Pasulka that the next big advance in his field would come from hers. Michels relays the exchange from Pasulka's book American Cosmic: when she asked Taylor why he was interested in her work on religion, he answered, "The next development in my field, rocket science, will come from yours, religion." Michels tells it because it would mean someone inside the space world saw belief and religious experience as a path to new technology.
taylor-says-bledsoe-may-need-to-hide-out: In 2008 a man named Timothy Taylor told Chris Bledsoe that he might have to go hide out in Nassau, in the Bahamas, for a while. Bledsoe, a man who says UFOs keep appearing around him, tells Michels this himself, as something said to him directly. He tells it as a sign of how serious, and possibly dangerous, his situation had become.
taylor-secretly-chief-scientist-of-uap-t: In 2020, a man named Travis Taylor was quietly called into meetings in Washington, D.C. and made chief scientist of the UAP Task Force, a Pentagon group set up to study UAP, the newer official term for UFOs. The owner of a ranch known as Skinwalker tells this to Michels, and says it happened "unbeknownst to us", meaning Taylor's colleagues at the ranch did not know at the time. If true, someone tied to the ranch was helping lead the government's own study of these objects.
taylor-warned-off-driving-up-the-road-at: A man named Timothy Taylor once asked a guard at Creech Air Force Base, in Indian Springs, Nevada, if he could just drive a mile or two up the road without getting out of the car, and was told, "Oh, that would be a very bad idea." The wife of Charles Hall, a former Air Force man who says he spent three years among tall white aliens near Area 51, relays this as Taylor told it. She tells it as a sign that something was being guarded out there that outsiders were not meant to see.
tayos-cave-metallic-library-of-alien-art: Deep in the Tayos Cave in Ecuador, the story goes, there is "an ancient alien metallic library", a store of metal objects and books. Michels tells it himself in several episodes without naming a source, once calling it a "well-known myth" of the area and once linking it to an expedition in 1976 that included the astronaut Neil Armstrong. It comes up as possible evidence of a lost, very old civilization or of visitors from elsewhere.
td-100-experiment-on-a-woman-on-film-196: Silent film footage from the early 1960s shows an experiment carried out on a woman at Intelectron, a company in New York City, according to the researcher Greg Malatzi. In his account the woman sits behind a wall in one room while the experimenters are in another with the TD 100, a device their inventor built in the early 1960s, and although there is no sound, Malatzi says "it's obvious what's happening." He describes the footage himself without naming where it came from, and tells it as a sign that the device could affect a person through a wall.
team-statement-that-limestone-absorbs-th: In 2025, the team behind a radar scan of the Khafre pyramid at Giza in Egypt said in a statement on their Facebook page that the pyramid's known chambers do not show up clearly because they sit inside a limestone slab that absorbs the signal. In the statement's words, "the structures are embedded in a limestone slab that absorbs the signal." The researcher Jeffrey Drum reads it out on Michels' show, crediting the team members Armando and Filippo Biondi, as their answer to critics of the scan, which they say found structures beneath the pyramids.
teardrop-shaped-transmedium-uap-video-sh: A video is said to show a teardrop-shaped unidentified object, maybe 20 feet long, moving under the ocean and also flying, shown inside a secure room for secret material at a military joint task force overseas. Tim Gallaudet, a retired Navy admiral, tells it, saying the video came attached to an email from a naval intelligence commander. If true, it would mean an unknown craft can move between sea and sky.
tech-sergeant-warns-borland-never-to-spe: In 2012 at Langley Air Force Base in Virginia, a tech sergeant, a mid-level Air Force rank, warned a young airman never to mention a triangle-shaped object again, telling him, "Dylan, don't talk about this ever again. You have no idea what you got yourself into." The airman, Dylan Borland, tells this himself as the person who got the warning. He describes the sergeant as a loadmaster, the crew member who handles cargo on aircraft, who "clearly knew something," which would suggest the sighting was already known and kept quiet.
technicians-at-a-book-signing-say-the-si: At a book signing in San Antonio, Texas, in the 2010s, a man came up to Whitley Strieber, a writer who says he has met alien beings, and said he was one of the technicians who picked up a certain signal. The man said it was the strangest signal they had ever received and that it was still being studied. Strieber repeats what the technician told him, as a sign that something real was recorded.
technology-transfer-with-aliens-who-deve: A friend of the retired Army sergeant Lyn Buchanan is said to have been in charge of a "technology transfer" from a group of extraterrestrials, aliens who had developed a kind of magnetic propulsion. Buchanan, who worked in an Army programme that trained people to sense distant places with the mind, tells it twice as what this friend told him, and the second time he says only that the friend ran the transfer, without mentioning magnetic propulsion. If true, it would mean humans have been receiving technology directly from aliens.
ted-owens-book-how-to-contact-space-peop: A man named Ted Owens wrote How to Contact Space People, a book published in 1969 that claims to teach readers how to reach beings from space. The researcher Jeffrey Mishlove, who holds a doctorate, brings it up in an episode on psychics and UFOs, telling it from his own knowledge: "in 1969 he published his book called How to Contact Space People." To Mishlove, it shows Owens openly claiming contact with such beings.
ted-owens-mr-pk-claimed-to-be-a-biologic: A man named Ted Owens, who called himself Mr PK (PK meaning psychokinesis, moving things with the mind), claimed to be almost a living sensor that could detect UFOs. Michels brings this up himself while talking with the UFO researcher Jacques Vallee, saying the writer Jeffrey Mishlove wrote about Owens. If true, it would suggest some people are tuned to the phenomenon in a way others are not.
ted-owens-warns-of-challenger-shuttle-lo: On Christmas Eve 1985, a man named Ted Owens, who spoke of UFOs as his own, phoned to say the US government must not launch the next space shuttle, because "my UFOs are going to knock it right out of the sky." The researcher of psychics Jeffrey Mishlove, who holds a doctorate, says he took that call himself, and that a few weeks later the Challenger shuttle exploded, which would mean the warning came true. The researcher Jason Jorjani tells it a little differently, saying Owens wrote a series of threatening letters to the government about targeting the shuttles one after another.
ted-owens-wills-an-airliner-to-crash: A man named Ted Owens is said to have willed a passenger plane flying ahead of him to crash, and the civilian airliner did crash. The researcher Jason Jorjani tells this on the show without naming a source, as an example of a mind seemingly acting on the world.
ted-rice-s-story-in-masquerade-of-angels: Masquerade of Angels, a book by the writer Karla Turner, tells the story of a man named Ted Rice, who is still alive. Tim Alberino, a guest who investigates giants and other ancient mysteries, mentions the book in passing to Michels as one of the works that records such experiences, without going into what happened to Rice.
ted-serios-thoughtographs-studied-by-jul: In the 1960s, a Chicago bellhop named Ted Serios was said to make pictures appear on Polaroid instant film using only his mind, which made him a famous "thoughtographer", and a psychiatrist named Jule Eisenbud studied him. The researcher Jeffrey Mishlove brings this up on the show, without naming a source, as one example of people said to affect the physical world with thought. If true, it would mean the mind can act directly on matter.
tedesco-brothers-data-on-orbs-entering-t: Two brothers, Jerry Tedesco and John Tedesco, are said to have gathered serious data on glowing orbs flying off the coast of Long Island, New York, some of them going down into the water. Tim Gallaudet, a retired Navy admiral, mentions their work as something he knows of from them. He tells it as part of his case that unexplained objects move in and out of the ocean.
teenage-alberino-finds-the-book-of-enoch: As a teenager, Tim Alberino, a filmmaker who now researches stories of ancient giants, drove to a Borders bookstore, browsed the shelves, and came across the Book of Enoch. That is an ancient Jewish text left out of most Bibles, here in a translation by R. H. Charles and grouped with the Pseudepigrapha, old writings credited to biblical figures. Alberino tells this himself as the moment his interest in these subjects began.
teenage-robert-temple-helps-arthur-young: In Philadelphia in the 1960s, a teenager named Robert Temple is said to have helped a thinker named Arthur Young write the first draft of Young's book The Reflexive Universe. The parapsychologist Jeffrey Mishlove passes this on to Michels as something he heard from people in that circle, saying Temple "actually helped Arthur write the first draft." If so, Temple was working on big ideas about mind and the universe while still very young.
telepathic-contact-with-the-orb-sylvia-2: Around 2008 to 2010, at Baker Victory Services, a children's care facility in Western New York, a glowing orb of what he calls "fractalizing type energy" spoke to a boy named Jordan Jose by thought and told him its name was Sylvia. Jose, who says he was taken into a secret UFO programme as a child, tells Jesse Michels this from his own experience and mentions a woman named Meg in connection with it.
telepathic-escape-plan-with-cousin-ian: The UFO investigator James Fox says that once, in downtown San Francisco, his cousin, named only as Ian, sent him a message by telepathy, mind to mind, laying out a plan to get away: "on the count of" three, as Fox puts it. Fox tells it to Michels as something he lived through himself, and it would mean the two cousins shared a link beyond ordinary words.
telepathic-friend-meets-an-unvoiced-tele: In 2024, a telepathic friend of the writer Whitley Strieber is said to have met an "unvoiced person", meaning someone who talks only mind to mind and never out loud. Strieber passes this on as something his friend told him, while talking about his belief that such beings live among us. If true, it would mean people who speak only by telepathy are walking around unnoticed.
telepathic-interview-with-a-live-et-at-s: A man named Oscar Wolf is said to have taken part in a telepathic interview with a living alien at S4, a secret site reported to lie near Area 51, the Air Force test base in Nevada, and to have seen the being, which he described as about five and a half feet tall. A guest named Dan Sheehan tells it on Michels' show as what Wolf told him, as a sign that the government holds live beings.
telepathic-projection-from-a-canadian-fa: Dan Sheehan says that in the 1970s a facility in south central Canada tried to beam thoughts by telepathy to people in Michigan's Upper Peninsula to get them to mail in their tax forms, and that "85% of the people did it next year." Sheehan, a guest on an episode about UFOs and President Kennedy, credits the story to reports by Ingo Swann and names Pat Price, two men tied to that kind of mind work, and he also places part of it in West Virginia. If true, it would mean governments had tested steering whole populations by thought.
telepathic-projection-test-makes-people-: In the 1970s, according to a man named Dan Sheehan, a secret program took a man named Pat Price up to southern Canada and Michigan's Upper Peninsula to test telepathic projection, meaning sending thoughts into other people's minds, and the test made ordinary people mail their tax forms to a post office box in West Virginia. Sheehan says he learned this from what he calls a deep inside report written by Ingo Swann, another man in the program. If true, it would mean the government had tested mind control on the public.
telepathy-tapes-experiments-with-nonverb: In experiments from 2024, a parent looks at a random image generated on an iPad, and the claim is that their nonverbal autistic child can then pick up what that image is without being shown it. Michels describes this in a conversation with the writer Whitley Strieber, drawing on The Telepathy Tapes, a podcast series made by the filmmaker Ky Dickens with the psychiatrist Diane Powell. If it holds, it would point to some kind of mind-to-mind communication.
telepathy-tapes-nonverbal-autistic-child: Some autistic children who cannot speak seem to know certain Egyptian hieroglyphics, the picture writing of ancient Egypt, according to The Telepathy Tapes, a series made by Ky Dickens about children who are said to communicate by telepathy. Michels passes this on from the series in a brief aside, as a sign that such children may reach knowledge they were never taught.
telepathy-tapes-you-don-t-get-my-powers-: In The Telepathy Tapes, a 2024 podcast by the filmmaker Ky Dickens about children said to read minds, one child reportedly tells their mother, "Mom, you don't get my powers if you lie." Michels repeats the line from the series, though he admits he can't remember which child said it. He brings it up because it suggests these abilities, if real, depend on honesty.
telephone-telepathy-experiments: The scientist Rupert Sheldrake says that people can sense who is calling them on the phone before they pick up, a kind of telepathy that he says he has tested in many experiments. He tells Michels that "virtually everyone," about 85% of the people he can test, shows the effect, and that he is "pretty sure it's real," which would mean minds can reach each other beyond the known senses.
televised-remote-viewing-by-japanese-sch: Schoolchildren in classrooms in Tokyo, Hokkaido and Kyushu in Japan took part in a televised test of remote viewing, the practice of trying to describe a hidden or faraway target using only the mind. The remote viewer Joe McMoneagle, who says he was part of it, recalls that the target was a small aquarium with a starfish in it. If true, it would suggest ordinary children could do this on camera.
teller-and-sakharov-meet-sakharov-says-t: The physicist Edward Teller and Andrei Sakharov, the father of the Russian hydrogen bomb, eventually met, and Sakharov looked over all of Teller's back-and-forth messages and said that Teller had been right. John Brandenburg, a scientist who argues that life on Mars was destroyed by nuclear war, tells this as something passed on to him. In his telling, it shows the Soviet side came to agree with Teller.
teller-letter-commending-john-alexander: Michels says there is a letter in which the physicist Edward Teller praises a man named John B. Alexander for important advances in non-lethal warfare, meaning weapons built to disable people rather than kill them. Michels mentions the letter in passing and does not show it or say where it can be found. He brings it up as a sign that Alexander was respected by top weapons scientists.
teller-refuses-on-camera-to-discuss-laza: In 1989 the famous physicist Edward Teller, a father of the hydrogen bomb, is said to have refused on camera to talk about Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft at a secret site in Nevada. Lazar himself tells it, saying he spoke beforehand to the man who went to interview Teller, who had been one of Teller's students. Lazar raises it because Teller's silence would suggest he knew who Lazar was.
teller-s-name-on-a-project-sign-grudge-u: The physicist Edward Teller, famous as a father of the hydrogen bomb, took part in a real government review of UFOs in the late 1940s, according to Michels. He says, without quoting it, that a document from Project Sign or Project Grudge, the US Air Force's early UFO studies before its better-known Blue Book study, has Teller's name on it. If so, it would mean top weapons scientists were brought into UFO questions from the very start.
teller-shown-townsend-brown-s-demo-floyd: Edward Teller, the physicist known as the father of the American hydrogen bomb, was shown a version of the inventor Thomas Townsend Brown's experiment with a device called a fan precipitator and said, "I have no idea how this works". Michels tells this across several episodes, placing it at Teller's home in Berkeley in 1965 with Brown's daughter Linda Brown and Teller's wife Augusta present, and in one telling adds that a backer named Floyd Odlum invested in Brown's work. Linda Brown also tells it herself as someone who was in the room, recalling Teller finally saying, "I don't understand how it works", which, if true, would mean a top physicist could not explain Brown's device.
templars-and-the-secrets-of-time-travel: The Knights Templar, a medieval order of warrior monks, are supposed to have held the secrets of time travel. Michels mentions this himself, saying "if you read the Umberto Eco Foucault's Pendulum," pointing to the novel by the Italian writer Umberto Eco, which is built around legends of hidden Templar knowledge.
templars-as-keepers-of-advanced-knowledg: The Knights Templar, a medieval order of Christian knights based in France, are said to have guarded advanced knowledge and possibly a bloodline descending from Christ. The researcher Randall Carlson offers this as his own view, without naming a source, and connects it to Jacques de Molay, the order's leader. He says he does think the Templars "were custodians of advanced knowledge" and were "supposed to have" protected that bloodline, which would make the order the keeper of a hidden inheritance.
templars-lalibela-and-the-ark-in-ethiopi: The Ark of the Covenant, the sacred chest the Bible says held the tablets of the law, may have ended up in Ethiopia, and someone linked to Lalibela, a place of ancient rock-cut churches in Ethiopia, may have told the Knights Templar so. The Templars were a medieval order of Christian knights based on the Temple Mount in Jerusalem. The writer Graham Hancock tells Michels this was his own speculation in his book The Sign and the Seal, a guess that would tie the knights' search for the Ark to Africa.
templars-persecuted-by-philip-the-fair-a: The Knights Templar, a medieval order of knights, were accused of rites such as spitting on the cross, and in 1307 they were persecuted by the French king Philip the Fair and burned at the stake. Michels tells this himself, in a passage where he also mentions the thinker Rudolf Steiner, and he names no source for the details.
temple-of-sais-as-a-record-keeping-site-: The Temple of Sais in ancient Egypt was, according to the researcher Matthew LaCroix, a place built to keep the records of history, and it was later destroyed and gone within some five hundred to a thousand years. LaCroix draws on the account by the ancient Greek writer Plutarch, in which a figure named Sonchis appears. He raises it on Michels' show because, if true, a store of very old knowledge would have been lost with it.
temporary-duty-at-the-pentagon-handling-: During the Vietnam War, sometime between 1967 and 1969, a military veteran named Joe McMoneagle says he was sent to the Pentagon on temporary duty, a short posting away from his usual unit, because protesters were throwing balloons full of blood. McMoneagle tells Michels this from his own service, as part of how he came into the Pentagon's orbit.
tens-of-thousands-of-alien-satellites-st: Tens of thousands of alien satellites may have been studying Earth before humans launched even one of their own, which happened with Sputnik, the first human-made satellite, in 1957. Michels puts it this way himself, framing the work of an astronomer named Beatriz Villarroel on an episode with her. If true, Earth was being watched from orbit before the space age began.
tentacle-shape-analysis-says-the-jellyfi: A startup called Skywatcher, whose team tries to call up and record UFOs at its own field site, says that the "jellyfish" objects it filmed between 2023 and 2025 are not drifting balloons, because their tentacle-like parts are sometimes held straight. The team speaks as the people who took the images, which they place in what they call their "7th class" of objects and published, comparing them with jellyfish-like footage put out by Jeremy Corbell, a filmmaker who releases UFO videos. If they are right, the objects would be moving under their own control rather than blowing in the wind.
teotihuacan-as-a-gold-and-silver-ore-pro: The pyramids of Teotihuacan, an ancient city in Mexico, were not temples but a plant for processing gold and silver ore. That is the idea of a researcher named Geoffrey Drumm, who calls it his own hypothesis and gives no source. The story's title links the plant to mercury, but in Drumm's own words on the show he says it was powered by lightning, which would mean the ancient builders had an industrial technology we have not recognised.
terence-mckenna-s-overdosing-girlfriend-: While overdosing, the girlfriend of Terence McKenna, a writer famous for talking about psychedelic drugs, saw a huge UFO made of energy up above and behind him, full of beings shaped like praying mantises. Jason Jorjani, a researcher who studies Nazi UFO stories, retells this to Michels from McKenna's own account. He tells it as a hint that such beings may show up at the edge of death or altered states.
terence-mckenna-staying-with-the-sheldra: A man named Terence McKenna stayed with the Sheldrake family in London whenever he was in town. The scientist Rupert Sheldrake tells this from his own life, calling McKenna "one of my very good friends."
tero-s-remark-to-merlin-sheldrake-on-mus: Mushrooms and other sacred foods tend to grow either at the very start of a forest's life cycle, when almost nothing else is growing, or at its end, when there is huge biodiversity, according to a mushroom specialist named Tero Isokauppila. He says he made this remark himself to Merlin Sheldrake, a biologist who studies fungi, and offers it as a hint that these foods play a special role in nature.
terra-exploration-group-survey-finds-tun: A straight, man-made tunnel about 50 feet wide runs underground from Secret Mountain past Bradshaw Ranch to the front gate of the Clarkdale Cement Plant in Arizona, according to ground surveys and magnetic readings (measurements of the magnetic field in the soil) by a company called Terra Exploration Group. Michels tells it from those surveys, adding that a man named John Bradshaw says the plant was once the town's biggest employer and was fenced and guarded like a military site. If true, it would suggest a hidden underground facility in the area.
terraforming-the-sahara-with-thunderstor: Long ago, when the Sahara was wetter and greener, someone supposedly used fertilizers together with machines that made huge thunderstorms to reshape the land of the upper eastern Sahara and make it livable. The researcher Geoffrey Drumm lays this out as his own theory, naming no source. If true, it would mean an ancient people could engineer the weather.
terry-and-linda-jamison-one-person-split: Terry Jamison and Linda Jamison, identical twins who are also psychics, say they were once a single person who was separated in two on arriving at Earth, as they put it. The philosopher Jason Jorjani brings them up as a prominent case of this kind, repeating what the twins report. He uses it to suggest that souls or minds may divide and come here from elsewhere.
terry-lovelace-and-partner-toby-never-re: In 1977 a man named Terry Lovelace and his partner, named only as Toby, went through some kind of incident on a camping trip. They were off duty at the time, and afterwards neither of them ever fully recovered, and Toby is now gone. Mario Woods, a guest on an episode about a nuclear guard's abduction story, passes this on as what Lovelace himself told him, as a sign of how deeply such an encounter can mark people.
terry-lovelace-hears-a-being-s-voice-tel: A man named Terry Lovelace, who has described meeting otherworldly beings, said that when he met one he nicknamed "Betty Rubble" he heard her voice inside his head rather than through his ears. A guest named Mike Masters recalls Lovelace telling this, on Michels' show, as an example of beings that speak by telepathy.
terry-lovelace-s-dr-bug-abduction-told-a: A man named Terry Lovelace says he was taken by aliens near Whiteman Air Force Base in Missouri and laid on a table, screaming as loud as he could, until a being he called Dr. Bug came over, looked at him, and told him to stop screaming. John Blitch, a scientist with DARPA, the Pentagon's advanced research agency, heard Lovelace tell this at a conference in 2018. Blitch repeats it as he heard it, and it struck him because of his own reported abduction.
terry-lovelace-s-phone-health-data-shows: A man named Terry Lovelace, who lives in a one-story house, is said to have phone health data showing he climbed six stories one day. John Blitch, a scientist with the Pentagon's advanced research agency who says he was himself abducted by an alien, mentions it as something Lovelace showed. The point is that Lovelace's body went somewhere higher than his house allows, as might happen if he were taken up into a craft.
tesla-and-marconi-claimed-alien-communic: Two famous early pioneers of electricity and radio, the inventor Nikola Tesla and the radio maker Guglielmo Marconi, both claimed they had picked up communication from aliens. Michels says this himself, in passing and without naming a source, in a conversation with the filmmaker Tim Alberino.
tesla-and-thomas-townsend-brown-discover: The inventor Nikola Tesla and the physicist Thomas Townsend Brown each discovered a little-known form of electrical physics, one that uses very high voltages across short distances, according to Michels. He says it himself, across three episodes and without naming a source. In one of them, talking with the Navy scientist Salvatore Pais, he places Tesla's version at the end of Tesla's career, at his Wardenclyffe lab and in Colorado Springs, and calls it the same thing Brown was doing. In another he says he is as sure about Brown as about anything in the UFO story, because this seems to be how the craft fly.
tesla-and-townsend-brown-collaboration-l: The inventor Nikola Tesla and Thomas Townsend Brown, an American researcher said to have worked on anti-gravity, supposedly worked together sometime between the 1920s and 1940s, and the evidence is said to come from foreign intelligence, not American sources. Harold Malmgren, a former presidential advisor, recalls asking where the finding came from and getting the answer "intelligence", followed by "I did not get that from any US source." The tellings disagree on who said that line: one credits Steven Greer, a campaigner for UFO disclosure, while another gives it to Malmgren himself and frames the work as anti-gravity research.
tesla-at-wardenclyffe-tapping-the-ether-: Around 1900 to 1903, at Wardenclyffe, his laboratory in New York, the inventor Nikola Tesla is said to have worked with high voltages over short distances while claiming he could tap the ether, an invisible medium once thought to fill all of space, for free energy. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, on an episode with a guest named Dave Rossi. If true, it would mean a source of limitless power was within reach more than a century ago.
tesla-causes-an-earthquake-in-manhattan-: The inventor Nikola Tesla once caused an earthquake in Manhattan by using what amounts to an earthquake weapon in his laboratory in the 1890s. That is according to a researcher named Jason Jorjani, who says Tesla described it himself but names no written source. Jorjani tells it as a sign that Tesla had built machines able to shake the earth.
tesla-killed-in-1943: The inventor Nikola Tesla was killed in 1943, according to Steven Greer, a researcher who campaigns for UFO disclosure. Greer says it in passing, without naming a source, while describing the 1920s, 30s and 40s: "Tesla was killed in 43." If true, it would mean the inventor's death was not natural.
tesla-offers-his-work-to-soviet-and-germ: The inventor Nikola Tesla is said to have tried to sell his work and ideas to Russian or Soviet contacts, and to the Germans. A former Senate staffer named Kurt McConnell mentions this in passing as stories that go around, without naming a source. If true, it would mean some of Tesla's technology may have ended up abroad.
tesla-reportedly-flew-scalar-powered-veh: The inventor Nikola Tesla may have actually flown vehicles powered by what fringe researchers call scalar energy, a kind of energy field that mainstream physics does not recognise. The claim comes from Steve Colbern, a scientist who studies objects said to be implanted in people's bodies, who passes it on as a rumour ("I think he actually flew, rumor has it") and links it to a source called Lost Silence. If true, it would mean Tesla built working craft on a power source science does not accept.
