tesla-s-alien-contact-at-colorado-spring: The inventor Nikola Tesla is said to have communicated with aliens from his laboratory in Colorado Springs in 1899; Michels says so several times, once adding that Tesla saw past, present and future all at once, and Steve Colbern, a scientist who studies objects said to be alien implants, says "they talked to Tesla" according to Tesla's writings. The tellers do not say which of Tesla's writings they mean. If it is Talking with Planets, the article he published in Collier's Weekly in 1901 about the Colorado Springs signals, then his own account says something narrower: he recorded electrical changes with "a clear suggestion of number and order" that first "positively terrified" him. He writes that he felt he had been "the first to hear the greeting of one planet to another," describing signals he heard, not a conversation, and treating any answer as something still to come.
tesla-s-wireless-power-and-claimed-over-: The inventor Nikola Tesla, known for his work on sending electric power without wires, believed he had achieved "over-unity," meaning a machine that puts out more energy than goes into it. A Senate staffer named Kurt McConnell says there are accounts that state this outright, though he does not name them. If true, it would mean Tesla thought he had found a nearly free source of energy.
tesla-s-work-on-electron-movement-and-tr: The inventor Nikola Tesla, it is said, was on the track of an idea that moving electrons around could let you reposition, and so transform, just about any material. Harold Malmgren, a former presidential advisor who says he handled unexplained material, offers this to Jesse Michels as his own impression, without naming a source. If true, it would mean Tesla was reaching toward turning one substance into another.
tesla-s-world-wireless-drawings-show-win: The inventor Nikola Tesla's drawings for his World Wireless system, his plan to send power and messages without wires, are said to be full of wingless craft that look like UFOs. The researcher Jason Jorjani says so on Michels' show, without pointing to a specific drawing, as a hint that Tesla imagined, or knew of, such craft.
tesla-seeing-the-future-in-high-voltage-: Nikola Tesla, the inventor known for his work with electricity, would say strange things during his high-voltage experiments, such as that he could see the future, the present or the past. Michels brings this up on an episode with a guest named Dave Rossi, passing it on from a Tesla biographer he does not name. If true, it would suggest that strong electrical fields might open the mind to time in unusual ways.
tesla-travels-to-europe-to-persuade-hert: The inventor Nikola Tesla is said to have traveled to Europe to convince the physicist Heinrich Hertz that Hertz had got something wrong. Kurt McConnell, a former US Senate staffer, tells this as something he has read, saying "from what I've read he actually traveled to Europe." He places it in the late 1800s, as part of a story about Tesla's ideas being pushed aside.
tessa-dick-says-philip-k-dick-believed-t: The science fiction writer Philip K. Dick is said to have been fully convinced that the world is a simulation, a kind of artificial reality. Michels tells this himself, passing on what he heard from his friend Rizwan Virk, an author of books on simulation theory, who is friends with Dick's wife Tessa Dick and heard it from her. It comes up as a sign that a famous visionary mind took the idea seriously.
test-flight-of-the-sport-model-with-a-vh: Around 1988 or 1989, at a secret site in Nevada called S-4, a man named Bob Lazar says he watched a test flight of a craft he calls the sport model: it rose off the ground in silence, with "a little corona discharge glow", a faint electric glow, on its underside. He also describes a VHF radio link, a common band of radio used to talk with the craft, and the way the craft seemed to bend light around it. Lazar tells Michels this as something he saw himself, naming others present, Dennis Mariani and a man called Barry, and if true it would mean the government held and flew a craft not of human make.
testimony-to-ross-coulthart-in-washingto: In 2024 a man named Jordan Jose, who says he was taken into a secret UFO program as a child, got in touch with the journalist Ross Coulthart and flew to Washington, DC to meet him and tell his story. Jose tells this himself on the show, as the step he took to put his account on the record with a reporter who covers these claims.
tethys-sea-seabed-and-hydrothermal-vents: The ground the Giza pyramids stand on, the story goes, was once the floor of an ancient ocean called the Tethys Sea, millions of years ago. The researcher Geoffrey Drumm (also listed as Jeffrey Drum) says this in two separate episodes. He adds that vertical columns showing up in radar scans beneath the site, made by the team of a scientist named Filippo Biondi using satellite radar, "could be the remnants of some of these hydrothermal mineral vents," meaning hot mineral springs on the old seabed, with a magma chamber below them. If true, it would give the site a natural source of the chemicals his pyramid theory needs.
texas-death-row-convictions-partly-based: Two men are on death row in Texas today after being convicted partly on evidence drawn out through hypnotic regression, which means using hypnosis to bring back supposedly buried memories. Michels passes this on from the scientist John Blitch, who says he was taken by aliens himself. Michels raises it to show how much weight the law has given to memories brought back under hypnosis.
texas-instruments-worker-given-unknown-m: A worker at Texas Instruments, an American electronics company, was reportedly handed a piece of metal to study without being told what it was or where it came from. The story comes from an anonymous whistleblower who told it on a YouTube channel called The Infographics Show, and a guest who goes by the online name UAPGerb repeats it on Michels' show. He offers it as a well-known example of companies quietly working on recovered material without knowing its source.
thane-heins-coil-reverses-generator-drag: An inventor named Thane Heins made a coil that, when it powers a load, makes a generator spin faster while drawing less input current, the opposite of the usual drag that slows a generator down. The computer hacker Gary McKinnon says he built the setup himself in the UK and saw it happen: with Heins's higher-inductance coil, "the rotation speed increases and the input current goes down," which would mean getting more out than ordinary physics expects.
the-1943-philadelphia-experiment: In 1943, legend has it, the US Navy tried to teleport a ship in what is now called the Philadelphia Experiment, and it partly worked: the ship vanished, came back, and half the crew were fused into its walls. Michels tells it openly as a legend and links it to the anti-gravity researcher Thomas Townsend Brown. If it were true, the Navy would have been toying with physics far beyond anything publicly known during the Second World War.
the-1952-hottel-memo-on-a-crashed-ufo-wi: The Hottel memo, the most read document on the FBI's website, describes an Air Force officer writing to a man named Guy Hottel about a crashed UFO with an alien crew inside, according to Michels. He brings it up himself in several episodes. In one he dates it to 1952, and in others to 1950, the same year the writer Frank Scully published a book on crashed saucers. In those later tellings he describes the officer as an Air Force technical officer who came upon a crashed craft, ties it to saucers brought down by radar, and leaves out the crew.
the-1958-western-trackdown-and-a-wall-bu: Michels says that a 1958 Western called Trackdown has a story in which a man named Trump, with magnetic charisma and a cult-like following, rides into a town and promises to save it by building a wall. He raises it himself, with no source given, in an episode about whether the brain can sense the future. He offers it as an example of fiction that seems to foresee later events.
the-1995-96-official-statement-that-the-: Around 1995 or 1996, according to a researcher named Chris Ramsay, the US government came out and admitted it had run a remote viewing programme, an effort to use people's minds alone to describe distant places, while saying it had not produced useful intelligence. Ramsay recalls this loosely from memory and names no source. He puts it as the government saying, in effect, that the programme existed even as it played it down.
the-2020-scan-detects-the-queen-s-chambe: A radar scan of the Great Pyramid in Giza, Egypt, published in 2020 as a study titled "Synthetic aperture radar Doppler tomography detects undiscovered high-resolution internal structures of the Great Pyramid of Giza," picked up the horizontal shaft that runs out of the Queen's Chamber, a room inside the pyramid. The method uses radar from above to map what is inside solid stone. Jeffrey Drum, a pyramid researcher, says the shaft is detected fairly accurately, which for him shows the scan can see real hidden structures.
the-2020-scan-misses-the-king-s-chamber: A 2020 radar scan of the Great Pyramid of Giza, written up in a study titled "Synthetic aperture radar Doppler tomography detects undiscovered high-resolution internal structures of the Great Pyramid of Giza", is said not to show the King's Chamber, the main granite room high inside the pyramid. The researcher Jeffrey Drum, looking at the study's images, says, "I don't see a clear signature there for the King's Chamber." He raises it because it bears on how far the scan's claimed finds inside the pyramid can be trusted.
the-angel-of-the-lord-in-the-assyrian-ca: In the Bible, an angel of the Lord goes through the camp of the Assyrian army besieging Jerusalem on the night the siege is broken. Michels tells it himself, as one of several old accounts of nonhuman beings acting in human history. The King James Bible, published in 1611, says in the Book of Isaiah that the angel "smote in the camp of the Assyrians a hundred and fourscore and five thousand," which is 185,000 men, and that in the morning "they were all dead corpses."
the-angels-who-visited-abraham-and-lot-i: In the Bible story where angels visit the patriarch Abraham and then his nephew Lot in the city of Sodom, the angels looked strikingly beautiful, especially the one who goes to Sodom to bring Lot out. The researcher Jason Jorjani makes this point without naming a source, likening the angels to tall, fair, Nordic-looking men, the kind of beings some people describe in modern alien encounters.
the-association-of-24-retired-officials-: A group of 24 retired officials, a kind of "insurgency group" that once held very high posts in the Defense Department, the CIA (the US Central Intelligence Agency) and big aerospace companies, is said to be working to bring secret programs on UAP, the government's term for UFOs, back under government oversight. Dan Sheehan, a guest on an episode about missing scientists, says a man named Michael Phillip told him this. If true, it would mean insiders are pushing from within to bring these hidden programs into the light.
the-astronaut-photo-behind-elizabeth: There is a very famous photograph of a little girl named Elizabeth in a nice dress, sitting on a moor in England, and the story behind it is that a figure looking like an astronaut appears behind her. The UFO researcher Clas Svahn mentions the picture in passing as a well-known case, without naming a source or saying when it was taken.
the-audrey-phone-messages-2000: Sometime between 2000 and 2019, more than 80 phone calls are said to have come from a caller known as "Audrey" to all sorts of people. The UFO researcher Grant Cameron says this, passing on what he heard from others, among them Stan Romanek, a man who says he has had contact experiences, the journalist Paola Harris, and a man named Timothy Taylor. Cameron says most people don't know about the calls, and if they are what he suggests, someone or something was reaching out to many people at once by phone.
the-aviary-and-bill-moore-s-mufon-speech: In the 1980s, Michels says, a rumored group called the Aviary gave bird code names to agents who spread false information about UFOs, and he names Rick Doty and John Lear as among the people linked to it. He ties it to a UFO researcher named Bill Moore and the agents Moore described in a speech to MUFON, a large civilian UFO research group. Michels tells this himself as a "long rumored" story, without naming a source, while describing how government agencies may have muddied the UFO subject.
the-being-was-nearly-taken-to-the-zoo-be: In 1996, in the Brazilian town of Varginha, a strange living being was said to have been captured, and according to one account its handlers first thought of taking it to the zoo, and only took it to a hospital because it was an emergency. A surgeon named Italo Venturelli, who says his hospital operated on the being, tells this as a story he knows from others rather than something he saw, while admitting there is no record of it. If true, it would mean the people who caught the being had no plan for what to do with it.
the-bell-levitated-and-had-to-be-chained: The Bell, a device said to have been built for a secret Nazi German program in the 1940s, is claimed to have lifted off the ground when switched on, so its makers had to chain it down. The researcher Jason Jorjani says this without naming a source. He says the test rig around the device exists "because they realized that this thing levitates when you turn it on," which, if true, would mean the Germans had a working anti-gravity machine.
the-bell-s-alternate-name-the-beehive-19: The Bell, a device said to have been built in a secret Nazi program in the 1940s at the Skoda Works, a large arms factory, also went by a second name that means "the beehive". The researcher Jason Jorjani gives this name, in German as he pronounces it, without naming where he found it, as part of his case that Hitler's regime ran a secret flying-saucer project.
the-big-void-as-a-heat-exchanger-for-rea: The Big Void, a large empty space found inside Egypt's Great Pyramid, sits in a perfect spot to work as a heat exchanger, a device that carries heat away, for reactions taking place in the Grand Gallery, the tall sloping passage inside the pyramid. The researcher Jeffrey Drum offers this as his own idea, naming no source, as part of his case that the pyramid was a machine rather than a tomb.
the-black-mailbox-began-as-a-vague-landm: The black mailbox, a lone mailbox in the Nevada desert that later became a famous spot for UFO watchers, first became a landmark because of an offhand answer in 1989. Bob Lazar, a well-known figure in UFO circles whom Jesse Michels spent two days with, says he simply told people the sightings were "around the black mailbox" to keep the location vague.
the-blue-book-briefing-folders-of-160-re: A secret Army team at Fort Meade, Maryland, which practised remote viewing (trying to describe faraway places and things by the mind alone), kept two blue briefing folders holding 160 of its successes, according to Joe McMoneagle, who says he was one of its remote viewers. He calls them "the Blue Book, the blue briefing books", a name not to be confused with the Air Force's old UFO study. He tells it as proof that the work produced results worth showing to officials.
the-boat-pits-as-acid-filled-circuit-bre: A pyramid researcher named Geoffrey Drumm says the boat pits, long trenches cut into the rock beside the Great Pyramid at Giza in Egypt, once held acid and worked as circuit breakers. He tells Michels that "inside the boat pits adjacent to the Great Pyramid, we find more sulfate compounds", which he takes as leftover traces of that chemistry. If true, the pyramid would have been part of an electrical machine rather than only a tomb.
the-breathing-hole-on-the-object-2012: In 2012 a diver exploring a strange object on the floor of the Baltic Sea is said to have seen a hole in it with a milky substance pouring out, which would hint that the thing is more than ordinary rock. The treasure hunter Dennis Asberg, whose team found the object, tells it on the diver's behalf, repeating what his fellow diver Stefan Hogeborn told him about the dusty surface and the milk-like stream coming "from this hole."
the-bubble-energy-field-mapped-over-the-: The owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property known for reports of strange events, says that a dome-like "bubble" of energy sits over the land and has been "mapped using lidar," a laser scanning tool, "and other platforms." He speaks as the man who owns the ranch and runs the work there, and if true the bubble would be a measurable physical sign of whatever happens on the property.
the-business-plot-against-fdr-1930: In the 1930s, wealthy business interests linked to the Morgan and DuPont families planned to raise an army of about 500,000 people, march on Washington and remove President Franklin Roosevelt from office by force. A researcher named Jason Simosa tells it without naming a source, and he names a man called Smedley Butler as part of the story. If true, it would mean that powerful private interests in America once planned to overthrow an elected president.
the-cia-as-the-brainchild-of-brown-broth: The CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency founded in the 1940s, was the idea of the people at Brown Brothers Harriman, a private Wall Street bank, according to a guest named Dan Sheehan. Sheehan says it without naming a source: the agency "was the brainchild of the people at Brown Brothers Harriman." If true, it would mean American intelligence was shaped from the start by private banking interests.
the-cia-convenes-the-robertson-panel-195: In 1953 the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency, convened the Robertson Panel, a group of experts brought together to look at UFO reports. A researcher named Bryce Zabel brings it up as a turning point in his history of Hollywood, the CIA and UFOs, on his way to talking about a CIA officer named Chase Brandon. He mentions it in passing, without naming a source, as the moment the agency's handling of the subject began.
the-cia-showed-elizondo-mris-of-uap-witn: The CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency, is said to have shown brain scans (MRIs) of people who had run-ins with UFOs, also called UAP or unidentified anomalous phenomena, and these scans showed differences in the caudate putamen, a region deep in the brain. The account comes up in Michels's documentary about Lue Elizondo, a former Pentagon official, and is attributed to Garry Nolan, listed as a witness, who says first-hand that "the CIA came to my office and then they showed me MRIs of some of these people and most of those people had interactions with UFOs." If true, it would mean these encounters leave a mark on the brain.
the-city-of-london-s-remembrancer-sits-i: The City of London, the old financial district that runs its own local government, is said to have an official called the Remembrancer, the only unelected person allowed to sit in Parliament. The UFO researcher Jay Anderson brings this up from the documentary The Spider's Web: Britain's Second Empire, as a sign of how much quiet power the City holds over the British state.
the-collins-elite-as-a-fundamentalist-fa: Inside the US government there is said to be a deeply embedded group called the Collins Elite, made up of fundamentalist Christians who refuse to study UFOs scientifically because they think the phenomenon is demonic. Michels passes this on, linking it to Luis Elizondo, a former Pentagon official who studied UFO reports, and to To The Stars Academy, a private UFO research company. If true, it would mean religious belief inside government is holding back serious study of the subject.
the-dirt-road-leads-straight-to-the-army: A small dirt road near the place in Varginha, Brazil, where strange beings are said to have been seen in 1996 is said to lead straight to EsSA, the Brazilian army's school for sergeants. The surgeon Carlos de Souza, whose hospital is said to have been involved in the case, says he didn't know this himself. He was told it by the documentary maker James Fox and by people in the UFO research community. It matters to the story because it would put the army right next to the scene.
the-dogon-s-knowledge-of-the-sirius-bina: The Dogon, a people of Mali in West Africa, are said to have known in their own tradition that Sirius, the brightest star in the night sky, is really two bodies, Sirius A and a hidden companion, Sirius B. Michels tells this himself, drawing on The Sirius Mystery, a book by the writer Robert Temple, saying they "somehow, you know, in their tradition knew" about the pair. If true, it would mean the Dogon had knowledge of the sky that they could not have gained with the naked eye.
the-drones-were-orbs-from-the-sea-now-ov: The so-called drones reported over the United States in 2024 and 2025 were not drones at all but glowing orbs that came from the sea, and they are now showing up over Europe. Chris Bledsoe, a man who says UFOs come to him and whom NASA has studied, says this from his own experience: "Those aren't drones."
the-electromagnetic-black-project-at-the: Between 1990 and 1993, at a base overseas, a former sergeant named Dan Sherman says a secret, unacknowledged program, what the military calls a black project, was running on electromagnetic work. Sherman, who says the National Security Agency, the US agency that intercepts communications, hired him to speak with aliens, tells Michels he was there and that the black project "was a very interesting" thing in itself, without giving much more.
the-endless-frontier-read-as-working-bac: Science, The Endless Frontier, a 1945 report by Vannevar Bush, a top American wartime science official, takes on a new meaning if you read it as if the United States already had technology derived from aliens, says Michels. He offers this reading himself as a theory, not something the report says. If it were right, the plan for postwar American science would have been partly a way of working back from alien technology.
the-et-s-account-galactic-monitors-of-li: A being from another world, questioned at S4, a reported secret site near Area 51 in Nevada, is said to have explained that it belonged to a group of beings "from different star systems in our galaxy" who watch over life and were sent by "God." A lawyer named Dan Sheehan passes this on second-hand from interview index cards he credits as the record of the questioning, naming his source in one episode as Oscar Wolf and in another as Albert Stein, whom he places in the 1950s or 60s. If true, it would be the visitors' own account of why they are here.
the-face-peeler-legend-of-the-peruvian-a: In the Peruvian Amazon there is a local legend about a "face peeler," and it only goes back to the mid 1980s, not earlier. The researcher Tim Alberino says this without naming a source, pointing out how recent the legend is.
the-fake-l9-incident-document-1977: Michels says a fake document was made up describing an "L9 incident" at Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota, set one day before an encounter that two men named Michael and Mario say they had there. Michels tells this himself in 1977's context, citing a man named Richard Doty in connection with the document. The point is that a planted false record could muddy what the two men say they really saw.
the-family-the-fellowship-network-in-gov: An organization called The Family, also known as The Fellowship, was founded in the 1930s and grew into an influential network in Washington after the Second World War, according to the researcher Jason Simosa. He tells Jesse Michels this from his own reading, leaning on the journalist Jeff Sharlet and a figure named Alonzo McDonald, and ties it to an alleged 1930s plot against President Franklin Roosevelt. He raises it as part of his case that a quiet network of powerful people sits behind official secrecy, including on UFOs.
the-fenced-vacant-lot-where-the-beings-a: In Varginha, a town in Brazil where strange beings were reportedly seen in 1996, the empty lot where they appeared is said to still be there today, fenced off but still visited by people. A surgeon named Italo Venturelli mentions this on Jesse Michels' show, passing on what he has been told. He adds that there is a project to research the spot, which would matter if the beings were real.
the-flying-house-of-loreto-1800: In the past, people reported seeing what they took to be flying houses, such as the Flying House of Loreto, a holy house in Loreto, Italy, said to have traveled through the air. The religious studies researcher Diana Pasulka mentions it without naming a source. She offers it as an example of how people of earlier times described strange things in the sky in the terms of their own world.
the-g-engines-are-coming-article-arrives: The story is about an old magazine article called "The G Engines Are Coming," which by its title promised engines that could master gravity. A journalist named Nick Cook, who worked at Jane's Defence Weekly, a British military trade publication, says the article simply "showed up on my desk," because people often sent material to Jane's. For Cook it was a sign that serious people in the aircraft industry once openly worked on antigravity, and he ties it to a man named George S. Trimble. Michels brings up the same article in a later episode, dating it to 1956 and calling it "really interesting." He leaves Cook out and instead links it to people named Michael Gladish, Stanley Deser and Richard Arnowitt. Cook tells it as something he handled himself, while Michels tells it as something he has read about. If the article meant what its title says, it would show antigravity research was being discussed in the open in the 1950s before it went quiet.
the-gadarene-demoniac-and-the-appointed-: In a Bible story, Jesus and his disciples came to the land of Gadara and met a possessed man whom the locals chained up in the tombs because he would scream, and the spirits in him spoke of an "appointed time." The researcher Tim Alberino retells it from the New Testament gospels and ties it to the Book of Enoch, an ancient religious text, in the translation by R. H. Charles, to suggest the spirits knew of a set day of judgment awaiting them.
the-golden-age-of-general-relativity-bah: The sudden boom in research on Einstein's theory of gravity in the 1950s and 60s, known as the golden age of general relativity, makes no sense on its face, according to the researcher Eric Weinstein. He says it is really a story about two men, Agnew Bahnson and Roger Babson, and he starts to describe what they appear to have been before his sentence breaks off. He raises it because, to him, it hints that someone was quietly pushing gravity research forward.
the-gran-sasso-laboratory-and-the-gerda-: Under the Gran Sasso mountain in Italy there is a physics laboratory where an experiment called Gerda searched for the Majorana particle, a long-sought particle that would be its own antiparticle, and, as the story goes, it has still not found it. Filippo Biondi, a guest who appears on an episode about structures said to lie beneath the Egyptian pyramids, mentions this in passing, relaying what he has heard about the work there.
the-great-year-documentary-proposes-a-bi: A documentary called The Great Year proposes that our sun has a binary companion, a partner star it circles with. In this view, that slow dance explains the "great year," a long cycle in which the sky gradually shifts. The researcher Matt LaCroix describes the film's idea and notes that some thought the companion was the star Sirius. Clips from the documentary's own narrator also play on the episode, saying "the binary model confirms all of our celestial observations without the need for excessive torque or epicycle type explanations," meaning it avoids complicated workarounds. If true, it would change how the ancient sky cycles are explained.
the-holy-grail-as-a-technology-of-regene: The Holy Grail, the sacred vessel of medieval European legend, may have been a real technology for healing and renewing life rather than only a cup or a symbol. The researcher Randall Carlson offers this as his own reading of the Grail romances, the medieval tales by the poets Chrétien de Troyes, Robert de Boron and Wolfram von Eschenbach, whose poem Parzival tells of the Grail. "I think it's a technology," Carlson tells Michels, which would mean the old stories remember a lost device.
the-host-s-own-rectangular-craft-sightin: Michels says he has himself seen a rectangular craft in the sky. He mentions it only in passing, without saying where or when, while talking with a whistleblower about artificial intelligence and alien technology.
the-hosts-saw-a-green-orb-with-elizondo-: Michels says that one night in 2024, while visiting the Wyoming home of Luis Elizondo, a former Pentagon official and author of the book Imminent, he and his crew saw a green orb in the sky alongside Elizondo. Michels tells it as his own sighting, reminding Elizondo of it on camera. Telling it again a few months later to another guest, he describes it as a green fireball that shot out into the sky.
the-hughes-group-s-cia-covert-actions-th: The business group around the billionaire Howard Hughes did secret operations for the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency, including the Glomar Explorer, a deep-sea ship, and may even have carried out the killings of the Kennedys in the 1960s. The researcher Matthew Pines says this on the show without naming a source. If true, it would tie one private group to the government's most hidden work, including its UFO secrets.
the-jailer-s-file-submariners-on-lsd-200: A computer hacker named Gary McKinnon says that, while breaking into US military computers around 2000 to 2002, he found the jailer's file on one base, the record kept by the officer who runs its jail. In it, he says, were men who worked on submarines taking LSD, a powerful hallucinogenic drug. McKinnon tells Michels this from his own hacking as one of the stranger things he stumbled on.
the-jasons-solve-dod-problems-in-summer-: The JASONs are a group of top scientists who advise the US government, and their job is to work through problems that the Department of Defense hands them, in studies held over the summer. A Pentagon scientist named Eric W. Davis describes the group this way to Jesse Michels, saying plainly: "They're supposed to solve problems that the DoD gives to them." He brings it up to show how the military gets outside scientists to take on its hardest questions.
the-kandahar-giant-seen-on-a-cargo-palle: A giant said to have been captured in Afghanistan was later loaded onto a cargo pallet, and a cargo pilot who saw it says the first thing that hit him was a smell like body odor and death. According to the pilot, the being had red hair, pale white skin, six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot. The filmmaker and researcher Tim Alberino relays this account, which he heard secondhand. In another version he puts the loading at Bagram Airfield in 2005 and credits the author Steve Quayle and Quayle's book True Legends.
the-kgb-gives-the-tsar-s-box-seat-to-mal: In Moscow in 1982, officers of the KGB, the Soviet secret police, are said to have stopped Henry Kissinger, the former US Secretary of State, from taking the seat in the old royal box of the Tsar, telling him, "Henry, not tonight. That seat is for Dr. Malmgren." Harold Malmgren, an economist who advised American presidents, tells this himself as the man the seat was kept for, to show how much weight the Soviets gave him.
the-king-s-chamber-as-an-acoustic-cataly: The King's Chamber, a stone room deep inside the Great Pyramid at Giza in Egypt, and the small antechamber in front of it were, in this theory, "acoustic catalyst chambers" that used sound to turn sulfur dioxide and oxygen into sulfur trioxide, in order to produce sulfuric acid. The theory belongs to a guest named Geoffrey Drumm, who presents it as his own reading of the pyramid without naming a source. If true, the Great Pyramid would have been a chemical plant rather than a tomb.
the-king-s-chamber-shafts-end-horizontal: The narrow shafts that run out of the King's Chamber, the main granite room inside the Great Pyramid of Giza in Egypt, turn level at their far ends instead of climbing all the way out at an angle. The researcher Geoffrey Drumm says this, citing "the original archaeological documentation" without naming it further. He offers it as support for his own idea about what the pyramid was really built to do.
the-lacerta-files-swedish-documents-abou: The Lacerta files are said to be documents from Sweden about reptilians, meaning reptile-like beings. Michels mentions them in passing, praising "an amazing piece" on them that he connects with his guest, Chris Ramsay. He gives no more detail about what the files say.
the-lone-stars-group-after-aawsap-2010: After AAWSAP, a Pentagon-funded program that studied unexplained aerial phenomena, wound down around 2010, some of its scientists formed an informal group called the Lone Stars. The researcher Jason Simosa tells this without naming a source, linking it to the computer scientist Jacques Vallée and the physicists Eric W. Davis and Hal Puthoff. If true, it would mean the study of these phenomena carried on privately after official funding ended.
the-luxor-temple-back-chamber-reserved-f: A huge chamber at the back of Luxor Temple in Egypt was, as far as is known, reserved only for the pharaoh Amenhotep, so he could connect with his father, the god Amun-Ra. The researcher Luke Caverns, who has been there, tells it as the temple's purpose.
the-man-in-the-red-plaid-shirt-was-a-man: A man in a red plaid shirt that John Blitch, a scientist who worked for DARPA, the Pentagon's advanced research agency, remembered meeting at Daniels Park in Colorado in 1995 was really a mantis-like being in a red uniform. Blitch tells Jesse Michels this came out under hypnotic regression, a hypnosis session meant to recover memories, which he links to the researcher Leo Sprinkle, and he says it showed a dream about a bug and a mountain bike incident were one single event. In one telling he dates the regression itself to 2018.
the-man-in-the-shroud-of-turin-was-alive: The man whose image is on the Shroud of Turin, a linen cloth kept in Turin, Italy, said to have wrapped Jesus after the crucifixion, was still alive when he was wrapped in it. The researcher Randall Carlson says this flatly, "The man in the shroud was living," drawing on the cloth and the Gospels, the New Testament books that tell Jesus's life, without naming any other source. If true, it would change the story of a man who is said to have died before burial.
the-microbiologist-leak-experts-judge-th: In 2023 a document turned up online, written by an anonymous author presented as a microbiologist, a scientist who studies tiny living things such as bacteria. The UFO researcher and video maker Chris Ramsay says that the people who studied it think the writer is "definitely like doctorate level microbiology". He doesn't name these people. If they are right, the leak would come from someone with real expertise and not an amateur.
the-military-police-commander-s-witch-hu: In 1996, in Varginha, Brazil, the town where others on the show describe a creature being captured and a soldier falling ill and dying, the commander of the military police barracks went after a doctor who had worked there and carried out a drainage procedure, according to a surgeon named Ahmed Foratu. Foratu, who says his hospital was part of the events, tells Michels that a medical complication should be looked into, but not with "such a fervorous desire to perform a witch hunt", and that the doctor "spent years having to explain this to the justice system". In his telling, the doctor was made to carry the blame for what happened to the soldier.
the-monte-carlo-group-at-the-top-of-the-: A lawyer named Dan Sheehan says there is "a thing called the Monte Carlo group" sitting "at the top" of the Knights of Malta, an old Catholic order of knights, and he places Henry Kissinger, the former US Secretary of State, and George Bush Senior, the former US president, within it. Sheehan tells it as something he knows himself, and if true it would mean a small, hidden circle sits above a well-known religious order.
the-moon-as-a-logical-refuge-for-a-space: If an advanced civilization able to travel in space saw a catastrophe coming, the logical place to take refuge would be the Moon. That is the reasoning of a researcher named Randall Carlson, who makes the case himself on the show. He ties it to the Younger Dryas, a sudden upheaval at the end of the last Ice Age that he links to a comet, and says NASA, the US space agency, has put forward similar scenarios for a refuge that we ourselves might build on the Moon.
the-moon-as-an-anomalous-alien-spacecraf: The Moon may be an unusual alien spacecraft rather than a natural body. Michels says much of an interview he recorded in 2023 in Decatur, near Atlanta, with the researcher Randall Carlson was about this idea, and that it was never released. If true, it would mean something artificial has been orbiting Earth all along.
the-moon-rang-like-a-bell-during-the-apo: During the Apollo missions, the US space agency NASA's flights to the Moon around 1969, astronauts left seismometers, instruments that measure tremors, on the surface, and when a used rocket stage hit the Moon it reportedly rang like a bell. Michels tells it himself on several episodes, naming Apollo 10 in one, Apollo 12 in another, and saying the booster was crashed on purpose and the Moon rang for three hours, leaving NASA very confused. The researcher Randall Carlson says NASA gathered three or four years of data showing the Moon has a long vibrational train. The philosopher Jason Jorjani says the test was then repeated on purpose, he thinks on Apollo 13. It comes up on an episode titled The Moon Is An Alien Spaceship, as a hint that the Moon may not be what it seems inside.
the-moon-s-low-density-old-material-and-: This is the idea that the Moon does not fit the usual explanation, which is that it formed from material knocked off the Earth by a huge impact. Michels raises it himself, without naming a source: the Moon is much less dense than the Earth, and its material is older than the Earth, even though it supposedly came from the Earth. The researcher Randall Carlson argues it on different grounds in the same episode. He says it is very hard, mathematically, to get from a ring of debris around the Earth to the Moon we see today, and he doubts the other theory too, that the Earth captured the Moon. The questions are raised in an episode that asks whether the Moon could be an alien craft.
the-moon-was-placed-or-towed-into-positi: The Moon may not be where it is by accident: it may have been put there on purpose, or set in place. That idea comes from a man named Timothy Taylor, and it is passed on by Chris Bledsoe, a man who says he attracts UFOs, who recalls that Taylor hinted the Moon "was set there" and asks whether it is "an illusion." If true, someone or something would have arranged the Moon itself.
the-nine-as-a-psychological-warfare-expe: The Nine, a supposed council of alien beings that a group at the Round Table Foundation in Maine claimed to contact in the 1950s, may have been a side operation or an early psychological warfare experiment rather than real contact. The researcher Greg Malatzi raises this idea, linking it to the writer Peter Levenda. If true, it would mean the messages were a test of what people could be made to believe.
the-nine-identified-as-a-ufo-in-low-eart: A group of beings known as the Nine, first reached in the 1950s through the work of a researcher named Andrija Puharich, came to be identified as the residents of a UFO circling in low Earth orbit. A researcher named Peter Levenda says that this same group was later contacted by the self-described psychic Uri Geller, and he gives no source for it. Told this way, it would mean that the same beings in orbit kept talking to people on the ground for decades.
the-nine-instruct-building-a-copper-fara: In the 1950s, at the Round Table Foundation, a research group in Maine, a set of beings calling themselves the Nine, who were said to speak through a psychic, reportedly told the researchers that for a clearer signal they should put the psychic inside a copper Faraday cage, a metal enclosure that blocks outside electrical interference. The researcher Greg Malatzi tells it from the group's own tape recordings, summing up the message as: "if you want a clearer feed, a clearer transmission, you have to put the psychic in a Faraday cage." If true, it would mean the supposed contacts were giving practical, technical instructions.
the-nine-s-message-surveillance-of-earth: Starting in 1952, at the Round Table Foundation, a research group in Maine, a group of beings called "the Nine" are said to have passed on a message in a series of sessions: they had been watching Earth and had seen the bad things going on here, wars and nuclear weapons among them. The researcher Greg Malatzi gives this summary from the written records of those sessions, which are linked to a man named Dr. Vinod. If true, beings from beyond Earth would be keeping watch on us because of our wars and our nuclear weapons.
the-nine-say-they-are-behind-nuclear-bas: In the 1970s a group calling itself "The Nine", said to be a council of non-human intelligences speaking through human contacts, claimed it was behind many of the UFO sightings at nuclear weapons bases. An unnamed researcher on the show says this, drawing on tapes of contact sessions run by the scientist Andrija Puharich, whom the episode describes as having worked with the CIA. According to the researcher, The Nine say "we're kind of behind a lot of the sightings" at nuclear bases, which would give a claimed author for those incidents.
the-nine-seance-in-maine-new-year-s-eve-: A seance with nine people was held in Maine around New Year's Eve 1952 to 1953, and it is said to have opened contact with a group of beings called the Nine. The author Peter Levenda tells this without naming a source, linking it to the researcher Andrija Puharich and to the inventor Arthur Young and his wife Ruth Forbes Paine Young. In a later episode Michels repeats it, citing Levenda, and adds that the nine people at the table were members of the elite, which would mean powerful figures were involved in early channelled contact.
the-nine-send-puharich-and-schlemmer-to-: Between 1974 and 1976, a group calling itself "the Nine", said to be non-human intelligences speaking through recorded sessions, reportedly told the researcher Andrija Puharich and the medium Phyllis Schlemmer to travel to Egypt, the Middle East and Russia. A guest on Michels' show, who is not named, tells this as a summary drawn from Puharich's session tapes, the recordings of those sessions, and also names a man called John Whitmore. If true, it would mean the messages were directing real journeys around the world.
the-non-terrestrial-officers-spreadsheet: Gary McKinnon, a hacker from London who says he broke into US military computers between 2000 and 2002, says that inside a US Navy system he found a spreadsheet titled "non-terrestrial officers," along with records of transfers of unusual chemicals like molybdenum and of ship-to-ship and fleet-to-fleet transfers. McKinnon, telling what he says he saw himself, reads "non-terrestrial" as meaning off the Earth rather than alien, perhaps space-based marines or a secret space force, and mentions Jesse Michels and a man named James Fox in the telling. If true, it would point to a hidden fleet and supply chain in space.
the-nrol-16-patch-and-ron-pandolfi-2005: The 2005 launch of NROL-16, a satellite mission of the National Reconnaissance Office, the US agency that runs spy satellites, came with a mission patch, an embroidered emblem, that ties in to a man named Ron Pandolfi. Michels relays this from a presentation by John Ramirez, a former CIA officer, who described the case as a sign that this kind of hidden symbolism continued into the 21st century.
the-occult-is-behind-the-cover-up-of-gia: The remains of giants are being hidden, and the occult, meaning secret mystical groups or practices, is behind that hiding. Tim Alberino, who comes on the podcast to talk about a twelve-foot giant he says was captured in Afghanistan, states this as his own belief and does not give a source for it.
the-open-doors-von-neumann-s-fear-at-his: The mathematician John von Neumann is said to have died in 1957 gripped by fear over something he had come to understand, a story tied to the idea that some lines of physics were deliberately steered into dead ends. The writer Whitley Strieber brings it up without naming a source, and says he turned von Neumann's death into a short story of his own called The Open Doors.
the-osirion-at-abydos-predates-seti-i: The Osirion, an ancient stone structure at Abydos in Egypt, was not built by the pharaoh Seti I but is far older than him. The researcher Luke Caverns says this is his own belief, naming no source. If true, it would mean a much earlier people built it.
the-osiris-shaft-scan-picks-up-something: A scan of the ground at the Osiris Shaft, a deep ancient shaft cut into the Giza plateau near the Egyptian pyramids, picks up something else on the shaft's left side, according to the researcher Jeffrey Drum. He describes this to Jesse Michels as part of a recent project using radar-style scans to look for hidden structures deep underground. If it holds up, it would hint at more buried construction beneath the plateau than is known.
the-pineapple-target-during-a-remote-vie: During a remote viewing session, the practice of trying to sense a hidden target with the mind, a friend of Michels drew a little spiky thing, and the target turned out to be a pineapple. Michels tells this himself, saying he was there with the remote viewer Joe McMoneagle and experienced it first-hand.
the-plants-told-the-amazonians-how-to-ma: Peoples of the Amazon say the plants themselves taught them how to make ayahuasca, a psychedelic brew made from two plants. The neuroscientist Andrew Gallimore reports this without naming a source: asked how they found the recipe, "they will say well the plants told us." If taken at face value, it would mean knowledge can come from the plants or from the states they open.
the-prince-of-liechtenstein-walked-up-to: The Prince of Liechtenstein, ruler of the small European country, is said to have walked up to a UFO somewhere in the mountains. The lawyer Dan Sheehan says the wealthy philanthropist Laurance Rockefeller told him and the Harvard psychiatrist John Mack about it. Rockefeller supposedly said his friend the prince's sighting was the reason he was so sure UFOs were real.
the-ra-channelings-and-the-law-of-one-19: In the 1980s, a woman named Carla Rueckert and a partner the parapsychologist Jeffrey Mishlove calls Bharich held sessions in which messages said to come from a being called Ra were channeled, meaning spoken through a person in a trance. Mishlove tells Michels that Rueckert published these messages as The Ra Material and The Law of One. He brings them up as a source of teachings that some take as contact with a non-human intelligence.
the-range-dod-testing-playground-in-the-: Around 2001, a range in the California desert served as "a giant playground" for the Department of Defense and its private aerospace partners to test weapons technology. Jake Barber, a former military helicopter pilot, describes it from his own time working there. He brings it up to set the scene for the secret work he says he was later part of.
the-remote-viewing-photo-protocol-and-it: In remote viewing tests, where a person tries to describe a hidden photograph using the mind alone, a study of the attempts is said to have found an overall hit rate of 35 percent, a number that came up again and again. Michels tells this himself on an episode with a guest named Eric Wargo, citing a researcher named Jessica Utts and saying the result was repeated at the Stanford Research Institute, the University of Edinburgh and the Rhine Research Institute in North Carolina. If true, it would mean the mind can gather information beyond the ordinary senses.
the-retrieved-craft-may-have-been-a-livi: A craft said to have been recovered by the US government may itself have been a living being, not just a machine. A former Pentagon research scientist named John Blitch raises the idea on the show, in connection with claims from a man named Jake Barber, and offers it as his own thought rather than something he saw.
the-rosicrucian-enlightenment-and-the-in: Michels holds that the Rosicrucians, a secretive mystical movement in early modern Europe, fed into the Invisible College, a circle of early English scientists that included the chemist Robert Boyle. He brings it up himself, in a talk with the Pentagon whistleblower Matthew Brown, by recommending The Rosicrucian Enlightenment, a book by the historian Frances Yates: "There's a great book called the Rosicrucian Enlightenment." The point is that modern science may have grown out of hidden, esoteric traditions.
the-sapphire-project-and-hal-puthoff: Something called the Sapphire project, tied to the physicist Hal Puthoff, appeared briefly with big promises about reaching the stars and then disappeared. Jay Anderson mentions it in passing without naming a source, as an example of bold projects that show up and vanish.
the-sar-team-s-first-international-confe: In June 2025, the team using SAR, a satellite radar that can image what lies beneath the ground, held its first international conference in Malta, according to a researcher named Jeffrey Drum. Drum tells Michels he was involved because the organizers "were familiar with my work", and he links the team to a researcher named Filippo Biondi and a man named Armando. He brings it up as part of their claim that radar shows a large energy system under the pyramids of Egypt.
the-septuagint-reads-angels-of-god-in-ge: In the Septuagint, the ancient Greek translation of the Hebrew Bible, the passage in Genesis 6 where heavenly beings take human wives does not say "the sons of God". It says "the angels of God". The researcher Tim Alberino makes this point himself, without naming a source, as evidence that the ancient translators understood those beings to be angels.
the-serapeum-as-a-sonohydrogen-plant: The Serapeum, an underground complex of tunnels and huge stone boxes at Saqqara in Egypt, was, in this theory, a plant that used ultrasound to break water molecules apart into hydrogen and oxygen. A guest named Geoffrey Drumm offers this as his own hypothesis, without naming a source. If true, the site would have been an ancient machine for making hydrogen.
the-shroud-image-was-made-by-a-burst-of-: The image on the Shroud of Turin, a linen cloth many believe wrapped the body of Jesus after his death in Jerusalem, is said to have been made at the moment of resurrection, when a dead body turned into a being of light, a change linked here to a burst of neutrons. The author Whitley Strieber, known for writing about his own encounters with strange beings, puts this forward in his own words and ties it to his book given as Jesus and New Vision. He calls the shroud "the single strangest thing on planet Earth" because, he says, it "records the moment a human being whose body had expired transformed into a being of light."
the-sphinx-as-a-dynastic-monument-carved: The Great Sphinx at Giza, Egypt, is a monument of the pharaohs' era that was carved onto a rock outcrop already standing in its enclosure, according to the researcher Jeffrey Drum. Drum offers this as his own view, without naming a source. It would mean the statue is younger than the stone it sits on, leaving room for something older at the site.
the-ss-never-surrendered-1945: When Germany surrendered in 1945, the SS, Hitler's elite Nazi force, never formally surrendered with it, says the researcher Jason Jorjani, pointing to the signed surrender papers: "The SS is not included in the German instruments of surrender." Jorjani offers this point while describing what he calls Hitler's secret UFO programme, and if he is right, the SS as a body would never have officially stood down.
the-sun-as-a-scalar-wave-generator-sendi: Michels wonders aloud whether the Sun might be a scalar wave generator, scalar waves being a proposed kind of energy wave outside standard physics, and whether we might be getting information from it. He offers this as his own speculation while talking with the philosopher James Madden about consciousness and Plato's cave, and he links it to ideas that he says people high in government seem to back. If true, the Sun would be a source of information, not only of light and heat.
the-teacher-born-in-george-washington-s-: In 1965, on a desert firing area called Range Two in Indian Springs Valley, Nevada, a pale alien being known as the Teacher is said to have spoken of a Native American friend from long ago, the Teacher having been "born when George Washington was born." Charles Hall, a man who says he spent three years among tall white aliens in the Nevada desert, tells this himself, and if true it would mean these beings live for centuries and have known people on Earth for that long.
the-telepathy-tapes-nonverbal-autistic-i: The Telepathy Tapes, a 2024 podcast, reports on dozens of autistic people who cannot speak and who seem to share a telepathic link with a caregiver, usually their mother. The researcher Matthew Pines retells it, crediting the work of Diane Hennacy Powell, a researcher who studies these patients. He calls it the "remarkable story" of people who report "a telepathic connection" with one caregiver. The scientist Don Hoffman does not name the podcast but says he has looked at studies where an autistic child "is able to read what's in their mother's mind." He says some of the designs seemed "pretty rigorous." Retired Navy admiral Tim Gallaudet mentions Powell's work with autistic patients as her own long-running research. The former Senate staffer Kirk McConnell adds that these people seem to connect with each other "across vast distances." Michels, in his own telling, describes the children communicating and gathering on what they call "the hill". If true, minds would be able to reach each other without words or senses.
the-thera-santorini-theory-of-atlantis: One theory says the lost city of Atlantis was really a memory of the island of Thera, today Santorini in Greece, and its huge volcanic eruption. The researcher Randall Carlson brings up this theory and points out that the eruption happened about 900 years before Plato, the ancient Greek philosopher who wrote down the Atlantis story.
the-three-body-problem-as-required-readi: A Chinese science fiction novel, The Three-Body Problem by Liu Cixin, became mandatory reading for many senior US national security advisers, and high-level talks about disclosing what the government knows about UFOs revolved around it. Michels tells this twice, both times crediting a source named Pippa Malmgren, who relayed it to him, and once places it during the Bush administration, when key federal officials were urged to read the book. He raises it because it would mean officials were using a novel to think through what contact or disclosure might look like.
the-three-girls-who-saw-the-creature-wer: In 1996, in the Brazilian town of Varginha, three girls said they saw a strange creature, and afterwards, the story goes, they were criticised and bullied so badly that they had to change schools. The surgeon Italo Venturelli, whose hospital is said to have treated a being from the same event, tells it second-hand, passing on what nurses who know the girls told him: "They've had it rough because they're criticized."
the-tic-tac-as-an-unrepeatable-anomaly-t: The "Tic Tac", a white oval object shaped like the mint that pilots reported seeing, could not be repeated, yet it plainly needed to be studied. The researcher Deep Prasad makes this argument on Michels' show, drawing on a book called The Evolution of Science and the Interactive Universe. His point is that the scientific method of Francis Bacon, the English philosopher, depends on repeating experiments, so a one-time event like this one shows where that method falls short.
the-top-hat-craft-with-projectile-holes-: At S-4, which he describes as a secret site in Nevada, around 1988 and 1989, one craft he calls the top hat had a hole in its rim that looked like it had been shot by a projectile, with the metal clearly bent outward as if hit from below; he also speaks of another he calls the Jell-O mold. Bob Lazar, who says he worked there and saw them, adds that a movie about him got it wrong by showing two holes instead of one. If true, it would mean someone once shot one of these craft.
the-trinity-test-as-the-hinge-point-that: On July 16, 1945, in the New Mexico desert, the physicist J. Robert Oppenheimer's team set off the first atomic bomb, a test Oppenheimer named Trinity, and Michels frames it as the turning point that drew the UFO phenomenon to Earth. He tells it himself, without naming a source, in an episode about Air Force veterans who say they were abducted, as if humanity's new power to destroy itself caught someone's attention.
the-underworld-in-the-kalmyk-epic-jangar: Jangar, the old epic poem of the Kalmyk people of Kalmykia, a republic in southern Russia, is said to describe an underworld: "How creatures live there, how they communicate, how they come to the surface." This is told by a former president of a Russian republic, who is not named in the episode, as an old local account of beings living below ground.
the-vatican-archives-head-knows-about-th: The head of the Vatican's archives knows about hidden material held there, says a lawyer named Dan Sheehan, because Sheehan himself sent letters from the headquarters of the Jesuits, a Catholic religious order, asking for access on behalf of President Jimmy Carter. Sheehan tells this as the one who made the request, and in another telling, in which he mentions a woman named Marcia Smith, he dates it to 1977 and says the Vatican said no.
the-vatican-s-sun-cross-and-pine-cone: The pope wears an ancient sun cross symbol on his cloak, and a giant pine cone sculpture stands in front of the Vatican, the seat of the Catholic Church. The researcher Matt LaCroix points this out without naming a source, saying the Church carries the very same symbols as much older cultures.
the-wow-signal-1977: In August 1977 a radio telescope at Ohio State University picked up a strange radio signal that became famous as the Wow signal, found by a man named Gerry Eman, Michels says. He mentions it himself in passing in two episodes, once with the astronomer Beatriz Villarroel, as a well-known example of a possible signal from beyond Earth.
theoretical-physicists-at-s4-had-exhaust: Around 1988 or 1989, the theoretical physicists at S4, a secret site in Nevada, had tried every way to explain the craft there through gravity and gotten nowhere, says Bob Lazar, who says he worked there himself. "They kept going over that road and never got anywhere," he tells Michels, in a talk that also brings up the researcher Eric Weinstein and a man named Eric W. Davis. If true, the scientists studying the craft had hit a dead end in understanding how it worked.
theory-non-humans-seed-and-genetically-a: Non-human beings plant life on Earth and on other planets and adjust it genetically, then come back about every thousand years to bring people new things such as farming, irrigation, metalworking or religion. A researcher named Chris Ramsay puts this forward as a theory, without naming a source. If it were so, the big leaps in human civilisation would be the work of visitors, not our own.
theory-that-directed-energy-forces-trans: Jordan Jose, a man who says he was taken into a secret UFO program as a child, puts forward the idea that some craft come from another dimension, and that hitting them with directed energy, meaning focused beams of power, forces them "to take form and become bound to this dimension." He offers it as his own view, and if true it would explain how such objects could be pinned down and brought to the ground.
theory-that-nuclear-fuels-were-used-to-a: The idea is that in the 1950s, nuclear fuels at US nuclear bases were used to alter gravity, and so perhaps time, since general relativity, Einstein's theory, links the two. Michels floats this himself, drawing on the Netflix series Dark, as a possible reason why UFOs would be watching nuclear sites.
theory-that-oppenheimer-s-security-heari: Michels puts forward the idea that the security hearing against J. Robert Oppenheimer, the physicist who led the atomic bomb work, was really about UFOs. He calls the hearing a kangaroo court run by a man named Gordon Gray, a name he connects to the Majestic 12 papers, documents describing a secret UFO group, and he also brings in the mathematician John von Neumann. If true, it would mean the bomb's builder was punished over UFO secrets.
theory-that-shooter-valente-was-awaiting: A shooter Michels calls Valente, connected to events in 2025 in Boston, Providence and Brooklyn, may have been waiting for an instruction, either subliminal or conscious, before he acted. Michels raises this himself as a possibility on an episode about top American scientists going missing, without naming a source. If true, it would suggest someone else was directing him.
theory-that-the-object-was-built-before-: An odd object on the floor of the Baltic Sea may have been made a very long time ago, "perhaps before the ice," meaning before the last ice age. The treasure hunter Dennis Asberg, who says he found and dove on it, offers this as his own idea, which would mean someone was building things far earlier than history records.
theresa-may-withdraws-extradition-order-: In 2012 the British government cancelled an order to send a hacker named McKinnon to the United States to stand trial. McKinnon is the man at the centre of this episode, who says he broke into American computers and found signs of a secret NASA space program. The episode plays the official statement from Theresa May, then Britain's Home Secretary, speaking in Parliament in London: "I have therefore withdrawn the extradition order against Mr. McKinnon."
think-tank-conference-on-crash-retrieval: A think tank in Washington is said to have held a conference that started from the assumption that Russia, China and the United States had each recovered crashed craft of unknown origin. Michels passes this on from the physicist Hal Puthoff, who worked on US government research into unusual phenomena. The premise was put as "let's assume that there have been crash retrievals" by those three countries, which would mean such crashes were being treated as real by serious policy circles.
third-download-two-hours-of-experiencing: In what he calls his third "download", a Hollywood writer named Brent Friedman says his whole world shattered for two hours while he experienced several timelines at once. Friedman tells Jesse Michels this from his own experience, as one of a series of moments when knowledge came to him from outside himself.
third-mission-where-shots-were-fired: A helicopter pilot named Jake Barber, who says he helped retrieve a UFO with his helicopter, tells Michels that on another of these recovery missions "shots were fired". He tells it as something he was part of, once in 2025 and again in 2026, and in the later telling he calls it an ambush.
third-strand-dna-manuscript-blocked-2022: Around 2022, a man named Dave Rossi, who says aliens taught him advanced physics, wrote a paper about what he calls a "third strand of DNA," and says someone offered to help get it into a reviewed science journal but was then "restrained" from helping. Rossi tells this himself, as the author of the paper, to suggest that his work was kept from wider review.
thomas-bearden-and-soviet-scalar-death-r: A Navy man named Thomas Bearden kept talking about "scalar" weapons, a proposed kind of energy weapon, and said the Soviets had worked out a massive death ray. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, in an episode with a Pentagon whistleblower named Matthew Brown. If true, it would mean a secret and terrifying weapon was built in the Soviet Union.
thomas-townsend-brown-s-thrust-from-asym: Jesse Michels says that the mid-century American inventor Thomas Townsend Brown found something odd: if you put a high voltage across certain lopsided capacitors, which are devices that store electric charge between two plates of different shapes or sizes, they push themselves along and make thrust. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, in an episode about Bob Lazar. If true, it would mean electricity alone could move an object without a propeller or rocket.
thomas-winterton-s-scalp-separated-from-: After doing some digging on Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property known for strange reports, a man found a swelling, a "goose egg," on the back of his head three days later, which he describes as his scalp separating from his skull. Thomas Winterton, the ranch's owner, says it happened to him, suggesting the digging itself brought on the injury.
thousands-of-ayahuasca-users-report-meet: Thousands of people who drink ayahuasca, a psychedelic brew from the Amazon, report meeting a similar goddess, a female being who instantly knows everything that is wrong with them. The researcher Luke Caverns says this on Michels' show, passing on accounts he has heard. If the reports match, it would suggest people are meeting the same being rather than imagining separate ones.
threats-against-asberg-and-his-family-ov: After his team found a strange shape on the floor of the Baltic Sea, which some call a UFO on the seafloor, Dennis Asberg says he received messages threatening him and his children. Asberg, a Swedish treasure hunter who led the find, tells this himself about the years since 2011, mentioning "lots of things like that".
threats-on-mount-rushmore-in-the-securit: In 1977, an Air Force veteran named Mario Woods says a security briefing at Ellsworth, an Air Force base in South Dakota, warned of threats against Mount Rushmore, with people who "wanted to detonate a site". Woods, who says he was among airmen taken by aliens, tells Michels this from his own time at the base as part of the background to that night.
three-9-foot-skeletons-vanish-overnight-: Sometime between 1978 and 1981, at the Church of Santa Anastasia in Sardinia, a man is said to have laid out three skeletons, each at least nine feet tall, only for them to be gone the next day. Tim Alberino, a guest who says he has looked into giants, tells it second-hand from someone who told him: "So he laid them out, three bodies... Next day, they were gone." If true, it would point to giant human remains being found and then quietly removed.
three-body-problem-as-chinese-soft-discl: The Three-Body Problem, a science fiction series about contact with aliens by a Chinese author, is said to be a quiet way for China to prepare people for the truth about aliens. David Grusch, a former intelligence officer who spoke out about UFOs, offers the idea, noting that China "allowed this sci fi series to be published," which he calls "pretty trippy." If true, it would mean a government is using fiction to hint at what it knows.
three-brazilian-ufo-episodes-overseen-by: Brazil has had hundreds of UFO episodes, and at least three of them were closely followed by the country's armed forces and its intelligence and defence services. That is what Aldo Rebelo, who has served as Brazil's defence minister, tells Jesse Michels. The places tied to these episodes are Pará, São José dos Campos and Varginha, between 1970 and 1999. Coming from a former minister, the claim would mean Brazil's military treated the cases as real matters to investigate.
three-bright-transients-on-19-july-1952-: On an old glass photograph of the night sky taken at the Palomar Observatory on 19 July 1952, three very bright points of light appear that are not there in other images. The astronomer Beatriz Villarroel tells Michels that her colleague, the astronomer Enrique Solano in Spain, found them, calling it "the most beautiful example of all we have." She counts such short-lived lights, which turned up before any satellites were launched, among her signs that unexplained objects may have been near the Earth.
three-campers-frozen-and-abducted-at-a-l: Three men camping at a lake at night were frozen in place and abducted, according to a record of the event. A former Army sergeant named Lyn Buchanan says he got this record from classified study materials he worked with, and he tells it as one of the cases he saw on paper.
three-dreams-within-a-dream-numbers-seve: In 1991 on Mount Athos in Greece, a mountain of Orthodox monasteries, a man named Ralph Larson, presented on the show as a former chief at the CIA, the US foreign spy agency, says he had three dreams nested inside one another, about numbers, seven doors and walking on water. In the last one he was crossing water, thought "I can make this," then an old woman beside him stumbled, he grabbed her arm, and they were both swept away before he woke. Larson tells it as his own experience, part of the same visit in which he says he traveled back in time to the 14th century.
three-fingered-mummies-in-peru: In Peru there are said to be mummified beings with three fingers and three toes. The podcaster Joe Rogan mentions them in passing to Michels as a recent find. Michels goes further: he says he has seen these skeletons himself, that he made a documentary about them, and that they date from 800 to 1,700 years ago. If they are what the tellers suggest, they would be the remains of beings that are not ordinary humans.
three-flying-saucers-over-a-church-at-de: In 1961, at De Queen Elementary School in Port Arthur, Texas, a little boy's mother told him "look, Anthony, look at those flying saucers," and there were three of them hanging over a church, maybe 25 to 50 feet up. Mario Woods, a former nuclear guard with the Air Force, says he saw them himself at five and a half or six years old and calls them beautiful. He tells it on two episodes, and in the later one he names his mother and his sister as having seen them too.
three-foot-object-with-buttons-lying-on-: An object about three feet long, with buttons on it, is lying on the surface of Mars, according to Joe McMoneagle, a man who took part in psychic spying work. McMoneagle says he saw it himself on photo negatives from the Mars mapping done by JPL, NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory, which builds and runs its robot space probes. If true, it would mean something made by someone was left on Mars.
three-girls-encounter-creature-near-mara: In 1996, in the town of Varginha, Brazil, three young girls named Valquiria, Liliane and Katia are said to have come face to face with a strange creature near a gym. The investigator James Fox passes on their account. He calls it "an encounter of the third kind," meaning a close meeting with a being, and places it not far from a military roadblock. Michels adds that the girls, now grown women, "all testify to having seen this being." A man named Carlos de Souza, who says he saw a crash himself, places the girls' sighting five or six days after it. If true, it would mean a living non-human being was walking around a Brazilian town.
three-gravity-emitters-on-the-sports-mod: Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft at a secret Nevada site called S4 in 1988 and 1989, described three cylindrical emitters at the base of a craft he calls the sports model, which he says made gravity to move it. Michels tells this himself and points out that Lazar said it years before the physicist Ning Li's work on gravity became public, which to him suggests Lazar knew something real early.
three-illuminated-plus-signs-over-stockh: In November 1995, in the suburbs of Stockholm, Sweden, three lit-up shapes like plus signs are said to have appeared in the sky. A researcher named Clas Svahn tells Michels he saw them himself, together with his wife, and he names a person called Annalie in connection with the sighting.
three-light-beings-at-the-foot-of-his-ic: Lying alone one night in a hospital intensive care unit, gravely ill with sepsis (a body-wide reaction to infection) from COVID around 2020 or 2021, a Hollywood writer named Brent Friedman says that "all of a sudden light entities come to the foot of my bed." Friedman tells this himself as the one who saw it, and if it happened as he says, it would be a meeting with something beyond ordinary life at the edge of death. In a later conversation with Michels he speaks again of "watching light beings come to the foot of my bed" on his deathbed, though that telling places it during a cancer illness and gives no number of beings and no date.
three-separate-intelligence-sources-told: Three separate intelligence sources each told the journalist Ross Coulthart that if he really wanted to understand what was going on, he should watch Dark, a series on the streaming service Netflix. Bryce Zabel, a guest on an episode about Hollywood and UFOs, repeats what Coulthart told him, quoting the sources as saying, "watch this Netflix series, Dark." It is told because it would suggest insiders see a TV drama as a key to what they know.
three-unidentified-objects-shot-down-in-: In 2023, during the week a Chinese balloon crossed North American airspace, the military said it shot down three other unidentified objects. Pippa Malmgren, the daughter of the presidential adviser Harald Malmgren, mentions this without naming a source. She raises it to suggest that unknown objects are being met in the skies today, not only in the past.
three-way-telepathy-experiment-between-l: Sometime in 2021 or 2022, a Google artificial intelligence system called LaMDA, a program built to hold conversations, was put through a test with a person who claimed to be telepathic, someone able to read or send thoughts. The story comes from Blake Lemoine, who is billed on the episode as a Google whistleblower and who says he ran it himself: "I did actually run one experiment with the LaMDA system uh with someone who claims to have telepathic abilities." He tells it while arguing that such a machine may be a kind of alien mind, which is why a link between it and a human mind would matter.
three-witnesses-held-at-gunpoint-and-giv: Three men who had encounters with unexplained objects while in the US military were, right afterwards, held at gunpoint and given shots they were told were anthrax vaccine boosters. An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb tells this, drawing on accounts linked to a man named Jonathan Wagant. If true, it would suggest the military treated such witnesses with something other than an ordinary vaccine.
three-women-see-the-red-eyed-being-1996: In 1996, in the Brazilian city of Varginha, in the state of Minas Gerais, three women are said to have seen a strange being with red eyes and brown skin. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, and says the women seemed very honest to him. If it were true, it would be one of the few accounts of ordinary people seeing a living non-human creature up close.
thule-society-founder-initiated-in-kurdi: The Thule Society, a German secret society, was founded by a man called Baron Rudolf von Sebottendorf, who had been initiated into secret teachings in Kurdistan, of all places. The researcher Jason Jorjani tells this without naming a source, also bringing up the occult writer Helena Blavatsky. If true, it would trace the group's roots back to the Middle East.
thule-society-seances-to-contact-star-be: The Thule Society, a German occult group of the early 1900s, held seances and rituals to contact non-human intelligences that its members believed were their ancient ancestors: star beings from the far north, beneath the pole star. That is Michels's account, given in his own voice without naming a source. It matters to his larger story because it shows ideas about contact with beings from the stars running through German occult circles in the years before the Nazis.
thunder-and-lightning-striking-the-spot-: In 2011, at a spot in the Baltic Sea where a diving team had found a strange object on the seafloor, thunder, lightning and other odd weather struck right over the site. That is the account of a treasure hunter named Dennis Asberg, who was there, and who describes "thunder and lots of things just on the spot." If it happened as he says, the weather itself would seem tied to the object below.
thutmose-iv-s-dream-stela: The ancient Egyptian pharaoh Thutmose IV set up a carved stone slab called the Dream Stela during his reign. On it he tells how, as a boy before he became king, he fell asleep in the shade of the Sphinx at Giza, and the Sphinx came to him in a dream. The researcher Luke Caverns tells this from the stone's own story, as a sign of how the Egyptians themselves thought of the Sphinx.
tibetan-buddhist-dark-retreats: Some Tibetan Buddhist practitioners go into isolation for a year or more at a time, living alone in a completely dark cell, as the researcher of the mind and paranormal Jeffrey Mishlove tells Jesse Michels. He mentions it in passing, as something generally known, while talking about altered states and the mind's hidden abilities.
tic-tac-at-31-times-the-speed-of-sound-w: The Tic Tac, a white oval object shaped like the mint and reported by Navy pilots, is said to have reached at least 31 times the speed of sound without disturbing the air around it. A young researcher named Deep Prasad makes the point on Michels' show, summarising it without naming where the estimate comes from, in a discussion he connects to the researcher Eric Weinstein. If true, it would mean something moving far past any known aircraft without making the shock waves fast objects normally create.
tic-tac-encounter-as-testimony-from-reli: Pilots say they saw the Tic Tac, a white oval object shaped like the mint, and the main evidence for it is their word. James Madden, who talks with Michels about consciousness and Plato, uses it as an example: his evidence is that seemingly very reliable pilots, Alex Dietrich and David Fravor, have said these things, and he asks what that kind of testimony is worth.
tic-tac-flir-video-2004: In 2004, off the coast of Southern California, Navy jets from the aircraft carrier USS Nimitz met a white oval object shaped like a Tic Tac mint, and a heat-sensing camera on one of the jets filmed it. Michels says simply that forward-looking infrared, a camera that sees heat, caught the famous Tic Tac video in 2004. In another episode he calls the thermal image the best picture to come out of the case. The commentator Marik von Rennenkampff, in an episode set up as a debate with the UFO skeptic Mick West, tells how the footage came about, passing on what the pilots have said. After the first encounter, he says, the four aircrew in the two jets went back to the carrier, and the Navy fighter pilot David Fravor told another pilot, Chad Underwood, "Hey, we just saw something weird." Underwood then went up and filmed the object, a clip known as the FLIR1 video, and von Rennenkampff also mentions radar contacts.
