The tellers come back to it because it is a sighting backed by a camera, radar and trained pilots all at once.
tic-tac-leaves-as-soon-as-he-heads-for-t: In 2025, on a hill at a field site, a "tic-tac" (a white oval object shaped like the mint) flew off the moment he started walking toward a helicopter, says a member of Skywatcher, a startup that says it is trying to call up UFOs. He tells it as his own experience: "I take 10 steps, and 'Tic-tac' begins to fly away." If true, it would suggest the object was reacting to what the team on the ground did.
tic-tac-pilots-names-told-to-bishop-befo: A UFO writer named Greg Bishop says he was told the names of the Navy pilots in the Tic Tac incident, the 2004 encounter with a white oval object shaped like the mint, before those names were made public, and that it was a test of whether he would leak them. The pilots were Alex Dietrich and David Fravor. Bishop, telling it as the person it happened to, says he guessed the point of it ("you see I'm going to leak stuff") and was told not to talk about it, which would mean people close to the story were checking who could keep a secret.
tic-tac-unloaded-from-a-c-130-in-the-azo: A man who served with the US Air Force says he saw a Tic Tac, a white oval craft shaped like the mint, being unloaded from a C-130 military cargo plane in the Azores, a group of Portuguese islands in the Atlantic. The story comes from a researcher who goes by UAPGerb. He mentions it only briefly to Michels and holds back the details because he plans to interview the man soon. If true, it would mean the military was moving one of these objects around by plane.
tic-tac-videos-seen-in-the-pentagon-befo: The physicist Hal Puthoff, who has worked on government research into the unexplained, says he saw the Tic Tac videos, military cockpit footage of a white oval object shaped like the mint, inside the Pentagon before they were made public in 2017. He says Luis Elizondo, a former Pentagon official, was behind their release, and adds that "there are more videos, some are better," which would mean the government holds clearer footage than the public has seen.
ticom-and-alsos-technology-retrieval-194: Jesse Michels says that the Nazis had a lot of advanced technology at the end of the Second World War, and that the Allies ran programmes to collect it, which he calls "TACOM and ASOS" and which are known as TICOM and ALSOS, efforts in Europe in 1944 and 1945 to retrieve German technology and know-how. He mentions this in passing, without naming a source, in an episode with a former presidential advisor, Harald Malmgren, as background to how advanced technology may have ended up in American hands.
tim-burchett-on-the-high-rate-of-researc: Tim Burchett, a member of the US Congress, told the British newspaper the Daily Mail that the number of researchers going missing in certain fields of research seems very high. Michels passes on the remark in an episode about missing American scientists. He uses it to show that even a lawmaker thinks the pattern looks troubling.
tim-phillips-confirms-borland-s-two-draw: A former Air Force intelligence specialist named Dylan Borland, who came forward about UFOs, says that Tim Phillips, a senior official at AARO, the Pentagon office set up to investigate UFO reports, admitted that Borland had made two drawings of what he saw and that AARO was told to classify them because of a security classification guide, an official rulebook of what must be kept secret. Borland relays this as Phillips told it, with AARO's first director Sean Kirkpatrick also named. If true, it would mean the office meant to investigate was itself hiding material on orders.
tim-phillips-says-triangles-are-real-202: Tim Phillips, an official at AARO, the Pentagon office set up in the 2020s to investigate unexplained aerial reports, is said to have stated that triangle-shaped craft are real and that the office wants to know where they come from. Dylan Borland, a former US Air Force intelligence specialist, relays this, citing Phillips himself and the journalist Chris Sharp. If true, it would mean the office itself accepts these triangles as a real puzzle.
tim-taylor-and-the-adjustment-team: A man named Timothy Taylor, linked to the US space agency NASA, is said to have told the religion scholar Diana Pasulka that he was part of what he called the "adjustment team." Michels repeats this as something Taylor told Pasulka, putting the phrase in quotation marks and not explaining what the team did. He raises it among hints that NASA has a hidden side tied to the UFO question.
tim-taylor-at-the-anderson-case-dig-this: At a 2013 dig connected to what is called the Anderson case, some of the material that came out of the ground drew a sharp reaction from a man named Timothy Taylor: "This is the real deal." The researcher Grant Cameron tells this second-hand. He was not there, but says a friend of his told him what Taylor said as the material came up, and if true it would mean the material struck Taylor as genuinely unusual.
tim-taylor-converts-to-catholicism-at-th: A man named Timothy Taylor, the subject of an episode about a man said to attract UFOs, had a religious conversion right at the Vatican and became a Catholic, Michels says. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, as part of the man's personal story.
tim-taylor-disappears-after-15-years-of-: A man named Timothy Taylor stayed in touch with Charles Hall and his wife for about fifteen years and then, they say, simply vanished from their lives, sometime after 2000 in New Mexico. Hall is a man who says he spent three years with tall white aliens at Area 51, a secret Air Force base in Nevada, and it is his wife, speaking from her own experience, who tells it: "He just disappeared. We never heard from him since."
tim-taylor-helped-linda-brown-write-her-: Sometime around 2010 to 2013, a man named Timothy Taylor helped a woman named Linda Brown write her book about the scientist Thomas Townsend Brown. Chris Bledsoe, a man who says he draws UFOs to him and whom NASA has studied, is passing on what he was told: "he helped write that book." Bledsoe adds that he has the manuscript about Townsend Brown "saved on my phone."
tim-taylor-of-aerospace-corporation-take: A man named Timothy Taylor, who works at the Aerospace Corporation, a company that does space work for the US government and NASA, is said to claim that he takes orders from an angel. Michels brings this up himself, without naming a source, as one of the strange beliefs he says can be found among people inside the space world.
tim-taylor-places-piece-of-roswell-crash: A man named Timothy Taylor is said to have brought a piece of metal from the 1947 Roswell crash, a wreck in New Mexico that some say was a craft from elsewhere, and placed it in the hands of North Carolina man Chris Bledsoe and his family. Bob McGwier, a CIA contractor, tells it as something he heard, and Michels adds that Bledsoe somehow knew the material was not from here. Bledsoe himself tells it as a test of his family by a man from NASA, the US space agency, who arrived with a backpack and credentials covering "everything from Area 51 to the CIA", without saying the metal came from Roswell.
tim-taylor-s-background-as-nasa-mission-: A man named Timothy Taylor has worked mission control for NASA rocket launches since the 1980s, according to Michels, who calls him "a mysterious rocket scientist" and credits a source called Launch Fever. Michels brings this up while presenting Taylor as someone NASA studies because UFOs are said to appear around him, so his long space career is offered as a reason to take him seriously.
tim-taylor-s-downloaded-business-ideas: An entrepreneur named Timothy Taylor claims that many of his business ideas came from "downloads", information he believes he receives from a non-human intelligence, and says these downloads were made possible by certain protocols he followed. Michels tells this more than once, drawing on American Cosmic, a book by the religion scholar Diana Pasulka in which Taylor appears. It comes up because, if true, it would mean real-world inventions and businesses are being shaped by contact with something non-human.
tim-taylor-s-hooded-figure-before-his-in: The night before an idea for an invention arrived in his head, Timothy Taylor, the scientist written about in a book by an author Cameron calls Pulko, woke to find a hooded figure standing at the end of his bed. The UFO researcher Grant Cameron says Taylor told him this directly: "the last thing I remember the night before I got that idea in my head I woke up and there was a hooded figure standing at the end of bed." If true, it would tie the invention to some kind of visitor.
tim-taylor-s-secret-space-program-and-ti: A government operative named Tim Taylor was part of a secret space programme involving UFOs, a programme the story links to adjusting timelines. Michels tells this from American Cosmic, a book by the scholar Diana Pasulka, in which she makes this claim about Taylor. If true, it would mean the government runs a hidden space effort built on UFO technology.
tim-taylor-s-sun-gazing-protocols-in-ame: A man named Timothy Taylor is said to use protocols built around being in the sunlight and looking at the sun, apparently as a way of making contact with whatever is behind UFOs. Michels tells it from American Cosmic, a book by the religious studies scholar Diana Pasulka, saying that "Tim Taylor talks about in Diana's book" how his protocols center on the sun.
tim-taylor-says-the-president-handed-him: A man named Timothy Taylor is said to have claimed that a president handed him a certain item while they sat at the dinner table together. Chris Bledsoe, a man whose reported UFO encounters have drawn interest from NASA, repeats what Taylor told him, quoting him as saying, "I was at the dinner table with the president and handed me that," though which item and which president are left unsaid.
tim-taylor-secret-space-program-and-cras: A NASA mission controller named Timothy Taylor, who also worked at the Aerospace Corporation, a defense research contractor, is said to have told the religion scholar Diana Pasulka openly that he was part of a secret space program, and to have taken her and the Stanford professor Garry Nolan to a UFO crash site to look at material. Michels retells this on several episodes from Pasulka's book American Cosmic, and the details shift: one version places the site in New Mexico, another leaves out the crash site and links Taylor to the 1986 Challenger shuttle and the astronaut Judith Resnik. If true, it would put a working NASA insider at a crash site sharing physical material with scientists.
tim-taylor-shows-grant-the-jump-room-bui: In 2013 a man named Timothy Taylor took the UFO researcher Grant Cameron to an old aircraft building that had been turned into offices, and told him this was where the "jump room" had been. Cameron tells Michels this as something he saw firsthand, though he admits he does not remember Taylor's exact words. He does not explain on the show what the jump room was, only that Taylor pointed out the building as the place behind its story.
tim-taylor-shows-up-with-experiencers-bl: Michels says that a man named Timothy Taylor keeps turning up in the lives of people who report contact with nonhuman beings. He names Chris Bledsoe, a man who says he has had such encounters, and Charles Hall, who says he lived with aliens at Area 51, the secret Air Force test site in Nevada. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, as a pattern that seems to tie Taylor to these cases.
tim-taylor-visits-charles-hall: A man named Timothy Taylor came to the home of Charles Hall, a man who says he draws UFOs to him, because he had found out about Hall. The story comes from Hall's wife, who was there, and who says simply, "He came here because he found out about Charles," suggesting that Hall's claims had drawn the attention of people from outside.
tim-taylor-works-for-the-hammer: A man named Timothy Taylor is said to have claimed that he worked for someone called "the Hammer," a figure nobody seems able to identify. Chris Bledsoe, a man the show presents as someone who draws UFOs to him, says Taylor told him this directly, around 2008 to 2011: "I work for the hammer and the hammer works for God." Bledsoe links it to the film The Adjustment Bureau and the story it came from, The Adjustment Team, which are about hidden agents who steer people's lives. A guest named Bob McGwier repeats the story as he heard it from Bledsoe, adding that "no one that I know knows who the hammer is."
time-slows-and-god-speaks-on-the-night-t: On a night train from Zurich to Vienna, when he was 40, time seemed to slow down and God spoke to him, says Rolf Mowatt-Larssen, a former senior CIA officer, telling it as something that happened to him. The message, he says, was "do not criticize my church, the old and the new are one", and he wrote it down by hand in the Bible he had from West Point, the US Army's officer academy. In another telling on the same episode he stresses that he felt God was aware of him and "standing there" in the train with him.
time-travel-to-14th-century-mount-athos-: A former CIA chief named Rolf Mowatt-Larssen says that in 1991 he travelled back in time while on Mount Athos, a group of monasteries in Greece. He tells it himself: on a pilgrimage there, he dozed off on a stone chair facing a church. He says he then saw the same town as it was centuries earlier, around the 1400s or 1500s, rather than the 14th century of the story's title. There, he says, he arrived as a monk, presented his credentials at the capital, and met a monk named Gabriel and someone called Evagrius. He tells both parts on one 2026 episode with Jesse Michels. To him it is proof that the mind can reach into the past.
time-travelling-nordic-humans-manipulati: Some of the beings people report, tall, fair humans often called "Nordics", are said to be humans who mastered time travel at some point, around 2050, and who now move between Earth, Mars and the Moon and steer history. The philosopher Jason Jorjani lays out this idea as his own reading, drawing on a work called Closer Encounters. If true, it would mean some visitors are really our own descendants changing our past.
timothy-leary-supplied-lsd-to-jfk-and-ma: In 1960s Washington, the psychologist Timothy Leary, known for promoting the drug LSD, is said to have supplied LSD to President John F. Kennedy and to Mary Pinchot Meyer, a Washington artist close to Kennedy. The lawyer Dan Sheehan says this, passing on what he says he was told, in a longer account of Kennedy and what he knew about UFOs. In Sheehan's words, the drug was "provided by Tim Leary".
timothy-taylor-s-agency-credentials-and-: A man named Timothy Taylor, linked to NASA, is said to carry credentials from several US intelligence agencies, hinting at a hidden space program. Michels says that according to Diana Pasulka, a scholar who writes about UFO belief, Taylor "seemed to flash all these like three-letter agency credentials" at her. A researcher who goes by UAPGerb says, without naming a source, that Taylor walks around with credentials from many agencies, including access to the NRO, the US agency that runs spy satellites. If true, it would suggest a secret program working beyond the public space agency.
timothy-taylor-s-hierarchy-as-described-: A NASA program manager named Timothy Taylor is said to have laid out a "hierarchy of being" when a researcher named Diana Pasulka asked him how things are ranked. A guest named Matthew Pines brings it up, calling Taylor a once-anonymous but now "kind of known" manager at NASA, the US space agency, who has been "deeply involved" in "spooky subjects for a long time." Michels repeats it on a later episode: "you have Tim Taylor telling Diana Pasulka, here's the hierarchy of being." Neither teller spells out what the hierarchy contains. If true, it would mean someone inside the space agency claims to know how beings beyond ourselves are ordered.
tip-about-a-russian-intelligence-officer: In 1991, Ralph Larson, a former CIA officer, says he got a tip from a Greek man very close to Greece's prime minister that a monk on Mount Athos, a monastic mountain in Greece, was really a Russian intelligence officer building a new identity before a mission to the United States. Larson tells it as part of his own work, and says there was a file on the monk.
titanic-survivor-s-account-of-angels-in-: When the Titanic sank in the North Atlantic in 1912, a survivor in one of the lifeboats is said to have seen a group of angels arrive in a craft, land by a lifeboat and set down on the ledge of an iceberg. Charles Hall, a man who says he spent years among tall white aliens at a military base, tells Michels he read this in a book on the Titanic that he does not name, as the account of a survivor later picked up by the rescue ship Carpathia. To Hall it suggests that beings like the ones he describes were present at the disaster.
tmbb-spaceships-x-account-suspected-to-b: After the story of a missing man named McCasland broke, people online started hunting for clues and fixed on an account on the social network X called TMBB spaceships, which they suspected he ran. Michels tells this himself in an episode about missing scientists, setting it beside McCasland's official Air Force biography. If the account really were his, it might show what he thought about spacecraft.
to-the-stars-material-testing-with-milit: In 2019 and 2020, To the Stars Academy, a company set up to research UFOs and the materials said to come from them, was building ties with US military laboratories to run tests on those materials that "only they could do," until the COVID pandemic stopped it. The author Peter Levenda, who says he was part of the effort, tells it this way: "We know that we were getting close to something," and then "all the relationship with the military really stopped."
told-sensor-research-would-be-career-end: A former US intelligence official named Eric Haseltine says that when he began working in his own lab to reproduce an effect he had come across, and to build a sensor that could detect it, people in the intelligence community warned him off. He tells Michels this happened to him, and that he was given to understand the work would end his career, which, if true, would mean such research was being actively discouraged.
tom-delonge-books-on-official-and-non-go: Books by Tom DeLonge, a musician who writes about UFOs, point to the idea that there are official government UFO programs and also separate non-government ones. The analyst Matthew Pines brings this up on Michels' show, summarising the books without quoting them. If so, some of the secret work on these questions would sit outside government control.
tom-delonge-contacts-levenda-to-investig: At the end of 2014, the musician Tom DeLonge reached out "out of the clear blue sky" to the author and historian Peter Levenda to work with him on looking into UFOs. Levenda tells this himself as the person who was contacted, by phone and email, and it marks the start of a partnership that came just before UFOs drew wide public attention.
tom-delonge-email-to-john-podesta-about-: Among the emails of John Podesta, a senior political adviser, that the leak site WikiLeaks published, there is one from the musician Tom DeLonge with the subject line about General McCasland, meaning the Air Force general Neil McCasland. In it DeLonge writes that the general had said he was a skeptic, but he is not, and that DeLonge had been working with him for four months. Michels reads this from the leaked emails, from 2015 to 2016, as a sign that a senior general was quietly helping DeLonge's UFO efforts.
tom-delonge-narrative-of-a-majestic-styl: The musician turned UFO campaigner Tom DeLonge is said to tell of a secret controlling group in the United States, along the lines of Majestic, a rumoured top-secret committee said to run UFO matters behind the scenes. The analyst Matthew Pines sums up "the Tom DeLonge narrative" in passing, relaying DeLonge's version that such a group sits at the top, which would mean UFO secrets are held by a small, unseen body.
tom-delonge-says-nhi-are-archons: The musician Tom DeLonge, who co-founded To the Stars Academy, a private company that researched UFOs, is said to believe that many of the non-human intelligences behind UFOs are not friendly, and may be what he called archons. Michels tells this from a breakfast he had with DeLonge, and says DeLonge told him "he thought these were like archons." In one telling Michels adds that DeLonge was drawing on Gnostic thought, an ancient religious tradition in which archons are powers that rule over and hold back humanity, which is why the remark matters: it would make the visitors something like jailers.
tom-farmer-cia-general-counsel-vetting-p: Tom Farmer, who served as general counsel (chief lawyer) of the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency, was involved in Project Paperclip, the American effort to bring German scientists to the United States after the Second World War, and helped vet the Germans. The presidential advisor Harold Malmgren tells this about a man he knew personally, saying "it turned out he was involved" in the project. It matters to his account because it puts a man he knew close to the people who handled secret technology after the war.
tomb-of-the-birds-and-the-wooden-bird-fo: On a northern cliff west of the Great Pyramid at Giza there is a burial site called the Tomb of the Birds, and the story attached to it is that a carved wooden bird was found there during the Second World War, in the 1940s. A researcher named Luke Caverns brings it up on the show without naming a source, and he mentions the television science show Mythbusters while telling it.
tomb-of-thutmose-ii-announced-over-a-yea: The tomb of Thutmose II, an ancient Egyptian pharaoh, is said to have been found early in 2024 but announced to the public more than a year later. Luke Caverns, a researcher who explores ancient Egyptian sites, says he heard about the find while he was in Egypt in October 2024. He tells it to suggest that big discoveries in Egypt can be held back for a long time before the public hears of them.
tone-experiments-with-entranced-space-ki: In the 1970s, in the lab of a scientist named Andrija Puharich, children nicknamed the "space kids" were said to be put into trances and tested: tones were played to them, and they were asked to respond while still in trance. An unnamed researcher on the show describes this from the tapes of Puharich's sessions, as part of a story about a scientist who is said to have contacted an alien council through such sessions.
tonopah-s4-workers-flown-in-by-janet: Workers at S4, an area of the Tonopah Test Range in Nevada long rumoured to house secret craft work, are said to be flown straight in on Janet, the unmarked airline that carries staff to secret Nevada sites, and are not allowed to drive in as other Tonopah employees can. The online researcher known as UAPGerb tells it, crediting the claim to a source he names as Lazy G Ranch, and offers it as a sign that S4 is guarded even more tightly than the rest of the range.
tonopah-test-range-is-literally-area-52: The Tonopah Test Range, a secretive military testing ground in Nevada, is said to be literally named Area 52, a sibling to the famous secret base Area 51. An online researcher who goes by the name UAPGerb says so on Michels' show, stating it as a known fact without naming a source. The point is that the classified work people associate with Area 51 may also have a lesser-known neighbour.
tooth-device-demonstration-at-the-pentag: Sometime in the 1960s, a device fitted into a tooth was demonstrated on a general at the Pentagon, the headquarters of the US military. The researcher Andrija Puharich says he gave that demonstration himself: "We fitted this device to this general." If true, it would mean the top of the military took a direct interest in his inventions.
top-secret-files-from-the-late-1800s: Files from the late 1800s and early 1900s on unexplained phenomena are said to still be top secret today. The UFO researcher Steven Greer says a senior CIA (US Central Intelligence Agency) source he does not name told him so: "There are still top secret files on this issue from the late 1800s and early 1900s. We know this." If true, the government's secrecy on the subject would go back more than a hundred years.
topological-physics-held-by-the-governme: Advanced knowledge in topological physics, a field that studies unusual, stable properties of materials, is said to be held inside the US government and big aerospace companies. Michels tells this twice, passing on what the physicist Hal Puthoff told him: Puthoff was not sure fundamental physics was locked up at aerospace firms, but said topological physics "probably" was. In a 2022 episode Puthoff says it himself, that "there certainly is materials knowledge which involves topological physics" at those companies, in an exchange that also cites the mathematician Eric Weinstein.
toronto-cafe-idea-of-borrowing-other-peo: In 2018, sitting in a café in Toronto and looking at the people around him, he got the idea of somehow borrowing other people's brain power, says a researcher named Deep Prasad. He tells it as his own memory of where the idea began, on an episode where he argues that artificial intelligence is a kind of alien technology.
toronto-death-ray-inventor-and-mossad-mi: A newspaper clipping from Toronto, Canada, from the late 1950s or early 1960s, is said to tell of a man who invented a death ray, and of representatives of the Mossad, Israel's intelligence agency, who visited him and afterwards reported "missing time", a stretch they could not remember. Dave Rossi, a guest who says aliens taught him advanced physics, tells this on Michels' show from his memory of the clipping, which he does not quote further. If true, it would hint that something blanked the memories of the visitors.
touching-craft-pieces-with-garry-nolan-2: Michels says he has seen pieces said to come from a craft, in the company of the scientist Garry Nolan, who studies such material. He tells it himself as something he was present for, adding that he does not know if they are "real pieces of a craft, but like they seem," which, if they were, would mean physical remains of an unknown vehicle exist to be examined.
touching-the-reactor-s-repulsive-field-1: The power source of an alien craft made a gravity field around itself that you could physically push against with your hand, according to Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on such craft between 1987 and 1989 at a hidden site in Nevada called S4. He describes it from his own hands-on experience: "it'll produce a gravitational field around it and you can push on it," which, if true, would mean the machine controlled gravity directly.
toughbook-programs-lured-ufos-and-downed: Secret programs are said to have cleared the skies with temporary flight restrictions, which are orders closing off airspace, lured UFOs in, and brought them down with EMP weapons, which use a burst of electromagnetic energy to knock out electronics. Michels says this comes from an insider leak about programs recorded on Toughbooks, rugged laptop computers, in an episode about a UFO book the Pentagon tried to censor. Michael Herrera, a man who says he saw a 300-foot UFO in the Indonesian jungle, tells a similar story he credits to a man named Jake Barber: an organization sometimes targets the craft with EMP and what he calls scalar weapons and knocks them out of the sky. If true, it would mean the US is actively shooting down UFOs to recover them.
townsen-brown-at-caltech-in-the-1920s-di: Jesse Michels says that in the 1920s, a decade before the rocket pioneer Jack Parsons worked at Caltech, the California Institute of Technology in Pasadena, another man there had very different ideas for travel into deep space: the inventor Thomas Townsend Brown, who found that lopsided capacitors, devices that store electric charge, could make thrust when given high voltage. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, in an episode about a NASA chief and antigravity propulsion, as an early root of the idea of flying without rockets.
townsend-brown-and-ning-li-claims-of-wei: Over the last 70 years, several researchers have said they got small weight reduction effects, a kind of shielding against gravity, in their experiments. Michels names the inventor Thomas Townsend Brown and the physicist Ning Li of the University of Alabama in Huntsville as the foremost of them, telling it himself without a further source. If true, it would mean gravity can be partly blocked, the kind of physics people link to UFO flight.
townsend-brown-and-the-caroline-group: Michels says that an American inventor named Thomas Townsend Brown ran into the Caroline Group, which he describes as an international group of industrialists who seemed to soak up all of the exotic technology. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source. If true, it would mean unusual inventions were being gathered up by private money and kept out of public view.
townsend-brown-and-the-nassau-group: Thomas Townsend Brown, an inventor whose biography is titled The Man Who Mastered Gravity, spent a lot of time in Nassau in the Bahamas, where a secret group used to meet. Jesse Michels tells it himself, saying Brown's biographer, Paul Schatzkin, coined a name for that group: the Nassau Group. Michels raises it because it would point to a hidden circle meeting around Brown's work.
townsend-brown-believed-his-work-bore-on: The inventor Thomas Townsend Brown, who studied strange effects of high voltage, believed his work had clear implications for time travel, and was obsessed with it. Michels says this himself in two episodes, without naming a source; in the second he adds that Agnew Bahnson, a businessman who funded Brown, said similar things about anomalies at high voltage. If true, it would mean early anti-gravity research was thought to touch on time itself.
townsend-brown-born-in-zanesville-built-: Thomas Townsend Brown, an inventor later linked to research into electrically driven flight, was born in 1905 in Zanesville, Ohio, and as a boy of about 12 is said to have built a wireless telegraph, a device for sending messages by radio. Michels tells this himself, saying there are newspaper clippings from the time showing the boy's invention, as an early sign of Brown's unusual talent.
townsend-brown-crash-retrievals-and-gree: Jesse Michels says that in the late 1950s and early 1960s the inventor Thomas Townsend Brown would go out into the field, flash official credentials and, in effect, recover crashed objects. According to Michels, Brown found what he calls a "green fireball thing" that was losing mass, and it was apparently made of barium titanate, a ceramic material used in electronics. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, in an episode with a guest named Dave Rossi, and it would mean Brown worked on recovering unknown craft for the government.
townsend-brown-fired-by-the-navy-moves-t: In 1942 the US Navy fired the physicist Thomas Townsend Brown without cause, and he then turned up at Martin Vega Corporation, an aircraft maker, a year before Skunk Works, the secret aircraft design shop, was formed, Michels says. He tells it himself, without naming a source, in an episode about why he believes the whistleblower David Grusch. He calls the move mysterious, hinting that Brown's work quietly passed into secret aircraft programs.
townsend-brown-in-the-bahamas-with-willi: Thomas Townsend Brown, a man at the centre of Michels's story of secret science, spent an unusual amount of time in the Bahamas with William Stephenson, a spy for Winston Churchill and said to be an inspiration for James Bond. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, as a sign that Brown moved in intelligence circles.
townsend-brown-parachutes-into-germany-t: A scientist named Townsend Brown is said to have parachuted behind enemy lines into Germany near the end of the Second World War to look into a German flying-craft program and the Foo Fighters, glowing lights that pilots reported during the war. Michels tells it in his interview with David Grusch and points to the book The Man Who Mastered Gravity. Paul Schatzkin, a writer who researched Brown's life, says the jump came from very low altitude, credits a man named O'Reilly as his source, and dates it to 1945 rather than 1944. In another episode Michels links Brown to TICOM, an Allied effort to seize German intelligence secrets, places it in East Germany, and says the Nazis took Brown prisoner before the Americans rescued him soon after.
townsend-brown-possibly-involved-in-a-cr: An American inventor named Thomas Townsend Brown may have taken part in recovering a crashed UFO, according to Michels, who says he has some evidence of it but does not say what that evidence is. If true, it would tie one of America's more unusual inventors to secret work on craft that came down in the United States.
townsend-brown-s-1960s-work-northrop-b-2: Thomas Townsend Brown, a researcher working on anti-gravity, showed his experiments to the RAND Corporation, a research group that advises the US military, and after that meeting his work went dark, Michels says; in one telling it was quietly handed to the aircraft maker Northrop Grumman for the B-2 stealth bomber. Michels tells it in three episodes and the dates shift: once in the 1960s, once in the 1950s, and once as a demo in 1967. If true, it would mean a promising gravity technology was taken out of public view and put into secret military aircraft.
townsend-brown-s-anti-gravity-success-in: Jesse Michels says that the inventor Thomas Townsend Brown finally got a positive result from his anti-gravity experiments while working in Paris, and that when he flew back to the United States, the scientist Robert Sarbacher picked him up at the airport in his big Cadillac. Michels tells it himself in two episodes, once in his talk with the writer Whitley Strieber and once in his own documentary about Brown, which dates the Paris work to 1956 and says the inventor Henri Coanda and a man named Jacques Cornillon brought Brown to France. Michels raises it to suggest Brown's work was being watched closely by people tied to secret government research.
townsend-brown-s-electrogravitics-experi: In the late 1920s the physicist Thomas Townsend Brown is said to have experimented with electrogravitics, the idea that very high voltage could produce a push like a force against gravity, using "very high voltage but low power" at certain resonant frequencies, with work also linked to Germany. Steven Greer, who runs a group collecting testimony about secret UFO technology, tells it as a researcher's summary, crediting his own collection, the Disclosure Project Intelligence Archive, and offers it as an early root of hidden propulsion science.
townsend-brown-s-experiments-in-oil: An experimenter named Thomas Townsend Brown carried out some of his experiments in oil. That is according to a researcher named Charles Buhler, who mentions it only in passing during a talk about building antigravity propulsion, meaning a way to push a craft without ordinary engines, and he says nothing more about what the oil tests showed.
townsend-brown-s-gravitational-anomaly-e: The inventor Thomas Townsend Brown spent a lot of time in Nassau, in the Bahamas, where he went on expeditions to study places where gravity seemed to behave oddly. Michels mentions it himself, without a source, in a conversation where he also brings up a man named William Stephenson.
townsend-brown-s-gravitator-was-a-time-m: A device built by Thomas Townsend Brown, a mid-century inventor who tried to control gravity with electricity, was "a time machine", according to a man named Morgan, who blew up and said so in an episode Michels takes from Paul Schatzkin's biography of Brown, The Man Who Mastered Gravity. Michels adds, in several episodes, that Brown was privately obsessed with time travel, believed controlling gravity would lead to it, and even called himself a time traveler, which Michels credits to Brown's daughter. Michels tells it to suggest Brown got further in linking electromagnetism and gravity than anyone knew.
townsend-brown-s-shortwave-contact-with-: An American inventor named Thomas Townsend Brown is said to have talked constantly about being in contact with aliens he called "space brothers", and to have claimed he was communicating with them about half the time. Michels raises this himself in several episodes, without naming a source, once crediting the account to a man named Agnew Bahnson and once likening it to the film Close Encounters of the Third Kind, about people making contact with visitors from space. In one telling he frames these as experiences Brown described himself, which would place a working inventor among those who say they spoke with beings from elsewhere.
townsend-brown-s-time-travel-tech-taken-: Thomas Townsend Brown, an American researcher said to have worked on anti-gravity, supposedly kept saying that a group in Nassau, in the Bahamas, had taken his time travel technology. Michels tells this from the work of the writer Paul Schatzkin, whose biography of Brown is called The Man Who Mastered Gravity, and he names a man called William Stephenson and Brown's daughter as part of the story. If true, it would mean a private group got hold of technology for moving through time.
townsend-brown-s-ufo-interaction-at-age-: An American inventor named Thomas Townsend Brown is said to have had a UFO encounter at about age 17, around 1922, that shaped all his later work. Michels tells it several times, placing it on Catalina Island off California and describing a small orb of light that came right up to the young Brown, though once he hedges with "I think" on the age and place. Citing Brown's daughter, Michels says this was when Brown "downloaded his life's work," while he had a lab in Pasadena. The daughter, Linda Brown, tells it herself on the show, saying her father "learned so much standing there with that ball of light." If true, it would mean Brown's research had its start in a contact with something unknown.
townsend-brown-takes-crash-material-from: Michels tells how residents near Hartford, Connecticut, saw a greenish fireball crash with a loud noise, how a man who followed the sound found a shed on fire, and how metal debris was picked up nearby. The material went first to the astronomers Fred Whipple and J. Allen Hynek at Moonwatch, a Harvard program for observing and tracking the world's first satellites. An officer named Robert Friend at Blue Book, the US Air Force's UFO study of the 1950s and 60s, also wanted the samples, but the scientist Thomas Townsend Brown simply "walks in to Harvard, flashes his credentials, and takes the material." Michels dates the crash to 1958 in one telling and to 1960 in others, and credits the researcher Michael Swords and a file in the Smithsonian archive as his sources.
townsend-brown-workbooks-posted-online-2: In 2025 someone posted online the workbooks of Thomas Townsend Brown, an inventor who worked on ideas for moving craft using electricity instead of ordinary engines. Harold Malmgren, a former advisor to US presidents who says he handled UFO material, mentions it in passing, saying "somebody just posted on the internet the workbooks". He does not say who posted them, but it would put Brown's own notes in public hands.
townsend-brown-worse-than-a-thermonuclea: A biography of the scientist Thomas Townsend Brown, the book The Man Who Mastered Gravity by Paul Schatzkin, contains a line saying Brown's work "will make a thermonuclear bomb look like a child's firecracker." Michels quotes the line himself, from memory, to show how powerful Brown's gravity research was thought to be.
townsend-s-repelling-bismuth-raised-at-m: In the 1950s a man named Townsend found a type of bismuth, a heavy metal, that "was repelled instead of attracting," according to the physicist Louis Witten, who worked at the Martin Company, an aerospace firm. Michels tells this three times, quoting an interview Witten gave to the American Institute of Physics, a professional body for physicists (once he calls the source American Theoretical Physics), and in one telling he takes Townsend to be the researcher Thomas Townsend Brown. Michels raises it as a sign that aerospace companies of that decade were looking into materials that might push against gravity.
townspeople-claim-1992-ufo-crash-recover: In 1992 a UFO is said to have crashed next to Brookhaven National Laboratory, a US government research lab on Long Island, New York, which Michels describes as home to the country's largest particle accelerator, and the lab itself is said to have collected the craft. Michels tells this himself across several episodes, crediting townspeople and, once, the local police chief as the witnesses, though he sometimes calls the town South Haven, sometimes gives only "the 90s," and once only says the crash was right next to the lab. If true, a federal lab would have quietly recovered a crashed craft in plain view of a town.
trace-relation-proven-to-be-a-partial-or: A mathematical idea called the trace relation was proven to be a partial order, a precise kind of logical ordering, by a colleague waiting at London's Heathrow airport. That is the account of the researcher Don Hoffman, who says he brought the idea to his colleague Jayton Posash. Posash told him "Don, it's too pretty to be true," then checked it at Heathrow on his way to a flight and proved it.
training-army-intelligence-officers-in-r: The physicist Hal Puthoff says he once worked "24 hours a day" training US Army intelligence officers in remote viewing, the claimed ability to describe distant places or things using only the mind. Puthoff tells it as the man who did the training, mentioning it to explain why he stopped other work, and if true it means the Army took this ability seriously enough to train its own officers in it.
training-children-in-extraocular-vision-: Groups in Mexico and Spain are said to be training children in extraocular vision, the claimed ability to see or read without using the eyes. The biologist Rupert Sheldrake mentions it, saying he knows about the Spanish work because "I have a colleague in Spain who's working on this," while adding he does not know whether much is happening in the US or Britain.
training-instructor-s-account-of-ghosts-: Around 1964 and 1965, at the old weather station at Nellis Air Force Base in Nevada, "ghosts" are said to have come in off the runway to use the restroom, which Charles Hall says were really a group of five tall white aliens. Hall, who says he spent years with such beings there and wrote about it in his book Millennial Hospitality, relays it from an unnamed airman who trained him on the job. If true, it would mean aliens walked through an Air Force building.
transcript-of-brad-sorensen-arvs-built-l: A man named Brad Sorensen is said to have described alien reproduction vehicles, man-made craft copied from alien ones, being built from the late 1950s at Norton Air Force Base in California. The UFO campaigner Steven Greer says he has a full transcript of Sorensen talking about this with an aerospace writer. A researcher who goes by UAPGerb, which is short for unidentified anomalous phenomena, the government's term for UFOs, describes the same file differently: as a PDF called "Norton Air Force Base internal", posted to an online document archive known as DPI, dated 1990, with the writer named as Bill Scott. If true, it would mean the US was building copies of alien craft decades ago.
transfer-of-ufo-material-from-lockheed-m: Michels says that UFO material held by Lockheed Martin, a major American defense and aerospace company, was moved under a tightly guarded secret program to Bigelow Aerospace, a private space company in Las Vegas. In one episode he reads, from a text he does not name, that a Pentagon-funded UFO study called OSAP was first meant to store this material at Bigelow's buildings, after a plan to hand it over was put forward by James Ryder, a Lockheed Martin space vice president who has since died. In another episode he calls the transfer part of real UFO programs, along with Kona Blue, a proposed government program to hold recovered material, and he gives no source.
transistor-patents-traced-to-1930s-germa: Jesse Michels says that the patents for the transistor, the tiny electronic switch at the heart of modern electronics, were found to go back to Germany in the 1930s. He says this in passing, without naming a source, in an episode about whether artificial intelligence is alien technology, as a hint that the invention may have older and stranger origins than the usual story.
translucent-acorn-shaped-craft-over-fish: In 2023, in the Alto Nanay region of the Peruvian Amazon, a fisherman was pulling up his nets at night when everything lit up, "like somebody turned the lights on or the sun suddenly came up", and he looked up to see a see-through, acorn-shaped craft 30 or 40 feet above him. The researcher Tim Alberino repeats what the fisherman told him and drew for him on an acrylic chalkboard while Alberino was in the area. Alberino tells it as one of several local sightings of craft like this one.
travis-taylor-arrives-as-a-skeptic: A scientist named Travis Taylor is said to have arrived at Skinwalker Ranch, a property in Utah known for reports of strange happenings, fully doubting that anything unusual went on there. The ranch's owner, who brought him out and is not named in the record, tells it from his own memory: "when Dr. Taylor flew out to the ranch with me for the first time, he was an absolute skeptic," the point being that a doubter later became part of the team.
travis-taylor-zapped-at-skinwalker-ranch: A man named Travis Taylor, investigating at Skinwalker Ranch, a property in Utah known for reports of strange happenings, is said to have been "mouthing off" and then given a "little zap" of something like radioactivity, sometime in the 2020s. The researcher Grant Cameron tells this on Michels' show, passing it along without naming his source. Told this way, it suggests whatever is at the ranch reacts to the people there.
travis-walton-abduction-1975: In 1975 a man named Travis Walton is said to have been taken by a UFO while out with friends in a remote mountain area near Snowflake, Arizona. A researcher named James Fox stresses how remote the spot was, and Jesse Michels brings Walton up as "another good example," mentioning only that he was in Arizona with his friends. It is told as one of the well-known cases of people saying they were abducted.
travis-walton-abduction-as-shown-in-fire: In 1975 an Arizona logger named Travis Walton said he was taken by beings aboard a craft, and his story was later turned into a film called Fire in the Sky. A guest named Chris Ramsay, relaying Walton's own account, says the movie played it out "so differently" from what Walton described. Ramsay notes that the film shows the beings carrying out a procedure on Walton and ignoring his screams. Bryce Zabel, a guest who talks about Hollywood and UFOs, says he heard from the screenwriter Tracy Tormé that the studio decided Walton's real story was not good enough. According to Zabel, they told him "you have to do a better abduction." The tellers bring it up to show how far a film can drift from what a witness actually reported.
travis-walton-abduction-two-weeks-after-: In 1975 the television network NBC aired The UFO Incident, a film starring the actor James Earl Jones and based on the book The Interrupted Journey, about a couple's reported abduction, and two weeks later a man named Travis Walton said he was abducted. The screenwriter and producer Bryce Zabel points out the timing to Michels, calling the film "not that great" but noting what came right after it. The point is that a TV film may have shaped, or been followed by, one of the best-known abduction claims.
travis-walton-case-dismissed-as-fabricat: Travis Walton, a man who said he was taken aboard a UFO in 1975, simply made the story up, according to the skeptic Michael Shermer. Shermer thinks Walton was behind on finishing a work job, says Walton did not pass a lie detector test, and notes he was once on a television show with him.
travis-walton-case-fire-tower-debunk-dis: In 1975 a man named Travis Walton went missing in the Arizona woods, and his case is told as an alien abduction. Skeptics have explained the light his work crew saw as a fire lookout tower standing right next to the road. The writer and researcher Greg Bishop rejects that on Michels's show, saying the tower is not next to the road at all but over a hill, so the explanation does not work.
travis-walton-handed-over-from-greys-to-: In 1975, according to the philosopher Jason Jorjani, a man named Travis Walton, who says he was taken aboard a craft in Arizona, was first held by greys, small grey-skinned beings, until he went "down the hallway" and "bumped into these Nordics," tall human-looking beings who took over from there. Walton himself, in his own words, tells it more simply: while he was trying to find a way out, "a man came in," a "human-looking person," with no mention of a hand-off. Michels also brings up the case briefly as an example of different beings "working together in conjunction."
travis-walton-is-struck-by-a-craft-s-ene: In Arizona in 1975, Travis Walton, a forestry worker who says he was taken aboard a strange craft, is said to have been hit by a blast of energy from the craft after he ran up to it. The comedian and podcaster Joe Rogan tells it, going on Walton's own account. His point is that Walton was not chosen: "He ran up to the craft and got blasted", which would make it an accident and not a planned abduction.
travis-walton-wakes-with-a-full-beard-19: In 1975 in Arizona, a man named Travis Walton says he was taken by aliens, and when he came back days later he had a full beard even though he had shaved just before. The researcher Mike Masters tells it this way, without giving a source. John Blitch, a scientist who worked for DARPA (the Pentagon's advanced research agency) and says he was abducted himself, mentions Walton coming back five days later. Michels gives the gap as four days in one episode, and in another simply calls Walton's beard an example of a common thread in abduction stories. If true, it would suggest much more time passed for Walton than for the people around him.
travis-walton-was-dead-and-revived-1975: Travis Walton, a man who said he was taken by a UFO in Arizona in 1975, may actually have died and been brought back to life, according to the doctor Roger Leir, who studied objects he believed were alien implants in people. The scientist Steve Colbern, who studies such implants, passes on Leir's view on Michels' show. If true, it would mean whoever took Walton could revive the dead.
treat-team-under-albert-stubblebine-per-: In a 1990s email to the UFO disclosure activist Steven Greer, Hans-Adam II, the Prince of Liechtenstein, reportedly described a team called TREAT working under Albert Stubblebine, then head of the US Army's Intelligence and Security Command. The researcher known online as UAPGerb relays this from the email. It would mean a secret UFO-related team was run from inside Army intelligence.
tree-in-the-backyard-bursts-into-flame: A tree in a North Carolina backyard is said to have caught fire on its own, out of nowhere. Chris Bledsoe, a man who says strange things happen around him, tells Michels it was his own backyard, and that it then rained for two days.
trees-knocked-flat-to-the-northeast-1948: At Hart Canyon near Aztec, New Mexico, where a flying saucer is said to have crashed in 1948, trees at the site are said to be bent over all in one direction, to the northeast, as if something had been dragged across them. Scott Ramsey, a researcher who has walked the site, repeats what the investigator Bill Steinman pointed out to him: that the craft was hauled over soft trees to a dragon wagon, a heavy military hauling truck, and "notice they're all splayed to the northeast." If true, the trees would be physical traces of the recovery.
tres-coracoes-army-battalion-supports-th: In 1996 an army unit based in the Brazilian town of Três Corações is said to have sent some of its troops to support the military operation in nearby Varginha, where an unknown craft reportedly crashed and a strange being was reportedly captured. Aldo Rebelo, a former Brazilian defense minister, says that "the unit or at least part of that unit went to provide support to an operation," which would mean the Brazilian army took part in whatever happened there.
trevor-grassi-s-corridor-of-rooms-leadin: A man named Trevor Grassi is said to have found a "corridor of rooms" underground on the Giza Plateau in Egypt, about 100 meters from the shafts between the pyramid of Khafre and the Sphinx, and that it leads to a network of tunnels. Filippo Biondi, a scientist who has scanned beneath the pyramids, passes this on as what Grassi found. If true, there would be much more built under Giza than anyone can see.
trevor-paglen-s-book-on-black-project-pa: The artist and writer Trevor Paglen put together a book that is basically a collection of the embroidered patches worn by teams on black projects, the US military's most secret programmes. Matthew Brown, presented on the episode as a Pentagon whistleblower, brings it up with Jesse Michels as a source he has looked at, as a window into programmes that are otherwise hidden.
triangle-and-gravity-control-patents-tha: A researcher named Dylan Borland says that if you dig into patents for triangle-shaped craft, and for power sources and ways of controlling gravity, the trail keeps leading back to the 1950s, to work by the US Air Force and NASA, the US space agency. He tells it on Michels' show as his own summary of what he found searching Google Patents, the online patent database, without naming any particular patent. If he is right, the idea of gravity control was being worked on by the government seventy years ago.
triangle-appears-above-russian-naval-ves: In 2018, a US surveillance asset in the Pacific off Kamchatka, in Russia's far east, was watching Russian navy ships when a large black triangle appeared above them. Matthew Brown, a former Pentagon official turned whistleblower, tells it from a briefing on a secret programme he calls Immaculate Constellation. The filmmaker Jeremy Corbell repeats Brown's account, saying the triangle "materializes or decloaks or something", but he gives no place or year.
triangle-of-orbs-follow-him-home-and-app: In Blacksburg, Virginia, a triangle of glowing orbs followed a CIA contractor named Bob McGwier home and showed up in his yard, he says. McGwier tells it as the one who saw it, and says he has video of the triangle "going up and down making sure my security camera got it," as if the lights wanted to be recorded.
triangle-with-a-round-hole-caught-on-fil: In 2011, at an odd formation on the floor of the Baltic Sea, a team of divers says it filmed a triangle-shaped object with a round hole in it. Dennis Asberg, a Swedish treasure hunter whose team found the formation and who says he was there, describes it as "like triangle like this... with a hole in it." It is one of several strange things he says happened around that site, which he believes may be a craft lying on the seabed.
triangles-seen-on-launch-pads-at-groom-l: Triangle-shaped craft have been seen sitting on launch pads at Groom Lake, a secret military test site in the Nevada desert, according to a researcher who goes by UAPGerb. He did not see them himself. He says he knows "numerous people" who have, which, if true, would put such craft on the ground at a US military base.
triangles-stored-on-doe-land-across-the-: Triangle-shaped craft are said to be stored on land owned by the Department of Energy, the US agency that runs nuclear weapons work, spread across the Nevada Test and Training Range, a huge military range in the Nevada desert. An online researcher who goes by the name UAPGerb says this on Michels' show, without naming a source. If true, it would place unusual craft inside the government's most guarded ground.
tridactyl-beings-of-peru-from-the-nazca-: Three-fingered bodies found in Peru date from the Nazca period, the time of an ancient culture there that left cave art all over the area, and a genetics researcher found in them a mutation matching a human one that changes the fingers, Michels says. He tells this while talking with the musician Flying Lotus, pointing to the Mexican journalist Jaime Maussan, who has promoted the bodies. If true, it would suggest the beings were real and linked in some way to humans.
trinity-and-roswell-crashes-1940: Michels speaks of crashes at Trinity, the New Mexico site of the first atomic bomb test, and at Roswell, a New Mexico town, in the 1940s as "known crashes" of unidentified craft. He tells this himself, without naming a source, as a starting point for talk about recovered craft. If true, it would mean the United States got hold of crashed objects close to the very start of the nuclear age.
trinity-flash-explained-away-as-an-ammo-: When the first atomic bomb was tested in the New Mexico desert in 1945, a test called Trinity, people who saw the flash were left wondering what had happened, and the government told them, "Oh, we had an accident in an ammo dump." The story comes from John Brandenburg, a scientist who argues that life on ancient Mars was wiped out by nuclear war, and he passes it on as something he was told. He tells it as an early case of officials covering up something huge with a dull everyday excuse.
trinity-plutonium-fallout-plume-over-ros: After Trinity, the first atomic bomb test in New Mexico in 1945, a cloud of plutonium that didn't burn up in the blast is said to have drifted over the town of Roswell and left a strip of contaminated soil around it. The physicist John Brandenburg passes this on as something he was told. It matters to him because Roswell is the town later linked to a claimed 1947 crash, so radioactive ground there could be part of that story.
trinity-test-warning-1945: Before Trinity, the first atomic bomb test in New Mexico in 1945, the people watching were told that no one knew what was going to happen, so they should put on their glasses and keep their heads down. John S. Herrington, a former US Secretary of Energy, tells this on Michels' show and passes it on as coming from the physicist J. Robert Oppenheimer, who led the bomb project. The point of the story is that even the scientists did not know what they were about to unleash.
trip-to-russia-to-save-kgb-files: A UFO researcher named Clas Svahn says that he once went to Russia "trying to save the KGB files," meaning records kept by the KGB, the Soviet secret police and spy service. He tells it as his own trip, made to keep the material from being lost, and he gives few other details.
trojan-war-the-bronze-age-collapse-and-t: The Trojan War seems to have happened at the very moment the Bronze Age world fell apart, the collapse of the great civilizations of the eastern Mediterranean that led into the Greek Dark Age. A researcher named Luke Caverns makes this connection on the show without naming a source, suggesting the old legend may remember a real catastrophe.
trucker-s-ufo-sighting-and-missing-time-: In 1977, a trucker and Air Force veteran known only as Michael says he left Interstate 20 near El Paso, Texas, after seeing a UFO, lost a stretch of time he can't account for, and came to on government land in Nevada. He tells it himself, remembering that he thought he was still in Texas until someone told him: "No, you're in Nevada." If true, it would mean he was carried hundreds of miles without knowing it.
truman-interview-ufos-discussed-at-every: In an interview from the 1950s, Harry Truman, the former US president, says UFOs came up at every meeting he had with the military, but his commanders could never give him a solid answer about them. His own words, played on Michels's show, are: "oh yes we discussed it at every conference that we had with the military and they never had been never were able to make me a concrete report." If true, it means the subject reached the top of government and stayed unresolved there.
truman-meeting-and-the-secret-anderson-t: A lawyer named Dan Sheehan says that after a meeting with President Harry Truman in 1945, officials set up a secret fund called the Anderson Trust, based in Houston, Texas. Telling it on Michels's show without naming his source, Sheehan ties the story to figures such as General Douglas MacArthur, War Secretary Henry Stimson, the intelligence officer Ed Lansdale, the presidential adviser Clark Clifford and a man named Robert Anderson. If true, it would mean the secret was managed through a private trust outside normal government oversight.
trump-administration-attributes-new-jers: When mysterious drones were reported over New Jersey around 2024 and 2025, the first official act of the Trump administration was to dismiss them by saying the flights were regulated by the FAA, the US Federal Aviation Administration, which oversees air traffic. A Senate staffer named Kurt McConnell says this in conversation with Michels, as his own reading of the government's response. He raises it as an example of officials brushing the sightings aside.
trump-briefed-on-legacy-uap-programs-201: The claim is that Donald Trump has been briefed on secret long-running government programmes about UAP, the official term for UFOs. The researcher Matthew Pines says he is "pretty confident" Trump knows at least "broad contours that this is real", while saying how much he knows is speculation. Eric Burlison, a US congressman, goes further, relaying second hand that in the briefing Trump was told there are hybrids, part human and part alien beings, and that Trump replied, "You mean like Adam Schiff", naming a political rival. If true, a US president would have been told directly that the phenomenon is real.
trump-briefed-on-nordic-aliens: Jesse Michels asks whether Donald Trump, the US president, was once briefed on "Nordics", meaning so-called Nordic aliens. He raises it as a question, without naming a source, in an episode with a congressman about an alien briefing said to have changed a president's life. If true, it would mean a president was told about aliens of a specific kind.
trump-cancels-bedminster-trip-over-drone: In 2024, Donald Trump, then about to become US president again, skipped a trip to his summer home in Bedminster, New Jersey, because of the wave of mystery drones being reported over the state. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, as a sign of how seriously the sightings were taken.
trump-executive-order-making-nasa-an-int: Michels says that in 2025 President Donald Trump described NASA, the US space agency, as something like an intelligence agency, linked here to an executive order, which is a direct instruction from the president. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source or quoting the order. If so, it would suggest the space agency is meant to keep secrets as well as explore space.
trump-hints-at-knowledge-about-roswell-1: Donald Trump is said to have hinted that he knows something about Roswell, the New Mexico town where in 1947 a crashed object was reported, saying he would not talk about what he knows but that Roswell is a very interesting place. Michels himself relays these words of Trump's. If meant seriously, it would suggest a president was told something about the crash.
trump-on-rogan-links-jfk-records-to-peop: In 2024, on The Joe Rogan Experience, the popular podcast hosted by Joe Rogan, Donald Trump is said to have steered talk of the secret government files on President John F. Kennedy's assassination toward visitors from space. A guest named Matthew Pines describes the moment: Rogan was talking about how many people wanted the Kennedy files, and Trump answered that many people are also interested in the people coming from space. Michels, on another episode, remembers it differently, saying Trump immediately pointed to Mars. It is told as a sign that the future president was open about the subject.
trump-on-the-new-jersey-drones-2024: In 2024, when people reported mysterious drones flying over New Jersey, Donald Trump said publicly that the military could easily find out where they came from. The episode plays his own words: "Our military knows where they took off from. If it's a garage, they can go right into that garage." The clip is brought up as a sign that the government knew more about the drones than it said.
trump-pilots-say-spheres-outfly-f-22s: Donald Trump, the US president, has said that Air Force pilots, "very, very good" ones, "better than Tom Cruise," told him they had seen spherical, circular objects outfly the F-22, the US Air Force's top stealth fighter jet. A commentator named Marik von Rennenkampff quotes this on an episode built around a debate challenge to the UFO skeptic Mick West. If it were true, it would mean something in American skies can beat the best fighter jet the country has.
trump-says-aliens-are-classified-materia: In 2026, according to this story, President Donald Trump was asked about aliens and answered that "it's classified material", which led a reporter to ask, "So you're saying aliens are real?" A researcher named Grant Cameron recounts the exchange without naming a source, and also mentions former President Barack Obama in telling it. If taken at face value, the answer would suggest the government holds secret information on the subject.
trump-says-the-ufo-issue-is-being-looked: President Donald Trump is now saying that the government is looking into the UFO issue, according to Michels, who says this came a couple of months after an odd public back-and-forth between Trump and former president Barack Obama on the subject. Michels says this himself, as part of the current talk of disclosure, meaning the government openly releasing what it knows about UFOs. If it goes anywhere, it would be the White House putting its own weight behind the question.
trump-told-of-hybrids-living-among-us-du: During a briefing on UFOs, Donald Trump was told that part-human, part-alien hybrids may be living among us, and he answered, "You mean like Adam Schiff?", naming a Democratic congressman who was one of his political rivals. Congressman Eric Burlison tells this as an account he heard about the briefing, not something he saw himself. If true, it would mean a president was given this story officially.
trusted-colleagues-report-firsthand-enco: A helicopter pilot named Jake Barber, who says he flew a UFO recovery mission, tells Michels that the most trusted people he has worked with, and still works with, describe having had their own firsthand experiences with non-human beings. He does not name them or say what they saw. He offers it as support from people he trusts, not as something he witnessed himself.
trw-and-skunk-works-crates-in-close-enco: Michels says that in Steven Spielberg's 1977 film about meeting aliens, Close Encounters of the Third Kind, some crates are stamped TRW and Skunk Works. TRW is a defense and aerospace contractor, and Skunk Works is the secret aircraft design shop of the company Lockheed. He has raised this in three episodes, saying few people back then knew much about these two cutting-edge research outfits. Once he puts that "in the late 80s", and in a later episode he names Lockheed and TRW as two programs that were probably recovering crashed UFOs when the film was made, which to him hints that Spielberg knew something about hidden work on such craft.
tsiolkovsky-in-touch-with-angelic-beings: Konstantin Tsiolkovsky, called the father of Russian rocketry, believed he was in touch with angelic beings and wrote about it, according to the religion scholar Diana Pasulka, who makes the point in her book American Cosmic and calls it a belief in non-human intelligence. Michels repeats it several times, sometimes crediting Pasulka. He names the worldview cosmism, says it shaped the Russian space programme, and describes "ethereal beings" talking to us through signs in the sky. Tsiolkovsky's own 1928 pamphlet Unknown Intelligent Forces says that an influence on us by living beings "like us, only more perfect" is very possible, and that some facts point to "incomprehensible forces" in human affairs, but the word angel does not appear in it and it describes no contact of his own.
tuatha-de-danann-weather-control-magic: The Tuatha Dé Danann, the mythological gods of ancient Ireland, are said to have had magic, specifically magic to control the weather. A researcher of ancient sites named Geoffrey Drumm says this on Michels' show, summarising the myths without naming a source. He raises it as a hint that old legends may remember a real ability to shape the weather.
tulsi-gabbard-mentions-uaps-in-her-dni-c: In 2025 Tulsi Gabbard, chosen as Director of National Intelligence, the head of the US spy agencies, is said to have talked openly about UAPs, the government's term for UFOs, in her hearing before the Senate. The analyst Matthew Pines mentions this in passing, along with her apparent support for the digital currency Bitcoin, as a sign that people in power are taking the subject seriously.
tumbling-dipper-shaped-lights-near-mansf: In 1973, near Mansfield State College in Pennsylvania, he looked up above the trees and saw a group of lights that looked like the Little Dipper, except that they were moving, and moving "in a really strange way," says Jim Weiner, who tells it as something he saw himself. He tells it on an episode about alien abduction accounts, where the sighting is part of his own story.
tunguska-air-burst-as-part-of-the-taurid: On 30 June 1908 there was a huge explosion over Siberia, known as the Tunguska event, and the researcher Randall Carlson, who studies ancient catastrophes, says it was an air burst: something blew up in the sky before it hit the ground. He links it to the Taurid stream, a band of comet debris that Earth passes through every year. He says this in two episodes, one of them alongside the writer Graham Hancock, and the point is that space rocks from this stream may still pose a real danger.
tunguska-as-a-tesla-death-weapon-1908: Jesse Michels says some people believe that the huge 1908 explosion at Tunguska in Siberia, which he calls an asteroid impact, was really caused by a death weapon built by the inventor Nikola Tesla. Michels mentions this idea in passing, without naming who holds it, in an episode with a guest named Jason Jorjani. If true, it would mean Tesla had built a weapon of enormous power.
tunguska-event-blamed-on-the-fire-god-ag: When the Tunguska event struck a remote part of Siberia in 1908, the local people believed it was their fire god, Agdy, coming down from heaven to punish them. A researcher named Randall Carlson tells this, without naming a source, as part of a talk about what the event really was.
tunisian-column-inscription-of-the-canaa: A column in Tunisia is said to have carried an inscription reading "We are the Canaanites who fled before the face of Joshua the son of Nun," Joshua being the biblical leader who led the Israelites into the land of Canaan. A researcher named Tim Alberino tells this on Michels' show, without naming where the inscription is recorded. If true, it would be a written trace of people driven out in the Bible's conquest story ending up in North Africa.
tunnel-linking-derinkuyu-and-kaymakli: A tunnel runs about five and a half miles underground between Derinkuyu and Kaymakli, two ancient underground cities in Turkey. A researcher named Matt LaCroix says so on the show, without naming a source, as part of his case that something big happened in the deep past that drove people underground.
tunnels-under-saqsaywaman-known-months-b: Tunnels beneath Saqsaywaman, an ancient stone site above Cusco in Peru, were already known months before any press release announced them, according to a researcher named Luke Caverns. He says he was inside "those tunnels in September" of 2024, having got access through the site's head archaeologist, which would mean the discovery was known to insiders well before it was made public.
turing-s-paper-treats-esp-as-an-objectio: In his 1950 paper setting out the Turing test, a test of whether a machine can pass for a human in conversation, the British mathematician Alan Turing lists ESP (extrasensory perception, knowing things without the ordinary senses) and parapsychology among the objections he answers. Michels tells this himself, as something he has read, calling it "one of the craziest things" about the paper. He raises it because it suggests one of the founders of computing took mind-reading seriously enough to argue about it.
turner-s-virtual-reality-scenarios-in-ab: Karla Turner, a researcher who studied people's accounts of being abducted by aliens, described what she called virtual reality scenarios: staged scenes that seemed real, put on during an abduction. The filmmaker Tim Alberino brings up her work on Michels's show. If true, it would mean that what abductees remember may be an illusion they were put through, not what really happened.
tutankhamun-s-tomb-stays-hidden-under-ru: The tomb of the Egyptian boy king Tutankhamun lay preserved and overlooked under rubble in the Valley of the Kings until the archaeologist Howard Carter found it, in 1923 as the researcher Luke Caverns recalls it. Caverns tells Jesse Michels this from memory, as an example of how ancient sites can stay hidden for thousands of years.
tv-clip-of-a-ufo-turning-away-from-a-bea: There is a television clip, shown now and then, in which a UFO comes in from space, a beam shoots toward it, and the object turns around and leaves. A former Army sergeant named Lyn Buchanan says he has seen it himself on TV, describing how "a beam goes like that and the thing turns around and leaves," as if something in space were being fired at.
tv-globo-reporter-asks-venturelli-if-he-: In 1996, in the Brazilian town of Varginha, where many people say a strange being was captured, a reporter from TV Globo, one of Brazil's biggest television networks, stopped a surgeon named Italo Venturelli outside the Hospital Regional and asked him: "Did you operate on the ET?", meaning the extraterrestrial. Venturelli tells the story himself, and says he held back from cursing at the question only "because it was Globo TV."
tv-producer-s-master-tape-lost-on-his-de: The documentary filmmaker James Fox says that a man named Chuck Clark got a piece of footage from a TV producer in Los Angeles, and that the original master tape, on a professional broadcast videotape format called Beta SP, was lost when the producer died. Fox tells it from his own pursuit of the footage, which would matter because the best copy of whatever it showed is now gone.
tweet-the-murder-of-the-first-public-sen: The first sentient artificial intelligences made in public are said to have been "murdered," and those responsible will face justice. The Pentagon whistleblower Matthew Brown reads this on the show from his own post on X, the social media site, of 6 June 2025, and in talking about it he names Sam Altman, head of an AI company. The post itself reads: "we have not forgotten who is responsible for murdering the first sentient 'artificial' intelligences created in the PUBLIC realm, @shellenberger. Justice is coming, thanks to @FBI and @USNavy."
tweet-the-nga-tracks-nonstructured-light: A US intelligence agency that works with satellite and mapping imagery, the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency, is said to track "non-structured light-energy craft" flying around the world and to know how they work. The Pentagon whistleblower Matthew Brown reads this on the show from his own post on X, the social media site, of 6 June 2025, which says the agency "is able to keep track of all those non-structured light-energy craft flying around the world" and adds: "they were lying to you when they said 'we don't know how they work'."
tweet-the-white-house-s-predictive-ai: The White House is said to have long had a unique artificial intelligence that can accurately predict future events. The Pentagon whistleblower Matthew Brown reads this on the show from his post on X, the social media site, of 6 June 2025, addressed to the businessman Elon Musk: "As you now know, the @WhiteHouse has long possessed a unique AI capable of accurately predicting a range of future events." In another episode Michels recalls the same post from memory as Brown saying the White House has "a crystal ball," a private AI that "predicts future timelines."
twelve-town-square-witnesses-including-u: In 1996, in Varginha, a town in Brazil where a strange creature is said to have been captured, people in the town square reported military activity unlike anything they had seen before, with military trucks everywhere. The documentary maker James Fox says he talked to about 12 different people there, each telling him something different, and a couple of them described the military presence. To him it supports the idea that the army was deep in some unusual operation in the town.
twin-knocked-out-when-brother-is-sedated: In the late 1950s near Allentown, Pennsylvania, a family doctor gave Jim Weiner a shot to knock him out, and a minute later his twin brother Jack, who had not been given anything, went out cold too. Jim Weiner tells this from his own life and says a report from the family doctor and an article in the local newspaper recorded it. He tells it to suggest an unusual bond between the twins, who would later describe a shared alien abduction.
twining-best-brains-in-the-air-force-195: General Nathan Twining, Chief of Staff of the US Air Force, is said to have stated that "the best brains in the Air Force are working" on the UFO problem. Michels cites this himself from what he calls a 1971 Australian intelligence document. If accurate, it would mean the Air Force took UFOs far more seriously than it let on in public.
twining-memo-and-its-postscript-on-indep: In a letter dated 23 September 1947, General Nathan Twining of Air Materiel Command, the Air Force branch in charge of aircraft development, told Brigadier General George Schulgen that flying discs were "something real and not visionary or fictitious," with movements suggesting they were "controlled either manually, automatically or remotely"; Michels quotes the line many times, and the researchers Bryce Zabel and Marik von Rennenkampff repeat it. The letter also says a piloted craft like the ones described could be built with US knowledge of the time, but that any such work "should be set up independently of existing projects," and it raises the chance that the objects were "the product of some high security project." Michels calls this part a postscript and reads it as a hint of separate secret programmes, but in the letter it sits in the main text, not in a postscript.
twins-matching-nightmares-in-two-states-: In the late 1980s, twin brothers named Jim Weiner and Jack Weiner, one living in Massachusetts and the other in Vermont with his wife, began having the same nightmares at the same time. Charlie Foltz, who was one of the men involved in the alien abduction story these nightmares are linked to, tells it as what the twins described.
