If true, it would suggest the brothers were reliving the same shared experience from far apart.
two-air-force-generals-at-the-pentagon-k: Two generals at the Pentagon, the US military's headquarters, are said to have known everything about the UFO subject. Chris Bledsoe, a man who says he attracts UFOs and whom the episode describes as studied by NASA, passes this on from a man named Timothy Taylor ("According to Tim, there were two generals at the Pentagon that knew everything"). He gives no names or details, but if true it would mean the full story sits with a few people at the top.
two-craft-scanning-low-for-plutonium-in-: The idea is that in 1947, near Roswell, New Mexico, the site of a famous crash that year, two craft were flying low and close together in a lightning storm, scanning for plutonium, the material in nuclear bombs. One craft measured the background noise and the other picked up the signal. Dr. John Brandenburg, a guest who argues that life on Mars was wiped out by nuclear war, puts this forward as his own theory, crediting a book called Cosmic Awakening, as a way to explain why craft would be over the area at all.
two-del-rio-crashes-willingham-and-the-m: Two separate UFO crashes are said to have happened around Del Rio, Texas: one in 1955 tied to a man named Robert Willingham, and an earlier one, around 1950, at El Indio-Guerrero on the Mexican side. A researcher who goes by the online name UAPGerb says this, without naming a source, and stumbles a little over the dates. He adds that the second crash is really only talked about in the Eisenhower briefing document, one of the Majestic 12 papers, which describe a secret panel said to have handled recovered craft and include a briefing said to be for President Eisenhower. If true, one small area would hold two crash stories, not one.
two-flaming-balls-of-fire-over-the-field: In January 2007, by the Cape Fear River in North Carolina, Chris Bledsoe says he reached the top of a hill and saw two huge glowing red and orange balls of fire, about 40 feet across, hanging over a field. Bledsoe, who says he is a commercial pilot, tells it as his own sighting, calls it a craft at one point, and says he knew right away it was nothing from Fort Bragg, the Army base, or from any military; he also tells it in the book UFO of God. To him it marked the start of the strange events that followed.
two-guards-found-nearly-naked-in-the-ech: In 1977, near the town of Wall, South Dakota, two Air Force guards who had gone to answer a call at a site in an area known as Echo were later found nearly naked, according to the story. Mario Woods, an Air Force veteran who says he was himself abducted, mentions it on Michels' show as an earlier case he heard about before his own unit got there. He tells it only in passing, as a sign that strange things had already happened in that area.
two-incomprehensible-beings-in-a-cave-on: Two beings, so strange they could not be understood, were found in a cave on Titan, the largest moon of Saturn. Lyn Buchanan, a former Army sergeant, tells this as his own experience. In his words: "I found these two beings in a cave."
two-lights-over-the-uss-holland-off-spai: In 1970, aboard the USS Holland, a US Navy ship off the coast of Spain, a man named Charlie Foltz says he looked back and "saw these two lights coming toward us." Foltz tells it as the one who saw it, an unexplained sighting over a military ship at sea.
two-men-at-the-door-explain-the-implant-: In 2025, two men came to an apartment in California, explained an implant, a small device said to have been placed in a person's body, and said it was invented by a man named Konstantin Raudive. The author Whitley Strieber, known for writing about his own encounters with beings he calls visitors, says this happened to him: the men told him it "was invented by a man named Constantine Raw. And they leave."
two-men-in-el-paso-say-they-are-escaped-: Two men in El Paso, Texas, are said to have claimed that they descend from humans whom extraterrestrials took off Earth as slaves long ago, and that they escaped back. Lyn Buchanan, a former Army sergeant, tells this on Michels' show, passing on what the UFO journalist Linda Moulton Howe told him. If true, it would mean people have been living off Earth for generations.
two-saucers-at-roswell-left-melted-fiber: The melted rocks found at Roswell, New Mexico, in 1947, where the military announced and then took back the recovery of a flying disc, were really melted fiber optics from two crashed saucers whose glass-fiber light cables overheated, according to Charles Hall. Hall is a former Air Force man who says he spent three years among tall white aliens near Area 51, the secret Nevada test base, and he also tells his story in his book The Valley of the Grays. If true, it would mean two craft came down at Roswell, not one.
two-sets-of-orders-real-ones-to-san-ange: In 1965, at Lackland Air Force Base in Texas, the Air Force gave Charles Hall two sets of orders: the real ones sent him to San Angelo, Texas, and a cover set sent him to the weather training school at Chanute Air Force Base in Illinois. Hall, an Air Force veteran who says he later spent three years with tall white aliens at a secret base in Nevada, tells this about himself. If true, it would mean his real assignment was hidden from the start.
two-star-general-furious-at-doctor-s-ali: A doctor near Wright-Patterson Air Force Base in Ohio is said to have asked a visiting two-star general about alien bodies, and the general "got furious with me." John Blitch, a former scientist at DARPA, the Pentagon's advanced research agency, who says he was abducted by an alien, tells it as what the unnamed doctor told him: the doctor had done "that same thing" to Blitch, and said a general who came in about six months earlier reacted with anger. Blitch tells it because the anger itself seemed to suggest the question hit something real.
two-years-packaging-the-thruster-into-gr: After a set of experiments in Florida in 2016 on a thruster meant to push without fuel, an engineer named Charles Buhler says he and a colleague named Andrew Arjima spent about two years, up to around 2018, trying to package the device into grounded casings. Buhler, presented on the show as a figure from the US space agency NASA, tells Michels this as someone who did the work, as part of his claim that they built a working propulsion system that does not rely on ordinary thrust.
tyler-as-secret-space-program-mission-co: The religion scholar Diana Pasulka has been working with a man called Tyler, who Michels says is a mission controller for a secret space program and has worked on all its missions since the time of the Challenger space shuttle in the 1980s. Michels says this himself, to Pasulka, and calls it wild. If true, it would mean a hidden space program has been running alongside the public one for decades.
tyler-cowen-s-2017-column-on-ufos: The economist Tyler Cowen says he wrote a column about UFOs in 2017, "before it was like a thing." He tells this himself as the column's author, pointing out that he took the subject seriously in print before it became widely discussed.
tyler-from-american-cosmic-identified-as: The man called "Tyler" in American Cosmic, a book by the religion scholar Diana Pasulka, is really a NASA mission controller named Timothy Taylor, says Michels. He states this himself, without saying how he knows, and it would give a real name and job to an insider the book kept anonymous.
tyler-on-several-1940s-crashes-in-new-me: Several crashes of unknown craft are said to have happened in the 1940s at a secret crash recovery site on government land in New Mexico, a place that was not Roswell. Diana Pasulka, a scholar of religion, says she was told this by a source she calls Tyler. If true, it would mean Roswell was not the only crash and the government picked up more than one craft in that decade.
tyler-reverse-engineering-ufo-crash-debr: A man in the US space programme known only as Tyler is said to have claimed that he had obtained debris from UFO crash sites and was reverse engineering it, that is, taking it apart to learn how it works, to create game-changing technology. The religious studies professor Diana Pasulka tells this from what Tyler told her, as she wrote in her book American Cosmic. If true, it would mean alien technology is already feeding into human inventions.
tyler-s-claimed-time-travel-group-with-t: A man named Timothy Taylor is said to have told Ryan Bledsoe, the son of Chris Bledsoe, a man known for reporting many UFO encounters, that he belonged to a secret time travel group based at NASA and in Nassau in the Bahamas, run by the mid-century anti-gravity inventor Thomas Townsend Brown. Michels repeats this again and again across many episodes, citing a Twitter post by the son, the documentary Launch Fever, and the scholar Diana Pasulka's book American Cosmic, and the details shift: sometimes it is NASA, sometimes only Nassau, and in one version the time travel is only "insinuated". If true, it would tie Brown's anti-gravity work to a hidden time travel effort.
tyler-s-constant-interest-in-time-travel: A man known only as Tyler was, through the 2010s, constantly talking about time travel. The religious studies professor Diana Pasulka, who writes about belief in UFOs, says this from knowing him personally: "when I knew Tyler he was always he was always talking about time travel," a detail she raises because it may hint at what he was really working on.
tyler-s-conversion-at-the-vatican-archiv: In the 2010s, a man called Tyler went through a religious conversion during a trip to the Vatican. Diana Pasulka, a scholar of religion who was with him, says they read the Vatican's records on the saint Joseph of Copertino and on a nun, Maria de Agreda, who was said to be in two places at once, and then visited the Vatican's observatory, which is run by Jesuit priests. She says he not only converted but also changed his idea of what was sending him the "signals" he felt, and Michels, citing her book American Cosmic, gives Tyler's real name as Timothy Taylor and calls it a revelation blending technology with the phenomenon.
tyler-s-machine-room-and-ideas-for-biome: A man known only as Tyler, said to be tied to a secret US space program, says he was taken to a room holding a machine whose purpose he did not understand. There he got many ideas for medical and biological inventions, and he went on to start very successful companies from them. Michels retells this from American Cosmic, a book by the religion scholar Diana Pasulka, in an episode with her, as a hint that hidden technology might be feeding real inventions.
tyler-s-protocols-and-the-incoming-signa: A man called Tyler, who worked in the space program and built technologies and businesses, described receiving ideas as if a signal was coming in, after which he would have the information he needed to make them. The religious studies scholar Diana Pasulka tells this on Michels' show, repeating what Tyler told her; he is a figure from her book American Cosmic. If true, it would mean some inventions arrive in the mind from outside, much like religious revelation.
uap-activity-at-nuclear-sites: UFO sightings tend to cluster around nuclear sites. That is the claim of Karl Nell, a retired US Army colonel who speaks as a former official, talking to Jesse Michels. He uses the term UAP, the government's newer word for UFOs. He names Pantex, a nuclear weapons plant in Texas, and Hanford, a plutonium production site in Washington state, as places with many sightings. He says the pattern reaches overseas too, and that even the Fukushima nuclear disaster in Japan had sightings linked to it, which would suggest whatever is behind them takes a special interest in nuclear material.
uap-class-objects-coming-down-from-the-o: In 2024, objects he calls "UAP class" (UAP is the government's term for unidentified anomalous phenomena, meaning UFOs) appeared south of Picatinny Arsenal, a US military site in New Jersey. According to Jake Barber, a man who says he once used his helicopter to retrieve a UFO, they came in from the outer atmosphere, hovered into place, and then went back into space. He tells it as something he and his team saw, and if true it would mean craft were moving freely between space and the skies over New Jersey.
uap-craft-manipulate-a-subquantum-inform: Unexplained flying craft, which the government now calls UAP for unidentified anomalous phenomena, may work by manipulating a hidden layer of information beneath the smallest scale of physics. The physicist Eric W. Davis, who has advised the Pentagon, offers this as his own idea, building on the late-1990s work of the physicist Roy Frieden at the University of Arizona, set out in two Cambridge University Press books and a New Scientist magazine article on Fisher information, a way of measuring how much information data carry. "I think that there's a subquantum domain of information," Davis tells Michels, which would mean the craft control reality at its deepest level.
uap-data-withheld-to-protect-classified-: Some footage and data on UAP, the official term for unidentified flying objects, may be kept secret not because of what they show but to hide the secret sensors that recorded them. Eric Haseltine, a former senior official at the National Security Agency, the US spy agency, says he has "no doubt" that some reluctance to release material comes from it being "captured by a collection system that we don't want people to know we have."
uap-disclosure-act-controlled-disclosure: A 2023 Senate bill on UFOs would have set up an independent board with real power to dig out and release the government's UFO records. The researcher Matthew Pines describes it on the show and credits the idea to Karl Nell, a retired Army colonel. The bill is the Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Disclosure Act of 2023, which Senator Chuck Schumer, the Senate's majority leader, submitted on 13 July 2023 ("unidentified anomalous phenomena" is the government's term for UFOs). Pines says the board would act like a government agency, with power to subpoena people and declassify records, and with the President able to override it. Schumer himself says in a clip on the show that the measure he "championed with Senator Rounds" would create a board "just like we did with the JFK assassination records". The bill's own text establishes "as an independent agency" an "Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Records Review Board" that could "hold hearings, administer oaths, and subpoena witnesses and documents". The board was to send a "Controlled Disclosure Campaign Plan" to the President and the national archivist for records still held back, including "recovered technologies of unknown origin, and biological evidence for non-human intelligence". The President would keep "sole and nondelegable authority" over whether to release them.
uap-disclosure-act-eminent-domain-over-p: The researcher Matthew Pines tells Michels that the 2023 UAP Disclosure Act deliberately reached for eminent domain, the government's power to take private property for public use, so it could seize unusual material held by private companies. This would mean lawmakers believed such material sits in private hands. The bill Senator Chuck Schumer submitted on 13 July 2023 does say: "The Federal Government shall exercise eminent domain over any and all recovered technologies of unknown origin and biological evidence of non-human intelligence that may be controlled by private persons or entities in the interests of the public good."
uap-fly-around-government-teams-at-event: At government test events sometime between 2021 and 2025, unidentified flying objects, which the government calls UAP (unidentified anomalous phenomena), flew around the government's own teams without those teams noticing, says James Valor of Skywatcher, a startup that tries to summon UFOs. Valor tells it as someone who was there, saying that on the first day the objects flew around the teams and "they have no idea," which would mean the official watchers were missing what was right in front of them.
uap-gerb-ties-elizondo-to-isa-gray-fox-a: A former Pentagon intelligence official named Luis Elizondo is said to have been part of the Intelligence Support Activity, also called Gray Fox, a secretive military unit that scouts very sensitive areas ahead of the elite forces of Joint Special Operations Command, the command over America's top special operations units. Michels tells this twice: once crediting an online researcher who goes by the name UAPGerb, who ties it to a hidden "legacy program" said to hold recovered craft, and once stating plainly himself that Elizondo is "an alumni of Greyfox", without crediting anyone or mentioning that program. The point is that the man who became a public face of UFO disclosure may come from the most secretive corner of the military.
uap-hedge-tweet-responding-to-ft-alphavi: A commentator named Matthew Pines says that around 2020 or 2021 he posted a half-joking tweet asking "What's your UAP hedge?" with the hashtag Bitcoin. UAP means unidentified anomalous phenomena, the government's term for UFOs, and he says the tweet answered an article on FT Alphaville, a finance blog of the Financial Times newspaper, about risks to financial stability if the government disclosed what it knows about them. The point is that some people take seriously that such disclosure could shake markets.
uap-hit-by-hellfire-missile-video-shown-: A video of a UAP, the government's term for a UFO, being hit by a Hellfire missile, a US air-to-surface missile, is said to have been shown before the US Congress in 2025. Dan Sherman, a former Air Force sergeant who says the National Security Agency, the US spy agency for intercepted signals, hired him to talk with aliens, mentions it in passing as something a man named Eric Brent was talking about. If true, it would mean the US military has fired on one of these objects and shown lawmakers the footage.
uap-incidents-routinely-in-counter-wmd-i: Around 2018, reports of UAP, the government's term for UFOs, often showed up in the stream of intelligence used at the Pentagon to fight weapons of mass destruction, according to Matthew Brown, who is presented as a Pentagon whistleblower and says he saw this in his own work: "These were incidents that were reported um in our intelligence stream very often." If true, it would mean these sightings were a routine part of military security work, not a rare oddity.
uap-moving-at-mach-40-explained-as-large: A UAP, the government's word for a UFO, seen moving at forty times the speed of sound might be explained by what the scientist Donald Hoffman calls larger observer matrices, a term from his own mathematical theory of observers. Hoffman brings this up as the point where his ideas meet UFO reports, offering it as his own theory rather than from any source.
uap-near-plants-ages-them-10-years: A UAP, the government's term for a UFO, was hovering near some plants, and when a person walked up to it, it shot away. Afterwards, tests showed the plants nearby had aged ten years. A guest named Dave Rossi tells this twice in the same interview as something he heard about. The second time he places it in a study from about the 1970s and says the ageing happened "within X amount of hours", as a sign that these objects can affect time itself.
uap-over-the-triangle-followed-by-hoveri: During a rocket launch at Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property known for strange reports, an unidentified aerial phenomenon (an unknown object in the sky) is said to have appeared over an area called the triangle. Within minutes a Blackhawk military helicopter came over the mesa, dropped down over the property and hovered above the south field. Brandon Fugal tells this as someone who was there. He says it was one of many times they had launched rockets. Michels tells a different moment from his own visit in 2022: a rocket swerved hard to the west, as if it were avoiding something, though there was no wind to push it. He says nothing of a helicopter. Both stories hint that something unseen is in the air over the ranch, and in Fugal's version the military is watching it.
uap-science-advisory-committee-s-first-z: In 2026, a White House science advisory committee on UAP, the government's term for UFOs, held its first meeting over Zoom, and one worry raised was that officials might hand them distracting material to keep them busy, telling the researcher Avi Loeb, say, "here's some stuff, now go spend a few weeks analyzing that." This is told by the well-known skeptic Michael Shermer, who says he sits on the committee and was in that meeting.
uap-secrecy-justified-under-a-law-enforc: The US government has been keeping records on UAP, its official term for UFOs, secret by citing a law enforcement provision rather than the usual national security grounds. Michael Shellenberger, a journalist, says this was noticed by John Greenewald Jr., a researcher who requests government records. Shellenberger tells it in an episode about Immaculate Constellation, a secret UFO program he reported on, as a sign that the secrecy is unusual.
uap-task-force-members-confirm-the-egg-w: A helicopter pilot named Jake Barber says that the egg-shaped object he flew on a recovery mission one night around 2014 was non-human intelligence, meaning something not made by people. He tells Michels that senior members of the UAP Task Force, a Pentagon group set up to study unidentified flying objects, confirmed this to him. He does not name them, but he offers their word as proof that what his team carried was not human.
uap-task-force-the-grusch-inquiry-and-co: Starting around 2019 and 2020, efforts to get at the government's UFO secrets picked up speed, with the UAP Task Force, a Pentagon group set up to study unexplained objects (UAP is the government's term for UFOs), doing its work under orders from Congress. The national security analyst Matthew Pines tells it this way. He says Congress heard things after the news stories of 2017 and 2018, along with private back-channel conversations, and decided a formal group was needed to dig in, including into hidden older programs. Pines also points to the yearly defense spending law, the National Defense Authorization Act, and to the work of an intelligence officer named David Grusch and a retired Army colonel named Karl Nell.
uapx-becomes-project-x-at-university-at-: A research group called UAPx, set up to study UAP (unidentified anomalous phenomena, the official term for UFOs), was dissolved at some point after 2020 and moved to the University at Albany in New York, where it now runs as Project X. Kevin Knuth, a scientist billed on the episode as a NASA whistleblower and who took part in the original group, says so, naming Matthew Szydagis, Cecilia Levy and Tony Gorman in connection with it. If so, the study of such sightings has found a home in a university.
uas-activity-over-wright-patterson-2024: In 2024, the control tower at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base in Ohio warned a medical flight about heavy drone or unidentified aircraft traffic over the base. Michels plays the tower audio himself: "Med flight at Patterson Tower use extreme caution for heavy UAS movement on the base," UAS meaning unmanned aircraft systems. He raises it in a conversation about UFOs showing up at military and nuclear sites, as a sign this is still happening now.
uc-provost-unaware-of-laws-secretly-bene: The mathematician Eric Weinstein says he spoke with the provost, the senior academic officer, of a major University of California research university, who had no idea how laws had been changed to secretly reward universities for doing certain kinds of work. Weinstein tells it as his own conversation, and if true it suggests that hidden incentives shape university research without even its leaders knowing.
udo-wartena-s-tour-of-a-craft-with-count: A miner named Udo Wartena is said to have been given a tour of a landed craft. He knew nothing about UFOs or electromagnetism, but the occupants explained that it was driven by flywheels spinning in opposite directions. The anthropologist Mike Masters tells this on Michels's show as an example of visitors explaining how their craft works.
uffington-white-horse-and-st-george-s-dr: Right next to the Uffington White Horse, an ancient giant horse figure on a hillside in England, there is a mound known as St George and the Dragon's Mound, said by local legend to be the spot where St George killed the dragon. A guest named Geoffrey Drumm points this out on the show, without naming a source, as part of his own ideas about ancient sites.
uffington-white-horse-hill-as-a-thunders: The Uffington White Horse, a giant ancient chalk figure of a horse cut into an English hillside, is said to have been used to generate cumulonimbus clouds, the towering clouds that bring thunderstorms, apparently for the ancient stone circle at Avebury nearby. A researcher of ancient sites named Geoffrey Drumm puts this forward on Michels' show, showing a picture and naming no source. If true, it would make the figure a piece of ancient weather machinery rather than just art.
ufo-and-consciousness-stories-intertwine: In the early 1950s, American intelligence was tangled up with both UFOs and the study of the mind, all at once: the discovery of LSD, a mind-altering drug, possible recovered craft, and the first test of the Teller-Ulam device, the design behind the hydrogen bomb. A researcher named Matthew Pines draws these threads together on the show without naming a source, suggesting the two stories share a common root in that period.
ufo-claims-raised-on-the-floor-of-congre: UFO claims have been raised on the floor of the US Congress, and the philosopher James Madden says on Michels' show that this has to raise the odds that something is there. He mentions it in passing, without saying which claims or when.
ufo-enters-east-field-below-helicopter-a: At Skinwalker Ranch in Utah, a property famous for reports of strange events, a UFO is said to have dropped out of the sky, flown into the east field of the ranch below a helicopter, and then left by way of a mesa, a flat-topped hill. Michels tells this himself, passing on what a man named Brandon Fugal described, on an episode about a UFO book the Pentagon tried to censor. If true, it would mean the object moved in and out under the nose of an aircraft watching it.
ufo-flying-figure-eights-shoots-into-mou: At Skinwalker Ranch, a ranch in Utah known for reports of strange events, witnesses are said to have watched an object fly figure eights. Then it suddenly broke off and shot at low altitude straight into the mountain, with no explosion: "It's just gone." Robert Bigelow, a guest on an episode about a UFO book the Pentagon tried to censor, passes this on as what the witnesses told him, as a case of an object behaving like no known aircraft.
ufo-history-hidden-in-tom-delonge-s-fict: Michels believes that a lot of real UFO history is hidden in plain sight inside a series of fiction books written in the 2010s by Tom DeLonge, the lead singer of the rock band Blink 182, together with the writers Peter Levenda and AJ Hartley. Michels offers this as his own view, without pointing to any one passage. If he is right, the novels would be a way of telling the public true things in the form of made-up stories.
ufo-looking-ancient-cave-art-in-australi: Australia has a lot of strange cave art, some thousands of years old, that looks like UFOs, according to the comedian and podcaster Joe Rogan. He mentions it in passing in a conversation with Michels, without pointing to any specific site. For him it hints that people may have been seeing such things for a very long time.
ufo-material-seemed-to-communicate-telep: In 1962 a presidential advisor named Harald Malmgren said he held pieces of a UFO, given to him by Lawrence Preston Gise, the maternal grandfather of the businessman Jeff Bezos, and that when he touched them he heard words in his head, as if the material spoke to him telepathically. Michels tells this from his own interview with Malmgren, which he describes as a deathbed account. He places the handover sometimes at Los Alamos and sometimes at Sandia National Labs and Kirtland Air Force Base in New Mexico, and once says the material came from the cloud of a 1962 nuclear test blast called Bluegill Triple Prime.
ufo-obsessed-japanese-town-near-fukushim: A small town in Japan, beside the Fukushima area where an earthquake set off a nuclear power plant meltdown in 2011, is said to be obsessed with UFOs, and a nearby mountain, Mount Senganmori, has a museum dedicated to them. Michels brings it up again and again, drawing on a piece by the news outlet Vice that he dates to 2022, and he quotes the chief monk of a local temple: "the UFOs came after the explosion, there were so many of them I was shocked." He gives the town's name in different ways (Iino, Eno, Leno) and in some tellings adds that over half the residents believe in UFOs and that people say the UFOs helped clean up the spill, all to suggest that UFOs are drawn to nuclear sites.
ufo-over-a-big-game-in-italy-1950: The documentary filmmaker James Fox mentions, only in passing, a UFO said to have been seen over a big game in Italy, around 1957 as far as he remembers. He gives no further details on Michels's show. It comes up as one of the cases where a crowd saw something at the same time.
ufo-over-sonoma-state-college-art-event-: In December 1976, about a hundred people from the art department at Sonoma State College in California were outside with cameras and videotape when a UFO appeared about 3,000 feet above the campus, just as a man named Ted Owens had predicted. The researcher Jeffrey Mishlove tells the story without naming a direct source, and says it made the front page of the Berkeley Gazette, a local newspaper, and the Channel 9 evening news. It is told because it would mean someone forecast a UFO appearance and a crowd saw it happen.
ufo-professor-privately-agrees-ufos-aren: A professor known for studying UFOs privately admitted, around 2019 or 2020, that he did not think they come from other planets. Michels tells this himself, without naming the professor: standing at a bar during a conference, he argued that careful reasoning shows "these things are not from other planets," and the professor looked at him and whispered, "you're right." Michels tells it as a sign that experts may believe something stranger in private than they say in public.
ufo-programs-hidden-under-the-department: The claim is that UFO programmes are tucked away under the US Department of Energy, because anything nuclear is automatically treated as national security. Michels says he was told this, he thinks by Chris Mellon, a former Pentagon intelligence official, and links it to the 1954 nuclear law. That law, the Atomic Energy Act of 1954, gives the Atomic Energy Commission control of "Restricted Data", meaning information on atomic weapons and nuclear material, "to assure the common defense and security". It does not mention the Department of Energy, which did not yet exist, or any flying object.
ufo-said-to-hover-over-channeling-sessio: In the 1970s, during channeling sessions, where people spoke messages said to come from non-human beings, at the lab of a researcher named Puharich, the messages reportedly announced that a UFO was hovering over the session right then, and some claim to have seen it. An unnamed researcher tells this on an episode about a CIA scientist who says he contacted an alien council, passing on what was said by the "space kids," the young people involved. If true, it would tie the spoken messages to something physical in the sky.
ufo-shines-light-at-chernobyl-reactor-19: At the height of the 1986 disaster at Chernobyl, the Soviet nuclear power plant in Ukraine, many people nearby saw a UFO arrive, stay for three minutes, shine a light at the reactor and leave. Michels tells this on several episodes, citing the writing of a Harvard PhD he names as Jensen Andreon. In one episode he says instead that radiation at the reactor tower was measured before and after, without mentioning the light. He puts it alongside other reports of UFOs at nuclear sites, which would suggest that something is watching nuclear facilities.
ufo-sightings-in-varese-1953: In 1953, people in Varese, a town in northern Italy, are said to have seen what were called UFOs. The account is passed along on Michels's show, credited to a grandson of the radio pioneer Marconi. It is told as a sign of early UFO activity in that part of Italy.
ufo-subreddit-growth-after-the-2017-arti: Before a New York Times article about UFOs came out in 2017, the UFO forum on Reddit, a discussion website, had about 70,000 members, and by 2026 it had about 4 million. A researcher named Jason Simosa gives these numbers on Michels' show as his own summary, crediting that article for the change. He tells it to show how much public interest in UFOs grew after the newspaper took the subject seriously.
ufo-targets-in-the-remote-viewing-unit-c: In the 1980s, the Army's remote viewing unit, a secret program that trained people to describe distant places and objects by mind alone, did "a lot of UFO stuff," but it came in as practice sessions or as favors for generals rather than as official tasks. That is the account of Lyn Buchanan, an Army sergeant who served in the unit himself. If true, it would mean UFOs were studied there unofficially, off the books.
ufo-that-came-down-through-redwood-trees: Somewhere in northern California or Oregon, among tall redwood trees, witnesses said a UFO came down at a 45-degree angle and left marks on the ground. The computer scientist Rizwan Virk tells this on Michels' show as a case that the UFO researcher Jacques Vallée told him about. Virk says it got him thinking, since an object passing through tall trees at that angle would be hard to explain.
ufo-tracking-a-soviet-boomer-submarine-f: In the 1970s, a man named Pat Price located a Soviet submarine carrying nuclear missiles, and directly above it on the water there was "a huge UFO" that "was tracking it and monitoring it," according to Dan Sheehan. Sheehan tells Michels this twice and says he saw it in a file of reports kept by a man named Ingo Swann, who worked alongside Price. If true, it would mean UFOs were watching Soviet nuclear forces and US files recorded it.
ufo-trapped-in-canyon-near-belt-montana-: In 1967 a UFO is said to have gone down into a canyon near Belt, a small Montana town not far from Malmstrom Air Force Base, and been trapped there. A man named Bob Jameson tells it on two episodes about UFOs at nuclear missile bases, as something he heard about. In the second telling he adds that he later learned helicopters were sent in at daylight, and the UFO "went right through the helicopters" and got away between them.
ufo-waves-in-dalarna: Dalarna, a region in the middle of Sweden, is said to have had several waves of UFO sightings. A Swedish UFO researcher named Clas Svahn says this on Michels' show, speaking from his own field without citing a particular source. It marks the region as a repeated hotspot for such reports.
ufo-working-group-funded-by-stubblebine-: In 1986 a secret group called the UFO Working Group was formed in the United States, with backing from the retired Army general Albert Stubblebine. An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb tells Michels this comes from Philip J. Corso, a former Army officer who wrote about UFOs, in his manuscript Dawn of a New Age; in a second pass UAPGerb says it looks as if Majestic 12, a supposed secret panel of officials handling UFO matters, simply took the new name and brought in fresh people such as Stubblebine and staff from the National Security Agency, the US code-breaking and surveillance agency. If true, the secret panel lasted decades under different names.
ufos-appear-at-the-time-of-the-manhattan: Michels suggests that UFO sightings began to surge in the 1940s, just as the Manhattan Project, the secret wartime US effort to build the atomic bomb, was under way. He raises this himself while talking about the physicists J. Robert Oppenheimer and Teller and the film Oppenheimer, saying "you have to wonder at that time because that's when all the UFOs pop up." The suggestion is that something may have been watching humanity's arrival at nuclear weapons.
ufos-appeared-the-day-after-the-fukushim: Michels says that UFOs appeared around the 2011 nuclear disaster at Fukushima in Japan, where an earthquake caused a nuclear plant to leak radiation. He tells it on several episodes without naming a source, but the details change. Once he says the UFOs came the very next day. Once he says a monk at a local Shinto temple, a shrine of Japan's native religion, claimed a UFO came and cleaned up the temple. And once he points to a video in which UFOs seem to be everywhere, as if doing cleanup. He raises it as a sign that UFOs take an interest in nuclear sites.
ufos-appearing-around-high-voltage-exper: Jesse Michels says that UFOs seem, by anecdote, to show up around high-voltage experiments and particle accelerators, the big machines that smash tiny particles together. In a later episode with a Secretary of Energy he calls it rumor and names two places: the Large Hadron Collider at CERN, a large particle accelerator lab in Europe, and the Cosmotron, an accelerator at Brookhaven National Laboratory in the United States. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, as a hint that whatever these objects are, they may be drawn to powerful energy experiments.
ufos-as-homeostasis-probes-showing-up-at: UFOs may be a kind of balancing kit for the Earth itself, showing up at turning points for civilization, such as nuclear sites, to keep things steady. Michels offers this idea himself, drawing on the UFO researcher Jacques Vallée and the historian Steven J. Dick. If true, it would mean UFOs are less visitors than a self-regulating part of the planet.
ufos-at-civilian-nuclear-sites-in-hastin: UFOs have been reported not only at military nuclear sites but also at civilian nuclear power plants, including Chernobyl and Bariloche in Argentina. Michels says the researcher Robert Hastings lists six to eight civilian nuclear sites in an appendix to a book of his, and points to a famous case at Bariloche. In a later episode Michels brings it up again without crediting Hastings, and dates the Bariloche sighting to 1995. Either way, it would mean the interest in nuclear sites goes beyond weapons.
ufos-at-nuclear-facilities: The claim is that UFOs show up again and again around nuclear weapons sites and nuclear plants all over the world. If true, it would mean whatever is behind them takes a special interest in humanity's most dangerous weapons. A former intelligence official named Eric Haseltine treats the idea carefully. He says the honest answer is "maybe yes, maybe no," and points out that there are simply far more sensors around nuclear plants, so more sightings would be logged there anyway. Michels, in another episode, states it more plainly as a known pattern, saying UFOs "show up around nuclear sites all over the world," without that caveat. A Pentagon whistleblower named Matthew Brown goes furthest. He says it is "established beyond a reasonable doubt" and that the attraction covers not only nuclear sites but weapons of mass destruction in general. Brown credits a former Air Force officer named Robert Salas and a work called UFOs and Nukes for this, so his telling leans on others' research while Haseltine and Michels speak in their own voices.
ufos-at-nuclear-facilities-as-future-hum: Michels raises the idea that UFOs show up near nuclear sites, more often around the time the nuclear weapons programs began, and seem to watch them, shut them down, or sometimes switch them on, because they may be future humans protecting their own timeline. He raises it himself across several episodes, once calling it a future time-travel program laid over all the nuclear sites and tying it to the aircraft maker Lawrence Bell, and once describing the sites as a lever on how history turns out. If true, the visitors would be our own descendants making sure the past goes the way they need it to.
ufos-come-from-whatever-direction-he-loo: During night skywatching, unexplained lights are said to arrive from whichever direction the group chooses to look. Chris Bledsoe, a man who says he attracts these objects, tells Michels this from his own experience: they can turn any way and focus there, and that is where the object comes from, which, if true, would suggest the lights respond to the watchers.
ufos-denature-nuclear-weapons-putin-s-te: Ever since the first atomic bombs of 1945, UFOs have taken a huge interest in nuclear weapons and have quietly disabled them so they will not go off, according to Joe McMoneagle, a remote viewer, someone who says he can perceive distant things with his mind. He tells Michels that the last missile Russian President Vladimir Putin tried to launch as a test blew up in its silo. If true, it would mean someone outside humanity is keeping nuclear weapons in check.
ufos-never-discussed-at-the-top-of-nsa-a: In the 2000s, at the top of American intelligence, nobody spent even a moment on UFOs. That is how Eric Haseltine tells it. He was a senior official at the National Security Agency, the US spy agency that intercepts communications, and at the Office of the Director of National Intelligence, which oversees all the US spy agencies. Speaking from his own time there, he tells Michels "this is not something we spent a fifth second thinking about," which would mean the subject never reached the people running intelligence.
ufos-over-bariloche-nuclear-site-1995: UFOs have shown up near Bariloche, Argentina, a place with its own civilian nuclear energy grid, and in a famous 1995 case a commercial pilot could not land his plane because of a power outage while a UFO chased him. Michels tells this himself in four episodes, without naming a source, adding the plane and the outage only in the later tellings and leaving out the year in one. He raises it as one more case of UFOs gathering around nuclear sites.
ufos-over-nuclear-bases-every-night-of-t: Every night that Travis Walton, a man who said he was taken by a UFO, was missing, from November 5 to 10, 1975, a UFO is said to have appeared over a nuclear missile site or nuclear weapons storage area in the United States, at Air Force bases such as Loring, Wurtsmith, Minot and Malmstrom. The UFO researcher Grant Cameron tells this as a little-known part of the case, without naming his source, and offers it as a sign that the two things were linked.
ufos-over-nuclear-icbms-as-a-message-not: An unnamed researcher who appears as a guest says that UFOs are seen over nuclear ICBMs, meaning long-range nuclear missiles kept in silos, and that this might be a message to humanity. The guest says this in an episode with Jesse Michels about whether artificial intelligence is alien technology, contrasting the missile sites with data centers, where the objects are not reported.
ufos-past-present-and-future-and-the-hol: The makers of the documentary UFOs Past, Present and Future, Robert Emenegger and Allan Sandler, with Rod Serling involved, are said to have been told of contact between aliens and the military at Holloman Air Force Base in New Mexico, in 1972 or 1974. The UFO investigator James Fox tells this as a summary of the film's background, without naming who told the filmmakers. If true, it would mean the military itself pointed filmmakers toward a contact event.
ufos-seen-cleaning-up-radiation-at-fukus: At both the Chernobyl nuclear disaster in Ukraine in 1986 and the Fukushima disaster in Japan in 2011, people saw UFOs come down and seemingly clean up the radiation, Michels says. He tells this to the magician and UFO enthusiast Chris Ramsay, pointing to a researcher named Jensine Andresen. If true, it would suggest whatever is behind the UFOs watches over, and even protects, humanity.
ufos-seen-on-pine-ridge-reservation-1970: An Air Force veteran named Michael Johnson says that in the 1970s he saw UFOs on the Pine Ridge Indian Reservation in South Dakota, first one and then two. He tells it himself on the episode where he meets up again with a fellow veteran, saying only "I saw one I saw two on Pine Ridge," which would add his own sighting to his account of strange events.
ufos-showing-up-at-nuclear-sites-waiting: Michels suggests that UFOs keep an eye on humanity and appear at all of our nuclear sites because they follow a kind of "prime directive", a rule of not interfering, while they wait for us to become less violent. He offers this himself, without naming a source. If true, the visitors would be patient watchers holding back until humans grow up.
ufos-shut-down-nuclear-missiles: US nuclear missiles are said to have been shut down while UFOs were seen at the missile sites. Michels says he has personally interviewed many of the men who tell these stories and believes they are all genuine, though here he does not name any of them or give dates. If true, it would mean something unknown was able to switch off America's nuclear weapons.
ugaritic-texts-summoning-dead-nephilim: Ancient writings from the city of Ugarit, in the old land of Canaan, are said to contain rites for summoning the dead Nephilim, the giants spoken of in the Bible. Tim Alberino, a researcher who says a 12-foot giant was captured in Afghanistan, states this without naming where he read it. He offers it as proof that ancient people treated the giants as real.
ukraine-peace-deal-of-april-2022: Jesse Michels says there was a peace deal for the war in Ukraine in April 2022, right after the war started. He mentions it in passing, without naming a source, in an episode with the former Air Force officer Robert Salas about a UFO said to have shut down nuclear missiles.
ultrasound-brain-targeting-breakthrough-: A member of Jake Barber's team has recently made a breakthrough with an ultrasound system that works from outside the head, passing through the skull to target parts of the brain and help a person move "out of intellect and into your intuition." That is how Barber describes it in 2025. He is a helicopter pilot who says he flew a UFO retrieval, and he speaks partly from inside the team and partly from what his colleague told him. In one version he adds that test subjects are checked with random number generators, machines that produce random results which a person tries to influence, and that the work is done with a partner organization.
uncle-matt-missiles-disabled-at-malmstro: In the early 1970s at Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana, unexplained things are said to have shut down the base's nuclear missiles, and this "happens all the time." Kevin Knuth, a guest on an episode billed as a NASA whistleblower's story, says his uncle Matt LaCroix told him this. If true, something unknown was repeatedly switching off America's nuclear weapons.
uncle-mickey-and-general-exon-at-air-mat: In 1947, the writer Whitley Strieber's uncle, whom he calls Uncle Mickey, and an Air Force general named Arthur Exon both worked at Air Materiel Command, the Air Force's supply and research headquarters at Wright Field in Ohio. Strieber tells this to Michels as family knowledge. He raises it because it ties his own relatives to the base where, in UFO lore, crash material from that year was said to have gone.
underground-atomic-blast-for-natural-gas: Near Aztec, New Mexico, the government once set off an atomic bomb underground to blast open natural gas reserves, a test known as Gasbuggy. Michels mentions it himself, without a source, while describing the area where he says alien bodies were recovered from a crash.
underground-cavern-on-mars-with-wiring-a: Joe McMoneagle says he came upon an underground cavern on Mars with what looked like wiring and a bright red light, which later went out: "when we first caught this on Mars it was a bright red light right here." He tells it as something he saw himself and ties it to Mars mapping negatives from the Jet Propulsion Laboratory, the NASA lab that runs Mars missions, as a sign that Mars once had intelligent life.
underground-cities-built-before-the-youn: The researcher Matt LaCroix believes the underground cities of Cappadocia in Turkey were dug well over 10,000 years ago. He says they must have been built before the Younger Dryas, a period of sudden disasters near the end of the last ice age, so that people could survive it. It is his own view, given on Michels's show, and if true it would push civilisation much further back than usually thought.
underground-cities-of-turkey: Turkey has huge cities dug out under the earth, looking like enormous ant farms, according to the writer on lost civilisations Graham Hancock. He tells Jesse Michels this as a well-known phenomenon, raising it as a sign that ancient people built ambitious hidden places underground.
underground-infrastructure-at-the-nevada: Underground facilities at the Nevada Test Site, the government's old nuclear testing ground, are said to exist to house craft linked to a man named Alfred O'Donnell, along with teams that retrieve such craft. An online researcher who goes by the name UAPGerb lays out this theory on Michels' show, without a named source, tying it to the story of Bob Lazar, a man who has claimed he worked on alien craft in Nevada. If true, it would put a hidden home for recovered craft beneath the test site.
underground-us-rapid-reaction-facility-a: There may be an underground US "rapid reaction" base at Coyame, in northern Mexico, a place from which crews could respond quickly to UFO events. The online researcher UAPGerb suggests this on Michels' show, summarising a work called Sentinels of Ether and naming a man called Jake Barber in connection with it. If true, it would mean the US keeps a hidden base on foreign soil for this purpose.
underwater-ufo-bases: Unidentified craft may have bases under Earth's oceans. A researcher named Kevin Knuth, speaking on an episode about claims that NASA suppresses UFO data, says this is probably the best bet for where they come from, offering it as his own view without a source.
underwater-ufo-cases-back-to-the-1800s: Reports of UFOs in and under the ocean are said to go back as far as the 1800s, according to a recent book on underwater UFOs by the author Richard Dolan. Kevin Knuth, a scientist the episode bills as a NASA whistleblower, mentions the book in passing without giving its title. If true, it would mean the sightings are far older than the modern UFO era.
underwood-says-the-flir-could-not-have-l: In 2004, off Southern California, a Navy jet filmed a white oval object shaped like the mint known as the Tic Tac, using its infrared camera pod. Chad Underwood, the back-seat weapons officer who shot the video, says there was "no way the system would have lost" track of the object, but an active-duty weapons officer says the camera is "finicky". The commentator Marik von Rennenkampff passes both views along. It matters because if the camera could lose track, the object's sudden exit in the video might just be the camera failing rather than the object speeding off.
undisclosed-drugs-administered-for-exper: Between 2008 and 2010, at a facility called Baker Victory Services in Western New York, a boy named Jordan Jose says he was given drugs his parents never knew about. Jose, who says a secret UFO program took him as a child, tells it from his own experience: he says his medical records "do not reflect what was being administered inside the facility", that there were "all sorts of substances", and that he was "essentially an experiment".
undisclosed-finding-at-the-signal-cutoff: Where the scanning signal cuts off deep beneath the Khafre pyramid, one of the three great pyramids at Giza in Egypt, there is something that has not yet been made public, says Filippo Biondi, a researcher who worked on the scans. He hints at it only briefly ("There is something.") as part of his larger claim that tunnels and structures lie under the Giza plateau.
unexplained-10-minute-delay-on-rescue-fl: Sometime between 1989 and 1993, a rescue flight over the Atlantic, about 130 miles out from Cape Canaveral along a set compass bearing, arrived ten minutes later than its crew expected, and nobody could explain why. Greg Rogers, a NASA doctor who says he was on the flight, tells Michels "we were 10 minutes later than what we expected." Lost time like that is the kind of detail people bring up when they wonder whether something strange happened on board.
unexplained-mass-caught-as-rockets-destr: The owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a property in Utah known for reports of strange events, says that during rocket launches above a part of the ranch called "the triangle," some of the rockets were destroyed, and at the same moment an unexplained mass was recorded. The owner speaks as someone involved in the work there, and if true it would mean something unseen in the air over the ranch was picked up just as the rockets failed.
unexplained-vertical-bedrock-shafts-besi: Vertical shafts are cut into the bedrock next to the causeway, a long stone road, that leads to the pyramid of the pharaoh Khafre at Giza in Egypt. The researcher Jeffrey Drum says on Michels's show that archaeology and Egyptology have no good explanation for them as part of a royal burial. For him this suggests the site served a purpose other than a tomb.
unexplored-martian-lava-tubes: Mars has many lava tubes, long underground tunnels left behind by flowing lava, and no one has ever been inside them, so no one knows what they hold. A guest named Chris Gilbert raises this on the show, without naming a source, as an open question about what could be hidden there.
unidentified-hyperobjects: A professor named James Madden has written a book called Unidentified Hyperobjects, which offers a way of thinking about UFOs. Michels mentions it himself in passing and calls Madden "a really cool professor", but he does not say what the book argues.
unidentified-objects-repeatedly-appearin: Things in the sky that no one can identify are said to show up again and again around the most sensitive nuclear sites in the United States. Michels states this himself, without naming a source, as a reason to take the subject seriously, since it would mean something unknown is taking an interest in the country's most dangerous weapons.
union-bank-and-dulles-financing-the-nazi: American money, the story goes, helped bring the Nazis to power in Germany in the 1920s and 1930s. Michels tells it himself, without a source, saying a bank called the Union Bank funded the Nazis and that a man named Allen Dulles helped finance them too, while stationed, he thinks, "in Norway or something." A researcher named Jason Jorjani says that Allen Dulles and his brother John Foster Dulles, together with the bank JP Morgan Chase, the Rockefeller family and a man named Prescott Bush, "funded the rise of the Nazis," and does not mention the Union Bank. A researcher named Dan Sheehan tells a broader version without those names: that American industrialists wanted Hitler to set up a fascist government. If true, it would mean powerful Americans helped build the regime their country later fought.
union-bank-and-dulles-in-nazi-financing: Michels says that the banker Prescott Bush was president of the Union Bank, and that Allen Dulles, who later ran America's main spy agency, helped with some Nazi financing. He says this tentatively, without a source, during an episode on UFO secrecy and secret societies. He brings it up to suggest that powerful American figures had ties to Nazi Germany.
unit-731-data-handed-to-the-us-in-exchan: Jesse Michels says that after the Second World War, the biological warfare data gathered by Unit 731, a secret Japanese wartime unit, was marked top secret and quietly handed to the United States, which was then occupying Japan, in exchange for immunity for the people involved, including the unit's commander, Shiro Ishii. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, in an episode with a guest named Brigham Buhler about the dark history of drug companies and human experiments, as an example of governments trading justice for secret research.
unit-731-human-experiments-1930: Unit 731 was a secret biological and chemical warfare program of the Imperial Japanese Army, set up in Manchuria, in northeast China, under General Shiro Ishii, and it ran human experiments from the 1930s until 1945, Michels says. He tells it himself, without naming a source, in an episode about human experiments and the drug industry's past, as an example of how far secret programs have gone in experimenting on people.
united-nuclear-supplies-dhs-and-fbi-trai: A company called United Nuclear trains people from the Department of Homeland Security, the US agency for domestic security, and from the FBI, the US federal police. That is what Bob Lazar says. He tells it from his own experience. Lazar is a man who says he once worked at a secret government test site in Nevada.
university-of-cagliari-people-collect-th: Between about 1978 and 1981, people connected to the University of Cagliari, in Sardinia's capital city, collected ancient artifacts and the bodies of giants found on the island, according to Tim Alberino, a filmmaker who has investigated giants. He tells Michels he got this from others and does not name the people involved. If true, it would mean evidence of giants was taken out of public view by academics.
unlit-drones-hovering-over-400-ft-above-: In 2024, drones with their lights off are said to have hovered, just sitting there, more than 400 feet above Picatinny Arsenal, a US military site in New Jersey. Jake Barber, a helicopter pilot who says he once took part in recovering a UFO, tells this as something he saw himself. In his words: "These were lights off over 400 feet over Picatinny Arsenal, just sitting there."
unmarked-black-helicopters-arrive-at-ell: In the 1960s, at Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota, a sudden wave of completely unmarked black helicopters is said to have arrived over a few weeks. Michels reads this out from a witness he does not name, in an episode with the researcher Robert Hastings about UFOs and nuclear bases. If true, someone with no visible markings was moving in force onto a military base.
unmarked-blackhawks-during-notam-experim: While experiments were running at Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property famous for reports of strange events, unmarked Black Hawk military helicopters showed up in the middle of the night. The experiments were run under notices to pilots, the official alerts that warn aircraft away from an area. The ranch's owner, who says he saw it himself, tells Michels about "unmarked Blackhawk helicopters showing up in the middle of the night," which would suggest someone with government resources was watching the work.
unnamed-group-extended-low-dose-dmt-to-6: An unnamed research group is said to have stretched a DMT experience, normally a short trip on this powerful psychedelic drug, to six hours by giving it at a very low dose. The neuroscientist Andrew Gallimore mentions this on Michels' show, without naming the group. It matters to him because a longer, steadier state would give people more time inside the realm the drug seems to open.
unnamed-insider-on-a-ufo-crash-retrieval: An unnamed insider is said to have worked on a team that recovers crashed UFOs, based out of the Nevada Test and Training Range, a huge military range that includes the Tonopah Test Range. The story comes from UAPGerb, an online researcher who goes by that name, who relays the person's claim and says they carried a badge from the National Reconnaissance Office, the US agency that runs spy satellites, and a Q clearance, the top clearance for US nuclear secrets. If true, it would mean crash recovery is a real, staffed operation in the Nevada desert.
unnamed-law-enforcement-entity-investiga: The UFO disclosure campaigner Steven Greer says that in 2025 he was passing intelligence to a law enforcement body he will not name, so that it could go to people inside secret UFO programmes, get their information and interrogate them. He tells this about his own work, and if true it would mean those insiders could face official questioning.
unnamed-major-we-got-it-from-them-1992: In 1992, at Cape Canaveral Air Force Station in Florida, a NASA doctor named Greg Rogers says he saw a strange craft in a secret hangar. He says a major whose name he does not give looked at him and said, "We got it from them." Rogers tells this as his own experience, and if it is true, the military would be holding a craft that came from someone else.
unnamed-president-and-wife-see-a-ship-wh: The president of a large country, one of the G7 group of rich nations, was on holiday fishing on the coast with his wife when they watched a ship come down from the sky. Kiran Ilum Xenov, who was once president of a Russian republic and says he was taken by aliens himself, says the president told him this but does not name him. If true, it would mean a sitting world leader saw one of these craft for himself.
unnamed-raytheon-engineer-and-academic-e: To make sense of the Gimbal video, a 2015 Navy cockpit recording of an object filmed off the US East Coast, a commentator named Marik von Rennenkampff says he and others consulted a senior engineer at the defence company Raytheon who was closely familiar with the camera system, along with academic experts. Von Rennenkampff tells Michels this as one of the people who did the consulting, in a debate over whether the video shows something truly unexplained.
unnamed-southern-california-facility-sto: Non-human bodies are being stored at a facility in California that has no name or official designation, according to UAPGerb, an online researcher who goes by that handle. On Michels' show he passes this on from a source he does not name, saying at one point simply that the bodies are stored in California and at another that it is a place without its own designation. If true, it would mean physical proof of non-human beings is being kept hidden on American soil.
unreleased-photo-of-massive-triangle-ove: There is said to be an unreleased photograph of a huge triangle-shaped object hanging above water. Bob Maguire, a former contractor for the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency, says he has seen it and tells Michels "this thing is huge." He does not say where the water was or who took the picture, but if the photo exists it would be striking evidence of a very large craft.
unsuccessful-search-for-partner-michael-: A former Air Force guard at a nuclear site named Mario Woods says he spent money looking for his old partner, Michael Johnson, after the strange events they went through together in 1977, even checking hospitals, and knew only that Johnson said he came from Chicago, Illinois, without knowing his middle initial. Michels adds that Woods hired private investigators, asked the FBI, the US federal police, set online amateur sleuths searching, and was promised help by AARO, the Pentagon's official UFO office, but all came up empty until a fan's tip finally found Johnson.
unusual-rate-of-carcass-decay-on-the-ran: Dead animals on Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property known for strange reports, are said to rot at a very different rate from anything normally seen in nature. The ranch's owner, Brandon Fugal, says this, citing a man named Ben Woodruff, and offers it as one more sign that something unusual is going on at the site.
upper-paleolithic-cave-art-showing-non-h: Paintings in deep caves from the Upper Paleolithic, the late Old Stone Age, clearly show beings that are neither human nor animal, according to the writer Graham Hancock in his book Supernatural. The neuroscientist Andrew Gallimore summarises Hancock's argument on Michels' show. If so, it would suggest people met such beings, perhaps in altered states, tens of thousands of years ago.
uranium-at-skinwalker-ranch: Skinwalker Ranch, a property in the American West famous for reports of strange happenings, is said to have a lot of uranium, a radioactive metal, in the ground around it. Michels repeats this as something "they say", without naming who. It comes up as a possible modern clue to why odd things are reported in some places, if such places really do share something in the earth.
urartians-as-a-later-culture-built-on-ol: Archaeologists credit the ruins, carvings and symbols around Lake Van in Turkey to the Urartians, a people of the region roughly 3,000 years ago, because they carved cuneiform, an ancient wedge-shaped script, into some of the temples. The researcher Matt LaCroix says on Michels's show that he believes the Urartians were a later people who built on top of much older work. If true, an older and unknown culture would have built the original sites.
uri-geller-abducted-as-a-child: Uri Geller, an Israeli man famous for claiming psychic powers, is said to have been abducted as a young child, and to have gained those powers through the experience. Michels brings this up himself, without naming a source and with a hedging "I think", in a conversation about UFOs, psychics and the afterlife. He offers it as a parallel to other stories of people who come back from such encounters changed.
us-air-force-plane-lands-at-campinas-and: In 1996, a US Air Force plane is said to have landed at Campinas in Brazil while helicopters picked something up from Varginha, a Brazilian town where a strange creature was reportedly captured that year. A witness named Jose Fernandez tells it on the strength of what he says he knows, "the US Air Force made a landing in Campinas," with the film Moment of Contact and the former Pentagon official Luis Elizondo in the background, and it would mean the United States had a hand in taking whatever was found.
us-and-china-crash-retrieval-and-back-en: The United States and China are both said to have recovered crashed non-human craft and to be racing to copy how they work. The podcaster Joe Rogan relays this from Dan Farah, the filmmaker behind The Age of Disclosure, a documentary in which senior officials such as Marco Rubio, James Woolsey, James Clapper and John Brennan appear. Rogan says that "both the United States and China has retrieved these crashed vehicles and that they are also in this back engineering program," meaning taking them apart to learn the technology. A co-host named Jack, on an episode with the Navy scientist Salvatore Pais, tells a fuller version with reference to the witness David Grusch. He says the US program was buried after the Cold War, that rivals got craft either from their own crash recoveries or by infiltrating the American program, and that "now there is a race and we are not in first." If true, it would mean the secret is not only America's, and that the US may be falling behind.
us-black-psychokinesis-unit-separate-fro: In the 1970s and 80s, a secret, off-the-books US unit is said to have worked on psychokinesis, moving or affecting things with the mind. The philosopher Jason Jorjani says the evidence comes from the testimony of some of the country's top remote viewers, people trained to sense distant places with the mind, and that this unit was kept apart from the remote viewing programs that Congress eventually stopped funding. If true, it would mean the government's mind research went further than the programs the public knows about.
us-fitted-a-non-human-power-source-into-: The United States is said to have managed to put a power source of non-human origin into a craft built by humans, something like fitting a Ferrari engine into a Pinto, a cheap small car. The filmmaker and journalist Jeremy Corbell says there is evidence of this, citing sources he names, which would mean the US has made partial use of technology it did not invent.
us-in-possession-of-exotic-material: The United States holds strange material of unknown origin, according to Luis Elizondo, a former Pentagon intelligence official. He tells Michels it is his "belief that the United States is in possession of exotic material". If he is right, the government would be keeping physical evidence of something it cannot explain.
us-pilot-testifies-about-scrubbed-cia-an: An American pilot named Fred Clawson says on the record that in 1996 there were secret flights linking the CIA, the US spy agency, and the US Air Force to Varginha, a town in Brazil where a craft is said to have crashed and a living creature to have been captured, and that those missions were later wiped from the record. Michels sums up Clawson's claim, and Clawson tells it himself, explaining that "in order to secure a cargo plane, a specific protocol must be adhered to," and pointing to Scott Air Force Base, a US Air Force base, as where the paperwork for the flights would sit. If true, it would mean the United States took part in the Varginha recovery.
us-racing-to-occupy-earth-moon-lagrangia: The United States government is racing to occupy a Lagrangian point between Earth and the Moon, a spot in space where the two bodies' gravity balances so that something can hold its position there. That is what Eric Burlison, a US congressman, tells Jesse Michels, saying he knows this firsthand. If true, it would mean a quiet contest is under way this decade to claim strategic positions in space.
us-scalar-weapons-rumor: The claim is that the United States has built so-called scalar weapons, a name used for supposed weapons that work through unusual energy fields. The journalist Ross Coulthart says people have told him this second hand, and he passes it on to Michels without saying more about what the weapons do. If it were true, it would mean the country holds a secret class of weapon outside known physics.
us-scientists-lose-clearances-while-nazi: After the Second World War, the Americans who had worked for the country during the war lost their security clearances, meaning their permission to see secret material, while former Nazis were put in charge. A researcher named Peter Levenda says this without naming a source, and gives as examples the physicist J. Robert Oppenheimer and the rocket engineer Jack Parsons. In his telling, it would mean that the people who ended up running America's most secret work after the war had come from the other side.
us-soviet-agreement-to-report-ufos-affec: The United States and the Soviet Union are said to have signed an agreement, still in force, in which each side promised to tell the other if UFOs interfered with its missile early warning systems, the radars that watch for a nuclear attack. A guest named Karl Nell, speaking as an official, describes it as a pact meant "to reduce the threat of nuclear war" with a clause that "either side will notify the other if UFOs impact their missile early warning systems." A Pentagon whistleblower named Matthew Brown dates it to about 1971 and calls it an outer space treaty in which the two nations agree to notify each other when they detect UFOs. A former CIA contractor, Bob Maguire, puts it in 1971 under President Richard Nixon, during the arms talks between the two powers, and goes further: he says the "red phone," the emergency hotline between the two capitals, "was invented to stop UFOs from starting thermonuclear war." The point, as they tell it, is that both superpowers took UFOs seriously enough to write them into nuclear safety rules.
us-soviet-deconfliction-on-ufos-and-nato: Matthew Brown, a former Pentagon official who has come forward as a whistleblower, says the United States and the Soviet Union set up arrangements on UFOs for deterrence and "deconfliction", meaning ways to make sure neither side mistook a UFO event for an attack by the other. He presents this as already known, and links it to cooperation within NATO, the Western military alliance.
us-strikes-on-iranian-nuclear-sites-as-p: The idea here is that the 2025 American strikes on Iran, in which President Donald Trump sent B-2 stealth bombers to hit three Iranian nuclear sites, might be part of a hidden war between unseen entities fighting over which version of the future comes to pass. Michels raises it himself, as an open question rather than a claim, in a 2025 conversation with the neuroscientist Andrew Gallimore, who studies the psychedelic drug DMT. He asks whether earthly conflicts like this one play out against a secret backdrop of a struggle to adjust the timeline, which would mean world events are moved by forces no one sees.
us-ufo-authorities-obsessed-with-mental-: In the 1950s, the American officials studying UFOs were said to be obsessed with the mental phenomena that came along with UFO research. The claim goes back to Wilbert B. Smith, a Canadian government engineer who ran Project Magnet, a 1950s Canadian government study of UFOs, and it is repeated on Michels' show by an online researcher who goes by the name UAPGerb. If true, it would mean the US effort was quietly as interested in the mind as in the machines.
usgs-prediction-of-a-la-palma-collapse-t: A collapse on the island of La Palma could set off a tsunami that would reach up to 26 miles inland in places on the US East Coast. That is the prediction Lyn Buchanan, a former Army sergeant, credits to the US Geological Survey, the American government's earth science agency. He gives it from memory, without naming a specific report, as a warning of what such an event would mean for the coast.
usgs-seismic-sensors-track-booms-toward-: In the late 1980s, sensors run by the US Geological Survey, the government's earth science agency, picked up sonic booms coming in from the Pacific and heading toward Area 51, the secret military test site in Nevada. A researcher named Nick Cook tells this on the show without naming a source, as a sign that something fast and unacknowledged was flying to the base.
uso-incident-at-pascagoula-1973: In 1973 in Pascagoula, Mississippi, a week or two after an earlier sighting there, there was what the UFO historian Richard Dolan calls a genuine USO incident: an unidentified submerged object, something seen moving underwater. He mentions it briefly on Michels's show without naming a source, as support for the strange events in that town.
uss-curtis-deck-log-luminous-object-1954: In 1954 at Bikini Atoll, the USS Curtis, the ship that set off the hydrogen bomb test there, logged an unknown glowing object in its deck log, the ship's official running record. Michels reads the entry himself: "at 2305 an unidentified luminous object passed over ship from bow to stern yellowish orange in color traveling at a high rate of speed and a low altitude." He brings it up in an episode about UFOs watching nuclear sites, as an early example of strange objects showing up near nuclear weapons.
uss-delarov-disc-rises-from-sea-near-ada: In 1945, near Adak Island in Alaska's Aleutian chain, people aboard a US Navy ship called the USS Delarov are said to have watched a disc-shaped object about 200 feet across rise out of the sea. The researcher Richard Dolan tells it second-hand, passing on what he credits to a witness named Robert Crawford and to James McDonald, a scientist who looked into UFO reports. If true, it would put a large craft coming out of the ocean two years before the UFO wave of the late 1940s.
uss-finch-cigar-shaped-object-shot-down-: In 1962, near Johnston Island, a small US base in the Pacific, sailors on the USS Finch, a Navy ship, are said to have watched a cigar-shaped object, a "bogey", that seemed to be shot out of the sky. The UFO historian Richard Dolan tells it, passing on what a man named David Noble White Horse told him: that the men were all talking about the object afterwards. If true, it would mean the US military brought down an unknown craft decades ago.
uss-jackson-video-of-multiple-erraticall: The crew of the USS Jackson, a Navy warship off Southern California, filmed several unexplained objects moving erratically at night. A retired Navy admiral named Tim Gallaudet says a Navy officer named Alexander Wiggins, who served on the ship, shared the video with him. Gallaudet tells it as more evidence that strange objects were active around Navy ships in that region.
uss-john-f-kennedy-orb-and-systems-failu: On 2 July 1971, at 8:30 at night aboard the US aircraft carrier John F. Kennedy at sea, every incoming communication suddenly turned to gibberish, in a story about a glowing orb and the ship's systems failing. The researcher Richard Dolan passes this on from a man named James Kopp, who says he was running communications that night, and whose account Dolan ties to the Disclosure Project, an effort that collected testimony from former military witnesses. If it is true, something near the ship was able to knock out a warship's communications.
uss-nautilus-fitted-with-a-side-hatch-to: Sometime between 1963 and 1966, the submarine USS Nautilus is said to have been fitted with a special side hatch so it could pick up unknown disc-shaped objects in the ocean. The UFO historian Richard Dolan tells this second-hand. He repeats what someone told him at the International UFO Congress, a UFO conference. If true, it would mean the Navy was set up to collect unknown craft from under the sea.
uss-omaha-sphere-as-a-heat-source-going-: A 2019 video taken from the US Navy ship USS Omaha off San Diego shows a round object that seems to drop into the sea, but if you zoom in, it looks more like an expanded heat source going down behind the horizon, says the UFO skeptic Mick West. He offers this reading to Jesse Michels in a debate, drawing on the scientist Phil Metzger. If he is right, the famous sphere did not plunge into the water at all.
uss-omaha-sphere-video-2019: In July 2019, off the coast of San Diego, a round object was filmed near the Navy warship USS Omaha, and it is said to have dropped down into the sea. Jesse Michels calls it a very controversial case while debating the skeptic Mick West, and he credits the reporters George Knapp and Jeremy Corbell, who brought the video out. A retired Navy admiral named Tim Gallaudet tells it secondhand from an officer named Alexander Wiggins, who Gallaudet thinks was on the Omaha's bridge, and for him the key point is the sphere going into the water, because that would mean such craft can travel under the sea.
uss-paul-hamilton-reports-an-object-spla: In 2019, off Southern California, the USS Paul Hamilton, a US Navy destroyer, is said to have reported an unknown object splashing down into the sea, about 24 hours after an earlier sighting. The writer Marik von Rennenkampff describes it, pointing to the ship's deck log and an event briefing released under FOIA, a US law that lets anyone request government records. If true, it would mean a Navy ship logged an unidentified object entering the ocean.
utopia-region-renamed-galaxias-chaos-aft: In the 1980s, after a second face-like shape was found on the surface of Mars, the region it sat in was renamed from "Utopia" to "Galaxias Chaos." That is what the physicist John Brandenburg says, speaking from his own involvement in the research. Brandenburg argues that life on Mars was destroyed in a nuclear war, and he does not say who made the name change.
v-shaped-object-in-the-desert-turns-out-: During the Race Across America, a long-distance bicycle race across the country, sometime in the 1980s, he saw what looked like a shiny V-shaped object over the desert, and it turned out to be a flock of geese, says Michael Shermer, a well-known skeptic.
