He tells it as his own experience, on an episode where he debates UFOs with Michels, to show how ordinary things can look strange.
v2-rocket-goes-off-course-into-mexico-as: In the late 1940s a V2, the long-range rocket Nazi Germany built during the Second World War, went off course and came down on a place in Mexico, and it was meant as a warning. The researcher Jason Jorjani tells this without naming a source. If true, it would mean the stray rocket was a message, not an accident.
va-ptsd-program-with-flashing-images-and: A military veteran named Dylan Borland says that in 2016 and 2017 the Department of Veterans Affairs, which cares for US veterans, put him in a strange treatment program for post-traumatic stress where they flashed images at him and blasted air horns. He tells it from his own experience, points to his medical records, and links the program to Langley, the home of the CIA, which would suggest the intelligence agency had a hand in his care.
va-treatment-program-with-flashing-image: In 2017, while working for BAE, a large defence contractor, Dylan Borland says the VA, the US government's health system for military veterans, put him through a treatment programme of flashing images and constant MRI brain scans, while at the same time denying all his veterans' benefits. Borland tells it as his own experience and points to his medical records, as a sign that he was being studied rather than cared for.
vacuum-energy-secrecy-to-prevent-weaponi: The idea is that the US government may have found out that it is "not that hard after all" to pull energy out of the physical vacuum, the seemingly empty background of space, and then kept it secret so the discovery could not be turned into a weapon. A researcher and former Senate staffer named Kurt McConnell offers this as a what-if, without naming a source, and links it to the work of the inventors Nikola Tesla and T. T. Brown. If it were true, a nearly limitless energy source would exist and be hidden on purpose.
vaddo-tungsten-fragment-from-1957-car-st: In 1957, two carpenters were driving through the night at Väddö, northeast of Stockholm in Sweden, when an object came in from the east, made a U-turn and hung in the air right in front of their car, and the car died completely. The Swedish UFO researcher Clas Svahn tells the case, which is remembered for a fragment of tungsten metal linked to it, as one he knows from his research, without naming a source. If it happened, it would be a close encounter that left something physical behind.
valentine-archuleta-sees-the-craft-hit-t: In 1948, on his family ranch near Aztec, New Mexico, a man named Valentine Archuleta looked up, saw a craft in the sky and watched it hit the mesa, according to his granddaughter. She tells it standing on the land, passing on what he told her: "he saw it hit right here." It is told as an eyewitness account backing the claim that a craft came down near Aztec that year.
valerie-ransone-arrives-at-lab-nine-1978: In 1978 a woman named Valerie Ransone, who was said to be able to channel information from beyond, somehow ended up at Lab Nine, the research lab run by a man the guest calls Puharich. An unnamed researcher on the show tells this without naming a source, and also mentions the astronaut Gordon Cooper in the same story.
valerie-ransone-runs-the-whip-inflation-: A woman named Valerie Ransone worked in President Gerald Ford's White House in the mid-1970s, where she ran Whip Inflation Now, Ford's public campaign urging Americans to help bring prices down. The researcher Jeffrey Mishlove, who holds a doctorate and studies psychic phenomena and the afterlife, says he knew her then: "when I knew her, she was working in the Gerald Ford White House." He tells it to show that someone in his circle had a real place at the center of government.
valerie-ransone-the-ether-ship-group-and: In the 1970s a woman named Valerie Ransone is said to have worked in the White House while also trying to talk with aliens through xenolinguistics, the study of alien languages, alongside a contact group called the Ether Ship, led by a man named Willard de Bogart. Michels tells this himself on two episodes, and the details shift: once he says she was simply in the White House, and once he calls her an intelligence operative of the Nixon years with ties to the top of government who reached out to the group, crediting the account to the researcher Jacques Vallée. If true, it would mean someone close to the highest levels of government was quietly trying to make contact.
validation-scan-of-the-gran-sasso-physic: The scientist Filippo Biondi, known for scanning beneath the pyramids of Egypt, says he took measurements of the physics laboratory at Gran Sasso d'Italia in Italy to test his scanning method on a known site. He tells it as his own work, adding on a later episode that he did it in 2024 and used a different, experimental processing technique, "like an experiment," which matters because a working test there would lend weight to his pyramid scans.
validation-scan-of-the-osiris-shaft: To check that their method worked, a scientist named Filippo Biondi says his team also scanned the Osiris shaft, a well-known underground structure at Giza in Egypt. Biondi uses scans to look beneath the pyramids, and he tells this as part of his own work. Testing the method on a structure everyone already knows is meant to show that the method can be trusted on the unknown ones.
vallee-and-davis-six-level-uap-paper: The UFO researcher Jacques Vallée and the physicist Eric W. Davis wrote a paper setting out six levels of UAP, the official term for unidentified flying objects, running from solid machines at the bottom to spiritual or otherworldly sides at the top. Michels mentions the paper himself, without giving its date, praising it as a good way to sort the many faces of the phenomenon.
vallee-argues-with-spielberg-on-close-en: The UFO researcher Jacques Vallée is said to have gotten into an argument with the film director Steven Spielberg on the set of Close Encounters of the Third Kind, the 1977 film about human contact with visitors from space. The story's title says the quarrel was about time travel. Michels tells this himself in passing, without naming a source or saying how it ended, as a sign that Vallée held views of his own that clashed with the filmmaker's.
vallee-finds-a-classified-battelle-lette: The scientist and UFO researcher Jacques Vallée is said to have found a classified letter showing that a private research contractor, Battelle, was quietly running a second UFO study alongside Blue Book, the US Air Force's UFO study of the 1950s and 60s. The story goes that Vallée came across it while going through Blue Book files kept by the astronomer J. Allen Hynek, who advised the Air Force study. A UFO investigator named James Fox tells it as he has heard it: Vallée "came upon a file" that "was classified that he shouldn't have seen", a letter signed by a Battelle man named Howard C. Cross. Fox credits the documentary The Phenomenon. Michels tells it several times himself and calls the paper the Pentacle memo. In one version he dates it to 1953 and ties it to the report of the Robertson panel, a government panel on UFOs. In another he says Battelle "was behind the scenes" from the start of Blue Book, and draws a line to modern Pentagon officials such as Sean Kirkpatrick and Ronald Moultrie. To those who tell it, the letter suggests the public study was not where the real work was done.
vallee-hints-bob-lazar-was-an-mk-ultra-s: Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on reverse engineering alien craft at a secret site in Nevada, may actually have been a subject of MK Ultra, a CIA mind control program, and brainwashed into believing his story. Michels says this is what the computer scientist and UFO researcher Jacques Vallée hints at in his book Revelations: Alien Contact and Human Deception. If so, Lazar's account would be a product of government manipulation rather than real work on UFOs.
vallee-in-james-fox-film-ai-created-by-a: The longtime UFO researcher Jacques Vallée has suggested that people may be dealing with an artificial intelligence that was itself built by a non-human intelligence from another planet. The researcher Jason Simosa passes this on second-hand. He says Vallée said it recently in a film by the documentary maker James Fox, which would make the phenomenon a machine sent by someone else and not the beings themselves.
vallee-knows-more-than-he-can-communicat: Jesse Michels says that when he talks with Jacques Vallée, a longtime researcher of UFOs, he gets the feeling that Vallée "knows a lot more than he can even communicate" about the subject. This is Michels's own impression from his conversations, shared in a 2025 episode with the philosopher James Madden. If he is right, one of the field's best-known figures would be holding back more than he says in public.
vallee-on-ransone-s-nro-satellite-work-1: In the late 1970s, around Houston, a woman named Valerie Ransone was doing some kind of work for the National Reconnaissance Office, the US agency that runs spy satellites, according to the UFO researcher Jacques Vallée, who says he spoke with her then. An unnamed researcher on the show summarises this from Vallée's published journals, Forbidden Science, without going into more detail, and offers it as a sign that she had ties to intelligence work.
vallee-pasulka-theory-that-the-1947-rosw: This theory holds that the reported crash of an unknown craft near Roswell, New Mexico, in 1947 marks a dividing line, separating the spirits and strange beings of older folklore from the 'aliens' people have described since. Michels says it is the theory he likes best, and credits it to the researcher Jacques Vallée and the religious studies scholar Diana Pasulka, in a 2021 episode with the Stanford scientist Garry Nolan. If true, it would mean the same phenomenon has always been with us and only changed its face in 1947.
vallee-s-1985-cia-document-on-staged-abd: A 1985 document from the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency, is said to describe operations in Argentina and Brazil in which peasants were abducted so they would believe aliens had taken them, for what the document calls, as Steven Greer quotes it, "psychological warfare value." Greer, a researcher, credits the writer Jacques Vallée, whose 1992 book is listed as the source, and in another moment urges listeners to look it up, saying the CIA states "black and white" that "we're conducting the abductions," speaking there as if this happened worldwide. If real, it would mean some abduction stories were staged by an intelligence agency.
vallee-s-260-000-case-capela-database: The UFO researcher Jacques Vallée is said to have built a collection of some 260,000 reported cases, called the Capela database. A researcher named Jason Simosa mentions it in passing, without saying more about where the figure comes from. It is raised to show how large a record of sightings one researcher has gathered.
vallee-s-assessment-of-the-billy-meier-p: In the late 1970s, a Swiss man named Billy Meier put out photographs that he said showed alien spacecraft, and according to the researcher and philosopher Jason Jorjani, the computer scientist and longtime UFO researcher Jacques Vallée studied some of them. Jorjani says only that "Jacques Vallée has looked at some of these photos". He mentions it as an expert's look at some much-argued-over pictures, and he does not say what Vallée concluded.
vallee-s-control-system-steps-in-when-a-: The idea here is that whatever lies behind UFOs acts like a control system over humanity: it "knows how to nip at the herd", and when a nuclear weapon is about to go off, it shows up. Michels brings this up himself, in a talk with a guest named James Madden, as a borrowing from the UFO researcher Jacques Vallée, who described the phenomenon as something that steers human behaviour. If true, it would mean the visitors step in at the moments when humanity is closest to destroying itself.
vallee-s-diaries-keep-pointing-to-the-ca: In his published diaries, Forbidden Science, which run to five volumes, the UFO researcher Jacques Vallée describes lunches with well-connected intelligence insiders who keep telling him to look at the Carlyle Group, a multinational investment firm with large defense interests, says Michels. Michels brings this up himself, around volume three or four, and asks his guest Matthew Pines whether there is anything to what he calls Vallée's theory. It would suggest a private defense-linked firm plays some part in the UFO secret.
vallee-s-fairy-alien-parallels-in-passpo: Old stories of fairies and elves are said to match modern alien abduction stories closely, an idea from the researcher Jacques Vallée in his book Passport to Magonia. The writer Graham Hancock lays it out: in the old tales, fairies and elves "would do surgery on people," abduct them, have sex with them and produce hybrid babies, just as in abduction accounts, and he links this to his own book Supernatural. Michels, in a later episode, calls Passport to Magonia a great book whose argument was "heretical to both believers and debunkers," framing it as the same phenomenon wearing different cultural masks over time. He applies it to a 1977 case at Ellsworth involving Air Force veterans who say they were abducted. If true, fairies and aliens would be one thing seen through different eras.
vallee-s-invisible-college-research-grou: In the 1970s, the UFO researcher Jacques Vallée called his independent group of fellow UFO researchers the Invisible College, and he gave the same name to his landmark book about what they learned. Michels tells this himself in two episodes, and in one he says the group included the astronomer J. Allen Hynek. He explains the name as a tribute to Robert Boyle, an early scientist, which links modern UFO study to an older tradition of scholars working quietly outside official institutions.
vallee-s-journals-pasulka-told-not-to-ta: In his published journals, the UFO researcher Jacques Vallée describes a conversation with the religion scholar Diana Pasulka, who told him that a man named Timothy Taylor had warned her against talking about 'the hybrid thing', meaning the idea of human and alien hybrids. The researcher Jason Simosa recounts this from the journals, and he is unsure of the details as he tells it. He offers it as a sign that someone wanted the hybrid subject kept quiet.
vallee-s-own-ufo-sighting-at-age-15-1950: In the 1950s, in France, a 15-year-old boy saw a strange object outside his room, above the yard. The boy was Jacques Vallée, who later became a well-known UFO researcher, and he tells it as his own sighting. He describes it simply as "that object outside the room over the yard," a sighting that came before his long study of the subject.
vallee-s-study-of-small-ufo-religions-19: In the 1970s, Jacques Vallée, a scientist who has studied UFO reports for decades, spent a while going around visiting little religions built around UFOs. He tells this himself, saying it went into other books of his, including Messengers of Deception, and it matters to him because it shows how UFO beliefs can be used to shape people.
vallee-s-the-invisible-college-1975: The Invisible College, a book by the UFO researcher Jacques Vallée published in 1975, is still "the tip of the spear now, in terms of theory on UFOs," according to Michels. He says this himself while interviewing a guest, pointing readers to the book. His point is that thinking from nearly fifty years ago is still ahead of today's ideas on the subject.
vallee-says-there-are-protocols-for-leav: The UFO researcher Jacques Vallée is said to have confirmed that there are "protocols" for leaving "the cave". The cave is Plato's allegory of the cave, an old Greek story about prisoners who take shadows on a wall for the whole of reality. Michels tells it as his own exchange: he asked Vallée whether such protocols exist and says Vallée answered, "Yes, there are," though Michels does not say what they are.
vallee-shows-pasulka-the-history-of-sata: The computer scientist and UFO researcher Jacques Vallée once showed his guest an odd book from his collection, titled The History of Satan, with "big words on it that says Satan". The guest was Diana Pasulka, a professor who studies religion and UFO belief, and she says it happened while she was with him, which she places in his study in the San Francisco Bay Area. In one telling she sets it over lunch and adds that the book had 666 pages, the number the Bible ties to the beast.
vallee-suspected-a-secret-real-project-b: In the 1960s, the French UFO researcher Jacques Vallée suspected that Project Blue Book, the US Air Force's public UFO study of the 1950s and 60s, was a front, and that a real, secret project was running behind it. Vallée says so himself, recalling that he felt "they had a real project going on that was secret." In a later episode Michels repeats it secondhand, placing it in the 1950s and 60s and saying Vallée "told me the exact same thing" to back up another guest's claim of a hidden program.
vallee-urges-hynek-to-review-blue-book-s: In 1964 the researcher Jacques Vallée met J. Allen Hynek, a scientist who worked with Project Blue Book, the US Air Force's UFO study of the 1950s and 60s, at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base in Dayton, Ohio, and urged him to look again at the cases the Air Force had filed away as "psychological." The UFO investigator James Fox tells it, repeating what he learned of the meeting and pointing to the Blue Book files. He tells it because it would mean cases the Air Force had written off may have held more than they seemed.
vallee-writes-the-foreword-to-the-french: The computer scientist and UFO researcher Jacques Vallée says that he wrote the foreword to the French edition of a book by Rizwan Virk, a writer who argues that our world may be a kind of simulation. Vallée tells it himself: he read Virk's second book, was asked to write the foreword, and agreed "because by then I was hooked." It shows a leading UFO researcher taking the simulation idea seriously.
van-allen-radiation-belt-impassable-1960: The Van Allen belts are bands of radiation circling the Earth, and the physicist they are named after, James Van Allen, is said to have warned that their radiation was 150 times what a human body can take. Michels passes this on from the podcaster Danny Jones, who raised it on his own show, and he also mentions the rocket engineer Wernher von Braun. It matters because, if true, it would raise questions about how astronauts could safely pass through the belts in the 1960s.
van-flandern-alerts-harrington-to-pionee: In the 1980s, an astronomer at the US Naval Observatory named Thomas Van Flandern is said to have phoned his colleague, the astronomer Robert Harrington, and told him he had to look at data from Pioneer 10, a NASA probe sent to the outer solar system, which seemed to point to a planet beyond the Kuiper belt, the ring of icy bodies past Neptune. The author Matt LaCroix tells this, relaying the call as the two men described it. If true, it would mean an unknown large planet sits at the edge of our solar system.
van-flandern-and-harrington-both-die-of-: Two astronomers, Thomas Van Flandern and Robert Harrington, led the search for an unknown planet, and possibly a companion star, at the edge of our solar system, and both later died of throat cancer even though neither smoked. The researcher Matt LaCroix tells this without naming a source, though once he points to a work called The Stage of Time, and he notes that the deaths came within a few years of each other. He brings it up because it hints that their deaths may have been linked to what they were looking for.
van-flandern-s-speed-of-gravity-argument: A physicist named Van Flandern argued that gravity's pull travels at least two billion times faster than light. The researcher Rupert Sheldrake passes this on as something Van Flandern argues, without naming where the argument appears. If it were true, it would break the accepted rule that nothing moves faster than light.
van-tassel-s-contact-with-venusians-1950: In the 1950s, a man named George Van Tassel said he was in contact with beings from the planet Venus. The philosopher Jason Jorjani mentions this in passing on Michels' show and does not name a source, as one of several claims of the time that, if taken seriously, would mean beings from elsewhere were speaking to people directly.
van-tassel-s-venusian-nordics-and-the-hy: In the 1950s, George Van Tassel, a man who held UFO gatherings at Giant Rock in the California desert, said that tall, fair-haired beings from Venus known as the Nordics had given him teachings. Among them, he said, was a story of hybrid 'lower races'. The philosopher Jason Jorjani relays this from a book called Closer Encounters, as an example of how contact claims came with their own religious account of human origins.
vandenberg-and-malmstrom-as-recurring-uf: Two American military bases are said to be places where UFO sightings keep coming back over the years. One is Vandenberg Air Force Base in California, the other is Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. Michels says this himself, without naming a source, in an episode about a guard at a nuclear missile site who says he was taken by aliens, and he uses it to suggest that these bases draw unexplained visitors again and again.
vandenberg-ufo-takes-down-dummy-warhead-: In September 1964, a test rocket called an Atlas was launched from Vandenberg Air Force Base in California carrying a dummy nuclear warhead, and on film a saucer-shaped object is said to have flown up to the warhead, circled it and fired beams of light at it until it tumbled off course. Bob Jacobs, an Air Force photo specialist who filmed it, tells it first hand. He says the launch "popped up through the fog," and that when the film was reviewed, "suddenly into that frame an object flew in chasing the warhead." Jacobs credits his supervisor, Major Florenze Mansmann, who Michels says backs the story. Michels tells the case many times, drawing on Robert Hastings's book UFOs and Nukes, and he cites Jacobs's DD214, a US military discharge record, as proof of his service. His details shift: he places Jacobs 100 miles up the coast at Big Sur with a telescope, gives speeds from 8,000 to 12,000 miles an hour, says "four directed energy beams" were fired, and says the film was taken away. The journalist Ross Coulthart, citing an Omni magazine article, says the film showed a UFO "shooting at it with a laser beam," though he puts the launch near Edwards Air Force Base. The filmmaker James Fox also brings it up. If true, something was able to track and disable a nuclear warhead in flight.
vanessa-found-the-teller-tape-for-the-do: A researcher named Luigi Vendittelli, who spent time with Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft in Nevada in 1989, says a woman named Vanessa is the one who found a recording he calls the teller tape. "We wouldn't have found the teller tape if it wasn't for Vanessa," he says, telling it as part of the work on a documentary in Las Vegas. He gives it as evidence tied to Lazar's story from 1989.
vanguard-enterprise-nonprofit-for-uap-wh: A Pentagon whistleblower named Matthew Brown says that in 2026 he and a fellow whistleblower named Dylan Borland started a nonprofit called Vanguard Enterprise, "Vanguard for short," to support people who come forward about UAP, the government's term for UFOs, and that Jeffrey Nusatelli has since joined. Borland, telling it on his own episode, says its aim is "to help whistleblowers and their families medically, financially, spiritually, emotionally."
vannevar-bush-and-the-early-ufo-program-: Vannevar Bush, the engineer who led American wartime science and wrote the report The Endless Frontier on the future of US research, is said to have been part of an early secret government UFO program. Michels raises this himself, in a talk with the UFO historian Richard Dolan, saying the physicist Robert Sarbacher said Bush "was part of the program initially." It would put one of the most powerful scientists of the era at the heart of the early UFO secret.
vannevar-bush-s-post-war-science-structu: The mathematician Eric Weinstein argues that in the 1940s gifted wartime science administrators such as Vannevar Bush built structures for running American research, and that these worked well but the knowledge of what they were was never passed on, so they carry on like a zombie. Weinstein offers this as his own reading, without naming a source. If he is right, parts of US science could still be run by systems that no one in charge fully understands.
vannevar-bush-s-wartime-research-and-dev: During the war, the engineer Vannevar Bush ran a research and development board that pulled professors out of universities to work on government projects, and those in charge realised this was a great way to run secret research. A researcher named Grant Cameron tells this without naming a source, in a talk about who ran the government's UFO work.
varginha-being-taken-alive-to-regional-a: In 1996, in the town of Varginha in Brazil, a strange being from a reported crash is said to have been taken alive first to a hospital called Regional and then on to another called Humanitas. The journalist James Fox, who has investigated the case and interviewed its witnesses, says this route has been known for decades: "it went initially alive to regional right that it was humanitas." If true, it would mean a living non-human creature was moved through ordinary town hospitals.
varginha-crash-and-captured-being-1996: In 1996, in the town of Varginha in Brazil, a cigar-shaped object "kind of like a Tic Tac" (a white oval shape, like the mint) is said to have fallen, and three beings came out. One was caught and taken to a hospital, where, as Michels puts it, "everyone who works at the hospital says they saw the being," and the beings are said to have smelled of sulfur and ammonia. Michels retells this from the filmmaker James Fox's research, his film Moment of Contact and a witness named Carlos de Souza, and says separate sources all describe it the same way.
varginha-et-as-a-national-celebrity-1996: In 1996 a strange being was reported in Varginha, a town in the Brazilian state of Minas Gerais, and the creature went on to become a famous figure across Brazil, known as the Varginha ET. Aldo Rebelo, a former defence minister of Brazil, tells Michels that "that event created a celebrity in Brazil." He says this to show how deep the case runs in Brazil's public life.
varginha-neurosurgeon-and-new-witness-te: In 1996 a strange creature is said to have been captured in the town of Varginha, Brazil, and now there are new witnesses: two forensic pathologists (doctors who examine bodies after death), the town's police chief, a new witness to the crash, and the head neurosurgeon at the regional hospital, a doctor named Italo Venturelli. The filmmaker James Fox, who made the documentary Moment of Contact, describes this new testimony on Michels's show in December 2025. He tells it because if these medical and police witnesses are right, a living or dead being was handled by real doctors and officials.
varginha-records-strictly-classified-at-: Brazil's Ministry of Defense keeps its files on the 1996 Varginha case secret. That case is the reported crash of a craft near the Brazilian town of Varginha and the capture of a creature there. Aldo Rebelo, a former Brazilian defense minister, says so himself: "The information that's held by the Ministry of Defense is strictly classified," which would mean the government holds records of the event that it has never released.
varginha-town-hall-creates-a-ufo-museum-: After the 1996 events in Varginha, a town in the Brazilian state of Minas Gerais where residents reported seeing a strange being, the town hall set up a museum to recognise the phenomenon. Aldo Rebelo, who has served as Brazil's defence minister, tells Jesse Michels that the town hall created it "to acknowledge and value the phenomenon." He offers this as a sign that local authorities took the episode seriously instead of dismissing it.
varginha-witness-held-shape-returning-ma: In 1996, after a craft is said to have crashed near Varginha, Brazil, a witness says he picked up a piece of it that sprang back into shape when he bent it. That witness, Carlos de Souza, tells it himself: "this foil or this sheet regained its shape." Jesse Michels interviewed him and repeats the story in other episodes. He describes the material as light and like tinfoil, and says it went back to its original form like a memory metal. He likens it to the debris from Roswell, the 1947 crash in New Mexico at the center of American UFO lore. Italo Venturelli, another guest in the same episode about the case, also mentions the testimony of the man who saw the craft and picked up a piece, though he does not mention the shape-returning. If true, it would mean two crashes decades apart left behind the same strange material.
varginha-witnesses-in-dc-and-fbi-letter-: Witnesses to a 1996 case from the town of Varginha in Brazil came to Washington DC, and a US congressman named Eric Burlison says he was there to hear them after their meeting. He says he was there with the documentary maker James Fox and the journalist Leslie Kean, and he tells it as something he took part in. The point of the story is that a sitting member of Congress heard the Brazilian witnesses in person.
vatican-archives-ceremony-with-bledsoe-s: In 2017 there was a ceremony at the Vatican archives where a photo taken by Chris Bledsoe was placed between books by Galileo and Copernicus, and his picture was hung beside the pope's outside the archives. That is according to Bledsoe himself, a man who says he has had repeated UFO encounters, and he passes it on from what he was told by Diana Pasulka, a religion professor, and a man named Timothy Taylor. To him it is a sign that the Church takes his experience seriously.
vatican-confiscated-the-fatima-prophecy-: Michels says the Vatican seized one of the prophecies given in 1917 at Fatima, Portugal, by children he vaguely calls "the orphans or whatever". He mentions it in passing, citing a source called Secrets of Fatima, in an episode about a secret society and a final event. To him it suggests the Church kept back something it had been told.
vatican-dossier-and-joint-ss-italian-stu: The Vatican, the seat of the Catholic Church, was told about a strange object he calls the Magenta object and keeps a file on it, and it joined a working group of scientists from the SS, Nazi Germany's elite paramilitary force, and Italian scientists who studied the object in a third country, which the story places in Czechoslovakia between the 1930s and the 1940s. The researcher Jason Jorjani tells this without naming his source, though he links it to the claims of a witness named David Grusch. If true, it would mean the Church and two wartime powers secretly studied the same object together.
vela-incident-labeled-the-747-incident-1: In 1979 a Vela satellite, one of the US satellites built to spot nuclear tests, recorded a flash over the South Atlantic that has been linked to South Africa or Israel, and according to a former CIA officer named Rolf Mowatt-Larssen, insiders labeled it "the 747 incident". He says he heard this from an unnamed scientist at the US Department of Energy. The label suggests the event was handled under a cover name inside government.
velikovsky-s-when-worlds-collide-the-ast: The asteroid belt, the ring of rocks between Mars and Jupiter, is said to be the remains of a planet that was destroyed. The lawyer Danny Sheehan tells it, crediting the theory to the writer Immanuel Velikovsky and a book he names as When Worlds Collide, "an old classic" piece. If true, it would mean a whole world was once broken apart in our solar system.
vera-rubin-telescope-to-remove-classifie: The Vera Rubin Observatory, a large new telescope for surveying the sky, is said to be removing classified satellites and other objects from its data before anyone sees them. The astronomer Beatriz Villarroel relays this second hand. She says the telescope "is going to remove a lot of classified satellites and other objects." Michels tells it in another episode, citing an article in The Atlantic. He says "all of Rubin's imagery has to be approved by the Pentagon," the US defense department, at a secure facility in California. Both raise it because it would mean that what scientists can see in the sky is filtered by the military.
verichip-implant-raytheon-lineage-and-re: VeriChip, a tiny chip made to be implanted under human skin by the company Applied Digital Solutions, came to market in 2002 and has roots tied to the defense contractor Raytheon, according to Michels, who draws on the company's investor filings. He notes it came out "just a few years before Gary's experience in 2005," Gary being the hacker Gary McKinnon, who broke into NASA computers, and suggests the chip could have been part of retaliation against him. If true, it would mean the government used implant technology to punish someone who found its secrets.
vesuvius-quiet-since-1948-and-accumulati: Mount Vesuvius, the volcano near Naples in Italy, has not smoked since 1948, and so it is "accumulating energy". That is how a researcher named Filippo Biondi, who uses satellite radar to scan beneath ancient sites, puts it, offering it in passing without citing a source. The point, as he tells it, is that the long quiet is not a sign of safety but of pressure building up.
vial-of-gold-flakes-it-s-all-about-the-m: In 1996, at the Los Angeles offices of Dark Skies, a television series about UFOs, a man known as the captain is said to have slammed a small vial down on the desk and said to forget everything else, because it is all about the moon. A screenwriter named Brent Friedman tells Michels he was there: he picked up the vial and shook it like a snow globe, but there was no liquid in it, only what is described as flakes of gold.
victim-sees-ufo-lights-at-zorro-ranch-an: Around 2002, at Zorro Ranch in New Mexico, a property tied in the episode to the financier Jeffrey Epstein, a woman stepped outside for a cigarette, saw strange lights flying overhead, and later woke up in what she calls a lab. Juliet Byron, who presents herself as one of the victims there, tells it from her own experience: "I saw a weird like lights flying and then I had the weird thing waking up in the lab." If true, it would tie the ranch to both UFOs and experiments on people.
victor-bertrandius-witnesses-brown-s-gra: In Los Angeles in 1952, an Air Force lieutenant colonel from Wright Airfield, a base in Ohio, named Victor Bertrandias, later a general, is said to have watched the inventor Townsend Brown test his "gravitator," a device Brown hoped could move things without propellers or rockets, and said: "Believe it or not, I think I just saw a flying saucer and it frightened me." Michels tells this in several episodes, once citing a biography of Brown by the writer Paul Schatzkin; in another he calls it an unannounced visit to a demo at Brown's foundation and gives the quote as "I saw a model of a flying saucer," and in a third he gives only the 1950s and also names the officer Albert Boyd. If true, a senior officer saw something in Brown's work that looked like the saucers people were reporting.
victor-lagno-arxiv-paper-backs-pais-room: A scientist named Victor Lagno, from the Russian Academy of Sciences, posted a paper on arXiv, a public website where scientists share research, showing that the room-temperature superconductor Salvatore Pais designed could work in principle. A superconductor carries electricity with no loss, and normally only works when deeply cooled. Pais, a Navy scientist known for unusual patents, says this himself and complains that the patent examiner still refused to grant his patent.
video-of-bill-lear-at-bahnsen-s-labs-195: Michels says there is film from the 1950s of the aviation businessman Bill Lear visiting the North Carolina laboratory of the businessman Agnew Bahnson, where he watched the inventor Townsend Brown's 'gravitator' experiments, devices Brown hoped would move by electric force in a way like anti-gravity. Michels mentions the video himself, without saying where it can be found, in his 2024 documentary on Brown. He brings it up to show that serious industry figures took Brown's work seriously.
video-of-smoke-rising-from-the-water-abo: In 2011, at the spot in the Baltic Sea where treasure hunters found a strange object lying on the seabed, smoke is said to have risen from the water right above it, as if the object were fuming or giving off gas. Michels tells this himself in his episode with the treasure hunter Dennis Asberg, saying "we have video" of it. It is one of several odd happenings reported around the site, which would suggest the object is somehow still active.
video-of-the-surgeon-operating-on-the-al: There is said to be a video showing a doctor performing surgery on an alien creature in Varginha, a town in Brazil where beings were reportedly captured in 1996. Michels brings it up while interviewing Italo Venturelli, a surgeon who presents himself as a witness to the affair, noting that Venturelli has mentioned "multiple times that there is a video of him essentially performing surgery on this alien." Such a tape would be direct evidence that a living or dead non-human body was handled in a Brazilian hospital.
video-of-townsend-brown-celebrating-at-u: There are said to be videos of an American inventor named Thomas Townsend Brown at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, celebrating because his experiments had apparently worked. The story places this in the 1950s. Michels tells it himself without naming the source of the footage, and he takes the celebration as a hint that Brown's unusual experiments, which his episode connects to strange flying objects, got results.
vietnam-veteran-on-shooting-at-spooks: A soldier in Vietnam once warned that firing at the strange things out there was pointless: you think you are shooting at somebody, but you hit nothing and just waste your ammunition. Michael Johnson, a guest on an episode about Air Force veterans who say they were taken by aliens, repeats it as something "a guy in Vietnam told me." The point is that soldiers may have faced things bullets could not touch.
vietnam-veteran-s-survivor-guilt: A Vietnam veteran who had been in a firefight carried deep guilt over having survived it. Greg Rogers, a doctor who worked for NASA, tells the story second-hand. The man was a patient Rogers saw when he was a very young doctor, and Rogers shares it to show how such experiences stay with a person.
view-from-the-ship-s-porthole-of-a-fiery: A former president of a Russian republic named Kiran Ilum Xenov says that when he was taken aboard an alien ship in 1997, he looked out of a porthole and saw something like a fiery planet giving off heat. He says, telling it as his own experience, that beings were taking out cylinders, or more like boxes, from there and loading them into the ship.
viewer-s-theory-that-the-stranger-was-a-: A viewer named Vince has a theory about a mysterious stranger that Geoffrey Drumm says he met in Egypt: the stranger was a kachina, a spirit being from the traditions of Native peoples of the American Southwest. Drumm, a researcher who says an alien explained the true purpose of the pyramids to him, repeats the viewer's words: "That's a kachina that came to make sure you were on the right path." If so, the stranger was a guide sent to keep Drumm's work on track.
viking-lander-life-tests-read-as-finding: In 1976 the Viking landers, NASA spacecraft that set down on Mars, ran experiments meant to detect life in the soil and got mixed results, which a researcher named John Brandenburg says can now be read as having found life. Brandenburg gives this as his own interpretation, without naming a source. If he is right, life on Mars would have been detected nearly fifty years ago.
viking-landing-at-cydonia-overruled-by-a: In 1976, as NASA chose where its Viking landers would touch down on Mars, the scientists picking the site near Cydonia, a region of Mars, are said to have been suddenly overruled by a group on the project they did not even know existed. The plasma physicist John Brandenburg tells it, calling it "kind of scandalous". If true, it would mean a hidden group steered where NASA looked on Mars.
viking-orbiter-image-of-the-face-on-mars: In the mid 1970s NASA's Viking orbiters, spacecraft circling Mars, sent back an image of a mile-long structure in the Cydonia region that looked like a human face, and it caused quite a stir. Michels tells this himself in introducing an episode about life on Mars, as a hint that something built may once have stood there.
villager-shoots-a-silver-suited-hovering: In 2023, in the Alto Nanay region of the Peruvian Amazon, a villager says he was attacked by a figure in a silver suit that hovered in the air, and he shot it with a shotgun. The researcher and filmmaker Tim Alberino passes on what the man told him: "I shot him at point blank range with a shotgun," and the man said he heard the pellets ping off armor as the blast knocked the figure onto its backside. If true, it would mean the attackers wore something like armor that could stop gunfire.
villarroel-approached-by-people-she-susp: In 2025, in Stockholm, the astronomer Beatriz Villarroel says people she suspects have intelligence backgrounds have approached her. Villarroel studies old sky images and speaks of huge numbers of unexplained objects around Earth. She tells this from her own experience, which suggests her research has caught the attention of spy agencies.
villarroel-on-multiple-transients-appear: On old photographic glass plates of the night sky taken at the Palomar Observatory in California in the 1950s, several points of light sometimes appear and then vanish within half an hour, according to the astronomer Beatriz Villarroel. She tells Jesse Michels this from her own study of the plates, which she has searched for such short-lived flashes. If real, they would be objects in the sky that no known star or planet explains.
villarroel-s-palomar-transients-1949: Old photographic plates from Palomar Observatory in California, taken between 1949 and 1957, before Sputnik, the first satellite, show tens of thousands of brief points of light, called transients, that Michels describes as flat, mirror-like objects orbiting the Earth, sometimes appearing to cluster near nuclear sites and tests. The finding belongs to the astronomer Beatriz Villarroel of Stockholm University, and Michels repeats it many times, giving counts that range from 10,000 a year to more than 100,000, and adding that the lights drop off inside the Earth's shadow, which he offers against the idea that they are flaws on the plates. Villarroel herself puts the sample at about 105,000 transients from the northern hemisphere alone and says 30 to 35 percent of them come from sunlight reflecting off something, which, if they are objects, would mean things were circling the Earth before anyone had launched one.
villarroel-transients-on-1950s-plates-co: Brief points of light, called transients, appear and then vanish on photographic plates from the Palomar sky survey, a 1950s photographic map of the night sky. According to a study, they turn up more often around the time of nuclear bomb tests. Michels says the work of the astronomer Beatriz Villarroel found them '68% more likely to show up within 24 hours of a nuclear detonation.' Villarroel and the Vanderbilt researcher Steven Bruel, who wrote the paper in the journal Scientific Reports, tell it more cautiously. Bruel says almost 19% of days after a test have a transient, and Villarroel calls the link 'weak, but it's there and it's statistically significant'. They also tie it to UFO reports in a catalogue kept by the Center for UFO Studies. If true, it would suggest something in orbit was paying attention to nuclear tests.
villarroel-transients-on-july-1952-plate: Old photographic plates of the night sky from July 1952 show points of light that appear and then vanish, according to the astronomer Beatriz Villarroel, who studies these short-lived "transients" herself. She describes one plate from 27 July 1952 showing five objects in a narrow band, and another from 19 July 1952 where her colleague Enrique found three of them together, a "triple transient." She also credits colleagues she names as Dave Altman and Lash, and Michels repeats the same examples on another episode. If these are real objects, they would be things in the sky before anyone had launched a satellite.
vimanas-and-self-guiding-arrows-in-the-v: The Vedic texts, India's ancient Hindu scriptures, describe vimanas, flying vehicles, along with arrows that could steer themselves to a target. Greg Rogers, a doctor who says he once saw a UFO in a secret hangar, brings this up as a researcher would, without naming a source. He offers it as a hint that ancient peoples may have known about flying craft.
vinod-s-hidden-background-as-friend-of-g: A man known as Dr. Vinod, who turns up in the early 1950s in a story about a CIA scientist contacting an alien council, had a background that stayed hidden: he was a professor in Bombay and a friend of Gandhi, the leader of India's independence movement. The researcher Greg Malatzi brings this up in passing, as a near question, without naming a source. If true, the man at the centre of that contact story had far deeper roots than most people knew.
viracocha-and-lake-titicaca-as-a-mirror-: At Lake Titicaca in Bolivia and Peru, near the ancient ruins of Tiwanaku and Puma Punku, there is a figure of Viracocha, a creator god of the Andes, holding a condor on either side. A researcher of ancient civilizations named Matt LaCroix says this is the same idea as the pillars "holding balance" found around Lake Van, a lake in eastern Turkey, and sees the two places as mirror civilizations. He gives it as his own reading, without naming a source, and if he is right it would point to a shared lost tradition on opposite sides of the world.
virk-advises-the-galileo-project-and-the: In the 2020s, the computer scientist Rizwan Virk, who is linked to MIT, became an advisor to the Galileo Project, a scientific effort that uses telescopes and sensors to look for signs of alien technology. He was also loosely involved with the Sol Project, a Stanford group studying unexplained phenomena. Virk says this about himself, telling Michels "I'm an advisor to the Galileo Project," to show that he works with serious scientific attempts to study the subject.
vision-foretelling-the-attempt-on-trump-: An unnamed speaker in a clip played on the episode with Eric Wargo, a writer on seeing the future, says he had a vision of an attempt on Donald Trump's life in which a bullet flew so close by Trump's ear that it "busted his drum." He tells it as something he saw before it happened in 2024, which if true would be a case of foreseeing the future.
vision-of-a-rocket-exploding-at-launch-1: Sometime between 1990 and 1993, while on duty in a work van at his base, Dan Sherman says he had a vision of a missile being launched and blowing up, possibly a Chinese rocket. Sherman, a former Air Force sergeant who says the National Security Agency, the US spy agency, hired him to talk with aliens, tells it as his own experience and in his book Above Black, as a sign that the contact also showed him real events.
visit-to-allen-dulles-s-former-office-in: On a visit to the old office in Switzerland of Allen Dulles, the American spymaster who later ran the CIA, Swiss officials are said to have told visitors that Dulles had boasted that as long as he was in Switzerland, "no American law could reach him." The former presidential advisor Harald Malmgren tells this, repeating what the Swiss officials told his group. It is told to suggest Dulles worked beyond the reach of his own government.
visit-to-drew-s-house-and-his-needle-and: In 2016, a NASA engineer named Charles Buhler says he and his wife Janessa spent four or five hours at the Florida home of an inventor named Andrew Arjima, known as Drew, studying a setup Drew had built from a needle and Teflon. Buhler says his wife was the one who saw the link between the forces at work. He tells it as something he saw himself, and he presents it as part of the road to what he calls antigravity propulsion, a way to move without pushing against anything.
visit-to-the-antikythera-mechanism: The owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a property famous for reports of strange events, says he recently went to Athens, Greece, to see the Antikythera mechanism, an ancient geared device found in the sea. He tells it as his own trip, in an episode where he speaks about the ranch. In his words: "I recently went to Athens, Greece to see the Antikythera mechanism."
visit-to-the-pantex-pits-1980: In the 1980s, John S. Herrington, who was US Secretary of Energy, went down into the pits at Pantex, the Texas plant where America's nuclear weapons are put together. He tells Michels about it himself: "I've been in Pantex. I've been down in the pits." He brings it up to show how close he got to the most secret parts of the nuclear program.
visit-to-the-serapeum-of-saqqara-and-its: The scientist Filippo Biondi, known for scanning beneath the pyramids, says he went into the Serapeum of Saqqara in Egypt, an ancient site known for its precisely made boxes, for the first time in 2025. He tells it as his own visit, alongside his work on what he describes as structures beneath the pyramids.
visitor-calls-strieber-the-luckiest-of-t: In the 1980s, during what he calls an abduction experience, the writer Whitley Strieber says one of the beings he calls "the visitors" told him, "You're the luckiest of the lucky." Strieber tells this as his own experience, and he presents his contact with these beings as a gift rather than a curse.
visitors-appear-when-anne-s-chosen-group: Between the late 1980s and the late 1990s, at a cabin in upstate New York, beings the family called the visitors are said to have shown up whenever certain groups gathered there. The writer Whitley Strieber tells Michels this from his own experience, saying it happened when his wife, Anne Strieber, brought her chosen groups up to the cabin.
visitors-base-under-the-mountains-at-dul: Visitors from elsewhere had already picked out a place to live under the mountains at Dulce, a town in New Mexico. Mario Woods, an Air Force veteran who says he was abducted by aliens, tells it as something that somebody told him long ago. If true, it would mean these visitors keep a home base here on Earth.
visitors-confirm-kennedy-ufo-connection-: In 1996, visitors came to the Los Angeles offices of Dark Skies, a TV series about a hidden history of UFOs, and told the makers that the show's link between President Kennedy and UFOs was correct. Bryce Zabel, a writer and producer behind the show, says he was there. He names the visitors only as JC and "the captain," and tells Michels that "definitely the Kennedy and UFOs were correct," which would mean the show's fiction came close to something real.
vitrification-evidence-of-ancient-nuclea: The philosopher Jason Jorjani says there is evidence of nuclear wars in the deep past, pointing to vitrification, rock and earth melted into glass, at various ancient sites. He mentions it in passing on the show and does not name the sites or a source. If true, it would mean a lost civilisation had nuclear weapons long before recorded history.
vitrified-basalt-blocks-at-kef-kalesi-co: A researcher of ancient sites named Matt LaCroix says the basalt stone blocks at Kef Kalesi, near Lake Van in Turkey, show "literal melting of the stone," and that the geologist Dr Robert Schoch confirmed on numerous stones that it is vitrification, meaning rock turned glassy by great heat. LaCroix tells it from his own visit, and if true it would mean the ancient walls were once hit by heat strong enough to melt rock.
vivex-biograft-based-on-recovered-metal-: In the 2010s, a medical material called a biograft, a substance placed in the body to help bone regrow, was made from metal recovered from a crashed craft. That is what Chris Bledsoe says. He is a man who says UFOs appear around him, and he tells it as something he was close to, naming a man called Timothy Taylor in connection with it. If true, material from a crash would have been turned into medicine.
voice-in-a-dream-urges-him-to-speak-1997: One night after his 1997 encounter, a voice came to him in his sleep and asked, "What are you afraid of? Why aren't you speaking? You met with us, didn't you?" So says Kiran Ilum Xenov, billed on the episode as a former president of one of Russia's republics. He tells it as his own experience, saying it pushed him to speak publicly about being taken by aliens.
voice-in-masters-head-behind-morton-hall: While standing behind Morton Hall at Ohio University, Mike Masters heard a small voice in his head suggesting a new way to explore the UFO question. Masters is a researcher who argues that the visitors may be humans from the future, and he tells Michels about the moment himself: "there was this little voice in my head that said maybe we should explore it this way." He treats it as the spark for his whole line of thinking.
voice-of-god-microwave-hearing-program: There is said to be a secret government program that uses microwave beams to make a person hear sound inside their head, and even to carry a spoken voice. Insiders reportedly call it the "Voice of God." The main account comes from Eric Haseltine, presented on the show as a former director at the National Security Agency, the US spy agency that intercepts communications. He says such beams can "create vibrations like sound," and that "there's a program to modulate that with voice. We call it the voice of God." He credits a document called The Shadow of Time. If true, it would mean the government can put words into someone's head with no speaker in the room. A second teller, a Pentagon whistleblower named Matthew Brown, tells it differently. He calls the crudest of these technologies by its public name, "voice to skull," and says he never saw it himself on the inside, where he knew it by another term. Neither man gives a date or a place.
volunteering-at-the-murrah-building-afte: A former scientist at DARPA, the Pentagon's agency for advanced research, named John Blitch says he volunteered at the Murrah Federal Building in Oklahoma City after it was bombed in 1995. In his telling, he remembers a piece of purple chiffon material from his time there, though he says little more about it.
von-braun-captured-in-bavaria-under-oper: In 1945 the German rocket engineer Wernher von Braun was captured in Bavaria, in southern Germany, and his record was then "scrubbed", or cleaned up. This happened under Operation Paperclip, the American programme that brought German scientists to the United States after the Second World War. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, and adds that a young Henry Kissinger, later one of America's best-known diplomats, was helping to run counterintelligence (the work of catching enemy spies) for the United States in that same area. He tells it to show that the American space effort began by quietly taking in men from Hitler's Germany.
von-braun-collecting-lunar-meteorites-in: In the 1960s, according to this story, the rocket engineer Wernher von Braun went to Antarctica to pick up meteorites that had come from the Moon, before anyone had gone to the Moon, and there is said to be a picture of this on the internet. A guest named Bart Sibrel tells it, without naming a source, alongside a claim involving a NASA ceramics lab and an unnamed contractor. His point is that rocks presented as Moon samples could have been gathered on Earth.
von-braun-encourages-mitchell-s-consciou: In the 1970s, the rocket engineer Wernher von Braun is said to have strongly backed the astronaut Edgar Mitchell's interest in studying human consciousness, and even urged him to find a place inside NASA, the US space agency, to do the research. Michels tells this second-hand, as Mitchell's own account. It would mean a top figure of the space program took the study of the mind seriously.
von-braun-in-puharich-s-circle-in-the-19: In the 1960s, the rocket engineer Wernher von Braun is said to have been in regular contact with Puharich, a scientist who, as the episode tells it, worked with the CIA and believed he had contacted an alien council. A researcher named Greg Malatzi passes this on from Puharich's assistant, the same person he says made a remark about President Kennedy, who told him von Braun "talked to him, you know, all the time." It would put one of America's top space engineers inside a circle that was chasing contact with beings from elsewhere.
von-braun-oversaw-slave-labor-camp-1940: Michels says that Wernher von Braun, the German rocket engineer later brought to the United States to build rockets, oversaw a brutal slave labor camp in 1940s Germany, whose prisoners were mostly Jewish and where very many died. He says this himself, without naming a source, in his 2023 interview with David Grusch, a former intelligence officer who went public about UFO secrets. He raises it as a reminder of the kind of men the American government was willing to take in after the war.
von-braun-passing-secrets-at-the-mexican: There is a story that the German rocket engineer Wernher von Braun handed over secret technical information at the border with Mexico, placed around 1945. Michels mentions it in passing during a talk with a guest named Peter Levenda, hedging that he thinks there is "some story" of this and naming no source. If true, it would mean one of the most important scientists brought to America was leaking its secrets.
von-braun-rudolph-and-the-nazi-transplan: NASA's Saturn rocket program, which built the giant rockets for the American Moon missions, was in effect the Nazi German space program moved to the United States. That is how Michels puts it in three different episodes: the German rocket engineers Wernher von Braun and Arthur Rudolph, together with 129 Nazi scientists, were "literally" the whole program. Michels tells it himself without naming a source, once calling the idea a "conspiracy" and leaving out the figure of 129, and he raises it to show how much secret wartime knowledge shaped American technology.
von-braun-s-deathbed-warning-about-a-sta: The rocket engineer Wernher von Braun is said to have warned, near the end of his life in 1977, that powerful people planned to fake an alien threat to unite the world. Steven Greer, a campaigner for UFO disclosure, says von Braun told this on his deathbed to his friend Carol Rosin, and in one telling calls it a false flag and dates von Braun's death to 1974. Michels also mentions von Braun talking about this at the end of his life, though he garbles the name of the woman as Carolyn Ross. If true, it would mean a future alien invasion could be staged on purpose.
von-braun-s-team-passed-data-to-argentin: In the late 1940s, the team of Wernher von Braun, the German rocket engineer brought to work for the United States after the war, crossed from Texas into Mexican border towns to meet Nazi contacts arriving from Argentina and hand them batches of data. The researcher Jason Jorjani tells this without naming a source. If true, Nazi networks were still trading rocket secrets after the war, right under American eyes.
von-braun-s-time-magazine-figure-for-the: In the 1960s the rocket engineer Wernher von Braun, talking about Moon facts in Time magazine, is said to have given a figure for the neutral gravity point, the spot between Earth and Moon where their pulls cancel out, that was about double the officially stated distance. The comedian Kurt Metzger repeats this from the author Joseph P. Farrell, as a hint that what the public was told about the Moon may not match what the experts knew.
von-braun-shows-uri-geller-a-piece-of-a-: Uri Geller, a performer known for claiming psychic powers, says the rocket engineer Wernher von Braun once took him into his office, opened a safe, and took out a light piece of metal in a colour Geller had never seen. Geller says he touched it and said, "this is not from here," and von Braun replied, "You're right. This is a piece of a UFO that crashed on our planet." Geller tells it himself in several episodes, once placing it at a secret NASA base. Michels also retells it, dating it to the 1970s and linking it to a researcher named Andrija Puharich.
von-braun-tells-edgar-mitchell-of-his-kn: According to the Apollo astronaut Edgar Mitchell, the rocket engineer Wernher von Braun once came to him and said he had knowledge of UFOs. Michels passes this on as something Mitchell said, in a 2025 episode with Robert Salas, a former Air Force officer. If true, one of the leading figures of the American space programme would have privately claimed inside knowledge of the subject.
von-braun-transmitted-speech-to-carol-ro: In the 1970s the rocket engineer Wernher von Braun is said to have used a kind of mind-to-mind link to pass a speech he wanted given at a big conference to his spokesperson, a woman named Carol Rosin. The UFO activist Steven Greer tells it, relaying what he was told. If true, it would mean von Braun had some form of mental communication.
von-daniken-s-ancient-alien-gods-as-spac: Ancient gods are said to have really been alien astronauts arriving in spaceships, and ancient sites such as Easter Island are offered as traces of their visits. This is the idea made famous by the writer Erich von Däniken. Michels sets it out in a 2022 episode, naming von Däniken's book Chariots of the Gods, published in 1968. As he puts it, "ancient alien astronauts came down to Earth around 10,000 years ago at the time of the agrarian revolution", when people first took up farming, and "taught us how to basically start modern civilization." If true, it would mean that human civilization was handed down to us rather than built by us. The skeptic writer Michael Shermer also brings it up, in passing, during a 2026 debate with Michels. He sums it up as "the ancient alien gods that are actually, you know, spaceships", and ties it to the wider ancient-alien genre. Shermer gives no date and no detail of the supposed visit.
von-daniken-s-ancient-astronaut-reading-: The Nazca Lines, huge figures marked into the ground in Peru, were tributes to ancient alien astronauts in the view of Erich von Däniken, author of the book Chariots of the Gods. He believed these were an extraterrestrial group that seeded human civilization. Michels sums up this view himself in an episode about strange three-fingered bodies found in Peru.
von-neumann-paper-the-presence-must-be-b: In the 1950s, the mathematician John von Neumann is said to have written a paper arguing that the visiting presence could only enter our reality if enough people believed in it. The author Whitley Strieber, known for writing about his own encounters, tells Michels that such a paper "supposedly" exists and that he heard of it from Arthur Exon, an Air Force general who "was no scientist" but knew scientists working on the matter. The writer Greg Bishop recalls Strieber's version differently, as the reason the government and its secret panel, Majestic, kept things hidden: belief itself might let it in.
von-neumann-starts-talking-about-self-re: The mathematician John von Neumann is said to have suddenly begun talking about machines that can build copies of themselves, now called von Neumann machines, in 1948, one year after Roswell, the 1947 New Mexico incident where many say a crashed flying saucer was recovered. The researcher Deep Prasad says that before then von Neumann's lectures had nothing to do with such ideas, and then he was talking about them like it was his job. Another, unnamed guest on the same episode says the same, adding 1949. On an episode titled AI Is ALIEN Technology, the timing is offered as a hint that the idea came from studying something recovered at Roswell.
vought-flying-pancake-as-early-saucer-at: The Flying Pancake, a round, flat American aircraft built by the Vought company in the 1940s, was, as one guest puts it, "literally" an early attempt to build a flying saucer with propellers. A researcher named Dan Sheehan says this in passing, without naming a source. He tells it as part of a wider story about how the US government's interest in saucer-shaped craft goes back to the war years.
voyager-1-reaches-one-light-day-on-the-a: Michels points out that on November 18, 2026, at 3:16 a.m. Mountain time, the space probe Voyager 1 will be exactly one light day from Earth, that is, as far as light travels in a day. He says this falls exactly 49 years after two Air Force veterans, whom the episode calls Mario and Michael, say they blacked out aboard a spacecraft in 1977. He offers the coincidence himself, in a 2026 episode reuniting the two men, as a striking echo of their abduction.
voyager-golden-record-carrying-the-navaj: In 1977 each of the two Voyager space probes was sent off carrying a golden record holding the sights and sounds of Earth, among them the Navajo Night Chant, a Native American ceremonial song. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, as an example of humanity sending a message to whoever might be out there.
voyager-golden-record-music-selection-ba: While the team was choosing music for the Golden Record, a disc of sounds and music sent into space on NASA's Voyager probes in the late 1970s, someone said they had to put Bach on it, and someone else answered that this "would just be bragging." The skeptic Michael Shermer tells it as his favorite story about the record. He says he heard it in the audio version of a book about the record, and he names the astronomer Carl Sagan and a woman called Annie among the people who made it.
vril-society-channels-anti-gravity-techn: In Germany between the 1920s and 1940s, a group called the Vril Society is said to have received secret knowledge from unseen beings through psychic contact. Michels tells it himself as a claim he has come across: the group is "said to have channeled anti-gravity technology and psychic powers from an ancient subterranean race," meaning a people living underground. The researcher Jason Jorjani, a guest who talks about Nazi UFO stories, tells it without naming a source, and in his version it is a group of mediums, mostly women, in telepathic contact with "basically a group of supermen." He does not mention the anti-gravity technology or the underground race. If true, it would mean some of Germany's strange science came from contact with something not human.
waking-with-three-bruises-on-the-arm-aft: In 2013, in Fort Collins, Colorado, a man is said to have woken up with three bruises on his arm after a visit by non-human beings that he had been expecting. The man is John Blitch, a scientist who worked for DARPA, the Pentagon's agency for advanced research, and he tells it as his own experience. If true, it would mean the visits he describes left marks on his body.
walker-and-the-cosmos-club: The UFO researcher Grant Cameron says that a man named Eric A. Walker was one of the people he and others discovered to be connected with the Cosmos Club, a private club in Washington, D.C. Cameron mentions it briefly as a finding of his research, without naming a source or saying more about what Walker did there. He brings it up because it would tie Walker to a circle of people involved in the government's handling of UFOs.
walker-how-do-you-know-they-didn-t-get-u: In 1987, when Grant Cameron asked Eric A. Walker about the dead bodies said to be held by MJ12, Walker answered: "How do you know they're dead? You assume too many things and they're all wrong. How do you know they didn't get up and walk away?" Cameron is a UFO researcher, MJ12 is a secret panel said to have managed the UFO question for the US government, and Cameron says he heard Walker say it himself. If Walker meant it, the beings would not have been dead at all.
walker-letter-worked-on-defense-policy-w: In a letter, the engineer and scientist Eric A. Walker wrote: 'I worked on defense policy in 1947 with Vannevar Bush,' a top science adviser to the US government. The UFO researcher Grant Cameron cites the letter, which he does not date, as proof that Walker was placed close to the people said to have handled crashed UFOs that year.
wall-street-journal-emp-explanation-for-: A Wall Street Journal article by the reporter Joel Schectman, put by the tellers in 2025, claimed that the 1967 incidents at Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana were a secret test, not a UFO event. At the base, nuclear missiles reportedly went offline while a glowing object was seen overhead. The article said the cause was an electromagnetic pulse, a burst of energy that destroys electronics, and that the device was wheeled up to the base to see whether America's own nuclear weapons could be shut down with people present. Michels tells it himself and rejects it, calling the piece disinformation and a test like that dangerous, reckless and without precedent. He also says a former Pentagon official named Sean Kirkpatrick was probably its only source.
wall-street-journal-op-ed-and-david-sper: Michels says that in 2024 his friend Karl Nell, who represented the Army on a government task force studying unidentified flying objects, wrote an opinion piece on UFOs with a former Secretary of Defense for The Wall Street Journal, and that Michels lobbied for it himself, even meeting the opinion editor, Lena Bell, at the paper's headquarters. He says the paper turned it down, and that Bell told him a man named David Spergel acts as their unofficial UFO advisor and says UFOs are all "space trash, light reflections, and temperature inversions." Michels tells it first-hand, citing his emails with the paper, as a sign that a major newspaper was leaning on one dismissive voice to keep the subject out.
wally-wallington-builds-a-stonehenge-in-: A man named Wally Wallington set up his own copy of Stonehenge, the ancient circle of huge standing stones in England, in his backyard and did it by himself. A researcher named Luke Caverns brings this up from Wallington's own videos, in a talk about how the pyramids were built, as a sign that one person can move giant stones without modern machines.
walrus-artwork-on-epstein-s-wall-2002: In 2002, a large artwork showing a woman being raped by a walrus hung on a wall at one of Jeffrey Epstein's properties. Epstein was a wealthy financier. The story comes from Jay Anderson, who passes on what he was told by a witness named Juliet Byron, and he tells it as a glimpse of the dark world around Epstein.
walter-b-smith-1953-letter-on-using-the-: In 1953, the story goes, Walter B. Smith, then head of the CIA, wrote that the US should use the UFO phenomenon for psychological warfare against the Soviets, playing up the sightings to unsettle them during the Cold War. Michels tells this himself in three episodes and says there are similar leaked letters from Allen Dulles, another CIA chief. In one telling he is less sure, calling it a memo, dating it to 1952 or 1953, and saying only that Smith asked how to use the phenomenon. If it is true, the US government saw UFOs as a weapon of persuasion.
walter-dornberger-at-wright-patterson-wh: Walter Dornberger, who ran Nazi Germany's rocket work at its Peenemünde research site, had Wright-Patterson, an Air Force base in Ohio, as his first American posting, and he was there in 1947 when debris from the Roswell crash, the wreckage found near Roswell, New Mexico, came in by train. The researcher Peter Levenda tells this without naming a source. If true, a top German rocket man was on hand when that wreckage arrived.
walter-haut-s-posthumous-affidavit-craft: An Army lieutenant named Walter Haut left a sworn statement, to be released only after his death, saying he had seen a crashed craft and bodies under a tarp at Roswell, New Mexico, in 1947. Michels brings this up himself while debating a skeptic. He points to the statement as one of the witness accounts that would mean something real came down at Roswell, if it is true.
wang-s-belongings-removed-from-his-house: When a man named Eric Henry Wang died, people came and took a lot of things out of his house, according to the writer and researcher Greg Bishop. Bishop says it briefly on Michels' show, without naming a source or saying who "they" were, and the hint is that someone wanted whatever Wang had kept.
war-department-asks-fbi-to-clear-gebauer: Around 1942 and 1943, the War Department, as the US military's home department was then called, is said to have asked the FBI under J. Edgar Hoover to give security clearance to a man named Leo Gaybower, also spelled GeBauer. A crash researcher named Scott Ramsey says he found this in Gaybower's FBI file, and takes it to mean the man "worked on some kind of topshelf project." It is told to show Gaybower had serious secret wartime work.
wargo-s-theory-that-remote-viewers-see-t: The writer Eric Wargo suggests that remote viewers, people trained in a US government psychic spy programme from the 1970s to the 1990s to describe distant places with their minds, may really be seeing the feedback they will be shown later, when they learn what the target was. Wargo offers this as his own theory. Michels adds that he spoke with Hal Puthoff, whom he calls the founder of the CIA psychic spy programme, and that Puthoff was open to Wargo being right that this later confirmation is needed for remote viewing to work. If so, the mind would be reaching into its own future rather than across space.
warning-call-after-a-howard-stern-produc: A former Air Force sergeant named Dan Sherman, who says the NSA, the US spy agency for intercepted communications, hired him to talk with aliens, says that after a producer from the Howard Stern radio show called him, a second call came telling him to drop the story, stay off the Stern show and stop talking about it. Sherman tells it as something that happened to him in his office, which if true would mean someone was watching who he spoke to and wanted him silent.
warning-not-to-disturb-the-earth-2016: Around 2016, Brandon Fugal, the owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property known for reports of strange events, says he got a warning: "when you disturb the earth, negative things happen." He tells Michels he was told this by someone else and passes it on. It matters because it suggests that digging on the ranch might bring on whatever is happening there.
wartime-intelligence-agencies-run-by-fin: During the Second World War, besides the better-known American spy agency, there was another US intelligence agency devoted to South America, the Office for the Coordination of Inter-American Affairs, according to the researcher Jason Simosa. He tells Jesse Michels this from his own research, naming figures such as William Donovan, Allen Dulles, Nelson Rockefeller, William Stephenson and Charles Hambro, and argues that wartime intelligence in the US and Britain was run largely by financiers. He raises it to suggest that private wealth and state secrecy have long been tangled together.
was-condon-blackmailed-by-fbi-agent-guy-: Michels raises the idea that Edward Condon, a scientist who publicly dismissed UFOs, may have been blackmailed into doing so. He says, without naming a source, that while Condon was being investigated in the 1950s for communist sympathies, an agent of the FBI, the US federal police agency, named Guy Hottel was quietly building a file of field reports on him in the background. If true, it would mean the scientific case against UFOs was shaped by pressure from the government.
was-randy-shown-alien-technology-as-a-re: A guest named Randy Anderson, a weapons expert, says he saw alien technology at a US military base, and Michels wonders whether he was shown it on purpose. The test, as Michels imagines it, would be whether Anderson could work out how the object functioned on the spot, as a way of seeing how an enemy might react if it ever got such technology. This is Michels's own guess, offered as a question rather than as anything Anderson was told.
washington-post-lucky-to-be-alive-articl: In 2001 the Washington Post ran an article called "Lucky to be alive" that told the stories of people who did not go to work in New York on the day of the September 11 attacks. The biologist Rupert Sheldrake brings it up as he talks about people who seem to sense danger before it comes, since if such stories hold, some people may have a feeling for what is about to happen.
washington-post-reporter-hunts-for-infor: A reporter at the Washington Post began hunting for information on the US government's secret program that used psychics to spy. A former Army psychic spy named Joe McMoneagle mentions this in passing, as part of how the program started to draw outside attention.
washington-quickly-ordered-roswell-bottl: When the Roswell crash happened in New Mexico in 1947, Washington reacted within a very short time and ordered the whole matter bottled up, according to Kurt McConnell, a former US Senate staffer. He tells it without naming a source and notes that the crash only allegedly happened. If true, it would mean the highest levels of government took the event seriously from the very first.
watchers-flew-to-mount-hermon-in-advance: The Watchers, fallen angels who come down to the summit of Mount Hermon in the ancient religious text the Book of Enoch, may really have arrived 'at the helms of advanced aerospace vehicles', what would be called UFOs today. That is the reading of the researcher Tim Alberino, who works from R. H. Charles's English translation of the book. He makes the point twice in the same conversation, as his own belief, and it would turn an old religious story into a record of a visit by flying craft.
watching-a-test-flight-with-john-lear-an: On 22 March 1989, Bob Lazar says he took the pilot John Lear and his friend Gene Huff to a spot about eight miles east of Groom Lake, Nevada, a secret government test site, to watch a craft fly. He says he knew it would fly on a Wednesday night because he had the test flight schedule. Lear's own recording from that night begins, "This is John Lear and today is March 22nd, 1989," and the researcher Grant Cameron adds that they drove there in Lear's motor home and filmed the craft.
watching-the-original-knapplazar-area-51: In 1989 a Las Vegas television reporter named George Knapp aired interviews with a man named Bob Lazar, who said he had worked on alien craft at Area 51, a secret military test site in Nevada. The writer Peter Levenda tells Michels he watched that original broadcast as it happened, and recalls that at the time no one knew what any of it meant.
watching-watergate-hearings-at-the-gold-: In 1973 a lawyer named Dan Sheehan says he sat in the Gold Key Motel in Washington with his investigator, William Johnstone Taylor, watching the Senate hearings into the Watergate scandal, the break-in affair that shook the Nixon White House, while the famous defense lawyer F. Lee Bailey made a call from a pay phone. Sheehan tells it as something he was there for, and he names others around the scene, including the lawyer Gerald Alch, a man named Andy Toney, and the senators Daniel Inouye and Sam Ervin. He tells it as a small first-hand piece of how the people behind the scenes of the scandal were moving.
